It is these whom He, exalted is His remembrance, meant by His saying: ﴿And among the people are those who say, "We believe in God and the Last Day," but they are not believers﴾, meaning by His statement, related as information about them: "We believed in God," that is: "We affirmed God."[[In the printed edition: "and we affirmed God." The added *wa* is an error.]]

We have already shown that the meaning of *iman* (faith) is *tasdiq* (affirmation/assent), in what has passed earlier in this book.[[See what has passed, pp. 234–235.]]

His saying: ﴿and the Last Day﴾ means: the Resurrection on the Day of Judgment. The Day of Judgment was called "the Last Day" only because it is the last day, after which there is no other day.

If someone says: How could there be no day after it, when the Hereafter has no end, no extinction, and no cessation? It is said: With the Arabs, a day is called a day only with the night that precedes it. So if no night precedes the daytime, it is not called a day. The Day of Resurrection is a day with no night after it, except the night in whose morning the Resurrection occurs; that day is therefore the last of the days. For this reason God, exalted is His praise, named it "the Last Day," and described it as "barren" (*'aqim*). He described it as a barren day because there is no night after it.[[This is the saying of our Lord, glorified is He, in Surat al-Hajj (22:55): ﴿And those who disbelieve will not cease to be in doubt about it until the Hour comes upon them suddenly, or there comes to them the punishment of a barren day.﴾]]

As for the interpretation of His saying: "and they are not believers," and His negation from them, exalted is His remembrance, of the name of faith, although He has informed of them that they have said with their tongues, "We believe in God and the Last Day": this is a denial from God, exalted and mighty is He, of what they reported of their belief in faith and their acknowledgment of the Resurrection, and an informing from Him to His Prophet (ﷺ) that what they show him with their mouths is contrary to what is in the hearts of their minds, and opposite to what is in the resolutions of their souls.

In this verse there is clear evidence against the falsehood claimed by the Jahmiyyah: that faith is only affirmation by speech, to the exclusion of all other meanings besides it. God, exalted is His praise, has informed about those of the hypocrites mentioned in His Book, that they said with their tongues, "We believe in God and the Last Day," then He negated from them that they were believers, since their belief did not affirm what they said.

His saying: "and they are not believers," meaning: "they are not affirmers" (*musaddiqin*), in what they claim to affirm.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 9:

The interpretation of His words, may His praise be exalted: ﴿They seek to deceive Allah and those who believe﴾

Abu Ja'far said: The deception of the hypocrite toward his Lord and the believers is his displaying, with his tongue, words of assent and affirmation, contrary to what is in his heart of doubt and denial, so that he may ward off from himself, by what he displays with his tongue, the ruling of Allah, mighty and majestic, which applies to one who is in a state like his of denial, if he had not displayed with his tongue what he displayed of affirmation and acknowledgment: namely killing and taking captive. That is his deceiving his Lord and the people of faith in Allah.

If someone says: How can the hypocrite be a deceiver of Allah and of the believers, when he only displays with his tongue what is contrary to what he believes, out of taqiyya (precautionary dissimulation)?

It is said: The Arabs do not refuse to call one who gives with his tongue something other than what is in his heart "taqiyya," so that he may escape what he fears, and thereby escapes what he feared, deceiving the one from whom he has been saved by the taqiyya he displayed to him. Likewise the hypocrite is called a deceiver of Allah and of the believers, by his displaying with his tongue what he displayed as taqiyya, whereby he is saved from killing, captivity and immediate punishment, while he conceals something other than what he displayed. And that is of his doing, and although it is a deception of the believers in the immediate life of this world, he is a deceiver of himself by that doing, because he shows to himself by that doing of his, that he gives it its wish, and gives it the cup of its joy, while he is bringing it to the pools of its ruin, and making it drink the cup of its punishment, and making it taste the wrath of Allah and His painful punishment, which it has no power to bear. [[In the printed edition: "ومذيقها من غضب الله"; in the manuscript: "ومربدها..."; in Tafsir Ibn Kathir 1:87: "ومز برها..."; the correct reading is what we have adopted. Azarahu means: to make him visit. In the hadith of Talha: "...until Shu'ub visited him," and Shu'ub is death, i.e. death brought him and he visited it. He made it a visit, though it is destruction.]] This is mockery of them and derision, for the ugliness of their delusion regarding their Lord, and their joy at the life, wealth and provision extended to them. So that is his deceiving himself, supposing, despite his harming himself in the matter of his return, that he is doing good to himself, as He, may His praise be exalted, said: "And they deceive none but themselves, and they perceive not" — informing His believing servants that the hypocrites, by harming themselves through angering their Lord with their disbelief, doubt and denial, are neither aware nor discerning, but they remain in blindness regarding their affair.

In a manner similar to what we have said regarding the interpretation of this, Ibn Zayd used to say.

320 — Yunus b. Abd al-A'la related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: I asked Abd al-Rahman b. Zayd about His words, dhikruhu: ﴿They seek to deceive Allah and those who believe﴾ to the end of the verse. He said: These are the hypocrites: they deceive Allah, His Messenger and those who believe, by claiming that they are believers in what they displayed. [[Report 320 is in al-Durr al-Manthur 1:30 and al-Shawkani 1:30 in full; its completion comes in the interpretation of the rest of the verse under no. 321.]]

This verse is among the clearest proofs against the claim of those who assert that Allah does not punish any of His servants except those who disbelieve in Him out of obstinacy, after knowing His oneness, and after the established soundness of what they obstinately opposed of His Lord, blessed and exalted, regarding His tawhid and acknowledgment of His books and messengers. For Allah, mighty is His praise, has informed of those He described with the hypocrisy He described them with, and their deceiving Him and the believers: that they do not perceive that they are in falsehood, persisting in it, and that by their deceit — through which they suppose they deceive their Lord and the people of faith in Him — they are the deceived. Then He, exalted is His remembrance, informed that for them is a painful punishment for their denial of what they used to deny of the prophethood of His Prophet, and their holding of disbelief in him, and for what they used to lie about in their claim that they are believers, while they persisted in disbelief.

If someone says to us: You have known that "mufa'ala" (the form expressing mutual action) occurs only between two parties, as when you say: "I struck your brother" or "I sat with your father," where each one is doing it to the other. But when the action comes from one party only, one says: "I struck your brother" and "I sat beside your father." So how is it permissible to say of one who deceives the hypocrite: "He deceived Allah and the believers"?

It is said: Some of those ascribed to knowledge of the Arabic dialects — meaning Abu Ubayda in his book "Majaz al-Qur'an" — said: this is a letter that came in this form, namely "yukhadi'u" in the pattern of "yufa'ilu," and it means "yaf'alu," in letters of this kind that are anomalous in Arab speech, like their saying: "qatalaka Allah" (may Allah fight you), meaning "qatalaka Allah" (may Allah kill you).

But the matter, in my view, is not as he said. Rather, this is from "tafa'ul" which occurs only between two, like all else that is known of the meaning of "yufa'ilu" and "mufa'il" in all Arabic speech. That is: the hypocrite deceives Allah, mighty is His praise, by his lying with his tongue — as already described — and Allah, blessed is His name, is the one who deceives him, by abandoning him from sound insight into what would save his soul in its eventual return, as He informed in His words: ﴿And let not those who disbelieve think that Our giving them respite is good for them; We give them respite only that they may increase in sin﴾ [Surah Al 'Imran: 178], and in the sense in which He informed that He will do to them in the Hereafter by His words: ﴿On the Day when the hypocrite men and hypocrite women will say to those who believe: "Wait for us that we may borrow some of your light." It will be said: "Go back behind you and seek light." So a wall will be set up between them with a gate; inside it is mercy, and outside it, facing it, is torment﴾ [Surah al-Hadid: 13]. That is a parallel to all other meanings in speech expressed by "yufa'ilu" and "mufa'il." Some grammarians of Basra used to say: "mufa'ala" occurs only between two things; but it is said "yukhadi'una Allah" (they deceive Allah) in their own estimation, by their supposing that they will not be punished, though they know the contrary within themselves, by the proof of Allah, blessed is His name, which is established upon His creatures through knowledge of Him, "and they deceive none but themselves." He said: Some have said: "wa-ma yakhda'una" means: they deceive themselves by isolating themselves with it [[i.e. by withdrawing alone and concealing what they conceal of disbelief; as if he intended to derive "yakhda'una" from "al-makhda'" — the small inner chamber within a larger room — and intended a stringent concealment of what they conceal. Akhla bi-fulan yukhli bihi ikhla' means: he was alone with him in an empty place. "Al-takhliya" is used in the sense that he was driven to seclusion, as if he drove himself to seclusion with it and to solitude, so that what is in it might be hidden. This explanation is a commentary on the rest of the verse that follows.]]. And mufa'ala may occur from one party in many things.

* *

The interpretation of His words, may His praise be exalted: ﴿And they deceive none but themselves﴾

If someone says: Have not the hypocrites deceived the believers — by what they displayed with their tongues of the word of truth — regarding their lives, their property and their offspring, so that their worldly affairs were preserved for them, even if they were deceived in the matter of their Hereafter?

It is said: It is an error to say that they deceived the believers. For if we said that, we would be attributing to them the real deception that they carried out upon the believers. Just as if we said: "So-and-so killed so-and-so," we would be attributing to him the actual killing which he carried out upon so-and-so. Rather, we say: The hypocrites deceived their Lord and the believers, but they did not deceive them; rather they deceived only themselves, as He, mighty is His praise, said, and no one else. This is like what you say of a man who fought another and killed himself but did not kill his opponent: "So-and-so fought so-and-so, but killed none but himself." You affirm for him the fighting of his opponent, and negate that he killed his opponent, and affirm for him the killing of himself. Likewise you say: "The hypocrite deceived his Lord and the believers, but deceived none but himself," affirming for him the deceiving of his Lord and the believers, and negating that he deceived anyone other than himself, because the deceiver is the one for whom the deception is truly valid and whose act of it has occurred. The hypocrites deceived none but themselves, because what they had of property and family was not held by the Muslims over them — during their deception of them through their hypocrisy, nor before it — so that they might recover it from them by their deceit. Rather, they defended it by their lying and their displaying with their tongues what was other than what was in their hearts; and Allah judges for them, regarding their property, their persons and their offspring, in the outward matters, by the ruling of the religious community to which they belonged; while Allah knows what they conceal of their affairs. The deceiver is only one who diverts another from his property, while the one deceived is unaware of the place of the deception by his deceiver. But when the one deceived knows of his companion's deception of him, nothing disagreeable befalls him from that deception; rather, it merely leads the one who supposes him to be his deceiver into a state of being gradually drawn on, so that he may reach a limit at which the proof against him is completed for the punishment with which he is about to be struck when he reaches it [[In the printed edition: "التي هو بها موقع"; meaning: the punishment which he is inflicting upon himself]]. The one being gradually drawn on is not aware of his own state in the eyes of the one drawing him on, nor of his having been apprised of his inner thoughts, and that the respite granted to him by the one drawing him on is his being left unpunished for his offence [[In the printed edition: "وأن إمهال مستدرجه، وتركه إياه معاقبته على جرمه"; this is an error that corrupts the meaning.]], so that the one who is cunning and deceiving may reach — by the desert of his punishment at the hands of the one drawing him on, through the abundance of his wrongdoing, the length of his disobedience toward him, and the abundance of the one drawing him on's forgiveness and the length of his pardon — the furthest limit [[The structure of this sentence: "so that the cunning deceiver may reach... the furthest limit", and the structure of what follows at the start: "But when the deceiver knows... then he is only deceiving himself", with a long digression between them.]] — then he is only deceiving himself, without doubt, and not the one whom he imagines to be his deceived. For this reason, Allah, mighty is His praise, negated of the hypocrite that he deceived anyone other than himself, since the attribute is the attribute we have described.

Since the matter is as we have described regarding the hypocrite's deceiving his Lord and the people of faith in Him, and that by his deceit he does not come to a sound deception except to himself and no other, because by his act he exposes himself to destruction and perdition, then it is necessary that the correct reading is: ﴿And they deceive none but themselves﴾ rather than ﴿And they deceive...﴾ [i.e. yukhadi'una], because the word "khadi'" (one who deceives) does not necessitate establishing a sound deception, whereas the word "khadi'" does necessitate establishing a sound deception. There is no doubt that the hypocrite has made the deception of Allah, mighty and majestic, valid against his own soul by what he has undertaken of deceiving his Lord, His Messenger and the believers through his hypocrisy; therefore the correctness is due to the reading of the one who read: ﴿wa-ma yakhda'una illa anfusahum﴾.

Another indication that the reading of the one who read ﴿wa-ma yakhda'una﴾ is more correct than the reading of the one who read ﴿wa-ma yukhadi'una﴾ is that Allah, mighty is His praise, has informed about them at the beginning of the verse that they deceive Allah and the believers; it is impossible that He negates of them what He has affirmed they have done, for that would be a contradiction in meaning, and that is not permissible from Allah, mighty and majestic.

The interpretation of the words of Allah, mighty is His praise: ﴿And they perceive not (9)﴾

By His words, mighty is His praise, "and they perceive not," is meant: and they do not know, and are not aware. It is said: "So-and-so did not perceive this matter, and he does not perceive it," when he does not know and does not realize it — "shi'r" and "shu'ur." The poet said:

They shot an arrow and no one perceived it, / then they retreated and said: "How good is the milk!"

[[The verse is by al-Mutanakhkhil al-Hudhali, Diwan al-Hudhaliyyin 2:31; Amali al-Qali 1:248; Simt al-La'ali 563. "Aqqa bi-sahm": he shot an arrow into the sky without intending anything by it; its origin is in blood-vengeance and blood-money, for they used to gather with the kin of the slain with a full blood-money and ask them to accept it. If they were strong, they refused; otherwise they took an arrow and shot it into the sky. If it returned stained with blood, they claimed their Lord forbade them to take blood-money; if it returned as it went up, they claimed their Lord commanded them to pardon and accept blood-money. Both were contrary to Islam. "Fa'a" and "istafa'a": returned. "Al-Wadh": milk. He satirizes them for baseness and meanness: they nullified the blood of their slain, and cast the arrow they claimed commanded and forbade them, and they turned back from seeking vengeance to accepting the blood-money, preferring the camels of the blood-money and their milk over the blood of the slayer of their companion, and said to themselves: milk is dearer to us than retaliation and more beneficial.]]

By his words — "it was not perceived" — is meant: no one knew it or was aware of it. So Allah, mighty is His praise, informed about the hypocrites that they do not perceive that Allah is deceiving them, through His giving them respite and drawing them on — which is from Allah, mighty is His praise, a conveyance to them of proof and excuse — and that for themselves there is a deception, and for them in the Hereafter there is harm. As in the following:

321 — Yunus b. Abd al-A'la related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: I asked Ibn Zayd about His words: ﴿And they deceive none but themselves, and they perceive not﴾; he said: They do not perceive that they harmed themselves, by what they concealed of disbelief and hypocrisy. And he recited the words of Allah, exalted is His remembrance: ﴿On the day when Allah will resurrect them all﴾, and said: They are the hypocrites, until reaching ﴿and they think that they are on something﴾ [Surah al-Mujadila: 18]: "Did faith benefit them, in your view?" [[Report 321 is the completion of the report that preceded: 320.]]

The Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 2, Verse 10 (Part 1 of 2)

On the interpretation of His words, may His praise be exalted: ﴿In their hearts is a disease﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: The original meaning of marad (disease) is sickness (saqam), and then the term is applied to both bodies and religions. God, may His praise be exalted, informed that there is a disease in the hearts of the hypocrites. By His statement about the disease of their hearts, He meant only to inform of the disease of what is in their hearts, that is, of their belief. But since it is known from the report about the disease of the heart that it refers to the disease of what they hold as belief, the report about the heart was sufficient in that respect, and the report did not need to explicitly mention their inner selves and beliefs (in the printed edition: "wa al-kinayah 'an tasrih al-khabar..." and his statement "wa al-kifayah 'an tasrih al-khabar..." is conjoined to his statement "al-khabar 'an marad ma fi qulubihim...") as the poet 'Umar ibn La'ja said:

And the city glorified (God), do not blame it, ... it saw a moon in their market by day.

(The verse appears in the interpretation of Surah al-Baqarah 110, vol. 1, p. 391, Bulaq edition.)

He means: "And the people of the city glorified (God)," and by the listeners' knowledge of the report about the city, he dispensed with a report about its people. A similar example is the saying of 'Antarah al-'Absi:

Why did you not ask the horsemen, O daughter of Malik? ... if you are ignorant of what you do not know.

(From his famous mu'allaqah.)

He means: "Why did you not ask the people of the horses?" And from this is the saying: "O horses of God, ride!", meaning: "O people of the horses of God, ride." The evidence for this is more than a book could count, and what we have mentioned is sufficient for one who is granted understanding of it.

Likewise, the meaning of God's words, may His praise be exalted: ﴿In their hearts is a disease﴾ means: in the belief of their hearts, which they hold in religion, and in their affirmation of Muhammad ﷺ and of what he brought from God, is a disease and sickness. So the report about their hearts sufficed for its meaning, without an explicit report about their belief.

The disease which God, may His praise be exalted, mentioned as being in the belief of their hearts that we have described, is their doubt concerning the matter of Muhammad and what he brought from God, and their bewilderment about it. Thus they are neither certain of it with the certainty of faith, nor do they deny it with the denial of polytheism, but, as God the Mighty and Majestic described them, they are wavering between that, belonging neither to these nor to those (Qur'an 4:143). It is as one says: "So-and-so is sick in this matter," meaning he weakens resolve and does not sharpen his judgment in it.

Commentators have concurred on an interpretation similar to what we have said. Those who said this include:

322. Muhammad ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Salamah related to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, client of Zayd ibn Thabit, from Ikrimah, or from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas: "In their hearts is a disease," meaning doubt.

323. And I was told by al-Minjab, who said: Bishr ibn 'Umarah related to us, from Abu Rawq, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The disease is hypocrisy.

324. Musa ibn Harun told me, he said: 'Amr ibn Hammad related to us, he said: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi in a report he mentioned, from Abu Malik, and from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas; and from Murrah al-Hamdani, from Ibn Mas'ud, and from some companions of the Prophet ﷺ: "In their hearts is a disease," he says: in their hearts is doubt.

325. Yunus ibn 'Abd al-A'la told me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd said, concerning His words "In their hearts is a disease," he said: This is a disease in religion, not a disease of the bodies. He said: They are the hypocrites.

326. Al-Muthanna ibn Ibrahim told me, he said: Suwayd ibn Nasr related to us, he said: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us by reading, from Sa'id, from Qatadah, concerning His words "In their hearts is a disease," he said: In their hearts is doubt and suspicion regarding the matter of God, may His praise be exalted.

327. And I was told by 'Ammar ibn al-Hasan, who said: Ibn Abi Ja'far related to us, from his father, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas: "In their hearts is a disease," he said: These are the people of hypocrisy, and the disease in their hearts is doubt regarding the matter of God, may His remembrance be exalted.

328. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd said: "And among the people are those who say, 'We believe in God and the Last Day,'" until "In their hearts is a disease," he said: The disease is the doubt which entered them into Islam.

(Reports 322–328 were transmitted by Ibn Kathir, 1:88, al-Suyuti, 1:30, and al-Shawkani, 1:30, together with their continuations below, numbered 329, 336, 330, 332, 331, 333 in that order. However, 336 does not mention "from Ibn 'Abbas." Al-Minjab in 323 and 336 is Ibn al-Harith ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Tamimi, one of the teachers of Muslim, from whom he related in his Sahih; Ibn Hibban mentioned him in al-Thiqat. The name is pronounced al-Minjab with a kasrah on the mim, a sukun on the nun, a fathah on the jim, and a final ba' with a single dot.)

* *

On the interpretation of His words, may His praise be exalted: ﴿So God increased them in disease﴾

We have already shown that the interpretation of the disease which God described as being in the hearts of the hypocrites is doubt in the beliefs of their hearts and their religion, and what they hold regarding the matter of Muhammad, the Messenger of God ﷺ, and the matter of his prophethood and what he brought, remaining steadfast in it.

So the disease which God informed was added to their disease is like what was in their hearts of doubt and bewilderment before the increase. God increased them, by what He introduced of His limits and obligations, which He had not imposed before the increase He added to the hypocrites, in doubt and bewilderment, since they doubted and were suspicious of what He newly introduced for them of that, (sentence structure: "God increased them by what He introduced of His limits... in doubt and bewilderment... to the disease and doubt that was in their hearts...") to the disease and doubt which was in their hearts formerly, from His limits and obligations which He had imposed before that. Just as He increased the believers in him, by their faith which they had before that, through what He introduced for them of obligations and limits when they believed in it, to their faith in the former of His limits and obligations, with faith. As His Exalted Majesty said in His revelation: ﴿And when a surah is revealed, some of them say, "Which of you has had its faith increased by this?" As for those who believed, it has increased them in faith, and they rejoice. But as for those in whose hearts is a disease, it has added to them uncleanness upon their uncleanness, and they die while they are disbelievers﴾ (Qur'an 9:124–125). The increase in uncleanness which the hypocrites were given to their uncleanness is what we have described, and the increase given to the believers in their faith is what we have explained. That is the interpretation agreed upon.

Mention of some of those among the people of interpretation who said this:

330. Musa ibn Harun told me, he said: 'Amr ibn Hammad informed us, he said: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, in a report he mentioned, from Abu Malik, and from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas; and from Murrah al-Hamdani, from Ibn Mas'ud, and from some companions of the Prophet ﷺ: "So God increased them in disease," he says: God increased them in doubt and suspicion.

331. Al-Muthanna ibn Ibrahim told me, he said: Suwayd ibn Nasr related to us, he said: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us by reading, from Sa'id, from Qatadah: "So God increased them in disease," he says: God increased them in doubt and suspicion regarding the matter of God.

332. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, concerning God's words: "In their hearts is a disease; so God increased them in disease," he said: He increased them in uncleanness, and he recited God's words, the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿As for those who believed, it has increased them in faith, and they rejoice. But as for those in whose hearts is a disease, it has added to them uncleanness upon their uncleanness﴾. He said: evil upon their evil, and misguidance upon their misguidance.

333. And I was told by 'Ammar ibn al-Hasan, who said: Ibn Abi Ja'far related to us, from his father, from al-Rabi': "So God increased them in disease," he said: God increased them in doubt.

* *

On the interpretation of His words, may His praise be exalted: ﴿And for them is a painful punishment﴾

Abu Ja'far said: al-Alim (painful) is al-Mujiʿ (causing pain). Its meaning is: "And for them is a painful punishment," with "mu'lim" (painful) being the form of "alim." It is like one says: "a striking that is painful (wajī')," meaning mujī' (causing pain), and "God is Badi' al-samawat wa al-ard," meaning Mubdi' (the Originator). From this is the saying of 'Amr ibn Ma'dikarib al-Zubaidi:

Is it because of Rayhanah, the summoner who hears, that I am kept awake while my companions sleep?

(Al-Asma'iyyat 43; it appears again in the interpretation of Surah Yunus 1, vol. 11, p. 58, Bulaq edition. Rayhanah was the daughter of Ma'dikarib, sister of 'Amr ibn Ma'dikarib, and she was the mother of Duraid ibn al-Simmah; her father al-Simmah captured her and married her. (Al-Aghani 10:4).)

meaning al-Musmi' (the one who makes to hear). From this is the saying of Dhu al-Rummah:

And you raise from the chests of swift she-camels ... the heat of the sun turns their faces, a painful blaze.

(His Diwan, p. 592. His words "and we raise from the chests" mean we urge them on in travel; when camels hasten, they lift their chests. Shamardalat is the plural of shamardalah: a fine, beautiful-formed, young, swift she-camel. His words "yasudd wujuhaha" mean that the painful blaze strikes their faces, so they turn their faces away as if averting from its sting. The Diwan's reading is "yasukk," and sakkah sakkah means a very strong blow. Wahj means the heat of the sun, or the heat of fire from afar.)

It is also transmitted as "yasukku," and al-alim is an adjective of the punishment, as if He said: "And for them is a painful punishment." It derives from alam (pain), and alam is wajaʿ (ache). As follows:

334. Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Ishaq related to us, he said: 'Abdullah ibn Abi Ja'far related to us, from his father, from al-Rabi', who said: al-Alim is al-Mujiʿ (the one causing pain).

335. Ya'qub related to us, he said: Hushaym related to us, he said: Juwaybir informed us, from al-Dahhak, who said: al-Alim is al-Mujiʿ.

(Report 335: Ya'qub is Ibn Ibrahim al-Dawraqi, the memorizer. Hushaym, with a damma on the ha', is Ibn Bashir, with a fathah on the ba' and a kasrah on the shin, Ibn al-Qasim, Abu Mu'awiyah al-Wasiti, a great memorizing imam from whom the imams Ahmad, Ibn al-Madini and others related. 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi said: "Hushaym had more memorization of hadith than Sufyan al-Thawri." The meaning of this report is included in the following one, 336.)

336. And I was told by al-Minjab ibn al-Harith, who said: Bishr ibn 'Umarah related to us, from Abu Rawq, from al-Dahhak concerning His words "alim," he said: It is the painful punishment. And everything in the Qur'an that is alim is mujiʿ.

(Report 336 is mentioned by al-Suyuti, 1:30, and alluded to by al-Shawkani, 1:30.)

* *

On the interpretation of His words, may His praise be exalted: ﴿because they used to lie (10)﴾

The readers differed in reading this. Some of them read ﴿yakdhibun﴾ with the dhal lightened and the ya' vowelled with a fathah, and this is the reading of the majority of the people of Kufa. Others read "yukadhdhibun," with the ya' vowelled with a damma and the dhal doubled, and this is the reading of the majority of the people of Madinah, the Hijaz and Basra.

It seems that those who read it with the dhal doubled and the ya' with a damma saw that God, may His majesty be exalted, only obligated the painful punishment for the hypocrites because of their denying His Prophet ﷺ and what he brought, and that lying, were it not for denial, would not necessitate for anyone even the slightest punishment, let alone a painful one. But the matter, in my view, is not as they said. That is because God, the Mighty and Majestic, informed about the hypocrites at the beginning of the account of them in this surah, that they lie in their claim of faith and their display of it with their tongues, deceiving God, the Mighty and Majestic, and His Messenger and the believers, when He said: ﴿And among the people are those who say, "We believe in God and the Last Day," but they are not believers. They deceive God and those who believe﴾ by that saying, along with their concealing doubt and suspicion, ﴿but they deceive none except themselves﴾ and not the Messenger of God ﷺ nor the believers; ﴿and they do not perceive﴾ the place of their deception of themselves, and God's gradual leading them on by giving them respite; ﴿in their hearts﴾ is the doubt of hypocrisy and its suspicion, ﴿and God increases them in doubt and suspicion, because they lie to God, His Messenger, and the believers with their words, "We believe in God and the Last Day," while they, in that saying, are liars, because of their concealing doubt and disease in the beliefs of their hearts regarding the matter of God and the matter of His Messenger ﷺ. So it is more fitting, in the wisdom of God, great is His majesty, that His threat to them should concern what the report about them began with of their ugly deeds and blameworthy characters, and not what has not been mentioned of their deeds. For all the verses of His revelation came in this manner: He begins mentioning the good deeds of one people, then concludes that with a threat concerning what He began mentioning of their deeds, and begins mentioning the bad deeds of others, then concludes that with a threat concerning what He began mentioning of their deeds.

Likewise, the sound view regarding the verses in which the mention of some bad deeds of the hypocrites begins is that it should conclude with a threat concerning what was begun in mentioning their ugly deeds. So this is this, together with the evidence of the other verse confirming the correctness of what we have said, and bearing witness that the obligatory reading is what we have chosen, and that the correct interpretation is what we have interpreted: that God's threat to the hypocrites in this verse is a painful punishment for lying, which combines the meaning of doubt and denial. This is the saying of God, may He be blessed and exalted: ﴿When the hypocrites come to you, they say, "We bear witness that you are indeed the Messenger of God." And God knows that you are His Messenger, and God bears witness that the hypocrites are indeed liars. They have taken their oaths as a shield, and so they have averted (people) from the way of God. Indeed, evil is what they have been doing﴾ (Qur'an 63:1–2). The other verse, in al-Mujadilah: ﴿They have taken their oaths as a shield, and so they have averted (people) from the way of God; so for them is a humiliating punishment﴾ (Qur'an 58:16). So He, may His praise be exalted, informed that the hypocrites, by their saying to the Messenger of God ﷺ what they said, along with their belief in him what they believe, are liars. Then He informed, may His remembrance be exalted, that the humiliating punishment is for them because of that lying. Had the sound reading been as the readers read in Surah al-Baqarah, "And for them is a painful punishment because they used to deny," then the reading in the other surah would have been: "And God bears witness that the hypocrites are indeed deniers (lamukadhdhibun)," so that the threat following it would be a threat for denial and not for lying. And the consensus of the Muslims that the correct reading in His words, "And God bears witness that the hypocrites are indeed liars" carries the meaning of lying, and that God's threat to the hypocrites of a painful punishment for that lying, is the clearest proof that the sound reading in Surah al-Baqarah, "bima kanu yakdhibun," carries the meaning of lying, and that God's threat to the hypocrites in it for lying is true, not for the denial which has not been mentioned, exactly like what is in Surah al-Munafiqun, without any difference.

Some grammarians of Basra claimed that "mā" in God's words, ﴿بِمَا كَانُوا يَكْذِبُونَ﴾ [2:10] ("for what they used to lie"), is a noun meaning a verbal noun (maṣdar), just as "an" and the verb are nouns for the verbal noun in your saying, "I like that you come to me." They held that the meaning is simply "for their lying and their lying-about." He said that "kāna" is inserted to indicate that it occurred in the past, as one says, "How excellent was ʿAbd Allāh!" You are marvelling at ʿAbd Allāh, not at his being, though the wording of the exclamation falls on his being.

Some grammarians of Kufa rejected this view and considered it erroneous. They said: "kāna" is nullified in the exclamation because the verb has preceded it. It is as if one said, "Good was Zayd" (ḥasanan kāna Zayd) and "Good is Zayd" (ḥasan kāna Zayd). "Kāna" nullifies [its own operation] and operates with nouns and adjectives which take the forms of nouns, when they come before "kāna" and "kāna" falls between them and the nouns. As for the reason for its nullification when it is nullified in this situation, it is because adjectives and nouns resemble the verbs "fa'ala" and "yaf'alu," in which the operation of "kāna" does not appear. Do you not see that you say, "Yaqūmu kāna Zayd" (he stands, Zayd was), and the operation of "kāna" does not appear in "yaqūmu"? Likewise, "qāma kāna Zayd." Therefore its operation is nullified with "fāʿil" (the active participle form), modelled on "fa'ala" and "yaf'alu," and at times it operates with "fāʿil" because it is a noun, as it operates with nouns. But when "kāna" precedes the nouns and verbs, and the noun or verb follows it, then in his view it is an error for "kāna" to be nullifying. Therefore he rejected the Basran's statement that we have related, and interpreted God, Mighty and Majestic, saying ﴿بِمَا كَانُوا يَكْذِبُونَ﴾ to mean: "that which they lie about."

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, may His praise be exalted: ﴿And when it is said to them, "Do not cause corruption on the earth"﴾

The scholars of tafsir (interpretation of the Qur'an) differed concerning the interpretation of this verse.

It is narrated from Salman al-Farisi that he used to say: "These people have not yet come."

337. Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Atham ibn Ali narrated to us, saying: al-A'mash narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Minhal ibn Amr narrating, from Abbad ibn Abd Allah, from Salman, who said: "Those who are meant by ﴿And when it is said to them, "Do not cause corruption on the earth," they say, "We are only reformers"﴾ have not yet come."[[Report 337. Atham (with a fatha on the ʿayn and a shaddah on the thāʾ) ibn Ali al-Amiri: reliable (thiqah); he was declared reliable by Abu Zurʿah, Ibn Saʿd and others. Ibn Saʿd mentions him in vol. 6, p. 273; al-Bukhari in al-Kabir 4/1/93; and Ibn Abi Hatim 3/2/44. Al-Minhal ibn Amr al-Asadi: reliable; we preferred his authentication in al-Musnad, no. 714. Al-Bukhari affirmed in al-Kabir 4/2/12 that Shuʿbah narrated from him, and Shuʿbah's narration from him is established in al-Musnad, no. 3133. Abbad ibn Abd Allah: he is al-Asadi al-Kufi. Al-Bukhari said: "there is something to examine in him" (fihi nazar). Ibn Hibban mentioned him in al-Thiqat, and Ibn al-Madini declared him weak. Ibn Abi Hatim (3/1/82) mentioned that he "heard from ʿAli." I have shown in the commentary on al-Musnad, no. 883, that his narration is good (hasan). Salman: he is Salman al-Khayr al-Farisi, the Companion, may Allah be pleased with him. This report was transmitted by Ibn Kathir (1:91) and al-Suyuti (1:30), who also attributed it to Waki' and Ibn Abi Hatim. Al-Shawkani mentioned it (1:31) and attributed it to Ibn Ishaq, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim. I did not find the attribution to Ibn Ishaq in any other source.]]

338. Ahmad ibn Uthman ibn Hakim narrated to me, saying: Abd al-Rahman ibn Shurayk narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: al-A'mash narrated to me, from Zayd ibn Wahb and others, from Salman, that he said concerning this verse, ﴿And when it is said to them, "Do not cause corruption on the earth," they say, "We are only reformers"﴾: "These people have not yet come."[[Report 338. Ahmad ibn Uthman ibn Hakim al-Awdi: reliable; he was declared reliable by al-Nasa'i, al-Bazzar and others. He narrated from him in the Two Sahihs (al-Bukhari and Muslim), and he is among the few shaykhs from whom al-Bukhari narrated while they were still alive. He died in the year 260 or 261, while al-Bukhari died in 256. Abd al-Rahman ibn Shurayk ibn Abd Allah al-Nakha'i: Ibn Hibban mentioned him in al-Thiqat, while Abu Hatim said: "weak in narration" (wahi al-hadith).

In my judgment its chain is good (hasan), and it has passed before it by another good chain. Each of the two strengthens the other. Ibn Kathir (1:91) transmitted it from al-Tabari with this chain.]]

Others said:

339. Musa ibn Harun narrated this to me, saying: Amr ibn Hammad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi in a report he mentioned, from Abu Malik and from Abu Salih, from Ibn Abbas; and from Murrah al-Hamdani, from Ibn Mas'ud; and from some people among the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ: ﴿And when it is said to them, "Do not cause corruption on the earth," they say, "We are only reformers"﴾. They are the hypocrites (munafiqun). As for "Do not cause corruption on the earth," corruption is disbelief and acting in disobedience.

340. And I was informed from Ammar ibn al-Hasan, who said: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi': ﴿And when it is said to them, "Do not cause corruption on the earth"﴾, he says: "Do not disobey on the earth." ﴿They say, "We are only reformers"﴾. He said: Their corruption was that disobedience to Allah, may His praise be exalted. For whoever disobeys Allah on the earth, or commands disobedience to Him, has caused corruption on the earth, because the reform of the earth and the heavens is by obedience.[[Report 340. The phrase "they say, 'We are only reformers'" is from the manuscript and is not in the printed edition. In the printed edition and the manuscript it reads: "their corruption was upon themselves, that disobedience to Allah..." The words "upon themselves" seem to be an addition by a copyist, and they are not in what Ibn Kathir transmitted from al-Tabari.]]

The more probable of the two interpretations of the verse is the view of those who say that the saying of Allah, blessed is His name, ﴿And when it is said to them, "Do not cause corruption on the earth," they say, "We are only reformers"﴾, was revealed concerning the hypocrites who were during the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, even though it also refers to everyone who had the same attributes as them among the hypocrites after them, until the Day of Resurrection.

Salman's saying when reciting this verse, "These people have not yet come," may mean that he said it after those who had these attributes during the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had passed away, as a report from him about those who came after them and had not yet come. It does not mean that no one with these attributes had passed away.[[In the printed edition: "concerning those who came after them," which distorts the meaning. The correct wording is from the manuscript.]]

We said that the more probable interpretation of the verse is what we have mentioned, because of the consensus (ijma') of the authoritative scholars of tafsir that these are the attributes of the hypocrites who were among the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ during his time, and that these verses were revealed concerning them. A consensus interpretation (al-ta'wil al-mujma' 'alayhi) is more worthy of being the meaning of the Qur'an than a saying for which there is no evidence of its soundness from a source or a parallel.

Causing corruption on the earth means acting on it in what Allah, may His praise be exalted, has forbidden, and neglecting what Allah has commanded to be preserved. That is the summary of corruption, as He, may His praise be exalted, said in His Book, reporting the saying of His angels: ﴿They said, "Will You place upon it one who causes corruption therein and sheds blood?"﴾ [Surah al-Baqarah: 30]. They meant by that: "Will You place on the earth one who disobeys You and opposes Your command?" Likewise, the attribute of the people of hypocrisy is that they cause corruption on the earth by their disobedience to their Lord on it, their committing on it what He forbade them to commit, their neglect of His obligations, their doubt about the religion of Allah, which accepts no deed from anyone except with belief in it and certainty of its reality,[[In the printed edition: "bihaqiqah." The correct wording is from the manuscript and Ibn Kathir.]] and their lying to the believers by claiming other than what they persist in of doubt and suspicion, and by supporting the people of denial of Allah, His Books and His messengers against the friends of Allah, whenever they find a way to do so. That is the corruption of the hypocrites on the earth of Allah, while they suppose that by their doing so they are reformers on it. Allah, may His praise be exalted, did not remove His punishment from them, nor did He lighten the painful torment He prepared as punishment for the people of disobedience to Him, because they suppose that in the acts of disobedience to Allah they are reformers. Rather, He made obligatory for them the lowest level of His Fire, the painful punishment from Him, and the immediate disgrace through Allah's cursing them and reviling them. He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Unquestionably, they are the corrupters, but they do not perceive﴾. That is from the judgment of Allah, may His praise be exalted, concerning them, and it is the strongest evidence against the claim of those who say that the punishments of Allah are deserved only by one who defies his Lord in what is obligatory upon him of His rights and duties, after he knows and after the proof has been established against him through his knowledge that such obligations are binding upon him.

* *

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, may His praise be exalted: ﴿They say, "We are only reformers"﴾ (11)

The interpretation of this is as Ibn Abbas said:

341. Muhammad ibn Humayd narrated this to us, saying: Salamah ibn al-Fadl narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, mawla of Zayd ibn Thabit, from Ikrimah, or from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His saying: ﴿We are only reformers﴾, meaning: they said, "We only intend reconciliation between the two groups, the believers and the People of the Book."

Others differed from him in this.

342. al-Qasim ibn al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn ibn Dawud narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid: ﴿And when it is said to them, "Do not cause corruption on the earth"﴾, he said: when they committed disobedience to Allah and were told, "Do not do such and such," they said, "We are only upon guidance, reformers."[[The two reports 341 and 342 were transmitted by Ibn Kathir (1:91), al-Suyuti (1:30) and al-Shawkani (1:30).]]

Abu Ja'far said: Whichever of the two matters was theirs in this, meaning their claim that they were reformers, there is no doubt that they supposed that in what they did they were reformers. Whether their claim of reform concerned the relations between the Jews and the Muslims, or concerned their religions and the disobedience to Allah they committed, and their lying to the believers in what they showed them of speech while concealing other than what they displayed, they were, in all of that, in their own eyes doers of good, while in the sight of Allah they were doers of evil and opposers of the command of Allah. This is because Allah, may His praise be exalted, had obligated them to oppose the Jews and to fight them alongside the Muslims, and had required them to affirm the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and what he brought from Allah, just as He required this of the believers. So their meeting with the Jews, in the manner of taking them as allies, and their doubt about the prophethood of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and about what he brought as coming from Allah, was the greatest corruption, even though it appeared to them as reform and guidance, whether for their religions or in the relations between the believers and the Jews. Therefore Allah, may His praise be exalted, said concerning them: ﴿Unquestionably, they are the corrupters﴾, rather than those among the believers who forbid them from causing corruption on the earth, ﴿but they do not perceive﴾.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 12:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is His praise: ﴿Surely they are the ones who spread corruption, but they do not perceive it.﴾

This statement from God, exalted is His praise, is a refutation of the hypocrites in their claim. When they are commanded to obey God in what God has commanded them, and forbidden from disobeying God in what God has forbidden them, they say: "We are only reformers, not corrupters, and we are upon right guidance and direction," regarding what you have denounced against us, "while you are the misguided." So God, mighty and majestic, refuted them in that their saying, and said: "Surely they are the ones who spread corruption, those who oppose the command of God, mighty and majestic, who transgress His limits, who engage in His disobedience, who abandon His obligations, and they do not perceive or realize that they are like this"; not those who command them to justice from among the believers, and forbid them from the disobedience of God on His earth among the Muslims.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 13:

The explanation of the words of Allah, may His praise be exalted: ﴿And when it is said to them, "Believe as the people have believed"﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: The interpretation of His words ﴿And when it is said to them, "Believe as the people have believed"﴾ means: and when it is said to those whom Allah has described and characterised as saying ﴿"We believe in Allah and the Last Day," but they are not believers﴾: "Affirm Muhammad and what he brought from Allah, as the people have affirmed it." By "the people" is meant the believers who believed in Muhammad, his prophethood, and what he brought from Allah. As:

343 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: 'Uthman ibn Sa'id narrated to us, from Bishr ibn 'Umara, from Abu Rawq, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words ﴿And when it is said to them, "Believe as the people have believed"﴾, he said: "When it is said to them, 'Affirm as the companions of Muhammad have affirmed; say that he is a Prophet and Messenger, and that what was revealed to him is true, and affirm the Hereafter, and that you will be resurrected after death.'" [[The report 343 is quoted by al-Suyuti 1:30 and al-Shawkani 1:31; its completion appears in the interpretation of the rest of the verse, under numbers 347 and 348.]]

The definite article "al-" was attached to "the people" although they were only some of the people and not all of them, because they were well known to those addressed by this verse by their persons. The meaning is: "Believe as the people whom you know, from among the people of certainty and affirmation of Allah, of Muhammad ﷺ, of what he brought from Allah, and of the Last Day, have believed." For this reason the article was attached, just as it was attached in His words (﴿Those to whom the people said, "Indeed the people have gathered against you, so fear them"﴾) [Surah Al ʿImran: 173], because the attachment of the article there points to people known to those addressed by it.

* *

The explanation of the words of Allah, may His praise be exalted: ﴿They said, "Shall we believe as the foolish have believed?"﴾

Abu Ja'far said: "Al-sufaha'" (the foolish) is the plural of "safih" (foolish), just as "al-'ulama'" (the scholars) is the plural of "'alim" (knowing), and "al-hukama'" (the wise) is the plural of "hakim" (wise). The "safih" is the ignorant one, weak in opinion, little acquainted with the places of benefit and harm. For this reason Allah, mighty and majestic, called women and children "foolish," saying: ﴿And do not give the foolish your wealth which Allah has made for you a means of support﴾ [Surah al-Nisa': 5]. The majority of the exegetes said: they are women and children, because of the weakness of their opinions and their lack of knowledge of the places of interest and harm toward which wealth is directed.

The hypocrites meant by their saying, "Shall we believe as the foolish have believed?", when they were called to affirm Muhammad ﷺ, what he brought from Allah, and the acknowledgement of resurrection, and it was said to them, "Believe as [the people] [[In the printed edition and manuscript: "so he said to them, 'Believe as the companions of Muhammad have believed...'", which is a confused statement; the correct reading is what we have adopted. His words "the companions of Muhammad" are the object of his words "The hypocrites meant by their saying..."]] the companions of Muhammad and his followers among the believers who affirmed him, from among the people of faith and certainty, and affirmation of Allah, and of what was made obligatory upon them through the tongue of His Messenger Muhammad ﷺ and in His Book, and of the Last Day." So they said, in answer to the one who said this to them: "Shall we believe as the ignorant have believed, and affirm Muhammad ﷺ as those who have no intellects or understanding have affirmed him?" As in what:

344 - Musa ibn Harun narrated to me, saying: 'Amr ibn Hammad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi in a report he mentioned, from Abu Malik, and from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas - and from Murra al-Hamdani, from Ibn Mas'ud, and from some companions of the Prophet ﷺ: ﴿They said, "Shall we believe as the foolish have believed?"﴾, meaning the companions of the Prophet ﷺ.

345 - al-Muthanna ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Ishaq ibn al-Hajjaj narrated to us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas: ﴿They said, "Shall we believe as the foolish have believed?"﴾, meaning the companions of Muhammad ﷺ.

346 - Yunus ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam narrated to us regarding His words "They said, 'Shall we believe as the foolish have believed?'", he said: "This is the saying of the hypocrites, meaning the companions of the Prophet ﷺ."

347 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: 'Uthman ibn Sa'id narrated to us, from Bishr ibn 'Umara, from Abu Rawq, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿They said, "Shall we believe as the foolish have believed?"﴾, they say: "Shall we say as the foolish say?", meaning the companions of Muhammad ﷺ, because of their opposition to their religion. [[Reports 344-347: cited by Ibn Kathir 1:92, al-Suyuti 1:30 and al-Shawkani 1:31; the last of them is the completion of report 343.]]

* *

The explanation of the words of Allah, may His praise be exalted: ﴿Surely they are the foolish, but they do not know﴾ (13)

Abu Ja'far said: This is a statement from Allah, exalted be He, about the hypocrites whose description has preceded, and whom He described with what He described them with of doubt and denial: that they are the ignorant in their religions, weak in opinion in their beliefs and in the choices they made for themselves, of doubt and suspicion regarding the matter of Allah, the matter of His Messenger, the matter of his prophethood, and what he brought from Allah, and the matter of resurrection; because they wrong themselves by what they did of that while they suppose that they are doing good by it. This is the very essence of foolishness, for the foolish person only corrupts while thinking he is putting right, and wastes while thinking he is preserving. Likewise the hypocrite disobeys his Lord while thinking he obeys Him, disbelieves in Him while thinking he believes in Him, and harms himself while thinking he does good to it, just as our Lord, great is His remembrance, described them, saying: ﴿Surely they are the corrupters, but they do not perceive﴾, and He said: ﴿Surely they are the foolish﴾ — not the believers who affirm Allah and His Book, His Messenger and His reward and punishment — ﴿but they do not know﴾. And thus Ibn 'Abbas used to interpret this verse.

348 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: 'Uthman ibn Sa'id narrated to us, from Bishr ibn 'Umara, from Abu Rawq, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding Allah, exalted be His praise, saying: ﴿Surely they are the foolish﴾, he said: "The ignorant", ﴿but they do not know﴾, he said: "but they do not understand." [[Report 348 is the completion of reports 343 and 347.]]

As for the manner in which the article "al-" enters "al-sufaha'" (the foolish), it is similar to the manner in which it enters "al-nas" (the people) in His words ﴿And when it is said to them, "Believe as the people have believed"﴾. We have already explained the reason for its entry there, and the reason for its entry in "al-sufaha'" is the same as its entry in "al-nas" there, exactly alike.

And the proof that this verse points to, refuting the view of whoever claims that punishment from Allah is only deserved by one who opposes his Lord knowingly after knowing the truth of what he opposes, is similar to the proof of the other verses whose interpretation we have previously mentioned in His words "but they do not perceive", and similar cases. [[In the printed edition: "with his knowledge of the truth of what he opposed", and also there: "...and similar to this".]]

**The Interpretation of His Words, may His praise be exalted: ﴿And when they meet those who believe, they say, "We believe"; but when they are alone with their devils, they say, "Indeed we are with you."﴾**

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: This verse is similar to the other verse in which God, may His praise be exalted, informed of the hypocrites and their deceiving of God, His Messenger and the believers. He said, exalted is He: ﴿And among the people are those who say, "We believe in God and the Last Day," but they are not believers.﴾ Then God, remembered be He, denied them with His words: ﴿but they are not believers﴾, and [He informed] that by their saying this they deceive God and those who believe. Likewise, He informed about them in this verse that they say to the believers, who affirm God, His Book and His Messenger, with their tongues: "We believe and we affirm Muhammad and what he has brought from God," deceiving them in order to protect their blood, their property and their offspring, and warding off harm from them. And [He informed] that when they are alone with their *maradah* (rebellious ones), and with the people of arrogance, evil and corruption among them and among the rest of the people of polytheism [[In the manuscript: "and that when they are alone with the people of their affection," but what is printed is more correct in the context of its explanation.]] who are upon the same disbelief in God, His Book and His Messenger as they are, and they are their devils (shayatin), and we have shown earlier in our book that the devils of everything are its rebellious ones, they say to them: "Indeed we are with you," meaning: indeed we are with you in your religion, and we are your supporters against those who oppose you in it, and your allies rather than the companions of Muhammad ﷺ. "We are only mockers" of God, His Book, His Messenger and his companions, as in what was reported:

**349.** Muhammad ibn al-Ala' [[“Muhammad ibn al-Ala'” is Abu Kurayb, from whom he narrated much, earlier and later.]] narrated to us, saying: 'Uthman ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Bishr ibn 'Umarah narrated to us, from Abu Rawq, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿And when they meet those who believe, they say, "We believe"﴾, he said: Some men from the Jews, when they met the companions of the Prophet ﷺ or some of them, would say: "We are upon your religion." And when they were alone with their companions, who are their devils, they would say: "Indeed we are with you; we are only mockers."

**350.** Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah ibn al-Fadl narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, mawla of Zayd ibn Thabit, from Ikrimah, or from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿And when they are alone with their devils﴾, he said: "When they are alone with their devils from the Jews, who order them to deny and to oppose what the Messenger brought" ﴿they say, "Indeed we are with you"﴾, meaning: indeed we are upon the same as what you are upon ﴿"Indeed we are only mockers"﴾.

**351.** Musa ibn Harun narrated to me, saying: 'Amr ibn Hammad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, in a report he mentioned from Abu Malik, and from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas, and from Murrah al-Hamdani, from Ibn Mas'ud, and from some people among the companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ: ﴿And when they are alone with their devils﴾; as for their devils, they are their leaders in disbelief.

**352.** Bishr ibn Mu'adh al-'Aqadi [[Bishr ibn Mu'adh al-'Aqadi: a well-known trustworthy narrator, from whom al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i, Ibn Majah and others narrated. "Al-'Aqadi" with an unpointed 'ayn and an open qaf, a nisba to "al-'Aqd," a clan of Bajilah.]] narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Zuray' narrated to us, from Sa'id, from Qatadah regarding His words: ﴿And when they are alone with their devils﴾, meaning their leaders in evil, ﴿they say, "Indeed we are only mockers"﴾.

**353.** Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah regarding His words: ﴿And when they are alone with their devils﴾; he said: "The polytheists."

**354.** Muhammad ibn 'Amr al-Bahili narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa ibn Maymun narrated to us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Najih narrated to us, from Mujahid regarding the saying of God, mighty and majestic: ﴿And when they are alone with their devils﴾, he said: "When the hypocrites are alone with their companions among the disbelievers."

**355.** Al-Muthanna ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, from Shibl ibn 'Abbad, from 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿And when they are alone with their devils﴾, he said: "Their companions from among the hypocrites and the polytheists."

**356.** Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq ibn al-Hajjaj narrated to us, from 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Ja'far, from his father, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas: ﴿And when they are alone with their devils﴾, he said: "Their brothers from among the polytheists," ﴿they say, "Indeed we are with you; we are only mockers"﴾.

**357.** Al-Qasim ibn al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn ibn Dawud narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, saying: Ibn Jurayj said regarding His words: ﴿And when they meet those who believe, they say, "We believe"﴾: "When prosperity befalls the believers, they say: 'Indeed we are with you; we are only your brothers.' And when they are alone with their devils, they mock the believers."

**358.** Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Mujahid said: "Their devils are their companions from among the hypocrites and the polytheists." [[These earlier reports, 349–358: most of them were cited by Ibn Kathir in his Tafsir, 1:93, al-Suyuti, 1:31, and al-Shawkani, 1:33.]]

If someone says to us: "Have you considered His words ﴿And when they are alone with their devils﴾? How is it said ﴿alone with their devils﴾ and not 'alone with (*bi*) their devils'? You know that what is common among people in their speech is 'I was alone with so-and-so' (*khalawtu bi-fulan*) more than and more widespread than 'I was alone with so-and-so' (*khalawtu ila fulan*); and from your saying, 'The Qur'an is the most eloquent of expression!'"

It is said: The scholars of the Arabic language have differed regarding this. Some of the grammarians of Basra used to say: It is said *khalawtu ila fulan* when what is intended is: "I was alone with him for a specific need." When it is said like this, it allows only the meaning of being alone with him for the fulfilment of a need. But when it is said *khalawtu bihi* ("I was alone with him"), it carries two meanings: one of them is being alone with him for a need, and the other is being alone with him in mockery. According to this view, ﴿and when they are alone with their devils﴾ is, without doubt, more eloquent than saying "and when they are alone with their devils (*bi*)," because in the saying of the speaker, "when they are alone with their devils," there is confusion of the meaning for its hearers, which is absent from His saying, "and when they are alone with their devils (*ila*)." This is one of the opinions.

The other opinion: that the meaning of His saying ﴿and when they are alone with their devils﴾ is to be directed as "and when they are alone with their devils (*ma'a*)," since the particles of attribution (*huruf al-sifat*) [[The particles of attribution: these are the prepositions, called "particles of jarr" because they govern (jarr) what follows them, and called "particles of attribution" because they produce a new attribute in the noun, as in your saying "I sat in the house," which indicates that the house is a container for sitting. It is also said that they were so named because they occur as qualifiers of what precedes them among indefinite nouns. The Kufans also call them "particles of idafah," because they connect the noun to the verb, that is, they convey it to it and bind it to it (Hama' al-Hawami' 2:19). They are also called "particles of meaning," as will come shortly. Mu'aqabah: that one of them is used in place of another with a similar meaning.]] substitute for one another, as God said, relating of 'Isa, son of Maryam, that he said to the disciples: ﴿Who are my helpers toward God?﴾ [Surah al-Saff: 14], meaning: "with God." And as "'ala" is placed in the position of "min," "fi," "'an," and "bi," as the poet said:

*When the Banu Qushayr were pleased with me, by the life of God, their pleasure pleased me.* [[The verse is by al-'Uqayf al-'Uqayli, praising Hakim ibn al-Musayyib al-Qushayri. Nawadir Abi Zayd: 176; Khizanat al-Adab 4:247; and others, many.]]

meaning "'anni" (from me).

As for some of the grammarians of Kufa, he used to interpret it as meaning: "And when they meet those who believe, they say, 'We believe,' and when they turn their solitude toward their devils"—and he claims that what governs *ila* is the meaning indicated by the speech: the turning of the hypocrites away from meeting the believers toward their devils, being alone with them, not His saying *khalaw*. According to this interpretation, no other particle is suitable in the place of *ila*, because the speech changes with the entry of another particle in its place.

This opinion, in my view, is more correct, because each particle of meaning (*huruf al-ma'ani*) has an aspect in which it is more appropriate than others. The particles of meaning are the particles of attribution and the particles of jarr, as has passed just before. [[Note: 1]] It is not permissible to shift that from it to another, except with a proof that must be accepted. For *ila* in every place it enters in speech has a ruling, and it is not permissible to strip it of its meanings in its places.

* *

**The Interpretation of His Words, may His praise be exalted: ﴿Indeed we are only mockers (14)﴾**

The people of interpretation (*ahl al-ta'wil*) all agreed, without any disagreement among them, that the meaning of His saying ﴿Indeed we are only mockers﴾ is: "Indeed we are only scoffers." So the meaning of the speech, then, is: "When the hypocrites turn away alone toward their *maradah* (rebellious ones) from among the hypocrites and the polytheists, they say: 'Indeed we are with you,' concerning what you are upon of denying Muhammad ﷺ and what he brought, opposing him and opposing his followers; indeed we are only scoffers at the companions of Muhammad ﷺ, by our saying to them when we meet them: 'We believe in God and the Last Day.'" As in what was reported:

**359.** Muhammad ibn al-Ala' narrated to us, saying: 'Uthman ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Bishr ibn 'Umarah narrated to us, from Abu Rawq, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn 'Abbas: They said: ﴿Indeed we are only mockers﴾, scoffing at the companions of Muhammad ﷺ.

**360.** Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, mawla of Zayd ibn Thabit, from Ikrimah, or from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿Indeed we are only mockers﴾, meaning: indeed we only mock the people and play with them.

**361.** Bishr ibn Mu'adh al-'Aqadi narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Zuray' narrated to us, from Sa'id, from Qatadah: ﴿Indeed we are only mockers﴾, indeed we mock these people and ridicule them.

**362.** Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq ibn al-Hajjaj narrated to us, from 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Ja'far, from his father, from al-Rabi': ﴿Indeed we are only mockers﴾, meaning we mock the companions of Muhammad ﷺ. [[These reports are a continuation of the earlier reports in the explanation of the beginning of the verse.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 15 (part 1 of 2):

The Interpretation of His Words, exalted is His praise: ﴿Allah mocks them﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Scholars differed concerning the manner of Allah's mockery (istihza') — exalted is His majesty — which He mentioned that He does to the hypocrites whose characteristics He described. Some of them said: His mockery of them is like what He informed us, blessed is His name, that He will do to them on the Day of Resurrection, in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿On the Day when the hypocrite men and the hypocrite women will say to those who believe, "Wait for us that we may acquire some of your light." It will be said, "Go back behind you and seek light." So a wall with a gate will be struck between them; its inner part will have mercy, and its outer part will be torment from before it. They will call to them, "Were we not with you?" They will say, "Yes"﴾ [Surah al-Hadid: 13, 14]. And the verse. And like what He informed us He did to the disbelievers, in His saying: ﴿And let not those who disbelieve think that Our giving them respite is good for themselves. We only give them respite that they may increase in sin﴾ [Surah Al 'Imran: 178]. So this, and what is similar to it, of Allah's mockery, exalted and mighty is He, and His derision, and His scheming, and His deception toward the hypocrites and the people of polytheism — according to those who hold this view and interpret it this way.

Others said: Rather, His mockery of them is His rebuke of them and His reproach to them for what they committed of acts of disobedience to Allah and disbelief in Him, as one says: "So-and-so is being mocked and ridiculed today," meaning by it that people rebuke him and reproach him, or His destruction of them and His annihilation of them by means of them [[The pronoun refers to Allah, exalted and mighty, and it is coordinated with his saying "His rebuke of them..."]], as 'Abid ibn al-Abras said:

Ask us about Hujr, son of Umm Qatam, when... the spear-shafts, the lances of thirst, were playing around him [[His Diwan: 16; Amali al-Murtada 1: 41. Hujr was the father of Imru' al-Qays, and it was the Banu Asad, the kin of 'Abid ibn al-Abras, who killed him. Umm Qatam is the mother of Hujr, king of Kinda. The "nawahil" are the plural of "nahil" and "nahila": "nahil" means thirsty, a description applied to spears, as though they thirst for blood; when they drink blood, they are quenched.]]

They claimed that the spear-shafts — which are the lances — have no play in them, but when they killed them and drove them away, he made that action of theirs a play upon those upon whom they did it. They said: So likewise the mockery of Allah, blessed is His praise, toward those who mocked Him among the people of hypocrisy and disbelief in Him: either His destruction of them and His annihilation of them, or His giving them respite so that He seizes them in a state of their security in themselves, suddenly, or His rebuke of them and of their leaders. They said: And likewise the meaning of scheming from Him, and deception, and derision.

Others said: The saying of Allah: ﴿They deceive Allah, and He is the one who deceives them﴾ [Surah al-Nisa': 142] is in the sense of reply, like the saying of a man to one who used to deceive him when he gained the upper hand over him: "I am the one who deceived you," when there had been no deception from him, but he said that when the matter came to him. They said: And likewise His saying: ﴿And they schemed, and Allah schemed, and Allah is the best of schemers﴾ [Surah Al 'Imran: 54], and "Allah mocks them," is in the sense of reply. Scheming and mockery do not proceed from Allah; the meaning is that scheming and mockery have befallen them.

Others said: His saying: ﴿Indeed, we are only mockers. Allah mocks them﴾, and His saying: ﴿They deceive Allah, and He is the one who deceives them﴾ [Surah al-Nisa': 142], and His saying: ﴿Those who mock them, Allah mocks them﴾ [Surah al-Tawbah: 79], ﴿They forgot Allah, so He forgot them﴾ [Surah al-Tawbah: 67], and what is similar to that, is an informing from Allah that He will requite them with the recompense of mockery and punish them with the punishment of deception. So He brought out His report about His recompense for them and His punishment of them in the form of His report about their action for which they deserved punishment in wording, even though the two meanings differ. Just as He, exalted is His praise, said: ﴿And the recompense for an evil is an evil like it﴾ [Surah al-Shura: 40]. It is known that the first is an evil from its doer, since it was an act of disobedience toward Allah, blessed and exalted, and the second is justice, because it is from Allah a recompense to the disobedient for disobedience. So the two, although their wordings agree, differ in meaning. Likewise His saying: ﴿So whoever transgresses against you, then transgress against him﴾ [Surah al-Baqarah: 194]; the first aggression is injustice, and the second is recompense, not injustice, but justice, because it is a punishment for the wrongdoer for his wrongdoing, even though its wording agrees with the wording of the first.

To this meaning they directed everything in the Qur'an of similar examples, which is a report about the scheming of Allah, exalted and mighty, against a people, and what is similar to that.

Others said: The meaning of that is that Allah, exalted and mighty, informed about the hypocrites that when they were alone with their devils [[mardah]] they said: "We are with you in your religion, in denying Muhammad (ﷺ) and what he brought," and "We are only mockers" with what we show them — from our saying to them: "We believe in Muhammad, peace be upon him, and what he brought" — meaning: we show them what is with us false, not true, nor guidance. They said: And that is one meaning of mockery, so Allah informed that He "mocks them," by showing them of His rulings in this world what is contrary to what they have with Him in the Hereafter, just as they showed the Prophet (ﷺ) and the believers in religion what they were contrary to in their inner selves.

The correct view on that from speech and interpretation, in our judgment, is: the meaning of mockery in the speech of the Arabs is the mocker's showing to the one mocked, by word and deed, what pleases him outwardly, while by that word and action toward him he causes him inward harm [[In the printed edition: "what pleases him and agrees with him outwardly".]]. Likewise the meaning of deception, derision and scheming.

Since that is so, and Allah, exalted is His praise, has made for the people of hypocrisy in this world, of the rulings — by what they showed with their tongues, of affirming Allah and His Messenger and what came from Allah, which admits them into the category of those covered by the name of Islam [[In the printed edition: "admitting them into the category..."; the phrase "al-mudkhili-hum" is a qualifier of "min al-iqrar".]] — even though they were concealing otherwise — the rulings of the Muslims who affirm their confession with their tongues, while their hearts' inner parts, their sound resolves, and their good deeds that confirm the soundness of their faith [[In the printed edition: "from the rulings of the Muslims..."; this is an erroneous addition; "ahkam" is in the accusative governed by "qad ja'ala li-ahl al-nifaq fi al-dunya min al-ahkam..."]] — together with Allah's knowledge of their lying, and His awareness of the corruption of their belief, and their doubt concerning what they claimed with their tongues that they affirmed — until they thought in the Hereafter, when they were gathered among those who were in their category in this world, that they would come to their place and enter their entrance. And Allah, majestic is His majesty — with His manifestation of what He had shown them of rulings that attached them in the hasty world and the delayed Hereafter, until the state of His distinguishing between them and His friends, and His separating them from them — [[The sentence structure: "And Allah, majestic is His majesty... prepared for them..."]] prepared for them from His painful punishment and His torment's retribution what He prepared for the greatest of His enemies and the worst of His servants, until He distinguished between them and His friends, and placed them from the levels of His hellfire in the lowest abyss — [[His saying: "It was known that He, exalted is His praise, by that from His action toward them..." is the answer to his saying "When that is so..." at the beginning of this paragraph.]] it was known that He, exalted is His praise, by that from His action toward them — even if it was a recompense for them for their actions, and justice in what He did of that to them because they deserved it from Him through their disobedience to Him — it was against them — by what He manifested to them of the matters He showed them: by attaching their rulings in this world to the rulings of His friends while they are His enemies, and gathering them in the Hereafter with the believers while they are among the deniers of Him, until He distinguished between them and them — mocking, and derisive toward them, and deceiving them, and scheming against them [[The author separated the speech in this paragraph; the arrangement of the phrase is as follows: "...it was known that He, exalted is His praise, by that from His action toward them... it was against them... mocking, and derisive toward them..." and what is between these two places is a separation for clarification.]]. Since the meaning of mockery, derision, scheming and deception is what we described before, not that this meaning in a state in which the one who mocks his companion is wronging him, or is unjust toward him in it, but that is its meaning in all its states, when the attributes that we have mentioned are found in the meaning of mockery and what is similar to it among its counterparts.

In agreement with what we have said about it, a report was transmitted from Ibn 'Abbas:

363 — Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: 'Uthman ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Bishr ibn 'Umarah narrated to us, from Abu Rawq, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: "Allah mocks them," he said: He mocks them for vengeance upon them [[Report 363: cited by Ibn Kathir in his Tafsir 1: 94, al-Suyuti 1: 31, and al-Shawkani 1: 33.]].

As for those who claimed that the saying of Allah, mentioned: "Allah mocks them," is only in the sense of a reply, and that there was no mockery, scheming or deception from Allah, they deny to Allah, exalted and mighty, what Allah has affirmed for Himself and made obligatory for Himself.
