426 - And al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: 'Ali ibn 'Asim narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, he said: The thunder is the name of an angel, and this sound is his glorification; when his driving of the clouds intensifies, the clouds are agitated and rub together, and the thunderbolts come out from between them.

427 - al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: 'Affan narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Awana narrated to us, from Musa al-Bazzar, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Ibn 'Abbas, he said: The thunder is an angel who drives the clouds with glorification, as the camel-driver drives the camels with his chant.

428 - al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn 'Abbad and Shababa narrated to us, both saying: Shu'ba narrated to us, from al-Hakam, from Mujahid, he said: The thunder is an angel who drives the clouds.

429 - Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad al-Zubayri narrated to us, saying: 'Attab ibn Ziyad narrated to us, from 'Ikrima, he said: The thunder is an angel in the clouds, who gathers the clouds as the shepherd gathers the camels.

430 - And Bishr narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, he said: The thunder is a creature of the creatures of Allah, mighty and majestic, who hears and obeys Allah, mighty and majestic.

431 - al-Qasim ibn al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn ibn Dawud narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from 'Ikrima, he said: Indeed the thunder is an angel commanded to drive the clouds, so he gathers them together, and that sound is his glorification.

432 - And al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, he said: The thunder is an angel.

433 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: al-Hajjaj ibn al-Minhal narrated to us, saying: Hammad ibn Salama narrated to us, from al-Mughira ibn Salim, from his father, or other than him, that 'Ali ibn Abi Talib said: The thunder: an angel.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 19 (part 2 of 4):

434- Al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, saying: Hammad narrated to us, saying: Musa ibn Salim Abu Jahdam, client of Ibn Abbas, informed us, saying: Ibn Abbas wrote to Abu al-Jald asking him about thunder (al-ra'd), and he said: "Thunder is an angel [[Report 434: This is a broken chain (isnad munqati'): Musa ibn Salim Abu Jahdam is trustworthy, but his narration from Ibn Abbas is mursal (missing a link). "Abu al-Jald," with a fatha on the jim, sukun on the lam, and a final unpointed dal, appears in the source manuscripts here and in the following reports as "Abu al-Khald" with a kha in place of the jim; this is a scribal error (tashif). Abu al-Jald is Jaylan (with a kasra on the jim) ibn Abi Farwa, also called Ibn Farwa al-Asadi al-Basri, as al-Bukhari mentioned in his biography in al-Kabir 1/2/250. Ibn Abi Hatim (1/1/547) said: "The author of books of the Torah and the like," and then narrated that Ahmad ibn Hanbal declared him reliable. Ibn Sa'd (7/1/161) also gave his biography, saying: "Abu al-Jald al-Juwni, a clan of the Azd, whose name is Jaylan ibn Farwa, was reliable." He is mentioned by Ibn Hibban in al-Thiqat (157), al-Duwlabi in al-Kuna (1:139), and al-Zabidi in Sharh al-Qamus (under jld and jyl). The Hafiz mentioned him in Lisan al-Mizan (2:144) under names, promised to give his biography under the kunyas (Abu al-Jald), but did not do so. Al-Tabari narrated a report from him in al-Tarikh (2:203). It will come in report 445 that he was "a man from the people of Hajar."]].
435- Al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muslim ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, saying: Umar ibn al-Walid al-Shanni narrated to us, from Ikrimah, who said: "Thunder is an angel who drives the clouds just as a shepherd drives camels." [[Umar ibn al-Walid al-Shanni Abu Salama al-Abdi is reliable; Ahmad, Ibn Ma'in and others declared him reliable, and Abu Hatim said: "I see no harm in his narrations." He is biographed in al-Ta'jil (304) and Ibn Abi Hatim (3/1/139). "Al-Shanni" is with a shin with a dot, as in al-Mushtabih (279); it appears in the printed edition without the dot, which is an error.]].
436- Sa'd ibn Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Hakam narrated to me, saying: Hafs ibn Umar narrated to us, saying: al-Hakam ibn Aban narrated to us, from Ikrimah, who said: "When Ibn Abbas heard thunder, he would say: 'Glory be to Him to whom thunder glorifies.'" He said: "And he used to say: Thunder is an angel who calls out to the rain just as a shepherd calls to his flock." [[Isnad 436: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Hakam: I found no biography for him except in Ibn Abi Hatim (2/1/92), who said: "I heard from him in Mecca and in Egypt; he is truthful (saduq)."]].

Others said: Thunder is wind that is suffocated beneath the clouds, so it rises, and that produces this sound.

Mention of those who said this:

437- Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad al-Zubayri narrated to us, saying: Bishr ibn Isma'il narrated to us, from Abu Kathir, who said: "I was with Abu al-Jald when a messenger of Ibn Abbas came to him with a letter, and he wrote back: 'You wrote asking me about thunder: thunder is wind.'" [[Isnad 437: This is a problematic isnad. I have found no biography of "Bishr ibn Isma'il," and I do not know who he is. Nor do I know who "Abu Kathir," the narrator from Abu al-Jald, is. This isnad will appear again: 443.]].

438- Ibrahim ibn Abd Allah narrated to me, saying: Imran ibn Maysara narrated to us, saying: Ibn Idris narrated to us, from al-Hasan ibn al-Furat, from his father [[Isnad 438: Imran ibn Maysara al-Minqari is reliable, one of the teachers of al-Bukhari, Abu Dawud, Abu Zur'a and Abu Hatim. Ibn Idris is Abd Allah ibn Idris al-Awdi: reliable, trustworthy, a proof. Al-Hasan ibn al-Furat is reliable; Muslim included him in his Sahih. His father: Furat ibn Abi Abd al-Rahman al-Qazzaz al-Tamimi, reliable, whose narrations were recorded by the authors of the six canonical books; however, his narration from Ibn Abbas is broken, as he narrates from the Successors (tabi'un).]] He said: "Ibn Abbas wrote to Abu al-Jald asking him about thunder, and he said: Thunder is wind."
[[Reports 419–438 together: Neither Ibn Kathir nor al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur mentioned them. Al-Baghawi in his tafsir (1:99–100) mentioned some of them, as did al-Qurtubi (1:187 onward).]]

Abu Ja'far said: If thunder is what Ibn Abbas and Mujahid mentioned, then the meaning of the verse is: "or like a downpour from the sky, in which are darkness, thunder and lightning." For if thunder is an angel who drives the clouds, it is not present in the downpour, since the downpour is only what pours down from the direction of the clouds, while thunder is in the atmosphere of the sky driving the clouds. Moreover, even if it were there, it would have no audible sound, so there would be no terror by which anyone is frightened. For it has been said that with every drop of rain there is an angel; so the angel named "thunder," if he were with the downpour, would not, when his voice is not heard, be other than one of those angels who descend with the rain to the earth, in that no one is terrified by his presence. Thus it is known—since the matter is as we have described according to the words of Ibn Abbas—that the meaning of the verse is: "or like a rain that pours from the sky, in which are darkness and the sound of thunder," if thunder is what Ibn Abbas said, and he relied on the mention of thunder by name to indicate what is meant in the speech about its sound. If thunder is what Abu al-Jald said, then nothing in the words "in which are darkness and thunder" is omitted, for the meaning of the speech then is: "in which are darkness and thunder, which is what we have described."

As for lightning (al-barq), the scholars differed about it. Some of them said:

439- Matar ibn Muhammad al-Dabbi narrated to us, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us (-h-); and Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to me, saying: Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to me (-h-); and Ahmad ibn Ishaq al-Ahwazi narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad al-Zubayri narrated to us, they all said: Sufyan al-Thawri narrated to us, from Salama ibn Kuhayl, from Sa'id ibn Ash'a, from Rabi'a ibn al-Abyad, from Ali, who said: "Lightning is the whips (makhariq) of the angels." [[Isnad 439: Salama ibn Kuhayl al-Hadrami is a well-known reliable narrator. Sa'id ibn Ash'a is Sa'id ibn Amr ibn Ash'a al-Kufi al-Qadi, named after his grandfather; he is reliable, and the two Shaykhs included him in their Sahihs. Rabi'a ibn al-Abyad, who narrated from Ali, I found no biography for except in Ibn Hibban's al-Thiqat (184), who said: "Rabi'a ibn al-Abyad narrates from Ali ibn Abi Talib; Ibn Ash'a narrated from him."
Makhariq is the plural of mikhraq: a cloth or the like that is twisted and struck with, and wrapped and used to frighten, and it is one of the games of children; from it the sword was named makhraq.]].

440- Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad al-Zubayri narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Malik ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, from Abu Malik, from al-Suddi, from Ibn Abbas: "Lightning is whips in the hands of the angels, with which they drive the clouds."

441- Al-Muthanna also narrated to me, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, saying: Hammad narrated to us, from al-Mughira ibn Salim, from his father or another, that Ali ibn Abi Talib said: "Thunder is the angel, and lightning is his striking of the clouds with an iron whip."

Others said: It is a whip of light with which the angel drives the clouds.

Mention of those who said this:

442- It was narrated to me from al-Minjab ibn al-Harith, who said: Bishr ibn Umara narrated to us, from Abu Rawq, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn Abbas, the same.

Others said: It is water.

Mention of those who said this:

443- Ahmad ibn Ishaq al-Ahwazi narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad al-Zubayri narrated to us, saying: Bishr ibn Isma'il narrated to us, from Abu Kathir, who said: "I was with Abu al-Jald when a messenger of Ibn Abbas came to him with a letter, and he wrote back: 'You wrote asking me about lightning: lightning is water.'"

444- Ibrahim ibn Abd Allah narrated to us, saying: Imran ibn Maysara narrated to us, saying: Ibn Idris narrated to us, from al-Hasan ibn al-Furat, from his father, who said: "Ibn Abbas wrote to Abu al-Jald asking him about lightning, and he said: Lightning is water."

445- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Ata', from a man from the people of Basra among their reciters, who said: "Ibn Abbas wrote to Abu al-Jald—a man from the people of Hajar—asking him about lightning, and he wrote back: 'You wrote asking me about lightning, and it is from the water.'"

Others said: It is the striking (masc) of an angel. [[Al-masc: striking with a sword, a whip or other things. Al-masa': fighting with swords. The meaning is that the angel strikes the clouds with his whip.]]

446- Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Uthman ibn al-Aswad, from Mujahid, who said: "Lightning is the striking of an angel." [[Isnad 446: Uthman ibn al-Aswad ibn Musa al-Makki: reliable, firm, prolific in narration; he narrates from Mujahid, and Sufyan al-Thawri narrates from him.]]

447- Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Hisham narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Muslim al-Ta'ifi, who said: "It reached me that lightning is an angel with four faces: the face of a man, the face of an ox, the face of an eagle, and the face of a lion. When he strikes with his wings, that is lightning." [[Isnad 447: Muhammad ibn Muslim ibn Sawsan al-Ta'ifi: Ibn Ma'in declared him reliable, Ibn Mahdi said: "His books are sound," and Ahmad ibn Hanbal weakened him; Muslim included one hadith from him in his Sahih as a supporting narration (mutaba'a).]]

448- Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Wahb ibn Sulayman, from Shu'ayb al-Ja'bai, who said: "In the Book of God: the angels who carry the Throne, each angel among them has the face of a man, an ox and a lion; when they move their wings, that is lightning." [[Report 448: Wahb ibn Sulayman al-Jundi, with a fatha on the jim and nun, Yemeni. Al-Bukhari said in al-Kabir (4/2/169–170): "From Shu'ayb al-Ja'bai, his statement; Ibn Jurayj narrated from him." I found no biography of him elsewhere. Shu'ayb al-Ja'bai: with a fatha on the jim and a light ba', attributed to "Ja'ba," a mountain in Yemen near al-Jund, as Yaqut and others said. Al-Bukhari gave him a biography in al-Kabir (2/2/219). Ibn Abi Hatim (2/1/353) also did, saying: "Shu'ayb al-Ja'bai: a Yemeni who narrates from the books [meaning the legends attributed to the People of the Book]; Salama ibn Wahram narrated from him," and then he affirmed that he is "Shu'ayb ibn al-Aswad," and narrated with his isnad from Zamʻa, from Shu'ayb ibn al-Aswad, who said: "I find in the Book of God..." Ibn Hajar's Lisan al-Mizan (3:150) says: "A storyteller, abandoned (matruk)." It then mentions some of his statements that reason does not accept, and says: "Ibn Hibban mentioned him in al-Thiqat and said: He had read the books."]]. Umayya ibn Abi al-Salt said:

A man, and an ox beneath the foot of his right side,
and the eagle for the other, and a watching lion.
[[His Diwan: 25. It will come in the commentary on the verse of thunder: 35 (13:109 Bulaq). The Diwan's version is: "beneath his right leg, and the eagle for the left." Al-Tabari said in the other place: "It is as if he said: beneath his leg, or beneath his right leg." The pronoun in "his leg" refers to Israfil, who was mentioned earlier in the poem. In the Diwan and in the other place in al-Tabari, the word is "Zahal" (?), as if he meant the constellations, but al-Tabari's argument here is clear, indicating that his version is "rijl" (leg).]]

449- Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Asim narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas: "Lightning is an angel."

450- And al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: "The thunderbolts (al-sawa'iq) are an angel who strikes the clouds with whips, striking whomever he wills with them." [[Reports 439–450: not mentioned by Ibn Kathir or in al-Durr al-Manthur. See al-Baghawi 1:99–100, and al-Qurtubi 1:188.]]

Abu Ja'far said: It is possible that what Ali ibn Abi Talib, Ibn Abbas and Mujahid said has one meaning. That is, the whips that Ali, may God be pleased with him, mentioned as being lightning are the whips of light with which the angel drives the clouds, as Ibn Abbas said. The angel's driving of the clouds with them is his striking of it (mas'uhu iyyahu). For the masa' among the Arabs originally means fighting with swords, and then they use it for everything that is struck with in war or otherwise, as the poet al-A'sha of Banu Tha'laba said, describing girls who play with their adornments and fight with them:

When they confront their equals,
and the masa' was with what is in the jawan.
[[His Diwan: 15. As you see, al-Tabari claimed he meant girls playing with their jewelry and fighting with them, but he erred in the meaning. al-A'sha meant something more eloquent. The "aqran" are the plural of qarn: one who matches you in strength and courage, and he meant men. "Yunazilna" refers to their coquetry and practice aiming to overcome men's minds and resolve. "Al-jawn" is the plural of jawna: a small round basket covered with leather in which perfume is kept; it is also said "ju'na" and "ju'n" with a hamza. Al-A'sha mentioned the ancient battle between men and women, in which women take adornment and perfume as weapons, confronting men seeking victory and dominance, and the temptation that overpowers minds and resolve, so that men fall captive in their hands.]]

It is said from it: "masa'ahu masa'an." It seems Mujahid only said "masa' malik" because the clouds do not strike the angel; rather, the thunder is the one who strikes with it, so he made it a verbal noun from "masa'ahu yamsa'uhu masa'an."

We have mentioned what is meant by "thunderbolt (al-sa'iqa)" in what Shahr ibn Hawshab said previously.

As for the interpretation of the verse, the people of interpretation differ about it:

Reports were transmitted from Ibn Abbas on this with several sayings. The first of them is what—

451- Muhammad ibn Humayd narrated it to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, client of Zayd ibn Thabit, from Ikrimah, or from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, regarding "or like a downpour from the sky, in which are darkness, thunder and lightning; they put their fingers in their ears because of the thunderbolts, fearing death": that is, they are in darkness from the disbelief they are in and fear of killing, upon what they are upon of opposition and intimidation from you, like the one described, who is in the darkness of the downpour; he puts his fingers in his ears from the thunderbolts, fearing death. The lightning nearly snatches away their sights—that is, because of the intensity of the light of truth. Whenever it shines for them, they walk in it, and when darkness falls on them, they stand still. That is, they recognize the truth and speak it, so they are upright in their speech; but when they turn back from it to disbelief, they stand bewildered. [[Report 451: al-Suyuti mentioned it in full in al-Durr al-Manthur (1:32–33), attributing it also to Ibn Ishaq and Ibn Abi Hatim. It contains, in both it and the manuscript, "from the opposition and intimidation from you"; Ibn Kathir quoted part of it (1:100).]]

And the other: what—

٤٥٢- حدثني به موسى بن هارون، قال: حدثنا عمرو، قال: حدثنا أسباط، عن السُّدّي في خبر ذكره، عن أبي مالك، وعن أبي صالح، عن ابن عباس، وعن مُرَّة، عن ابن مسعود، وعن ناس من أصحاب النبي (ﷺ): ﴿أَوْ كَصَيِّبٍ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ فِيهِ ظُلُمَاتٌ وَرَعْدٌ وَبَرْقٌ﴾ إلى ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ﴾. أما الصيب فهو المطر [[في المطبوعة: "وأما الصيب والمطر"، وهو خطأ.]]. كان رجلان من المنافقين من أهل المدينة قد هربا من رسول الله (ﷺ) إلى المشركين، فأصابهما هذا المطر الذي ذكره الله، فيه رعد شديد وصواعق وبرق، فجعلا كلما أضاءت لهما الصواعق جعلا أصابعهما في آذانهما، خوفًا أن تدخل الصواعق في مسامعهما فتقتلهما. وإذا لمع البرق مشيا في ضوئه [[في الأصول: "مشوا"، وصححناه من الدر المنثور والشوكاني.]]، وإذا لم يلمع لم يبصرا، وقاما مكانهما لا يمشيان [[في الأصول: "قاما مكانهما" بغير واو، وفي إحدى النسخ المخطوطة: "فقاما مكانهما"، واتفقت سائر الأصول وما نقل في الدر المنثور والشوكاني على حذف الفاء، والجملة لا تستقيم، فجعلناها "وقاما"، وهو صواب العبارة.]]، فجعلا يقولان: ليتنا قد أصبحنا فنأتي محمدًا فنضع أيدينا في يده. فأصبحا، فأتيا النبي (ﷺ) فأسلما، ووضعا أيديهما في يده، وحَسُن إسلامهما. فضرب الله شأن هذين المنافقين الخارجين مثلًا للمنافقين الذين بالمدينة. وكان المنافقون إذا حضروا مجلس النبي (ﷺ) جعلوا أصابعهم في آذانهم، خوفًا من كلام النبي (ﷺ)، أن ينزل فيهم شيء أو يُذكروا بشيء فيُقتلوا، كما كان ذانك المنافقان الخارجان يجعلان أصابعهما في آذانهما، وإذا أضاء لهم مشوا فيه. فإذا كثرت أموالهم، وولد لهم الغلمان [[في الدر المنثور: "وولدهم، وأصابوا..."، وفي الشوكاني: "وأولادهم وأصابوا..."]]، وأصابوا غنيمة أو فتحًا، مشوا فيه، وقالوا: إن دين محمد (ﷺ) دين صدق. فاستقاموا عليه، كما كان ذانك المنافقان يمشيان، إذا أضاء لهم البرق مشيا فيه، وإذا أظلم عليهم قاموا [[في المخطوطة: "إذا أضاء لهما مشيا، وإذا أظلم عليهما قاما". وفي الدر المنثور: "يمشيان إذا أضاء بهما البرق، وإذا أظلم عليهم قاموا"، وفي الشوكاني: "يمشيان إذا أضاء لهم البرق، وإذا أظلم عليهم قاموا"، وأجودهن ما في المخطوطة، وما في المطبوعة.]]. فكانوا إذا هلكت أموالهم، وولد لهم الجواري، وأصابهم البلاء [[في الدر المنثور والشوكاني: "إذا هلكت أموالهم وأولادهم وأصابهم البلاء".]]، قالوا: هذا من أجل دين محمد. فارتدوا كفارًا، كما قام ذانك المنافقان حين أظلم البرق عليهما [[الحديث ٤٥٢- نقل في الدر المنثور ١: ٣٢، والشوكاني ١: ٣٦ - ٣٧، وسيأتي في ص ٣٥٤ قول الطبري عن هذا الحديث وعن إسناده: "ولست أعلمه صحيحًا، إذ كنت بإسناده مرتابًا." وانظر ما كتبه أخي السيد أحمد محمد شاكر في هذا الإسناد فيما مضى في الخبر رقم: ١٦٨.
ويقول أحمد محمد شاكر عفا الله عنه: وحق لأبي جعفر رحمه الله أن يرتاب في إسناده. فإن هذا الإسناد فيه تساهل كثير، من جهة جمع مفرق التفاسير عن الصحابة في سياق واحد، تجمعه هذه الأسانيد، كما بينا آنفًا. فإذا كان الأمر في تفسير معنى آية، كان سهلًا ميسورًا قبوله، إذ يكون رأيًا أو آراء لبعض الصحابة في معنى الآية، وما في ذلك بأس. أما إذا ارتفع الخبر إلى درجة الحديث، بالإخبار عن واقعة معينة أو وقائع، كانت على عهد رسول الله (ﷺ)، من أسباب لنزول بعض الآيات، أو نحو ذلك، مما يلحق بالحديث المرفوع لفظًا أو حكمًا، كان قبول هذا الإسناد، إسناد تفسير السدي، محل نظر وارتياب. إذ هو رواية غير معروف مصدرها معرفة محددة: أي هؤلاء الذي قال هذا؟ وأيهم الذي عبر عنه باللفظ الذي جاء به؟ نعم، إن ظاهره أنه عن الصحابة: إما ابن عباس، وإما ابن مسعود، وإما "ناس من أصحاب النبي (ﷺ)"، فقد يقول قائل: إن مرجع الرواية فيه إلى الصحابة، وسواء أعرف الصحابي الراوي أم أبهم اسمه، فإن ذلك لا يخرجه عن رواية الصحابة، وجهالة الصحابي لا تضر؟ ولكن سياق هذه الروايات المطولة المفصلة، في التفسير وفي الحوادث المتعلقة بأسباب النزول، مثل الرواية التي هنا في هذا الموضع، مع إعراض أئمة الحديث، الذين أخرجوا الروايات الصحيحة، والروايات المقبولة مما هو دون الصحيح، عن إخراج هذه الرواية ونحوها، وإعراض مؤرخي السيرة عن روايتها أيضًا، كل أولئك يوجب الريبة في اتصال مثل هذه الرواية، وفي الجزم بنسبتها إلى الصحابة. إذ لعلها مما أُدرج في الرواية أثناء الحديث بها. والاحتياط في نسبة الحديث المرفوع وما في حكمه واجب.]].
والثالث: ما-

٤٥٣- حدثني به محمد بن سعد، قال: حدثني أبي، قال: حدثني عمي، عن أبيه، عن جده، عن ابن عباس: ﴿أَوْ كَصَيِّبٍ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ﴾، أي كمطر، ﴿فِيهِ ظُلُمَاتٌ وَرَعْدٌ وَبَرْقٌ﴾ إلى آخر الآية، هو مثل المنافق في ضوء ما تكلم به مما معه من كتاب الله وعمل، مراءاةً للناس، فإذا خلا وحده عمل بغيره. فهو في ظلمة ما أقام على ذلك. وأما الظلمات فالضلالة، وأما البرق فالإيمان، وهم أهل الكتاب.
وإذا أظلم عليهم، فهو رجل يأخذ بطرف الحق لا يستطيع أن يجاوزه [[الخبر ٤٥٣- في الدر المنثور ١: ٣٢، والشوكاني ١: ٣٧، مع اختلاف يسير في اللفظ.]].
والرابع: ما-

٤٥٤- حدثني به المثنى، قال: حدثنا عبد الله بن صالح، قال: حدثني معاوية بن صالح، عن علي بن أبي طلحة، عن ابن عباس: ﴿أَوْ كَصَيِّبٍ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ﴾، وهو المطر، ضرب مثله في القرآن، يقول: ﴿فِيهِ ظُلُمَاتٌ﴾، يقول: ابتلاء، ﴿وَرَعْدٌ﴾ يقول فيه تخويف، ﴿وَبَرْقٌ﴾، ﴿يَكَادُ الْبَرْقُ يَخْطَفُ أَبْصَارَهُمْ﴾ [[في الدر المنثور والشوكاني: "رعد وبرق - تخويف".]]، يقول: يكاد محكم القرآن يدل على عورات المنافقين، ﴿كُلَّمَا أَضَاءَ لَهُمْ مَشَوْا فِيهِ﴾. يقول: كلما أصاب المنافقون من الإسلام عزًّا اطمأنوا، وإن أصاب الإسلام نكبةٌ قاموا ليرجعوا إلى الكفر [[في المطبوعة: "قالوا رجعوا إلى الكفر"، وهو خطأ محض.]]. يقول: ﴿وَإِذَا أَظْلَمَ عَلَيْهِمْ قَامُوا﴾، كقوله: ﴿وَمِنَ النَّاسِ مَنْ يَعْبُدُ اللَّهَ عَلَى حَرْفٍ فَإِنْ أَصَابَهُ خَيْرٌ اطْمَأَنَّ بِهِ وَإِنْ أَصَابَتْهُ فِتْنَةٌ انْقَلَبَ عَلَى وَجْهِهِ خَسِرَ الدُّنْيَا وَالْآخِرَةَ ذَلِكَ هُوَ الْخُسْرَانُ الْمُبِينُ﴾ [سورة الحج: ١١] [[الخبر ٤٥٤- في الدر المنثور ١: ٣٢، والشوكاني ١: ٣٦، وبعضه في تفسير ابن كثير ١: ١٠٠.]].
ثم اختلف سائر أهل التأويل (أي أهل تفسير القرآن وتأويله) بعدُ في ذلك، نظيرَ ما روي عن ابن عباس من الاختلاف:

٤٥٥- فحدثني محمد بن عمرو الباهلي، قال: حدثنا أبو عاصم، عن عيسى بن ميمون، عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد، قال: إضاءة البرق وإظلامه، على نحو ذلك المثل.

٤٥٦- حدثني المثنى، قال: حدثنا أبو حذيفة، قال: حدثنا شبل، عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد، مثلَه.

٤٥٧- حدثنا عمرو بن علي، قال: حدثنا أبو عاصم، قال: حدثنا عيسى، عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد، مثله.

٤٥٨- وحدثنا بشر بن معاذ، قال: حدثنا يزيد بن زُرَيع، عن سعيد، عن قتادة، في قول الله: ﴿فِيهِ ظُلُمَاتٌ وَرَعْدٌ وَبَرْقٌ﴾ إلى قوله ﴿وَإِذَا أَظْلَمَ عَلَيْهِمْ قَامُوا﴾، فالمنافق إذا رأى في الإسلام رخاءً أو طمأنينة أو سلوة من عيش، قال: أنا معكم وأنا منكم، وإذا أصابته شديدة حقحق (أي تحير وجزع) والله عندها، فانقطع به، فلم يصبر على بلائها، ولم يحتسب أجرها، ولم يرج عاقبتها [[الأثر ٤٥٨- في الدر المنثور ١: ٣٣، وهو جزء من أثر قتادة بتمامه، ونصه هناك: "فإذا رأى المنافق من الإسلام طمأنينة وعافية ورخاء وسلوة عيش، قالوا: إنا معكم ومنكم. وإذا رأى من الإسلام شدة وبلاء، فقحقح عند الشدة، فلا يصبر لبلائها، ولم يحتسب أجرها، ولم يرج عاقبتها". وقوله في الدر المنثور "قحقح"، أظنه خطأ، وإنما هو حقحق كما في أصول الطبري. والحقحقة: أرفع السير وأتعبه للظهر. يريد أنه يسرع إسراعًا في حيرته حتى يهلكه التعب، وذلك أن المنافق لا يصبر على البلوى صبر المؤمن الراضي بما شاء الله وقدر. وقوله "فانقطع به" بالبناء للمجهول، يقال للدابة وللرجل "قُطع به وانقُطع به" بالبناء للمجهول، إذا عجز فلم ينهض، وأتاه أمر لا يقدر على أن يتحرك معه، وانقطع رجاؤه. وفي المخطوطة "فتقطع به" وليست بشيء. وفي المطبوعة: "وإذا أصابته شدة".]].

٤٥٩- وحدثنا الحسن بن يحيى، قال: أخبرنا عبد الرزاق، قال: أخبرنا معمر، عن قتادة: ﴿فِيهِ ظُلُمَاتٌ وَرَعْدٌ وَبَرْقٌ﴾، يقول: أجبنُ قوم [[في المطبوعة: "أخبر عن قوم"، وهو كلام بلا معنى.]] لا يسمعون شيئًا إلا إذا ظنوا أنهم هالكون فيه حذرًا من الموت، ﴿وَاللَّهُ مُحِيطٌ بِالْكَافِرِينَ﴾. ثم ضرب لهم مثلًا آخر فقال: ﴿يَكَادُ الْبَرْقُ يَخْطَفُ أَبْصَارَهُمْ كُلَّمَا أَضَاءَ لَهُمْ مَشَوْا فِيهِ﴾، يقول: هذا المنافق، إذا كثر ماله، وكثرت ماشيته، وأصابته عافية قال: لم يصبني منذ دخلت في ديني هذا إلا خير. ﴿وَإِذَا أَظْلَمَ عَلَيْهِمْ قَامُوا﴾ يقول: إذا ذهبت أموالهم، وهلكت مواشيهم، وأصابهم البلاء، قاموا متحيرين [[الأثر ٤٥٩- لم أجده بلفظه، وأثر قتادة في الدر المنثور ١: ٣٣ شبيه به في المعنى دون اللفظ.]].

٤٦٠- حدثني المثنى، قال: حدثنا إسحاق بن الحجاج، عن عبد الله بن أبي جعفر، عن أبيه، عن الربيع بن أنس: ﴿فِيهِ ظُلُمَاتٌ وَرَعْدٌ وَبَرْقٌ﴾، قال: مثلهم كمثل قوم ساروا في ليلة مظلمة، ولها مطر ورعد وبرق على جادة، فلما أبرقت أبصروا الجادة فمضوا فيها، وإذا ذهب البرق تحيروا. وكذلك المنافق، كلما تكلم بكلمة الإخلاص أضاء له، فإذا شك تحير ووقع في الظلمة، فكذلك قوله: ﴿كُلَّمَا أَضَاءَ لَهُمْ مَشَوْا فِيهِ وَإِذَا أَظْلَمَ عَلَيْهِمْ قَامُوا﴾، ثم قال: ﴿وَلَوْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ لَذَهَبَ بِسَمْعِهِمْ وَأَبْصَارِهِمْ﴾ في أسماعهم وأبصارهم التي عاشوا بها في الناس.
قال أبو جعفر (أي الطبري):

٤٦١- حدثنا القاسم، قال: حدثنا الحسين، قال: حدثنا أبو تميلة، عن عبيد بن سليمان الباهلي، عن الضحاك بن مزاحم: ﴿فِيهِ ظُلُمَاتٌ﴾، قال: أما الظلمات فالضلالة، والبرق الإيمان [[الأثر ٤٦١- في الأصول "أبو نميلة" بالنون، وهو خطأ، والصواب "أبو تميلة" بالتاء مصغرًا، وهو يحيى بن واضح، كما مضى في: ٣٩٢.]].

٤٦٢- حدثني يونس، قال: أخبرنا ابن وهب، قال: حدثني عبد الرحمن بن زيد في قوله: ﴿فِيهِ ظُلُمَاتٌ وَرَعْدٌ وَبَرْقٌ﴾، فقرأ حتى بلغ: ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ﴾، قال: هذا أيضًا مثلٌ ضربه الله للمنافقين، كانوا قد استناروا بالإسلام، كما استنار هذا بنور هذا البرق.

٤٦٣- حدثنا القاسم، قال: حدثنا الحسين، قال: حدثني حجاج، قال: قال ابن جريج: ليس في الأرض شيء سمعه المنافق إلا ظن أنه يراد به، وأنه الموت، كراهيةً له، والمنافق أكره خلق الله للموت، كما إذا كانوا بالبَراز في المطر، فرّوا من الصواعق [[في المخطوطة: "كما إذ كانوا بالبر في المطر..."، وهو شبيه بالصواب. والبراز: الفضاء من الأرض البعيد الواسع، ليس به شجر ولا غيره مما يُستتر به.]].

٤٦٤- حدثنا عمرو بن علي، قال: حدثنا أبو معاوية، قال: حدثنا ابن جريج، عن عطاء في قوله: ﴿أَوْ كَصَيِّبٍ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ فِيهِ ظُلُمَاتٌ وَرَعْدٌ وَبَرْقٌ﴾، قال: مثَلٌ ضُرب للكافر [[الآثار ٤٦٠ - ٤٦٤: لم أجدها في مكان.]].

وهذه الأقوال التي ذكرنا عمن رويناها عنه، فإنها، وإن اختلفت فيها ألفاظ قائليها، متقاربات المعاني، لأنها جميعًا تنبئ عن أن الله ضرب الصيب لظاهر إيمان المنافق مثلًا، ومثّل ما فيه من ظلمات لضلالته، وما فيه من ضياء برق لنور إيمانه [[في المخطوطة: "بضلالته... بنور إيمانه".]]؛ واتقاءه من الصواعق بتصيير أصابعه في أذنيه، لضعف جنانه ونخب فؤاده من حلول عقوبة الله بساحته [[في المطبوعة: "وتحير فؤاده". والنخب: الجبن وضعف القلب. ورجل نخب ونخيب ومنخوب الفؤاد: جبان لا خير فيه، كأنه منتزع الفؤاد، فلا فؤاد له.]]؛ ومشيه في ضوء البرق باستقامته على نور إيمانه؛ وقيامه في الظلام، لحيرته في ضلالته وارتكاسه في عمهه [[في المطبوعة: "باستقامته... بحيرته في ضلالته..."]].

فتأويل الآية إذًا، إذ كان الأمر على ما وصفنا، أو مثل ما استضاء به المنافقون، من قيلهم لرسول الله (ﷺ) وللمؤمنين بألسنتهم: آمنا بالله وباليوم الآخر وبمحمد وما جاء به، حتى صار لهم بذلك في الدنيا أحكام المؤمنين، وهم، مع إظهارهم بألسنتهم ما يُظهرون، بالله وبرسوله (ﷺ) وما جاء به من عند الله وباليوم الآخر مكذِّبون، ولخلاف ما يُظهرون بالألسن في قلوبهم معتقدون، على عمًى منهم، وجهالة بما هم عليه من الضلالة، لا يدرون أيّ الأمرين اللذين قد شرعا لهم [فيه] الهداية [[في المخطوطة: "سرعا" غير واضحة ولا منقوطة. ولعل الصواب "شرعا" من قولهم شرعت الإبل الماء: أي دخلته وخاضت فيه لتشرب منه. والمنافق يخوض في الإيمان بلسانه وفي الكفر بقلبه. وزدت ما بين القوسين ليستقيم المعنى. وفي المطبوعة بعد: "الهداية في الكفر الذي كانوا عليه"، بغير ألف الاستفهام، وهو خطأ لا يستقيم.]]، أفي الكفر الذي كانوا عليه قبل إرسال الله محمدًا (ﷺ) بما أرسله به إليهم، أم في الذي أتاهم به محمد (ﷺ) من عند ربهم؟ فهم من وعيد الله إياهم على لسان محمد (ﷺ) وجلون، وهم مع وجلهم من ذلك في حقيقته شاكُّون، في قلوبهم مرض فزادهم الله مرضًا. كمثل غيثٍ سرى ليلًا في مُزنة ظلماء وليلة مظلمة [[في المطبوعة: "وليل مظلمة"، وهو خطأ بيّن.]] يحدوها رعدٌ، ويستطير في حافاتها برقٌ شديد لمعانه [[في المطبوعة والمخطوطة: "يحذوها" بالذال المعجمة، وهو خطأ. وإنما هو من حداء السائق بإبله: وهو غناؤه لها وزجره إياها، وهو يسوقها. جعل صوت الرعد حداءً للسحاب. واستطار البرق: سطع وشق السحاب وانتشر في جوانب الغمام.]]، كثير خطرانه [[في المخطوطة: "خطواته" غير منقوطة، وهو تحريف. من قولهم خطر بسيفه أو سوطه يخطر خطرانًا: إذا رفعه مرة ووضعه أخرى، شبه شقائق البرق بالسوط يلمع مرة ويخفى أخرى.]]، يكاد سنا برقه يذهب بالأبصار ويختطفها من شدة ضيائه ونور شعاعه، وينهبط منها تارات صواعق، تكاد تدع النفوس من شدة أهوالها زواهق.

The passage is "the rain-cloud" is a parable for the outward profession of the hypocrites with their tongues, of affirmation and assent. The darkness within it is a parable for the doubt, denial and sickness of heart they conceal inwardly. As for the thunder and the lightning, they are a parable for the fear they feel of God's threat, which He conveyed through the tongue of His Messenger (ﷺ) in the verses of His Book, whether in this world or the next, that it might befall them, together with their doubt about it: Will it actually happen or not? Is it real, or is it a lie and falsehood? [[The word "مثل" (a parable) is the predicate of an omitted subject. The construction of the sentence, as you see, is: "As for the thunder and the lightning, they are a parable for the fear they feel."]] So, out of their fear that it might be true, they guard against it by affirming with their tongues what Muhammad (ﷺ) brought, out of concern for their own selves about destruction and the descent of punishments [[The "نقمات" (naqamat, punishments) is the plural of "نقمة" (niqmah), like "كلمات" and "كلمة", and means punishments.]]. This is the ta'wil (interpretation, explanation) of His saying, may His praise be exalted: ﴿They put their fingers in their ears because of the thunderclaps, fearing death﴾ [2:19]. He means by this: they guard against the threat of God, which He sent down in His Book through the tongue of His Messenger (ﷺ), by what they display with their tongues of outward affirmation, just as one who is afraid guards against the sounds of thunderclaps by covering his ears and putting his fingers in them, out of fear for himself from them.

I have mentioned the report narrated from Ibn Mas'ud and Ibn 'Abbas, that they both used to say: "The hypocrites, whenever they attended the assembly of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), would put their fingers in their ears out of dread of the words of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), lest something be revealed concerning them, or they be mentioned with something and then be killed." If that is sound, and I do not know it to be sound, since I am doubtful about its chain of transmission, then the saying narrated from them both is the correct one [[See hadith no. 452 and the commentary upon it.]]. But if it is not sound, then what we have said is more fitting as an interpretation of the verse, because God only related to us of their news at the beginning of the account of their story [[In the printed edition: "قصصهم" (qisasahum), which is acceptable. Next, in the manuscript: "أنهم عارفون يخادعون الله. . ." ("that they are knowing, deceiving God. . ."), but there is no sense in inserting the word "عارفون" (knowing).]], that they deceive God and His Messenger and the believers by their saying: "We believe in God and the Last Day", while their hearts are doubtful and their hearts are sick regarding the reality of what they claimed to believe in, of what the Messenger of God (ﷺ) brought from their Lord. By this He described them in all the verses of the Qur'an in which He mentioned their description. So likewise is it in this verse.

God made their putting their fingers in their ears a parable for their guarding against the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and the believers by what we have mentioned, that they guard against them with it, just as the one who hears the sound of the thunderclap puts his fingers in his ears. Such is the parable, a counterpart to God's, may His praise be exalted, portraying the threat He sent down concerning them in the verses of His Book by the sounds of thunderclaps. Likewise His saying "fearing death": He, may His praise be exalted, made it a parable for their fear and apprehension of the imminent arrival of the destroying punishment that was threatened against them, as the one who hears the sounds of thunderclaps puts his fingers in his ears, fearing destruction and death for himself, lest it snatch him away by its violence.

The accusative of His saying "fearing death" is in the manner in which "al-tikrimah" (honour, as a reason) is put in your saying: "I visited you as an honour to you", meaning: "for the sake of your honour." And as He, may His praise be exalted, said: ﴿And they call upon Us in hope and fear﴾ [21:90], as an explanation of the verb [[His saying "على التفسير للفعل" ("as an explanation of the verb") means that it is an object of purpose (maf'ul li-ajlihi).]].

It has been narrated from Qatadah that he used to interpret His saying "fearing death" as "guarding against death."

4 6 5 — Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated this to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from him.

That is a weak line of interpretation, because the people did not put their fingers in their ears out of fear of death, so that its meaning would be what he said it refers to, "out of fear of death." Rather, they put them in their ears out of fear of death [[In the printed edition: "مراد به" (murad bih), and both are the same.]].

Qatadah and Ibn Jurayj used to interpret His saying "They put their fingers in their ears because of the thunderclaps, fearing death" to mean that it is a description by God, may His praise be exalted, of the hypocrites, as having panic, weakness of heart and aversion to death. They based this interpretation on His saying: ﴿They think every shout is against them﴾ [63:4].

But the matter, in my view, is not as they both said. This is because among them there were those whose courage cannot be denied and whose valour cannot be repelled, such as Quzman, whom none of the believers equalled at Uhud, or fell short of [[In the manuscript this sentence reads: "كقزمان الذي لم يقم مقامه من المؤمنين كثير أحد ودونه" ("like Quzman, whom none of the believers equalled, many at Uhud and below him"), which is an obscure phrasing. I have adopted what is in the printed edition, and made "ودونه" and "أو دونه" ("or below him") so that the meaning is consistent. This is shown by the fact that the number of the polytheists killed on the day of Uhud was twenty-two men: Quzman alone killed ten of them, 'Ali ibn Abi Talib killed four, Hamzah ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib killed three, 'Asim ibn Thabit ibn al-Aqlah killed two, and Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas killed one man. As for the Messenger of God (ﷺ), he killed a man by patience (i.e., by holding him captive and executing him), and another was killed by his own hand (ﷺ). Quzman was an ally of the Banu Zafar. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Indeed he is among the people of the Fire." When he had shown his valour on the day of Uhud, he was told: "Rejoice!" He said: "With what should I rejoice? By God, I only fought for the honour of my people! Had it not been for that, I would not have fought." When his wound became severe and hurt him, he took an arrow from his quiver and killed himself with it.]]. Their aversion to attending the battles with the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and their abandonment of supporting him against his enemies, was because they were not perceptive in their religion, nor were they believers in the Messenger of God (ﷺ). So they were averse to being present with him at his battles, except to discourage others from him [[Al-takhdhil (discouragement): causing a man to forsake his companion, and deterring him from supporting him.]]. But this is a description by God, may His praise be exalted, of them, as those apprehensive of the descent of God's punishment upon them for their hypocrisy, whether in this world or the next.

Then He, may His praise be exalted, informed that the hypocrites, whom God described with the description He mentioned and to whom He gave the parables He described, even if they guard against His punishment and fear His chastisement with the apprehension of one who puts his fingers in his ears out of dread of the arrival of the threat He threatened them with in the verses of His Book, will not be saved by that from its descent upon their dwelling [[In the printed edition: "بعقوبتهم" (bi-'uqubatihim), and in some manuscripts: "بعقولهم" (bi-'uqulihim), and both are plainly erroneous. The "عقوة" ('aqwah) is the courtyard of a house and what is around it and near it.]] and its arrival at their courtyard, whether immediately in this world or in the next, because of what is in their hearts of sickness and doubt in its belief. So He said: ﴿And God encompasses the disbelievers﴾ [2:19], meaning: gatherer of them, so His punishment will descend upon them.

Mujahid used to interpret that as follows:

4 6 6 — Muhammad ibn 'Amr al-Bahili narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, from 'Isa ibn Maymun, from 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning the saying of God: ﴿And God encompasses the disbelievers﴾, he said: "He gathers them in Hell" [[The narration 466 is a completion of a narration in al-Durr al-Manthur 1:33.]].

As for Ibn 'Abbas, there was narrated from him concerning that:

4 6 7 — Ibn Humayd narrated it to me, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, client of Zayd ibn Thabit, from 'Ikrimah, or from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿And God encompasses the disbelievers﴾, he says: "God sends that punishment down upon them" [[The report 467 is a completion of a report in al-Durr al-Manthur 1:32–33.]].

4 6 8 — Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, concerning His saying: ﴿And God encompasses the disbelievers﴾, he said: "gatherer of them."

Then He, may His remembrance be exalted, returned to describing the hypocrites' profession with their tongues, and the account of it and of them and of their hypocrisy, and the completion of the parable He began to give for them, and for their doubt and the sickness of their hearts. So He said: ﴿The lightning almost snatches away their sight﴾ [2:20]. By "the lightning" He means the profession that they displayed with their tongues, of God and His Messenger and what he brought from their Lord. So He made the lightning a parable for it, according to the description we have already mentioned.

﴿Almost snatches away their sight﴾: He means, it takes it away, seizes it, and dazzles it with the intensity of its light and the brilliance of its radiance.

4 6 9 — As I was informed by al-Minjab ibn al-Harith, who said: Bishr ibn 'Umarah narrated to us, from Abu Rawq, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying: ﴿The lightning almost snatches away their sight﴾, he said: "It dazzles their sight, but does not do it." [[Report 469: I have not found it. "التمع البصر" (iltama'a al-basar) or other means: he snatched it away, seized it and departed with it. From the hadith: "When one of you is in prayer, let him not raise his gaze to the sky, lest his sight be dazzled (yaltami'), i.e., snatched away."]]

Abu Ja'far said: "al-khatf" is "plunder", and from it is the report narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he forbade "al-khatfah," meaning by it "plunder" [[As mentioned by Ibn al-Athir in al-Nihayah: "al-khatfah" is what a wolf snatches of the limbs of a sheep while it is alive, because whatever is severed from a living thing is dead. The prohibition on "al-khatfah" came when the Messenger of God (ﷺ) arrived in Medina and saw the people cutting off the humps of camels and the rumps of sheep and eating them. He said: "al-khatfah" is the single act of snatching, so the snatched limb is named by it. As for "al-nahbah" and "al-nahbaa," it is the name of what is plundered, and its explanation came in a hadith in Sunan Abi Dawud 3:88: "The people obtained booty and plundered it, so 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Samurah stood up to address them and said: I heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ) forbid "al-nahbaa." In the same chapter of Sunan Abi Dawud, there is a report from a man of the Ansar who said: "We set out with the Messenger of God (ﷺ) on a journey, and the people suffered great hardship and distress. They obtained some sheep and plundered them, and our cooking pots were boiling when the Messenger of God (ﷺ) came walking on his bow, and overturned our pots with his bow, then began to cover the meat with dust, and then said: Indeed plundering is no more lawful than carrion."]]. From it is also said of the hook with which one draws the bucket from the well: "khutaf" (a grappling hook), because of its snatching and seizing what clings to it. From it is the saying of the poet Nabighah of the Banu Dhubyan:

*Khataatif hujnun fi hibaalin matinatin... tamudd bi-ha aydin ilayka nawaz'i*
[[His Diwan: 41. Before it is the famous verse: "Indeed you are like the night which overtakes me, and even if I suppose that escape from you is wide..." "Khataatif": plural of "khuttaf." "Hujn": plural of "ahjan," which is the crooked thing that has a hook at its head. He said "tamudd bi-ha" and did not say "tamuddu-ha," because he did not intend the pulling of the ropes with the hooks, but rather the hand which extends with them, and in which are the hooks, because the hand is that which follows a thing wherever it goes (see what will come later about the introduction of the preposition "bi" with a verb like this, p. 360, lines 6–9). His saying "ilayka" is connected to "nawaz'i." "Nawaz'i" is the plural of "nazi'" and "nazi'ah," from the saying "nazaʻa al-dalw min al-bi'r yanzi'uha," meaning: he pulled it and drew it out. That is, these hands pull whatever they will to you and return it to you. The verse is connected to the one before it and explains his saying "fa-innaka ka-l-layl alladhi huwa mudriki" ("indeed you are like the night which overtakes me"). He intended to make the night and what is seen in it appear terrifying; the hooked hooks follow it wherever it goes, from which there is no escape.]]. So He made the light of the lightning and the intensity of its radiance a parable for the brightness of their profession with their tongues of God and His Messenger (ﷺ) and what he brought from God and the Last Day, and the radiance of its light.

Then He, may His remembrance be exalted, said: ﴿Whenever it illuminates for them, they walk in it﴾ [2:20], meaning that whenever the lightning illuminates for them, and He made the lightning a parable for their faith. He only intends by that: whenever faith illuminates for them, and its illumination for them is that they see in it what pleases them in the immediate affairs of their worldly life: victory over enemies, gaining spoils in raids, abundance of conquests and their benefits, prosperity in wealth, and safety of bodies, family and children. That is its illumination for them, because they only display with their tongues what they display of affirmation, seeking that, and as a defence for themselves, their wealth, their families and their offspring. And they are, as God, may His praise be exalted, described them with His saying: ﴿And among the people is he who worships God on an edge; if good befalls him, he is content with it, but if a trial befalls him, he turns back on his face﴾ [22:11].

By His saying "they walk in it", He means: they walk in the light of the lightning. That is only a parable for their profession according to what we have described. The meaning is: whenever they see in faith what pleases them in the immediate affairs of their worldly life, as we have described, they remain firm in it and persist in it, just as a traveller walks in the darkness of the night and the darkness of the rain-cloud which God, may His praise be exalted, described, whenever lightning flashes in it, he sees his path in it.

﴿And when it grows dark﴾ [2:20]: meaning, the light of the lightning departs from them.

By His saying "upon them" He means: upon the travellers in the rain-cloud which He described, may His remembrance be exalted. That is a parable for the hypocrites. The meaning of the darkening of that is: whenever the hypocrites do not see in Islam what pleases them in their worldly life, at the time when God tests the believers among His servants with adversity, and purifies them with hardships and trials, through their failure in their raids, the enemy's triumph over them [[In the printed edition: "وإنالة عدوهم" (wa-inalat 'aduwwihim), which is an error. "Al-idalah" is victory, which comes from the turn of fortune in war, namely that one army is defeated once, and another army defeats it at another time. One says: "O God, grant us victory over our enemy!" meaning: O God, grant us the ascendancy over him and help us.]], or the withdrawal of their worldly life from them, they remain in their hypocrisy and persist in their error, just as the traveller stands in the rain-cloud which God, may His remembrance be exalted, described, when it grows dark and the light of the lightning vanishes, so he is perplexed in his path and does not know his way [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "كما قام السائرون في الصيب" ("as the travellers stood in the rain-cloud"), which is an error. The correct reading is from another manuscript: "كما قام السائر في الصيب"]].

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 20:

The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And if Allah had willed, He could have taken away their hearing and their sight﴾

Abu Ja'far said: The reason Allah, mentioned in His majesty, singled out hearing and sight, saying that if He willed He could have taken them away from the hypocrites rather than the rest of the limbs of their bodies [[In the manuscript: "rather than the rest of their bodies."]], is because of what was mentioned of them in the two verses, namely His words: "They put their fingers in their ears against the thunderclaps," and His words: "The lightning nearly snatches away their sight; every time it lights up for them they walk in it." Their mention in these two verses came by way of a parable. Then, mentioned in His praise, He followed this mention by saying that if He willed He could have taken it away from the hypocrites as a punishment for their hypocrisy and disbelief, a threat from Allah to them, just as He threatened them in the verse before it with His words: "And Allah encompasses the disbelievers." In this way He, mentioned in His majesty, described Himself as the One who has power over them and over their gathering, to make His wrath descend upon them and to send down His vengeance on them, warning them of His might and frightening them with His punishment, so that they might guard against His might and hasten to Him in repentance.

470. As Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, from Ikrimah, or from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas: "And if Allah had willed, He could have taken away their hearing and their sight," because of what they abandoned of the truth after knowing it [[Report 470 is the completion of the report he cited in al-Durr al-Manthur 1: 32–33; its beginning has passed earlier: 451, 467.]].

471. And al-Muthanna narrated to me, he said: Ishaq narrated to us, he said: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, who said: Then He said — meaning Allah said — concerning their hearing, meaning the hearing of the hypocrites, and their sight, by which they lived among people: "And if Allah had willed, He could have taken away their hearing and their sight" [[Report 471 is part of the earlier report no. 460.]].

Abu Ja'far said: The meaning of His words "to take away their hearing and their sight" is: to take away their hearing and their sight. But when the Arabs insert the preposition bi (with) in such constructions they say: "I took away with his sight" (dhahabtu bi-basarihi), and when they omit the bi they say: "I took away his sight" (adhhabtu basarahu). As Allah, mentioned in His majesty, said: ﴿Bring us our morning meal﴾ [Surah al-Kahf: 62]; and if the bi were inserted before the morning meal it would be said: "Bring us with our morning meal" (i'tina bi-ghada'ina) [[See Ma'ani al-Qur'an by al-Farra' 1: 19. And see what has passed, p. 357, note 3.]].

Abu Ja'far said: If someone asks us: how is it said "to take away their hearing" in the singular, and "their sight" in the plural? You know that the report concerning hearing is a report about the hearing of a group, just as the report concerning sight is a report about the sight of a group? [[In the manuscript: "that the report concerning hearing", and this is better; and better still is "the report concerning hearing" as will come in what follows. In the printed edition: "as the report concerning sight", and the manuscript reading is better.]]

It is said: The grammarians of Arabic have differed on this. Some of the grammarians of Kufa said: he used the singular for hearing because he meant by it the verbal noun and intended by it the faculty in general, and he used the plural for sight because he meant by it the eyes. And some of the grammarians of Basra held that hearing, although in singular form, carries the meaning of a plural [[In the manuscript: "in the meaning of a group", which is a good reading.]]. He argued for this with Allah's words: ﴿Their glance does not return to them﴾ [Surah Ibrahim: 43], meaning: their glances do not return to them; and with His words: ﴿And they turn their backs﴾ [Surah al-Qamar: 45], meaning: their backs. In my view this is permissible because the speech contains what indicates that the plural is intended, so its indication of the intended meaning, and its conveying the sense of a group through the singular of hearing, makes it sufficient without its pluralization [[In the printed edition the wording is garbled; the manuscript reading has been corrected as shown. His phrase "its pluralization" (jim'ihi) means its plural form, as al-Tabari often uses jima' for jam'.]]. If one did with sight the parallel of what was done with hearing, or did with hearing the parallel of what was done with sights, in either pluralizing or singularizing, it would be eloquent and sound, for the reason we have mentioned, as the poet said:

Eat in part of your bellies, so you may be chaste, for our time is a lean time [[A line from the verses of Sibawayh whose speaker is unknown: Sibawayh 1: 108; al-Khizana 3: 379–381; see also Amali Ibn al-Shajari 1: 311, 2: 35, 38, 343, where the version reads "in half of your bellies." In the manuscript: "so you may live" instead of "so you may be chaste," a version mentioned by the author of al-Khizana. All versions read "for our time..."]]

So he used the singular "belly" while meaning the bellies, for the reason we have described.

* *

The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, Allah is over all things Competent﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Allah, mentioned in His majesty, described Himself here as having power over all things, because He warned the hypocrites of His might and His might's violence, and informed them that He encompasses them, and that He is capable of taking away their hearing and their sight. Then He said: So fear Me, O hypocrites, and beware of deceiving Me and deceiving My Messenger and the people of faith in Me, lest I bring My vengeance upon you, for I am capable of that and of other things. The meaning of "qadir" is "qadir" (capable), just as the meaning of "alim" is "alim" (knowing), according to what I have described before concerning its like, namely the increase in the meaning of the form fa'il over fa'il in praise and blame [[See the explanation of His words "al-Rahim" earlier: p. 126.]].

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 21:

On the interpretation of the words of God, exalted is He: ﴿O mankind, worship your Lord, who created you and those before you﴾

Abu Ja'far said: God, mighty is His praise, commanded both groups, of whom He informed that one of them, for whom it is the same whether they are warned or not warned, that they do not believe [[In the manuscript: "Whether you warn them or do not warn them", and both are the same in meaning.]], because He has sealed their hearts and their hearing [[In the printed edition: "and their hearing and their sight", and the correct reading is to omit "and their sight", since it does not fall within the meaning of sealing, as has passed in the explanation of the verse.]], and of the other, that he deceives God and those who believe with what he displays with his tongue of his saying: "We believe in God and the Last Day", while concealing within himself the opposite of that, and a sickness in his heart, and doubt regarding the reality of what he displays of that; and [He commanded] the rest of His created beings who are obligated, to humble themselves and submit to Him in obedience, and to single out Lordship and worship for Him alone, apart from idols, images and deities. For He, mighty is His remembrance, is their Creator and the Creator of those before them among their forefathers and grandfathers, and the Creator of their images, idols and deities. So He, mighty is His remembrance, said to them: He who created you and created your forefathers and grandfathers and all creation other than you, and who is able to harm and benefit you, is more deserving of obedience than one who cannot benefit or harm you [[In the manuscript: "for harm nor benefit", and both are the same.]].

Ibn 'Abbas, as has been transmitted to us from him, said regarding this the like of what we have said, except that it is reported from him that he said concerning the meaning of "worship your Lord": make your Lord one (waḥḥidū). We have already shown, in what has passed in this our book, that the meaning of worship ('ibadah) is submission to God in obedience and humbling oneself to Him in submission [[It has passed in the explanation of His saying "You alone we worship" (iyyaka na'budu), p. 160.]]. What Ibn 'Abbas intended, God willing, by his saying in explaining His words "worship your Lord" is: make Him one, that is, single out obedience and worship for your Lord apart from the rest of His creation [[In the manuscript: "make Him one for Him, single out...", which has no meaning.]].

472 – Muhammad ibn Humayd narrated to us, who said: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, from 'Ikrimah, or from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: God said: "O mankind, worship your Lord", addressed to both groups together, of the disbelievers and the hypocrites, meaning: make your Lord one, who created you and those before you [[Report 472 – in al-Durr al-Manthur 1: 33, Ibn Kathir 1: 105, al-Shawkani 1: 38. In al-Durr and al-Shawkani: "of the disbelievers and the believers", and Ibn Kathir agrees with the sources of al-Tabari.]].

473 – Musa ibn Harun narrated to me, who said: 'Amr ibn Hammad narrated to us, from Asbat, from al-Suddi in a report he mentioned, from Abu Malik, and from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas – and from Murrah, from Ibn Mas'ud, and from some of the companions of the Prophet (ﷺ): "O mankind, worship your Lord who created you and those before you," he says: He created you and created those before you [[Report 473 – in al-Durr al-Manthur 1: 33, where its takhrij is not attributed to Ibn Jarir. In the manuscript: "created you and those...".]].

Abu Ja'far said: This verse is among the strongest proofs against the view of one who claims that it is impermissible to impose on people what they cannot bear unless God first gives the obligated person the help (ma'unah) to fulfil what He has imposed on him. This is because God commanded those we have described to worship Him and to repent from their disbelief, after informing about them that they do not believe and that they will not return from their misguidance.

* *

On the interpretation of His words: ﴿so that you may be God-conscious (la'allakum tattaqun)﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Its interpretation is: so that you may be God-conscious by worshipping your Lord who created you, and by your obedience to Him in what He commanded you and forbade you, and by your singling Him out in worship, so that you may guard against His wrath and anger lest they descend upon you, and that you may be among the God-conscious whom their Lord is pleased with [[In the printed edition: "له بالعبادة" ("for Him in worship"), which is an error.]].

Mujahid used to say concerning the interpretation of His saying "so that you may be God-conscious": "you obey."

474 – Ibn Waki' narrated to us, who said: my father narrated to me, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying "so that you may be God-conscious", he said: so that you may obey [[Report 474 – in al-Durr al-Manthur 1: 34.]].

Abu Ja'far said: What I think Mujahid intended by this saying is: so that you may guard yourselves against your Lord by your obedience to Him and your turning away from your misguidance.

Abu Ja'far said: If someone says to us: how then did He, mighty is His praise, say "so that you may be God-conscious"? Was He not knowing of what their affair would come to if they worshipped Him and obeyed Him, so that He said to them: "perhaps if you do that you will be God-conscious," thereby conveying the report about the outcome of their worship of Him in the manner of doubt?

It is said to him: that is not the meaning you imagine. The meaning is: worship your Lord who created you and those before you, so that you may guard yourselves through His obedience, His unity, and singling Him out in lordship and worship [[Al-Tabari means that the Arabs use "la'alla" stripped of doubt, in the sense of the particle "li" of purpose (kay), as Ibn al-Shajari said in his Amali 1: 51.]], as the poet said:

"You said to us, 'Cease the wars, so that perhaps we might cease,' and you pledged to us every pledge.
So when we ceased the war, your covenants were like the flash of a mirage in the wide desert, sparkling."

[[I do not know who said them; Ibn al-Shajari transmitted them from al-Tabari, as I probably recall, in his Amali 1: 51.]] [[Ibn al-Shajari's version reads "in the mula" (the open expanse). Al-falah is the plural of falat, meaning level land with nothing in it and a wide desert; al-mula is the desert and the expanse of land – both are the same in meaning.]]

He means by this: You said to us, "Cease fighting so that we may cease," and that is because "la'alla" in this place, if it were doubt, they would not have pledged every pledge to them.

The Exegesis of His Words, Glorified Be His Praise: ﴿Who made the earth a bed for you﴾

His words, "Who made the earth a bed for you," are a continuation of the first "who" in His words, "Worship your Lord, who created you" (Q 2:21), and both are descriptions (naʿt) of "your Lord." It is as if He said: Worship your Lord, who created you and those before you, who made the earth a bed for you. He means by this that He made the earth for you a spread-out, prepared (muwaṭṭa’) cradle and a place of settlement upon which you can rest. Our Lord, glorified be His remembrance, by this speech reminds His servants of His blessings toward them and His favours upon them, so that they may remember His bounties to them and then turn in repentance to His obedience, out of His kindness towards them, His compassion for them, and His mercy upon them, without any need on His part for their worship, but so that He may complete His blessing upon them and that they may perhaps be guided.

475 – As Mūsā ibn Hārūn related to me, saying: ʿAmr told us, saying: Asbāṭ told us, from al-Suddī in a report he mentioned, from Abū Mālik and Abū Ṣāliḥ, from Ibn ʿAbbās – and from Murrah, from Ibn Masʿūd, and from some companions of the Prophet ﷺ: "Who made the earth a bed for you": it is a bed upon which one walks, and it is a cradle and a resting-place.

476 – Bishr ibn Muʿādh told us, saying: Yazīd ibn Zurayʿ told us, from Saʿīd, from Qatādah: "Who made the earth a bed for you," he said: a cradle for you.

477 – Al-Muthannā related to me, saying: Isḥāq told us, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Abī Jaʿfar, from his father, from al-Rabīʿ ibn Anas: "Who made the earth a bed for you," i.e., a cradle.

* *

The Exegesis of His Words: ﴿and the sky a canopy﴾

Abū Jaʿfar said: The sky was named "sky" (samāʾ) because of its height above the earth and above its inhabitants among His creation. Everything that is above something else is a samāʾ for what is beneath it. For this reason the ceiling of a house is called samāwah, because it is high above it. For this reason it is said: "samā Fulān li-Fulān," when he rose up for him and aimed towards him from on high, as al-Farazdaq said:

They rose against Najrān of Yemen and its people… and Najrān is a land whose camel has not been tamed by its chieftains.

And as the poet Nābighah of Banū Dhubyān said:

A glance rose up for me, and I saw from it… the curtain of the howdah and the thin veil of the litter.

He means by this: a glance rose up for me and appeared, so likewise the sky was named "sky" for the earth because of its height and its overlooking of it.

478 – As Mūsā ibn Hārūn related to me, saying: ʿAmr ibn Ḥammād told us, saying: Asbāṭ told us, from al-Suddī in a report he mentioned, from Abū Mālik and Abū Ṣāliḥ, from Ibn ʿAbbās – and from Murrah, from Ibn Masʿūd, and from some companions of the Prophet ﷺ: "And the sky a canopy": the construction of the sky over the earth is like a dome, and it is a roof over the earth.

479 – Bishr ibn Muʿādh told us, saying: Yazīd told us, from Saʿīd, from Qatādah, concerning the word of God: "and the sky a canopy," he said: He made the sky a ceiling for you.

It is only that He, dhikruhu ta‘ālā, mentioned the sky and the earth among the blessings He had bestowed upon them, because from them come their sustenance, their provisions and their livelihoods, and by them their worldly affairs are sustained. He informed them that the One who created them and created all that is in them and the blessings they enjoy is the one deserving their obedience and worthy of their gratitude and worship, not the idols and images which neither harm nor benefit.

* *

The Exegesis of the Word of God, Glorified Be His Praise: ﴿And He sent down from the sky water, and brought forth thereby fruits as provision for you﴾

He, dhikruhu ta‘ālā, means by this that He sent down rain from the sky, and by that rain brought forth from what they had planted in the earth of their crops and their palm-trees, fruits – as provision for them, nourishment and sustenance. Thereby He alerted them to His power and authority, and reminded them of His blessings toward them, and that He is the One who created them, the One who provides for them and sustains them, not those whom they had made equals and rivals to Him among the idols and deities.

Then He rebuked them against making rivals to Him, though they knew that this is as He informed them, and that He has no rival or equal, and that for them there is no one who benefits or harms, no creator or provider, apart from Him.

* *

The Exegesis of His Words, Exalted Be He: ﴿So do not set up rivals to God﴾

Abū Jaʿfar said: "Andād" is the plural of "nidd," and "nidd" means an equal and a like, as Ḥassān ibn Thābit said:

Would you satirise him, when you are not his nidd? Then the evil of you both is the ransom for the good of you both.

He means by his words, "you are not his nidd": you are not his like nor his equal. Everything that is a counterpart to something and resembles it is its nidd.

480 – Bishr ibn Muʿādh told us, saying: Yazīd told us, from Saʿīd, from Qatādah: "So do not set up rivals to God," i.e., equals.

481 – Al-Muthannā related to me, saying: Abū Ḥudhayfah related to me, saying: Shibl told us, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid: "So do not set up rivals to God," i.e., equals.

482 – Mūsā ibn Hārūn related to me, saying: ʿAmr told us, saying: Asbāṭ told us, from al-Suddī, in a report he mentioned, from Abū Mālik and Abū Ṣāliḥ, from Ibn ʿAbbās – and from Murrah, from Ibn Masʿūd, and from some companions of the Prophet ﷺ: "So do not set up rivals to God," he said: equals among men whom you obey in disobedience to God.

483 – Yūnus ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning the word of God: "So do not set up rivals to God," he said: the andād are the gods which they set up alongside Him, and they gave them the like of what they gave Him.

484 – I was told from al-Minjāb, saying: Bishr told us, from Abū Rawq, from al-Ḍaḥḥāk, from Ibn ʿAbbās, concerning His words: "So do not set up rivals to God," he said: likenesses.

485 – Muḥammad ibn Sinān related to me, saying: Abū ʿĀṣim told us, from Shabīb, from ʿIkrimah: "So do not set up rivals to God," that you say: "Were it not for our dog, a thief would have entered the house on us; were it not for our dog, it would have barked in the house," and similar things.

Then God, exalted be He, forbade them to associate anything with Him, or to worship other than Him, or to take for Him a rival and equal in obedience. He said: just as there is no partner to Me in your creation, in your provision which I give you, in My sovereignty over you, and in My blessings which I have bestowed upon you, so likewise devote to Me obedience, and make worship sincerely for Me, and do not make for Me a partner and rival from among My creatures, for you know that every blessing upon you is from Me.

* *

The Exegesis of His Words: ﴿while you know﴾

Abū Jaʿfar said: The interpreters differed concerning those who are meant by this verse:

Some of them said: it means all the polytheists, both the Arab polytheists and the People of the Book.

Others said: it means the two groups of the People of the Book, the People of the Torah and the Gospel.

Mention of those who said: it means all worshippers of idols among the Arabs and the disbelievers of the two groups of the People of the Book:

486 – Muḥammad ibn Ḥumayd told us, saying: Salamah ibn al-Faḍl told us, from Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq, from Muḥammad ibn Abī Muḥammad, mawlā of Zayd ibn Thābit, from ʿIkrimah, or from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: That was revealed concerning both groups, the disbelievers and the hypocrites. He, dhikruhu ta‘ālā, meant by His words: "So do not set up rivals to God while you know," i.e., do not associate with God anything other than Him, of the rivals which neither benefit nor harm, while you know that you have no lord who provides for you other than Him, and you have known that what the Messenger calls you to of His oneness is the truth without doubt.

487 – Bishr told us, saying: Yazīd told us, from Saʿīd, from Qatādah, concerning His words: "while you know," i.e., you know that God created you and created the heavens and the earth, and then you make for Him rivals.

Mention of those who said: it means the People of the Book:

488 – Abū Kurayb told us, saying: Wakīʿ told us, from Sufyān, from a man, from Mujāhid: "So do not set up rivals to God while you know," that He is one God in the Torah and the Gospel.

489 – Al-Muthannā ibn Ibrāhīm related to me, saying: Qabīṣah told us, saying: Sufyān told us, from Mujāhid, the like of it.

490 – Al-Muthannā related to me, saying: Abū Ḥudhayfah told us, saying: Shibl told us, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid: "while you know," he says: while you know that He has no rival in the Torah and the Gospel.

Abū Jaʿfar said: I think that what led Mujāhid to this interpretation, and to attributing it to the address to the People of the Torah and the Gospel to the exclusion of others, is his supposition that the Arabs did not know that God is their Creator and Provider, given their denial of His oneness and their association with Him in worship of others. But that is a saying! Yet God, exalted be His praise, has informed in His Book about them that they acknowledged His oneness, though they associated with Him in worship what they associated. So He, exalted be His praise, said: ﴿And if you asked them who created them, they would surely say: God﴾ (Q 43:87), and He said: ﴿Say: Who provides for you from the sky and the earth, or who controls hearing and sight, and who brings forth the living from the dead and brings forth the dead from the living, and who arranges the affair? They will say: God. Say: Will you not then be wary?﴾ (Q 10:31).

So the more correct interpretation of His words, "while you know," since the knowledge of the Arabs of God's oneness, that He is the Originator of creation, its Creator and Provider, was like the knowledge of the two groups of the People of the Book, and since the verse contains no indication that God, exalted be His praise, meant by "while you know" one of the two parties, but rather the address is general to all mankind, for He challenged all people by His words, "O people, worship your Lord," is that its interpretation be what Ibn ʿAbbās and Qatādah said: that it means every responsible person who knows God's oneness, that He has no partner in His creation, and who associates with Him in worship another, whoever he may be among people, Arab or non-Arab, literate or unlettered; even if the address was to the disbelievers of the People of the Book who were around the abode of the Messenger of God ﷺ, and the hypocrites among them, and those among them who were polytheists and then moved to hypocrisy upon the arrival of the Messenger of God ﷺ.

The commentary on the verse: "And if you are in doubt about what We have sent down upon Our servant, then produce a surah like it, and call upon your witnesses other than Allah, if you are truthful" (2:23).

Abu Ja'far said: This is an argument from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, addressed to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) against the polytheists of his people among the Arabs, their hypocrites, and the disbelievers and misguided of the People of the Book, the very ones with whose account He opened His saying, "Indeed, those who disbelieve, it is alike for them whether you warn them or do not warn them" (2:6). It is to them that these verses are addressed, and by them He means their counterparts [[In the printed edition: "and He informs of their attributes," but in the manuscript it reads "wa-harnahum ta'nā bihā," unpointed and unclear, so the editors chose a reading that carries no meaning! Al-darība (pl. of ḍarīb): "fulān ḍarīb fulān" means his equal or like.]]. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: And if you, O polytheists of the Arabs and disbelievers of the two scriptures, are in doubt—and doubt is ar-raib—about what We have sent down upon Our servant Muhammad (ﷺ) of light, proof, and the verses of the Criterion, that it is from Me, and that I am the One who sent it down to him, and you did not believe in it nor confirm him in what he says, then produce a proof that refutes his proof, for you know that the proof of every one possessing prophethood for the truth of his claim to prophethood is that he brings a sign that all creation is unable to match. And the proof of Muhammad (ﷺ) for his truthfulness, and his evidence for the reality of his prophethood [[In the printed edition: "and his evidence for his prophethood."]], and that what he brought is from Me, is the inability of all of you and all whom you seek help from among your helpers and supporters to produce a surah like it. And if you are unable to do that—while you are people of eloquence in fluency, rhetoric, and sharpness [[In the printed edition: "and al-darāya," which has no meaning here; a few lines later the correct word appears. Al-dharāba: sharpness in everything, sharpness and fluency and eloquence of the tongue. Dharuba al-rajul yadhrubu dharban wa-dharāba: he became eloquent and sharp-tongued, so he is dharib al-lisān (with fatḥa on the dhāl and kasra on the rā’).]]—then you know that others are even more unable than you to do what you could not. Just as the proof of the messengers and prophets before Me for their truthfulness, and the signs for their prophethood, were things that all My creation could not match, so it will be established for you that Muhammad did not invent it or fabricate it, for if it were fabrication and invention from him, you and all My creation would not be unable to match it. For Muhammad (ﷺ) is no more than a human like you, in a situation like yours in body, physical ability and sharpness of tongue, so it could be supposed that he has power over what you were unable to do, or that you might imagine inability in yourselves regarding what he was able to do.

Then the interpreters differed regarding His saying: "Then produce a surah like it."

491- Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, from Sa'id, from Qatada: "Then produce a surah like it," meaning: like this Qur'an in truth and sincerity, with no falsehood or lie in it.

492- Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, he said: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, he said: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada regarding His saying: "Then produce a surah like it," he says: a surah like this Qur'an [[Narration 492 is in al-Durr al-Manthur 1:35 and al-Shawkani 1:40.]].

493- Muhammad ibn 'Amr al-Bahili narrated to me, he said: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, from 'Isa ibn Maymun, from 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "Then produce a surah like it," like the Qur'an.

494- al-Muthanna narrated to us, he said: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, he said: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.

495- al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraj, from Mujahid: "Then produce a surah like it," he said: "like it" like the Qur'an [[Narrations 493–495 are in al-Durr al-Manthur 1:35, al-Shawkani 1:40, and Ibn Kathir 1:108.]].

So the meaning of the sayings of Mujahid and Qatada that we cited is: Allah, the Mighty One, said to those who disputed with Him concerning His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) among the disbelievers: "Produce a surah like this Qur'an from your speech, O Arabs, as Muhammad brought it in your languages and the meanings of your speech."

Others have said: The meaning of His saying, "Then produce a surah like it," is: like Muhammad from among the human beings, for Muhammad is a human like you [[That is, produce a surah from one like Muhammad among humans.]].

Abu Ja'far said: The first interpretation, that of Mujahid and Qatada, is the correct one, because Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said in another surah: "Or do they say he has invented it? Say: Then produce a surah like it" (10:38). It is known that a surah is not a counterpart or equal to Muhammad, so it is not permissible to say: produce a surah like Muhammad.

If someone says: You have mentioned that Allah meant by His saying "Then produce a surah like it" a surah like this Qur'an—so is there a like of the Qur'an, such that it can be said: produce a surah like it?

It is said: He did not mean by it: produce a surah like it in composition and meanings by which it is distinguished from all other speech. Rather He meant: produce a surah like it in eloquence, because the Qur'an was sent down by Allah in the Arabic tongue, and the speech of the Arabs has undoubtedly a like in Arabic meaning. As for the aspect in which the Qur'an is distinguished from all created speech, it has no like, equal, or counterpart in that respect.

Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, argued against them for His Prophet (ﷺ) with the Qur'an itself, since the people's inability to produce a surah like it in eloquence became evident, for the Qur'an is eloquence like their eloquence, and speech sent down in their tongue. So He said to them, the Mighty and Majestic: "And if you are in doubt that what I have sent down upon My servant of the Qur'an is from Me, then produce a surah from your speech which is like it in Arabic, since you are Arabs, and it is eloquence like your eloquence, and speech like your speech." He did not charge them to produce a surah from a tongue other than the tongue in which the Qur'an was sent down, lest they say: You have charged us with what, if we did it well, we would produce, but we cannot produce it because we are not people of the tongue you charged us with, so you have no proof against us in this [[In the printed edition: "proof against us in this," with the order reversed.]]. For we—though we are unable to produce its like from other than our tongues, because we are not of its people—among mankind there are many non-speakers of our language who can produce its like in the tongue you charged us with. Rather, He, the Mighty and Majestic, said to them: "Produce a surah like it," because its like among languages is your language, and you—if Muhammad invented and fabricated it—when you gather and support one another to produce a surah like a part of it in your tongue and eloquence, are more able to invent it, arrange it, and compose it than Muhammad (ﷺ) [[He says: "and you ... are more able to invent it..." as subject and predicate, with the intervening material being a parenthesis. In the printed edition, instead of "wa-rasfihi" it reads "wa-waḍ'ihi." Al-rasf: joining one thing to another, ordering and firmly arranging it until it is even. From it: kalām raṣīf, meaning sound and without inconsistency.]], and if you are not more able than him in it, then you will not be unable—while you are all together—to match what Muhammad was able to do alone [[In the printed edition: "wa-huwa wahdahu," which is better.]], if you are truthful in your claim and your assertion that Muhammad fabricated and invented it, and that it is from someone other than Me.

The interpreters differed regarding the interpretation of His saying: "And if you are in doubt about what We have sent down upon Our servant, then produce a surah like it, and call upon your witnesses other than Allah, if you are truthful" (2:23).

Ibn 'Abbas said:

496- Muhammad ibn Humayd narrated it to us, he said: Salama narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, client of Zayd ibn Thabit, from 'Ikrima, or from Sa'id, from Ibn 'Abbas: "And call upon your witnesses other than Allah," meaning your helpers in what you are upon, if you are truthful.

497- Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, he said: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, from 'Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "And call upon your witnesses," people who bear witness.

498- al-Muthanna narrated to me, he said: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, he said: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.

499- Abu Kurayb narrated to us, he said: Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from a man, from Mujahid, he said: a people who will bear witness for you.

500- al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraj, from Mujahid: "And call upon your witnesses," he said: people who bear witness.
