He said: "O 'Umar, return, for your anger is honour and your pleasure is judgement. Indeed, for Allah in the seven heavens there are angels who pray, and He has no need of the prayer of so-and-so." 'Umar said: "O Prophet of Allah, and what is their prayer?" He did not answer him anything, so Jibril came to him and said: "O Prophet of Allah, did 'Umar ask you about the prayer of the people of heaven?" He said: "Yes." Jibril said: "Convey the greeting of peace to 'Umar, and inform him that the people of the lowest heaven are in prostration until the Day of Resurrection, saying: 'Glory be to the Lord of dominion and sovereignty' (Subhana dhi al-mulk wa al-malakut). The people of the second heaven are in bowing until the Day of Resurrection, saying: 'Glory be to the Lord of might and majesty' (Subhana dhi al-'izza wa al-jabarut). The people of the third heaven are standing until the Day of Resurrection, saying: 'Glory be to the Living One who does not die' (Subhana al-hayy alladhi la yamut)." [[Hadith 617 is a marfu' hadith (traced to the Prophet ﷺ), but it is mursal, because Sa'id ibn Jubayr is a Successor (tabi'i). Its isnad to him is a good isnad. Ya'qub ibn 'Abd Allah al-Ash'ari al-Qummi, Abu al-Hasan: trustworthy (thiqa), included in al-Tahdhib, and al-Bukhari mentioned him in al-Kabir 4/2/391, and did not mention any criticism of him. In al-Tahdhib: "Muhammad ibn Humayd al-Razi [who is al-Tabari's teacher here] said: 'I entered Baghdad, and Ahmad and Ibn Ma'in met me and asked me about the hadiths of Ya'qub al-Qummi.'" Ja'far ibn Abi al-Mughira al-Khuza'i al-Qummi: trustworthy, mentioned by al-Bukhari in al-Kabir 1/2/200, and Ibn Abi Hatim in al-Jarh 1/1/490-491, and neither of them mentioned any defect in him. In al-Tahdhib, Ibn Hibban transmitted in al-Thiqat his authentication from Ahmad ibn Hanbal. This hadith in its entirety was narrated by Abu Nu'aym in al-Hilya 4: 277-278, through Muhammad ibn Humayd, the teacher of al-Tabari, with this isnad. al-Suyuti mentioned its end in al-Durr al-Manthur 1: 46, from the beginning of 'Umar's question about the prayer of the angels, and did not attribute it to anyone other than al-Tabari and Abu Nu'aym.]]

618- Abu Ja'far said: Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim and Sahl ibn Musa al-Razi narrated to me, both saying: Ibn 'Ulayya narrated to us, saying: al-Juraybi informed us, from Abu 'Abd Allah al-Jasri, from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Samit, from Abu Dharr: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ visited him, or that Abu Dharr visited the Prophet ﷺ, and he said: "O Messenger of Allah, may my father be ransomed for you, which speech is most beloved to Allah?" He said: "What Allah has chosen for His angels: 'Glory be to my Lord and praise be to Him, glory be to my Lord and praise be to Him.'" [[Hadith 618: al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur did not attribute it to Ibn Jarir, and said: "Ibn Abi Shayba, Ahmad, Muslim, al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i narrated it from Abu Dharr..." 5: 161, 176. It is in the Musnad 5: 148 and Muslim 2: 319, 8: 86.]]

- Among the various reports we have mentioned, we disliked lengthening the book by exhausting them.

The root meaning of tasbih (glorification) to Allah among the Arabs is to declare Him far exalted (tanzih) above the attribution to Him of what is not among His attributes, and to clear Him of that, as the poet A'sha of Banu Tha'laba said:

"I say, when his boasting came to me: Glory be to the one who is more boastful than 'Alqama..."

[[His Diwan: 106, from his famous qasida, which he composed in satirising 'Alqama ibn 'Ullatha, in the account of the contest between 'Alqama ibn 'Ullatha and 'Amir ibn al-Tufayl (al-Aghani 15: 50-56). Ibn al-Shajari mentioned in his Amali 1: 348, from Abu al-Khattab al-Akhfash, who said: "He left off the tanwin in 'subhan' and did not inflect it, because it became a definite proper noun (ma'rifa) for them." He said in 2: 250: "He did not inflect it, because it contains the two added letters alif and nun, and it is a proper name for glorification; if you make it indefinite, you inflect it." See p. 495 and footnote no. 3.]]

He means: "Glory be to Allah from the boasting of 'Alqama," that is, declaring Allah far exalted above what 'Alqama has done of boasting, in a manner of rejecting that from him.

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have differed concerning the meaning of tasbih and taqdis in this place. Some of them said: their saying "we glorify You with Your praise" means: we pray to You.

Those who said that:

619- Musa ibn Harun narrated to me, saying: 'Amr ibn Hammad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, in a report he mentioned, from Abu Malik, and from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas, and from Murra, from Ibn Mas'ud, and from some companions of the Prophet ﷺ: "And we glorify You with Your praise and sanctify You," he said: they say: we pray to You.

Others said: "we glorify You with Your praise" [[In the originals: "nusabbih laka", and the correct reading is what we have written, which is the text of the verse.]] is the known glorification.

Those who said that:

620- al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada, concerning His saying: "And we glorify You with Your praise," he said: the tasbih is the tasbih. [[The two reports 619 and 620 are in Ibn Kathir 1: 129, al-Durr al-Manthur 1: 46, and al-Shawkani 1: 50.]]

* *

On the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And we sanctify You﴾

Abu Ja'far said: taqdis is purification and exaltation. From it comes their saying: "Subbuh, Quddus" (Subbuh, Quddus being epithets of Allah). By their saying "Subbuh" they mean declaring Allah far exalted, and by their saying "Quddus" they mean His purity and exaltation. For this reason the land is called "a holy land" (ard muqaddasa), meaning purified. So the meaning of the angels' words then is: "And we glorify You with Your praise": we declare You far exalted and clear You of what the people of polytheism attribute to You, and we pray to You. "And we sanctify You": we ascribe to You what is among Your attributes, of purity from impurities, and what the people of disbelief in You attribute to You. It has been said that the sanctification of the angels of their Lord is their prayer to Him, as:

621- al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada, concerning His saying: "And we sanctify You," he said: taqdis is prayer. [[Report 621 is in Ibn Kathir 1: 129, al-Durr al-Manthur 1: 46, and al-Shawkani 1: 50.]]

Others said: "we sanctify You" means: we exalt You and glorify You.

Those who said that:

622- Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Hashim ibn al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Abu Sa'id al-Mu'addib narrated to us, saying: Isma'il narrated to us, from Abu Salih, concerning His saying: "And we glorify You with Your praise, and sanctify You," he said: we exalt You and glorify You. [[Report 622 is in al-Durr al-Manthur 1: 46.]]

623- Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to me, and al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning the saying of Allah: "And we sanctify You," he said: we exalt You and magnify You. [[Report 623 is in Ibn Kathir 1: 129 and al-Durr al-Manthur 1: 46.]]

624- Ibn Humayd also narrated to us, saying: Salama ibn al-Fadl narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq: "And we glorify You with Your praise and sanctify You": we do not disobey, and we do not do anything You dislike. [[Report 624 is in Ibn Kathir 1: 129.]]

625- It was narrated to me from al-Minjab, saying: Bishr narrated to us, from Abu Rawq, from al-Dahhak, concerning His saying: "And we sanctify You," he said: taqdis is purification. [[Report 625 is in Ibn Kathir 1: 129. In al-Durr al-Manthur 1: 46: "Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, he said: taqdis is purification," and it is not attributed to al-Dahhak or to Ibn Jarir.]]

As for the saying of the one who said that taqdis is prayer or exaltation, its meaning returns to the meaning we have mentioned, purification, because their prayer to their Lord is an exaltation of Him by them, and a purification from what the people of disbelief in Him attribute to Him. If it were said in place of "wa-naqaddisu laka" and "naqaddisuka", it would be eloquent speech. This is because the Arabs say: "So-and-so glorifies Allah and sanctifies Him," and "glorifies for Allah and sanctifies for Him," with one meaning. The Qur'an has also come with this. Allah, mighty is His praise, said: ﴿That We may glorify You much and remember You much﴾ [Surah Ta-Ha: 33-34], and He said in another place: ﴿Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth glorifies Allah﴾ [Surah al-Jumu'a: 1].

* *

On the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿He said: Indeed, I know what you do not know﴾ (30)

Abu Ja'far said: The people of interpretation have differed concerning the interpretation of that. Some of them said: By His saying "I know what you do not know" He means: what He has known of Iblis, his concealing disobedience to Allah and hiding his arrogance, which Allah, blessed and exalted is He, knew of him, and which was hidden from His angels.

Those who said that:

626- Muhammad ibn al-'Ala narrated to us, saying: 'Uthman ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Bishr ibn 'Imara narrated to us, from Abu Rawq, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn 'Abbas: "Indeed I know what you do not know," he says: I have looked into the heart of Iblis and seen what you did not see of his arrogance and self-deception. [[Report 626 is not mentioned in the earlier sources. "Bishr ibn 'Imara": his biography has passed at 137, and it recurs many times, but the correctors of the Bulaq edition said in this place: "So it is in the manuscripts with a taa', and it recurs with it throughout all of them. In al-Khulasa it is without a taa'!!" It is "'Imara" with a taa' in all the books and registers. What is in al-Khulasa is merely a printing error!!]]

627- Musa narrated to me, saying: 'Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, in a report he mentioned, from Abu Malik, and from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas, and from Murra, from Ibn Mas'ud, and from some companions of the Prophet ﷺ: "Indeed I know what you do not know," meaning concerning the affair of Iblis.

628- Ahmad ibn Ishaq al-Ahwazi narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, and Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Mu'ammal narrated to us, both of them saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "Indeed I know what you do not know," he said: He knew from Iblis disobedience and created him for it.

629- Musa ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Masruqi narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Bishr narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from 'Ali ibn Badhima, from Mujahid, the like of it. [[Report 629: "'Ali ibn Badhima", with a fath on the ba' and a kasra on the dhal with a dot, and he is trustworthy.]]

630- Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Sufyan, from 'Ali ibn Badhima, from Mujahid, the like of it. [[Report 630: "Ibn Yaman", with a fath on the ya' and a lightened mim: he is Yahya ibn Yaman al-'Ijli al-Kufi, and he is truthful, one of the teachers of Ahmad ibn Hanbal. "Sufyan" in this and in the preceding report is al-Thawri.]]

631- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us, from 'Anbasa, from Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza, from Mujahid, concerning His saying: "Indeed I know what you do not know," he said: He knew from Iblis disobedience and created him for it. [[Report 631: "al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza", with a fath on the ba' and a shadda on the zay: a trustworthy Meccan. Ibn Hibban said: "None of those who narrate tafsir from Mujahid heard the tafsir except al-Qasim, and everyone who narrates tafsir from Mujahid took it only from the book of al-Qasim." Ibn Abi Hatim said in al-Jarh wa al-Ta'dil 3/2/122: "He is al-Qasim ibn Nafi' ibn Abi Bazza, and the name of Abi Bazza is Yasar." And "Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman", who narrates from him here, is Ibn Abi Layla.]]

632- Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Buzuri narrated to me, saying: Hasan ibn Bishr narrated to us, from Hamza al-Zayyat, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His saying: "Indeed I know what you do not know," he said: He knew from Iblis that he concealed the pride that he would not prostrate to Adam.

633- Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa ibn Maymun narrated to us, and al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning the saying of Allah: "Indeed I know what you do not know," he said: He knew from Iblis disobedience.

634- Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from a man, from Mujahid, the like of it.

635- al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Suwayd narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Sufyan, who said: Mujahid said concerning His saying: "Indeed I know what you do not know," he said: He knew from Iblis disobedience and created him for it. [[Report 635 is mentioned by al-Suyuti 1: 46, and al-Shawkani 1: 50. But the name "Mujahid" dropped out of al-Durr al-Manthur, a printing error.]]

And at another time he said: Adam.

636- al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Hajjaj ibn al-Minhal narrated to us, saying: al-Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman narrated to us, saying: I heard 'Abd al-Wahhab ibn Mujahid narrate from his father, concerning His saying: "Indeed I know what you do not know," he said: He knew from Iblis disobedience and created him for it, and He knew from Adam obedience and created him for it. [[Report 636: As for "Mujahid ibn Jabr", he is the great Successor, the trustworthy jurist and exegete. But his son "'Abd al-Wahhab ibn Mujahid" is very weak. Ahmad ibn Hanbal said: "He did not hear from his father; he is nothing, weak in hadith." Ibn Ma'in and Abu Hatim also weakened him. 'Abd al-Wahhab passed by Sufyan al-Thawri in the Masjid al-Haram, and Sufyan said: "This is a liar." As for this report, with the addition "and He knew from Adam obedience...", we have not found it in any other place.]]

637- al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, from Ma'mar, from Ibn Tawus, from his father, and al-Thawri, from 'Ali ibn Badhima, from Mujahid, concerning His saying: "Indeed I know what you do not know," he said: He knew from Iblis disobedience and created him for it. [[Report 637 is in the meaning of the earlier reports 633-635.]]

638- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq: "Indeed I know what you do not know": that is, among you and from you, and He did not reveal it to them, of disobedience, corruption and shedding of blood.

Others said: The meaning of that is: "Indeed I know what you do not know": that among that successor there will be people of obedience and loyalty to Allah.

Those who said that:

639- Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Zuray' narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, who said: "Indeed I know what you do not know": so it was in Allah's knowledge that there would be from that successor prophets, messengers, righteous people and inhabitants of Paradise. [[Report 639 is in Ibn Kathir 1: 130, al-Durr al-Manthur 1: 46, and al-Shawkani 1: 50. In Ibn Kathir: "in that creation" (fi tilka al-khaliqa), and in al-Durr al-Manthur: "from that creation" (min tilka al-khaliqa), and in al-Shawkani: "will be from the creation" (sa-yakun min al-khaliqa): all with the qaf, and that is an error; the correct reading is what is in Tabari's text.]]

This report from Allah, mighty is His praise, indicates that the angels who said: ﴿Will You place therein one who will cause corruption therein and shed blood?﴾ were appalled that there should be a creation of God that disobeys Him, and they wondered at it, when they reported that this would happen. For this reason their Lord said to them: "Indeed I know what you do not know." He means by that, and Allah knows best: Indeed you wonder at the command of Allah and find it appalling, and I know that it is in some of you; and you describe yourselves with an attribute whose opposite I know among some of you; and you hint at a matter which I have placed for others. This is because when their Lord informed the angels of what would occur from the offspring of His successor, of corruption and shedding of blood, they said to their Lord: "O Lord, will You place in the earth a successor other than us, from whose offspring there will be one who disobeys You, or from us, for we exalt You, pray to You, obey You and do not disobey You?" But they did not have knowledge of what Iblis had concealed in his breast of arrogance toward his Lord. So their Lord said to them: "Indeed I know other than what you say, from some of you." That is what was hidden from them of the affair of Iblis, and his concealing of the arrogance he had concealed. And for their saying that, and their describing themselves with generality of attribute, they were rebuked.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 31 (part 1 of 2):

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is His remembrance: ﴿And He taught Adam﴾

640. Muhammad ibn Jarir narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Ya'qub al-Qummi narrated to us, from Ja'far ibn Abi al-Mughira, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Lord of Might sent the Angel of Death, and he took from the surface of the earth, from its sweet and its salty parts, and from it He created Adam. It is for this reason that he was named Adam, because he was created from the surface (adim) of the earth. [[Report 640: This is a sound isnad. Al-Tabari also narrated it in his History (al-Tarikh) 1:46, with this same isnad, with an addition at the end. However, in that version it says: "The Lord of Might sent Iblis" instead of "the Angel of Death." This is the correct version, in agreement with all the other narrations, so what is here may be an old error by the copyists. Likewise Ibn Sa'd narrated it in al-Tabaqat 1/1/6, from Husayn ibn Hasan al-Ashqar, from Ya'qub ibn 'Abd Allah al-Qummi, with this isnad. Likewise al-Suyuti quoted it at length, 1:47, from Ibn Sa'd, al-Tabari, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Ibn 'Asakir.]]

641. And Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad al-Zubayri narrated to us, saying: 'Amr ibn Thabit narrated to us, from his father, from his grandfather, from 'Ali, who said: Adam was created from the surface of the earth, and in it there is the good, the righteous, and the bad, so you see all of that in his offspring, the righteous and the wicked. [[Report 641: Al-Tabari narrated it in his History 1:46, with this isnad. Al-Suyuti mentioned it, 1:47, attributing it to al-Tabari alone, and I have not found it with anyone else. Its isnad is extremely weak. 'Amr ibn Thabit is Ibn Abi al-Miqdam al-Haddad, extremely weak; Ibn Ma'in said: "He is not trustworthy nor reliable." As for his father, Thabit ibn Hurmuz Abu al-Miqdam, he is trustworthy. This isnad is made weaker and more problematic by its statement "from his grandfather"! For the biography of Thabit in all the sources contains no mention that he narrates from his father "Hurmuz." Then we find no mention or biography of this Hurmuz, so I do not know what this is about.]]

642. And Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Mis'ar narrated to us, from Abu Husayn, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: Adam was created from the surface of the earth, and so he was named Adam.

643. And Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Abu Dawud narrated to us, saying: Shu'ba narrated to us, from Abu Husayn, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: He was only named Adam because he was created from the surface of the earth. [[Reports 642 and 643: Al-Tabari narrated both in his History 1:46, with these two isnads. Al-Suyuti 1:49 and al-Shawkani 1:52 mentioned something similar. "Abu Husayn" in both is pronounced with a fatha on the ḥā' and a kasra on the unpointed ṣād; he is 'Uthman ibn 'Asim ibn Husayn al-Asadi, trustworthy, firm, and a proponent of the Sunna.]]

644. And Musa ibn Harun narrated to me, saying: 'Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, in a report he mentioned, from Abu Malik and from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas, and from Murra, from Ibn Mas'ud, and from some of the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ): that when the Angel of Death was sent to take a portion of earth for Adam, he took from the surface of the earth and mixed it, not taking from a single place, and he took from red, white, and black soil, and that is why the children of Adam came out differing. And that is why he was named Adam, because he took it from the surface (adim) of the earth. [[Report 644: It has already passed as part of a longer report with this isnad: 607.]]

It has been related from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) a report that confirms what we have quoted from those who explained the meaning of "Adam." It is this:

645. Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated it to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayya narrated to us, from 'Awf. And Muhammad ibn Bashshar and 'Umar ibn Shabba narrated to us, both saying: Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: 'Awf narrated to us. And Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi 'Adi, Muhammad ibn Ja'far, and 'Abd al-Wahhab al-Thaqafi narrated to us, all saying: 'Awf narrated to us. And Muhammad ibn 'Ammara al-Asadi narrated to me, saying: Isma'il ibn Aban narrated to us, saying: 'Anbasa narrated to us, from 'Awf al-A'rabi, from Qasama ibn Zuhayr, from Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: Allah created Adam from a handful He took from all the earth, so the children of Adam came according to the earth's variety: among them were the red, the black, the white, and what is between them, the easy-going and the harsh, and the wicked and the good. [[Hadith 645: It is a sound hadith. Ahmad narrated it in his Musnad 4:400, 406 (Halabi edition); Ibn Sa'd in al-Tabaqat 1/1/5-6; Abu Dawud: 4693; al-Tirmidhi 4:67-68; and al-Hakim 2:261-262, all by way of 'Awf ibn Abi Jamila al-A'rabi, from Qasama ibn Zuhayr, with this isnad. Al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan sahih." Al-Hakim said: "Its isnad is sound, though they did not include it," and al-Dhahabi agreed with him. Al-Suyuti mentioned it, 1:46, attributing it to these and to 'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Mardawayh, and others. Al-Tabari also narrated it in his History 1:46, with these same isnads that are here, with an addition at the end.]]

So, according to the interpretation of those who explained "Adam" as meaning that he was created from the surface (adim) of the earth, the root of "Adam" must be a verb by which the father of mankind was named, just as "Ahmad" is from the verb "ahmada" (to praise) and "As'ad" is from "as'ada" (to make happy), and for this reason it is not declined. Its interpretation then would be: "Adam al-malik al-ard," meaning: he reached its adma (complexion). The adma is its apparent face that is visible to the eye, just as the skin of every thing with skin has an adma. From this root, condiment is called idam (idam), because it becomes like the uppermost layer of what it is part of. Then it was transferred from the verb and made a proper name for that specific person.

* *

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿all the names﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed about the names that He taught Adam and then presented to the angels. Ibn 'Abbas said:

646. Abu Kurayb narrated it to us, saying: 'Uthman ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Bishr ibn 'Umara narrated to us, from Abu Ruq, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Allah taught Adam all the names, and they are these names by which people are known: human, animal, earth, plain, sea, mountain, donkey, and similar names of peoples and other things. [[Report 646: In Ibn Kathir 1:132, al-Durr al-Manthur 1:49, and al-Shawkani 1:52, and it has passed as number 606, in a longer form.]]

647. And Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to me, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid. And al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding Allah's words "And He taught Adam all the names," who said: He taught him the name of every thing.

648. And Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Khusayf, from Mujahid: "And He taught Adam all the names," who said: He taught him the name of every thing. [[Reports 647 and 648: In al-Durr al-Manthur 1:49, and it seems they are abridgements of what follows them.]]

649. And 'Ali ibn al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Muslim al-Jarmi narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Mus'ab, from Qays ibn al-Rabi', from Khusayf, from Mujahid, who said: He taught him the name of the crow, the dove, and the name of every thing. [[Report 649: I have not found it in this exact wording; perhaps it is an extended form of the one before it, and see what will come below, number 666. "Muslim al-Jarmi" is firmly established in the sources with a ḥā'. We have already preferred in 154 that it is with a jīm.]]

650. And Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Sharik, from Salim al-Aftas, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: He taught him the name of every thing, even the camel, the cow, and the sheep. [[Report 650: In al-Durr al-Manthur 1:49.]]

651. And Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Sharik, from 'Asim ibn Kulayb, from Sa'id ibn Ma'bad, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: He taught him the name of the bowl (qus'a), the fusa, and the fusayya. [[Report 651: Sa'id ibn Ma'bad is a Successor (tabi'i) who narrates from Ibn 'Abbas. I have found no biography of him except in al-Bukhari's al-Tarikh al-Kabir 2/1/468 and Ibn Abi Hatim's al-Jarh 2/1/63. Both mention that he narrates from Ibn 'Abbas, and that al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza narrates from him. Al-Tabari has therefore brought an added benefit in this isnad, and in isnad 653 that he also narrates from him 'Asim ibn Kulayb. This report was mentioned in a similar wording by Ibn Kathir 1:132 and al-Suyuti 1:49, and they attributed it also to Ibn Abi Hatim. This report and the three after it have closely related meanings; they are narrations of one report.]]

652. And Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Sharik narrated to us, from 'Asim ibn Kulayb, from al-Hasan ibn Sa'd, from Ibn 'Abbas: "And He taught Adam all the names," who said: even the fusa and the fusayya.

653. 'Ali ibn al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Muslim narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Mus'ab narrated to us, from Qays, from 'Asim ibn Kulayb, from Sa'id ibn Ma'bad, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding Allah's words "And He taught Adam all the names," who said: He taught him the name of every thing, even the hanna, the hunayya, the fusa, and the darta.

654. And al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: 'Ali ibn Musahhir narrated to us, from 'Asim ibn Kulayb, who said: Ibn 'Abbas said: He taught him the qas'a from the qusay'a, and the fusa from the fusiyya. [[Report 654: 'Asim ibn Kulayb al-Jarmi is trustworthy and may be relied on as proof. However, he only narrates from the Successors, so his narration here from Ibn 'Abbas is disconnected (munqati'). The three isnads preceding have shown that he only related this meaning from Sa'id ibn Ma'bad and from al-Hasan ibn Sa'd, from Ibn 'Abbas.]]

655. And Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Zurayʿ narrated to us, from Sa'id, from Qatada regarding His words "And He taught Adam all the names," up to "Indeed You are the Knowing, the Wise." He said: "O Adam, inform them of their names." So he informed each kind of creation of its name, and made it cling to its species. [[Report 655: In al-Durr al-Manthur 1:49, with a different wording. See number 697.]]

656. And al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, saying: Ma'mar narrated to us, from Qatada regarding His words "And He taught Adam all the names," who said: He taught him the name of every thing: "This is a mountain, this is a sea, this is such-and-such, and this is such-and-such," for everything. Then He presented those things to the angels, saying: "Inform Me of the names of these, if you are truthful." [[Report 656: In Ibn Kathir 1:133, abridged, and in al-Durr al-Manthur 1:49 in longer form. In Ibn Kathir it says: "Then He presented those names."]]

657. And al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Jarir ibn Hazim, and Mubarak, from al-Hasan, and Abu Bakr from al-Hasan and Qatada, both saying: He taught him the name of every thing: these are horses, and these are mules, camels, jinn, and wild beasts, and He began naming every thing by its name. [[Report 657: In Ibn Kathir 1:133 in a different wording, abridged, and in al-Durr al-Manthur 1:49. It will come as it appears in both, as number 667.]]

658. And it was related to me from 'Ammar, who said: 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi', who said: the name of every thing. [[Report 658: I have not found it.]]

Others said: He taught Adam all the names, the names of the angels.

Those who said that:

659. It was related to me from 'Ammar, who said: 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi', regarding His words "And He taught Adam all the names," who said: the names of the angels. [[Report 659: In Ibn Kathir 1:132, al-Durr al-Manthur 1:49, and al-Shawkani 1:52.]]

Others said: He taught him only the names of all his descendants.

Those who said that:

660. Muhammad ibn Jarir narrated to me, saying: Yunus ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words "And He taught Adam all the names," the names of all his descendants. [[Report 660: In Ibn Kathir 1:132, al-Durr al-Manthur 1:49, and al-Shawkani 1:52.]]

The most correct of these opinions, and the one most consistent with what the apparent recitation (zahir al-tilawa) indicates, is the view of the one who said that regarding His words "And He taught Adam all the names," they are the names of his offspring and the names of the angels, but not the names of the rest of the kinds of creation. This is because Allah, majestic is His praise, said: "Then He presented them to the angels," meaning by that the very persons named by the names that Adam was taught. The Arabs hardly ever refer with the pronoun of the hā' and mīm except to the names of the children of Adam and the angels. When referring to the names of animals and the rest of creation other than those described, they refer to them with the hā' and the alif, or the hā' and the nūn, saying "'aradahunna" or "'aradaha" ("He presented them," feminine or neuter). They do the same when referring to kinds of creation such as animals, birds, and the rest of the categories of peoples, and where the names of the children of Adam and the angels are among them: they refer to them with the hā' and nūn or the hā' and alif that we have described. Sometimes, when that is the case, they refer to them with the hā' and mīm, as His majestic praise said: ﴿And Allah created every moving creature from water; of them is one that goes on its belly, of them is one that walks on two legs, and of them is one that walks on four﴾ [Surah al-Nur: 45]. Here He referred to them with the hā' and mīm, while they are different kinds including the human and other than the human. And although that is permissible, the prevalent and widespread usage in Arabic speech is what we have described: that they bring the pronoun for the names of mixed kinds of peoples with the hā' and alif or the hā' and nūn. Therefore I have said that the more correct interpretation of the verse is that the names Adam was taught are the names of the individual children of Adam and the names of the angels. Yet what Ibn 'Abbas said is also permissible, after the example of what came in the Book of Allah, such as His words: "And Allah created every moving creature from water; of them is one that goes on its belly," up to the verse. It has been mentioned that in the reading of Ibn Mas'ud it is "thumma 'aradahunna" (then He presented them, feminine plural), and in the reading of Ubayy it is "thumma 'aradaha" (then He presented it). [[See Ibn Kathir's commentary 1:132 in response to al-Tabari's statement.]]

It may be that Ibn 'Abbas interpreted his saying "He taught him the name of every thing, even the fusa and the fusayya" according to the reading of Ubayy, for it has reached us that he used to recite in the reading of Ubayy. Ibn 'Abbas's interpretation, according to what is related from Ubayy's recitation, is not objectionable; rather it is sound and widespread in Arabic speech, in the manner that I have already described.

* *

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿then He presented them to the angels﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: We have already mentioned the interpretation that is more correct for the verse, according to our reading and the orthography of our copy of the Qur'an, and that His words "thumma 'aradahum" (then He presented them), with reference to the children of Adam and the angels, are more correct than referring it to all kinds of creation, although it is not corrupt to say that it refers to all the categories of peoples, for the reasons we have described.

Allah, majestic is His praise, by His words "thumma 'aradahum" means: then He presented the possessors of the names to the angels.

The exegetes differed about the interpretation of His words "then He presented them to the angels," in the same way as they differed regarding His words "And He taught Adam all the names." I will mention the statement of those from whom a statement has reached us about it.

661. Muhammad ibn al-'Ala' narrated to us, saying: 'Uthman ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Bishr ibn 'Umara narrated to us, from Abu Ruq, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn 'Abbas: "then He presented them to the angels," then He presented these names, meaning the names of all things that Adam was taught from the categories of all creation. [[Report 661: It is part of the completion of the reports just preceding it.]]

662. And Musa narrated to me, saying: 'Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, in a report he mentioned, from Abu Malik and from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas, and from Murra, from Ibn Mas'ud, and from some of the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ): "then He presented them," then He presented the creation to the angels. [[Report 662: An abridgement of the long report that passed shortly before, and in Ibn Kathir 1:132.]]

663. And Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: the names of all his descendants; He took them from his back. He said: Then He presented them to the angels. [[Report 663: In al-Durr al-Manthur 1:49.]]

664. And al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada: "then He presented them," who said: He taught him the name of every thing, then presented those names to the angels. [[Report 664: An abridgement of a report that passed with this isnad, and in Ibn Kathir 1:133.]]

665. And al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid: "then He presented them," who presented the possessors of the names to the angels. [[Report 665: In Ibn Kathir 1:133, al-Durr al-Manthur 1:49, and al-Shawkani 1:52.]]

666. And 'Ali ibn al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Muslim narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Mus'ab narrated to us, from Qays, from Khusayf, from Mujahid: "then He presented them to the angels," meaning He presented the names: the dove and the crow. [[Report 666: In Ibn Kathir 1:134, and see what has passed shortly before with this isnad.]]

[Hadith 667 and the chain]

667 – Al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Jarir ibn Hazim – and Mubarak from al-Hasan – and Abu Bakr from al-Hasan and Qatadah – the two of them said: "He taught him the names of everything: these horses, and these mules, and what is similar to that. And he began naming everything by its name, and they were presented to him community by community" [[The report: 667 – see what passed, no. 657, and Ibn Kathir 1:133, and al-Durr al-Manthur 1:49.]].

* *

On the interpretation of His words: ﴿Then He said: Inform Me of the names of these﴾

Abu Ja'far said: The interpretation of His words "Anbi'uni" is: inform me, as follows:

668 – Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Uthman related to us, saying: Bishr related to us, from Abu Rawq, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn Abbas: "Anbi'uni", he says: inform me of the names of these.[[The report: 668 – an abridgement of the report no. 606.]]

And from it is the saying of al-Nabighah of Banu Dhubyan:

"And the informer informed him that a tribe / had settled between Haram and Judham"[[His Diwan: 87, from a qasidah of his concerning Amr ibn Hind, who had raided Syria after the killing of his father al-Mundhir. Abu Ubaydah said: this qasidah belongs to Amr ibn al-Harith al-Ghassani, on the raid on Iraq. The Diwan's reading is "anna hayyan hululun" with the accusative, as an epithet of "hayyan", and this is the good reading. The predicate of "anna" is omitted, as if he said: they have gathered, lying in wait for you. Its omission serves to magnify the matter of their assembling and their lying in wait. The verse that follows indicates this, namely his saying: "And that the people's aid is all together, / groups calling to groups." The reading with the nominative is acceptable, though I do not find it fine. His saying "Haram" appears to mean the Banu Haram ibn Dinnah ibn Abd ibn Kabir ibn Udhrah ibn Sa'd Hudhaym, or as if he means the Banu Haram ibn Judham ibn Adi ibn al-Harith ibn Murrah ibn Udd ibn Zayd. The abode of Judham is the mountains of Hasma, and its land lies between Aylah and the side of the wilderness of the Children of Israel that adjoins Aylah, and between the land of the Banu Udhrah from the upper part of the Harrat Nuhayl (Mu'jam al-Buldan: Hasma). Because the dwellings of these Banu Udhrah are near Judham, I was uncertain whom al-Nabighah meant by Banu Haram in this verse.]]

By his saying "anba'ahu" he means: informed him and made him know.

* *

On the interpretation of His exalted words: ﴿with the names of these﴾

Abu Ja'far said:

669 – Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us – and al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Abu Hudhayfah related to us, saying: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning the words of God: "with the names of these," he said: with the names of these which I related to Adam.

670 – al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid: "Inform Me of the names of these if you are truthful," he says: with the names of these which I related to Adam.[[The two reports: 669, 670 – I have not found them elsewhere.]]

* *

On the interpretation of His exalted words: ﴿if you are truthful﴾

Abu Ja'far said: The people of interpretation differed concerning this.

671 – Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Uthman ibn Sa'id related to us, saying: Bishr ibn Umarah related to us, from Abu Rawq, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn Abbas: "if you are truthful," if you know why I place a khalifah on the earth.[[The report: 671 – an abridgement of the earlier report no. 606; see the commentary there on this passage. And see al-Shawkani 1:52.]]

672 – And Musa ibn Harun related to us, saying: Amr ibn Hammad related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, in a report he mentioned, from Abu Malik and from Abu Salih, from Ibn Abbas – and from Murrah, from Ibn Mas'ud, and from some companions of the Prophet ﷺ: "if you are truthful" – that the children of Adam would corrupt in the earth and shed blood.[[The report: 672 – an abridgement of the earlier report no. 607; Ibn Kathir 1:133; al-Durr al-Manthur 1:50; al-Shawkani 1:52.]]

673 – And al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to us, from Jarir ibn Hazim – and Mubarak from al-Hasan – and Abu Bakr from al-Hasan and Qatadah – the two of them said concerning "Inform Me of the names of these if you are truthful": that I did not create a creature except that you would know more than it; so inform Me of the names of these if you are truthful.[[The report: 673 – an abridgement of the earlier report no. 611; Ibn Kathir 1:133.]]

Abu Ja'far said: The most preferable of these sayings as an interpretation of the verse is the interpretation of Ibn Abbas and of whoever speaks by his saying. The meaning of that is: He said: "Inform Me of the names of those whom I presented to you, O angels, who said: Will You place in it one who corrupts in it and sheds blood, from among others than us, or from among us? While we glorify You with Your praise and sanctify You?" If you are truthful in your saying that if I make My khalifah on the earth from among others than you, he will disobey Me and his descendants will corrupt in it and shed blood; and if I make you in it, you will obey Me and follow My command with exalting Me and sanctifying Me. For if you do not know the names of these whom I presented to you from My creatures, who are created and existent, whom you see and witness, and whom others have learned from My teaching of it, then you, concerning what is not yet existent of the occurring matters that have not yet come into being, and concerning what is hidden from your eyes of matters that are existent, are more deserving of being those who do not know. So do not ask Me what you have no knowledge of, for I know what is good for you and good for My creatures.

This act of God, exalted be His praise, toward His angels – who had said to Him "Will You place in it one who corrupts in it?" – by way of His rebuke of them, is the parallel of His saying, exalted be His majesty, to His prophet Noah, peace be upon him, when He said: ﴿My Lord, indeed my son is of my family, and indeed Your promise is the truth, and You are the most just of judges﴾ [Surah Hud: 45] – : ﴿Do not ask Me what you have no knowledge of; I admonish you lest you be among the ignorant﴾[[In the printed edition: "and You are the most just of judges, so do not ask," which is a gross error, for the verse following "and You are the most just of judges" is: "He said: O Noah, he is not of your family; he is one of unrighteous deed, so do not ask Me what you have no knowledge of..." and al-Tabari did not intend to cite the two verses, but only God's words to His prophet when He said what He said. The correct text is that in the manuscript, as we have recorded it.]]. So likewise the angels asked their Lord that they be His khalifahs on the earth to glorify and sanctify Him therein, since the descendants of the one whom He had informed them He would make a khalifah on the earth were those who would corrupt in it and shed blood. So He, exalted be His praise, said to them: ﴿Indeed I know what you do not know.﴾ He means by that: Indeed I know that among you is the one who initiates sins and seals them, and that is Iblis; denying thereby, exalted be His praise, their saying. Then He made them know the place of their error in what they had said of that, by making them know the insufficiency of their knowledge regarding what they were witnessing by sight – so how then regarding what they had not seen and had not been informed about? – by presenting to them what He presented of His creatures existing that day, and by His saying to them: "Inform Me of the names of these if you are truthful," that is, that if I make you khalifahs in My earth, you would glorify and sanctify Me; and if I make others in it, My descendants would disobey Me and corrupt and shed blood. So when the place of their error in their saying became clear to them, and their slip was revealed, they turned in repentance to God, saying: ﴿Glory be to You, we have no knowledge except what You have taught us﴾, and they hastened to return from the slip and hurried to repent from the lapse, just as Noah said – when he was rebuked concerning his request and it was said to him: do not ask Me what you have no knowledge of –: ﴿My Lord, I seek refuge in You from asking You what I have no knowledge of; and unless You forgive me and have mercy on me, I shall be among the losers﴾ [Surah Hud: 47]. And so is the act of everyone who is guided to the truth and granted success in it: swift to the truth in his return, near to it in his repentance.

It has been claimed by some grammarians of Basra that His saying "Inform Me of the names of these if you are truthful" was not because the angels had claimed anything; rather God informed of their ignorance of the knowledge of the unseen, and of His knowledge of that and His favour, so He said: "Inform Me if you are truthful" – as a man says to a man: "Inform me of this if you know." And he knows that he does not know; he means that he is ignorant.

This is a saying which, when one who reflects on it considers it, one knows that part of it corrupts another part. For its speaker claims that God, exalted be His praise, said to the angels – when He presented to them the bearers of the names –: "Inform Me of the names of these," while He knows that they do not know, and they had not claimed knowledge of anything that would require them to be rebuked by this saying. And he claims that His saying "if you are truthful" is like a man's saying to a man: "Inform me of this if you know," and he knows that he does not know, meaning that he is ignorant.

And there is no doubt that the meaning of His saying "if you are truthful" is only: if you are truthful, either in your saying or in your deed. For truthfulness in the speech of the Arabs is only truthfulness in report, not in knowledge. For it is not understood in any language that one says "the man was truthful" meaning "he knew." Since that is so, it must be that God, exalted be His praise, said to the angels – according to the interpretation of this saying we have related – "Inform Me of the names of these if you are truthful," while He knows that they are not truthful, meaning thereby that they are liars. And that is precisely what he denied, for he claimed that the angels had claimed nothing; so how could it be right to say to them: "If you are truthful, inform Me of the names of these"? This is in addition to the fact that this saying which we have related from its proponent is outside the sayings of all the earlier and later people of interpretation and exegesis.

It has been related from some people of exegesis that he used to interpret His saying "if you are truthful" to mean: "since you are truthful."

If "in" were in the sense of "since" in this place, its initial alif would have to be read with a fatḥah, because "idh" (since), when a future verb precedes it, becomes a cause of the verb and a reason for it. This is like the speaker's saying: "I will stand since you stood" – meaning, I will stand because you have stood. The command carries the sense of the future, so the meaning of the sentence – if "in" were in the sense of "idh" – would be: "Inform Me of the names of these because you are truthful." But when "in" is put in that place, one says: "Inform Me of the names of these, in that you are truthful," with the alif vowelled with a fatḥah. And the consensus of all the readers of the Muslims on the kasrah of the alif of "in" is clear evidence of the error of the interpretation of whoever interprets "in" in this place as "idh."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 32:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is His mention: ﴿They said, "Glory be to You; we have no knowledge except what You have taught us. Indeed, You are the Knowing, the Wise."﴾ (32)

Abu Ja'far said: This is a report from God, exalted is His mention, about His angels, concerning their return to Him, their submission of knowledge of what they did not know to Him, and their disavowal that they or anyone know anything except what He, exalted is His mention, has taught them.

In these three verses there is a lesson for whoever takes heed, a reminder for whoever is mindful, and clarification for whoever has a heart or gives ear while being a witness, concerning the subtle wisdoms that God, exalted is His praise, has deposited in the verses of this Qur'an, which the tongues cannot describe.

That is because God, exalted is His praise, argued in them on behalf of His Prophet ﷺ against those among the Jews of the Children of Israel who were in his midst, by informing him of knowledge of the unseen, which God, exalted is His mention, had not disclosed to His creation except to a select few, and whose knowledge could not be attained except through information and report, so that the authenticity of his prophethood would be established for them and they would know that what he brought them was from Him. And in them He also indicated that everyone who reports a report about what has already occurred, or about what is to occur but has not yet occurred, without having received it by report and without having a proof established for its soundness, is one who fabricates, for which he deserves punishment from his Lord. Do you not see that God, exalted is His mention, refuted His angels' statement: "Will You place in it one who causes corruption therein and sheds blood, while we glorify You with Your praise and sanctify You?" He said: "Indeed, I know that which you do not know." And He made them aware that such a statement was not permissible for them, by what He made them aware of concerning the deficiency of their knowledge when He presented to them what He presented of the people of the names, saying: "Inform Me of the names of these, if you are truthful." So there was no refuge for them except acknowledging incapacity and disavowing before Him that they know anything except what He taught them, by their saying: "Glory be to You; we have no knowledge except what You have taught us." In that there was the clearest indication and the most evident proof against the falsehood of the claim of everyone who claims some knowledge of the unseen from the diviners [[al-Huzzah, plural of hazin: one like the soothsayer, who guesses at things and estimates them by his conjecture. It is said of one who looks at the stars and divines: hazin and hazza'. In the hadith of Heraclius that he "was a hazzah," and in the hadith: "Pharaoh had a hazin," meaning a soothsayer. And al-kahanah, plural of kahin: one who engages in reporting about occurrences in the time to come and claims knowledge of secrets. In the printed edition it reads "al-qafah" instead of "al-'afah," which is a clear error, for qiyafah is not at all what al-Tabari intended, and it is true, not false like the falsehood of hazw and kahanah and astrology. Al-'afah is the plural of 'a'if: one who examines birds, drives them away, and takes omens or auspices from their names, voices and flight. The name of his craft is 'iyafah. In the hadith: "'Iyafah and tarq are of jibt." It is a kind of soothsaying. The munajjim and mutanajjim: one who looks at the stars, calculating their times and courses, then links that to the conditions of the world and of people, and speculates about the hidden matters of their affairs.]] and the astrologers, and the augurs. And He reminded by it those of the People of the Book whose condition we described, of the bounties He had bestowed upon their forefathers and His favors upon their predecessors, when they turned back to Him and came to obey Him, seeking to win them over thereby to right guidance, and to make them seek forgiveness by it for salvation. And He warned them, by persistence and continuing in rebellion and error, of the descent of punishment upon them, like the one that descended upon His enemy Iblis when he persisted in error and perdition [[In the printed edition: "in rebellion and perdition," and the correct reading is what is in the manuscript.]].

He said: As for the interpretation of His saying, "Glory be to You; we have no knowledge except what You have taught us," it is as follows:

674 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: 'Uthman ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Bishr ibn 'Imarah narrated to us, from Abu Rawq, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn 'Abbas: "They said, 'Glory be to You'" declaring God free from anyone knowing the unseen other than Him, "we repent to You," "we have no knowledge except what You have taught us," disavowing from themselves knowledge of the unseen, "except what You have taught us" as You taught Adam [[The report 674 is an abridgment of the report no. 606. In the printed edition here it reads "tabarru'an minhum" (disavowal from them).]].

"Subhan" is a verbal noun with no conjugation. Its meaning: we glorify You, as if they said: we glorify You with glorification, and we declare You free with declaration, and we disavow ourselves from knowing anything other than what You have taught us.

* *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿Indeed, You are the Knowing, the Wise﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Its interpretation is: You, O our Lord, are the Knowing without instruction of all that has occurred and all that is to occur, and the one who knows the unseen, apart from all Your creation. That is because they negated from themselves, by their saying "we have no knowledge except what You have taught us," that they have any knowledge except what their Lord taught them, and they affirmed for their Lord what they had negated from themselves of that by their saying "Indeed, You are the Knowing," meaning by that the Knower without instruction, since whoever other than You knows nothing except by the instruction of another. And "the Wise" means the one possessing wisdom. As:

675 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas: "Al-'Alim" is the one whose knowledge is perfect, and "al-Hakim" is the one whose judgment is perfect [[The report 675 is in al-Durr al-Manthur 1:49, and al-Shawkani 1:52.]].

It has also been said that the meaning of "al-Hakim" is "al-Hakim" (the Judge), just as "al-'Alim" means "al-'Alim" (the Knower), and "al-Khabir" means "al-Khabir" (the Informed).

The commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 33:

The exposition of the words of Him, exalted is He: ﴿He said, "O Adam, inform them of their names." So when he had informed them of their names, He said, "Did I not tell you that I know the unseen of the heavens and the earth?"﴾

Abu Ja'far said: God, glorified is His praise, made known to His angels, who had asked Him to make them the successors on the earth, and who described themselves as obedient to Him and submissive to His command, unlike others who would corrupt in it and shed blood, that they, in their ignorance of the places of His planning and the seat of His decree, before He informed them of it, were like their ignorance of the names of those whom He presented to them, since that was among the things He had not taught them so that they might know it. They and other servants do not know any knowledge except what their Lord has taught them, and He singles out with whatever knowledge He wills whomever He wills of creation, and withholds it from whomever He wills, just as He taught Adam the names of what was presented to the angels, and withheld their knowledge of them until after he had taught it to them.

As for the interpretation of His words, "He said, 'O Adam, inform them'": it says, inform the angels. The pronoun in "inform them" refers to the angels. "Of their names" means the names of those whom He presented to the angels, and the pronoun in "their names" refers back to "these" in His words, "Inform Me of the names of these." "So when he informed them" means: when Adam informed the angels of the names of those whom He had presented to them, and they did not know their names, and they realized the error of their statement, "Will You place therein one who will cause corruption therein and shed blood while we exalt You with praise and sanctify You?", and that they had erred in that and said what they did not know, the manner in which their Lord's decree would take effect in that, had it taken effect, as they had uttered it, their Lord said to them: "Did I not tell you that I know the unseen of the heavens and the earth?" The unseen is what is hidden from their sight so that they did not witness it, as a rebuke from God, exalted is His praise, to them for that, for what had preceded from their statement and what had slipped from them of error in their question. As:

676 - Muhammad ibn al-'Ala narrated to us, saying: 'Uthman ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Bishr ibn 'Umarah narrated to us, from Abu Rawq, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn 'Abbas: "He said, 'O Adam, inform them of their names,'" meaning: inform them of their names. "So when he informed them of their names, He said: Did I not tell you" O angels, specifically, "that I know the unseen of the heavens and the earth," and no one knows it but Me. [[The report: 676 - an abridgment of the report earlier, no. 606.]]

677 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning the story of the angels and Adam: God said to the angels: "Just as you did not know these names, you have no knowledge. I only wished to make them, that they would corrupt in it; this, in my view, I have known. Likewise I concealed from you that I would make in it those who disobey Me and those who obey Me." He said: And there preceded from God: "I will surely fill Hell with jinn and men all together" [Surah Hud 11:119; Surah al-Sajdah 32:13]. He said: The angels did not know that and did not realize it. He said: So when they saw what God had given Adam of knowledge, they acknowledged Adam's superiority. [[The report: 677 - in Ibn Kathir 1:135. In the manuscript: "knowledge by what I willed... this is My servant."]]

* *

The exposition of the words of Him, exalted is He: ﴿And I know what you disclose and what you were concealing﴾

Abu Ja'far said: The people of interpretation differed concerning its interpretation, and it is related from Ibn 'Abbas concerning that:

678 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: 'Uthman ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Bishr ibn 'Umarah narrated to us, from Abu Rawq, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn 'Abbas: "And I know what you disclose," he says: what you make apparent, "and what you were concealing," he says: I know the secret as I know the open. He means: what Iblis concealed within himself of pride and deception. [[The report: 678 - in Ibn Kathir 1:135, al-Durr al-Manthur 1:50, al-Shawkani 1:52.]]

679 - Musa ibn Harun narrated to me, saying: Amr ibn Hammad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi in a report he mentioned, from Abu Malik, and from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas, and from Murrah, from Ibn Mas'ud, and from some companions of the Prophet ﷺ: "And I know what you disclose and what you were concealing," he said: their statement, "Will You place therein one who will corrupt therein," this is what they disclosed; "and what you were concealing," meaning what Iblis secretly held within himself of pride. [[The report: 679 - in Ibn Kathir 1:135, al-Durr al-Manthur 1:50, al-Shawkani 1:52; it is an abridgment of the report earlier, no. 606.]]

680 - Ahmad ibn Ishaq al-Ahwazi narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad al-Zubayri narrated to us, saying: 'Amr ibn Thabit narrated to us, from his father, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, his saying: "And I know what you disclose and what you were concealing," he said: what Iblis secretly held in himself. [[The report: 680 - I have not found it elsewhere. 'Amr ibn Thabit and his father were mentioned earlier at 641, and I noted there the possible error in his saying "from his grandfather." This chain here is correct, since Thabit ibn Hurmuz is known for narrating from Sa'id ibn Jubayr.]]

681 - Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us concerning His words: "And I know what you disclose and what you were concealing," he said: what Iblis secretly held in himself of pride, not to prostrate to Adam. [[The report: 681 - I have not found it elsewhere.]]

682 - al-Muthanna ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: al-Hajjaj al-Anmati informed us, saying: Mahdi ibn Maymun narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Hasan ibn Dinar say to al-Hasan, while we were sitting with him at his house: O Abu Sa'id, what do you say about God's words to the angels, "And I know what you disclose and what you were concealing"? What did the angels conceal? Al-Hasan said: When God created Adam, the angels saw a wondrous creation, and something seemed to enter them about it, so some of them turned to others and secretly discussed it among themselves, saying: What concern is this creature to us? God will never create a creation except that we are more honored by Him than it. [[The report: 682 - in al-Durr al-Manthur 1:50. "al-Hajjaj al-Anmati" is al-Hajjaj ibn al-Minhal, a trustworthy narrator among the teachers of al-Bukhari and al-Darimi and others. "Mahdi ibn Maymun" is a well-known trustworthy narrator who related from al-Hasan al-Basri, Ibn Sirin and others. In this chain he explicitly states that he heard al-Hasan al-Basri's answer when al-Hasan ibn Dinar asked him, and I note this lest one think it is Mahdi's narration from al-Hasan ibn Dinar. Al-Hasan ibn Dinar is a liar whose reliability cannot be trusted; his biography is full of rejected and fabricated reports, in Ibn Hibban's al-Majruhin no. 208, al-Mizan, Lisan al-Mizan, al-Tahdhib, and al-Bukhari in al-Kabir 1/2/290-291 and al-Saghir 185, Ibn Abi Hatim 1/2/11-12, and Ibn Sa'd 7/2/37.]]

683 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, concerning His words "And I know what you disclose and what you were concealing," he said: they secretly said among themselves: God creates what He wills to create, so He will never create a creation except that we are more honored by Him than it. [[The report: 683 - in al-Durr al-Manthur 1:50, with different wording, attributed to al-Tabari "from Qatadah and al-Hasan."]]

684 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: 'Abdullah ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas: "And I know what you disclose and what you were concealing": what they disclosed was when they said, "Will You place therein one who will corrupt therein," and what they concealed among themselves was their saying: Our Lord will never create a creation except that we are more knowledgeable and more honorable than it. So they knew that God had preferred Adam over them in knowledge and generosity. [[The report: 684 - in Ibn Kathir 1:135.]]

Abu Ja'far said: The most accurate of these interpretations of the verse is that of Ibn 'Abbas, namely that the meaning of His words "And I know what you disclose" is: and I know, along with My knowledge of the unseen of the heavens and the earth, what you make apparent with your tongues, "and what you were concealing" is what you hid in your souls, so nothing is hidden from Me; My knowledge of your inner thoughts and your outward acts is the same.

What they made apparent with their tongues is what God, exalted is His praise, reported that they said: "Will You place therein one who will corrupt therein and shed blood, while we exalt You with praise and sanctify You?" What they were concealing is what Iblis harbored of opposition to God in His command and arrogance toward His obedience. For there is no disagreement among all the people of interpretation that the interpretation of this is not outside one of the two aspects I have described: the first is what we stated, and the other is what we mentioned from the saying of al-Hasan and Qatadah, and whoever said that the meaning is the angels' concealment among themselves that God would never create a creation except that they would be more honored by Him than it. Since there is no interpretation of this except one of the two views I have described, and since one of them lacks, in its soundness, evidence from a valid aspect that must be accepted, the other view is established.

So what is related from al-Hasan and Qatadah and those who hold their view as an interpretation of this lacks evidence for its soundness, neither from the Book nor from a report that establishes proof. What Ibn 'Abbas said is supported in its soundness by God's report, exalted is His praise, about Iblis and his disobedience, when He called him to prostrate to Adam and he refused and was arrogant, and his display to all the angels of his disobedience and pride, which he had concealed before that.

If someone supposes that the report about the angels' concealment of what they were concealing, since it is phrased as a report about all of them, makes it impermissible that what is related from Ibn 'Abbas, and from whoever holds his view, that this is a report about Iblis's concealment of pride and disobedience, is sound, then he has supposed wrongly. For it is the way of the Arabs, when they report about a part of a group without naming a specific individual, to phrase the report about him as though it were about all of them. Like their saying: "The army was slain and routed," when in fact only one or some of them were slain and routed. So they phrase the report about the one routed or slain as a report about all of them, just as He, exalted is His praise, said: ﴿Indeed, those who call you from behind the chambers, most of them do not reason﴾ [Surah al-Hujurat 49:4]. It is mentioned that the one who called out to the Messenger of God ﷺ, about whom this verse was revealed, was a man from a group of the Banu Tamim who had come to the Messenger of God ﷺ. So the report about him was phrased as a report about the group. Likewise His words: "And I know what you disclose and what you were concealing," the report is phrased as a report about all of them, while the intended meaning is one of them.

The commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan), on 2:34 (part 1 of 2):

**The exposition of His words, may His remembrance be exalted: ﴿And when We said to the angels, "Prostrate yourselves before Adam," they prostrated, except Iblis. He refused and was arrogant, and he was among the disbelievers.﴾ (2:34)**

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: As for His words, "And when We said," it is joined to His words, "And when your Lord said to the angels" (2:30). It is as if He, great is His remembrance, said to the Jews, who lived among the emigrants of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) from the Children of Israel, enumerating His blessings upon them and reminding them of His favours, in the manner we described earlier: "Remember My action toward you when I bestowed My favour upon you. I created for you all that is on the earth (2:29), and when I said to the angels, 'I am placing a successor on the earth' (2:30), I honoured your father Adam with what I gave him of My knowledge, My grace and My generosity, and when I commanded My angels to prostrate to him, they prostrated to him." Then He made an exception of Iblis from all of them. By excepting him from them, He indicated that he was one of them and that he was among those commanded to prostrate along with them, as He, great is His praise, said: ﴿except Iblis; he was not among those who prostrated. He said, "What prevented you from prostrating when I commanded you?"﴾ (7:11–12). Thus He informed us that He had commanded Iblis along with those angels He commanded to prostrate to Adam. Then He, great is His praise, excepted him from what He had reported of them, that they had done, of prostration to Adam, and He removed him from the description with which He had characterized them, of obedience to His command, and He negated for him what He had affirmed for His angels, of prostration to His servant Adam.

Then the people of ta'wil (interpretation) differed concerning him: was he one of the angels, or was he of some other kind? Some of them said:

685 – Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Uthman ibn Sa'id narrated to us, from Bishr ibn Umara, from Abu Rawq, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Iblis was from a tribe of the angels' tribes called "al-Hinn," created from the fire of the scorching wind (al-samum) among the angels. He said: His name was al-Harith. He said: He was one of the treasurers of Paradise. He said: The angels were created from a light other than this tribe's. He said: The jinn mentioned in the Qur'an were created from smokeless fire (marij min nar), which is the tongue of fire that appears at its edge when it blazes.[[Report 685: it appears in full in report no. 606 above, and in Ibn Kathir 1:136; in both places it reads "when it burns" (idha alhabat), while Ibn Kathir repeated it at 5:296 with "when it blazes" (idha iltahabat) as here. There it reads "al-Jinn" with a jim, and see what preceded at p. 455, note 1.]]

686 – Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from Khallad, from Ata', from Tawus, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Before he committed disobedience, Iblis was among the angels, and his name was "Azazil." He was one of the inhabitants of the earth, and he was one of the most diligent of the angels in worship and the most knowledgeable of them. That led him to pride. He was from a tribe called the jinn.[[Report 686: in Ibn Kathir 1:139 and 5:296, al-Durr al-manthur 1:150, and al-Shawkani 1:53. Khallad is Ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Sana'ani, who is trustworthy. He narrates from Tawus and Mujahid directly, but here and in the following report he narrated from them through Ata'.]]

687 – Ibn Humayd narrated this to us again, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from Khallad, from Ata', from Tawus, or Mujahid Abu al-Hajjaj, from Ibn Abbas and others, with similar wording, except that he said: He was a king among the angels, named "Azazil." He was one of the inhabitants of the earth and its builders, and the inhabitants of the earth among them were called "the jinn," from among the angels.[[Report 687: in Ibn Kathir 1:139, after the previous one.]]

688 – Musa ibn Harun narrated to me, saying: Amr ibn Hammad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi in a report he mentioned, from Abu Malik, and from Abu Salih, from Ibn Abbas, and from Murrah, from Ibn Mas'ud, and from some companions of the Prophet (ﷺ): Iblis was placed in charge of the kingdom of the lowest heaven. He was from a tribe of the angels called "the jinn," and they were only named "jinn" because they were guardians of Paradise. Iblis, along with his kingship, was a guardian.[[Report 688: an abridgment of report no. 607 above.]]

689 – Al-Qasim ibn al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, who said: Ibn Abbas said: Iblis was one of the noblest of the angels and the most honoured of them in lineage. He was a guardian over the gardens (of Paradise), and he had authority over the lowest heaven, and he had authority over the earth. Ibn Abbas said: As for His words, ﴿he was of the jinn﴾ (18:50), he was only called "of the gardens" (al-jinan) because he was a guardian over them, just as a man is called Makkan, Madinan, Kufan or Basran.[[Report 689: in Ibn Kathir 1:139 and 5:296, and al-Durr al-manthur 1:178.]]

Ibn Juraij said: Others said: They were a tribe of the angels, and their tribe's name was the jinn.

690 – Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Salih, the freedman of al-Tawama, and Shurayk ibn Abi Namir, one of them or both, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Among the angels there is a tribe of the jinn, and Iblis was one of them, and he governed what was between the heaven and the earth.[[Report 690: in Ibn Kathir 5:296–297, with additional material there. A fuller report with another chain will come at 700.]]

691 – It was reported to me from al-Hasan ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh al-Fadl ibn Khalid say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim say concerning His words, ﴿they prostrated, except Iblis, who was of the jinn﴾ (18:50): Ibn Abbas used to say: Iblis was one of the noblest of the angels and the most honoured of them in lineage. Then he mentioned the same as the first report of Ibn Juraij.[[Report 691: I have not identified al-Hasan ibn al-Faraj. Abu Mu'adh al-Fadl ibn Khalid is the grammarian of Marw, who is trustworthy; Ibn Hibban mentioned him among the trustworthy, Ibn Abi Hatim gave his biography at 3/2/61, Yaqut in al-Udaba' 6:140, and al-Suyuti in al-Bughya p. 373. Yaqut said: "al-Azhari narrated from him in the book al-Tahdhib, and much." He does not mean narration by direct hearing, but that he transmitted his opinions or what he related in lexicography. As for direct hearing, there is none, because this al-Fadl died in 211 AH, and al-Azhari was born in 282 AH. So this statement is misleading, and al-Suyuti, who was a traditionist, should not have followed it without reflection!]]

692 – Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Shaybān narrated to me, saying: Salam ibn Miskin narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, who said: Iblis was the chief of the angels of the lowest heaven.[[Report 692: in Ibn Kathir 1:139. Shaybān is Ibn Farrukh, who is trustworthy. Salam ibn Miskin al-Azdi is trustworthy; the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim) narrated from him.]]

693 – Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning His words: ﴿And when We said to the angels, "Prostrate to Adam," they prostrated, except Iblis, who was of the jinn﴾ (18:50). He was from a tribe of the angels called "the jinn." Ibn Abbas used to say: If he had not been of the angels, he would not have been commanded to prostrate. He was over the treasury of the lowest heaven. He said: Qatadah used to say: He rebelled (janna) against the obedience of his Lord.[[Report 693: I have not found it anywhere else.]]

694 – Al-Husayn ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, concerning His words: "except Iblis, who was of the jinn." He said: He was from a tribe of the angels called the jinn.[[Report 694: I have not found it either. The Hafiz Ibn Kathir said at 5:297, after citing many reports on such meanings: "Many reports have been transmitted on this from the early generation (al-salaf). Most of them are from the Isra'iliyyat (narratives derived from Jewish and Christian sources), which are related so that they may be examined, and God knows best the state of many of them. Some of them may be definitively judged false, because they contradict the truth we possess. The Qur'an is sufficient without all other reports, because they hardly escape alteration, addition and omission, and many things have been forged in them. They do not have among them the precise memorizers who negate from them the distortion of extremists and the fabrications of falsifiers, as this community has among its imams and scholars, its masters and pious people, its righteous and noble ones, its critical experts and excellent memorizers, who recorded the hadith and verified it, and distinguished its sound from its good, its weak, its rejected, its fabricated, its abandoned and its false. They knew the forgers, the liars and the unknown narrators, and other categories of men, all of this to protect the Prophetic presence and the Muhammadan station, the seal of the messengers and the master of mankind (ﷺ), from having falsehood attributed to him or narrations related from him that are not his. May God be pleased with them and make them pleased, and make the Gardens of Paradise their abode. And He has done so."]]

695 – Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: As for the Arabs, they say: "The jinn" is only whatever is concealed (ijtanna) and not seen. As for His words, "except Iblis, who was of the jinn," it means he was of the angels, because the angels were concealed and not seen. God, great is His praise, has said: ﴿And they made between Him and the jinn a kinship, but the jinn know that they will be brought forth﴾ (37:158). That was in response to the saying of Quraysh that the angels are the daughters of God. God says: If the angels are My daughters, then Iblis is among them, and they have made a kinship between Me and Iblis and his offspring. He said: al-A'sha, the A'sha of Bani Qays ibn Tha'laba al-Bakri, has said, mentioning Solomon son of David and what God gave him:

"Even if something were eternal or long-lived,
Solomon would be the one free of the ages." [[Supplement to the Diwan of al-A'sha, p. 243; al-Adhdad by Ibn al-Anbari, p. 293. "The ages" (al-dahr) here does not mean the extended duration but the calamities and misfortunes of time, as 'Adi ibn Zayd said, making the calamities of time to be time itself: "O mocker who reproaches with time, are you the one exempted and abundantly blessed?"]]

"My God created him and chose him as His servant,
and made him king of what lies between the Thurayya and Egypt [[al-Thurayya: so it is vocalized in the supplement to al-A'sha's Diwan. I did not know the place and did not find it. I have not been guided to its distortion, if it is distorted. In al-Adhdad it reads "tawfa."]],
and subjected to him from the jinn of the angels nine,
standing before him, working without wage."

He said: The Arabs insisted in their language that "the jinn" is whatever is concealed. He says: God did not name the jinn except because they were hidden and not seen, and the children of Adam were not named "mankind" (al-ins) except because they appeared and were not concealed. So what appears is human (ins), and what is concealed and not seen is jinn.[[Report 695: abridged by the author of al-Adhdad, p. 293. I have not found it anywhere else.]]

Others said:

696 – Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Adi narrated to us, from Awf, from al-Hasan, who said: Iblis was never of the angels for the blink of an eye, and he is the origin of the jinn, just as Adam is the origin of mankind.[[Report 696: in Ibn Kathir 1:139 and 5:296. He said: "This chain is sound from al-Hasan."]]

697 – Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Zuray' narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, who said: Al-Hasan used to say concerning His words, "except Iblis, who was of the jinn": He returned him to his lineage (alja'ahu ila nasabihi), and God said: ﴿Will you take him and his offspring as allies instead of Me, while they are enemies to you? Wretched is the exchange for the wrongdoers﴾ (18:50). They reproduce just as the children of Adam reproduce.[[In the printed edition: "ilja' ila nasabihi" ("a return to his lineage"). "Alja'ahu ila nasabihi" means he restored him to it. See no. 655. Report 697: I have not found it anywhere.]]
