698 – Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, saying: Abu Sa'id al-Yahmadi narrated to us, saying: Isma'il ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, saying: Sawwar ibn al-Ja'd al-Yahmadi narrated to us, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, concerning His words "of the jinn," who said: Iblis was of the jinn whom the angels expelled, and some of the angels captured him and took him to heaven.[[Report 698: in Ibn Kathir 1:139.]]

699 – Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Abu Nasr Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Khallal narrated to me, saying: Sunayd ibn Dawud narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman ibn Yahya informed us, from Musa ibn Numayr, and Uthman ibn Sa'id ibn Kamil, from Sa'd ibn Mas'ud, who said: The angels used to fight the jinn, and Iblis was taken captive while he was young, so he was with the angels and worshipped with them. When they were commanded to prostrate to Adam, they prostrated. Iblis refused. Therefore God said: "except Iblis, who was of the jinn."[[Report 699: in Ibn Kathir 1:139.]]

700 – Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah ibn al-Fadl narrated to us, saying: al-Mubarak ibn Mujahid Abu al-Azhar narrated to us, from Shurayk ibn Abd Allah ibn Abi Namir, from Salih, the freedman of al-Tawama, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Among the angels there is a group called the jinn, and Iblis was of them. Iblis governed what was between the heaven and the earth. He disobeyed, so God transformed him into a stoning devil (shaytan rajim).[[Report 700: in Ibn Kathir 1:139. A similar report, in abridged form, with a different chain, appeared at 690.]]

701 – He said: Yunus narrated to us, from Ibn Wahb, who said: Ibn Zayd said: Iblis is the father of the jinn, just as Adam is the father of mankind.[[Report 701: I have not found it anywhere.]]

The reason for those who held this view is that God, great is His praise, informed in His Book that He created Iblis from the fire of the scorching wind and from smokeless fire, and He did not inform us that He created the angels from any of that. And God, great is His praise, informed that he was of the jinn. They said: It is not permissible to attribute him to other than what God attributed him to. They said: Iblis has offspring and progeny, and the angels do not reproduce or multiply.

702 – Muhammad ibn Sinan al-Qazzaz narrated to us, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, from Shurayk, from a man, from Ikrima, from Ibn Abbas, who said: God created a creation and said: "Prostrate to Adam." They said: "We will not do so." So God sent upon them a fire that burned them. Then He created another creation and said: "I am creating a human from clay; prostrate to Adam." They refused, so God sent upon them a fire that burned them. He said: Then He created these, and said: "Prostrate to Adam." They said: "Yes." And Iblis was among those who refused to prostrate to Adam.[[Report 702: in Ibn Kathir 1:139, and al-Durr al-manthur 1:50. Ibn Kathir said about its chain: "This is strange, and its chain hardly sound, for it contains an unnamed man, and such a report cannot be used as proof, and God knows best."]]

Abu Ja'far said: These are reasons that reveal the weakness of the knowledge of their holders. That is because it is not objectionable that God, great is His praise, created various kinds of His angels from various kinds of His diverse creation: He created some from light, some from fire, and some from other things as He willed. The fact that God, great is His praise, did not report what He created His angels from (in the printed edition: "And there is nothing in what God, great is His praise, revealed..." which is a clear error; and his words after this, "and His reporting what Iblis was created from," are conjoined to his words "And in God's omission..."), and His reporting what Iblis was created from, does not necessitate that Iblis is outside their category. For it is permissible that He created a kind of His angels from fire, of whom Iblis was one, and that He singled out Iblis by creating him from the fire of the scorching wind apart from the rest of His angels. Likewise, it does not exclude him from being of the angels that he had offspring and progeny, because of the appetite and pleasure that were implanted in him, which were removed from the rest of the angels, due to what God willed for him of disobedience. As for God's report that he was "of the jinn," it is not disputed that whatever is concealed from sight of all things may be called "jinn," as we have already mentioned in the poetry of al-A'sha. Thus Iblis and the angels are of them, because they are concealed from the sight of the children of Adam.

**The exposition of the meaning of "Iblis"**

Abu Ja'far said: Iblis is on the pattern "ifʿil," derived from al-iblas, which means despair of good, remorse and grief. As for the evidence:

703 – Abu Kurayb narrated this to us, saying: Uthman ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Bishr ibn Umara narrated to us, from Abu Rawq, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Iblis (Iblis) — God made him despair (abla-hu) of all good, and made him a stoning devil as a punishment for his disobedience.[[Report 703: an abridgment of report no. 606 above. It appears in al-Durr al-manthur 1:50 and al-Shawkani 1:53.]]

٧٠٤ - Musa ibn Harun narrated to us, saying: Amr ibn Hammad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, who said: The name of Iblis was "al-Harith," and Iblis was so named when he was made desperate (abalsa), bewildered.[[The narration: 704 - in al-Durr al-Manthur 1:50, abridged to its beginning up to his saying: "al-Harith." The text in the printed edition reads thus: "and Iblis was named when he was made desperate, so he was changed, as Allah, may His praise be exalted, said..." They omitted what we have recorded from the manuscript, because they did not read the last word well; they changed it and joined the speech after the omission, which is a faulty alteration. As for his saying "mutahayyiran" (bewildered), it was written in the manuscript in a blurred form, thus "mujra," without dots. Al-iblas means bewilderment, and so I read it.]]

Abu Ja'far said: As Allah, may His praise be exalted, said: ﴿Then, behold, they are despairing﴾ [Surah al-An'am: 44], meaning: they are hopeless of good, grieving with remorse, as al-Ajjaj said:

"O companion, do you recognize a dwelling-place covered with dung?" ... "He said: Yes, I recognize it, and it was made desperate (abalsa)!"[[His Diwan 1:31; al-Kamil 1:352; al-Lisan: (balas), (karas). Al-mukarras is the place where karas has formed, which is the urine and dung of camels, piled upon one another in the courtyard. And abalsa al-rajul: he fell silent from grief, was broken, bewildered, and did not speak.]]

And Ru'ba said:

"And there came on the day of Thursday, the fifth-days... and in the faces is yellowness and iblas (dejection)."[[His Diwan: 67; al-Lisan (balas); the reading in his Diwan is "wa-'arafat yawm al-Khamis." Between the two verses is another verse: "And the breaths have rattled between the collarbones."]]

Meaning by it: depression and dejection.

If someone says: If Iblis, as you said, is "ifil" from al-iblas, why then is it not declined and treated as diptote? It is said: its being treated as a diptote was left out because of its heaviness, since it is a name with no counterpart among Arabic names; so the Arabs, given that situation, likened it to foreign names which are not declined. They have said: "I passed by Ishaq," and they did not decline it. And it is from "asḥaqahu Allah ishaqan" [Allah destroyed him]; since it fell as an initial foreign name for non-Arabs, then Arabs adopted it and it took its place, being in the category of foreign names in case-inflection, so it was not declined. Likewise "Ayyub" is only "fay'ul" from "aba yu'ibu."

As for the interpretation of his saying "abā" (refused), Allah, may His praise be exalted, means by it Iblis: that he refused to prostrate to Adam and did not prostrate to him. "And he was arrogant" means that he magnified himself and was too proud to obey Allah in prostrating to Adam. This, although it is Allah's report about Iblis, is a rebuke to his peers among Allah's creation who are arrogant against submitting to Allah's command and yielding to His obedience in what He commanded them and what He forbade them, and submitting to Him in what He made obligatory for some of them toward others of rights. Among those who were arrogant against submitting to Allah's command, humbling themselves to His obedience, and submitting to His decree in what He imposed on them of the rights of others were the Jews who lived among the environs of the emigration place of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and their rabbis who knew the Messenger of Allah ﷺ by his description and knew that he was truly Allah's Messenger. Then, despite their knowledge of that, they were arrogant against acknowledging his prophethood and submitting to his obedience, out of rebellion and envy toward him. So Allah rebuked them with His report about Iblis, who, in his arrogance against prostrating to Adam, acted out of envy and rebellion, like their action in being arrogant against submitting to Muhammad, the Prophet of Allah ﷺ, and his prophethood, when he came to them with the truth from their Lord, out of envy and rebellion.

Then He described Iblis with the same description with which He described those whom He set up as an example for him in arrogance, envy, and refusal to submit to the one whom Allah commanded them to submit to. So He, may His praise be exalted, said: "And he was" - meaning Iblis - "of the disbelievers" - among those who denied the blessings of Allah upon him and His favors bestowed upon him, by disobeying Him in what He commanded him of prostrating to Adam, just as the Jews disbelieved in the blessings of their Lord which He gave them and their forefathers before: such as Allah feeding their ancestors manna and quails, and the clouds shading them, and countless other blessings that were theirs, especially what was specific to those who met Muhammad ﷺ by encountering him and witnessing the proof of Allah against them; yet they denied his prophethood after knowing him and recognizing his prophethood, out of envy and rebellion. So Allah, may His praise be exalted, attributed him to "the disbelievers," making him among their number in religion and creed, even though he differed from them in kind and lineage. Just as He made the hypocrites some of them from others, because they gathered together in hypocrisy, even though their lineages and kinds differed, He said: ﴿The hypocrite men and the hypocrite women are of one another﴾ [Surah al-Tawbah: 67], meaning by it that some of them are from others in hypocrisy and misguidance. Likewise His saying about Iblis: "he was of the disbelievers," meaning he was among them in disbelief in Allah and in disobeying His command, even though his kind differed from theirs and his lineage differed from theirs. The meaning of His saying "and he was of the disbelievers" is that he was, at the time he refused to prostrate, among the disbelievers at that time.

It has been narrated from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, from Abu al-'Aliyah, that he used to say: in the interpretation of His saying "and he was of the disbelievers" in this place, it means "and he was of the disobedient."

٧٠٥ - Al-Muthanna ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Adam al-'Asqalani narrated to us, saying: Abu Ja'far narrated to us, from al-Rabi', from Abu al-'Aliyah, regarding His saying "and he was of the disbelievers," meaning the disobedient.[[The narration 705 - in Ibn Kathir 1:140.]]

٧٠٦ - And it was reported to me from Ammar ibn al-Hasan, who said: 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi', with the like of it.

That is similar in meaning to what we have said about it.

The prostration of the angels to Adam was an honoring of Adam and an obedience to Allah, not a worship of Adam, as:

٧٠٧ - Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Zuray' narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying "And when We said to the angels: Prostrate to Adam": the obedience was to Allah, and the prostration was to Adam; Allah honored Adam by having His angels prostrate to him.[[The narration 707 - in Ibn Kathir 1:140, and in al-Durr al-Manthur 1:50 at length.]]

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 35 (part 1 of 2)**

The discussion of the ta'wil (interpretation) of His saying, exalted is His remembrance: ﴿And We said, "O Adam, dwell, you and your wife, in the Garden"﴾

Abu Ja'far said: In this verse there is clear evidence for the correctness of the view of those who said that Iblis was expelled from the Garden after his arrogance in refusing to prostrate to Adam, and that Adam was settled in it before Iblis was sent down to the earth. Do you not hear Allah, may His praise be exalted, saying: "And We said, 'O Adam, dwell, you and your wife, in the Garden, and eat from it in abundance wherever you wish, but do not approach this tree, or you will be among the wrongdoers.' Then Satan caused them to slip from it and removed them from that in which they were"? It is therefore clear that Iblis led them astray from obedience to Allah only after he had been cursed and had shown arrogance, because the angels' prostration to Adam took place after the spirit had been breathed into him. At that point Iblis's refusal to prostrate occurred, and upon that refusal the curse descended upon him. As follows:

708 - Musa ibn Harun narrated to me, saying: Amr ibn Hammad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, in a report he mentioned, from Abu Malik and from Abu Salih, from Ibn Abbas, and from Murrah, from Ibn Mas'ud, and from some companions of the Prophet ﷺ: that the enemy of Allah, Iblis, swore by the might of Allah that he would mislead Adam and his offspring and his wife, except for His sincere servants among them, after Allah had cursed him, after he had been expelled from the Garden, and before he was sent down to the earth. And Allah taught Adam all the names. [[The report: 708 - I have not found it in any place.]]

709 - Ibn Humayd also narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: When Allah had finished with Iblis and his rebuke, and he refused anything but disobedience, and the curse fell upon him, and then He expelled him from the Garden, He turned to Adam, who had been taught all the names, and said: "O Adam, inform them of their names," up to His saying: "Indeed You are the Knowing, the Wise." [[The report: 709 - I have not found it in this exact wording, but it is from the beginning of the report that follows after number 711.]]

Then the people of ta'wil differed regarding the circumstance in which Adam's wife was created, and the time at which she was made a dwelling for him. Ibn Abbas said, as follows:

710 - Musa ibn Harun narrated to me, saying: Amr ibn Hammad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, in a report he mentioned, from Abu Malik, and from Abu Salih, from Ibn Abbas, and from Murrah, from Ibn Mas'ud, and from some companions of the Prophet ﷺ: Iblis was expelled from the Garden when he was cursed, and Adam was settled in the Garden. He would walk in it alone (wahshan), having no wife with whom to find comfort. Then he slept a sleep and awoke, and at his head was a woman sitting, whom Allah had created from his rib. He asked her, "Who are you?" She said, "A woman." He said, "And why were you created?" She said, "So that you may find comfort in me." The angels, who were watching to see how far his knowledge extended, said to him: "What is her name, O Adam?" He said: "Hawwa'." They said: "And why was she named Hawwa'?" He said: "Because she was created from something living (hayy)." Then Allah said to him: "O Adam, dwell, you and your wife, in the Garden, and eat from it in abundance wherever you wish." [[The report: 710 - In Tarikh al-Tabari 1: 52, with some variation in wording. Also Ibn Kathir 1: 142 and al-Shawkani 1: 56. His saying "wahshan" means that there was no one with him besides himself, alone. A place is called wahsh when it is empty.]]

This report indicates that Hawwa' was created after Adam had dwelt in the Garden, and so she was made a dwelling for him.

Others said: Rather, she was created before Adam dwelt in the Garden.

Those who said that:

711 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: When Allah had finished rebuking Iblis, He turned to Adam, who had been taught all the names, and said: "O Adam, inform them of their names," up to His saying: "Indeed You are the Knowing, the Wise." He said: Then He cast sleep upon Adam, as we have been informed from the People of the Book, from the People of the Torah and others of the learned, from Abd Allah ibn Abbas and others. Then He took one of his ribs from his left side and filled its place with flesh, while Adam was asleep and did not stir from his sleep, until Allah created from that rib his wife Hawwa', and fashioned her as a woman so that he might find comfort in her. When the sleep was lifted from him and he awoke from his sleep, he saw her beside him, and he said, as they claim, and Allah knows best: "Flesh of my flesh, blood of my blood, and my wife," and he found comfort in her. When Allah, blessed and exalted, married him to her and made for him a dwelling from himself, He said to him, face to face: "O Adam, dwell, you and your wife, in the Garden, and eat from it in abundance wherever you wish, but do not approach this tree, or you will be among the wrongdoers." [[The report: 711 - In Tarikh al-Tabari 1: 52 and Ibn Kathir 1: 141-142. His saying "qabilan" means "face to face," visibly. In a report of Abu Dharr (Ibn Kathir 1: 141), he said: "I said, 'O Messenger of Allah, tell me: was Adam a prophet?' He said, 'Yes, a prophet and messenger, whom Allah addressed qabilan,' that is, face to face." This word appears in the printed edition as "qala lahu fatala," which is an error. In Tarikh al-Tabari it is "qala lahu qeelan," which is also an error.]]

Abu Ja'far said: The wife of a man is called zawjuhu and zawjatuhu. The form with the ta' marker (zawjah) is more common in the speech of the Arabs than the form without it. The form without the ta' (zawj) is said to be the dialect of the Azd Shanu'ah. As for zawj (husband) of a woman, there is no disagreement among the Arabs about it. [[For their differences on this, see the entry (z-w-j) in Lisan al-Arab.]]

* *

The discussion of the ta'wil of His saying: ﴿And eat from it in abundance wherever you wish﴾

Abu Ja'far said: As for al-raghad (abundance), it is the wide and pleasant living, free of hardship for its possessor. It is said: "Arghada fulan," when he attained wide and pleasant living, as Imru' al-Qays ibn Hujr said:

"While a man is seen by you as comfortable,
secure from misfortunes, in a life of abundance (raghad)." [[I have not found this verse in what they collected of the poetry of Imru' al-Qays.]]

712 - As Musa ibn Harun narrated to me, saying: Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, in a report he mentioned, from Abu Malik, and from Abu Salih, from Ibn Abbas, and from Murrah, from Ibn Mas'ud, and from some companions of the Prophet ﷺ, regarding "and eat from it in abundance," he said: al-raghad is pleasant. [[The report: 712 - In al-Durr al-Manthur 1: 52, and al-Shawkani 1: 56.]]

713 - Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying "raghadan," he said: there is no reckoning for them.

714 - Al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.

715 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us, from Anbasa, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman, from al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazzah, from Mujahid: "And eat from it in abundance," meaning: there is no reckoning for them. [[The reports: 713-715 - In al-Durr al-Manthur 1: 52, and al-Shawkani 1: 56.]]

716 - It was narrated to me from al-Minjab ibn al-Harith, who said: Bishr ibn Umarah narrated to us, from Abu Rawq, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn Abbas: "And eat from it in abundance wherever you wish," he said: al-raghad is the breadth of livelihood. [[The report: 716 - In al-Durr al-Manthur 1: 52 and al-Shawkani 1: 56.]]

So the meaning of the verse is: "And We said, 'O Adam, dwell, you and your wife, in the Garden, and eat from the Garden a wide and pleasant provision of living, wherever you wish.'"

717 - As Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Zurayi' narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: "O Adam, dwell, you and your wife, in the Garden, and eat from it in abundance wherever you wish." Then, the trial that was decreed upon creation was decreed upon Adam, just as creation had been tried before him: Allah, may His praise be exalted, made lawful for him whatever is in the Garden, that he might eat from it in abundance wherever he wished, except for one tree which was forbidden to him, and he was warned about it. The trial did not cease to beset him until he fell into what had been forbidden. [[The report: 717 - In al-Durr al-Manthur 1: 53, by a route other than al-Tabari's. His saying "qudima ilayhi fiha" means that he was given a command in it not to approach it. It is said: "taqaddamtu ilayhi bi-kadha" and "qaddamtu ilayhi bi-kadha," meaning: I commanded him with such and such.]]

* *

The discussion of the ta'wil of His, exalted is He, saying: ﴿And do not approach this tree﴾

Abu Ja'far said: In the speech of the Arabs, al-shajar (tree) is everything that stands upon a stem. And from the saying of Allah, may His praise be exalted: ﴿And the star and the tree prostrate﴾ [Surah al-Rahman: 6], by "the star" He means what rises from the earth as plants, and by "the tree" what stands upright upon a stem.

Then the people of ta'wil differed regarding the specific tree from whose fruit Adam was forbidden to eat. Some of them said: It is the sunbulah (ear of grain).

Those who said that:

718 - Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Ahmasi narrated to me, saying: Abd al-Hamid al-Himmani narrated to us, from al-Nadr, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The tree from whose fruit Adam was forbidden to eat is the sunbulah. [[The report: 718 - In Ibn Kathir 1: 142, al-Durr al-Manthur 1: 53, and al-Shawkani 1: 56, and it is a weak isnad. Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Ahmasi has already been mentioned: 405. Abd al-Hamid ibn Abd al-Rahman, Abu Yahya al-Hammani, is trustworthy; Ibn Ma'in and others declared him trustworthy, and al-Shaykhan (al-Bukhari and Muslim) narrated from him. Al-Nadr is Ibn Abd al-Rahman, Abu Umar al-Khazzaz, with dotted letters, and he is extremely weak. Al-Bukhari said in al-Kabir 4/2/91: "munkar al-hadith" (rejected in narration). Ibn Abi Hatim 4/1/475 narrated from Ahmad ibn Hanbal, who said: "He is nothing, weak in hadith." It is also reported from Ibn Ma'in that he said: "It is not lawful for anyone to narrate from him."]]

719 - Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, and Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Umran ibn Uyaynah narrated to us, all from Husayn, from Abu Malik, regarding His saying "and do not approach this tree," he said: It is the sunbulah.

720 - Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Ibn Mahdi narrated to us, and Ahmad ibn Ishaq al-Ahwazi narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad al-Zubayri narrated to us, both saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Husayn, from Abu Malik, the same. [[The two reports: 719, 720 - In Ibn Kathir 1: 142, and al-Durr al-Manthur 1: 53.]]

721 - Abu Kurayb and Ibn Waki' narrated to us, both saying: Ibn Idris narrated to us, saying: I heard my father, from Atiyyah, regarding His saying "and do not approach this tree," he said: the sunbulah. [[The report: 721 - Atiyyah is al-Awfi. Ibn Kathir 1: 142 pointed to this report from him.]]

722 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, from Sa'id, from Qatadah, who said: The tree from which Adam was forbidden is the sunbulah. [[The report: 722 - I have not found it in any place.]]

723 - Al-Muthanna ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Muslim ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, saying: al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: A man of the Banu Tamim narrated to me, that Ibn Abbas wrote to Abu al-Jald asking him about the tree from which Adam ate, and the tree at which he repented. Abu al-Jald wrote back to him: "You asked me about the tree that Adam was forbidden, and it is the sunbulah; and you asked me about the tree at which Adam repented, and it is the zaytunah (olive tree)." [[The report: 723 - In Ibn Kathir 1: 142. In the originals it is "Abu al-Khald," and see what passed in the note on report no. 434. This isnad is weak, because the man from the Banu Tamim is unidentified.]]

724 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from a man of the learned, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas, that he used to say: The tree that Adam was forbidden is al-Burr (wheat). [[The report: 724 - Ibn Kathir 1: 142, al-Durr al-Manthur 1: 52, and al-Shawkani 1: 56. What is in Ibn Kathir reads: "from a man of the learned, from Hajjaj, from Mujahid..."]]

725 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, saying: Ibn Uyaynah and Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from al-Hasan ibn Umarah, from al-Minhal ibn Amr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The tree which Allah forbade to Adam and his wife was the sunbulah. [[The report: 725 - In Ibn Kathir 1: 142.]]

726 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from some people of Yemen, from Wahb ibn Munabbih al-Yamani, that he used to say: It is al-Burr, but its grain in Paradise is like the kidneys of a cow, softer than butter and sweeter than honey. And the People of the Torah say: It is al-Burr. [[The report: 726 - In Ibn Kathir 1: 142-143, and al-Durr al-Manthur 1: 52-53. However, the phrase "and the People of the Torah..." is not in them.]]

727 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to me, from Ya'qub ibn Utbah, that he was told that it is the tree against which the angels rub themselves for immortality.

728 - Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Jabir ibn Yazid ibn Rifa'ah, from Muharib ibn Dithar, who said: It is the sunbulah.

729 - Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Abu Usamah narrated to us, from Yazid ibn Ibrahim, from al-Hasan, who said: It is the sunbulah that Allah made a provision for his offspring in this world. [[The reports: 727-729 - I have not found them in these exact words in any place.]]

Abu Ja'far said: Others said: It is the vine (karmah).

Those who said that:

730 - Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Abd Allah narrated to us, from Isra'il, from al-Suddi, from one who narrated to him, from Ibn Abbas, who said: It is the karmah.

731 - Musa ibn Harun narrated to me, saying: Amr ibn Hammad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, in a report he mentioned, from Abu Malik, and from Abu Salih, from Ibn Abbas, and from Murrah, from Ibn Mas'ud, and from some companions of the Prophet ﷺ, regarding "and do not approach this tree," he said: It is the karmah, and the Jews claim that it is the wheat.

732 - Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Amr ibn Hammad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, who said: The tree is the karm (vine).

733 - Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, from Mughirah, from al-Sha'bi, from Ja'dah ibn Hubayrah, who said: It is the grape (inab), in His saying "and do not approach this tree."

734 - Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to me, from Khallad al-Saffar, from Bayan, from al-Sha'bi, from Ja'dah ibn Hubayrah, regarding "and do not approach this tree," he said: It is the karm.

735 - Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Khalid al-Wasiti narrated to us, from Bayan, from al-Sha'bi, from Ja'dah ibn Hubayrah, regarding "and do not approach this tree," he said: the karm.

736 - Ibn Humayd and Ibn Waki' narrated to us, both saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mughirah, from al-Sha'bi, from Ja'dah ibn Hubayrah, who said: The tree that Adam was forbidden is the tree of wine (khamr).

737 - Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad al-Zubayri narrated to us, saying: Abbad ibn al-Awwam narrated to us, saying: Sufyan ibn Husayn narrated to us, from Ya'la ibn Muslim, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, regarding His saying "and do not approach this tree," he said: the karm.

738 - Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-Suddi, who said: the grape (inab).

739 - Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Abu Ma'shar, from Muhammad ibn Qays, who said: grapes ('inab). [[The reports: 730-739 - Mentioned without specification in Ibn Kathir 1: 142, al-Durr al-Manthur 1: 53, and al-Shawkani 1: 56.]]

Others said: It is the fig (tinah).

Those who said that:

740 - Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from one of the companions of the Prophet ﷺ, who said: It is a fig tree (tinah). [[The report: 740 - In Ibn Kathir 1: 143, al-Durr al-Manthur 1: 53, and al-Shawkani 1: 56.]]

Abu Ja'far said: Our view on this matter is that Allah, may His praise be exalted, informed His servants that Adam and his wife ate from the tree which their Lord had forbidden them to eat from. They committed the transgression He had forbidden them from committing by eating what they ate from it, after Allah, may His praise be exalted, had made clear to them the specific tree which He had forbidden them to eat from, and indicated it to them by His saying: "And do not approach this tree." Allah, may His praise be exalted, did not place for His servants addressed in the Qur'an any indication as to which of the trees of the Garden His prohibition to Adam to approach was, neither by explicitly naming it, nor by any clear pointer to it. Had Allah been pleased that His servants know which of these it was, He would not have left them without setting a sign by which they could arrive at knowledge of its identity, so that they might obey Him through their knowledge of it, as He has done in everything in which He is pleased that knowledge be sought.

The correct view on this is to say: God, may His praise be exalted, forbade Adam and his wife from eating from one particular tree among the trees of the Garden, apart from its other trees. They disobeyed what God had forbidden them and ate from it, as God, may His praise be exalted, described them. We have no knowledge of which tree it was specifically, because God did not place for His servants any evidence of that in the Qur'an or in the sound Sunnah. How could that be known? [[The manuscript differs from the printed edition, and this is its text: "ولا علم عندنا بأي ذلك. وقد قيل كانت شجرة البر. . . "، as if the copyist had dropped a line and the sentence became disordered. The printed edition read: "فأنى يأتي ذلك من أتى" with the addition of "من أتى". The error appears to be old, for Ibn Kathir quoted this passage of al-Tabari in his tafsir (1: 143) and dropped the words "فأنى يأتي ذلك". I have concluded that the correct reading omits "من أتى", so that the interrogative bears on how this knowledge of this tree could be obtained, and there is no evidence for it in the Qur'an or the sound Sunnah. As the sentence appears in the printed edition, it is corrupt and defeats what al-Tabari intended.]] It has been said: it was the wheat tree (شجرة البر); it has been said: it was the grape vine; it has been said: it was the fig tree. It is possible that it was one of these, but that is a piece of knowledge which, if it is known, does not benefit the one who knows it, and if it is unknown, the ignorance of the ignorant does not harm him.

* *

Discussion of the words of God, may His remembrance be exalted: ﴿And do not approach this tree, or you will be among the wrongdoers﴾

Abu Ja'far said: The grammarians of the Arabic language (ahl al-'Arabiyya, the scholars of Arabic grammar) differed over the interpretation of His words: "And do not approach this tree, or you will be among the wrongdoers."

Some of the grammarians of Kufa (nahwiyyi al-Kufiyyin) said: The interpretation of that is: "And do not approach this tree, for if you approach it, you will be among the wrongdoers." So the second verb stands in the position of the answer to a conditional. The answer to a conditional is governed by its first part, as when you say: "If you stand, I will stand," where the second is put in the jussive by the jussive of the first. Likewise His words "fatakunā" (so you would be): since the fa' came in the place of the conditional of the first, it was put in the subjunctive by it, and it was made equal in function to "kay" (in order that) in putting future verbs in the subjunctive, because of its necessary association with the future, since the original form of the conditional is the future.

Some of the grammarians of Basra said: The interpretation of that is: "Let there not occur from you approach to this tree, so that you would be among the wrongdoers." However, he claimed that "an" (that) may not be expressed with "la" (not), but that it is necessarily implied, so that the sentence may be correct by conjoining a noun, namely "an", to a noun, just as it is not permitted in their saying "'asā an yafʿala" (it may be that he does), with "'asā" followed by a verb, nor in your saying "mā kāna liyaf'ala" (he was not going to do), with "mā kāna li-an yaf'ala".

This second view is refuted by the consensus of all of them on the incorrectness of a speaker's saying, "Sarrani taqūm yā hādhā" (your standing pleased me, O so-and-so) when he means "Sarrani qiyāmuk" (your standing pleased me), since it is an error to put the verb without "an". So, according to this school, it would also be incorrect to say "lā taqum" (do not stand) when the meaning is "let there be no standing from you". Their consensus on the correctness of "lā taqum" and the incorrectness of "sarrani taqūm" with the meaning "sarrani qiyāmuk" is clear evidence against the claim of the one who asserts that with the "la" in His words "wa lā taqrabā hādhihi al-shajara" there is an implied "an", and in favour of the other view.

As for His words "fatakūnā min al-ẓālimīn" (so you would be among the wrongdoers), there are two interpretations:

The first is that "fatakūnā" is intended as a conjunction with His words "wa lā taqrabā" (and do not approach), so that its interpretation becomes: "And do not approach this tree, and do not be among the wrongdoers." Then "fatakūnā" has the force of a jussive, put in the jussive by what "wa lā taqrabā" is put in the jussive by, as a speaker says: "Do not speak to ʿAmr and do not harm him," and as Imru' al-Qays said:

"I said to him: Guide (the horse) gently, and do not push him hard,
lest he throw you from the rump of the mare and you slide down."

So "fayudrika" (lest he throw you) is put in the jussive by "lā tajhadnahu" (do not push him hard), as though he repeated the prohibition.

[[Dīwān, from the recension of al-Aʿlam al-Shantamarī, poem no. 30, verse 26. It is in Maʿānī al-Qurʾān of al-Farrāʾ (1: 26), and Sībawayh attributed it in al-Kitāb (1: 452) to ʿAmr ibn ʿAmmār al-Ṭāʾī; al-Ṭabarī will mention it later (15: 164, Bulaq edition) without attribution. Sībawayh's version reads "fayadnaka min ukhrā al-qaṭāh" and his phrase "faqultu lahu" refers to his servant, and he mentioned it a few verses earlier. "Ṣawwib" means take the horse at a moderate pace and treat it gently, and do not exhaust it with a severe run, lest it throw you. "Adhrāhu ʿan farasihi" means to cast him down and throw him. "Al-qaṭāh" is the seat at the back of the horse; "ukhrā al-qaṭāh" is the rear of the seat. Al-Shantamarī's version reads "min aʿlā al-qaṭāh" (from the top of the qaṭāh). They have the same meaning.]]

The second is that "fatakūnā min al-ẓālimīn" is in the sense of the answer to the prohibition. Its interpretation then becomes: "Do not approach this tree, for if you approach it you will be among the wrongdoers," as you say, "Do not insult ʿAmr, or he will insult you," by way of reciprocation. In that case "fatakūnā" stands in the accusative position, since it is a conjunction in a form not its own, because in "wa lā taqrabā" there is a governing particle affecting it, and it is not proper to repeat it in "fatakūnā," so it is put in the accusative in the manner I have explained at the beginning of this question.

As for the interpretation of His words "fatakūnā min al-ẓālimīn," He means by it: "so that you would be among those who transgress beyond what was permitted to them and allowed them." He meant by this that if you approach this tree, you would be following the course of those who transgress My limits, disobey My command, and make lawful what I have forbidden, because the wrongdoers are allies of one another, and God is the Protector of the righteous.

The root meaning of "ẓulm" (wrongdoing) in the speech of the Arabs is placing a thing in other than its proper place. From it is the saying of Nābigha of the Banū Dhubyān:

"Except that I cover (the traces) with difficulty, what I make clear of them,
while the ditch, like a pool, is in the hard, wronged ground."

He made the ground "wronged" (maẓlūma), because the one who dug the trench in it dug it in a place not fit for digging, so he made it wronged, because the digging in it was in other than its proper place. [[In the printed edition: "لوضع الحفرة منها في غير موضعها"; and in the manuscript also: "لموضع الحفر فيها في غير موضعها".]] Among this is the verse of Ibn Qumayʾa describing rain:

"The downpour of a cloud that scrapes the earth wronged the valley-beds with it,
so the drops were cleared up after the cloud had passed."

[[It also occurs in his tafsir (2: 50, Bulaq edition) attributed to ʿAmr ibn Qumayʾa. The correct attribution is to al-Ḥādira al-Dhubyānī; it is in the Dīwān of al-Ḥādira, poem no. 4, verse 7, and in the Sharḥ al-Mufaḍḍaliyyāt, p. 54. "Biṭāḥ" is the plural of biṭāḥāʾ and abṭaḥ, meaning the bed of the valley. "Anhalla al-maṭar inhilālan" means the rain intensified in its pouring and impact. "Al-ḥarīṣa" and "al-ḥāriṣa" are the cloud whose rain scrapes the face of the earth, that is, strips it from the force of its impact. "Al-niṭāf" is the plural of nuṭfa, the little water that remains in a bucket or elsewhere. "Baʿīd al-maqlaʿ" means after this cloud had cleared away. In al-Mufaḍḍaliyyāt the reading is "ẓalama al-biṭāḥ lahu," and "lahu" means on account of it.]]

To wrong it (ẓulmuhu iyyāhu) means its coming at other than its time and its pouring in other than its place of pouring. From it: "ẓalama al-rajulu jazūrahu," meaning the man slaughtered his camel for no reason. Among the Arabs that is the placing of the slaughter in other than its proper place.

Wrongdoing branches out into meanings whose enumeration would make the book too long, and we will explain them in their places, if we reach them, God willing. The root of all of that is what we have described: placing a thing in other than its proper place.

**The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted Is He: ﴿Then Satan caused them both to slip from it﴾**

Abu Ja'far said: The readers (*al-qurra'*, the transmitters of the Qur'anic recitations) differed concerning the recitation of this word.[[In the printed edition: "اختلف القراء", "the readers differed." The word "القَرَأة" is the plural of "قارئ", reader. See above: 51 n., and pp. 64, 109 and elsewhere.]] Most of them recited it as "*fa-azallahumā*" with a doubled *lām*, meaning *istazallahumā* (he caused them to slip), from your saying, "*zalla al-rajulu fī dīnihi*," when a man stumbles in his religion, errs in it, and commits what he has no right to commit. And "*azallahu ghayruhu*" means that he caused him to be led into what makes him slip, in his religion or his worldly affairs. For this reason, God, remembered be He, attributed to Iblis the expulsion of Adam and his wife from the Garden, saying: ﴿So he expelled them﴾, meaning Iblis expelled them ﴿from what they were in﴾, because he was the cause of the sin for which God punished them by expelling them from the Garden.

Others recited it as "*fa-azālahumā*," meaning the removal of a thing from another thing, which is moving it away from it.

It has been related from Ibn 'Abbas concerning the interpretation of His words, "*fa-azallahumā*," that:

741 - Al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn 'Abbas said concerning the interpretation of the words of God, exalted is He, "*fa-azallahumā al-shaytān*" (Then Satan caused them both to slip): "He led them astray." [[The report: 741. In al-Durr al-Manthur 1:53, and al-Shawkani 1:56.]]

The more correct of the two recitations is the recitation of the one who recited "*fa-azallahumā*," because God, great is His praise, has informed us in the following phrase that Iblis expelled them from what they were in. That is the meaning of His words "*fa-azālahumā*" (He removed them). Since the meaning of removal is the meaning of moving away and expelling, there is no sense in saying, "*fa-azālahumā al-shaytānu 'anhā fa-akhrajahumā mimmā kānā fīh*" (Satan removed them from it and so expelled them from what they were in), for that would be like saying, "*fa-azālahumā al-shaytānu 'anhā fa-azālahumā mimmā kānā fīh*" (Satan removed them from it and removed them from what they were in). Rather, the meaning that is understood is to say: "*fa-istazallahumā Iblīsu 'an ṭā'ati Allāh*" (Iblis caused them to slip away from obedience to God), as God, great is His praise, said: "*fa-azallahumā al-shaytān*," and as the readers recited it, and so he expelled them from the Garden by causing them to slip.[[In the printed edition: "But the meaning that is understood," with an extra word that adds nothing.]]

If someone says to us: How did Iblis cause Adam and his wife to slip, such that their expulsion from the Garden was attributed to him?

It is said: The scholars have given several opinions on that, and we will mention some of them.

It has been related on the authority of Wahb ibn Munabbih concerning this:

742 - Al-Hasan ibn Yahya related it to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhrib informed us,[[In the printed edition: "'Amr" instead of "'Umar," and in the manuscript and Ibn Kathir: "Mihran" instead of "Muhrib." Both are errors. The correct form is what we have written: "'Umar ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhrib." Ibn Abi Hatim included this shaykh in al-Jarh wa'l-Ta'dil 3/1/121, and said: "He heard Wahb ibn Munabbih; Ibrahim ibn Khalid al-San'ani and 'Abd al-Razzaq related from him." He then related from Yahya ibn Ma'in, who said: "'Umar ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhrib is reliable (thiqah)." I did not find another biography of him. As for "Muhrib," I did not find a text giving its vocalization in this lineage, except the statement of the author of al-Qamus that they named people from the root (h-r-b) in the pattern "Muhsin," meaning with a vowelled first letter, a quiescent second, and a kasra on the third. The name of this shaykh was distorted into two shaykhs in the chain in the History of al-Tabari 1:54, thus: "Ma'mar from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mihran."]] who said: I heard Wahb ibn Munabbih say: When God caused Adam and his descendants (or his wife)[[The doubt is from Abu Ja'far; in the original of his book it reads "wa-dhurriyyatihi," "and his descendants."]] to dwell (in the Garden) and forbade him the tree, which had branches intertwined with one another, and had fruit that the angels ate for eternity, and it was the fruit that God forbade Adam and his wife. When Iblis wanted to cause them to slip, he entered the belly of the serpent. The serpent had four legs like a Bactrian camel, and was the most beautiful creature God created. When the serpent entered the Garden, Iblis came out of its belly, took from the tree that God had forbidden to Adam and his wife, and brought it to Eve, and said: "Look at this tree! How good its fragrance is, how good its taste, and how beautiful its colour!" Eve took it and ate from it, then she went with it to Adam and said: "Look at this tree! How good its fragrance is, how good its taste, and how beautiful its colour!" Adam ate from it, and their private parts became visible to them. Adam then hid in the tree, and his Lord called to him: "O Adam, where are you?" He said: "Here I am, O Lord!"[[In the printed edition: "Here I am, O Lord," which we have corrected to match the manuscript and the History of al-Tabari.]] He said: "Will you not come out?" He said: "I am ashamed before You, O Lord." He said: "Cursed is the earth from which you were created, with a curse that will turn its fruit into thorns." He said: There was no tree in the Garden or on earth better than the acacia (talh) and the lote tree (sidr). Then He said: "O Eve, you are the one who deceived My servant. You will bear a child only in hardship, and whenever you wish to give birth to what is in your womb, you will come close to death many times." He said to the serpent: "You are the one into whose belly the accursed one entered until he deceived My servant. Cursed are you with a curse: your legs will shrink into your belly, you will have no sustenance but dust, you are the enemy of the children of Adam and they are your enemies; wherever you meet one of them you will strike his heel, and wherever he meets you he will crush your head." 'Umar said: It was said to Wahb: "What did the angels eat?" He said: "God does what He wills."[[The report: 742, in the History of al-Tabari 1:54, with this chain, and its beginning in Ibn Kathir 1:143.]]

It has been related from Ibn 'Abbas something similar to this story:

743 - Musa ibn Harun related to me, saying: 'Amr related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi in a report he mentioned, from Abu Malik, and from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas; and from Murra, from Ibn Mas'ud, and from some of the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ): When God, mighty and majestic, said to Adam: "Dwell, you and your wife, in the Garden, and eat from it freely wherever you wish, but do not approach this tree, or you will be among the wrongdoers," Iblis wanted to enter the Garden to them, but the guardians (*al-khazanah*) prevented him. So he came to the serpent, which is a creature with four legs like a camel, and it is the most beautiful of animals. He spoke to it, asking it to let him enter its mouth, so that it could carry him to Adam. It let him enter its jaw (*fuqm*) — Abu Ja'far said: *al-fuqm* is the side of the cheek (*shidq*)[[In the printed edition and the History of al-Tabari 1:53: "it let him enter its mouth, and the serpent passed..." What we have written is from the manuscript.]] — and the serpent passed by the guardians and entered, and they did not know what God intended by the affair. He spoke to him from its jaw, but he did not pay attention to his speech.[[In the printed edition and the History of al-Tabari: "He spoke to him from its mouth," and in the printed edition: "he did not pay attention to his speech."]] He came out to him and said: ﴿O Adam, shall I direct you to the tree of eternity and a kingdom that does not decay?﴾ [Qur'an 20:120], meaning: Shall I direct you to a tree which, if you eat from it, you will become a king like God, mighty and majestic, or you will be among the eternal, so that you will never die. He swore to them both by God: ﴿Indeed, I am to you both among the sincere advisers.﴾ He only intended by this to reveal to them what was hidden from them of their private parts by tearing off their clothing. He had known that they had private parts, because of what he read from the books of the angels, but Adam did not know that. Their clothing was of nail-like (*al-zufr*) material. Adam refused to eat from it, so Eve went forward and ate, then said: "O Adam, eat! I have eaten and it has not harmed me." When Adam ate, their private parts became visible to them, and they began to cover themselves with leaves from the Garden. [[The report: 743. Verbatim in the History of al-Tabari 1:53, and with some variation in al-Durr al-Manthur 1:53, and al-Shawkani 1:56.]]

744 - I was told on the authority of 'Ammar ibn al-Hasan, who said: Ibn Abi Ja'far related to us, from his father, from al-Rabi', who said: A narrator related to me that Satan entered the Garden in the form of a creature with legs, so it appeared that he was a camel. He said: Then he was cursed, his legs fell off, and he became a serpent. [[The report: 744, in the History of al-Tabari 1:55.]]

745 - And I was told on the authority of 'Ammar, who said: Ibn Abi Ja'far related to us, from his father, from al-Rabi', who said: Abu al-'Aliyah related to me that among the camels there is one whose origin was from the jinn. He said: So the whole Garden was made lawful to him, except the tree, and it was said to them both: "Do not approach this tree, or you will be among the wrongdoers." He said: Satan came to Eve and began with her, and said: "Have you been forbidden anything?" She said: "Yes, from this tree." He said: ﴿Your Lord has forbidden you from this tree only lest you become angels or become among the eternal﴾ [Qur'an 7:20]. He said: Eve began and ate from it, then she commanded Adam, and he ate from it. He said: It was a tree whoever ate from it would have his excrement emitted (*ahdatha*), and it is not fitting for there to be excrement in the Garden. He said: ﴿So Satan caused them both to slip from it and removed them from what they were in﴾ [[In the History of al-Tabari 1:55: "So Satan caused them both to slip."]]. He said: So Adam was expelled from the Garden. [[The report: 745, in the History of al-Tabari 1:55.]]

746 - Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salamah related to us, saying: Ibn Ishaq related to us, from some of the people of knowledge: When Adam entered the Garden and saw what was in it of honour and what God had given him from it, he said: "If only eternity were ours!" Satan seized upon this (*fa-ightamazahā*) when he heard it from him,[[In the History: "If only we were made eternal." In the printed edition: "Satan seized it from him," which they misread from the manuscript and so changed the word; we have written what is in the manuscript and the History. One says: "He heard a word from me and *ightamazahā*," meaning he found it weak and found in it an opening (*maghmaz*) through which it could be attacked from its side.]] and came to him through the matter of eternity. [[The report: 746, in the History of al-Tabari 1:55.]]

747 - Ibn Humayd also related to us, saying: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: I was told that the first thing with which he began his scheming against them both was that he wailed over them with a wailing that saddened them when they heard it. They said: "Why are you weeping?" He said: "I weep for you both: you will die and be separated from the blessing and honour in which you are." That fell into their hearts. Then he came to them and whispered to them, saying: "O Adam, shall I direct you to the tree of eternity and a kingdom that does not decay?" And he said: ﴿Your Lord has forbidden you from this tree only lest you become angels or become among the eternal﴾, and he swore to them: ﴿Indeed, I am to you both among the sincere advisers.﴾ That is, "that you become angels, or that you live forever, if you are not angels, in the blessing of the Garden, so that you will not die." God, exalted is He, says: ﴿So he brought them down by deception﴾. [[The report: 747, in the History of al-Tabari 1:55.]]

748 - Yunus ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: Satan whispered to Eve about the tree until he brought it to her, then made it attractive to Adam's eye. He said: Adam called her for his need, and she said: "No! Unless you come here." When he came, she said: "No! Unless you eat from this tree." He said: So they both ate from it, and their private parts became visible to them. He said: Adam fled in the Garden, and his Lord called to him: "O Adam, are you fleeing from Me?" He said: "No, O Lord, but out of shame before You." He said: "O Adam, from where did you come?" He said: "From the side of Eve, O Lord." God said: "As for her, I will make her bleed every month, as this tree was made to bleed, and I will make her foolish, though I had created her gentle; and I will make her carry in hardship and give birth in hardship, though I had made her carry with ease and give birth with ease." Ibn Zayd said: Had it not been for the trial that befell Eve, the women of this world would not menstruate, and they would be gentle, and they would carry with ease and give birth with ease. [[The report: 748, in the History of al-Tabari 1:55.]]

749 - Ibn Humayd also related to us, saying: Salamah related to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from Yazid ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Qusayt, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, who said: I heard him swear by God, without making an exception, that Adam did not eat from the tree while he was in his right mind; rather, Eve gave him wine to drink, until when he became drunk she led him to it, and he ate. [[The report: 749, in the History of al-Tabari 1:55–56, where it is complete.]]

750 - Ibn Humayd also related to us, saying: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from Layth ibn Abi Sulaym, from Tawus al-Yamani, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The enemy of God, Iblis, offered himself to the beasts of the earth, asking which of them would carry him so that he could enter the Garden with it and speak to Adam and his wife.[[In the manuscript, the printed edition and al-Durr al-Manthur: "that it would carry him until he entered...". We have written what is in the History of al-Tabari 1:54, as it is better and more correct.]] All the beasts refused him, until he spoke to the serpent and said to it: "I will protect you from the son of Adam; you will be under my protection if you let me enter the Garden." So it placed him between two of its fangs, then entered with him, and he spoke to them from its mouth. It had been clothed and walked on four legs, so God stripped it and made it walk on its belly. He said: Ibn 'Abbas said: "Kill it wherever you find it; you have violated the protection of the enemy of God concerning it." [[The report: 750, in the History of al-Tabari 1:53–54, and al-Durr al-Manthur 1:53. *Akhfara* the protection and the covenant means: to break them and not keep them.]]

751 - Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salamah related to us, saying: Ibn Ishaq said: The People of the Torah study that it was only the serpent that spoke to Adam, and they did not explain it as Ibn 'Abbas did.

752 - Al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Abu Ma'shar, from Muhammad ibn Qays, who said: God forbade Adam and Eve to eat from one tree in the Garden, and to eat from it freely wherever they wished. Satan came and entered the belly of the serpent, and spoke to Eve, and Satan whispered to Adam, saying: ﴿Your Lord has forbidden you from this tree only lest you become angels or become among the eternal,﴾ and he swore to them: ﴿Indeed, I am to you both among the sincere advisers.﴾ He said: Eve cut (*faqa'at*) the tree, and the tree bled.[[In the printed edition: "Eve bit the tree," and we have written what is in the manuscript and the History of al-Tabari 1:54.]] Their garments of finery (*riyash*) that had been on them fell off, and they began to cover themselves with leaves from the Garden. Their Lord called to them: ﴿Did I not forbid you from that tree, and tell you that Satan is to you a clear enemy?﴾ [Qur'an 7:22]. "Why did you eat it when I had forbidden you from it?" He said: "O Lord, Eve gave me food." He said to Eve: "Why did you give him food?" She said: "The serpent commanded me." He said to the serpent: "Why did you command her?" It said: "Iblis commanded me." He said: "Cursed and expelled! As for you, O Eve, just as you made the tree bleed, you will bleed every month. As for you, O serpent, I will cut off your legs, so you will walk crawling on your face, and whoever meets you will crush your head with a stone. Go down, some of you to others, as enemies." [[The report: 752, in the History of al-Tabari 1:54.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: These reports have been transmitted, from those from whom we have related them, from the Companions, the Successors and others, describing how the enemy of God, Iblis, caused Adam and his wife to slip until he expelled them from the Garden.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 36 (part 2 of 3):

The view most worthy of acceptance in our opinion is the one that agrees with the Book of God. God, may His remembrance be exalted, has informed us about Iblis (Satan) that he whispered to Adam and his wife in order to reveal to them what had been concealed from them of their private parts, and that he said to them: ﴿Your Lord has forbidden you this tree only lest you become angels or become of the immortal.﴾ And that he ﴿swore to them, "Indeed, I am to you of the sincere advisors."﴾ He led them on with deception. In God's report, may His praise be exalted, about the enemy of God that he swore to Adam and his wife by his saying to them, "Indeed, I am to you of the sincere advisors," there is clear evidence that he addressed them directly himself, either openly before their eyes or hidden within something else. This is because it is not understood in the speech of the Arabs to say, "So-and-so swore to so-and-so about such-and-such," when he merely caused a means to reach him without swearing to him. Swearing cannot occur through causing a cause. Likewise His saying, ﴿So Satan whispered to him﴾: had it been that his whispering to Adam was of the same kind as his whispering to Adam's descendants, namely adorning for him the eating of what God had forbidden Adam from eating from the tree, without directly addressing him with the enticements and tricks by which he made him slip, then He, may His praise be exalted, would not have said, ﴿And he swore to them, "Indeed, I am to you of the sincere advisors."﴾ Just as it is impermissible for someone today who has committed a sin to say, "Iblis swore to me that he is sincere to me regarding the sin he adorned for me, which I committed." Similarly, what occurred between Adam and his wife, had it been in the manner that occurs between Iblis today and the descendants of Adam, He, may His praise be exalted, would not have said, ﴿And he swore to them, "Indeed, I am to you of the sincere advisors."﴾ Rather, that occurred, God willing, in the manner that Ibn Abbas and those who share his view have stated.

As for the means by which he reached Paradise so that he spoke to Adam after God had expelled him from it and banished him from it, there is nothing in what has been related from Ibn Abbas and Wahb ibn Munabbih on this matter that contains a meaning which a person of understanding may reject, since it is a statement that no reason repels and no report that must be accepted refutes with proof to the contrary[[In the printed edition: "since that is a statement that no statement repels."]], and it is among the possible matters. The position on this is that he reached their address in the manner God, may His praise be exalted, has informed us[[In the printed edition: "And the position on this..."]]. It is also possible that he reached that by means similar to what the interpreters have said. Indeed, that is, God willing, so, because the sayings of the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) agree on confirming it. Although Ibn Ishaq has said on this matter what follows:

753 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, saying: Ibn Ishaq said regarding this, and God knows best, as Ibn Abbas and the People of the Torah said: He reached Adam and his wife with his authority that God gave him to test Adam and his descendants, and he comes to the son of Adam in his sleep and in his waking, and in every one of his states, until he reaches what he wants from him, until he calls him to disobedience and places desire in his soul while he does not see him. God, mighty and majestic, has said: ﴿So Satan caused them to slip from it and removed them from that in which they had been.﴾[[In the printed edition and manuscript: "And God has said: So Satan whispered to them and removed them from what they were in," which is not a verse; the correct reading is that he meant the verse of Surah al-Baqara here.]] He said: (O children of Adam, let not Satan tempt you as he removed your parents from Paradise, stripping from them their clothing to show them their private parts. Indeed, he sees you, he and his tribe, from where you do not see them. Indeed, We have made the devils allies for those who do not believe.) [Surah al-A'raf: 27]. And God said to His Prophet, peace be upon him: ﴿Say, "I seek refuge in the Lord of mankind, the King of mankind"﴾ to the end of the surah. Then he mentioned the reports narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Indeed, Satan flows through the son of Adam as blood flows."[[The hadith "Indeed, Satan flows through the son of Adam as blood flows" is very sound. It was related by Ahmad, the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim), and Abu Dawud, from the hadith of Anas; and it was related by the two Shaykhs, Abu Dawud and Ibn Majah, from the hadith of Safiyya, daughter of Huyayy, Mother of the Believers, as in al-Jami' al-Saghir: 2036.]] Then Ibn Ishaq said[[In the printed edition, "then" is omitted.]]: The matter of the son of Adam between himself and the enemy of God is like his matter between himself and Adam. God said: ﴿So descend from it, for it is not for you to be arrogant therein. So get out; indeed, you are of the humiliated.﴾ [Surah al-A'raf: 13]. Then he reached Adam and his wife until he spoke to them, as God has recounted to us of their story, saying: ﴿Then Satan whispered to him, saying, "O Adam, shall I direct you to the tree of eternity and a kingdom that does not decay?"﴾ [Surah Ta-Ha: 120]. So he reached them with what he reached his descendants with, from where they could not see him. God knows best which of these was the case. So they repented to their Lord.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: Neither in Ibn Ishaq's certainty, even if he had been certain within himself, that Iblis did not reach Adam and his wife by addressing them with what God informed us He said to them and addressed them with, is there anything that a person of understanding may object to, contrary to what has come as widely transmitted speech from the people of knowledge, along with the Book's indication of the soundness of what is widely transmitted among them. How then can there be doubt? And from God we seek success.

* *

On the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So He caused them to slip from it and removed them from that in which they had been﴾

Abu Ja'far said: As for the interpretation of His saying, "So He removed them," it means: Satan removed Adam and his wife, "from that in which they had been," meaning from the ease of life in Paradise and the breadth of its bliss in which they had been. We have already explained that God, may His praise be exalted, attributed their removal from Paradise to Satan, though God is the one who removed them, because their departure from it was due to a cause from Satan. So that was attributed to him because of his causing it, just as a person says to a man from whom harm reached him until he was moved from a place he used to live in on account of it: "You alone moved me from the place I was in," although the other did not actually move him, but because his moving was caused by him, it is permissible to attribute his moving to him.

* *

On the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We said, "Descend, some of you to others an enemy."﴾

Abu Ja'far said: It is said, "So-and-so descended the land of such-and-such and the valley of such-and-such," when he settled in that place[[The likely correct wording is: "when he settled in that place," as a word was dropped by the copyists.]], as the poet said:

"I kept watching them until, when the hands of the riding-camels brought them down from Rakis, Falaq" [[The verse is by Zuhayr ibn Abi Sulma, his Diwan: 37. "Armuquhum" means: I look at them, meaning his departing beloved ones, watching them sorrowful and grief-stricken. "Rikab": the camels ridden upon. "Rakis": a valley in the lands of Banu Sa'd ibn Tha'laba, of Banu Asad. "Falaq" and "Falq": the level ground between two mounds, or two mountains, or two hills; they said "Faliq" and "Falq," as they said "Yabis" and "Yabs" (with two fatha vowels).]].

This statement from God, may His praise be exalted, has made clear the soundness of what we have said: that the one who removed Adam from Paradise is God, may His praise be exalted, and that God's attribution of their removal to Iblis was as we have described. It also indicates that the descent of Adam and his wife and their enemy Iblis occurred at one time, by God's gathering them together in the report of their descent after the sin of Adam and his wife, and Iblis's causing that for them, as His Lord, mentioned, may His remembrance be exalted, described them.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The interpreters have differed about who is meant by His saying "descend," although they agree that Adam and his wife are among those intended.

754 - Sufyan ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Abu Usama narrated to us, from Abu Awana, from Isma'il ibn Salim, from Abu Salih: "Descend, some of you to others an enemy." He said: Adam, Eve, Iblis, and the serpent. [[The report: 754 - in al-Durr al-Manthur 1: 55.]]

755 - Ibn Waki' and Musa ibn Harun narrated to us, both saying: 'Amr ibn Hammad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "Descend, some of you to others an enemy." He said: He cursed the serpent, cut off its legs, and left it to walk on its belly, and made its sustenance from dirt. And Adam, Eve, Iblis, and the serpent were sent down to the earth. [[The report: 755 - in Tarikh al-Tabari 1: 56. It appears that a chain was dropped here; its completion in the History reads: "...from al-Suddi, in a report he mentioned from Abu Malik, and from Abu Salih, from Ibn Abbas, and from Murra al-Hamdani, from Ibn Mas'ud, and from some companions of the Messenger of God (ﷺ): 'Descend...'" This is the chain by which al-Tabari often narrates.]]

756 - Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa ibn Maymun narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding God's saying: "Descend, some of you to others an enemy": Adam, Iblis, and the serpent. [[The report: 756 - in Tarikh al-Tabari 1: 56.]]

757 - al-Muthanna ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "Descend, some of you to others an enemy": Adam, Iblis, and the serpent, descendants some of whom are enemies to others.

758 - al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid: "some of you to others an enemy": Adam and his descendants, and Iblis and his descendants.

759 - al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Adam ibn Abi Iyas narrated to us, saying: Abu Ja'far narrated to us, from al-Rabi', from Abu al-Aliya regarding His saying: "some of you to others an enemy," he said: He means Iblis and Adam. [[The reports 757-759: I have not found them with their chains elsewhere.]]

760 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: 'Ubayd Allah ibn Musa narrated to us, from Isra'il, from al-Suddi, from one who narrated to him from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: "Descend, some of you to others an enemy," he said: Some of them to others an enemy: Adam, Eve, Iblis, and the serpent. [[The report: 760 - like the one following it, from another route.]]

761 - Yunus ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to me, from Isra'il, from Isma'il al-Suddi, who said: One who heard Ibn Abbas say narrated to me: "Descend, some of you to others an enemy," he said: Adam, Eve, Iblis, and the serpent. [[The report: 761 - in Tarikh al-Tabari 1: 56.]]

762 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying: "Descend, some of you to others an enemy," he said: For them and their descendants. [[The report: 762 - I have not found it elsewhere.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: If someone asks: What was the enmity between Adam and his wife, Iblis, and the serpent? It is said: As for Iblis's enmity toward Adam and his descendants, it is his envy of him and his arrogance in refusing to obey God by prostrating to him, when he said to his Lord: ﴿I am better than him; You created me from fire and created him from clay.﴾ [Surah Sad: 76]. As for the enmity of Adam and his descendants toward Iblis, it is the enmity of the believers toward him because of his disbelief in God and his disobedience to his Lord in his arrogance toward Him and his opposition to His command. This, from Adam and the believing among his descendants, is faith in God. And Iblis's enmity toward Adam is disbelief in God.

As for the enmity between Adam and his descendants and the serpent, we have mentioned what has been related on this from Ibn Abbas and Wahb ibn Munabbih, and that is the enmity between us and it, as has been related from the Messenger of God (ﷺ) that he said: "We have not made peace with them since we went to war with them. Whoever leaves them out of fear of their vengeance is not of us."

763 - Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Hakam narrated to me, saying: Hajjaj ibn Rishdin narrated to me, saying: Haywa ibn Shurayh narrated to us, from Ibn 'Ajlan, from his father, from Abu Hurayra, from the Messenger of God (ﷺ) that he said: "We have not made peace with them since we went to war with them. Whoever leaves any of them out of fear, is not of us." [[The hadith: 763 - its chain is good. The hadith is related through other sound chains, as we shall mention, God willing. Hajjaj: he is Ibn Rishdin ibn Sa'd al-Misri. Ibn Abi Hatim included him in al-Jarh wa'l-Ta'dil 1/2/160, and mentioned that he narrates from "Haywa ibn Shurayh" and that "Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Hakam" narrates from him. He mentioned that he asked Abu Zur'a about him, and he said: "I have no knowledge of him; I did not write from anyone who narrated from him." The Hafiz included him in Lisan al-Mizan and reported that Ibn 'Adi declared him weak, that he died in the year 211, that Ibn Yunus mentioned no criticism of him, and "al-Khalili said: he is more reliable than his father; Maslama ibn Qasim said: there is nothing wrong with him," and that Ibn Hibban mentioned him among the trustworthy. This suffices as his authentication, especially since Ibn Yunus knew best the history of the Egyptians.
His father's name is "Rishdin," with a kasra on the ra and a dal between them, with an unpointed sukun shin, and after the dal a ya and a nun. In the printed edition it appears as "Rushd," which is an error.
The hadith was related by Ahmad in al-Musnad: 9586, from Yahya (al-Qattan), and 10752, from Safwan (ibn 'Isa al-Zuhri), both from Ibn 'Ajlan with it (2: 432, 520 of the Halabi edition). He also related it earlier in abridged form: 7360 (2: 247), from Sufyan ibn 'Uyayna. Abu Dawud related it: 5248 (4: 534 'Awn al-Ma'bud), through Sufyan, in full. These are sound chains.
Its meaning is also transmitted from the hadith of Ibn Abbas, in al-Musnad also: 2037, 3254. And something close in meaning from the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud, in al-Musnad also: 3984.]]

Abu Ja'far said: I think that the war between us had its origin in what our scholars, whose reports we have already cited, mentioned about Iblis's entering Paradise after God had removed him from it, until he made him slip from obedience to his Lord by eating what he had been forbidden to eat from the tree.

764 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya ibn Hisham narrated to us, and Muhammad ibn Khalaf al-'Asqalani narrated to me, saying: Adam narrated to me, all from Shaybān, from Jabir, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) was asked about killing snakes, and the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "They and humankind were created, each of them an enemy to the other. If it sees him, it frightens him, and if it bites him, it hurts him. So kill it wherever you find it." [[The hadith: 764 - in al-Durr al-Manthur 1: 55, attributed to al-Tabari only. It is in Majma' al-Zawa'id 4: 45 with a different wording, and he said: al-Tabarani related it in al-Awsat, and in it Jabir is unnamed; the apparent one is al-Ju'fi, whom al-Thawri and Shu'ba considered reliable, while the imams including Ahmad and others declared him weak.]]

* *

On the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And for you on the earth is a dwelling place﴾

Abu Ja'far said: The interpreters differed on the interpretation of this. Some of them said:

765 - al-Muthanna ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Adam al-'Asqalani narrated to us, saying: Abu Ja'far al-Razi narrated to us, from al-Rabi', from Abu al-Aliya regarding His saying: "And for you on the earth is a dwelling place," he said: It is His saying: ﴿He who made the earth for you a bed﴾ [Surah al-Baqara: 22].

766 - It was narrated to me from 'Ammar ibn al-Hasan, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi' regarding His saying: "And for you on the earth is a dwelling place," he said: It is His saying: ﴿He made the earth a resting place for you﴾ [Surah Ghafir: 64]. [[The two reports 765-766: I have not found them elsewhere.]]

Others said: The meaning is: "And for you on the earth is a resting place in the graves."

Mention of those who said this:

767 - Musa ibn Harun narrated to me, saying: 'Amr ibn Hammad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "And for you on the earth is a dwelling place," meaning the graves. [[The report: 767 - I have not found it elsewhere.]]

768 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to me, from Isra'il, from Isma'il al-Suddi, who said: One who heard Ibn Abbas narrated to me, saying: "And for you on the earth is a dwelling place," he said: The graves. [[The report: 768 - in al-Durr al-Manthur 1: 55; it is the continuation of report 761.]]

769 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: "And for you on the earth is a dwelling place," he said: Their station therein. [[The report: 769 - I have not found it elsewhere.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: In the Arabic language, "mustaqarr" is the place of settling. Since that is so, wherever those on the earth are present at the moment, that place on the earth is their dwelling.

God, may His praise be exalted, only meant by that: that for them on the earth is a dwelling place and an abode, corresponding to their places of residence and dwelling in Paradise and the heavens. Likewise His saying, "and enjoyment," means that for them therein is enjoyment, in accordance with their enjoyment in Paradise.

* *

On the interpretation of His saying, may His remembrance be exalted: ﴿And enjoyment for a time﴾ (36)

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 36 (part 3 of 3):

Abu Ja'far said: The exegetes (ahl al-ta'wil) differed in their interpretation of this. Some of them said: "And for you therein is a provision (balagh) until death."

Those who said this:

770 - Musa ibn Harun related to me, saying: Amr ibn Hammad related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His words: "And a provision for a time," he said: it means a provision until death. [Report 770: I have not found it elsewhere.]

771 - Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi related to us, from Isra'il, from Isma'il al-Suddi, who said: One who heard Ibn Abbas related to me: "And a provision for a time," he said: it is life. [Report 771: In al-Durr al-manthur 1:55; it is part of the two reports 761 and 768.]

* *

Others said: By His words "and a provision for a time" He means until the Hour rises.

Those who said this:

772 - Al-Muthanna ibn Ibrahim related to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa related to us, saying: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "And a provision for a time," he said: until the Day of Resurrection, until the cessation of this world.

* *

Others said: "For a time" means until a term (ajal).

Those who said this:

773 - I was told by Amar ibn al-Hasan, saying: Abd Allah ibn Abi Ja'far related to us, from his father, from al-Rabi': "And a provision for a time," he said: until a term. [Reports 772 and 773: I have not found them elsewhere.]

* *

Provision (mata') in the Arabic language is everything that one enjoys of a thing: of livelihood enjoyed, or clothing (riyash), or adornment, or pleasure, or other than that. [In the manuscript: "in livelihood enjoyed..."] Given that this is so, and given that God, may His praise be exalted, has made the life of every living being a provision for it, to enjoy during the days of its life; and has made the earth a provision for man during the days of his life, by his dwelling upon it, his nourishment from what God has brought forth from it of sustenance and fruits, and his delight in the pleasures He has created in it; and has made it, after his death, a receptacle (kifat) for his corpse [Kifat: the place in which a thing is gathered and held], and a dwelling and resting place for his body; and since the term "provision" encompasses all of that, the most correct interpretation of the verse is [In the printed edition: "if God..." which is an error] that, since God, may His praise be exalted, has not placed any indication showing that by His words "and a provision for a time" He intended some part rather than another, or a specific rather than a general sense, neither by reason nor by report, then it is required that it carry the general meaning, and that the report be likewise, until a time when the enjoyment of the children of Adam and the children of Iblis of it will last, and that is until the earth is replaced by another earth. Since this is the most correct interpretation of the verse for the reasons we have described, it is necessary that the interpretation of the verse be: "And for you on the earth are dwellings and homes where you settle, as you settle [was] in the heavens and in the Gardens, in your dwellings therein; and enjoyment from you of it and of what it has brought forth for you, and of what I have made for you in it of livelihood, clothing, adornment and pleasures, and of what I have given you upon its surface during the days of your life and after your death, for your graves (armas) and tombs (ajdath) in which you are buried [Armas is the plural of rams, and ajdath the plural of jadath (both vowels open): both mean grave]; and you will reach, through your enjoyment of it, the point at which I replace it with something else."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 37:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then Adam received from his Lord words﴾
