For they interpreted the words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿and they spare your women﴾ as meaning that they keep the female children alive at birth and do not kill them.

Ibn Juraij denied this from their saying, and said:
898 - al-Qasim ibn al-Hasan narrated this to us, saying: al-Husayn ibn Dawud narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, regarding His words ﴿and they spare your women﴾: he said: they enslave your women.

Ibn Juraij, by this saying, deviated from what those we have mentioned said regarding His words ﴿and they spare your women﴾: that it means sparing the young girl children, since he did not find that the name "women" applied to them; then he fell into something greater than what he denied by his interpretation of "they spare", as enslaving. That interpretation does not exist in Arabic or in any non-Arabic language. For istihya' (sparing) is an ist'fa'al form from hayah (life), like istibqa' from baqa' and istisqa' from saqy. It has nothing to do with the meaning of enslavement.

* *

Others have interpreted His words ﴿they slaughter your sons﴾ as meaning they slaughter your men, the fathers of your sons, and they denied that the slaughtered were children, since women are mentioned alongside them. They said: In Allah's, mighty is His praise, report that those who spare are the women, there is clear evidence that those who slaughter are the men and not the boys; for if the slaughtered were the children, then the spared would have to be the young girls. They said: And in Allah's, Mighty and Majestic, report that they are the women, there is clear evidence that the slaughtered are men.

Abu Ja'far said: Those who make this statement have, in addition to departing from the interpretation of the Companions and the Successors, missed the correct point. For Allah, mighty is His praise, has reported of His revelation to the mother of Musa that He commanded her to suckle Musa, and when she feared for him she should place him in the chest and then cast him into the river. It is thus known that if the people were only killing men and leaving women, the mother of Musa would have had no need to cast Musa into the river; or if Musa had been a man, his mother would not have placed him in the chest.

Rather, this, in our view, is according to what Ibn 'Abbas interpreted, and those whose saying we have related before: that the people of Pharaoh slaughtered the boys and left the girls alive from killing. It was said: ﴿and they spare your women﴾ because the young girls were included with their mothers, and their mothers are undoubtedly women in the matter of sparing, since they did not kill small women nor big ones. So it was said: ﴿and they spare your women﴾, meaning by that the mothers and the newborn girls, just as one says "the men have come" though there are boys among them. So likewise His words: ﴿and they spare your women﴾. As for the males, since only those newly born were slaughtered, it was said: "they slaughter your sons", and it was not said: "they slaughter your men".

* *

Concerning the interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿And in that was a great trial from your Lord﴾ [al-Baqarah: 49].

As for His words ﴿And in that was a great trial from your Lord﴾, it means: and in what We did to you by saving you - from what you were in of the torment of the people of Pharaoh upon you, as I have described - was a great trial for you from your Lord.

And by "trial" (bala') is meant a blessing, as:
899 - Al-Muthanna ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah ibn Salih narrated to me, from Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿a great trial from your Lord﴾, he said: a blessing.

900 - Musa ibn Harun narrated to me, saying: 'Amr ibn Hammad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi regarding His words: ﴿And in that was a great trial from your Lord﴾: as for "trial", it is a blessing.

901 - Sufyan narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to me, from Sufyan, from a man, from Mujahid: ﴿And in that was a great trial from your Lord﴾, he said: a great blessing from your Lord.

902 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, similar to the narration of Sufyan.

903 - al-Qasim narrated to me, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij: ﴿And in that was a great trial from your Lord﴾, he said: a great blessing. [[Narration 903: placed before the preceding one in the manuscript.]]

* *

The root meaning of "bala'" in the speech of the Arabs is testing and examination, and then it is used for both good and evil. For testing and examination may be by good as well as by evil, as our Lord, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿And We tested them with good things and bad that they might return﴾ [al-A'raf: 168], meaning: We tested them; and as His, dhikruhu Mighty, said: ﴿And We test you with evil and with good as a trial﴾ [al-Anbiya': 35]. Then the Arabs call good "bala'" and evil "bala'". However, the more common usage for evil is "balawtuhu abluhu bala'", and for good: "abliytuhu ublihi iblaa' and bala'", and from this is the saying of Zuhayr ibn Abi Sulma:

May Allah reward with goodness what the two did for you... and tested them [with] the best testing which tests [...]
[[His Diwan: 109, and its reading is "ra'a Allah... fa-ablahuma". This verse is from a poem of fine and pure poetry by Zuhayr.]]

So he combined the two usages, for he meant: then Allah bestowed upon them the best of the blessings by which He tests His servants.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 50 (part 1 of 2):

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿And when We parted the sea for you﴾

As for the interpretation of His saying, ﴿And when We parted [faraqna] the sea for you﴾, it is linked by conjunction to ﴿And when We delivered you﴾, meaning: remember My favor which I bestowed upon you; remember when We delivered you from the people of Pharaoh, and when We parted the sea for you.

The meaning of His saying ﴿faraqna bikum﴾ is: We divided the sea for you. For they were twelve tribes, and the sea was split into twelve paths, and each tribe took one of these paths. This is what is meant by God, mighty and majestic, parting the sea with them and dividing it through them, by their being spread across its twelve paths, as related:

904. Musa ibn Harun related to me, saying: 'Amr ibn Hammad related to us, saying: Asbat ibn Nasr related to us, from al-Suddi: When Musa came to the sea, he gave it the kunya "Abu Khalid," and struck it, and it split, and each part was like a great mountain, and the children of Israel entered. In the sea there were twelve paths, and in each path a tribe. [Note: This report is from a long account in Tarikh al-Tabari; this paragraph from it is at 1:214; see also no. 910.]

* *

Some grammarians of Basra said: the meaning of His saying ﴿And when We parted the sea for you﴾ is: We separated you from the water. He means by this: We divided between you and it, and held it back where you passed by it. But that contradicts the apparent wording of the recitation [Note: see the tafsir of "the apparent" above: 2:15, and the references], because God, may His praise be exalted, only informed that He parted the sea with the people, and did not inform that He parted between the people and the sea; so the interpretation is not what the sayers of this view said. Rather, His parting of the sea with the people is His dividing the sea with them, according to what we have described of its paths being split by them, as the reports have transmitted.

* *

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿Then We delivered you and drowned the people of Pharaoh while you were watching﴾ (50)

Abu Ja'far said: If someone asks us, "How did God, may His praise be exalted, drown the people of Pharaoh and deliver the children of Israel?"
It is said to him, as follows:

905. Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, from Abdullah ibn Shaddad ibn al-Had, who said: It has been mentioned to me that Pharaoh set out in pursuit of Musa with seventy thousand of dark-colored horses, besides the grey-spotted horses in his army. [Note: In the manuscript and printed edition: "min shiyat al-khayl"; shiyat al-faras means its color, so it would have been better to say "min shiyat al-khayl." In Tarikh: "min shuhub al-khayl," as we have recorded. Shuhb is the plural of ashhab, and shuhba in horse colors means that a few white hairs streak the main color, whether the horse is bay, chestnut, or black.]

And Musa set out, until the sea confronted him and he had no way to turn, and Pharaoh appeared with his army behind them. ﴿When the two hosts saw one another, the companions of Musa said, "We are surely overtaken." He said﴾ — Musa — ﴿"No! Indeed my Lord is with me; He will guide me."﴾ [Surah al-Shu'ara: 61-62], meaning to safety, and He had promised me that, and there is no breaking of His promise. [Note: The report 905 is in Tarikh al-Tabari 1:217, where it reads "wa la khalf li-mawu'udihi." Al-mawud, like al-wa'd, is among the verbal nouns that came in the form of maf'ul.]

906. Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salamah related to us, saying: Ibn Ishaq related to me, saying: God revealed to the sea — so it was mentioned to me: "When Musa strikes you with his staff, split for him." He said: So the sea began to strike itself, part against part, out of fear of God and awaiting His command. [Note: In the printed edition: "fa-thaba al-bahr," which is a misreading; the correct form is in the manuscript and Tarikh. In the printed edition: "wa-intizar amrihi," and in Tarikh "wa-intizaran li-amrihi"; I have adopted what is in the manuscript, which is good.] Then God, mighty and majestic, revealed to Musa: Strike the sea with your staff. He struck it with it, and in it was the authority of God which He had given him, and it split, and each part was like a great mountain, that is, like a mountain upon a rise of land. [Note: In the printed edition: "upon dryness of the land," but I have adopted what is in the manuscript and Tarikh. Al-nashz is the raised ground, or what rises from the valley up to the land, and is not thick.] God says to Musa: ﴿So strike for them a dry path in the sea, not fearing being overtaken, nor fearing﴾ [Ta-Ha: 77]. So when the sea became firm for him in a straight, dry path, Musa led the children of Israel along it, and Pharaoh followed him with his armies. [Note: Report 906 is in Tarikh al-Tabari 1:217.]

907. Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salamah related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq related to me, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, from Abdullah ibn Shaddad ibn al-Had al-Laythi, who said: It was related to me that when the children of Israel had entered the sea, and not one of them remained, Pharaoh came forward on a stallion of his, until he stood at the edge of the sea, while still in that state, and the stallion feared to go forward. [Note: So it is in the manuscript and printed edition, "an yanfudh," while in Tarikh it is "an yataqaddam," which is probably the correct reading; the other is an error, the final mim having dropped off.] Then Gabriel appeared to him on a female mare in heat, [Note: A mare in heat (wadiq) is one that desires the stallion.] and brought her near to him, and the stallion smelled her, and when he smelled her, he pressed forward, [Note: In the printed edition: "fa-lamma shammaha tab'aha," which is an error and confusion. The correct reading is in the manuscript and Tarikh. His words "qaddamaha" mean he urged her on, by their saying to the mare "aqdim," meaning go forward ahead.] and the stallion with Pharaoh on it advanced after her. When the army of Pharaoh saw that Pharaoh had entered, they entered after him, with Gabriel in front of them, while they followed Pharaoh, and Michael on a mare behind the people, driving them and saying: "Join your companion!" Until, when Gabriel came out of the sea with no one in front of him, and Michael stood at its other side, with no one behind him, the sea closed over them. Pharaoh cried out, when he saw the power and might of God, mighty and majestic, which he saw, and knew his humiliation, and his own self forsook him [Note: in the printed edition alone: "dhillatahu"]: ﴿"There is no god except He in whom the children of Israel believe, and I am among the Muslims."﴾ [Yunus: 90]. [Note: Report 907 is in Tarikh al-Tabari 1:217. In the printed edition: "amantu annahu la ilaha illa alladhi. . . ," and in Tarikh: "nada an la ilaha illa alladhi. . . ," and I have adopted what is in the manuscript.]

908. al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Abu Ishaq al-Hamdani, from Amr ibn Maymun al-Awdi, concerning His saying: ﴿And when We parted the sea for you, and delivered you, and drowned the people of Pharaoh while you were watching﴾, he said: When Musa set out with the children of Israel, news of that reached Pharaoh, and he said: Do not follow them until the rooster crows. He said: By God, that night no rooster crowed until they were in the morning. Then he called for a sheep, which was slaughtered, and then he said: I will not finish with its liver until six hundred thousand of the Copts gather to me. So he had not finished with its liver when six hundred thousand of the Copts had gathered to him. Then he set out, and when he reached Musa at the sea, a man among his companions called Yusha ibn Nun said to him: Where has your Lord commanded you, O Musa? He said: Before you — pointing to the sea. Yusha urged his horse into the sea until it reached the deep water, and it carried him off, then he returned. [Note: In Ibn Kathir 1:165: "fa-dhahaba bihi al-ghamr, thumma raja'a."] He said: Where has your Lord commanded you, O Musa? By God, you have not lied, nor have you been lied to. He did this three times. Then God, may His praise be exalted, revealed to Musa: ﴿Strike the sea with your staff, so it split, and each part was like a great mountain﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 63] — he says: like a mountain. He said: Then Musa and those with him set out, and Pharaoh followed them on their path, until when they had all gathered within it, God closed it over them. Therefore He said: ﴿And We drowned the people of Pharaoh while you were watching﴾. Ma'mar said, Qatadah said: Musa had with him six hundred thousand, and Pharaoh followed him with one million one hundred thousand horses.

909. Abd al-Karim ibn al-Haytham related to me, saying: Ibrahim ibn Bashshar al-Ramadi related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, saying: Abu Sa'id related to us, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: God, mighty and majestic, revealed to Musa: Travel by night with My servants, for you will be pursued. He said: So Musa traveled with the children of Israel by night, and Pharaoh pursued them with one million horses, besides the females, while Musa had six hundred thousand. When Pharaoh saw them, he said: ﴿Indeed these are a small band, and they have enraged us, and we are a vigilant host﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 54-56]. So Musa traveled with the children of Israel until they reached the sea, and they turned around and saw the dust of Pharaoh's beasts, and they said: O Musa, we were harmed before you came to us, and after you came to us! This sea is before us, and this is Pharaoh, who has overtaken us with those who are with him! [Note: "rahiqahu" means it covered him and nearly reached him.] He said: Perhaps your Lord will destroy your enemy and make you successors in the land, and He will see how you act. He said: Then God, may His praise be exalted, revealed to Musa: Strike the sea with your staff; and He revealed to the sea: Hear and obey Musa when he strikes you. He said: So the sea trembled for him with a shudder [afkal] — meaning: a quaking — not knowing from which of its sides he would strike it. He said: Yusha said to Musa: With what were you commanded? He said: I was commanded to strike the sea. He said: Then strike it. He said: So Musa struck the sea with his staff, and it split, and there were twelve paths in it, each path like a great mountain; so each tribe had a path they took. When they took the path, some of them said to others: Why do we not see our companions? They said to Musa: Where are our companions? We do not see them. He said: Proceed, for they are on a path like your path. They said: We will not be content until we see them.

Sufyan said, Ammar al-Dahni said: Musa said: O God, help me against their bad characters. He said: Then God revealed to him: Say with your staff like this. Ibrahim gestured with his hand, turning it over the sea. Musa, with his staff, [made a motion] on the walls like this, [Note: "qala bi-'asahu aw bi-yadihi" means he indicated with them; gesture is a kind of expression and explanation, so the figurative sense of "said" toward the meaning of gesture is apt.] so there appeared in them openings through which some looked at others.

Sufyan said: Abu Sa'id said, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas: So they proceeded until they came out of the sea. When the last of the people of Musa had passed, Pharaoh and his companions rushed upon the sea, and Pharaoh was on a dark-colored, long-tailed stallion. [Note: "adham" means black; "dhanub" means a horse with a full, long tail; and "hisan" here means a stallion that withheld its water and did not mount a female.] When he rushed upon the sea, the stallion feared to plunge into the sea, so Gabriel appeared to him in the form of a female mare in heat, [Note: al-Wadiq was explained above at p. 46, note 4.] and when the stallion saw her, he plunged after her. It was said to Musa: Leave the sea ""rahwan"" — he said: a path, in its state. [Note: In the manuscript: "'ala hiyalihi," which is an error; see what preceded at p. 46, and also see the explanation of "rahwan" at 25:73 (Bulaq).] He said: Pharaoh and his people entered the sea, and when the last of the people of Pharaoh entered, and the last of the people of Musa had passed, the sea closed over Pharaoh and his people, and they were drowned. [Note: Report 909 is like the earlier report 892, with the same chain. See the completion of this report at no. 918. Sufyan inserted his narration from Ammar al-Dahni into his narration from Abu Sa'id. Ammar is Ammar ibn Mu'awiyah al-Dahni (with a damma on the dal and sukun on the ha'), whom Ahmad, Ibn Ma'in, Abu Hatim and al-Nasa'i declared trustworthy, and Ibn Hibban mentioned in al-Thiqat (Tahdhib al-Tahdhib).]

910. Musa ibn Harun related to us, saying: Amr ibn Hammad related to us, saying: Asbat ibn Nasr related to us, from al-Suddi: God commanded Musa to bring out the children of Israel, and said: Travel by night with My servants, for you will be pursued. So Musa and Harun went out with their people, and death was cast upon the Copts, so every firstborn man died, and in the morning they were burying them, and they were occupied and did not pursue them until the sun rose. This is the time God, may His praise be exalted, refers to in His saying: ﴿So they followed them at sunrise﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 60]. Musa was at the rear of the children of Israel, and Harun was in front of them, leading them. The believer said to Musa: O Prophet of God, where have you been commanded? He said: The sea. He wanted to rush in, but Musa prevented him. Musa went out with six hundred thousand and twenty thousand fighting men, not counting anyone under twenty for being young, nor anyone over sixty for being old; they counted only those between these ages, apart from the offspring. Pharaoh pursued them, and at his front was Haman, with one million and seven hundred thousand horses, among which there was no mare — meaning the female — and this is the time God, may His praise be exalted, refers to in His saying: ﴿So Pharaoh sent into the cities gatherers, "Indeed these are a small band"﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 53-54], meaning the children of Israel. Harun went forward and struck the sea, but the sea refused to open, and said: Who is this tyrant who strikes me? until Musa came to it, gave it the kunya "Abu Khalid," struck it, and it split, and each part was like a great mountain — he says: like a great mountain — and the children of Israel entered. In the sea there were twelve paths, in each path a tribe — and the paths had split with walls [Note: in Tarikh al-Tabari: "wa-ka'anna al-turuq idha infalaqat bi-judran"] — and each tribe said: Our companions have been killed! When Musa saw that, he called upon God, and He made them for them as arches like vaulted passages [Note: al-tiqan and al-atwaq are plurals of taq, meaning the arch of a structure wherever it is], so the last of them looked at the first of them, until they all came out. Then Pharaoh and his companions approached, and when Pharaoh looked at the sea split open, he said: Do you not see that the sea has split from fear of me? It has opened for me until I reach my enemies and kill them! This is the time God, may His praise be exalted, refers to in His saying: ﴿And We brought near there the others﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 64], he says: We brought near there the others, meaning the people of Pharaoh. When Pharaoh stood at the mouths of the paths, his horses refused to plunge, so Gabriel descended upon a mare in heat, and the stallions smelled the scent of the mare, and they plunged after her. When the first of them was about to come out and the last of them had entered, He commanded the sea to seize them, and it closed over them. [Note: Report 910 is in Tarikh al-Tabari 1:213-214; a paragraph of it appeared earlier as no. 904. To "iltatama al-bahr 'alayhim" means it closed over them and sealed, while its waves clashed. I did not find this in the lexicons, but they say: "iltatamat al-amwaj wa-talatamat," meaning some waves struck others; and they say: "lataма al-kitab," meaning he sealed it. So what came in the report is an Arabic expression, deeply rooted in its figurative use.]

911. Yunus ibn Abd al-A'la related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: When Pharaoh drove them to the sea, Pharaoh said to them: Tell them to enter the sea, if they are truthful! When the companions of Musa saw them, they said: Indeed we are overtaken! He said: No! Indeed my Lord is with me; He will guide me. Then Musa said to the sea: Do you not know that I am the Messenger of God? It said: Yes. He said: And do you know that these are servants of the servants of God whom I was commanded to bring? It said: Yes.

He said: "Do you know that this is the enemy of Allah?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Then part the sea for me and for those with me." [[In the printed edition: "fa-infaraq li tariqan," which is an error.]] He said: "O Musa, I am only a created servant; I have no command except that which Allah, the Exalted, commands me." So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to the sea: "When Musa strikes you with his staff, then part." And He revealed to Musa that he should strike the sea, and he recited the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿So strike for them a dry path through the sea, not fearing being overtaken nor being afraid﴾ [Surah Ta-Ha: 77], and he recited His saying: ﴿And leave the sea at rest (rahwan)﴾ [al-Dukhan: 24] — meaning, calm, with no hollows in it [[In the printed edition: "laysa fihi ta'addin," and in the manuscript: "nafad," where the dal resembles a ra'. I have therefore preferred what is recorded here. Al-naqr is the plural of naqrah, which is a round depression in the ground, or a small pit that is not large. This is more fitting for the speech and the meaning.]] — so it parted into twelve paths, and each tribe walked in a path. He said: They said to Pharaoh: "They have entered the sea." He said: "Enter after them." He said: Jibril, at the rear of the Children of Israel, was saying to them: "Let your last catch up with your first." And at the front of Pharaoh's family he was saying to them: "Slowly, so that your last may catch up with your first." Each tribe in the sea began saying to the tribe that had entered before them: "They have perished!" When that entered their hearts, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to the sea, and it made arches for them, so that these looked at those, until the last of these had come out and the last of those had entered, and Allah commanded the sea and it closed over those.

* *

By His saying: ﴿and you are looking on﴾, He means: you are looking at Allah parting the sea for you and destroying the family of Pharaoh at the place where He rescued you, and at His great authority, in what He showed you of the sea's obedience to Him, as it became heaps, split apart like lofty mountains, [[In the printed edition: "rukaman farqan," which is an unjustified change. Rukam: things piled one upon another; and falq is the plural of falqah (with a kasra and sukun), which is a split.]] not departing from its limit, submitting to Allah's command and yielding to His obedience, though before that it had been flowing and liquid.

By this, Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, makes them stand before the place of His proofs against them, reminds them of His blessings upon their forebears, and warns them—in their denial of our Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ)—that there may befall them what befell Pharaoh and his family in their denial of Musa (ﷺ).

* *

Some scholars of Arabic have claimed that the meaning of His saying ﴿and you are looking on﴾ is like the meaning of the speaker's words: "I struck while your family were looking on, but they neither came to you nor helped you," meaning: they were near, within sight and hearing; and like the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Have you not considered your Lord, how He extended the shade?﴾ [al-Furqan: 45], where there is no seeing, only knowledge.

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: What led him to this interpretation is that he took His saying ﴿and you are looking on﴾ to mean "and you are looking at Pharaoh's drowning," and so he said: They were too occupied, by what surrounded them of the sea, to look at Pharaoh and his drowning. But the interpretation he gave is not the correct sense of the words. The true meaning is: "and you are looking on at Allah's parting of the sea for you—as we have described just above—and the sea's waves crashing down upon Pharaoh's family, in the place which He made a dry path for you in the sea." That was, without doubt, seeing with one's own eyes, not knowledge-based seeing, as the one who stated the view we have quoted supposed.

**The Explanation of His Words, Exalted is He: ﴿And when We appointed⁠﴾**

The readers (qurra') differed concerning the reading of this word. [[In the printed edition, in both places: "al-qara'" (the readers), as it often does in earlier passages. Al-qara'a is the plural of qari' (reader).]] Some of them read ﴿wa'adna﴾ ("We appointed") in the sense that God, exalted is He, made an appointment with Moses to meet at Mount Sinai (al-Tur) for His private conversation, so the appointing came from God to Moses and from Moses to his Lord. [[In the printed edition: "mulaqat al-Tur" (meeting at Mount Sinai). I do not know why someone changed it!]] Among their arguments for preferring the reading ﴿wa'adna﴾ (with the alif, "We appointed") over "wa'adna" (without it, "We promised") was their claim that every mutual arrangement between two parties for meeting and gathering is an ittila' (mutual agreement, from the form ittá'ada, "to agree on a time"), so each of them appoints the other. For this reason, they claimed, the reading of the one who reads ﴿wa'adna﴾ by choice must be given precedence over the reading of the one who reads "wa'adna." [[In the printed edition: "kull ibad" (every distancing) "aw al-ijtima'" (or gathering), and I do not know why it was done! Ittá'ada is a form of the verb wa'ada, from the root w-'-d.]] [[In the printed edition: "fa-li-dhalika rammaw annahu wajaba" with an added "annahu," which is an addition that corrupts the meaning.]]

Others read "wa'adna" (without the alif), in the sense that God is the One who promises and the sole Promiser, not anyone else. Among their arguments for this choice was their claim that mutual appointment occurs only among humans, whereas God, mighty is His praise, is alone in promising and threatening in every good and evil. They said: "The Revelation in the entire Qur'an came in this way. He, mighty is His praise, said: ﴿Indeed, God has promised you a promise of truth⁠﴾ [Ibrahim: 22], and He said: ﴿And when God promised you one of the two groups, that it would be yours⁠﴾ [al-Anfal: 7]." They said: "So likewise it is necessary that He is the sole Promiser in His words: ﴿And when We promised Moses⁠﴾."

* *

Our view on this matter is that these are two readings which the Muslim community (ummah) has transmitted and which the readers have recited, and recitation with one of them does not invalidate the meaning of the other. Although one of them carries an additional meaning over the other in terms of the apparent sense (zahir) and recitation, [[See what passed in the explanation of "al-zahir" (the apparent): p. 44, and the references.]] in terms of the understood meaning they are in agreement. That is because whoever reports that a person promised another to meet at some place, it is known that the one promised has likewise appointed his companion for a meeting at that place, just as the other promised him, if his promise was made by mutual agreement. It is known that God did not appoint Moses, peace be upon him, to Mount Sinai except with Moses' consent, since there is no doubt that Moses was pleased with everything God commanded and was hastening toward loving it. And it is understood that God, exalted is He, did not appoint Moses to that unless Moses was responding to Him. Since that is so, it is known that God, mighty is His remembrance, promised Moses the Mount, and Moses promised Him the meeting. So God, mighty is His remembrance, was the Promiser to Moses, appointing Him to private conversation on the Mount, and Moses was the one appointing his Lord, appointing Him to a meeting. Thus, whichever of the two readings, "wa'ada" or "wa'ada" (with alif), the reciter recites, he is correct in the truth of that matter, in terms of interpretation (ta'wil) and language, for the reasons we have described earlier. [[In the printed edition: "fa-huwa al-haqq fi dhalika..." which is an error.]]

There is no sense in the statement of the one who says: "Mutual appointment only occurs among humans, and God alone is the One who promises and threatens in every good and evil." That is because God's exclusive authority over promise and threat regarding reward and punishment, good and evil, benefit and harm, which is in His hand and to Him, and not in the hands of any of His creatures, does not turn the speech that flows among people in their usage away from its meanings, nor change it from its understood sense. What flows among people of understood speech is what we have described: that every mutual agreement between two parties is a promise from each of them to the other and a mutual appointment between them, and that each of them appoints his companion, and that the promise by which one party alone is the promiser, not the one promised, is only that which means the "promise" which is the opposite of the "threat." [[In the printed edition here also, as before: "kull ibad," which is corrupt and an error.]]

* *

**The Explanation of His Words, Exalted is He: ﴿Moses⁠﴾**

"Musa" (Moses), as has reached us, in Coptic is two words, meaning by them: water and tree. "Mu" is water, and "sha" is tree. [[In the printed edition and manuscript: "sa," and I have restored what is in the History (Tarikh).]] He was named that, as has reached us, because his mother, when she placed him in the chest (tabut), out of fear for him from Pharaoh, and cast him into the river (al-yamm), as God had revealed to her, and it is said the river into which she cast him was the Nile, the waves of the river pushed him until they brought him in among trees near Pharaoh's house. The maidservants of Asiya, Pharaoh's wife, came out to bathe, found the chest, and took it. So he was named after the place where he was found, which was a place with water and trees, [[In the printed edition: "wa-kana dhalika al-makan fihi" which is nothing.]] so he was called Musa, water and tree. Thus:

**(912)** Musa ibn Harun narrated to me, saying: 'Amr ibn Hammad narrated to us, from Asbat ibn Nasr, from al-Suddi. [[The report: 912, History of al-Tabari 1:201, in a long report.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: He is Musa ibn 'Imran ibn Yasjar ibn Qahath ibn Lawi ibn Ya'qub, Isra'il of God, ibn Ishaq the Sacrificed of God, ibn Ibrahim the Friend of God, according to what Ibn Ishaq claimed.

**(913)** This was narrated to me by Ibn Humayd, saying: Salama ibn al-Fadl narrated to us, from him. [[The report: 913, an abridgment of a report on his lineage in the History of al-Tabari 1:198.]]

* *

**The Explanation of His Words, Exalted is He: ﴿forty nights⁠﴾**

The meaning of that: "And when We appointed Moses forty nights in full." So the forty nights are all included in the appointment.

Some grammarians of Basra claimed that its meaning is: "And when We appointed Moses for the completion of forty nights," that is, the beginning of the forty, and they gave as an example His words: ﴿And ask the town⁠﴾ [Yusuf: 82], and their saying: "Today is forty since so-and-so left," and "Today is two days," meaning: today is the completion of two days, and the completion of forty.

Abu Ja'far said: That contradicts what has been transmitted from the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) and contradicts the apparent recitation. As for the apparent recitation, God, mighty is His praise, has informed that He appointed Moses forty nights, so no one may turn the apparent sense of His report into a hidden sense without proof that establishes its correctness. [[See the explanation of "zahir" (apparent) and "batin" (hidden) above, p. 44, and the references before it.]]

* *

As for the people of interpretation, they said about it what I will mention, which is:

**(914)** Al-Muthanna ibn Ibrahim narrated to me with it, saying: Adam narrated to us, saying: Abu Ja'far narrated to us, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, from Abu al-'Aliya concerning His words: ﴿And when We appointed Moses forty nights⁠﴾. He said: That is, Dhu al-Qa'da and ten of Dhu al-Hijja. That was when Moses left his companions and appointed Harun over them, and he remained on the Mount forty nights, and the Torah was sent down to him on the tablets, and the tablets were of chrysolite [[In the printed edition: "min zabarjad" (of chrysolite). The correct reading is what I have restored from the manuscript and from what came from Abu al-'Aliya on the description of the tablets, 9:46 (Bulaq).]] — and the Lord brought him near as a confidant (najiyyan), spoke to him, and he heard the sound of the pens (sarif al-qalam). It has reached us that he did not commit any impurity (hadath) during the forty nights until he came down from the Mount. [[The sound of the pens: their sound and their scratching as they run with what the angels write. His words "he did not commit any impurity" mean he was not distressed by what distresses people, such as relieving oneself.]]

**(915)** And it was reported from 'Ammar ibn al-Hasan, who narrated to us: 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi', similarly.

**(916)** Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salama ibn al-Fadl narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: God promised Moses, when He destroyed Pharaoh and his people, and saved him and his people, thirty nights, then completed them with ten, so the appointment of his Lord was completed as forty nights, when his Lord would meet him therein as He willed. [[In the printed edition: "tulaqqihi rabbuhu fiha bima sha'a" (his Lord would meet him therein with what He willed).]] Moses appointed Harun over the Children of Israel and said: "Indeed, I am hastening to my Lord, so take my place among my people and do not follow the way of the corrupters." So Moses went out to his Lord hastening to meet Him, out of longing for Him, [[In the printed edition: "li-liqa'ihi" (to his meeting), and both are the same in meaning.]] and Harun remained among the Children of Israel, and with him was al-Samiri, guiding them along the trail of Moses so they might catch up with him. [[The report: 916. The beginning of this report appears in the History of al-Tabari 1:217-218, but al-Tabari cut it off and completed it from the report of al-Suddi.]]

**(917)** Musa ibn Harun narrated to me, saying: 'Amr ibn Hammad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, who said: Moses set out and appointed Harun over the Children of Israel, and he promised them thirty nights, and God completed them with ten. [[The report: 917. In the History of al-Tabari, in a long report, 1:218. Its completion will come in no. 919.]]

* *

**The Explanation of His Words, Exalted is He: ﴿Then you took the calf after him, while you were wrongdoers (51)⁠﴾**

The interpretation of His words: ﴿Then you took the calf after him⁠﴾ means: then you took the calf as a god during the days of Moses' appointment, after Moses had left you heading to the appointed meeting. The pronoun "him" in His words "after him" refers back to the mention of Moses.

So He, mighty is His praise, informed the opponents of our Prophet ﷺ from among the Jews of the Children of Israel, who denied him, those addressed by this verse, about the deed of their fathers and forefathers, and their denial of their messengers, and their opposition to their prophets, despite the continuous succession of His blessings upon them and the spreading of His bounties among them, [[In the printed edition: "subugh ala'ihi" (abundance of His bounties). The spreading of His bounties: their manifestation and generality such that all of them shared in them. See what will come after, p. 77, note 2.]] informing them that they, in their opposition to Muhammad ﷺ and their denial of him, and their rejection of his message, despite their knowledge of his truthfulness, [[In the printed edition: "min khilafihim Muhammadan" (from their opposing Muhammad).]] are following the same path as their fathers and forefathers, and warning them that the descent of His punishment upon them, by their standing on that denial, would be like what befell their predecessors who denied the messengers: transformation, cursing, and various kinds of vengeance.

The cause of their taking the calf was what follows:

**(918)** Abd al-Karim ibn al-Haytham narrated to me with it, saying: Ibrahim ibn Bashshar al-Ramadi narrated to us, saying: Sufyan ibn 'Uyayna narrated to us, saying: Abu Sa'id narrated to us, from 'Ikrima, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: When Pharaoh and his companions came upon the sea, Pharaoh was on a black horse, a stallion with a dhu'ub (a pale white mark on the leg?) [[dhu'ub: a horse with a white blaze, or the rest of its meaning is unclear; I have rendered it literally.]], and when he came upon the sea, the horse feared to plunge into the sea, so Gabriel appeared to him in the form of a mare in heat, and when the horse saw her, it plunged after her. [[See the end of the report no. 909, which is this one verbatim, and its completion will come later.]] He said: al-Samiri recognized Gabriel, because his mother, when she feared that he would be slaughtered, placed him in a cave and sealed it over him, and Gabriel would come to him and nourish him with his fingers, and he would find in one of his fingers milk, in another honey, and in another butter, and he kept nourishing him until he grew up. When he saw him in the sea, he recognized him, so he took a handful of the dust of his horse's track. He said: He took a handful from beneath the hoof. Sufyan said: Ibn Mas'ud used to read it: "So I took a handful from the track of the messenger's horse" [Taha: 96].

Abu Sa'id said: 'Ikrima said, from Ibn 'Abbas: And it was cast into the heart (raw') of al-Samiri, [[Al-raw' (with a dammah on the ra): the heart and the intellect. "It occurred to my raw'": that is, in my soul and mind and inner thought.]] "You will not throw it on anything saying 'Be, such and such' except that it will be." The handful stayed with him in his hand until he crossed the sea. When Moses and the Children of Israel crossed the sea, and God drowned the family of Pharaoh, Moses said to his brother Harun: "Take my place among my people and set things right." And Moses went on to the appointment with his Lord. He said: With the Children of Israel was some ornament from the ornaments of Pharaoh's family, which they had borrowed, [[ta'awwara al-shay' and ista'arahu: he took it as a loan, as one says ta'ajjaba and ista'jaba.]] so they felt sinful about it, and they brought it out so that fire would descend and consume it. When they gathered it, al-Samiri with the handful that was in his hand did this [[qala bi-l-qabdah: he raised it, pointing with his hand, in order to throw it. Its explanation has passed on p. 54, note 3.]] — and he threw it into it — and Ibn Ishaq gestured with his hand thus — and said: "Be a calf, a body that lows." So it became a calf, a body that lows, and wind would enter its back and come out its mouth, and a sound was heard from it, and he said: "This is your god and the god of Moses." So they devoted themselves to the calf, worshipping it. Harun said: "O my people, you have only been tested by it, and your Lord is the Most Merciful, so follow me and obey my command!" They said: "We will not cease to remain devoted to it until Moses returns to us."

**(919)** Musa ibn Harun narrated to me, saying: 'Amr ibn Hammad narrated to us, saying: Asbat ibn Nasr narrated to us, from al-Suddi: When God commanded Moses to bring the Children of Israel out — meaning from the land of Egypt — Moses commanded the Children of Israel to go out, and commanded them to borrow the ornaments from the Copts. When God saved Moses and those with him from the Children of Israel from the sea, and the family of Pharaoh drowned, Gabriel came to Moses to take him to God. He came on a horse, and al-Samiri saw him and disapproved, and said: "This is the horse of life!" He said when he saw it: "Indeed, this has an affair." So he took some of the dust of the hoof, the hoof of the horse. Moses departed, and appointed Harun over the Children of Israel, and promised them thirty nights, and God completed them with ten. Harun said to them: "O Children of Israel, indeed the spoils of war are not lawful for you, and indeed the ornaments of the Copts are only spoils of war, so gather them all together, dig a pit for them and bury them, for if Moses comes and makes them lawful, you may take them, and otherwise they will be something you have not eaten." So they gathered those ornaments into that pit, and al-Samiri came with that handful and threw it, and God brought forth from the ornaments a calf, a body that lows. The Children of Israel counted the appointment of Moses, counting the night as a day and the day as a day, and when it was the completion of twenty, the calf came out for them. When they saw it, al-Samiri said to them: "This is your god and the god of Moses, but he forgot" — meaning: Moses left his god here and went off to seek him. So they devoted themselves to it, worshipping it, and it would low and walk. Harun said to them: "O Children of Israel, you have only been tested by it" — meaning: you have only been afflicted by it, meaning: by the calf — "and your Lord is the Most Merciful." So Harun and those with him among the Children of Israel remained, not fighting them, and Moses went to his god to speak with Him, and when he spoke to Him, He said: "What hastened you from your people, O Moses?" He said: "They are upon my trail, and I hastened to You, my Lord, that You might be pleased." He said: "Indeed, We have tested your people after you, and al-Samiri has led them astray," so He informed him of their news. Moses said: "O Lord, this al-Samiri commanded them to make the calf. Did You see the spirit (rih), who breathed it into it?" The Lord said: "I did." He said: "Lord, then You are the one who led them astray." [[The report: 919. Its beginning passed in no. 917. In the History, 1:218.]]

**(920)** Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: It was, as was related to me, that Moses said to the Children of Israel, regarding what God, mighty and majestic, had commanded him: "Borrow from them — meaning from the family of Pharaoh — the goods, the ornaments, and the garments, for I will make you inherit their wealth along with their destruction." When Pharaoh gave permission to the people, among what he incited them with against the Children of Israel was that he said: "When they set out, they were not content to leave with themselves alone, until they took your wealth with them!" [[The report: 920. In the History of al-Tabari 1:216. In the printed edition: "an yakhrujuu bi-anfusihim" (to leave with themselves), and I have restored what is in the manuscript and the History. Nafal al-shay': he made it a nafl, that is, a spoil that is lawfully taken.]]

**(921)** Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to me, from Hakim ibn Jubayr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: al-Samiri was a man from the people of Bajarma, and he was from a people who worshipped cows, and the love of cow worship was in his soul, and he had displayed Islam among the Children of Israel. When Harun was left in charge among the Children of Israel, and Moses departed to his Lord, [[Fasala fulan 'an al-balad yafsulu fusulan: when he went out and separated from it.]] Harun said to them: "You have been burdened with the burdens of the ornaments of the people — the family of Pharaoh — and goods and jewelry, so purify yourselves of them, for they are unclean." And he lit a fire for them and said: "Throw whatever you have of that into it." They said: "Yes."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 51–52 (part 2 of 2):

They began bringing whatever of those goods and that jewelry they had with them, [[In the printed edition: "بما كان معهم" (with what they had with them); it was altered to fit the common usage they were accustomed to.]] and casting it into it. Until, when the jewelry had melted in it, the Samiri saw the hoofprint of Gabriel's horse, so he took a handful of dust from the print of its hoof. [[In the printed edition: "أخذ ترابا" (he took dust), with the fa' omitted so that it would fit their Arabic, so they claimed.]] Then he came to the fire and said to Harun: [[In the History of al-Tabari: "ثم أقبل إلى الحفرة" (then he came to the pit).]] "O Prophet of Allah, shall I throw what is in my hand?" He said: "Yes." Harun did not suspect anything other than that it was like some of the other jewelry and goods that others had brought. So he threw it into it and said: "Be a calf, a body with a lowing," and it became so, as a trial and a test. He said: "This is your god and the god of Musa." So they clung to it (in devotion) and loved it with a love they had never shown anything before. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿So he forgot﴾ [Ta-Ha: 88], meaning he abandoned what he had been upon of Islam - meaning the Samiri - (﴿Do they not see that it does not return to them a word, and that it possesses for them no harm nor benefit?﴾) [Ta-Ha: 89]. The name of the Samiri was Musa ibn Zafar; he came into the land of Egypt and entered among the Children of Israel. [[He is, as mentioned at the beginning of the report, from the people of "Bajarma," and Bajarma is a village among the districts of al-Balikh near ar-Raqqa, in the land of al-Jazira (Yaqut). It is said to be a place before Nasibin (Mu'jam ma Ista'jam). Al-Maydani said in his explanation of the proverb "خطب يسير في خطب كبير" that az-Zabba' was from the people of Bajarma and spoke Arabic.]] When Harun saw what they had fallen into, he said: ﴿O my people, you are only being tested by it, and indeed your Lord is the Most Merciful, so follow me and obey my command.﴾ They said: ﴿We will not cease to be devoted to it until Musa returns to us.﴾ [Ta-Ha: 90-91] So Harun remained with those among the Muslims who had not been tested, while those who worshipped the calf remained at their worship of the calf. Harun feared that if he set out with those Muslims who were with him, Musa would say to him: "You caused division among the Children of Israel and did not heed my word." He had been in awe of him and obedient to him. [[Report: 921 - in the History of al-Tabari 1: 219-220.]]

922 - Yunus ibn Abd al-A'la related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: When Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, delivered the Children of Israel from Pharaoh, and drowned Pharaoh and those with him, Musa said to his brother Harun: "Take my place among my people, act righteously, and do not follow the way of the corrupters." He said: When Musa went out, Harun was commanded with what he was commanded, and Musa went out hastening, joyful, toward Allah. Musa knew that when a man succeeds in the need of his master, it pleases him that he hasten to him. [[In the printed edition: "نجح" (he succeeded); and anjaha: attained his request and reached success. Though I fear there may be a subtle corruption in the word that has escaped me.]] He said: When they set out, they had borrowed jewelry and garments from the family of Pharaoh, and Harun said to them: "These garments and jewelry are not lawful for you; gather a fire, throw it in and burn it." He said: So they gathered a fire. He said: The Samiri had seen the track of Gabriel's mount, and it was a female horse - and the Samiri was among the people of Musa - he said: He looked at its track and took a handful from it, and his hand became stuck to it. When the people of Musa threw the jewelry into the fire, and the Samiri threw the handful with them, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, formed for them a golden calf, and the wind entered it, so it had a lowing. They said: "What is this?" The wicked Samiri said: ﴿This is your god and the god of Musa, but he forgot﴾, the verse, to His saying: ﴿until Musa returns to us﴾ [Ta-Ha: 88-91]. He said: Until Musa came to the appointed time, Allah said: ﴿And what hastened you from your people, O Musa? He said: They are close upon my footsteps﴾, and he recited until he reached: ﴿Has the covenant seemed long to you?﴾ [Ta-Ha: 86].

923 - al-Qasim ibn al-Hasan related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿Then you took the calf after him﴾, he said: The calf: the hasil of the cow [[al-Hasil (with fatha then kasra): the young of a cow.]]. He said: Jewelry they had borrowed from the family of Pharaoh. Harun said to them: "Bring it out, purify yourselves of it, and burn it." The Samiri had taken a handful from the track of Gabriel's horse and cast it into it, and it melted, so it had a hollow into which the winds blew.

924 - al-Muthanna ibn Ibrahim related to me, saying: Adam related to us, saying: Abu Ja'far related to us, from al-Rabi', from Abu al-Aliyah, who said: It was only named the calf because they hastened (ajjalu) and made it before Musa came to them.

925 - Muhammad ibn Amr al-Bahili related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to me, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, similar to the report of al-Qasim from al-Husayn.

926 - al-Muthanna ibn Ibrahim related to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah related to us, saying: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, similarly [[The two reports 925 and 926: in the manuscript, the isnad of both reports was given together in one place, saying: "qala haddathana Isa - wa-haddathani al-Muthanna ibn Ibrahim, qala, haddathana Abu Hudhayfah qala, haddathana Shibl - jami'an an Abi Najih, an Mujahid fi qawlihi: 'thumma ittakhadtumu al-'ijl' qala: al-'ijl: hasil al-baqarah..." then he cited the text of report 924. I preferred to leave what is in the printed edition as it stands.]]

* *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And you were wrongdoers﴾ [2:51]

It means: "And you were placing worship in other than its proper place, for worship is not befitting except to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic; and you worshipped the calf, wronging yourselves and placing worship in other than its proper place." We have explained in another place earlier in our book that the root of every wrong is placing a thing in other than its proper place, so that suffices and there is no need to repeat it here. [[See what passed: 1: 523-524.]]

* *

The interpretation of His saying, exalted be His mention: ﴿Then We pardoned you after that, that you might be grateful﴾ [2:52]

Abu Ja'far said: The meaning of His saying: ﴿Then We pardoned you after that﴾ is: We withheld hastening punishment upon you, "after that," that is, after your taking the calf as a god. As follows:

926 - al-Muthanna ibn Ibrahim related this to me, saying: Adam al-Asqalani related to us, saying: Abu Ja'far related to us, from al-Rabi', from Abu al-Aliyah: ﴿Then We pardoned you after that﴾, meaning after you had taken the calf.

* *

As for the interpretation of His saying: ﴿that you might be grateful﴾, it means: that you might give thanks. The meaning of "la'alla" in this place is the meaning of "kay" (so that). I have already explained earlier that one of the meanings of "la'alla" is "kay," which is sufficient so that it need not be repeated here. [[See what passed: 1: 364-365.]]

* *

So the meaning of the speech is: Then We pardoned you after your taking the calf as a god, so that you might give thanks to Me for My pardon of you, since pardon necessitates gratitude from people of understanding and intellect.

**The Explanation of His Words, Exalted is He: ﴿And when We appointed⁠﴾**

The readers (qurra') differed concerning the reading of this word. [[In the printed edition, in both places: "al-qara'" (the readers), as it often does in earlier passages. Al-qara'a is the plural of qari' (reader).]] Some of them read ﴿wa'adna﴾ ("We appointed") in the sense that God, exalted is He, made an appointment with Moses to meet at Mount Sinai (al-Tur) for His private conversation, so the appointing came from God to Moses and from Moses to his Lord. [[In the printed edition: "mulaqat al-Tur" (meeting at Mount Sinai). I do not know why someone changed it!]] Among their arguments for preferring the reading ﴿wa'adna﴾ (with the alif, "We appointed") over "wa'adna" (without it, "We promised") was their claim that every mutual arrangement between two parties for meeting and gathering is an ittila' (mutual agreement, from the form ittá'ada, "to agree on a time"), so each of them appoints the other. For this reason, they claimed, the reading of the one who reads ﴿wa'adna﴾ by choice must be given precedence over the reading of the one who reads "wa'adna." [[In the printed edition: "kull ibad" (every distancing) "aw al-ijtima'" (or gathering), and I do not know why it was done! Ittá'ada is a form of the verb wa'ada, from the root w-'-d.]] [[In the printed edition: "fa-li-dhalika rammaw annahu wajaba" with an added "annahu," which is an addition that corrupts the meaning.]]

Others read "wa'adna" (without the alif), in the sense that God is the One who promises and the sole Promiser, not anyone else. Among their arguments for this choice was their claim that mutual appointment occurs only among humans, whereas God, mighty is His praise, is alone in promising and threatening in every good and evil. They said: "The Revelation in the entire Qur'an came in this way. He, mighty is His praise, said: ﴿Indeed, God has promised you a promise of truth⁠﴾ [Ibrahim: 22], and He said: ﴿And when God promised you one of the two groups, that it would be yours⁠﴾ [al-Anfal: 7]." They said: "So likewise it is necessary that He is the sole Promiser in His words: ﴿And when We promised Moses⁠﴾."

* *

Our view on this matter is that these are two readings which the Muslim community (ummah) has transmitted and which the readers have recited, and recitation with one of them does not invalidate the meaning of the other. Although one of them carries an additional meaning over the other in terms of the apparent sense (zahir) and recitation, [[See what passed in the explanation of "al-zahir" (the apparent): p. 44, and the references.]] in terms of the understood meaning they are in agreement. That is because whoever reports that a person promised another to meet at some place, it is known that the one promised has likewise appointed his companion for a meeting at that place, just as the other promised him, if his promise was made by mutual agreement. It is known that God did not appoint Moses, peace be upon him, to Mount Sinai except with Moses' consent, since there is no doubt that Moses was pleased with everything God commanded and was hastening toward loving it. And it is understood that God, exalted is He, did not appoint Moses to that unless Moses was responding to Him. Since that is so, it is known that God, mighty is His remembrance, promised Moses the Mount, and Moses promised Him the meeting. So God, mighty is His remembrance, was the Promiser to Moses, appointing Him to private conversation on the Mount, and Moses was the one appointing his Lord, appointing Him to a meeting. Thus, whichever of the two readings, "wa'ada" or "wa'ada" (with alif), the reciter recites, he is correct in the truth of that matter, in terms of interpretation (ta'wil) and language, for the reasons we have described earlier. [[In the printed edition: "fa-huwa al-haqq fi dhalika..." which is an error.]]

There is no sense in the statement of the one who says: "Mutual appointment only occurs among humans, and God alone is the One who promises and threatens in every good and evil." That is because God's exclusive authority over promise and threat regarding reward and punishment, good and evil, benefit and harm, which is in His hand and to Him, and not in the hands of any of His creatures, does not turn the speech that flows among people in their usage away from its meanings, nor change it from its understood sense. What flows among people of understood speech is what we have described: that every mutual agreement between two parties is a promise from each of them to the other and a mutual appointment between them, and that each of them appoints his companion, and that the promise by which one party alone is the promiser, not the one promised, is only that which means the "promise" which is the opposite of the "threat." [[In the printed edition here also, as before: "kull ibad," which is corrupt and an error.]]

* *

**The Explanation of His Words, Exalted is He: ﴿Moses⁠﴾**

"Musa" (Moses), as has reached us, in Coptic is two words, meaning by them: water and tree. "Mu" is water, and "sha" is tree. [[In the printed edition and manuscript: "sa," and I have restored what is in the History (Tarikh).]] He was named that, as has reached us, because his mother, when she placed him in the chest (tabut), out of fear for him from Pharaoh, and cast him into the river (al-yamm), as God had revealed to her, and it is said the river into which she cast him was the Nile, the waves of the river pushed him until they brought him in among trees near Pharaoh's house. The maidservants of Asiya, Pharaoh's wife, came out to bathe, found the chest, and took it. So he was named after the place where he was found, which was a place with water and trees, [[In the printed edition: "wa-kana dhalika al-makan fihi" which is nothing.]] so he was called Musa, water and tree. Thus:

**(912)** Musa ibn Harun narrated to me, saying: 'Amr ibn Hammad narrated to us, from Asbat ibn Nasr, from al-Suddi. [[The report: 912, History of al-Tabari 1:201, in a long report.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: He is Musa ibn 'Imran ibn Yasjar ibn Qahath ibn Lawi ibn Ya'qub, Isra'il of God, ibn Ishaq the Sacrificed of God, ibn Ibrahim the Friend of God, according to what Ibn Ishaq claimed.

**(913)** This was narrated to me by Ibn Humayd, saying: Salama ibn al-Fadl narrated to us, from him. [[The report: 913, an abridgment of a report on his lineage in the History of al-Tabari 1:198.]]

* *

**The Explanation of His Words, Exalted is He: ﴿forty nights⁠﴾**

The meaning of that: "And when We appointed Moses forty nights in full." So the forty nights are all included in the appointment.

Some grammarians of Basra claimed that its meaning is: "And when We appointed Moses for the completion of forty nights," that is, the beginning of the forty, and they gave as an example His words: ﴿And ask the town⁠﴾ [Yusuf: 82], and their saying: "Today is forty since so-and-so left," and "Today is two days," meaning: today is the completion of two days, and the completion of forty.

Abu Ja'far said: That contradicts what has been transmitted from the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) and contradicts the apparent recitation. As for the apparent recitation, God, mighty is His praise, has informed that He appointed Moses forty nights, so no one may turn the apparent sense of His report into a hidden sense without proof that establishes its correctness. [[See the explanation of "zahir" (apparent) and "batin" (hidden) above, p. 44, and the references before it.]]

* *

As for the people of interpretation, they said about it what I will mention, which is:

**(914)** Al-Muthanna ibn Ibrahim narrated to me with it, saying: Adam narrated to us, saying: Abu Ja'far narrated to us, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, from Abu al-'Aliya concerning His words: ﴿And when We appointed Moses forty nights⁠﴾. He said: That is, Dhu al-Qa'da and ten of Dhu al-Hijja. That was when Moses left his companions and appointed Harun over them, and he remained on the Mount forty nights, and the Torah was sent down to him on the tablets, and the tablets were of chrysolite [[In the printed edition: "min zabarjad" (of chrysolite). The correct reading is what I have restored from the manuscript and from what came from Abu al-'Aliya on the description of the tablets, 9:46 (Bulaq).]] — and the Lord brought him near as a confidant (najiyyan), spoke to him, and he heard the sound of the pens (sarif al-qalam). It has reached us that he did not commit any impurity (hadath) during the forty nights until he came down from the Mount. [[The sound of the pens: their sound and their scratching as they run with what the angels write. His words "he did not commit any impurity" mean he was not distressed by what distresses people, such as relieving oneself.]]

**(915)** And it was reported from 'Ammar ibn al-Hasan, who narrated to us: 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi', similarly.

**(916)** Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salama ibn al-Fadl narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: God promised Moses, when He destroyed Pharaoh and his people, and saved him and his people, thirty nights, then completed them with ten, so the appointment of his Lord was completed as forty nights, when his Lord would meet him therein as He willed. [[In the printed edition: "tulaqqihi rabbuhu fiha bima sha'a" (his Lord would meet him therein with what He willed).]] Moses appointed Harun over the Children of Israel and said: "Indeed, I am hastening to my Lord, so take my place among my people and do not follow the way of the corrupters." So Moses went out to his Lord hastening to meet Him, out of longing for Him, [[In the printed edition: "li-liqa'ihi" (to his meeting), and both are the same in meaning.]] and Harun remained among the Children of Israel, and with him was al-Samiri, guiding them along the trail of Moses so they might catch up with him. [[The report: 916. The beginning of this report appears in the History of al-Tabari 1:217-218, but al-Tabari cut it off and completed it from the report of al-Suddi.]]

**(917)** Musa ibn Harun narrated to me, saying: 'Amr ibn Hammad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, who said: Moses set out and appointed Harun over the Children of Israel, and he promised them thirty nights, and God completed them with ten. [[The report: 917. In the History of al-Tabari, in a long report, 1:218. Its completion will come in no. 919.]]

* *

**The Explanation of His Words, Exalted is He: ﴿Then you took the calf after him, while you were wrongdoers (51)⁠﴾**

The interpretation of His words: ﴿Then you took the calf after him⁠﴾ means: then you took the calf as a god during the days of Moses' appointment, after Moses had left you heading to the appointed meeting. The pronoun "him" in His words "after him" refers back to the mention of Moses.

So He, mighty is His praise, informed the opponents of our Prophet ﷺ from among the Jews of the Children of Israel, who denied him, those addressed by this verse, about the deed of their fathers and forefathers, and their denial of their messengers, and their opposition to their prophets, despite the continuous succession of His blessings upon them and the spreading of His bounties among them, [[In the printed edition: "subugh ala'ihi" (abundance of His bounties). The spreading of His bounties: their manifestation and generality such that all of them shared in them. See what will come after, p. 77, note 2.]] informing them that they, in their opposition to Muhammad ﷺ and their denial of him, and their rejection of his message, despite their knowledge of his truthfulness, [[In the printed edition: "min khilafihim Muhammadan" (from their opposing Muhammad).]] are following the same path as their fathers and forefathers, and warning them that the descent of His punishment upon them, by their standing on that denial, would be like what befell their predecessors who denied the messengers: transformation, cursing, and various kinds of vengeance.

The cause of their taking the calf was what follows:

**(918)** Abd al-Karim ibn al-Haytham narrated to me with it, saying: Ibrahim ibn Bashshar al-Ramadi narrated to us, saying: Sufyan ibn 'Uyayna narrated to us, saying: Abu Sa'id narrated to us, from 'Ikrima, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: When Pharaoh and his companions came upon the sea, Pharaoh was on a black horse, a stallion with a dhu'ub (a pale white mark on the leg?) [[dhu'ub: a horse with a white blaze, or the rest of its meaning is unclear; I have rendered it literally.]], and when he came upon the sea, the horse feared to plunge into the sea, so Gabriel appeared to him in the form of a mare in heat, and when the horse saw her, it plunged after her. [[See the end of the report no. 909, which is this one verbatim, and its completion will come later.]] He said: al-Samiri recognized Gabriel, because his mother, when she feared that he would be slaughtered, placed him in a cave and sealed it over him, and Gabriel would come to him and nourish him with his fingers, and he would find in one of his fingers milk, in another honey, and in another butter, and he kept nourishing him until he grew up. When he saw him in the sea, he recognized him, so he took a handful of the dust of his horse's track. He said: He took a handful from beneath the hoof. Sufyan said: Ibn Mas'ud used to read it: "So I took a handful from the track of the messenger's horse" [Taha: 96].

Abu Sa'id said: 'Ikrima said, from Ibn 'Abbas: And it was cast into the heart (raw') of al-Samiri, [[Al-raw' (with a dammah on the ra): the heart and the intellect. "It occurred to my raw'": that is, in my soul and mind and inner thought.]] "You will not throw it on anything saying 'Be, such and such' except that it will be." The handful stayed with him in his hand until he crossed the sea. When Moses and the Children of Israel crossed the sea, and God drowned the family of Pharaoh, Moses said to his brother Harun: "Take my place among my people and set things right." And Moses went on to the appointment with his Lord. He said: With the Children of Israel was some ornament from the ornaments of Pharaoh's family, which they had borrowed, [[ta'awwara al-shay' and ista'arahu: he took it as a loan, as one says ta'ajjaba and ista'jaba.]] so they felt sinful about it, and they brought it out so that fire would descend and consume it. When they gathered it, al-Samiri with the handful that was in his hand did this [[qala bi-l-qabdah: he raised it, pointing with his hand, in order to throw it. Its explanation has passed on p. 54, note 3.]] — and he threw it into it — and Ibn Ishaq gestured with his hand thus — and said: "Be a calf, a body that lows." So it became a calf, a body that lows, and wind would enter its back and come out its mouth, and a sound was heard from it, and he said: "This is your god and the god of Moses." So they devoted themselves to the calf, worshipping it. Harun said: "O my people, you have only been tested by it, and your Lord is the Most Merciful, so follow me and obey my command!" They said: "We will not cease to remain devoted to it until Moses returns to us."

**(919)** Musa ibn Harun narrated to me, saying: 'Amr ibn Hammad narrated to us, saying: Asbat ibn Nasr narrated to us, from al-Suddi: When God commanded Moses to bring the Children of Israel out — meaning from the land of Egypt — Moses commanded the Children of Israel to go out, and commanded them to borrow the ornaments from the Copts. When God saved Moses and those with him from the Children of Israel from the sea, and the family of Pharaoh drowned, Gabriel came to Moses to take him to God. He came on a horse, and al-Samiri saw him and disapproved, and said: "This is the horse of life!" He said when he saw it: "Indeed, this has an affair." So he took some of the dust of the hoof, the hoof of the horse. Moses departed, and appointed Harun over the Children of Israel, and promised them thirty nights, and God completed them with ten. Harun said to them: "O Children of Israel, indeed the spoils of war are not lawful for you, and indeed the ornaments of the Copts are only spoils of war, so gather them all together, dig a pit for them and bury them, for if Moses comes and makes them lawful, you may take them, and otherwise they will be something you have not eaten." So they gathered those ornaments into that pit, and al-Samiri came with that handful and threw it, and God brought forth from the ornaments a calf, a body that lows. The Children of Israel counted the appointment of Moses, counting the night as a day and the day as a day, and when it was the completion of twenty, the calf came out for them. When they saw it, al-Samiri said to them: "This is your god and the god of Moses, but he forgot" — meaning: Moses left his god here and went off to seek him. So they devoted themselves to it, worshipping it, and it would low and walk. Harun said to them: "O Children of Israel, you have only been tested by it" — meaning: you have only been afflicted by it, meaning: by the calf — "and your Lord is the Most Merciful." So Harun and those with him among the Children of Israel remained, not fighting them, and Moses went to his god to speak with Him, and when he spoke to Him, He said: "What hastened you from your people, O Moses?" He said: "They are upon my trail, and I hastened to You, my Lord, that You might be pleased." He said: "Indeed, We have tested your people after you, and al-Samiri has led them astray," so He informed him of their news. Moses said: "O Lord, this al-Samiri commanded them to make the calf. Did You see the spirit (rih), who breathed it into it?" The Lord said: "I did." He said: "Lord, then You are the one who led them astray." [[The report: 919. Its beginning passed in no. 917. In the History, 1:218.]]

**(920)** Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: It was, as was related to me, that Moses said to the Children of Israel, regarding what God, mighty and majestic, had commanded him: "Borrow from them — meaning from the family of Pharaoh — the goods, the ornaments, and the garments, for I will make you inherit their wealth along with their destruction." When Pharaoh gave permission to the people, among what he incited them with against the Children of Israel was that he said: "When they set out, they were not content to leave with themselves alone, until they took your wealth with them!" [[The report: 920. In the History of al-Tabari 1:216. In the printed edition: "an yakhrujuu bi-anfusihim" (to leave with themselves), and I have restored what is in the manuscript and the History. Nafal al-shay': he made it a nafl, that is, a spoil that is lawfully taken.]]

**(921)** Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to me, from Hakim ibn Jubayr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: al-Samiri was a man from the people of Bajarma, and he was from a people who worshipped cows, and the love of cow worship was in his soul, and he had displayed Islam among the Children of Israel. When Harun was left in charge among the Children of Israel, and Moses departed to his Lord, [[Fasala fulan 'an al-balad yafsulu fusulan: when he went out and separated from it.]] Harun said to them: "You have been burdened with the burdens of the ornaments of the people — the family of Pharaoh — and goods and jewelry, so purify yourselves of them, for they are unclean." And he lit a fire for them and said: "Throw whatever you have of that into it." They said: "Yes."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 51–52 (part 2 of 2):

They began bringing whatever of those goods and that jewelry they had with them, [[In the printed edition: "بما كان معهم" (with what they had with them); it was altered to fit the common usage they were accustomed to.]] and casting it into it. Until, when the jewelry had melted in it, the Samiri saw the hoofprint of Gabriel's horse, so he took a handful of dust from the print of its hoof. [[In the printed edition: "أخذ ترابا" (he took dust), with the fa' omitted so that it would fit their Arabic, so they claimed.]] Then he came to the fire and said to Harun: [[In the History of al-Tabari: "ثم أقبل إلى الحفرة" (then he came to the pit).]] "O Prophet of Allah, shall I throw what is in my hand?" He said: "Yes." Harun did not suspect anything other than that it was like some of the other jewelry and goods that others had brought. So he threw it into it and said: "Be a calf, a body with a lowing," and it became so, as a trial and a test. He said: "This is your god and the god of Musa." So they clung to it (in devotion) and loved it with a love they had never shown anything before. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿So he forgot﴾ [Ta-Ha: 88], meaning he abandoned what he had been upon of Islam - meaning the Samiri - (﴿Do they not see that it does not return to them a word, and that it possesses for them no harm nor benefit?﴾) [Ta-Ha: 89]. The name of the Samiri was Musa ibn Zafar; he came into the land of Egypt and entered among the Children of Israel. [[He is, as mentioned at the beginning of the report, from the people of "Bajarma," and Bajarma is a village among the districts of al-Balikh near ar-Raqqa, in the land of al-Jazira (Yaqut). It is said to be a place before Nasibin (Mu'jam ma Ista'jam). Al-Maydani said in his explanation of the proverb "خطب يسير في خطب كبير" that az-Zabba' was from the people of Bajarma and spoke Arabic.]] When Harun saw what they had fallen into, he said: ﴿O my people, you are only being tested by it, and indeed your Lord is the Most Merciful, so follow me and obey my command.﴾ They said: ﴿We will not cease to be devoted to it until Musa returns to us.﴾ [Ta-Ha: 90-91] So Harun remained with those among the Muslims who had not been tested, while those who worshipped the calf remained at their worship of the calf. Harun feared that if he set out with those Muslims who were with him, Musa would say to him: "You caused division among the Children of Israel and did not heed my word." He had been in awe of him and obedient to him. [[Report: 921 - in the History of al-Tabari 1: 219-220.]]

922 - Yunus ibn Abd al-A'la related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: When Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, delivered the Children of Israel from Pharaoh, and drowned Pharaoh and those with him, Musa said to his brother Harun: "Take my place among my people, act righteously, and do not follow the way of the corrupters." He said: When Musa went out, Harun was commanded with what he was commanded, and Musa went out hastening, joyful, toward Allah. Musa knew that when a man succeeds in the need of his master, it pleases him that he hasten to him. [[In the printed edition: "نجح" (he succeeded); and anjaha: attained his request and reached success. Though I fear there may be a subtle corruption in the word that has escaped me.]] He said: When they set out, they had borrowed jewelry and garments from the family of Pharaoh, and Harun said to them: "These garments and jewelry are not lawful for you; gather a fire, throw it in and burn it." He said: So they gathered a fire. He said: The Samiri had seen the track of Gabriel's mount, and it was a female horse - and the Samiri was among the people of Musa - he said: He looked at its track and took a handful from it, and his hand became stuck to it. When the people of Musa threw the jewelry into the fire, and the Samiri threw the handful with them, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, formed for them a golden calf, and the wind entered it, so it had a lowing. They said: "What is this?" The wicked Samiri said: ﴿This is your god and the god of Musa, but he forgot﴾, the verse, to His saying: ﴿until Musa returns to us﴾ [Ta-Ha: 88-91]. He said: Until Musa came to the appointed time, Allah said: ﴿And what hastened you from your people, O Musa? He said: They are close upon my footsteps﴾, and he recited until he reached: ﴿Has the covenant seemed long to you?﴾ [Ta-Ha: 86].

923 - al-Qasim ibn al-Hasan related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿Then you took the calf after him﴾, he said: The calf: the hasil of the cow [[al-Hasil (with fatha then kasra): the young of a cow.]]. He said: Jewelry they had borrowed from the family of Pharaoh. Harun said to them: "Bring it out, purify yourselves of it, and burn it." The Samiri had taken a handful from the track of Gabriel's horse and cast it into it, and it melted, so it had a hollow into which the winds blew.

924 - al-Muthanna ibn Ibrahim related to me, saying: Adam related to us, saying: Abu Ja'far related to us, from al-Rabi', from Abu al-Aliyah, who said: It was only named the calf because they hastened (ajjalu) and made it before Musa came to them.

925 - Muhammad ibn Amr al-Bahili related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to me, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, similar to the report of al-Qasim from al-Husayn.

926 - al-Muthanna ibn Ibrahim related to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah related to us, saying: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, similarly [[The two reports 925 and 926: in the manuscript, the isnad of both reports was given together in one place, saying: "qala haddathana Isa - wa-haddathani al-Muthanna ibn Ibrahim, qala, haddathana Abu Hudhayfah qala, haddathana Shibl - jami'an an Abi Najih, an Mujahid fi qawlihi: 'thumma ittakhadtumu al-'ijl' qala: al-'ijl: hasil al-baqarah..." then he cited the text of report 924. I preferred to leave what is in the printed edition as it stands.]]

* *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And you were wrongdoers﴾ [2:51]
