[[al-dhull: softness, the opposite of difficulty.]] And one says of a similar man among the sons of Adam: "a humble man, between humility and lowliness."

1248 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿Indeed, it is a cow neither broken﴾, he said: difficult, not made docile by work, ﴿to plow the earth, nor to water the tilth﴾.

1249 - Musa narrated to me, saying: Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿Indeed, it is a cow neither broken to plow the earth﴾, he said: a cow that is not docile, on which one cultivates, and which does not water the tilth.

1250 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Adam narrated to us, saying: Abu Ja'far narrated to us, from al-Rabi', from Abu al-'Aliyah: ﴿Indeed, it is a cow neither broken﴾, that is, work has not made it docile. ﴿To plow the earth﴾, meaning: it is not docile so as to plow the earth. ﴿Nor to water the tilth﴾, he says: nor does it labour in the tilth.

1251 - I was told by Ammar, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi': ﴿Indeed, it is a cow neither broken﴾, he says: work has not made it docile. ﴿To plow the earth﴾, he says: it plows the earth with its hooves. [[In the printed edition: "tubayyin al-ard" (it makes the earth clear), which is a scribal error.]] ﴿Nor to water the tilth﴾, he says: it does not labour in the tilth.

1252 - al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, saying: Ibn Jurayj said, al-A'raj said, Mujahid said, regarding His saying: ﴿neither broken to plow the earth nor to water the tilth﴾, he says: it is not docile so as to do that.

1253 - al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Abu Sufyan narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: it is not docile to plow the earth nor to water the tilth.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: By His saying ﴿to plow the earth﴾ He means: to turn the earth for tilling. It is said of this: "athartu al-ard uthiruha ithara," when one turns the earth for planting.

And He, may His praise be exalted, described it with this attribute because it was, as has been said, wild.

1254 - Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Juwaybir informed us, from Kathir ibn Ziyad, from al-Hasan who said: it was wild. [[The report: 1254 - previously mentioned briefly as no. 1221.]]

* *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿sound﴾

Abu Ja'far said: The meaning of "musallamah" is "mufa'alah" from "al-salamah" (soundness). It is said of this: "sullimat, tasallamu, fa-hiya musallamah."

* *

Then the interpreters differed regarding the thing from which it was free, which Allah described it as being free from. Mujahid said that:

1255 - Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, from 'Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "musallamah," he says: free from blemish (shiyah), and ﴿no blemish in it﴾, no whiteness in it nor blackness.

1256 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, similarly.

1257 - al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Mujahid said: ﴿musallamah﴾, he said: free from blemish, ﴿no blemish in it﴾, no whiteness in it nor blackness.

* *

Others said: free from defects.

Mention of those who said this:

1258 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿sound, no blemish in it﴾, that is, free from defects.

1259 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah: ﴿sound﴾, he says: there is no defect in it.

1260 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Adam narrated to us, saying: Abu Ja'far narrated to us, from al-Rabi', from Abu al-'Aliyah: ﴿sound﴾, meaning free from defects.

1261 - I was told by Ammar, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi', similarly.

1262 - al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, saying: Ibn Jurayj said, Ibn 'Abbas said regarding His saying: ﴿sound﴾, there is no fault (awar) in it. [[al-awar (with fatha or damma on the ayn): defect.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: What Ibn 'Abbas and Abu al-'Aliyah said, and whoever said the same as them in interpreting this, is more correct as an interpretation of the verse than what Mujahid said. For if its soundness were from all types of colours other than the colour of its hide, then His saying ﴿sound﴾ would suffice without His saying ﴿no blemish in it﴾. And in His saying ﴿no blemish in it﴾ there is what clarifies that the meaning of His saying ﴿musallamah﴾ is other than the meaning of His saying ﴿no blemish in it﴾. Since this is so, the meaning of the statement is: it says, "Indeed, it is a cow that has not been made docile by plowing the earth and turning it for tillage, nor by irrigation for the fields, and it is, besides that, sound and free from defects."

* *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿no blemish in it﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His saying ﴿no blemish in it﴾ He means: no colour in it that differs from the colour of its hide. Its origin is from "washy al-thawb," which is embellishing its flaws that are in it with various kinds of colours of its warp and weft. [[al-sada: the lower part of the cloth; al-luhma: the upper part, which interlaces with the sada.]] It is said of this: "washaytu al-thawb fa-ana ashiyuhu shiyatan wa washyan," and from it is said of the one who informs on a man to the ruler or others: "wash" (informer), because of his lying about him before him, and his embellishing his lie with falsehoods. It is said of this: "washaytu bihi ila al-sultan wishayatan." And from it is the saying of Ka'b ibn Zuhayr:

The informers run at his flanks, and their saying: "Indeed, you, son of Abi Sulma, are to be killed." [[His Diwan: 19; Sirat Ibn Hisham 4: 153; al-Raw al-Anf 2: 314; al-Fa'iq (qahl). The Diwan reading is "bijanbayha" and Ibn Hisham's: "tasa al-ghuwat." The poet means the side of his camel, and "janab" means the side. "Janabayhi, janibayhi, janabayhi." The pronoun in "janabayha" refers to his she-camel mentioned earlier. "Wa qawluhum: innaka" is a circumstantial clause: they keep saying it, meaning they repeatedly say to him: "Indeed you, son of Abi Sulma, are to be killed," as if they say nothing else, to terrify and frighten him.]]

"Al-wushat" is the plural of "wash," meaning that they invent falsehoods and inform him that if he joins the Prophet ﷺ, he will be killed.

Some scholars of Arabic have claimed that "al-washy" means a mark. That has no meaning, unless he intended by it the embellishment of cloth with patterns, because it is known that one who says "I informed on so-and-so to so-and-so" cannot be supposed to mean that he made a mark for him with him.

It was said ﴿no blemish (shiyah) in it﴾ though it derives from "washaytu", because the "waw" was dropped from its beginning and the "ha'" was substituted at its end, as is said: "wazantuhu zinah" and "wasana sinah" [[In the printed edition: "wawasaytuhu siyah", which is a statement without basis; it appears to be a corruption of what is established here.] and "wa'adtuhu 'idah" and "wadaytuhu diyah".

* *

In accordance with what we have said regarding the meaning of His saying ﴿no blemish in it﴾, the people of interpretation said:

1263 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿no blemish in it﴾, that is, no whiteness in it.

1264 - al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, similarly.

1265 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Adam narrated to us, saying: Abu Ja'far narrated to us, from al-Rabi', from Abu al-'Aliyah: ﴿no blemish in it﴾, he says: no whiteness in it.

1266 - Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿no blemish in it﴾, that is, no whiteness in it nor blackness.

1267 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, similarly.

1268 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Idris narrated to us, from his father, from 'Atiyyah: ﴿no blemish in it﴾, he said: its colour is uniform; there is nothing in it other than its colour.

1269 - Musa narrated to me, saying: 'Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿no blemish in it﴾, neither whiteness, nor blackness, nor redness.

1270 - Yunus ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: ﴿no blemish in it﴾, it is yellow, with no whiteness nor blackness in it.

1271 - I was told by Ammar, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi': ﴿no blemish in it﴾, he says: no whiteness in it.

* *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿They said: Now you have brought the truth﴾

Abu Ja'far said: The interpreters differed regarding the interpretation of His saying: ﴿They said: Now you have brought the truth.﴾ Some of them said: the meaning of that is: "Now you have made the truth clear to us, so we understood it, and we knew which cow was meant." [[In the printed edition: "fa-tabayyanahu wa 'arafnahu annahu baqarah 'uyyinat", a corruption and a severe distortion, and very corrupt. Al-Tabari has already refuted, on p. 209, the view of those who claimed they thought they were commanded to slaughter a specific cow, so they asked him to describe it so they could recognise it, and he called the one who said that ignorant, and explained his ignorance. If God had "specified" it for them, He would have clarified what He specified when He commanded its slaughter.]] Among those who said this was Qatadah:

1272 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿They said: Now you have brought the truth﴾, that is: now you have made it clear to us.

* *

Others said: that is a report from Allah, may His praise be exalted, about the people, that they attributed to the Prophet of Allah Musa, may Allah's blessings be upon him, that he had not been bringing them the truth regarding the matter of the cow before that. Among those from whom this view is related is 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd:

1273 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: They were compelled to a cow for which they knew no description other than it, and it was yellow, with no black or white in it. So they said: this is the cow of so-and-so: ﴿Now you have brought the truth﴾, while before that, by God, he had brought them the truth. [[The report: 1273 - part of the report is 1247, and here is an addition completing it.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The more correct of the two interpretations in our view, regarding His saying ﴿They said: Now you have brought the truth﴾, is Qatadah's view: that its interpretation is: "Now you have made the truth clear to us regarding the matter of the cows, so we knew which of them it is obligatory for us to slaughter." Because Allah, may His praise be exalted, has informed of them that they then obeyed Him and slaughtered it after this statement, despite the heavy burden of slaughtering it upon them and the difficulty of the matter. He said: ﴿So they slaughtered it, though they had almost not done so﴾. Even if they said, by their statement "Now you have made the truth clear to us," idle words and erred out of ignorance: For the Prophet of Allah Musa ﷺ was making things clear to them in every question they asked him, and in every matter they raised regarding the cow, with the truth. And one says "Now you have made the truth clear to us" only to someone who had not made it clear before. As for one whose every statement, in what he makes known about Allah, is truth and clarity, it is not permissible to say to him, regarding some of what he makes known about Allah in His commands and prohibitions, and what he conveys from Him to His servants of His obligations upon them: ﴿Now you have brought the truth﴾, as if he had not brought them the truth before that!

* *

Some of the earlier scholars claimed that the people apostatised from their religion and disbelieved by their saying to Moses: ﴿Now you have brought the truth﴾, and claimed that they denied that Moses had brought them the truth regarding the cow before that, and that this act of theirs and their statement was disbelief.

What he said about this is not, in our view, as he said, because they submitted in obedience by slaughtering it, although their statement which they said to Moses was ignorance on their part and one of their blunders.

* *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿So they slaughtered it, though they had almost not done so (71)﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His saying ﴿So they slaughtered it﴾ He means: the people of Moses slaughtered the cow which Allah described to them and commanded them to slaughter.

By His saying ﴿though they had almost not done so﴾ He means: they came close to abandoning its slaughter and leaving aside the obligation Allah had placed upon them in that.

* *

Then the interpreters differed regarding the cause for which they almost failed to fulfil Allah's obligation upon them in slaughtering what He had commanded them to slaughter. Some said: that cause was the high price of the cow which they were commanded to slaughter, and which was described to them.

Mention of those who said this:

1274 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Abu Ma'shar al-Madani informed us, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi regarding His saying ﴿So they slaughtered it, though they had almost not done so﴾, he said: because of its high price.

1275 - Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Ubayd al-Hilali narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn al-Khattab narrated to us, saying: Abu Ma'shar narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi: ﴿So they slaughtered it, though they had almost not done so﴾, he said: because of the greatness of its value. [[The report: 1275 - Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Ubayd ibn 'Aqil al-Hilali, Tabari's teacher: reliable; Abu Dawud, al-Nasa'i, Ibn Majah and others also narrated from him. Listed in al-Tahdhib, and I have found no biography of him elsewhere. 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn al-Khattab al-Kufi Abu al-Hasan: reliable; Abu Zur'ah, Abu Hatim and others narrated from him, listed in al-Tahdhib, and Ibn Abi Hatim 2/2/381. Abu Ma'shar: he is Najih, with the nun vowelled with fatha, ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Sindi, with the sin vowelled with kasra, al-Madani, and he is weak. Al-Bukhari in al-Kabir 4/2/114 said: "munkar al-hadith" (his narrations are rejected); Ibn Abi Hatim 4/1/495. Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi: a well-known reliable Successor.]]

1276 - al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn informed us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, and Hajjaj, from Abu Ma'shar, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi and Muhammad ibn Qays, in a long report in which the report of one of them entered into the report of another, regarding His saying ﴿So they slaughtered it, though they had almost not done so﴾, because of the high price: they took it for the filling of its hide with gold from the property of the murdered man. [[al-misk (with fatha then sukun): the hide of the cow or other animal.]] So it was as if there were no excess, and they slaughtered it.

1277 - I was told by al-Minjab, saying: Bishr ibn 'Imarah narrated to us, from Abu Rawq, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿So they slaughtered it, though they had almost not done so﴾, he says: they almost did not do it, and what they wanted did not happen, because they wanted not to slaughter it. And every word in the Qur'an with "kada" or "kadu" or "law" means it will not happen. It is like His saying: ﴿I almost conceal it﴾ [Ta-Ha: 15].

* *

Others said: they almost did not do that out of fear of disgrace, if Allah revealed the killer of the slain man about whom they disputed before Moses.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct interpretation in our view is that the people almost did not do what Allah commanded them, the slaughter of the cow, for both reasons together: one, the high price of it, along with what was reported to us of its small worth and low value; the other, the great fear of disgrace upon themselves, by Allah's exposing of His Prophet Musa, may Allah's blessings be upon him, and his followers, regarding its killer.

* *

As for the high price, various reports have been transmitted to us about it.

1278 - Musa ibn Harun narrated to me, saying: 'Amr ibn Hammad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi who said: They bought it for ten times its weight in gold, and its owner sold it to them and took its price.

1279 - Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: al-Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman narrated to us, saying: I heard Ayyub, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, from 'Ubaydah who said: They bought it for the filling of its hide with dinars.

1280 - Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid who said: The cow belonged to a man who was dutiful to his mother, so Allah granted him that the cow became his, and he sold it for its hide filled with gold.

1281 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, saying: Khalid ibn Yazid narrated to me, from Mujahid who said: They gave its owner the filling of its hide with gold, and he sold it to them.

1282 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Isma'il ibn 'Abd al-Karim narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Samad ibn Ma'qil narrated to me that he heard Wahb say: They bought it from him on condition that they would fill its hide with dinars. Then they slaughtered it, and they took the hide of the cow and filled it with dinars, then handed it to him.

**1283** - Muhammad ibn Sa'd told me, saying: My father told me, saying: My paternal uncle told me [[In the printed edition: "Muhammad ibn Sa'id said: My father told me, saying: Yahya told me." This is an error; the correct reading is what I have recorded. This isnad has already been discussed at 1:263-264, and it recurs frequently in Tafsir al-Tabari. It will come again below as no. 1290, in its correct form.]], saying: My father told me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: They found it with a man who claimed that he would never sell it for any money. So they kept at him until they offered him that they would flay its hide and fill it for him with gold dinars. He agreed to this, and they gave it to them.

**1284** - al-Muthanna told me, saying: Adam told us, saying: Abu Ja'far told us, from al-Rabi', from Abu al-'Aliyah, who said: They did not find it except with an old woman, and she asked them for many times its price. Then Musa said to them: "Give her what satisfies her and what she judges." So they did this, bought it, and slaughtered it.

**1285** - al-Hasan ibn Yahya told us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, saying: Ayyub said, from Ibn Sirin, from 'Ubaydah, who said: They did not find this cow except with one man, and he sold it for its weight in gold, or for gold filling its hide, and they slaughtered it.

**1286** - al-Muthanna told me, saying: Adam told us, saying: Abu Ja'far told us, from Hisham ibn Hassan, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, from 'Ubaydah al-Salmani, who said: They found the cow with a man, and he said: "I will not sell it except for its hide filled with gold." So they bought it for its hide filled with gold.

**1287** - Yunus told me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: They kept raising the price for its owner until they filled for him its hide, which is its skin, with gold.

* *

As for the smallness of its value and the lowness of its price, al-Hasan ibn Yahya [reports]:

**1288** - He told us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq told us, saying: Ibn 'Uyaynah informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Suqah told me, from Ikrimah, who said: Its price was only three dinars.

As for what we have said about their fear of disgrace for themselves, Wahb ibn Munabbih used to say: When the people were commanded to slaughter the cow, they only said to Musa: ﴿Do you take us in mockery?﴾, because they knew that they would be disgraced if it were slaughtered, so they evaded slaughtering it.

**1289** - This was related to me from Isma'il ibn 'Abd al-Karim, from 'Abd al-Samad ibn Ma'qil, from Wahb ibn Munabbih.

Ibn 'Abbas used to say: The people, after God had brought the dead man to life and he informed them of his killer, denied the killing, saying: "By God, we did not kill him," after they had seen the sign and the truth.

**1290** - Muhammad ibn Sa'd told me of this, saying: My father told me, saying: My paternal uncle told me, saying: My father told me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 72:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿And when you killed a soul and then disputed about it﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His words, may His praise be majestic, ﴿And when you killed a soul﴾, He means: and remember, O Children of Israel, when you killed a soul. The "soul" they killed is the soul whose story we mentioned in the interpretation of His words: ﴿And when Moses said to his people, "Indeed, Allah commands you to slaughter a cow"﴾.

* *

As for His words ﴿then disputed about it﴾, He means: they differed and contended. It is actually "tadara'tum fihā" (fa-tadārra'tum) on the pattern of "tafā'altum", from al-darr' (الدرء). Al-darr' means crookedness, and from it is the statement of Abu al-Najm al-'Ijli:

Fearing a fierce one, when he attacks boldly... he devours the one of crookedness and expels the one who is low [[I did not find the verse in its place; it was in the printed edition as: "khashyat ṭaghām idhā hamm ḥasar..." which is a corrupt text. Al-ḍaghām is from al-ḍaghm: that one fills his mouth with whatever he desires. "Jasara jusūran and jasāra" means he proceeded and pressed on out of intensity of his boldness.]]

meaning: the one of crookedness and difficulty. From it is the statement of Ru'bah ibn al-'Ajjaj:

I overtook them before every champion, repelling from me the darr' of every arrogant one [[From his Diwan, p. 166, from a poem in which he describes himself. The pronoun in "adraktuhā" refers to what preceded in his rajaz. And a dispute that is not a speech of the ...

As for His words "ḥaqqah", it means a dispute, a quarrel, a boasting, or what resembles that. The mudarrih is the one who defends and comes forward in a dispute, with tongue or hand. The 'anjah and 'anjahī is the one of pride and grandeur to the point of nearly reaching ignorance and folly, and from it comes 'anjahiyyah.]] And from it is the report that:

1291 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Mus'ab ibn al-Miqdam narrated to us, from Isra'il, from Ibrahim ibn al-Muhajir, from Mujahid, from al-Sa'ib, who said: Uthman and Zuhayr, the two sons of Umayya, came to me and asked permission for me to enter upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I know him better than you two. Were you not my partner in the Jahiliyyah?" I said: "Yes, may my father and mother be your ransom! You were an excellent partner: you did not dispute and did not hide things from me [wa-lā tudārī]."

[[The hadith: 1291 – There is weakness in this chain, and the hadith itself has confusion, as will come. Abu Kurayb: Muhammad ibn al-'Ala' ibn Kurayb al-Hafiz, a great trustworthy narrator, among the teachers of the authors of the Six Books, from whom al-Tabari narrated much. He died in 248. Mus'ab ibn al-Miqdam al-Khath'ami: trustworthy, though some criticised him; Muslim included him in his Sahih; biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir of al-Bukhari 4/1/354, and Ibn Abi Hatim 4/1/308. Isra'il: Ibn Yunus ibn Abi Ishaq al-Sabi'i, a known trustworthy and memorising narrator. Ibrahim ibn al-Muhajir ibn Jabir al-Bajali: trustworthy, though spoken of by some without proof; Muslim narrated from him. Biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir of al-Bukhari 1/1/328, where he states he heard Mujahid, and Ibn Abi Hatim 1/1/132–133. Al-Sa'ib: a Companion, as is apparent from this and other hadith, though much disputed. It was said: "al-Sa'ib ibn Abi al-Sa'ib Sayfi ibn 'A'idh"; it was said: "al-Sa'ib ibn 'Abd Allah al-Makhzumi"; it was even said: "Qays ibn al-Sa'ib"! What al-Bukhari affirmed in al-Kabir 2/2/152 and limited himself to: "al-Sa'ib ibn Abi al-Sa'ib al-Qurashi al-Makki, who has companionship." Ibn Abi Hatim did likewise, 2/1/242, and said: "Some say he has companionship, and some say his father had companionship. Mujahid narrated from him. It is said he is a mawla of Mujahid from above." In al-Isabah 3:60, citing Ibn Abi Shaybah, it is reported through Yunus ibn Khabbab from Mujahid: "I used to lead al-Sa'ib, and he would say to me: O Mujahid..." Had this been sound, the continuity of the chain would be established, but Yunus ibn Khabbab is weak.

The hadith was narrated by Ahmad in al-Musnad: 15566 (3:425, Halabi) with similar meaning, with additions and omissions, from Aswad ibn 'Amir, from Isra'il, from Ibrahim ibn al-Muhajir, from Mujahid, "from al-Sa'ib ibn 'Abd Allah." Then he narrated after it something similar, in meaning, lengthy and abridged, through several chains, and in some of them: "from Mujahid, from the leader of al-Sa'ib, from al-Sa'ib."

Abu Dawud narrated, 4836, something similar, through al-Thawri, from Ibrahim ibn al-Muhajir, from Mujahid, from the leader of al-Sa'ib, from al-Sa'ib. Al-Mundhiri said in Tahdhib al-Sunan: 4669, "It was also narrated by al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah... This hadith has been greatly disputed in its chain." Abu 'Umar Yusuf ibn 'Abd al-Barr al-Namari mentioned that this hadith is extremely confused... This confusion does not sustain a proof.

An error has occurred in the text of this hadith here, and we do not know whether it is from the transmission or from the copyists. That is his saying: "Uthman and Zuhayr, the two sons of Umayya came to me." No one among the Companions is named by this or that. The correct version is what is in the Musnad narration 15566: "Uthman ibn 'Affan and Zuhayr brought me." Zuhayr is Ibn Abi Umayya, brother of Umm Salamah, the Mother of the Believers, and she is the daughter of Abu Umayya. As al-Isabah 3:13–14 explains, when it said: "Ibn Mandah narrated through Mujahid, from al-Sa'ib, partner of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who said: Uthman and Zuhayr ibn Abi Umayya took me..."

See the Nasab Quraysh of al-Mus'ab, p. 333, where he affirmed that "al-Sa'ib ibn Abi al-Sa'ib Sayfi" was killed at Badr as a disbeliever; see also the reference to the origin of the story in al-Isabah 3:13–14, 60, and 4:74, and 5:253–254. The matter still needs verification and research.]] By his saying "lā tudārī" he means: you did not oppose your companion and partner, nor dispute with him, nor contend with him.

* *

The original form of ﴿fa-dārā'tum﴾ is "fa-tadārā'tum", but the tā' is close in articulation to the dāl: the tā' is produced from the tip of the tongue and the roots of the lips, while the dāl is produced from the tip of the tongue and the tips of the upper incisors. So the tā' was assimilated into the dāl, making it a doubled dāl, as the poet said:

She turns from her bedfellow when he sniffs her, a slender one... sweet in taste when the kisses follow one another [[I do not know its speaker. It will come in 10:94 (Bulaq). In the printed edition here it reads "ishtāqahā", which is an error; the correct reading is what I have set down from there. Sāfa al-shay' yasūfuhu sawfan and istāfahu: he approached it and smelled it. He used it metaphorically for kissing, as they used smelling for kissing, because the nearness of the nose precedes what the seeker desires. Al-Ra'i said, describing kissing: he bends his mosaddiqatuhā... (the poetic verse is cited). Al-Zamakhshari said: "sāwafatahā" means he lay with her, but in the line it is the one who kisses.]]

He means: when kisses follow one another. So one of the two tā's was assimilated into the other. When the tā' was assimilated into the dāl, making it a dāl like it, it became quiescent, so they brought in an alif to be able to pronounce it, and this is when there is something before it, because assimilation occurs only when something precedes it. From it is the saying of God, may His praise be majestic: ﴿until, when they have all overtaken one another therein﴾ [al-A'raf: 38]; it is actually "tadārakū", but the tā' in it was assimilated into the dāl, so it became a doubled dāl, and an alif was added to it when it was connected to what preceded it, so that the assimilation would be sound. If nothing precedes it, and it is begun with, one says "tadārakū" and "tathāqalū", showing the assimilation. It has also been said that one says "idārakū" and "idārā'ū".

It has been said that the meaning of His words ﴿fa-dārā'tum fīhā﴾ is: "fa-tadāfa'tum fīhā" (you pushed one another away concerning it), from the saying of one who says: "darra'tu hādhā al-amr 'annī" (I pushed this matter away from me), and from God's words: ﴿and it turns away from her the punishment﴾ [al-Nur: 8], meaning: it repels from her the punishment. This saying is close in meaning to the first saying, because the people only pushed away the killing of the slain, so each party denied that it was their killer, as we have explained before in this book of ours. [[See what passed, numbers 1172, 1180.]] The people of interpretation said in a manner close to what we have said regarding the meaning of His words ﴿fa-dārā'tum fīhā﴾.

1292 - Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to me, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning God's words ﴿fa-dārā'tum fīhā﴾, he said: You differed concerning it.

1293 - al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

1294 - al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj: ﴿And when you killed a soul and then disputed about it﴾. Some of them said: You killed him. The others said: You killed him.

1295 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said concerning His words ﴿fa-dārā'tum fīhā﴾: they differed, and it is contention; they contended about it. These said: You killed him. These said: No.

* *

Their dispute concerning the slain soul was as follows:

1296 - Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, from 'Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: The owner of the cow was a man from the Children of Israel; a man killed him and threw him at the door of other people. The heirs of the slain came and claimed his blood against them, and they disavowed it — or they repudiated it — from him. Abu 'Asim was uncertain. [[intafala min al-shay': he disowned it and disclaimed it, and denied that he had done it or known of it. In a hadith of Ibn 'Umar: "Indeed so-and-so disowned his child" meaning he disclaimed him.]]

1297 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same exactly, except that he said: they claimed his blood against them, and they disowned him — without doubt.

1298 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, who said: There was a slain man among the Children of Israel. Each tribe cast it upon [a tribe with it], until strife grew severe among them, until they took the matter to the Prophet of God ﷺ. God revealed to Moses: "Slaughter a cow and strike him with part of it." It was mentioned to us that his heir, who was seeking his blood, was the one who had killed him, because of an inheritance that was between them.

1299 - Ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas concerning the matter of the cow. An old man from the Children of Israel in the time of Moses had much wealth, and his brother's sons were poor with no wealth, and the old man had no child, and his brother's sons were his heirs. They said: Would that our uncle would die so we could inherit his wealth! When his not dying seemed long to them, Satan came to them and said: Would you like to kill your uncle, so you inherit his wealth, and make the people of the city in which you are not to pay his blood-money? — for there were two cities, and they were in one of them, and when the slain was killed and cast between the two cities, the distance between the slain and the two cities was measured, and whichever was nearer to him had to pay the blood-money. When Satan adorned this for them, and his not dying seemed long to them, they went to him and killed him, then they went and cast him at the gate of the city in which they were not. When the people of the city awoke, the sons of the old man's brother came and said: Our uncle has been killed at the gate of your city; by God, you must pay us our uncle's blood-money. The people of the city said: We swear by God we did not kill him, nor did we know a killer, nor did we open the gate of our city since it was closed until we woke up. They went to Moses. When they came, the sons of the old man's brother said: We found our uncle killed at the gate of their city. The people of the city said: We swear by God we did not kill him, nor did we open the gate of the city from the time we closed it until we woke. Gabriel came with the command of our Lord, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, to Moses, and said: Tell them: Indeed God commands you to slaughter a cow and strike him with part of it.

1300 - al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid — and Hajjaj from Abu Ma'shar, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi and Muhammad ibn Qays — the narrations of some entered into the narrations of others. They said: A tribe of the Children of Israel, when they saw the great evil of people, built a city and withdrew from the evils of people. When they evened, they did not leave anyone of them outside without admitting him, and when they awoke, their leader stood, looked, and surveyed [[tashrafa al-shay' and istashrafa: he placed his hand over his brow as one who shades from the sun, until he sees it and makes it clear.]] If he saw nothing, he opened the city, and they were with the people until evening. A man from the Children of Israel had much wealth, and he had no heir except his brother's son. His life lasted long for him, so he killed him to inherit him, then carried him and placed him at the gate of the city, then lay in ambush in a place with his companions. The leader of the city surveyed the gate of the city, looked, and saw nothing. He opened the gate, and when he saw the slain, he closed the gate again. The son of the slain man and his companions called out to him: Far from it! You killed him, then you close the gate? Moses, when he saw many killings among his companions, the Children of Israel [perhaps the correct reading is "kathura fī aṣḥābihi"], whenever he saw a slain man among the people, he took them to account. Fighting almost broke out between the brother of the slain and the people of the city, until both parties put on weapons, then some of them held back from others. They came to Moses and told him their affair, saying: O Messenger of God, these people killed a slain man, then closed the gate. The people of the city said: O Messenger of God, you know our withdrawal from evils, and we built a city, as you have seen, to withdraw from the evils of people; we did not kill, nor did we know a killer. God, may His remembrance be exalted, revealed to him that they should slaughter a cow. Moses said to them: Indeed God commands you to slaughter a cow.

1301 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Adam narrated to us, saying: Abu Ja'far narrated to us, from Hisham ibn Hassan, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, from 'Ubaydah, who said: There was among the Children of Israel a childless man who had much wealth. A nephew of his killed him, dragged him, and threw him at the door of other people.

Then they woke, and he claimed it against them, until these and those armed themselves, and they wanted to fight. The men of wisdom among them said: Will you fight while the Prophet of God is among you? They held back until they came to Moses and related the story to him. He commanded them to slaughter a cow and strike him with part of it. They said: Do you make us a laughingstock? He said: I seek refuge in God from being among the ignorant.

1302 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: A slain man of the Children of Israel was cast into one of the tribes. The people of that tribe came to that tribe and said: By God, you killed our companion. They said: No, by God. They came to Moses and said: This is our slain among them, and by God they killed him. They said: No, by God, O Prophet of God, he was cast upon us. Moses ﷺ said to them: Indeed God commands you to slaughter a cow.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: Their disagreement, their contention, and their quarrel among themselves regarding the affair of the slain man we have mentioned, as we have narrated from our scholars among the people of interpretation, is the "darr'" that God, may His praise be majestic, spoke of to their descendants and the remnants of their children: ﴿and then disputed about it, and God is bringing out what you were concealing﴾.

* *

The interpretation of His words: ﴿And God is bringing out what you were concealing﴾ (72)

Abu Ja'far said: By His words ﴿And God is bringing out what you were concealing﴾, He means: God is making manifest what you were hiding of the killing of the slain, which you killed, and then disputed about.

* *

The meaning of "ikhrāj" (bringing out) in this place is making manifest and announcing to whoever was unaware of it, and informing them of it, as God, may His remembrance be exalted, said: ﴿Why do they not prostrate to God, who brings forth what is hidden in the heavens and the earth?﴾ [al-Naml: 25], meaning: He brings it out and makes it appear from its concealment after its hiddenness.

* *

What they were concealing and He brought forth is the killing of the slain by the killer. When that killer and those who sided with him concealed that, until God manifested and brought it out, and announced its affair to whoever did not know its affair.

* *

By His words ﴿tukhtafūn/tukhtamūn﴾ [tukhtamūn], may His remembrance be exalted, means: you conceal and hide, as:

1303 - Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning God's words ﴿And God is bringing out what you were concealing﴾, he said: you hide.

1304 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿what you were concealing﴾, what you were hiding.

**The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿So We said, "Strike him with part of it."﴾**

Abu Ja'far said: By His words, exalted is His mention, "So We said" to the people of Musa (Moses) who disputed concerning the slain person [[In the printed edition: ". . by His words, 'So We said to the people of Musa,' and the correct reading is to add the wording of the verse, as I have done.]], whose matter we have already described, "Strike him," meaning: strike the slain person. The "hu" (him) in His words ﴿Strike him﴾ refers to the slain person. ﴿With part of it﴾ means with part of the cow which Allah had commanded them to slaughter, and they slaughtered it.

* *

Then the scholars differed concerning the part of the cow with which the slain person was struck, and which limb of it that was. Some of them said: he was struck with the thigh of the cow.

Those who said this:

1305 - He related to me Muhammad ibn 'Amr, who said: He related to us Abu 'Asim, who said: He related to us 'Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: He was struck with the thigh of the cow, and he rose alive and said, "So-and-so killed me." Then he returned to his death.

1306 - He related to me al-Muthanna, who said: He related to us Abu Hudhayfa, who said: He related to us Shibl, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: He was struck with the thigh of the cow, and then he mentioned the like of it.

1307 - Abu Kurayb related to us, who said: Jabir ibn Nuh related to us, from al-Nadr ibn 'Arabi, from 'Ikrima: ﴿So We said, "Strike him with part of it,"﴾ he said: with its thigh. When he was struck with it, he came to life and said, "So-and-so killed me." Then he returned to his former state. [[The report 1307: al-Nadr ibn 'Arabi al-Bahili: a trustworthy (thiqa) of the generation after the Followers; Ibn Ma'in and others declared him trustworthy; he died in the year 168. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib, in al-Kabir of al-Bukhari 4/2/89, and in Ibn Abi Hatim 4/1/475.]]

1308 - He related to me al-Muthanna, who said: He related to us Abu Hudhayfa, who said: He related to us Shibl, from Khalid ibn Yazid, from Mujahid, who said: The man was struck with its thigh, and he rose alive and said, "So-and-so killed me." Then he returned to his death.

1309 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, who said: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, who said: Ma'mar informed us, who said: Ayyub said, from Ibn Sirin, from 'Ubayda: They struck the slain man with some of its flesh. [And Ma'mar said, from Qatada:] They struck him with the flesh of the thigh, and he came to life and said, "So-and-so killed me."

1310 - Bishr related to us, who said: Yazid related to us, who said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, who said: It was mentioned to us that they struck him with its thigh, and Allah revived him, and he informed them of his killer who had slain him, and he spoke, and then he died.

* *

And others said: The part with which they struck him from it was the piece of flesh between the shoulders. [[al-Bid'a: a piece of flesh; their saying "bada'a al-lahm" means he cut it.]]

Those who said this:

1311 - Musa related to me, who said: 'Amr related to us, who said: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿So We said, "Strike him with part of it,"﴾ so they struck him with the piece of flesh between the shoulders, and he came to life. They asked him, "Who killed you?" He said to them, "My nephew."

And others said: The part with which they were commanded to strike him from it was a bone of its bones.

Those who said this:

1312 - al-Muthanna related to me, who said: Adam related to us, who said: Abu Ja'far related to us, from al-Rabi', from Abu al-'Aliya, who said: Musa commanded them to take a bone from it and strike the slain man with it. They did so, and his soul returned to him, and he named for them his killer; then he returned dead as he was. So they seized his killer, and he was the one who came to Musa and complained to him, and Allah killed him for his evil deed.

* *

And others said something else:

1313 - Yunus ibn 'Abd al-A'la related it to me, who said: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd said: They struck the dead man with some of its limbs, and he was sitting up. [[Arab (plural of irb, with a kasra and sukun): a limb; it is said "qata'ahu irban irban," meaning he cut it limb by limb.]] They said, "Who killed you?" He said, "My nephew." He said: And his killing and throwing him down was on that path; he wanted to take his blood-money.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct statement regarding the interpretation of His words, in our view, ﴿So We said, "Strike him with part of it,"﴾ is that it should be said: Allah, exalted is His praise, commanded them to strike the slain man with part of the cow, so that the one struck would come to life. There is no indication in the verse, nor in any report on which a proof could rest, [the parenthetical addition is preferable to omitting it] as to which of its parts the people were commanded to strike the slain man with. It is permissible that the part they were commanded to strike him with was the thigh, and it is permissible that it was the tail, and the cartilage of the shoulder, and other of its parts. Ignorance of which of these they struck the slain man with does no harm, and knowledge of it brings no benefit, given the affirmation that the people struck the slain man with part of the cow after slaughtering it, and Allah revived him.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: If someone says: What was the meaning of the command to strike the slain man with part of it? It is said: So that he would come to life and inform the Prophet of Allah Musa (ﷺ) and those who disputed concerning him, of his killer.

If someone says: And where is the report that Allah, exalted is His praise, commanded them to do that for that purpose? It is said: That is omitted, being sufficient with the indication of what has been mentioned of the speech that points to it, like what we have mentioned of its parallels in the past. The meaning of the speech: "So We said: Strike him with part of it, so that he may live," and they struck him and he was revived, as His words, exalted is His praise, say: ﴿Strike the sea with your staff, and it parted﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 63], the meaning being: he struck and it parted. What indicates this is His words: [In the printed edition: "indicates this His words," which is not right.] ﴿Thus Allah gives life to the dead, and shows you His signs, that you may understand.﴾

* *

**The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Thus Allah gives life to the dead﴾**

Abu Ja'far said: His words, ﴿Thus Allah gives life to the dead,﴾ are an address from Allah to His believing servants, and a proof from Him against the polytheists who denied the Resurrection, and a command to them to take lesson from what Allah, exalted is His praise, did in reviving the slain man of the Children of Israel after his death in this world. He, exalted is His mention, said to them: O you who deny resurrection after death, take lesson from My reviving this slain man after his death; for just as I revived him in this world, so I revive the dead after their death, and I will resurrect them on the Day of Resurrection.

Allah, exalted is His mention, only argued with this against the polytheists of Arabia [In the printed edition: "So He only argued. . ," where the fa' is not right here], who were an unlettered people with no scripture, because those among the Children of Israel who knew this knowledge were among them, and these verses were revealed among them. So He, exalted is His mention, informed them of this, that they might learn the knowledge from those who preceded them.

* *

**The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿and He shows you His signs, that you may understand﴾**

Abu Ja'far said: He, exalted is His mention, means: and Allah shows you, O disbelievers who deny Muhammad (ﷺ) and what he brought from Allah, of His signs. And His signs are His indications and His proofs which show His prophethood [see what has passed, 1:552, and this part, 2:139], ﴿that you may understand﴾ and comprehend that he is truthful and sincere, so that you may believe in him and follow him.

* *

**The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Then your hearts hardened after that﴾**

Abu Ja'far said: By this He means the disbelievers among the Children of Israel, who, as it is mentioned, were the nephews of the slain man. So He said to them, "Then your hearts hardened": that is, they became dry, coarse, and stiff, as the rajiz said:

*And I have hardened, and my contemporaries have hardened* [[I do not know its speaker; it will come at 6:99 (Bulaq). In the original here it read "wa-qasa ladanā," which is an error. Ladāt is the plural of ladda; the ladda of a man is his peer, the one born with him. Qasa here means: aged, grown old, and his youth passed, and his stalk dried out. This meaning is not found in the lexicons.]]

It is said: "qasa," " 'asa," and "'ata" with one meaning, which is when it becomes harsh, coarse, and hard. It is said of it: qasa his heart yaqsu qasaw, qasawa, qasawa, and qasa'. [[I am in doubt about the vocalization of the first of these four verbal nouns, which is "qasuw," and I followed the vocalization in al-Qamus al-Muhit, although it was vocalized with the pen, and I fear that it may be a verbal noun on the pattern "fu'ul," like dana yadnu dunuwwan, and sama yasmu sumuwwan.]]

* *

By His words, "from after that," He means: after He revived the dead man for them, the one whose killing they disputed, and He informed them of his killer and the cause for which he was killed, as we have already described, according to what the reports and accounts have transmitted; and Allah, exalted is His mention, separated by His news between the truthful among them and the falsifier [the wording without a break: "after He revived the dead man for them. . and separated by His news between the truthful among them and the falsifier"]. The hardness of their hearts with which Allah described them was that they, as has reached us, denied that they had killed the slain man whom Allah revived, so He informed the Children of Israel that they were the killers, after His informing them of that, and after his second death, as follows:

1314 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, who said: My father related to me, who said: My paternal uncle related to me, who said: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: When the dead man was struck with part of it, meaning part of the cow, he sat up alive, and it was said to him, "Who killed you?" He said, "The sons of my nephew killed me." Then he died, and the sons of his nephew said when he died: "By Allah, we did not kill him!" So they disbelieved in the truth after they had seen it. And Allah said: ﴿Then your hearts hardened after that﴾ — meaning the sons of the old man's nephew — ﴿so they are like stones, or even harder in hardness.﴾

1315 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh related to us, who said: Yazid related to us, from Sa'id, from Qatada: ﴿Then your hearts hardened after that,﴾ he says: after what Allah had shown them of the reviving of the dead, and after what He had shown them of the matter of the slain man — what He showed them — ﴿so they are like stones, or even harder in hardness.﴾

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 74 (part 1 of 2):

The discourse on the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Then your hearts became hardened after that, so they were like rocks or even harder in hardness﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His words ﴿then they were﴾ He means "your hearts." He says: Then your hearts became hard, after you had seen the truth, distinguished it and recognized it, refusing to submit to it and to acknowledge the binding right of God upon you. So your hearts are like rocks in hardness, dryness, coarseness and severity, ﴿or even harder in hardness﴾, meaning: their hearts, in refusing to submit to the binding right of God upon them and to acknowledge the rights He is owed from them, are harder in hardness than rocks. [[In the printed edition this sentence read as follows: "like rocks in hardness, dryness, coarseness and severity, or harder in hardness, meaning your hearts in refusing to submit to the binding right of God upon them, and acknowledging what is owed to Him of their rights, from the rocks." This appears to be a copyist's error, and I have restored it to its original form, praise be to God.]]
* *
If a questioner asks: What is the meaning of His words ﴿so they were like rocks or even harder in hardness﴾, given that "or" in the view of the grammarians (ahl al-'arabiyya) is used in speech to express doubt, and God, exalted is His remembrance, may not be described as doubtful in what He reports?
It is said: That is not in the manner you imagine, that it is doubt on God's part, exalted is His remembrance, concerning what He reports. Rather it is a report from Him about their hearts, which are hard: that they, in the sight of His servants who are their owners, those who denied the truth after seeing the great signs of God, are like rocks in hardness, or harder than rocks, in the sight of those servants and in the sight of those who know their condition.
* *
Some of the grammarians (ahl al-'arabiyya) have stated several views on this. Some of them said: God, His praise is mighty, by His words ﴿so they were like rocks or even harder in hardness﴾, and similar reports that come with "or", such as His words: ﴿And We sent him to a hundred thousand or more﴾ [al-Saffat: 147], and the words of God, exalted is His remembrance: ﴿And indeed we or you are surely upon guidance or in clear error﴾ [Saba': 24], intend concealment from the one addressed [[al-Lisan (s-k-n): "ghalahu al-shay' yaghulahu" means: it took him away so that you do not know where he is; and ajanna means: he concealed and hid]], so He knows which of these it is. They said: The parallel to this is the statement of a speaker: "I ate a green date or a ripe date," and he knows which one he ate, but he concealed it from the addressee. [[What is between the brackets is an addition that is necessary for the sentence to be sound; I inferred it from what follows, "but he obscured it from the addressee," and from Ibn Kathir's tafsir 1: 209, 210.]] As Abu al-Aswad al-Du'ali said:

I love Muhammad with an intense love, and 'Abbas, and Hamza, and the successor (al-Wasiyy)
If their love is right guidance, I attain it, and I am not mistaken if it is error.

[[Diwan: 32 (from the rare manuscripts); al-Aghani 11: 113; Inbah al-Ruwat 1: 17; the second line alone will appear later at 22: 65 (Bulaq); the Diwan's version reads: "And among them is an exemplar, if it was misguidance."]]

They said: There is no doubt that Abu al-Aswad was not uncertain that the love of those he named was right guidance, but he obscured it from the one he addressed. It is mentioned of Abu al-Aswad that when he recited these verses it was said to him: "You have doubted!" He said: "Not at all, by God!" Then he cited the words of God, mighty and majestic: ﴿And indeed we or you are surely upon guidance or in clear error﴾, and said: "Was the one who reported this uncertain about the guided one versus the one in error?" [[His words "about the guided one versus the one in error" mean His Prophet ﷺ. The wording in al-Aghani is: "Do you think God, mighty and majestic, doubted about His Prophet?"]]
* *
Some of them said: This is like the statement of a speaker: "I did not feed you except something sweet or sour," when he has in fact fed him both kinds. They said: The speaker of that was not uncertain that he had fed his companion both the sweet and the sour, but he intended to report that what he fed him did not fall outside these two kinds. They said: Likewise His words ﴿so they were like rocks or even harder in hardness﴾ mean: their hearts do not fall outside one of these two comparisons, either they are a likeness of rocks in hardness, or they are harder than them in hardness. The meaning according to this interpretation is: some of them are like rocks in hardness, and some of them are harder than rocks in hardness.

Some of them said: "or" in His words ﴿or even harder in hardness﴾ has the sense of "and," meaning "and harder in hardness," as the Blessed and Exalted said: ﴿And do not obey from among them a sinner or a disbeliever﴾ [al-Insan: 24], meaning "and a disbeliever." And as Jarir ibn 'Atiyya said:

He attained the caliphate, or it was for him a decree,
As his Lord came to Moses at a measure.

[[The earlier occurrence and takhrij of this line is at 1: 337.]]

meaning: he attained the caliphate, and it was for him a decree. And as al-Nabigha said:

She said: "Would that this dove were ours,
to our dove, or half of it, [would be] enough."

[[Diwan: 32, and its version there is "wa-nisfuhu." It is from his well-known poem in which he apologizes to al-Nu'man. The pronoun in "she said" refers to "the girl of the tribe," mentioned in a poem before it, and she is Zarqa' al-Yamama. It is a well-known report, and we will not lengthen by mentioning it.]]

He means: "and half of it."
* *
Others said: "or" in this place has the sense of "bal" (rather), so its interpretation for them is: "so they were like rocks, rather even harder in hardness," as His words, praise be to Him, ﴿And We sent him to a hundred thousand or more﴾ [al-Saffat: 147] mean: "rather they are more."
* *
Others said: The meaning is: "so they were like rocks, or harder in hardness in your sight."
* *
Abu Ja'far said: Each of the views we have related has an aspect and an exit in the speech of the Arabs. However, the most preferable of these views to me is what we stated first, and then the view we mentioned from those who interpreted it to mean: "so they were more intense in hardness: either they are like rocks, or harder," [[In the printed edition: "so they were more intense in hardness than being like rocks or harder." I have adopted this correction from what preceded and from his later interpretation, placing "immā" in place of "min."]] with the interpretation that some of them are like rocks and some of them are harder in hardness. This is because "or," although it is used in some places where "waw" (and) is used, so that its meaning and the meaning of "waw" become confused, due to the closeness of their meanings in some of those places [[See what preceded at 1: 327–328]], its origin is to come in the sense of one of two. Directing it to its origin is, as far as we have found a way to it, more preferable to me than removing it from its origin and its known meaning.
* *
Abu Ja'far said: As for the raising (nominative case) in His words ﴿or harder in hardness﴾, it is in two ways. One: that it is a conjunction upon the meaning of the "kaf" in His words ﴿like rocks﴾, because its meaning is the meaning of "like," so its interpretation is: "so they are like rocks, or harder in hardness than rocks."

The other way: that it is nominative upon repetition of "hiya" (they/it) before it, so its interpretation becomes: "so they are like rocks, or they are harder in hardness than rocks."
* *
The discourse on the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And indeed among the rocks is that from which rivers gush forth﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His words, exalted is His remembrance: ﴿And indeed among the rocks is that from which rivers gush forth﴾: And indeed among the rocks are rocks from which water gushes forth, from which rivers come into being; so mention of the rivers dispenses with mention of the water. [[In the printed edition: "mention of the water dispenses with mention of the rivers," which is a clear error.]] He said "from it" (minhu) with regard to the word "mā" (that which). [[In the printed edition: "He said 'it was mentioned' (dhukira faqila)," which is meaningless.]]
* *
And "tafajjur" is the form "tafa''ul" from "tafajjara al-ma'" (the water gushed forth), which is when it descends outwardly from its source. Every flowing thing that moves outward from its place and location has "infajara" (burst forth), whether it is water, blood, pus or other than that, and from it is the statement of 'Umar ibn La'a:

And when I was yoked to Jarir,
his belly refused except to burst forth.

[[Tabaqat Fuhul al-Shu'ara': 369; al-Aghani 8: 72; their version reads "illa infihadan" (except to descend), and al-Tabari's narration is more eloquent in poetry. In the printed edition it is "qurribat," which is a pure error. He said it when Abu Bakr ibn Hazm took them both by the order of al-Walid ibn 'Abd al-Malik, yoked them together, and set them up on the pillory (al-Balas) to disgrace them, so the Tamimi would recite this verse in satire of Jarir. His words "dhu batnihi" (the one with the belly) are a fine kinaya for what makes one recoil from mentioning it.]]

He means: except emergence and flowing.
* *
The discourse on the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And indeed among them is that which splits open, so water comes out of it﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His words, exalted is His praise: "And indeed among them is that which splits" — meaning: and indeed among the rocks are rocks that split. Its "tashaqquq" is its "tasaddu'" (cracking open). [[The verse was dropped from the printed edition, apparently as a repetition; we have restored the discourse to Abu Ja'far's method. In the printed edition: "rocks that split," which I have also corrected to the proper text.]] Originally it is "lamā yatashaqqaq," but the "tā'" was assimilated into the "shīn" and became a doubled "shīn."

And His words ﴿so water comes out of it﴾ mean that it becomes gushing springs and flowing rivers.
* *
The discourse on the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And indeed among them is that which falls down out of fear of God﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He means by this, His praise is mighty: "And indeed among the rocks is that which falls down" — meaning it tumbles from the top of the mountain to the earth and the slope [[tardā min al-jabal tardiyan: he fell and dropped from the mountain]] out of fear and awe of God. We have already explained the meaning of "hubūt" (falling) earlier, in what sufficed without repeating it in this place. [[See what preceded at 1: 534, and this part 2: 132.]]
* *
Abu Ja'far said: These "lams" that are in "mā" were introduced for emphasis of the report.

God, exalted is His remembrance, described the rocks with what He described them: that among them is that from which rivers gush forth, that among them is that which splits and yields water, and that among them is that which falls down out of fear of God. After He made them a likeness for the hearts of those He reported the hardness of their hearts, the Children of Israel, [[The context of this phrase: "made them a likeness for the hearts of those..."]] as an excuse from Him, His praise is mighty, for them [[The context of this sentence: "He described them with what He described them... as an excuse from Him for them," i.e., for the rocks; what lies between is a digression, as is the custom of Abu Ja'far, may God have mercy on him.]], rather than those whom He reported the hardness of their hearts from the Children of Israel, since they were in the attribute by which God described them: denying His messengers, rejecting His signs, after He showed them the signs and lessons, and they witnessed the wonders of proofs and evidences, along with what God, exalted is His remembrance, gave them of sound intellects, and what He bestowed upon them of the soundness of souls which He did not give to stone and clay. Then, along with that, among the rocks is that which gushes with rivers, and among them is that which splits with water, and among them is that which falls down out of fear of God. So He, exalted is His remembrance, reported that among the rocks is that which is softer than their hearts in what they are called to of the truth, as:

1316 – Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq.
* *
And in accordance with what we have said in interpreting this, the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) said:

Mention of those who said that:

1317 – Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning the words of God, His praise is mighty: ﴿Then your hearts became hardened after that, so they were like rocks or even harder in hardness. And indeed among the rocks is that from which rivers gush forth, and indeed among them is that which splits and water comes out of it, and indeed among them is that which falls down out of fear of God﴾, he said: Every rock from which water gushes, or which splits to yield water, or which tumbles from the top of a mountain, is out of fear of God, mighty and majestic; the Qur'an was revealed with that.

1318 – al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.

1319 – Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to me, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿so they were like rocks or even harder in hardness﴾; then He excused the rocks and did not excuse the wretched son of Adam. He said: ﴿And indeed among the rocks is that from which rivers gush forth, and indeed among them is that which splits and water comes out of it, and indeed among them is that which falls down out of fear of God﴾.

1320 – al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, the same.

1321 – Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Then God excused the rocks, saying: ﴿And indeed among the rocks is that from which rivers gush forth, and indeed among them is that which splits and water comes out of it﴾.

1322 – al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, that he said: Among them is every rock from which water gushed forth, or which split to yield water, or which tumbled from a mountain, is out of fear of God. The Qur'an was revealed with it.
* *
Abu Ja'far said: Then the people of interpretation differed about the meaning of the falling of what falls from the rocks out of fear of God.

Some of them said: The falling of what falls of them out of fear of God is the shifting of its shadows. [[He means His words in Surat al-Nahl 48: "Have they not considered what things God has created, how their shadows turn from the right and the left, prostrating to God while they are humbled?" See the tafsir of this verse in Tafsir al-Tabari 14: 78, 79 (Bulaq).]]

Others said: That refers to the mountain that became dust when His Lord manifested Himself to it. [[He means His words in Surat al-A'raf 143: "And when his Lord manifested Himself to the mountain, He made it crumble to dust, and Moses fell down unconscious."]]

Some of them said: That was and will be, in that God, mighty is His remembrance, gave some of the rocks recognition and understanding, so it comprehended obedience to God and obeyed Him.

1324 – Like what is reported about the trunk on which the Messenger of God ﷺ used to lean when he delivered the sermon, and when he moved away from it, it moaned. [[The hadith: 1324 – the story of the trunk moaning for the Messenger of God ﷺ is mutawatir and authentic; none doubts its authenticity except one who does not wish to believe. Al-Hafiz Ibn Kathir devoted a chapter to it in al-Tarikh 6: 125–132, saying at its beginning: "Chapter on the moaning of the trunk out of longing for the Messenger of God ﷺ and compassion at his separation. It has come through the narration of a group of Companions, by multiple chains, which yield certainty according to the imams of this matter and the champions of this field," then he cited sound hadiths from the collections of the Sunnah. See among them in the Musnad: 2236, 3430 from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas; 2237, 3431 from the hadith of Anas; 3432 from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas and Anas; and Sahih al-Bukhari 6: 443 (Fath edition).]]

1325 – And like what is reported from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "Indeed a stone used to greet me in the Jahiliyyah; indeed I recognize it now." [[The hadith: 1325 – Muslim reported in his Sahih 2: 203–204, from Jabir ibn Samurah, who said: "The Messenger of God ﷺ said: 'Indeed I recognize a stone in Makkah which used to greet me before I was sent; indeed I recognize it now.'" Ibn Kathir mentioned it in al-Tarikh 6: 134, from the Musnad of Ahmad, then attributed it to Sahih Muslim and the Musnad of al-Tayalisi.]]

Others said: Rather, His words ﴿falls down out of fear of God﴾ are like His words ﴿a wall that wants to collapse﴾, though it has no will. They said: What is meant by that is that from the greatness of God's command, it is seen as if it were falling down, humble and submissive from the humiliation of fear of God, as Zayd al-Khayl said:

With a host that makes the bulls go astray in its wilderness,
you see the hills in it prostrating to the hooves.

[[This line occurred in this part 2: 104, and here it appears as "tara al-akam fiha" (you see the hills in it); the correct reading is what I have given, as was noted above; in al-Addad of Ibn al-Anbari it is "minha" in place of "fiha."]]

And as Suwayd ibn Abi Kahil said, describing an enemy of his:

Prostrating in the nostril, he does not raise it,
humble in the glance, deaf in the hearing.

[[Al-Mufaddaliyyat: 407; al-Addad of Ibn al-Anbari: 257, from his well-crafted qasidah. "Sajid" is in the accusative because before it, in mentioning this enemy of his: "Then he turned and fled, not protecting his backside, a bird of ill-omen having alighted upon him." In the printed original: "idh yarfa'uhu," which is a flaw in the sense. I have set what is in al-Mufaddaliyyat, and the version of Ibn al-Anbari: "ma yarfa'uhu." The meaning: he humbled him, so he lowered his head in disgrace and fixed his gaze on the ground, and became as if deaf, not hearing what is said to him; he does not move, dead while alive and standing, unable to return an answer. That is why he says after it: "His devil fled from me, where none is given, nor anything withheld."]]

He means that he is humbled. [[This sentence was before the line; I have returned it to where it should go.]]

And as Jarir ibn 'Atiyya said:

When the news of the Messenger came, the walls of the city and the humbled mountains were abased.

[[This line occurred before in this part 2: 17, and its version there is "khabar al-Zubayr," which is more sound and better.]]
* *
Others said: The meaning of His words ﴿falls down out of fear of God﴾ is: it makes the fear arise in another, by its indication of its Maker, as it is said: "a camel that brings profit (tājira)," when, from its nobility and excellence, it calls people to desire it, as Jarir ibn 'Atiyya said:

And one-eyed from Nabhan: by day he is blind,
and by night he is sighted.

[[This line occurred before with its takhrij at 1: 317 of this edition of ours, and I neglected there to return it to this place in the tafsir; so I have noted it here.]]

Then he attributed the description to the night and the day, while meaning by it his companion al-Nabhani, whom he was satirizing, because the thing he described him with occurred in them both.

* *

These opinions, although their meanings are not far from what the verse may bear as interpretation (ta'wil, the explanation of a verse's meaning), the interpretation of the people of ta'wil among the scholars of the earlier generations (salaf, the first generations of Muslims) is contrary to them. For this reason, we did not permit ourselves to turn the interpretation of the verse toward any of these meanings. [[Would that whoever among the people of our time has been reckless, and has dared to make the Book of his Lord a source from which he draws whatever he wishes for his own desires and the desires of the rulers, had heard what Abu Ja'far says, regarding what the Arabic language permits. How much more so, then, for one who attacks the words of his Lord without knowledge, guidance, or proof? O God, we disavow ourselves before You from them, and we seek refuge in You from going astray in their footsteps.]]

* *

We have already explained earlier the meaning of "khashyah" (fear), that it is dread and apprehension, so we disliked repeating that here. [[See what has preceded, 1:559-560, which is from the commentary on ﴿fa-arhabun﴾ (fear Me). The root (kh-sh-y) does not occur in the Qur'an before this place, so I am certain that he was referring to this verse.]]

* *

The commentary on the words of His, the Exalted, ﴿And Allah is not unaware of what you do﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His saying ﴿And Allah is not unaware of what you do﴾, He means: Allah is not unaware, O you who deny His signs, who reject the prophethood of His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ), and who fabricate falsehoods against him from among the Children of Israel and the rabbis of the Jews, of what you do of your wicked deeds and your bad actions. Rather, He records them against you, and will repay you for them in the Hereafter, or punish you for them in this world. [[In the printed edition it was "yuhsiha... fa-yujazikum... aw yu'aqibukum" with the yā' at the beginning of all of them. I preferred to return them to the nominal form, because al-Tabari speaks this way, and such a thing has preceded many times. I found that the copyists had altered it, as I explained in its place. So I have been comfortable with his method in his exposition, and it is more eloquent and upright.]]

The root of "ghaflah" (heedlessness) regarding a thing is to leave it in the manner of forgetting it and neglecting it.

* *

So He, the Exalted, informed them that He is not unaware of their wicked actions, nor heedless of them, but rather He counts them and keeps watch over them.

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Do you hope that they will believe you?﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His saying, majestic is His praise, ﴿Do you hope﴾, He means: O companions of Muhammad, that is, do you hope, O believers in Muhammad ﷺ and those who confirm what has come to you from God, that the Jews of the Children of Israel will believe you?

* *

By His saying, ﴿that they will believe you﴾, He means: that they will confirm you in what your Prophet Muhammad ﷺ has brought you from your Lord, as related:

1326 - I was told by ʿAmmar ibn al-Hasan, from Ibn Abi Jaʿfar, from his father, from al-Rabiʿ, regarding His saying ﴿Do you hope that they will believe you?﴾, meaning the companions of Muhammad ﷺ, "that they will believe you," he says: Do you hope that the Jews will believe you?

1327 - Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Saʿid related to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿Do you hope that they will believe you?﴾ the verse: He said, "They are the Jews."

* *

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿And there was a party among them﴾

Abu Ja'far said: As for "al-fariq" (party), it is a plural, like "al-taʾifah" (group), having no singular from its own form. It is of the pattern "faʿil" from "al-tafarruq" (dispersion), and the assembly was named by it, just as the group is named "al-hizb" (faction) from "al-tahazzub" (forming factions), and similar things. From this is the saying of Aʿsha of Banu Thaʿlabah:

They hastened, and when I feared they would separate
into two parties, some ascending and some descending [[His Diwan: 137; in the printed edition "akhadhu" is an error. Ajadda al-sayr: he hurried in travel. Musʿid: one beginning his ascent toward Najd and the Hijaz. Musawwib: one descending in his return toward Iraq and al-Sham and similar places. The line is completed by what follows: "I pursued them, the desert folds up under me a long-striding camel..."]]

By His saying, ﴿among them﴾, He means: from the Children of Israel. God only made those who were in the time of Moses and after him from the Children of Israel, from the Jews whom God mentioned to the companions of Muhammad ﷺ in His saying ﴿Do you hope that they will believe you?﴾, because they were their fathers and forebears, so He made them of them, since they were their kin, their predecessors and forefathers, just as a man today mentions a man, having followed the path and method of the one who mentions him. He was of his people and kin, so he says, "So-and-so was among us," meaning that he was of the people of his path or creed, or of his people and kin. Thus is His saying, ﴿And there was a party among them﴾.

* *

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿They hear the speech of God, then they distort it after they had understood it, and they know﴾ (75)

Abu Ja'far said: The people of interpretation differed concerning those whom God meant by His saying: ﴿And there was a party among them who heard the speech of God, then distorted it after they had understood it, and they knew.﴾ Some of them said:

1328 - Muhammad ibn ʿAmr related to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim related to us, saying: ʿIsa related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding God's saying: ﴿Do you hope that they will believe you, when there was a party among them who heard the speech of God, then distorted it after they had understood it, and they knew?﴾ Those who distort it and those who conceal it are their scholars.

1329 - al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah related to us, saying: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, similarly.

1330 - Musa related to me, saying: ʿAmr ibn Hammad related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿Do you hope that they will believe you, when there was a party among them who heard the speech of God, then distorted it after they had understood it﴾, he said: It is the Torah; they distorted it.

1331 - Yunus related to us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying ﴿They hear the speech of God, then they distort it﴾, he said: It is the Torah that He sent down to them, which they distort, making the lawful in it unlawful and the unlawful in it lawful, the truth in it falsehood and the falsehood in it truth. When the one with the right comes to them with a bribe, they produce for him the Book of God, and when the one with falsehood comes to them with a bribe, they produce for him that book, [[meaning: "that book," the distorted one, not "the Book of God" which is true.]] so he is right in it. And if anyone comes to ask them about something in which there is neither right nor bribe nor anything, they order him to do right. So He said to them: ﴿Do you enjoin righteousness on the people and forget yourselves, while you recite the Book? Will you not then reason?﴾ [al-Baqarah: 44].

* *

Others said concerning this:

1332 - I was told by ʿAmmar ibn al-Hasan, saying: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar informed us, from his father, from al-Rabiʿ, regarding His saying: ﴿And there was a party among them who heard the speech of God, then distorted it after they had understood it, and they knew﴾, they heard from it as the people of prophethood hear, then they distorted it after they had understood it, and they knew.

1333 - Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Ishaq, regarding His saying: ﴿And there was a party among them who heard the speech of God﴾ the verse, he said: His saying ﴿who heard the speech of God﴾ does not mean they heard the Torah; all of them had heard it, but they were the ones who asked Moses to see their Lord, and the thunderbolt seized them for it.

1334 - Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salamah related to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq who said: It reached me from some people of knowledge that they said to Moses: O Moses, the seeing of God, mighty and majestic is He, has been barred from us, so let us hear His speech when He speaks to you. Moses asked his Lord for that, and He said: Yes, so command them to purify themselves, wash their garments, and fast. They did so. Then he went out with them until he came to the Mount; when the cloud overshadowed them, Moses, peace be upon him, commanded them [to prostrate], and they fell prostrate. [[What is between the brackets is an addition from Ibn Kathir 1: 212.]] Then his Lord spoke to him and they heard His speech, commanding them and forbidding them, until they understood what they heard. Then he returned with them to the Children of Israel. When they came to them, a party among them distorted what he had commanded them.
