When Moses said to the Children of Israel, "God has commanded you with such and such," that party whom God mentioned said: He only said such and such, contrary to what God, mighty and majestic, had said to them. They are those whom God meant to His messenger Muhammad ﷺ.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The better of the two interpretations I have mentioned for the verse, and the closer to what the apparent recitation indicates, is what al-Rabiʿ ibn Anas said, and what Ibn Ishaq related from some people of knowledge: that God, mighty is His mention, meant by this those among the Children of Israel who heard the speech of God, the hearing that Moses heard from Him, then distorted and changed it after their hearing, knowledge and understanding of it. This is because God, majestic is His praise, only informed that the distortion came from a party among them who were hearing the speech of God, mighty and majestic, as a magnification by God of what they used to commit of slander after the confirmation of the proof and the evidence against them, and as an announcement by Him, exalted is His mention, to His believing servants, that He cut off their hopes of the faith of the remnants of their offspring in what Muhammad brought of truth, light, and guidance. [[In the printed edition it reads "wa-idhanan minhu. . . wa-qata'a" with a conjunction, which does not hold. Adhanahu al-amr and adhanahu bihi idhanan: informed him. So "qata'a" is the second object of the verbal noun "idhanan."]] So He said to them: How do you hope for these Jews to confirm you, when you inform them, with what you inform them of the reports about God, mighty and majestic, of an unseen matter that they have not witnessed or observed, while some of them used to hear God's speech, His command and prohibition, and then changed it, distorted it, and denied it? So these among you, the remnants of their offspring, are more likely to deny what you have brought them of truth, while they do not hear it from God but hear it from you, [[the phrase "wa-aqrab" is conjoined to "ahra" in the previous clause.]] and more likely to distort what is in their books of the description and attributes of your Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and change it, while they know it, so they deny and lie, [[the phrase "min awa'ilihim" relates to what was said earlier: "ahra an yajhadu. . . wa-aqrab ila an yuharrifu. . ."]] from their forebears who directly received God's speech from God, mighty is His praise, then distorted it after they had understood and known it, deliberately distorting it.

If the interpretation of the verse were as those claimed, that by His saying ﴿who hear the speech of God﴾ it means they hear the Torah, then mention of His saying ﴿who hear the speech of God﴾ would have no understood meaning, because the distorter among them and the non-distorter both heard it, so singling out the distorter among them as one who heard the speech of God, if the interpretation were as those we mentioned said, over others who heard it in the same way as they did, would have no meaning. [[The construction: "then singling out the distorter as one who. . . has no meaning."]]

If someone supposes that this statement was only fit because of His saying ﴿they distort it﴾, he has overlooked the correct point in this. For if that were so, it would be said: "Do you hope that they will believe you, when a party among them distorted the speech of God after they had understood it, and they knew." But He, majestic is His praise, informed of a particular group among the Jews who had been given, through their direct hearing of God's speech, what no one other than the prophets and messengers had been given, and then they changed and distorted what they had heard of it. Therefore He described them with what He described them, due to the particularity with which this party was singled out, whom He mentioned in His Book, mighty is His mention.

* *

By His saying, ﴿then they distort it﴾, He means: then they alter its meaning and interpretation and change it. Its root is from "the deviation of a thing from its direction," which is its inclination away from it toward something else. Likewise His saying ﴿they distort it﴾ means they incline it away from its face and its meaning that is its meaning, toward something else. God, majestic is His praise, informed that they did what they did of that with knowledge on their part of the interpretation of what they distorted, and that it was contrary to what they distorted it toward. He said: ﴿they distort it after they had understood it﴾, meaning: after they had understood its interpretation, ﴿and they know﴾, that is: they know that in their distortion of what they distorted of it, they are falsifiers and liars. This is an announcement from God, majestic is His praise, of their proceeding to slander, and their hostility toward Him and His messenger Moses, peace be upon him, and that their remnants, in their hostility toward God and His messenger Muhammad ﷺ out of rebellion and envy, are upon the same as their forebears were in that regard in the time of Moses, peace and blessings be upon him.

The Interpretation of His Words, the Exalted: "And when they meet those who believe, they say, 'We believe.'"

Abu Ja'far said: As for His words, "And when they meet those who believe, they say, 'We believe,'" this is a report from God, dhikruhu the Mighty, about those who despaired the companions of Muhammad ﷺ of their faith: from the Jews of the Children of Israel, among whom a group used to hear the speech of God and then distort it after they had understood it while knowing (what they did). They are the ones who, when they meet those who believe in God and His Messenger Muhammad ﷺ, say: "We believe." He means by this: when they meet those who affirmed God and Muhammad ﷺ and what he brought from God, they say, "We believe"—that is, we affirm Muhammad and what you affirmed, and we acknowledge that. God, Mighty and Majestic, informs that they had adopted the character of the hypocrites and followed their path, as:

1335 – Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from his grandfather, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words: "And when they meet those who believe, they say, 'We believe'; and when some of them are alone with others, they say, 'Do you tell them what God has opened up to you?'" The reason was that a group of Jews, when they met Muhammad ﷺ, would say, "We believe," and when some of them were alone with one another they would say, "Do you tell them what God has opened up to you?"

1336 – Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: 'Uthman ibn Sa'id narrated to us, from Bishr ibn 'Umara, from Abu Rawq, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn 'Abbas: "And when they meet those who believe, they say, 'We believe'"—meaning the hypocrites among the Jews; when they met the companions of Muhammad ﷺ they said, "We believe."

* *

It has been related from Ibn 'Abbas another interpretation of this, which is that:

1337 – Ibn Humayd narrated this to us, saying: Salama ibn al-Fadl narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, from 'Ikrima, or from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas: "And when they meet those who believe, they say, 'We believe'"—i.e., (they say that they believe) in your companion, the Messenger of God ﷺ, but (they say) that he is only for you specifically.

1338 – Musa narrated to us, saying: 'Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "And when they meet those who believe, they say, 'We believe'," etc. He said: These are people from the Jews who believed and then became hypocrites.

* *

The Interpretation of His Words, the Exalted: "And when some of them are alone with others, they say, 'Do you tell them what God has opened up to you, so that they may argue with you before your Lord? Do you not understand?'" (76)

Abu Ja'far said: By His words, "And when some of them are alone with others," he means: when some of these Jews—whom God has described—are alone with some of their own, so that they are in privacy away from other people, that being the place where no others are present—"they say," meaning: some of them say to others—"Do you tell them what God has opened up to you?"

* *

Then the people of interpretation differed concerning the interpretation of His words, "what God has opened up to you." Some of them said:

1339 – Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: 'Uthman ibn Sa'id narrated to us, from Bishr ibn 'Umara, from Abu Rawq, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn 'Abbas: "And when some of them are alone with others, they say, 'Do you tell them what God has opened up to you?'" meaning: what God has commanded you. Others would say: We only mock them and laugh at them.

* *

And others said:

1340 – Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, from 'Ikrima, or from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas: "And when they meet those who believe, they say, 'We believe'," i.e., (they say that they believe) in your companion, the Messenger of God, but he is only for you specifically; "and when some of them are alone with others, they say: Do not tell the Arabs about this, for you used to seek victory through him over them, and so he has come from them." [[Their saying "so he has come from them" means: the Prophet who they used to seek victory through against the polytheists of the Arabs, and whom they hoped would come from them, has come from the Arabs. The report of their seeking victory will come later in the commentary on verse 89 of Surat al-Baqara in this part.]] Then God revealed: "And when they meet those who believe, they say, 'We believe'; and when some of them are alone with others, they say, 'Do you tell them what God has opened up to you, so that they may argue with you before your Lord?'" i.e., you acknowledge that he is a prophet, and you know that a covenant was taken from you to follow him, and he informs them that he is the prophet we were awaiting and whom we find in our book? Deny him and do not admit it to them. God says: "Do they not know that God knows what they conceal and what they reveal?"

1341 – Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Adam narrated to us, saying: Abu Ja'far narrated to us, from al-Rabi', from Abu al-'Aliya, regarding His words: "Do you tell them what God has opened up to you?" i.e., by what God has revealed to you in your book of the description of Muhammad ﷺ.

1342 – Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Zuray' narrated to us, from Sa'id, from Qatada: "They say, 'Do you tell them what God has opened up to you?'" i.e., by what God has bestowed upon you in your book of the description of Muhammad ﷺ; for if you do that, they will argue against you with it. "Do you not understand?"

1343 – al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada: "Do you tell them what God has opened up to you?" so that they may argue against you with it.

1344 – Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Adam narrated to me, saying: Abu Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Qatada said: "Do you tell them what God has opened up to you?" i.e., by what God has revealed to you concerning the matter of Muhammad ﷺ and his description.

* *

And others said concerning this:

1345 – Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, from 'Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "by what God has opened up to you, so that they may argue with you before your Lord." He said: It is the saying of the Jews of Banu Qurayza [[In the printed edition: "Jews of Qurayza," which is not correct.]] when the Prophet ﷺ reviled them as "brothers of the apes and the swine." They said: "Who told you this?" This was when he sent 'Ali to them, and they harmed Muhammad, and he said: "O brothers of the apes and the swine." [[From his words "They said: Who told you this?" to the end of the statement, is an explanation of the story before it. And his words "he said: O brothers of the apes and the swine" are the words of the Messenger of God ﷺ, not the words of 'Ali (may God be pleased with him). This will become clear in the two reports following it.]]

1346 – Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it, except that he said: This was when 'Ali ibn Abi Talib (may God be pleased with him) was sent to them, and they harmed the Prophet ﷺ, and he said: "Begone, O brothers of the apes and the swine!"

1347 – al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza informed me, from Mujahid regarding His words: "Do you tell them what God has opened up to you?" He said: The Prophet ﷺ stood on the day of Qurayza beneath their fortresses and said: "O brothers of the apes, O brothers of the swine, O worshippers of the taghut!" They said: "Who informed Muhammad of this? This statement came only from you!" "Do you tell them what God has opened up to you?" by what God judged for the conquest, so that it becomes an argument against you. Ibn Jurayj said, from Mujahid: This was when he sent 'Ali to them, and they harmed Muhammad ﷺ. [[The report 1347: in Ibn Kathir 1:214, and there: "Who informed Muhammad of this matter? This statement came only from you."]]

* *

And others said:

1348 – Musa narrated to us, saying: 'Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "They say, 'Do you tell them what God has opened up to you'"—of punishment—"so that they may argue with you before your Lord." These are people from the Jews who believed and then became hypocrites; they used to tell the believers among the Arabs about the punishment with which they had been afflicted. Some of them said to others: Do you tell them what God has opened up to you of punishment, so that they say: We are more beloved to God than you, and more honored by God than you?

* *

And others said:

1349 – Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words: "And when some of them are alone with others, they say, 'Do you tell them what God has opened up to you, so that they may argue with you before your Lord?'" He said: When they were asked about something they would say: "Do you not know in the Torah such-and-such?" They said: "Yes!"—he said: and they were Jews—and their leaders to whom they returned would say to them: "What is wrong with you, telling them what God has revealed to you, so that they argue with you before your Lord? Do you not understand?" He said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "None but a believer shall enter the central town of Medina." [[Qasabat al-qarya: its middle and interior. Qasabat al-bilad: its city, because it is in its middle.]] Their leaders, from among the people of disbelief and hypocrisy, said: "Go and say 'We believe,' and disbelieve when you return." He said: They would come to Medina in the early morning and return to them after the afternoon prayer. [[Al-bukar, plural of bukra (with a vowel on the first letter and a sukun on the second): the morning, the early part of the day.]] And he recited God's words: "And a group of the People of the Book said: Believe in what has been revealed to those who believe at the beginning of the day, and disbelieve at its end, that perhaps they will return" [Al 'Imran: 72]. They would say, when they entered Medina: "We are Muslims," so that they might learn the news and affair of the Messenger of God ﷺ, and when they returned they would return to disbelief. When God informed His Prophet ﷺ about them, this was cut off from them, and they no longer entered. The believers who were with the Messenger of God ﷺ thought they were believers, so they would say to them: "Did God not say to you such-and-such?" They would say: "Yes!" When they returned to their people [meaning the leaders], they said: "Do you tell them what God has opened up to you?" etc. [[Report 1349: in Ibn Kathir 1:213-214; the bracketed addition is from him.]]

* *

The root of "al-fath" in the speech of the Arabs is: victory, judgment, and ruling. From it one says: "O God, open (judge) between me and so-and-so," i.e., judge between me and him. And from it is the saying of the poet:

Let it be known to Banu 'Usm, a messenger: that I am independent of your judging (futtahatikum)... [[Attributed to al-Asa'ar al-Ju'fi and Muhammad ibn Hamran ibn Abi Hamran. See the commentary of al-Rajkuti in Simt al-La'ali: 927.]]

Abu Ja'far said: It is said of the judge "al-fattah" [[Amali al-Qali 2:281 and Lisan (f-t-h) (r-s-l), and others; Banu 'Usm are the kinsmen of 'Amr ibn Ma'd Yakrib al-Zubaydi. The versions of the verse differ greatly, and this is not the place to verify them, given their length.]]. And from it is God's words, Mighty and Majestic: "Our Lord, judge between us and our people with truth, for You are the best of judges" [al-A'raf: 89], i.e., judge between us and them.

* *

If the meaning of "al-fath" is what we have described, it becomes clear that the meaning of His words, "They say, 'Do you tell them what God has opened up to you, so that they may argue with you before your Lord?'" is only: "Do you tell them what God has judged against you and decreed upon you?" Among His judgments upon them is that He took their covenant of faith in Muhammad ﷺ and in what came in the Torah. And among His decrees concerning them is that He made of them apes and swine, and other of His judgments and decrees concerning them. All of that was for the Messenger of God ﷺ and for those who believed in him as proof against the Jews who denied, who acknowledged the judgment of the Torah, and other [of His judgments and decrees]. [[What is between the brackets is an addition I have deduced from the preceding explanation, to make the sentence consistent.]]

Since that is so, [[In the printed edition: "If that is so," the addition continues the method of Abu Ja'far.]] the view that is more preferable to me regarding the interpretation of the verse is the view of the one who said: the meaning of that is: "Do you tell them what God has opened up to you of the sending of Muhammad ﷺ to His creation?" Because God, Mighty and Majestic, at the beginning of this verse only related the report of their saying to the Messenger of God ﷺ and to his companions: "We believe in what Muhammad ﷺ brought." So the more fitting view for its end is that it should be parallel to the report of what its beginning began with.

And since that is so, it is necessary that their mutual blaming, which took place among themselves, concerned what they had displayed to the Messenger of God ﷺ and his companions of their saying to them: "We believe in Muhammad ﷺ and in what he brought." Their saying that was because they found it in their books, and they used to inform the companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ of it. So their blaming one another when they were alone was over their informing the companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ of what would be proof for the Muslims against them before their Lord. For they used to inform them of the existence of the description of Muhammad ﷺ in their books, and then disbelieve in him; and the victory God had granted the Muslims over the Jews, and His judgment against them in their favor from their own book, was that they should believe in Muhammad ﷺ when he was sent. When he was sent, they disbelieved in him, despite their knowledge of his prophethood.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: As for His words, "Do you not understand?" it is a report from God, dhikruhu the Exalted, about the Jews who blamed their brethren for what they had informed the companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ of what God had opened for them against them: that they said to them: "Do you not comprehend and understand, O people, that your informing the companions of the Prophet ﷺ of what is in your books, that he is a prophet sent, is an argument for them against you before your Lord, by which they will argue against you?" That is: do not do that, and do not say to them the like of what you said, and do not inform them of the like of what you informed them of. Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said: "Do they not know that God knows what they conceal and what they reveal?"

**The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Do they not know that God knows what they conceal and what they reveal?﴾ (2:77)**

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: By His words, majestic is His praise, ﴿Do they not know that God knows what they conceal and what they reveal?﴾, He means: Do not these Jews who blame [their fellows] know, [concerning] their brethren from among the people of their religion, that when they meet those who believe they say, "We believe," and that when they inform the believers of what is in their books about the description of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and his mission, [and] those who say to them, "Do you tell them what God has disclosed to you, so that they may argue with you before your Lord?" [do not know] that God knows what they conceal, so that they hide it from the believers in their private gatherings, of their disbelief and their mutual reproach for having displayed to the Messenger of God and to the believers in him what they displayed, of acknowledgment of Muhammad (ﷺ), and for their saying to them, "We believe," and that some of them forbade others from informing the believers of what God had disclosed to the believers concerning them, and what He had decided against them in their books, of the reality of the prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ), his description and his mission; ﴿and what they reveal﴾, by declaring it to Muhammad (ﷺ) and to his companions who believe in him when they meet them, of their saying to them, "We believe in Muhammad (ﷺ) and in what he has brought," out of hypocrisy and deception toward God, His Messenger and the believers? As follows:

1350 – Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿Do they not know that God knows what they conceal﴾: [it means] their disbelief and their denial of Muhammad (ﷺ) when some of them are alone with others, ﴿and what they reveal﴾: when they meet the companions of Muhammad (ﷺ), they say, "We believe," in order to please them by that.

1351 – al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Adam narrated to us, saying: Abu Ja'far narrated to us, from al-Rabi', from Abu al-'Aliyah, regarding ﴿Do they not know that God knows what they conceal and what they reveal?﴾: he means what they conceal of their disbelief in Muhammad (ﷺ) and their denial of him, while they find him written down among them; ﴿and what they reveal﴾, he means: what they declared when they said to the believers, "We believe."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 78 (part 1 of 2):

The discussion on the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And among them are unlettered ones﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: By His words, majestic is His praise, ﴿And among them are unlettered ones﴾, and [among] these [are] the Jews whose accounts Allah has related in these verses, and He despaired the companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ of their faith, so He said to them: "Do you hope that they will believe in you, when a group of them used to hear the speech of Allah, then they would distort it after they had understood it, and when they meet you they say: 'We believe'," as:

1352 - Al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Adam narrated to us, saying: Abu Ja'far narrated to us, from al-Rabi', from Abu al-Aliyah: ﴿And among them are unlettered ones﴾, meaning: from the Jews.

1353 - And it was narrated to me from Ammar, who said: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi', the like of it.

1354 - Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid: ﴿And among them are unlettered ones﴾, he said: People from among the Jews.
* *
Abu Ja'far said: By "al-ummiyyun" (the unlettered ones) he means those who do not write and do not read.

From it is the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: "We are an unlettered nation, we do not write and we do not calculate" [[The hadith: 1355 - It is a sound hadith. It is narrated by al-Bukhari 4: 108-109 (from al-Fath), and also narrated by Muslim, Abu Dawud and al-Nasa'i, as in al-Jami' al-Saghir of al-Suyuti, no.: 2521.]] It is said of it: "A man who is unlettered (ummi), of unlettered status" [[In the printed edition it was: "ay bayn al-ummiyyah" ("i.e. of unlettered status"); I removed "ay", as that is not something that is said.]]. As:

1356 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Suwayd ibn Nasr narrated to me, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Ibrahim: ﴿And among them are unlettered ones who do not know the Book﴾, he said: Among them is one who does not know how to write. [[His saying "does not know how to write" is a negation of knowledge of writing, not of the excellence of knowledge of writing, as might come to mind. Some of our teachers have long argued that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ knew how to write but did not write well, on the basis of a report, which he used as evidence—or which some Orientalist followers used as evidence—namely what is related in the History of al-Tabari 3: 80 in the account of al-Hudaybiyah, when Suhayl ibn Amr came to write the treaty. Al-Tabari narrated from al-Bara' ibn Azib, who said: "... When he wrote the document, he wrote: 'This is what Muhammad the Messenger of Allah has agreed to,' and they said: 'If we knew that you were the Messenger of Allah, we would not have prevented you, but you are Muhammad ibn Abdullah.' He said: 'I am the Messenger of Allah, and I am Muhammad ibn Abdullah.' He said to Ali: 'Erase "Messenger of Allah".' He said: 'No, by Allah, I will never erase you, ever.' So the Messenger of Allah took it, and he did not know how to write well: 'He wrote in place of "Messenger of Allah" "Muhammad", and he wrote: "This is what Muhammad has agreed to".'

He first thought that the subject pronoun in his saying "he wrote in place of 'Messenger of Allah' – Muhammad" refers to the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him. This is not so; rather it is Ali ibn Abi Talib, the scribe. There is an ellipsis in the speech: when he commanded Ali to erase the document and he refused, the Messenger of Allah took it, and he did not know how to write well, so he erased it. The explanation of this has come in the hadith of al-Bukhari from al-Bara' ibn Azib also, 3: 184: "So he said to Ali: 'Erase it.' Ali said: 'I will not be the one who erases it,' so the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, erased it with his own hand." And another point: he erred in the meaning of "yuhsinu" (know well), for here it means "ya'lamu" (knows), and this is a good courtesy of expression, so as not to negate knowledge from him. It has come in al-Tabari's Tafsir 21: 6 in the interpretation of His words: "who made everything He created good", the text of which is: "The meaning of that is: He knew everything He created. As if they directed the interpretation of the speech to mean that He inspired each creature with what it needs. And that His saying 'ahsana' is only from the speech of the speaker: 'so-and-so does not do it well' when he knows it." Moreover, the Arabs observe courtesy with the like of this, placing one expression in place of another and nullifying part of its meaning, to purify the tongue or to honor the one spoken of. So the meaning of his saying "he does not do it well" is that he does not know how to write. Al-Suhayli has gone on at length in al-Rawd al-Unuf 1: 230 with speech that does not suffice in the explanation of this word.]]

1357 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words: ﴿And among them are unlettered ones﴾, he said: Unlettered ones who do not read the Book from among the Jews.
* *
It has been related from Ibn Abbas a saying contrary to this view, which is what:

1358 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Uthman ibn Sa'id narrated to us, from Bishr ibn Umarah, from Abu Rawq, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿And among them are unlettered ones﴾, he said: The unlettered ones are a people who did not believe a messenger Allah had sent, nor a book Allah had revealed, so they wrote a book with their own hands, then they said to a lowly, ignorant people: "This is from Allah." He said: He has informed that they write with their hands, then He named them unlettered ones, due to their denial of the books and messengers of Allah. [[Ibn Kathir said in his Tafsir 1: 215, after relating the report and the words of al-Tabari: "I say: there is scrutiny regarding the authenticity of this from Ibn Abbas through this chain, and Allah knows best."]]
* *
Abu Ja'far said: This interpretation is an interpretation contrary to what is known from the widespread speech of the Arabs among themselves, for "al-ummi" among the Arabs is the one who does not write.
* *
Abu Ja'far said: I think that the unlettered one was called "ummi" by attribution, by saying that he does not write, to "his mother" (umm), because writing was among men and not women; so the man who does not write or scribe was attributed—to his mother—in his ignorance of writing, rather than to his father, as we mentioned from the Prophet ﷺ in his saying: "We are an unlettered nation, we do not write and we do not calculate," and as He said: ﴿It is He who raised among the unlettered ones a messenger from among them, reciting to them His verses and purifying them and teaching them the Book and wisdom﴾ [al-Jumu'ah: 2]. [[The printed edition contented itself with his saying "a messenger from among them"; I completed the verse, because he uses it as evidence that he came to teach the unlettered "the Book".]] So if the meaning of "al-ummi" in the speech of the Arabs is what we have described, then the interpretation of the verse most fitting is what al-Nakha'i said, that the meaning of His saying: ﴿And among them are unlettered ones﴾ is: among them are those who do not know how to write.
* *
The discussion on the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿They do not know the Book except wishful fancies﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His words: ﴿They do not know the Book﴾, he means: they do not know what is in the Book that Allah revealed, and they do not understand what Allah deposited in it of its limits, its rulings and its obligations, like the state of cattle, as:

1359 - Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to me, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah regarding His words: ﴿And among them are unlettered ones who do not know the Book except wishful fancies﴾: They are only like cattle, knowing nothing.

1360 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah regarding His words: ﴿They do not know the Book﴾, he says: they do not know the Book and do not understand what is in it.

1361 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Adam narrated to us, saying: Abu Ja'far narrated to us, from al-Rabi', from Abu al-Aliyah: ﴿They do not know the Book﴾, they do not understand what is in it.

1362 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, from Ikrimah, or from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿They do not know the Book﴾, he said: they do not understand what is in it.

1363 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: ﴿They do not know the Book﴾, they know nothing, they do not read the Torah. It is not memorized, it is only read thus. So if one of them does not write, he cannot read. [[The report 1363: in the printed edition it was: "Bishr narrated to us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us..." which is a slip by the copyist; the chain recurs frequently in the tafsir, the nearest being no. 1357.]]

1364 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Uthman ibn Sa'id narrated to us, from Bishr ibn Umarah, from Abu Rawq, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn Abbas regarding His words: ﴿They do not know the Book﴾, he said: they do not recognize the Book that Allah revealed.
* *
Abu Ja'far said: By "the Book" is meant only the Torah, and for that reason the definite article "al-" was attached to it, because it intends a book known by its specific identity.
* *
Its meaning: among them is a group who do not write, and do not understand what is in the Book that you know, which is with them—and they claim it and profess to acknowledge it—of the rulings of Allah and His obligations, and what is in it of its limits which He clarified in it.

[The scholars of interpretation differed regarding the interpretation of His words] [[What is between the brackets is an addition required by the sense; it seems the copyist omitted it through inattention.]] ﴿except wishful fancies﴾. Some of them said, with what:

1365 - Abu Kurayb narrated it to us, saying: Uthman ibn Sa'id narrated to us, from Bishr ibn Umarah, from Abu Rawq, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿except wishful fancies﴾, he says: except a saying they say with their mouths, falsely.

1366 - Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿They do not know the Book except wishful fancies﴾: except falsehood.

1367 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.
* *
And others said, with what:

1368 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Zuray' narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿except wishful fancies﴾, he says: they wish upon Allah what is not theirs.

1369 - Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah: ﴿except wishful fancies﴾, he says: they wish upon Allah falsehood and what is not theirs.

1370 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih [from Mu'awiyah ibn Salih] narrated to us, from Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn Abbas, his saying: ﴿They do not know the Book except wishful fancies﴾, he says: except tales.

1371 - Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid: ﴿And among them are unlettered ones who do not know the Book except wishful fancies﴾, he said: People from among the Jews who did not know anything of the Book, and they used to speak by conjecture, other than what is in the Book of Allah, and they would say: "It is from the Book." Wishful fancies they wished for.

1372 - Al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Adam narrated to us, saying: Abu Ja'far narrated to us, from al-Rabi', from Abu al-Aliyah: ﴿except wishful fancies﴾, they wish upon Allah what is not theirs.

1373 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words: ﴿except wishful fancies﴾, he said: They wished and said: "We are of the People of the Book," and they were not of them.
* *
Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of what we have related regarding the interpretation of His words: ﴿except wishful fancies﴾, in truth, and most similar to the correct meaning, is what Ibn Abbas said—which al-Dahhak related from him—and the saying of Mujahid: that the "unlettered ones" whom Allah described with what He described them in this verse are those who do not understand anything of the Book which Allah revealed to Musa, but they fabricate lies and invent falsehoods, falsely and deceitfully. [[In the printed edition it was: "wa-annahum la yafqahuna" with an added waw, which is an error that does not fit; the correct reading is what I have set down from Ibn Kathir 1: 216.]]
* *
And "tamanni" (wishing) in this place is the fabrication of lies, their invention and their contrivance. It is said from it: "tamannaytu kadha" (I wished such-and-such) when I fabricated it and invented it. And from it is the report related from Uthman ibn Affan, may Allah be pleased with him: "I have not sung nor wished" [[In al-Fa'iq 1: 163, from Uthman, may Allah be pleased with him: "I have stored up with Allah qualities: I am the fourth of Islam; the Messenger of Allah ﷺ married me to his daughter, then to another daughter; and I pledged allegiance to him with this right hand of mine, and I have never touched my private part with it; I have not sung, nor wished, nor drunk wine in the Jahiliyyah or in Islam." And al-Tabari related in his History, in the account of his killing, may Allah be pleased with him, 5: 130, that the man who undertook to kill him entered upon him and said: "Remove it and we will leave you." He said: "Woe to you! I have not uncovered a woman in the Jahiliyyah or Islam, nor sung, nor wished, nor placed my right hand on my nakedness since I pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and I am not removing a shirt which Allah, mighty and majestic, has clothed me with."]] meaning by his saying "I have not wished": I have not fabricated falsehood, nor invented lies and calumny.
* *
And what indicates the correctness of what we have said in this regard—and that it is more fitting for the interpretation of His words: ﴿except wishful fancies﴾ than other sayings—is the saying of Allah, majestic is His praise: ﴿and they only conjecture﴾. He informed about them, majestic is His praise, that they wish what they wish of falsehoods, out of conjecture on their part, not certainty. Had the meaning been that they "recite" it, they would not be conjecturing; and likewise had the meaning been "they desire" it. For one who recites it, when he contemplates it, knows it; and one who recites a book he has read, even if he does not reflect upon it, does not deserve, by neglecting reflection, to be said to be conjecturing about what he recites, unless he were doubting the very thing he recites, not knowing whether it is true or false. And the people who were reciting the Torah in the time of our Prophet Muhammad ﷺ from among the Jews were not—as far as we have been informed—doubting that the Torah was from Allah. Likewise, the "one who wishes" who is in the sense of "one who desires" cannot rightly be said to be conjecturing in his wishing, for wishing is by one who wishes for what has already been found in its essence. It is impermissible to say: he doubts what he knows, for knowledge and doubt are two meanings each of which negates its companion, and their coexistence in one place is not permitted. And the one who wishes, in the state of his wishing, his wishing exists, so it is impermissible to say: he conjectures his wishing. [[In the printed edition it was: "ghayr jA'iz", and the correct form restores the fa'.]]
* *
And it was only said: ﴿They do not know the Book except wishful fancies﴾, and "wishful fancies" are not of the same kind as "the Book", as our Lord, majestic is His praise, said: ﴿They have no knowledge of it except following conjecture﴾ [al-Nisa': 157], and "conjecture" is far removed from "knowledge". And as He said: ﴿And for no one with Him is any favor to be repaid, except the seeking of the Face of his Lord, the Most High﴾ [al-Layl: 19-20]. And as the poet said: [[He is Amr ibn al-Ayham al-Taghlibi, the Christian; it is said his name was 'Umayr, and it is said he was A'sha Taghlib. It is related from al-Akhtal that when he was dying he was asked: "Over whom will your people be left?" He said: "Over the two Umayrs," meaning Umayr al-Qutami ibn Ushaym and Umayr ibn al-Ahtam.]]

There is no reproach between me and Qays except the thrust of the kidneys and the striking of necks. [[Sibawayh 1: 365; al-Wahshiyyat no. 55; Mu'jam al-Shu'ara' p. 242; Hamasa of al-Buhturi p. 32; see the edition of al-Rajkoti in Simt al-La'ali p. 184. The poem is said in satire of Qays 'Aylan, in which he says: May Allah fight Qays 'Aylan, all of them ... what they have beyond treachery of a veil.
Then Sibawayh recited the verse with "ghayr" in the nominative, as a substitute for "'itab", by extension and metaphor.]]

And as the poet of the Banu Dhubyan said:

I swore an oath, without exception, ... nor knowledge except a good assumption about a companion. [[His Diwan: 42; Sibawayh 1: 365, and others; all their versions have "bi-sahib", and in the original printed edition it was "bi-gha'ib", and I think that what was in al-Tabari is an error of the copyists, because it does not fit the poetry. The Nabigha praises with these verses 'Amr ibn al-Harith al-A'raj al-Ghassani, and before it he says: For 'Amr a favor after favor ... to his father, not with scorpions.
I swore an oath ... ...
If it was for the two graves: a grave in Jalaq ... and a grave in Sayda' which is near Harith.
And for al-Harith al-Jafni, lord of his people ... he will surely seek the house of the warrior by the army.
And his saying: "mathnawiyya" means exception. He says to 'Amr: I swore an oath that if he who is from the sons of those kings, among his fathers, whose graves and glories he enumerates, shall surely raid whoever fights him in his own land and surely defeat him, and I did not say this from knowledge except what I have in my companion of good assumption. So the report of al-Tabari does not hold, if it is correct from him.]] Among similar examples of what we have mentioned, whose enumeration would lengthen the book. [[See Sibawayh 1: 363-366: "This is a chapter in which the accusative is chosen, because the latter is not of the kind of the former." Then the chapter following it: "This is a chapter which can only be upon the meaning of: but."]]

And "illa" (except) brings out what follows it from the meaning of what precedes it and from its description, even if each of them is not of the same form as the other and not of its kind. Some grammarians call this "exception that is disjunctive" (istithna' munqati'), because the speech that comes after "illa" is disconnected from the meaning of what precedes it. And this is only so in every place where it is good to place "lakin" (but) instead of "illa"; then the disconnection of the meaning of the second from the meaning of the first is known. Do you not see that if you say: ﴿And among them are unlettered ones who do not know the Book except wishful fancies﴾, then you wish to place "lakin" in place of "illa" and omit "illa", you find the speech sound in meaning, its soundness and it having "illa"? That is when you say: "And among them are unlettered ones who do not know the Book, but wishful fancies," meaning: "but they wish." Likewise His saying: ﴿They have no knowledge of it except following conjecture﴾, "but following conjecture," meaning: "but they follow conjecture." And likewise all this type of speech, according to what we have described.
* *

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 78 (part 2 of 2):

It has been reported from some of the readers (qurra') that he recited: [[In the printed edition: "some of the readers" and "by the consensus of the readers." I have restored it to what al-Tabari followed above.]] ﴿illa amani﴾ with a light (mukhaffafa) pronunciation. Whoever reads it lightly directs it to the pattern of their plurals such as "al-miftah" becoming "mafatih" (keys), "al-qurqur" becoming "qaraqir" (a kind of jar), [[See Ma'ani al-Qur'an by al-Farra': 1:49.]] and that when the plural ya' was dropped, the original ya' (that is, the one in "al-amani") was lightened, just as they formed the plural of "al-uthfiyah" as "uthafi" lightened, as Zuhayr ibn Abi Sulma said:

Uthafiya suf'an fi mu'arrasi mirjal... wa nu'yan kajidhm al-hawd lam yatathallam
[[His Diwan: 7. The mirjal is the cooking pot; mu'arras al-mirjal is the place where it is set down, from ta'ris, meaning to halt and stay. Suf'a is the plural of asfa', and the sufa is blackness mixed with redness, from the trace of fire and its smoke. The nu'y is what is set up of stones around the tent so that rainwater does not enter. Jidhm al-hawd is its edge and base. He means: the nu'y has lost its top but its base remains unbroken, like the remains of a basin. He says: I recognised the dwelling by these traces; before it is: "fa-la'iyan 'arafta al-dar ba'da tawahhum." "Uthafiya" is in the accusative governed by "tawahhum."]]

As for the one who pronounces it heavily, ﴿amani﴾ with a doubled ya', he directs it to the pattern of their plurals such as "al-miftah, mafatih; al-qurqur, qaraqir; al-zunbur, zanabir," so the ya' of the form "fa'ali'il" and its lam came together, both being ya's, so one was assimilated into the other, and they became a single doubled ya'.
* *
As for the reading which, in my view, is the only one permissible for any reader in this matter, it is the doubling of the ya' of "al-amani," by the consensus of the readers that this is the reading which the predecessors (al-salaf) followed, which is widely transmitted among them, and whose authenticity is not disputed. The deviation of a reader in lightening it is contrary to what the consensus of proof has established in this matter. [[The construction of the phrase: "by the consensus of the readers that it is the reading... and by the deviation of the reader in lightening it," joined by coordination.]] And the consensus of the readers on refuting it is sufficient proof of the error of the one who reads it lightly. [[In the printed edition: "and sufficient as an error upon the reader of it," which is not correct speech; the correct text is what I have adopted, inferred from al-Tabari's wording elsewhere in similar cases.]]
* *
On the interpretation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿wa in hum illa yazunnun﴾ (78)
Abu Ja'far said: By His, the majestic and praised One's, saying: ﴿wa in hum illa yazunnun﴾ He means: "and they are not," as the Exalted said: ﴿Their messengers said to them: We are only men like yourselves﴾ [Ibrahim: 11], meaning: "We are not but men like you."
* *
The meaning of His saying ﴿illa yazunnun﴾ is: "only conjecture"; they do not doubt and do not know its reality and truth. The "zann" in this place means doubt.
So the meaning of the verse is: among them are those who do not write, nor read, nor know the Book of God, nor understand what is in it, except by fabrication and speaking falsehood against God, supposing that they are right in their fabrication and their false speech.
* *
The Exalted described them as being, in their fabrications, supposing themselves to be right while they are in falsehood, because they had heard from their chiefs and rabbis matters which they reckoned to be from the Book of God, but which were not from the Book of God. So He, the majestic and praised One, described them as abandoning belief in what they are certain comes from God, of what Muhammad ﷺ brought, and following what they are doubtful about and uncertain of in its reality, of what their elders, chiefs and rabbis told them, out of obstinacy towards God and His Messenger, opposition to God's command, and deception by God's respite granted to them. Of the same sense as what we have said concerning the interpretation of His saying ﴿wa in hum illa yazunnun﴾, the early interpreters (al-mutawwilun min al-salaf) said:

1374 - Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿wa in hum illa yazunnun﴾ "except that they lie."
1375 - al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa related to us, saying: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.
1376 - al-Qasim related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the like of it.
1377 - Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salama related to us, from Ibn Ishaq, saying: Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad related to me, from Ikrima or from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿la ya'lamun al-kitab illa amani wa in hum illa yazunnun﴾, that is: they do not know and do not understand what is in it, and they deny your prophethood by conjecture.
1378 - Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada: ﴿wa in hum illa yazunnun﴾, he said: they conjecture conjectures without truth.
1379 - al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Adam related to us, saying: Abu Ja'far related to us, from al-Rabi', from Abu al-'Aliya, he said: they conjecture conjectures without truth.
1380 - It was related to me from 'Ammar, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far related to us, from his father, from al-Rabi', the like of it.

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 79:**

**On the interpretation of His words, ﴿Fawaylun﴾ (So woe)**

Abu Ja'far said: The interpreters (ahl al-ta'wil) differed concerning the interpretation of His words, ﴿fawaylun﴾. Some of them said:

1381 - Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: 'Uthman ibn Sa'id related to us, from Bishr ibn 'Umara, from Abu Rawq, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning ﴿fawaylun﴾, that he said: "Then the punishment is upon them."[[In the printed edition: "fawaylun lahum" (woe to them). The correct reading omits "lahum," which is not part of the verse here.]]

* *

Others said:

1382 - Ibn Bashshar related this to us, saying: Ibn Mahdi related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Ziyad ibn Fayyad, who said: I heard Abu 'Iyad say: "Al-waylu is what flows of pus at the base of Jahannam."[[Report 1382: Sufyan is al-Thawri. Ziyad ibn Fayyad al-Khuza'i: trustworthy (thiqah), died in the year 129. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir of al-Bukhari 2/1/334, and Ibn Abi Hatim 1/2/542. Abu 'Iyad is 'Amr ibn al-Aswad al-'Ansi, a trustworthy Successor (tabi'i), who was among the devout worshippers and ascetics of Syria. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib and Ibn Abi Hatim 3/1/220-221.]]

1383 - Bishr ibn Aban al-Hattab related to us, saying: Waki' related to us, from Sufyan, from Ziyad ibn Fayyad, from Abu 'Iyad, concerning His words ﴿fawaylun﴾, that he said: "A cistern at the base of Jahannam, into which their pus flows."[[Report 1383: Bishr ibn Aban al-Hattab, Tabari's shaykh: I have found no biography of him nor any mention of him in the sources available to me.]]

1384 - 'Ali ibn Sahl al-Ramli related to us, saying: Zayd ibn Abi al-Zarqa' related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Ziyad ibn Fayyad, from Abu 'Iyad, who said: "Al-waylu is a valley of pus in Jahannam."[[Report 1384: 'Ali ibn Sahl al-Ramli, Tabari's shaykh: trustworthy, died in the year 261. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib and Ibn Abi Hatim 3/1/189. Zayd ibn Abi al-Zarqa' al-Mawsili, who settled in Ramla: trustworthy, died in the year 194. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir 2/1/361, and Ibn Abi Hatim 1/2/575. Sufyan is al-Thawri. "From Ziyad ibn Fayyad," as in the two isnads before it. In the printed edition: "Sufyan ibn Ziyad ibn Fayyad," which is a distortion.]]

1385 - Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Shaqiq, who said: "Waylun is what flows of pus at the base of Jahannam."

* *

Others said:

1386 - al-Muthanna related this to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn 'Abd al-Salam ibn Salih al-Tustari related to us, saying: 'Ali ibn Jarir related to us, from Hammad ibn Salama ibn 'Abd al-Hamid ibn Ja'far, from Kinana al-'Adawi, from 'Uthman ibn 'Affan, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "Al-waylu is a mountain in the Fire."[[Hadith 1386: This isnad is problematic, and an error occurred in it, either by the copyist or the printer. We corrected it from the later narration, 1395, where it read "Hammad ibn Salama ibn 'Abd al-Hamid ibn Ja'far," whereas the correct reading is "from 'Abd al-Hamid ibn Ja'far," as is evident.

What troubled us in it are two narrators for whom we found no mention and no biography.

The first: "Ibrahim ibn 'Abd al-Salam ibn Salih al-Tustari." In the other isnad, "Ibrahim ibn 'Abd al-Salam" appears alone. I could not determine who he is. Ibn Kathir (1:217) quoted the report that follows, 1395, and completed this shaykh's lineage, but in his text it reads: "Ibrahim ibn 'Abd al-Salam, related to us Salih al-Qushayri"! I am not confident in the accuracy of the correction in the edition of Ibn Kathir's tafsir, and I consider that the version in the copy of al-Tabari is closer to correct.

The second narrator: "'Ali ibn Jarir." I have labored to identify him, searching all the sources and examining every possibility.

As for 'Abd al-Hamid ibn Ja'far: he is al-Ansari al-Awsi al-Madani, and he is trustworthy. Ahmad, Ibn Sa'd, and others declared him trustworthy. He died in the year 153. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib and Ibn Abi Hatim 3/1/10. As for "Kinana al-'Adawi": he is Kinafa ibn Nu'aym, a trustworthy Successor, biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir of al-Bukhari 4/1/236, and Ibn Abi Hatim 3/2/169. But I fear that he did not meet 'Uthman ibn 'Affan, for they mention no narration of his except from Abu Barza al-Aslami and Qabisa ibn al-Mukhariq, and both are much later than 'Uthman.

In any case, I do not think this hadith's isnad can be sustained. It is an abridgement of the hadith that follows, 1395. Al-Hafiz Ibn Kathir, when he cited it from al-Tabari, described it as "very strange" (gharib jiddan). Al-Suyuti also mentioned it (1:82) and attributed it to no one other than al-Tabari. And Allah knows best.]]

1387 - Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Amr ibn al-Harith related to me, from Darraj, from Abu al-Haytham, from Abu Sa'id, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Waylun is a valley in Jahannam, into which the disbeliever plunges for forty autumns before reaching its bottom."[[Hadith 1387: Its isnad is sound. 'Amr ibn al-Harith ibn Ya'qub al-Ansari al-Misri: trustworthy, a memorizer (hafiz), precise. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib, Ibn Sa'd 7/2/203, and Ibn Abi Hatim 3/1/225. Darraj, with a fatha on the dal and a shadda on the ra', is Ibn Sam'an, Abu al-Samh, the Egyptian storyteller (al-qass). He is trustworthy, though there is much disagreement about him. Our preference is that he is trustworthy, as we explained in our commentary on the Musnad (6634) and in our annotations on Tahdhib al-Athar (2388). Abu al-Haytham is Sulayman ibn 'Amr al-'Itwari al-Misri. He was an orphan raised by Abu Sa'id al-Khudri in his care. He is a trustworthy Successor, biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir of al-Bukhari 2/2/28-29, and Ibn Abi Hatim 2/1/131-132.

Ibn Abi Hatim related this hadith, as Ibn Kathir (1:217) quoted from him, from Yunus ibn 'Abd al-A'la, Tabari's shaykh here, with this same isnad.

Al-Hakim related it in al-Mustadrak (4:596), through Bahr ibn Nasr, from Ibn Wahb, with this isnad, with an addition at its end. He said: "This hadith has a sound isnad, but the two (Bukhari and Muslim) did not record it." Al-Dhahabi agreed with him.

Ahmad related it in his Musnad (11735; vol. 3, p. 75, Halabi edition), from Hasan ibn Musa, from Ibn Lahi'a, from Darraj, with the same wording, with an addition at its end. Ibn Kathir said, following Ibn Abi Hatim's narration: "al-Tirmidhi related it from 'Abd ibn Humayd, from al-Hasan ibn Musa... and he said: 'This is a strange hadith, which we know only from the hadith of Ibn Lahi'a.' I say [the speaker is Ibn Kathir]: Ibn Lahi'a is not alone in it, as you see. But the defect lies with those after him! This hadith with this isnad, traced to the Prophet, is munkar!"

I say: Ibn Kathir intends by this to impugn Darraj Abu al-Samh and to make him the cause of the hadith's defect. The correct view is what we have taken. It was also related by Ibn Hibban in his Sahih, as in al-Durr al-Manthur (1:82).]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The meaning of the verse, according to what has been related from those whose statements I have cited regarding the interpretation of ﴿waylun﴾, is: Then the punishment, which is the drinking of the pus of the people of Jahannam at the bottom of the Blazing Fire, is for the Jews who write falsehood with their own hands, then say: "This is from Allah."

* *

On the interpretation of His words, the Exalted:

﴿Li-lladhina yaktubuna al-kitaba bi-aydihim thumma yaqulina hadha min 'indi Allahi li-yashtaru bihi thamanan qalilan﴾
(For those who write the Book with their own hands, then say, "This is from Allah," that they may trade it for a small price.)

Abu Ja'far said: He means by this those among the Jews of the Children of Israel who distorted the Book of Allah. They wrote a book according to their own interpretations, opposed to what Allah had revealed to His Prophet Musa (ﷺ). Then they sold it to a people who had no knowledge of it, nor of what is in the Torah, ignorant of what is in the Books of Allah, seeking a base worldly gain. So Allah said to them: ﴿So woe to them for what their hands have written, and woe to them for what they earn﴾, as:

1388 - Musa related to me, saying: 'Amr related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, concerning ﴿So woe to those who write the Book with their own hands, then say, "This is from Allah," that they may trade it for a small price﴾, that he said: "Some of the Jews wrote a book from themselves, which they sold to the Arabs, telling them it was from Allah, so that they might take a small price for it."

1389 - Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: 'Uthman ibn Sa'id related to us, saying: Bishr ibn 'Umara related to us, from Abu Rawq, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "The Ummiyyun are a people who did not believe in a messenger whom Allah sent, nor in a book which Allah revealed. So they wrote a book with their hands, then said to a base and ignorant people: 'This is from Allah,' ﴿that they may trade it for a small price﴾." He said: "A commodity from the commodities of this world."

1390 - Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, from 'Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning the words of Allah, ﴿For those who write the Book with their own hands, then say, "This is from Allah"﴾, that he said: "These are the ones who knew that it is from Allah, yet they distort it."

1391 - al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa related to us, saying: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it, except that he said: "then they distort it."

1392 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, from Qatada: ﴿So woe to those who write the Book with their own hands﴾, to the end of the verse; and they are the Jews.

1393 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada, concerning His words, ﴿So woe to those who write the Book with their own hands, then say, "This is from Allah"﴾, that he said: "Some people from the Children of Israel wrote a book with their own hands, in order to devour people's wealth, and they said: 'This is from Allah,' but it was not from Allah."[[One says: "Fulan yasta'kilu al-du'afa'" (so-and-so devours the weak): he takes their wealth and consumes it. As for his words "li-yata'akalu" (so that they might devour), I found no "yata'akkalu" in the lexicons. If the text of al-Tabari is correct, then it is an Arabic form that is rare or irregular, whether it is correct or not.]]

1394 - al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Adam related to us, saying: Abu Ja'far related to us, from al-Rabi', from Abu al-'Aliya, concerning His words: ﴿So woe to those who write the Book with their own hands, then say, "This is from Allah," that they may trade it for a small price﴾, that he said: "They resorted to what Allah had revealed in their Book concerning the description of Muhammad (ﷺ), and distorted it from its places, seeking thereby a commodity of worldly goods." Then He said: ﴿So woe to them for what their hands have written, and woe to them for what they earn﴾.

1395 - al-Muthanna ibn Ibrahim related to me, saying: Ibrahim ibn 'Abd al-Salam related to us, saying: 'Ali ibn Jarir related to us, from Hammad ibn Salama, from 'Abd al-Hamid ibn Ja'far, from Kinana al-'Adawi, from 'Uthman ibn 'Affan (may Allah be pleased with him), from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): ﴿So woe to them for what their hands have written, and woe to them for what they earn﴾. "Al-waylu is a mountain in the Fire, and it was revealed concerning the Jews, because they distorted the Torah, added to it what they liked, and erased from it what they disliked. They erased the name of Muhammad (ﷺ) from the Torah. Therefore Allah became angry with them, and He removed part of the Torah, and so He said: ﴿So woe to them for what their hands have written, and woe to them for what they earn﴾."[[Hadith 1395: Its discussion has already been given in detail under 1386.]]

1396 - Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Sa'id ibn Abi Ayyub informed me, from Muhammad ibn 'Ajlan, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from 'Ata' ibn Yasar, who said: "Waylun is a valley in Jahannam; if the mountains were set moving in it, they would melt from the intensity of its heat."[[Sayyarat: were made to enter and pushed to move. Inmaa'a al-milhu fi al-ma': the salt dissolved in the water. In Lisan al-'Arab it is related as the tafsir of 'Ata', and in it: "lamma'at," meaning it melted and flowed.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: If someone says to us: What is the meaning of His words: [[In the printed edition: "fa-ma wajhu fawaylun lilladhina," as if a letter had been dropped by the copyist or printer.]] ﴿So woe to those who write the Book with their own hands﴾? Is writing ever done without the hand, so that those addressed by this address needed to inform us about these people, whose story Allah has related, that they used to write the Book with their own hands?

It is said to him: The Book is from the children of Adam, and although it is by their hand, the Book may be attributed to someone other than its writer, and to one who did not himself take charge of forming its letters. One says: "So-and-so wrote to so-and-so with such-and-such." Even if the one who took charge of writing it by his own hand is not the one to whom the book is attributed, when the writer wrote it by the command of the one to whom the book is attributed. So our Lord informed His believing servants, by His words ﴿So woe to those who write the Book with their own hands﴾, that the rabbis of the Jews take charge of writing lies and slander against Allah with their own hands, knowingly and deliberately lying against Allah, then attribute it falsely to be from Allah and in the Book of Allah, [[One says: "nahala fulanun fulanan shi'ran" (so-and-so attributed a poem to so-and-so): he ascribed it to him falsely. Al-Tabari disliked saying what is not permissible for anyone to say about his Lord, the Glorified and Exalted, so he took a path among the styles of Arabic and said: "fa-nahalahu ila annahu min 'indi Allah," meaning he ascribed it falsely to being from Allah. He did not make the verb reach its two objects.]] as a lie upon Allah and a fabrication against Him. By His words ﴿those who write the Book with their own hands﴾, the Exalted negated that the one who took charge of writing that was some of their ignorant people, without the knowledge of their scholars and rabbis. This is similar to the saying of one who says: "So-and-so sold me his eye such-and-such, and so-and-so bought his self such-and-such," meaning by including "the self and the eye" in that statement, to remove any confusion for the listener, so that he would not think the one who took charge of selling or buying it was other than the one described as having the matter under his command, [[In the printed edition: "an yakuna al-mutawalla bay'a dhalika aw shira'ahu, ghayra al-mawsufi lahu amruhu," which is unclear and not intelligible, so I preferred to correct it as best I could.]] and to establish the true reality of the act for the one spoken of. Likewise is His words: ﴿So woe to those who write the Book with their own hands﴾.

* *

On the interpretation of His words, the Exalted:

﴿So woe to them for what their hands have written, and woe to them for what they earn (79)﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His words, the Exalted, ﴿So woe to them for what their hands have written﴾, He means: then the punishment, in the valley flowing with the pus of the people of the Fire at the bottom of Jahannam, is for them, that is, for those who write the Book, which we have described, among the Jews of the Children of Israel, distorted, then say: "This is from Allah," seeking a worldly gain, a small one, from those who buy it from them.

* *

As for His words ﴿for what their hands have written﴾, He says: For what their hands have written of that, and woe to them also ﴿for what they earn﴾, meaning: for what they do of the sins, what they commit of the transgressions, and what they gain of the unlawful through their book which they write with their own hands, contrary to what Allah has revealed, then they consume its price, and they have sold it to those among them who bought it, claiming it is from the Book of Allah, as:

1397 - al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Adam related to us, saying: Abu Ja'far related to us, from al-Rabi', from Abu al-'Aliya: ﴿And woe to them for what they earn﴾, meaning: for the wrongdoing.

1398 - Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: 'Uthman ibn Sa'id related to us, from Bishr ibn 'Umara, from Abu Rawq, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿So woe to them﴾, he says: "Then the punishment is upon them." He said: "He says: for what they wrote with their hands of that falsehood, ﴿and woe to them for what they earn﴾, he says: for what they eat by means of it from the base and others."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The root of "al-kasb" is work. Whoever works at something, by his own direct engagement with what he does and by toil in a trade, is a "kasib" of what he has done, as Labid ibn Rabi'a said:

*Li-mu'fari qahdin tanazza'a shalwuhu / ghabsun kawasibu la yumannu ta'amuha*
(For a dust-covered young cow whose limb they fought over, / wild wolves that earn their food and are not beholden to anyone for it.) [[From his noble Mu'allaqa. The "li-" in his words "li-mu'fari" refers it back to the verse before it: "khansa'u daye'at al-farira fa-lam yarim / 'urda al-shaqa'iqi tawfuhā wa-bughamuha" (A wild cow that lost her calf, and did not leave / the wide plain of al-Shaqa'iq, her circling and her lowing). Al-khansa': the wild cow; al-farir: her calf. Al-shaqa'iq: rough land between two sand dunes, where she had left her calf. Tawfuha: her circling, wandering in confusion. Bughamuha: her calling, crying out in grief. She kept circling and calling for her calf. His words "li-mu'fari," meaning her circling and lowing were on account of "mu'far." Al-mu'far: the one cast into the dust, which is 'afar, the earth; the wolves had hunted her calf. Qahd: a young cow, slender of body and white in color. Al-shalw: a limb of meat, or the whole body. Ghabs: ghabr, which means wolves. La yumannu ta'amuha: they earn their food by themselves, so no one can claim favor over them.]]

Commentary on the interpretation of His words, the Exalted: ﴿And they say: The Fire will not touch us except for numbered days﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His words ﴿And they say﴾ He means the Jews. The meaning is: the Jews said, ﴿The Fire will not touch us﴾, meaning our bodies will not meet the Fire and we will not enter it, ﴿except for numbered days﴾. The phrase "numbered" (ma'dudah) was used although its number is not specified in the revelation, because God, mighty is His praise, related this of them while they knew the number of the days which they had set for their stay in the Fire. Therefore He omitted mention of the number of those days and described them as "numbered" for the reason we have stated.

* *

Then the interpreters differed about the extent of the numbered days which the Jews had specified, those who said what God related of them on this matter. Some of them said:

1399 - Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: 'Uthman ibn Sa'id related to us, from Bishr ibn 'Ammarah, from Abu Rawq, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿And they say: The Fire will not touch us except for numbered days﴾. He said: This was said by the enemies of God, the Jews. They said: God will not make us enter the Fire except for the period of the oath (tahillat al-qasam), the days in which we worshipped the calf: forty days. When those days have passed, the punishment and the oath will end for us.

1400 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, concerning His words: ﴿The Fire will not touch us except for numbered days﴾. They said: numbered days, corresponding to what we worshipped the calf.

1401 - Musa related to us, saying: 'Amr related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿And they say: The Fire will not touch us except for numbered days﴾. He said: The Jews said: God will make us enter the Fire and we will remain in it forty nights, until the Fire has consumed our sins and cleansed us, [[naqqaytu al-thawb (with shaddah on the qaf) and anqaytuhu naqa'an, so it is naqiy: clean. "Istanqaytuhu" is not in the lexicons, but its formation and meaning are sound.]] then a caller will call out: Bring out every circumcised man of the children of Israel. That is why we were commanded to be circumcised. They said: So they will not leave anyone of us in the Fire without bringing him out.

1402 - al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Adam related to us, saying: Abu Ja'far related to us, from al-Rabi', from Abu al-'Aliyah, who said: The Jews said: Our Lord was displeased with us in our affair, so He swore that He would punish us forty nights, then bring us out. God refuted them.

1403 - al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Adam related to us, saying: Abu Ja'far related to us, from Qatadah, who said: The Jews said: We will not enter the Fire except for the period of the oath, the number of days in which we worshipped the calf.

1404 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: My father related to me, saying: My paternal uncle related to me, saying: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His words: ﴿The Fire will not touch us except for numbered days﴾, the verse. Ibn 'Abbas said: It is mentioned that the Jews found written in the Torah that the distance between the two edges of Hell is a forty-year journey, until one reaches the tree of al-Zaqqum growing at the root of the blazing Fire. (Ibn 'Abbas used to say: al-Jahim is Saqar, and in it is the tree of al-Zaqqum.) The enemies of God claimed that when the number they found in their book had passed, namely the numbered days, (and by that they meant the journey which ends at the root of the blazing Fire), they said: When the number has passed, the term has ended, and there will be no punishment, and Hell will go away and perish. [[khala yakhlu: passed, went away, came to an end.]] This is His words: ﴿The Fire will not touch us except for numbered days﴾, meaning by that the term. Ibn 'Abbas said: When they plunged through the gate of Hell, they went on in punishment until they reached the tree of al-Zaqqum on the last of the numbered days. The guardians of Saqar said to them: You claimed you would not be touched by the Fire except for numbered days! The number has passed, and you are in eternity! Then they were driven up into the ascent in Hell, ﴿they will be overwhelmed﴾. [[al-Su'ud: the hardship of punishment; but he meant here what they said: a mountain in Hell of a single ember, which the disbeliever is compelled to climb, and he is struck with maqami'; whenever he places his foot upon it, it melts down to the lowest level, then it returns to its place sound again, and God knows best.]]

1405 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: My father related to me, saying: My paternal uncle related to me, saying: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿And they say: The Fire will not touch us except for numbered days﴾, namely forty nights.

1406 - al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Ishaq related to us, saying: Hafs ibn 'Umar related to us, from al-Hakam ibn Aban, from 'Ikrimah, who said: The Jews disputed with the Messenger of God ﷺ and said: We will not enter the Fire except for forty nights, and other people will succeed us in it, meaning Muhammad and his companions. The Messenger of God ﷺ pointed with his hand at their heads [[qala biyadihi: he gestured. The like of this has passed many times.]] and said: "Rather, you will abide in it forever; no one will succeed you in it." Then God, mighty is His praise, revealed: ﴿And they say: The Fire will not touch us except for numbered days﴾.

1407 - al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to us, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: al-Hakam ibn Aban informed me, from 'Ikrimah, who said: The Jews gathered one day disputing with the Prophet ﷺ. They said: ﴿The Fire will not touch us except for numbered days﴾, and they named forty days, then people will succeed us or join us in it. They pointed to the Prophet ﷺ and his companions. The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "You have lied; rather, you will abide in it eternally, forever. We will not join you nor succeed you in it, God willing, ever."
[[The two reports, 1406 and 1407, are one hadith with two chains. al-Suyuti also attributed it (1:84) to 'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim. It is a mursal hadith, and it does not establish proof.]]

1408 - Yunus ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to me, saying: 'Ali ibn Ma'bad informed us, from Abu Mu'awiyah, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak concerning His words: ﴿The Fire will not touch us except for numbered days﴾, who said: The Jews said: We will not be punished in the Fire on the Day of Resurrection except for forty days, the measure of what we worshipped the calf.

1409 - Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: My father related to me that the Messenger of God ﷺ said to them: "I adjure you by God and by the Torah which God sent down to Moses on the day of Mount Sinai: who are the people of the Fire whom God mentioned in the Torah?" They said: Their Lord became angry with them with a great anger, so we will remain in the Fire forty nights, then we will come out, and you will succeed us in it. The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "You have lied, by God; we will never succeed you in it." So the Qur'an was revealed confirming the Prophet's ﷺ words and refuting them: ﴿And they say: The Fire will not touch us except for numbered days. Say: Have you taken a covenant with God, so that God will not break His covenant? Or do you say about God what you do not know?﴾ up to His words: ﴿they will abide therein forever﴾.
[[The hadith 1409 is also a mursal hadith.]]

* *

And others said concerning this:

1410 - Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Yunus ibn Bukayr related to us, saying: Ibn Ishaq related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, client of Zayd ibn Thabit, related to me, saying: Sa'id ibn Jubayr or 'Ikrimah related to me, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Jews used to say: The duration of the world is only seven thousand years, and God only punishes people on the Day of Resurrection with one day of the Hereafter for every thousand years of the days of this world, and that makes seven days. So God revealed concerning their saying: ﴿And they say: The Fire will not touch us except for numbered days﴾, the verse.

1411 - Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salamah related to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, who said: Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad related to me, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr or 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ came to Medina, while the Jews were saying: The duration of the world is only seven thousand years, and people are punished in the Fire for every thousand years of the days of this world with one day in the Fire of the days of the Hereafter; so it is only seven days, then the punishment ends. So God, mighty and majestic, revealed concerning their saying: ﴿The Fire will not touch us﴾, the verse.

1412 - Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, from 'Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning God's words: ﴿They said: The Fire will not touch us except for numbered days﴾, who said: They used to say: The world is only seven thousand years, and we will be punished for each thousand years with one day.

1413 - al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah related to us, saying: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it, except that he said: The Jews used to say: The world only... and the rest of the report is like it.

1414 - al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, saying: Ibn Jurayj said: Mujahid said: ﴿And they said: The Fire will not touch us except for numbered days of time﴾. They named the number seven thousand years, one day for every thousand years. The Jews were saying it.

* *

Concerning the interpretation of His words, the Exalted: ﴿Say: Have you taken a covenant with God? For God will not break His covenant. Or do you say about God what you do not know?﴾ (80)

Abu Ja'far said: When the Jews said what they said, ﴿The Fire will not touch us except for numbered days﴾, as we have explained of its interpretation, God said to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: Say, O Muhammad, to the company of the Jews: ﴿Have you taken a covenant with God?﴾ Have you received from God a pledge for what you say on this matter? For God does not break His pledge, nor change His promise and His bond. Or do you say about God falsehood, out of ignorance and audacity against Him? As:

1415 - Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to us, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, from 'Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿Say: Have you taken a covenant with God?﴾, i.e., a binding pledge from God that it is as you say.

1416 - al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah related to us, saying: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

1417 - al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Adam related to us, saying: Abu Ja'far related to us, from Qatadah, who said: The Jews said: We will not enter the Fire except for the period of the oath, the number of days in which we worshipped the calf. God said: ﴿Have you taken a covenant with God?﴾ For this that you say? Do you have proof and evidence for this? God will not break His covenant. So bring your proof and evidence, or do you say about God what you do not know?

1418 - Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: 'Uthman ibn Sa'id related to us, from Bishr ibn 'Ammarah, from Abu Rawq, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: When the Jews said what they said, God, mighty is His praise, said to Muhammad: Say, "Have you taken a covenant with God?" That is: have you stored up a covenant with God? That is: did you say "There is no god but God" without associating anything with Him or disbelieving in Him? If you said it, then hope by it. If you did not say it, why do you say about God what you do not know? That is: if you had said "There is no god but God" and not associated anything with Him, and then died upon that, it would have been a treasure for you with Me, and I would not break My promise to you that I would reward you for it.

1419 - Musa ibn Harun related to me, saying: 'Amr related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, who said: When the Jews said what they said, God, mighty and majestic, said: ﴿Say: Have you taken a covenant with God? For God will not break His covenant﴾. And He said in another place: ﴿And what they used to fabricate deceived them in their religion﴾ [Al 'Imran: 24], then He informed of the matter, saying: ﴿Nay, whoever earns an evil deed﴾.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: These sayings which we have related from Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid and Qatadah are close to what we have said in the interpretation of His words: ﴿Say: Have you taken a covenant with God?﴾ For among what God gave His servants of His covenant is that whoever believes in Him and obeys His command, He will save him from His Fire on the Day of Resurrection.
