Some of them recited it: ﴿And God is not unaware of what they do﴾ with the *yā'* (third person), in the manner of reporting about them, so it is as if by their recitation they intended the meaning: "Then what is the recompense of those among you who do that except disgrace in the life of this world, and on the Day of Resurrection they will be returned to the most severe punishment, and God is not unaware of what they do," meaning: of what those whom God informed about, that there is no recompense for their deed except disgrace in the life of this world, and their return in the Hereafter is to the most severe punishment.
* *
Others recited it: ﴿And God is not unaware of what you do﴾ with the *tā'* (second person), in the manner of addressing them.
He said: So it is as if by their recitation they intended: ﴿Do you believe in part of the Book and disbelieve in part?﴾ And God is not unaware, O assembly of Jews, of what you yourselves do.
* *
The more pleasing of the two readings to me is the reading of the one who recited it with the *yā'*, following His saying: ﴿Then what is the recompense of those among you who do that﴾ and His saying: ﴿And on the Day of Resurrection they will be returned﴾. This is because His saying ﴿And God is not unaware of what they do﴾ is closer to that than to His saying ﴿Do you believe in part of the Book and disbelieve in part?﴾, and following the closer one is more appropriate than attaching it to the more distant one. The other reading is not far from correct.
* *
As for the interpretation of His saying "And God is not unaware of what they do," [[In the printed edition: "وتأويل قوله: وما الله بساه" (wa-ta'wil qawlihi: wa-ma Allah bi-sahin), which does not mention the verse, and the correct form is to include it.]] it means: God is not heedless of their corrupt deeds; rather, He counts them and keeps them recorded against them until He recompenses them for them in the Hereafter, and disgraces them in this world, humiliating them and exposing them. [[The explanation of the meaning of "heedlessness" (*ghafla*) has passed earlier in this part, 2: 244.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 86:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, saying: ﴿Those are the ones who have bought the worldly life with the Hereafter; so the punishment will not be lightened for them, nor will they be helped.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His saying, may His praise be great, "Those," He means those whom He informed about, that they believe in part of the Book, so they ransom their captives from among the Jews, and disbelieve in part, so they kill those among their own religious community whom God forbade them to kill, and expel from his home whom God forbade them to expel from his home, in violation of the covenant of God and His pact with them in the Torah. Then He, may His praise be great, informed that these [are] the ones who have bought the leadership of the worldly life over the weak and the ignorant and foolish among their own religious community, [[The words between the brackets are an addition; the sentence is not sound without omitting them.]] and purchased with faith the base and inferior foods of this world, the eternal abiding in the Gardens that would have been theirs in the Hereafter had they brought faith instead of disbelief. God, may His praise be great, described them as having bought the worldly life with the Hereafter only because they were content with the world by their disbelief in God therein, in exchange for the bliss of the Hereafter that God had prepared for the believers. So He made their portion of the bliss of the Hereafter, through their disbelief in God, a price for what they had purchased with the base worldly life. [[See what has passed, 1: 312-315, on the meaning of "purchasing" (al-ishtira').]] As follows:

1482 - Bishr narrated to us, Yazid said, Yazid said, Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿Those who have bought the worldly life with the Hereafter﴾, they preferred the little of the world over the much of the Hereafter. [[The narration: 1482 - In the printed edition it read: "Yazid narrated to us..." with the omission of "Bishr said", and this is its chain to Qatadah, which recurs frequently; the closest previous instance is no. 1475.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: Then God, may His praise be great, informed that when they sold their portion of the bliss of the Hereafter, by abandoning His obedience and preferring disbelief in Him and the base of the world over it, they have no portion in the bliss of the Hereafter, and that what awaits them in the Hereafter is punishment, the punishment not being lightened for them therein. For the one whose punishment is lightened therein is the one who has a portion of its bliss, and these have none, because they bought their worldly life with their Hereafter in exchange for what was in the world. [[In the printed edition: "because of their purchase of what was in the world and their worldly life with their Hereafter", which is a faulty sentence; the correct reading is likely what has been adopted here.]]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿nor will they be helped﴾, He informed about them that no one will help them in the Hereafter, so as to repel from them the punishment of God through His help, neither by his strength, nor by his intercession, nor by anything else.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 87:

The discussion on the interpretation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿And We certainly gave Moses the Book, and We followed up after him with messengers﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿We gave Moses the Book﴾, He means: We sent it down to him. We have already explained that the meaning of "al-iytaa'" (giving) is "al-i'taa'" (bestowal), earlier on. [[See what has preceded, 1:574.]]

* *

The "Book" which Allah gave Moses, peace be upon him, is the Torah.

As for His saying: ﴿wa-qaffaynaa﴾ (and We followed up), it means: We sent after and caused some of them to follow others one after another, just as a man follows (yaqfu) another man when he walks in his track from behind. Its root is from "al-qafa" (the back of the neck/back), and one says from it: "qafawtu fulaanan" (I followed so-and-so), when I came behind his back, just as one says "dabbartuhu" (I came behind him) when I came into his rear.

* *

By His saying: ﴿min ba'dihi﴾ (after him), He means: after Moses.

* *

By ﴿ar-Rusul﴾ (the messengers) He means: the prophets, and it is the plural of "rasul" (messenger). One says: "huwa rasoolun wa-hum rusulun" (he is a messenger and they are messengers), just as one says: "huwa saboorun wa-hum qawmun sabrun" (he is patient and they are a patient people), and "huwa rajulun shakoorun wa-hum qawmun shukrun" (he is a grateful man and they are a grateful people).

* *

What the Exalted means by His saying: ﴿And We followed up after him with the messengers﴾ is that We caused some of them to follow others, upon one method and one law. For everyone whom Allah sent as a prophet after Moses, peace be upon him, until the time of Jesus son of Mary, He sent only to command the Children of Israel to uphold the Torah, to act upon what is in it, and to call to what is in it. Therefore it is said: ﴿And We followed up after him with the messengers﴾, meaning upon his method and his law, and acting by what he acted upon.

* *

The discussion on the interpretation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿And We gave Jesus son of Mary the clear signs﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His saying: ﴿And We gave Jesus son of Mary the clear signs﴾, He means: We bestowed upon Jesus son of Mary.

* *

By "al-bayyinaat" (the clear signs) which Allah gave him, He means: the proofs and evidences of his prophethood which were manifested at his hands: the raising of the dead, the healing of the blind and the leper, and similar signs, which made clear his station with Allah and indicated his truthfulness and the soundness of his prophethood, as:

1483 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, or Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿And We gave Jesus son of Mary the clear signs﴾: that is, the signs which were set in motion at his hands: the raising of the dead, and his fashioning from clay the likeness of a bird, then he breathed into it and it became a bird by Allah's permission, and the healing of diseases, and the informing of many unseen matters which they stored in their houses, and what was returned to them of the Torah, along with the Gospel which Allah revealed to him.

* *

The discussion on the interpretation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿And We strengthened him with the Holy Spirit﴾

Abu Ja'far said: As for the meaning of His saying: ﴿wa-ayyadnaahu﴾ (and We strengthened him), it means: We made him strong and aided him, as:

1484 - Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abu Zuhayr narrated to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak: ﴿wa-ayyadnaahu﴾, he says: We aided him. One says from it: "ayyadaka Allah" (may Allah strengthen you), that is, "qawwaaka" (He made you strong), and "wa-huwa rajulun dhu ayd, wa-dhu aad" (he is a man of strength), meaning: possessing strength. And from it is the saying of al-'Ajjaj:

[poetry, translated as it stands] ...

By "al-ayd" he means: strong.

* *

Then they differed concerning the interpretation of His saying: ﴿bi-ruh al-qudus﴾ (with the Holy Spirit). Some of them said: "Ruh al-Qudus", with which Allah, mentioned and exalted, informed that He strengthened Jesus, is Gabriel, peace be upon him.

Mention of those who said that:

1485 - Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, concerning His saying: ﴿And We strengthened him with the Holy Spirit﴾, he said: It is Gabriel.

1486 - Musa ibn Harun narrated to me, saying: 'Amr ibn Hammad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, concerning His saying: ﴿with the Holy Spirit﴾, he said: It is Gabriel, peace be upon him.

1487 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abu Zuhayr narrated to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, concerning His saying: ﴿with the Holy Spirit﴾, he said: The Holy Spirit is Gabriel.

1488 - 'An 'Ammar narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi': ﴿with the Holy Spirit﴾, he said: He strengthened Jesus with Gabriel, who is the Holy Spirit.

1489 - Ibn Humayd said: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi al-Husayn al-Makki narrated to me, from Shahr ibn Hawshab al-Ash'ari: that a group of Jews asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "Inform us about the Spirit." He said: "I adjure you by Allah and by His days among the Children of Israel: do you know that it is Gabriel, and that he is the one who comes to me?" They said: "Yes." [[Hadith 1489: In the printed edition it reads "Salamah narrated to us, from Ishaq", which is an error; the correct reading is "from Ibn Ishaq". 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi al-Husayn al-Makki: a trustworthy jurist, one of the teachers of al-Layth and Malik. Shahr ibn Hawshab al-Ash'ari: a trustworthy Successor, and whoever spoke against him has no proof against him. This hadith is mursal, since Shahr is a Successor as we have said. Its meaning, that "the Spirit" is Gabriel, is established in many sound reports, of which Ibn Kathir mentions (1:227) the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud in Sahih Ibn Hibban, raised: "Ruh al-Qudus breathed into my heart that no soul will die until it completes its provision and its term, so fear Allah and be graceful in seeking." This hadith is part of a longer hadith which will come with this chain later, no. 1606.]]

Others said: The Spirit with which Allah strengthened Jesus is the Gospel.

Mention of those who said that:

1490 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying: ﴿And We strengthened him with the Holy Spirit﴾: Allah strengthened Jesus with the Gospel as a spirit, just as He made the Qur'an a spirit; both are the Spirit of Allah, as Allah says: ﴿And thus We revealed to you a spirit from Our command﴾ [al-Shura: 52].

* *

Others said: It is the Name with which Jesus used to revive the dead.

Mention of those who said that:

1491 - It was narrated to me from al-Minjab, who said: Bishr ibn 'Ammarah narrated to us, from Abu Rawq, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿with the Holy Spirit﴾, he said: It is the Name with which Jesus used to revive the dead.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of these interpretations is the saying of the one who said that "the Spirit" in this place is Gabriel. For Allah, mentioned and exalted, informed that He strengthened Jesus with it, as He informed in His saying: (When Allah said: "O Jesus son of Mary, remember My favour upon you and upon your mother, when I strengthened you with the Holy Spirit, you spoke to people in the cradle and in maturity, and when I taught you the Book, wisdom, the Torah and the Gospel") [al-Ma'idah: 110]. If the Spirit with which Allah strengthened him were the Gospel, then His saying "when I strengthened you with the Holy Spirit" and "when I taught you the Book, wisdom, the Torah and the Gospel" would be a repetition of a statement with no meaning. That is because, according to the interpretation of the one who said that the meaning of "when I strengthened you with the Holy Spirit" is only "when I strengthened you with the Gospel, and when I taught you the Gospel", and one is not strengthened by it unless one is taught it, this is a repetition of one statement, without any added meaning in one over the other. That is a defect in speech ("khalf": corrupt, bad speech; one says in the proverb: "He kept silent a thousand years and spoke nonsense," of a man who prolongs silence, then when he speaks he speaks error and folly), and Allah, mentioned and exalted, is far above addressing His servants with what gives them no benefit. Since this is so, the corruption of the saying of the one who claimed that "the Spirit" in this place is the Gospel is clear, even though all of the books of Allah which He revealed to His messengers are a spirit from Him, since by them dead hearts come to life, souls turning away are revived, and erring minds are guided.

* *

Allah, mentioned and exalted, called Gabriel "a spirit" and attributed him to "al-Qudus" (the Holy), because he was, by Allah's creating him, a spirit from Him, without a father's begetting a child. So He named him "a spirit" and attributed him to "al-Qudus" — and "al-Qudus" is purity — just as Jesus son of Mary was named "a spirit from Allah" because of His creating him as a spirit from Him without a father's begetting a child.

* *

We have explained earlier in this book that the meaning of "taqdis" (sanctification) is purification, and "al-qudus" is purity, from this root. The people of interpretation have differed about its meaning in this place, similar to their disagreement in the place we mentioned.

[[See what has preceded, 1:475–476.]]

1492 - Musa narrated to me, saying: 'Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, who said: "al-Qudus" is blessing.

1493 - It was narrated to me from 'Ammar, who said: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, who said: "al-Qudus" is the Lord, mentioned and exalted.

1494 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: ﴿And We strengthened him with the Holy Spirit﴾, he said: "Allah, al-Qudus", and He strengthened Jesus with His spirit. He said: a description of Allah, al-Qudus. And he recited the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿He is Allah, other than whom there is no god, the King, the Holy (al-Quddus)﴾ [al-Hashr: 23], and said: "al-Qudus" and "al-Quddus" are one.

1495 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: 'Amr ibn al-Harith informed me, from Sa'id ibn Abi Hilal, [from Hilal] ibn Usamah, from 'Ata' ibn Yasar, who said: Ka'b said: "Allah, al-Qudus." [[This report is a saying of Ka'b al-Ahbar. The chain to him contains a difficulty, and it is perhaps an error of the copyists, since none of the narrators known to us is called "Sa'id ibn Abi Hilal ibn Usamah" as in the printed edition. The correct reading is what we have preferred, with the addition of "[from Hilal]".]]

* *

The discussion on the interpretation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿Is it that whenever a messenger came to you with what your souls did not desire, you waxed proud, so a group of them you denied and a group of them you killed?﴾ (87)

Abu Ja'far said: By His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿Is it that whenever a messenger came to you with what your souls did not desire﴾, He means the Jews of the Children of Israel.

1496 - Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, with this.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: Allah, mentioned and exalted, says to them: O assembly of the Jews, the Children of Israel, We indeed gave Moses the Torah, and We followed up after him with messengers to you, and We gave Jesus son of Mary the clear signs and proofs when We sent him to you, and strengthened him with the Holy Spirit. And you, whenever a messenger from My messengers came to you with other than what your souls desired, you waxed proud against them, with tyranny and transgression, like the pride of your leader Iblis, so you denied some of them and killed some. This has always been your conduct toward My messengers.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Is it that whenever﴾, although it comes in the form of a question addressed to them, it carries the meaning of a statement.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 88:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, saying: ﴿And they say, "Our hearts are closed (ghulf)."﴾

Abu Ja'far said: The readers differed concerning the recitation of this. Some of them read it: ﴿وقالوا قلوبنا غُلْف﴾ with the lam lightened and quiescent (ghulf). This is the recitation of the common folk of the cities in all the regions. Others read it: "وقالوا قلوبنا غُلُف" with the lam heavy and vowelled with a damma (ghuluf).

* *

As for those who read it with the lam quiescent and lightened, they interpreted it as meaning that they said: "Our hearts are in coverings, and wrappings, and sheaths (ghulf)." The word "ghulf," according to the reading of these people, is the plural of "aghlaf" (ajlaf), which is one who is in a sheath or covering, just as a man who has not been circumcised is called "aghlaf," and a woman "ghalfa'." And just as a sword that is in its scabbard is called "sword aghlaf," and a bow "ghalfa'," whose plural is "ghulf." Likewise, the plural of adjectives whose masculine is on the pattern "af'al" and whose feminine is on "fa'la'" is formed on "fu'l," with the first vowelled with a damma and the second quiescent, such as "ahmar and humr, and asfar and safr," so that this serves as the plural for both feminine and masculine. It is not permissible to make the middle letter of "fa'l" heavy in this form except out of poetic necessity, as Tarafa ibn al-Abd said:

O youths in our gathering, bring forth from them the ready and the bay(?)...

[Note: "jarradu" means: advance them for the raid. Tajarrada al-faras: the horse advanced in the race and came out of it. Ward (pl. warid) are horses between the dark bay and the chestnut. Ashqar: a clear red...]

He means "shuqran," but the poetry compelled him to move its second letter, so he moved it. From this is the report that:

1497 - Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: al-Hakam ibn Bashir ibn Salman related to us, saying: Amr ibn Qays al-Mala'i related to us, from Amr ibn Murra al-Jamali, from Abu al-Bakhtari, from Hudhayfa, who said: "The hearts are four," and he mentioned them, and among what he mentioned: "And a heart that is sheathed and bound upon, that is the heart of the disbeliever."

[Commentary note: this report is a mawquf report from Hudhayfa; its isnad is good but disconnected, as we will explain. ... Abu al-Bakhtari, died 83; Hudhayfa ibn al-Yaman died early 36 AH... This report is cited by al-Suyuti, and its meaning is also attested marfu' in Ahmad's Musnad from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, with a sound isnad...]

* *

Mention of those who said this, meaning that they are in coverings.

1498 - Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salama related to us, saying: Ibn Ishaq related to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad related to me, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, or Ikrima, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿And they said, "Our hearts are closed (ghulf)."﴾ — meaning, "in coverings."

1499 - al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiya ibn Salih related to us, from Abu Talha, from Ibn Abbas, his saying: ﴿Our hearts are ghulf﴾ — meaning, "in a covering."

1500 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿And they said, "Our hearts are closed (ghulf)."﴾ — they are the hearts upon which a seal has been set.

1501 - Abbas ibn Muhammad related to me, saying: Hajjaj related to us, saying: Ibn Jurayj said: Abd Allah ibn Kathir informed me, from Mujahid, his saying: ﴿And they said, "Our hearts are closed (ghulf)."﴾ — upon them is a veil.

1502 - al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa related to us, saying: Shibl related to us, saying: Abd Allah ibn Kathir informed me, from Mujahid: ﴿And they said, "Our hearts are closed (ghulf)."﴾ — upon them is a veil.

1503 - Ahmad ibn Ishaq al-Ahwazi related to us, saying: Abu Ahmad al-Zubayri related to us, saying: Sharik related to us, from al-A'mash, his saying: ﴿Our hearts are ghulf﴾ — he said: they are in ghulf.

1504 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh related to us, saying: Yazid ibn Zuray' related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada: ﴿And they said, "Our hearts are closed (ghulf)."﴾ — meaning, they do not understand.

1505 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada: ﴿And they said, "Our hearts are closed (ghulf)."﴾ He said: it is like His saying: ﴿Our hearts are in coverings﴾ [Fussilat: 5].

1506 - al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Ishaq related to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada concerning His saying: ﴿Our hearts are ghulf﴾, he said: upon them is a seal. He said: it is like His saying: ﴿Our hearts are in coverings﴾.

1507 - al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Adam related to us, saying: Abu Ja'far related to us, from al-Rabi', from Abu al-Aliya: ﴿Our hearts are ghulf﴾ — meaning, they do not understand.

1508 - Musa related to me, saying: Amr related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿And they said, "Our hearts are closed (ghulf)."﴾ He said: they say: upon them is a sheath, which is a covering.

1509 - Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said concerning His saying: ﴿Our hearts are ghulf﴾, he said: he says: "My heart is in a sheath, so nothing of what you say reaches it," and he recited: ﴿And they said, "Our hearts are in coverings from what you call us to"﴾ [Fussilat: 5].

* *

Abu Ja'far said: As for those who read "ghulf" with the lam vowelled and heavy, they interpreted it as meaning that they said: "Our hearts are ghulf for knowledge," in the sense that they are receptacles.

He said: "Ghulf," according to the interpretation of these people, is the plural of "ghilaf," just as "kitab" is pluralized as "kutub," "hijab" as "hujub," and "shihab" as "shuhub." So the meaning of the speech according to the interpretation of the reading of one who reads "ghulf" with the lam vowelled and heavy is: and the Jews said, "Our hearts are receptacles for knowledge, and receptacles for it and for other than it."

Mention of those who said this:

1510 - Ubayd ibn Asbat ibn Muhammad related to me, saying: my father related to us, from Fudayl ibn Marzuq, from Ata': ﴿And they said, "Our hearts are closed (ghulf)."﴾ He said: receptacles for remembrance.

1511 - Muhammad ibn Ammara al-Asadi related to me, saying: Ubayd Allah ibn Musa related to us, saying: Fudayl informed us, from Ata' concerning His saying: ﴿Our hearts are ghulf﴾ — he said: receptacles for knowledge.

1512 - Ahmad ibn Ishaq al-Ahwazi related to us, saying: Abu Ahmad related to us, saying: Fudayl related to us, from Ata' the like of it.

1513 - It was related to me from al-Minjab, saying: Bishr ibn Ammara related to us, from Abu Rawq, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn Abbas concerning His saying: ﴿And they said, "Our hearts are closed (ghulf)."﴾ He said: filled with knowledge, not needing Muhammad ﷺ or anyone else.

* *

The recitation that is not permissible other than it, concerning His saying: ﴿Our hearts are ghulf﴾, is the recitation of one who reads ﴿ghulf﴾ with the lam quiescent — in the sense that they are in veils and coverings — because the proof of the readers and the people of interpretation converges upon its soundness, and the aberration of whoever departs from them by what contradicts it, reading it with a damma on the lam.

We have shown that what the consensus of proof has brought is binding upon those who have received it, and what a lone transmitter has brought may not be set against what the body that constitutes proof has transmitted, in narration, statement and practice, in other places; this suffices against repeating it here. [See what has preceded in this volume, 2: 210, 211, 265, 295.]

* *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿Nay, Allah has cursed them for their disbelief﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His saying, may His praise be great: ﴿Nay, Allah has cursed them﴾, He means: Nay, Allah has distanced them, removed them far away, expelled them, humiliated them, and destroyed them, for their disbelief, their denial of the signs and proofs of Allah, what He sent His messengers with, and their denial of His prophets. He, may He be exalted, informs that He has removed them far from Himself and from His mercy because of what they used to do of that.

* *

The root of "la'n" (cursing) is expulsion, distancing, and removal; one says: "Allah curse so-and-so, cursing him, and he is cursed (malʿun)." Then the form "maf'ul" is inflected to "la'in" (accursed). From it is the saying of al-Shammakh ibn Dirar:

She was startled by it, the sandgrouse, and it was removed from it,
the place of the wolf, like the accursed man...

* *

Abu Ja'far said: In the saying of Allah, may His remembrance be great: ﴿Nay, Allah has cursed them for their disbelief﴾ is a denial by Him of the Jews' statement: ﴿Our hearts are ghulf﴾, because His saying "Nay" indicates His rejection and denial of what they claimed, since "bal" is only introduced into speech to negate something denied. Given that this is so, it is clear that the meaning of the verse is: the Jews said: "Our hearts are in coverings from what you call us to, O Muhammad." Then Allah, may His remembrance be great, said: it is not as they claim, but Allah has removed the Jews far away from His mercy, expelled them from it, and humiliated them for their denial of Him and His messengers; "so little is it that they believe."

* *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿So little is it that they believe﴾

Abu Ja'far said: The people of interpretation differed concerning the interpretation of His saying: ﴿So little is it that they believe﴾. Some of them said, its meaning is: few of them believe, i.e., only a few of them believe.

Mention of those who said this:

1514 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh related to us, saying: Yazid ibn Zuray' related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, his saying: ﴿Nay, Allah has cursed them for their disbelief; so little is it that they believe﴾ — by my life, those among the people of polytheism who turned back are more than those among the People of the Book who turned back; only a small company of the People of the Book believed.

1515 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada: ﴿So little is it that they believe﴾ — he said: only a few of them believe.

* *

Others said: rather, the meaning of that is: they do not believe except in a little of what is in their hands.

Mention of those who said this:

1516 - al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Abu Sufyan related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada: ﴿So little is it that they believe﴾ — he said: only a few of them believe. Ma'mar said: and another said: they do not believe except in a little of what is in their hands.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of the interpretations of His saying: ﴿So little is it that they believe﴾, which we shall establish, God willing, is that Allah, may His praise be great, informed that He cursed those whose description He gave in this verse, then informed concerning them that they are few in belief in what Allah sent down to His prophet Muhammad ﷺ. For this reason "qalilan" (little) is in the accusative, because it is an adjective of the omitted verbal noun. Its meaning is: Nay, Allah has cursed them for their disbelief, so little is their belief that they believe. Thus it has become clear, by what we have shown, the corruption of the statement related from Qatada on this. For if the meaning were as related, that it means: none of them believes except a few, or: few of them believe, then "qalil" would be in the nominative, not the accusative, because when that is its interpretation, "qalil" would then be the subject of "ma." Since "qalil" is in the accusative — and "ma" is in the sense of "min" or "alladhi" — "ma" would be left without a subject, and that is not permissible in the language of any Arab.

* *

As for the grammarians, they differed concerning the meaning of the "ma" in His saying: ﴿So little is it that they believe﴾. Some of them said: it is superfluous, having no meaning, and the sense of the speech is: "so little they believe," like His, may His remembrance be great: ﴿So it was by a mercy from Allah that you were gentle with them﴾ [Al 'Imran: 159], and the like. He claimed that "ma" in that is superfluous and that the meaning of the speech is: "by a mercy from Allah you were gentle with them." He recited in support of his saying the verse of Muhalhil:

If he came to propose to her at the two Abans, the nose of the suitor would be dyed with blood...

[Note: al-Kamil 2: 68 ... Abu al-Abbas said: "Aban is a mountain, and there are two Abans..."]

He claimed that he means: the nose of the suitor was dyed with blood, and that "ma" is superfluous.

* *

Others rejected what the speaker of this view said about "ma," in the verse and in the verse he recited, and said: that is rather from the speaker beginning speech with a statement about the generality of all things, since "ma" is a word that encompasses all things, then it is specified and generalized by what is mentioned after it.

* *

This view is, in our opinion, the more correct, because the addition to speech of something that conveys no meaning is not permissible to attribute to Allah, may His praise be great.

* *

Perhaps someone will say: Did those whom Allah informed were "so little that they believe" have any belief, little or much, that it is said of them: "So little is it that they believe"?

It is said: The meaning of "faith" is affirmation. The Jews of whom Allah gave this report did affirm the oneness of Allah, and the resurrection, reward and punishment, and they disbelieved in Muhammad ﷺ and his prophethood. All of that was obligatory for them to believe in, because it is in their books and in what Moses brought them. They affirmed some of it — and that is the little of their belief — and denied some of it, and that is the much which Allah informed they disbelieve in.

* *

Some have said: they were not believers in anything at all, and it is said, "So little is it that they believe," while they were disbelievers in all of it, as the Arabs say: "Seldom have I seen the like of this ever." And it has been related from them by direct hearing: "I passed through lands where hardly grows anything except leeks and onions," meaning: nothing grows except leeks and onions; and the like of such speech which is uttered by describing a thing with "scarcity," the meaning of which is negation of the whole. [See what preceded in 1: 554, note 1; and see al-Farra's Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1: 59–60.]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 89:

The explanation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿And when there came to them a Book from Allah, confirming what was with them﴾

Abu Ja'far said: His, the Exalted's, words mean: when there came to the Jews of the Children of Israel, whose characteristics He, the Exalted, has described, ﴿a Book from Allah﴾, meaning by "the Book" the Qur'an which Allah sent down to Muhammad (ﷺ), ﴿confirming what was with them﴾, meaning confirming what was with them of the Books which Allah had sent down before the Qur'an, as:

1518 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿And when there came to them a Book from Allah, confirming what was with them﴾: it is the Qur'an which was sent down to Muhammad, confirming what was with them of the Torah and the Gospel.

1518 - I was told on the authority of Ammar ibn al-Hasan, who said: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi' regarding His words: ﴿And when there came to them a Book from Allah, confirming what was with them﴾: it is the Qur'an which was sent down to Muhammad (ﷺ), confirming what was with them of the Torah and the Gospel.

* *

The explanation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿And they had before been seeking victory over those who disbelieved; but when there came to them that which they recognised, they disbelieved in it﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿And they had before been seeking victory over those who disbelieved﴾, meaning: these Jews, who, when there came to them a Book from Allah confirming what was with them of the Books which Allah had sent down before the Criterion, disbelieved in it, used to seek victory (istiftah, meaning istinsar, seeking aid) through Muhammad (ﷺ) [see what has preceded in this volume 2: 524] — seeking Allah's help through him against the polytheists of the Arabs before his mission, i.e. before he was sent, as:

1519 - Ibn Humayd narrated to me, saying: Salamah narrated to us, saying: Ibn Ishaq narrated to me, from Asim ibn Umar ibn Qatadah al-Ansari, from elders among them, who said: By Allah, this account was revealed concerning us and concerning them — meaning concerning the Ansar, and the Jews who were their neighbours — the account being: ﴿And when there came to them a Book from Allah, confirming what was with them, and they had before been seeking victory over those who disbelieved﴾. They said: We had overcome them for a long time in the Jahiliyyah — [in Ibn Hisham's Sirah 2: 190 "overcame them by force"] — while we were people of polytheism and they were people of the Book. They would say: A prophet whose mission is now near has drawn close in time; he will kill you with the killing of 'Ad and Iram. [In Ibn Hisham's Sirah 2: 190: "we will kill you with him..." and so it is in Ibn Kathir 1: 230, and it seems to be the correct reading.] When Allah, dhikruhu, sent His Messenger from Quraysh and we followed him, they disbelieved in him. Allah says: ﴿But when there came to them that which they recognised, they disbelieved in it﴾. [Report 1519: this has the ruling of a marfu' hadith, since it is a narration of events in the time of prophethood which were the cause of the revelation of the verse, to which the verse alludes. The more likely view is that it is connected (mawsul), because Asim ibn Umar ibn Qatadah al-Ansari al-Zafari al-Madani is a reliable Successor (tabi'i), and he narrates from "elders among them", who are his family among the Ansar. For this reason we have preferred its connection. Al-Suyuti 1: 87 cited this report and attributed it to Ibn Ishaq, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Abu Nu'aym and al-Bayhaqi, both in al-Dala'il.]

1520 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, saying: Ibn Ishaq narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, client of the family of Zayd ibn Thabit, narrated to me, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, or Ikrimah the client of Ibn Abbas, from Ibn Abbas: that the Jews used to seek victory over the Aws and the Khazraj through the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) before his mission. When Allah sent him from among the Arabs, they disbelieved in him and denied what they had been saying about him. Mu'adh ibn Jabal and Bishr ibn al-Bara' ibn Ma'rur, brother of the Banu Salamah, said to them: O assembly of Jews, fear Allah and submit, for you used to seek victory over us through Muhammad (ﷺ) while we were people of polytheism, and you told us that he would be sent, and you described him to us by his description! Salam ibn Mishkam, brother of the Banu al-Nadir, said: He has not brought us anything we recognise, and he is not the one we used to mention to you! Then Allah, the Exalted, revealed concerning that His words: ﴿And when there came to them a Book from Allah, confirming what was with them, and they had before been seeking victory over those who disbelieved; but when there came to them that which they recognised, they disbelieved in it. So the curse of Allah is upon the disbelievers﴾. [Report 1520: in Ibn Hisham's Sirah 2: 196.]

1521 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Yunus ibn Bukayr narrated to us, saying: Ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, client of the family of Zayd ibn Thabit, narrated to me, saying: Sa'id ibn Jubayr, or Ikrimah, narrated to me, from Ibn Abbas, the like of it.

1522 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿And they had before been seeking victory over those who disbelieved﴾, he said: they would seek victory through the emergence of Muhammad (ﷺ) against the polytheists of the Arabs — meaning by that the People of the Book. So when Allah sent Muhammad (ﷺ) and they saw him from others (than themselves), they disbelieved in him and envied him.

1523 - And Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to me, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Ali al-Azdi, regarding the saying of Allah: ﴿And they had before been seeking victory over those who disbelieved﴾, he said: the Jews. They used to say: O Allah, send us this Prophet who will judge between us and the people; they seek victory — seek help — through him over the people.

1524 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Ali al-Azdi — he is al-Bariqi — regarding the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And they had before been seeking victory﴾, and he mentioned the like of it. [Reports 1523, 1524: Ali al-Azdi al-Bariqi is Ali ibn Abd Allah, Abu Abd Allah, son of Abu al-Walid al-Bariqi. He narrated from Ibn Umar, Ibn Abbas, Abu Hurayrah, Ubayd ibn Umayr, and he narrated mursal from Zayd ibn Harithah. From him narrated Mujahid ibn Jabr, who was of his contemporaries. Ibn Adi said: he does not have many narrations, and in my view he is not objectionable (Tahdhib 7: 358, 359).]

1525 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿And they had before been seeking victory over those who disbelieved﴾: the Jews used to seek victory through Muhammad (ﷺ) over the disbelievers of the Arabs before him, and they said: O Allah, send this Prophet whom we find in the Torah, who will punish them and kill them! But when Allah sent Muhammad (ﷺ) and they saw that he was sent from others than themselves, they disbelieved in him out of envy of the Arabs, while they knew that he was the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), finding him written with them in the Torah: ﴿But when there came to them that which they recognised, they disbelieved in it﴾.

1526 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Adam narrated to us, saying: Abu Ja'far narrated to us, from al-Rabi', from Abu al-Aliyah, who said: The Jews used to seek help through Muhammad (ﷺ) against the polytheists of the Arabs, saying: O Allah, send this Prophet whom we find written with us, so that he may punish the polytheists and kill them! But when Allah sent Muhammad, and they saw that he was from others, they disbelieved in him out of envy of the Arabs, while they knew that he was the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). So Allah said: ﴿But when there came to them that which they recognised, they disbelieved in it. So the curse of Allah is upon the disbelievers﴾.

1527 - Musa narrated to me, saying: Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿And when there came to them a Book from Allah, confirming what was with them, and they had before been seeking victory over those who disbelieved; but when there came to them that which they recognised, they disbelieved in it﴾. He said: The Arabs would pass by the Jews and harm them, and they would find Muhammad (ﷺ) in the Torah, and ask Allah to send him so that they might fight alongside him against the Arabs. But when Muhammad came to them, they disbelieved in him, because he was not from the Children of Israel.

1528 - Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: I said to Ata regarding His words: ﴿And they had before been seeking victory over those who disbelieved﴾. He said: They would seek victory over the disbelieving Arabs through the coming forth of the Prophet (ﷺ), hoping that he would be from among them. But when he came forth and they saw that he was not from them, they disbelieved, though they knew that he was the truth and that he was the Prophet. He said: ﴿But when there came to them that which they recognised, they disbelieved in it. So the curse of Allah is upon the disbelievers﴾.

1529 - He said: Ibn Jurayj narrated to us, and Mujahid said: They seek victory through Muhammad (ﷺ), saying: he will come forth. ﴿But when there came to them that which they recognised﴾ — and he was from others — they disbelieved in him. [Report 1529: this is an isnad whose beginning has fallen away, so I do not know who it is. Its wording is also disordered.]

1530 - Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, saying: Ibn Jurayj said — and Ibn Abbas said: they used to seek victory over the disbelieving Arabs.

1531 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Al-Hammani narrated to me, saying: Shurayk narrated to me, from Abu al-Jahhaf, from Muslim al-Battin, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr regarding His words: ﴿But when there came to them that which they recognised, they disbelieved in it﴾, he said: They were the Jews; they recognised Muhammad as a prophet and disbelieved in him.

1532 - I was told on the authority of al-Minjab, who said: Bishr narrated to us, from Abu Rawq, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn Abbas regarding His words: ﴿And they had before been seeking victory over those who disbelieved﴾, he said: They would seek support, saying: We will help Muhammad against them. But they were not so; they were lying.

1533 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: I asked Ibn Zayd about the saying of Allah, mighty and majestic: ﴿And they had before been seeking victory over those who disbelieved; but when there came to them that which they recognised, they disbelieved in it﴾. He said: The Jews used to seek victory over the disbelieving Arabs, saying: By Allah, if the Prophet whom Musa and Isa gave glad tidings of, Ahmad, comes, we will have the upper hand over you! They thought he was of them, while the Arabs were around them, and they would seek victory through him and seek help through him. But when there came to them that which they recognised, they disbelieved in it and envied him. He recited the saying of Allah, mighty and majestic: ﴿Out of envy from themselves, after the truth had become clear to them﴾ [Surah al-Baqarah: 109]. He said: It had become clear to them that he was a Messenger; from that point Allah benefited the Aws and the Khazraj with what they heard from them, that a prophet was about to emerge.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: If someone says to us: Where is the response (jawab) to His words: ﴿And when there came to them a Book from Allah, confirming what was with them﴾?

It is said: The scholars of Arabic have differed concerning its response. Some of them said: It is among what has had its response omitted, being sufficient by the listeners' knowledge of its meaning and by what has been mentioned of its like throughout the Qur'an. [I am in doubt about this last sentence, whether there is a distortion in it.]

The Arabs do this when speech is long: they produce things which have responses, and then omit their responses, relying on the listeners' knowledge of their meaning to dispense with mentioning the responses, as His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿And if there were a Qur'an by which mountains were moved, or the earth were split, or the dead were made to speak — but to Allah belongs the affair entirely﴾ [Surah al-Ra'd: 31], where its response is omitted. The meaning: "If there were a Qur'an other than this Qur'an by which the mountains were moved, the mountains would have been moved by this Qur'an" — relying on the knowledge of the listeners of its meaning. They said: likewise His words: ﴿And when there came to them a Book from Allah, confirming what was with them﴾.

* *

Others said: The response to His words: ﴿And when there came to them a Book from Allah﴾ is in the "fa'" in His words: ﴿But when there came to them that which they recognised, they disbelieved in it﴾, and the response of both conditionals is in "they disbelieved in it", as when you say: "When I stood, and when you came to us, you did well", meaning: when you came to us, since I stood, you did well. [See al-Farra's Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1: 59.]

* *

The explanation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿So the curse of Allah is upon the disbelievers﴾ (89)

Abu Ja'far said: We have already explained sufficiently in what has passed the meaning of la'nah (curse) and the meaning of "kufr" (disbelief). [See what has preceded (kufr) 1: 255, 382, 522, and in this volume (la'nah) 2: 328.]

* *

So the meaning of the verse: the disgrace and removal of Allah upon those who deny what they had recognised of the truth incumbent upon them, for Allah and His prophets, denying what had been established as true for them concerning the prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ). In Allah, the Exalted's, informing about the Jews — by what He informed about them in His words: ﴿But when there came to them that which they recognised, they disbelieved in it﴾ — is the clear proof that they deliberately disbelieved in Muhammad (ﷺ), after the establishment of the proof of his prophethood against them, and after Allah cut off their excuse by making him His messenger to them.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 90 (part 1 of 2):

The explanation of the words of His, the Exalted, ﴿Wretched is that for which they have sold their souls, [in] that they disbelieve in what Allah has sent down, out of insolence﴾

Abu Ja'far said: The meaning of His words, may His praise be exalted, ﴿Wretched is that for which they have sold their souls﴾ is: Evil is that for which they have sold their souls.
* *
The original form of "bi's" (بئس, wretched/evil) is "ba'is," from "al-bu's" (distress). Its hamza was made quiescent, then its vowel was transferred to the "ba'," as it is said "zalitu" becoming "zilt" (ẓalt), and as it is said "li-l-kabd" becoming "kibd" (liver). So the vowel of the "ba'" was transferred to the "kaf" once the "ba'" became quiescent.

It is also possible that "bi's," although its original form is "ba'is," comes from the dialect of those who transfer the vowel of the middle radical of "fa'ila" to the first radical when the middle radical is one of the six guttural letters, as they said "li'b" from "la'iba" and "si'm" from "sa'ima." This, it is said, is a widespread dialect among Tamim.

Then it was made to indicate blame and reproach, and it was joined to "ma" (what).

The grammarians differed concerning the meaning of the "ma" that comes with "bi'sa-ma." Some of the grammarians of Basra said: it alone is a noun, and "an yakfuru" (that they disbelieve) is its explanation [[The "explanation" is what the Basrans termed "tamyiz" (specification), and it is also called "tabyin" (clarification). (Hama' al-Hawami' 1: 250).]] like "ni'ma rajulan Zayd" (excellent is Zayd as a man), and "an yunzila Allah" is a substitute for "anzala Allah."

And some of the grammarians of Kufa said: the meaning of that is: "Wretched is the thing for which they have sold their souls, [namely] that they disbelieve." So "ma" is the noun of "bi's," and "an yakfuru" is the second noun. He claimed that "an yakfuru," if you wish, you may make "an" in the nominative position, and if you wish, in the genitive position. [[In the printed edition: "and he claimed that an yunzila min fadlihi in shi'ta ja'altu..." which is a scribal error; the correct text is as recorded from al-Farra's Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1: 56.]] As for the nominative: "Wretched is this thing, that they should do it." As for the genitive: "Wretched is the thing for which they have sold their souls, that they disbelieve in what Allah has sent down, out of insolence." He said: His words, ﴿Wretched is that for which their own souls have sent ahead for them, that Allah became wrathful against them﴾ [Surah al-Ma'idah: 80] are similar to this. The Arabs make "ma" alone in this construction, in the position of a complete noun, as in His words ﴿How excellent it is﴾ [Surah al-Baqarah: 271], and "bi'sa-ma anta" (how wretched you are). For his statement he cited a verse of one of the rajaz poets:
"Do not hasten in the march, and lead them gently, / How wretched is the slowness, and let us not pasture them."[[I do not know the rajaz poet; the two verses are in Lisan al-Arab (d-l-w). "Dalawtu al-naqata" means I drove the she-camel gently and slowly; "ra'a al-mashiya" and "arsaha" mean to let the livestock out to pasture.]]

Abu Ja'far said: The Arabs say: "Wretched is the marriage, and no dowry," making "ma" alone a noun without a complement. The proponent of this view does not permit that the word following "bi's" be a definite determinate noun while its predicate is a definite determinate noun. He claimed that "bi'sama" is in the sense of: "Wretched is the thing for which they have sold their souls," so "ma" with its complement has become a determinate noun, because "ishtaraw" is a past verb in the complement of "ma," according to the proponent of this view. When it is joined to a past verb, it becomes a known, determinate definite, so the sense of the statement becomes: "Wretched is their purchase, their disbelief." That, in his view, is impermissible, and the corruption of this view has been made clear. [[See al-Farra's Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1: 56–57, apparently the view of al-Kisa'i. "Al-ma'rifa al-muwaqqata" is the determinate definiteness, meaning the specified definite. See the explanation of this above 1: 181, note 1.]]

Another of them claimed that "an" may be in the genitive position if you wish, and in the nominative if you wish. As for the genitive: you take it as a repetition of the "ha'" in "bihi" (by it), in two statements, as if you had said: "they sold their souls for disbelief." As for the nominative: it is repeated on the position of "ma" that follows "bi's." [[In the printed edition: "mukarran," the correct form from al-Farra's Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1: 56.]] He said: it is not permissible that it be nominative in your saying, "Wretched is the man, Abdullah." [[This paragraph is the verbatim text of al-Farra's words in Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1: 56.]]

Some of them said: "bi'sama" is one thing that raises what follows it, [[In the printed edition: "ya'rifu ma ba'duhu," the correct text is as recorded.]] as is related from the Arabs: "Wretched is the marriage, and no dowry," where "marriage" is raised by "bi'sama," [[In the printed edition: "fa-raf'a," the correct text is as recorded.]] as one says "Wretched is Zayd, and wretched is Amr," so "bi'sama" is nominative by the pronoun that refers back to it from the "ha'." As if you said: "Wretched is the thing for which they have sold their souls," and "an" is a rendering of "bi'sama." [[Rendering (tarjamah): this is what the Basrans call "'atf al-bayan" (explicative apposition) and "al-badal" (substitution); so his saying "mutarjaman 'an bi'sama" means explicative apposition.]]
* *
Of these opinions, the most correct is the view of the one who makes "bi'sama" nominative by the returning pronoun "ha'" in His words ﴿they sold by it﴾, just as they made that nominative by "Abdullah" when they said "wretched is Abdullah," and makes "an yakfuru" a rendering of "bi'sama." [[Rendering: this is what the Basrans call "'atf al-bayan" and "al-badal"; so his saying "mutarjaman 'an bi'sama" means explicative apposition.]] The meaning of the statement then becomes: "Wretched is the thing the Jews sold their souls for: their disbelief in what Allah sent down out of insolence and envy that Allah should send down of His bounty." The "an" in His words "an yunzila Allah" is in the accusative position, because it means "an yakfuru bima anzala Allah": for the sake of Allah sending down of His bounty upon whom He wills of His servants. The position of "an" is an object of purpose. [[The "jaza'" here is the object for which (maf'ul li-ajlihi); in the printed edition it reads "jarr" (genitive), which is an error; the correct text is in al-Farra's Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1: 58.]] Some of the Kufan grammarians claimed that "an" is in the genitive position with an implied "ba'" (by). We chose the accusative for it because the statement before it is complete, and there is no governing particle with it to put it in the genitive. A governing particle does not govern a pronoun.
* *
As for His words ﴿they sold by it their souls﴾, He means by it: they sold their souls. As related:

1534 - Musa ibn Harun related to me, saying: Amr related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿Wretched is that for which they have sold their souls﴾: he says, "they sold their souls, [in] that they disbelieve in what Allah has sent down, out of insolence."

1535 - Al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Mujahid said regarding ﴿Wretched is that for which they have sold their souls﴾: the Jews, who exchanged the truth for falsehood, and concealed what Muhammad ﷺ had brought, rather than making it clear. [[In the printed edition: "bi-an bayyanuhu," which is an error; the correct text is from Tafsir Ibn Kathir 1: 231. The meaning is that they bought concealment with clarification.]]

Abu Ja'far said: The Arabs say "sharaytu" meaning "I sold." And "ishtaraw," in this place, is "iftaʿalu" from "sharaytu." The speech of the Arabs, as it has reached us, is that they say "sharaytu" meaning "I sold," and "ishtaraytu" meaning "I bought." It has been said that the "shari" (seller) was named "shari" because he sold his soul and his worldly life for his afterlife. [[The shari is the singular of al-shurah (with a damma on the shin), who are the Kharijites. Qatari ibn al-Fuja'a al-Kharijī said in the sense of this, mentioning Umm Hakim, on the day of Dulab: "If you had witnessed us that day, with our horses / sweeping away every sanctuary among the unbelievers. / She saw young men who sold their souls to God / for gardens of Eden with Him and bliss." The Kharijites said: "We are the shurah," based on the words of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: "And among mankind is one who sells his soul seeking the pleasure of Allah" [Surah al-Baqarah: 207], meaning he sells it and expends it in jihad, and its price is Paradise. It is also said they were named so because they said: "We have sold our souls in obedience to Allah when we separated from the unjust leaders," meaning: we sold them for Paradise.]]

From this is the saying of Yazid ibn Mufarrigh al-Himyari:
"I sold Bard, would that I had been / before Bard, a ghoul [hama]" [[From a qasida of his in Tabaqat Fuhul al-Shu'ara' p. 555, satirizing Abbad ibn Ziyad, when he sold his property to settle a debt he owed, and the creditors were paid. Among what he sold was a slave of Ibn Mufarrigh called "Bard" and a slave girl called "Arakah." His saying "kuntu hamah" means "I was dead" (a ruin). One says: so-and-so is a hamah today or tomorrow, meaning his death is near, and then he becomes a hamah. This was a pre-Islamic belief which Allah annulled with Islam: that the bone or soul of the dead becomes a hamah (a bird like an owl) that flies about. Another transmission reads "min ba'di Bard."]]

And from it is the saying of al-Musayyib ibn 'Alas:
"Its price is offered, yet he withholds it, / and its owner says: will you not buy?" [[From his Diwan p. 352 (in the appendix to the Diwan of al-A'sha, al-Musayyib being al-A'sha's maternal uncle, and al-A'sha his transmitter). The Diwan reads "yaqulu sahibuhu," which is correct. The verse is from a set of outstanding verses describing a poor diver who has found a pearl without equal, and holds it back from sale though he has been offered a price enough to make him rich; its owner urges him to sell it. The verse following: "And you see the sailors prostrating to it / and clasping it with their hands to their chests." Al-sarari: the sailors, companions of the divers.]] He means by it: he sold Bard. Sometimes "ishtaraytu" is used in the sense of "I sold," and "shariytu" in the sense of "I bought." The widely known usage regarding them is what I have described.
* *
As for the meaning of His words ﴿out of insolence﴾, He means by it: transgression and envy, as related:

1536 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah: ﴿out of insolence﴾, he said: that is, out of envy, and they are the Jews.

1537 - Musa related to me, saying: Amr related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿out of insolence﴾, he said: they rebelled against Muhammad ﷺ and envied him, and said: "The messengers were only from the Children of Israel, so what is the matter with this one from the Children of Ishmael?" So they envied him that Allah should send down His bounty upon whom He wills of His servants.

1538 - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Adam related to us, saying: Abu Ja'far related to us, from al-Rabi', from Abu al-'Aliyah: ﴿out of insolence﴾, meaning: envy that Allah should send down His bounty upon whom He wills of His servants, and they are the Jews who disbelieved in what was sent down upon Muhammad ﷺ.

1539 - I was told from Ammar ibn al-Hasan, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far related to us, from his father, from al-Rabi', the like of it.
* *
Abu Ja'far said: The meaning of the verse is: Wretched is the thing for which they have sold their souls, namely the disbelief in what Allah sent down in His Book to Musa, including the prophethood of Muhammad ﷺ and the command to confirm and follow him, because Allah sent down of His bounty, and His bounty is His wisdom, His signs and His prophethood, upon whom He wills of His servants, meaning upon Muhammad ﷺ, out of insolence and envy toward Muhammad ﷺ, because he was from the descendants of Ishmael and not from the Children of Israel.
* *
If someone says: How did the Jews sell their souls for disbelief, so that it is said: "Wretched is that for which they have sold their souls, that they disbelieve in what Allah has sent down"? Can anything be bought with disbelief?

It is said: The meaning of "shira'" (buying) and "bay'" (selling) among the Arabs is the removal of one's ownership of a thing to another in exchange for a compensation received in return. Then the Arabs use this for anyone who receives in return for his deed a compensation, whether bad or good, and they say: "Excellent is what so-and-so sold his soul for," and "Wretched is what so-and-so sold his soul for," meaning: an excellent gain is what it gained, and a wretched gain is what it gained, when by its striving it brings upon itself good or evil. Likewise is the meaning of His words, may His praise be exalted, ﴿Wretched is that for which they have sold their souls﴾: since they ruined their souls by disbelieving in Muhammad ﷺ and destroyed them, Allah addressed them and the Arabs in the language they understand, saying ﴿Wretched is that for which they have sold their souls﴾, meaning by it: wretched is what they gained by their striving, and wretched is the exchange they accepted for their disbelief in Allah in denying Muhammad, since they were content to take in exchange, instead of the reward of Allah and what He had prepared for them, had they believed in Allah and what He sent down to His prophets, the Fire and what has been prepared for them through their disbelief in that.
* *
This verse, and what Allah reports in it about the envy of the Jews toward Muhammad ﷺ and his people from among the Arabs, because Allah placed prophethood and wisdom among them rather than among the Jews of the Children of Israel, to the point that this led them to disbelieve in him, despite their knowledge of his truthfulness and that he is a prophet of Allah, sent, and a messenger dispatched, [[His words "its parallel is the verse..." are the predicate of his earlier statement in this paragraph: "And this verse..."]] has a parallel in another verse in Surat al-Nisa', namely His words: ﴿Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Book? They believe in idols and false gods, and they say of those who disbelieve, "These are better guided than those who believe, in the way." Those are the ones whom Allah has cursed; and whoever Allah curses, you will not find for him a helper. Or do they have a share of the kingdom? And in that case they would not give the people even a speck. Or do they envy the people for what Allah has given them of His bounty? We had already given the family of Abraham the Book and wisdom, and We gave them a great kingdom﴾ [Surah al-Nisa': 51–54].
* *
The explanation of His words: ﴿that Allah should send down of His bounty upon whom He wills of His servants﴾

Abu Ja'far said: We have already mentioned its interpretation and explained its meaning, but we will mention the report confirming what we have said about it:

1540 - Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salamah related to us, saying: Ibn Ishaq related to me, from Asim ibn Umar ibn Qatadah al-Ansari, from some of their elders, regarding His words ﴿out of insolence that Allah should send down of His bounty upon whom He wills of His servants﴾: that is, that Allah, the Exalted, placed it in others than them. [[Report 1540: Ibn Hisham's Sirah 2: 190.]]

1541 - Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, who said: They are the Jews. When Allah sent His prophet Muhammad ﷺ, and they saw that he had been sent from others than them, they disbelieved in him out of envy of the Arabs, while knowing that he is the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, finding him written with them in the Torah.

1542 - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Adam related to us, saying: Abu Ja'far related to us, from al-Rabi', from Abu al-'Aliyah, the like of it.

1543 - I was told from Ammar, who said: Ibn Abi Ja'far related to us, from his father, from al-Rabi', the like of it.

1544 - Musa related to me, saying: Amr ibn Hammad related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, who said: They said: "The messengers were only from the Children of Israel, so what is the matter with this one from the Children of Ishmael?"

1545 - Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Ali al-Azdi, who said: It was revealed concerning the Jews. [[Report 1545: see the commentary on reports 1523 and 1524.]]
* *
The explanation of His words: ﴿So they returned with wrath upon wrath﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His words ﴿So they returned with wrath upon wrath﴾ [[See the explanation of "baa" (returned) earlier in this part, 2: 138.]] He means: the Jews of the Children of Israel returned, after their former state of seeking victory through Muhammad ﷺ and seeking opening through him, and after what they used to tell the people before his mission, that he is a prophet to be sent, turning back on their heels when Allah sent him as a prophet and messenger. So they returned with wrath from Allah, deserved by them through their disbelief in Muhammad when he was sent, and their denial of his prophethood, and their denial that he is the one whose description they find in their Book, out of obstinacy toward him, insolence and envy toward him and the Arabs, upon an earlier wrath which had come from Allah upon them before that, preceding His second wrath, because of their disbelief that existed before Jesus son of Mary, or because of their worship of the calf, or because of other sins of theirs that had passed, by which they deserved wrath from Allah, as related:

1546 - Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salamah ibn al-Fadl related to us, saying: Ibn Ishaq related to me, from Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, as he narrated from Sa'id ibn Jubayr or Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿So they returned with wrath upon wrath﴾: wrath upon wrath, His wrath upon them for what they had neglected of the Torah, which was with them, and wrath for their disbelief in this prophet whom Allah had brought to them. [[Report 1546: Ibn Hisham's Sirah 2: 190.]]

1547 - Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Yahya ibn Sa'id and Abd al-Rahman related to us, both saying: Sufyan related to us, from Abu Bukayr, from Ikrimah: ﴿So they returned with wrath upon wrath﴾, he said: their disbelief in Jesus, and their disbelief in Muhammad ﷺ. [[Report 1547: in al-Durr al-Manthur it reads "kufrahum" in both places; the two are the same.]]

1548 - Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Yahya ibn Yaman related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Abu Bukayr, from Ikrimah: ﴿So they returned with wrath upon wrath﴾, he said: their disbelief in Jesus and Muhammad ﷺ.

1549 - Al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: al-Thawri informed us, from Abu Bukayr, from Ikrimah, the like of it.

1550 - Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Jarir related to us, from Mughirah, from al-Sha'bi, who said: People on the Day of Resurrection are in four stations: a man who was a believer in Jesus and believed in Muhammad, may the two of them be blessed, so he has two rewards. And a man who was a disbeliever in Jesus and believed in Muhammad ﷺ, so he has one reward. And a man who was a disbeliever in Jesus and disbelieved in Muhammad ﷺ, so he returns with wrath upon wrath. And a man who was a disbeliever in Jesus from among the polytheist Arabs, who died in his disbelief before Muhammad ﷺ, so he returns with wrath.

1551 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah regarding His words ﴿So they returned with wrath upon wrath﴾: Allah's wrath upon them for their disbelief in the Gospel and in Jesus, and His wrath upon them for their disbelief in the Qur'an and in Muhammad ﷺ.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 90 (part 2 of 2):

1552 - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah related to us, saying: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿So they returned with wrath upon wrath﴾: "The Jews, for what they did of altering the Torah before the coming out of the Prophet (ﷺ), ﴿upon wrath﴾: their denial of the Prophet (ﷺ), and their disbelief in what he brought."

1553 - Al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Adam related to us, saying: Abu Ja'far related to us, from al-Rabi', from Abu al-Aliyah, regarding ﴿So they returned with wrath upon wrath﴾, he said: "The wrath of Allah upon them for their disbelief in the Injil and in Jesus, then His wrath upon them for their disbelief in Muhammad (ﷺ) and in the Qur'an."

1554 - Musa related to me, saying: Amr related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿So they returned with wrath upon wrath﴾: "As for the first wrath, it is when Allah became wrathful with them over the calf; and as for the second wrath, He became wrathful with them when they disbelieved in Muhammad (ﷺ)."

1555 - Al-Qasim related to us, saying: Al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, 'Ata' and 'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr, in their saying: ﴿So they returned with wrath upon wrath﴾, he said: "The wrath of Allah upon them for what they were engaged in before the coming out of the Prophet (ﷺ) - of altering and disbelief -, then He became wrathful with them concerning Muhammad (ﷺ) when he came out, and they disbelieved in him."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: We have already explained the meaning of "wrath" from Allah toward whomever He is wrathful with among His creatures, and the disagreement of those who differ regarding its attributes, earlier in this our book, in a manner sufficient to dispense with repeating it.[[See what preceded, 1: 188-189, and what passed in this part, 2: 138. In the printed edition, after his words "in a manner sufficient to dispense with repeating it" there was the text: "And Allah the Exalted knows best", which has no place here, and is undoubtedly an addition by some copyists, so I have left it out.]]

* *

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And for the disbelievers is a humiliating punishment (90)﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His words, may His praise be exalted: ﴿And for the disbelievers is a humiliating punishment﴾, meaning: for those who deny the prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ) from all of mankind, is a punishment from Allah, either in the Hereafter, or in this world and the Hereafter. ﴿Humiliating﴾ is the one that humbles its possessor, disgraces him, and clothes him in abasement and humiliation.

* *

If someone says: What punishment is there that does not humiliate its possessor, such that the humiliating one would be specified for the disbelievers?

It is said: The humiliating one is what we have already explained is the one that bequeaths to its possessor abasement and humiliation, in which its possessor abides forever, never passing from his humiliation to honor and dignity, and it is what Allah has singled out for those who disbelieve in Him and His messengers. As for the punishment that does not humiliate its possessor, it is that which is an expiation for its possessor. Such is the thief from among the people of Islam who steals what makes the hand amputation obligatory for him, so his hand is cut off; and the adulterer among them who commits adultery, so the prescribed punishment is carried out upon him; and whatever resembles that of punishment and chastisement which Allah made as expiations for the sins for which their people were punished; and like the people of major sins among the people of Islam who are punished in the Hereafter according to the measure of their crimes which they committed, so that they may be purified of their sins, then they enter Paradise. For all of that, though it is a punishment, is not humiliating for the one punished by it, since Allah's punishing him with it is to purify him of his sins, then He brings him to the source of honor and dignity, and makes him abide forever in the bliss of the Gardens.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 91:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿And when it is said to them, "Believe in what Allah has sent down," they say, "We believe in what was sent down to us."﴾

Abu Ja'far said: The meaning of His, the Majestic and Praised's, saying: ﴿And when it is said to them﴾, and when it is said to the Jews of the Children of Israel - to those who were in the vicinity of the emigration place of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): ﴿Believe﴾, i.e., affirm as true, ﴿in what Allah has sent down﴾, meaning in what Allah has sent down of the Qur'an to Muhammad (ﷺ), ﴿they say: "We believe"﴾, i.e., we affirm as true, ﴿in what was sent down to us﴾, meaning in the Torah which Allah sent down to Moses.

* *

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿while they deny what is beyond it﴾

Abu Ja'far said: The meaning of His, the Majestic and Praised's, saying: ﴿while they deny what is beyond it﴾ is: and they disbelieve and reject "what is beyond it", meaning: what is beyond the Torah.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The interpretation of "beyond it" (warā'ahu) in this place is "other than". As one says of a man speaking well: "There is nothing beyond this speech", meaning: the speaker has nothing other than that speech. So too the meaning of His saying: ﴿while they deny what is beyond it﴾ is: what is other than the Torah, and what comes after it of the books of Allah which He sent down to His messengers, as:

1556 - Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿while they deny what is beyond it﴾: he says: what comes after it.

1557 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, he said: Adam narrated to us, he said: Abu Ja'far narrated to us, from al-Rabi', from Abu al-'Aliyah, regarding ﴿while they deny what is beyond it﴾: i.e., what comes after it - meaning: what comes after the Torah.

1558 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, he said: Ishaq narrated to us, he said: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi', regarding ﴿while they deny what is beyond it﴾: he says: what comes after it.

* *

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿while it is the truth, confirming what is with them﴾

Abu Ja'far said: The meaning of His, the Majestic and Praised's, saying: ﴿while it is the truth, confirming﴾ is: what is beyond the Book that was sent down to them - from the books which Allah sent down to His prophets - is the truth. And by this, may His remembrance be exalted, He means only the Qur'an which He sent down to Muhammad (ﷺ), as:

1559 - Musa narrated to me, he said: Amr narrated to us, he said: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿And when it is said to them, "Believe in what Allah has sent down," they say, "We believe in what was sent down to us" and deny what is beyond it﴾: it is the Qur'an. Allah, the Majestic and Praised, says: ﴿while it is the truth, confirming what is with them﴾. He, the Majestic and Praised, said ﴿confirming what is with them﴾ because the books of Allah confirm one another. In the Gospel and the Qur'an there is the command to follow Muhammad (ﷺ), to believe in him and in what he brought, like what is in the Torah of Moses (peace be upon him). Therefore, the Majestic and Praised said to the Jews - when He informed them about what is beyond their Book which He sent down to Moses (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him), of the books which He sent down to His prophets - that it is the truth confirming the Book that is with them, meaning: it agrees with them in what the Jews deny.

He said: That is a report from Allah that they deny the Torah in the same way that they are in denial of the Gospel and the Criterion (al-Furqan), out of obstinacy toward Allah, opposition to His command, and transgression against His messengers, may the blessings of Allah be upon them.

* *

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿Say, "Then why did you kill the prophets of Allah before, if you were believers?"﴾

Abu Ja'far said: The meaning of His, may His remembrance be exalted, saying: ﴿Say, "Then why did you kill the prophets of Allah"﴾ is: Say, O Muhammad, to the Jews of the Children of Israel - who, when you say to them, "Believe in what Allah has sent down," say, "We believe in what was sent down to us": Why do you kill - if you, O assembly of Jews, are believers in what Allah sent down to you - His prophets, when Allah has forbidden in the Book sent down to you their killing, and rather commanded you in it to follow them, obey them, and affirm them? This is from Allah, the Majestic and Praised, a denial of their saying "We believe in what was sent down to us" and a rebuke to them, as:

1560 - Musa narrated to me, he said: Amr narrated to us, he said: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, who said: Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, said - rebuking them, meaning the Jews: ﴿Then why did you kill the prophets of Allah before, if you were believers?﴾

* *

If someone says: How is it said to them, "Then why did you kill the prophets of Allah before," beginning the report in the form of the present/future verb, then informing that it has already passed?

It is said: The people of Arabic grammar differ in the interpretation of this. Some of the Basran grammarians said: the meaning is: "Why did you kill the prophets of Allah before," as He, the Majestic and Praised, said: ﴿And they followed what the devils recited﴾ [Surah al-Baqarah: 102], i.e., what they recited. And as the poet said: [He is a man of the Banu Sulayl.]

"And indeed a base man passed by me, insulting me... so I went on past him and said: it does not concern me."

He means by his saying "and indeed [he] passes by" (wa-laqad amurru): and indeed I passed by. He cited as proof that this is so his saying "so I went on" (fa-madaytu), and he did not say "so I go on" (fa-amdi). He claimed that the form fa'ala and yafʿalu may share one meaning, and he cited as evidence the saying of a poet: [He is al-Tirimmah ibn Hakim al-Ta'i.]

"And indeed I come to you, thanking you for what has passed of the matter, and seeking what will be in the future,"

meaning: what will be in the future. And by the saying of al-Hutay'ah:

"Al-Hutay'ah testified on the day he meets his Lord that al-Walid deserves the excuse,"

meaning: he testifies. And as another said:

"I do not enter the morning or the evening except that I see myself among you in a turmoil,"

so he said "I enter the morning" (adhha), then said "nor do I enter the evening" (wa-la amsaytu).

* *

Some of the Kufan grammarians said: It is said: ﴿Then why did you kill the prophets of Allah before﴾, so He addressed them with the verb in the future form while its meaning is the past, as a man reproaches another for what has already occurred from him, saying to him: "Woe to you, why did you lie? Why did you make yourself hateful to people?" As the poet said:

"When we trace lineage, you were not born of a base woman, and you could not avoid being ascribed to her,"

so the conditional is in the future, while the birth has entirely passed. This is because the meaning is known, so it is permissible. He said: Similar to it in speech is: "When you look into the biography of 'Umar, you do not find him doing evil," meaning: you did not find him doing evil. Since the matter of 'Umar is not doubted to be past, it did not occur to the mind that it is future. Therefore "before" (min qabl) fits with His saying: ﴿Then why did you kill the prophets of Allah before﴾. He said: Those who were addressed with the killing are not the killers themselves; rather, it was their forefathers who were past who killed the prophets, and they [the later ones] took them as allies in that and were pleased with it, so the killing was attributed to them.

* *
