Abu Ja'far said: The correct view on this, according to us, is that Allah addressed those among the Jews of the Children of Israel who lived to see the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) - with what He addressed them in Surat al-Baqarah and other surahs - by what had passed of His favor to their forefathers, and what had passed of their forefathers' ingratitude for His blessings, their committing of His disobedience, and their audacity toward Him and His prophets, attributing that to those addressed, in the manner of the Arabs saying to one another: "We did such-and-such to you on such-and-such a day, and you did such-and-such to us on such-and-such a day" - as we have explained in other places in this book, meaning by that that our forefathers did that to your forefathers, and our ancestors did that to your ancestors. Thus it is with His saying: ﴿Then why did you kill the prophets of Allah before﴾, since it came in the form of a report addressed to those so addressed, a report from Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, about the deed of their predecessors, in the manner we have explained, it is permissible to say "before", since its meaning is: say, "Why did your forefathers kill the prophets of Allah before?" And it was known that His saying ﴿Then why did you kill the prophets of Allah before﴾ is only a report about the deed of their predecessors.

* *

And the interpretation of His saying: ﴿before﴾ is: before today.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿if you were believers﴾, it means: if you are believers in what Allah sent down to you, as you claim. By this He means only the Jews who lived to see the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and their forefathers - if they were and you were, O Jews, as you claim, believers. And the Majestic and Praised rebuked them for the killing of their forefathers of His prophets, at the point of their saying when it was said to them: "Believe in what Allah has sent down." They said: "We believe in what was sent down to us," because they were, for their forefathers who undertook the killing of the prophets of Allah, along with their saying "We believe in what was sent down to us," allies and pleased with their deed. So He said to them: If you are, as you claim, believers in what was sent down to you, then why do you side with the killers of Allah's prophets? That is, you are pleased with their deeds.

The exegesis of His words, may He be exalted: ﴿And Moses certainly came to you with clear signs; then you took the calf [for worship] after him, while you were wrongdoers﴾ (92).

Abu Ja'far said: By His words, "And Moses certainly came to you with clear signs," He, may His praise be great, means: he came to you with signs that indicate his truthfulness and the soundness of his prophethood, [[In the printed edition: "wa-haqiyyat nubuwwatihi" (and the reality of his prophethood), but this is not what Abu Ja'far says. Similar substitutions by copyists have occurred earlier; in the ancient manuscript it stood as I have recorded it. See what has preceded, 2:318.]] like the staff that turned into a manifest serpent, and his hand that he brought out white to the onlookers, and the splitting of the sea and the making of its dry ground a dry path for him, and the locusts, the lice and the frogs, and the rest of the signs that made clear his truthfulness and the soundness of his prophethood. [[See what has preceded in this part, 2:318, 354.]]

God named them "clear signs" (bayyinat) because they make clear to those who look at them that they are a miracle that no human can produce except by God's subjecting that to him. They are the plural of bayyina, like tayyiba and tayyibat. [[See what has preceded in this part, 2:318, 319.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The meaning of the statement is: And Moses certainly came to you, O assembly of the Children of Israel, with the clear signs concerning his affair, his truthfulness and the soundness of his prophethood. [[See what has preceded in this part, 2:318, 354.]]

* *

As for His words, "then you took the calf after him, while you were wrongdoers," He, may His praise be great, says to them: then you took the calf as a god after Moses. The pronoun in His words "after him" refers to Moses. He said "after Moses" because they took the calf after Moses had left them, going on to his Lord for his appointment, as we have explained earlier in this book. [[See what has preceded in this part, 2:60–69.]]

It is also permissible that the pronoun in "after him" refers to the coming. The meaning of the statement would then be: And Moses certainly came to you with clear signs, then you took the calf after the coming of the clear signs, while you were wrongdoers, as you say: "You came to me and I disliked it," meaning, I disliked your coming.

* *

As for His words, "while you were wrongdoers," He means by it that you did what you did of worshipping the calf, which was not yours to do, and you worshipped other than the one you should have worshipped, for worship is not fitting for anyone other than God. This is a rebuke from God to the Jews and a reproach from Him to them, and an informing from Him to them that, when they had done what they did, taking the calf as a god, though it possesses no power to harm or benefit them, after they had known that their Lord is the Lord who performs wonders and marvelous acts, which He brought about through the hands of Moses, peace and blessings of God be upon him, matters that no one among God's creation is able to do, and which Pharaoh and his soldiers could not do despite his tyranny and the large number of his followers, and despite the nearness of their time to the wonders of God's wisdom that they witnessed, then they are, in denying Muhammad ﷺ and rejecting what is in their books, which they claimed they believe in, concerning his description and attributes, despite the long distance between them and the time of Moses, quicker, and closer, to denying what Moses brought them of that.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 93:

The explanation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And [recall] when We took your covenant and raised above you the mount, [saying], "Take what We have given you with determination and listen." They said, "We hear and we disobey."﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His words, majestic is His praise: ﴿And when We took your covenant﴾, [it means] remember when We took your pledges, that you should take what We gave you of the Torah, which We sent down to you, and act upon what is in it of My command, and refrain from what I forbade you in it, with earnestness and eagerness on your part in that. So you gave your covenant to act upon that when We raised the mountain above you. [[The earlier explanation of the words of this verse, "mithaq" (covenant), "al-Tur" (the mount), "al-itaa" (giving), and "quwwa" (strength), is to be sought in the following places: 2:156, 157, 160 and the references.]]

As for His words ﴿and listen﴾, its meaning is: listen to what I have commanded you and accept it with obedience, like the saying of a man to another who orders him to do something: "I heard and I obeyed," meaning: I heard your words and obeyed your command, as the rajiz (poet) said:

"Hearing and obedience and submission... are better and more protective for the sons of Mim" [[The verse is said by a man of Dabba, of the Banu Dirar, called Jubayr ibn al-Dahhak. His story is that Abdullah ibn Amr ibn Ghaylan al-Thaqafi, governor of Basra in the year 55, gave a sermon from its pulpit, and this Jubayr pelted him with pebbles, so Abdullah ibn Amr ordered that his hand be cut off. Then he recited the rajaz. They referred the matter to Mu'awiya, who dismissed him (Tarikh al-Tabari 6:167).]]

By His words "hearing" is meant accepting what is heard, and "obedience" is to what one is commanded. Likewise the meaning of His words ﴿and listen﴾ is: accept what you have heard and act upon it.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: So the meaning of the verse is: And when We took your covenant that you take what We gave you with strength, and act upon what you have heard, and obey God, and We raised the mount above you on account of that.

* *

As for His words ﴿They said, "We hear"﴾, the speech came in the form of a report about an absent party, after the address had begun as direct address. This is as we have described, [[In the printed edition: "mimma wasafna" (from what we described), which is not correct.]] that when the opening of speech is a narration, the Arabs address within it and then return to reporting about an absent party, and report about an absent party and then address, as we explained earlier. [[See what has passed at 1:153-154, and this part 2:293, 294.]] Likewise in this verse, because His words ﴿And when We took your covenant﴾ mean: We said to you, and you answered Us.

* *

As for His words ﴿They said, "We hear"﴾, it is a report from God about the Jews whose covenant was taken that they would act upon what is in the Torah and obey God in what they hear from it: that when it was said to them, they said: "We heard your words, and we disobey your command."

* *

The explanation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And they were made to drink into their hearts the calf because of their disbelief﴾

Abu Ja'far said: The people of interpretation differ regarding the interpretation of this. Some of them said: it means they were made to drink into their hearts the love of the calf.

Those who said this:

1561 - Al-Hasan ibn Yahya told us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar told us, from Qatada, regarding ﴿And they were made to drink into their hearts the calf﴾, he said: they were made to drink its love, until that reached their hearts.

1562 - Al-Muthanna told me, saying: Adam told us, saying: Abu Ja'far told us, from al-Rabi', from Abu al-'Aliya, regarding ﴿And they were made to drink into their hearts the calf﴾, he said: they were made to drink the love of the calf because of their disbelief.

1563 - Al-Muthanna told me, saying: Ishaq told us, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far told us, from his father, from al-Rabi', regarding ﴿And they were made to drink into their hearts the calf﴾, he said: they were made to drink the love of the calf into their hearts.

* *

Others said: the meaning of that is that they were given to drink water in which the filings of the calf had been scattered. [[Al-sahala: what falls off gold, silver and the like when filed, i.e., when rubbed with a file.]]

Those who said this:

1564 - Musa ibn Harun told me, saying: Amr told us, saying: Asbat told us, from al-Suddi: When Musa returned to his people, he took the calf which he found them devoted to, slaughtered it, then burned it by filing it, [[Harraqahu: he filed it with a file; see what has passed in this part 2:74.]] then scattered it into the sea, and no sea flowing that day failed to receive some of it. Then Musa said to them: Drink from it, so they drank from it, and whoever loved it came out with gold on his lip. This is when God, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿And they were made to drink into their hearts the calf because of their disbelief﴾. [[The report 1564 has passed as number 937.]]

1565 - Al-Qasim told us, saying: Al-Husayn told us, saying: Hajjaj told me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: When it was filed and thrown into the sea, they confronted the stream of water and drank until they filled their bellies, and that caused cowardice in those of them who did it.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: Of the two interpretations I mentioned, the more preferred regarding God's words, majestic is His praise, ﴿and they were made to drink into their hearts the calf﴾, is the interpretation of those who said: they were made to drink into their hearts the love of the calf. Because one does not say of water: "So-and-so was made to drink it into his heart"; rather this is said of the love of a thing, so it is said: "The heart of so-and-so was made to drink the love of such-and-such," meaning it was given to drink until it overcame him and mixed with his heart, as Zuhayr said:

"I sobered from her after a penetrating love, and love, which your heart drinks, is a disease" [[His Diwan: 339, where it reads "tashrabuhu" with a damma on the ta', sukun on the shin, kasra on the ra', and nasb on "fu'adaka"; its explanation there is evidence for this, for he said "tudkhiluhu" (lets it enter) and said "tashrabuhu" (binds/permeates it), but al-Tabari's reasoning, as you see, indicates its vocalization as passive, with "fu'adaka" in the nominative. "Hubb dakhil" and "da' dakhil": that which has mixed into the inside and introduced corruption into the mind and body.]]

Abu Ja'far said: But He omitted mention of "love" relying on the listener's understanding of the meaning of the speech, since it is known that the calf does not drink into the heart, and that what drinks into the heart from it is its love, as His majestic praise said: ﴿And ask them about the town that was by the sea﴾ [Surah al-A'raf: 163], ﴿And ask the town in which we were, and the caravan in which we came﴾ [Yusuf: 82], and as the poet said:

"Indeed I have been given to drink a black, dark black... Indeed, my portion of drink is enough, indeed enough." [[His Diwan: 343 (Ash'ar al-Sitta al-Jahiliyyin), and Nawadir Abi Zayd: 83, and al-Lisan (sawd). It is disputed what he meant by "aswad" (black). It was said: water; and it was said: death and destruction. Abu Zayd said in his Nawadir: "It is said: so-and-so did not give me a drop of suwayd (diminutive), which is water, called 'the black one'," and he cited the verse as evidence. The correct view is as al-Tabari says, meaning by it: the evil of grief and wretched dark suffering that befell him in love of his beloved of the Hanzaliyya, whom he mentioned in his poetry before the verse: "Say to the phantom of the Hanzaliyya, let it return to her, for I am joining a rope of union..."

"Indeed I weep only for a day I met at Jurtham, a harsh one, after which everything is trivial..."

"When what is unavoidable comes, then welcome to it when it comes — neither a liar nor an excuse..."

"Indeed I..." (verse incomplete)

It is also narrated: "Indeed my portion of life..." and this is better. The version in the Diwan and al-Lisan is "Indeed I drank a black...", and the one here is better. His saying "bajal" means: enough for me is what I have been given to drink of you and of life.]] He means by that a black poison, and he omitted mention of "poison" relying on the listener's knowledge of what he meant by "I was given to drink black." It is narrated:

"Indeed I have been given to drink a black viper that sheds its skin"[[The sālikh among snakes is the very black one, which is most deadly when its skin is shed in its season each year.]]

And the Arabs say: "If it pleases you to look at generosity, look at Hirm or at Hatim," [[Hirm ibn Sinan, companion of Zuhayr ibn Abi Sulma; Hatim is the Ta'i whose fame is not hidden. Much of this is in al-Farra's Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1:61-62.]] so they suffice with mentioning the name instead of mentioning his deed, when he is known for bravery, generosity, or similar qualities, and from this is the poet's saying:

"They say: 'Fight, O Jamil, in a raid,' while the fighting of Tayy and its battles..." [[Ma'ani al-Qur'an of al-Farra 1:62, Majalis Tha'lab: 76, and al-Lisan (ghaza). He attributed it to Jamil, and I do not think it is except a mistake, because Jamil is mentioned in the verse, and it resembles Jamil's saying: "They say: 'Fight, O Jamil, in a raid!' ... And what other fighting do I want?" But this verse is from other poetry, which I have not been able to identify after searching. The first intends: "And indeed the jihad is the jihad of Tayy and its fighting," so he omitted and abbreviated.]]

* *

The explanation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Say: Wretched is what your faith commands you, if you are believers﴾ [2:93]

Abu Ja'far said: By this, majestic is His praise means: Say, O Muhammad, to the Jews of the Children of Israel: Wretched is the thing your faith commands you, if it commands you to kill God's prophets and messengers, and to deny His books, and to reject what came from Him. And the meaning of "their faith" is their affirmation, which they claimed they affirmed from the Book of God, when it was said to them: "Believe in what God has sent down." They said: "We believe in what was sent down to us." His words ﴿if you are believers﴾ mean: if you are affirmers, as you claim, of what God sent down to you. [[See what has passed regarding the meaning of "iman" (faith) at 1:235, 2:143, and others.]] God only refuted them in this, because the Torah forbids all of that and commands the opposite. He informed them that their affirmation of the Torah, if it commands them to that, then wretched is the command it gives. This is only a denial by God, exalted is His mention, that the Torah commands anything of what God dislikes of their actions, or that affirming it indicates any opposition to God's command, and a declaration from Him, majestic is His praise, that what commands them to that is their desires, and what drives them to it is transgression and aggression.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 94:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿Say: If the Last Abode with Allah is yours exclusively, to the exclusion of the people, then wish for death, if you are truthful﴾ (94).

Abu Ja'far said: This verse is among those by which Allah argued against the Jews who were living amongst the inhabitants of the place of his emigration (hijrah), the Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), and by it He exposed their rabbis and scholars. That is because Allah, the Majestic, the Praised, commanded His Prophet (ﷺ) to invite them to a just resolution between him and them regarding the dispute that existed between him and them, just as Allah commanded him to invite the other group, the Christians, when they disagreed with him concerning Jesus (peace be upon him) and disputed about him, to a decisive settlement between him and them through mubahalah (mutual invocation of divine curse). [[This is what came in Surah Al 'Imran: 61; see its account in the exegesis and the biographical literature.]] He said to the group of Jews: If you are truly correct, then wish for death, for that will not harm you, if you are correct in what you claim of faith and nearness of station with Allah. Indeed, if you are given your wish for death when you wish it, you will only pass to rest from the toil of this world, its fatigue and the turbidity of its life, and to the triumph of being in Allah's proximity in His gardens, if the matter is as you claim: that the Last Abode is yours exclusively, to the exclusion of us. But if you do not give it, people will know that you are the falsifiers and that we are the ones who are correct in our claim, and our affair and yours will be revealed to them. So the Jews refrained from answering the Prophet (ﷺ) in this, knowing that if they wished for death they would perish, their worldly life would be gone, and they would go to everlasting disgrace in their afterlife. Just as the group of Christians, who disputed with the Prophet (ﷺ) about Jesus, refrained from mubahalah when they were called to it.

It has reached us that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "If the Jews had wished for death, they would have died, and they would have seen their seats in the Fire. And if those who were going to perform mubahalah with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had gone out, they would have returned without finding family or property."

1566 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Zakariyya ibn 'Adi narrated to us, saying: 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Amr narrated to us, from 'Abd al-Karim, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

[[Hadith 1566: Its isnad is sound. Abu Kurayb is Muhammad ibn al-'Ala'. Zakariyya ibn 'Adi ibn Zurayq al-Taymi al-Kufi: a trustworthy, eminent and pious narrator. Ibn Sa'd said: "He was a righteous man, truthful." He is biographically recorded in al-Tahdhib, in al-Kabir of al-Bukhari 2/1/387-388, al-Saghir: 232, Ibn Sa'd 6: 284, and Ibn Abi Hatim 1/2/600. In the printed edition here it reads "Abu Zakariyya," and the addition of "Abu" is an error of a copyist or printer. 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Amr is Abu Wahb al-Jazari al-Raqqi, a well-known trustworthy narrator from whom the authors of the six books narrated; his biography is in al-Tahdhib, Ibn Sa'd 7/2/182, al-Saghir of al-Bukhari: 203, and Ibn Abi Hatim 2/2/328-329. 'Abd al-Karim is Ibn Malik al-Jazari al-Harrani, a trustworthy, firm narrator and a proponent of the Sunnah, one of the teachers of Ibn Jurayj, Malik, al-Thawri and their peers. His biography is in al-Tahdhib, al-Saghir of al-Bukhari: 148, and Ibn Abi Hatim 3/1/58-59.

This hadith was also narrated by Ahmad in his Musnad: 2226, from Ahmad ibn 'Abd al-Malik al-Harrani, from 'Ubayd Allah, namely Ibn 'Amr, with this isnad, but he did not mention its wording, referring to the preceding narration: 2225, by way of Furat ibn Salman al-Hadrami, from 'Abd al-Karim, with it, with an addition at its beginning. al-Haythami mentioned the fuller narration in Majma' al-Zawa'id 8: 228, and said: "In the Sahih there is a portion of its beginning," then said: "Ahmad narrated it, Abu Ya'la narrated it, and the narrators of Abu Ya'la are the narrators of the Sahih." I say: the narrators of Ahmad in this isnad, 2226, are also the narrators of the Sahih. al-Suyuti mentioned part of it at 1: 89 and also attributed it to the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim), al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i, Ibn Mardawayh, and Abu Nu'aym.]]

1567 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: 'Utham ibn 'Ali narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿so wish for death, if you are truthful﴾, he said: If they had wished for death, one of them would have choked on his saliva.

[[Report 1567: It is a statement attributed to Ibn 'Abbas (mawquf), with the same meaning as the preceding hadith. But this isnad is interrupted (munqati'): al-A'mash did not meet Ibn 'Abbas.]]

1568 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from 'Abd al-Karim al-Jazari, from 'Ikrimah regarding His words: ﴿so wish for death, if you are truthful﴾, he said: Ibn 'Abbas said: If the Jews had wished for death, they would have died.

[[Report 1568: It is part of the preceding hadith, 1566, and its isnad is sound. Its apparent meaning here is that it is mawquf upon Ibn 'Abbas, but it is marfu' (traced to the Prophet) according to the other narrations.]]

1569 - Musa narrated to me, saying: 'Amr informed us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, from Ibn 'Abbas, the like of it.

1570 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, saying: Ibn Ishaq narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad narrated to me - Abu Ja'far said: "in what I narrate, it was reported to us" - from Sa'id, or 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: If they had wished it on the day he said that to them, not a Jew would have remained on the face of the earth but would have died.

[[Report 1570: It is in Ibn Hisham 2: 191.]]

Abu Ja'far said: Thereby is made clear, to whoever was confused about the affair of the Jews on that day, their lying, their slander and their transgression against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the proof of the Messenger of Allah and of his companions over them became manifest. And it has not ceased, praise be to Allah, to prevail over them and over other than them of all the peoples of religions.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was only commanded to say to them: ﴿wish for death, if you are truthful﴾, because, as has been reported to us, they said: ﴿We are the children of Allah and His beloved ones﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 18], and they said: ﴿None will enter Paradise except one who is a Jew or a Christian﴾ [al-Baqarah: 111]. So Allah said to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Say to them: if you are truthful in what you claim, then wish for death. Allah thus made clear their lying by their refusal to wish for that, and He vindicated the proof of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

* *

The interpreters differed regarding the reason for which Allah commanded His Prophet (ﷺ) to call the Jews to wish for death, and in what manner they were commanded to wish it. Some of them said: They were commanded to wish it in the manner of a supplication against the lying party of the two.

Those who said this:

1571 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, saying: Ibn Ishaq narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad narrated to me, from Sa'id, or 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Allah said to His Prophet (ﷺ): ﴿Say: If the Last Abode with Allah is yours exclusively, to the exclusion of the people, then wish for death, if you are truthful﴾, meaning: invoke death upon whichever of the two groups is more lying. [[Report 1571: In Ibn Hisham's Sirah 2: 191, where it reads "more lying before Allah"; see also no. 1578.]]

* *

Others said:

1572 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to me, saying: Yazid ibn Zuray' narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah regarding His words: ﴿Say: If the Last Abode with Allah is yours exclusively, to the exclusion of the people﴾, and that is because they said: ﴿None will enter Paradise except one who is a Jew or a Christian﴾ [al-Baqarah: 111], and they said: ﴿We are the children of Allah and His beloved ones﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 18]. So it was said to them: ﴿then wish for death, if you are truthful﴾.

1573 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Adam narrated to us, saying: Abu Ja'far narrated to us, from al-Rabi', from Abu al-'Aliyah, who said: The Jews said: ﴿None will enter Paradise except one who is a Jew or a Christian﴾, and they said: ﴿We are the children of Allah and His beloved ones﴾. So Allah said: ﴿Say: If the Last Abode with Allah is yours exclusively, to the exclusion of the people, then wish for death, if you are truthful﴾, and they did not do it.

1574 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to me, from his father, from al-Rabi' regarding His words: ﴿Say: If the Last Abode with Allah is yours exclusively﴾ to the end of the verse, and that is because they said: ﴿None will enter Paradise except one who is a Jew or a Christian﴾, and they said: ﴿We are the children of Allah and His beloved ones﴾. [[Report 1574: In the printed edition: "...Ishaq narrated to me, Abu Ja'far narrated to me, from al-Rabi'," which is a corrupt isnad; this narrator frequently recurs in the tafsir, and the closest parallel is no. 1563.]]

* *

As for the interpretation of His words: ﴿Say: If the Last Abode with Allah is yours exclusively﴾, He means: Say, O Muhammad: If the bliss of the Last Abode and its pleasures are yours, O assembly of Jews, with Allah. He mentioned only "the Abode," omitting the mention of its bliss, because the addressees of the verse know its meaning. We have already explained the meaning of "the Last Abode" earlier, in what suffices to avoid repeating it here. [[See what preceded at 1: 245.]]

* *

As for the interpretation of His words: ﴿exclusively (khalisah)﴾, it means: pure. As one says: "Such-and-such became purely mine" (khalasa li fulan), meaning it became mine alone and was purely mine. From this one says: "This thing became purely mine, so it becomes pure (yakhlus), purity (khulus) and exclusivity (khalisah)." "Khalisah" is a verbal noun like "al-'afiyah." And a man is called "hadha khulsani," meaning: my exclusive possession, to the exclusion of my companions.

* *

It has been reported from Ibn 'Abbas that he interpreted His words ﴿khalisah﴾ as: specific (khassah). That is an interpretation close in meaning to the one we have given.

1575 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: 'Uthman ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Bishr ibn 'Umarah narrated to us, from Abu Rawq, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn 'Abbas: "Say" — ﴿Say: If the Last Abode with Allah is yours exclusively﴾: "Say," O Muhammad, to them - meaning the Jews: If the Last Abode - meaning Paradise [[In the printed edition: "meaning the good," which is a misreading; the correct text is what is given here.]] - ﴿with Allah is exclusive﴾, he says: specific to you.

* *

As for His words: ﴿to the exclusion of the people﴾, what the apparent sense of the revelation indicates is that they said: the Last Abode with Allah is ours exclusively, to the exclusion of all people. What shows that this was their statement, without them exempting any one of the children of Adam from it, is Allah's report about them that they said: ﴿None will enter Paradise except one who is a Jew or a Christian﴾. However, a different statement has been reported from Ibn 'Abbas:

1576 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: 'Uthman ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Bishr ibn 'Umarah narrated to us, from Abu Rawq, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿to the exclusion of the people﴾, he says: to the exclusion of Muhammad (ﷺ) and his companions, whom you mocked, and whom you claimed the truth was in your hands, and that the Last Abode was yours to the exclusion of them.

* *

As for His words: ﴿then wish for death﴾, its interpretation is: desire it and want it. It has been reported from Ibn 'Abbas that he said in its interpretation: "ask for death." The meaning "tamanni" as "request" is not known in the speech of the Arabs. But I think Ibn 'Abbas directed the meaning of "umniyah" - since it is the love and craving of the soul - toward the meaning of desire and request, since a request is the seeker's desire toward Allah for what he asks.

1577 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: 'Uthman ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Bishr ibn 'Umarah narrated to us, from Abu Rawq, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿then wish for death﴾, "ask for death," ﴿if you are truthful﴾.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 95:

The explanation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿But they will never wish for it, because of what their hands have put forward. And Allah is Knowing of the wrongdoers.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: This is information from Allah, mighty and majestic is His praise, about the Jews, their aversion to death, and their refusal to respond to what they were called to, namely wishing for death. This is because they knew that if they did that, the threat would descend upon them and death would come upon them. And because of their knowledge of Muhammad ﷺ, that he is a messenger sent to them from Allah, while they deny him, and that he never told them any report except that it was true, as he reported it. So they were wary of wishing for death, fearing that the punishment of Allah would befall them because of what their hands had earned of sins, as in the following:

1578 - Muhammad ibn Humayd narrated to me, who said: Salamah narrated to us, who said: Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to me, who said: Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad narrated to me, in what Abu Ja'far transmits, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, or Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿Say: If the Last Abode with Allah is yours exclusively, then wish for death, if you are truthful﴾ - the verse - meaning: call down death upon whichever of the two groups is more false. But they refused that before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Allah says to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: ﴿But they will never wish for it, because of what their hands have put forward﴾, meaning: because of their knowledge of what they have of knowledge about you, and their disbelief in that. [[The report: 1578 - it passed as no. 1571, and here is its completion. In Ibn Hisham's Sirah 1: 191 it reads "akdhab 'inda Allah" (more false in the sight of Allah). In the printed edition: "wa-qalu dhalika 'ala rasul Allah..." which is an error; its correct form is what is in Ibn Hisham's Sirah. In the printed edition: "ay li-'ilmihim bima 'indahum..." and what I have established is the text of Ibn Hisham.]]

1579 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, who said: Uthman ibn Sa'id narrated to us, who said: Bishr ibn Umarah narrated to us, from Abu Rawq, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿And they will never wish for it﴾, he says: O Muhammad, and they will never wish for it, because they know that they are liars. Had they been truthful, they would have wished for it and desired to hasten to My honour, but they will never wish for it, because of what their hands have put forward.

1580 - al-Qasim narrated to me, who said: al-Husayn narrated to us, who said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, his saying: ﴿So wish for death, if you are truthful﴾; the Jews were most eager to flee from death, and they would never wish for it.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿because of what their hands have put forward﴾, He means by it: because of what their hands have sent ahead. This is only an figure of speech, in the manner that the Arabs use in their speech. You say to a man who is seized for a crime he committed or a wrong he perpetrated, and is punished for it: "This has befallen you because of what your two hands have done, and what your two hands have earned, and what your two hands have sent ahead," attributing that to "the hand." Perhaps the wrong he committed for which he deserved punishment was by the tongue, or by the private parts, or by other limbs of his body besides the hand.

Abu Ja'far said: This was said by attributing it to "the hand" because the greater part of people's wrongdoings are by their hands, so the speech proceeded using the attribution of the wrongs that people commit to "their hands," until every punishment a person receives for what he has committed, from the rest of his body's limbs, is attributed to what his hand has committed.

Therefore He, mighty and majestic is His praise, said to the Arabs: ﴿But they will never wish for it, because of what their hands have put forward﴾, meaning: the Jews will never wish for death, because of what they sent ahead in their lives of their disbelief in Allah, in their opposing His command and obedience in following Muhammad ﷺ and what he brought from Allah, while they find it written in their Torah, and know that he is a commissioned prophet. He, mighty and majestic is His praise, attributed what their hearts harboured, what their souls concealed, and what their tongues uttered, namely envy of Muhammad ﷺ, transgression against him, denial of him and rejection of his prophethood, to their hands, and that it is among what their hands sent ahead, because the Arabs know the meaning of that in their speech and discourse, since Allah, mighty and majestic, only revealed the Qur'an in their tongue and their language. It is narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding that:

1581 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, who said: Uthman ibn Sa'id narrated to us, who said: Bishr ibn Umarah narrated to us, from Abu Rawq, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿because of what their hands have put forward﴾, he says: because of what their hands have sent ahead.

1582 - al-Qasim narrated to us, who said: al-Husayn narrated to us, who said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj: ﴿because of what their hands have put forward﴾, he said: They knew that Muhammad ﷺ was a prophet, but they concealed him.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And Allah is Knowing of the wrongdoers﴾, He, mighty and majestic is His praise, means: And Allah is possessor of knowledge of the wrongdoing of the children of Adam - its Jews, its Christians, and the rest of the people of other religions - and what they do.

The wrongdoing of the Jews is their disbelief in Allah in opposing His command and obedience in following Muhammad ﷺ, after they used to seek victory through him and his mission, and their denial of his prophethood while they knew that he is the prophet and messenger of Allah to them.

We have already explained the meaning of "wrongdoing" earlier, in a way that makes repeating it unnecessary. [[See what has passed: 1: 523-524.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 96:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, saying: ﴿And you will surely find them the most avid of the people for life, and [even] more than those who associated others with Allah. Each one of them wishes he could be granted a life of a thousand years﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His saying, may His praise be exalted: ﴿And you will surely find them the most avid of the people for life﴾ He means the Jews. He says: O Muhammad, you will surely find the people most eager for life in this world, and most averse to death, to be the Jews. As related:

1583 - Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salamah related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq related to me, from Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad - in what Abu Ja'far narrates - from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, or Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿And you will surely find them the most avid of the people for life﴾, meaning the Jews.

1584 - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Adam related to us, saying: Abu Ja'far related to us, saying: al-Rabi' related to us, from Abu al-'Aliyah: ﴿And you will surely find them the most avid of the people for life﴾, meaning the Jews. [[Report 1584: In the printed edition: "Abu Ja'far related to us from Abu al-'Aliyah," with "al-Rabi' related to us" dropped; this is a circular isnad, and its closer version is at no. 1573.]]

1585 - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Ishaq related to us, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far related to us, from his father, from al-Rabi' the like of it. [[Report 1585: In the printed edition: "Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far related to us," with "Ishaq related to us" dropped; this is a circular isnad, and its closer version is no. 1574.]]

1586 - Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

* *

Their aversion to death is only because of their knowledge of the long disgrace and humiliation that await them in the Hereafter.

* *

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, saying: ﴿and [even] more than those who associated others with Allah﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His saying, may His praise be exalted: ﴿and [even] more than those who associated others with Allah﴾, [He means] that they are more avid for life than those who associated others with Allah, just as one says: "He is the bravest of people, and [even] more than 'Antarah," meaning: he is braver than people and than 'Antarah. Likewise His saying: ﴿and [even] more than those who associated others with Allah﴾, because the meaning of the speech is: "And you will surely find them - O Muhammad - the Jews of the Children of Israel, the most avid of the people [[the addition in brackets is indispensable; its context indicates it]] for life, and [even more than] those who associated others with Allah." So when "most avid" was made to modify "the people," which implicitly carries the sense of "than," [the particle] was made to appear after the conjunction, in response to the interpretation we mentioned.

And Allah, may His praise be exalted, described the Jews as the most avid of the people for life because of their knowledge of what has been prepared for them in the Hereafter as a consequence of their disbelief, which those who associate partners with Allah do not acknowledge. So they are more averse to death than the polytheists who do not believe in resurrection, since they (the Jews) believe in resurrection and know the punishment that awaits them there. The polytheists do not affirm resurrection or punishment, so the Jews are more avid for life and more averse to death than they are.

* *

It has also been said that those who associated others with Allah - those whom Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, informs us the Jews are more avid for life than in this verse - are the Magians who do not affirm resurrection. [[Mention of those who said they are the Magians:]]

1587 - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Adam related to us, saying: Abu Ja'far related to us, from al-Rabi', from Abu al-'Aliyah: ﴿and [even] more than those who associated others with Allah. Each one of them wishes he could be granted a life of a thousand years﴾, meaning the Magians.

1588 - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Ishaq related to us, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far related to us, from his father, from al-Rabi': ﴿and [even] more than those who associated others with Allah. Each one of them wishes he could be granted a life of a thousand years﴾, he said: the Magians.

1589 - Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed me, saying: Ibn Zayd said: ﴿and [even] more than those who associated others with Allah﴾, he said: Jews, more avid for life than these.

* *

Mention of those who said: they are those who deny resurrection:

1590 - Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salamah related to us, saying: Ibn Ishaq related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad related to me - in what Abu Ja'far narrates - from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, or Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿And you will surely find them the most avid of the people for life, and [even] more than those who associated others with Allah﴾, and that is because the polytheist does not hope for resurrection after death, so he loves long life; and the Jew has known what disgrace awaits him in the Hereafter, because of what he squandered of the knowledge in his possession. [[Report 1590: Sirah of Ibn Hisham 2: 191.]]

* *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿Each one of them wishes he could be granted a life of a thousand years﴾

Abu Ja'far said: This is a report from Allah, may His praise be exalted, by His saying concerning those who associated others with Allah - those whom He informed that the Jews are more avid for life than them. He, may His praise be exalted, says: each one of these polytheists - hopeless of the perishing of this world and the ending of the days of life [[In the printed edition: "each one of these who associated others with Allah, except that... with the perishing of his world and the ending of the days of his life," with a gap there and in the original. I have inferred the reading as given, since it is the meaning on which Abu Ja'far's explanation turns: that this polytheist has despaired that after the perishing of the world and the ending of life there would be any resurrection, revival, joy or happiness for him, so he wishes he could be granted a life of a thousand years.]] - wishes that there might be for him, after that, resurrection, revival, joy or happiness, were he granted a life of a thousand years. So much so that some of them made their greeting to one another "ten thousand years," out of their avidity for life, as related:

1591 - Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Shaqiq related to us, saying: I heard my father 'Ali say: Abu Hamzah informed us, from al-A'mash, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿Each one of them wishes he could be granted a life of a thousand years﴾, he said: it is the saying of the non-Arabs: "Sal zeh nowruz mihrjan har." [[Report 1591: Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Shaqiq and his father are both trustworthy; we have given their biographies in the commentary on the Musnad: 7437. Abu Hamzah is al-Sukkari, Muhammad ibn Maymun, a trustworthy leading authority. This isnad is sound and connected. See the following isnad. In Tafsir Ibn Kathir 1: 238, the Persian text there reads: "hazar sal nowruz mihrjan". I asked one of our companions who knows Persian, and he said that this text does not conform to the rules of Persian, and that he suspects the correct form is: "zeh dar mihrjan nou vurouz hazar sal", where "zeh" means "live," "dar" is a locative meaning "in," mihrjan is a festival for them, nowruz is another festival at the beginning of the year, "hazar" means thousand, and "sal" means year. So the "har" at the end of the wording in al-Tabari's text is likely a corruption of "dar." The rest of the Persian texts are correct, and their meaning is: live a thousand years.

In al-Mustadrak of al-Hakim 2: 264 there is: "hazar sal surur mihrjan bukhur," and its editor said: it means "enjoy a thousand years, like the festival of Mihrjan, which is a festival for them," and this seems to be the correct reading.]]

1592 - And it was related to me from Nu'aym al-Nahwi, from 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr: ﴿Each one of them wishes he could be granted a life of a thousand years﴾, he said: it is the saying of the polytheists to one another when one of them sneezes: "Zeh hazar sal."

1593 - Ibrahim ibn Sa'id and Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim related to us, both saying: Isma'il ibn 'Ulayyah related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Qatadah regarding His saying: ﴿Each one of them wishes he could be granted a life of a thousand years﴾, he said: wrongdoing made long life beloved to them.

1594 - Yunus ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to me, saying: 'Ali ibn Ma'bad related to me, from Ibn 'Ulayyah, from Ibn Abi Najih regarding His saying: ﴿Each one of them﴾, he mentioned the like of it.

1595 - Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: ﴿And you will surely find them the most avid of the people for life﴾ up to: ﴿could be granted a life of a thousand years﴾: the Jews are more avid for life than these. And these wish that each of them could be granted a life of a thousand years.

1596 - And it was related to me from Abu Mu'awiyah, from al-A'mash, from Sa'id, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿Each one of them wishes he could be granted a life of a thousand years﴾, he said: it is the saying of one of them when he sneezes: "Zeh hazar sal," meaning: ten thousand years. [[Report 1596: Al-Tabari related this with an unidentified isnad, saying: "it was related to me from Abu Mu'awiyah," etc. The reason for this, in my view, is that al-A'mash did not hear it directly from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, although he met him and narrated from him.

Al-Hakim related this report in al-Mustadrak 2: 263-264, through Ishaq ibn Ibrahim: "Abu Mu'awiyah related to us, saying: al-A'mash related to us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas" - in similar wording. Then al-Hakim said: "Qays ibn al-Rabi' narrated it from al-A'mash, from Ja'far ibn Iyas, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas." Then he narrated it with his isnad to Muhammad ibn Yusuf: "Qays ibn al-Rabi' related to us, from al-A'mash, from Ja'far ibn Iyas, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas..." This is a sound and connected isnad, which shows the break in the isnad "al-A'mash from Sa'id ibn Jubayr."]]

* *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And he is not one to remove him from the punishment by being granted life﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His saying, may His praise be exalted: ﴿And he is not one to remove him from the punishment by being granted life﴾, [He means that] the granting of long life - which is prolonged survival - does not remove him from the punishment of Allah.

* *

His saying: ﴿huwa﴾ is a supporting pronoun (imad) for the subject of "ma," since the noun is more often its subject than the verb, as the poet said:

"Is then he raised by what is here, a head..." [[This is a half-line of a verse that has passed in a set of three verses in this part, 2: 313.]]

The "an" in ﴿an yu'ammar﴾ is in the nominative case, governed by "muzahzihih," and the "huwa" which is with "ma" is a repetition, a supporting pronoun for the verb, because the Arabs find it objectionable to place an indefinite before a definite.

* *

Some have said: the "huwa" with "ma" refers back to the mention of age. As if he said: "Each one of them wishes he could be granted a life of a thousand years, and that age is not what removes him from the punishment." And "an yu'ammar" is taken as explaining "huwa," meaning: "he is not one to remove him from the punishment by being granted life." [[See what passed in this part, 2: 340, on the meaning of "translation" (tarjamah).]]

* *

Some have said: His saying: ﴿And he is not one to remove him from the punishment by being granted life﴾ is like your saying: "Zayd is not one to remove him from being granted life."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The closest of these sayings to correctness in our view is what we have said, namely that "huwa" is a supporting pronoun, like your saying: "ma huwa qa'im 'Amr" ("Amr is not standing").

* *

Some people of interpretation have said: the "an" in His saying "an yu'ammar" means "even if he is granted life." But that is a view contrary to the well-known meanings of Arabic speech.

Mention of those who said that:

1597 - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Adam related to us, saying: Abu Ja'far related to us, from al-Rabi', from Abu al-'Aliyah: ﴿And he is not one to remove him from the punishment by being granted life﴾, he says: "even if he is granted life."

1598 - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Ishaq related to us, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far related to us, from his father, from al-Rabi', the like of it.

1599 - Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: "an yu'ammar" - "even if he were granted life."

* *

As for the interpretation of His saying: ﴿bi-muzahzihih﴾, it means: removing him far away and keeping him off, as al-Hutay'ah said:

"They said: 'Move back! There is no need of ours for you, and none of us can mend your rags...'" [[The verse is not by al-Hutay'ah; it belongs to Qays ibn al-Hudadiyyah, from a long and fine ode of his that Abu al-Faraj related in al-Aghani 13: 6. Before the verse he describes coming to his beloved Umm Malik: "...", and then: "'Move back! We have no great need of you, nor are we of your poverty mending..."]]

By His saying "tazahzah" he means: move away. It is said from it: "zahzahahu, yuzahzihuhu, zahzahatan wa zihzaxan," and "he is zahzah from you," meaning: distant.

* *

So the interpretation of the verse is: the prolongation of life does not keep him far from the punishment of Allah, nor keep him away from it, because life must end, and its destination is Allah, as related:

1600 - Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salamah related to us, saying: Ibn Ishaq related to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad related to me - in what I relate - [[In the printed edition: "in what I see," an error; the correct reading is what I have given. See isnad no. 1590.]] from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, or from Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿And he is not one to remove him from the punishment by being granted life﴾, i.e., he is not one to keep him away from the punishment.

1601 - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Adam related to us, saying: Abu Ja'far related to us, from al-Rabi', from Abu al-'Aliyah: ﴿And he is not one to remove him from the punishment by being granted life﴾, he says: "even if he is granted life, that will not be a help to him against the punishment, nor will it keep him away from it."

1602 - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Ishaq related to us, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far related to us, from his father, from al-Rabi', the like of it.

1603 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿Each one of them wishes he could be granted a life of a thousand years, and he is not one to remove him from the punishment﴾, [meaning] they are those who opposed Gabriel, peace be upon him.

1604 - Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: ﴿Each one of them wishes he could be granted a life of a thousand years, and he is not one to remove him from the punishment by being granted life﴾, and the Jews are more avid for life than these. And these wish that each of them could be granted a life of a thousand years, but that would not remove him from the punishment if he were granted it, just as Iblis was granted life and it did not benefit him, since he was a disbeliever, and that did not remove him from the punishment.

* *

The interpretation of His saying, may His praise be exalted: ﴿And Allah is Seeing of what they do﴾ (96)

Abu Ja'far said: By His saying, may His praise be exalted: ﴿And Allah is Seeing of what they do﴾, [He means] Allah possesses sight of what they do; nothing of their deeds is hidden from Him, rather He encompasses all of them, and keeps a watchful record of them, until He makes them taste the punishment for them as their recompense.

* *

The root of "basir" (seeing) is "mubsir," from the saying of the speaker: "absartu fa-ana mubsir" ("I saw, so I am seeing"), but it was transferred to the form "fa'il," just as "musmi'" was transferred to "sami'," and "'adhab mu'lim" to "alim," and "mubdi' al-samawat" to "badi'," and the like. [[See what passed in 1: 283, and in this part 2: 140.]]

The interpretation of His words, exalted is His praise: ﴿Say, "Whoever is an enemy to Gabriel, indeed he has brought it down upon your heart by God's permission"﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: The scholars of tafsir (exegesis) unanimously agree that this verse was revealed in response to the Jews of the Children of Israel, when they claimed that Gabriel was their enemy and that Michael was their ally. Then they differed about the cause that led them to say this. Some of them said: The reason for their saying that was a debate that took place between them and the Messenger of God ﷺ concerning the matter of his prophethood.

Mention of those who said this:

1605 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Yunus ibn Bukayr narrated to us [[In the printed edition: "Yunus 'an Bukayr," which is a clear error.]] from 'Abd al-Hamid ibn Bahram, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Ibn 'Abbas, that he said: A group of Jews came to the Messenger of God ﷺ and said: "O Abu al-Qasim, tell us about some matters we will ask you about, which none but a prophet knows." The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "Ask whatever you wish, but give me the covenant of God and what Jacob took from his sons, that if I tell you something and you recognize it, you will follow me in Islam." They said: "That is agreed." The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "Ask me what you wish." They said: "Tell us about four matters we will ask you about: Tell us, which food did Israel forbid himself before the Torah was revealed? And tell us how the water of the woman and the water of the man are, and how a male and a female are produced from it? And tell us about this unlettered Prophet in sleep, and who among the angels is his ally?" The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "Upon you is the covenant of God: if I inform you, will you follow me?" So they gave him whatever covenant and pact he wished. He said: "I adjure you by He who revealed the Torah to Moses: Do you know that Israel fell gravely ill and his sickness lasted long, so he vowed that if God healed him, he would forbid himself the food and drink he loved most? His most beloved food was the flesh of camels" — Abu Ja'far said: "as I am told" [[In the printed edition: "fima ara" (as I see), and see what preceded shortly: 376.]] — "and his most beloved drink was their milk?" They said: "O God, yes." The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "I call God to witness against you, and I adjure you by God, besides whom there is no god, who revealed the Torah to Moses: Do you know that the water of the man is white and thick, and the water of the woman is yellow and thin, and whichever of the two prevails, the child takes the resemblance and the likeness by God's permission; so if the man's water prevails over the woman's, the child is a male by God's permission, and if the woman's water prevails over the man's, the child is a female by God's permission?" They said: "O God, yes." He said: "O God, bear witness!" He said: "And I adjure you by He who revealed the Torah to Moses: Do you know that this unlettered Prophet's eyes sleep but his heart does not sleep?" They said: "O God, yes!" He said: "O God, bear witness!" They said: "Now tell us who among the angels is your ally, [[In Tafsir Ibn Kathir 1:239: "Anta al-an fa-haddithna..." which is good.]] then we will follow you or part from you." He said: "My ally is Gabriel, and God has never sent a prophet except that he was his ally." They said: "At that, we part from you; if your ally were another of the angels, we would have followed you and believed you." He said: "What prevents you from believing him?" They said: "He is our enemy." So God, mighty and majestic, revealed: ﴿Whoever is an enemy to Gabriel, indeed he has brought it down upon your heart by God's permission﴾ up to His words ﴿as if they did not know﴾. At that, they returned laden with wrath upon wrath. [[The report 1605: its isnad is sound. Yunus ibn Bukayr ibn Wasil al-Shaybani: trustworthy; whoever spoke against him has no argument, and Muslim included him in his Sahih. His biography is in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir of al-Bukhari 4/2/411, Ibn Sa'd 6:279, and Ibn Abi Hatim 4/2/236. In the printed edition here it reads "Yunus 'an Bukayr," which is a clear error. 'Abd al-Hamid ibn Bahram (with fatha on the ba' and sukun on the ha'), al-Fazari: trustworthy; Ahmad and Ibn Ma'in and others declared him trustworthy. Some spoke against him because of his narration from Shahr ibn Hawshab, but Shahr is also trustworthy, as we indicated in 1489.
The hadith was also narrated by Ahmad in his Musnad, at length: 2514, and by Ibn Sa'd in al-Tabaqat 1/1/115-116, both from Hashim ibn al-Qasim, from 'Abd al-Hamid ibn Bahram, with this isnad. Then Ahmad narrated it at 2515, from Muhammad ibn Bakkar, from 'Abd al-Hamid ibn Bahram, with it, but without mentioning its wording, referring to what came before. Ahmad also narrated it at 2471, abridged, from Husayn — that is Ibn Muhammad al-Marwazi — from 'Abd al-Hamid ibn Bahram.
He also narrated it at 2483, by another route, slightly longer. Abu Nu'aym also narrated it in al-Hilya 4:304-305 by this route. Al-Haythami mentioned the report 2483 in Majma' al-Zawa'id 8:241-242, and pointed to the addition found in report 2514, and said: "Ahmad and al-Tabarani narrated it, and its narrators are trustworthy." Ibn Kathir in his Tafsir 1:238-239 quoted the report of al-Tabari that is here, then pointed to the Musnad report 2514. Then he quoted the Musnad report 2483 in 1:240, and the two Musnad reports in 2:186-187.]]

1606 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to me, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi al-Husayn — meaning the Meccan — narrated to me, from Shahr ibn Hawshab al-Ash'ari: That a group of Jews came to the Messenger of God ﷺ and said: "O Muhammad, tell us about four things we will ask you about; if you do, we will follow you, believe you, and believe in you." The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "Upon you is the covenant of God and His pact concerning that: if I inform you of it, will you believe me?" They said: "Yes." He said: "Then ask about whatever occurs to you." They said: "Tell us how a child resembles its mother, when the seed is from the man?" The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "I adjure you by God and by His days among the Children of Israel: Do you know that the man's seed is white and thick, and the woman's seed is yellow and thin, and whichever of them overcomes its companion, the resemblance is for it?" [[In the printed edition: "fa-ayyuhuma ghalabat sahibatha," and the correct reading is from the text of Ibn Hisham's Sira 2:191-192.]] "Yes." They said: "Then tell us about your sleep." He said: "I adjure you by God and by His days among the Children of Israel: Do you know that this unlettered Prophet's eyes sleep but his heart does not sleep?" [[The text of Ibn Ishaq in Ibn Hisham's narration 2:192: "Do you know that the sleep of the one you claim I am not, his eyes sleep while his heart is awake?" They said: "O God, yes." He said: "So my sleep is likewise: my eyes sleep while my heart is awake." They said: "Then tell us what Israel forbade himself." And after that there is also a difference in al-Tabari's narration from Ibn Ishaq.]] They said: "O God, yes." He said: "O God, bear witness!" They said: "Tell us which food Israel forbade himself before the Torah was revealed." He said: "Do you know that the food and drink he loved most was camels' milk and their flesh, and that he suffered an ailment from which God healed him, so he forbade the food and drink he loved most in thanks to God, and forbade himself the flesh of camels and their milk?" They said: "O God, yes." They said: "Then tell us about the Spirit." He said: "I adjure you by God and by His days among the Children of Israel: Do you know that it is Gabriel, [[In Ibn Hisham's Sira: "Do you know him," which is closer to the correct reading.]] who comes to me?" They said: "Yes, but he is our enemy; he is an angel who brings only harshness and the shedding of blood. Were it not for that, we would have followed you." So God revealed concerning them: ﴿Say, "Whoever is an enemy to Gabriel, indeed he has brought it down upon your heart"﴾ up to His words ﴿as if they did not know﴾. [[The report 1606: it is a mursal hadith, part of which has passed with this isnad: 1489. Ibn Kathir referred to it at 1:239-240, after the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas before it, and also stated that Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated it as mursal. It is in Ibn Hisham's Sira 2:191-192, with some difference in wording. Ibn Kathir quoted these two reports (1605 and 1606) and traced them, and completed the discussion of this story in his Tafsir 1:238-245.]]

1607 - al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza narrated to me: that the Jews asked the Prophet ﷺ: "Who is the companion who brings down the revelation to you?" He said: "Gabriel." They said: "He is our enemy, and he comes only with war, harshness and fighting!" So it was revealed: ﴿Whoever is an enemy to Gabriel﴾ — the verse. Ibn Jurayj said: Mujahid said: The Jews said: "O Muhammad, Gabriel descends only with harshness and war!" And they said: "He is our enemy!" [[In Tafsir Ibn Kathir 1:240: "only with harshness, war and fighting, for he is our enemy."]] So it was revealed: ﴿Whoever is an enemy to Gabriel﴾ — the verse. [[The report 1607: this is disconnected (munqati'), and Ibn Kathir mentioned it at 1:240 from this place. Al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza was mentioned at 631; he narrates from the Successors (tabi'un).]]

* *

Others said: Rather, the reason for their saying that was a debate that took place between 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, and them, concerning the matter of the Prophet ﷺ.

Mention of those who said this:

1608 - Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Rib'i ibn 'Ulayya narrated to us, from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from al-Sha'bi, who said: 'Umar stopped at al-Rawha', and saw men hastening toward stones and praying toward them. He said: "What are these?" They said: "They claim that the Messenger of God ﷺ prayed here." He disliked that and said: "Ayma? The Messenger of God ﷺ was overtaken by the prayer in a valley and prayed, then departed and left it!" [[In the printed edition: "Wa-qala: innama rasul Allah ﷺ adrakathu al-salat," which is an awkward phrase. I have adopted what appears in Ibn Kathir's quotation from al-Tabari, 1:240. His saying "ayma" is an interrogative and exclamatory particle; it is most often written "aym" (with fatha, then sukun, then fatha), with the alif dropped. One says: Aym taqulu? meaning: what do you say? See al-Lisan (ayama). 'Umar is expressing amazement at their action.]] Then he began to narrate to them, saying: "I used to attend the Jews on the day of their study-house. I marvelled at how the Torah confirms the Furqan, and how the Furqan confirms the Torah! One day while I was with them, they said: 'O Ibn al-Khattab, none of your companions is more beloved to us than you.' I said: 'Why is that?' They said: 'You visit us and come to us.' I said: 'I come to you, and I marvel at how the Furqan confirms the Torah, and how the Torah confirms the Furqan!'" He said: "The Messenger of God ﷺ passed by, and they said: 'O Ibn al-Khattab, that is your companion, so go to him!'" He said: "I said to them then: 'I adjure you by God, besides whom there is no god, and by what He has entrusted you with of His right and deposited with you of His Book: Do you know that he is the Messenger of God?'" He said: "They fell silent." He said: "Their scholar and their elder said: 'He has weighed heavily upon you; answer him.'" [[In Tafsir Ibn Kathir 1:242: "He has been harsh with you."]] They said: "You are our scholar and our master; you answer him." He said: "As for when you adjure us by Him, we know that he is the Messenger of God." I said: "Woe to you! [You will be] destroyed!" [[In the printed edition: "ayy halaktum," and the correct reading is in Ibn Kathir's Tafsir.]] They said: "We have not been destroyed." I said: "How so, when you know that he is the Messenger of God ﷺ, yet you neither follow him nor believe him?" They said: "We have among the angels an enemy, and among the angels a peaceful one, and he has been paired with our enemy among the angels." [[Al-silm: one who makes peace. One says: "I am at peace with whoever makes peace with me." A man is salm, a people are salm, and a woman is salm.]] I said: "Who is your enemy, and who is your peaceful one?" They said: "Our enemy is Gabriel, and our peaceful one is Michael." I said: "Why did you oppose Gabriel, and why did you make peace with Michael?" They said: "Gabriel is the angel of roughness, harshness, hardship, severity, punishment and the like; and Michael is the angel of compassion, mercy, lightness and the like." I said: "What is their station with their Lord?" They said: "One is at His right hand and the other at His left." I said: "By God, besides whom there is no god, they and whoever is between them are an enemy to whoever opposes them, and at peace with whoever makes peace with them. It is not fitting for Gabriel to make peace with the enemy of Michael, nor for Michael to make peace with the enemy of Gabriel!" He said: "Then I rose and followed the Prophet ﷺ, and caught up with him as he was coming out of an orchard belonging to such-and-such people, [[In the printed edition: "khirqa"; in Ibn Kathir's Tafsir: "khawkha"; the correct reading is "mikhrafa," as I have given it. A mikhrafa is an orchard, or a path between two rows of palms. Kharafa al-nakhl wa-al-thamar: he gathered them; gathering fruit is called "al-kharfa" (with damma then sukun).]] and he said to me: 'O Ibn al-Khattab, shall I recite to you verses that have been revealed?' Then he recited to me: ﴿Say, 'Whoever is an enemy to Gabriel, indeed he has brought it down upon your heart by God's permission, confirming what is before it'﴾, until he recited the verses." He said: "I said: 'May my father and mother be your ransom, O Messenger of God, [[In the printed edition: "bi-abi wa-ummi ya rasul Allah," with "anta" omitted; I have restored what is in Ibn Kathir's Tafsir.]] and by Him who sent you with the truth, I came intending to inform you of the news, but the All-Subtle, All-Aware had already preceded me to you with the news!'" [[The hadith 1608: this too is mursal. Ibn Kathir mentioned it at 1:241-243 from this place, and then from the Tafsir of Ibn Abi Hatim, from the narration of Mujalid from 'Amir, that is al-Sha'bi; a similar one will come from Mujalid's narration as no. 1614. Ibn Kathir then said: "These two isnads indicate that al-Sha'bi narrated it from 'Umar; but there is a disconnection between him and 'Umar, for he did not live in his time." And al-Suyuti said in al-Durr al-Manthur 1:90: "Its isnad is sound, but al-Sha'bi did not live to see 'Umar."
Rib'i, with a kasra on the ra' and the unpointed 'ayn, between them a sukun on the ba', and ending with a doubled ya': he is Rib'i ibn Ibrahim ibn Miqsam al-Asadi, known as Ibn 'Ulayya, like his brother Isma'il ibn 'Ulayya. Rib'i is trustworthy and reliable, one of Ahmad's and Abu Khaythama's teachers and others. 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi said: "We used to count Rib'i ibn 'Ulayya among the remnants of our teachers." In the Musnad at 7444, Ahmad ibn Hanbal said: "He was preferred over his brother." He is biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir 2/1/299, and Ibn Abi Hatim 1/2/509-510.
Dawud ibn Abi Hind: trustworthy, of good isnad, raised (rafa'), one of the memorizers of Basra. His biography is in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir 2/1/211-212, al-Saghir: 160, and Ibn Abi Hatim 1/2/411-412.
al-Sha'bi: he is 'Amir ibn Shurahil al-Hamdani, a great imam, one of the senior Successors. But he did not live to see 'Umar, as Ibn Kathir said, for he was born in the year 19 or 20 (AH).]]

1609 - Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayya narrated to us, from Dawud, from al-Sha'bi, who said: 'Umar said: "I was a man who used to frequent the Jews on the day of their study-house," then he mentioned something like the hadith of Rib'i. [[The report 1609: in the printed edition: "Yaʿqub narrated to me, saying: Ibrahim narrated to us, saying: Ibn 'Ulayya narrated to us," but the correct reading is what I have recorded: Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim al-Dawraqi, who has been mentioned many times with this isnad, and his narration is from Ibn 'Ulayya.]]

1610 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Zuray' narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, who said: It was related to us that 'Umar ibn al-Khattab went one day to the Jews, and when they saw him they welcomed him. 'Umar said to them: "By God, I did not come for your love or for desire for you, but I came to listen to you." He asked them and they asked him. They said: "Who is the companion of your companion?" He said to them: "Gabriel." They said: "That is our enemy among the people of heaven; he informs Muhammad of our secret, and when he comes, he comes with war and famine. [[al-Sanah: drought and dearth.]] But the companion of our companion is Michael, and when he comes, he comes with abundance and peace." 'Umar said to them: "Do you recognize Gabriel and deny Muhammad?" 'Umar then left them and set out toward the Messenger of God ﷺ to tell him their account, but he found that this verse had been revealed to him: ﴿Whoever is an enemy to Gabriel, indeed he has brought it down upon your heart by God's permission﴾.

1611 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Adam narrated to us, saying: Abu Ja'far narrated to us, from Qatada, who said: It reached us that 'Umar ibn al-Khattab once turned to the Jews, and he mentioned something similar.

1612 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada, concerning His words: ﴿Whoever is an enemy to Gabriel﴾, who said: The Jews said: "Gabriel is our enemy, for he descends with harshness, war and famine, while Michael descends with ease, well-being and abundance; so Gabriel is our enemy." Then God, exalted is His praise, said: ﴿Whoever is an enemy to Gabriel﴾.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 97 (part 2 of 3):

1613 - Musa ibn Harun narrated to me, saying: Amr ibn Hammad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿Say: Whoever is an enemy to Gabriel - indeed, he has brought it down upon your heart by the permission of Allah, confirming what was before it﴾, that he said: Umar ibn al-Khattab had land at the upper part of Madinah, and he used to go to it, and his route passed by the study-house (midras) of the Jews. Whenever he entered upon them, he would hear from them. One day he entered upon them, and they said: "O Umar, there is no one among the companions of Muhammad ﷺ more beloved to us than you. They pass by us and harm us, but you pass by us and do not harm us, and we hope for you." Umar said to them: "Which oath is greatest among you?" They said: "The Merciful who sent down the Torah to Moses at Mount Sinai." Umar said to them: "I adjure you by the Merciful who sent down the Torah to Moses at Mount Sinai: do you find Muhammad ﷺ with you?" And they fell silent. [[Sakata al-rajul: he became silent. Asakta al-rajul (intransitive): his speech was cut off so that he did not speak, and he lowered his head from a thought that seized him and interrupted him.]] He said: "Speak, what is the matter with you? By Allah, I did not ask you while I was in doubt about anything of my religion." They looked at one another, and a man among them stood and said: "Tell the man, either you tell him or I will tell him." They said: "Yes, we find it written with us, but its bearer among the angels who brings the revelation is Gabriel, and Gabriel is our enemy; he is the lord of every punishment, war, and earth-swallowing. Had it been that Michael was his ally, we would have believed in him, for Michael is the lord of every mercy and every rain." Umar said to them: "I adjure you by the Merciful who sent down the Torah to Moses at Mount Sinai: where is the place of Gabriel with respect to Allah?" They said: "Gabriel is on His right, and Michael is on His left." Umar said: "I bear witness that whoever is an enemy to the one on His right is an enemy to the one on His left; and whoever is an enemy to the one on His left is an enemy to the one on His right; and whoever is an enemy to both of them, then he is an enemy of Allah." Then Umar returned to inform the Prophet ﷺ, but found that Gabriel had preceded him with the revelation. The Prophet ﷺ called him, and he recited to him. Umar said: "By the One who sent you with truth, I came to you only wanting to inform you!" [[The report: 1613 - in al-Durr al-Manthur 1/91, with slight difference in wording and abridgment in its transmission.]]

1614 - Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq ibn al-Hajjaj al-Razi narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman ibn Mughra' Abu Zuhayr narrated to us, from Mujalid, from al-Sha'bi, who said: Umar went to the Jews and said: "I adjure you by the One who sent down the Torah to Moses: do you find Muhammad in your book?" They said: "Yes." He said: "Then what prevents you from following him?" They said: "Indeed Allah has not sent a messenger except that he had a share (kafl) of the angels, and Gabriel is the one who takes charge of Muhammad, and he is our enemy among the angels, while Michael is our ally. So if it were he who came to him, we would follow him." He said: "I adjure you by the One who sent down the Torah to Moses: what is the rank of the two of them with the Lord of the worlds?" They said: "Gabriel is on His right, and Michael is on his other side." He said: "I bear witness that they do not descend except by the permission of Allah, [[In Tafsir Ibn Kathir 1/243: "ma yanzilan illa bi-idhn Allah" (they do not descend except by the permission of Allah), and it seems to be the correct reading.]] and it is not for Michael to be hostile to the ally of Gabriel, nor for Gabriel to make peace with the enemy of Michael." [While he was with them,] the Prophet of Allah ﷺ passed by [[What is between the brackets is an addition that is necessary; I added it from Tafsir Ibn Kathir 1/242, from the narration of Ibn Abi Hatim in his tafsir.]] and they said: "This is your companion, O son of al-Khattab." So he rose and went to him, and when he reached him, the following had been revealed: ﴿Whoever is an enemy to Gabriel - indeed, he has brought it down upon your heart by the permission of Allah﴾ up to His words: ﴿indeed, Allah is an enemy to the disbelievers﴾. [[The hadith: 1614 - this is also a mursal isnad, and an error occurred in it in the printed edition in two places, which we have corrected since we are certain of the correction. The printed edition read: "Abd al-Rahman ibn Mughra' narrated to us, saying: Zuhayr narrated to us, from Mujahid, from al-Sha'bi." But there is no one named "Zuhayr" among the teachers of Ibn Mughra', nor among the transmitters from "Mujahid" or "Mujalid." And "Mujahid from al-Sha'bi" is also an error, since both are senior Successors of the same generation, Mujahid being slightly older. Abd al-Rahman ibn Mughra' did not live to narrate from Mujahid, nor from al-Sha'bi.
Mujalid is Ibn Sa'id al-Hamdani, a trustworthy narrator whom some imams declared weak. Among the imams who narrated from him are Shu'bah, the two Sufyans, and Ibn al-Mubarak. We favored authenticating the reports of the earlier narrators from him, in Sharh al-Musnad: 3781, because the most balanced statement about him is the saying of Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi: "The hadith of Mujalid among the younger ones, Yahya ibn Sa'id and Abu Usamah, is worth nothing; but the hadith of Shu'bah, Hammad ibn Zayd, Hushaym and these early ones..." Ibn Hatim said: "He means that his memory changed at the end of his life." Ibn Sa'd, in his biography of him (6/243), mentioned the criticism of Yahya al-Qattan of him, then said: "Yet Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Qattan narrated from him despite this, and Sufyan al-Thawri and Shu'bah and others narrated from him." His biography is in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir of al-Bukhari 4/2/9, al-Saghir: 168-169, and Ibn Abi Hatim 4/1/361-362.
Ishaq ibn al-Hajjaj al-Razi is al-Tahhan al-Muqri, whose biography we previously gave: 230. Abd al-Rahman ibn Mughra' ibn Iyad al-Dawsi, Abu Zuhayr: trustworthy; some spoke about his narration from al-A'mash. He is in al-Tahdhib and Ibn Abi Hatim 2/2/290-291.
This hadith was transmitted by Ibn Kathir 1/242-243 from the tafsir of Ibn Abi Hatim: "Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj narrated to us, Abu Usamah narrated to us, from Mujalid, from Amir..." - meaning al-Sha'bi - and he mentioned something similar. Then Ibn Kathir clarified that it is interrupted (munqati'), as we indicated above.
My preferred view is that Abd al-Rahman ibn Mughra' is among those who narrated from Mujalid after his change.]]

1615 - Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Husayn ibn Abd al-Rahman informed us, from Ibn Abi Layla, regarding His words: ﴿Whoever is an enemy to Gabriel﴾. He said: The Jews said to the Muslims: "If Michael were the one who descended upon you, we would have followed you, for he descends with mercy and rain, while Gabriel descends with punishment and vengeance, and he is an enemy to us." He said: Then this verse was revealed: ﴿Whoever is an enemy to Gabriel﴾.

1616 - Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Malik informed us, from Ata', with something similar.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: As for the interpretation of the verse - I mean His words: ﴿Say: Whoever is an enemy to Gabriel - indeed, he has brought it down upon your heart by the permission of Allah﴾ - it is: Allah says to His Prophet: Say, O Muhammad, to the assembly of Jews from the Children of Israel, who claimed that Gabriel is their enemy because he is the bearer of punishments, torments and penalties, not the bearer of revelation, sending down and mercy, so they refused to follow you, denied your prophethood, and rejected what I brought them of My signs and clear judgments, because Gabriel is your ally and the bearer of My revelation to you, and they claimed that he is their enemy: whoever among the people is an enemy to Gabriel, and denies that he is the bearer of Allah's revelation to His prophets and the bearer of His mercy, then I am his enemy and opponent; while I affirm that he is the bearer of revelation to His prophets and messengers, and that he is the one who sends down Allah's revelation upon my heart from my Lord, by my Lord's permission to him in that, to bind my heart with it and strengthen my heart, as:-

1617 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Uthman ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Bishr ibn Ammarah narrated to us, from Abu Rawq, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn Abbas regarding His words: ﴿Say: Whoever is an enemy to Gabriel﴾, he said: That is because the Jews said - when they asked Muhammad ﷺ about many things, and he informed them of them as they were in their own books - "Except Gabriel." For Gabriel, to the Jews, was the bearer of punishment and violence, and he was not for them a bearer of revelation - meaning: sending down from Allah upon His messengers - nor a bearer of mercy.
