So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ informed them, regarding what they asked him about, that Gabriel is the bearer of Allah's revelation, and the bearer of His vengeance and the bearer of His mercy. They said: "He is not a bearer of revelation or mercy; he is an enemy to us!" So Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed, refuting them: ﴿Say﴾, O Muhammad: ﴿Whoever is an enemy to Gabriel - indeed, he has brought it down upon your heart﴾, meaning: indeed Gabriel brought it down - by Allah's command, strengthening your heart and binding your heart with it - meaning: with Our revelation which Gabriel brought down to you from Allah - and thus He does with the messengers and prophets before you.

1618 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿Whoever is an enemy to Gabriel - indeed, he has brought it down upon your heart by the permission of Allah﴾, meaning: He sent down the Book upon your heart by the permission of Allah.

1619 - And it was reported to me from Ammar, who said: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi': ﴿Indeed, he has brought it down upon your heart﴾, meaning: Gabriel sent down the Book upon your heart.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: When He, great is His praise, said: ﴿Indeed, he has brought it down upon your heart﴾, He means by that the heart of Muhammad ﷺ, and He had commanded Muhammad at the beginning of the verse to inform the Jews of that about himself. He did not say "he has brought it down upon my heart" - and had it been said "upon my heart," it would have been correct speech - because it is the custom of the Arabs, when they command a man to relate what was said to him about himself, that they sometimes express the action of the one commanded as attached to a pronoun referring to the speaker himself, since he is the one relating about himself; and sometimes attached to his name, in the form of a pronoun of the addressee, because he is addressed. So you say in the like of this: "Say to the people: indeed the good is with me, much" - so the pronoun of the speaker's own name appears, because he is commanded to inform of that about himself; and "Say to the people: indeed the good is with you, much" - so the pronoun of his name appears in the form of the pronoun of the addressee, because although he is commanded to say it, he is addressed and commanded to relate what was said to him. Likewise: "Do not say to the people: indeed I am standing," and "Do not say to them: indeed you are standing," where the "ya'" in "inni" is the name of the one commanded to say it, as we have described. From this is the saying of Allah, mighty and majestic: ﴿Say to those who disbelieve: you will be overcome﴾ and ﴿will be overcome﴾ [Al 'Imran: 12], with the ya' and the ta'.

* *

As for "Jibril," the Arabs have dialects in it. The people of the Hijaz say "Jibril, and Mikal" without hamza, with a kasra on the jim and the ra' of "Jibril," and with lightening. The majority of the readers of Madinah and Basra recite accordingly.
As for Tamim, Qays and some of Najd, they say "Jabra'il and Mika'il" on the pattern of "Jabra'il and Mika'il," with a fatha on the jim and the ra', with hamza, and with an added ya' after the hamza. The majority of the readers of Kufa recite accordingly, as Jarir ibn Atiyyah said:
They worshipped the cross and denied Muhammad, and denied Jabra'il and denied Mikal...
[[His Diwan: 450, and Naqa'id Jarir wa al-Akhtal: 87, from his crushing qasidah in satire of al-Akhtal, and the pronoun refers to Taghlib, the kin of al-Akhtal; and before it: "May God disfigure the faces of Taghlib, whenever ... the pilgrims raise their voices and glorify with the call (ihlal)."]]
It is reported from al-Hasan al-Basri and Abdullah ibn Kathir that they used to recite "Jibril" with a fatha on the jim, and without hamza.
Abu Ja'far said: This reading is not permissible to recite, because "fa'il" (fi'lil) does not exist in the speech of the Arabs. [[In the printed edition: "fa'il," which is an error.]] Some have chosen it and claimed it is a foreign name, as one says "Samu'il," and recited in this regard: [[He is al-Rabi' ibn Ziyad al-Absi, one of the perfect men from the Banu Fatimah bint al-Kharashb al-Anmariyyah.]]
Were all of Lakhm weighed together, it would not weigh a single feather of the feathers of Sam'uyl...
[[Al-Aghani 14/92, 16/22, and al-Lisan (s-m-l), from verses which al-Rabi' sent to al-Nu'man ibn al-Mundhir in a long report, when Labid said in his rajaz: "Be calm, may you not be cursed, do not eat with him," and claimed that he was the leprous, vile one, and mentioned from his action something ugly and repulsive; so al-Rabi' departed from al-Nu'man, who had been his boon companion, and sent his verses to him: "If my camels depart, not toward a land of ease, no such ease exists in breadth or length..." "Were all of Lakhm weighed together, they would not equal a feather of Sam'uyl..." "The Ruwa'im graze the noble herbs there, not like your grazing of salt and gharwil..." "So remain in your land after me, and lean with the physician at times and with Ibn Tawfil..." And Lakhm are the kin of the house of al-Mundhir, the kings of al-Hirah.]]
As for the Banu Asad, they say "Jibrin" with a nun. It has been related from some Arabs that they add an "alif" to "Jibril," saying: Jibra'iyl and Mika'iyl.
It has been related from Yahya ibn Ya'mar that he used to recite "Jabra'illa" with fatha on the jim, hamza, leaving out the madd, and shaddah on the lam.
As for "Jabr" and "Mik," they are the two names one of which means "servant" and the other "servants."

* *

As for "Il," it is Allah, dhikruhu - exalted be He - as:-

1620 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Jarir ibn Nuh al-Hamma'i narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from al-Minhal, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: Ibn Abbas said: "Jibril" and "Mikail," like your saying: Abd Allah.

1621 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn ibn Waqid narrated to us, from Yazid al-Nahwi, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "Jibril" is Abd Allah; and "Mikail" is Ubayd Allah. And every name with "Il" is: Allah.

1622 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Isma'il ibn Raja', from Umayr, mawla of Ibn Abbas: that "Isra'il, Mikail, Jibril, and Israfil" are like your saying: Abd Allah.

1623 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from al-Minhal ibn Amr, from Abd Allah ibn al-Harith, who said: "Il" is Allah, in Hebrew.

1624 - al-Husayn ibn Yazid al-Dahhak narrated to us, saying: Ishaq ibn Mansur narrated to us, saying: Qays narrated to us, from Asim, from Ikrimah, who said: "Jibril" his name is Abd Allah; and "Mikail" his name is Ubayd Allah. "Il": Allah.

1625 - al-Husayn ibn Amr ibn Muhammad al-Anqazi narrated to me, saying: Abu Ahmad al-Zubayri narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Ata', from Ali ibn Husayn, who said: The name "Jibril" is Abd Allah, the name "Mikail" is Ubayd Allah, and the name "Israfil" is Abd al-Rahman. And every name with "Ma'bad" ("servant of") "Il" is Abd Allah. [[The report: 1625 - al-Husayn ibn Amr ibn Muhammad al-Anqazi: weak; Abu Zur'ah said: "He is not truthful." He is in Lisan al-Mizan, Ibn Abi Hatim 1/2/61-62, and al-Ansab, folio 401. "Al-Anqazi" with a ghayn (or 'ayn) mahmalah, a qaf, between them a silent nun, and a zay. In the printed edition it appears as "al-Abqari," which is a distortion; and similarly it will come in no. 1655 with the distortion, which we corrected there.]]

1626 - al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Qabisah ibn Uqbah narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Muhammad al-Madani - al-Muthanna said: Qabisah said: I think it is Muhammad ibn Ishaq - from Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Ata', from Ali ibn Husayn, who said: What do you count "Jibril" among your names? He said: "Jibril" is Abd Allah, and "Mikail" is Ubayd Allah. And every name containing "Il" is a name made servant to Allah.

1627 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Ata', from Ali ibn Husayn, who said: He said to me: Do you know what the name "Jibril" is among your names? I said: No. He said: Abd Allah. He said: Do you know what the name "Mikail" is among your names? I said: No. He said: Ubayd Allah. And he named "Isra'il" for me with a similar name, but I forgot it, except that he said to me: Do you see, every name that refers to "Il" is a name made servant to Him.

1628 - Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Khusayf, from Ikrimah regarding His words: ﴿Jibril﴾, he said: "Jibr" is servant, "Il" is Allah; and "Mika" he said: servant. "Il": Allah. [[Perhaps it is "wa-Mika"; he said "Ubayd" with diminutive, as previously mentioned.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: This is the interpretation of one who recites "Jabra'il" with fatha, hamza and madd. And it is - God willing - the meaning of one who recites with kasra and leaves out the hamza.
As for the interpretation of one who recites it with hamza, leaving out the madd, and shaddah on the lam, he intended by his saying so, to attribute "Jibr" and "Mika" to the name of Allah which is named by it in the language of the Arabs, rather than the Syriac and Hebrew. For "Il" in the language of the Arabs is Allah, as He said: ﴿They do not observe toward a believer any bond of kinship (il) or covenant (dhimmah)﴾ [al-Tawbah: 10]. A group of the people of knowledge said: "Il" is Allah. From this is the saying of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him, to the delegation of Banu Hanifah, when he asked them what Musaylimah used to say, and they informed him, so he said to them: "Woe to you! Where has your minds gone? By Allah, this speech did not come forth from an 'il' nor a 'bir.'" He means "from 'il'": from Allah. * And:-

1629 - Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, from Sulayman al-Taymi, from Abu Mijlaz regarding His words: ﴿They do not observe toward a believer any bond of kinship or covenant﴾, he said: The saying of "Jibril," "Mikail," and "Israfil."

As if he is saying: when he adds "Jabr," "Mika," and "Isra" to "Il," he says: Servant of God. [[Perhaps the correct reading is "Israf" instead of "Isra," or the first should be "Isra'il" instead of "Israfil."]] ﴿They do not observe regarding a believer any tie of kinship or any pact﴾. As if he is saying: they do not observe God, Mighty and Majestic.

* *

On the interpretation of His words, ﴿confirming what was before it﴾:

Abu Ja'far said: By His words, may His praise be exalted, ﴿confirming what was before it﴾, He means the Qur'an. "Confirming" (muṣaddiqan) is in the accusative as a qat' (here, the circumstantial accusative, al-ḥāl) from the pronoun "hu" in His words ﴿sent it down upon your heart﴾. [[Al-qat': here, the circumstantial accusative (al-ḥāl). See what has passed: 1: 230-232, 330, 561.]]

So the meaning of the statement is: Indeed Gabriel sent down the Qur'an upon your heart, O Muhammad, confirming what was before the Qur'an. He means by this: confirming what had passed of the Books of God before it, and what was sent down to His messengers who came before Muhammad (ﷺ). Its confirmation of them is the agreement of its meanings with theirs in commanding the following of Muhammad (ﷺ) and what he brought from God, and they confirm it. [[In the printed edition: "and they are its confirmation," but the correct reading is what I have set down; he means: they agree with it. As explained earlier.]]

As related:

1630 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Uthman ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Bishr ibn Umara narrated to us, from Abu Rawq, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿confirming what was before it﴾, he says: of the books that God sent down before it, and the revelations, and the messengers whom God sent with the signs, such as Moses, Noah, Hud, Shu'ayb, Salih, and their likes among the messengers, may peace be upon them.

1631 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Zuray' narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada: ﴿confirming what was before it﴾, of the Torah and the Gospel.

1632 - I was told by Ammar, who said: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi' the like of it.

* *

On the interpretation of His words, ﴿a guidance and good tidings for the believers﴾:

Abu Ja'far said: By His words, may His praise be exalted, ﴿guidance﴾ he means: proof and evidence. God, may His praise be exalted, named it "guidance" because the believer is guided by it. And "his being guided by it" means taking it as a guide that he follows, and a leader to whose command, prohibition, lawful and unlawful he submits. And "al-hadi" (the forerunner) of anything is what goes ahead of it. From this it is said of the first of the horses: "hawadiha," which is what goes ahead of them; and likewise the neck is called "al-hadi," because it goes ahead of the rest of the body. [[See what has passed: 1: 166-170, 230, 249, then 549-551.]]

* *

As for "good tidings" (bushra), it is glad tidings. God informed His believing servants, may His praise be exalted, that the Qur'an is for them good tidings from Him, because He informed them of what He has prepared for them of honour with Him in His gardens, and of what they are coming to in their return of His reward. That is the "good tidings" with which God gave the believers glad news in His Book. For "bashara" in the speech of the Arabs means: informing a man of what he did not know, of something that pleases him, before he hears it from another, or learns it from another. [[See what has passed: 1: 383.]]

It has been related on this from Qatada a statement close in meaning to what we have said:

1633 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His words: ﴿guidance and good tidings for the believers﴾: because the believer, when he hears the Qur'an, memorises it and retains it, benefits from it and is at peace with it, and believes in the promise of God which He made in it, and is certain of that.

The discussion on the interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿Whoever is an enemy to Allah, His angels, His messengers, Jibril and Mika'il, then indeed Allah is an enemy to the disbelievers﴾ (2:98)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: This is a report from Allah, may His praise be exalted, that whoever is an enemy to Allah, who opposes Him and opposes all His angels and messengers, [[In the printed edition it reads: "man kana 'aduwwan lillah" ("whoever is an enemy to Allah"), which is not correct. The correct reading appears to be: "anna man kana 'aduwwan lillah, 'adahu wa 'ada jami'a mala'ikatihi wa rusulihi" ("that whoever is an enemy to Allah, he opposes Him and opposes all His angels and messengers"), with the word "min" removed from "min 'adahu".]] and an announcement from Him that whoever opposes Jibril has opposed Him, and opposes Mika'il, and opposes all His angels and messengers. This is because those whom Allah named in this verse are the friends of Allah and the people of His obedience, and whoever opposes a friend of Allah has opposed Allah and waged war against Him, and whoever opposes Allah has opposed all the people of His obedience and His friendship. For an enemy of Allah is an enemy of His friends, and an enemy of the friends of Allah is an enemy of Him. Likewise He said to the Jews, who said: "Jibril is our enemy among the angels, and Mika'il is our ally": ﴿Whoever is an enemy to Allah, His angels, His messengers, Jibril and Mika'il, then indeed Allah is an enemy to the disbelievers﴾, because the enemy of Jibril is an enemy of every friend of Allah. So He informed them, may His praise be exalted, that whoever is an enemy to Jibril is an enemy to everyone mentioned, from His angels, His messengers, and Mika'il, and likewise whoever is an enemy to any of the messengers of Allah is an enemy to Allah and to every friend (of His). And:

1634 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, saying: Ubayd Allah, that is al-Ataki, narrated to us, from a man of Quraysh, who said: The Prophet ﷺ asked the Jews: "I ask you by your Book which you recite, do you find that Jesus son of Mary gave good news of me, that a messenger named Ahmad would come to you?" They said: "O Allah, we found you in our book, but we disliked you because you make lawful wealth and shed blood." So Allah revealed: ﴿Whoever is an enemy to Allah and His angels﴾, to the end of the verse. [[The hadith 1634: Ubayd Allah al-Ataki is Ubayd Allah ibn Abd Allah, Abu al-Munib al-Ataki, and he is trustworthy; Ibn Ma'in and others declared him trustworthy. Al-Bukhari mentioned him in al-Du'afa' (The Weak Narrators), p. 22, and said: "He has munkar (odd) narrations." Ibn Abi Hatim (2/2/322) said in his biography: "I heard my father say: he is sound in narration." He objected to al-Bukhari including him in al-Du'afa' and said: "He is yahul" (i.e., his narrations are questionable). But this hadith is munqati' (disconnected) and weak in its chain, because Abu al-Munib only narrates from the Successors (tabi'un).

The report was also transmitted by al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak (2/265), through the route of Ishaq ibn Ibrahim, from Jarir, with the same content. Al-Dhahabi affirmed its soundness in his abridgement. Ibn Kathir transmitted it from al-Tabari (1/248-249), then referred to the narration of al-Hakim.]]

1635 - It was related to me from Ammar, who said: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from Husayn ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, who said: A Jew met Umar and said to him: "Jibril, whom your companion mentions, is our enemy." Umar said to him: ﴿Whoever is an enemy to Allah and His angels and His messengers and Jibril and Mika'il, then indeed Allah is an enemy to the disbelievers﴾. He said: So it was revealed upon the tongue of Umar.

* *

This report indicates that Allah revealed this verse as a rebuke to the Jews for their disbelief in Muhammad ﷺ, and as an announcement from Him to them that whoever is an enemy to Muhammad, Allah is an enemy to him, and that the enemy of Muhammad, from all of mankind, is among the disbelievers in Allah who deny His signs.

* *

If someone says: Are not Jibril and Mika'il among the angels?

It is said: Yes.

If he says: What is the meaning of repeating their mention by name, when they have already been mentioned in the verse among the names of the angels?

It is said: The meaning of singling out their mention by name is that when the Jews said: "Jibril is our enemy, and Mika'il is our ally," and claimed that they disbelieved in Muhammad ﷺ because Jibril is the companion of Muhammad ﷺ, Allah informed them that whoever is an enemy to Jibril, Allah is an enemy to him, and that he is among the disbelievers. So He specified him by name, and specified Mika'il by name, lest someone among them say: "Allah only said: whoever is an enemy to Allah, His angels and His messengers, and we are not enemies of Allah, nor of His angels and messengers." For "the angels" is a general term that may (be taken to) include a particular, and Jibril and Mika'il were not included in it. Likewise His saying "His messengers": you, O Muhammad, are not included among them. So Allah, exalted is He, named by their very names those whom they claimed to be His enemies, in order to cut off by this their deception toward the weak among them, and to close off their obscuring of matters to the hypocrites.

* *

As for the manifest mention of the name of Allah in His saying: ﴿then indeed Allah is an enemy to the disbelievers﴾, and its repetition there, although the beginning of the report had already mentioned Him in saying: ﴿Whoever is an enemy to Allah and His angels﴾, (this is) so that there would be no ambiguity for the listener, had it been expressed by a pronoun, saying "fa-innahu 'aduwwun lil-kafirin" ("then indeed He is an enemy to the disbelievers"): to whom does the "hu" (He) in "fa-innahu" refer, Allah, or the messengers of Allah, may His praise be exalted, or Jibril, or Mika'il? For if that were expressed by a pronoun as I have described, the meaning would become ambiguous to whoever does not know what is intended by it, because the speech allows what I have described. Some grammarians have directed this toward a line of the poet: [[He is Jarir.]]

"Would that the crow, on the morning it caws continuously..., had been a crow with its jugular veins cut."

[[In his Diwan, p. 89, and Amali Ibn al-Shajari 1/243, and elsewhere. The narration in the Diwan is "yan'atu bil-nawa" ("it describes with separation"), which is the better one, for before it is: "Indeed the crow, with what you disliked, is devoted to the separation of the beloved, constantly cawing." Al-awdaj is the plural of wadaj, which is a vein among the veins surrounding the throat.]]

And (they say) it is the manifestation of a noun whose proper place is pronominalization. But the matter in that is contrary to what he said. That is because if the second "al-ghurab" (crow) had been expressed by a pronoun, no one who understands the speech of the Arabs would have been confused that it is a pronoun for the noun "al-ghurab" (crow) first, since there is nothing before it that the speech could be directed to other than a pronoun for the first "al-ghurab." And since before His saying: ﴿then indeed Allah is an enemy to the disbelievers﴾ there are nouns, if the name of Allah, exalted is His remembrance, had come expressed by a pronoun, one would not know who was intended by the pronoun, except through a proof from authoritative testimony. Therefore the two matters differ.

**The interpretation of His words, the Exalted: ﴿And We have certainly sent down to you clear signs﴾**

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: By His words, the Exalted, ﴿And We have certainly sent down to you signs﴾, He means: We have sent down to you, O Muhammad, clear signs indicating your prophethood. These signs are what the Book of God contains, which He sent down to Muhammad ﷺ, of the hidden knowledge of the Jews and the concealed secrets of their reports and the reports of their ancestors from the Children of Israel, and the news of what their books contained, which only their rabbis (aḥbār) and scholars knew, and of what their forebears and successors had distorted and altered from their rulings that were in the Torah. So God made these manifest in His Book which He sent down to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ.[[In the printed edition: "fa-aṭlaʿ Allah fī kitābihi" ("God made [it] appear in His Book..."), which is not a sound sentence; the correct reading is what I have recorded. The meaning is: God revealed these hidden things, those reports, and what they had distorted of the rulings in their Torah.]] Thus, in that is from Him the clear signs for whoever is fair to himself, and whom envy and insolence did not drive to destroy them. For it is in the natural disposition of everyone with a sound nature to affirm the one who brings the like of what Muhammad ﷺ brought, of clear signs described without his having learned them from any human being, nor having taken anything of it from any mortal. It is in accordance with what we have said that a report was transmitted from Ibn Abbas.

1636 – Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Uthman ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Bishr ibn Umara narrated to us, from Abu Rawq, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿And We have certainly sent down to you clear signs﴾ – he says: You recite it to them and inform them of it morning and evening and in between, and you are among them unlettered, not having read a book, and you inform them of what is in their hands precisely as it is. God says: In that is a lesson and clarification for them, and proof against them, if they had knowledge.

1637 – Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, saying: Ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, the client (mawlā) of Zayd ibn Thabit, narrated to me, from Ikrima, the client of Ibn Abbas, and from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Ibn Suriya al-Fiṭyūnī said to the Messenger of God ﷺ:[[In the printed edition it is "al-Qiṭyūnī" with a qāf, which is an error. He is of the clan of Tha'laba ibn al-Fiṭyūn (with a kasra on the fā', a sukūn on the ṭā', and a ḍamma on the yā'). Al-Suhaylī said: "Al-Fiṭyūn is a Hebrew word applied to whoever governs the affairs and kingship of the Jews." Al-Tabari's narration reads "Ibn Suriya," while in Ibn Hisham's Sira (2:196) it is "Ibn Ṣalūbā al-Fiṭyūnī." Ibn Hisham, in what he narrated from the Sira of Ibn Ishaq (1:160–161), mentions "the enemies among the Jews" and counts among the clan of Tha'laba: Ibn al-Fiṭyūn – "ʿAbd Allah ibn Suriya al-Aʿwar, and there was no one in his time more knowledgeable in the Torah than him; and Ibn Ṣalūbā; and Mukhayrīq. He was their rabbi and became Muslim." I have not been able to determine whether it is Ibn Suriya or Ibn Ṣalūbā, the one whose affair was what it was. Perhaps these are two different narrations from Ibn Ishaq. See also the report 1638.]] O Muhammad, you have brought us nothing that we recognize, and God has not sent down to you any clear sign that we would follow you with! [[In Ibn Hisham: "min āyatin fa-nattabiʿaka laha" ("a sign that we would follow you for"). Then God the Mighty and Majestic revealed concerning that from His words: "And We have certainly sent down to you..."]] So God, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿And We have certainly sent down to you clear signs, and none disbelieve in them except the defiantly disobedient﴾![[The two reports 1637–1638 are in Ibn Hisham's Sira, 2:196.]]

1638 – Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Yunus ibn Bukayr narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, the client of Zayd ibn Thabit, narrated to me, saying: Sa'id ibn Jubayr, or Ikrima, narrated to me, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Ibn Suriya said to the Messenger of God ﷺ, and he mentioned the like of it.[[The two reports 1637–1638 are in Ibn Hisham's Sira, 2:196.]]

* *

**The interpretation of His words, the Exalted: ﴿And none disbelieve in them except the defiantly disobedient﴾**

Abu Ja'far said: By His words, the Exalted: ﴿And none disbelieve in them except the defiantly disobedient﴾, He means: and none deny them. We have already shown earlier in this book that the meaning of "kufr" (disbelief) is denial, which suffices here without repeating it.[[See what preceded at 1:255, 382, 552, and this volume 2:140, 337.]] Likewise we have explained the meaning of "fisq" (defiant disobedience), that it is leaving the thing for something else.[[See what preceded at 1:409–410, and this volume 2:118.]]

* *

So the interpretation of the verse: And We have certainly sent down to you, in what We revealed to you of the Book, clear signs which make plain to the scholars of the Children of Israel and their rabbis – those who deny your prophethood and reject your message – that you are a messenger to them from Me, and a prophet sent. And none deny those signs – those that indicate your truthfulness and prophethood, which I sent down to you in My Book – among them, so as to disbelieve in them, except those among them who have left their religion, who have abandoned My obligations upon them in the Book to whose truth they profess adherence. As for those among them who hold fast to their religion and follow the rulings of their Book, they affirm what I have sent down to you of My signs. These are the ones who had believed in God and affirmed His Messenger Muhammad ﷺ from among the Jews of the Children of Israel.

* *

**The interpretation of His words, the Exalted: ﴿Is it not that whenever they make a covenant, a party of them throws it aside? Rather, most of them do not believe﴾**

Abu Ja'far said: The scholars of Arabic (ahl al-ʿarabiyya) differed regarding the function of the "wāw" in His words: ﴿Awa-kullamā ʿāhadū ʿahdan﴾ (Is it that whenever they made a covenant?). Some of the Basran grammarians said: It is a "wāw" which is placed together with the interrogative particles, and it is like the "fā'" in His words: ﴿Afa-kullamā jāʾakum rasūlun bimā lā tahwā anfusukumu istakbartum﴾ (Is it, then, whenever a messenger came to you with what your souls did not desire, that you were arrogant?) [al-Baqara: 87]. He said: Both are redundant in this usage, and it is like the "fā'" in His words: "By God, you will do such and such." [[I do not know what al-Tabari meant by this.]] And like your saying to a man: "Afa-lā taqūm?" (Then will you not stand?). If you wish, you may make the "fā'" and the "wāw" here conjunctions.

Some of the Kufan grammarians said: It is a conjunction to which the interrogative particle has been prefixed.

* *

The correct view on this, in my opinion, of these sayings, is that it is a conjunctive "wāw," to which the interrogative "alif" has been prefixed. It is as if He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And when We took your covenant and raised the mountain above you: Take what We have given you with strength, and hear. They said: We hear and we disobey﴾, and whenever they made a covenant, a party of them threw it aside. Then He prefixed the interrogative "alif" to "wa-kullamā," saying: ("They said: We hear and we disobey"), is it that whenever they made a covenant, a party of them threw it aside?

We have already shown earlier that it is impermissible for there to be in the Book of God a letter without meaning,[[See what preceded at 1:439–441.]] and that suffices so as to dispense with repeating the clarification of the corruption of the view of whoever claims that the "wāw" and the "fā'" in His words ﴿Awa-kullamā﴾ and ﴿Afa-kullamā﴾ are redundant and without meaning.

* *

As for "ʿahd" (covenant), it is the pledge which the Children of Israel gave their Lord that they would act upon what is in the Torah, time after time, and then some of them broke that again and again. So He, the Mighty in remembrance, rebuked them for what they had done of this, and reproached their descendants for following their path in some of what He, the Mighty in remembrance, had taken from them by way of covenant and pledge to believe in Muhammad ﷺ, and they disbelieved and denied what was in the Torah of his description and attributes. So the Exalted said: Is it that whenever the Jews of the Children of Israel made a covenant with their Lord and confirmed a pledge, a party of them threw it aside, abandoned and broke it? As:

1639 – Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Yunus ibn Bukayr narrated to us, saying: Ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, the client of Zayd ibn Thabit, narrated to me, saying: Sa'id ibn Jubayr, or Ikrima, narrated to me, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Malik ibn al-Sayf said – when the Messenger of God ﷺ was sent, and he mentioned what was taken from them of the covenant and what God had charged them with concerning it: "By God, He has not charged us concerning Muhammad ﷺ, nor has He taken from us a covenant for him!" So God, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿Is it not that whenever they made a covenant, a party of them threw it aside? Rather, most of them do not believe﴾.[[The report 1639 is in Ibn Hisham's Sira, 2:196, with a slight difference in wording. Ibn Hisham mentioned "Malik ibn al-Sayf" at 2:161 and said: "It is also said: Ibn Ḍayf."]]

1640 – Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, the client of the family of Zayd ibn Thabit, narrated to me, from Ikrima, the client of Ibn Abbas, or from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, the like of it.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: As for "nabdh" (throwing aside), its origin in the speech of the Arabs is casting away. For this reason the foundling is called "al-manbūdh," [[In Ibn Kathir's Tafsir, 1:247: "and he was called a foundling (laqīṭ)..." Laqīṭ is better than "malqūṭ."]] because he is cast away and thrown off. From this the drink "nabīdh" was named "nabīdh," because it is raisins or dates thrown into a vessel, then treated with water. Its origin is the form "mafʿūl," which was changed to "faʿīl"; I mean that "nabīdh" originally was "manbūdh," then it was changed to the form "faʿīl" and was called "nabīdh," just as they said "kaffun khaḍīb" (a dyed hand) and "liḥyatun dahīn" (an oiled beard), meaning dyed and oiled. [[See what preceded at 1:112.]] From it one says: "nabadhtuhu, anbadhuhu, nabdhan," as Abu al-Aswad al-Du'ali said:

*I looked at its title and cast it aside, as you cast aside a sandal worn out from your sandals.*[[From his Dīwān, 21 (in Nafāʾis al-Makhṭūṭāt, 2), and it will come in 20:49–50 (Bulaq edition), and in Majāz al-Qurʾān, 48. From verses he wrote to his friend al-Ḥuṣayn ibn al-Ḥurr, who was governor of Maysān. He had written to him about a matter that concerned him, but he was preoccupied and did not respond. Before the verse is: "And informed me, whom I had sent, that you took my letter, turning away from it with your left hand."]]

* *

So the meaning of His words, the Mighty in remembrance: ﴿A party of them threw it aside﴾, is: a party of them cast it off, abandoned it, rejected and broke it. As:

1641 – Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada: ﴿A party of them threw it aside﴾ – he says: a party of them broke it.

1642 – Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, concerning His words: ﴿A party of them threw it aside﴾, he said: There was no covenant on earth that they made and did not break, and they make covenants today and break them tomorrow. He said: And in the reading of ʿAbd Allah: ﴿A party of them broke it﴾.

* *

The "hā'" in His words ﴿nabadhahu﴾ refers to the mention of the covenant. So its meaning: Is it that whenever they made a covenant, a party of them cast that covenant aside?

* *

"Firq" (party) is a group, which has no singular from its own root, like "jaysh" (army) and "rahṭ" (company), which have no singular from their own root.[[See what preceded in this volume at 2:244–245.]]

* *

The "hā'" and "mīm" in His words ﴿a party of them﴾ refer to the mention of the Jews of the Children of Israel.

* *

As for His words: ﴿Rather, most of them do not believe﴾, He, the Mighty in remembrance, means: Rather, most of these – who, whenever they made a covenant with God and confirmed a pledge to Him, a party of them broke it – do not believe.

* *

For this there are two interpretations. One: that the statement indicates an increase and multiplication in the number of those who deny and break God's covenant, over the number of the party. The meaning of the statement would then be: Is it that whenever the Jews of the Children of Israel made a covenant with their Lord, a party of them broke that covenant? No – it is not a party of them that breaks it, but the one who breaks it and disbelieves in God is most of them, not the few among them. This is one of its two interpretations.

The other interpretation: that its meaning is: Is it that whenever the Jews made a covenant with their Lord, a party of them cast that covenant aside? No – it is not a party of them that casts it aside and breaks it, out of belief among them that this is not permissible for them, but most of them do not affirm God and His messengers, nor His promise and His threat. We have already shown earlier in this book the meaning of "īmān" (belief), that it is affirmation.[[See what preceded at 1:234–235, 271, 560, and this volume 2:143, 348.]]

See also the report 1638.]] O Muhammad, you have brought us nothing that we recognize, and God has not sent down to you any clear sign that we would follow you with! [[In Ibn Hisham: "min āyatin fa-nattabiʿaka laha" ("a sign that we would follow you for"). Then God the Mighty and Majestic revealed concerning that from His words: "And We have certainly sent down to you..."]] So God, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿And We have certainly sent down to you clear signs, and none disbelieve in them except the defiantly disobedient﴾![[The two reports 1637–1638 are in Ibn Hisham's Sira, 2:196.]]

1638 – Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Yunus ibn Bukayr narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, the client of Zayd ibn Thabit, narrated to me, saying: Sa'id ibn Jubayr, or Ikrima, narrated to me, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Ibn Suriya said to the Messenger of God ﷺ, and he mentioned the like of it.[[The two reports 1637–1638 are in Ibn Hisham's Sira, 2:196.]]

* *

**The interpretation of His words, the Exalted: ﴿And none disbelieve in them except the defiantly disobedient﴾**

Abu Ja'far said: By His words, the Exalted: ﴿And none disbelieve in them except the defiantly disobedient﴾, He means: and none deny them. We have already shown earlier in this book that the meaning of "kufr" (disbelief) is denial, which suffices here without repeating it.[[See what preceded at 1:255, 382, 552, and this volume 2:140, 337.]] Likewise we have explained the meaning of "fisq" (defiant disobedience), that it is leaving the thing for something else.[[See what preceded at 1:409–410, and this volume 2:118.]]

* *

So the interpretation of the verse: And We have certainly sent down to you, in what We revealed to you of the Book, clear signs which make plain to the scholars of the Children of Israel and their rabbis – those who deny your prophethood and reject your message – that you are a messenger to them from Me, and a prophet sent. And none deny those signs – those that indicate your truthfulness and prophethood, which I sent down to you in My Book – among them, so as to disbelieve in them, except those among them who have left their religion, who have abandoned My obligations upon them in the Book to whose truth they profess adherence. As for those among them who hold fast to their religion and follow the rulings of their Book, they affirm what I have sent down to you of My signs. These are the ones who had believed in God and affirmed His Messenger Muhammad ﷺ from among the Jews of the Children of Israel.

* *

**The interpretation of His words, the Exalted: ﴿Is it not that whenever they make a covenant, a party of them throws it aside? Rather, most of them do not believe﴾**

Abu Ja'far said: The scholars of Arabic (ahl al-ʿarabiyya) differed regarding the function of the "wāw" in His words: ﴿Awa-kullamā ʿāhadū ʿahdan﴾ (Is it that whenever they made a covenant?). Some of the Basran grammarians said: It is a "wāw" which is placed together with the interrogative particles, and it is like the "fā'" in His words: ﴿Afa-kullamā jāʾakum rasūlun bimā lā tahwā anfusukumu istakbartum﴾ (Is it, then, whenever a messenger came to you with what your souls did not desire, that you were arrogant?) [al-Baqara: 87]. He said: Both are redundant in this usage, and it is like the "fā'" in His words: "By God, you will do such and such." [[I do not know what al-Tabari meant by this.]] And like your saying to a man: "Afa-lā taqūm?" (Then will you not stand?). If you wish, you may make the "fā'" and the "wāw" here conjunctions.

Some of the Kufan grammarians said: It is a conjunction to which the interrogative particle has been prefixed.

* *

The correct view on this, in my opinion, of these sayings, is that it is a conjunctive "wāw," to which the interrogative "alif" has been prefixed. It is as if He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And when We took your covenant and raised the mountain above you: Take what We have given you with strength, and hear. They said: We hear and we disobey﴾, and whenever they made a covenant, a party of them threw it aside. Then He prefixed the interrogative "alif" to "wa-kullamā," saying: ("They said: We hear and we disobey"), is it that whenever they made a covenant, a party of them threw it aside?

We have already shown earlier that it is impermissible for there to be in the Book of God a letter without meaning,[[See what preceded at 1:439–441.]] and that suffices so as to dispense with repeating the clarification of the corruption of the view of whoever claims that the "wāw" and the "fā'" in His words ﴿Awa-kullamā﴾ and ﴿Afa-kullamā﴾ are redundant and without meaning.

* *

As for "ʿahd" (covenant), it is the pledge which the Children of Israel gave their Lord that they would act upon what is in the Torah, time after time, and then some of them broke that again and again. So He, the Mighty in remembrance, rebuked them for what they had done of this, and reproached their descendants for following their path in some of what He, the Mighty in remembrance, had taken from them by way of covenant and pledge to believe in Muhammad ﷺ, and they disbelieved and denied what was in the Torah of his description and attributes. So the Exalted said: Is it that whenever the Jews of the Children of Israel made a covenant with their Lord and confirmed a pledge, a party of them threw it aside, abandoned and broke it? As:

1639 – Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Yunus ibn Bukayr narrated to us, saying: Ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, the client of Zayd ibn Thabit, narrated to me, saying: Sa'id ibn Jubayr, or Ikrima, narrated to me, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Malik ibn al-Sayf said – when the Messenger of God ﷺ was sent, and he mentioned what was taken from them of the covenant and what God had charged them with concerning it: "By God, He has not charged us concerning Muhammad ﷺ, nor has He taken from us a covenant for him!" So God, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿Is it not that whenever they made a covenant, a party of them threw it aside? Rather, most of them do not believe﴾.[[The report 1639 is in Ibn Hisham's Sira, 2:196, with a slight difference in wording. Ibn Hisham mentioned "Malik ibn al-Sayf" at 2:161 and said: "It is also said: Ibn Ḍayf."]]

1640 – Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, the client of the family of Zayd ibn Thabit, narrated to me, from Ikrima, the client of Ibn Abbas, or from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, the like of it.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: As for "nabdh" (throwing aside), its origin in the speech of the Arabs is casting away. For this reason the foundling is called "al-manbūdh," [[In Ibn Kathir's Tafsir, 1:247: "and he was called a foundling (laqīṭ)..." Laqīṭ is better than "malqūṭ."]] because he is cast away and thrown off. From this the drink "nabīdh" was named "nabīdh," because it is raisins or dates thrown into a vessel, then treated with water. Its origin is the form "mafʿūl," which was changed to "faʿīl"; I mean that "nabīdh" originally was "manbūdh," then it was changed to the form "faʿīl" and was called "nabīdh," just as they said "kaffun khaḍīb" (a dyed hand) and "liḥyatun dahīn" (an oiled beard), meaning dyed and oiled. [[See what preceded at 1:112.]] From it one says: "nabadhtuhu, anbadhuhu, nabdhan," as Abu al-Aswad al-Du'ali said:

*I looked at its title and cast it aside, as you cast aside a sandal worn out from your sandals.*[[From his Dīwān, 21 (in Nafāʾis al-Makhṭūṭāt, 2), and it will come in 20:49–50 (Bulaq edition), and in Majāz al-Qurʾān, 48. From verses he wrote to his friend al-Ḥuṣayn ibn al-Ḥurr, who was governor of Maysān. He had written to him about a matter that concerned him, but he was preoccupied and did not respond. Before the verse is: "And informed me, whom I had sent, that you took my letter, turning away from it with your left hand."]]

* *

So the meaning of His words, the Mighty in remembrance: ﴿A party of them threw it aside﴾, is: a party of them cast it off, abandoned it, rejected and broke it. As:

1641 – Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada: ﴿A party of them threw it aside﴾ – he says: a party of them broke it.

1642 – Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, concerning His words: ﴿A party of them threw it aside﴾, he said: There was no covenant on earth that they made and did not break, and they make covenants today and break them tomorrow. He said: And in the reading of ʿAbd Allah: ﴿A party of them broke it﴾.

* *

The "hā'" in His words ﴿nabadhahu﴾ refers to the mention of the covenant. So its meaning: Is it that whenever they made a covenant, a party of them cast that covenant aside?

* *

"Firq" (party) is a group, which has no singular from its own root, like "jaysh" (army) and "rahṭ" (company), which have no singular from their own root.[[See what preceded in this volume at 2:244–245.]]

* *

The "hā'" and "mīm" in His words ﴿a party of them﴾ refer to the mention of the Jews of the Children of Israel.

* *

As for His words: ﴿Rather, most of them do not believe﴾, He, the Mighty in remembrance, means: Rather, most of these – who, whenever they made a covenant with God and confirmed a pledge to Him, a party of them broke it – do not believe.

* *

For this there are two interpretations. One: that the statement indicates an increase and multiplication in the number of those who deny and break God's covenant, over the number of the party. The meaning of the statement would then be: Is it that whenever the Jews of the Children of Israel made a covenant with their Lord, a party of them broke that covenant? No – it is not a party of them that breaks it, but the one who breaks it and disbelieves in God is most of them, not the few among them. This is one of its two interpretations.

The other interpretation: that its meaning is: Is it that whenever the Jews made a covenant with their Lord, a party of them cast that covenant aside? No – it is not a party of them that casts it aside and breaks it, out of belief among them that this is not permissible for them, but most of them do not affirm God and His messengers, nor His promise and His threat. We have already shown earlier in this book the meaning of "īmān" (belief), that it is affirmation.[[See what preceded at 1:234–235, 271, 560, and this volume 2:143, 348.]]

**The discourse on the interpretation of His, exalted is He, saying:** ﴿And when there came to them a messenger from Allah confirming what was with them, a party of those who had been given the Scripture cast the Book of Allah behind their backs, as if they did not know.﴾ (101)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: By His saying, exalted is His praise, ﴿when there came to them﴾, He means the rabbis of the Jews and their scholars from the Children of Israel. ﴿A messenger﴾ means Muhammad (ﷺ). As follows:

1643 - Musa ibn Harun narrated to me, saying: Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His saying: ﴿And when there came to them a messenger﴾, he said: When Muhammad (ﷺ) came to them.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿confirming what was with them﴾, He means by it that Muhammad (ﷺ) confirms the Torah, and the Torah confirms him, in that he is a prophet of Allah sent to His creation.

* *

The interpretation (ta'wil, i.e., the explanation of the meaning) of His saying: ﴿And when there came to them a messenger from Allah confirming what was with them﴾ refers to what was with the Jews, namely the Torah. Allah, exalted is His praise, informs that when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came to the Jews from Allah, confirming what was in their hands of the Torah, that Muhammad (ﷺ) is a prophet of Allah, ﴿a party cast﴾ means: they denied him and rejected him after they had acknowledged him, out of envy toward him and insolence against him. His saying: ﴿of those who had been given the Scripture﴾ refers to the scholars of the Jews to whom Allah gave knowledge of the Torah and what is in it. By His saying: ﴿the Book of Allah﴾ He means the Torah.

His saying: ﴿behind their backs﴾ [[In the printed edition: "وقوله نبذوه وراء ظهورهم" ("and His saying: they cast it behind their backs"); I have deleted "نبذوه" because al-Tabari quoted the verse in full, and this wording is an intrusion into it.]] means they put it behind their backs. This is a metaphor: it is said of everyone who rejects a matter that was on his mind, "So-and-so has made this matter a thing behind his back and put it behind his back," meaning he turned away from it, shunned it, and departed from it. As follows:

1644 - Musa narrated to me, saying: Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿And when there came to them a messenger from Allah confirming what was with them, a party of those who had been given the Scripture cast the Book of Allah behind their backs﴾, he said: When Muhammad (ﷺ) came to them, they confronted him with the Torah and disputed with him by it, and the Torah and the Qur'an agreed, so they cast aside the Torah and took up the book of Asaf and the sorcery of Harut and Marut. [[In Tafsir Ibn Kathir 1:247 there is an addition, after his saying "and Marut": "so the Qur'an did not agree with it, and that is the saying of Allah." Asaf was the scribe of Solomon. He knew the Greatest Name, and he wrote everything by Solomon's command, and he would bury it beneath his throne. When Solomon died, the devils dug it up and wrote between every two lines sorcery and disbelief (Ibn Kathir 1:248).]] That is the meaning of Allah's saying: ﴿as if they did not know﴾.

* *

The meaning of His saying: ﴿as if they did not know﴾ is: as if these who cast aside the Book of Allah from among the rabbis of the Jews, who broke the covenant of Allah by abandoning acting upon what they had pledged to Allah to act upon, do not know what is in the Torah of the command to follow Muhammad (ﷺ) and to confirm him. This is an information from Allah, exalted is His praise, about them: that they denied the truth while having knowledge and recognition of it, and that they opposed the command of Allah while knowing its obligation upon them. As follows:

1645 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His saying: ﴿A party of those who had been given the Scripture cast﴾, he says: a party of those who had been given the Scripture broke ﴿the Book of Allah behind their backs, as if they did not know﴾: that is, the people were knowing, but they corrupted their knowledge, denied, disbelieved, and concealed.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 102 (part 1 of 8):

The explanation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿And they followed what the devils recited during the reign of Solomon﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: By His words, ﴿And they followed what the devils recited﴾, He means the group of rabbis and scholars of the Jews, whom God, may His praise be exalted, described as having cast the Book He revealed to Moses behind their backs, out of wilful ignorance and disbelief in what they knew, as if they did not know. He informs us that they rejected His Book, which they know was sent down from Him to His Prophet ﷺ, broke the covenant He had taken from them to act upon what is in it, and preferred the magic that the devils recited during the reign of Solomon son of David, and followed it. That is the loss and the manifest error.
* *
The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed about those meant by His words: ﴿And they followed what the devils recited during the reign of Solomon﴾. Some of them said: God meant by this the Jews who were living among the Emigrants' settlement of the Messenger of God ﷺ, because they disputed with the Messenger of God ﷺ using the Torah, and they found the Torah in agreement with the Qur'an, commanding the following of Muhammad ﷺ and affirming him, in the same way the Qur'an commands. So they argued with books that people had transcribed from the priests (kahana) in the time of Solomon.

Mention of those who said this:

1646 - Musa ibn Harun narrated to me, saying: 'Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His words: ﴿And they followed what the devils recited during the reign of Solomon﴾ - "during the reign of Solomon" - he said: The devils used to ascend to the heaven, and sit there in places for listening, and they would hear the words of the angels concerning what would happen on earth, of death or rain or a matter, [[In Tafsir Ibn Kathir 1: 249: "what happens on earth... or the unseen".]] and then they would come to the priests and inform them. The priests would tell the people, and they would find it as they had said. Until, when the priests had won the people's trust, they lied to them and added to it something else, and they added seventy words with every word. The people wrote that narration down in books, and it spread among the Children of Israel that the jinn know the unseen. So Solomon sent among the people and gathered those books, and placed them in a chest, then buried them beneath his throne. No devil could approach the throne without being burned, and he said: "I will not hear anyone claim that the devils know the unseen without striking off his neck!" When Solomon died, and the scholars who knew the affair of Solomon passed away, and after that successors came, a devil took the form of a man, and then came to a group of the Children of Israel and said: "Shall I show you a treasure that you will never consume?" [[La tu'kiluhu: i.e., you will never exhaust it. It is said: "So-and-so consumed his life" when he finished it.]] They said: "Yes." He said: "Dig beneath the throne." He went with them and showed them the place, and stood to one side. [[In the printed edition: "fa-qama", and the correct reading is what I have recorded from Tafsir Ibn Kathir.]] They said to him: "Come closer!" He said: "No, but I am here in your hands; if you do not find it, then kill me!" They dug and found those books. When they took them out the devil said: "Solomon only controlled humans, devils and birds by this magic." Then he flew off and departed. It spread among the people that Solomon was a sorcerer, and the Children of Israel took those books, and when Muhammad ﷺ came to them they disputed with him using them. That is the occasion of His saying: ﴿But Solomon did not disbelieve, rather the devils disbelieved, teaching people magic﴾. [[The report: 1646 - in Tafsir Ibn Kathir 1: 249.]]

1647 - I was told on the authority of Ammar ibn al-Hasan, who said: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi' regarding His words: ﴿And they followed what the devils recited during the reign of Solomon﴾; they said: The Jews once asked Muhammad ﷺ for a period about matters of the Torah, and he would not be asked about anything of that except that God revealed to him what they asked, and he would overcome them. [[Khasamani fa-khasamtuhu akhsimuhu: I defeated him with argument in my dispute.]] When they saw that, they said: "This man knows what has been sent down to us better than we do!" And they asked him about magic and disputed with him concerning it, and God, mighty and majestic, sent down: ﴿And they followed what the devils recited during the reign of Solomon, and Solomon did not disbelieve, but the devils disbelieved, teaching people magic﴾. The devils had devised a book, in which they wrote magic, soothsaying and whatever God willed of that, and buried it beneath the seat of Solomon's assembly - [[In Tafsir Ibn Kathir: "beneath the throne-seat of Solomon's assembly".]] and Solomon did not know the unseen. When Solomon departed the world, they extracted that magic and deceived people with it, saying: "This is knowledge that Solomon kept hidden and was jealous of people for it!" Then the Prophet ﷺ informed them of this narration, and they returned from him grieved, and God refuted their argument. [[The report: 1647 - in Tafsir Ibn Kathir 1: 249-250.]]
* *
1648 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words: ﴿And they followed what the devils recited during the reign of Solomon﴾: When the Messenger of God ﷺ came to them confirming what was with them, ﴿a party of those given the Book cast away﴾ the verse, he said: They followed magic, and they are the People of the Book. Then he recited until he reached: ﴿But the devils disbelieved, teaching people magic﴾.
* *
Others said: Rather, God meant by this the Jews who were in the time of Solomon.

Mention of those who said this:

1649 - al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, saying: Ibn Jurayj said: The devils recited magic to the Jews during the reign of Solomon, and the Jews followed it during his reign; that is, they followed magic during the reign of Solomon.
1650 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, saying: Ibn Ishaq narrated to me, saying: The devils, when they learned of the death of Solomon son of David, peace be upon him, devised kinds of magic: "Whoever wishes to reach such-and-such, let him do such-and-such." Until, when they had composed kinds of magic, [[In Tafsir Ibn Kathir: "they arranged the kinds of magic", which is better.]] they put it in a book and sealed it with a seal bearing the design of Solomon's seal, and they wrote on its cover: "This is what Asif ibn Barkhiya the Truthful wrote for King Solomon son of David from the treasures of the stores of knowledge," and then they buried it beneath his throne. Then remnants of the Children of Israel extracted it after that, when they did what they did, and when they found it they said: "Solomon son of David was only by this!" So they spread magic among the people and learned it and taught it, and no one is more associated with it than the Jews. When the Messenger of God ﷺ mentioned, in what was revealed to him from God, Solomon son of David, counting him among the messengers, the Jews in Medina said: "Do you not marvel at Muhammad! He claims that Solomon son of David was a prophet! By God, he was only a sorcerer!" So God sent down concerning their saying against Muhammad ﷺ: ﴿And they followed what the devils recited during the reign of Solomon, and Solomon did not disbelieve, but the devils disbelieved﴾. [[Up to here is what Ibn Kathir quoted in his tafsir from Abu Ja'far 1: 250. As for the rest of the report, he narrated it at 1: 247, beginning with the words: "al-Awfi said in his tafsir on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding His words, the Exalted: 'And they followed what the devils recited' - the verse - and that was when Solomon's rule departed..." and he cited the report in this same wording. I do not know whether there is a lacuna in the copies of al-Tabari, or whether this is part of al-Tabari's narration from Ibn Ishaq from the hadith of Ibn Abbas.]]
* *
He said: When Solomon's rule departed, a group of jinn and humans apostatised and followed their desires. [[Al-fi'am: a group of people, having no singular from its own form.]] When God returned his rule to Solomon, the people stood upright in the religion as they had been. And Solomon came upon their books and buried them beneath his throne, and Solomon died shortly after that. [[Hadthan al-shay' (with kasra then sukun): its beginning and onset, and nearness of time to it; it is in the accusative of time.]] Then the jinn and humans came upon the books after Solomon's death, and said: "This is a book from God sent down upon Solomon, which he hid from us!" They took hold of it and made it a religion. So God sent down: ﴿And when a messenger from God came to them confirming what was with them, a party of those given the Book cast the Book of God behind their backs as if they did not know, and followed what the devils recited﴾, and that is musical instruments and play, and everything that turns away from the remembrance of God.
* *
Abu Ja'far said: The correct view concerning the interpretation of His words: ﴿And they followed what the devils recited during the reign of Solomon﴾ is that this is a rebuke from God to the rabbis of the Jews who lived to see the Messenger of God ﷺ, and who denied his prophethood while knowing that he is a messenger sent by God, and a reproach from Him to them for rejecting His revelation and abandoning acting upon it, while it is in their hands, they know it and recognise that it is the Book of God, and for their following, and the following of their predecessors and forefathers, what the devils recited in the time of Solomon. The manner of attributing the actions of their forefathers to them has already been explained by us, so that suffices and there is no need to repeat it here. [[See what has passed in this part 2: 38-39.]]
* *
We have chosen this interpretation because those who followed what the devils recited, in the time of Solomon and after him until God sent His Prophet with the truth, and the matter of magic remained among the Jews. There is no indication in the verse that God intended by His words "and they followed" some of them to the exclusion of others, since it is permissible and eloquent in the speech of the Arabs to attribute what we have described, namely the following by the forefathers of those spoken of in His words "and they followed what the devils recited," to their descendants after them, and there is no transmitted report from the Messenger of God ﷺ specifying that, nor any proof indicating it. So the proper statement on this is to say: every follower of what the devils recited in the time of Solomon among the Jews falls within the meaning of the verse, in the manner we have stated.
* *
The explanation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿What the devils recited﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His words, may His praise be exalted, ﴿what the devils recited﴾, He means what they recited. So the meaning of the speech is: "And they followed what the devils recited."
* *
Scholars differed about the meaning of His words: ﴿recited﴾ (tatlu). Some of them said: By His words ﴿recited﴾ He means: they related, narrated, spoke it and informed of it, like a man's "recitation" (tilawa) of the Qur'an, which is its reading. Those who held this view interpreted it on the basis that it is the devils who taught people magic and transmitted it to them.

Mention of those who said this:

1651 - al-Muthanna ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from 'Amr, from Mujahid regarding God's words: ﴿And they followed what the devils recited during the reign of Solomon﴾, he said: The devils used to overhear revelation, and whatever word they heard they added two hundred like it to it. Solomon sent for what they had written of that and gathered it. When Solomon died, the devils found it and taught it to the people, and it is magic. [[The report: 1651 - in Tafsir Ibn Kathir 1: 250.]]
1652 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His words: ﴿And they followed what the devils recited during the reign of Solomon﴾, of soothsaying and magic. It was mentioned to us, God knows best, that the devils invented a book containing magic and a great matter, then they spread it among the people and taught it to them.
1653 - al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: 'Ata' said regarding His words: ﴿And they followed what the devils recited﴾: he said: "We consider it to mean what they related."
1654 - Salm ibn Junada al-Suwa'i narrated to me, saying: Abu Mu'awiya narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from al-Minhal, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The devils set out in the days in which Solomon was tested, and wrote books in which there was magic and disbelief, then they buried them beneath Solomon's throne, then they extracted them and read them to the people. [[The report: 1654 - in the printed edition it read "Salim ibn Junada", which is an error; see the note on report no. 48 in the first part. It is part of a report that will come later under no. 1660.]]
* *
Others said: The meaning of His words ﴿recited﴾ is: follows it, narrates it and acts upon it.

Mention of those who said this:

1655 - al-Hasan ibn 'Amr al-'Anqazi narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to me, from Asbat, from al-Suddi, from Abu Malik, from Ibn Abbas regarding ﴿tatlu﴾, he said: "It means follows." [[The report: 1655 - in the printed edition "al-'Abqari", which is an error; see the note on report no. 1625.]]
1656 - Nasr ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Azdi narrated to me, saying: Yahya ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, from Sufyan al-Thawri, from Mansur, from Abu Razin, the same. [[The report: 1656 - in the printed edition "Nasr ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Awdi", which is an error; see the note on report no. 423 in the first part.]]
* *
Abu Ja'far said: The correct statement on this is to say: God, mighty and majestic, informed about those of whom He informed that they followed what the devils recited in the time of Solomon, by their following what the devils had recited.
* *
In the speech of the Arabs, the saying "he recites such-and-such" has two meanings. One is following, as one says "I tala So-and-so" when I walk behind him and follow his tracks, as He, may His praise be exalted, said: ﴿There every soul will recite what it had sent before﴾ [Yunus: 30], [["There tatlu" is one of the two readings; the other is "there tabluu", which is the one in our mushafs today. Abu Ja'far said in his tafsir 11: 79: "They are two well-known readings, and both have been recited by imams of the readers."] meaning: will follow.

The other is reading and studying, as you say "So-and-so recites the Qur'an," meaning he reads it and studies it, as Hassan ibn Thabit said:

A prophet who sees what the people do not see around him... and recites the Book of God in every gathering. [[From his Diwan, p. 88, from verses Hassan said concerning the story of Umm Ma'bad, when the Messenger of God set out as an emigrant to Medina. The Diwan reads "in every masjid", and the reading of al-Tabari is better.]]

God, may His praise be exalted, has not informed us, by which of the two meanings the "recitation" of the devils, who recited what they recited of magic in the time of Solomon, was, with a report that closes the excuse. It is possible that the devils recited it by study, narration and practice, so they were following it in practice, and studying it by narration. Then the Jews followed their method in that, acted upon it, and narrated it. [[There should have been an explanation of His words "what they recite" in this place, which will come at: 418.]]
* *
The explanation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿during the reign of Solomon﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His words, may His praise be exalted, ﴿upon the reign of Solomon﴾, He means: during the reign of Solomon. That is because the Arabs place "fi" (in) in the position of "ala" (upon), and "ala" in the position of "fi".
[[See what has passed: 1: 299.]] Of this is God's words, may His praise be exalted: ﴿And I will crucify you upon the trunks of palm trees﴾ [Ta-Ha: 71], meaning: in the trunks of palm trees. And as they say: "I did such-and-such in the time of such-and-such, and upon the time of such-and-such," with one meaning. [[In the printed edition: "as he said: I did such-and-such..." which is only correct as a weak attribution.]] On the basis of what we have said about this, Ibn Jurayj and Ibn Ishaq used to say in its interpretation:

1657 - al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, saying: Ibn Jurayj: ﴿upon the reign of Solomon﴾, he says: during the reign of Solomon.
* *
1658 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Ishaq said regarding His words: ﴿upon the reign of Solomon﴾, that is: during the reign of Solomon.
* *
The explanation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿And Solomon did not disbelieve, but the devils disbelieved, teaching people magic﴾

Abu Ja'far said: If someone said to us: What is this statement, from His words: ﴿And they followed what the devils recited during the reign of Solomon﴾, [[His words "what is this statement" refer to the verse he is interpreting: "And Solomon did not disbelieve." They ask: what is the place of this statement within this statement, which is His words: "and they followed what the devils recited."]] and no report before us has been given from anyone attributing disbelief to Solomon, but rather it only mentions the following by those Jews whom the devils had recited to? So what is the reason for negating disbelief from Solomon, right after the report about those who followed what the devils had recited in practising magic and transmitting it among the Jews?

It was said: the reason for this is that those whom God, may His praise be exalted, described as following what the devils recited in the reign of Solomon, of sorcery and disbelief, were the Jews. They attributed to Solomon son of David what God, may His remembrance be exalted, had ascribed to the devils. They claimed that this was from his knowledge and transmission, and that he only subjugated, through sorcery, whomever he subjugated among humans, jinn, devils, and the rest of God's creation. By this, through their practice of what God had forbidden them of sorcery, they made themselves appear good [[In the printed edition it reads "li-anfusihim" (for themselves), but the correct reading is to drop this lam, as the context shows.]] to those who were ignorant of God's command and prohibition, and to those who had no knowledge of what God had revealed on this in the Torah. By attributing this to Solomon, they disassociated some people from Solomon, who was the prophet of God (ﷺ) [[The sentence structure is: "they disassociated themselves... from Solomon... some of them." Perhaps this "bashar" is "nafar," meaning a group. It says: another group disassociated itself from Solomon when he was ascribed to sorcery, and declared him a disbeliever.]] and they denied that he had been a messenger of God, and said: rather, he was a sorcerer. So God cleared Solomon son of David of sorcery and disbelief in the eyes of those among them who attributed sorcery and disbelief to him, for reasons they claimed against him, some of which we have mentioned and we will mention the rest of what has come to our attention. He also refuted the others who practised sorcery, adorning themselves before the ignorant with this practice, by claiming that Solomon used to practise it. God thus negated that Solomon, peace be upon him, had been a sorcerer or a disbeliever, and informed them that in their practice of sorcery they had only followed what the devils recited during the reign of Solomon, rather than what Solomon commanded them of obedience to God and following what He commanded them in His Book which He revealed to Moses, may God's blessings be upon him.

* *

Mention of the proofs for the correctness of what we have said, from reports and transmitted accounts:

* *

1659 – Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Ya'qub al-Qummi narrated to us, from Ja'far ibn Abi al-Mughira, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: Solomon used to seek out what was in the hands of the devils of sorcery, and he would take it and bury it beneath his throne in the chamber of his treasury. The devils were unable to reach it, so they approached humankind and said to them: Do you want the knowledge by which Solomon subjugated the devils and the winds and other things? They said: Yes. They said: It is in the chamber of his treasury, beneath his throne. So humans searched for it, extracted it, and practised it. The people of the Hijaz said: Solomon used to practise this, and this is sorcery! So God, may His praise be exalted, sent down through the tongue of His prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) the exoneration of Solomon. He said: ﴿And they followed what the devils recited over the kingdom of Solomon﴾ [Qur'an 2:102], the verse, and God sent down the exoneration of Solomon through the tongue of His prophet, peace be upon them both. [[Reported in Tafsir Ibn Kathir 1:250.]]

1660 – Abu al-Sa'ib al-Suwa'i narrated to me, saying: Abu Mu'awiya narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from al-Minhal, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: What befell Solomon son of David was on account of some people from the household of a woman called Jarada, who was among the most honoured of his wives in his sight. He said: Solomon's inclination was that the right should belong to the people of Jarada, and that he should judge in their favour, so he was punished when his inclination was not uniformly in their favour. He said: When Solomon son of David wished to enter the privy or to approach some of his wives, he would give his ring to Jarada. When God willed to test Solomon with what He tested him with, He gave Jarada his ring one day. A devil came in the form of Solomon and said to her: Give me my ring! So he took it and put it on. When he had put it on, the devils, the jinn and humans submitted to him. He said: Then Solomon came to her and said: Give me my ring! She said: You are lying, you are not Solomon! He said: So Solomon knew that it was a trial with which he had been tested. He said: The devils went and wrote books in those days, containing sorcery and disbelief, then buried them beneath Solomon's throne, then dug them up and read them to the people, saying: Solomon only overcame people by these books! He said: So the people disassociated from Solomon and declared him a disbeliever, until God sent Muhammad (ﷺ), and He, may His praise be exalted, revealed: ﴿And they followed what the devils recited over the kingdom of Solomon﴾, meaning what the devils had written of sorcery and disbelief, ﴿and Solomon did not disbelieve, but the devils disbelieved﴾ [Qur'an 2:102], so God, may He be mighty and majestic, sent down His excuse for him. [[Reported with the earlier report 1654 and the commentary on it.]]

1661 – Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la al-San'ani narrated to me, saying: al-Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman narrated to us, saying: I heard Imran ibn Hudayr, from Abu Mijlaz, who said: Solomon took a covenant from every beast, so that when a man was struck he would be asked by that covenant and released. The people saw the rhyming prose [saj'] and sorcery, and said: This is what Solomon used to practise! So God, may His praise be exalted, said: ﴿And Solomon did not disbelieve, but the devils disbelieved, teaching people sorcery﴾ [Qur'an 2:102]. [[Reported in Tafsir Ibn Kathir 1:251, where it reads "fa-zada al-nas" (so the people increased) instead of "fa-ra'a" (so he saw); the correct reading is what is in al-Tabari.]]

1662 – Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Husayn ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Imran ibn al-Harith, who said: While we were with Ibn Abbas, a man came to him, and Ibn Abbas said to him: Where have you come from? He said: From Iraq. He said: From which part? He said: From Kufa. He said: What is the news? He said: I left them talking that Ali was going out against them! He was alarmed and said: What are you saying? Woe to you! If we had known, we would not have married his wives nor divided his inheritance! But I will tell you something of it: the devils used to steal hearing from the heaven, and one of them would bring a word of truth that he had heard, and when he related it, it was true, but he would add seventy lies with it. He said: So the hearts of the people absorbed it. God made Solomon aware of it, so he buried it beneath his throne. When Solomon son of David died, a devil stood on the road and said: Shall I guide you to his hidden treasure, which has no equal? Beneath the throne! They dug it up, and they said: This is sorcery! Then the nations copied it, until even their remnants speak of it, the people of Iraq. So God sent down the excuse of Solomon: ﴿And they followed what the devils recited over the kingdom of Solomon, and Solomon did not disbelieve, but the devils disbelieved, teaching people sorcery﴾ [Qur'an 2:102]. [[Reported in Tafsir Ibn Kathir 1:248–249, with some variation in wording other than what is mentioned here.]]

1663 – Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, who said: It was mentioned to us, and God knows best, that the devils invented a book containing sorcery and a great matter, then spread it among the people and taught it to them. [[In the printed edition: "wa-a'lamuhum iyyahu" (and they informed them of it), but earlier in no. 1652 it reads "wa-allamuhum" (and they taught them), and it is so given here.]] When Solomon, the prophet of God (ﷺ), heard of this, he sought out those books, brought them, and buried them beneath his throne, [[In the printed edition: "fa-tatabba'a tilka al-kutub" with an added fa', which has no place.]] out of dislike that people should learn them. When God took his prophet Solomon, the devils set out and extracted them from the place where they had been, and taught them to the people, informing them that this was knowledge that Solomon had kept hidden and reserved for himself. So God excused His prophet Solomon and cleared him of that, and He, may His praise be exalted, said: ﴿And Solomon did not disbelieve, but the devils disbelieved﴾ [Qur'an 2:102].

1664 – al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada, who said: The devils wrote books containing sorcery and polytheism, then those books were buried beneath Solomon's throne. When Solomon died, the people brought out those books and said: This is knowledge that Solomon kept hidden! So God, may He be mighty and majestic, said: ﴿And they followed what the devils recited over the kingdom of Solomon, and Solomon did not disbelieve, but the devils disbelieved, teaching people sorcery﴾ [Qur'an 2:102].

1665 – al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿And they followed what the devils recited over the kingdom of Solomon﴾ [Qur'an 2:102]: He said: The devils used to listen to revelation from the heaven, and whatever word they heard, they would add to it a similar one. Solomon took what they had written of that and buried it beneath his throne, and when he died the devils found it and taught it to the people. [[In the printed edition, "al-Husayn qal" (al-Husayn said) is omitted from the chain, a chain that recurs in al-Tabari; the nearest instance is no. 1657, and it comes in the following.]]

1666 – al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Abu Bakr, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, who said: When Solomon was deprived of his kingdom, the devils were writing sorcery during Solomon's absence. They wrote: "Whoever wishes to do such-and-such, let him face the sun and say such-and-such, and whoever wishes to do such-and-such, let him turn his back to the sun and say such-and-such." They wrote it and titled it: "This is what Asaf ibn Barakhya wrote for King Solomon son of David from the treasures of the hoards of knowledge," then they buried it beneath his throne. When Solomon died, Iblis stood up preaching and said: O people, Solomon was not a prophet, but only a sorcerer, so search for his sorcery among his belongings and houses. Then he pointed them to the place where it was buried. They said: By God, Solomon was indeed a sorcerer! This is his sorcery! By this we were made to worship, and by this we were overcome! The believers said: Rather, he was a believing prophet! When God sent the prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), he began to mention the prophets, until he mentioned David and Solomon. The Jews said: Look at Muhammad! He mixes truth with falsehood! He mentions Solomon among the prophets, but he was only a sorcerer who rode the wind!
