So God sent down the excuse of Solomon: ﴿And they followed what the devils recited over the kingdom of Solomon﴾, the verse. [[Reported in Tafsir Ibn Kathir 1:251.]]

1667 – Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, saying: Ibn Ishaq narrated to me: ﴿And Solomon did not disbelieve, but the devils disbelieved, teaching people sorcery﴾ [Qur'an 2:102]. This is because the Messenger of God (ﷺ), as has reached me, when he mentioned Solomon son of David among the messengers, one of the Jewish rabbis said: Do you not marvel at Muhammad! He claims that the son of David was a prophet! By God, he was nothing but a sorcerer! So God sent down, concerning their statement: ﴿And Solomon did not disbelieve, but the devils disbelieved﴾ [Qur'an 2:102], that is, by their following sorcery and practising it, ﴿and what was sent down upon the two angels at Babylon, Harut and Marut﴾ [Qur'an 2:102]. [[Reported in Sirat Ibn Hisham 2:192–193.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: Since the matter regarding this is as we have described, and the interpretation of His saying: ﴿And they followed what the devils recited over the kingdom of Solomon, and Solomon did not disbelieve, but the devils disbelieved﴾ is what we have mentioned, then it is clear that the sentence contains an omitted element, which was left out because what was mentioned is sufficient for it. The meaning of the sentence is: and they followed what the devils recited of sorcery over the kingdom of Solomon, so they attributed it to Solomon, and Solomon did not disbelieve so as to practise sorcery; but the devils disbelieved, teaching people sorcery. [[In the printed edition it reads "fa-tabayyana" (so it became clear), but what is recorded is closer to al-Tabari's phrasing.]] Qatada used to interpret His saying: ﴿And Solomon did not disbelieve, but the devils disbelieved﴾ in the way we have said.

1668 – Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada regarding His saying: ﴿And Solomon did not disbelieve, but the devils disbelieved﴾, he said: It was not by his counsel nor with his consent, but a thing the devils invented without him.

* *

We have already shown earlier the disagreement of those who differ over the meaning of "tatlu" [recite/follow], and the position of those who understood it as "talat" [recited, past tense], since what precedes it is a past-tense report, namely His saying: ﴿And they followed﴾, and the position of those who directed it otherwise. We have demonstrated there and in its parallel the correct view, and that suffices so that it need not be repeated here. [[Referring to what precedes: 2:91, pp. 350–352.]]

* *

As for the meaning of His saying: ﴿mā tatlū﴾ [what they recited], it means: that which they recite, namely sorcery. [[This paragraph, the one before it, and the following report no. 1669 would have been better placed at the end of the explanation of His saying "mā tatlū al-shayāṭīn" earlier, at no. 411.]]

1669 – Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq: ﴿And they followed what the devils recited over the kingdom of Solomon﴾, that is, sorcery. [[Reported in Sirat Ibn Hisham 2:192.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: Perhaps someone will say: Was sorcery only in the days of Solomon?

It is said to him: Indeed not; it existed before that. God has told us of the sorcerers of Pharaoh what He has told us, and they existed before Solomon, and He told us that the people of Noah said to Noah that he was a sorcerer.

[If] he says: Then how did He report about the Jews that they followed what the devils recited in the time of Solomon? It is said: Because they attributed it to Solomon, as we have already explained. God, may His remembrance be exalted, intended to exonerate Solomon of what they had fabricated and attributed to him, from what they had found, either in his treasuries or beneath his throne, as the reports we have mentioned state. So the report confined what the Jews had followed to what the devils recited in the days of Solomon, rather than anything else, for this reason, even though the devils had been reciting sorcery and disbelief before that.

* *

On the interpretation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿And what was sent down upon the two angels at Babylon, Harut and Marut﴾

Abu Ja'far said: The scholars have differed on the interpretation of the "mā" [what/that] in His saying: ﴿And what was sent down upon the two angels﴾. Some of them said: its meaning is negation, and it has the sense of "lam" [not].

Those who said this:

1670 – Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿And what was sent down upon the two angels at Babylon, Harut and Marut﴾, he said: God did not send down sorcery.

1671 – Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to me, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas: ﴿And what was sent down upon the two angels﴾, he said: God did not send down sorcery upon them both.

* *

So the interpretation of the verse, according to this meaning which we have mentioned from Ibn Abbas and al-Rabi', in which they direct the meaning of His saying "and what was sent down upon the two angels" to "and was not sent down upon the two angels" is: and they followed what the devils recited over the kingdom of Solomon of sorcery, and Solomon did not disbelieve, nor did God send down sorcery upon the two angels, but the devils disbelieved, teaching people sorcery at Babylon: Harut and Marut. In this case, His saying "at Babylon, Harut and Marut" comes from what is postponed in meaning yet is taken as anterior.

* *

If someone says to us: And how is the anterior order of that to be understood?

It is said: Its anterior order is that one would say: "And they followed what the devils recited over the kingdom of Solomon [of sorcery], and what God did not send down [sorcery] upon the two angels, but the devils disbelieved, teaching people sorcery at Babylon, Harut and Marut." In that case, "the two angels" means Gabriel and Michael, because the Jewish sorcerers, as is reported, claimed that God sent down sorcery through the tongue of Gabriel and Michael to Solomon son of David. God refuted them in this, and informed His prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) that Gabriel and Michael had never descended with sorcery, and He exonerated Solomon of the sorcery they attributed to him. He informed them that sorcery is the work of the devils, and that they teach people [that] at Babylon, and that the two who teach them are two men: one named Harut and the other named Marut. [[In the printed edition and in Ibn Kathir: "wa-anna alladhina yu'allimunahum" (and that those who teach them), and what is recorded is correct.]] So "Harut and Marut", on this interpretation, is an apposition ["tarjama", which in the Kufan usage is "badal" (substitution)] for "the people" and a refutation of them. [[Ibn Kathir 1:252 has these additions in parentheses, and it quotes al-Tabari's words verbatim.]]

* *

Others said: Rather, the "mā" in His saying: ﴿And what was sent down upon the two angels﴾ means "that which" [alladhī].

Those who said this:

1672 – al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar said: Qatada and al-Zuhri said, from Abd Allah: ﴿And what was sent down upon the two angels at Babylon, Harut and Marut﴾. They were two angels from among the angels, who were sent down to judge between people. That was because the angels mocked the judgments of the sons of Adam. He said: A woman came to them for judgment, and they were unjust to her [hafa], then they went to ascend, but they were prevented from doing so, and they were given the choice between the punishment of this world and the punishment of the Hereafter, and they chose the punishment of this world. Ma'mar said, Qatada said: They used to teach people sorcery, and it was stipulated of them that they should not teach anyone until they said: "We are only a trial, so do not disbelieve."

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 102 (part 3 of 8):**

1673. Musa told me, saying: Amr told us, saying: Asbat told us, from al-Suddi, regarding His words, ﴿And what was sent down to the two angels at Babylon, Harut and Marut﴾: "This is another kind of sorcery, with which they also disputed him. He means: they disputed him with what was sent down to the two angels, and that the speech of the angels among themselves, if mankind learns it and makes and practises it, is sorcery." [[The report: 1673 is part of the preceding report, 1646, and the pronoun in his words "and they also disputed him with it" refers to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and then the Jews, as becomes clear by consulting the report there.]]

1674. Bishr ibn Mu'adh told us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatadah, regarding his words: ﴿They teach people sorcery and what was sent down at Babylon to Harut and Marut﴾. "So sorcery is of two kinds: sorcery which the devils teach, and sorcery which Harut and Marut teach."

1675. Al-Muthanna told me, saying: Abdullah ibn Salih told us, saying: Mu'awiyah ibn Salih told me, from Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿And what was sent down to the two angels at Babylon, Harut and Marut﴾, he said: "The separation between a man and his wife."

1676. Yunus told me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding ﴿But the devils disbelieved, teaching people sorcery and what was sent down to the two angels﴾, and he recited until he reached ﴿So do not disbelieve﴾: "The devils and the two angels teach people sorcery."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The meaning of the verse according to the interpretation of this view that we have mentioned from those we have mentioned is: The Jews followed what the devils recited in the reign of Solomon, and what was sent down to the two angels at Babylon, Harut and Marut. They are two angels of Allah's angels, and we will mention what has been transmitted in reports about them, if Allah the Exalted wills.

* *

Abu Ja'far [[In the printed edition here it reads: "And they said: If a sayer says to us..." The pronoun in "they said" does not refer to anyone mentioned before. It seems the copyist found it too grave that the following reply should be part of Abu Ja'far's speech, so he deleted what was in his tafsir (commentary) of the words "Abu Ja'far said" and inserted "and they said" in its place, then he further worsened these following paragraphs with the word "and they said", as we will clarify in their places in the annotation. This is a style Abu Ja'far never used in his entire tafsir.

What some copyists found objectionable, as we think, will come shortly after, on pages 423 to 426, more clearly than what he said here. Ibn Kathir considered Abu Ja'far's view an odd course, and he said in his tafsir 1:253, mentioning what Abu Ja'far mentioned from the one who said "ma" means "lam": "Then Ibn Jarir began to refute this view, and that "ma" means "alladhi" (who/which), and he extended the discussion on this, and claimed that Harut and Marut were two angels whom Allah sent down to the earth, and permitted them to teach sorcery as a trial and test for His servants, after He had made clear to His servants that this is something forbidden by the tongues of the messengers, and he claimed that Harut and Marut were obedient in teaching this, because they carried out what they were commanded. This course he took is very odd."

I do not object to what Abu Ja'far said, as Ibn Kathir objected to it. If you were fair and followed Abu Ja'far's words, you would see in them a clear proof of the correctness of his position, and you would see subtlety and precision in handling meanings and arranging words, which you can hardly find except in this tafsir of great stature.]] If a sayer says to us: Is it permissible for Allah to send down sorcery, or is it permissible for His angels to teach it to people?

We say to him: Allah the Mighty and Majestic has sent down all good and evil, and has made all of it clear to His servants. He revealed it to His messengers, and commanded them to teach His creation and to make known to them what is lawful for them and what is forbidden to them. This is like fornication, theft, and all the sins which He made known to them, and forbade them from committing. So sorcery is one of those sins which He informed them of, and forbade them from practising.

[[In the printed edition here it reads: "(They said) there is no sin in knowledge..." See what preceded.]] There is no sin in knowing sorcery, just as there is no sin in knowing the making of wine, the carving of idols, the lutes, and the games. The sin is only in practising it and carrying it out. Likewise, there is no sin in knowing sorcery; the sin is only in practising it, and in harming with it someone whom it is not lawful to harm.

[[In the printed edition here it reads: "(They said) so there is no sin in Allah's sending down..." See what preceded.]] Therefore there is no sin in Allah's sending it down to the two angels, nor in the two angels teaching it to those among mankind who learn it, since their teaching of those who learn it is by Allah's permission to them to teach it, after they inform the one learning it that they are a trial, and forbid him from sorcery, practising it, and disbelief. The sin is only upon the one who learns it from them and practises it, since Allah the Exalted has forbidden him from learning it and practising it. [[In the printed edition here it reads: "(They said) And if Allah had permitted..." See what preceded.]] And if Allah had permitted the children of Adam to learn that, learning it would not have been sinful for them, just as the two angels would not have been sinful for knowing it. [[Abu Ja'far used "harij" (sinful), on the pattern of "fariḥ" (joyful), meaning "sinful". The lexicographers reject this. The sinful person is only called "ḥārij" as a noun of relation, because "ḥaraj" in the sense of sin has no verb form. Perhaps the copyist erred in writing "ḥarajan... wa ḥarajayn" in place of "ḥārijan... wa ḥārijayn", meaning sinful and sinners. But I left it here as it is, for fear that it might be an error of Abu Ja'far's ijtihad (independent judgment), or a correctness known to him which has not reached us.]] Since their knowledge of that was from Allah's sending it down to them. [[The explanation of this statement will come more fully and completely than this, on pages 423 to 426.]]

* *

Others said: The meaning of "ma" is the meaning of "alladhi" (who/which), and it is coordinated with the first "ma". However, the first refers to sorcery, and the second refers to the separation between a man and his wife.

So the interpretation of the verse according to this view is: They followed the sorcery which the devils recited in the reign of Solomon, and the separation between a man and his wife, which was sent down to the two angels at Babylon, Harut and Marut.

Mention of those who said that:

1677. Al-Muthanna told me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah told us, saying: Shibl told us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿And what was sent down to the two angels at Babylon, Harut and Marut﴾: "And they were teaching what they separate a man and his wife with." That is the saying of Allah the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿And Solomon did not disbelieve, but the devils disbelieved﴾. He used to say: As for sorcery, the devils teach it; and as for what the two angels teach, it is the separation between a man and his wife, as Allah the Exalted said.

* *

Others said: It is permissible that "ma" means "alladhi" (who/which), and it is permissible that "ma" means "lam" (not).

Mention of those who said that:

1678. Yunus ibn Abd al-A'la told me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Al-Layth ibn Sa'd told me, from Yahya ibn Sa'id, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, when a man asked him about Allah's words: ﴿They teach people sorcery and what was sent down to the two angels at Babylon, Harut and Marut﴾, and the man said: "Do they teach people what was sent down to them, or do they teach people what was not sent down to them?" Al-Qasim said: "I do not mind which of them it was."

1679. Yunus ibn Abd al-A'la told me, saying: Anas ibn Iyad told us, from some of his companions, that al-Qasim ibn Muhammad was asked about the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And what was sent down to the two angels﴾, and it was said to him: "Was it sent down or not?" He said: "I do not mind which of those it was, except that I believe in it." [[The report: 1679. Yunus ibn Abd al-A'la al-Sadafi al-Misri: a well-known imam, from whom al-Tabari narrates a great deal, and from whom Abu Hatim and Abu Zur'ah narrated. Ibn Abi Hatim (4/2/243) said: "I wrote from him, and I stayed with him for seven months." And he said: "I heard my father rate Yunus ibn Abd al-A'la as trustworthy and speak highly of him." He was born in 170 and died in 264.

As for his teacher here, he is "Anas ibn Iyad ibn Dumrah": he is trustworthy, and the authors of the six books narrated from him. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir of al-Bukhari (1/2/34), and Ibn Abi Hatim (1/1/289).

In the printed edition, "Bishr" was written in place of "Anas". This is a clear distortion. The correct form is in Ibn Kathir 1:253, quoting this place in al-Tabari. We have not found anyone among the narrators named "Bishr ibn Iyad" at all.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct view in this matter, in my opinion, is the view of those who interpret "ma" in His words ﴿And what was sent down to the two angels﴾ as meaning "alladhi" (who/which), rather than the "ma" which is in the sense of negation. I chose that because if "ma" is interpreted as negation, it negates that the two angels were sent down to them. [[In the printed edition: "then it negates..." with an added fa' which has no benefit.]] And the two names that follow them, that is "Harut and Marut", are either a substitution for them and an explanation of them [[See the meaning of "tarjamah" (explanatory rendering) above: 420, note 2.]], or a substitution for "people" in His words ﴿they teach people sorcery﴾, and an explanation of them. [[In the printed edition: "they teach people sorcery", which is an error. See what preceded: 420.]] If they are made a substitution for "the two angels" and an explanation of them, the meaning of His words is nullified: ﴿And they do not teach anyone until they say, "We are only a trial, so do not disbelieve." Then they learn from them what they separate a man and his wife with﴾. For if they do not know what a man and his wife are separated with, then what is it that the one who separates a man and his wife learns from them? [[In the printed edition: "what separates", and the correct reading is what I have recorded.]] Furthermore, if the "ma" in His words ﴿And what was sent down to the two angels﴾ is in the sense of negation, coordinated with His words ﴿And Solomon did not disbelieve﴾, then Allah the Mighty and Majestic by His words ﴿And Solomon did not disbelieve﴾ has negated from Solomon that sorcery was of his practice, or of his knowledge, or his teaching. If what He negated from the two angels is similar to what He negated from Solomon, and Harut and Marut are the two angels, then what is it that is learned from them to separate a man and his wife? And about whom is the report which He informed of with His words ﴿And they do not teach anyone until they say, "We are only a trial, so do not disbelieve"﴾? The error of this view is clear and evident.

And if the words "Harut and Marut" are an explanation of "people" in His words ﴿But the devils disbelieved, teaching people sorcery﴾, then it must be that the devils are the ones who taught Harut and Marut sorcery, and the sorcerers learned sorcery from Harut and Marut through the devils' teaching of them. If that is so, then "Harut and Marut", according to the speaker of this statement, must be one of two things:

Either they are two angels. If they are angels in his view, then he has attributed to them disbelief in Allah and disobedience to Him, by claiming that they learn sorcery from the devils and teach it to people, and persist in that and remain upon it, which is greater than what is mentioned of them, that they committed the disobedience for which they deserved punishment. And in the report of Allah the Mighty and Majestic about them, that they do not teach anyone who learns from them until they say ﴿We are only a trial, so do not disbelieve﴾, there is what suffices instead of much argument to show the error of this view.

Or they are two men from the children of Adam. If that is so, then it must be that with their destruction sorcery, its knowledge, and its practice would have been lifted from the children of Adam. [[He says in its context: "sorcery, its knowledge, and its practice would have been lifted from the children of Adam."]] For if the knowledge of it were taken from them and learned from them, then it is necessary that with their destruction and non-existence, the way to reach the meaning which could only be reached through them would be cut off.

And the existence of sorcery in every age and time is the clearest proof against this view. The one who claims this view may claim that they are two men from the children of Adam who have never ceased from the earth since it was created, and will not cease after sorcery was found among people, and that is a claim whose falsehood is not hidden. [[The word "batala" means to be void, with the verbal nouns "buṭūl" and "buṭlān". This is clearly void and false.]]

* *

Since these aspects which we have shown to be corrupt are corrupt, it is clear that the meaning of "ma" in His words ﴿And what was sent down to the two angels﴾ is in the sense of "alladhi" (who/which), and that "Harut and Marut" are a rendering of the two angels, and for that reason the endings of their names are vowelled with a fatha, because they are in the genitive position as a repetition of "the two angels". But since they do not take the genitive case, the endings of their names are vowelled with a fatha. [[Here the Arabic words "Harut and Marut" are kept in the Arabic form; the explanation is that they are in the genitive position as a substitution for "the two angels", and since they are not declinable (ghayr munsarif), they take a fatha ending.]]

* *

If what we have said is confusing to one who is dull-minded, and he says: How is it permissible for the angels of Allah to teach people the separation between a man and his wife? Or how is it permissible to attribute to Allah the Blessed and Exalted the sending down of that to the angels?

It is said to him: Allah the Mighty and Majestic made known to His servants everything He commanded them to do and everything He forbade them from, and then He commanded and forbade them after they had knowledge of what they were commanded and forbidden. If the matter were otherwise, the command and prohibition would have no understood meaning. Sorcery is among what He has forbidden His servants from the children of Adam. It is not objectionable that He, the Mighty and Majestic, taught it to the two angels whom He named in His revelation, and made them a trial for His servants from the children of Adam, as He informed about them that they say to whoever learns that from them: ﴿We are only a trial, so do not disbelieve﴾, so that by them He tests His servants whom He forbade from separating a man and his wife, and from sorcery. So the believer is purified by leaving learning from them, and the disbeliever is disgraced by learning sorcery and disbelief from them. And the two angels, in their teaching of those who learn it from them, are obedient to Allah, since they teach by Allah's permission to them to teach it to those who know it. [[The explanation: the two angels teach by Allah's permission, which is the teaching to those who learn it.]] And a group of the friends of Allah were worshipped besides Allah, and that did not harm them, since it was not by their command to them, but some of them were worshipped while the one worshipped forbade it. [[This is the argument of a man who perceives subtle meanings, and does not overlook the points of omission in the speech of one who speaks without controlling what his speech requires. Ibn Kathir made light of him, because he did not control what this imam, firmly grounded in his intellect and understanding, controlled.]] Likewise, the two angels are not harmed by the sorcery of one who learned it from them, after they forbade him from it and admonished him by saying ﴿We are only a trial, so do not disbelieve﴾, since they had discharged what they were commanded by saying that, as:

1680. Muhammad ibn Bashshar told us, saying: Yahya ibn Sa'id told us, from Awf, from al-Hasan, regarding His words: ﴿And what was sent down to the two angels at Babylon, Harut and Marut﴾ to His words ﴿So do not disbelieve﴾: "He took the covenant from them concerning that."

* *

Mention of some reports which explain the two angels, and of those who said that Harut and Marut are the two angels whom Allah the Mighty and Majestic mentioned in His words ﴿at Babylon﴾:

* *

1681. Muhammad ibn Bashshar told us, saying: Mu'adh ibn Hisham told us, saying: My father told me, from Qatadah, who said: Abu Shu'bah al-Adawi told us at the funeral of Yunus ibn Jubayr, Abu Ghallab, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "Allah opened the heaven for His angels so they could look at the deeds of the children of Adam. When they saw them committing sins, they said: 'O Lord, these are the children of Adam whom You created with Your hand, and whom You made Your angels prostrate to, and whom You taught the names of everything. They commit sins!' He said: 'Indeed, if you were in their place you would do the same as their deeds.' They said: 'Glory be to You! It would not have been right for us!' He said: 'Then command them to choose someone who will descend to the earth.' He said: 'So they chose Harut and Marut. So descend to the earth, and everything in it is made lawful for you, except that you must not associate anything with Allah, nor steal, nor commit fornication, nor drink wine, nor kill a soul which Allah has forbidden except by right.' He said: 'They had not continued until a woman appeared to them, to whom half of beauty had been allotted, called Bidhakht. When they saw her, they wanted to commit fornication with her. She said: "No, unless you associate with Allah, drink wine, kill a soul, and prostrate to this idol!" They said: "We would never associate anything with Allah!" One of them said to the other: "Go back to her." She said: "No, unless you drink wine." So they drank until they were intoxicated, and a beggar came in upon them and they killed him. When they fell into what evil they fell into, Allah opened the heaven for His angels, and they said: "Glory be to You! You knew best!"' He said: 'Allah revealed to Solomon son of David that he should give them the choice between the punishment of this world and the punishment of the Hereafter. They chose the punishment of this world, so they were bound from their ankles up to their necks like the necks of Bakhti camels, and they were placed at Babylon.'" [[The report: Abu Shu'bah al-Adawi, the one narrated here from Ibn Abbas: I do not know who he is, and I have found no mention of him in any of the references. In my view the most probable is that his name is a distortion of something I do not know.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 102 (part 4 of 8):

1682. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: al-Hajjaj ibn al-Minhal narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, from Ali ibn Zayd, from Abu Uthman al-Nahdi, from Ibn Mas'ud and Ibn Abbas, that they both said: When the children of Adam increased and disobeyed, the angels, the earth, the heavens and the mountains invoked curses upon them, saying: "Our Lord, will You not destroy them?" [[In the Tafsir of Ibn Kathir 1: 256 and al-Durr al-Manthur 1: 99: "Our Lord, do not give them respite" (lā tumhilhum), and this seems to be the correct reading, although the first is sound in meaning.]] So God revealed to the angels: "If I were to send down desire and Satan from your hearts and you were to descend, you would also commit [sins]!" [[This phrase is sound in meaning, but it appears in the Tafsir of Ibn Kathir as: "I removed desire and Satan from your hearts, and I placed desire and Satan in their hearts, and if you were to descend, you would also [sin]." It appears in al-Durr al-Manthur as: "I removed desire and Satan from your hearts, and if you were to descend, you would also [sin]," in abridged form.]] He said: So they said to themselves that if they were tested, they would hold fast. So God revealed to them: "Choose two angels from among your best." So they chose Harut and Marut, and they were sent down to the earth, and the Venus (al-Zuhara) was sent down to them in the form of a woman from the people of Persia, and the people of Persia called her "Baydakht." He said: So they fell into sin. The angels used to seek forgiveness for those who believed, [[In the printed edition: "wa-kānat al-malā'ika" with a wāw, but the correct reading is from Ibn Kathir and al-Durr al-Manthur.]] saying: ﴿Our Lord, You have encompassed everything in mercy and knowledge, so forgive those who repent﴾. When they fell into sin, they sought forgiveness for those on the earth. Indeed God is the Forgiving, the Merciful. They were given the choice between the punishment of this world and the punishment of the Hereafter, and they chose the punishment of this world. [[The report 1682: al-Hajjaj ibn al-Minhal al-Anmati: trustworthy and excellent, and the group (al-jama'a) narrated from him. As for his teacher "Hammad": in our view the more likely is "Hammad ibn Salama," although in al-Tahdhib it is stated that he narrated from "the two Hammads," meaning Hammad ibn Zayd and Hammad ibn Salama. However, al-Bukhari in his biography in al-Kabir 1/2/376 mentioned only "Hammad ibn Salama," and Ibn Abi Hatim did likewise, 1/2/167. Their practice indicates that he was known for narrating from him more often. In the printed edition here "Hajjaj" appears instead of "Hammad," and the correction is from Ibn Kathir 1: 256, which transmitted this report from al-Tabari.]]

1683. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: al-Hajjaj narrated to me, saying: Hammad narrated to us, from Khalid al-Hadhdha', from Umayr ibn Sa'id, who said: I heard Ali say: Al-Zuhara was a beautiful woman from the people of Persia, and she brought a dispute before the two angels Harut and Marut, and they solicited her, but she refused unless they taught her the word which, when spoken, would cause her to ascend to the heavens. So they taught her, and she spoke it, and she ascended to the heavens, and was transformed into a star. [[The report 1683: Khalid al-Hadhdha': he is Khalid ibn Mihran, trustworthy and a prolific transmitter. He is mentioned in al-Tahdhib, in al-Bukhari's al-Kabir 2/2/159, and in Ibn Abi Hatim 1/2/352-353. Umayr ibn Sa'id al-Nakha'i: a trustworthy Successor (tabi'i). He is mentioned in al-Tahdhib and in Ibn Abi Hatim 3/1/376. In the printed edition here "Amr" appears instead of "Umayr," which is an error; the correct form is in Ibn Kathir 1: 255 on the authority of this report of al-Tabari. The report was also transmitted by al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak 2: 265-266, at length, through Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, "from Umayr ibn Sa'id al-Nakha'i who said: I heard Ali..." and he cited it in full.]]

1684. Muhammad ibn Bashshar and Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, both saying: Mu'ammal ibn Isma'il narrated to us, and al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, all from al-Thawri, from Musa ibn Uqba, from Salim, from Ibn Umar, from Ka'b, who said: The angels mentioned the deeds of the children of Adam and the sins they commit, so it was said to them: "Choose two from among you," and al-Hasan ibn Yahya said in his narration: "Choose two angels." So they chose Harut and Marut, and it was said to them: "I send messengers to the children of Adam, and there is no messenger between Me and you. Descend; do not associate anything with Me, do not commit adultery, and do not drink wine." Ka'b said: By God, they had not finished that day, the day on which they were sent down to the earth, before they had completed all that they had been forbidden, and al-Hasan ibn Yahya said in his narration: They did not complete their day on which they were sent down until they had done what God had forbidden them. [[The report 1684: al-Bukhari transmitted it by two isnads: through Mu'ammal ibn Isma'il, and through Abd al-Razzaq, both from al-Thawri. Musa ibn Uqba ibn Abi Ayyash al-Asadi: he is the author of the Maghazi (military campaigns), and he was trustworthy and firm. Malik used to say: "Hold to the Maghazi of Musa ibn Uqba, for he is trustworthy." He is mentioned in al-Bukhari's al-Kabir 4/1/292 and in Ibn Abi Hatim 4/1/154-155.
What we have adopted is the correct reading; in the printed edition it appeared as "Muhammad ibn Uqba" instead of "Musa." "Muhammad ibn Uqba" is the brother of Musa ibn Uqba. He too is trustworthy, mentioned in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir 1/1/198-199, and Ibn Abi Hatim 4/1/35.
It would have been possible for the printed reading to be correct, since Sufyan al-Thawri narrates from Muhammad ibn Uqba as he narrates from his brother Musa, were it not for the indications and evidence by which we have definitively judged that to be an error:
First: Muhammad ibn Uqba is not mentioned in his biography as narrating from Salim ibn Abd Allah ibn Umar.
Second: Ibn Kathir transmitted this report from the Tafsir of Abd al-Razzaq, from al-Thawri, from Musa ibn Uqba, 1: 255, and then mentioned that al-Tabari transmitted it through Abd al-Razzaq.
Third: The report is established in the Tafsir of Abd al-Razzaq, in a photographic copy in my possession, from a manuscript of the Dar al-Kutub al-Misriyya (Egyptian National Library), copied in the year 724 AH. In it is "from Musa ibn Uqba."
Thus the two books agree: the book from which al-Tabari transmitted, and the book which transmitted from al-Tabari.
Fourth: Ibn Kathir also said: "Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted it, from Ahmad ibn Isam, from Mu'ammal, from Sufyan al-Thawri, with the same [chain]."
Al-Tabari here transmitted it, as we have mentioned, from Mu'ammal ibn Isma'il, from al-Thawri. Thus his transmission agrees with the transmission of Ibn Abi Hatim.
There is no firmer or more certain proof beyond this.]]

1685. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Mu'alla ibn Asad narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Aziz ibn al-Mukhtar narrated to us, from Musa ibn Uqba, who said: Salim narrated to me that he heard Abd Allah narrate from Ka'b al-Ahbar that he said: The angels disapproved of the deeds of the children of Adam and the sins they commit on the earth, so God said to them: "If you were in their place, you would commit the sins that they commit. So choose from among you two angels." They chose Harut and Marut. God said to them: "I send My messengers to people, and there is no messenger between Me and you two. Descend to the earth, do not associate anything with Me, and do not commit adultery." Ka'b said: By Him in whose hand is the soul of Ka'b, they had not completed their day on which they descended until they committed what God had forbidden them. [[The report 1685: It is a repetition of the report before it, through the narration of Abd al-Aziz ibn al-Mukhtar, from Musa ibn Uqba. Abd al-Aziz ibn al-Mukhtar al-Dabbagh: trustworthy, and the group narrated from him. He is mentioned in al-Tahdhib and Ibn Abi Hatim 2/393-394.]]

1686. Musa ibn Harun narrated to me, saying: Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: Regarding the matter of Harut and Marut, they reproached the people of the earth for their judgments, so it was said to them: "I have given the children of Adam ten desires, and by them they disobey Me." Harut and Marut said: "Our Lord, if You had given us those desires and then we had descended, we would have judged with justice." So He said to them: "Descend, for I have given you those ten desires; judge between the people." So they descended to Babil Dunbawand, and they used to judge, until when evening came they ascended, and when morning came they descended. They continued like that until a woman came to them, disputing with her husband, and her beauty pleased them. Her name in Arabic was "al-Zuhara," and in Nabataean "Baydakht," and her name in Persian was "Anahid." One of them said to his companion: "She truly pleases me!" The other said: "I wanted to mention her to you, but I was too shy before you!" He said: The other said: "Shall we make a proposal to her?" He said: "Yes, but how shall we face the punishment of God?" The other said: "We hope for the mercy of God!" When she came again disputing with her husband, they put themselves forward to her. She said: "No, unless you two rule in my favour against my husband." So they ruled in her favour against her husband. Then she arranged to meet them in a ruined place among the ruins, where they would come to her. They came to her for that purpose. When the one who was going to lie with her wished to, she said: "I will not do it until you tell me by which word you ascend to the heavens and by which word you descend from them." So they told her, and she spoke it and ascended. God made her forget the word by which she would descend, so she remained in her place, [[In Ibn Kathir 1: 259: "so she remained in her place."]] and God made her a star. Abd Allah ibn Umar, whenever he saw her, would curse her and say: "This is the one who tempted Harut and Marut!" When night came, they wanted to ascend, but they could not, so they knew their doom, [[In Ibn Kathir 1: 259: "al-halakah," and both are the same.]] and they were given the choice between the punishment of this world and the punishment of the Hereafter, and they chose the punishment of this world over the punishment of the Hereafter, and so they were bound at Babil, and they began speaking to people in their own tongue, which was magic.

1687. Al-Muthanna ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi', who said: When people after Adam fell into what they fell into of sins and disbelief in God, the angels in heaven said: "O Lord, this world You created only for Your worship and obedience, and they have engaged in disbelief, the killing of a soul which is forbidden, the consumption of wealth which is forbidden, theft, adultery and the drinking of wine!" They began to invoke curses upon them and did not excuse them. It was said to them: "They are in the unseen [ghayb]." [[I do not know what is meant by his saying "they are in the unseen," unless he intended by ghayb: that which is hidden from you of the earth, because of its distance and remoteness and its being low relative to what is around it. As if he is saying: they are in a place hidden from what you, O angels, witness of the signs of your Lord. See p. 433.]] But they did not excuse them, so it was said to them: "Choose from among you two angels, whom I will command with My command and forbid from disobeying Me." They chose Harut and Marut. They were sent down to the earth, and the desires of the children of Adam were placed in them, [[In the Tafsir of Ibn Kathir 1: 257: "So He placed for them..."]] and they were commanded to worship God and not associate anything with Him, and they were forbidden the killing of a soul which is forbidden, the consumption of forbidden wealth, theft, adultery and the drinking of wine. They remained in that state on earth for a time, judging between the people with truth, and that was in the time of Idris. In that time there was a woman whose beauty among all people was like the beauty of Venus among the stars, and she came upon them, [[In the Tafsir of Ibn Kathir: "they both came upon her."]] and they yielded to her with words and solicited her, but she refused unless they would follow her affair and her religion, and they asked her about the religion which she followed. She brought out an idol for them and said: "This is what I worship." They said: "We have no need to worship this!" They went away and stayed for as long as God willed, [[In the printed edition: "fa-sabarā mā shā'a Allāh," and in Ibn Kathir: "fa-'abarā." Ghabara means to remain and to stay.]] then they came upon her again, yielded to her with words and solicited her, and she said: "No, unless you are upon what I am upon." They said: "We have no need to worship this!" When she saw that they refused to worship the idol, she said to them: "Choose one of the three qualities: either you worship the idol, or you kill a soul, or you drink wine." They said: "All of this is not fitting, and the least of the three is drinking wine." So she gave them wine to drink, until the wine took hold of them, and they fell into adultery with her. A man passed by them while they were in that state, and they feared that he would reveal them, so they killed him. When the intoxication left them, they knew what they had fallen into of sin, and they wanted to ascend to heaven, but they could not, and they were prevented from doing so. The veil was lifted between them and the people of heaven, and the angels looked at the sin into which they had fallen, and they were astonished with the greatest astonishment, and they knew that whoever is in the unseen is less fearful [of God]. [[See p. 432, note 1.]] After that, the angels began to seek forgiveness for those on the earth. When they had fallen into what they had fallen into of sin, it was said to them: "Choose the punishment of this world or the punishment of the Hereafter!" They said: "As for the punishment of this world, it will end; as for the punishment of the Hereafter, it has no end." They chose the punishment of this world, so they were placed at Babil, and they are being punished there. [[The report 1687: In the Tafsir of Ibn Kathir 1: 257-258, from Abu Hatim, who said: "Isam ibn Rawad informed us, Adam informed us, Abu Ja'far informed us, al-Rabi' ibn Anas narrated to us, from Qays ibn Abbad, from Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both," which is not the isnad of Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari). Both are through Abu Ja'far from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, but Ibn Jarir did not trace it back to Ibn Abbas. Their wording is the same, except for some slight differences in some phrasing.]]

1688. Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Faraj ibn Fudala narrated to us, from Mu'awiya ibn Salih, from Nafi', who said: I travelled with Ibn Umar, and when it was the last part of the night, he said: "O Nafi', look, has the red star risen?" I said: "No," twice or three times. [[In the printed edition: "qālahā marratayn aw thalāthan" (he said it twice or three times), and the correct version is from Ibn Kathir in his Tafsir 1: 255, and al-Durr al-Manthur 1: 97.]] Then I said: "It has risen!" He said: "No, welcome and no greeting!" I said: "Glory be to God, a subjugated star that hears and obeys!" He said: "I only said to you what I heard from the Messenger of God (ﷺ)," [[In Ibn Kathir: "or he said: the Messenger of God said to me..."]] and he said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said to me: "The angels said: O Lord, how is Your patience with the children of Adam in their errors and sins? He said: I have tested them and granted you well-being. They said: If we were in their place, we would not disobey You! He said: Choose two angels from among you! He said: They did not hesitate to choose, so they chose Harut and Marut." [[Faraj ibn Fudala al-Tanukhi al-Qudda'i: weak. al-Bukhari said: "munkar al-hadith" (his narrations are rejected). He is mentioned in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir 4/1/134, al-Saghir pp. 192, 199, al-Du'afa' of al-Bukhari p. 29, al-Nasa'i p. 25, and Ibn Abi Hatim 3/2/85-86.
This hadith is abridged here. It was transmitted in full by al-Khatib in his biography of Sunayd, through Abd al-Karim ibn al-Haytham, from Sunayd, with this isnad.
These reports, concerning the story of Harut and Marut, and the story of al-Zuhara, that she was a woman who was transformed into a star, are reports which the people of knowledge of hadith have criticised as defective. This meaning has come in a raised (marfu') hadith, transmitted by Ahmad in al-Musnad (6178), through Musa ibn Jubayr, from Nafi', from Ibn Umar. I have explained at length its defect in my commentary on the Musnad, and I quoted the words of Ibn Kathir in the Tafsir 1: 255: "The closest to being correct is that it is from the narration of Abd Allah ibn Umar from Ka'b al-Ahbar, not from the Prophet (ﷺ)." He cited the two earlier reports of al-Tabari, 1684 and 1685, from Salim from Ibn Umar from Ka'b al-Ahbar, as evidence.
Ibn Kathir also mentioned in al-Tarikh (History) 1: 37-38, saying: "This, I think, was fabricated by the Israelites, although Ka'b al-Ahbar did transmit it, and a group of the early generations received it from him, and they mentioned it by way of narration and recounting from the Children of Israel." He also said, after referring to other isnads: "If we think well of it, we say: this is from the reports of the Children of Israel, as was stated earlier from the narration of Ibn Umar from Ka'b al-Ahbar, and it is among their myths which are not to be relied upon."
He also said in the Tafsir 1: 260, after mentioning many of the reports found in al-Tabari and elsewhere: "It has been narrated in the story of Harut and Marut from a group of the Successors, such as Mujahid, al-Suddi, al-Hasan al-Basri, Qatada, Abu al-'Aliya, al-Zuhri, al-Rabi' ibn Anas, Muqatil ibn Hayyan, and others, and the story has been told by a host of exegetes, both earlier and later. Its essence, in its details, goes back to reports of the Children of Israel, since there is among them no raised, sound hadith with a continuous isnad to the truthful and believed one (al-Sadiq al-Masduq), the infallible who does not speak from desire. The apparent context of the Qur'an is a summary of the story without expansion or elaboration. So we believe in what is in the Qur'an, in the sense that God intended. And God knows best the reality of the matter."
This is the truth, and in it is the decisive word. And praise be to God.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 102 (part 5 of 8):

1689 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: As for the matter of Harut and Marut, the angels marvelled at the wrongdoing of the children of Adam, when the messengers, the scriptures and the clear proofs had come to them. Their Lord said to them: "Choose from among you two angels, and I will send them down to judge among the children of Adam on earth." So they chose Harut and Marut. When He sent them down, He said to them: "You marvel at the children of Adam and at their wrongdoing and disobedience. Messengers and scriptures come to them from behind one another [in the printed text of Ibn Kathir 1:259: "Do you marvel at the children of Adam? Indeed, between me and you there is no messenger."], and between me and you there is no messenger. So do this and that, and forbid that and this." He commanded them with commands and forbade them [in Ibn Kathir: "He commanded them with commands and forbade them."]. Then they descended upon that, and no one was more obedient to God than they. They judged justly, and they were fair. They would judge among the children of Adam by day, and when evening came they would ascend and be with the angels, and they would descend when morning came and judge justly. Then there came down to them Venus, in the most beautiful form of a woman, bringing a dispute. They ruled concerning her, and when she rose, each of them felt something in himself. One of them said to his companion: "Did you feel what I felt?" He said: "Yes." So they sent to her: "Come to us, and we will give you a verdict." When she returned, they said to her, and they had ruled in her favour: "Come to us!" So she came to them [in Ibn Kathir: "They said, and they had ruled in her favour, 'She came to them,' and this is not correct."]. They uncovered their private parts for her. Their desire was only within themselves, and they were not like the children of Adam in the desire for women and its pleasure. When they reached that and found it sweet, and were tempted, Venus flew off and returned to where she had been. When evening came, they ascended, but they were repulsed and were not given permission [in Ibn Kathir: "They were rebuffed and were not given permission, and both were the same."], and their wings did not carry them. So they sought help from a man of the children of Adam, and they came to him and said: "Pray to your Lord for us!" He said: "How can the people of the earth intercede for the people of heaven?" They said: "We heard your Lord mention you favourably in heaven!" So he promised them a day, and on the next day he prayed for them, and his prayer was answered. They were given the choice between the punishment of this world and the punishment of the Hereafter. One of them looked at his companion, and they said: "We know that the forms of God's punishment in the Hereafter are such-and-such, for eternity, and with the punishment of this world, seven times that." [In Ibn Kathir: "Do you not know that the ranks of God's punishment... and in this world nine times that." In al-Durr al-Manthur: "They said: We know that the ranks of God's punishment... yes, and with this world seven times..." His saying "and with this world..." means that when it is measured against the punishment of this world, it is seven times its punishment.] So they were ordered to descend to Babel, where their punishment is. It is claimed that they are suspended in iron, folded over, beating their wings. [Narration 1689: in Ibn Kathir 1:259-260, and in al-Durr al-Manthur 1:102.]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: It has been related from some reciters that he used to read: ﴿And what was sent down to the two angels﴾, meaning by it two men from the children of Adam. We have already shown the error of this reading by way of reasoning [see what has passed, pp. 425-426]. As for transmission, there is the ijma' (scholarly consensus) of the authorities, from the Companions, the Successors and the reciters of the major cities, that this reading is incorrect. That is sufficient as evidence of its error.

* *

As for His saying ﴿at Babel﴾, it is the name of a town or a place on the earth. The people of ta'wil (interpretation) have differed concerning it. Some of them said: it is "Babel of Dunbawand."

1690 - Musa narrated to me this, saying: Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi. [Narration 1690: it is the previous narration, 1686.]

* *

Others said: rather, it is "Babel of Iraq."

Mention of those who said this:

1691 - Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Abi al-Zinad, from Hisham ibn 'Urwa, from his father, from 'A'isha, in an account I have mentioned of a woman who came to Medina, and she mentioned that she had gone to Iraq, to Babel, and that Harut and Marut came to her, and she learned sorcery from them. [Narration 1691: al-Husayn is Sunayd, as has passed many times. Hajjaj is Ibn Muhammad al-Misisi al-A'war, a trustworthy narrator of high standing, among the teachers of Ahmad and Ibn Ma'in. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir of al-Bukhari 1/2/376, Ibn Abi Hatim 1/2/166, and Tarikh Baghdad 8:236-239. This report is a portion of a longer report that will come: 1692, also through Ibn Abi al-Zinad.]

Abu Ja'far said: The meaning of sihr (sorcery) has been disputed. Some of them said: it is deceptions, trickery and devices that the sorcerer performs, so that the thing appears to the one who is bewitched as being other than what it is, like one who sees a mirage from afar and imagines it to be water, or who sees a thing from afar and fixes it in his mind as being other than its reality. And like the rider of a ship moving swiftly, who imagines that the trees and mountains he sees are moving with him. They said: so likewise the bewitched person is described thus: after what the sorcerer's magic has reached him with, he thinks that what he sees or does is other than what it really is, as in what was narrated:

1692 - Ahmad ibn al-Walid and Sufyan ibn Waki' narrated to me, both saying: Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, from Hisham ibn 'Urwa, from his father, from 'A'isha: that the Prophet (ﷺ), when he was bewitched, would imagine that he was doing something when he had not done it. [Hadith 1692: Ahmad ibn al-Walid, Ibn Jarir's teacher: I do not know who he is. Sufyan ibn Waki' ibn al-Jarrah is weak. Al-Bukhari said in al-Tarikh al-Saghir, p. 246: "They spoke of him for things they had taught him." Al-Nasa'i said in al-Du'afa', p. 16: "He is nothing." Abu Zur'a even accused him of lying. Abu Hatim defended him against this charge and said it came to him from his copyist, who corrupted his narrations. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib, Ibn Abi Hatim 2/1/231-232, and al-Majruhin of Ibn Hibban (manuscript photocopy), no. 470. His weakness is not a reason for the weakness of this hadith, for it has come through sound chains, which we will point out in the next hadith. Yahya ibn Sa'id is al-Qattan, the imam and memoriser.]

1693 - Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Ibn Numayr narrated to us, from Hisham ibn 'Urwa, from his father, from 'A'isha, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) was bewitched by a Jew from the Jews of Banu Zurayq, called Labid ibn al-A'sam, until the Messenger of God (ﷺ) would imagine that he was doing something when he was not doing it. [Hadith 1693: it is a repetition of the previous hadith with another chain, narrated by Sufyan ibn Waki' from Ibn Numayr. Ibn Numayr is 'Abdullah ibn Numayr al-Hamdani: trustworthy, a man of the Sunna, narrated from by the leading scholars Ahmad and Ibn al-Madini. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib, Ibn Sa'd 6:274-275, and Ibn Abi Hatim 2/2/186. This hadith, through both its chains, is abridged from a longer hadith. As for the narration of Ibn Numayr, Ahmad narrated it in al-Musnad 6:57 (Halabi) from Ibn Numayr. Muslim narrated it in his Sahih 2:180, from Abu Kurayb. Ibn Majah narrated it, no. 3545, from Abu Bakr ibn Shayba, both from Ibn Numayr, in its longer form. Many trustworthy and reliable narrators have related it from Hisham ibn 'Urwa, from his father, from 'A'isha: Ahmad narrated it in al-Musnad 6:63, through Ma'mar. Ahmad also narrated it, 6:63, through Abu Usama Hammad ibn Usama, and likewise al-Bukhari 10:201 and Muslim 2:180, both through Abu Usama. Ahmad also narrated it, 6:96, and Ibn Sa'd 2/2/4, both through Wuhayb. Al-Bukhari narrated it, 10:192-197, through 'Isa ibn Yunus; 10:199-201, through Ibn 'Uyayna; 10:200, through Sufyan, who is Ibn 'Uyayna; 11:163, through Anas ibn 'Iyad Abu Damra. He also narrated it, 6:239, as a mu'allaq (suspended narration) through al-Layth ibn Sa'd. All of these narrated it from Hisham ibn 'Urwa, from his father, from 'A'isha. Al-Bukhari said, 10:197, after the narration of 'Isa ibn Yunus, that he had heard it before from Ibn Jurayj saying: "Ibn Ibn Jurayj told me: the family of 'Urwa narrated to me from 'Urwa," and that Ibn 'Uyayna asked Hisham about it, and he narrated it to him from his father, from 'A'isha. Ibn Kathir mentioned some of its chains in his commentary on Surat al-Falaq, 9:353-354. We have expanded upon its chains here because al-Tabari did not mention it in its proper place there. A similar account has been established from the hadith of Zayd ibn Arqam. Ahmad narrated it in al-Musnad 4:367 (Halabi), from Abu Mu'awiya, from al-A'mash, from Yazid ibn Hayyan, from Zayd ibn Arqam, and this is a sound chain. Yazid ibn Hayyan Abu Hayyan al-Taymi is a trustworthy Successor, biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir of al-Bukhari 4/2/324-325, and Ibn Abi Hatim 4/2/255-256. He also narrated it, Ibn Sa'd 2/2/6, from Musa ibn Mas'ud, from Sufyan al-Thawri, from al-A'mash, from Thumama al-Muhalliml, from Zayd ibn Arqam. This chain is also sound. Musa ibn Mas'ud al-Nahdi: his reliability was previously noted, 280. Thumama ibn 'Uqba al-Muhallimi is trustworthy, biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir of al-Bukhari 1/2/176, and al-Jarh 1/1/465-466. "Al-Muhallimi" is with a damma on the m, a fatha on the h, a kasra on the doubled l, followed by m, a nisba to "Muhallim ibn Tamim." Al-Haythami mentioned it in Majma' al-Zawa'id 6:281, with two narrations, and said: "al-Nasa'i narrated it in abridged form," then said: "al-Tabarani narrated it through several chains, and the narrators of one of them are the narrators of the Sahih." Al-Hafiz (Ibn Hajar) mentioned it in al-Fath 10:194, that it was "authenticated by al-Hakim and 'Abd al-Hamid."
This story of sorcery has been challenged by many of our contemporaries, who in their denial are imitators, and claim that they are guided by their own reason. Others before them have also taken this path, and the scholars have refuted them. Al-Hafiz said in al-Fath 10:192: "Al-Mazari said: some innovators denied this hadith, claiming that it diminishes the station of prophethood and casts doubt upon it! They said: everything that leads to that is false. They claimed that accepting this undermines trust in the laws they have legislated, since it would be possible that he imagined seeing Gabriel when he was not there, and that he was inspired with something when he had not been inspired!" Al-Mazari said: All of this is rejected. For evidence has established the truthfulness of the Prophet (ﷺ) in what he conveys from God Most High, and his infallibility in conveying it, and the miracles bear witness to his truthfulness. So accepting what evidence has established to be contrary is false. As for what relates to some matters of this world for which he was not sent, nor was the message for their sake, he is subject in that to what afflicts human beings, such as illnesses. It is not far-fetched that he could imagine something in a matter of worldly affairs that has no reality, while being protected from such things in matters of religion." Then al-Hafiz expanded on this subtle discussion, with his well-known strength, in gathering the narrations and interpreting them, in a way that leaves no doubt for anyone who is fair. Qadi 'Iyad devoted a fine chapter to this topic in his book al-Shifa. See it in the commentary of al-'Allama 'Ali al-Qari, 2:190-193, from the Bulaq edition of 1257 AH.]

1694 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Yunus informed me, from Ibn Shihab, who said: 'Urwa ibn al-Zubayr and Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib used to narrate that the Jews of Banu Zurayq tied knots of sorcery for the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and placed them in a well called Bi'r Hazm, until the Messenger of God began to lose his sight. God informed him of what they had done, and the Messenger of God (ﷺ) sent to the well of Hazm where the knots were, and took them out. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) used to say: "The Jews of Banu Zurayq bewitched me." [Hadith 1694: this is on the same subject as the two preceding hadiths, but this one is mursal (a narration whose chain omits a Companion). Ibn Sa'd 2/2/5 narrated something similar, abridged, from al-Zuhri, "from Ibn al-Musayyib and 'Urwa ibn al-Zubayr, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) would say: 'The Jews of Banu Zurayq bewitched me.'" Al-Hafiz in al-Fath 10:193 pointed out that the mursal of Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib was narrated by 'Abd al-Razzaq, and mentioned some of its wording that indicates it is longer than what is here. His saying "Bi'r Hazm" is not known. In all the narrations, it is "Bi'r Dharwan."]

* *

The one who holds this view denied that a sorcerer could, by his sorcery, change something from its reality, or compel something from God's creation to serve him, except for what any other human being can do, or create physical bodies other than through trickery and deception that appear to the eyes of observers to be other than their realities as we have described. They said: If the sorcerers had the power to create bodies and to change the realities of things from their forms, there would be no distinction between truth and falsehood, and it would be possible that all perceptible things were bewitched by sorcerers and their essences changed. They said: In God's description of the sorcerers of Pharaoh, with His saying ﴿Then their ropes and their staffs seemed to him, by their sorcery, to be moving﴾ [Surat Ta-Ha: 66], and in the report of 'A'isha about the Messenger of God (ﷺ) that when he was bewitched, he would imagine that he was doing something when he was not doing it, there is clear evidence against the claims of the claimants, that the sorcerer creates the essences of things by his sorcery, and compels what is impossible for others among the children of Adam to compel, such as the lifeless, the inanimate and the animals, and that our view is correct. [The construction of the sentence: "clear evidence against the claims of the claimants... and the correctness of what we have said" is conjoined.]

* *

Others said: A sorcerer may, by his sorcery, be able to turn a person into a donkey, and to bewitch a person and a donkey, and to create essences and bodies. They relied for that upon what:

1695 - Al-Rabi' ibn Sulayman narrated this to us, saying: Ibn Wahb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi al-Zinad informed us, saying: Hisham ibn 'Urwa narrated to me, from his father, from 'A'isha, wife of the Prophet (ﷺ), that she said: A woman from the people of Dumat al-Jandal came to me. She came seeking the Messenger of God (ﷺ) after his death, shortly after that event [it is said: "It was in the ḥadathān of such-and-such" (with kasra then sukun), and "in his ḥadātha": meaning close to his time], asking him about something she had become involved in concerning sorcery, which she had not practised. 'A'isha said to 'Urwa: O nephew! I saw her weeping, when she did not find the Messenger of God (ﷺ) to cure her [yashfīhā: meaning to answer her in a way that brings her peace of heart, so that she is freed from her perplexity. From this comes: "The cure of ignorance is asking." Ignorance and perplexity are sicknesses of hearts and souls], she was weeping until I pitied her! And she was saying: "I fear that I have perished! I had a husband who went away from me, and an old woman came to me, and I complained to her about that. She said: If you do what I command you, I will make him come to you! When night came, she brought me two black dogs, and I mounted one and mounted the other, and it was as nothing until we stood at Babel [In Ibn Kathir 1:260: "it was not a thing," and the correct version is what is here and in al-Durr al-Manthur 1:101. Her saying "it was as nothing" is a good expression, meaning that what had passed was not counted as anything, but rather less than a little. The Arabs say: "I was delayed from you a little (shay'an)." From this is the saying of 'Umar ibn Abi Rabi'a: "She said to them: wait a little while, perhaps... and if he blames me for what I have decided, I am blameworthy."]

Say, "Wait a little." They also say in such cases, "It was nothing but a 'kalla' and a 'la'," all of which mean a swift, flashing moment.]] Then suddenly there were two men hanging by their feet, and they said, "What brought you here?" I said, "I want to learn magic." They said, "We are only a trial, so do not disbelieve and return." But I refused and said, "No." They said, "Go to that oven and urinate in it." [[In the printed edition: "They said, 'Go...'", and I have adopted what is in al-Durr al-Manthur and Ibn Kathir, as it is better.]] So I went, became terrified, and did not do it. I returned to them, and they said, "Did you do it?" I said, "Yes." They said, "Did you see anything?" I said, "I saw nothing!" They said to me, "You did not do it. Return to your land and do not disbelieve." But I hesitated and refused. They said, "Go to that oven and urinate in it." So I went, and I shivered. Then I returned to them and said, "I have done it." They said, "What did you see?" I said, "I saw nothing." They said, "You are lying, you did not do it. Return to your land and do not disbelieve, for you are at the head of your affair!" [[It is said: "You are at the head of your affair" (anta 'ala ra's amrika), and "'ala ra'as amrika": that is, at its beginning and on the verge of it. Al-Jawhari claimed that their saying "'ala ra's amrika" belongs to the speech of the common people, but this report refutes what he said.]] So I hesitated and refused, and they said, "Go to that oven and urinate in it." I went to it and urinated in it, and I saw a horseman, armored in iron, come out of me, go up into the sky, and vanish from me until I could no longer see him. I came back to them and said, "I have done it!" They said, "What did you see?" I said, "A horseman, armored, came out of me and went up into the sky until I could no longer see him." [[In the Tafsir of Ibn Kathir and al-Durr al-Manthur: "So I saw a horseman," and what is here is a good and sound reading.]] They said, "You have spoken the truth. That was your faith leaving you. Go." Then I said to the woman, "By God, I know nothing! And they told me nothing!" She said, "Yes, indeed. Whatever you desire, it will come to pass! Take this wheat and sow it." So I sowed it and said, "Sprout!" and it sprouted. I said, "Ear!" and it formed ears. I said, "Ripen!" and it ripened. I said, "Dry!" and it dried. I said, "Grind!" and it was ground. I said, "Bake!" and it was baked. [[In this passage there are words which the lexicons have not recorded; I will mention them in the explanation of their meaning. "Atli'i, fa-atla'at" means: bring forth your shoot, from the saying "atla'a al-zar'" (the crop sprouted), when the first growth of the plant appears from the ground. "Ahqili al-zar'": its leaves branched out before its stalk thickened. "Afrki, fa-afrakat": be freekeh, which is the grain of the ear when it has hardened and is fit to be rubbed. "Afrak al-sunbul": it became freekeh, which is when it is fit to be rubbed and eaten. "Ayba si, fa-ayba sat": be dry grain; "ayba al-baql": it dried and withered. "Atihni, fa-atahanat": be flour. The lexicons do not record "atahin," but it follows its predecessors in form and is sound Arabic in this place, in accordance with the patterns of the language. "Akhbizi, fa-akhbazat": be bread that can be eaten. This too is not recorded in the lexicons, but it is as ancient as its predecessors. Ibn Kathir said that the isnad of this report to 'A'isha is good, and that al-Hakim authenticated it. If it is as they both said, then there is no doubt in the Arabic of these words from the transmission side as well.]] When I saw that whatever I desired came to pass, I was seized with regret, and I said, "By God, O Mother of the Believers! By God, I never did anything, and I will never do it."

[[The report: part of it has passed, with another isnad to Ibn Abi al-Zinad: 1691.
Ibn Kathir narrated this report in full, 1: 260–261, from al-Tabari. He introduced it with the words: "A strange report has been transmitted on this matter, with a wondrous context. We wished to draw attention to it." Then, after quoting it, he said: "This is a good isnad to 'A'isha, may Allah be pleased with her." He mentioned that Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from al-Rabi' ibn Sulayman, with a longer version.
al-Suyuti mentioned it, 1: 101, and attributed it also to al-Hakim, who authenticated it, and to al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan.
It is a strange story, and we do not know whether that woman spoke the truth about what she reported to 'A'isha. As for 'A'isha, she was truthful in that the woman told her. The isnad to 'A'isha is good, indeed sound.
al-Rabi' ibn Sulayman: he is al-Muradi al-Misri al-Mu'adhdhin, the companion of al-Shafi'i and transmitter of his books, and he is trustworthy (thiqa). He is biographed in al-Tahdhib and in Ibn Abi Hatim 1/2/464. Ibn Abi al-Zinad: he is "'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi al-Zinad 'Abd Allah ibn Dhakwan," and he is trustworthy. Some imams criticized him regarding his narration from his father and in the narration of the Baghdadis from him. The truth is that he is trustworthy, especially in the hadith of Hisham ibn 'Urwa. Ibn Ma'in said, as narrated by Abu Dawud to him, recorded by al-Khatib and others: "The most reliable of people in (transmitting from) Hisham ibn 'Urwa is 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi al-Zinad." al-Tirmidhi also declared him trustworthy and authenticated several of his hadiths. Indeed, he said in the Sunan, 3: 59, concerning a hadith of his that he authenticated, which contains a word transmitted by no one else: "It was mentioned only by 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi al-Zinad, who is trustworthy and a memorizer (hafiz)."]]

Those who held this view spoke as we have described, relied on what we have mentioned, and said: "Were it not that the magician is able to do what he claims he can do, he would not be able to separate a man from his wife." They said: "Allah, mighty and majestic is He, has informed us that they learn from the two angels that by which they separate a man from his wife. Had this been not in reality, but by way of imagination and supposition, it would not be a separation in truth, yet Allah, mighty and majestic is He, has informed us that they separate in truth."

* *

Others said: "Rather, 'sihr' (magic) is an effect on the eye."

* *

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And they teach no one until they say, "We are only a trial, so do not disbelieve."﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: The meaning of this is: The two angels teach no one of mankind what was sent down to them of separating a man from his wife until they say to him: "We are only a trial and a test for the children of Adam, so do not disbelieve in your Lord." As:

1696 – Musa narrated to me, saying: 'Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, who said: When a person came to them, meaning Harut and Marut, seeking magic, they admonished him and said: "Do not disbelieve, we are only a trial!" If he refused, they said to him: "Go to this ash and urinate on it." When he urinated on it, a light came out of it that rose until it entered the sky, and that is faith. A black thing like smoke came and entered his ears and every part of him, and that is the wrath of Allah. When they informed him of that, they taught him magic. This is the saying of Allah: ﴿And they teach no one until they say, "We are only a trial, so do not disbelieve"﴾ to the end of the verse. [[In the printed edition: "Wa-qila shay' aswad..." is meaningless speech. The correction is from Ibn Kathir, 1: 262.]]

1697 – Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, from Sa'id, from Qatada and al-Hasan, regarding ﴿until they say, "We are only a trial, so do not disbelieve"﴾, he said: It was taken from them as a covenant that they would not teach anyone until they said, "We are only a trial, so do not disbelieve." [[In the printed edition: "It was taken from her a covenant that they would not teach," and the addition is from Ibn Kathir, 1: 262.]]

1698 – al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, saying: Qatada said: They used to teach people magic, so a covenant was taken from them that they would not teach anyone until they said, "We are only a trial, so do not disbelieve."

1699 – al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Abu Sufyan narrated to us, from Ma'mar, who said: Someone other than Qatada said: A covenant was taken from them that they would not teach anyone until they came forward to him and said, "We are only a trial, so do not disbelieve."

1700 – Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, from 'Awf, from al-Hasan, who said: A covenant was taken from them that they would say this.

1701 – al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: A binding pledge was taken from them that they would not teach anyone until they said, "We are only a trial, so do not disbelieve." No one would dare practice magic except a disbeliever.

* *

As for "fitna" (trial) in this place, its meaning is testing and trial. From this is the saying of the poet: [[Al-Tabari attributed it in his History, 1: 151–152, to al-Hutat ibn Yazid al-Mujashi'i, paternal uncle of al-Farazdaq. Al-Baladhuri, in Ansab al-Ashraf, 5: 104, attributed it to 'Ali ibn al-Ghadir ibn al-Mudarris al-Ghanawi, and to Ihab ibn Hammam ibn Sa'sa'a ibn Najiya ibn 'Iqal al-Mujashi'i, and to Ibn al-Gharira al-Nahshali, who is Kathir ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Malik al-Nahshali, who is a mukhadram (one who lived in both the Jahiliyya and Islam), and it is also attributed to him in Mu'jam al-Shu'ara', p. 349, and in al-Kamil of al-Mubarrad, 2: 34. Abu al-Hasan al-Akhfash said: "Ibn al-Gharira al-Dabbi," which is pure error; it is in fact al-Nahshali.]]

"They have tested people in their religion... and Ibn 'Affan left a long evil."
[[The beginning of this qasida: "Umama has distanced herself from you, a long distance... and love has loaded you with a heavy burden."
Then he said: "By the life of your father, do not grieve, for good has departed except a little. People have been tested in their religion, and Ibn 'Affan left a long evil. O blamer of every doomed man, he will go to God on a fine journey. Time has a pleasure, and its pleasure must pass away." Al-Tabari narrated the first half of the verse cited here in his History: "Surely the people have been made foolish in their religion."]]

And from it is his saying: "I tested the gold in the fire," when you examined it to know its quality from its inferiority, and "I tested him a trial and a testing." As:

1702 – Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding ﴿We are only a trial﴾, that is, a test.

* *

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿So they learn from these two what they use to separate between a man and his wife﴾

Abu Ja'far said: His words, may His praise be great: ﴿So they learn from them﴾ are a report beginning a new subject about those who learn from the two angels what was sent down to them, and it is not an answer to His words: ﴿And they teach no one﴾. Rather, it is a new statement, and therefore it is in the nominative, so it is said: "fa-yata'allamun" (so they learn). The meaning of the sentence, then, is: "And they teach no one until they say, 'We are only a trial,' and they refuse to accept that from them, so they learn from them what they use to separate a man from his wife." [[Al-Tabari means that the speech contains an omission, relying on the listener's understanding without mention of it, which is His words: "so they refuse to accept that from them."]]

It has been said that His words ﴿So they learn﴾ are a report about the Jews, conjoined to His words: "But the devils disbelieved, teaching people magic, and what was sent down to the two angels at Babylon, Harut and Marut" and "so they learn from them what they use to separate a man from his wife." They made this a later element whose meaning is an earlier one.

* *

What we have said is more fitting to the interpretation of the verse, because attaching it to what immediately precedes it, where the sense of the interpretation is correct, is better than attaching it to what has been cut off from it by an intervening statement. [[His words "ma kana lil-ta'wil" ("what was for the interpretation") are what they say in weak Arabic: "ma dama lil-ta'wil" ("as long as it is for the interpretation").]]

The "ha'" (ه), the "mim" (م), and the "alif" (ا) in His words ﴿minhuma﴾ ("from them") refer to the two angels. The meaning is: people learn from the two angels that by which they separate a man from his wife.

* *

The "ma" (ما) that comes with "yufarriquna" (they separate) has the sense of "alladhi" (that which). It has been said: the meaning is: the magic by which they separate. It has been said: it is something other than magic. We have already mentioned their disagreement on this previously. [[See what has passed: 423–424.]]

As for "al-mar'" (المرء, the man), it means a male human, and the feminine of it is "al-mar'a" (المرأة, the woman). It is used in the singular and dual, but its plural is not formed on its pattern. It is said: "hadha imru' salih, wa-hadhan imra'an salihan" (this is a righteous man, and these are two righteous men). One does not say "ha'ula' imru'u sidq" (these are truthful men), but rather "ha'ula' rijal sidq" (these are truthful men) and "qawm sidq" (a truthful people). Likewise, "al-mar'a" is used in the singular and dual and is not pluralized on its own pattern. It is said: "hadhihi imra'a, wa-hatani imra'atan." One does not say "ha'ula' imra'at," but rather "ha'ula' niswa" (these are women).

* *

As for "al-zawj" (الزوج, spouse), the people of the Hijaz say of a man's wife, "hiya zawjuh" (she is his spouse), in the position of the masculine "zawj." Among this is the saying of Allah, exalted is His mention: ﴿Keep your wife (zawjaka) to yourself﴾ [Surat al-Ahzab: 37]. The Tamim, many of Qays, and the people of Najd say, "hiya zawjatuh" (she is his wife). As the poet said: [[This is al-Farazdaq.]]

"Indeed, one who walks to stir up my wife,
is like one who walks to a lion of the thicket, seeking to make her urinate for him."
[[His Diwan: 605; al-Aghani 9: 326 and 19: 8 (Sasa), in his story with al-Nawwar. He recites this poetry about the sons of Umm al-Nusayr (Tabaqat Fuhul al-Shu'ara': 281, and al-Aghani). She had gone out with a man named Zuhayr ibn Tha'laba, along with the sons of Umm al-Nusayr, and he composed this poetry. After the verse: "And beyond the urine of lions is courage, and the might of a strong arm that repels oppression." The version in the Diwan and elsewhere reads: "Indeed a man who walks to tempt my wife." And his saying "yukhabbibu" means he corrupts her against me. "Yuharrish" means he incites and stirs up enmity between me and her. "Yastabilaha": he seeks that she urinate in his hand.]]

If someone says: How does the magician separate a man from his wife? It is said: We have already shown previously that the meaning of "sihr" (magic) is the imagining of a thing to a man contrary to what it is in its reality and essence, sufficient for one who is guided to understand it. [[See what has passed: 435 and following.]] If this is correct by what we have cited as evidence, [[In the printed edition: "fa-in kana dhalika sahihan," and what is adopted is better.]] then his separating between a man and his wife is that, by his magic, he makes each of them imagine the other's person contrary to what it is in reality, in beauty and good looks, until he makes her ugly in his eyes, so he turns away his face and withdraws from her, until the husband causes the wife to separate. Thus the magician, by bringing about the cause, is the one separating them, since the cause by which they became separated came from him. We have shown, in more than one place in this book of ours, that the Arabs attribute a thing to its causer because of his causing it, even if he did not directly perform the act that resulted from the cause, which is sufficient to avoid repeating it here. [[See what has passed: 1: 196.]] Likewise, the magician's separating a man from his wife by his magic. Those of the interpreters have said something similar to what we have said.

Those who said that:
