The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿Many of the People of the Book wish they could turn you back to disbelief after your belief﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: This statement from the words of God, may His praise be exalted, has made clear that His address in all these verses, from His words ﴿O you who believe, do not say, "Ra'ina"﴾ onward, although its meaning is directed toward the Prophet ﷺ, is in fact an address from Him to the believers among his Companions [In the printed edition: "to the believers and his Companions", and what is established here seems to be the correct reading], and a reproach from Him to them, and a prohibition against taking the advice of the Jews and their counterparts among the people of polytheism, and accepting their opinions in any matter of their religion. It is also evidence that they had used, or some of them had used, rudeness in addressing and questioning the Messenger of God ﷺ, and had used with him what was not proper for them to use, imitating the Jews in that or some of them. So their Lord said to them, forbidding the use of that [In the printed edition: "their Lord said to them", and the correct reading includes the fa'] : Do not say to your Prophet ﷺ what the Jews say to him, "Ra'ina", imitating them, but say, "Unzurna wa-isma'u" [Look at us and listen]. For harming the Messenger of God ﷺ is disbelief in Me and a denial of the right I am owed by you in honoring and revering him, and for whoever disbelieves in Me there is a painful punishment. For the Jews and the polytheists do not wish that any good should be sent down to you from your Lord, but many of them wished to turn you back to disbelief after your belief, out of envy from themselves toward you and toward your Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, after the truth had become clear to them regarding the matter of Muhammad, and that he is a Prophet to them and to all of My creation.

* *

It has been said that God, may His praise be exalted, by His words ﴿Many of the People of the Book﴾ meant Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf.

1786 - Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, regarding His words ﴿Many of the People of the Book﴾: he is Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf.

1787 - al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Abu Sufyan al-Amari narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri and Qatada, regarding ﴿Many of the People of the Book﴾: he said, Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf. [Report 1787: In the printed edition: "Abu Sufyan al-Ma'mari". This is Muhammad ibn Humayd al-Yashkuri al-Ma'mari al-Basri, resident of Baghdad, called "al-Ma'mari" because he travelled to Ma'mar ibn Rashid al-Azdi. He is trustworthy and truthful, and Ibn Hibban mentioned him among the trustworthy. al-Uqayli mentioned him among the weak narrators and said: "There is something to be examined in his narrations." He died in 182 AH (Tahdhib al-Tahdhib 9: 132).]

Some others said:

1788 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, saying: Ibn Ishaq narrated to me; and Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Yunus ibn Bukayr narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, client of Zayd ibn Thabit, narrated to me, saying: Sa'id ibn Jubayr, or Ikrima, narrated to me, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Huyayy ibn Akhtab and Abu Yasir ibn Akhtab were among the Jews most envious of the Arabs, since God had singled them out with His Messenger ﷺ, and the two of them strove hard to turn people away from Islam by whatever means they could, so God revealed concerning them: ﴿Many of the People of the Book wish they could turn you back﴾, the verse. [Report 1788: in the Sira of Ibn Hisham 2: 197.]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The claim of the one who says that by His words ﴿Many of the People of the Book﴾ He meant Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf has no understandable meaning. For Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf was one person, and God, may His praise be exalted, has informed that many of them wish to turn the believers back to disbelief after their belief; and one is not called "many" in the sense of numerical plurality, unless the speaker intends by it the kind of abundance which God describes in this verse, the abundance of honor and elevated rank among his people and clan, as one says, "So-and-so is many among the people," meaning abundance of status and standing. If that is what he intended, he has erred, because God, may His praise be exalted, has described them with the attribute of a group, saying ﴿they wish to turn you back to disbelief after your belief out of envy﴾; this is evidence that He meant abundance in number. Or he may have thought it is one of the expressions that take the form of a report about a group while the intended subject of the report is one person, similar to what we mentioned earlier regarding the verse of Jamil. [See what has preceded shortly: 487, his saying: "Surely my neighbors this evening have departed."] That too would be an error. For when speech is of that meaning, there must be an indication within it showing that this is its meaning; and there is no indication in His words ﴿Many of the People of the Book﴾ that the intended referent is one person rather than a large group, so that the interpretation of the verse could be turned in that direction and evidence whose apparent sense points to the rule would be diverted to something other than the common usage.

* *

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿out of envy from themselves﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His words, may His praise be exalted, ﴿out of envy from themselves﴾, He means that many of the People of the Book wish for the believers what God, may His praise be exalted, has informed us they wish for them, namely the return from their faith to disbelief, out of envy from them and aggression against them.

* *

"Envy" (ḥasad) here is in the accusative not as an adjective of the disbelievers, but in the manner of a verbal noun (maṣdar) that comes out of the meaning of the sentence while its wording differs from the form of the verbal noun, as when a speaker says to another, "I wished for you the evil I wished, out of envy of you," so that "envy" is a verbal noun from the meaning of his saying "I wished evil." For in his saying "I wished that for you" there is the meaning "I envied you for that." Accordingly "ḥasad" is in the accusative, because in His words ﴿Many of the People of the Book wish they could turn you back to disbelief after your belief﴾ there is the meaning: the People of the Book envied you for what God has bestowed upon you of success, and granted you of right guidance to His religion and belief in His Messenger, and singled you out by making His Messenger a man from among you, kind and merciful to you, and not making him from among them, so that you would be followers of them. So His saying ﴿ḥasadan﴾ is a verbal noun from that meaning.

* *

As for His saying ﴿from themselves﴾, He means by it: from their own side, just as a speaker says, "I have such-and-such with you," meaning "from your side," and as:

1789 - I was told by Ammar, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, regarding His words ﴿from themselves﴾, he said: from their own side. [Report 1789: This chain was incomplete, and I completed it from the chain recurring in the tafsir in hundreds of earlier places, the closest being no. 1647, and it will also come at no. 1792; the report itself was incomplete and I completed it from Ibn Kathir's tafsir 1: 280 and al-Durr al-Manthur 1: 107.]

God, may His praise be exalted, only informed about them, the believers, that they wished that for the believers from their own selves, to inform them that they had not been commanded to this in their Book, and that they commit what they commit of that with knowledge of God's prohibition to them against it.

* *

The interpretation of His words: ﴿after the truth has become clear to them﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His words, may His praise be exalted, ﴿after the truth has become clear to them﴾, He means: after the truth had become clear to these many of the People of the Book, who wish that they could turn you back to disbelief after your belief, concerning the matter of Muhammad ﷺ, and what he brought from his Lord, and the religion to which he called, and it shone upon them: that this is the truth about which they have no doubt. As:

1790 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Zuray' narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada: ﴿after the truth has become clear to them﴾, after it had become clear to them that Muhammad is the Messenger of God ﷺ, and Islam is the religion of God.

1791 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi', from Abu al-Aliya: ﴿after the truth has become clear to them﴾, he says: it became clear to them that Muhammad is the Messenger of God; they find him written with them in the Torah and the Gospel.

1792 - I was told by Ammar, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi', the like of it; and he added in it: so they disbelieved in him out of envy and aggression, since he was from other than them.

1793 - Musa narrated to me, saying: Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿after the truth has become clear to them﴾, he said: the truth is Muhammad ﷺ, so it became clear to them that he is the Messenger.

1794 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: ﴿after the truth has become clear to them﴾, he said: it has become clear to them that he is the Messenger of God.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: By His saying that, it is shown that the disbelief of those whose story is recounted in this verse in God and His Messenger is obstinacy, and that they act with knowledge and awareness that they are fabricators against God, as:

1795 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Uthman ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Bishr ibn Umara narrated to us, from Abu Rawq, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿after the truth has become clear to them﴾, God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: after the truth had shone upon them, they did not ignore any of it, but envy drove them to denial. So God reproached them, blamed them, and rebuked them with the severest censure.

* *

The interpretation of His words: ﴿So pardon and overlook until God brings His command﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His words, may His praise be exalted, ﴿So pardon﴾, He means: overlook what came from them of harm and error in an opinion they proposed to you regarding your religion, desiring to turn you away from it and attempting to make you apostatize after your belief; and overlook what had passed from them of their saying to your Prophet ﷺ: ﴿and listen, unheard, and "Ra'ina," distorting with their tongues and attacking the religion﴾ [al-Nisa: 46]; and overlook what came from them of ignorance in that, until God brings His command, so that He may bring about for you from His command concerning them what He wills, and decree concerning them what He desires. Then He, may His remembrance be exalted, decreed concerning them and brought His command, and said to His Prophet ﷺ and to the believers in him: ﴿Fight those who do not believe in God nor in the Last Day, nor forbid what God and His Messenger have forbidden, nor adopt the religion of truth from among those who were given the Book, until they give the jizya willingly while they are humbled﴾ [al-Tawba: 29]. So God, may His praise be exalted, abrogated the pardon and overlooking of them by making fighting them obligatory upon the believers, until their word and the word of the believers become one, or they pay the jizya with humiliation, as:

1796 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya ibn Salih narrated to me, from Ali ibn Abi Talha, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿So pardon and overlook until God brings His command; surely God is capable of all things﴾; and this was abrogated by His words: ﴿So kill the polytheists wherever you find them﴾ [al-Tawba: 5].

1797 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada: ﴿So pardon and overlook until God brings His command﴾, then God brought His command and said: ﴿Fight those who do not believe in God nor in the Last Day﴾, up to ﴿and they are humbled﴾, that is, humiliation and retribution for them. This verse abrogated what came before it: ﴿So pardon and overlook until God brings His command﴾.

1798 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi', regarding His words: ﴿So pardon and overlook until God brings His command﴾, he said: pardon the People of the Book until God brings about a matter. Then God brought about afterward: ﴿Fight those who do not believe in God nor in the Last Day﴾, to: ﴿and they are humbled﴾.

1799 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada regarding His words: ﴿So pardon and overlook until God brings His command﴾, he said: it was abrogated by: ﴿Kill the polytheists wherever you find them﴾.

1800 - Musa narrated to me, saying: Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿So pardon and overlook until God brings His command﴾, he said: this is abrogated; it was abrogated by ﴿Fight those who do not believe in God nor in the Last Day﴾, to His words: ﴿and they are humbled﴾.

* *

The interpretation of His words: ﴿Surely God is capable of all things﴾

Abu Ja'far said: We have already explained the meaning of "qadir" (capable) earlier, that it means powerful. [See what has preceded shortly: 484, and in 1: 361.]

So the meaning of the verse here is: surely God, over all that He wills concerning those whose affair I have described to you from the People of the Book and others, is capable; if He wills, He will take vengeance upon them for their obstinacy toward their Lord, and if He wills, He will guide them to what God has guided you to of faith, nothing He wills is beyond His power, and no matter He wills to decree is beyond His ability, for to Him belong creation and command.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 110:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿And establish prayer and give zakah. And whatever good you put forward for yourselves - you will find it with Allah﴾

Abu Ja'far said: We have already shown earlier the meaning of "establishing the prayer," that it is performing it within its limits and obligations, and [we have explained] the interpretation of "the prayer" and its origin, and the meaning of "giving zakah," that it is giving it willingly, as it has been prescribed and made obligatory, and the meaning of "zakah" and the disagreement of those who differ concerning it, and the evidences indicating the soundness of the view we have chosen in that, in a way that suffices without repeating it in this place. [[See what has passed: 1:241-242, then 1:573-574.]]

* *

As for His words: ﴿And whatever good you put forward for yourselves - you will find it with Allah﴾, He, may His praise be exalted, means by this: Whatever righteous deed you do during the days of your life, and send ahead before your death as a store for yourselves in your return, you will find its reward with your Lord on the Day of Resurrection, and He will recompense you for it.

* *

And "good" (khayr) is the deed that Allah is pleased with. He said ﴿you will find it﴾, and the meaning is: you will find its reward, as:

1801- It was related to me from Ammar ibn al-Hasan, who said: Ibn Abi Ja'far related to us, from his father, from al-Rabi', regarding His words ﴿you will find it﴾: meaning, you will find its reward with Allah.

Abu Ja'far said: [This is] because the listeners to that are sufficiently informed by an apparent indication of the intended meaning, as 'Umar ibn La'ja said: [[In the printed edition: "Amr ibn La'ja," which is an error.]]

"The people of Medina glorified [Allah], do not blame them... they saw the moon in their market by day."* [[This verse has already passed with its takhrij at 1:279.]]

And what he meant was: "The people of Medina glorified [Allah]."

And in this place, He, may His praise be exalted, commanded them with what He commanded them: establishing prayer, giving zakah, and sending ahead good deeds for themselves, so that they might be purified thereby from the error that had preceded from them in seeking counsel from the Jews, and the inclination of those among them who had inclined towards them, and the harshness of those among them who had been harsh in addressing the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with the words ﴿Ra'ina﴾ — since the establishment of prayers is an expiation for sins, and giving zakah is a purification of souls and bodies from the defilements of sins, and in sending ahead good deeds is the attainment of success through the good pleasure of Allah.

* *

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿Indeed, Allah is Seeing of what you do (110)﴾

Abu Ja'far said: This is an information from Allah, may His praise be exalted, to those among the believers whom He addressed with these verses, that whatever good or evil they do, openly or secretly, He is Seeing of it, and nothing of it is hidden from Him, so He will recompense them for good with good, and for evil with its like. [[In the printed edition: "jaza'ahu" (its recompense), and the correct reading is from Tafsir Ibn Kathir 1:281.]]

And although this speech comes in the form of information, it contains a promise and a warning, a command and a prohibition. That is because He informed the people that He sees all their deeds, so that they would strive in obedience to Him, since that is stored up for them with Him until He rewards them for it, as He said: ﴿And whatever good you put forward for yourselves - you will find it with Allah﴾; and so that they would beware of disobeying Him, since He is watching the one who commits it, after He has warned them in advance concerning it with a threat. What our Lord, may His praise be exalted, threatens against is forbidden, and what He promises reward for is commanded.

* *

As for His words: ﴿Seeing (baṣīr)﴾, it is a transformed form of "mubṣir" (one who sees), changed to "baṣīr," just as "mubdi'" was changed to "badī'" and "mu'lim" to "alīm" [i.e., "alīm" from "mu'lim"]. [[See what has passed: 1:283, and this part 2:140, 377.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 111:

The explanation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿And they say: None will enter Paradise except those who were Jews or Christians. Those are their wishful thinking.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His words, may His praise be majestic, ﴿And they say﴾, He means: the Jews and the Christians said: ﴿None will enter Paradise﴾.

* *

If someone says: How did He combine the Jews and the Christians in this report, given that the statements of the two groups differ? The Jews reject the Christians from having any share in God's reward, and the Christians reject the Jews from the same?

It is said: The meaning of that is other than what you have understood. What is meant is: the Jews said, "None will enter Paradise except those who were Jews," and the Christians said, "None will enter Paradise except the Christians." But since the meaning of the speech was understood by those addressed, the two groups were combined in the report about them, so it is said: ﴿And they say: None will enter Paradise except those who were Jews or Christians﴾, the verse—that is, the Jews said: "None will enter Paradise except one who was a Jew," and the Christians said: "None will enter Paradise except one who was a Christian."

* *

As for His words ﴿hudan﴾ (Jews), there are two opinions regarding "al-Hud." One is that it is the plural of "ha'id" (one who repents), as "'uwut" is the plural of "'a'it," "'uwudh" the plural of "'a'idh," and "hul" the plural of "ha'il," so that it is a plural applying to the masculine and feminine with one form. "Al-ha'id" is the one who repents and returns to the truth. [[See what has passed in this volume, 2:143.]]

The other is that it is a verbal noun (masdar) applying to all, as one says "rajul sawm, wa-qawm sawm" (a man who fasts, and people who fast), and "rajul fitr, wa-qawm fitr, wa-nuswa fitr." [[I fear that Abu Ja'far has slipped in the manner of a hasty one. For he mentioned earlier (2:143) the verbal noun of the verb "hada," which is "hudan" with a fatha and then sukun, and the consensus of the lexicographers is upon that; no verbal noun with a damma on the ha' has come from it, so that it would resemble their saying "sawm" and "fitr," which are both verbal nouns. Abu Ja'far's statement does not stand unless there is a verbal noun "hada yahudu hudan" with a damma on the ha', and neither he nor anyone else has said it. So this view falls, until you establish it with a sound transmitted report.]]

It has been said that His words ﴿illa man kana hudan﴾ are in fact "illa man kana yahudiyyan," but He dropped the extra ya' and returned to the verb from "al-yahudiyya." It has also been said that in the reading of Ubayy it is: "illa man kana yahudiyyan aw nasraniyyan." [[See the Ma'ani al-Qur'an of al-Farra' 1:73.]]

* *

We have already explained what "al-Nasara" means, and why they were so named and so pluralized, in a manner that suffices without repeating it. [[See what has passed in this volume, 2:143-145.]]

* *

As for His words ﴿Those are their wishful thinking﴾, it is a report from God, may His remembrance be exalted, about the statement of those who said: ﴿None will enter Paradise except those who were Jews or Christians﴾, that they are wishes which they desire of God without right, proof, or demonstration, and without certain knowledge of the soundness of what they claim, but by asserting falsehoods and the wishes of lying souls, as:

1802- Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Zurai' narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿Those are their wishful thinking﴾, wishes they desire of God, false.

1803- Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi': ﴿Those are their wishful thinking﴾, he said: wishes they desired of God without the truth.

* *

The explanation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿Say: Bring your proof, if you are truthful﴾ (111)

Abu Ja'far said: This is a command from God, may His praise be majestic, to His Prophet ﷺ to call upon those who said: "None will enter Paradise except those who were Jews or Christians"—to a just judgment between all the sects: its Muslims, its Jews, and its Christians. It is the establishing of proof against their claim which they asserted: that Paradise will not be entered except by one who was a Jew or a Christian. God says to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: O Muhammad, say to those who claim that Paradise will not be entered except by one who was a Jew or a Christian, to the exclusion of all other mankind: ﴿Bring your proof﴾ for what you claim in this, and we will accept your claim, if you in your claim—that Paradise will not be entered except by one who was a Jew or a Christian—are truthful.

* *

Al-burhan (proof): it is the clarification, the argument, and the evidence, as:

1804- Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Zurai' narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿Bring your proof﴾, bring your evidence.

1805- Musa narrated to me, saying: Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿Bring your proof﴾, bring your argument.

1806- Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid: ﴿Say: Bring your proof﴾, he said: your argument. [[In the printed edition it read "Al-Hasan narrated to us," which is an error; the isnad is circular, and al-Husayn is al-Husayn ibn Dawud al-Massisi, known by the epithet "Sunayd."]]

1807- Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi': ﴿Say: Bring your proof﴾, i.e., your argument.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: Although this statement apparently resembles the call of those who said ﴿None will enter Paradise except those who were Jews or Christians⁠﴾ to produce a proof for their claim, it means a rebuke from God against them in their claim and their saying, because they were never able to produce a proof for that claim at any time. His words ﴿Yes, whoever submits his face to God while being a doer of good﴾ have made clear that the statement we have mentioned means a refutation of the Jews and Christians in their claim of what God mentioned about them.

* *

As for the interpretation of His words ﴿Say: Bring your proof﴾, it means: produce it and bring it forth.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 112:

The explanation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿Yes, whoever submits his face to Allah while being a doer of good﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His, the Majestic's, words ﴿Yes, whoever submits﴾, He means: it is not as the claimants said, ﴿None will enter Paradise except those who were Jews or Christians﴾, but rather whoever submits his face to Allah while being a doer of good, it is he who will enter it and be blessed therein, as:

1809- Musa related to me, saying: Amr related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, who said: "He informed them that whoever enters Paradise is the one who submits his face to Allah," (the verse).

* *

We have already explained the meaning of ﴿bala (yes)﴾ earlier. [[See what has preceded in this volume 2: 280, 281.]]

* *

As for His words ﴿whoever submits his face to Allah﴾, by "submission of the face" He means: humbling oneself to His obedience and yielding to His command. The origin of "Islam" (submission) is "istislam" (surrender), because one says "I surrendered (istaslamtu) to his command," meaning I submitted to his command. The "Muslim" is so called because his limbs submit to the obedience of his Lord. As:

1810- Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Ishaq related to us, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far related to us, from his father, from al-Rabi', regarding ﴿Yes, whoever submits his face﴾, he said: "He sincerely devotes himself to Allah."

And as Zayd ibn 'Amr ibn Nufayl said:

"And I submitted my face to the One to whom the clouds have submitted,
Carrying sweet, pure water."

[[Sirat Ibn Hisham 1: 246 and elsewhere.]]

He means by this: I surrendered to the obedience of Him to whom the clouds surrendered and whom they obeyed.

* *

Allah, the Exalted, specified in the report about those of whom He spoke in His words ﴿Yes, whoever submits his face to Allah﴾, the submission of the face to Him, rather than the rest of the limbs, because the most honoured of the members and limbs of the son of Adam is his face, and it is the greatest of them in sanctity and right. So when the face, which is the most honoured part of his body, submits to something, the other parts of his body are all the more fitting to be submissive to it. For this reason, the Arabs, in their speech, describe a thing and attribute it to its "face," meaning by that the very thing and its essence, as the saying of al-A'sha:

"I interpret the judgment in its face;
My judgment is not by unjust desire."

[[His Diwan: 106, from his famous qasida, in the contest between Alqama ibn Ulatha and Amir ibn al-Tufayl, in which al-A'sha satirised Alqama over a matter between them and preferred Amir over him. (See al-Aghani 15: 50-56). "Awwal al-hukm": he estimated it, arranged it, and returned it to its correctness and origin. "Al-jair": one who deviates from the path of truth. Jara: wronged, and deviated. Before the verse: "Alqama, do not be foolish, and do not make your honour exposed to the one who comes and goes..."
After it: "You have said a word and so judged between you, and the one who was reproached acknowledged it to the one who reproached."]]

He means by His words "in its face": in accordance with what it truly is in its soundness and correctness. And as Dhu al-Rummah said:

"My resolve obeyed me, and the face of a matter became clear, a splitting matter whose cutting left no doubt,"

[[His Diwan: 560, praising Ubayd Allah ibn Umar ibn Ubayd Allah ibn Ma'mar al-Tamimi, at the end of the qasida, where he said after the verse: "She said: Ubayd Allah from the family of Ma'mar, to him, travel the camels, guided by their journeying."
His words "I obeyed my resolve" refer to what he had determined in himself; he says: I obeyed what my self had resolved upon. His words "a splitting matter" mean a course one undertakes. This is a metaphor. It is said: the camel's tooth splits (bazala) with bazul, meaning it cracked, split and appeared. From this it is said: he split the matter or opinion: he decided it. A "bazla' course" is one that separates truth from falsehood. So his words "a splitting matter" are an attribute of what he implied from his words "a course," and he used it in the masculine form, just as they used it in the masculine in saying "a splitting she-camel." "Al-khilaj" means doubt, hesitation, and dispute. He says: I obeyed what moved in my self, and it cleared to a plain course that had split and appeared, leaving the self no path of doubt or hesitation, when it said: aim for Ubayd Allah ibn Umar ibn Ubayd Allah ibn Ma'mar.]] He means: and the splitting matter was made clear, and it became evident; and similar to this, since the goodness and badness of everything lies in its face. And since in describing a thing, they describe its face with what they describe it by, this indicates the essence and self of the thing. Likewise the meaning of His, the Majestic's, words ﴿Yes, whoever submits his face to Allah﴾: He means only: Yes, whoever submits his body to Allah, his body humbling itself to Him in obedience, while being a doer of good in his submission with his body; for him is his reward with his Lord. He suffices with mentioning "the face" from mentioning "his body," since the speech indicates the meaning intended by mentioning "the face."

* *

As for His words ﴿while being a doer of good﴾, He means by it: in the state of his doing good. The interpretation of the speech: Yes, whoever sincerely devotes his obedience and worship to Allah, being a doer of good in that act.

* *

The explanation of His words: ﴿For him is his reward with his Lord, and no fear will be upon them, nor will they grieve﴾ (112)

Abu Ja'far said: By His, the Majestic's, words ﴿For him is his reward with his Lord﴾, He means: for the one who submits his face to Allah while doing good, his recompense and reward for his submission and obedience to his Lord is with Allah in his return.

* *

By His words ﴿and no fear will be upon them﴾, He means: upon those who submit their faces to Allah while doing good, those who sincerely devote the religion to Him, in the Hereafter, from His punishment and the torment of His Hellfire, and from what they have sent ahead of their deeds.

* *

By His words ﴿nor will they grieve﴾, He means: nor will they grieve over what they left behind in the world, nor that they would be prevented from the bliss prepared by Allah for the people of His obedience which they have sent ahead.

* *

As for why He, the Majestic, said ﴿no fear will be upon them nor will they grieve﴾ after having said ﴿for him is his reward with his Lord﴾: this is because the "man" (min) in His words ﴿Yes, whoever submits his face to Allah﴾ is singular in wording and plural in meaning. So the singular in ﴿for him is his reward﴾ is for the wording, and the plural in ﴿no fear will be upon them﴾ is for the meaning.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 113:

The discussion of the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And the Jews say, "The Christians are not upon anything," and the Christians say, "The Jews are not upon anything," while they recite the Scripture﴾

Abu Ja'far said: It is mentioned that this verse was revealed concerning a group of the People of the Two Scriptures who disputed in the presence of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and some of them said to others.

Mention of those who said this:

1811 - Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salamah related to us. And Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Yunus ibn Bukayr related to us; both of them said: Muhammad ibn Ishaq related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, mawla (client) of Zayd ibn Thabit, related to me, saying: Sa'id ibn Jubayr or Ikrimah related to me, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: When the Christians of Najran came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), the rabbis of the Jews came to them, and they disputed in the presence of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Rafi' ibn Huraymilah said: "You are not upon anything," and he disbelieved in 'Isa ibn Maryam and in the Gospel. A man from the Christians of Najran said: "You are not upon anything," and he denied the prophethood of Musa and disbelieved in the Torah. So Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed concerning that, from their words: ﴿And the Jews say, "The Christians are not upon anything," and the Christians say, "The Jews are not upon anything"﴾, up to His words: ﴿concerning that wherein they used to differ﴾. [[Report 1811 - in Ibn Hisham's Sirah 2: 197-198.]]

1812 - It was related to me from 'Ammar, who said: Ibn Abi Ja'far related to us, from his father, from al-Rabi' concerning His words: ﴿And the Jews say, "The Christians are not upon anything," and the Christians say, "The Jews are not upon anything"﴾. He said: These are the People of the Scripture who were in the time of the Prophet (ﷺ).

* *

Abu Ja'far said: As for the interpretation of the verse: the Jews said, "The Christians are not correct in their religion!" and the Christians said, "The Jews are not correct in their religion!" Allah informed the believers of their saying that as a notice from Him to them of the loss by each group of them of the ruling of the Scripture which they profess the truth of and that it is from Allah, and their denial, along with that, of what Allah revealed in it of its obligations. For the Gospel, whose authenticity and truth the Christians hold to, confirms what is in the Torah of the prophethood of Musa, peace be upon him, and of the obligations Allah imposed upon the Children of Israel in it. And the Torah, whose authenticity and truth the Jews hold to, confirms the prophethood of 'Isa, peace be upon him, and what he brought from Allah of rulings and obligations.

Then each group said to the other what Allah reported of them in His words: ﴿And the Jews say, "The Christians are not upon anything," and the Christians say, "The Jews are not upon anything"﴾, while each of the two groups recites its Scripture, which testifies to the falsehood of their saying that. So He, majestic is His praise, informed that each group of them said what they said, knowing that in what they said they were falsifiers; and they committed what they committed of disbelief with what they disbelieved in, with knowledge on their part that they were deviators in it.

If someone says to us: Were the Jews and the Christians upon anything after Allah sent His Messenger, so that the group saying that to the other group would be a falsifier in its saying it?

It is said: We have already related the report we mentioned from Ibn 'Abbas, that the denial of each group of them was only a denial of the prophethood of the Prophet (ﷺ), which the other group claims to affirm, and of what the other group brought, not a repudiation by them that the other group was, in the state in which Allah sent our Prophet (ﷺ), upon anything of its religion, because of its denial of the prophethood of our Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ). And how could it be permissible that the meaning of that be each group's denial that the other group was upon anything after the mission of our Prophet (ﷺ), when both groups were denying the prophethood of our Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) in the state in which Allah revealed this verse? Rather, the meaning of that is: The Jews said: "The Christians are not upon anything of their religion since they adopted their religion, and the Christians said: The Jews are not upon anything since they adopted their religion." And that is the meaning of the report we related from Ibn 'Abbas just before. So Allah denied both groups in what the two of them said. As:

1813 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah concerning His words: ﴿And the Jews say, "The Christians are not upon anything"﴾. He said: Yes! The early Christians were indeed upon something, but they innovated and split apart. And the Christians said: ﴿The Jews are not upon anything﴾, but these people innovated and split apart.

1814 - Al-Qasim related to us, saying: Al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj: ﴿And the Jews say, "The Christians are not upon anything," and the Christians say, "The Jews are not upon anything"﴾. He said: Mujahid said: The early Jews and Christians were indeed upon something.

* *

As for His words: ﴿while they recite the Scripture﴾, He means by it the Book of Allah, the Torah and the Gospel, and both of them are witnesses against the two groups of Jews and Christians of disbelief, and of their opposition to the command of Allah that He commanded them in it. As:

1815 - Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Yunus ibn Bukayr related to us - and Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salamah ibn al-Fadl related to us - both of them said: Ibn Ishaq related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, mawla of Zayd ibn Thabit, related to me, saying: Sa'id ibn Jubayr or Ikrimah related to me, from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His words: ﴿while they recite the Scripture. Thus said those who do not know the like of their saying﴾. That is, each one recites in its book the confirmation of what it disbelieves in: the Jews disbelieve in 'Isa while they have the Torah, in which is what Allah took from them of the covenant through the tongue of Musa, to affirm 'Isa, peace be upon him; and in the Gospel is what 'Isa brought, confirming Musa and what he brought of the Torah from Allah. And each disbelieves in what is in the hand of the other. [[Report 1815 - in Ibn Hisham's Sirah 2: 198.]]

* *

The discussion of the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Thus said those who do not know, the like of their saying﴾

Abu Ja'far said: The people of interpretation differed concerning those whom Allah meant by His words: ﴿Thus said those who do not know﴾. Some of them said:

1816 - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Ishaq related to us, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far related to us, from his father, from al-Rabi': ﴿Those who do not know said the like of their saying﴾. He said: The Christians said the like of the saying of the Jews before them.

1817 - Bishr ibn Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah: ﴿Those who do not know said the like of their saying﴾. He said: The Christians said the like of the saying of the Jews before them.

* *

And others said:

1818 - Al-Qasim related to us, saying: Al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, saying: Ibn Jurayj said: I said to 'Ata': Who are these who do not know? He said: Nations that were before the Jews and the Christians, and before the Torah and the Gospel.

* *

And some of them said: He meant by that the polytheists of the Arabs, because they were not People of a Scripture, so they were attributed to ignorance, and knowledge was negated of them for that reason.

Mention of those who said that:

1819 - Musa ibn Harun related to me, saying: 'Amr related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿Thus said those who do not know the like of their saying﴾. They are the Arabs, who said: Muhammad (ﷺ) is not upon anything.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct view in this matter, in our opinion, is to say: Allah, blessed and exalted, informed about a people whom He described as ignorant, and negated from them the knowledge that the Jews and Christians possessed - that they said, in their ignorance, a counterpart of what the Jews and Christians said to one another, which Allah reported of them in His words: ﴿And the Jews say, "The Christians are not upon anything," and the Christians say, "The Jews are not upon anything"﴾. It is possible that they were the polytheists of the Arabs, and it is possible that they were a nation that existed before the Jews and Christians. Neither nation is more deserving than the other of being said to be the one meant by that, since there is no indication in the verse as to which of them, and no report from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) whose proof is established by way of a single reliable transmitter, nor by way of a widely transmitted report.

Allah, majestic is His praise, intended by His words: ﴿Thus said those who do not know, the like of their saying﴾, to inform the believers that the Jews and Christians had come with the saying of falsehood, and the fabrication of lies against Allah, and the denial of the prophethood of the prophets and messengers, while they are People of a Scripture who know that in what they say they are falsifiers, and by their denial of what they deny they have departed from their religion, and are fabricators against Allah - like what was said by the people of ignorance of Allah, His Books, and His Messengers, to whom Allah did not send a messenger nor reveal a book.

This verse indicates that whoever commits some of the acts of disobedience to Allah with knowledge of Allah's prohibition of them, his affliction in his religion is greater than the affliction of one who commits it in ignorance. For Allah, exalted is His remembrance, magnified the rebuke of the Jews and Christians for what He rebuked them for in their saying which He reported of them in His words: ﴿And the Jews say, "The Christians are not upon anything," and the Christians say, "The Jews are not upon anything"﴾, because they were People of a Scripture who said what they said with knowledge that they were falsifiers.

* *

The discussion of the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿So Allah will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that wherein they used to differ﴾ (113)

Abu Ja'far said: By this He, majestic is His praise, means: Allah will decide and separate between these disputants, those saying to one another "You are not upon anything of your religion," on the Day when creation stands before their Lord from their graves, so that the one upheld is distinguished from the falsifier: by rewarding the upheld with what He promised the people of His obedience for their righteous deeds, and by requiting the falsifier among them with what He threatened the people of disbelief with for their disbelief - concerning that wherein they used to differ about their religions and creeds in the house of the world.

* *

As for "al-Qiyamah" (the Resurrection), it is a verbal noun from the speaker's saying: "qumtu qiyaman wa qiyamah" (I stood, standing and resurrection), just as one says: "'adtu fulanan 'iyadah" (I visited so-and-so as a visitor) and "suntu hadha al-amr siyanah" (I guarded this matter with protection).

* *

He meant by "al-Qiyamah" only the standing of creatures from their graves before their Lord. So the meaning of "Yawm al-Qiyamah" (the Day of Resurrection) is: the day when the creatures stand up from their graves for their gathering.

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 114:**

The discussion of the interpretation (*ta'wil*, the explanation of what a verse means) of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And who is more unjust than one who prevents the mosques of God from having His name mentioned in them and strives for their ruin﴾

Abu Ja'far said: We have already shown earlier that the meaning of *zulm* (injustice) is placing a thing in other than its proper place. [[See what has passed: 1: 523-524, and this part 2: 101-102, 369]] The interpretation of His words ﴿And who is more unjust﴾ means: what man is more transgressive, more audacious toward God, and more opposed to His command, than a man who prevents the mosques of God from having God worshipped in them?

* *

"Al-masajid" (the mosques) is the plural of *masjid*, which is every place where God is worshipped. We have already explained the meaning of prostration (*sujud*) earlier. [[See what has passed in this part 2: 104-105.]] So the meaning of *masjid* is the place in which one prostrates to God, just as the place where one sits is called *majlis* and the place where one alights is called *manzil*, and their plurals are *manazil* and *majalis*, on the pattern of *masjid* and *masajid*. It has been transmitted by hearing from some Arabs that *masajid* is used as the singular of *masajid*, but that is like an error on the part of the one who said it.

* *

As for His words ﴿that His name be mentioned in them﴾, there are two possible interpretations. The first is that its meaning is: "And who is more unjust than one who prevents the mosques of God from having His name mentioned in them," so that *an* (that) would then be in the accusative according to the view of some grammarians, by the omission of the preposition, and the verb is connected to it.

The second interpretation is that its meaning is: "And who is more unjust than one who prevents the mention of God's name in His mosques," so that *an* would then be in the accusative position as a substitution (*takrir*, here meaning *badal al-ishtimal*, substitution of inclusion) for the position of "the mosques" and a restatement of it. [[His words "takrir" mean badal al-ishtimal (substitution by inclusion).]]

* *

As for His words ﴿and strives for their ruin﴾, its meaning is: "And who is more unjust than one who prevents the mosques of God from having His name mentioned in them, and than one who strives for the ruin of the mosques of God." So "strives" (*sa'a*) is a conjunction (*'atf*) to "prevents" (*man'a*).

* *

If someone asks: Who is meant by His words ﴿And who is more unjust than one who prevents the mosques of God from having His name mentioned in them and strives for their ruin﴾? And which mosques are they?

It is said: The people of interpretation differ about this. Some of them said: Those who prevented the mosques of God from having His name mentioned in them are the Christians, and the mosque is the Holy House (Bayt al-Maqdis, Jerusalem).

Mention of those who said this:

1820. Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: My father related to me, saying: My paternal uncle related to me, saying: My father related to me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding His words ﴿And who is more unjust than one who prevents the mosques of God from having His name mentioned in them﴾, that they are the Christians.

1821. Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Najih, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the saying of God: ﴿And who is more unjust than one who prevents the mosques of God from having His name mentioned in them and strives for their ruin﴾: The Christians used to throw filth into the Holy House and prevent people from praying in it.

1822. Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah related to us, saying: Shibl related to us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Najih, on the authority of Mujahid, the same.

* *

Others said: It is Bukhtansar (Nebuchadnezzar) and his army, and those among the Christians who helped them, and the mosque is the mosque of the Holy House.

Mention of those who said this:

1823. Bishr ibn Mu'adh related to us, saying: Yazid ibn Zuray' related to us, on the authority of Sa'id, on the authority of Qatadah regarding His words ﴿And who is more unjust than one who prevents the mosques of God from having His name mentioned in them﴾, the verse: Those are the enemies of God, the Christians. The hatred of the Jews drove them to help Bukhtansar the Babylonian, the Magian, in the destruction of the Holy House.

1824. Al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, on the authority of Qatadah regarding His words ﴿And who is more unjust than one who prevents the mosques of God from having His name mentioned in them and strives for their ruin﴾, he said: It is Bukhtansar and his companions, who ruined the Holy House, and the Christians helped him in that.

1825. Musa related to me, saying: Amr related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, on the authority of al-Suddi: ﴿And who is more unjust than one who prevents the mosques of God from having His name mentioned in them and strives for their ruin﴾, he said: The Romans. They supported Bukhtansar in the ruin of the Holy House until he destroyed it, and he ordered that carrion be thrown into it. The Romans only helped him in its ruin because the Children of Israel had killed Yahya ibn Zakariyya (John the son of Zechariah).

* *

Others said: Rather, God, mighty and majestic is He, meant by this verse the polytheists of Quraysh, when they prevented the Messenger of God (ﷺ) from the Sacred Mosque.

Mention of those who said this:

1826. Yunus ibn Abd al-A'la related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb related to us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words ﴿And who is more unjust than one who prevents the mosques of God from having His name mentioned in them and strives for their ruin﴾: These are the polytheists, when they stood between the Messenger of God (ﷺ) on the day of Hudaybiyyah and entering Makkah, until he slaughtered his offering at Dhu Tuwa and made a truce with them. He said to them: "No one has ever been turned back from this House, and a man used to meet the killer of his father or brother in it, and he would not be prevented." They said: "The one who killed our fathers on the day of Badr will not enter upon us while there is one of us left!"

And regarding His words ﴿and strives for their ruin﴾, he said: When they cut off those who would maintain it by mentioning God in it [[In the printed edition: "qalu idha qat'u", and the correct reading from Tafsir Ibn Kathir 1: 285 is this, as it is part of the report, and the speaker is Ibn Zayd.]] and come to it for Hajj and 'Umrah.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of the interpretations I have mentioned for the explanation of this verse is the saying of the one who said: God, mighty and majestic is He, meant by His words ﴿And who is more unjust than one who prevents the mosques of God from having His name mentioned in them﴾ the Christians. That is because they are the ones who strove for the ruin of the Holy House, and helped Bukhtansar in that, and prevented the believing Children of Israel from praying in it after Bukhtansar had departed from them to his lands.

The proof of the correctness of what we have said in this matter is that the argument is established that there is no statement regarding the meaning of this verse except one of the three sayings we have mentioned, and that the mosque meant by God, mighty and majestic is He, in His words ﴿and strives for their ruin﴾ is only one of the two mosques: either the mosque of the Holy House, or the Sacred Mosque. Since that is so, and since it is known that the polytheists of Quraysh never strove in the ruin of the Sacred Mosque, even though they did prevent the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and his companions from praying in it at some times, it is established and confirmed that those whom God described as striving for the ruin of His mosques are not those whom God described as maintaining them. For the polytheists of Quraysh had built the Sacred Mosque in the pre-Islamic period, and their pride was in its maintenance, and though some of their actions in it were done in a way that God would not be pleased with.

Another proof: the verse before His words ﴿And who is more unjust than one who prevents the mosques of God from having His name mentioned in them﴾ speaks of the Jews and Christians and censures their deeds, and the verse after it warns against the Christians and reports their fabrications against their Lord, and there is no mention of Quraysh, nor of the polytheists of the Arabs, nor of the Sacred Mosque before it, so that the report by the words of God, "And who is more unjust than one who prevents the mosques of God from having His name mentioned in them," would be directed toward them and toward the Sacred Mosque.

Since that is so, the interpretation most fitting to direct the verse toward is that which is parallel to the story of the verse before it and the verse after it, since its report is parallel to theirs in form and kind, unless a proof that must be accepted establishes otherwise, even if their narratives agree and are thereby confused.

[[Ibn Kathir wished to refute what al-Tabari adopted in interpreting the verse, in his Tafsir 1: 285/287, and said: "Ibn Jarir chose the first saying, arguing that Quraysh did not strive for the ruin of the Ka'bah, whereas the Romans did strive for the destruction of the Holy House." Ibn Kathir said: "What appears, and God knows best, is the second saying, as said by Ibn Zayd..." Then he said: "As for his reliance on the fact that Quraysh did not strive for the ruin of the Ka'bah, what ruin is greater than what they did? They expelled the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and his companions, and seized it with their idols, their rivals, and their polytheism..."

Then he cited verses from the Book of God and said: "The purpose of its maintenance is not its ornamentation and the erection of its structure only, but its maintenance is by mentioning God in it and establishing His law in it," and so on to the end of what he said.

This objection of Ibn Kathir against Abu Ja'far, may God have mercy on them both, does not stand against the argument of al-Tabari for the correctness of what he adopted in interpreting the verse. Al-Tabari was not unaware of an objection like Ibn Kathir's, but Ibn Kathir overlooked the context of al-Tabari's interpretation. It is true that what the polytheists of the pre-Islamic period did regarding the Sacred House falls within the general meaning of His words ﴿and strives for their ruin﴾, but the context of the preceding verses, and then the following ones, requires, as al-Tabari held, that the one meant be the one whose story the verses were revealed about.

All the preceding verses are a report about the Children of Israel who were in the time of Moses, and a rebuke to the Children of Israel who were among the migrants of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), then what they did against the believers, the companions of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), then a warning from the People of the Book in general, Jews and Christians alike, and a mention of the fabrication of each of the two groups against the other, and each group's claim that it is the saved group on the Day of Resurrection. Then after that he singled out the reports about the Christians, just as he had earlier singled out the reports about the Children of Israel. He enumerated their evil conduct in preventing the mosques of God from having His name mentioned in them, then their lying against their Lord that He had taken a son, then the saying of some of them: ﴿Why does God not speak to us or a sign come to us?﴾, and that this resembled the saying of the Jews: ﴿Show us God openly﴾. Then He informed that He had sent His Messenger Muhammad as a bringer of good news and a warner, and commanded him to turn away from the people of the Fire from these and those, then He declared that the Jews and Christians together would never be pleased with him until he follows their creed and their path in fabricating against the Lord of the worlds. So the context, as you see, has nothing to do with the polytheists of the Arabs. But Ibn Kathir and others among our imams, may God be pleased with them, have their meanings confused when they are close together. But Abu Ja'far was patient with the Book of his Lord, capable of bearing it, not hurried by anything from one thing to another as far as he could. He extracts the meanings of the Book of his Lord with an extraction I have never found from anyone after him who has read his book. Most of them object to him, and had they been patient with the precision of this imam, that would have been more fitting for him and more like the character of the people of knowledge, and they are worthy of it. May God forgive us and them.]]

If someone supposes that what we have said in this matter is not so, since the Muslims were never obligated to pray in the [sacred mosque, so they were prevented from praying in it, and they would be driven] to direct His words [[What is between the parentheses appears thus in the printed and the corrupt manuscript copies. I found no quotation from Abu Ja'far that guides me to correct this confusion. I endeavored to deduce the context of his speech. The closest I reached is that there is a lacuna and distortion in it, and that its context is as follows:

[Since the Muslims were the ones addressed by the verses preceding this verse, and the Muslims were never obligated to pray in the mosque of Bayt al-Maqdis, so they were prevented from praying in it, and the Christians and Jews never prevented them from praying in it, it is permissible to direct His words — {And who is more unjust than one who prevents the mosques of God from having His name mentioned in them} — to the meaning of the mosque of Bayt al-Maqdis.] This is my effort in reading this confused text, and God knows best.]] ﴿And who is more unjust than one who prevents the mosques of God from having His name mentioned in them﴾ to mean the mosque of Bayt al-Maqdis, then he has erred in what he supposed. That is because God, great is His mention, only mentioned the injustice of those who prevented those whose obligation was to pray in Bayt al-Maqdis from the believers among the Children of Israel, and it is them that the report about injustice and striving for the ruin of the mosque was intended for. Although the general wording of His words ﴿And who is more unjust than one who prevents the mosques of God from having His name mentioned in them﴾ indicates that every one who prevents a worshipper from praying in a mosque of God, whether the prayer there is obligatory or voluntary, and every one who strives for its ruin, is among the transgressors and the wrongdoers.

* *

The interpretation of His words, great is His mention: ﴿Those — it was not for them to enter them except in fear﴾

Abu Ja'far said: This is a report from God, mighty and majestic is He, about those who prevented the mosques of God from having His name mentioned in them: that He has forbidden them to enter the mosques they strove to ruin, and prevented the believing servants of God from mentioning God, mighty and majestic is He, in them, as long as they remain in hostility to war, except in fear and dread of punishment for entering them. As follows:

1827. Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, on the authority of Qatadah: ﴿It was not for them to enter them except in fear﴾, and they are so today: no Christian is found in Bayt al-Maqdis except that he is beaten severely and subjected to the greatest punishment.

1828. Al-Hasan related to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, on the authority of Qatadah: God, mighty and majestic is He, said: ﴿It was not for them to enter it except in fear﴾, and they are the Christians. They do not enter the mosque except furtively, and if they are caught, they are punished.

1829. Musa related to us, saying: Amr related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, on the authority of al-Suddi: ﴿Those — it was not for them to enter it except in fear﴾. There is no Roman in the earth who enters it today except that he is fearful that his neck will be struck, or he has been cowed by the payment of the poll-tax, so he pays it.

1830. Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words ﴿Those — it was not for them to enter it except in fear﴾: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) proclaimed: "No polytheist shall perform Hajj after this year, and no one shall circumambulate the House naked." He said: The polytheists began saying: "O God, we have been prevented from entering!"

* *

It was said ﴿Those — it was not for them to enter them except in fear﴾, and it was expressed in the form of a report about all of them, and it is a report about ﴿those who prevented the mosques of God from having His name mentioned in them﴾, because the word "man" (those who) carries the meaning of the plural, even though its form is singular. [[See what has passed in this part 2: 513.]]

* *

The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿For them in this world is disgrace, and for them in the Hereafter is a great punishment﴾ (114)

Abu Ja'far said: As for His words, mighty and majestic is He, ﴿For them﴾, it means: those about whom He reported that they prevented the mosques of God from having His name mentioned in them. As for His words ﴿For them in this world is disgrace﴾, it means by "disgrace": shame, evil, and humiliation [[See what has passed in this part 2: 314.]], whether it be killing and captivity, or abasement and humiliation through paying the poll-tax. As follows:

1831. Al-Hasan related to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq related to us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, on the authority of Qatadah: ﴿For them in this world is disgrace﴾, he said: They give the poll-tax from the hand while they are humbled.

1832. Musa related to us, saying: Amr related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, on the authority of al-Suddi regarding His words ﴿For them in this world is disgrace﴾: As for their disgrace in this world, when the Mahdi arises and Constantinople is conquered, he will kill them. That is the disgrace. As for the great punishment, it is the punishment of Hell, which is not lightened for its people, and no decree is passed upon them so that they die in it. The interpretation of the verse: For them in this world is abasement, humiliation, killing, and captivity, for their preventing the mosques of God from having His name mentioned in them and their striving for their ruin; and for them, for their disobedience and their disbelief in their Lord and their striving in the earth to cause corruption, is the punishment of Hell, and that is the great punishment.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 115 (part 1 of 2):

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿To Allah belong the east and the west; wherever you turn, there is the Face of Allah﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His saying, majestic is His praise, ﴿To Allah belong the east and the west﴾, He means: to Allah belongs their dominion and their management, just as one says, "This house belongs to so-and-so," meaning that it is his, as a possession. That is His saying, ﴿To Allah belong the east and the west﴾, meaning that they belong to Him, as possession and as creation.
* *
And "al-mashriq" (the east) is the place where the sun rises, the place of its rising, just as the place of its rising is called "matla'" (with a kasra on the lam), and as we have explained concerning the meaning of "al-masajid" (the mosques) earlier. [[See what has passed shortly before: 519.]]
* *
If someone says: Did Allah not have only one east and one west, so that it is said: ﴿To Allah belong the east and the west﴾? It is said: The meaning of that is other than what you have taken it to be. Rather, the meaning of that is: To Allah belongs the east from which the sun rises every day, and the west in which it sets every day. Its interpretation, given that this is its meaning, is: To Allah belongs what lies between the two extremes of the east and what lies between the two extremes of the west, since the sun rises every day from a place in it to which it does not return for its rising until the year after, and likewise it sets every day.
If he says: Is it not the case that, even if the interpretation of that is what you have mentioned, then all that is other than Him [[His saying "fa-lillahi kullu ma dunahu": that is, everything else besides Him from any thing.]] is His creation? It is said: Indeed!
If he says: Then why were the easts and the wests singled out in this report, that they belong to Him, in this place, rather than other things besides them?
It is said: The people of interpretation have differed concerning the reason for which Allah specified the mention of that with what He specified it with in this place. We shall explain which is more appropriate for the interpretation of the verse after we have mentioned their sayings on that. Some of them said: Allah, majestic is His praise, singled out that report because the Jews used to direct their faces in prayer toward Bayt al-Maqdis, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did likewise for a period, then they were turned toward the Ka'bah. The Jews found fault with this action of the Prophet ﷺ and said: "What turned them away from their qiblah which they had been upon?" So Allah, blessed and exalted, said to them: The easts and the wests are all Mine; I turn the faces of My servants wherever I will from among them, so wherever you turn, there is the Face of Allah.

Mention of those who said that:

1833- Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah ibn Salih related to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The first thing abrogated in the Qur'an was the qiblah. That was because when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ migrated to Madinah, and most of its people were Jews, Allah, mighty and majestic, commanded him to face Bayt al-Maqdis, and the Jews rejoiced. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ faced it for sixteen months or so, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ loved the qiblah of Ibrahim, peace be upon him, so he would supplicate and look toward the sky. Then Allah, blessed and exalted, revealed: ﴿We have certainly seen the turning of your face toward the sky﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 144] up to His saying: ﴿So turn your faces toward it﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 144-150]. The Jews were suspicious of that and said: ﴿What turned them away from their qiblah which they had been upon?﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 142]. So Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed: ﴿Say: To Allah belong the east and the west﴾, and He said: ﴿Wherever you turn, there is the Face of Allah﴾. [[The hadith: 1833 - 'Ali: he is Ibn Abi Talhah al-Hashimi: trustworthy, though people have spoken about him. The preferred view is that their speech about him was on account of his Shi'ism. But he did not hear from Ibn 'Abbas. Ibn Abi Hatim in al-Marasil, p. 52, related from Duhaym who said: "'Ali ibn Abi Talhah did not hear the tafsir from Ibn 'Abbas." Similar was related from his father Abu Hatim. In al-Tahdhib it is mentioned that Ibn Hibban mentioned him in al-Thiqat and said: "He related from Ibn 'Abbas but did not see him." So this chain is weak due to its disconnection.
But its meaning is established from Ibn 'Abbas through a sound route. Abu 'Ubayd al-Qasim ibn Salam related it in his book al-Nasikh wa al-Mansukh, as quoted by Ibn Kathir 1: 288: "Hajjaj ibn Muhammad informed us, Ibn Juraij and 'Uthman ibn 'Ata' informed us, from 'Ata', from Ibn 'Abbas..." and then he mentioned something similar. This chain is sound through Ibn Juraij's narration from 'Ata', who is Ibn Abi Rabah. As for "Uthman ibn 'Ata'", he is al-Khurasani, and he is weak. Hajjaj ibn Muhammad heard it from both, one trustworthy and one weak, so there is no harm. Al-Hakim related it 2: 267-268, through Ibn Juraij, from 'Ata', from Ibn 'Abbas, and said: "This hadith is sound according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs, though they did not record it with this wording." Al-Dhahabi agreed with him. And it is as they both said. Al-Suyuti mentioned it 1: 108, attributing it to Abu 'Ubayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Hakim who authenticated it, and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan.]]
1834- Musa related to me, saying: 'Amr related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, something similar.
* *
Others said: Rather, Allah revealed this verse before He made it obligatory upon His Prophet ﷺ and the believers in him to turn toward al-Masjid al-Haram. He revealed it to him only to inform His Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and his companions that they may turn their faces in prayer wherever they wished from the directions of the east and the west, because they do not turn their faces in any direction or to any side except that He, majestic is His praise, is in that direction and that side, since the easts and the wests are His, and since no place is void of Him, [[Ibn Kathir said in his tafsir 1: 289, commenting on the words of Abu Ja'far, may Allah have mercy on him: "As for his saying: 'and that He is not void of any place' - if he means His knowledge, then it is correct, for His knowledge encompasses all known things. But as for His Essence, exalted is He, it is not confined within any of His creation, exalted is Allah far above that." I say: What Ibn Kathir said is the creed of Abu Ja'far, may Allah have mercy on him, and he clarified that in the tafsir of Surah al-Mujadilah in his tafsir 28: 10, so there is no sense in Ibn Kathir's doubt about the speech of a precise imam of the imams of the people of truth. His expression is correct in wording, but the people of desires made people understand from the Arabic of eloquent speakers a meaning other than what it indicates.]] as He, majestic and exalted, said: ﴿And there is no private conversation of three but that He is the fourth of them, nor of five but that He is the sixth, nor less than that or more but that He is with them wherever they are﴾ [Al-Mujadilah: 7]. They said: Then that was abrogated by the obligation which was imposed upon them to turn toward al-Masjid al-Haram.

Mention of those who said that:

1835- Bishr ibn Mu'adh related to us, saying: Yazid ibn Zuray' related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, concerning His saying, majestic and exalted: ﴿To Allah belong the east and the west; wherever you turn, there is the Face of Allah﴾, then that was abrogated afterward, when Allah said: ﴿And from wherever you go out, turn your face toward al-Masjid al-Haram﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 149-150].
1836- Al-Hasan related to us [[In the printed edition: "I was told from al-Hasan", and the correct reading is what is established here; it is a chain recurring in his tafsir, the nearest of which is number 1731.]] saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah concerning His saying: ﴿Wherever you turn, there is the Face of Allah﴾, he said: It is the qiblah, then the qiblah toward al-Masjid al-Haram abrogated it.
1837- Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: al-Hajjaj ibn al-Minhal related to us, saying: Hammam related to us, saying: Yahya related to us, saying: I heard Qatadah concerning Allah's saying: ﴿Wherever you turn, there is the Face of Allah﴾, he said: They used to pray facing Bayt al-Maqdis while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was in Makkah before the migration, and after the Messenger of Allah ﷺ migrated, he prayed facing Bayt al-Maqdis for sixteen months, then he was turned afterward toward the Ka'bah, the Sacred House. Allah abrogated it in another verse: ﴿So We will surely turn you to a qiblah that you will be pleased with﴾ up to ﴿And wherever you are, turn your faces toward it﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 144]. He said: This verse abrogated what came before it concerning the matter of the qiblah.
1838- Yunus related to us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: I heard him - meaning Zayd - say: He, majestic and exalted, said to His Prophet ﷺ: ﴿Wherever you turn, there is the Face of Allah. Indeed, Allah is All-Encompassing, All-Knowing﴾. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "These are a people of Jews who face a house of the houses of Allah; if only we faced it!" So the Prophet ﷺ faced it for sixteen months. Then it reached him that the Jews were saying: "By Allah, Muhammad and his companions did not know where their qiblah was until we guided them!" The Prophet ﷺ disliked that and raised his face toward the sky, so Allah, majestic and exalted, said: ﴿We have certainly seen the turning of your face toward the sky﴾, the verse [Al-Baqarah: 144].
* *
Others said: This verse was revealed to the Prophet ﷺ as a permission from Allah, majestic and exalted, for him to offer voluntary prayer wherever his face turned, east or west, while on his journey during travel, in a state of close fighting, in intense fear, and in the meeting of armies during obligatory prayers. He informed him that wherever he turned his face, he was there, by His saying: ﴿To Allah belong the east and the west; wherever you turn, there is the Face of Allah﴾.

Mention of those who said that:

1839- Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Ibn Idris related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Malik related to us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Umar, that he used to pray wherever his mount turned with him, and he mentioned that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to do that, and he interpreted this verse: ﴿Wherever you turn, there is the Face of Allah﴾. [[The hadith: 1839 - Ibn Idris: he is Abdullah ibn Idris al-Awdi, whose authentication has already passed: 438. 'Abd al-Malik: he is Ibn Abi Sulayman, as will come in the next chain, and his authentication has already passed: 1455.
This hadith was related by Ahmad in al-Musnad: 5001, from Abdullah ibn Idris, with this chain. The complete takhrij will come in the one after it.]]
1840- Abu al-Sa'ib related to me, saying: Ibn Fudayl related to us, from 'Abd al-Malik ibn Abi Sulayman, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Umar, that he said: "This verse was only revealed: ﴿Wherever you turn, there is the Face of Allah﴾ - that you may pray wherever your mount turns with you on a journey, voluntarily. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ, when he returned from Makkah, would pray on his mount voluntarily, gesturing with his head toward Madinah." [[The hadith: 1840 - Ibn Fudayl: he is Muhammad ibn Fudayl ibn Ghazwan al-Dabbi, who is trustworthy, one of the shaykhs of Ahmad and Ishaq and others. Indeed al-Thawri related from him, though he was older than him. He is biographied in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir 1/1/1207-208, and Ibn Abi Hatim 4/1/57-58.
This hadith was also related by Ahmad: 4714, from Yahya al-Qattan, from 'Abd al-Malik ibn Abi Sulayman, something similar. Muslim related it 1: 195, through Yahya and others. Likewise al-Bayhaqi related it in al-Sunan al-Kubra 2: 4, with chains through 'Abd al-Malik.
We have preferred, in the explanation of the Musnad, the earlier narration, that this verse was not revealed concerning that; rather, it has a more general meaning, and it only serves as evidence and proof, as becomes clear from the jurisprudence of its interpretation in its context.]]
* *
Others said: Rather, this verse was revealed concerning a people for whom the qiblah had been obscured, so they did not know its direction, and they prayed in various directions. Allah, majestic and exalted, said to them: To Me belong the easts and the wests; wherever you turn your faces, there is My Face, [[In the printed edition: "fa-in waliytum wujuhakum". The correct reading is what is established.]] and it is your qiblah, informing them by that that their prayer is valid.

Mention of those who said that:

1841- Ahmad related to us, saying: Abu Ahmad related to us, saying: Abu al-Rabi' al-Samman related to us, from 'Asim ibn 'Ubaydullah, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Amir ibn Rabi'ah, from his father, who said: "We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on a dark, black night, and we alighted at a station, and a man would take stones and make a mosque to pray in. When we awoke, we found that we had prayed other than toward the qiblah. We said: 'O Messenger of Allah, we prayed this night toward other than the qiblah.' So Allah, majestic and exalted, revealed: ﴿To Allah belong the east and the west; wherever you turn, there is the Face of Allah. Indeed, Allah is All-Encompassing, All-Knowing﴾." [[The hadith: 1841 - Ahmad, the shaykh of al-Tabari: he is Ahmad ibn Ishaq ibn 'Isa al-Ahwazi, whose full lineage was mentioned earlier at 159; he is truthful, one of the shaykhs of Abu Dawud, biographied in al-Tahdhib. Abu Ahmad: he is al-Zubayri, whose name is Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr ibn 'Umar ibn Dirham; he is trustworthy and a memorizer, one of the shaykhs of Imam Ahmad, biographied in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir 1/1/133-134, Ibn Sa'd 6: 281, and Ibn Abi Hatim 3/2/297. Abu al-Rabi' al-Samman: he is Ash'ath ibn Sa'id, whom we noted at 24 as very weak. 'Asim ibn 'Ubaydullah ibn 'Asim ibn 'Umar ibn al-Khattab: he is weak, and we explained his weakness in the explanation of the Musnad: 5229.
'Abdullah ibn 'Amir ibn Rabi'ah: trustworthy, one of the senior Successors. His father is a well-known companion, one of the earliest emigrants, who made both migrations and witnessed Badr and all the battles.
Ibn Kathir mentioned the hadith 1: 289-290, from this place. There is an error in the name of al-Tabari's shaykh, where it was written "Muhammad ibn Ishaq" instead of "Ahmad"; this is a scribal or printer's error. Then Ibn Kathir pointed to its later narration: 1843. Then he mentioned that al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Majah, and Ibn Abi Hatim also related it. Then he quoted al-Tirmidhi's statement: "This hadith's chain is not of that quality; we only know it from the hadith of Ash'ath al-Samman, and Ash'ath ibn Sa'id Abu al-Rabi' al-Samman is weakened in hadith." Ibn Kathir said: "I say: its shaykh 'Asim is also weak; al-Bukhari said: munkar al-hadith. Ibn Ma'in said: weak, not to be used as proof. Ibn Hibban said: abandoned."
I had, in my explanation of al-Tirmidhi, number 345, leaned toward grading its chain as good. But I now retract that, and I consider it a weak hadith.
Al-Suyuti quoted it 1: 109, with its takhrij and an explanation of its weakness.]]
1842- Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: al-Hajjaj related to me, saying: Hammad related to us, saying: I said to al-Nakha'i: "I had awoken - or said 'I was awakened,' al-Tabari is in doubt - [[The word "ayqazt" (I was awakened) intransitively is not recorded in the lexicons; I fear al-Tabari is correcting it, and similar forms in Arabic are numerous.]] and there was cloud in the sky, so I prayed toward other than the qiblah." He said: "Your prayer is valid; Allah, majestic and exalted, says: ﴿Wherever you turn, there is the Face of Allah﴾."
1843- Sufyan ibn Waki' related to us, saying: My father related to us, from Ash'ath al-Samman, from 'Asim ibn 'Ubaydullah, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Amir ibn Rabi'ah, from his father, who said: "We were with the Prophet ﷺ on a dark night during a journey, and we did not know where the qiblah was, so we prayed, and each one of us prayed according to his own direction, [[In Lisan al-'Arab: "fa-salla kull minna hiyalahu," meaning facing his own direction; the addition of "'ala" does not harm the meaning.]] then we awoke and mentioned it to the Prophet ﷺ, and Allah, majestic and exalted, revealed: ﴿Wherever you turn, there is the Face of Allah﴾." [[The hadith: 1843 - it is a repetition of hadith 1841.]]
* *
Others said: Rather, this verse was revealed concerning the occasion of al-Najashi, because the companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ disputed about his affair, on account of the fact that he died before praying toward the qiblah. So Allah, majestic and exalted, said: The easts and the wests are all Mine; whoever turns his face toward any of them, seeking Me and desiring thereby My obedience, will find Me there. The meaning is that al-Najashi, although he had not prayed toward the qiblah, had nonetheless been turning his face toward some of the easts and wests, seeking thereby the pleasure of Allah, majestic and exalted, in his prayer.

Mention of those who said that:
