The first: its meaning is: "And We charged Ibrahim and Isma'il that they build My House purified from shirk and doubt [[al-rayb here means evil and fear, from their saying 'rabani amruhu', i.e. it brought me evil and fear; this is traced back to His words, Exalted is He: 'a place of return for people and a sanctuary']], as He, mentioned be He, said: 'Is he who founds his building upon piety from God and His good pleasure better, or he who founds his building upon the edge of a crumbling bank that collapses?' [Surah al-Tawbah: 109]. Likewise His words: 'And We charged Ibrahim and Isma'il that they purify My House' means: build My House upon purity from associating anything with Me and from doubt, as:

2009 – Musa ibn Harun told me, saying: ʿAmr ibn Hammad told us, saying: Asbat told us, from al-Suddi: "And We charged Ibrahim and Isma'il that purify My House," he says: "Build My House [for those who circumambulate]." [[This addition is from Tafsir Ibn Kathir 1:315.]]

This is one of its two aspects.

The other aspect is that they were commanded to purify the site of the House before its building, and the House after its building, from what the people of shirk with God used to place in it – in the time of Nuh and those before him – of idols, so that this would be a sunnah for those after them, since God, mentioned be He, had made Ibrahim an imam to be followed after him, as:

2010 – Yunus told me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words: "that purify," he said: "From the idols they worshipped, which the polytheists used to venerate." [[Ibn Kathir said in his tafsir 1:314–315, after citing this aspect and this report: "I say: this answer is based on the premise that idols were worshipped there before Ibrahim, peace be upon him, and proving this requires evidence from the infallible Muhammad (ﷺ)."]]

2011 – Ahmad ibn Ishaq told us, saying: Abu Ahmad al-Zubayri told us, saying: Sufyan told us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from ʿAta', from ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr: "that purify My House for those who circumambulate," he said: "From the idols and doubt."

2012 – Al-Muthanna told me, saying: Abu Nuʿaym told us, saying: Sufyan told us, from Ibn Jurayj, from ʿAta', from ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr, the like of it.

2013 – Ahmad ibn Ishaq told me, saying: Abu Ahmad told us, saying: Sufyan told us, from Layth, from Mujahid, who said: "From shirk."

2014 – Ahmad ibn Ishaq told us, saying: Abu Ahmad told us, saying: Abu Israʾil told us, from Abu Husayn, from Mujahid: "Purify My House for those who circumambulate," he said: "From idols."

2015 – Al-Hasan ibn Yahya told us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah regarding His words: "Purify My House for those who circumambulate," he said: "From shirk and the worship of idols."

2016 – Bishr ibn Muʿadh told us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Saʿid told us, from Qatadah, the like of it – and he added in it: "and false speech."

* *

On the interpretation of His words: "for those who circumambulate" (lil-ṭā'ifīn)

Abu Jaʿfar said: The people of interpretation differ on the meaning of "al-ṭā'ifīn" in this place. Some of them said: they are the strangers who come to the Sacred House from afar. [[Al-ghurba and al-gharb (with fatha then sukun): distance and remoteness; meaning whoever comes to it from a distant place.]]

Mention of those who said this:

2017 – Abu Kurayb told us, saying: Abu Bakr ibn ʿAyyash told us, saying: Abu Husayn told us, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr regarding His words: "for those who circumambulate," he said: "Whoever comes to it from far away."

* *

Others said: Rather, "al-ṭā'ifūn" are those who circumambulate it, whether they are strangers or from its people.

Mention of those who said this:

2018 – Muhammad ibn al-ʿAla' told us, saying: Waki' told us, from Abu Bakr al-Hudhali, from ʿAta': "for those who circumambulate," he said: "If someone is circumambulating the House, he is among 'the circumambulants'."

* *

The interpretation closest to the verse is what ʿAta' said, because "al-ṭā'if" is one who circles a thing exclusively. A stranger who has arrived from afar does not deserve the name "one who circumambulates the House" unless he circumambulates it.

* *

On the interpretation of His words: "and those who stay (al-ʿākifīn)"

Abu Jaʿfar said: By His words, "and those who stay," He, mentioned be He, means: those who remain there. "Al-ʿākif ʿalā al-shay'" is one who remains upon it, as the poet Nabigha of Banu Dhubyan said:

ʿUkūfan ladā abyātihim yuthmidūnahum ... ramā Allāhu fī tilka al-ukuffi al-kawāniʿ
[[From his Diwan, 63, from verses he said concerning Zur'a ibn ʿAmir al-ʿAmiri, when the Banu ʿAmir sent to Hisn ibn Hudhayfah and his son ʿUyayna ibn Hisn: cut the alliance between you and Banu Asad, and join them with Banu Kinanah, and we will ally with you, for we are the sons of your father. ʿUyayna was determined on this, but Banu Dhubyan said: Let those among you who are allies go out, and we will go out from among us! They refused, and Nabigha said: Let the Banu Dhubyan rejoice that their land has been emptied for them of every client and follower, except Asad, who protect it against every raider, with two thousand armoured, armed men... He then praised Banu Asad, disparaged Banu ʿAbs, belittled Banu Sahm and Malik of Ghatafan and ʿAbd ibn Saʿd ibn Dhubyan, and satirized them with this verse which al-Tabari cited. The Diwan reads "qu'ūdan" and "yuthmidūnahā" with the pronoun referring to the houses. "Yuthmiduhum" derives from "thamada al-ma' yuthmiduhu thamadan", i.e. they removed the dust from it so that it would come out. "Ma' mathmud": many people crowded it until it ran dry except a little. And "rajul mathmud" is said of a man whom people pressed with requests until he gave away everything he had. He means: the Banu Saʿd and Malik remain at the houses of ʿAbd ibn Saʿd draining their wealth. He describes them with baseness and the loss of ambition. Whoever reads "yuthmiduhā" and returns the pronoun to "abyātihim" has the same meaning, that they cling to their houses and seek their livelihood from them, mocking them. "Al-kawāniʿ" is the plural of "kāniʿ": the submissive one who draws in and shrinks, gathering close to one another as if he is contracting from his humiliation. He describes them with baseness, greed and humble begging. "Ramā Allāh" means He struck them with what uproots them; the Diwan reads "fī tilka al-unūf", meaning He hit them with mutilation of the nose, which is a curse upon them and a expression of disgust at their meanness.]]
"Mu'takif" is said of one who stays in the place where he confines himself to God, mentioned be He.

* *

Then the people of interpretation differed about whom God meant by His words, "and those who stay."

Some of them said: He meant by it the one who sits in the Sacred House without circumambulating or praying.

Mention of those who said this:

2019 – Abu Kurayb told us, saying: Waki' told us, from Abu Bakr al-Hudhali, from ʿAta', who said: If someone is circumambulating the House, he is among "the circumambulants"; and if he is sitting, he is among "those who stay."

* *

Others said: "Those who stay" are those who remain in seclusion and dwell (al-mujāwirūn) there.

Mention of those who said this:

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 125 (part 3 of 3):

2020- Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad al-Zubayri narrated to us, saying: Sharik narrated to us, from Jabir, from Mujahid and Ikrimah: "Purify My House for those who circumambulate and those who devote themselves to it [al-'akifin]," said: "the residents (al-mujawirun)."
* *
Others said: "al-'akifun" are the people of the Sacred City (ahl al-balad al-haram).
Mention of those who said this:
2021- Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Abu Bakr ibn 'Ayyash narrated to us, saying: Abu Husayn narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, regarding His saying: "and those who devote themselves to it," he said: the people of the city.
2022- Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Zuray' narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding "and those who devote themselves to it," he said: "al-'akifun" are its people.
* *
Others said: "al-'akifun" are those who pray.
Mention of those who said this:
2023- al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn 'Abbas said regarding His saying: "Purify My House for those who circumambulate and those who devote themselves to it," he said: "al-'akifun" are those who pray.
* *
Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of these interpretations is what 'Ata' said, namely that "al-'akif" in this place is the one who stays in the House, dwelling in it as a neighbor, without circumambulating or praying. This is because the attribute of "al-'ukuf" is what we have described: remaining in a place. One who remains in a place may be remaining there while sitting, praying, circumambulating, standing, or in other states. Since He, may His remembrance be exalted, mentioned in His saying: "that purify My House for those who circumambulate and those who devote themselves to it and those who bow and prostrate," those who pray and those who circumambulate, it is known by this that the state meant by Allah, exalted be His remembrance, from "al-'akif" is other than the state of the one who prays and the one who circumambulates, and that what He meant from its states is devotion to the House by way of dwelling in it, even if one is not praying in it, nor bowing, nor prostrating.
* *
The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted be He: ﴿and those who bow and prostrate (125)﴾
Abu Ja'far said: By His saying "those who bow" (al-rukka'), Allah, exalted be His remembrance, means the group of people who bow in it to Him; its singular is "rakic" (one who bows). Likewise "al-sujud" are the group of people who prostrate in it to Him; its singular is "sajid" (one who prostrates), just as it is said "rajul qa'id wa-rijal qu'ud" and "rajul jalis wa-rijal julus," so likewise "rajul sajid wa-rijal sujud." [[From what I have deduced about the form of this plural, the plural of fa'il on fu'ul: that every triliteral verb whose verbal noun (masdar) comes in the pattern "fu'ul" with the fa' vocalized with a damma, its fa'il plural is formed on "fu'ul," like these examples mentioned here, and everything other than them which the lexicon books have recorded and which is scattered in poetry.]]
* *
It was said: rather, by "those who bow and prostrate" He means those who pray.
Mention of those who said this:
2024- Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Abu Bakr al-Hudhali, from 'Ata': "and those who bow and prostrate," said: whoever prays is among "those who bow and prostrate."
2025- Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: "and those who bow and prostrate," the people of prayer.
* *
We have already explained, in what has passed, the meaning of "ruku'" (bowing) and "sujud" (prostration), so that suffices and need not be repeated here. [[See what preceded: 1:574-575, then 2:103-105, 519.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 126 (part 1 of 2):

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And when Abraham said: "My Lord, make this a secure city"﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His words, exalted is His remembrance, "And when Abraham said, 'My Lord, make this a secure city'," He means: "Remember when Abraham said: 'My Lord, make this city a secure city'."
* *
Abu Ja'far said: By His words "secure," He means: secure from tyrants and others, so that they cannot gain power over it, and secure from God's punishment reaching it as it reaches other lands: by sinking (khasf), by overturning (i'tifak), by drowning, [[In the printed edition, the word is "wantiqal" in place of "wa'tifak," which is a word without meaning here and without any indication. Al-i'tifak means overturning, and it is the severe punishment of God that He sent down upon the people of Lot. He, glorified is He, said in Surat Hud: "When Our command came, We made its highest part its lowest" (11:82). This is the i'tifak: the land was overturned with them, that is, it turned over so that its top became its bottom. God called these towns, the towns of Lot, "the overturned" (al-mu'tafikat) in Surat al-Tawba (9:70) and in Surat al-Haqqa (69:9), and He said in Surat al-Najm (53:52–53): "And the overturned cities, He threw them down, and covered them with what covered them."]] and other than that, from the wrath of God and His chastisements, which strike other lands besides it, as:
2026 – Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, who said: It was mentioned to us that the Sacred Precinct was made sacred up to the Throne in its vicinity. And it was mentioned to us that the House descended with Adam when he descended. God said to him: "I will send down with you My House, around which people will circumambulate as they circumambulate around My Throne." So Adam and whoever came after him of the believers circumambulated it, until, at the time of the Flood, when God drowned the people of Noah, He raised it up and purified it, and the punishment of the people of the earth did not reach it. Then Abraham followed its traces and built it upon an ancient foundation that had existed before him.
* *
If someone says to us: "Was the Sacred Precinct not secure except after Abraham asked his Lord for its security?"
It is said to him: People have differed on this. Some of them said: The Sacred Precinct has never ceased to be secure from God's punishment and from the punishment of His tyrannical creatures, since the heavens and the earth were created. They argued for this with what follows:
2027 – Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Yunus ibn Bukayr narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, who said: Sa'id ibn Abi Sa'id al-Maqburi narrated to me, who said: I heard Abu Shurayh al-Khuza'i say: When Mecca was conquered, the Khuza'a killed a man from Hudhayl, so the Messenger of God (ﷺ) stood up to deliver a sermon and said: "O people, God made Mecca sacred on the day He created the heavens and the earth, so it is sacred by God's sanctity until the Day of Resurrection. It is not lawful for any person who believes in God and the Last Day to shed blood in it or to cut down a tree in it. Beware, it is not lawful for anyone after me, and it was made lawful for me only for this hour, out of anger at its people. Beware, it has returned to its previous state of yesterday. Let the one present convey it to the one absent. And whoever says that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) killed people in it, say: God permitted it to His Messenger but did not permit it to you." [[The hadith: 2027 – This is an abridgement of a sound, lengthy hadith.
It was narrated by Ahmad in al-Musnad: 16448 (vol. 4, p. 32, Halabi edition), from Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim ibn Sa'd, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, with this chain.
Ibn Ishaq's narration is also established, in its longer form, in Ibn Hisham's Sira 4:57–58 (Halabi), and 823–824 (Europe edition), and 2:277–278 (from al-Rawd al-Unuf).
Ahmad also narrated it, in similar wording: 16444 (vol. 4, p. 31), and al-Bukhari 1:176–177 and 4:35–39 (Fath), and Muslim 1:383–384, all through the route of al-Layth ibn Sa'd, from Sa'id ibn Abi Sa'id al-Maqburi, from Abu Shurayh.
His words in the hadith, "or cut down a tree in it" (aw ya'dhud bihā shajaran), mean: cut it. It is said "'adhada al-shajar" (from the pattern ḍaraba), meaning he cut it.
His words "out of anger at its people": this is the correct and established wording in Ibn Ishaq's narration in al-Musnad and in Ibn Hisham's Sira. In the printed edition it reads "'aṣā 'alā ahlihā" (he disobeyed its people), which is a mistake (taṣḥīf).]]
2028 – Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahim ibn Sulayman narrated to us – and Ibn Humayd and Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, both saying: Jarir narrated to us – all of them from Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said, regarding Mecca when he conquered it: "This is a sanctuary which God made sacred on the day He created the heavens and the earth, and created the sun and the moon, and set these two mountains (al-akhshabayn). It was not lawful for anyone before me, and it is not lawful for anyone after me. It was made lawful for me for an hour of a day. [[The hadith: 2028 – Al-Tabari narrated this hadith by two chains from three teachers. He narrated it from Abu Kurayb Muhammad ibn al-'Ala', from Abd al-Rahim ibn Sulayman al-Razi. Then he narrated it from Ibn Humayd – that is Muhammad ibn Humayd al-Razi – and from Ibn Wakī' – that is Sufyan ibn Wakī' – both of them (Ibn Humayd and Ibn Wakī') from Jarir ibn Abd al-Hamid al-Dabbi. Then the two chains converge: Abd al-Rahim ibn Sulayman and Jarir ibn Abd al-Hamid narrated "together, from Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad."
Apparently these chains look sound, although Sufyan ibn Wakī' is weak, as we explained in 1692. Al-Tabari did not transmit from him alone; he paired him with Muhammad al-Razi, who is trustworthy. However, there is a break (inqita') in the hadith between Mujahid and Ibn Abbas. Mujahid did hear many hadiths from Ibn Abbas, but this particular hadith was narrated by him "from Tawus, from Ibn Abbas."
As for "Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad al-Kufi, mawla of the Banu Hashim": he is truthful (saduq), but there is some weakness in his memory after he grew old. Ibn Sa'd said (6:237): "He was trustworthy in himself, but he became confused (ikhtalaṭa) in the end of his life, and so he brought strange reports." Ya'qub ibn Sufyan said: "Yazid – although they spoke about him because he changed – is upright and trustworthy, though not like al-Hakam or Mansur." He is biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir (4/2/334), and Ibn Abi Hatim (4/2/265). Perhaps he made a mistake in omitting "Tawus" between Mujahid and Ibn Abbas.
The hadith itself is sound.
Ahmad narrated it in a longer form, similar in wording: 2353 and 2898, through the route of Mansur ibn al-Mu'tamir, from Mujahid, from Tawus, from Ibn Abbas.
Likewise al-Bukhari narrated it (4:40–42) and Muslim (1:383), through the route of Mansur.
Mansur ibn al-Mu'tamir was previously declared trustworthy (177). He was more precise in memory than a hundred like Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad. Indeed Yahya al-Qattan said: "No one is more reliable from Mujahid and Ibrahim than Mansur." The imams preferred him in memory over al-A'mash and al-Hakam.
Moreover, for this very hadith, al-Hafiz (Ibn Hajar) in Fath al-Bari mentioned that al-A'mash narrated it from Mujahid from the Prophet (ﷺ), as a mursal (a report in which the Successor (tabi'i) attributes directly to the Prophet, omitting the Companion), meaning omitting Tawus and Ibn Abbas. Then he said: "Mansur is a trustworthy and retentive transmitter, so the ruling goes to the one who connected it (wasl)." That is, this addition is the addition of a trustworthy transmitter, which must be accepted and given preference.
As for his words in this narration: "and set these two mountains (al-akhshabayn)." I have not found this addition in any of the other narrations. "Al-Akhshabān," in the dual form, are the two mountains of Mecca that surround it. See al-Nihaya by Ibn al-Athir and Mu'jam al-Buldan by Yaqut.]]
* *
They said: Mecca, since its creation, has been a secure sanctuary from God's punishment and the punishment of tyrants. They said: The second narration from the Messenger of God (ﷺ) that we mentioned has confirmed the correctness of what we have said. They said: Abraham did not ask his Lord to secure it from His punishment and the punishment of tyrants, but he asked Him to secure its people from famine and drought, and to provide its inhabitants with fruits, as his Lord reported that he asked, in His words: "And when Abraham said, 'My Lord, make this a secure city, and provide its people with fruits, such of them as believe in God and the Last Day'." They said: He only asked his Lord this because he settled his offspring in it, and it was "without crops or livestock," so he sought refuge with his Lord lest He destroy them by hunger and thirst, so he asked Him to secure them from what he feared for them.
They said: How could it be that Abraham asked his Lord to make the Sanctuary sacred and to secure it from His punishment and the punishment of His tyrannical creatures, when he himself said, when he settled and lodged his family and offspring there: ﴿Our Lord, I have settled some of my offspring in an uncultivated valley near Your Sacred House﴾ [Surat Ibrahim: 37]? They said: If Abraham had been the one who made the Sanctuary sacred, or had asked his Lord to make it sacred, he would not have said "near Your Sacred House" when he arrived there. Rather, it had been made sacred before him, and it remained sacred after him.
* *
Others said: The Sanctuary was lawful (halal) before Abraham's supplication, like other lands besides it, and it only became forbidden (haram) through Abraham's making it sacred, just as the city of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) was lawful before the Messenger of God (ﷺ) made it sacred. They said: The evidence for what we have said is what follows:
2029 – Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir ibn Abd Allah, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Abraham made the House of God sacred and secured it, and I have made Medina sacred between its two lava-fields (al-laban), its trees (idah) and its game, and its trees shall not be cut. [[The hadith: 2029 – Its chain is sound. Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi is the eminent and retentive imam. Sufyan is al-Thawri.
Abu al-Zubayr is al-Makki, Muhammad ibn Muslim ibn Tadrus, a trustworthy Successor. The group (al-jama'a) narrated from him. Jabir is Ibn Abd Allah, the well-known Companion.
The hadith was narrated by Muslim (1:385), in similar wording, through the route of Muhammad ibn Abd Allah al-Asadi, from Sufyan, with this chain, with the wording "Abraham made Mecca sacred," etc.
Ibn Kathir (1:316) also cited it and said: "Thus did al-Nasa'i narrate it, from Muhammad ibn Bashshar Bundar, with it." "Bundar" is the epithet (laqab) of Muhammad ibn Bashshar.
Al-Laabatan (the two lava-fields) are the two rocky tracts on either side of Medina, the land covered with black stones which have been thickly strewn.
Al-Idah, with a kasra on the 'ayn, a lightened ḍād, and a ha' at the end: every large tree that has thorns.]]
2030 – Abu Kurayb and Abu al-Sa'ib narrated to us, both saying: [Ibn Idris narrated to us, and Abu Kurayb informed us, saying], Abd al-Rahim al-Razi narrated to us, [both of them together]: We heard from Ash'ath, from Nafi', from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Abraham was the servant of God and His friend, and I am the servant of God and His Messenger. Abraham made Mecca sacred, and I have made Medina sacred between its two lava-fields, its trees and its game. No weapon shall be carried in it for fighting, and no tree in it shall be cut except for fodder for a camel." [[The hadith: 2030 – Abu al-Sa'ib is Muslim ibn Janada, whose biography has passed (48). Ibn Idris is Abd Allah ibn Idris al-Awdi, whose biography was already given (438).
Abd al-Rahim al-Razi is Abd al-Rahim ibn Sulayman al-Razi al-Ashall al-Kinani, whose narration appeared in hadith 2028. He is trustworthy and narrates much. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib and Ibn Abi Hatim (2/2/239).
Ash'ath is Ibn Sawwar al-Kindi. Some weakened him and others declared him trustworthy. We preferred his authentication in Sharh al-Musnad (661). He is biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir of al-Bukhari (1/2/430), and Ibn Abi Hatim (1/1/271–272).
Nafi' is the mawla of Ibn Umar, the trustworthy, firm, and authoritative transmitter.
This chain appeared garbled in the printed edition as: "Abu Kurayb and Abu al-Sa'ib narrated to us, both saying: Abd al-Rahim al-Razi narrated to us: I heard Ash'ath..." omitting "Ibn Idris." This gave the impression that Abu Kurayb and Abu al-Sa'ib narrated it from Abd al-Rahim al-Razi from Ash'ath. The correct form is what we have written, following Ibn Kathir (1:316), from this place in al-Tabari.
The correct chain is that al-Tabari narrates it from Abu Kurayb and Abu al-Sa'ib, both of them from Abd Allah ibn Idris; then al-Tabari narrates it from Abu Kurayb alone, from Abd al-Rahim al-Razi; and that Abd Allah ibn Idris and Abd al-Rahim al-Razi both heard it from Ash'ath.
Regarding this hadith in this form, Ibn Kathir said: "This route is strange; it is not in any of the six books (al-kutub al-sitta)." I add to this: I have not found it in al-Musnad either, nor in any other source I was able to consult.
Then Ibn Kathir pointed out that the essence of its meaning is established from Abu Hurayra through another route, in Sahih Muslim. This is the hadith of Malik in the Muwatta' (p. 885), from Suhayl, from his father, from Abu Hurayra: "When people saw the first fruit, they brought it to the Messenger of God (ﷺ). When the Messenger of God (ﷺ) took it, he said: 'O God, bless us in our fruit, bless us in our city, bless us in our ṣā', bless us in our mudd. O God, Abraham is Your servant, Your friend, and Your prophet, and I am Your servant and Your prophet, and he supplicated You for Mecca, and I supplicate You for Medina with the like of what he supplicated You for Mecca, and the like of it along with it'." It is in Sahih Muslim (1:387), from Qutayba, from Malik.]]
2031 – Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Qutayba ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Bakr ibn Mudar narrated to us, from Ibn al-Hadi, from Abu Bakr ibn Muhammad, from Abd Allah ibn Amr ibn Uthman, from Rafi' ibn Khadij, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Abraham made Mecca sacred, and I make Medina sacred between its two lava-fields. [[The hadith: 2031 – Bakr ibn Mudar ibn Muhammad ibn Hakim al-Misri: trustworthy; the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim) and others narrated from him. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir of al-Bukhari (1/2/95), and Ibn Abi Hatim (1/1/392–393), and Tadhkirat al-Huffaz, where he is described as "the imam, the narrator of hadith, the truthful, the worshipper."
Ibn al-Hadi is Yazid ibn Abd Allah ibn Usama ibn al-Hadi al-Laythi al-Madani. He is trustworthy and narrates much; the authors of the six books narrated from him. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir (4/2/344), and Ibn Abi Hatim (4/2/275). Abu Bakr ibn Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Hazm al-Ansari: a trustworthy and authoritative Successor, whose like is not asked about.
Abd Allah ibn Amr ibn Uthman ibn Affan: a trustworthy Successor, who was noble, generous, and praiseworthy. His maternal grandfather was Abd Allah ibn Umar ibn al-Khattab.
The hadith was narrated by Muslim in his Sahih (1:385), from Qutayba ibn Sa'id, with this chain. Ibn Kathir (1:316) cited it and said: "Muslim alone narrated it," meaning without al-Bukhari.]] And what is similar to that of the reports, which would take too long in the book to enumerate."
* *
They said: "God, exalted is His remembrance, has informed us in His Book that Abraham said: 'My Lord, make this a secure city,' and He did not inform us that he asked that it be secure from some things but not from others. So no one may claim that what he asked for was security from some things and not others, except with a proof which must be accepted. They said: As for the report of Abu Shurayh and Ibn Abbas, they are two reports by which no proof is established, because of the defects (asbab) in their chains, for which acceptance is not required."
* *
Abu Ja'far said: The correct position on this matter, in our view, is that God, exalted is His remembrance, made Mecca a sanctuary (haram) when He created and brought it into being, as the Prophet (ﷺ) reported, "that He made it sacred on the day He created the heavens and the earth," without any prohibition from Him through the tongue of any of His prophets and messengers, but by His preventing those who intended it harm, and by His warding off from it and from its inhabitants the afflictions and punishments that He sent upon other lands and their inhabitants. This remained its condition until God settled it upon His friend Abraham, and he lodged his family, Hajar, and his son Isma'il there. Then Abraham asked his Lord to make obligatory the prohibition of it upon His servants through his tongue, so that this would become a sunnah for those after him among His creatures, who would follow it in this matter, since God, exalted is His remembrance, had taken him as a friend and informed him that He would make him "an imam for the people to be followed." So his Lord granted him what he asked, and obligated His servants, at that time, to observe the prohibition of it through his tongue.
Thus Mecca, which had been forbidden by God's prohibition of it, without God making it obligatory upon His servants to refrain from it, and sacred by God's warding off from it, without His making it sacred through the tongue of any of His messengers, [[The structure of this parenthetical interruption: "after it had been forbidden..." and "and sacred..."; and the structure of the sentence interrupted: "Mecca became... the prohibition of it was made obligatory upon His creatures through the tongue of His friend Abraham, peace be upon him, and it became obligatory upon His servants to refrain from making it lawful, and from making its game and its trees lawful, by His making obligatory the refraining from that through Abraham's delivering God's message to them concerning that."]] became, through the tongue of His friend Abraham, peace be upon him, a prohibition made obligatory upon His creatures, and it became obligatory upon His servants to refrain from making it lawful, and from making lawful its game and its trees, by His making obligatory their refraining from that, through Abraham's delivering God's message to them about it.

That is why its prohibition was attributed to Abraham, and the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "God made Mecca sacred," because the obligation of its prohibition, which God imposed upon His servants as an act of worship to Him through it, is distinct from the prohibition by which He had long been worshipped through it in the sense of protection and guarding before that, [[Kalaahu Allah yaklaʾuhu kalā' (with a fatḥa then sukūn), and kalaʾ (with a kasra then sukūn), and kalāʾa (with a kasra on the kāf): He guarded it and protected it. In the printed edition it read "al-kalā'" with a single hamza and a long vowel, which is not correct. Furthermore, the sense of the sentence is: "because the obligation of its prohibition... was on account of Abraham's request to his Lord to make obligatory the imposition of that upon his tongue."]] was on account of Abraham's request to his Lord that this obligation be imposed through his tongue, [and it is that] which became obligatory upon the servants, rather than anything else. [[What is between the parentheses is an addition that is necessary so that the sentence is sound.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 126 (part 2 of 2):

So it has become clear, from what we have said, that both reports are sound in meaning: I mean the report of Abu Shurayh and Ibn Abbas from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Indeed God made Makkah sacred on the day He created the sun and the moon," and the report of Jabir, Abu Hurayrah, Rafi' ibn Khadij and others that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "O God, indeed Abraham made Makkah sacred." Neither of them negates the soundness of the meaning of the other, as some ignorant people have supposed.

It is not permissible for the reports of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) that one of them should negate another, once their authenticity is established. The two reports narrated from the Messenger of God (ﷺ) on this matter have come down in a manner that is apparent and widely transmitted, which cuts off any excuse for one who has received them.

As for the words of Abraham (peace be upon him) [[In the originals: "wa-qawl Ibrahim" (and the saying of Abraham), and the correct reading is the addition of "amma" (as for), as the context indicates.]] ﴿Our Lord, I have settled some of my offspring in a valley without cultivation, by Your sacred House﴾ [Surah Ibrahim: 37], then if he said it before God imposed the obligation of its sanctity upon His creatures through his tongue, [[In the originals: "in yakun qala qabl iijab Allah", and the correct reading is what I have set down.]] he meant by it the sanctity God had given it through His protection and safeguarding of it, not a sanctity imposed upon His creatures by way of worship obligating them to it. And if he said it after God had imposed its sanctity upon His creatures by way of worship, then no one has any question for us regarding that.

* *

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And provide its people with fruits, those among them who believe in God and the Last Day﴾

Abu Ja'far said: This is a request from Abraham to his Lord that He provide the believing people of Makkah with fruits, to the exclusion of its disbelievers. He singled out the believers for this request rather than the disbelievers because God had informed him, when he asked that He make from his offspring imams to be followed, that among them would be the disbeliever to whom His covenant would not reach, and the wrongdoer whose guardianship would not attain. Since he knew that among his descendants there would be the wrongdoer and the disbeliever, he specifically asked his Lord to provide fruits to the inhabitants of Makkah who were believers, not the disbelievers. God said to him: I have answered your supplication, and I shall provide for the disbelievers of the people of this land along with its believers, but I will let them enjoy it for a little.

* *

As for "man" in His words "those among them who believe in God and the Last Day," it is in the accusative as a restatement and clarification of "its people" [[Al-tarjamah (restatement): it is the badal or ʿatf al-bayan (apposition) according to the Kufans, as previously mentioned 2: 340, 420.]], as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿They ask you about the sacred month, about fighting in it﴾ [Surah al-Baqarah: 217], meaning: they ask you about fighting in the sacred month; and as He, mentioned is He, said: ﴿And due to God from the people is the pilgrimage to the House, for whoever is able to find a way to it﴾ [Surah Al ʿImran: 97], meaning: and due to God is the pilgrimage to the House upon whoever is able to find a way to it.

* *

Abraham asked his Lord for this only because he had settled in a valley without crops, water or people, so he asked that its people be provided with fruit and that the hearts of people be made to incline toward them. It is reported that when Abraham asked this of his Lord, God transported al-Ta'if from Palestine.

2032 – Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Ishaq ibn al-Hajjaj related to us, saying: Hisham related to us, saying: I read to Muhammad ibn Muslim that when Abraham supplicated for the Sanctuary: "And provide its people with fruits," God transported al-Ta'if from Palestine.

* *

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿He said: As for him who disbelieves, I shall let him enjoy for a little﴾

Abu Ja'far said: The people of interpretation differed concerning the speaker of this statement and the manner of its recitation. Some of them said: the speaker of this statement is our Lord, exalted is His mention, and its interpretation according to their saying is: He said: "And whoever disbelieves, I shall let him enjoy for a little," by My provision of fruits in this world, until his term comes. Those who held this view recited it as "fa-umatti'uhu qalilan" with a shaddah on the "ta'" and a raf' on the "ayn."

Those who said so:

2033 – Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Ishaq related to us, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far related to us, from his father, from al-Rabi', who said: Abu al-'Aliyah related to me, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, concerning His words: "And whoever disbelieves, I shall let him enjoy for a little, then I will compel him to the punishment of the Fire," he said: it is the saying of the Lord, exalted is His mention.

2034 – Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salamah related to us, saying: Ibn Ishaq said: When Abraham said: "My Lord, make this a secure land and provide its people with fruits, those among them who believe in God and the Last Day," and he turned the supplication away from those whom God refused to grant guardianship, = devoting himself to God, and out of love for and separation from those who opposed His command, even if they were from his offspring, when he knew that a wrongdoer among them would not attain His covenant, by God's informing him of that when He told him = God said: "And whoever disbelieves, I shall provide for the righteous and the wicked alike, and let him enjoy for a little." [[Report 2034: in Tafsir Ibn Kathir 1: 319, with some variation in wording; I did not find it in the Sirah of Ibn Hisham.]]

* *

Others said: rather, Abraham, the Friend of the Merciful, said this, as a request to his Lord that He provide the disbeliever also with fruits in the sacred land, like what He provides the believer, and let him enjoy it for a little, "then I will compel him to the punishment of the Fire." They recited it with a light "ta'," a jazm on the "ayn," a fath on the "ra'" of "adtarrahu," and "thumma adtarrahu" separated without a hamzah cut on its alif [[This is the written form of the recitation: "fa-umatti'hu qalilan thumma adtarrahu," taking them as imperatives meaning supplication and request.]], as a supplication and request from Abraham to his Lord on their behalf.

Those who said so:

2035 – Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Ishaq related to us, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far related to us, from his father, from al-Rabi', who said: Abu al-'Aliyah said: Ibn Abbas used to say: that is the saying of Abraham, asking his Lord that He let the disbeliever enjoy a little.

* *

2036 – Al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Ishaq related to us, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far related to us, from Layth, from Mujahid: "And whoever disbelieves, I shall let him enjoy for a little," he says: And whoever disbelieves, I shall provide for him also, then I will compel him to the punishment of the Fire. [[Report 2036: this report ought to have been placed before the mention of this recitation which al-Tabari is about to reject. According to what Ibn Kathir quotes from al-Tabari, its position was before report 2034, and what al-Tabari says shortly after will settle that this report from Mujahid is quite separate from this recitation. I fear the copyist omitted the report during copying and then returned to place it here when he noticed the omission. I almost restored it to its place, but preferred to leave it as it is with a note on the error, and separated it from the preceding by the dividing asterisks.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct recitation and interpretation in this matter, in our view, is what Ubayy ibn Ka'b said and recited, because the proof stands by the widely transmitted report, which indicates its correctness, and the anomaly of what contradicts it in recitation. It is not permissible to object, on the basis of one who was capable of error and forgetfulness in his transmission, against one for whom that was not permissible in his transmission. Since this is so, the meaning of the verse is: God said: O Abraham, I have answered your supplication, and I have provided the believing people of this land with fruits and its disbelievers as well, as enjoyment for them until the attainment of their terms; then afterward I will compel their disbelievers to the Fire.

* *

As for His words "fa-umatti'hu qalilan," it means: I shall make what I provide him from that during his life an enjoyment he takes pleasure in until the time of his death. [[See the explanation of "al-mata'" previously, 1: 539-541.]]

We said that this is so because God, mentioned is He, only said that to Abraham in answer to his request for fruit-provision for the believing people of Makkah. Thus it was known from that that the answer concerns what Abraham asked, and not anything else. Mujahid said what we have said in this matter, and we have mentioned the report from him. [[See report no. 2036 and the commentary upon it.]]

Some said: its interpretation is: "fa-umatti'hu" by remaining in the world.

Others said: "fa-umatti'hu qalilan" in his disbelief for as long as he remains in Makkah, until I send Muhammad (ﷺ) and he kills him, if he remains upon his disbelief, or expels him from it. Although this is an aspect the wording may bear, the evident sense of the wording opposes it, for the reasons we have described. [[How well Abu Ja'far said this, for most speech admits of several aspects, but the sequence and coherence of meanings requires one meaning out of those the wording may bear. This is what he means by "the evident sense of the wording." See the explanation of "al-zahir" previously 2: 15 and the references before and after it.]]

* *

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Then I will compel him to the punishment of the Fire﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His words, mentioned is He, "then I will compel him to the punishment of the Fire," He means: then I will push him toward the punishment of the Fire and drive him to it, as He, mentioned is He, said: (On the Day they will be pushed toward the Fire of Hell with a violent push) [Surah al-Tur: 13]. [[Abu Ja'far said in explaining this verse (27: 13-14, Bulaq): "They will be pushed with force and violence. It is said from it: 'daʿaʿtu fi qafahu' when I pushed him in his nape."]]

* *

The meaning of "al-idtirar" is compulsion. It is said: "I compelled so-and-so to this matter" when I forced him to it and drove him to it.

That is the meaning of His words: "then I will compel him to the punishment of the Fire," I push him toward it and drive him, dragging him and pulling him on his face.

* *

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And evil is the destination﴾ (126)

Abu Ja'far said: We have shown that "bi'sa" originally was "bi'is," from "al-bu's" (misery), its second vowel was made quiescent and its movement transferred to the first, as it is said "kibd" for "kabid" (liver), and the like. [[See what was previously said 2: 338-340.]]

* *

The meaning of the speech is: and evil is the destination, the punishment of the Fire, after what they had been in of the enjoyment of this world, which We gave them enjoyment of therein.

* *

As for "al-masir," it is a "maf'il" form from the saying of the speaker: "I became a good destination (sirtu masiran salihan)," and it is the place to which the disbeliever in God arrives, of the punishment of the Fire. [[Al-Tabari means that it is the abode one arrives at, from their saying: "Where is your masir?", i.e., your abode. Al-masir: the outcome and what a thing comes to.]]

**The interpretation of His words, the Exalted: ﴿And when Abraham was raising the foundations of the House, and Ishmael﴾**

Abu Ja'far said: By His words, may His remembrance be exalted, "And when Abraham was raising the foundations of the House," He means: remember when Abraham was raising the foundations of the House.

* * *

*Al-qawa'id* is the plural of *qa'ida*. For one of the foundations of the House, the singular is *qa'ida*. For one of the women's *qawa'id* (those past menstruation) and their elderly women, the singular is *qa'id*, with the feminine *ha'* dropped, because it is of the pattern *fa'il* from the speaker's statement, "I have ceased (*qadat*) from menstruation." There is no share of masculinity in it, just as one says *imra'a tahir* and *tamith* (a woman who is pure, or who has ceased menstruating), since there is no share of masculinity in that. If it were meant as *al-qu'ud*, which is the opposite of *al-qiyam* (standing), it would be said *qa'ida*, and it would not then be permissible to drop the feminine *ha'*. *Qawa'id al-bayt* means its *asas* (foundations). [[*Al-asas* (with a kasra on the hamza) is the plural of *ass* (with a damma on the hamza), and the plural of *al-asas* is *usus* (with two dammas), and the plural of *al-usus* is *asas* (with two fathas and a long vowel), and all of these have one meaning.]]

* * *

Then the interpreters differed concerning the "foundations" that Abraham and Ishmael raised from the House: did they themselves establish them, or were they foundations that existed before them?

Some people said: They are the foundations of a House that Adam, father of mankind, built by God's command to him to do so. Then its place was effaced and its trace obliterated after him, until God settled Abraham, peace be upon him, there, and he built it.

Those who said this:

2037- Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ibn Jurayj informed us, from Ata', who said: Adam said: "O Lord, I do not hear the voices of the angels!" He said: "Because of your sin. But descend to the earth and build a house for Me, then circle around it as you saw the angels circling around My house which is in heaven." It is claimed by people that he built it from five mountains: from Hira', Tur Zaytha, Tur Sayna, the Mountain of Lebanon, and al-Judi. Its *rabad* was from Hira'. This was the building of Adam until Abraham built it afterward. [[The report: 2037 is in Ibn Kathir's *Tafsir* 1:325, where he said: "This is sound up to Ata', but in some of it there is strangeness, and God knows best." *Rabad al-bina'* (with two fathas) and *rabduhu* (with a damma and a sukun) is its middle, on which it rests, i.e., it is established and fixed.]]

2038- Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Ayyub, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas: "And when Abraham was raising the foundations of the House," he said: The foundations were the foundations of the House before that.

* * *

Others said: Rather, they are the foundations of a House that God had sent down for Adam from heaven to earth, circling it as He had circled His Throne in heaven. Then He raised it to heaven in the days of the Flood, and Abraham raised the foundations of that House.

Those who said this:

2039- Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to me, saying: Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us, saying: Ayyub narrated to us, from Abu Qilaba, from Abd Allah ibn Amr, who said: When God sent Adam down from Paradise, He said: "I am sending down with you, or placing with you, a house that will be circled around as My Throne is circled, and prayed at as My Throne is prayed at." When the time of the Flood came, it was raised, and the prophets used to make pilgrimage to it without knowing its place, until God settled Abraham there, informed him of its place, and he built it from five mountains: from Hira', Thabir, Lebanon, the Mountain of Tur, and the Mountain of al-Khamr. [[The report: Abd al-Wahhab is Ibn Abd al-Majid al-Thaqafi, who is trustworthy, one of the teachers of al-Shafi'i and Ahmad and their like. He is biographed in *al-Tahdhib*, Ibn Abi Hatim 3/1/71, and Ibn Sa'd 7/2/44.
Ayyub is Ibn Abi Tamima al-Sakhtiyani, who is trustworthy and an authority. Shu'ba said: "He was the master of the jurists." He is biographed in *al-Tahdhib*, *al-Kabir* 1/1/409-410, Ibn Sa'd 7/2/14-17, and Ibn Abi Hatim.
Abu Qilaba, with a kasra on the qaf and a light lam, is Abd Allah ibn Zayd al-Jarmi. He is a trustworthy and well-known Successor (*tabi'i*). He is biographed in *al-Tahdhib*, Ibn Sa'd 7/1/133-135, and Ibn Abi Hatim 2/2/57-58.
This report was mentioned by al-Suyuti 1:127, who attributed it to al-Tabari, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Tabarani, from "Abd Allah ibn Amr ibn al-As."
Al-Haythami also mentioned it in *Majma' al-Zawa'id* 3:288, and said: "al-Tabarani narrated it in *al-Kabir*, as a statement of a Companion (*mawquf*), and its narrators are the narrators of the sound (collection)." That is as he said. But there is no proof in it, and perhaps it is from what Abd Allah ibn Amr used to hear from the reports of the People of the Book. *Jabal al-Khamr* is the mountain of Jerusalem, named so for the abundance of its vineyards (Yaqut). [[
2040- Yaqub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Isma'il ibn Ulayya narrated to us, saying: Ayyub narrated to us, from Abu Qilaba, who said: When Adam was sent down... then he mentioned something similar.

2041- Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Hisham ibn Hassan informed us, from Sawwar [the son-in-law of Ata'], from Ata' ibn Abi Rabah, who said: When God sent Adam down from Paradise, his feet were on the earth and his head was in heaven. He would hear the speech and supplications of the people of heaven, and be at ease with them. The angels feared him, until they complained to God in their supplication and in their prayer, so He lowered him to the earth. When he lost what he used to hear from them, he was lonely, until he complained of that to God in his supplication and in his prayer. So he was directed to Mecca. The place of his footstep was a town, and his stride was a desert, until he reached Mecca. God sent down a ruby of the ruby of Paradise, and it was in the place of the House now. He kept circling around it until God sent the Flood, and that ruby was raised, until God sent Abraham and he built it. That is the saying of God: "And when We settled for Abraham the place of the House." [[The report: 2041 is in *Tarikh al-Tabari* 1:61, and the addition in parentheses is from it. It is also in Ibn Kathir's *Tafsir* 1:325, where he said: "This is sound up to Ata', but in some of it there is strangeness, and God knows best," along with the report mentioned before, number 2037.]]

2042- Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada, who said: God placed the House with Adam when God sent Adam down to the earth. Its place of descent was the land of India, and his head was in heaven and his feet on the earth. The angels feared him, so he was reduced to sixty cubits. Adam grieved because he lost the voices of the angels and their glorification, and he complained of that to God, the Exalted. God said: "O Adam, I have sent down to you a house that you will circle around as one circles My Throne, and you will pray at it as one prays at My Throne."

So Adam set out toward it and went forth, and his stride was lengthened for him, so that between every two steps there was a desert. Those deserts have remained since then. Adam came to the House, circled it, and so did the prophets after him.

2043- Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Aban, that the House was sent down as one ruby, or one pearl, until God drowned the people of Noah, raised it, and its foundation remained. Then God settled Abraham there, and he built it afterward.

* * *

Others said: Rather, the place of the House was a red mound like the shape of a dome. That is because when God wanted to create the earth, water rose into a foam, red or white, [[*Al-zabad* (with two fathas) is what floats on the water from its white froth. A piece of foam is *zabda* (with a fatha and a sukun).]] and that was in the place of the Sacred House. Then He spread out the earth from beneath it, and it remained so until God settled Abraham there, and he built it on its foundation. They said: Its foundation rests on four pillars in the seventh earth.

Those who said this:

2044- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Jarir ibn Hazim said: Hamid ibn Qays narrated to me, from Mujahid, who said: The place of the House was on the water before God created the heavens and the earth, like a white foam, and beneath it the earth was spread out.

2045- Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ibn Jurayj informed us, who said: Ata' and Amr ibn Dinar said: God sent winds that struck the water, and it exposed at the place of the House a rocky mound like a dome, and this House is from it. Therefore it is "the Mother of the Cities." Ibn Jurayj said: Ata' said: Then He pegged it with mountains so that it would not capsize with sway, and the first mountain was Abu Qubays. [[*Safaqat al-rih al-ma'* (with a fatha on the fa', and with its doubling along with the fatha) means: the wind struck the water and turned it right and left.
*Al-hashfa* is a soft rock in a flat plain. It is also said of an island in the sea that water does not reach, "hashfa," and its plural is *hishaf* (with a kasra on the ha'), when it is small and round. *Kafa'a al-shay' yakfa'uhu* means: he turned it over. *Mada al-shay' yamidu maydan* means: it moved and inclined.]]

2046- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Ya'qub al-Qummi narrated to us, from Hafs ibn Humayd, from Ikrima, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The House was placed upon the pillars of the water, on four pillars, two thousand years before the world was created, then the earth was spread out from beneath the House. [[The editor of the printed edition said: "His words: 'The House was placed upon the pillars of the water...' are thus in the original, and the phrasing of *al-Durr al-Manthur* is: 'The House was on four pillars in the water.' This is an extremely strange comment, for the text of *al-Durr al-Manthur* 1:127 is the same as the text of al-Tabari, and it is the same as what Ibn Kathir transmitted in his *Tafsir* from al-Tabari 1:326. The wording of al-Tabari is correct."]]

2047- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Ya'qub narrated to us, from Harun ibn Anzara, from Ata' ibn Abi Rabah, who said: They found in Mecca a stone on which was written: "I am God, Lord of Bakka. I built it on the day I made the sun and the moon, and I encircled it with seven angels, upright in faith." [[The report: 2047 I have not found through the route of Ata' ibn Abi Rabah, but it is narrated from Ibn Abbas and Mujahid in *Akhbar Makka* of al-Azraqi 1:37-38, with different wording, in a complete long report which Abu Ja'far abridged. The text of Mujahid's report: "It was found in some of the Psalms: I am God, Lord of Bakka; I made it between these two mountains, and I formed it on the day I formed the sun and the moon, and I encircled it with seven angels, upright in faith..." As for Ibn Ishaq, he said (*Sirat Ibn Hisham* 1:208): "I was told that the Quraysh found in the Corner a writing in Syriac, and they did not know what it was, until a man of the Jews read it for them. It was: 'I am God, Lord of Bakka; I created it on the day I created the heavens and the earth, and I fashioned the sun and the moon, and I encircled it with seven angels, upright in faith. Its two mountains shall not move, blessed for its people in water and milk.'" Ibn Hisham said: *Akhshabaha*: its two mountains.
As for his words, "upright in faith" (*hunafa'*): it is the plural of *hanif*, who is the Muslim who says "There is no god but God" and then keeps to the path. The angels are described as *hunafa'* for their obedience and uprightness in worshipping their Lord, and for their patience with themselves in what they were commanded concerning guarding this pure House. For the explanation of "*hunafa'*" in the reports, see numbers 2096, 2098, 2099. It was in the printed edition: "*hafafathu bi-sab'at amlak hafa*," which is an error; its correct form is what is recorded here, from the references: *Akhbar Makka* of al-Azraqi 1:37-38, *Sirat Ibn Hisham* 1:208, and al-Suhayli in *al-Rawd al-Unuf* 1:131.]]

2048- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: Abd Allah ibn Abi Najih narrated to me, from Mujahid and others among the people of knowledge, that when God settled Abraham at the place of the House, he went forth from Syria, and went forth with him Ishmael and his mother Hagar, while Ishmael was a small child who was nursing. They were carried, as I was told, on the Buraq, with Gabriel guiding him to the place of the House and the landmarks of the Sanctuary. He set out and Gabriel set out with him, and every time he passed a town he would say: "Is it this one that I am commanded, O Gabriel?" Gabriel would say: "Proceed!" until he brought him to Mecca. At that time it was a wilderness of *idah* trees, *salam* and *samur*, and there were people called the Amalek outside Mecca and around it, [[In the printed edition: "*yarubuha* people..." which is correct in meaning: that is, the Amalek, who were its masters and owners, possess it. Of this is the hadith of Safwan ibn Umayya when he said to Abu Sufyan: "That a man of Quraysh should be a master over me (*yarubuni*) is dearer to me than that a man of Hawazin should be." That is, he would be a lord above me and a chief who owns me. But I have kept what is in the *Tarikh* of al-Tabari, and what Ibn Kathir transmitted from it, and *Akhbar Makka* of al-Azraqi.]] and the House at that time was a red mound of clay. Abraham said to Gabriel: "Was it here that I was commanded to place them?" He said: "Yes." So he went with them to the place of the Stone, and set them down there, and commanded Hagar, the mother of Ishmael, to make a shelter there. Then he said: "Our Lord, I have settled some of my offspring in a valley without cultivation, by Your Sacred House," to His words: "perhaps they will give thanks." [Surah Ibrahim: 37]

Ibn Humayd said: Salama said, Ibn Ishaq said: And they claim, and God knows best, that an angel came to Hagar, the mother of Ishmael, when Abraham settled them in Mecca, before Abraham and Ishmael raised the foundations of the House. He pointed out the House to her, and it was a red mound of clay, and he said to her: [[In the printed edition: "he pointed to them... he said to them..." in the dual, which is a pure error, for the address is to Hagar alone, as the context before and after shows, and the correct form is in the *Akhbar Makka* of al-Azraqi.]] "This is the first House placed on the earth, and it is the Ancient House of God, and know that Abraham and Ishmael are raising it for the people."
[[The report: 2048. The first part of this report is in *Tarikh al-Tabari* 1:130, with some difference in wording at the beginning of the report, and in *Akhbar Makka* of al-Azraqi 1:19, and in Ibn Kathir's *Tafsir* 1:326. As for its last part, it is in *Akhbar Makka* of al-Azraqi 1:20-21, where the words at its end "yarfa'anihi lil-nas" [they raise it for the people] were "yarfa'anihi fa-llahu a'lam" [they raise it, and God knows best], which is most likely an addition by a copyist. I have given the text of what came in *Akhbar Makka*.
*Al-idah* is every tree that is large and has strong thorns. *Al-salam* and *al-samur* are two kinds of *idah* trees. As for his word "*madara*": it is dried, sticky clay with no sand in it, and it is pure clay.]]

2049- Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to me, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Hisham ibn Hassan informed us, saying: Hamid informed me, from Mujahid, who said: God created the place of this House two thousand years before He created any part of the earth, and its foundations are in the seventh earth.

2050- Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ibn Uyayna informed us, saying: Bishr ibn Asim informed me, from Ibn al-Musayyab, who said: Ka'b narrated to us: The House was a foam upon the water forty years before God created the earth, and from it the earth was spread out. [Sa'id] said: And we were told from Ali ibn Abi Talib: that Abraham came from Armenia with the *sakina* guiding him to the settling of the House, as the spider settles its house. He said: Then there were lifted from it stones which thirty men could bear, or could not bear. He said: I said: "O Abu Muhammad, God says: 'And when Abraham was raising the foundations of the House.'" He said: That was after. [[The report: 2050. Bishr ibn Asim ibn Sufyan ibn Abd Allah ibn Rabi'a ibn al-Harith al-Ta'ifi is trustworthy, and narrates from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab. He is biographed in *al-Tahdhib*, *al-Kabir* 1/2/77-78, Ibn Sa'd 5:380, and Ibn Abi Hatim 1/1/360.
This report consists of two reports: the first from Ka'b al-Ahbar, which has no value, and the second from Ali ibn Abi Talib. It seems apparent that it is from what the Companions used to narrate of the reports of the People of the Book.
Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted both parts, as Ibn Kathir reported 1:324-325, from Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Yazid al-Muqri', from Sufyan, that is Ibn Uyayna, with this chain.
Al-Hakim in *al-Mustadrak* 2:267 narrated the report of Ali alone, through the route of Zakariya ibn Ishaq, from Bishr ibn Asim, with it. Zakariya ibn Ishaq al-Makki is trustworthy.
Likewise, the report of Ali alone was narrated by al-Azraqi, Abu al-Walid Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Ahmad, in *Tarikh Makka* 1:25 (the Makka edition of the year 1352 AH), from his grandfather, from Sufyan ibn Uyayna, from Bishr ibn Asim, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, who said: "Ali ibn Abi Talib informed me."
In the printed edition here, at the beginning of the report of Ali, it reads: "He said: And we were told from Ali ibn Abi Talib." So the one who says this is Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab. I do not know whether the narration of al-Tabari was like this, or whether it is an error of the copyists. In the narration of Ibn Abi Hatim it reads: "Sa'id said: And Ali ibn Abi Talib narrated to us." The narration of al-Hakim supports it: "from Bishr ibn Asim, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, who said: Ali ibn Abi Talib narrated to us." Likewise the narration of al-Azraqi. This is the correct version in my view.
The report of Ali was also transmitted by al-Suyuti 1:126, who attributed it above this to Sa'id ibn Mansur, Abd ibn Humayd, and Ibn al-Mundhir.
*Al-ghuthaa'a* is the singular of *al-ghuthaa'*, which is what the torrent and water carry of foam and of the perished, decayed matter of trees and other things, mixed with the foam. In Ibn Kathir: "Then stones were uncovered which only thirty men could lift." The pronoun in his words "*tutiquhu*" [which is able to bear it] refers to one of the stones mentioned, unless there is distortion or omission in the originals.]]

* * *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct view on this matter, in our opinion, is to say that Allah, may He be remembered, informed us about Ibrahim, His friend (khalil), and his son Isma'il, that they both raised the foundations of the Sacred House. It is permissible that these were the foundations of a house that He had sent down with Adam, and that He then placed it in the position of the Sacred House which is in Makkah. It is also permissible that this was the dome which 'Ata' mentioned, which Allah had created from the foam of water. It is also permissible that it was a ruby or a pearl that had been sent down from the sky. It is also permissible that Adam had built it and then it collapsed, until Ibrahim and Isma'il raised its foundations. We have no knowledge of which of these was the case, [[A similar expression occurred at 1:520, line 16, and then at 2:517, line 15.]] because the reality of this cannot be known except through a report from Allah and from His Messenger (ﷺ), by widely transmitted narration. There is no report on this which establishes proof and which must be accepted. Nor is it, since there is no report about it, as we have described, something that can be indicated by reasoning and analogy, so that it may be compared with other things and its knowledge derived through ijtihad (independent reasoning). Therefore, there is no view on this which is more correct than what we have said. And Allah knows best.

* *

The explanation of the words of Allah, may He be exalted: ﴿Our Lord, accept from us﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By this, Allah, may He be remembered, means: "And when Ibrahim and Isma'il were raising the foundations of the House, they were saying: Our Lord, accept from us." It is reported that this is how it is in the recitation of Ibn Mas'ud. This is the view of a group of the people of ta'wil (exegesis, ta'wil: the interpretation of the meaning of the Qur'an).

Those who said this:

2051- Musa ibn Harun narrated to me, saying: 'Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, who said: While they were building and calling upon the words with which Ibrahim was tested by his Lord, he said: "Our Lord, accept from us; indeed You are the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing. Our Lord, and make us Muslims [in submission] to You, and from our descendants a Muslim community [submissive] to You. Our Lord, and send among them a messenger from themselves."

2052- Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn Kathir informed me, saying: Sa'id ibn Jubayr narrated to us, from Ibn 'Abbas: "And when Ibrahim and Isma'il were raising the foundations of the House," he said: They were raising the foundations of the House and saying: "Our Lord, accept from us; indeed You are the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing." He said: And Isma'il was carrying the stones on his neck, while the old man (Ibrahim) was building.

* *

So the interpretation of the verse according to this view is: "And when Ibrahim is raising the foundations of the House, and Isma'il, saying: Our Lord, accept from us."

* *

Others said: Rather, the one who was saying it was Isma'il. So the interpretation of the verse according to this view is: "And when Ibrahim was raising the foundations of the House, and when [Isma'il] was saying: Our Lord, accept from us." In this case, "Isma'il" is in the nominative case by the sentence that follows it, and "saying" (yaqulu) is then a predicate for him, not for Ibrahim.

* *

Then the people of ta'wil differed about who raised the foundations, after they agreed that Ibrahim was among those who raised them.

Some of them said: Ibrahim and Isma'il both raised them.

Those who said this:

2053- Musa ibn Harun narrated to me, saying: 'Amr ibn Hammad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "And We charged Ibrahim and Isma'il: Purify My House for those who circumambulate." [[The beginning of this report in the tafsir of Ibn Kathir reads: "Al-Suddi said: Allah, mighty and majestic, commanded Ibrahim to build the House, he and Isma'il: Build My House for those who circumambulate, and those who stay in devotion, and those who bow and prostrate. So Ibrahim set out..." And in Tarikh al-Tabari, 1:129: "He said: When Allah charged Ibrahim and Isma'il that they should purify My House for those who circumambulate, Ibrahim set out..."]]
He said: So Ibrahim set out until he came to Makkah, and he and Isma'il stood up and took up the pickaxes, not knowing where the House was. Then Allah sent a wind called the wind of al-Khajuj, which had two wings and a head in the form of a snake, and it swept clear for them what was around the Ka'bah, from the foundation of the first House, [[In the printed edition it reads: "and from the foundation of the House," with the added waw, and there is no good in adding it; I have kept what is in the Tarikh and in Ibn Kathir. In Ibn Kathir it reads: "it uncovered for them" instead of "it swept." The wind al-Khajuj is the strong wind, which twists in its blowing and splits with the violence of its gust.]] and they followed it with the pickaxes, digging, until they laid the foundation. This is when He says: ﴿And [mention] when We settled for Ibrahim the place of the House﴾ [Surah al-Hajj: 26]. When they had built the foundations and reached the place of the corner, Ibrahim said to Isma'il: "O my son, seek for me a fine stone that I may place here." He said: "O father, I am lazy and tired." He said: "Go and do it." So he went and sought a stone for him, and brought him a stone, but he did not accept it, and said: "Bring me a stone better than this." So he went seeking a stone for him, and Jibril brought him the Black Stone from India; it was white, a white ruby like the thaghamah. [[Al-thaghamah: a plant with a stalk whose tuft is like the head of an old man, white in fruit and flower, and whiteness of gray hair is likened to it. In a hadith: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was brought Abu Quhafah on the day of the Conquest, and his head was like thaghamah, so he commanded them to change its color.]] And Adam had descended with it from Paradise, and it had blackened from the sins of people. Then Isma'il came to him with a stone and found it at the corner, so he said: "O father, who brought you this?" He said: "One more energetic than you!" So they built it.
[[The report: 2052. In Tarikh al-Tabari, 1:129, its beginning until the words: "And [mention] when We settled for Ibrahim the place of the House," and its complete text is in the tafsir of Ibn Kathir, 1:325. A part of its beginning has already passed under number 2009.]]

2054- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from 'Umar ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Urwah, from 'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr al-Laythi, who said: It reached me that Ibrahim and Isma'il were the ones who raised the foundations of the House. [[The report: 2054- 'Umar ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr ibn al-'Awwam: one of the reliable successors of the successors, who also narrates from his grandfather 'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, and al-Shaykhan (al-Bukhari and Muslim) included him in their Sahihs. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib. Also Ibn Abi Hatim 3/1/117, and the book al-Jam' bayn rijal al-Sahihayn, p. 341.
In the printed edition it appears as "'Amr ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Utbah," which is a major error; there is no narrator among the transmitters by this name.
Moreover, this report itself is a few words from a long story, which al-Tabari narrated in the Tarikh 1:134, with this chain: "From 'Umar ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Urwah: that 'Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr said to 'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr al-Laythi: How did it reach you that Ibrahim called to the Hajj?..."
'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr al-Laythi: his biography has passed at 1768.]]

* *

Others said: Rather, Ibrahim raised the foundations of the House, and Isma'il was handing him the stones.

Those who said this:

2055- Ahmad ibn Thabit al-Razi narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Ayyub and Kathir ibn Kathir ibn al-Muttalib ibn Abi Wada'ah (one of them exceeding the other), from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Ibrahim came, and Isma'il was whittling an arrow near Zamzam. When he saw him, he stood up to him, and they did as a father does with a son and a son with a father. Then he said: "O Isma'il, Allah has commanded me with a command." He said: "Do what your Lord has commanded you." He said: "Will you help me?" He said: "I will help you." He said: "Allah has commanded me to build a house here!" And he pointed to the Ka'bah, which was raised above what was around it. He said: At that point they raised the foundations of the House. He said: So Isma'il began bringing the stones, and Ibrahim was building, until when the building had risen, he brought this stone and placed it for him, and he stood upon it while building, and Isma'il was handing him the stones, and they were saying: "Our Lord, accept from us; indeed You are the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing," until he circled around the House. [[The hadith: 2055- Ahmad ibn Thabit ibn 'Attab al-Razi, known as Farkhawayh, the teacher of al-Tabari. Ibn Abi Hatim mentioned him at 1/1/44, and Lisan al-Mizan 1:143. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Abu al-'Abbas al-Tahrani who said: "They had no doubt that Farkhawayh was a liar."
But a liar may speak the truth! The hadith in itself is sound. It was narrated by al-Bukhari, in very great length, from 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad, from 'Abd al-Razzaq, with this chain, 6:283-289 (Fath). What is here is a piece of it.
Ibn Kathir mentioned the narration of al-Bukhari in full at 1:320-322, then pointed to this narration of al-Tabari.]]

2056- Ibn Sinan al-Qazzaz narrated to us, saying: 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Majid Abu 'Ali al-Hanafi narrated to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Nafi' narrated to us, saying: I heard Kathir ibn Kathir narrating, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: He (Ibrahim) came and found Isma'il repairing an arrow behind Zamzam. Ibrahim said: "O Isma'il, your Lord has commanded me to build a house for Him." Isma'il said to him: "Then obey your Lord in what He has commanded you." Ibrahim said to him: "He has commanded you to help me in it." He said: "I will do so." He said: So he stood up with him, and Ibrahim began building it, and Isma'il was handing him the stones, and they were saying: "Our Lord, accept from us; indeed You are the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing." When the structure rose, and the old man became too weak to lift the stones, he stood upon a stone, which is the Station of Ibrahim, and he began handing them to him, and they were saying: "Our Lord, accept from us; indeed You are the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing." [[The hadith: 2056- Ibn Sinan al-Qazzaz: he is Muhammad ibn Sinan, whose biography has passed at 157. In the printed edition here it reads "Ibn Bashshar"! This is a misreading.
This hadith is also part of a long hadith, narrated by al-Bukhari 6:290 (Fath), from 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad, from Abu 'Amir al-'Aqadi 'Abd al-Malik ibn 'Amr, from Ibrahim ibn Nafi', with this chain.
Ibn Kathir also quoted it at 1:322-323, from the narration of al-Bukhari.
Al-Hakim narrated it in al-Mustadrak 2:551-552, in abridged form, from Abu al-'Abbas al-Asamm Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Muhammad ibn Sinan al-Qazzaz, your teacher here, with this chain. He declared it sound according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim), and al-Dhahabi agreed, without pointing out al-Hakim's error in his correction, since al-Bukhari narrated it. Ibn Kathir pointed this out, and marveled that al-Hakim would correct it while it is in Sahih al-Bukhari!]]

* *

Others said: Rather, the one who raised the foundations of the House was Ibrahim alone, while Isma'il was then a small child.

Those who said this:

2057- Muhammad ibn Bashshar and Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, both saying: Mu'ammal narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Harithah ibn Mudarrib, from 'Ali, who said: When Ibrahim was commanded to build the House, he set out with him, Isma'il and Hajar. He said: When he came to Makkah, he saw upon his head, at the place of the House, something like a cloud, in which there was something like a head. It spoke to him, saying: "O Ibrahim, build upon my shadow, or upon my measure, and do not add or subtract." When he built [he went out] and left Isma'il and Hajar behind. [[The addition between brackets is from Tarikh al-Tabari 1:129 and Tafsir Ibn Kathir 1:324.]] Hajar said: "O Ibrahim, to whom are you leaving us?" He said: "To Allah." She said: "Go, for He will not abandon us." He said: Isma'il became extremely thirsty. He said: Hajar climbed al-Safa, looked, and saw nothing. Then she came to al-Marwah, looked, and saw nothing. Then she returned to al-Safa, looked, and saw nothing, until she had done that seven times. She said: "O Isma'il, die where I cannot see you." She came to him, and he was scraping the ground with his foot from thirst. [[Fahasat al-dajajah wa ghayriha bi-rijliha fi al-turab: she scraped the earth with her foot in the dust, searching and removing the dirt from a hole.]] Then Jibril called to her and said: "Who are you?" She said: "I am Hajar, the mother of Ibrahim's child." He said: "To whom have you both been entrusted?" She said: "We have been entrusted to Allah." He said: "You have both been entrusted to the one who suffices (kafin)!" He said: [The boy] scraped the ground with his finger, [[The addition between brackets is from Tarikh al-Tabari 1:129; it is not in Ibn Kathir.]] and Zamzam gushed forth, and she began to hold back the water. He said: "Leave it, for it is abundant (rawa')." [[The hadith: 2057- Mu'ammal, with the pattern of Muhammad, is Ibn Isma'il al-'Adawi, and he is reliable. We have demonstrated his reliability in the explanation of the Musnad, 2173.
Sufyan is al-Thawri. And Abu Ishaq is al-Sab'i.
Harithah ibn Mudarrib al-'Abdi: a reliable successor. Biographed in al-Tahdhib, and in al-Kabir of al-Bukhari 2/1/87, and Ibn Abi Hatim 1/2/255.
"Mudarrib" with a damma on the mim, a fatha on the ḍad with dots, a kasra on the doubled ra, and ending with a single ba. In the printed edition it reads "Musarrif," which is a misreading.
The report was also narrated by al-Tabari in the Tarikh 1:129, with this chain.
Ibn Kathir narrated it in the tafsir 1:324, from al-Tabari. Then he said: "In this context, it indicates that he built the House before he parted from them. It may be possible, if it is preserved, that initially he set up a boundary and a marker, not that he built it to its top, until Isma'il grew up, and then they built it together, as Allah the Exalted said."
His words "fa-innaha rawa'" (with a fatha on the ra and the waw): one says water is rawa (with fatha on ra and kasra on waw and shadda on ya), and riwa' (kasra then fatha), and rawa': abundant, sweet, flowing, never ceasing.]]

2058- Hannad ibn al-Sari narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Ahwas narrated to us, from Simak, from Khalid ibn 'Ar'arah: that a man stood before 'Ali and said: "Will you not tell me about the House? Is it the first house placed on earth?" He said: "No, but it is the first house in which blessing was placed, [[In the printed edition and in Tarikh and Ibn Kathir: "placed in the blessing." In al-Hakim's al-Mustadrak 1:293, and al-Durr al-Manthur: "placed for the people, in it is blessing and guidance," so I have corrected it from there.]] the Station of Ibrahim, and whoever enters it is safe. And if you wish, I will inform you how it was built: Allah revealed to Ibrahim that he should build a house on earth." He said: Ibrahim was distressed by this, so Allah sent al-Sakinah, which is a wind of al-khajuj with two heads, [[See what passed shortly before: 66, note number 1.]] and one of them followed its companion until it reached Makkah, and it coiled around the place of the House as a shield coils, [[Tataw'at: it circled. Tawwat al-hayyah: the snake coiled and wound some of itself around others, and became circular like a collar. Al-hajfah: a shield of leather which is pressed together, with no wood in it. In al-Tabari's narration in the Tarikh it reads "like the coiling of a snake," and similarly in al-Mustadrak it reads "like the coiling of a snake's collar," and Ibn Kathir has "al-jahfah," which is an error.]] and Ibrahim was commanded to build where al-Sakinah settled. So Ibrahim built, and one stone remained, and the boy went to seek something, and Ibrahim said: "Do not seek a stone for me as I command you." [[In the Tarikh: "I do not seek a stone...," which is an error; and in Ibn Kathir: "Ibrahim said: seek a stone as I command you," which is also an error. One says "ibghini kadhā wa kadhā" (seek for me such and such), and "ibgh li kadhā wa kadhā": that is, look for it for me and seek it. "Baghā fulān fulānan shay'an": he sought for him something.]] He said: So the boy set out seeking a stone for him, and he came and found that [Ibrahim] had set the Black Stone in its place. He said: "O father, who brought you this stone?" He said: "It was brought to me by one who did not depend on your building; Jibril brought it from the sky." So they completed it.
[[The reports 2058-2060 are a single report with three chains.
