On the interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿As We have sent among you a messenger from yourselves, who recites to you Our verses, purifies you, teaches you the Book and wisdom, and teaches you what you did not know﴾ (2:151).

Abu Ja'far said: By His, the Majestic and Exalted's, words "As We have sent among you a messenger," He means: and that I may complete My blessing upon you by clarifying the laws of your Hanifi religion, and guide you to the religion of My friend (khalil) Ibrahim, peace be upon him. So I make for you the supplication he made and the request he asked of Me when he said: ﴿Our Lord, and make us Muslims [submitting] to You, and of our descendants a Muslim nation [submitting] to You. And show us our rites [of worship] and accept our repentance. Indeed, You are the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful﴾ (2:128). Just as I made for you the supplication he made, and the request he asked of Me when he said: (﴿Our Lord, and send among them a messenger from themselves who will recite to them Your verses and teach them the Book and wisdom and purify them. Indeed, You are the Exalted in Might, the Wise﴾) (2:129). So I sent to you from among you My messenger, whom Ibrahim, My friend, and his son Isma'il asked Me to send from their descendants.

"Kama" (as) here, since that is the meaning of the speech, is connected (ṣila) to the words of God, the Mighty and Majestic: "and that I may complete My blessing upon you." The words "As We have sent among you a messenger from yourselves" are not connected to His words "so remember Me, I will remember you."

* *

Some people said: the meaning is: "Remember Me as We have sent among you a messenger from yourselves, I will remember you." They claimed that this is an antecedent (muqaddam) whose meaning is a delay (ta'khir) [[This is the view of al-Farra', see Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1: 92.]], so they overdrew the bowstring [[To overdraw (aghraqa al-nazₒ) the bow means to pull it too far, exceeding its limit, so the tip reaches the bow's grip and may cut the archer's hand. The saying "he overdrew in the pull" is a metaphor for excess and extremism.]], strayed from the correct target, and carried the speech away from its known meaning and its clear direction.

This is because the customary usage of the Arabs, understood in their speech among themselves, when one of them says to another, "As I did good to you, O so-and-so, so do good," is that they do not make it conditional for the other, since the "kaf" in "kama" is a condition whose meaning is: do as you did. The coming of the answer "remember Me" after it, namely "I will remember you," is the clearest evidence that "As We have sent" is connected to the verb before it, and that "remember Me, I will remember you" is a separate new statement cut off from the first, and that it is far removed from the cause of "As We have sent among you."

* *

Some grammarians claimed that His words "so remember Me," when "As We have sent among you" is made its answer together with "I will remember you," is like a conditional that has two answers, as one says: "If so-and-so comes to you, go to him, he will be pleased," so that "go to him" and "he will be pleased" become two answers to "if he comes to you," and like His words: "If you come to me, I will do good to you, I will honour you." [[This is also from al-Farra's statement, see Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1: 92.]]

This view, though it is one of the views, is not the easiest or most eloquent in the speech of the Arabs. What is more fitting for the Book of God, the Mighty and Majestic, to be directed toward among the forms of speech is the most eloquent and most familiar of Arabic usage, not the most unusual and least known of its expression. Moreover, its direction is far from the understood meaning in the interpretation.

* *

Mention of those who said: "As We have sent" is the answer to "so remember Me."

2309 - Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, saying: I heard Ibn Abi Najih say concerning the words of God, the Mighty and Majestic, "As We have sent among you a messenger from yourselves": as I did, so remember Me.

2310 - al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

* *

As for His words "As We have sent among you a messenger from yourselves," He means by it the Arabs. The Exalted said to them: Hold fast, O Arabs, to My obedience and turn toward the qibla I commanded you to face, so that the proof of the Jews against you is cut off and they have no argument against you, and that I may complete My blessing upon you, and that you may be guided, just as I began My blessing upon you when I sent among you a messenger from yourselves. That messenger sent to them from among them is Muhammad (ﷺ), as:

2311 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi' concerning His words "As We have sent among you a messenger from yourselves," meaning Muhammad (ﷺ).

* *

As for His words "who recites to you Our verses," He means the verses of the Qur'an. By His words "and purifies you," He means cleansing you from the filth of sins. "And teaches you the Book," which is the Furqan, meaning He teaches them its rulings. By "wisdom" He means the sunnah and understanding of the religion. We have already explained all of this earlier with its evidence. [[See what has passed in this volume 3: 86-88 and the references.]]

* *

As for His words "and teaches you what you did not know," He means: and He teaches you news of the prophets, the stories of earlier nations, and information about what is occurring and will occur of matters which the Arabs did not know, and they came to know them from the Messenger (ﷺ). He, the Exalted, informed them that they would grasp all of that only through His Messenger (ﷺ).

**On the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So remember Me, and I will remember you﴾**

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: By this, exalted is His remembrance, He means: Remember Me, O believers, by obeying Me in what I command you and in what I forbid you. I will remember you with My mercy toward you and My forgiveness of you, as related:

2312. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, from Ibn Lahi'a, from 'Ata' ibn Dinar, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, regarding ﴿So remember Me, I will remember you﴾: "Remember Me by obeying Me, and I will remember you by forgiving you."

* *

Some of them interpreted it as remembrance by praise and commendation.

Those who said this:

1313. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi' regarding His saying, ﴿So remember Me, I will remember you, and give thanks to Me and do not deny Me﴾: Indeed God remembers whoever remembers Him, increases the one who thanks Him, and punishes the one who disbelieves in Him.

2314. Musa narrated to me, saying: 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi regarding ﴿remember Me, I will remember you﴾: "There is no servant who remembers God except that God remembers him. No believer remembers Him except that He remembers him with mercy, and no disbeliever remembers Him except that He remembers him with punishment."

* *

**On the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And give thanks to Me and do not deny Me﴾ (2:152)**

Abu Ja'far said: By this, exalted is His remembrance, He means: Give thanks to Me, O believers, for what I have bestowed upon you of Islam and of guidance to the religion that I have prescribed for My prophets and chosen servants. "And do not deny Me" means: do not reject My kindness toward you, lest I strip you of the blessing that I have bestowed upon you. Rather, give thanks to Me for it, and I will increase you, and complete My blessing upon you, and guide you to what I have guided those of My servants with whom I am pleased. For I have promised My creation that whoever thanks Me, I will increase, and whoever denies Me, I will deprive and strip of what I have given him.

* *

The Arabs say: "I advised you and gave thanks to you" (nasahtu laka wa shakartu laka), and they hardly say "nasahtuka" (I advised you without the preposition). Sometimes they say: "shakartuka wa nasahtuka" (I thanked you and advised you). Among this is the poet's saying:

[The poem is attributed by Abu Hayyan in his tafsir (1:447) to 'Umar ibn La'j, and I did not find the verse elsewhere.]

They gathered for you both hardship and ease,
So why did you not thank the people when you did not fight?

[Ma'ani al-Qur'an by al-Farra' (1:92). In the printed edition it read "in lam tuqatil" (if you did not fight), and I have restored what is in al-Farra'. Al-bu's̱a and al-ba's̱a: hardship. Al-na'ma and al-ni'ma: blessing.]

And al-Nabigha said, using "nasahtu" (I advised):

I advised the Banu 'Awf, but they did not accept
My message, and my pleas did not succeed among them.

[His Diwan (p. 89), Ma'ani al-Qur'an by al-Farra' (1:92), and Amali Ibn al-Shajari (1:362). It concerns the raid of 'Amr ibn al-Harith al-Asghar against the Banu Murra ibn 'Awf ibn Sa'd ibn Dhubyan. The Diwan has "fa-lam yataqabbalu wasati" (they did not accept my advice). Wasa'il is the plural of wasila: what one draws near to another by way of kinship or tie.]

* *

We have already shown that the meaning of "shukr" (thanks) is praising a man for his praiseworthy deeds, and that the meaning of "kufr" (denial) is covering a thing. This was explained earlier, so there is no need to repeat it here.

[On the meaning of "shukr," see 1:135–138. On the explanation of the meaning of "kufr," see what preceded it at 1:255, 1:382, 1:522, and many other places. Look them up in the language index.]

The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted Is He: ﴿O you who have believed, seek help through patience and prayer. Indeed, Allah is with the patient.﴾ (2:153)

Abu Ja'far said: This verse is an exhortation from Allah, may He be remembered, to obey Him and to bear what is disliked of it by the bodies and the wealth. So He said: ﴿O you who have believed, seek help through patience and prayer﴾, for standing in obedience to Me and performing My obligations, in the abrogating of My rulings, and turning away from what I abrogate of them to what I establish for you of My obligations and transfer you to from My rulings, and submitting to My command in what I order you, at the time I impose its ruling upon you, and turning away from it after My transferring you from it. This applies even if there befalls you in that some disliked thing from the speech of your enemies, the unbelievers, in their casting falsehood at you, or hardship upon your bodies in your standing by it, or loss in your wealth. [[These are interlinked clauses, and the construction of the conjunction in this sentence is: seek help through patience and prayer for standing in My obedience and performing My obligations. . . and turning away from what I abrogate. . . and submitting to My command. . . and turning away from it. . . and for striving against your enemies. . . through patience. . .]] And for striving against your enemies and fighting them in My way, through your patience toward Me in bearing that disliked thing and its hardship upon you, and enduring its toil and weight. Then, through your turning in dread, in what befalls you of grave affairs, to prayer to Me. For indeed, by patience under hardships you attain My good pleasure, and by prayer to Me you succeed in your requests before Me, and attain your needs with Me. Indeed, I am with the patient, in standing to perform My obligations and abandon My disobedience, helping them, guarding them, and protecting them, until they triumph in what they sought and hoped for from Me.

* *

The meaning of "patience" and "prayer" has already been explained earlier, so we disliked repeating it. [[See above the explanation of "prayer" in 1:242-243, then 2:11. And the explanation of "patience" in 2:11, 124, and see the index of language.]] As follows:

2315 - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Adam related to us, saying: Abu Ja'far related to us, from al-Rabi', from Abu al-'Aliyah, regarding His words: ﴿and seek help through patience and prayer﴾, he said: Seek help through patience and prayer for the good pleasure of Allah, and know that they are from the obedience of Allah.

2316 - I was told by Ammar, who said: Ibn Abi Ja'far related to us, from his father, from al-Rabi', regarding His words: ﴿O you who have believed, seek help through patience and prayer﴾, he said: Know that they are a support for obedience to Allah.

* *

As for His words: ﴿Indeed, Allah is with the patient﴾, its interpretation is: Indeed, Allah is their helper, their supporter, and is pleased with their action. It is like the saying of one who says: "Do it, O so-and-so, and I am with you," meaning: I will help you in doing that and assist you in it.

The commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 2, verse 154:

**On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: "And do not say of those who are killed in the way of Allah, 'They are dead.' Rather, they are alive, but you do not perceive" (2:154).**

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: Exalted is His remembrance, means: O you who have believed, seek help through patience in obeying Me in fighting your enemy, in abandoning My disobedience, and in performing the other obligations I have imposed upon you. "And do not say of those who are killed in the way of Allah, 'He is dead'." For the dead among My creation is the one whose life I have taken away and whose senses I have annihilated, so that he feels no pleasure and perceives no bliss. Indeed, whoever among you, and among the rest of My creation, is killed in My way is alive with Me, in life and bliss, in a pleasant and agreeable existence and abundant provision, rejoicing in what I have given them of My bounty and what I have bestowed upon them of My honour. As:

2317. Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words, "Rather, they are alive": [they are alive] with their Lord, provided for from the fruit of Paradise, and they smell its fragrance, but they are not in it.

2318. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

2319. Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His words, "And do not say of those who are killed in the way of Allah, 'They are dead; rather, they are alive, but you do not perceive'": We used to be told [in the printed edition: "as is narrated", and the correct reading is what has been established] that the souls of the martyrs are in the form of white birds that eat from the fruits of Paradise, that their dwellings are the Lote-tree of the Utmost Boundary (Sidrat al-Muntaha), and that the one who strives in the way of Allah has three kinds of good: whoever is killed in the way of Allah among them becomes living and provided for; whoever is defeated, Allah gives him a great reward; and whoever dies, Allah provides him a goodly provision.

2320. Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada, regarding His words, "And do not say of those who are killed in the way of Allah, 'They are dead; rather, they are alive'," he said: The souls of the martyrs are in the forms of white birds.

2321. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi', regarding His words, "And do not say of those who are killed in the way of Allah, 'They are dead; rather, they are alive'": in the forms of green birds that fly in Paradise wherever they wish, and eat from wherever they wish.

2322. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Uthman ibn Ghiyath narrated to us, saying: I heard Ikrimah say regarding His words, "And do not say of those who are killed in the way of Allah, 'They are dead; rather, they are alive, but you do not perceive'": The souls of the martyrs are in green birds in Paradise.

* * *

Abu Ja'far said: If someone says to us: What is the particularity in His words, "And do not say of those who are killed in the way of Allah, 'They are dead; rather, they are alive'," concerning the one killed in the way of Allah, which is not shared by others? For you know that the reports from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) are abundant describing the condition of believers and disbelievers after their death. He informed that for believers doors are opened for them from their graves to Paradise, from which they smell its fragrance, and that they hasten Allah to establish the Hour so that they may reach their dwellings therein and be gathered with their families and children in it. And [he informed] that for disbelievers doors are opened for them from their graves to the Fire, through which they look at it, and its stench and hardship reach them, and that there is set over them therein someone who subdues them until the establishment of the Hour, and they ask Allah therein to delay the Hour, out of fear of arriving at what Allah has prepared for them therein; along with the like of these reports. If the reports concerning this are abundant from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), then what is it that the one killed in the way of Allah has been singled out with, of the life that no one else among mankind shares with him? For the rest of the disbelievers and believers, other than him, are alive in the barzakh (the intermediate state between death and resurrection). As for the disbelievers, they are punished therein with a constricted life; and as for the believers, they are given bliss with rest, sweet basil, and the breeze of the Gardens?

It is said: What Allah has singled out the martyrs with in this matter, and what He has informed the believers of through His report about them, exalted is His remembrance, is His informing them that they are provided for from the food and provisions of Paradise in their barzakh before their resurrection, and that they are given bliss with what those who enter it after resurrection from among the rest of mankind are given bliss with, from its delicious foods, which Allah has not fed to anyone else in his barzakh before his resurrection. That is the virtue with which He has favoured them and singled them out over others, and that is the benefit which He conveyed to the believers through the report about them. So exalted is His remembrance said to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): "And do not think of those who were killed in the way of Allah as dead; rather, they are alive, with their Lord, being provided for, rejoicing in what Allah has given them of His bounty" (Al 'Imran 3:169–170). And the like of what we have said has come in the report from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

2323. Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahim ibn Sulayman and Abdah ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from al-Harith ibn Fudayl, from Mahmud ibn Labid, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The martyrs are at Bariq, a river at the gate of Paradise, in a green dome — and Abdah said: in a green meadow — there their provision comes out to them from Paradise, morning and evening."[[Hadith 2323: Abdah ibn Sulayman al-Kalabi al-Kufi: trustworthy, one of the teachers of Ahmad and Ishaq. Biographised in al-Tahdhib, Ibn Sa'd 6:272, and Ibn Abi Hatim 3/1/89.

al-Harith ibn Fudayl al-Ansari al-Madani: trustworthy; Ibn Ma'in, al-Nasa'i and others declared him trustworthy. Biographised in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir 1/2/277, and Ibn Abi Hatim 1/2/86.

Mahmud ibn Labid ibn Uqbah ibn Rafi' al-Ashhali, al-Awsi, al-Ansari: a companion according to the preponderant view, which al-Bukhari affirmed; he died in the year 96 or 97. Al-Waqidi said: He died at the age of 99 years. Al-Hafiz said in al-Tahdhib: "According to al-Waqidi's statement on the year, he would have been 13 years old on the day the Prophet (ﷺ) died. This strengthens the view of those who affirm his companionship." Al-Bukhari reported in al-Kabir 4/1/402, with a sound chain: "From Mahmud ibn Labid who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) hastened until our sandals broke, on the day Sa'd ibn Mu'adh died." This is sufficient proof of his companionship. But Ibn Abi Hatim (4/1/289–290) said: "Al-Bukhari said: he has companionship. My father put a line through it and said: his companionship is not known," which is a negation without evidence, and it does not stand against an affirmation supported by sound evidence. Therefore Ibn Abd al-Barr said, as in al-Tahdhib: "Al-Bukhari's statement is more preferable." He is also biographised in Ibn Sa'd 5:55–56 and al-Isabah 6:66–67.

This hadith was also narrated by Ahmad in al-Musnad (2390), from Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim ibn Sa'd, from his father, from Ibn Ishaq, with this chain.

Likewise Ibn Hibban narrated it in his Sahih 7:69 (from the manuscript of al-Ihsan), by way of Ya'qub, with it. Al-Hakim narrated it in al-Mustadrak 2:74, by way of Yazid ibn Harun, from Ibn Ishaq, and said: "This is a hadith whose chain is sound according to the condition of Muslim, though they (Bukhari and Muslim) did not record it." Al-Dhahabi agreed with him.

Ibn Kathir mentioned it in his Tafsir 2:292, from the narration of the Musnad, and said: "Ahmad alone narrated it." Then he pointed to this narration of al-Tabari and said: "And its chain is good." It is in Majma' al-Zawa'id 5:298, where he attributed it to Ahmad and al-Tabarani, and said: "The men of Ahmad are trustworthy."

Al-Suyuti mentioned it at 2:96 and added its attribution to Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn al-Mundhir, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Ba'th.

As for his words, "And Abdah said…": he means that "Abdah ibn Sulayman" said "in a meadow" instead of "in a dome." In the printed edition it reads "or Abdah said," and placing "or" here instead of the conjunctive "and" is an error that is not acceptable. We incline to think it is from a copyist or a typesetter.]]

2324. Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Jabir ibn Nuh narrated to us, from al-Ifriqi, from Ibn Bashshar al-Sulami — or Abu Bashshar, Abu Ja'far was in doubt — who said: The souls of the martyrs are in white domes from the domes of Paradise; in each dome are two wives. Their provision each day the sun rises is a bull and a fish. As for the bull, in it is the taste of every fruit in Paradise, and as for the fish, in it is the taste of every drink in Paradise.[[The report 2324: This is a report I do not know what it is! Its head, "Ibn Bashshar al-Sulami, or Abu Bashshar," about which Ibn Jarir expressed doubt, I have not been able to find anything that indicates it. Al-Suyuti mentioned it at 2:96 from this place in al-Tabari, and then did nothing!]]

* * *

Abu Ja'far said: If someone says: Indeed, the report of what you mentioned, that Allah, exalted is His remembrance, conveyed to the believers through His report about the martyrs of the bounty He singled them out with in the barzakh, is not present in His words, "And do not say of those who are killed in the way of Allah, 'They are dead; rather, they are alive'." Rather, what is in it is a report about their state: whether they are dead or alive.

It is said: The purpose of mentioning the report about their life is only the report about the bounty they are in. But since He, exalted is His remembrance, had already informed His servants about what He singled out the martyrs with in His words, "And do not think of those who were killed in the way of Allah as dead; rather, they are alive, with their Lord, being provided for" (3:169), and they knew their state by that report, then the intent of Allah, exalted is His remembrance, in His words, "And do not say of those who are killed in the way of Allah, 'They are dead; rather, they are alive'," is the prohibition to His creation against saying to the martyrs that they are dead[[Context of the speech: "But since He, exalted is His remembrance, had already informed His servants… he omitted the repetition of…".]] — He omitted repeating what had already been made clear to them of their condition.

* * *

As for His words, "but you do not perceive," He means by it: "but you do not see them so that you would know that they are alive; you only know that by My informing you of it."

* * *

As for the word "dead" (amwatun) being in the nominative, it is due to an implied pronoun referring back to the noun "those who are killed in the way of Allah." The meaning is: "Do not say of those who are killed in the way of Allah, 'They are dead'." The accusative case for "amwat" is not permissible, because the verb "say" does not govern them. Likewise His words, "Rather, they are alive," is in the nominative, meaning: "they are alive."[[In the printed edition: "they are alive," but the context requires what has been established. See al-Farra's Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1:93–94, for he fully covered what al-Tabari abridged.]]

**The interpretation of His words, the Exalted: ﴿And We will surely test you with something of fear and hunger, and a loss of wealth and lives and fruits. But give good tidings to the patient.﴾ [2:155]**

Abu Ja'far said: This is an announcement from Allah, dhikruhu (may His remembrance be exalted), to the followers of His Messenger (ﷺ), that He will try them and test them with severe matters, so that He may know who follows the Messenger from among those who turn back on their heels. He tested them, putting them to the trial, by changing the qibla from Bayt al-Maqdis to the Ka'bah, and as He tested His chosen ones before them. He promised them this in another verse, when He said to them: ﴿Or do you think that you will enter Paradise while there has not yet come to you the example of those who passed away before you? Adversity and hardship touched them, and they were shaken until the Messenger and those who believed with him said, "When is the help of Allah?" Unquestionably, the help of Allah is near.﴾ [2:214]. Ibn 'Abbas and others said in a manner similar to what we have said about this.

2325 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His words: "And We will surely test you with something of fear and hunger," and similar to this, he said: Allah informed the believers that the world is a abode of trial (ibtila', meaning testing by hardship), that He tests them therein, and He commanded them to be patient and gave them good tidings, saying: "But give good tidings to the patient." Then He informed them that He did the same with His prophets and His chosen ones, so that their souls would be at ease, saying: ﴿Adversity and hardship touched them, and they were shaken.﴾

* *

The meaning of His words "wa-la-nabluwannakum" is: "and We will surely test you." We have already explained that the meaning of ibtila' is testing (ikhtibar), in what has passed before. [See what preceded: 2:48, 49; then this part, 3:7.]

* *

His words "with something of fear" mean fear of the enemy. "And hunger" means famine. He says: We will test you with something of fear that will befall you from your enemy, and with a drought that will strike you, in which a famine and hardship will befall you, and your means of livelihood will become difficult for you, so that your wealth will decrease because of that, and with wars that will occur between you and your enemies from among the unbelievers, so that your numbers will decrease because of them, and with the death of your offspring and children, and with droughts that will occur, so that your crops will decrease because of them. All of that is a trial from Me for you, and a test from Me for you, so that your truthful ones in their faith will be distinguished from your liars regarding it, and so that the people of insight in their religion will be recognized among you, apart from the people of hypocrisy, doubt and suspicion regarding it.

All of that is an address from Him to the followers of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his Companions, as:

2326 - Harun ibn Idris al-Kufi al-Asamm narrated to me, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad al-Muharibi narrated to us, from 'Abd al-Malik, from 'Ata', concerning His words: "And We will surely test you with something of fear and hunger," he said: They are the Companions of Muhammad (ﷺ). [The report: this chain of narration has preceded at 1455, and we do not know the shaykh of al-Tabari in it.]

* *

Allah, dhikruhu, said "with something of fear" and did not say "with things," because of the difference in the types of what He informed His servants He would test them with. Since that was varied, and "min" (from/with, a partitive particle) indicates that each type contains an implied "shay'" (thing), the meaning is: "And We will surely test you with something of fear, and with something of hunger, and with something of loss of wealth." He was satisfied with the indication of the mention of "shay'" at the beginning, without repeating it with each type.

He, dhikruhu, did all of that to them, and tested them with various kinds of trials, as:

2327 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi' concerning His words: "And We will surely test you with something of fear and hunger and a loss of wealth and lives and fruits," he said: That has indeed happened, and what is even more severe than that will happen.

At that, Allah said: ﴿But give good tidings to the patient, who, when disaster strikes them, say, "Indeed, we belong to Allah, and indeed to Him we will return." Those are the ones upon whom are blessings from their Lord and mercy, and those are the guided.﴾ [2:155–157]

* *

Then He, dhikruhu, said to His Prophet (ﷺ): O Muhammad, give good tidings to those who are patient in My trial with what I test them with, and who restrain their souls from transgressing My prohibition against what I have forbidden them, and who hold themselves to performing what I have obligated them with of My obligations, along with My testing them with what I test them with, those who say when a disaster strikes them: "Indeed, we belong to Allah, and indeed to Him we will return." So Allah, dhikruhu, commanded him to single out, with the good tidings regarding the hardships with which He tests them, the people of patience whom Allah described with their attribute.

* *

The origin of "tabshir" (giving good tidings) is: a man informing another man of news that gladdens him or grieves him, which had not preceded him to someone else. [See what preceded: 1:383 / 2:393.]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 156:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿Those who, when a misfortune strikes them, say, "Indeed we belong to Allah, and indeed to Him we will return."﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, means: And give good news, O Muhammad, to the patient ones (al-sabirin) who know that all the blessing they have is from Me. So they acknowledge their servitude to Me, affirm My lordship alone, believe in the Resurrection and their return to Me, submit to My decree, hope for My reward, and fear My punishment. And they say, when I test them with some of My trials, and I afflict them with what I promised I would afflict them with, such as fear, hunger, loss of wealth, lives, and fruits, and other calamities by which I test them: "Indeed we are the possessions of our Lord and our Worshipped One, alive, and we are His servants, and indeed to Him we shall return after our deaths." This is submission to My decree and contentment with My judgments.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 157:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, saying: ﴿Those are the ones upon whom are blessings from their Lord, and mercy. And those are the guided.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His, may His remembrance be exalted, saying "those" He means these patient ones whom He has described and characterized. "Upon them" means: for them. "Blessings" means: forgiveness. "And the blessings of God" upon His servants is His forgiveness of His servants, as was narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said:

2328 - "O God, bless the family of Abi Awfa." [[The hadith 2328 is part of a sound hadith. It was narrated by al-Bukhari (3: 286, from al-Fath) and Muslim (1: 297). Both from the route of Shu'ba, from Amr ibn Murra, from Abdullah ibn Abi Awfa, who said: "When a people came to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) with their charity, he would say: O God, bless them. My father Abu Awfa came to him with his charity, and he said: O God, bless the family of Abi Awfa."

The Hafiz said: "He means Abu Awfa himself, because 'family' (al) is applied to the essence of a thing... And it was said that this is not said except regarding a man of great standing."

This is an excellent benefit from the Hafiz Ibn Hajar, may God have mercy on him.]]

* *

That is: forgive them. We have explained "prayer" (salah) and its origin in other places. [[See what has passed: 1: 242; then 2: 505; then 2: 37, 213, 214.]]

As for His saying "and mercy," it means: and for them, along with the forgiveness by which He pardons their sins and covers them, is mercy and compassion from God.

Then God, may His remembrance be exalted, informed, along with what He mentioned that He gives them for their patience in His trials, their submission to His decree, of forgiveness and mercy, that they are the guided, those who hit upon the path of truth, and who say what pleases Him, and who do what earns them from God great reward.

We have already explained the meaning of "guidance" (ihtida') earlier, that it means being rightly guided to what is correct. [[See what has passed: 1: 166-170, 230, 249, 549-551; then 2: 211; then this part 3: 101, 140, 141.]]

* *

Those who held the same view as what we have said about this were a group of the people of interpretation.

Mention of those who said that:

2329 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abdullah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya ibn Salih narrated to me, from Ali ibn Abi Talha, from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: "Those who, when a misfortune strikes them, say: Indeed we belong to God and indeed to Him we return. Those are the ones upon whom are blessings from their Lord and mercy, and those are the guided." He said: God informed that the believer, when he submits the matter to God, and returns and says "we belong to God" at the time of calamity, three qualities of good are written for him: the blessings from God, mercy, and the realization of the path of guidance. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: Whoever says "we belong to God" at the time of calamity, God will repair his calamity, grant him a better end, and give him a righteous successor whom he is pleased with. [[The hadith 2329 was mentioned by al-Haythami in Majma' al-Zawa'id (2: 330-331), who said: "It was narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Kabir, and in its chain is Ali ibn Abi Talha, who is weak."

Al-Suyuti mentioned it in al-Durr al-Manthur (1: 156), and added its attribution to Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman.

Ali ibn Abi Talha was mentioned earlier at 1833 as trustworthy, and the defect of this chain, which recurs frequently in Tabari's Tafsir, is its discontinuity, since Ibn Abi Talha did not hear from Ibn Abbas nor did he meet him.]]

2330 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi' regarding His saying: "Those upon whom are blessings from their Lord and mercy," he said: the blessings and mercy are upon those who were patient and said "we belong to God."

2331 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan al-'Usfuri, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: No one has been given what this community has been given: "Those who, when a misfortune strikes them, say: Indeed we belong to God and indeed to Him we return. Those are the ones upon whom are blessings from their Lord and mercy." And if anyone had been given it, Ya'qub (peace be upon him) would have been given it. Did you not hear his saying: ﴿O my sorrow over Joseph!﴾ [Surah Yusuf: 84]. [[The report 2331: Sufyan al-'Usfuri is Sufyan ibn Ziyad al-'Usfuri, who is trustworthy; he was declared trustworthy by Ibn Ma'in, Abu Hatim, and Abu Zur'a. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib (4: 111, no. 198); Ibn Abi Hatim (2/1/221, no. 966); and al-Kabir of al-Bukhari (2/2/93, no. 2076), though it does not mention the nisba "al-'Usfuri." He is often confused by many scholars with another, "Sufyan ibn Dinar, Abu al-Warqa' al-Ahmari." Ibn Abi Hatim biographed him (2/1/220-221, no. 695), and in some manuscripts of his work the nisba "al-'Usfuri" appears. Al-Bukhari biographed "al-Ahmari" (2/2/92, no. 2073) without mentioning "al-'Usfuri" as well. Al-Tahdhib biographed him (4: 109, no. 193), with some confusion in the two entries, apparent upon reflection. Despite this confusion, al-Hafiz held that they are two persons, and said in the biography of "Sufyan ibn Dinar": "The verified view is that this Sufyan ibn Dinar al-Tammar is also called al-'Usfuri, and that Sufyan ibn Ziyad al-'Usfuri is another, distinguished by al-Bahi." And he said in the biography of the other: "The correct view is that they are two, as Ibn Ma'in and others said." Whatever the case, both are reliable.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 158 (part 1 of 4):

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿Indeed, al-Safa and al-Marwa are among the rites of Allah﴾

Abu Ja'far said: "Al-Safa" is the plural of "safah" (a smooth rock), and from it is the verse of al-Tarmah:

"Dhu al-quwa wa al-tawl (the Possessor of strength and bounty) refused me that any hoof should ever make smooth my safa (rocks)."
[[His Diwan: 134. In the printed edition it reads "yunis hafir abadi," which is an error. Al-tawl means power and wealth; Dhu al-tawl wa al-quwwa is Allah, glorified is He. "Abassa al-shay' yu'abbisuhu" means he subdued and softened it, or broke it. Similar is the verse of Abbas ibn Mirdas:
"If it is a boulder of rock, I shall not make it smooth; I will kindle a fire upon it, heat it, and it will split.
Peace takes from it what you are content with, and war suffices you with its sips (jur'a) of breath."]]

It has also been said that "al-safa" is singular, that its dual is "safawan," and its plurals are "asfa'," "sufiyyan," and "sifiyyan." They cited in support the verse of the rajaz poet
[[He is al-Akhyal al-Ta'i.]]
"As if his two flanks, from the spray (nafy), were landing places of birds upon the smooth rock (al-sufiyy)."
[[It will come in the tafsir at 6:142; also in al-Jamharah 3:135, al-Mukhassas 10:90, Majalis Tha'lab 249, al-Hayawan 2:339, al-Qali 2:8, and al-Lisan (safa) and (nafa). All of them narrate "matnayhi" except Ibn Duraid, who recited: "As if my two flanks, from the spray, from the length of my gazing over the well." The nafy is what flies off from the bucket of the one drawing water. Whoever narrates "matni" means that al-Akhyal describes himself; whoever narrates "matnayhi" means someone else, and this is more correct in my judgment. Al-Azhari said: "This is a camel whose skin was black, which drew water from a salt well, so the spray of water on its back would whiten when it splashed, because it was salty." If this is established, then the narration of the following verse as "min tawl ishraf" (without the ya' of possession) is correct, and the meaning of the poem is closer to what al-Azhari said, given the comparison in the third verse. "Al-tawiyy" is a well lined with stones.]]

They said: it is a counterpart of "asa, wa 'usiyy [wa 'isiyy, wa a'sa'], and rahaa, wa ruhiyy [wa rihiyy] wa arhaa'." [[The additions between the brackets are necessary for the comparison of the one who gives the example with these plurals to be sound, according to their counterparts; that is his saying just before: safa, asfa', safa, and safiyy.]]

* *

As for "al-marwa," it is the small pebble, [[Al-Tabari's explanation of the meaning of "al-maru" is not good; the better is what the lexicographers said: al-maru are white, glittering stones, from which fire is produced, and which are struck to produce fire, and from which a tool like a knife is made with which one slaughters; it is hard.]] whose few are called "marwat," and whose many are called "al-maru," like "tamrah, tamarat, tamr." Al-A'sha Maymun ibn Qays said:

"You see on the earth a passing hoof, and when it meets al-maru, it crushes."
[[His Diwan: 161. In the first half there is a corruption whose correct form I have not determined; the Diwan's version reads: "wa tuwalli al-ard khufan mujmaran." He describes his she-camel, her strength and vigor. The "khuff mujmar" is the hardy, firm, compact hoof, struck by stones so that it becomes hard. "Rad'ha al-hasa wa al-nawa radhan": he crushed and broke it. He means, by the strength and hardness of the hoof, and that is praiseworthy in camels.]]

He means by "al-maru": the small rocks. From this is the verse of Abu Dhu'ayb al-Hudhali:

"Until I am, for the calamities, like a marwah struck every day upon the rock of al-Mushariq."
[[His Diwan: 3, and al-Mufaddaliyyat: 587, from his masterful elegy on his children, in which he says the successive calamities have left him like this rock he described. Al-Mushariq: the one who prays at Mina. Ibn al-Anbari said: "He specified al-mushariq because people pass by it frequently." Then he said: "Abu 'Ubaydah narrated it as 'al-mushaqqar,' meaning the market of al-Ta'if. He says: as if I am a marwah in the market, which people pass by, each striking it one after another."]]

It is also said "al-mushaqqar."

* *

Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, by His words "Indeed, al-Safa and al-Marwa" in this place, meant the two mountains named by these two names within His sanctuary, to the exclusion of all other safa and maru. For this reason He added the definite article "al-" to them, to let His servants know that He meant by that the two mountains known by these two names, to the exclusion of all other rocks and pebbles.

* *

As for His words "from the rites of Allah," it means: from the signs of Allah which He, may His remembrance be exalted, made for His servants as a sign and a rite at which they worship Him, either by supplication, or by remembrance, or by performing what He imposed upon them of acts there. From this is the verse of al-Kumayt:

"We kill them generation after generation; you see them as rites of sacrifice, by which one draws near."
[[Al-Hashimiyyat: 21, and al-Lisan (sh'r), and others. The pronoun in "naqtiluhum" refers to the Kharijites whose names he enumerated in two verses before: "Why, then, did we visit al-Zubayr and Nafi' in our raid, after the troops, a troop..." and "Shabib and Q'anab exceeded in their claim on our spears and in turning them away from you." Al-jil: the community, or the class of people. In the printed edition and al-Lisan: "tarahum" with a ta', which is an error. The "sha'a'ir" here is the plural of sha'irah: the camel offered to the House, and it was named so because marks are impressed upon it. "Ish'ar al-badan" is making it bleed by stabbing, shooting, or an iron until it bleeds.]]

Mujahid used to say about the sha'a'ir:

2332 - Muhammad ibn 'Amr told me, saying: Abu 'Asim told us, from 'Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "Indeed, al-Safa and al-Marwa are among the rites of Allah," he said: "from the news which I inform you of concerning it."
[[In the printed edition: "min al-khayr" with a ya' underneath, which does not fit; the correct form is what is recorded here, and al-Tabari's comment on Mujahid's saying shows that it is from ish'ar, which means informing.]]

2333 - Al-Muthanna told me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah told us, saying: Shibl told us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

* *

So Mujahid seems to have held that the sha'a'ir is only the plural of "sha'irah," from Allah's informing His servants of the matter of al-Safa and al-Marwa and what is incumbent on them in circumambulating them. Its meaning is: informing them of that.

This interpretation from the understood is distant. Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, informed by His words "Indeed, al-Safa and al-Marwa are among the rites of Allah" His believing servants that running between them is among the rites of the Hajj which He prescribed for them, and which He commanded His friend Ibrahim ﷺ, when he asked Him to show him the rites of the Hajj. And although its form is the form of a report, what is intended is a command. For Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, has commanded His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ to follow the religion of Ibrahim, peace be upon him, saying to him: ﴿Then We revealed to you: follow the religion of Ibrahim, a hanif﴾ [Surah al-Nahl: 123], and He, may His remembrance be exalted, made Ibrahim an imam for those after him. Since it is correct that circumambulating and running between al-Safa and al-Marwa are among the rites of Allah and among the rites of the Hajj, it is known that Ibrahim ﷺ acted upon it and prescribed it for those after him, and our Prophet ﷺ and his community were commanded to follow him, so it is incumbent upon them to act accordingly, as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ explained.

* *

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿So whoever performs the Hajj to the House or makes the 'umrah﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, means: "whoever performs the Hajj to the House," i.e., whoever comes to it returning to it after the beginning. Likewise, everyone who frequently goes to something is a "hajj" to it, and from it is the poet's verse: [[He is al-Mukhbil al-Sa'di, and he is a mukhadram (one who lived in both eras).]]

"To witness from 'Awf many gatherings, going on pilgrimage to the abuse of al-Zibriqan the saffron-dyed."
[[Al-Ma'ani al-Kabir: 478; al-Ishtiqaq of Ibn Duraid: 77, 156; Tahdhib al-Alfaz: 563; Islah al-Mantiq: 411; al-Bayan wa al-Tabyin 3:97; Sharh Adab al-Katib of al-Jawaliqi: 313, and of al-Batalyusi: 405; al-Lisan (sabb), (hajj), (qahar), (zibriq); al-Jamharah of Ibn Duraid 1:31, 49/3:434; Samt al-Lali: 191; al-Khizanah 3:427. In the printed edition: "bayt al-Zibriqan," and the correct form is what is recorded here.

Al-Tabari, as Ibn Duraid, Ibn Qutaybah, al-Jahiz and others did, held that "al-sabb" here is the turban, and that the chiefs of the Arabs used to dye their turbans with saffron, among them Husayn ibn Badr, who is al-Zibriqan, and he was named so for the yellowness of his turban and his lordship. Abu 'Ubaydah and Qutrub held that "al-sabb" here is the buttocks, and that he was ridiculed; they claimed that Qutrub's view is an anomalous view. My view is that Abu 'Ubaydah and Qutrub were correct, and that they were mistaken in rejecting what they said. Al-Mukhbil had a foul tongue, to the extent that it is attributed to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that he said: "It is only a punishment which Allah sends upon whomever of His servants He wills" (al-Naqa'id: 1048). Abu 'Ubaydah said in al-Naqa'id: "Al-Mukhbil al-Qurayri was the most satirical of the Arabs... then after him came Hassan ibn Thabit, then al-Hutay'ah, al-Farazdaq, Jarir, and al-Akhtal. These six are the pinnacle in satire and other things, and in the Jahiliyyah and in Islam they had no equal." Now, as for the matter of al-Mukhbil and al-Zibriqan ibn Badr, there was what there was regarding the hospitality of al-Hutay'ah (see Tabaqat Fuhul al-Shu'ara': 96-100), and his satire of him, then what spread of al-Mukhbil's satire against him when he proposed to his sister Khulaydah, and al-Zibriqan refused to marry her to him, and he disparaged him. He satirized him and his sister with obscenity, and belittled him until he said to him:

"O Zibriqan, brother of Banu Khalaf, what are you and the glory and boasting of your father?
You are only among Banu Khalaf like the two buttocks upon which the clitoris has risen."

All of his poetry about al-Zibriqan and his sister is obscene. This verse which al-Tabari cited is from that obscenity. Before the verse: "Do you not know, O Umm 'Amrah, that the misfortunes of time have stumbled upon me, to the greatest degree?"
"To witness from 'Awf many gatherings, going on pilgrimage to the abuse of al-Zibriqan the saffron-dyed."
"Husayn wished to be lord over his people, but Husayn became humiliated and subdued."

In the Sirah of Ibn Hisham 2:275-276 is the saying of 'Utbah ibn Rabi'ah about Abu Jahl: "He will know whose genitals are swollen with pride, I or he!" and he threw at him a similar foulness which al-Mukhbil al-Sa'di said. Whoever claims that al-Mukhbil says he "disliked that he live and last until he sees al-Zibriqan with such majesty and grandeur that the Banu 'Awf go on pilgrimage to his turban," has erred; the third verse has refuted what he claimed, for it describes him as having wished for lordship, but that only increased him in humiliation and subjugation, so how could it be that he says what this one claims he meant? Rather, al-Mukhbil meant to mock him and ridicule him, as he did in all his satire of him.

As for His words "and witness" it is in the accusative, coordinated with His words "li-akbara" (in the verse above).]] He means by His words "yahujjun" (they go on pilgrimage): they frequently go to it because of its lordship and leadership. The pilgrim is only called "hajj" because he comes to the House before the 'Arafat standing, then returns to it for the circumambulation on the day of sacrifice after the 'Arafat standing, then departs from it to Mina, then returns to it for the farewell circumambulation. [[ 'Arafa, ya'rifu, ta'riyfan: he stood at 'Arafat. "Tawaf al-sadr" is from their saying: the people departed from their Hajj, meaning they returned after completing their rites.]] Because of his repeated return to it time after time, he is called "hajj."

* *

As for the "mu'tamir," he is only called "mu'tamir" because when he circumambulates it he departs from it after visiting it. Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, by His words "or makes the 'umrah" means: or makes the 'umrah to the House, and by "i'timar" He means visiting. Every one who sets out for something is a "mu'tamir" to it, and from it is the verse of al-'Ajjaj:

"Indeed Ibn Ma'mar rose high when he set out (i'tamar), a raid far off from far, and he leapt."
[[His Diwan: 19, from a qasidah praising 'Umar ibn 'Ubayd Allah ibn Ma'mar al-Tamimi, of which parts have passed at 1:190, 2:157. His words "maghza," meaning a raid. "Dabar": he gathered his legs to leap and then leapt. He describes the army of 'Umar ibn 'Ubayd Allah, who conquered many conquests, and whose matter grew great in fighting the Kharijites.]]

He means by His words "when he set out" (i'tamar): when he aimed for it and headed toward it.

* *

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿there is no sin upon him in circumambulating them﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, means by His words "there is no sin upon him in circumambulating them": he says, there is no blame upon him and no sin in his circumambulation between them.

* *

If someone says: What is the sense of this statement, when you have told us that His words "Indeed, al-Safa and al-Marwa are among the rites of Allah," although its outward form is that of a report, is in meaning a command to circumambulate them? How can it be a command to circumambulate, and then it is said: there is no blame upon whoever performs the Hajj or makes the 'umrah in circumambulating them? Is blame not removed only from one who does what, by doing it, incurs blame and sin? And the command to circumambulate them and the permission to circumambulate them cannot both be together in one situation?

It is said: That is contrary to what you have gone to. [[In the printed edition: "ilayhi dhahab," and the correct form is what is recorded, because al-Tabari quoted the speaker's statement as addressed to him, since he said to al-Tabari: "You have said to us." So the reply should be directed to him as address, as he addressed him.]] The meaning of that according to some people is: when the Prophet ﷺ performed the 'umrah of the Qada' (making up), some people who used to circumambulate them in the pre-Islamic era, because of two idols that were upon them, as a glorification of them, feared, and they said: How shall we circumambulate them, when we know that glorifying idols and everything that was worshipped besides Allah is shirk? In our circumambulation around these two stones there is a fear of that [[In the printed edition: "ahad dhalika," which has no meaning, and there is a corruption without doubt. For they did not mention multiple sins so as to make for it "one"; rather they meant: the greatest sin and shirk. "Dhalika" refers to shirk. And if it were also read "akhaf dhalika" it would be correct, because he will mention that they feared circumambulating them. He means: the fear of shirk.]], because circumambulating them in the Jahiliyyah was only for the two idols that were upon them, and Allah has brought Islam today, and there is no way to glorify anything alongside Allah in the sense of worship of it!

So Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, revealed concerning their matter: "Indeed, al-Safa and al-Marwa are among the rites of Allah," meaning: indeed circumambulating them. He omitted mention of "circumambulating them," being content with mentioning them instead. And since it was known to those addressed that its meaning is: among the signs of Allah which He made markers for His servants to worship Him at, by circumambulating between them, and remembering Him upon them and at them with what is fitting for Him of remembrance, "so whoever performs the Hajj to the House or makes the 'umrah," let him not fear circumambulating them, because of what the people of the Jahiliyyah used to circumambulate them for, on account of the two idols that were upon them. For the people of shirk used to circumambulate them as disbelief, while you circumambulate them in faith and in affirmation of my messenger and obedience to my command, so there is no sin upon you in circumambulating them.

* *

And the "junah" (sin) is the transgression, as:

2334 - Musa ibn Harun told me, saying: 'Amr told us, saying: Asbat told us, from al-Suddi: "there is no sin upon him in circumambulating them," he says: there is no transgression upon him, but there is a reward for him.

* *

And in accordance with what we have said concerning that, the reports from the early generations, from the Companions and the Successors, have been abundantly transmitted.

Mention of the reports transmitted to that effect:

2335 - Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Malik ibn Abi al-Shawarib told us, saying: Yazid ibn Zurai' told us, saying: Dawud told us, from al-Sha'bi: that there was an idol in the Jahiliyyah upon al-Safa called "Isaf," [[In the printed edition: "Isaf," and the correct form is what is recorded, for it is not prohibited from diptotic inflection.]] and an idol upon al-Marwah called "Na'ilah." The people of the Jahiliyyah, when they circumambulated the House, would wipe the two idols. When Islam came and the idols were broken, the Muslims said: Indeed al-Safa and al-Marwah were only circumambulated for the sake of the two idols, and circumambulating them is not among the rites! He said: So Allah revealed: indeed they are among the rites, "so whoever performs the Hajj to the House or makes the 'umrah, there is no sin upon him in circumambulating them."

**Commentary of al-Ṭabarī (Jāmiʿ al-Bayān) on Surah 2, verse 158 (part 2 of 4)**

2336. Muḥammad ibn al-Muthannā narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Wahhāb narrated to us, saying: Dāwūd narrated to us, from ʿĀmir, who said: There was an idol at al-Ṣafā called "Isāf" [[In the printed edition: "Isāf," but the correct form is what is recorded here, since it is not diptote (ghayr munṣarif).]] and an idol at al-Marwah called "Nāʾilah." Then he mentioned something similar to the report of Ibn Abī al-Shawārib, and added to it: He said: "So al-Ṣafā was made masculine because of the idol that was on it, and al-Marwah was made feminine because of the idol that was on it, being feminine." [[The report: This report appears in this form in al-Durr al-Manthūr 1:160. In my view the correct wording is to delete "feminine," or to say: "Because the idol that was on it was masculine, and al-Marwah was made feminine because the idol that was on it was feminine."]]

2337. Yaʿqūb ibn Ibrāhīm narrated to me, saying: Ibn ʿUlayyah narrated to us, from Dāwūd ibn Abī Hind, from al-Shaʿbī, and he mentioned something similar to the report of Ibn Abī al-Shawārib from Yazīd, and added to it: He said: "So Allah made it a voluntary act of goodness (taṭawwuʿ khayr)."

2338. Yaʿqūb narrated to me, saying: Ibn Abī Zāʾidah narrated to us, saying: ʿĀṣim al-Aḥwal informed me, saying: I said to Anas ibn Mālik: "Did you used to dislike circumambulating between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah until this verse was revealed?" He said: "Yes, we used to dislike circumambulating between them, because they were among the symbols (shaʿāʾir) of the Jāhiliyyah, until this verse was revealed: ﴿Indeed, al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah are among the symbols of Allah﴾." [[The report: Yaʿqūb is Ibn Ibrāhīm al-Dawraqī. Ibn Abī Zāʾidah is Yaḥyā ibn Zakariyyā ibn Abī Zāʾidah al-Hamdānī al-Wādiʿī, a ḥāfiẓ and trustworthy (thiqah) narrator, who is paired with Ibn al-Mubārak. It is said that he was the first to compile books in Kufa. He died in 183 AH. He is biographed in al-Tahdhīb, al-Kabīr 4/2/273-274, al-Ṣaghīr p. 206, Ibn Saʿd 6:274, Ibn Abī Ḥātim 4/2/144-145, and Tadhkirat al-Ḥuffāz 1:226-247.
ʿĀṣim: he is Ibn Sulaymān al-Aḥwal, who was mentioned previously at 184. He is among the younger Successors (ṣighār al-tābiʿīn). Sufyān al-Thawrī counted him among the three most retentive memories in Basra. He is biographed in al-Tahdhīb, Ibn Saʿd 7/2/20-65, and Ibn Abī Ḥātim 3/1/343-344.
The report was narrated by al-Bukhārī 3:402 (Fatḥ), through ʿAbd Allāh, who is Ibn al-Mubārak, from ʿĀṣim al-Aḥwal, in similar wording. It was also narrated by Muslim, al-Tirmidhī, and al-Nasāʾī, as in al-Qasṭallānī 3:153-154.]]

2339. ʿAlī ibn Sahl al-Ramlī narrated to me, saying: Muʾammal ibn Ismāʿīl narrated to us, saying: Sufyān narrated to us, from ʿĀṣim, who said: I asked Anas about al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah, and he said: "They were among the places of worship (mashāʿir) of the Jāhiliyyah. When Islam came, they refrained from them, and then this was revealed: ﴿Indeed, al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah are among the symbols of Allah﴾." [[The report: Sufyān is al-Thawrī. This report is an abridgement of the one before it. al-Bukhārī narrated it in abridged form at 8:132 (Fatḥ), from Muḥammad ibn Yūsuf, from Sufyān. al-Ḥākim narrated it at 2:270, through Ḥusayn ibn Ḥafṣ, from Sufyān, and said: "This is a sound report according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhārī and Muslim), though they did not record it." al-Dhahabī agreed with him. But al-Ḥākim erred in his correction, since al-Bukhārī did narrate it, as we mentioned earlier.
Some of its meaning will come later in abridged form: 2346 and 2347, through the narration of Jarīr, from ʿĀṣim, from Anas.]]

2340. ʿAbd al-Wārith ibn ʿAbd al-Ṣamad ibn ʿAbd al-Wārith narrated to me, saying: Abū al-Ḥusayn al-Muʿallim narrated to me, saying: Shaybān Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, from Jābir al-Juʿfī, from ʿAmr ibn Ḥabashī, who said: I said to Ibn ʿUmar: "Indeed, al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah are among the symbols of Allah; so whoever makes the pilgrimage to the House or performs the ʿumrah, there is no blame upon him for circumambulating between them," and he said: "Go to Ibn ʿAbbās and ask him, for he is the most knowledgeable of those remaining regarding what was revealed to Muḥammad (ﷺ)." So I went to him and asked him, and he said: "There used to be idols on both of them. When they were removed, they refrained from circumambulating between them, until this was revealed: ﴿Indeed, al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah are among the symbols of Allah. So whoever makes the pilgrimage to the House or performs the ʿumrah, there is no blame upon him for circumambulating between them﴾." [[The report: ʿAbd al-Wārith ibn ʿAbd al-Ṣamad ibn ʿAbd al-Wārith ibn Saʿīd al-ʿAnbarī is trustworthy, one of the teachers of Muslim, al-Tirmidhī, al-Nasāʾī, Abū Ḥātim and others. He is biographed in al-Tahdhīb and Ibn Abī Ḥātim 3/1/76.
Ḥusayn al-Muʿallim: he is Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad ibn Bahrām al-Tamīmī al-Marwadhī, the tutor (al-Muʾaddib), as he is titled in al-Tahdhīb. He is also called "al-Muʿallim," as al-Bukhārī and Ibn Abī Ḥātim titled him. He is trustworthy and one of the teachers of Aḥmad, Yaḥyā and the leading scholars. He is biographed in al-Tahdhīb, al-Kabīr 1/2/386-387, Ibn Saʿd 7/2/79, Ibn Abī Ḥātim 1/2/64, and Tārīkh Baghdād 8:88-90. He was known for narrating "the Tafsīr of Shaybān al-Naḥwī." Ibn Abī Ḥātim narrated from his father, who said: "I came to him many times after he finished the Tafsīr of Shaybān and asked him to repeat some of the session, and he said: 'Bakr, Bakr' (a term of mockery or dismissal). I did not hear anything from him."
What causes confusion is the mix-up between ʿAbd al-Wārith ibn ʿAbd al-Ṣamad, with his teacher "Ḥusayn al-Muʿallim" here, and ʿAbd al-Wārith ibn Saʿīd, whose teacher was also Ḥusayn al-Muʿallim.
So ʿAbd al-Wārith, the teacher of al-Ṭabarī, is the one we have biographed here. His teacher is Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad al-Marwadhī. ʿAbd al-Wārith ibn Saʿīd is the grandfather of this ʿAbd al-Wārith. The Ḥusayn al-Muʿallim who was his teacher is Ḥusayn ibn Dhakwān al-Muʿallim, who is an earlier figure who narrated from the Successors.
Shaybān Abū Muʿāwiyah: he is Shaybān ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Tamīmī al-Naḥwī, an imam, a proof (ḥujjah), and a ḥāfiẓ. He narrated to Abū Ḥanīfah, and was a contemporary of his. Among those who narrated from him were the leading scholars al-Ṭayālisī and Ibn Mahdī, and others. He is biographed in al-Tahdhīb, al-Kabīr 2/2/255, Ibn Saʿd 6:262 and 7/2/67-68, Ibn Abī Ḥātim 1/1/355-356, Tārīkh Baghdād 9:271-274, and Tadhkirat al-Ḥuffāz 1:202-203.
An error occurred in the printed edition regarding his name and the name of the one who narrated from him: it mentions "Abū al-Ḥusayn al-Muʿallim!" which is a confusion, and it mentions "Sinān Abū Muʿāwiyah!" which is, beyond that, a scribal distortion (taṣḥīf).
Jābir al-Juʿfī, with a ḍammah on the jīm and a sukūn on the ʿayn: he is Jābir ibn Yazīd ibn al-Ḥārith, who is very weak, and was accused of lying. He is biographed in al-Tahdhīb, al-Kabīr 1/2/210, al-Ḍuʿafāʾ of al-Bukhārī p. 7, al-Nasāʾī p. 7, Ibn Abī Ḥātim 1/1/497-498, al-Majrūḥīn of Ibn Ḥibbān no. 175, pp. 140-141, and al-Mīzān 1:176-178.
ʿAmr ibn Ḥabashī, with a ḍammah on the unpointed ḥāʾ, a sukūn on the unpointed bāʾ with a dot below, and a kasrah on the shīn with a dot above: he is a trustworthy Successor, biographed in al-Tahdhīb and Ibn Abī Ḥātim 3/1/226.
This report, whose chain is weak, I have not found except in this place. al-Suyūṭī mentioned it at 1:159, and attributed it only to al-Ṭabarī.]]

2341. al-Muthannā narrated to me, saying: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ṣāliḥ narrated to us, saying: Muʿāwiyah ibn Ṣāliḥ narrated to me, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed, al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah are among the symbols of Allah﴾. The reason was that some people used to feel uneasy about circumambulating between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah. So Allah informed that they are among His symbols, and that circumambulating between them is more beloved to Him, and so the sunnah of circumambulating between them was established.

2342. Mūsā narrated to me, saying: ʿAmr narrated to us, saying: Asbāṭ narrated to us, from al-Suddī, regarding ﴿Indeed, al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah are among the symbols of Allah. So whoever makes the pilgrimage to the House or performs the ʿumrah, there is no blame upon him for circumambulating between them﴾. He said: Abū Mālik claimed, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that during the Jāhiliyyah there were devils that played music all night between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah, and there were gods between them. When Islam came and became dominant, the Muslims said: "O Messenger of Allah, we do not circumambulate between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah, for it is polytheism that we used to practice in the Jāhiliyyah!" So Allah revealed: ﴿there is no blame upon him for circumambulating between them﴾. [[The report: This chain is one of the three chains of the Tafsīr of al-Suddī, and we discussed them in detail at 168.
The report was narrated by Abū Bakr ibn Abī Dāwūd in Kitāb al-Maṣāḥif, pp. 100-101, from al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī ibn Mihrān, from ʿĀmir ibn al-Furāt, from Asbāṭ, with this chain, in similar wording.
In the chain of Ibn Abī Dāwūd there is a new benefit: there is another narrator of the Tafsīr of al-Suddī, other than ʿAmr ibn Ṭalḥah al-Qannād, who narrates it from Asbāṭ ibn Naṣr. Here is ʿĀmir ibn al-Furāt also narrating part of it from Asbāṭ. As for ʿĀmir ibn al-Furāt, I have found no biography for him at all. It is strange that Ibn Abī Ḥātim mentions him, in the biography of al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī ibn Mihrān at 1/2/56, as a teacher of his, and then does not give him a biography in his own section!
It was also narrated by al-Ḥākim at 2:271, through ʿAmr ibn Ṭalḥah al-Qannād, from Asbāṭ, with this chain, in similar wording. He added at its end: "He says: upon him is sin, but for him is reward." al-Ḥākim said: "This is a sound report according to the conditions of Muslim, though he did not record it." al-Dhahabī agreed with him.
Regarding this, we have a correction against al-Ḥākim and al-Dhahabī: Abū Mālik, the Successor who narrated it from Ibn ʿAbbās, who is Ghazwān al-Ghifārī, was not narrated from by Muslim in his Ṣaḥīḥ at all. So the report is not according to the conditions of Muslim, in al-Ḥākim's terminology!
In this narration of al-Ḥākim there is also a benefit: when we discussed the three chains of the Tafsīr of al-Suddī, we thought that al-Ḥākim had chosen only two of them, but this chain shows that he deemed all three sound.
al-Suyūṭī also mentioned the report at 1:159, and additionally attributed it to Ibn Abī Ḥātim.]]

2343. Yaʿqūb ibn Ibrāhīm narrated to me, saying: Ibn ʿUlayyah narrated to us, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed, al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah are among the symbols of Allah﴾, who said: The Anṣār said: "Indeed, the running (saʿy) between these two stones is a matter of the Jāhiliyyah!" So Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, revealed: ﴿Indeed, al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah are among the symbols of Allah﴾.

2344. Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abū ʿĀṣim narrated to us, saying: ʿĪsā narrated to us, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, similarly.

2345. Yūnus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿there is no blame upon him for circumambulating between them﴾: The people of the Jāhiliyyah had placed on each of them an idol, which they venerated. When the Muslims accepted Islam, they disliked circumambulating between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah because of the two idols. So Allah, may He be exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah are among the symbols of Allah. So whoever makes the pilgrimage to the House or performs the ʿumrah, there is no blame upon him for circumambulating between them﴾. He recited: ﴿And whoever honours the symbols of Allah, indeed it is from the piety of hearts﴾ [Sūrat al-Ḥajj: 32], and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) established the circumambulation between them as a sunnah.

2346. Ibn Ḥumayd narrated to us, saying: Jarīr narrated to us, from ʿĀṣim, who said: I said to Anas: "Al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah: did you used to dislike circumambulating between them along with the idols that you were forbidden from?" He said: "Yes, until this was revealed: ﴿Indeed, al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah are among the symbols of Allah﴾."

2347. Ibn Ḥumayd narrated to us, saying: Jarīr narrated to us, saying: ʿĀṣim informed us, saying: I heard Anas ibn Mālik say: "Indeed, al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah were among the places of worship (mashāʿir) of Quraysh in the Jāhiliyyah, and when Islam came, we abandoned them." [[The two reports: 2346-2347. Jarīr is Ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd al-Ḍabbī, who is trustworthy, a proof, and a ḥāfiẓ. He is biographed in al-Tahdhīb, al-Kabīr 1/2/214, Ibn Saʿd 7/2/110, Ibn Abī Ḥātim 1/1/505-507, Tārīkh Baghdād 7:253-261, and Tadhkirat al-Ḥuffāz 1:250.
The meaning of both reports has passed, through the narration of ʿĀṣim from Anas: 2338 and 2339.]]
* * *

Others said: Rather, Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, revealed this verse concerning a people who, in the Jāhiliyyah, did not run between them. When Islam came, they feared running between them, as they had feared it in the Jāhiliyyah.

Those who said this:

2348. Bishr ibn Muʿādh narrated to us, saying: Yazīd narrated to us, from Saʿīd, from Qatādah, regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed, al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah are among the symbols of Allah﴾, the verse: In the Jāhiliyyah there was a tribe from Tihāmah that did not run between them. So Allah informed them that al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah are among the symbols of Allah, and that circumambulating between them was part of the sunnah of Ibrāhīm and Ismāʿīl.

2349. al-Ḥasan ibn Yaḥyā narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, saying: Maʿmar informed us, from Qatādah, who said: Some people from Tihāmah did not circumambulate between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah, so Allah revealed: ﴿Indeed, al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah are among the symbols of Allah﴾.

2350. al-Muthannā narrated to me, saying: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ṣāliḥ narrated to us, saying: al-Layth narrated to me, saying: ʿUqayl narrated to me, from Ibn Shihāb, who said: ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr narrated to me, saying: I asked ʿĀʾishah, and I said to her: "What do you think of the saying of Allah: ﴿Indeed, al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah are among the symbols of Allah. So whoever makes the pilgrimage to the House or performs the ʿumrah, there is no blame upon him for circumambulating between them﴾?" And I said to ʿĀʾishah: "By Allah, there is no blame upon anyone for not circumambulating between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah?" ʿĀʾishah said: "Evil is what you said, O nephew! If this verse were as you interpreted it, it would read: 'There is no blame upon him for not circumambulating between them.' Rather, it was revealed concerning the Anṣār: before they accepted Islam, they used to pronounce the talbiyah for Manāh, the idol which they worshipped at al-Mushallal, and whoever pronounced it would feel uneasy about circumambulating between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah. So when they asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about that, saying: 'O Messenger of Allah, we feel uneasy about circumambulating between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah,' Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, revealed: ﴿Indeed, al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah are among the symbols of Allah. So whoever makes the pilgrimage to the House or performs the ʿumrah, there is no blame upon him for circumambulating between them﴾." ʿĀʾishah said: "Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) established the circumambulation between them, so no one may abandon the circumambulation between them." [[The report: ʿUqayl, with a ḍammah on the ʿayn, is Ibn Khālid al-Ayлī, who is trustworthy, firm, and a proof. Ibn Maʿīn said: "The most reliable of those who narrated from al-Zuhrī are Mālik, then Maʿmar, then ʿUqayl." He is biographed in al-Tahdhīb, al-Kabīr 4/1/94, and Ibn Abī Ḥātim 3/2/43.
ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr ibn al-ʿAwwām: a trustworthy, learned, firm, and reliable Successor. Abū al-Zinād said: "The jurists of the people of Madīnah were four: Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab, ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr, Qabīṣah ibn Dhuʾayb, and ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Marwān." His mother was Asmāʾ Dhāt al-Niṭāqayn, the daughter of Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq, and ʿĀʾishah, the Mother of the Believers, was his maternal aunt, may Allah be pleased with them. He is biographed in al-Tahdhīb, al-Kabīr 4/1/31-32, Ibn Saʿd 2/2/134-135 and 5:132-135, Ibn Abī Ḥātim 3/1/395-396, Tadhkirat al-Ḥuffāz 1:58-59, and Tārīkh al-Islām 3:31-34.
This report, through this route, was narrated by Muslim 1:362, through ʿUqayl, from Ibn Shihāb, who is al-Zuhrī, and he did not mention its full wording, referring instead to earlier narrations.
al-Bukhārī narrated it in full at 3:397-401, through Shuʿayb, from al-Zuhrī, in the wording here, except for slight differences in a few words: "When they asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about that, they said... Allah revealed..." In al-Bukhārī it reads: "When they became Muslims, they asked... they said... so Allah revealed..." But al-Bukhārī added at its end the statement of al-Zuhrī that he mentioned this to Abū Bakr ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, which will come in the following report, with similar meaning.
It is established through many routes, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿUrwah, both in full and abridged form:
Mālik narrated it in al-Muwaṭṭaʾ, p. 373, from Hishām ibn ʿUrwah, from his father. al-Bukhārī narrated it at 8:132. Ibn Abī Dāwūd narrated it in al-Maṣāḥif, p. 100, without giving its wording; both of these are through Mālik's route.
Aḥmad narrated it in al-Musnad 6:144, 227 (Ḥalabī), through Ibrāhīm ibn Saʿd, from al-Zuhrī. Likewise Ibn Abī Dāwūd narrated it, p. 100, without giving its wording, through Ibrāhīm ibn Saʿd.
Muslim narrated it in full at 1:361-362, through Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah, from al-Zuhrī. Likewise al-Bukhārī narrated it at 8:472, through Sufyān, but he abridged it greatly.
Muslim and Ibn Abī Dāwūd narrated it, before and after that, through many routes.
al-Suyūṭī mentioned it at 1:159, and additionally attributed it to Abū Dāwūd, al-Nasāʾī, Ibn Mājah, Ibn al-Anbārī in al-Maṣāḥif, Ibn Abī Ḥātim, and al-Bayhaqī in al-Sunan.
See the report that follows this one.
His saying "yuhillūna li-Manāh": that is, they make the pilgrimage (yaḥuddūn). Manāh, with a fatḥah on the mīm and a light nūn: an idol that was in the Jāhiliyyah. Ibn al-Kalbī said: it was a rock that ʿAmr ibn Luḥayy set up for the tribe of Hudhayl, and they used to worship it. "al-Ṭāghiyah" is an Islamic epithet for it. This was stated by al-Ḥāfiẓ in Fatḥ al-Bārī.
"al-Mushallal": with a ḍammah on the mīm, a fatḥah on the unpointed shīn with a dot above, and two lāms, the first with a fatḥah and a shaddah: it is the mountain pass overlooking Qudayd. Qudayd, with a ḍammah on the qāf and two unpointed dāls, in diminutive form: a village situated between Mecca and Madīnah, abundant in water. From Fatḥ al-Bārī.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 158 (part 3 of 4):

2351. Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from 'Urwa, from 'A'isha, who said: Some men from the Ansar, who used to assume the state of ihram for Manat in the Jahiliyya (the Age of Ignorance), and Manat was an idol between Mecca and Medina, said: "O Prophet of God, we used not to circumambulate between al-Safa and al-Marwa out of reverence for Manat. Is there any blame on us if we circumambulate between them?" So God, may His remembrance be exalted, revealed: ﴿Indeed, al-Safa and al-Marwa are among the symbols of God. So whoever makes pilgrimage to the House or performs 'umra, there is no blame upon him for going around between them.﴾

'Urwa said: I said to 'A'isha: "I do not mind not circumambulating between al-Safa and al-Marwa!" God said: ﴿there is no blame upon him﴾. She said: "O son of my sister, do you not see that He says: ﴿Indeed, al-Safa and al-Marwa are among the symbols of God﴾!"

al-Zuhri said: I mentioned that to Abu Bakr ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Harith ibn Hisham, and he said: "This is knowledge!" Abu Bakr said: "I have indeed heard men of knowledge say: When God revealed the circumambulation of the House but did not reveal the circumambulation between al-Safa and al-Marwa, it was said to the Prophet ﷺ: 'We used to circumambulate between al-Safa and al-Marwa in the Jahiliyya, and God has mentioned the circumambulation of the House but has not mentioned the circumambulation between al-Safa and al-Marwa. Is there any blame upon us if we do not circumambulate between them?' So God, may His remembrance be exalted, revealed: ﴿Indeed, al-Safa and al-Marwa are among the symbols of God﴾, the whole verse." Abu Bakr said: "I have heard that this verse was revealed concerning both groups: those who circumambulated and those who did not."

[[Hadith 2351: It is a repetition of the previous hadith in meaning, through another route, which is sound, from al-Zuhri. In it is the addition of al-Zuhri's statement that he mentioned that to Abu Bakr ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Harith ibn Hisham, etc. This addition was mentioned by al-Bukhari in his narration through the route of Shu'ayb from al-Zuhri, as we said just before.

The narration of Ma'mar from al-Zuhri here: al-Bukhari mentioned part of it as a suspended narration (mu'allaq) in 8:472, saying: "Ma'mar said, from al-Zuhri..." And al-Hafiz (Ibn Hajar) said: "al-Tabari connected it, from al-Hasan ibn Yahya, from 'Abd al-Razzaq, in full." This is a reference to the narration here, and he pointed to it in al-Fath 3:399, and mentioned that Ahmad and others connected it.

Ibn Abi Dawud also narrated it in al-Masahif, p. 100, from "Khushaysh ibn Asram and al-Hasan ibn Abi al-Rabi', that 'Abd al-Razzaq informed them from Ma'mar..." He did not give the wording of the hadith, referring to what precedes it. "Khushaysh" is pronounced with a dammah on the kha, a fatha on the shin, and ends with a shin, all with dots. "al-Hasan ibn Abi al-Rabi'" is "al-Hasan ibn Yahya", the teacher of al-Tabari, whose father's kunya was "Abu al-Rabi'". The orientalist who edited the Kitab al-Masahif made an error, writing "Hushaysh" with an unpointed ha, and wrote "al-Hasan ibn Abi al-Rabi' ibn 'Abd al-Razzaq"!!

"Abu Bakr ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Harith ibn Hisham" al-Makhzumi al-Qurashi al-Madani: one of the great leading Successors (tabi'un) and among the nobles of Quraysh. He is one of the seven jurists (fuqaha' al-sab'a). He is biographed in al-Tahdhib, in al-Kuna of al-Bukhari no. 51, Ibn Sa'd 2/2/133 and 5:153-154, Tadhkirat al-Huffaz 1:59-60, and Tarikh al-Islam 4:72-73.

Abu Bakr ibn 'Abd al-Rahman's statement "I have heard that this verse was revealed..." etc. is also in al-Bukhari's narration, 3:401. al-Hafiz said: "So it is in most of the narrations, with a hamza and a damma on the 'ayn, in the present tense of the first person speaker. Al-Dimyati vocalized it in his copy [meaning of Sahih al-Bukhari] with a wasl and a sukun on the 'ayn, in the imperative form. The first is more correct, for in the narration of Sufyan mentioned it has: fa-ara-ha nuzilat (I think it was revealed). It is with a hamza with a damma, meaning 'I think'."

See also many routes of this hadith in al-Sunan al-Kubra of al-Bayhaqi 5:96-97.]]

2352. Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada, who said: "Some people from the people of Tihama did not circumambulate between al-Safa and al-Marwa, so God revealed: ﴿Indeed, al-Safa and al-Marwa are among the symbols of God.﴾"

[[Report 2352: In the printed edition it read: "al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Ma'mar informed us," with the omission of "'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying," and this is a chain that recurs in the Tafsir; it is a repetition of no. 2349 with the same wording, and I fear that it is an addition by a copyist who erred.]]

* * *
