Moreover, the consensus of the authoritative scholars against what he said on this matter is sufficient to demonstrate its invalidity without anything else.

The commentary of Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) on surah 2, verses 179–180 (part 1 of 2):

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And in retaliation (qisas) there is life for you, O people of understanding﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His saying, may His remembrance be exalted, "And in retaliation there is life for you, O people of understanding," He means: and for you, O people of intellect, in what I have enjoined upon you and made obligatory for some of you upon others, of retaliation for lives, wounds and fractures, is that by which I restrain some of you from killing others and deter some of you from others, so you are given life by it. Thus, in My judgment among you by this, there is life for you. [[Qada'a yaqda'uhu qad'an: he restrained it. From it: "Restrain these souls, for they are aspiring," meaning, hold them back from what they desire and want.]]
* *
The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed regarding the meaning of this.
Some of them said, regarding this, something similar to what we have said.
Those who said this:
2617. Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying, "And in retaliation there is life for you, O people of understanding," he said: a deterrent (nakal), a restraint (tanahin).
2618. Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Za'idah narrated to us, from Warqa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying, "And in retaliation there is life for you," he said: a deterrent, a restraint.
2619. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.
2620. Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, from Sa'id, from Qatadah, regarding "And in retaliation there is life for you": God made this retaliation a life, and a deterrent and an admonition for the people of foolishness and ignorance among men. How many a man has resolved upon a calamity, but for fear of retaliation he would have fallen into it; yet God restrains some of them from others through retaliation. God has never commanded a matter except that it is a matter of righteousness in this world and the Hereafter, and He has never forbidden a matter except that it is a matter of corruption in this world and in religion. And God knows best what sets right His creation.
2621. Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying, "And in retaliation there is life for you, O people of understanding," he said: God has placed life in retaliation; when the oppressive transgressor remembers it, he refrains from killing.
2622. It was narrated to me from Ammar ibn al-Hasan, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi', his saying: "And in retaliation there is life for you," the verse. He says: God made this retaliation a life and a lesson for you. How many a man has resolved upon a calamity, and fear of retaliation prevented him from falling into it! Indeed God has restrained His servants from one another through retaliation.
2623. Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraj, from Mujahid, his saying: "And in retaliation there is life for you," he said: a deterrent, a restraint. Ibn Juraj said: "life" means a protection (mani'ah).
2624. Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying, "And in retaliation there is life for you," he said: life, baqiyah. [[Baqiyah: that is, preservation. I fear it may be "taqiyah" with a ta', that is, guarding oneself, as the whole report indicates. Both are sound in meaning.]] When this one fears that he may be killed on my account, he refrains from me. Perhaps he would be an enemy of mine who wants to kill me, so he remembers that he would be killed in retaliation, and he fears he would be killed on my account, so he refrains through the retaliation he fears; had it not been for that, this one would have killed him.
2625. It was narrated to me from Ya'la ibn Ubayd, saying: Isma'il narrated to us, from Abu Salih, regarding His saying, "And in retaliation there is life for you," he said: survival (baqa').
* *
Others said: The meaning of that is: and in retaliation against the killer there is survival for others, because no one other than the killer is killed for the victim in God's judgment. In the Jahiliyyah they would kill a male for a female, and a free man for a slave.
Those who said this:
2626. Musa ibn Harun narrated to me, saying: Amr ibn Hammad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding "And in retaliation there is life for you," he says: survival; none is killed except the killer for his crime.
* *
As for the interpretation of His saying, "O people of understanding," it means: O people of intellect. "Al-albab" is the plural of "al-lubb," and "al-lubb" is intellect.
* *
God, may His remembrance be exalted, specified the address to the people of intellect because they are the ones who understand from God His command and prohibition, and who ponder His signs and proofs, to the exclusion of others.
* *
The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So that you may be God-fearing﴾ (179)
Abu Ja'far said: The interpretation of His saying, "So that you may be God-fearing," means: that you may fear retaliation, and so refrain from killing, as:
2629. Yunus narrated to me this, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying, "So that you may be God-fearing," he said: perhaps you fear that you would kill him and be killed for it.
* *
The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿It has been prescribed for you, when death approaches one of you, if he leaves wealth, that he make a bequest to parents and relatives according to what is reasonable, a duty upon the God-fearing﴾ (180)
Abu Ja'far said: By His saying, may His remembrance be exalted, "It has been prescribed for you," He means: it has been obligated upon you, O believers, the bequest, when death approaches one of you, if he leaves wealth, and "wealth" means property, for parents and relatives who do not inherit from him, "according to what is reasonable," which is what God has permitted and allowed in bequest, so long as it does not exceed one-third, and the testator did not intentionally wrong his heirs, "a duty upon the God-fearing," meaning: He has obligated this upon you and made it a binding duty upon whoever fears God and obeys Him, to act upon it.
* *
If someone says: Is it an obligation upon a man of wealth to bequeath to his parents and relatives who do not inherit from him?
It is said: Yes.
If he says: If he neglects this and does not bequeath to them, will he be one who has neglected an obligation, the neglect of which is sinful?
It is said: Yes.
If he says: What is the evidence for that?
It is said: The saying of God, may His remembrance be exalted: "It has been prescribed for you, when death approaches one of you, if he leaves wealth, that the bequest be to parents and relatives." So He informed that He has prescribed it upon us and made it obligatory, as He said: ﴿Fasting has been prescribed for you﴾ (Surah al-Baqarah: 183). There is no disagreement among all that one who abandons fasting while able to do it is negligent of an obligation God has placed upon him. Likewise, one who abandons bequest to his parents and relatives, while he has wealth from which he can bequeath to them, is neglecting an obligation of God, may He be mighty and majestic.
If he says: You know that a group of scholars have said that bequest to parents and relatives is abrogated (mansukh) by the verse of inheritance?
It is said to him: Others besides them have disagreed and said: it is muhkam (established) and not abrogated. When there is dispute among the scholars regarding its abrogation, it is not for us to rule that it is abrogated except by a proof that must be accepted, since it is not impossible that the ruling of this verse and the ruling of the verse of inheritance both hold correctly in one state without one ruling negating the other. Abrogation (naskh) and what is abrogated are two matters whose rulings cannot both hold correctly in one state, because one negates the other.
Those who have said this include a group of earlier and later scholars.
Those who said this:
2628. Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, that he used to say: Whoever dies without bequeathing to his close relatives has ended his deeds with disobedience.
2629. Salm ibn Janadah narrated to me. [[In the printed edition: "Salim ibn Janadah." That is an error. It has passed several times, and see his biography at no. 48.]] saying: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Muslim, from Masruq: that he attended a man who made bequests of things that were not fitting. Masruq said to him: God has distributed among you and distributed well, and whoever turns from the opinion of God by his own opinion, God will misguide him. Bequeath to your relatives who do not inherit from you, then leave the wealth as God has apportioned it.
2630. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Abu Tumaylah Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, saying: Ubayd narrated to us, from al-Dahhak, who said: No bequest is permitted to an heir, and one should bequeath only to a close relative. If he bequeaths to someone who is not a close relative, he has acted in disobedience, unless there is no relative, in which case he bequeaths to the poor of the Muslims.
2631. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mughirah, who said: It is strange that Abu al-Aliyah, whom a woman of Banu Riyah had freed, bequeathed his wealth to Banu Hashim!
2632. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from a man, from al-Sha'bi, who said: He had no [mawali] (clients), nor any honour. [[In the printed edition: "He had no hal (condition) nor honour." This is clearly an error in my view. This report is a comment on the earlier report in which al-Mughirah wondered at Abu al-Aliyah's action: a woman of Banu Riyah had freed him, and he bequeathed his wealth to Banu Hashim! Al-Sha'bi rejected al-Mughirah's wonder, saying: Abu al-Aliyah has no clients, and no honour belongs to anyone (from him).
The account of that is that a woman bought Abu al-Aliyah, then took him to the mosque and seized his hand. She said: "O God, store him with You as a treasure. Witness, O people of the mosque, that he is a sa'ibah for God, and no one has any claim over him except the claim of kindness." Abu al-Aliyah said: The sa'ibah places himself wherever he wishes. (Ibn Sa'd 7/1/81).
The sa'ibah is a slave freed on the condition that he has no walā' (right of patronage). The jurists differed about the inheritance of the sa'ibah if he leaves an inheritance: does his manumitter inherit from him, or is it not lawful for him to take any of his wealth? It is said: When Abu al-Aliyah died, his master brought his inheritance and said: He is a sa'ibah! And he refused to take it. In a report from Umar: "The sa'ibah and the charity belong to their day," Abu Ubaydah said: that is, to the Day of Resurrection, and the day on which he freed his sa'ibah and gave charity on it. He says: so he does not return to benefit from any of it afterward in this world. See the biography of Salim, freedman of Abu Hudhayfah (Ibn Sa'd 3/1/60), for he was a sa'ibah, and was killed on the day of Yamamah in the time of Abu Bakr; Abu Bakr sent his wealth to his mistress, but she refused to accept it, so Umar placed it in the public treasury.
So this is what al-Sha'bi meant to say: Abu al-Aliyah was a sa'ibah, so he has no clients, and his wealth he places wherever he wishes, and there is no reproach in that for any client, because that is the ruling for a sa'ibah.
This is what I saw in correcting this sentence, and I did not find it elsewhere. I ask God to grant that I have reached success and avoided error.]]
2633. Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, saying: Ayyub narrated to us, from Muhammad, who said: Abd Allah ibn Ma'mar said about bequest: whoever names someone, we place it where he named; and whoever says: where God commanded, we place it among his relatives.
2634. Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la al-San'ani narrated to me, saying: al-Mu'tamir narrated to us, saying: Imran ibn Hudayr narrated to us. [[In the printed edition: "Imran ibn Jarir," which is an error; the correct reading is what I have set down. He is Imran ibn Hudayr al-Sadusi, Abu Ubaydah al-Basri, who led a funeral prayer behind Anas. He narrated from Abu Mijlaz, Abu Qilabah and others, and from him ...
Abu Mijlaz is Lahiq ibn Humayd, mentioned in the following chain.]] He said: I said to Abu Mijlaz: Is bequest obligatory upon every Muslim? He said: Upon the one who leaves wealth.
2635. Sawwar ibn Abd Allah narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Malik ibn al-Sabbah narrated to us, saying: Imran ibn Hudayr narrated to us. [[In the printed edition: "Imran ibn Jarir," which is an error; the correct reading is what I have set down. He is Imran ibn Hudayr al-Sadusi, Abu Ubaydah al-Basri, who led a funeral prayer behind Anas. He narrated from Abu Mijlaz, Abu Qilabah and others, and from him ...
Abu Mijlaz is Lahiq ibn Humayd, mentioned in the following chain.]] He said: I said to Lahiq ibn Humayd: Is bequest a right upon every Muslim? He said: It is a right upon the one who leaves wealth.
* *
The scholars differed regarding the ruling of this verse.
Some of them said: God has not abrogated any part of its ruling; rather, it is a verse whose apparent meaning is general to every parent and relative, and what is intended in ruling is some of them, not all: namely, those among them who do not inherit from the deceased, to the exclusion of those who do inherit. This is the saying of those whose statement I mentioned, and the saying of others along with them.
Mention of those whose statements were not mentioned among them regarding this:
2636. Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Mu'adh ibn Hisham narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to me, from Qatadah, from Jabir ibn Zayd: concerning a man who bequeathed to someone not a relative, while he had needy relatives, he said: two-thirds of the third is returned to them, and one-third of the third goes to the one he bequeathed to.
2637. Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to us, from Qatadah, from al-Hasan, Jabir ibn Zayd and Abd al-Malik ibn Ya'la, that they said, concerning a man who bequeaths to someone not of his close relatives while he has relatives among those who do not inherit from him: they used to give two-thirds of the third to the close relatives, and one-third of the third to the one he bequeathed to.
2638. Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Humayd informed us, from al-Hasan, that he used to say: If a man bequeaths a third to someone not a close relative, then they have one-third of the third, and two-thirds of the third go to his relatives.
2639. Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Ibn Tawus, from his father, who said: Whoever bequeaths to a group and names them, and leaves his needy close relatives, it is taken from them and returned to his close relatives.
* *
Others said: Rather, it is a verse whose ruling was binding and acted upon for a time, then God abrogated by the verse of inheritance the bequest to the parents of the testator and his relatives who inherit from him, and confirmed the obligation of bequest to those among them who do not inherit from him.
Those who said this:
2640. Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Zurayc narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: "It has been prescribed for you, when death approaches one of you, if he leaves wealth, that the bequest be to parents and relatives." So the bequest was made to parents and relatives; then that was abrogated afterward, so a fixed share was given to them, and the bequest became for close relatives who do not inherit, while for the parents a known share was set. And no bequest is permitted to an heir.
2641. Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: "If he leaves wealth, the bequest to parents and relatives," he said: the parents were abrogated from it, and the relatives who do not inherit remained.
2642. Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraj, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, his saying: "If he leaves wealth, the bequest to parents and relatives," he said: whoever inherits was abrogated, and the relatives who do not inherit were not abrogated.
2643. Yahya ibn Nasr narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Hassan narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Ibn Tawus, from his father, who said: The bequest before inheritance was to parents and relatives; when inheritance was revealed, the inheritance abrogated those who inherit, and those who do not inherit remained. So whoever bequeathed to a close relative, his bequest was not valid. [[Report 2643: Yahya ibn Nasr, the teacher of al-Tabari: I do not know who he is. I have not found among the narrators anyone called by this name, except an early man whom al-Tabari did not meet, namely "Yahya" ibn Nasr ibn Hajib al-Qurashi, who died in the year 215, before Abu Ja'far was born. He is biographed in Ibn Abi Hatim 4/2/193, Tarikh Baghdad 14: 159–160, and Lisan al-Mizan 6: 278–279.
In Tarikh Baghdad 14: 225–226 there is a biography of "Yahya ibn Abi Nasr, Abu Sa'd al-Harawi," whose father's name is Mansur ibn al-Hasan. He died in 287. But it is unlikely that he heard from "Yahya ibn Hassan," who died in 208.
In al-Tahdhib 11: 292–293 there is a third biography: "Yahya ibn al-Nadr ibn Abd Allah al-Asbahani al-Daqqaq," who narrates from Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi, and from whom Abu Bakr ibn Abi Dawud al-Sijistani narrates. He is also biographed in Tarikh Isbahan 2: 257–258. This is from this edition. It is very probable that he is the one from whom al-Tabari narrated here.
As for his teacher, "Yahya ibn Hassan," he is al-Tinnisi al-Bakri, and he is trustworthy. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir 4/2/269, al-Saghir 229, and Ibn Abi Hatim 4/2/135.]].
2644. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Suwayd ibn Nasr narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Isma'il al-Makki, from al-Hasan, regarding His saying: "If he leaves wealth, the bequest to parents and relatives," he said: the parents were abrogated, and the close relatives who are deprived and therefore do not inherit were confirmed.
2645. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Suwayd narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Mubarak ibn Fudalah, from al-Hasan, regarding this verse: "The bequest to parents and relatives," he said: for the parents it is abrogated, and the bequest to relatives remains, even if they are wealthy.
2646. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah ibn Salih narrated to me, from Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn Abbas, his saying: "If he leaves wealth, the bequest to parents and relatives." There was no heir with the parents except others, except a bequest if it was to the close relatives. Then God revealed after this: ﴿As for his parents, each of them receives a sixth of what he leaves, if he has a child; but if he has no child and his parents inherit from him, then his mother has a third﴾ (Surah al-Nisa': 11). So God explained the inheritance of the parents, and confirmed the bequest to the close relatives within one-third of the deceased's property.

**2647** — ʿAlī ibn Dāwūd related to us, saying: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ṣāliḥ related to us, saying: Muʿāwiyah ibn Ṣāliḥ related to me, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥah, from Ibn ʿAbbās regarding His words: ﴿If he leaves behind wealth, [he should make] a bequest to parents and relatives﴾. He said: [The bequest to] the parents was abrogated (*nasakha*, "abrogated" or "annulled"), and the bequest to the relatives who do not inherit was confirmed.

**2648** — I was told from ʿAmmār, who said: Ibn Abī Jaʿfar related to us, from his father, from al-Rabīʿ regarding His words: ﴿It is prescribed for you that when death approaches one of you, if he leaves behind wealth, [he should make] a bequest to parents and relatives, according to what is reasonable﴾. He said: This was before *Sūrat al-Nisāʾ* was revealed. When the verse of inheritance was revealed, it abrogated the ruling concerning the parents, placing them among the heirs, and the bequest became for the relatives who do not inherit.

**2649** — al-Muthannā related to me, saying: al-Ḥajjāj ibn al-Minhāl related to us, saying: Ḥammād ibn Salamah related to us, saying: ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Maymūnah informed us, saying: I asked Muslim ibn Yasār and al-ʿAlāʾ ibn Ziyād about the words of God, blessed and exalted: ﴿if he leaves behind wealth, [he should make] a bequest to parents and relatives﴾. They both said: [It refers] to the relatives.

**2650** — al-Muthannā related to me, saying: al-Ḥajjāj related to us, saying: Ḥammād related to us, from Iyās ibn Muʿāwiyah, who said: [It refers] to the relatives.

* *

Others said: Rather, God abrogated all of that and imposed the obligatory shares and inheritances, so no bequest is obligatory for anyone toward anyone, near or distant.

Those who said this:

**2651** — Yūnus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words: ﴿If he leaves behind wealth, [he should make] a bequest to parents and relatives﴾ — the verse — he said: God abrogated all of that and imposed the obligatory shares.

**2652** — Yaʿqūb ibn Ibrāhīm related to me, saying: Ibn ʿUlayyah related to us, from Yūnus, from Ibn Sīrīn, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that he stood up and addressed the people here, and he recited to them *Sūrat al-Baqarah* in order to explain it to them. When he came to this verse: ﴿If he leaves behind wealth, [he should make] a bequest to parents and relatives﴾, he said: This was abrogated.

**2653** — Muḥammad ibn Saʿd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās regarding His words: ﴿If he leaves behind wealth, [he should make] a bequest to parents and relatives﴾. He said: The obligatory shares for parents and relatives abrogated the bequest.

**2654** — Muḥammad ibn Bashshār related to me, saying: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī related to us, saying: Sufyān related to us, from Jahḍam, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Badr, who said: I heard Ibn ʿUmar say regarding His words: ﴿If he leaves behind wealth, [he should make] a bequest to parents and relatives﴾: The verse of inheritance abrogated it. Ibn Bashshār said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said: I asked Jahḍam about it, but he did not remember it.

**2655** — Ibn Ḥumayd related to us, saying: Yaḥyā ibn Wāḍiḥ related to us, saying: al-Ḥusayn ibn Wāqid related to us, from Yazīd al-Naḥwī, from ʿIkrimah and al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī, who both said: ﴿If he leaves behind wealth, [he should make] a bequest to parents and relatives﴾. The bequest remained so until the verse of inheritance abrogated it.

**2656** — Aḥmad ibn al-Miqdām related to me, saying: al-Muʿtamir related to us, saying: I heard my father say: Qatādah claimed, regarding this verse: ﴿If he leaves behind wealth, [he should make] a bequest to parents and relatives﴾, that [Shurayḥ] said: A man would bequeath all his wealth until the verse of inheritance was revealed.

**2657** — Aḥmad ibn al-Miqdām related to us, saying: al-Muʿtamir related to us, saying: I heard my father say: Qatādah claimed that the two verses of inheritance in *Sūrat al-Nisāʾ* abrogated the verse in *Sūrat al-Baqarah* concerning the bequest.

**2658** — Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr related to me, saying: Abū ʿĀṣim related to us, saying: ʿĪsā related to us, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid regarding the words of God: ﴿If he leaves behind wealth, [he should make] a bequest to parents and relatives﴾. He said: The inheritance was for the child, and the bequest was for the parents and relatives, and it has been abrogated.

**2659** — al-Muthannā related to me, saying: Abū Ḥudhayfah related to us, saying: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, who said: The inheritance was for the child, and the bequest was for the parents and relatives, and it has been abrogated. A verse in *Sūrat al-Nisāʾ* abrogated it: ﴿God enjoins you concerning your children﴾ [al-Nisāʾ 4:11].

**2660** — Mūsā ibn Hārūn related to me, saying: ʿAmr ibn Ḥammād related to us, saying: Asbāṭ related to us, from al-Suddī: ﴿It is prescribed for you that when death approaches one of you, if he leaves behind wealth, [he should make] a bequest to parents and relatives﴾. As for the parents and relatives: on the day this verse was revealed, people did not have a known inheritance; rather, a man would bequeath to his parent and his family, and they would divide it among themselves, until *al-Nisāʾ* abrogated it, saying: ﴿God enjoins you concerning your children﴾.

**2661** — Yaʿqūb related to me, saying: Ibn ʿUlayyah related to us, saying: Ayyūb related to us, from Nāfiʿ: that Ibn ʿUmar did not make a bequest, and he said: As for my property, God knows what I would have done with it in life; and as for my real estate (*ribāʿī*), I do not wish that any of my children be made partners in it with anyone.

**2662** — Muḥammad ibn Khalaf al-ʿAsqalānī related to me, saying: Muḥammad ibn Yūsuf related to us, saying: Sufyān related to us, from Nusayr ibn Dhaʿlūq, who said: ʿUrwah — meaning Ibn Thābit — said to Rabīʿ ibn Khuthaym: [[In the printed edition: "Ibn Khuthaym," and I have adopted what is in *al-Tahdhīb*; see his biography.]] Bequeath to me your copy of the Qurʾān. He said: Then he looked at his father and said: ﴿And those of blood relationship are more entitled to one another in the Book of God﴾ [al-Anfāl 8:75].

**2663** — ʿAlī ibn Sahl related to us, saying: Yazīd related to us, from Sufyān, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Ibrāhīm, who said: We mentioned to him that Zayd and Ṭalḥah used to be strict regarding the bequest. He said: There was nothing wrong with them doing so; the Prophet (ﷺ) died without making a bequest, and Abū Bakr made a bequest. Whichever of the two you do is good.

**2664** — al-Ḥasan ibn Yaḥyā related to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, saying: al-Thawrī informed us, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Ibrāhīm, who said: Ṭalḥah and Zayd were mentioned in his presence, and he related something similar.

* *

As for the "good" (*khayr*) which, if a person leaves it behind, makes it obligatory for him to bequeath it to his parents and relatives who do not inherit, it is: wealth, as follows:

**2665** — al-Muthannā ibn Ibrāhīm related to me, saying: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ṣāliḥ related to us, from Muʿāwiyah ibn Ṣāliḥ, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥah, from Ibn ʿAbbās regarding His words: ﴿If he leaves behind wealth﴾, meaning property.

**2666** — Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr related to me, saying: Abū ʿĀṣim related to us, saying: ʿĪsā related to us, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid regarding the words of God: ﴿If he leaves behind wealth﴾, [meaning] property.

**2667** — al-Muthannā related to me, saying: Abū Ḥudhayfah [[In the printed edition: "Abū Jaʿfar," but the correct reading is "Abū Ḥudhayfah," and it is a recurring chain in the commentary; see the nearest instance above, no. 2659.]] related to us, saying: Shibl related to us, from Abū Najīḥ, from Mujāhid: ﴿If he leaves behind wealth﴾. He used to say: "Khayr" in the whole Qurʾān means wealth: ﴿And indeed, he is intense in his love of wealth﴾ [al-ʿĀdiyāt 100:8] — "khayr" means wealth; ﴿Indeed I have preferred the love of wealth over the remembrance of my Lord﴾ [Ṣād 38:32] — wealth; ﴿So make a contract with them if you know any good in them﴾ [al-Nūr 24:33] — wealth; and ﴿If he leaves behind wealth, [he should make] a bequest﴾ — wealth.

**2668** — Bishr ibn Muʿādh related to us, saying: Yazīd related to us, saying: Saʿīd related to us, from Qatādah: ﴿If he leaves behind wealth, [he should make] a bequest﴾, that is: property. [[Report 2668 — in the printed edition, "Bishr ibn Muʿādh related to us, saying: Saʿīd related to us" omits "Yazīd related to us." This is a recurring chain in the commentary; see the nearest instance above, no. 2640.]]

**2669** — Mūsā ibn Hārūn related to me, saying: ʿAmr ibn Ḥammād related to us, saying: Asbāṭ related to us, from al-Suddī: ﴿If he leaves behind wealth, [he should make] a bequest﴾. As for "khayr," it is property.

**2670** — I was told from ʿAmmār ibn al-Ḥasan, who said: Ibn Abī Jaʿfar related to us, from his father, from al-Rabīʿ: ﴿If he leaves behind wealth﴾. He said: If he leaves behind property.

**2671** — al-Qāsim related to us, saying: al-Ḥusayn related to us, saying: Ḥajjāj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās regarding His words: ﴿If he leaves behind wealth﴾. He said: The "khayr" is property.

**2672** — al-Muthannā related to me, saying: Suwayd related to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubārak informed us, from al-Ḥasan ibn Yaḥyā, from al-Ḍaḥḥāk regarding His words: ﴿If he leaves behind wealth, [he should make] a bequest﴾. He said: Property. Do you not see that He says: Shuʿayb said to his people: ﴿Indeed I see you in prosperity﴾ [Hūd 11:84], meaning wealth?

**2673** — Yūnus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr al-Yāfiʿī informed us, from Ibn Jurayj, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Rabāḥ, who recited: ﴿It is prescribed for you that when death approaches one of you, if he leaves behind wealth﴾. ʿAṭāʾ said: The "khayr," as it is understood, is property.

* *

Then they differed over the amount of property which, if a man leaves it behind, makes him subject to the ruling of this verse.

Some of them said: That is a thousand dirhams.

Those who said this:

**2674** — al-Muthannā related to me, saying: al-Ḥajjāj ibn al-Minhāl related to us, saying: Hammām ibn Yaḥyā related to us, from Qatādah regarding this verse: ﴿If he leaves behind wealth, [he should make] a bequest﴾. He said: The "khayr" is a thousand or more.

**2675** — al-Muthannā related to me, saying: al-Ḥajjāj related to us, saying: Ḥammād related to us, saying: Hishām ibn ʿUrwah informed us, from ʿUrwah: that ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib entered upon a paternal cousin of his to visit him, and he said: I want to make a bequest. ʿAlī said: Do not make a bequest, for you have not left behind any "khayr" to bequeath.

He said: The estate of [the one he visited] was between seven hundred and nine hundred.

**2676** — Yūnus ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: ʿUthmān ibn al-Ḥakam al-Ḥizāmī [[He is vocalized in *al-Khulāṣah* with a broken-ʿayn (*bi-kasr al-muhmalah*); in *al-Tahdhīb* and *al-Mīzān* it is "al-Judhāmī," with a dammah on the jīm followed by a dhāl with a dot.]] and Ibn Abī al-Zinād related to me, from Hishām ibn ʿUrwah, from his father, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib: that he entered upon a sick man, and the bequest was mentioned to him. He said: Do not make a bequest, for God only said: ﴿If he leaves behind wealth﴾, and you have not left behind any "khayr." Ibn Abī al-Zinād said in his version: So leave your property to your children.

**2677** — Muḥammad ibn Bashshār related to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān related to us, saying: Sufyān related to us, from Manṣūr ibn Ṣafiyyah, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUyaynah — or ʿUtbah, the doubt is mine — that a man wished to make a bequest, and he had many children and had left four hundred dinars. ʿĀʾishah said: I see no excess in it.

**2678** — al-Ḥasan ibn Yaḥyā related to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, saying: Maʿmar informed us, from Hishām ibn ʿUrwah, from his father, who said: ʿAlī entered upon a client of theirs at the time of death, who had seven hundred dirhams or six hundred dirhams. He said: Should I not make a bequest? He said: No! For God only said: ﴿If he leaves behind wealth﴾, and you do not have much property.

* *

Others said: That is what is between five hundred dirhams and a thousand.

Those who said this:

**2679** — al-Ḥasan ibn Yaḥyā related to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, saying: Maʿmar informed us, from Qatādah, from Abān ibn Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī regarding His words: ﴿If he leaves behind wealth﴾. He said: From a thousand dirhams down to five hundred.

* *

Others said: The bequest is obligatory, whether the property is little or much.

Those who said this:

**2680** — al-Ḥasan ibn Yaḥyā related to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, saying: Maʿmar informed us, from al-Zuhrī, who said: God made the bequest a right, whether little or much.

* *

Abū Jaʿfar said: The most correct of these opinions regarding the interpretation of His words: ﴿It is prescribed for you that when death approaches one of you, if he leaves behind wealth, [he should make] a bequest﴾ is what al-Zuhrī said. This is because little property and much property both fall under the term "khayr," and God did not limit it by any limit, nor did He specify any part of it, so it is not permissible to transfer the apparent meaning to the hidden. Therefore, whoever is approached by death while he has property, whether little or much, is obligated to bequeath from it, in kindness, to those of his fathers, mothers, and relatives who do not inherit from him, just as God, mighty is His remembrance, said and commanded.

The commentary of Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) on surah 2, verses 179–180 (part 1 of 2):

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And in retaliation (qisas) there is life for you, O people of understanding﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His saying, may His remembrance be exalted, "And in retaliation there is life for you, O people of understanding," He means: and for you, O people of intellect, in what I have enjoined upon you and made obligatory for some of you upon others, of retaliation for lives, wounds and fractures, is that by which I restrain some of you from killing others and deter some of you from others, so you are given life by it. Thus, in My judgment among you by this, there is life for you. [[Qada'a yaqda'uhu qad'an: he restrained it. From it: "Restrain these souls, for they are aspiring," meaning, hold them back from what they desire and want.]]
* *
The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed regarding the meaning of this.
Some of them said, regarding this, something similar to what we have said.
Those who said this:
2617. Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying, "And in retaliation there is life for you, O people of understanding," he said: a deterrent (nakal), a restraint (tanahin).
2618. Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Za'idah narrated to us, from Warqa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying, "And in retaliation there is life for you," he said: a deterrent, a restraint.
2619. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.
2620. Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, from Sa'id, from Qatadah, regarding "And in retaliation there is life for you": God made this retaliation a life, and a deterrent and an admonition for the people of foolishness and ignorance among men. How many a man has resolved upon a calamity, but for fear of retaliation he would have fallen into it; yet God restrains some of them from others through retaliation. God has never commanded a matter except that it is a matter of righteousness in this world and the Hereafter, and He has never forbidden a matter except that it is a matter of corruption in this world and in religion. And God knows best what sets right His creation.
2621. Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying, "And in retaliation there is life for you, O people of understanding," he said: God has placed life in retaliation; when the oppressive transgressor remembers it, he refrains from killing.
2622. It was narrated to me from Ammar ibn al-Hasan, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi', his saying: "And in retaliation there is life for you," the verse. He says: God made this retaliation a life and a lesson for you. How many a man has resolved upon a calamity, and fear of retaliation prevented him from falling into it! Indeed God has restrained His servants from one another through retaliation.
2623. Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraj, from Mujahid, his saying: "And in retaliation there is life for you," he said: a deterrent, a restraint. Ibn Juraj said: "life" means a protection (mani'ah).
2624. Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying, "And in retaliation there is life for you," he said: life, baqiyah. [[Baqiyah: that is, preservation. I fear it may be "taqiyah" with a ta', that is, guarding oneself, as the whole report indicates. Both are sound in meaning.]] When this one fears that he may be killed on my account, he refrains from me. Perhaps he would be an enemy of mine who wants to kill me, so he remembers that he would be killed in retaliation, and he fears he would be killed on my account, so he refrains through the retaliation he fears; had it not been for that, this one would have killed him.
2625. It was narrated to me from Ya'la ibn Ubayd, saying: Isma'il narrated to us, from Abu Salih, regarding His saying, "And in retaliation there is life for you," he said: survival (baqa').
* *
Others said: The meaning of that is: and in retaliation against the killer there is survival for others, because no one other than the killer is killed for the victim in God's judgment. In the Jahiliyyah they would kill a male for a female, and a free man for a slave.
Those who said this:
2626. Musa ibn Harun narrated to me, saying: Amr ibn Hammad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding "And in retaliation there is life for you," he says: survival; none is killed except the killer for his crime.
* *
As for the interpretation of His saying, "O people of understanding," it means: O people of intellect. "Al-albab" is the plural of "al-lubb," and "al-lubb" is intellect.
* *
God, may His remembrance be exalted, specified the address to the people of intellect because they are the ones who understand from God His command and prohibition, and who ponder His signs and proofs, to the exclusion of others.
* *
The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So that you may be God-fearing﴾ (179)
Abu Ja'far said: The interpretation of His saying, "So that you may be God-fearing," means: that you may fear retaliation, and so refrain from killing, as:
2629. Yunus narrated to me this, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying, "So that you may be God-fearing," he said: perhaps you fear that you would kill him and be killed for it.
* *
The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿It has been prescribed for you, when death approaches one of you, if he leaves wealth, that he make a bequest to parents and relatives according to what is reasonable, a duty upon the God-fearing﴾ (180)
Abu Ja'far said: By His saying, may His remembrance be exalted, "It has been prescribed for you," He means: it has been obligated upon you, O believers, the bequest, when death approaches one of you, if he leaves wealth, and "wealth" means property, for parents and relatives who do not inherit from him, "according to what is reasonable," which is what God has permitted and allowed in bequest, so long as it does not exceed one-third, and the testator did not intentionally wrong his heirs, "a duty upon the God-fearing," meaning: He has obligated this upon you and made it a binding duty upon whoever fears God and obeys Him, to act upon it.
* *
If someone says: Is it an obligation upon a man of wealth to bequeath to his parents and relatives who do not inherit from him?
It is said: Yes.
If he says: If he neglects this and does not bequeath to them, will he be one who has neglected an obligation, the neglect of which is sinful?
It is said: Yes.
If he says: What is the evidence for that?
It is said: The saying of God, may His remembrance be exalted: "It has been prescribed for you, when death approaches one of you, if he leaves wealth, that the bequest be to parents and relatives." So He informed that He has prescribed it upon us and made it obligatory, as He said: ﴿Fasting has been prescribed for you﴾ (Surah al-Baqarah: 183). There is no disagreement among all that one who abandons fasting while able to do it is negligent of an obligation God has placed upon him. Likewise, one who abandons bequest to his parents and relatives, while he has wealth from which he can bequeath to them, is neglecting an obligation of God, may He be mighty and majestic.
If he says: You know that a group of scholars have said that bequest to parents and relatives is abrogated (mansukh) by the verse of inheritance?
It is said to him: Others besides them have disagreed and said: it is muhkam (established) and not abrogated. When there is dispute among the scholars regarding its abrogation, it is not for us to rule that it is abrogated except by a proof that must be accepted, since it is not impossible that the ruling of this verse and the ruling of the verse of inheritance both hold correctly in one state without one ruling negating the other. Abrogation (naskh) and what is abrogated are two matters whose rulings cannot both hold correctly in one state, because one negates the other.
Those who have said this include a group of earlier and later scholars.
Those who said this:
2628. Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, that he used to say: Whoever dies without bequeathing to his close relatives has ended his deeds with disobedience.
2629. Salm ibn Janadah narrated to me. [[In the printed edition: "Salim ibn Janadah." That is an error. It has passed several times, and see his biography at no. 48.]] saying: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Muslim, from Masruq: that he attended a man who made bequests of things that were not fitting. Masruq said to him: God has distributed among you and distributed well, and whoever turns from the opinion of God by his own opinion, God will misguide him. Bequeath to your relatives who do not inherit from you, then leave the wealth as God has apportioned it.
2630. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Abu Tumaylah Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, saying: Ubayd narrated to us, from al-Dahhak, who said: No bequest is permitted to an heir, and one should bequeath only to a close relative. If he bequeaths to someone who is not a close relative, he has acted in disobedience, unless there is no relative, in which case he bequeaths to the poor of the Muslims.
2631. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mughirah, who said: It is strange that Abu al-Aliyah, whom a woman of Banu Riyah had freed, bequeathed his wealth to Banu Hashim!
2632. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from a man, from al-Sha'bi, who said: He had no [mawali] (clients), nor any honour. [[In the printed edition: "He had no hal (condition) nor honour." This is clearly an error in my view. This report is a comment on the earlier report in which al-Mughirah wondered at Abu al-Aliyah's action: a woman of Banu Riyah had freed him, and he bequeathed his wealth to Banu Hashim! Al-Sha'bi rejected al-Mughirah's wonder, saying: Abu al-Aliyah has no clients, and no honour belongs to anyone (from him).
The account of that is that a woman bought Abu al-Aliyah, then took him to the mosque and seized his hand. She said: "O God, store him with You as a treasure. Witness, O people of the mosque, that he is a sa'ibah for God, and no one has any claim over him except the claim of kindness." Abu al-Aliyah said: The sa'ibah places himself wherever he wishes. (Ibn Sa'd 7/1/81).
The sa'ibah is a slave freed on the condition that he has no walā' (right of patronage). The jurists differed about the inheritance of the sa'ibah if he leaves an inheritance: does his manumitter inherit from him, or is it not lawful for him to take any of his wealth? It is said: When Abu al-Aliyah died, his master brought his inheritance and said: He is a sa'ibah! And he refused to take it. In a report from Umar: "The sa'ibah and the charity belong to their day," Abu Ubaydah said: that is, to the Day of Resurrection, and the day on which he freed his sa'ibah and gave charity on it. He says: so he does not return to benefit from any of it afterward in this world. See the biography of Salim, freedman of Abu Hudhayfah (Ibn Sa'd 3/1/60), for he was a sa'ibah, and was killed on the day of Yamamah in the time of Abu Bakr; Abu Bakr sent his wealth to his mistress, but she refused to accept it, so Umar placed it in the public treasury.
So this is what al-Sha'bi meant to say: Abu al-Aliyah was a sa'ibah, so he has no clients, and his wealth he places wherever he wishes, and there is no reproach in that for any client, because that is the ruling for a sa'ibah.
This is what I saw in correcting this sentence, and I did not find it elsewhere. I ask God to grant that I have reached success and avoided error.]]
2633. Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, saying: Ayyub narrated to us, from Muhammad, who said: Abd Allah ibn Ma'mar said about bequest: whoever names someone, we place it where he named; and whoever says: where God commanded, we place it among his relatives.
2634. Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la al-San'ani narrated to me, saying: al-Mu'tamir narrated to us, saying: Imran ibn Hudayr narrated to us. [[In the printed edition: "Imran ibn Jarir," which is an error; the correct reading is what I have set down. He is Imran ibn Hudayr al-Sadusi, Abu Ubaydah al-Basri, who led a funeral prayer behind Anas. He narrated from Abu Mijlaz, Abu Qilabah and others, and from him ...
Abu Mijlaz is Lahiq ibn Humayd, mentioned in the following chain.]] He said: I said to Abu Mijlaz: Is bequest obligatory upon every Muslim? He said: Upon the one who leaves wealth.
2635. Sawwar ibn Abd Allah narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Malik ibn al-Sabbah narrated to us, saying: Imran ibn Hudayr narrated to us. [[In the printed edition: "Imran ibn Jarir," which is an error; the correct reading is what I have set down. He is Imran ibn Hudayr al-Sadusi, Abu Ubaydah al-Basri, who led a funeral prayer behind Anas. He narrated from Abu Mijlaz, Abu Qilabah and others, and from him ...
Abu Mijlaz is Lahiq ibn Humayd, mentioned in the following chain.]] He said: I said to Lahiq ibn Humayd: Is bequest a right upon every Muslim? He said: It is a right upon the one who leaves wealth.
* *
The scholars differed regarding the ruling of this verse.
Some of them said: God has not abrogated any part of its ruling; rather, it is a verse whose apparent meaning is general to every parent and relative, and what is intended in ruling is some of them, not all: namely, those among them who do not inherit from the deceased, to the exclusion of those who do inherit. This is the saying of those whose statement I mentioned, and the saying of others along with them.
Mention of those whose statements were not mentioned among them regarding this:
2636. Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Mu'adh ibn Hisham narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to me, from Qatadah, from Jabir ibn Zayd: concerning a man who bequeathed to someone not a relative, while he had needy relatives, he said: two-thirds of the third is returned to them, and one-third of the third goes to the one he bequeathed to.
2637. Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to us, from Qatadah, from al-Hasan, Jabir ibn Zayd and Abd al-Malik ibn Ya'la, that they said, concerning a man who bequeaths to someone not of his close relatives while he has relatives among those who do not inherit from him: they used to give two-thirds of the third to the close relatives, and one-third of the third to the one he bequeathed to.
2638. Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Humayd informed us, from al-Hasan, that he used to say: If a man bequeaths a third to someone not a close relative, then they have one-third of the third, and two-thirds of the third go to his relatives.
2639. Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Ibn Tawus, from his father, who said: Whoever bequeaths to a group and names them, and leaves his needy close relatives, it is taken from them and returned to his close relatives.
* *
Others said: Rather, it is a verse whose ruling was binding and acted upon for a time, then God abrogated by the verse of inheritance the bequest to the parents of the testator and his relatives who inherit from him, and confirmed the obligation of bequest to those among them who do not inherit from him.
Those who said this:
2640. Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Zurayc narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: "It has been prescribed for you, when death approaches one of you, if he leaves wealth, that the bequest be to parents and relatives." So the bequest was made to parents and relatives; then that was abrogated afterward, so a fixed share was given to them, and the bequest became for close relatives who do not inherit, while for the parents a known share was set. And no bequest is permitted to an heir.
2641. Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: "If he leaves wealth, the bequest to parents and relatives," he said: the parents were abrogated from it, and the relatives who do not inherit remained.
2642. Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraj, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, his saying: "If he leaves wealth, the bequest to parents and relatives," he said: whoever inherits was abrogated, and the relatives who do not inherit were not abrogated.
2643. Yahya ibn Nasr narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Hassan narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Ibn Tawus, from his father, who said: The bequest before inheritance was to parents and relatives; when inheritance was revealed, the inheritance abrogated those who inherit, and those who do not inherit remained. So whoever bequeathed to a close relative, his bequest was not valid. [[Report 2643: Yahya ibn Nasr, the teacher of al-Tabari: I do not know who he is. I have not found among the narrators anyone called by this name, except an early man whom al-Tabari did not meet, namely "Yahya" ibn Nasr ibn Hajib al-Qurashi, who died in the year 215, before Abu Ja'far was born. He is biographed in Ibn Abi Hatim 4/2/193, Tarikh Baghdad 14: 159–160, and Lisan al-Mizan 6: 278–279.
In Tarikh Baghdad 14: 225–226 there is a biography of "Yahya ibn Abi Nasr, Abu Sa'd al-Harawi," whose father's name is Mansur ibn al-Hasan. He died in 287. But it is unlikely that he heard from "Yahya ibn Hassan," who died in 208.
In al-Tahdhib 11: 292–293 there is a third biography: "Yahya ibn al-Nadr ibn Abd Allah al-Asbahani al-Daqqaq," who narrates from Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi, and from whom Abu Bakr ibn Abi Dawud al-Sijistani narrates. He is also biographed in Tarikh Isbahan 2: 257–258. This is from this edition. It is very probable that he is the one from whom al-Tabari narrated here.
As for his teacher, "Yahya ibn Hassan," he is al-Tinnisi al-Bakri, and he is trustworthy. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir 4/2/269, al-Saghir 229, and Ibn Abi Hatim 4/2/135.]].
2644. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Suwayd ibn Nasr narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Isma'il al-Makki, from al-Hasan, regarding His saying: "If he leaves wealth, the bequest to parents and relatives," he said: the parents were abrogated, and the close relatives who are deprived and therefore do not inherit were confirmed.
2645. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Suwayd narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Mubarak ibn Fudalah, from al-Hasan, regarding this verse: "The bequest to parents and relatives," he said: for the parents it is abrogated, and the bequest to relatives remains, even if they are wealthy.
2646. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah ibn Salih narrated to me, from Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn Abbas, his saying: "If he leaves wealth, the bequest to parents and relatives." There was no heir with the parents except others, except a bequest if it was to the close relatives. Then God revealed after this: ﴿As for his parents, each of them receives a sixth of what he leaves, if he has a child; but if he has no child and his parents inherit from him, then his mother has a third﴾ (Surah al-Nisa': 11). So God explained the inheritance of the parents, and confirmed the bequest to the close relatives within one-third of the deceased's property.

**2647** — ʿAlī ibn Dāwūd related to us, saying: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ṣāliḥ related to us, saying: Muʿāwiyah ibn Ṣāliḥ related to me, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥah, from Ibn ʿAbbās regarding His words: ﴿If he leaves behind wealth, [he should make] a bequest to parents and relatives﴾. He said: [The bequest to] the parents was abrogated (*nasakha*, "abrogated" or "annulled"), and the bequest to the relatives who do not inherit was confirmed.

**2648** — I was told from ʿAmmār, who said: Ibn Abī Jaʿfar related to us, from his father, from al-Rabīʿ regarding His words: ﴿It is prescribed for you that when death approaches one of you, if he leaves behind wealth, [he should make] a bequest to parents and relatives, according to what is reasonable﴾. He said: This was before *Sūrat al-Nisāʾ* was revealed. When the verse of inheritance was revealed, it abrogated the ruling concerning the parents, placing them among the heirs, and the bequest became for the relatives who do not inherit.

**2649** — al-Muthannā related to me, saying: al-Ḥajjāj ibn al-Minhāl related to us, saying: Ḥammād ibn Salamah related to us, saying: ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Maymūnah informed us, saying: I asked Muslim ibn Yasār and al-ʿAlāʾ ibn Ziyād about the words of God, blessed and exalted: ﴿if he leaves behind wealth, [he should make] a bequest to parents and relatives﴾. They both said: [It refers] to the relatives.

**2650** — al-Muthannā related to me, saying: al-Ḥajjāj related to us, saying: Ḥammād related to us, from Iyās ibn Muʿāwiyah, who said: [It refers] to the relatives.

* *

Others said: Rather, God abrogated all of that and imposed the obligatory shares and inheritances, so no bequest is obligatory for anyone toward anyone, near or distant.

Those who said this:

**2651** — Yūnus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words: ﴿If he leaves behind wealth, [he should make] a bequest to parents and relatives﴾ — the verse — he said: God abrogated all of that and imposed the obligatory shares.

**2652** — Yaʿqūb ibn Ibrāhīm related to me, saying: Ibn ʿUlayyah related to us, from Yūnus, from Ibn Sīrīn, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that he stood up and addressed the people here, and he recited to them *Sūrat al-Baqarah* in order to explain it to them. When he came to this verse: ﴿If he leaves behind wealth, [he should make] a bequest to parents and relatives﴾, he said: This was abrogated.

**2653** — Muḥammad ibn Saʿd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās regarding His words: ﴿If he leaves behind wealth, [he should make] a bequest to parents and relatives﴾. He said: The obligatory shares for parents and relatives abrogated the bequest.

**2654** — Muḥammad ibn Bashshār related to me, saying: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī related to us, saying: Sufyān related to us, from Jahḍam, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Badr, who said: I heard Ibn ʿUmar say regarding His words: ﴿If he leaves behind wealth, [he should make] a bequest to parents and relatives﴾: The verse of inheritance abrogated it. Ibn Bashshār said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said: I asked Jahḍam about it, but he did not remember it.

**2655** — Ibn Ḥumayd related to us, saying: Yaḥyā ibn Wāḍiḥ related to us, saying: al-Ḥusayn ibn Wāqid related to us, from Yazīd al-Naḥwī, from ʿIkrimah and al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī, who both said: ﴿If he leaves behind wealth, [he should make] a bequest to parents and relatives﴾. The bequest remained so until the verse of inheritance abrogated it.

**2656** — Aḥmad ibn al-Miqdām related to me, saying: al-Muʿtamir related to us, saying: I heard my father say: Qatādah claimed, regarding this verse: ﴿If he leaves behind wealth, [he should make] a bequest to parents and relatives﴾, that [Shurayḥ] said: A man would bequeath all his wealth until the verse of inheritance was revealed.

**2657** — Aḥmad ibn al-Miqdām related to us, saying: al-Muʿtamir related to us, saying: I heard my father say: Qatādah claimed that the two verses of inheritance in *Sūrat al-Nisāʾ* abrogated the verse in *Sūrat al-Baqarah* concerning the bequest.

**2658** — Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr related to me, saying: Abū ʿĀṣim related to us, saying: ʿĪsā related to us, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid regarding the words of God: ﴿If he leaves behind wealth, [he should make] a bequest to parents and relatives﴾. He said: The inheritance was for the child, and the bequest was for the parents and relatives, and it has been abrogated.

**2659** — al-Muthannā related to me, saying: Abū Ḥudhayfah related to us, saying: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, who said: The inheritance was for the child, and the bequest was for the parents and relatives, and it has been abrogated. A verse in *Sūrat al-Nisāʾ* abrogated it: ﴿God enjoins you concerning your children﴾ [al-Nisāʾ 4:11].

**2660** — Mūsā ibn Hārūn related to me, saying: ʿAmr ibn Ḥammād related to us, saying: Asbāṭ related to us, from al-Suddī: ﴿It is prescribed for you that when death approaches one of you, if he leaves behind wealth, [he should make] a bequest to parents and relatives﴾. As for the parents and relatives: on the day this verse was revealed, people did not have a known inheritance; rather, a man would bequeath to his parent and his family, and they would divide it among themselves, until *al-Nisāʾ* abrogated it, saying: ﴿God enjoins you concerning your children﴾.

**2662** — Muḥammad ibn Khalaf al-ʿAsqalānī related to me, saying: Muḥammad ibn Yūsuf related to us, saying: Sufyān related to us, from Nusayr ibn Dhaʿlūq, who said: ʿUrwah — meaning Ibn Thābit — said to Rabīʿ ibn Khuthaym: [[In the printed edition: "Ibn Khuthaym," and I have adopted what is in *al-Tahdhīb*; see his biography.]] Bequeath to me your copy of the Qurʾān. He said: Then he looked at his father and said: ﴿And those of blood relationship are more entitled to one another in the Book of God﴾ [al-Anfāl 8:75].

**2663** — ʿAlī ibn Sahl related to us, saying: Yazīd related to us, from Sufyān, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Ibrāhīm, who said: We mentioned to him that Zayd and Ṭalḥah used to be strict regarding the bequest. He said: There was nothing wrong with them doing so; the Prophet (ﷺ) died without making a bequest, and Abū Bakr made a bequest. Whichever of the two you do is good.

**2664** — al-Ḥasan ibn Yaḥyā related to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, saying: al-Thawrī informed us, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Ibrāhīm, who said: Ṭalḥah and Zayd were mentioned in his presence, and he related something similar.

* *

As for the "good" (*khayr*) which, if a person leaves it behind, makes it obligatory for him to bequeath it to his parents and relatives who do not inherit, it is: wealth, as follows:

**2665** — al-Muthannā ibn Ibrāhīm related to me, saying: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ṣāliḥ related to us, from Muʿāwiyah ibn Ṣāliḥ, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥah, from Ibn ʿAbbās regarding His words: ﴿If he leaves behind wealth﴾, meaning property.

**2666** — Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr related to me, saying: Abū ʿĀṣim related to us, saying: ʿĪsā related to us, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid regarding the words of God: ﴿If he leaves behind wealth﴾, [meaning] property.

**2667** — al-Muthannā related to me, saying: Abū Ḥudhayfah [[In the printed edition: "Abū Jaʿfar," but the correct reading is "Abū Ḥudhayfah," and it is a recurring chain in the commentary; see the nearest instance above, no. 2659.]] related to us, saying: Shibl related to us, from Abū Najīḥ, from Mujāhid: ﴿If he leaves behind wealth﴾. He used to say: "Khayr" in the whole Qurʾān means wealth: ﴿And indeed, he is intense in his love of wealth﴾ [al-ʿĀdiyāt 100:8] — "khayr" means wealth; ﴿Indeed I have preferred the love of wealth over the remembrance of my Lord﴾ [Ṣād 38:32] — wealth; ﴿So make a contract with them if you know any good in them﴾ [al-Nūr 24:33] — wealth; and ﴿If he leaves behind wealth, [he should make] a bequest﴾ — wealth.

**2668** — Bishr ibn Muʿādh related to us, saying: Yazīd related to us, saying: Saʿīd related to us, from Qatādah: ﴿If he leaves behind wealth, [he should make] a bequest﴾, that is: property. [[Report 2668 — in the printed edition, "Bishr ibn Muʿādh related to us, saying: Saʿīd related to us" omits "Yazīd related to us." This is a recurring chain in the commentary; see the nearest instance above, no. 2640.]]

**2669** — Mūsā ibn Hārūn related to me, saying: ʿAmr ibn Ḥammād related to us, saying: Asbāṭ related to us, from al-Suddī: ﴿If he leaves behind wealth, [he should make] a bequest﴾. As for "khayr," it is property.

**2670** — I was told from ʿAmmār ibn al-Ḥasan, who said: Ibn Abī Jaʿfar related to us, from his father, from al-Rabīʿ: ﴿If he leaves behind wealth﴾. He said: If he leaves behind property.

**2671** — al-Qāsim related to us, saying: al-Ḥusayn related to us, saying: Ḥajjāj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās regarding His words: ﴿If he leaves behind wealth﴾. He said: The "khayr" is property.

**2672** — al-Muthannā related to me, saying: Suwayd related to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubārak informed us, from al-Ḥasan ibn Yaḥyā, from al-Ḍaḥḥāk regarding His words: ﴿If he leaves behind wealth, [he should make] a bequest﴾. He said: Property. Do you not see that He says: Shuʿayb said to his people: ﴿Indeed I see you in prosperity﴾ [Hūd 11:84], meaning wealth?

**2673** — Yūnus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr al-Yāfiʿī informed us, from Ibn Jurayj, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Rabāḥ, who recited: ﴿It is prescribed for you that when death approaches one of you, if he leaves behind wealth﴾. ʿAṭāʾ said: The "khayr," as it is understood, is property.

* *

Then they differed over the amount of property which, if a man leaves it behind, makes him subject to the ruling of this verse.

Some of them said: That is a thousand dirhams.

Those who said this:

**2674** — al-Muthannā related to me, saying: al-Ḥajjāj ibn al-Minhāl related to us, saying: Hammām ibn Yaḥyā related to us, from Qatādah regarding this verse: ﴿If he leaves behind wealth, [he should make] a bequest﴾. He said: The "khayr" is a thousand or more.

**2675** — al-Muthannā related to me, saying: al-Ḥajjāj related to us, saying: Ḥammād related to us, saying: Hishām ibn ʿUrwah informed us, from ʿUrwah: that ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib entered upon a paternal cousin of his to visit him, and he said: I want to make a bequest. ʿAlī said: Do not make a bequest, for you have not left behind any "khayr" to bequeath.

He said: The estate of [the one he visited] was between seven hundred and nine hundred.

**2676** — Yūnus ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: ʿUthmān ibn al-Ḥakam al-Ḥizāmī [[He is vocalized in *al-Khulāṣah* with a broken-ʿayn (*bi-kasr al-muhmalah*); in *al-Tahdhīb* and *al-Mīzān* it is "al-Judhāmī," with a dammah on the jīm followed by a dhāl with a dot.]] and Ibn Abī al-Zinād related to me, from Hishām ibn ʿUrwah, from his father, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib: that he entered upon a sick man, and the bequest was mentioned to him. He said: Do not make a bequest, for God only said: ﴿If he leaves behind wealth﴾, and you have not left behind any "khayr." Ibn Abī al-Zinād said in his version: So leave your property to your children.

**2677** — Muḥammad ibn Bashshār related to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān related to us, saying: Sufyān related to us, from Manṣūr ibn Ṣafiyyah, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUyaynah — or ʿUtbah, the doubt is mine — that a man wished to make a bequest, and he had many children and had left four hundred dinars. ʿĀʾishah said: I see no excess in it.

**2678** — al-Ḥasan ibn Yaḥyā related to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, saying: Maʿmar informed us, from Hishām ibn ʿUrwah, from his father, who said: ʿAlī entered upon a client of theirs at the time of death, who had seven hundred dirhams or six hundred dirhams. He said: Should I not make a bequest? He said: No! For God only said: ﴿If he leaves behind wealth﴾, and you do not have much property.

* *

Others said: That is what is between five hundred dirhams and a thousand.

Those who said this:

**2679** — al-Ḥasan ibn Yaḥyā related to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, saying: Maʿmar informed us, from Qatādah, from Abān ibn Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī regarding His words: ﴿If he leaves behind wealth﴾. He said: From a thousand dirhams down to five hundred.

* *

Others said: The bequest is obligatory, whether the property is little or much.

Those who said this:

**2680** — al-Ḥasan ibn Yaḥyā related to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, saying: Maʿmar informed us, from al-Zuhrī, who said: God made the bequest a right, whether little or much.

* *

Abū Jaʿfar said: The most correct of these opinions regarding the interpretation of His words: ﴿It is prescribed for you that when death approaches one of you, if he leaves behind wealth, [he should make] a bequest﴾ is what al-Zuhrī said. This is because little property and much property both fall under the term "khayr," and God did not limit it by any limit, nor did He specify any part of it, so it is not permissible to transfer the apparent meaning to the hidden. Therefore, whoever is approached by death while he has property, whether little or much, is obligated to bequeath from it, in kindness, to those of his fathers, mothers, and relatives who do not inherit from him, just as God, mighty is His remembrance, said and commanded.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 181:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then whoever alters it after he has heard it - the sin is only upon those who alter it﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is He, by this He means: Whoever changes what the testator has bequeathed - from his bequest of what is fair to his parents or relatives who do not inherit from him - after he has heard the bequest, then the sin of the alteration is only upon the one who altered his bequest.

* *

If someone says to us: To what does the "ha'" (the pronoun) in His saying "fa-man baddalahu" ("whoever alters it") refer?

It is said: It refers to an omitted element of the speech that is indicated by the apparent context. That is the command of the deceased, and his entrusting to the one to whom he entrusts it what he bequeathed, for the one to whom he bequeathed.

The meaning of the speech is: "It has been prescribed for you that when death approaches one of you, if he leaves wealth, a bequest to the parents and the relatives in a fair manner, as a duty upon the God-fearing." So bequeath to them. Whoever alters what you have bequeathed to them after you have heard them bequeathing to them, then the sin of what he did from that is upon him alone, not upon you.

We only said that the "ha'" in His saying "fa-man baddalahu" refers to an omitted element of the speech indicated by the apparent context, because His saying "It has been prescribed for you, when death approaches one of you, if he leaves wealth, the bequest" is from the speech of God, and the alteration of the one who alters can only be of the bequest of the testator. As for God's command concerning bequest, neither He nor anyone else can alter it, so it is permissible that the "ha'" in His saying "fa-man baddalahu" refers to "the bequest".

As for the "ha'" in His saying "ba'da ma sami'ahu" ("after he has heard it"), it refers to the first "ha'" in His saying "fa-man baddalahu".

As for the "ha'" in His saying "fa-innama ithmuhu" ("the sin is only its"), it is the pronoun of "the alteration" (al-tabdil), as if he said: The sin of what he altered of that is only upon those who alter it.

Those of the exegetes said in agreement with what we have said.

Mention of those who said that:

2682 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.

2683 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya ibn Salih narrated to me, from Ali ibn Abi Talha, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His saying: "Whoever alters it after he has heard it, the sin is only upon those who alter it." The reward of the testator has fallen upon God and he is free of its sin, and if he bequeathed with harm, his bequest is not permitted, as God said: ﴿not causing harm﴾ [Surah al-Nisa': 12].

2684 - al-Husayn ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada concerning His saying: "Whoever alters it after he has heard it," he said: Whoever alters the bequest after he has heard it, the sin of what he altered is upon him.

2685 - Musa ibn Harun narrated to me, saying: Amr ibn Hammad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "Whoever alters it after he has heard it, the sin is only upon those who alter it." 2687 - Sufyan ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Yazid ibn Ibrahim, from al-Hasan: "Whoever alters it after he has heard it," he said: whoever alters a bequest after he has heard it.

2688 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, from al-Hasan concerning this verse: "Whoever alters it after he has heard it, the sin is only upon those who alter it," he said: This is concerning the bequest; whoever alters it after he has heard it, the sin is only upon the one who altered it.

2689 - Ibn Bashshar and Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, both saying: Mu'adh ibn Hisham narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to me, from Qatada, from 'Ata', Salim ibn 'Abd Allah and Sulayman ibn Yasar, that they said: The bequest is carried out for the one to whom it was bequeathed. (Here ends the narration of Ibn al-Muthanna, and Ibn Bashshar added in his narration:) Qatada said: 'Abd Allah ibn Ma'mar said: It pleases me more that he bequeath to his close relatives, and I do not like to take it away from the one to whom he bequeathed it. Qatada said: And what pleases him more is for the one to whom he bequeathed it, as God the Mighty and Majestic said: "Whoever alters it after he has heard it, the sin is only upon those who alter it."

* *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah is Hearing, Knowing﴾ (181)

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is He, by this He means: "Indeed Allah is Hearing" of your bequest which I commanded you to make to your fathers, mothers and relatives when you make it, whether you are just in it according to what I permitted you to do of that in fairness, or you deviate, turning away from the truth and transgressing the right course? "Knowing" of what your breasts conceal of inclination toward truth and justice, or of injustice and deviation.

The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Then whoever fears injustice or sin from a testator and makes reconciliation between them, there is no sin upon him. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ (2:182).

Abu Ja'far [al-Tabari] said: The scholars of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed regarding the interpretation of this verse.

Some of them said: Its interpretation is: Whoever attends a sick person who is making a bequest as he approaches death, and fears that he may err in his bequest and do what is not his right, or that he may deliberately be unjust in it and command what he has no right to command, then there is no blame upon the one who attends him and hears that from him if he makes reconciliation between him and his heirs, by commanding him to be just in his bequest and forbidding them from preventing him from what Allah has permitted him and allowed him to do.

Mention of those who said this:

2690- Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding His words: "Whoever fears injustice or sin from a testator and makes reconciliation between them, there is no sin upon him." He said: This is when a man is present while he is dying. If he goes to excess, they command him to be just, and if he falls short, they say: Do such-and-such, give so-and-so such-and-such.

2691- al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding His words: "Whoever fears injustice or sin from a testator," he said: This is when a man is present while he is in dying. When he inclines toward injustice, they command him to be just. [[In the printed edition: "When he inclines toward death, they command him to be just," which does not fit the context of the report, nor the report from Mujahid before it. I judged that the copyist misread "al-jawr" (injustice) as "al-mawt" (death), or made a slip of the pen. Or perhaps he erred, made a mistake and added, and the original wording was like the context before it: "When he goes to excess, they command him to be just." Both are permissible and correct in meaning.]] And when he falls short of the right, they say: Do such-and-such, give so-and-so such-and-such.

* *

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: Whoever fears, from among the guardians of a deceased person [[In the printed edition: "guardians (awsiya') of a deceased person," and both are the same.]] or the ruler of the Muslims, injustice from a testator in his bequest which he made, and makes reconciliation between his heirs and the beneficiaries of what he bequeathed to them, returning the bequest to justice and right, then there is no blame and no sin.

Mention of those who said this:

2692- al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih, scribe of al-Layth, narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah ibn Salih narrated to me, from Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn Abbas regarding His words: "Whoever fears injustice from a testator" – meaning: sin – he says: If the deceased errs in his bequest or deviates in it, then there is no blame upon the guardians in returning his error to what is correct.

2693- al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us [[In the printed edition: "al-Hasan ibn 'Isa," which is a clear error. It is a chain that recurs in the tafsir, the nearest to us being number 2684.]], saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah regarding His words: "Whoever fears injustice or sin from a testator," he said: It is the man who bequeaths and deviates in his bequest, so the guardian returns it to right and justice. [[In the printed edition: "al-wali" (the ruler), and the correct reading is what I have written, i.e., the guardian of the deceased.]]

2694- Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Zuray' narrated to us, from Sa'id, from Qatadah regarding His words: "Whoever fears injustice or sin from a testator." Qatadah used to say: Whoever bequeaths with injustice or deviation in his bequest, and the guardian of the deceased or an imam of the imams of the Muslims returns it to the Book of Allah and to justice, then that is for him (the one who does so).

2695- al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Sa'd and Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi': "Whoever fears injustice or sin from a testator." Whoever makes a bequest with injustice, and the executor returns it to the truth after his death, there is no sin upon him. 'Abd al-Rahman said in his narration: "and makes reconciliation between them," meaning: the executor returned it to the truth after his death, so there is no sin upon him.

2696- al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Qabisah narrated to us, from Sufyan, from his father, from Ibrahim: "Whoever fears injustice or sin from a testator and makes reconciliation between them," he said: He returned it to the truth.

2697- Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad al-Zubayri narrated to us, saying: Isra'il narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Masruq, from Ibrahim, who said: I asked him about a man who bequeathed more than one third? He said: Return it. Then he recited: "Whoever fears injustice or sin from a testator."

2698- 'Amr ibn 'Ali narrated to us, saying: Khalid ibn Yazid, the owner of the pearls, narrated to us, saying: Abu Ja'far al-Razi narrated to us, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas: "Whoever fears injustice or sin from a testator and makes reconciliation between them, there is no sin upon him." He said: The executor returned it to the truth after his death, so there is no sin upon the executor.

* *

Some said: Rather, the meaning of that is: Whoever fears, from a testator, injustice or sin in his gift at the approach of his term, favoring some of his heirs over others, then there is no sin upon the one who makes reconciliation between them, i.e., between the heirs.

Mention of those who said this:

2699- al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, from Ibn Juraij, who said: I said to 'Ata' regarding His words: "Whoever fears injustice or sin from a testator," he said: It is the man who inclines unjustly or commits sin at his death, giving some of his heirs over others. Allah says: There is no sin upon the one who makes reconciliation between them. I said to 'Ata': Is it permissible for him to give to his heir at death? It is only a bequest, and there is no bequest to an heir? He said: That is in what he distributes among them.

* *

Others said: The meaning of that is: Whoever fears injustice or sin from a testator in his bequest to one who does not inherit from him, the benefit of which returns to one who does inherit from him, and makes reconciliation between his heirs, then there is no sin upon him.

Mention of those who said this:

2700- al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, saying: Ibn Juraij said: Ibn Tawus informed me, from his father, that he used to say: His injustice and sin is that a man bequeaths to the sons of his son so that the wealth remains for their father, and a woman bequeaths to the husband of her daughter so that the wealth remains for her daughter.
