He was patient in constant hunger, and he is the one who entered upon al-Hajjaj in the days of al-Jama'im and admonished him. Al-Hajjaj seized him to kill him, and put him in a dark room and sealed the door for fifteen days. Then he ordered the door opened so that he might come out to be buried. They entered upon him and found him standing in prayer. Al-Hajjaj said to him: "Go wherever you wish."]

= Then, concerning the continuous mass-transmitted reports from the Messenger of God (ﷺ) forbidding continuous fasting—of which the mention would lengthen the book—we have left out most of them, being content with mentioning some, since what we have mentioned suffices, without needing to cite anything else to prove the disapproval of continuous fasting.

3033. Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, from 'Ubayd Allah, who said: Nafi' informed me, from Ibn 'Umar: that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) forbade continuous fasting. They said: "You practise continuous fasting, O Messenger of God!" He said: "I am not like any of you; I spend the night being fed and given drink." [Note: Yahya ibn Sa'id is al-Qattan. 'Ubayd Allah is Ibn 'Umar ibn Hafs ibn 'Asim, whose biography has already passed (2740). In the printed edition here it reads "'an 'Abd Allah," with the takbir, meaning 'Abd Allah. 'Abd Allah is al-'Umari, the brother of 'Ubayd Allah (with diminutive). In this chain it is 'Ubayd Allah, because al-Qattan narrated from 'Ubayd Allah, and because al-Qattan did not narrate from 'Abd Allah, as reported in Ibn Abi Hatim (2/2/109) in the biography of 'Abd Allah, and so it is recorded in al-Tahdhib in his biography. The hadith was transmitted by Ahmad in al-Musnad (4721) from Yahya al-Qattan, from 'Ubayd Allah, with this chain; also (5795) from Muhammad ibn 'Ubayd, and (6299) from Ibn Numayr, both from 'Ubayd Allah. Likewise Muslim (1:303) through Ibn Numayr. Malik transmitted it in the Muwatta (p. 300) from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar; Ahmad (5917, 6125) and al-Bukhari (4:177) likewise through Malik. Ahmad also (6416) and Muslim (1:303) through 'Abd al-Warith, from Ayyub, from Nafi'. As for the narration of 'Abd Allah al-'Umari, Ahmad transmitted it (4752) from Waki', from al-'Umari, from Nafi'.]

It has also been related from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he permitted continuous fasting from the pre-dawn meal (sahar) to the pre-dawn meal.

3034. Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Hakam al-Misri narrated to me, saying: Shu'ayb narrated to us, from al-Layth, from Yazid ibn al-Hadd, from 'Abd Allah ibn Khabbab, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri: that he heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ) say: "Do not practise continuous fasting. Whoever among you wishes to fast continuously, let him continue until the pre-dawn meal." They said: "O Messenger of God, you practise continuous fasting!" He said: "I am not in your condition; I spend the night with one who feeds me and one who gives me drink." [Note: Shu'ayb is Ibn al-Layth ibn Sa'd the Imam, a well-known reliable transmitter from whom Muslim and others transmitted. In the printed edition it reads "Abu Shu'ayb," and the addition of "Abu" is an error with no meaning or place. Yazid ibn al-Hadd is Yazid ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Usamah ibn al-Hadd, whose biography has passed (2031). 'Abd Allah ibn Khabbab, with a fatha on the kha and doubled ba, client of Banu 'Adi ibn al-Najjar, is a reliable Successor; Abu Hatim and al-Nasa'i declared him reliable, and the authors of the six books transmitted from him. The hadith was transmitted by al-Bukhari (4:177) from 'Abd Allah ibn Yusuf, from al-Layth, with this chain. Ahmad in al-Musnad (11070; 3:8 Halabi) transmitted it from Qutaybah ibn Sa'id, from Bakr ibn Mudar, from Ibn al-Hadd; likewise Abu Dawud (2361) from Qutaybah. Ahmad also (11845; 3:87 Halabi) from Abu Sa'id, from 'Abd Allah ibn Ja'far, from Ibn al-Hadd. Al-Bukhari also transmitted it (4:181) through Ibn Abi Hazim, from Ibn al-Hadd. al-Suyuti mentioned it (1:200) and attributed it to al-Bukhari and Abu Dawud. Ibn Kathir also mentioned it (1:426) and said: "They both included it in the two Sahihs," which is a great error, may God have mercy on him, for Muslim did not include it in his Sahih. Al-Hafiz in Fath al-Bari (4:217), at the end of the book of fasting, stated that it is one of al-Bukhari's solitary narrations (afrad).]

3035. Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Abu Nu'aym narrated to us, saying: Abu Isra'il al-'Absi narrated to us, from Abu Bakr ibn Hafs, from the umm walad of Hatib ibn Abi Balta'ah: that she passed by the Messenger of God (ﷺ) while he was taking the pre-dawn meal, and he invited her to eat. She said: "I am fasting." He said: "How do you fast?" She mentioned this to the Prophet (ﷺ), and he said: "Where are you from continuous fasting of the family of Muhammad (ﷺ), from the pre-dawn meal to the pre-dawn meal?" [Note: Abu Nu'aym is al-Fadl ibn Dukayn, with a damma on the dal and fatha on the kaf, a reliable, memorising teacher of Ahmad. Ahmad said: "Despite his few narrations, he is more reliable than Waki'," and said also: "He was alert in hadith, knowledgeable about it." Abu Isra'il al-'Absi is Isma'il ibn Khalifah al-Mala'i, with a damma on the mim, lightening of the lam and a hamzah after the alif. He is weak; I have explained his weakness in the commentary on the Musnad (974). Abu Bakr ibn Hafs is 'Abd Allah ibn Hafs ibn 'Umar ibn Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, a reliable Successor, from whom the authors of the six books transmitted. The umm walad of Hatib ibn Abi Balta'ah: I do not know who she is, nor have I found a biography or mention of her. If the chain to her were sound, there would be no harm in it, since the unknown identity of a Companion does not harm; but the chain is weak.]

This hadith I have not found with anyone other than al-Tabari. Ibn Kathir transmitted it from him, 1:426, with its chain, and added nothing to its takhrij. Al-Suyuti did not mention it.]]
* *
So the interpretation of the verse is: then complete the abstention from what God commanded you to abstain from, from the time the white thread becomes distinct to you from the black thread, which is the dawn, until the night. Then that becomes lawful for you after it until the same time. As follows:

3036 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words, "Then complete the fast until the night," he said: "From these four limits." He then recited, "It is made lawful for you on the night of the fast to go in unto your wives," and he recited until he reached, "Then complete the fast until the night." My father and others of our shaykhs used to say this and recite it to us. [[The report 3036: His father is Zayd ibn Aslam al-Adawi Abu Usama al-Faqih, mawla of Umar. He related from his father, Ibn Umar, Abu Hurayrah, Aisha and a group of the Companions of the Messenger of God. He was a trustworthy (thiqah) scholar of jurisprudence and knowledge, and he was knowledgeable in the tafsir of the Qur'an. He died in the year 136 AH.]]
* *
Discussion concerning God's words, the Exalted: ﴿And do not have intercourse with them while you are staying (i'tikaf) in the mosques﴾
Abu Ja'far said: By His words, may His remembrance be exalted, "And do not have intercourse with them," He means: do not have sexual relations with your wives. [[See the explanation of "mubashara" (intimate contact) earlier: 503-505.]]
* *
= And by His words, "while you are staying in the mosques," He says: during the state of your staying (i'tikaf) in the mosques, and that is the state of confining themselves to the worship of God in their mosques.
[[The author's discourse has been abridged due to its great length.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 188:

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And do not consume one another's wealth unjustly, nor send it [as a bribe] to the rulers in order that you may consume a portion of the wealth of the people sinfully while you know [it is unlawful]﴾.

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: Exalted is He, by this He means: Let not some of you consume the property of others unjustly. Thus, by this, He made the one who consumes his brother's property unjustly like the one who consumes his own property unjustly.

A parallel to this is His words, exalted is He: ﴿And do not defame yourselves﴾ [Surah al-Hujurat: 11], and His words: ﴿And do not kill yourselves﴾ [Surah al-Nisa: 29], meaning: Let not some of you defame others, and let not some of you kill others [[See what has preceded of similar examples at 2:300; then verse 85 of Surah al-Baqarah, 2:303, in which he mentioned nothing of that. He did not explain this clarification in what preceded. This is evidence that he sometimes abridged speech considerably, relying on what had passed in his discourse or what would come in it, as I said in the introduction to the tafsir.]] because God, exalted is He, made the believers brothers, so the one who fights his brother is like the one who fights himself, and the one who defames him is like one who defames himself. Likewise, the Arabs refer to themselves by their brothers, and to their brothers by themselves, saying: "My brother and your brother, which of us is stronger in grappling?" meaning: you and I wrestle, and we see which of us is stronger [[See the explanation of Mushkil al-Qur'an: 114, this exact text.]] - so the speaker refers to himself by his brother, because a man's brother is to them like himself. Among that is the saying of the poet: [[He is Tha'labah ibn 'Amr (Hazn) al-'Abdi, son of Umm Hazna. It is also said he is from Banu Shayban, an ally within 'Abd al-Qays. He was among the horsemen (al-Ishtiqaq of Ibn Duraid: 197). See the next note.]]

My brother and your brother in the bottom of al-Nusayr... there is not in it any Arab of Ma'add

[[Al-Mufaddaliyyat: 513, Mushkil al-Qur'an: 114, Mu'jam ma Ista'jam: 1038. In the printed edition: "laysa lana" ("there is not for us"), and I have kept what is in the sources, as it seems to be correct. It is said: "laysa bil-dar 'arib," meaning there is no one in it. "Al-Nusayr" is the diminutive of "al-Nasr," a place in the dwellings of Banu Sulaym. However, Yaqut quoted from al-Hazimi that it is in the region of Nahawand, and cited this verse. If that is so, then this Ibn Umm Hazna is an Islamic-era figure. Yaqut said, citing Sayf: "The Muslims marched from Marj al-Qal'ah toward Nahawand, until they reached a fortress in which there were people; they conquered it and left al-Nusayr ibn Thawr in charge of it, with 'Ajl and Hanifah. It was conquered after the conquest of Nahawand, and neither 'Ajli nor Hanafi attended Nahawand, because they remained with al-Nusayr at the fortress, so it was named after him" (see Tarikh al-Tabari 4: 243, 251).

If it is correct that Ibn Umm Hazna was in the expedition of the Muslims, this verse supports this view, for he says to him: you and I are in the bottom of al-Nusayr, with no one of the sons of Ma'add (that is, the Arabs) with us in it. As for al-Hazimi's statement, if the place was in the lands of the Arabs, then he means: there is no one in it, and his phrase "of Ma'add" is superfluous speech. It has become clear to me that he is an Islamic poet, from some of his poetry in al-Mufaddaliyyat no. 74, in al-Wahshiyyat no. 217 (see also those attributed to their mothers, nos. 22, 32), and he has poetry in Hamasat al-Buhturi: 97, 103.

And if the narration of al-Tabari is correct, "laysa lana min Ma'add 'arib," then 'arib in this verse is his companion whom he mentioned at the beginning of the poem, saying: Indeed a 'Arib, even if it grieves me, is the dearest beloved and the nearest kin.

Then his saying "Ma'add" is the verbal noun of "'adda yaʿuddu" (to count). He says: you and I are in the bottom of al-Nusayr alone; no one is counted with us, meaning that the two of them are alone in the place, you have no one to help you, nor do I have anyone to help me, so there the one of courage among them appears. He said after the verse: So he swears by God that he will not hesitate, and I swear that if I reach him he will not return...

Then he approached me with power, and when he drew near, the liar spoke the truth to him.]]

* *

So the meaning of the speech is: Let not some of you consume the property of others among yourselves unjustly.

"Consuming it unjustly" means consuming it in a manner other than that which God has permitted to those who consume it.

* *

As for His words, "and send it to the rulers," He means: and dispute with it, meaning with your property, before the rulers, "in order that you may consume a portion" = a group = [[See what has preceded in the explanation of "fariq" at 2:224, 402.]] "of the wealth of the people sinfully while you know."

By His words "sinfully" He means by the unlawful which God has forbidden you [[See what has preceded in the explanation of "al-ithm" in this part, 3: 399-408.]] "while you know," that is: while you deliberately consume that sinfully, intending what God has forbidden you of it, and knowing that your act is disobedience to God and sin. [[In the printed edition: "disobedience to God," an error.]] As follows:

3059 - Al-Muthanna told me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah ibn Salih told me, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn 'Abbas: "And do not consume your property among yourselves unjustly and send it to the rulers." This concerns a man who owes property, but has no proof of it, so he denies the property and disputes about it before the rulers while he knows the right is upon him, and he knows he is sinful, a consumer of the unlawful.

3060 - Muhammad ibn 'Amr told me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding God's words: "and send it to the rulers," he said: Do not dispute while you are a wrongdoer.

3061 - Al-Muthanna told me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

3062 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah regarding His words: "And do not consume your property among yourselves unjustly and send it to the rulers." It was said: whoever walks with his opponent while he is a wrongdoer toward him, is sinful until he returns to the truth. Know, O son of Adam, that the judgment of a judge does not make unlawful for you what is lawful, nor make lawful for you falsehood; the judge only rules according to what he sees and what the witnesses testify, and the judge is a human who errs and is correct. Know that whoever is judged in his favor by falsehood, his dispute is not concluded until God gathers them together on the Day of Resurrection, and He judges between the wrongdoer and the rightful with better than what was judged for the wrongdoer against the rightful in this world [[In the printed edition: "and takes from what was judged...", the correct reading is what is adopted from Tafsir Ibn Kathir 1: 430.]].

3063 - Al-Hasan ibn Yahya told us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah regarding His words: "and send it to the rulers," he said: Do not send your brother's property to the judge while you know you are a wrongdoer, for his judgment does not make lawful for you anything that was unlawful for you.

3064 - Musa ibn Harun told me, saying: 'Amr ibn Hammad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "And do not consume your property among yourselves unjustly and send it to the rulers in order that you may consume a portion of the wealth of the people sinfully while you know." As for "unjustly," it says: a man among you wrongs his companion, then disputes with him to cut off his property while knowing he is a wrongdoer; this is His words: "and send it to the rulers."

3065 - Al-Qasim told us, saying: Al-Husayn told us, saying: Khalid al-Wasiti told me, from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from 'Ikrimah regarding His words: "And do not consume your property among yourselves unjustly," he said: it is the man who buys a commodity then returns it and returns with it dirhams.

3066 - Yunus told me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words: "And do not consume your property among yourselves unjustly and send it to the rulers," he says: he is more cunning than him and more knowledgeable of the argument, so he disputes with him over his property unjustly in order to consume his property unjustly. And he recited: ﴿O you who believe, do not consume one another's wealth unjustly, except [in the case of] trade by mutual consent among you﴾ [Surah al-Nisa: 29], and said: this is the gambling that the people of the Jahiliyyah used to practice.

* *

The root of "al-idla'" is a man lowering his bucket on a rope into a well, clinging to it. So it is said of one who argues for his claim: "He presented (adla) with such-and-such a proof," when his proof, by which he argues, is a means for him, to which he clings in his dispute, like the one who draws water from a well clinging to a bucket he has lowered into it by its rope. It is said of both - I mean of argumentation and of lowering a bucket into a well by a rope: "So-and-so presented (adla) his proof, and he presents it (yudli) with it; and he lowered (adla) his bucket into the well, and he lowers it (yudlīha) with it."

* *

As for His words, "and send it to the rulers," there are two grammatical possibilities in it:

The first: that His words "wa-tudlu" be jussive, conjoined to His words "wa la ta'kulu amwalakum baynakum bil-batil," meaning: and do not send it to the rulers. It has been mentioned that this is so in the reading of Ubayy, with the repetition of the negative particle: "wa la tudlu bihā ilal-hukkām."

The second: the accusative in the manner of "al-sarf" [[In the printed edition: "al-zarf," which is an outright error. The meaning of "al-sarf" has passed at 1: 569-570, and the note: 1.]], so its meaning then is: do not consume your property among yourselves unjustly while you send it to the rulers, as the poet said:

Do not forbid a trait and then do its like; it is a great shame upon you if you do it.

Meaning: do not forbid a trait while you do its like.

And the one in the jussive position - according to what is mentioned in the reading of Ubayy - is better than that it be in the accusative.

**The interpretation of His saying, ﴿They ask you, [Muhammad], about the new moons. Say, "They are measurements of time for the people and for the Hajj."﴾**

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: It is mentioned that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) was asked about the waxing and waning of the new moons and the variation of their phases, so God, may His remembrance be exalted, revealed this verse as an answer to what they had asked.

**Reports on this:**

3067. Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying, ﴿They ask you about the new moons. Say, "They are measurements of time for the people."﴾ Qatadah said: They asked the Prophet of God (ﷺ) about that: "Why were these new moons created?" So God revealed about them what you hear: ﴿"They are measurements of time for the people,"﴾ and He made them for the fasting and breaking of the fast of the Muslims, for their rites and their Hajj, for the waiting periods of their women, and for the maturity of their debts, and in other matters. And God knows best what sets right His creation.

3068. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi', who said: It was mentioned to us that they said to the Prophet (ﷺ): "Why were the new moons created?" So God, may He be exalted, revealed: ﴿They ask you about the new moons. Say, "They are measurements of time for the people and for the Hajj."﴾ God made them measurements of time for the fasting and breaking of the fast of the Muslims, for their Hajj and their rites, for the waiting periods of their women, and for "the lawfulness of their debts" [[It is so in these reports, 3068, 3070, 3072 and 3073: "حل ديونهم" (the lawfulness of their debts). What is in the lexicons is: "حل الدين يحل حلولا ومحلا" (with a kasra on the ḥāʾ in the second form), meaning it became due. I think the verbal noun here should be "حلا" with a fatḥa on the ḥāʾ, like its counterparts in the language, as in their saying "صد يصد صدا وصدودا". If the ḥāʾ were read with a kasra it would be acceptable. This narration, however, settles the correctness of this form.]].

3069. Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying, ﴿measurements of time for the people and for the Hajj,﴾ he said: They are measurements of time for the people in their Hajj, their fasting, their breaking of the fast, and their rites.

3070. Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: The people said: "Why were the new moons created?" So it was revealed: ﴿They ask you about the new moons. Say, "They are measurements of time for the people,"﴾ for their fasting and breaking of the fast, their Hajj and their rites. He said: Ibn ʿAbbas said: and the time of their Hajj, the waiting periods of their women, and "the lawfulness of their debts."

3071. Musa ibn Harun narrated to me, saying: ʿAmr ibn Hammad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿They ask you about the new moons. Say, "They are measurements of time for the people,"﴾ so they are measurements of time for divorce, menstruation, and the Hajj.

3072. It was reported from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: Al-Fadl ibn Khalid narrated to us, saying: ʿUbayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from al-Dahhak: ﴿They ask you about the new moons. Say, "They are measurements of time for the people,"﴾ meaning: the lawfulness of their debts, the time of their Hajj, and the waiting periods of their women.

3073. Muhammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: The people asked the Messenger of God (ﷺ) about the new moons, so this verse was revealed: ﴿They ask you about the new moons. Say, "They are measurements of time for the people,"﴾ by which they know the lawfulness of their debts, the waiting periods of their women, and the time of their Hajj.

3074. Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, from Sharik, from Jabir, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Yahya, from ʿAli: that he was asked about His saying, ﴿measurements of time for the people,﴾ and he said: They are the measurements of the month: "like this, like this, like this," and he closed his thumb [i.e., counted three]. "When you see it, fast, and when you see it, break your fast. If it is hidden from you by clouds, then complete thirty [days]." [[The report 3074. Jabir: he is Ibn Yazid al-Ju'fi, whom we have shown to be very weak, in 2340. As for his teacher "ʿAbd Allah ibn Yahya": I do not know who he is. My strong suspicion is that the name is distorted, and I have not been able to establish its correct form.
This report is not mentioned by Ibn Kathir or al-Suyuti. Ibn Kathir referred to it only briefly, in 1:430.
Its meaning has also been transmitted as a raised (marfuʿ) report, in a sound hadith narrated by al-Hakim in 1:423, from the hadith of ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUmar. He declared it sound and al-Dhahabi agreed. Ibn Kathir mentioned it in 1:430 from the narration of ʿAbd al-Razzaq, then pointed to al-Hakim's narration of it. Al-Suyuti mentioned it in 1:203–204 and also attributed it to al-Bayhaqi.]]

\* \*

Abu Ja'far said: The interpretation of the verse, given that the matter is as we have stated from those whose words we have cited on it, is: They ask you, O Muhammad, about the new moons, their disappearance, their crescent phase, their fullness, their being balanced [as a half-moon], and the change of their states through waxing, waning, disappearance and concealment. And what is the reason that He made a difference between them and the sun, which is always constant in one state that does not change through increase or decrease? Then say, O Muhammad: Your Lord made a difference in this, by making the new moons, about which you asked, and the difference between them and what He differentiated them from, measurements of time for you and for others of the children of Adam in their livelihoods. By their waxing, waning, disappearance, concealment, and your sighting of them, you know the times of the maturity of your debts, the end of the term of the employment of those you hired, the passing of your women's waiting periods, and the time of your fasting and breaking your fast. Thus He made them measurements of time for the people.

\* \*

As for His saying, ﴿and for the Hajj,﴾ it means: and for the Hajj. He says: He also made them a measurement for your Hajj, by which you know the time of your rites and your pilgrimage.

\* \*

**The interpretation of His saying, ﴿It is not righteousness that you enter houses from their backs, but righteousness is [in] one who fears God. So enter houses through their doors, and fear God that you may succeed.﴾**

Abu Ja'far said: It was said that this verse was revealed concerning a people who, when they were in the state of ihram, would not enter their houses through their doors.

**Those who said this:**

3075. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, from Shu'bah, from Abu Ishaq, who said: I heard al-Bara' say: The Ansar, when they performed the Hajj and returned, would not enter the houses except from their backs. He said: So a man from the Ansar came and entered through his door, and he was asked about that, so this verse was revealed: ﴿It is not righteousness that you enter houses from their backs.﴾ [[The hadith 3075: Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi narrated it in 717 from Shu'bah, with this chain, in a similar form. Al-Bukhari narrated it at length in 3:494 from Abu al-Walid, from Shu'bah, with this chain.
Al-Suyuti mentioned it in 1:204 and added its attribution to ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim. Its meaning will come with another chain after it.]]

3076. Sufyan ibn Waki' narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from Isra'il, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Bara', who said: In the Jahiliyyah, when they entered the state of ihram, they would come to their houses from their backs and would not enter through their doors, so this was revealed: ﴿It is not righteousness that you enter houses from their backs...﴾ to the end of the verse. [[The hadith 3076 is a repetition of the preceding one. It is in the tafsir of Waki', as al-Suyuti mentioned in 1:204.
Al-Bukhari narrated it in 8:137, from ʿUbayd Allah ibn Musa, from Isra'il, with this chain.]]

3077. Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, saying: Al-Muʿtamir ibn Sulayman narrated to us, saying: I heard Dawud, from Qays ibn Habtar, that some people, when they entered the state of ihram, would not enter an enclosure through its door, nor a house through its door, or a tent. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) and his companions entered a house, and there was a man from the Ansar called "Rifa'ah ibn Tabut," who came, climbed over the wall, and entered upon the Messenger of God (ﷺ). When [the Prophet] came out through the door of the house, or he said: the door of the tent, Rifa'ah came out with him. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "What led you to do that?" He said: "O Messenger of God, I saw you come out of it, so I came out of it!" The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "I am a man of the Ahmas!" [He] said: "If you are a man of the Ahmas, then our religion is one!" So God, may His remembrance be exalted, revealed: ﴿It is not righteousness that you enter houses from their backs, but righteousness is [in] one who fears God. So enter houses through their doors.﴾ [[The hadith 3077: Dawud is Ibn Abi Hind, whose biography has passed in 1608.
Qays ibn Habtar al-Nahshali al-Tamimi: a trustworthy Successor (tabiʿi). Abu Zurʿah, al-Nasa'i and others declared him trustworthy.
"Habtar": with an unmarked ḥāʾ, an unmarked tāʾ, and a silent bāʾ between them. In the printed edition here, it appears as "Jubayr," which is a misreading. It also appears in this distorted form in the places we will point out in al-Fath, al-Isabah and al-Durr al-Manthur, regarding this hadith.
This is a mursal chain, since it is from a Successor directly from the Prophet (ﷺ), so it is weak.
Al-Suyuti mentioned the hadith in 1:204 and added its attribution to ʿAbd ibn Humayd and Ibn al-Mundhir.
Al-Hafiz [Ibn Hajar] mentioned it in al-Isabah 2:209, from the tafsir of ʿAbd ibn Humayd. He also mentioned it in al-Fath 3:494, in abridged form, attributing it to ʿAbd ibn Humayd and Ibn Jarir, and in both places he stated explicitly that it is a mursal hadith.
Al-Ahmas: he is the one who is strict in his religion and firm in it. Then al-Hums (plural of Ahmas) were the Quraysh, Khuza'ah, because they settled in Makkah and lived beside the Quraysh, and everyone among the Arabs whom the Quraysh gave birth to, the Kinanah, and Judaylah of Qays, who are Fahm and ʿAdwan, the two sons of ʿAmr ibn Qays ʿAylan, and the Banu ʿAmir ibn Sa'sa'ah, and every tribe of Arabs that settled in Makkah. The Hums had been strict in their religion upon themselves: when they performed the rites, they would not melt ghee, nor cook curd, nor store milk, nor separate a nursing mother from her nursing until it was weaned; they would not move hair or nails, nor would they make from their hair or fleece or wool or cotton any tents in their pilgrimage; they would not eat meat, nor wear anything except new clothes; they would not circumambulate the House except in their shoes and clothes; they would not walk to the mosque on foot, out of reverence for its precinct; they would not enter houses through their doors, and would not go out to ʿArafat. They would say: "We are the People of God," and they would remain at Muzdalifah until they completed their rites, and they would walk between al-Safa and al-Marwah when they departed from Muzdalifah, and they would dwell during their travels in tents of red leather (al-Muhabbar of Ibn Habib: 178–180, then the Sirah of Ibn Hisham 1:211–216 / and al-Tabari in the tafsir, number 3840).]]

3078. Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to us, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the saying of God, may His remembrance be exalted, ﴿It is not righteousness that you enter houses from their backs,﴾ he said: It is not righteousness that you enter houses through openings in the backs of the houses, and doors in their sides, which the people of the Jahiliyyah made. They were forbidden to enter through them, and were commanded to enter through their doors.

3079. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, similarly.

3080. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mughirah, from Ibrahim, who said: Some people from the Hijaz, when they entered the state of ihram, would not enter through the doors of their houses, but would enter from their backs. So this was revealed: ﴿but righteousness is [in] one who fears God...﴾ the verse.

3081. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿It is not righteousness that you enter houses from their backs, but righteousness is [in] one who fears God. So enter houses through their doors,﴾ he said: The polytheists, when one of them entered the state of ihram, would make an opening in the back of his house and place a ladder, and he would enter through it. He said: One day the Messenger of God (ﷺ) came with a man of the polytheists, and he came to the door to enter, so he entered through it. He said: Then the man went to enter through the opening. He said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "What is your matter?" He said: "I am a man of the Ahmas!" The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "And I am a man of the Ahmas."

3082. Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: Some men of the Ansar, when they began the ihram for ʿUmrah, did not allow anything to come between them and the sky, considering it a sin. A man would go out in ihram for ʿUmrah, then need something after he had left his house, so he would return and not enter through the door of the chamber, because of the roof of the door, which would come between him and the sky. Instead, he would open the wall behind him, then stand in his chamber and command his need, and it would be brought out to him from his house. Until it reached us that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) entered the state of ihram for ʿUmrah during the year of al-Hudaybiyah, and entered a chamber. A man from the Ansar, from the Banu Salimah, entered after him, and the Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: "I am a man of the Ahmas!" Al-Zuhri said: The Hums did not mind that. The Ansari said: "And I am a man of the Ahmas!" meaning: "I am also upon your religion." So God, may His remembrance be exalted, revealed: ﴿It is not righteousness that you enter houses from their backs.﴾

3084. Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿It is not righteousness that you enter houses﴾ the whole verse. Qatadah said: This tribe of the Ansar, in the Jahiliyyah, when one of them entered the state of ihram for Hajj or ʿUmrah, would not enter a house through its door, but would climb over the wall. Even after they became Muslims, they remained so. So God, may His remembrance be exalted, revealed concerning that what you hear, and forbade them from their practice, informing them that their practice was not righteousness, and commanded them to enter houses through their doors.

3085. Musa ibn Harun narrated to me, saying: ʿAmr ibn Hammad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His saying: ﴿It is not righteousness that you enter houses from their backs,﴾ that some people of the Arabs, when they performed the Hajj, would not enter their houses through their doors; they would make openings at their backs. When the Messenger of God (ﷺ) performed the Farewell Pilgrimage, he came walking, and with him was a man of those people, who was a Muslim. When the Messenger of God (ﷺ) reached the door of the house, the man stayed behind him and refused to enter. He said: "O Messenger of God, I am a man of the Ahmas!" — meaning: "I am in ihram." Those who did that were called "al-Hums." The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "I too am a man of the Ahmas! Enter." So the man entered, and God, may His remembrance be exalted, revealed: ﴿and enter houses through their doors.﴾

3086. Muhammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas: ﴿It is not righteousness that you enter houses from their backs, but righteousness is [in] one who fears God. And enter houses through their doors,﴾ and that some men of Madinah, when one of them feared something from his enemy, would enter the state of ihram and be safe; and when he entered ihram, he would not enter through the door of his house, but would make an opening in the back of his house. When the Messenger of God (ﷺ) came to Madinah, there was a man there in ihram in this way. The people of Madinah called the orchard "al-Hushsh." The Messenger of God (ﷺ) entered an orchard through its door, and that man in ihram entered with him. A man called to him from behind: "O so-and-so, you are in ihram, and you have entered!" He said: "I am a man of the Ahmas!" He said: "O Messenger of God, if you are in ihram, then I am in ihram, and if you are a man of the Ahmas, then I am a man of the Ahmas!" So God, may His remembrance be exalted, revealed: ﴿It is not righteousness that you enter houses from their backs,﴾ to the end of the verse, and God permitted the believers to enter through their doors.

3087. It was reported from ʿAmmar ibn al-Hasan, who said: ʿAbd Allah ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabiʿ regarding His saying: ﴿It is not righteousness that you enter houses from their backs, but righteousness is [in] one who fears God. And enter houses through their doors.﴾ He said: The people of Madinah and others, when they entered the state of ihram, would not enter houses except from their backs, by climbing over them. So when one of them entered ihram, he would not enter the house except by climbing over it from its back. The Prophet (ﷺ) entered one day a house of one of the Ansar, and a man who had entered ihram came in after him. They objected to that and said: "This is a wicked man!" The Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: "Why did you enter through the door when you are in ihram?" He said: "I saw you, O Messenger of God, enter, so I entered after you!" The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "I am a man of the Ahmas!" — and Quraysh at that time were called the Hums. When the Prophet (ﷺ) said that, the Ansari said: "My religion is your religion!" So God, may His remembrance be exalted, revealed: ﴿It is not righteousness that you enter houses from their backs,﴾ the verse.

3088. Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, who said: Ibn Jurayj said: I asked ʿAta' about His saying: ﴿It is not righteousness that you enter houses from their backs.﴾ He said: The people of the Jahiliyyah would enter houses from their backs and considered that righteousness. So He said: "Righteousness," then described what righteousness is, and commanded that they enter houses through their doors. Ibn Jurayj said: ʿAbd Allah ibn Kathir informed me that he heard Mujahid say: This verse was about the Ansar, who entered houses from their backs, seeking blessing by doing so.

\* \*

Abu Ja'far said: So the interpretation of the verse is: It is not righteousness, O people, that you enter houses from their backs while you are in the state of ihram. But righteousness is [in] one who fears God, fearing Him and avoiding what He has forbidden, and obeying Him by performing the obligations He has commanded. As for entering houses from their backs, there is no righteousness with God in it. So enter them from wherever you wish, through their doors or other than their doors, so long as you do not believe that it is forbidden to enter them through their doors in any circumstance, for it is not permitted for you to hold that belief, since it is something I have not forbidden you.

\* \*

**The interpretation of His saying, ﴿And fear God that you may prosper.﴾**

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 189–190 (part 2 of 2):

Abu Ja'far said: By this, His mention (exalted is He) means: "And fear Allah, O people, so beware of Him and dread Him by obeying Him in what He has commanded you of His obligations, and by avoiding what He has forbidden you, so that you may prosper (tufliḥū), succeeding in your pursuits with Him, and attain by it endurance in His gardens and eternity in His bounty."
* *
We have already explained the meaning of "al-falāḥ" (prosperity, success) earlier, with what indicates it [see what preceded, 1: 249–250].
* *
The discussion on the interpretation of His words (exalted is He): ﴿And fight in the way of Allah those who fight you, but do not transgress. Indeed, Allah does not love the transgressors﴾ (190)

Abu Ja'far said: The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wīl) differed regarding the interpretation of this verse.

Some of them said: This verse is the first verse revealed concerning the command to the Muslims to fight the people of polytheism. They said: In it the Muslims were commanded to fight those among the polytheists who fought them, and to refrain from those who refrained from them; then it was abrogated (nusikha) by "Bara'ah" (Surat al-Tawbah).

Mention of those who said this:

3089 – Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman ibn Sa'd and Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Rabi' regarding His words: "And fight in the way of Allah those who fight you, but do not transgress. Indeed, Allah does not love the transgressors." He said: This is the first verse revealed about fighting in Medina. When it was revealed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would fight whoever fought him, and refrain from whoever refrained from him, until "Bara'ah" was revealed. Abd al-Rahman did not mention "Medina."

3090 – Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words: "And fight in the way of Allah those who fight you," to the end of the verse: "This has been abrogated!" And he recited the words of Allah: ﴿And fight the polytheists all together as they fight you all together﴾ [Surat al-Tawbah: 36], "and this is the abrogating (nāsikha) [verse]." And he recited: ﴿A declaration of disassociation from Allah and His Messenger﴾ until he reached: ﴿And when the sacred months have passed, then kill the polytheists wherever you find them﴾, to: ﴿Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [Surat al-Tawbah: 1–5].

* *

Others said: Rather, that is a command from Allah (exalted is His mention) to the Muslims to fight the disbelievers, and it was not abrogated. What "transgression" (i'tidā') that Allah forbade them from is His prohibition of killing women and offspring. They said: The prohibition of killing them is established and its ruling holds today. They said: Nothing of the ruling of this verse has been abrogated.

Mention of those who said this:

3091 – Sufyan ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Sadaqa al-Dimashqi, from Yahya ibn Yahya al-Ghassani, who said: I wrote to Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz asking him about His words: "And fight in the way of Allah those who fight you, but do not transgress. Indeed, Allah does not love the transgressors." He said: So he wrote back to me: "Indeed, that concerns women, offspring, and whoever among them has not set up war against you."

3092 – Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding the words of Allah (exalted is His mention): "And fight in the way of Allah those who fight you," [addressed] to the companions of Muhammad (ﷺ): they were commanded to fight the disbelievers.

3093 – Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.

3094 – Ali ibn Dawud narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas: "And fight in the way of Allah those who fight you, but do not transgress. Indeed, Allah does not love the transgressors." He says: Do not kill women, children, or the old man, nor whoever offers you peace and withholds his hand. If you do this, then you have transgressed.

3095 – Ibn al-Barqi narrated to me, saying: Amr ibn Abi Salama narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Abd al-Aziz, who said: Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz wrote to Adi ibn Artah: "I have found a verse in the Book of Allah: 'And fight in the way of Allah those who fight you, but do not transgress. Indeed, Allah does not love the transgressors.' That is: do not fight those who do not fight you, meaning: women, children, and monks."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The more correct of these two opinions is the one stated by Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, because the claim of one who asserts the abrogation of a verse, when it may be non-abrogated, without evidence for the soundness of his claim, is arbitrary (tahakkum), and arbitrariness is not beyond anyone.

* *

We have already explained the meaning of "naskh" (abrogation), and the meaning on which the soundness of abrogation depends, with what has made repeating it in this place unnecessary [see what preceded, 2: 471–483, and this part, 3: 385].

* *

So the interpretation of the verse, given that the matter is as we have described, is: "And fight, O believers, in the way of Allah" — and His way (sabīluhu) is His path which He has made clear and His religion which He has legislated for His servants. He (exalted is His mention) says to them: Fight in obedience to Me and upon what I have legislated for you of My religion, and call to it whoever turns away from it and is arrogant, with force and with tongues, until they return in obedience to Me, or they give you the jizya (poll-tax) in humiliation, if they are People of the Book. He (exalted is His mention) commanded them to fight those among the combatants of the people of disbelief who engage in fighting, not those among their women and offspring who have not engaged in fighting, for they are property and servants for them when the combatants among them are overcome and subdued. That is the meaning of His words: "Fight in the way of Allah those who fight you," because He permitted refraining from those who refrain, so one does not fight the polytheist idolaters and those among the People of the Book who refrain from fighting the Muslims by giving the jizya in humiliation.

So the meaning of His words "but do not transgress" is: do not kill a child or a woman, nor anyone among the People of the Two Books and the Magians who has given you the jizya, "Indeed, Allah does not love the transgressors" who exceed His limits, so that they make lawful what Allah has forbidden them, namely killing those whom He has forbidden to be killed, from among the women and offspring of the polytheists.

**The interpretation of His saying, ﴿They ask you, [Muhammad], about the new moons. Say, "They are measurements of time for the people and for the Hajj."﴾**

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: It is mentioned that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) was asked about the waxing and waning of the new moons and the variation of their phases, so God, may His remembrance be exalted, revealed this verse as an answer to what they had asked.

**Reports on this:**

3067. Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying, ﴿They ask you about the new moons. Say, "They are measurements of time for the people."﴾ Qatadah said: They asked the Prophet of God (ﷺ) about that: "Why were these new moons created?" So God revealed about them what you hear: ﴿"They are measurements of time for the people,"﴾ and He made them for the fasting and breaking of the fast of the Muslims, for their rites and their Hajj, for the waiting periods of their women, and for the maturity of their debts, and in other matters. And God knows best what sets right His creation.

3068. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi', who said: It was mentioned to us that they said to the Prophet (ﷺ): "Why were the new moons created?" So God, may He be exalted, revealed: ﴿They ask you about the new moons. Say, "They are measurements of time for the people and for the Hajj."﴾ God made them measurements of time for the fasting and breaking of the fast of the Muslims, for their Hajj and their rites, for the waiting periods of their women, and for "the lawfulness of their debts" [[It is so in these reports, 3068, 3070, 3072 and 3073: "حل ديونهم" (the lawfulness of their debts). What is in the lexicons is: "حل الدين يحل حلولا ومحلا" (with a kasra on the ḥāʾ in the second form), meaning it became due. I think the verbal noun here should be "حلا" with a fatḥa on the ḥāʾ, like its counterparts in the language, as in their saying "صد يصد صدا وصدودا". If the ḥāʾ were read with a kasra it would be acceptable. This narration, however, settles the correctness of this form.]].

3069. Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying, ﴿measurements of time for the people and for the Hajj,﴾ he said: They are measurements of time for the people in their Hajj, their fasting, their breaking of the fast, and their rites.

3070. Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: The people said: "Why were the new moons created?" So it was revealed: ﴿They ask you about the new moons. Say, "They are measurements of time for the people,"﴾ for their fasting and breaking of the fast, their Hajj and their rites. He said: Ibn ʿAbbas said: and the time of their Hajj, the waiting periods of their women, and "the lawfulness of their debts."

3071. Musa ibn Harun narrated to me, saying: ʿAmr ibn Hammad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿They ask you about the new moons. Say, "They are measurements of time for the people,"﴾ so they are measurements of time for divorce, menstruation, and the Hajj.

3072. It was reported from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: Al-Fadl ibn Khalid narrated to us, saying: ʿUbayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from al-Dahhak: ﴿They ask you about the new moons. Say, "They are measurements of time for the people,"﴾ meaning: the lawfulness of their debts, the time of their Hajj, and the waiting periods of their women.

3073. Muhammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: The people asked the Messenger of God (ﷺ) about the new moons, so this verse was revealed: ﴿They ask you about the new moons. Say, "They are measurements of time for the people,"﴾ by which they know the lawfulness of their debts, the waiting periods of their women, and the time of their Hajj.

3074. Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, from Sharik, from Jabir, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Yahya, from ʿAli: that he was asked about His saying, ﴿measurements of time for the people,﴾ and he said: They are the measurements of the month: "like this, like this, like this," and he closed his thumb [i.e., counted three]. "When you see it, fast, and when you see it, break your fast. If it is hidden from you by clouds, then complete thirty [days]." [[The report 3074. Jabir: he is Ibn Yazid al-Ju'fi, whom we have shown to be very weak, in 2340. As for his teacher "ʿAbd Allah ibn Yahya": I do not know who he is. My strong suspicion is that the name is distorted, and I have not been able to establish its correct form.
This report is not mentioned by Ibn Kathir or al-Suyuti. Ibn Kathir referred to it only briefly, in 1:430.
Its meaning has also been transmitted as a raised (marfuʿ) report, in a sound hadith narrated by al-Hakim in 1:423, from the hadith of ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUmar. He declared it sound and al-Dhahabi agreed. Ibn Kathir mentioned it in 1:430 from the narration of ʿAbd al-Razzaq, then pointed to al-Hakim's narration of it. Al-Suyuti mentioned it in 1:203–204 and also attributed it to al-Bayhaqi.]]

\* \*

Abu Ja'far said: The interpretation of the verse, given that the matter is as we have stated from those whose words we have cited on it, is: They ask you, O Muhammad, about the new moons, their disappearance, their crescent phase, their fullness, their being balanced [as a half-moon], and the change of their states through waxing, waning, disappearance and concealment. And what is the reason that He made a difference between them and the sun, which is always constant in one state that does not change through increase or decrease? Then say, O Muhammad: Your Lord made a difference in this, by making the new moons, about which you asked, and the difference between them and what He differentiated them from, measurements of time for you and for others of the children of Adam in their livelihoods. By their waxing, waning, disappearance, concealment, and your sighting of them, you know the times of the maturity of your debts, the end of the term of the employment of those you hired, the passing of your women's waiting periods, and the time of your fasting and breaking your fast. Thus He made them measurements of time for the people.

\* \*

As for His saying, ﴿and for the Hajj,﴾ it means: and for the Hajj. He says: He also made them a measurement for your Hajj, by which you know the time of your rites and your pilgrimage.

\* \*

**The interpretation of His saying, ﴿It is not righteousness that you enter houses from their backs, but righteousness is [in] one who fears God. So enter houses through their doors, and fear God that you may succeed.﴾**

Abu Ja'far said: It was said that this verse was revealed concerning a people who, when they were in the state of ihram, would not enter their houses through their doors.

**Those who said this:**

3075. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, from Shu'bah, from Abu Ishaq, who said: I heard al-Bara' say: The Ansar, when they performed the Hajj and returned, would not enter the houses except from their backs. He said: So a man from the Ansar came and entered through his door, and he was asked about that, so this verse was revealed: ﴿It is not righteousness that you enter houses from their backs.﴾ [[The hadith 3075: Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi narrated it in 717 from Shu'bah, with this chain, in a similar form. Al-Bukhari narrated it at length in 3:494 from Abu al-Walid, from Shu'bah, with this chain.
Al-Suyuti mentioned it in 1:204 and added its attribution to ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim. Its meaning will come with another chain after it.]]

3076. Sufyan ibn Waki' narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from Isra'il, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Bara', who said: In the Jahiliyyah, when they entered the state of ihram, they would come to their houses from their backs and would not enter through their doors, so this was revealed: ﴿It is not righteousness that you enter houses from their backs...﴾ to the end of the verse. [[The hadith 3076 is a repetition of the preceding one. It is in the tafsir of Waki', as al-Suyuti mentioned in 1:204.
Al-Bukhari narrated it in 8:137, from ʿUbayd Allah ibn Musa, from Isra'il, with this chain.]]

3077. Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, saying: Al-Muʿtamir ibn Sulayman narrated to us, saying: I heard Dawud, from Qays ibn Habtar, that some people, when they entered the state of ihram, would not enter an enclosure through its door, nor a house through its door, or a tent. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) and his companions entered a house, and there was a man from the Ansar called "Rifa'ah ibn Tabut," who came, climbed over the wall, and entered upon the Messenger of God (ﷺ). When [the Prophet] came out through the door of the house, or he said: the door of the tent, Rifa'ah came out with him. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "What led you to do that?" He said: "O Messenger of God, I saw you come out of it, so I came out of it!" The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "I am a man of the Ahmas!" [He] said: "If you are a man of the Ahmas, then our religion is one!" So God, may His remembrance be exalted, revealed: ﴿It is not righteousness that you enter houses from their backs, but righteousness is [in] one who fears God. So enter houses through their doors.﴾ [[The hadith 3077: Dawud is Ibn Abi Hind, whose biography has passed in 1608.
Qays ibn Habtar al-Nahshali al-Tamimi: a trustworthy Successor (tabiʿi). Abu Zurʿah, al-Nasa'i and others declared him trustworthy.
"Habtar": with an unmarked ḥāʾ, an unmarked tāʾ, and a silent bāʾ between them. In the printed edition here, it appears as "Jubayr," which is a misreading. It also appears in this distorted form in the places we will point out in al-Fath, al-Isabah and al-Durr al-Manthur, regarding this hadith.
This is a mursal chain, since it is from a Successor directly from the Prophet (ﷺ), so it is weak.
Al-Suyuti mentioned the hadith in 1:204 and added its attribution to ʿAbd ibn Humayd and Ibn al-Mundhir.
Al-Hafiz [Ibn Hajar] mentioned it in al-Isabah 2:209, from the tafsir of ʿAbd ibn Humayd. He also mentioned it in al-Fath 3:494, in abridged form, attributing it to ʿAbd ibn Humayd and Ibn Jarir, and in both places he stated explicitly that it is a mursal hadith.
Al-Ahmas: he is the one who is strict in his religion and firm in it. Then al-Hums (plural of Ahmas) were the Quraysh, Khuza'ah, because they settled in Makkah and lived beside the Quraysh, and everyone among the Arabs whom the Quraysh gave birth to, the Kinanah, and Judaylah of Qays, who are Fahm and ʿAdwan, the two sons of ʿAmr ibn Qays ʿAylan, and the Banu ʿAmir ibn Sa'sa'ah, and every tribe of Arabs that settled in Makkah. The Hums had been strict in their religion upon themselves: when they performed the rites, they would not melt ghee, nor cook curd, nor store milk, nor separate a nursing mother from her nursing until it was weaned; they would not move hair or nails, nor would they make from their hair or fleece or wool or cotton any tents in their pilgrimage; they would not eat meat, nor wear anything except new clothes; they would not circumambulate the House except in their shoes and clothes; they would not walk to the mosque on foot, out of reverence for its precinct; they would not enter houses through their doors, and would not go out to ʿArafat. They would say: "We are the People of God," and they would remain at Muzdalifah until they completed their rites, and they would walk between al-Safa and al-Marwah when they departed from Muzdalifah, and they would dwell during their travels in tents of red leather (al-Muhabbar of Ibn Habib: 178–180, then the Sirah of Ibn Hisham 1:211–216 / and al-Tabari in the tafsir, number 3840).]]

3078. Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to us, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the saying of God, may His remembrance be exalted, ﴿It is not righteousness that you enter houses from their backs,﴾ he said: It is not righteousness that you enter houses through openings in the backs of the houses, and doors in their sides, which the people of the Jahiliyyah made. They were forbidden to enter through them, and were commanded to enter through their doors.

3079. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, similarly.

3080. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mughirah, from Ibrahim, who said: Some people from the Hijaz, when they entered the state of ihram, would not enter through the doors of their houses, but would enter from their backs. So this was revealed: ﴿but righteousness is [in] one who fears God...﴾ the verse.

3081. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿It is not righteousness that you enter houses from their backs, but righteousness is [in] one who fears God. So enter houses through their doors,﴾ he said: The polytheists, when one of them entered the state of ihram, would make an opening in the back of his house and place a ladder, and he would enter through it. He said: One day the Messenger of God (ﷺ) came with a man of the polytheists, and he came to the door to enter, so he entered through it. He said: Then the man went to enter through the opening. He said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "What is your matter?" He said: "I am a man of the Ahmas!" The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "And I am a man of the Ahmas."

3082. Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: Some men of the Ansar, when they began the ihram for ʿUmrah, did not allow anything to come between them and the sky, considering it a sin. A man would go out in ihram for ʿUmrah, then need something after he had left his house, so he would return and not enter through the door of the chamber, because of the roof of the door, which would come between him and the sky. Instead, he would open the wall behind him, then stand in his chamber and command his need, and it would be brought out to him from his house. Until it reached us that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) entered the state of ihram for ʿUmrah during the year of al-Hudaybiyah, and entered a chamber. A man from the Ansar, from the Banu Salimah, entered after him, and the Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: "I am a man of the Ahmas!" Al-Zuhri said: The Hums did not mind that. The Ansari said: "And I am a man of the Ahmas!" meaning: "I am also upon your religion." So God, may His remembrance be exalted, revealed: ﴿It is not righteousness that you enter houses from their backs.﴾

3084. Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿It is not righteousness that you enter houses﴾ the whole verse. Qatadah said: This tribe of the Ansar, in the Jahiliyyah, when one of them entered the state of ihram for Hajj or ʿUmrah, would not enter a house through its door, but would climb over the wall. Even after they became Muslims, they remained so. So God, may His remembrance be exalted, revealed concerning that what you hear, and forbade them from their practice, informing them that their practice was not righteousness, and commanded them to enter houses through their doors.

3085. Musa ibn Harun narrated to me, saying: ʿAmr ibn Hammad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His saying: ﴿It is not righteousness that you enter houses from their backs,﴾ that some people of the Arabs, when they performed the Hajj, would not enter their houses through their doors; they would make openings at their backs. When the Messenger of God (ﷺ) performed the Farewell Pilgrimage, he came walking, and with him was a man of those people, who was a Muslim. When the Messenger of God (ﷺ) reached the door of the house, the man stayed behind him and refused to enter. He said: "O Messenger of God, I am a man of the Ahmas!" — meaning: "I am in ihram." Those who did that were called "al-Hums." The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "I too am a man of the Ahmas! Enter." So the man entered, and God, may His remembrance be exalted, revealed: ﴿and enter houses through their doors.﴾

3086. Muhammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas: ﴿It is not righteousness that you enter houses from their backs, but righteousness is [in] one who fears God. And enter houses through their doors,﴾ and that some men of Madinah, when one of them feared something from his enemy, would enter the state of ihram and be safe; and when he entered ihram, he would not enter through the door of his house, but would make an opening in the back of his house. When the Messenger of God (ﷺ) came to Madinah, there was a man there in ihram in this way. The people of Madinah called the orchard "al-Hushsh." The Messenger of God (ﷺ) entered an orchard through its door, and that man in ihram entered with him. A man called to him from behind: "O so-and-so, you are in ihram, and you have entered!" He said: "I am a man of the Ahmas!" He said: "O Messenger of God, if you are in ihram, then I am in ihram, and if you are a man of the Ahmas, then I am a man of the Ahmas!" So God, may His remembrance be exalted, revealed: ﴿It is not righteousness that you enter houses from their backs,﴾ to the end of the verse, and God permitted the believers to enter through their doors.

3087. It was reported from ʿAmmar ibn al-Hasan, who said: ʿAbd Allah ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabiʿ regarding His saying: ﴿It is not righteousness that you enter houses from their backs, but righteousness is [in] one who fears God. And enter houses through their doors.﴾ He said: The people of Madinah and others, when they entered the state of ihram, would not enter houses except from their backs, by climbing over them. So when one of them entered ihram, he would not enter the house except by climbing over it from its back. The Prophet (ﷺ) entered one day a house of one of the Ansar, and a man who had entered ihram came in after him. They objected to that and said: "This is a wicked man!" The Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: "Why did you enter through the door when you are in ihram?" He said: "I saw you, O Messenger of God, enter, so I entered after you!" The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "I am a man of the Ahmas!" — and Quraysh at that time were called the Hums. When the Prophet (ﷺ) said that, the Ansari said: "My religion is your religion!" So God, may His remembrance be exalted, revealed: ﴿It is not righteousness that you enter houses from their backs,﴾ the verse.

3088. Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, who said: Ibn Jurayj said: I asked ʿAta' about His saying: ﴿It is not righteousness that you enter houses from their backs.﴾ He said: The people of the Jahiliyyah would enter houses from their backs and considered that righteousness. So He said: "Righteousness," then described what righteousness is, and commanded that they enter houses through their doors. Ibn Jurayj said: ʿAbd Allah ibn Kathir informed me that he heard Mujahid say: This verse was about the Ansar, who entered houses from their backs, seeking blessing by doing so.

\* \*

Abu Ja'far said: So the interpretation of the verse is: It is not righteousness, O people, that you enter houses from their backs while you are in the state of ihram. But righteousness is [in] one who fears God, fearing Him and avoiding what He has forbidden, and obeying Him by performing the obligations He has commanded. As for entering houses from their backs, there is no righteousness with God in it. So enter them from wherever you wish, through their doors or other than their doors, so long as you do not believe that it is forbidden to enter them through their doors in any circumstance, for it is not permitted for you to hold that belief, since it is something I have not forbidden you.

\* \*

**The interpretation of His saying, ﴿And fear God that you may prosper.﴾**

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 189–190 (part 2 of 2):

Abu Ja'far said: By this, His mention (exalted is He) means: "And fear Allah, O people, so beware of Him and dread Him by obeying Him in what He has commanded you of His obligations, and by avoiding what He has forbidden you, so that you may prosper (tufliḥū), succeeding in your pursuits with Him, and attain by it endurance in His gardens and eternity in His bounty."
* *
We have already explained the meaning of "al-falāḥ" (prosperity, success) earlier, with what indicates it [see what preceded, 1: 249–250].
* *
The discussion on the interpretation of His words (exalted is He): ﴿And fight in the way of Allah those who fight you, but do not transgress. Indeed, Allah does not love the transgressors﴾ (190)

Abu Ja'far said: The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wīl) differed regarding the interpretation of this verse.

Some of them said: This verse is the first verse revealed concerning the command to the Muslims to fight the people of polytheism. They said: In it the Muslims were commanded to fight those among the polytheists who fought them, and to refrain from those who refrained from them; then it was abrogated (nusikha) by "Bara'ah" (Surat al-Tawbah).

Mention of those who said this:

3089 – Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman ibn Sa'd and Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Rabi' regarding His words: "And fight in the way of Allah those who fight you, but do not transgress. Indeed, Allah does not love the transgressors." He said: This is the first verse revealed about fighting in Medina. When it was revealed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would fight whoever fought him, and refrain from whoever refrained from him, until "Bara'ah" was revealed. Abd al-Rahman did not mention "Medina."

3090 – Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words: "And fight in the way of Allah those who fight you," to the end of the verse: "This has been abrogated!" And he recited the words of Allah: ﴿And fight the polytheists all together as they fight you all together﴾ [Surat al-Tawbah: 36], "and this is the abrogating (nāsikha) [verse]." And he recited: ﴿A declaration of disassociation from Allah and His Messenger﴾ until he reached: ﴿And when the sacred months have passed, then kill the polytheists wherever you find them﴾, to: ﴿Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [Surat al-Tawbah: 1–5].

* *

Others said: Rather, that is a command from Allah (exalted is His mention) to the Muslims to fight the disbelievers, and it was not abrogated. What "transgression" (i'tidā') that Allah forbade them from is His prohibition of killing women and offspring. They said: The prohibition of killing them is established and its ruling holds today. They said: Nothing of the ruling of this verse has been abrogated.

Mention of those who said this:

3091 – Sufyan ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Sadaqa al-Dimashqi, from Yahya ibn Yahya al-Ghassani, who said: I wrote to Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz asking him about His words: "And fight in the way of Allah those who fight you, but do not transgress. Indeed, Allah does not love the transgressors." He said: So he wrote back to me: "Indeed, that concerns women, offspring, and whoever among them has not set up war against you."

3092 – Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding the words of Allah (exalted is His mention): "And fight in the way of Allah those who fight you," [addressed] to the companions of Muhammad (ﷺ): they were commanded to fight the disbelievers.

3093 – Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.

3094 – Ali ibn Dawud narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas: "And fight in the way of Allah those who fight you, but do not transgress. Indeed, Allah does not love the transgressors." He says: Do not kill women, children, or the old man, nor whoever offers you peace and withholds his hand. If you do this, then you have transgressed.

3095 – Ibn al-Barqi narrated to me, saying: Amr ibn Abi Salama narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Abd al-Aziz, who said: Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz wrote to Adi ibn Artah: "I have found a verse in the Book of Allah: 'And fight in the way of Allah those who fight you, but do not transgress. Indeed, Allah does not love the transgressors.' That is: do not fight those who do not fight you, meaning: women, children, and monks."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The more correct of these two opinions is the one stated by Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, because the claim of one who asserts the abrogation of a verse, when it may be non-abrogated, without evidence for the soundness of his claim, is arbitrary (tahakkum), and arbitrariness is not beyond anyone.

* *

We have already explained the meaning of "naskh" (abrogation), and the meaning on which the soundness of abrogation depends, with what has made repeating it in this place unnecessary [see what preceded, 2: 471–483, and this part, 3: 385].

* *

So the interpretation of the verse, given that the matter is as we have described, is: "And fight, O believers, in the way of Allah" — and His way (sabīluhu) is His path which He has made clear and His religion which He has legislated for His servants. He (exalted is His mention) says to them: Fight in obedience to Me and upon what I have legislated for you of My religion, and call to it whoever turns away from it and is arrogant, with force and with tongues, until they return in obedience to Me, or they give you the jizya (poll-tax) in humiliation, if they are People of the Book. He (exalted is His mention) commanded them to fight those among the combatants of the people of disbelief who engage in fighting, not those among their women and offspring who have not engaged in fighting, for they are property and servants for them when the combatants among them are overcome and subdued. That is the meaning of His words: "Fight in the way of Allah those who fight you," because He permitted refraining from those who refrain, so one does not fight the polytheist idolaters and those among the People of the Book who refrain from fighting the Muslims by giving the jizya in humiliation.

So the meaning of His words "but do not transgress" is: do not kill a child or a woman, nor anyone among the People of the Two Books and the Magians who has given you the jizya, "Indeed, Allah does not love the transgressors" who exceed His limits, so that they make lawful what Allah has forbidden them, namely killing those whom He has forbidden to be killed, from among the women and offspring of the polytheists.

Commentary on the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And kill them wherever you overtake them, and expel them from where they expelled you﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By this, exalted is His remembrance, He means: O believers, kill those among the polytheists who fight you wherever you find their vulnerable points and are able to kill them. This is the meaning of His words, "wherever you overtake them."

* *

As for "al-thiqfah" (skill, keenness) in the matter [[This is a verbal noun I have not found in the lexicographical books; it seems to be, as I have vocalised it, with a kasra on the thā', on the pattern of "ḥikmah" and "nushdah." What they have mentioned is: "thaqifa al-shay' thaqfan, wa thiqafan, wa thaqufah."]], it means skill in it and perception. It is said, "He is indeed thaqif laqif," when he is very wary in fighting and perceptive of the places of killing. As for "al-tathqif," it has a meaning other than this, namely straightening.

* *

So the meaning of "And kill them wherever you overtake them" is: kill them in whatever place you are able to kill them and perceive their vulnerable points.

* *

As for His words, "and expel them from where they expelled you," it refers to the emigrants who were driven out of their homes and dwellings in Makkah. So He, exalted is His remembrance, said to them: Expel these who fight you, since they have expelled you from your homes, from their dwellings and homes just as they expelled you from them.

* *

Interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And persecution is worse than killing﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His words, exalted is His remembrance, "and persecution is worse than killing," He means: associating partners with God is worse than killing.

* *

I have already explained earlier that the origin of "fitnah" (persecution, trial) is testing and examination [[See what has preceded, 2:444.]].

* *

So the meaning of the statement is: the trial of the believer in his religion, until he turns back from it and becomes a polytheist after his Islam, is harder on him and more harmful than being killed while remaining upon his religion, holding fast to it, and right in it. As:

3096 - Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the words of God, "and persecution is worse than killing," he said: The apostasy of the believer to idolatry is harder on him than killing.

3097 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.

3098 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words, "and persecution is worse than killing," he said: Shirk is worse than killing.

3099 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, the same.

3100 - I was told from 'Ammar ibn al-Hasan, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi', regarding "and persecution is worse than killing," he said: Shirk is worse than killing.

3101 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abu Zuhayr narrated to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, regarding "and persecution is worse than killing," he said: Shirk.

3102 - al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, saying: Ibn Juraij said: 'Abd Allah ibn Kathir informed me, from Mujahid regarding His words, "and persecution is worse than killing," he said: The persecution is shirk.

3103 - I was told from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, saying: I heard al-Fadl ibn Khalid say: 'Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from al-Dahhak, regarding "and persecution is worse than killing," he said: Shirk is worse than killing.

3104 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words, exalted is His remembrance, "and persecution is worse than killing," he said: the persecution of disbelief.

* *

Interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And do not fight them at the Sacred Mosque until they fight you there; but if they fight you, then kill them. Such is the recompense of the disbelievers﴾ (2:191)

Abu Ja'far said: The reciters differ in the reading of this.

The majority of the reciters of Madinah and Makkah read: "wa-la tuqatiluhum 'inda al-masjid al-haram hatta yuqatilukum fihi fa-in qatalukum faqtuluhum," meaning: do not begin fighting the polytheists at the Sacred Mosque, O believers, until they begin fighting you there. If they begin fighting you there at the Sacred Mosque, within the sanctuary, then kill them, for God has made the reward of the disbelievers for their disbelief and evil deeds: killing in this world and long disgrace in the next. As:

3105 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah regarding His words, "And do not fight them at the Sacred Mosque until they fight you there": they did not fight there until they were attacked with fighting. Then this was abrogated afterward, when He said: "And fight them until there is no persecution" = until there is no shirk, "and religion is for God" = that it be said: There is no god but God; upon this the Prophet of God fought, and to it he called.

3106 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: al-Hajjaj ibn al-Minhal narrated to us, saying: Hammam narrated to us, from Qatadah: "And do not fight them at the Sacred Mosque until they fight you there; but if they fight you, then kill them." God commanded His Prophet ﷺ not to fight them at the Sacred Mosque except if they began fighting there. Then God abrogated that with His words: ﴿So when the sacred months have passed, kill the polytheists wherever you find them﴾ [Surah al-Tawbah: 5]. So God commanded His Prophet, when the term had expired, to fight them in the non-sacred and sacred areas and at the House, until they testify that there is no god but God and that Muhammad is the Messenger of God.

3107 - I was told from 'Ammar ibn al-Hasan, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi', regarding His words: "And do not fight them at the Sacred Mosque until they fight you there," that they did not fight them there. Then this was abrogated afterward, when He said: "Fight them until there is no persecution."

* *

Others said: This is a decisive verse, not abrogated.

Those who said that:
