3108 - al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "But if they fight you" in the sanctuary, then kill them; such is the recompense of the disbelievers. Do not fight anyone there; but whoever transgresses against you and fights you, fight him as he fights you.

* *

The majority of the Kufan reciters read: "wa-la taqtuluhum 'inda al-masjid al-haram hatta yaqtulukum fihi fa-in qatalukum faqtuluhum," meaning: do not begin killing them until they begin killing you.

Those who said that:

3109 - al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hammad narrated to us, from Abu Hammad, from Hamzah al-Zayyat, who said: I said to al-A'mash: What do you say of your reading, "wa-la taqtuluhum 'inda al-masjid al-haram hatta yaqtulukum fihi fa-in qataluhum faqtuluhum kadhalika jaza' al-kafirin, fa-in intahaw fa-inna Allaha ghafurun rahim," if they kill them, how do they kill them? He said: The Arabs, when one of them is killed, say "we were killed," and when one of them is struck, they say "we were struck."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The more correct of these two readings is the reading of one who reads: "wa-la tuqatiluhum 'inda al-masjid al-haram hatta yuqatilukum fihi fa-in qatalukum faqtuluhum," because God, exalted is His remembrance, did not command His Prophet ﷺ and his companions, in a situation where the polytheists fight them, to submit to them until they kill some of them, after He had permitted them and the polytheists to fight. So the reading with permission to kill them after they have killed some of them is more correct than the reading we have chosen. And if that is so, it is known that He, exalted is His remembrance, had permitted them to fight them when the polytheists began the fighting, before they killed any of them and after they had killed some of them.

God, exalted is His remembrance, abrogated this verse with His words, "And fight them until there is no persecution," and His words: ﴿Kill the polytheists wherever you find them﴾ [Surah al-Tawbah: 5], and similar verses.

* *

We have mentioned some of the statements of those who said it was abrogated, and we will mention the statements of those whose statements have been reported to us without being mentioned.

3110 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah: "And do not fight them at the Sacred Mosque until they fight you there." He said: His words abrogated it: ﴿Kill the polytheists wherever you find them﴾.

3111 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words: "And do not fight them at the Sacred Mosque until they fight you there," he said: until they begin with you. This had been forbidden, then God made it lawful for him, and it remained so until God commanded him to fight them afterward.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 192:

The explanation of His saying, ﴿Then if they desist, indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ (2:192):

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: By this, may His remembrance be exalted, He means: Then if the disbelievers who are fighting you desist from fighting you and from their disbelief in Allah, and they abandon that and repent, ﴿indeed Allah is Forgiving﴾ of the sins of those among them who believe and repent of their polytheism and turn back to Allah from the acts of disobedience that they committed earlier and the days that have passed, ﴿Merciful﴾ toward them in the Hereafter, by His bounty upon them, and by His giving them what He gives the people of obedience in reward, for their turning back to His love from disobedience to Him. As:

3112 - Al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Abu Huthayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿Then if they desist﴾ means: if they repent. ﴿Indeed Allah is Forgiving, Merciful﴾.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 193:

The discussion of His saying, Most High: ﴿And fight them until there is no more fitnah and religion is for Allah﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): And fight the polytheists who fight you, until there is no fitnah, meaning: until there is no shirk (association of partners with Allah), and until none is worshipped besides Him, and the worship of idols, gods and rivals perishes, and worship and obedience belong to Allah alone, apart from other idols and images. As Qatadah said, concerning this:

3113 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning His saying: "And fight them until there is no fitnah," he said: until there is no shirk.

3114 - Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, concerning His saying: "And fight them until there is no fitnah," he said: until there is no shirk.

3115 - Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "And fight them until there is no fitnah," he said: the shirk. "And religion is for Allah."

3116 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.

3117 - Musa ibn Harun narrated to me, saying: Amr ibn Hammad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "And fight them until there is no fitnah," he said: As for fitnah, it is shirk.

3118 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, His saying: "And fight them until there is no fitnah," meaning: fight until there is no shirk.

3119 - It was narrated to me from Ammar ibn al-Hasan, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi': "And fight them until there is no fitnah," i.e., shirk.

3120 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said concerning His saying: "And fight them until there is no fitnah," he said: until there is no kufr, and he recited: ﴿You will fight them, or they will submit﴾ [Surah al-Fath: 16].

3121 - Ali ibn Dawud narrated to me, saying: Abd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah ibn Salih narrated to me, from Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn Abbas: "And fight them until there is no fitnah," he says: shirk.

* *

As for "religion" (al-din), which Allah mentions in this place [[See the meaning of "al-din" above, 1: 155, 221.]], it is worship and obedience to Allah in His commands and prohibitions. From this is the saying of al-A'sha:

He subjugated the Rabab when they disliked the religion, by successive raids and assaults...

[[His Diwan: 12, and it will come in the tafsir 3: 141 (Bulaq). He said it in praise of al-Aswad ibn al-Mundhir al-Lakhmi, brother of al-Nu'man ibn al-Mundhir on his mother's side, and al-Aswad's mother was from Taym al-Rabab. This is the view of Abu Ubaydah, but the correct view is what others said: that he said it in praise of al-Mundhir ibn al-Aswad, who raided the two allies Asad and Dhubyan, then attacked al-Tuff, and seized camels, captives and captives of the family of al-A'sha, the Banu Sa'd ibn Dubay'ah ibn Tha'labah, while al-A'sha was absent. When he returned he found the tribe plundered, so he came to him and recited to him and asked him to grant him the captives and transport them, and he did so.

Al-Rabab (with a kasra on the ra) are the Banu Abd Manat ibn Ud: Taym, Adi, Awf and Thawr, who gathered and made an alliance with their cousins Dabbah ibn Ud against their cousins Tamim ibn Ud. They brought rabb (cooked dates) and dipped their hands in it, so they were called "al-Rabab," then Dabbah separated from them and was content with its numbers.

His saying "dan al-Rabab" means: he humiliated them, enslaved them, and compelled them to obedience. His saying "daraka," meaning successive, one following another. And al-Sayal: the assault. He attacked his enemy: leapt upon him and seized him. He means: he continued raiding and plundering them until they submitted in obedience.]]

By his saying "when they disliked the religion," he means: when they disliked obedience and refused it.

* *

Ahl al-ta'wil (the scholars of interpretation) have said the same as what we have said on this.

Those who said this:

3122 - It was narrated to me from Ammar ibn al-Hasan, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi': "And religion is for Allah," he says: until none is worshipped but Allah, and that is "There is no god but Allah," upon which the Prophet (ﷺ) fought and to which he called. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "I have been commanded to fight the people until they say there is no god but Allah, and establish the prayer, and give zakah. When they do that, they have protected their blood and property from me, except by its right, and their reckoning is with Allah."

3123 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: "And religion is for Allah," that it be said: "There is no god but Allah." It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) used to say: "Allah has commanded me to fight the people until they say there is no god but Allah." Then he mentioned the like of the hadith of al-Rabi'.

* *

The discussion of His saying, Most High: ﴿But if they desist, then there is no aggression except against the wrongdoers﴾ (193)

Abu Ja'far said: By His saying, may His remembrance be exalted, "But if they desist," He means: if those who fight you of the disbelievers desist from fighting you, enter your religion, acknowledge what Allah has obligated upon you of His duties, and abandon what they were upon of worshipping idols, then leave off aggression against them, fighting them and striving against them, for it is not fitting to act aggressively except against the wrongdoers, who are the polytheists with Allah, and those who abandoned His worship and worshipped other than their Creator.

* *

If someone says: Is it permissible to act aggressively against the wrongdoer, so that it is said: "there is no aggression except against the wrongdoers"?

[[See the meaning of "al-'udwan" above, 2: 307, and this part 3: 376, 564.]]

It is said: The meaning of this is other than the way you have taken. Rather, it is by way of recompense, for what the polytheists did of aggression. He says: Do to them the like of what they did to you, as one says: "If you attack me unjustly, I will attack you in return," and the second is not an injustice, as 'Amr ibn Shas al-Asadi said:

We repaid those of aggression yesterday for their injury, retaliation, equal, your measure matching the sandal's measure to the sandal.

[[I did not find the verse, and most of the poetry of 'Amr ibn Shas, despite its abundance and quality, has been lost.]]

This is similar to His saying: ﴿Allah mocks them﴾ [Surah al-Baqarah: 15], and ﴿They mock them, so Allah mocks them﴾ [Surah al-Tawbah: 79]. We have already explained this and its parallels earlier [[See above, 1: 301-306.]].

* *

Several scholars of interpretation said what we have said as the interpretation.

Those who said this:

3124 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning His saying: "But if they desist, then there is no aggression except against the wrongdoers," the wrongdoer being one who refused to say "There is no god but Allah."

3125 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi': "Then there is no aggression except against the wrongdoers," he said: they are the polytheists.

3126 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Uthman ibn Ghiyath narrated to us, saying: I heard Ikrimah concerning this verse: "Then there is no aggression except against the wrongdoers," he said: they are those who refused to say "There is no god but Allah."

* *

Others said: The meaning of His saying, "Then there is no aggression except against the wrongdoers," is: do not fight except those who fight.

Those who said this:

3127 - Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "But if they desist, then there is no aggression except against the wrongdoers," he says: do not fight except those who fight you.

3128 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.

3129 - Musa ibn Harun narrated to me, saying: Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, who said: "But if they desist, then there is no aggression except against the wrongdoers," for Allah does not love aggression against the wrongdoers or against others, but He says: act aggressively against them with the like of what they did against you.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: Some grammarians of Basra said concerning His saying, "But if they desist, then there is no aggression except against the wrongdoers," that one may not say "if they desist" unless it is known that they will not all desist, only some of them. So it is as if He said: If some of them desist, then there is no aggression except against the wrongdoers among them, and the object is omitted, as in His saying: ﴿So whoever enjoys the 'umrah until the hajj, then what is easy of the offering﴾ [Surah al-Baqarah: 196], meaning: then upon him is what is easy of the offering; and as one says: "To whomever you intend, intend," meaning: to him.

Others among them denied the omission in this and interpreted it: "But if they desist, then indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful toward whoever desists, and there is no aggression except against the wrongdoers who do not desist."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 194:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿The sacred month for the sacred month, and violations of sacred things are subject to retribution﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His saying, majestic is His praise: "The sacred month for the sacred month" is Dhu al-Qa'dah, the month in which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ performed the 'umrah of al-Hudaybiyah, when the polytheists of the people of Makkah prevented him from the House and from entering Makkah, in the sixth year of his migration. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ made a treaty with the polytheists in that year, on condition that he return the following year, enter Makkah and stay there three days. When the following year came, which was the seventh year of his migration, he set out to perform 'umrah with his Companions in Dhu al-Qa'dah, which was the month in which the polytheists had barred him from the House in the sixth year. The people of Makkah vacated the city for him until the Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered it, fulfilled his need there, completed his 'umrah, stayed there three days, and then left it, returning to Madinah. So Allah, majestic is His praise, said to His Prophet ﷺ and the Muslims with him: "The sacred month" – that is, Dhu al-Qa'dah, in which Allah brought you to His sanctuary and House, despite the displeasure of the polytheists of Quraysh, until you had fulfilled your purpose from it – "for the sacred month", which the polytheists of Quraysh had barred you from in the previous year, so that you turned back, unwillingly, from the Sanctuary, and did not enter it nor reach the House of Allah. Thus Allah granted you retribution, O believers, against the polytheists by your entering the Sanctuary in the sacred month despite their displeasure, in return for what they had done to you in the sacred month of barring and preventing you from reaching the House. As:

3130 - Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Bazi' narrated to me, saying: Yusuf – meaning Ibn Khalid al-Samti – narrated to us, saying: Nafi' ibn Malik narrated to us, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: "And violations of sacred things are subject to retribution," he said: They are the polytheists, who detained Muhammad ﷺ in Dhu al-Qa'dah, so Allah returned him in Dhu al-Qa'dah and caused him to enter the Sacred House, and took retribution for him from them. [[The report 3130: Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Bazi' – with the ba' vowelled with fatha and the zay with kasra – the teacher of al-Tabari: trustworthy; Abu Hatim and others deemed him trustworthy, and Muslim related from him in his Sahih. A similar chain has passed before, but its name for his grandfather was altered to "Zuray'", and we noted that this is not known, and the possibility that the correct form is "Ibn Bazi'" [was raised]; in 2451 the correct form has become clear here.

Yusuf ibn Khalid al-Samti: extremely weak, a liar, as we mentioned in that chain. In the printed edition here "al-Sahmi" occurs instead of "al-Samti"; this is an error.]]

3131 - Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning the saying of Allah, majestic is His praise: "The sacred month for the sacred month and violations of sacred things are subject to retribution," he said: Quraysh boasted of having turned back the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at al-Hudaybiyah, in sacred state, in Dhu al-Qa'dah, away from the sacred city. So Allah caused him to enter Makkah in the following year, in Dhu al-Qa'dah, and he fulfilled his 'umrah, and took retribution for him by what had been prevented between him and it at al-Hudaybiyah.

3132 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to me, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

3133 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning His saying: "The sacred month for the sacred month and violations of sacred things are subject to retribution": The Prophet of Allah ﷺ and his Companions set out and performed 'umrah in Dhu al-Qa'dah, with the offering animals with them, until when they reached al-Hudaybiyah the polytheists barred them, and the Prophet of Allah ﷺ made peace with them on condition that he return that year and come back the following year, to be in Makkah three days, entering only with weapons as a rider, and leave, and not take out anyone of the people of Makkah. They slaughtered the offering at al-Hudaybiyah and shaved and shortened their hair. When the following year came, the Prophet of Allah ﷺ and his Companions set out until they entered Makkah and performed 'umrah in Dhu al-Qa'dah, and stayed there three nights. The polytheists had boasted over him when they had turned him back on the day of al-Hudaybiyah, so Allah took retribution for him from them, and caused him to enter Makkah in that month in Dhu al-Qa'dah in which they had turned him back. Allah said: "The sacred month for the sacred month and violations of sacred things are subject to retribution."

3134 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, and from 'Uthman, from Miqsam, concerning His saying: "The sacred month for the sacred month and violations of sacred things are subject to retribution," they both said: This was during the journey of al-Hudaybiyah, when the polytheists barred the Prophet ﷺ and his Companions from the House in the sacred month, and then they settled with the polytheists on that day an agreement [[qadha al-rajul yuqadihi qada' wa-qadiyyah: he judged him in a dispute, and reached with him a decisive judgement that both agreed to. In the opening of the Treaty of al-Hudaybiyah: "This is what Muhammad settled," i.e., concluded a truce. Accordingly this 'umrah of al-Hudaybiyah was named "the 'umrah of the settlement" and "the 'umrah of the truce."]] that you may perform 'umrah the following year, in this month in which they barred you. So Allah, exalted is His remembrance, made for them a sacred month in which to perform 'umrah in place of their month in which they had been barred. Therefore He said: "And violations of sacred things are subject to retribution."

3135 - Musa ibn Harun narrated to me, saying: 'Amr ibn Hammad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "The sacred month for the sacred month and violations of sacred things are subject to retribution." He said: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ performed the 'umrah of al-Hudaybiyah in Dhu al-Qa'dah in the sixth year of his migration, the polytheists barred him and refused to let him be. Then they made a treaty with him, in their settlement, that they would vacate Makkah for him the following year for three days, leaving it to him. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to them after the conquest of Khaybar in the seventh year, and they vacated Makkah for him for three days, and in that 'umrah he married Maymunah bint al-Harith al-Hilaliyyah.

3136 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abu Zuhayr narrated to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, concerning His saying: "The sacred month for the sacred month and violations of sacred things are subject to retribution": They besieged the Prophet ﷺ in Dhu al-Qa'dah from the Sacred House [[ahsarahu al-marad wa-ghayruhu: it prevented and detained him.]], so Allah caused him to enter the Sacred House the following year, and took retribution for him from them. So He said: "The sacred month for the sacred month and violations of sacred things are subject to retribution."

3137 - al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi', who said: The Prophet of Allah ﷺ and his Companions set out, entering ihram for 'umrah in Dhu al-Qa'dah, with the offering animals with them, until when they reached al-Hudaybiyah the polytheists barred them, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ made peace with them that he return that year and come back the following year, to stay in Makkah three days, not taking out anyone of the people of Makkah with him. They slaughtered the offering at al-Hudaybiyah and shaved and shortened their hair. When the following year came, the Prophet ﷺ and his Companions set out until they entered Makkah, performed 'umrah in Dhu al-Qa'dah, and stayed there three days. The polytheists had boasted over him when they turned him back on the day of al-Hudaybiyah, so Allah granted him retribution against them, and caused him to enter Makkah in that month in Dhu al-Qa'dah in which they had turned him back. Allah, majestic is His praise, said: "The sacred month for the sacred month and violations of sacred things are subject to retribution."

3138 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, His saying: "And violations of sacred things are subject to retribution": they are the polytheists, who had detained Muhammad ﷺ in Dhu al-Qa'dah from the House, and they boasted over him by that, so Allah returned him in Dhu al-Qa'dah, caused him to enter the Sacred House, and took retribution for him from them.

3139 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying: "The sacred month for the sacred month," up to the end of the verse, he said: All of this has been abrogated; He commanded him to fight the polytheists. And he recited: ﴿And fight all the polytheists as they fight you all﴾ [Surah al-Tawbah: 36], and recited: ﴿Fight those of the disbelievers who are near to you﴾ [Surah al-Tawbah: 123], the Arabs. When he finished with them, Allah, majestic is His praise, said: ﴿Fight those who do not believe in Allah or the Last Day and do not forbid what Allah and His Messenger have forbidden﴾ until His saying: ﴿while they are humbled﴾ [Surah al-Tawbah: 29]. He said: They are the Romans. He said: So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent forces against them.

3140 - Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Wahhab al-Thaqafi narrated to us, saying: Ayyub narrated to us, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning this verse: "The sacred month for the sacred month and violations of sacred things are subject to retribution," he said: Allah commanded you to retaliate, [and take] from you transgression [[What is between the brackets is thus in the original. I did not find the report elsewhere. It is an undoubted error, or there is a lacuna between the two statements that I have not discerned. The meaning in any case: Allah commanded you to retaliate, and disliked transgression from you, i.e., He commanded them to retaliate and not to transgress. This is what I consider preferable, God willing.]].

3141 - al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, from Ibn Juraij, who said: I said to 'Ata', and asked him about His saying: "The sacred month for the sacred month and violations of sacred things are subject to retribution." He said: It was revealed concerning al-Hudaybiyah; they were prevented in the sacred month, so it was revealed: "The sacred month for the sacred month": an 'umrah in a sacred month for an 'umrah in a sacred month.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: Allah, majestic is His praise, named Dhu al-Qa'dah "the sacred month" because the Arabs in the Jahiliyyah used to make fighting and killing forbidden in it, lay down weapons in it, and no one would kill another in it, even if a man met the slayer of his father or son. They called it "Dhu al-Qa'dah" because they sat (qu'ud) in it, refraining from raids and wars. So Allah named it by the name by which the Arabs called it.

* *

As for "al-hurumat" (the violations), it is the plural of "hurmah," like "al-zulumat," the plural of "zulmah," and "al-hujurat," the plural of "hujrah." Allah, majestic is His praise, said "violations of sacred things are subject to retribution" in the plural because He meant: the sacred month, the sacred city, and the sanctity of the ihram.

* *

So He, majestic is His praise, said to His Prophet Muhammad and the believers with him: your entering the Sanctuary in this state of ihram, in this sacred month of yours, is retribution for what you were prevented from in the like of it in your past year; and that is the "violations" which Allah made retribution.

* *

We have explained that "qisas" (retribution) is requital by way of action, speech or body, and in this place it is by way of action [[See what has preceded in this volume 3: 357-366.]].

* *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿Whoever transgresses against you, then transgress against him in the same manner as he transgressed against you﴾

Abu Ja'far said: The people of interpretation differed concerning what this saying was revealed about: "Whoever transgresses against you, then transgress against him in the same manner as he transgressed against you."

Some of them said:

3142 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah ibn Salih narrated to me, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying: "Whoever transgresses against you, then transgress against him in the same manner as he transgressed against you." He said: This and its like was revealed in Makkah when the Muslims were few and had no authority to subdue the polytheists, and the polytheists were assailing them with abuse and harm. So Allah commanded the Muslims: whoever among them is to requite, let him requite with the like of what was done to him, or be patient, or pardon, which is better. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ migrated to Madinah and Allah strengthened His authority, He commanded the Muslims to refer their grievances to their authority, and not to transgress against one another as the people of the Jahiliyyah did.

* *

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: whoever among the polytheists fights you, O believers, then fight them as they fought you. They said: This verse was revealed to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in Madinah, after the 'umrah of the settlement.

Those who said so:

3143 - al-Qasim narrated to me, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, who said: Mujahid said: "Whoever transgresses against you, then transgress against him in the same manner as he transgressed against you": fight them in it as they fought you.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The more apt of the two interpretations, by what the apparent sense of the verse indicates, is the one related from Mujahid, because the verses before it are a command from Allah to the believers to fight their enemy in a certain manner, namely His saying: "And fight in the way of Allah those who fight you," and the verses after it, and His saying: "Whoever transgresses against you, then transgress against him," are within the context of the verses containing the command to fight and to wage jihad. Allah, majestic is His praise, only enjoined fighting upon the believers after the migration.

It is thus known that His saying: "Whoever transgresses against you, then transgress against him in the same manner as he transgressed against you" is Madinan, not Meccan, since the obligation of fighting the polytheists had not yet been imposed on the believers in Makkah. And His saying: "Whoever transgresses against you, then transgress against him in the same manner as he transgressed against you" is parallel to His saying: "And fight in the way of Allah those who fight you," and its meaning is: whoever transgresses against you in the Sanctuary and fights you, then retaliate against him by fighting, in the manner of his transgression against you by fighting you, for I have made the violations retribution. Whoever among the polytheists makes lawful against you, O believers, a sanctity in My sanctuary, then make lawful against him the like of it therein.

This verse was abrogated, by Allah's permission, for His Prophet, by fighting the people of the Sanctuary from the outset within the Sanctuary, and by His saying: ﴿And fight all the polytheists as they fight you all﴾ [Surah al-Tawbah: 36].

* *

... [[These dots were inserted, and I separated between his saying: "And fight the polytheists all together" and his saying: "according to what we have mentioned", because of a lacuna beyond doubt. For he will say a few lines later: "And the other: that it means the enemy." He is here dealing with the explanation of His saying: "Whoever transgresses against you, then transgress against him in the same manner as he transgressed against you", from the linguistic aspect. There is no connection between his discussion of whether the verse is abrogated or not. And his saying "and the other" is evidence that he mentions two aspects of explaining "i'tada": whether it is from "'udwan" (transgression) or from "'adw" (enemy). It seems al-Tabari's text at the place of this lacuna was:

[As for His saying: (Whoever transgresses against you, then transgress against him in the same manner as he transgressed against you). In "i'tida'" there are two aspects of interpretation:

One: that "i'tida'" is from "'udwan," which is exceeding the limit by injustice and aggression. The meaning of the verse would be: whoever exceeds his limit unjustly and aggressively, and fights you in the sacred month, then requite him in the same manner as he did to you, in the way we mentioned...]

This is what I have deduced from al-Tabari's tafsir previously at 2: 307, and in this part 3: 375, 376, 564, 573. Then a lacuna remains before that in his discussion of the verse, as to whether it is abrogated or not.]] in the manner we mentioned, that it means requital and following word with word, even though their meanings differ, as He said: ﴿And they schemed, and Allah schemed﴾ [Surah Al 'Imran: 54], and He said: ﴿They mock them, so Allah mocks them﴾ [Surah al-Tawbah: 79], and what is similar to that, where one word follows another and the meanings differ [[See what has preceded at 2: 307, and in this part 3: 375, 376, 564, 573.]].

* *

The other: that it means "'adw," which is attacking and leaping, from the saying of the speaker: "The lion leapt upon its prey." So the meaning of the speech is: whoever leaps upon you – that is, whoever attacks you and leaps – unjustly, then leap upon him – that is, attack him and leap toward him – as retribution for what he did to you, not unjustly. Then a "ta'" is inserted into "'ada," so it is said "i'tada" in place of "'ada," as one says "iqtaraba hadha al-amr" meaning "qaruba," and "ijtalaba kadhalika" meaning "jalaba," and what is similar to that.

* *

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And fear Allah, and know that Allah is with the righteous﴾ (194)

Abu Ja'far said: By this, majestic is His praise, means: fear Allah, O believers, regarding His sanctities and limits, that you not transgress in them, exceeding what He has made clear and set as limits for you; and know that Allah loves the righteous, who fear Him by performing His obligations and avoiding His prohibitions.

The discussion on the interpretation of His, the Exalted, words: ﴿And spend in the way of God, and do not cast yourselves with your own hands into destruction, and do good; indeed God loves the good-doers﴾ (2:195)

Abu Ja'far said: The interpreters (ahl al-ta'wil) differed about the interpretation of this verse, and about whom His words "and do not cast yourselves with your own hands into destruction" refer to.

Some of them said: It refers to His words "and spend in the way of God." The "way of God" (sabil Allah) [see the explanation of "sabil Allah" above, 2:497, and in this part, 3:564] is His path, which He commanded to be followed against His enemies among the polytheists, for striving (jihad) against them and warring with them. "And do not cast yourselves..." means: do not abandon spending in the way of God, for God will compensate you for it with a reward and provide for you in this world. [Footnote: So it is in the printed edition, "ajran" (a reward). I fear it may be a distortion of "ajilan" (in this world), so that the context runs consistently in its proper direction, and that is what I prefer.]

Those who said this:

3144: Abu al-Sa'ib Salm ibn Junada and al-Hasan ibn Arafa told me, saying: Abu Mu'awiya narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Sufyan, from Hudhayfa, regarding "and do not cast yourselves with your own hands into destruction," he said: It means in abandoning spending.

3145: Muhammad ibn Bashshar told me, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Shu'ba narrated to us. And Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Adi narrated to us, from Shu'ba, from al-A'mash, from Abu Wa'il, from Hudhayfa. And Muhammad ibn Khalaf al-Asqalani told me, saying: Adam narrated to us, saying: Abu Ja'far al-Razi narrated to us, from al-A'mash. And Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Asim. All of them, from Shaqiq, from Hudhayfa, who said: It is abandoning spending in the way of God.

3146: Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'ba narrated to us, from Mansur, from Abu Salih, from Abd Allah ibn Abbas, that he said regarding this verse, "and do not cast yourselves with your own hands into destruction": "Spend in the way of God, even if you have only a mishqas (the iron blade of an arrow when it is long and not broad) or an arrow." Shu'ba is the one who was doubtful about this.

3147: Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Adi narrated to us, from Shu'ba, from Mansur, from Abu Salih, whom al-Kalbi used to narrate from, from Ibn Abbas, who said: If you have only an arrow or a mishqas, spend it.

3148: Ibn Bashshar told me, saying: Yahya narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Abu Salih, from Ibn Abbas: "and do not cast yourselves with your own hands into destruction." He said: It is in spending.

3149: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us, from Amr ibn Abi Qays, from Ata', from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas: "and do not cast yourselves with your own hands into destruction." He said: Destruction is not that a man be killed in the way of God, but rather withholding spending in the way of God.

3150: Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim told me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid informed us, from Ikrima, who said: It was revealed concerning expenditures in the way of God, meaning His words "and do not cast yourselves with your own hands into destruction."

3151: Yunus ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Wahb narrated to us, saying: Abu Sakhr informed me, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, that he used to say regarding this verse, "and do not cast yourselves with your own hands into destruction": The people were in the way of God, and a man would take provisions, and one of them had better provisions than the other. The needy one spent from his provisions until nothing of his provisions remained, and wished to console his companion, so God revealed: "And spend in the way of God and do not cast yourselves with your own hands into destruction."

3152: Muhammad ibn Khalaf al-Asqalani told me, saying: Adam narrated to us, saying: Shayban narrated to us, from Mansur ibn al-Mu'tamir, from Abu Salih, the client of Umm Hani, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words "and do not cast yourselves with your own hands into destruction": None of you should say, "I do not find anything." If he finds only a mishqas, let him equip himself with it in the way of God.

3153: Ibn Abd al-A'la al-San'ani narrated to us, saying: al-Mu'tamir narrated to us, saying: I heard Dawud, that is, Ibn Abi Hind, from Amir: that some of the Ansar had been short of provisions, and they had spent considerable expenditures. He said: Their opinion grew bad (sa'a zannuhum) [i.e., evil suspicions overcame them and they doubted], and they withheld. He said: So God revealed: "And spend in the way of God and do not cast yourselves with your own hands into destruction." He said: And the destruction was their bad opinion and their withholding. [Footnote: His words "sa'a zannuhum" mean that evil and ugly suspicions overtook them, and they doubted. The Arabs use "sa'a zannuhu" in many contexts to express different meanings, and I have explained that in the journal al-Risala, issue 910 (20 Safar 1370 AH, December 1950), and in Tabaqat Fuhul al-Shu'ara', p. 510, note 1.]

3154: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us. And al-Muthanna told me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us. [Both] from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding God's words "and do not cast yourselves with your own hands into destruction," he said: It prevents you from spending on a right out of fear of poverty. [Footnote: A man becomes 'a'il (poor) and his poverty is 'aila; in the Book of God: "And He found you poor (a'ilan) and enriched you" (93:8). The 'a'il is the poor, the one in need.]

3155: Bishr ibn Mu'adh told me, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His words "And spend in the way of God and do not cast yourselves with your own hands into destruction." He said: Qatada used to narrate that al-Hasan had narrated to him that they used to travel and raid, and not spend from their wealth, or he said: and not spend during that. So God commanded them to spend on their raids in the way of God.

3156: al-Hasan ibn Yahya told me, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada, regarding His words "and do not cast yourselves with your own hands into destruction": He says: do not hold back your hands from spending in the way of God.

3157: Musa ibn Harun told me, saying: Amr ibn Hammad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "And spend in the way of God" = spend in the way of God even if it is only an 'iqal (a rope with which a camel is tied, i.e., bound at its foreleg together with its forearm so that it cannot move) "and do not cast yourselves with your own hands into destruction": You say, "I have nothing."

3158: al-Muthanna told me, saying: Abu Ghassan narrated to us, saying: Zuhayr narrated to us, saying: Khusayf narrated to us, from Ikrima, regarding His words "and do not cast yourselves with your own hands into destruction." He said: When God commanded spending, some of them, or most of them, said: "We spend and our wealth is lost, and nothing remains for us!" He said: So He said: "Spend and do not cast yourselves with your own hands into destruction." He said: Spend, and I will provide for you.

3159: al-Muthanna told me, saying: Amr ibn Awn narrated to us, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, from Yunus, from al-Hasan, who said: It was revealed concerning spending.

3160: al-Muthanna told me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Ibn Hammam al-Ahwazi informed us, saying: Yunus informed us, from al-Hasan, regarding "destruction": God commanded them to spend in the way of God, and informed them that abandoning spending in the way of God is destruction.

3161: al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj told me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: I asked Ata' about His words "And spend in the way of God and do not cast yourselves with your own hands into destruction." He said: He says: Spend in the way of God, whether little or much. He said: And Abd Allah ibn Kathir said to me: It was revealed concerning spending in the way of God.

3162: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mansur, from Abu Salih, from Ibn Abbas, who said: A man should not say, "I do not find anything! I am ruined!" Let him equip himself, even with a mishqas.

3163: Muhammad ibn Sa'd told me, saying: My father told me, saying: My paternal uncle told me, saying: My father told me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding his words: "And spend in the way of God and do not cast yourselves with your own hands into destruction." He says: Spend whatever there is, of little or much. And do not submit (la tastaslimu) nor spend anything, lest you be destroyed.

3164: al-Muthanna told me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abu Zuhayr narrated to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, who said: "Destruction" is that a man withholds himself and his wealth from spending in striving (jihad) in the way of God.

3165: Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Wahid ibn Ziyad narrated to us, from Yunus, from al-Hasan, regarding His words "and do not cast yourselves with your own hands into destruction": that is, leaving off spending in the way of God.

* *

Others said, among those who directed the interpretation of this to mean spending: The meaning is: "And spend in the way of God, and do not cast yourselves with your own hands into destruction," by going out in the way of God without expense or strength.

Those who said this:

3166: Yunus told me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words "And spend in the way of God and do not cast yourselves with your own hands into destruction": If you do not have anything to spend, do not go out yourself without expense or strength, so that you cast your hands into destruction.

* *

Others said: Rather, its meaning is: "Spend in the way of God, and do not cast your hands" (by way of sins you have committed) "into destruction, so that you despair of God's mercy. But hope for His mercy and do good deeds."

Those who said this:

3167: Muhammad ibn Ubayd al-Muharibi told me, saying: Abu al-Ahwas narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Bara' ibn Azib regarding His words "and do not cast yourselves with your own hands into destruction." He said: It is the man who commits sins and so casts his hand into destruction, saying: "There is no repentance for me."

3168: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash narrated to us, saying: Abu Ishaq narrated to us, from al-Bara', who said: A man asked him: "Shall I charge the polytheists alone, and they kill me? Would I have cast my hand into destruction?" He said: No. Destruction is only in spending. God sent His Messenger, and He said: ﴿So fight in the way of God; you are not charged except with yourself﴾ (Surah al-Nisa' 4:84).

3169: al-Hasan ibn Arafa and Ibn Wakī' told me, both saying: Waki' ibn al-Jarrah narrated to us, from Sufyan al-Thawri, from Abu Ishaq al-Sabi'i, from al-Bara' ibn Azib, regarding God's words "and do not cast yourselves with your own hands into destruction." He said: It is the man who commits a sin and says, "God will not forgive him."

3170: Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Isra'il narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, who said: I heard al-Bara', and a man asked him, saying: "O Abu Umara, what do you think of God's words 'and do not cast yourselves with your own hands into destruction'? Is it the man who advances and fights until he is killed?" He said: No, but it is the man who does sinful deeds, then casts his hand (into destruction) and does not repent.

3171: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, who said: I heard al-Bara', and a man asked him, saying: "A man charges a troop alone and fights. Is he among those who cast their hand into destruction?" He said: No, but destruction is that a man commits a sin and then casts his hand, saying: "No repentance will be accepted for me."

3172: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us, from al-Jarrah, from Abu Ishaq, who said: I said to al-Bara' ibn Azib: "O Abu Umara, a man meets a thousand of the enemy and charges them, while he is alone. Would he be among those of whom God said: 'and do not cast yourselves with your own hands into destruction'?" He said: No, "so that he fights until he is killed!" God said to His Prophet ﷺ: ﴿So fight in the way of God; you are not charged except with yourself﴾.

3173: Mujahid ibn Musa told me, saying: Yazid informed us, saying: Hisham informed us. And Ya'qub told me, saying: Ibn Ulayya narrated to us, from Hisham, from Muhammad, who said: I asked Ubayda about God's words "And spend in the way of God and do not cast yourselves with your own hands into destruction," the verse. Ubayda said: A man would commit a sin, (I think he said: a great one), and so he would cast his hand and be destroyed. Ya'qub added in his narration: So they were forbidden from that, and it was said: "Spend in the way of God and do not cast your hands into destruction."

3174: Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim told me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Hisham informed us, from Ibn Sirin, who said: I asked Ubayda al-Salmani about that, and he said: It is the man who commits a sin and then submits, and casts his hand into destruction, saying: "There is no repentance for him!" meaning His words: "and do not cast yourselves with your own hands into destruction."

3175: Ya'qub told me, saying: Ibn Ulayya narrated to us, saying: Ayyub informed us, from Muhammad, from Ubayda, regarding His words "and do not cast yourselves with your own hands into destruction." He said: A man would commit a sin and so cast his hand.

3176: Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Ibn Awn, from Ibn Sirin, from Ubayda: "and do not cast yourselves with your own hands into destruction." He said: It is despair (al-qunut).

3177: al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Amr ibn Awn narrated to us, saying: Hushaym informed us, from Yunus and Hisham, from Ibn Sirin, from Ubayda al-Salmani, who said: It is the man who commits a sin and submits, saying: "There is no repentance for me!" and so casts his hand.

3178: al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, saying: Ayyub narrated to me, from Ibn Sirin, from Ubayda, that he said: It concerns the man who commits a great sin, casts his hand, and thinks that he has perished.

* *

Others said: Rather, the meaning is: "And spend in the way of God, and do not abandon striving (jihad) in His way."

Those who said this:

3179: Yunus told me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Haywa informed me, from Yazid ibn Abi Habib, from Aslam Abu Imran, who said: We raided Constantinople (al-Qustantiniyya), and over the people of Egypt was Uqba ibn Amir, and over the main body was Abd al-Rahman ibn Khalid ibn al-Walid. He said: We drew up two lines, and I had never seen two lines more extended or longer than them, while the Romans had their backs pressed against the wall of the city. He said: A man from among us charged the enemy, and people said: "Mah! There is no god but God! He casts his hand into destruction!" Abu Ayyub al-Ansari said: You interpret this verse in this way? It was revealed concerning us, the group of the Ansar! When God gave victory to His Prophet and made Islam prevail, we said among ourselves, the group of the Ansar, secretly from the Messenger of God ﷺ: "We had left our families and our wealth to stay and tend them until God gave victory to His Prophet. Come, let us stay in our wealth and tend it!" So God sent down the report from heaven: "And spend in the way of God and do not cast yourselves with your own hands into destruction," the verse. So casting oneself by one's hands into destruction is: to remain in our wealth and tend to it, and to leave off striving. Aslam Abu Imran said: Abu Ayyub never ceased striving in the way of God until he was buried in Constantinople. [Footnote: Hadith 3179: Haywa is Ibn Shurayh. Aslam Abu Imran: the Tahdhib (of Ibn Hajar) attributes him as "Aslam ibn Yazid," a reliable Successor (tabi'i), who was a notable in Egypt, and a client of Tujib. The takhrij of this hadith will come in the following narration.]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 195 (part 2 of 2):

3180 – Muhammad ibn ʿUmara al-Asadi and ʿAbd Allah ibn Abi Ziyad related to me, both saying: Abu ʿAbd al-Rahman ʿAbd Allah ibn Yazid related to us, who said: Haywa and Ibn Lahiʿa informed me, both saying: Yazid ibn Abi Habib related to us, who said: Aslam Abu ʿImran, mawla of Tujib, related to me, who said: We were at Constantinople, and over the people of Egypt was ʿUqba ibn ʿAmir al-Juhani, companion of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and over the people of Syria was Fadala ibn ʿUbayd, companion of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). A great line of the Romans came out from the city, and we lined up a great line of the Muslims. A man from the Muslims charged at the line of the Romans until he entered among them, then came back out toward us. The people cried out and said: "Subhan Allah! He has thrown himself into destruction with his own hands!" Abu Ayyub al-Ansari, companion of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), stood up and said: "O people, you interpret this verse in this way! This verse was only revealed about us, the company of the Ansar! When Allah made His religion mighty and multiplied its helpers, we said among ourselves, secretly from the Messenger of Allah: 'Our wealth has been lost, so if we were to stay with it and repair what was lost of it!' So Allah revealed in His Book, refuting what we had intended, saying: ﴿And spend in the way of Allah and do not throw yourselves with your own hands into destruction﴾, meaning by staying to dwell on the wealth and repair it. So He commanded us to fight." Abu Ayyub continued to fight in the way of Allah until Allah took him.

[[Hadith 3180 – Abu ʿAbd al-Rahman ʿAbd Allah ibn Yazid al-Muqri: a reliable and well-known narrator, among the teachers of Ahmad and al-Bukhari. He was an imam in hadith, renowned in the readings (qira'at), and taught the Qur'an in Basra for 36 years, then in Mecca for 35 years. He was a mawla of the family of ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab. Ibn Hazm made a strange error concerning him, a curious slip: he made him an Arab of Himyar, then of "Banu Sabiʿ"! Then he attributed him to a clan he claimed was named "Muqar", with the mim vowelled and the qaf unvowelled! He said in Jamharat al-Ansab, p. 409: "Among the descendants of the aforementioned Sabiʿ: Muqar, a large clan, to which ʿAbd Allah ibn Yazid al-Muqri (meaning without a hamza) is attributed; he was not a reciter of the readings but a transmitter of hadith!" Ibn Hazm erred and was confused, bringing a tribe no one has mentioned at all, as far as we know. His attention had shifted to something else far off: "ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn ʿAbd al-Qari" with the yaʾ doubled and without hamza, from the descendants of "al-Qara ibn al-Dish". He was a Tabiʿi and was not a reciter. It is to this that his error went. Then we do not know how he placed the invented tribe among "Banu Sabiʿ"!!
What appears in the printed edition here is "thana Abu ʿAbd al-Rahman ʿan ʿAbd Allah ibn Yazid", which is an error in the addition of "ʿan". "Abu ʿAbd al-Rahman" is the kunya of "ʿAbd Allah ibn Yazid", not another narrator.
The hadith was related by Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi in his Musnad: 599, from ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Mubarak, from Haywa.
It was related by Abu Dawud al-Sijistani: 2512, through Ibn Wahb, from Haywa and Ibn Lahiʿa.
It was related by al-Tirmidhi 4: 72-73, through Abu ʿAsim al-Nabil, from Haywa, and he said: "A hasan gharib sahih hadith."
It was related by al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak 2: 275, through ʿAbd Allah ibn Yazid al-Muqri, from Haywa alone, and he said: "This hadith is sahih according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs, though they did not record it." al-Dhahabi agreed with him.
Ibn ʿAbd al-Hakam related it in Futuh Misr: 269-270, by two chains: he related it from ʿAbd Allah ibn Salih, from al-Layth ibn Saʿd, and he related it from ʿAbd Allah ibn Yazid al-Muqri, from Haywa ibn Shurayh; both from Yazid ibn Abi Habib, with it.
As for his words in the previous narration, "We raided Medina, meaning Constantinople" – this is how it stands in the printed edition here. The wording of Abu Dawud al-Sijistani is: "We raided from Medina, desiring Constantinople." Perhaps what is here is more accurate and sounder, for Aslam Abu ʿImran was Egyptian. The apparent context indicates that the army was from Egypt and Syria.
His words in that narration: "And over the body was ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Khalid ibn al-Walid" indicate that this raid was in the year 46 or before it, because ʿAbd al-Rahman died that year. This raid is other than the famous raid in which Abu Ayyub al-Ansari died. Yazid ibn Muʿawiya raided it after that in the year 49, with groups of the noble Companions. Then Yazid raided it in the year 52, and it was in that raid that Abu Ayyub, may Allah be pleased with him, died; he had bequeathed to Yazid that, when he died, they should carry him and enter him into the land of the enemy and bury him beneath their feet where they meet the enemy. Yazid did what Abu Ayyub had bequeathed. His grave there is known to this day. See Tabaqat Ibn Saʿd 3/2/49-50, Tarikh al-Tabari 6: 128, 130, Tarikh Ibn Kathir 8: 30-31, 32, 58-59, and Tarikh al-Islam of al-Dhahabi 2: 231, 327-328.
His words in this second narration: "And over the people of Syria was Fadala ibn ʿUbayd" – this is the correct reading established in the narrations of al-Tayalisi, Ibn ʿAbd al-Hakam and al-Hakim. In the narration of al-Tirmidhi occurs: "And over the body was Fadala ibn ʿUbayd." This is an error, perhaps from al-Tirmidhi or from his teacher ʿAbd ibn Humayd.
The hadith was mentioned by Ibn Kathir 1: 437-438, from the narration of al-Layth ibn Saʿd, without attributing it. Then he took it out from Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i, ʿAbd ibn Humayd in his tafsir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Mardawayh, Abu Yaʿla, Ibn Hibban and al-Hakim. Then he mentioned a narration of it, as the wording of Abu Dawud – but it does not match his wording, and in it there is much distortion.
al-Suyuti mentioned it 1: 207-208, and added its attribution to al-Tabarani and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan.]]
* * *
Abu Jaʿfar said: The correct view on this matter, in my opinion, is to say: Allah, mighty is His praise, commanded spending in His way by His saying: "And spend in the way of Allah." His way (sabil) is His path which He legislated for His servants and made clear to them. The meaning is: spend in exalting My religion which I have legislated for you, by striving against your enemy who set against you war upon disbelief in Me. And He forbade them to throw their hands into destruction, saying: "and do not throw your own hands into destruction."
* * *
This is a metaphor. The Arabs say of one who submits to a matter: "So-and-so gave with his hands" (aʿta bi-yadayhi), and likewise said of one who gives himself up to what is demanded of him: "He gave with his hands."
* * *
So the meaning of His saying "and do not throw your own hands into destruction" is: do not submit to destruction, so that you give it your reins and perish.
One who withholds spending in Allah's way when it is obligatory upon him submits to destruction by abandoning the performance of the obligation Allah has placed on his wealth. This is because Allah, mighty is His praise, made one of the eight categories of obligatory charity "in His way", saying: ﴿Alms are only for the poor and the needy﴾ to His saying: ﴿and in the way of Allah and the wayfarer﴾ [Surah al-Tawba: 60]. So whoever withholds spending what is due from him in Allah's way, as is due upon him, has submitted to destruction and thrown his hands into destruction.
Likewise the one who despairs of Allah's mercy because of a sin that has passed from him throws his hands into destruction, since Allah has forbidden that, saying: ﴿And do not despair of Allah's mercy; surely none despairs of Allah's mercy except the disbelieving people﴾ [Surah Yusuf: 87].
Likewise the one who abandons raiding and fighting the polytheists, when that is obligatory upon him and when the Muslims need him, neglects an obligation and throws his hand into destruction.
Since all these meanings are borne by His saying "and do not throw your own hands into destruction", and Allah, mighty and majestic, did not specify any one of them over the others, the correct view is to say: Allah forbade us from casting our hands into what brings about our ruin, and from submitting to destruction – which is punishment – by abandoning what He has made obligatory upon us of His duties. It is therefore not permissible for any of us to enter into something Allah dislikes from us, by which we would merit His punishment through entering it.
However, although this is so, the more prevalent interpretation of the verse is: "And spend, O believers, in the way of Allah, and do not abandon spending in it, lest you perish, by deserving – through your abandonment of that – My punishment," as:
3181 – al-Muthanna related to me, who said: Abu Salih related to us, who said: Muʿawiya related to us, from ʿAli ibn Abi Talha, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His saying: "and do not throw your own hands into destruction": he said: "destruction" is the punishment of Allah.
* * *
Abu Jaʿfar said: So this is an informing from Him to them – after His command to them to spend – of what the one who abandons the obligatory spending in His way will suffer of punishment in the Hereafter.
* * *
If someone says: What is the purpose of introducing the "bi" (with) in His saying "and do not throw your hands", when you know that the common usage of the Arabs is "I threw to so-and-so a dirham" and not "I threw to so-and-so with a dirham"?
It is said: It has been said that it is an added particle, like the adding by the speaker of the "ba'" in his saying "I pulled with the garment, and I pulled the garment," and "I clung to it and I clung it," and ﴿grows with the oil﴾ [Surah al-Mu'minun: 20], when it is really: "grows the oil" [[See al-Insaf of Ibn al-Anbari: 128.]].
* * *
Others said: The "ba'" in His saying "and do not throw your hands" is the origin of the kinaya (pronominal substitution), because every transitive verb that is substituted for is in need of it, as in your saying about a man "I spoke to him", when you wish to refer to his action by substitution; when you wish that, you say "I did with him" (fa'altu bihi). They said: Since the "ba'" is the origin, it is permissible to include and exclude the "ba'" in every verb whose path is the path of its kinaya.
* * *
As for "al-tahlukah" (destruction), it is the form "tafʿula" from "al-halak" (perishing).

**The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿And do good; surely Allah loves the good-doers﴾**

Abu Jaʿfar said: By His saying "and do good", mighty is His praise, He means: do good, O believers, in performing what I have obliged you to of My duties, and in avoiding what I have commanded you to avoid of My acts of disobedience, and in spending in My way, and in the stronger among you returning to the weak who is in need (dhu al-khalla) [[Dhu al-khalla: the needy and poor one, the one whose condition is disturbed by poverty or weakness.]], for indeed I love the good-doers in that [[See what has passed concerning the meaning of "ihsan" in 2: 292.]], as:
3182 – al-Muthanna related to me, who said: Ishaq related to us, who said: Zayd ibn al-Hubab related to us, who said: Sufyan informed us, from Abu Ishaq, from a man of the Companions, regarding His saying: "and do good; surely Allah loves the good-doers": he said: "performing the obligations."
* * *
Some said: its meaning is: think well of Allah.
Those who said that:
3183 – al-Muthanna related to me, who said: Ishaq related to us, who said: Hafs ibn ʿUmar related to us, from al-Hakam ibn Aban, from ʿIkrima: "and do good; surely Allah loves the good-doers": he said: "Think well of Allah; He will be good to you."
* * *
Others said: do good by returning to the one in need.
Those who said that:
3184 – Yunus related to me, who said: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying: "and do good; surely Allah loves the good-doers": "Return to one who has nothing in his hand."
* * *
In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 2, verse 196 (part 1 of 7)**

The discussion of the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And complete the Hajj and the 'Umrah for Allah﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: The scholars of interpretation (ta'wil) differed regarding the interpretation of this.

* *

Some of them said: The meaning of that is: complete the Hajj with its rites (manasik) and its sunan (the recommended practices), and complete the 'Umrah with its limits and its sunan.

Mention of those who said that:

3185 - Ubayd ibn Isma'il al-Habbari narrated to me, saying: Abdullah ibn Numayr narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, from Alqamah: "And complete the Hajj and the 'Umrah for Allah." He said: It is in the recitation of Abdullah (ibn Mas'ud): "وَأَقِيمُوا الْحَجَّ وَالْعُمْرَةَ إِلَى الْبَيْتِ" (And establish the Hajj and the 'Umrah to the House). He said: Do not go beyond the House with the 'Umrah. Ibrahim said: I mentioned that to Sa'id ibn Jubayr, and he said: Thus Ibn Abbas said.

3186 - Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, that he recited: "And establish the Hajj and the 'Umrah to the House."

3187 - Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, from Alqamah, that he recited: "And establish the Hajj and the 'Umrah to the House."

3188 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn Abbas: "And complete the Hajj and the 'Umrah for Allah," meaning: Whoever enters ihram for Hajj or for 'Umrah, it is not permitted for him to exit (the state of ihram) until he completes it. The completion of the Hajj is on the Day of Sacrifice, when he throws the Jamrat al-'Aqabah and visits the House; then he has exited his ihram entirely. The completion of the 'Umrah is when he circumambulates the House and (performs the sa'y) between al-Safa and al-Marwah; then he has exited (the ihram).

3189 - Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words: "And complete the Hajj and the 'Umrah for Allah," he said: (It means) what they were commanded regarding them.

3190 - It was related to me from Ammar ibn al-Hasan, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi', (his) saying: "And complete the Hajj and the 'Umrah for Allah." He said: Alqamah ibn Qays said: "The Hajj" means the rites of the Hajj, and "the 'Umrah" means: he does not go beyond the House with it.

3191 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mansur, from Ibrahim: "And complete the Hajj and the 'Umrah for Allah." He said: The rites of the Hajj are fulfilled at 'Arafah and Muzdalifah and their stations, and the 'Umrah (is fulfilled) by going to the House, circumambulating the House and (performing the sa'y) between al-Safa and al-Marwah, and then exiting (the ihram).

* *

Others said: Their completion is that you enter ihram for both separately (mufridin) from the dwelling of your family.[[Al-duwayrah is the diminutive of "al-dar" (the house/home): it is every place where a people has settled, so it is their dar. Note: the numbering here has omitted number 3192, and I was unable to change the entire numbering, so I left it as it is.]]

Mention of those who said that:

3193 - Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Amr ibn Murrah, from Abdullah ibn Salamah, from Ali, that he said: A man came to Ali and said to him, concerning this verse: "And complete the Hajj and the 'Umrah for Allah": (it means) that you enter ihram from the dwelling of your family.

3194 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Harun ibn al-Mughirah narrated to us, from Anbasah, from Shu'bah, from Amr ibn Murrah, from Abdullah ibn Salamah, who said: A man came to Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, and said: Tell me about the saying of Allah, mighty and majestic: "And complete the Hajj and the 'Umrah for Allah"? He said: That you enter ihram from the dwelling of your family.

3195 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Muhammad ibn Suqah, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: Among the completion of the 'Umrah is that you enter ihram from the dwelling of your family.

3196 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Thawr ibn Yazid, from Sulayman ibn Musa, from Tawus, who said: Their completion is to single them out (ifrad) as (acts) begun (mu'tanafatayn) from your family.[[Iti'naf al-shay' means: to take a thing from its beginning and start it. It means: singling them out from the start of your entering into them. See the report that follows it and the comment on it.]]

3197 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Thawr, from Sulayman ibn Musa, from Tawus: "And complete the Hajj and the 'Umrah for Allah." He said: That you single them out as (acts) timed (muwaqqatatayn) from your family; that is their completion.[[Thus it came in this report "muwaqqatatayn," from timing (tawqit), which is determination; and the miqat is the appointed time for an act, or the place. It is said: this is the miqat of the people of Syria or Egypt, for the place from which they enter ihram. It means that its miqat is from the dwelling of one's family.]]

* *

Others said: The completion of the 'Umrah is that you perform it outside the months of Hajj,[[This is as it stands in the original: "an ta'mal" (that you act), and perhaps the correct reading is "an ta'tamir" (that you perform 'Umrah).]] and the completion of the Hajj is that its rites are all performed, so that the one who does it is not obligated to pay a sacrifice (dam) because of qiran or tamattu'.

Mention of those who said that:

3198 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding his words: "And complete the Hajj and the 'Umrah for Allah," he said: And the completion of the 'Umrah is what is performed outside the months of Hajj.
As for one who performs it during the months of Hajj and then stays until he performs Hajj, it is tamattu'; for him in it is the hady (sacrificial animal) if he finds it, and otherwise he fasts three days during Hajj and seven when he returns.[[In the printed edition: "wa-ma kana fi ashhur al-hajj" (and what was in the months of Hajj), and the correct reading is what I have written.]]

3199 - Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding his words: "And complete the Hajj and the 'Umrah for Allah," he said: What is performed outside the months of Hajj is a complete 'Umrah, and what is performed in the months of Hajj is tamattu', and upon him is the hady.

3200 - Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, from Ibn Awn, who said: I heard al-Qasim ibn Muhammad say: Indeed the 'Umrah performed in the months of Hajj is not complete. It was said to him: (What about) the 'Umrah in Muharram? He said: They used to consider it complete.

* *

Others said: Their completion is that you go out from your family intending nothing but them (both).

Mention of those who said that:

3201 - al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: A man narrated to me, from Sufyan, who said: He means by their completion that you go out from your family intending nothing but the Hajj and the 'Umrah, and you enter ihram from the miqat. (You do) not (go out) for trade or for a need. Then, when you are near Makkah, you say: "If only I had performed Hajj or 'Umrah." That suffices, but the completion is that you go out for it and do not go out for anything else.

* *

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: complete the Hajj and the 'Umrah for Allah when you have entered into them.

Mention of those who said that:

3202 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: The 'Umrah is not obligatory upon anyone among mankind. I said to him: (What about) the saying of Allah, exalted is He: "And complete the Hajj and the 'Umrah for Allah"? He said: There is no one among the creation who, when he has entered upon a matter, ought not to complete it. So when he has entered into it, it is not fitting for him to enter ihram for a day or two and then return, just as if he fasted a day, it would not be fitting for him to break his fast at midday.

* *

Al-Sha'bi used to recite that in the nominative (raf').

3203 - Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, from Shu'bah, who said: Sa'id ibn Abi Burdah narrated to me that al-Sha'bi and Abu Burdah discussed the 'Umrah. Al-Sha'bi said: It is a voluntary act (tatawwu')... "And complete the Hajj and the 'Umrah for Allah." Abu Burdah said: It is obligatory: "And complete the Hajj and the 'Umrah for Allah."

3204 - Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Ibn Awn narrated to us, from al-Sha'bi, that he used to recite: "And complete the Hajj and the 'Umrah(u) for Allah" (with 'Umrah in the nominative).

* *

Something contrary to this opinion has been narrated from al-Sha'bi, although what is well known from him is this view. That is:

3205 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: al-Hajjaj ibn al-Minhal narrated to us, saying: Abu Awanah narrated to us, from al-Mughirah, from al-Sha'bi, who said: The 'Umrah is obligatory.

* *

The reading of the one who says the 'Umrah is obligatory has the accusative (nasb) on it, meaning: establish the obligation (fard) of the Hajj and the 'Umrah(a) as well, as in:

3206 - Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far informed us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, saying: I heard Abu Ishaq say: I heard Masruq say: You have been commanded in the Book of Allah with four: establishing the prayer, giving the zakah, the Hajj, and the 'Umrah. He said: Then he recited this verse: "And due to Allah from the people is Hajj to the House" (Surah Al 'Imran, 97), and "And complete the Hajj and the 'Umrah(a) for Allah to the House."

3207 - Abu al-Sa'ib narrated to me, saying: Ibn Idris narrated to us, saying: I heard Layth narrating from al-Hasan, from Masruq, who said: We were commanded to establish four: the prayer and the zakah, and the 'Umrah and the Hajj. So the 'Umrah was placed in relation to the Hajj as the zakah is placed in relation to the prayer.

3208 - Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Bakr informed us, saying: Ibn Juraij narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Husayn and Sa'id ibn Jubayr were asked, "Is the 'Umrah obligatory upon the people?" Both of them said: We know of it only as obligatory, as Allah said: "And complete the Hajj and the 'Umrah for Allah."

3209 - Sawwar ibn Abd Allah narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Qattan narrated to us, from Abd al-Malik ibn Abi Sulayman, who said: A man asked Sa'id ibn Jubayr: Is the 'Umrah an obligation or a voluntary act? He said: An obligation. He said: Al-Sha'bi says it is voluntary. He said: Al-Sha'bi lied, and he recited: "And complete the Hajj and the 'Umrah for Allah."[[His words "kadhaba al-Sha'bi" mean: he erred. This is very common in reports, hadiths and Arabic poetry, in the sense of error, not in the sense of falsehood, which is the opposite of truth. It means: al-Sha'bi erred in his independent reasoning (ijtihad).]]

3210 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, from one who heard Ata' say regarding His words: "And complete the Hajj and the 'Umrah(a) for Allah," he said: Both are obligatory: the Hajj and the 'Umrah.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The interpretation of these scholars regarding His words, blessed and exalted is He: "And complete the Hajj and the 'Umrah(a) for Allah," is that both are obligatory duties (fardan wajibani), which Allah, blessed and exalted, commanded to establish, just as He commanded the establishment of the prayer, and that they are two obligations, and that He made the 'Umrah obligatory just as the Hajj is obligatory.[[In the printed edition: "fi anna-huma" with an extra "fi," which is an error; then it reads "qaradan wajibani min Allah," and what I have written is correct.]] They are a large number of the Companions and the Successors, and those who came after them of the successors of successors.[[It is said: one people succeeded another, and one authority succeeded another, they succeed (yakhlufuna) with succession (khalfan). So they are khalifun. You say: I am his successor (khalifuhu) and I succeeded him (khalaftuhu): that is, I came after him.]] We disliked lengthening the book by mentioning them and the reports from them.

And they said: The meaning of His words, "And complete the Hajj and the 'Umrah for Allah," is: "And establish the Hajj and the 'Umrah."

Mention of some of those who said that:

3211 - Musa ibn Harun narrated to us, saying: Amr ibn Hammad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His words: "And complete the Hajj and the 'Umrah for Allah," he said: That is: establish the Hajj and the 'Umrah.

3212 - Ahmad ibn Hazim narrated to us, saying: Abu Nu'aym narrated to us, saying: Isra'il narrated to us, from Thuwayr, from his father, from Ali: "And establish the Hajj and the 'Umrah to the House," then it is obligatory like the Hajj.[[The report: 3212 - Ahmad ibn Hazim ibn Muhammad ibn Yunus ibn Qays ibn Abi Gharzah al-Ghifari, the teacher of al-Tabari: his narrations have passed (earlier) in 44 and 164. Ibn Abi Hatim recorded his biography (1/1/48) and mentioned that he wrote to him. Thawbar ibn Abi Fakhitah (the name here given as Thuwayr): very weak. Al-Bukhari recorded in al-Kabir (1/2/183) and al-Saghir (128), from al-Thawri, who said: "Thuwayr was one of the pillars of lying." (It is with a diminutive form of the letter thaa with a dot above, i.e., Thuwayr.) His father, Abu Fakhitah: his name is Sa'id ibn Alaqah; he was a client (mawla) of Umm Hani bint Abi Talib. He is a trustworthy Successor who narrated from Ali, from Ibn Mas'ud, and others.]]

3213 - Ahmad ibn Hazim narrated to us, saying: Abu Nu'aym narrated to us, saying: Isra'il narrated to us, saying: Thuwayr narrated to us, from his father, from Abdullah: "And establish the Hajj and the 'Umrah to the House." Then Abdullah said: By Allah, were it not for the scruple (tahrruj), and that I did not hear from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ anything regarding it, I would have said that the 'Umrah is obligatory like the Hajj.[[The report: 3213 - It has the same meaning as the one before it, with the same chain. It adds attributing a recitation to Ibn Mas'ud, which is one of the irregular recitations (qira'at shadhdhah) that contradict the orthography of the Mushaf. It was narrated by al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan al-Kubra (4:351), through Abd Allah ibn Raja', from Isra'il, with it. The chain of the report is weak, as we explained just above.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: It seems that by His words, "Establish the Hajj and the 'Umrah," they meant: bring them about with their limits and their rulings, as they were prescribed for you.

* *

Others said, from among those who recited with the accusative for "the 'Umrah" in the manner of these people: The 'Umrah is a voluntary act (tatawwu'). They saw that there is no proof of its obligation in their reading "the 'Umrah" with the accusative, since among the acts is that which may become binding upon the servant to perform and complete by entering into it, even though entering into it at the outset was not obligatory for him. This is like the voluntary Hajj, about which there is no disagreement among all of them that if one enters ihram for it, then he must continue with it and complete it, though entering into it at the outset was not obligatory for him. They said: Likewise the 'Umrah is not an obligation whose entry is obligatory from the start, except that whoever enters into it and makes it binding upon himself must complete it after entering into it. They said: Therefore, in the command of Allah to complete the Hajj and the 'Umrah there is no proof of the obligation of their being fard. They said: We made the Hajj obligatory only by His saying, mighty and majestic: "And due to Allah from the people is the Hajj to the House, for whoever is able to find a way to it" (Surah Al 'Imran, 97).

Among those who said that were a group of the Companions, the Successors, and those who came after them of the successors of successors.

Mention of those who said that:

3214 - Abu Kurayb and Abu al-Sa'ib narrated to us, both saying: Ibn Idris narrated to us, saying: I heard Sa'id ibn Abi Arubah, from Abu Ma'shar, from Ibrahim, who said: Abdullah said: The Hajj is an obligation, and the 'Umrah is voluntary.

3215 - Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Arubah, from Abu Ma'shar, from al-Nakha'i, from Ibn Mas'ud, the like of it.

3216 - Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Ibn Uthmah narrated to us, saying: Sa'id ibn Bashir narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: The 'Umrah is not obligatory.

3217 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mughirah, from Simak, who said: I asked Ibrahim about the 'Umrah, and he said: A good sunnah.

3218 - Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, from Mughirah, from Ibrahim, the like of it.
