3219 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, saying: Abu Awanah narrated to us, from al-Mughirah, from Ibrahim, the like of it.

3220 - Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-Mughirah, from Ibrahim, the like of it.

3221 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: al-Hajjaj narrated to us, saying: Hammad narrated to us, saying: Abd Allah ibn Awn narrated to us, from al-Sha'bi, who said: The 'Umrah is voluntary.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: As for those who recited that with the nominative for "the 'Umrah," they said: There is no basis for its accusative, for the 'Umrah is only the visiting of the House, and no one deserves the title of one who performs 'Umrah unless he has visited it. They said: And when one does not deserve the title of one performing 'Umrah except by visiting it, and when he arrives there, circumambulates it, and (performs the sa'y) between al-Safa and al-Marwah, then no act remains after that for which he is commanded to complete it afterward, just as the one performing Hajj is commanded to complete it after reaching it, circumambulating it, and (performing the sa'y) between al-Safa and al-Marwah, by going to 'Arafah and Muzdalifah, standing at the places where he was commanded to stand, and performing the remaining acts of the Hajj which are part of its completion after reaching the House. Thus there is no clear meaning in the saying of one who says to the one performing 'Umrah: "Complete your 'Umrah." And since it has no clear meaning, the correct reading of "the 'Umrah" is the nominative, on the basis that it is among the acts of righteousness for Allah, so it is nominative by its predicate that follows it, which is His saying: "for Allah."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The more correct of the two readings in our view is the reading of the one who recited "the 'Umrah" in the accusative, as a conjunction with "the Hajj," meaning the command to complete both for Him.

There is no validity to the argument of those who objected to its nominative reading on the grounds that "the 'Umrah" is the visiting of the House, since the one performing 'Umrah, when he arrives, has no remaining act for which he is commanded to complete. That is because when he reaches the House, his visit has ended, and what remains upon him is completing the act that Allah commanded him in his 'Umrah, namely his visit to the House, which is circumambulating the House, performing the sa'y between al-Safa and al-Marwah, and avoiding what Allah has commanded him to avoid until he completes that. That is an act which, although it is among what has become binding upon him by making the visit obligatory upon himself, is other than the visit. Moreover, there is consensus of the authorities (ijma' al-hujjah) upon reading "the 'Umrah" in the accusative, and the reading of all the readers of the metropolitan cities (qurra' al-amsar) disagrees with the reading of one who recites it in the nominative. In that, there is sufficient reason to dispense with argumentation regarding the error of the one who recited it in the nominative.

* *

The better of the two opinions we have mentioned concerning the interpretation of His words ﴿and complete the ʿumrah for Allah﴾, on the reading of those who read it in the accusative, is the view of ʿAbd Allah ibn Masʿud and of those who share his view, that the meaning is: complete the Hajj (pilgrimage) and the ʿumrah (lesser pilgrimage) for Allah to the House after you have made them obligatory on yourselves. It is not that this verse is a command from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, to begin their performance, to enter into them, and to perform them in full.

This is because the verse can bear both meanings we have described: that it is a command from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, to establish them from the outset, making their observance an obligation on His servants, and that it is a command from Him to complete them after one has entered into them, and after the one who makes them obligatory has made them obligatory on himself. Since the verse can bear both meanings we have described, there is no proof in it for either party against the other, except that the other party has an equal claim to it. Since this is so, and since there is no clear report from the Prophet's (ﷺ) explicit statement establishing the obligation of ʿumrah as decisive evidence, and since the community has disagreed about its obligation, the statement of one who says "it is an obligatory duty" has no weight without a proof that confirms the soundness of his claim, since obligatory duties do not bind the servants except by clear evidence that they are binding upon them.

If someone supposes that it is obligatory in the manner of the Hajj, and that the interpretation of those who interpret His words ﴿and complete the Hajj and the ʿumrah for Allah﴾ to mean "establish their limits and their obligations" is preferable to our interpretation, [then we say, supported by what follows]:

3222 - Hatim ibn Bukayr al-Dabbi narrated to me, saying: Ashhal ibn Hatim al-Arṭabā'i narrated to us, saying: Ibn ʿAwn narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Jahadah, from a man, from a colleague of his, from his father, and his father was known as Abu al-Muntafiq. He said: I came to the Prophet (ﷺ) at ʿArafah, and I drew near to him until the necks of my mount and his mount touched. I said: "O Messenger of Allah, inform me of a deed that will save me from the punishment of Allah and admit me to His Paradise!" He said: "Worship Allah and do not associate anything with Him, establish the prescribed prayer, pay the obligatory zakah, and perform the Hajj and the ʿumrah." Ashhal said: "And I think he said: and fast Ramadan. And consider what you would like people to do to you, and do that to them; and what you dislike people doing to you, leave them alone in it."

[[Hadith 3222: This isnad is weak, because of the ambiguity of some of its narrators, who were not named.

Hatim ibn Bukayr al-Dabbi, the teacher of al-Tabari: he is also one of the teachers of Ibn Majah and Ibn Khuzaymah. He is listed in al-Tahdhib and al-Khulasah without an explanation of his condition. In al-Taqrib he is described as "acceptable" (maqbul). The name of his father is confirmed as "Bukayr" (diminutive) here and in al-Khulasah. "Bakr" (without diminutive) is confirmed in al-Tahdhib and al-Khulasah, but I have not found it in any other source, so I cannot weigh between them.

Ashhal (with a shin marked with a dot) ibn Hatim, Abu Hatim al-Basri al-Jumahi: his reliability is disputed. Ibn Maʿin declared him weak. Abu Zurʿah said: "His standing is truthfulness, but he is not strong. I saw him attributing to Ibn ʿAwn a hadith which people stop at the companion's statement." Al-Bukhari included him in al-Kabir (1/2/69) and mentioned no criticism of him. Moreover, al-Bukhari narrated from him in the Sahih one connected hadith and one suspended hadith. (Muqaddimat al-Fath, p. 389.)

As for his nisbah here, "al-Arṭabā'i," I do not know what it is, and I do not know any explanation for it, unless he was among those who narrated most often from his teacher Ibn ʿAwn, whose full name is ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAwn ibn Arṭabān, with a nun at the end, and so he was attributed to "Arṭabān" for that reason, and then "al-Arṭabāni" was distorted to "al-Arṭabā'i." But I have found nothing that proves this, nor anything indicating that he narrated much from Ibn ʿAwn; it is merely a guess I have made.

Muhammad ibn Jahadah: his biography has already passed (no. 34).

Abu al-Muntafiq (also said to be Ibn al-Muntafiq): Ibn al-Athir included him in Usd al-Ghabah (5:306) and narrated this hadith with its isnad through Muʿadh ibn Muʿadh, from Ibn ʿAwn, with this isnad. In it appears "Ibn ʿAwf," which is a clear printing error.

Al-Hafiz (Ibn Hajar) included him in al-Isabah (7:181) and mentioned this hadith from the narration of al-Tabarani, but in it is "Muhammad ibn Jahadah, from a colleague of his," with the omission of "from a man" between them.

Ibn Abi Hatim included him (4/2/327) under the name "Ibn al-Muntafiq," thus: "that he described the Prophet's (ﷺ) description, as narrated by Muhammad ibn Jahadah, from al-Mughirah ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Yashkuri, from his father, from him."

The hadith was also mentioned by al-Haythami in Majmaʿ al-Zawaid (1:43-44) through another route, not this one. He said: "And from Hujayr, from his father, who was known as Abu al-Muntafiq," and he mentioned something similar, in which, as here, is "and perform the ʿumrah." He had mentioned before that (1:43), from two other routes, in which this wording does not appear.

Al-Hafiz said in al-Isabah, after pointing to al-Tabarani's narration through Ibn ʿAwn: "Al-Tabarani said: Ibn ʿAwn was confused in its isnad, and did not preserve it from Muhammad ibn Jahadah, but Hammam preserved it." Then he took it out through Hammam's route, from Muhammad ibn Jahadah, from al-Mughirah ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Yashkuri, from his father, who said: "I came to Kufah, and I entered the mosque, and there was a man from Qays called Ibn al-Muntafiq. I heard him say..." This is the narration which the author of al-Zawaid first mentioned.

The routes of this hadith are of several kinds, among them Hammam's narration which al-Hafiz mentioned, in al-Musnad 15948-15950 (3:472-473, Halabi edition), and 16774 (4:76-77, Halabi), and (5:372-373, and 6:383-384, Halabi). I did not find in these narrations of al-Musnad any mention of the ʿumrah.]]

And:

3223 - Yaʿqub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi and Muhammad ibn Abi ʿAdi narrated to us, from Shuʿbah, from al-Nuʿman ibn Salim, from ʿAmr ibn Aws, from Abu Razin al-ʿUqayli, a man of the Banu ʿAmir, who said: "I said: O Messenger of Allah, my father is a very old man who cannot perform the Hajj, nor the ʿumrah, nor travel, and Islam has reached him. Shall I perform the Hajj on his behalf?" He said: "Perform the Hajj on behalf of your father and the ʿumrah."

[[Hadith 3223: Yaʿqub ibn Ibrahim: he is al-Dawraqi the hafiz, who has passed in nos. 237 and 335. He narrates from ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi. In the printed edition, between them appears an addition, "qala khadathana Ibn Ibrahim" (he said: Ibn Ibrahim narrated to us), which is an erroneous addition from a copyist or printer, and has no meaning, so we have removed it.

Al-Nuʿman ibn Salim al-Taʾifi: reliable; Ibn Maʿin and others declared him reliable, and Muslim narrated from him in the Sahih.

ʿAmr ibn Aws ibn Abi Aws al-Thaqafi al-Taʾifi: a reliable Follower (tabiʿi). The compilers of the six books narrated from him.

Abu Razin al-ʿUqayli: he is Luqayt ibn ʿAmir ibn al-Muntafiq ibn ʿAmir, and he is a well-known Companion. Whoever considered him and "Luqayt ibn Subrah ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Muntafiq" to be one person has erred; rather, they are two Companions, and Ibn Saʿd distinguished between them (5:379, 340).

This hadith is sound, contrary to what al-Tabari said a few lines later, when he weakened all these hadiths, including this one.

It was narrated by al-Tayalisi (1091) from Shuʿbah. Ahmad narrated it in al-Musnad (16253) from Waki', from Shuʿbah, with this isnad (4:10-12, Halabi). Abu Dawud narrated it (1810) from Hafs ibn ʿUmar and Muslim ibn Ibrahim, both from Shuʿbah. Al-Mundhiri said (1736): "It was narrated by al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah. al-Tirmidhi said: hasan sahih. Imam Ahmad said: I know of no hadith on the obligation of ʿumrah that is better than this, nor more sound than it." Al-Bayhaqi narrated it (4:350) through Abu Dawud's route, then narrated Ahmad ibn Hanbal's statement on its authentication.]]

= And:

3224 - Yaʿqub narrated to me with it, saying: Ibn ʿUlayyah narrated to us, from Ayyub, from Abu Qilabah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) delivered a sermon and said: "Worship Allah and do not associate anything with Him; establish the prayer, pay the zakah, perform the Hajj and the ʿumrah, and be upright, and you will be made upright."

[[Hadith 3224: Abu Qilabah, with a kasra on the qaf and a light lam, is ʿAbd Allah ibn Zayd al-Jarmi, one of the great scholars, from among the Followers.]]

* *

And similar reports. These are reports by which no proof in religion is established, because their isnads are weak; and besides the weakness of their isnads, the reports have forms which indicate that ʿumrah is a voluntary act, not an obligatory duty. Among them is:

3225 - Muhammad ibn Humayd and Muhammad ibn ʿIsa al-Damghani narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, from al-Hajjaj ibn Artah, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Jabir ibn ʿAbd Allah, from the Prophet (ﷺ): that he was asked about ʿumrah, "Is it obligatory?" He said: "No, but if you perform it, it is better for you."

[[Hadith 3225: Muhammad ibn ʿIsa al-Damghani, the teacher of al-Tabari: Abu Hatim narrated from him and said: "His hadith is written down." al-Nasa'i also narrated from him, and Ibn Khuzaymah, and others.

The hadith was narrated by Ahmad (14449, 3:316, Halabi), from Ibn Muʿawiyah, from al-Hajjaj ibn Artah, with this isnad, similar to it.

It was narrated by al-Tirmidhi (2:113) through ʿUmar ibn ʿAli, and by al-Bayhaqi (4:349) through ʿAbd al-Wahid ibn Ziyad, both from al-Hajjaj, similar to it.

al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a hasan sahih hadith." Al-Bayhaqi concluded that what is preserved is its narration as a mawquf report, from Jabir's own statement. al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar extended his discussion in al-Talkhis (p. 204) on the defect of the marfuʿ form and the preference for the mawquf form.]]

3226 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us; and Yahya ibn Talhah al-Yarbuʿi narrated to me, saying: Sharik narrated to us, from Muʿawiyah ibn Ishaq, from Abu Salih al-Hanafi, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The Hajj is jihad, and the ʿumrah is a voluntary act."

[[Hadith 3226: Sharik: he is Ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Nakhaʿi, whose biography has passed (no. 2527).

Muʿawiyah ibn Ishaq ibn Talhah ibn ʿUbayd Allah al-Taymi: a reliable Follower.

Abu Salih al-Hanafi: he is ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Qays al-Kufi, and he is a reliable Follower. Some erred in naming him "Mahan," but the correct kunyah of "Mahan" is "Abu Salim al-Hanafi." See both biographies in al-Tahdhib. Although al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar verified this in both places in al-Tahdhib, he erred in al-Talkhis (p. 204), saying: "Abu Salih is not Dhakwan al-Sammān; rather he is Abu Salih Mahan al-Hanafi"!

This hadith is mursal. al-Shafiʿi narrated it in al-Umm (2:113), saying: "The people differed concerning ʿumrah. Some of the Easterners said: ʿumrah is voluntary. Saʿid ibn Salim (he is al-Qaddah, the teacher of al-Shafiʿi) said, and argued that Sufyan al-Thawri informed him, from Muʿawiyah ibn Ishaq, from Abu Salih al-Hanafi, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'The Hajj is jihad, and the ʿumrah is voluntary.' I said to him: 'Do you confirm such a thing from the Prophet (ﷺ)?' He said: 'It is munqati' (disconnected).' Then al-Shafiʿi proceeded to establish the proof against it—that ʿumrah is obligatory..." and so on to the end of what he said.

Al-Bayhaqi narrated this mursal hadith (4:348) through al-Shafiʿi's route, then quoted from him some of what I have quoted.]]

* *

Abu Jaʿfar (al-Tabari) said: Some people of dullness have claimed that it has been confirmed to them that ʿumrah is obligatory, because they found no voluntary act without an obligatory counterpart. So when it is established that ʿumrah is voluntary, it must be that it has an obligatory form, because the obligatory act is the counterpart of the voluntary act in all deeds.

It is said to the one who says this: The fasting of i'tikaf (seclusion in the mosque) has been made voluntary; so what is its obligatory form which is its counterpart?

Then he is asked: Is i'tikaf obligatory or not obligatory?

If he says, "It is obligatory," he has left the position of the whole community.

And if he says, "It is voluntary,"

it is said: What is it that requires i'tikaf to be voluntary while ʿumrah is obligatory, in a manner that must be accepted?

He will not say anything about one of them except that he is bound to say the same about the other.

* *

= And by what we have cited as evidence, the better of the two readings regarding "ʿumrah" is the reading of the one who reads it in the accusative; and the better of the two interpretations of His words ﴿and complete the Hajj and the ʿumrah for Allah﴾ is the interpretation of Ibn ʿAbbas that we have mentioned from him, through the narration of ʿAli ibn Abi Talhah from him, that it is a command from Allah to complete their acts after entering into them, and to make them obligatory as commanded concerning their limits and their sunnahs. And the better of the two views regarding "ʿumrah" is the view of the one who says, "It is voluntary, not obligatory." The meaning of the verse is: "Complete, O believers, the Hajj and the ʿumrah for Allah, after entering into them and making them obligatory upon yourselves, in accordance with what Allah has commanded you regarding their limits."

* *

Allah, Blessed and Exalted, sent down this verse to His Prophet (ﷺ), peace be upon him, concerning the ʿumrah of al-Hudaybiyah, in which he was prevented from the House. It informed the believers of what was incumbent upon them in their state of consecration if they were allowed to reach the House, and explained to them what would release them from their state of consecration if they were consecrated and were prevented from the House.

And for the mention of what is required of them in their ʿumrah which they performed in the year of al-Hudaybiyah, and what would be required of them thereafter in their ʿumrah and Hajj, He opened with His words: ﴿They ask you about the crescent moons. Say: they are times set for people, and for the Hajj.﴾ [[In the printed edition: "wa bidhikr al-lazim" (and by mention of what is required), but the correct reading seems to be what I have adopted, so that the sentence is sound.]]

We have already shown the meanings of "Hajj" and "ʿumrah" by evidence earlier, and we disliked lengthening the book by repeating it. [[See what has passed: 3: 228-229.]]

* *

Concerning the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿But if you are prevented, then [offer] what is feasible of the sacrificial animal﴾

Abu Jaʿfar said: The people of interpretation differed concerning the "ihsar" (being prevented) for which Allah prescribed what is feasible of the offering for the one who is afflicted with it in his Hajj and ʿumrah.

* *

Some of them said: It is every obstacle or restrainer that prevents the consecrated one and holds him back from the act which Allah obligated upon him in his state of consecration, and from reaching the Sacred House.

Mention of those who said this:

3227 - Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, that he used to say: "Al-ḥaṣr is the entire restraint." He says: "Whatever man is blocked on his Hajj or ʿumrah, he sends his offering from where he is held back." He said: And Mujahid said concerning His words, "But if you are prevented": if you are prevented: a man falls ill or is injured, or something holds him back and overpowers him, whatever it is; then let him send what is feasible of the offering, and let him not shave his head, nor exit the state of consecration, until the day of sacrifice.

3228 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.

3229 - al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Abu Nuʿaym narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from ʿAta', who said: "Ihsar is everything that holds him back."

3230 - And Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, from Saʿid, from Qatadah, that he said concerning the one who is prevented: it is fear, sickness, and the restrainer. If that happens to him, he sends his offering, and when the offering reaches its place, he exits the state of consecration.

3231 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, from Saʿid, from Qatadah, concerning His words, "But if you are prevented, then [offer] what is feasible of the offering": he said: this is a man who is afflicted by fear or sickness or a restrainer who holds him back from the House; he sends his offering, and when it reaches its place, he becomes free from the state of consecration.

3232 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abu Muʿawiyah narrated to us, from Hisham ibn ʿUrwah, from his father, who said: "Everything that holds back the consecrated one is ihsar."

3233 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Suwayd narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Ibrahim— Abu Jaʿfar said: I think it is from Sharik, from Ibrahim ibn al-Muhajir, from Ibrahim— concerning "But if you are prevented": sickness, injury, or fear.

3234 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Muʿawiyah narrated to me, from ʿAli, from Ibn ʿAbbas, concerning His words, "But if you are prevented, then [offer] what is feasible of the offering," he says: whoever enters the state of consecration for Hajj or ʿumrah, then is held back from the House by a sickness that overwhelms him or an excuse that restrains him, upon him is its making up (qada').

* *

Abu Jaʿfar said: The reason for those who held this view is that "ihsar," in the language of the Arabs, means the restraint of illness and the like, not compulsion and overpowering by a compeller or an overpowering one; except the overpowering of an illness, such as sickness, a bite, a wound, the loss of provisions, or the breaking of a mount. As for the prevention by an enemy, the imprisonment of one who restrains someone in jail, or the overpowering of an overpowerer who stands between the consecrated one and reaching the House, whether by a ruler or by a compelling, restraining person, then the Arabs call that "ḥaṣr," not "iḥṣār."

They said: And what shows this is the saying of Allah, exalted is His praise: ﴿And We made Hell a confinement (ḥaṣīr) for the disbelievers﴾ [al-Isra' 17:8], meaning: a confiner, that is, a restrainer.

They said: If the restraint by a compelling, overpowering enemy, other than the causes we have described, were called "iḥṣār," it would be necessary to say, "the enemy has been ahsara" (prevented).

They said: And in the agreement of the Arabic dialects on "ḥūṣira al-ʿaduww (the enemy was besieged) and al-ʿaduww muḥāṣar (the enemy is besieged)," rather than "ahṣara al-ʿaduww" and "hum muḥṣarūn," and "uḥṣira al-rajul" by illness or fear, there is the greatest indication that Allah, exalted is His praise, intended by His words, "But if you are prevented," [being prevented] by sickness, fear, or a restraining illness.

They said: We have taken the prevention of the enemy from restraining the one in ihram (the state of ritual consecration) from reaching the House to fall under the meaning of "the being besieged by illness" (*ihsar al-marad*), by analogy with what God, may His praise be exalted, made for the sick person whom illness prevented from reaching the House. It is not by the apparent indication of His words: ﴿But if you are besieged, then (send) what offering is feasible﴾, since the restraint of an enemy, or of a ruler or a dominant force, is a preventing cause, parallel to the preventing cause of illness and injury.

* *

Others said: The meaning of His words ﴿But if you are besieged, then (send) what offering is feasible﴾ is: if an enemy restrains you from reaching the House, or a dominant restrainer from among the sons of Adam does. They said: As for the conditions that afflict the body, such as illness, wounds and what is similar to them, these are not included in His words ﴿if you are besieged﴾.

Mention of those who said this:

3235 - Muhammad ibn Amr related to us, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid and Ata', from Ibn Abbas that he said: "Al-hasr (besieging)" is the besieging by an enemy. A man sends his offering, and if he cannot reach the House because of the enemy, and he finds someone who will convey it to Makkah on his behalf, then he sends it and enters the state of ihram – Muhammad ibn Amr said, Abu Asim said: we do not know whether he said "yuhrim" (enters ihram) or "yahill" (leaves ihram) – from a day on which he arranges with the owner of the offering when he buys it. When he is safe, it is incumbent on him to perform hajj or 'umrah. If illness afflicts him and holds him back, and he has no offering with him, then he leaves the state of ihram where he is held back. If he has an offering with him, he does not leave ihram until the offering reaches its place of sacrifice. When he sends it, he is not obliged to perform hajj or 'umrah the following year unless he wishes.

3236 - It was related to me on the authority of Abu Ubayd al-Qasim ibn Salam, saying: Yahya ibn Sa'id related to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Ibn Tawus, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, who said: There is no besieging except by the restraint of an enemy.

3237 - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah related to us, saying: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid and Ata', from Ibn Abbas, like the report of Muhammad ibn Amr from Abu Asim, except that he said: "then he sends it and enters ihram from the day on which he arranged with the owner of the offering when he bought it." Then he mentioned the rest of the report like the report of Muhammad ibn Amr from Abu Asim.

* *

Malik ibn Anas said: It has reached me that the Messenger of God ﷺ and his Companions left ihram at al-Hudaybiyah. They sacrificed the offerings, shaved their heads, and became free of everything, before they circumambulated the House and before the offering reached it. Then we do not know that the Messenger of God ﷺ ordered any of his Companions, or any of those who were with him, to make up anything or to repeat anything. [[The text of Malik's words in the Muwatta' (Malik's compiled collection of hadith and law): 360; it will come below under no. 3287.]]

3238 - Yunus related to me this, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us from him, saying: Malik was asked about the one who is besieged by an enemy and is prevented from reaching the House. He said: He leaves ihram from everything, sacrifices his offering, and shaves his head where he is held back, and there is no making up for it, [[Up to here is the text in the Muwatta': 360; what follows is an addition not found there. It will come at the end of no. 3288.]] except that if he has never performed hajj, then it is incumbent on him to perform the Hajj of Islam (the obligatory pilgrimage).

He said: Our position regarding the one who is besieged without an enemy, by illness or what is similar to it, is that he is treated with what is necessary and makes a ransom (fidyah), [[In the printed edition: "an yabda' bima la budda minhu" (that he begin with what is necessary); the correct reading is what I have recorded, from the Muwatta': 362, so consult it there. See also what will come under no. 3289.]] then he makes it an 'umrah, and performs hajj the following year and offers a sacrifice.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The reason for those who held this view, meaning those who said Malik's position, is that this verse was revealed concerning the besieging of the Messenger of God ﷺ and his Companions by the polytheists from the House, so God commanded His Prophet and those with him to sacrifice their offerings and leave ihram.

They said: God revealed this verse only concerning the besieging by an enemy, so its ruling may not be diverted to other than the meaning for which it was revealed.

They said: As for the sick man, if his illness prevents him from travelling until he misses 'Arafah, then he is simply a man who has missed hajj, and he must come out of his ihram by what one who has missed hajj comes out by. He is not in the meaning of the "muhsar" (one besieged) concerning whom this verse was revealed.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of the two interpretations regarding His words ﴿But if you are besieged﴾ is the interpretation of those who understood it to mean: if the fear of an enemy, or illness, or an ailment prevents you from reaching the House, that is, your fear or your illness makes you besiege yourselves, so you hold yourselves back from proceeding because of what you have made obligatory upon yourselves of the act of hajj and 'umrah. Hence it is said ﴿you are besieged﴾, when the fear and the illness are omitted. It is said of this: "My fear of so-and-so prevented me from meeting you, and my illness (prevented me) from so-and-so," meaning: it made me hold myself back from that. But when the restrainer is a man or a person, it is said: "So-and-so restrained me from meeting you," meaning he held me back from it.

Had the meaning of the verse been what the one who interpreted it thought, from His words ﴿if you are besieged﴾: if a restrainer from the enemy holds you back from reaching the House, then it would have had to be: ﴿if you are restrained﴾ (uhsirtum, passive form).

What clarifies the soundness of what we have said, that the verse's interpretation intends the besieging by other than the enemy, and that it means only the fear of the enemy, is His words: ﴿So when you are secure, then whoever enjoys (tamattu') by 'umrah until hajj...﴾

Security (al-amn) comes only with the removal of fear. Since that is so, it is known that the besieging God intends in this verse is the fear whose removal brings security.

Since that is so, the restraint of a restrainer, with which there is no fear for one's life from his restraint, does not fall within the ruling of the verse by its recited apparent meaning. Although we consider its ruling to be joined to his by way of analogy, because the restraint of one from whose restraint there is no fear for one's life, such as a ruler whose punishment is not feared, a parent, or a woman's husband, [[In the printed edition: "wa-in kana..." (and if...); the correct reading omits the waw.]] if any of them or some of them holds him back and prevents him from setting out for the work of hajj, or from reaching the House after the one prevented has become obliged to enter ihram, [[His words "not included" are the predicate of his words "because the restraint of one from whose restraint there is no fear for one's life".]] this is not included in the apparent meaning of His words ﴿So when you are besieged﴾, for what we have described, that its meaning is: if the fear of an enemy besieges you, as evidenced by His words ﴿So when you are secure, then whoever enjoys by 'umrah until hajj﴾. Ibn Abbas's report mentioned just above has clarified that he said: "Al-hasr (besieging) is the besieging by an enemy."

Since that is the more correct of the two interpretations of the verse, as we have described, and since it was a prevention from reaching the House, then every impediment that befalls the one in ihram and turns him away from reaching the House has a counterpart to it in ruling.

* *

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 196 (part 4 of 7):

3283 - Al-Rabi' related to us, saying: Ibn Wahb related to us, saying: Usamah related to me, from Nafi', from Ibn Umar, that he used to say: "What is easy of the offering" — a cow.

3284 - And al-Rabi' related to us, saying: Ibn Wahb related to us, saying: Usamah ibn Zayd related to me that Sa'id related to him, saying: I saw Ibn Umar, and people of Yemen came to him, asking him about "what is easy of the offering," and they said: "A sheep! A sheep!" He would reply to them: "A sheep! A sheep!" — urging them — "except that a camel is not a substitute for a camel, nor a cow for a cow, but what is 'easy of the offering' is a cow."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The more correct of the two opinions is the view of the one who said: "What is easy of the offering" is a sheep. This is because Allah, mighty and majestic is He, only obligated "what is easy of the offering," and that applies to whatever is easy for the one making an offering to offer, whatever that thing may be. Unless Allah, mighty and majestic is He, has specified something from that, in which case what is specified is excluded from the whole that the apparent revelation admits, and all other things are sufficient when the one making the offering gives them, provided they deserve the name "offering" (hady).

* *

If someone says: Those who refuse that a sheep is among "what is easy of the offering" argue that it does not deserve the name "offering," just as if he offered a hen or an egg, he would not be considered to have made a valid offering.

It is said in reply: If a hen and an egg differed in the same way that a sheep differs (regarding the offering), their case would be one: each of them would have fulfilled what is incumbent upon him by the apparent revelation, if neither of the two offerings would exclude its giver from being one who fulfills — by offering what he offered of that — what Allah obligated upon him in his being prevented. [[In the printed edition: "if neither of the two offerers excludes him..." and the correct reading is what is established.]] But since the offering excluded what is less than a jadha' of sheep, and a thaniyy of goats, camels and cattle and above in age — from being an offering that fulfills what Allah obligated upon him in his being prevented or in his tamattu' — by a decisive proof and a clear excuse, transmitted from our Prophet (ﷺ) by inheritance, that was excluded from being intended by His words "what is easy of the offering," even though it is among what is easy for us of the offerings.

And since there was disagreement about a jadha' of sheep and a thaniyy of goats, it was sufficient as an offering from the one making it, by the apparent revelation, because it is among what is easy of the offering.

* *

If someone says: What is the grammatical position of "mā" in His words, "fa-mā istaysara mina al-hady"? It is said: it is in the nominative case (raf').

If he says: Governed by what?

It is said: By an omitted element, which is "fa-'alayhi" (then upon him). This is because the meaning of the sentence is: "And complete the Hajj and the 'Umrah, O believers, for Allah. But if something prevents you from completing it, an enemy, an illness, or an injury, then upon you — for your release, if you wish to be released from your state of ihram — is what is easy of the offering."

We chose the nominative because most of the Qur'an comes with the nominative in its parallels, such as His words: ﴿So whoever among you is ill or has an ailment of his head, then a ransom of fasting﴾ and His words: ﴿So whoever does not find [the means], then a fast of three days﴾, and other similar examples, which would take long to enumerate in the book; we have left mentioning them, being content with what we mentioned.

And if it were said that the position of "mā" is accusative, in the sense of: "If you are prevented, then offer what is easy of the offering," the one who said it would not be wrong.
[[See the Ma'ani al-Qur'an of al-Farra' 1: 118.]]

* *

As for "al-hady," it is a plural, and its singular is "hadyah," by analogy with "jadyat al-sarj" (the saddle's pommel), and its plural is "al-jadi," lightened.
[["Hadyah" and "jadyah" with the yā' doubled; the editor of Majaz al-Qur'an of Abu 'Ubaydah vocalized it as fatḥah then sukūn, which is an error. The jadyah is a stuffed piece of cloth placed beneath the two pommels of the saddle and the pommel of the riding saddle; these are two jadiyyatān.]]

3285 - It is related from Abu 'Ubaydah Ma'mar ibn al-Muthanna, from Yunus, who said: Abu 'Amr ibn al-'Ala' used to say: "I do not know of a letter in speech resembling it."
[[Majaz al-Qur'an of Abu 'Ubaydah: 69.]]

* *

With the lightening of the yā' and the sukūn of the dāl in "al-hady," the readers in every region recited it, except what is reported from al-A'raj, for:

3286 - Abu Hisham al-Rifa'i related to us, saying: Ya'qub related to us, from Bashshar, from Asad, from al-A'raj, that he recited: ﴿hadyan bāligha al-Ka'bah﴾ [Surah al-Ma'idah: 95] with a kasrah on the dāl, doubled, and he recited: "until the offering reaches its place" with a kasrah on the dāl, doubled. It is differently reported from 'Asim: it is reported that he agreed with al-A'raj and disagreed with him, and his reading agreed with the rest of the readers.

* *

In my view, the "hady" was only named "hady" because its giver draws near to Allah, mighty and majestic is He, by it, in the manner of the gift which a man gives to another, drawing near to him by it. It is said of it: "I gave the offering to the House of Allah, so I give it as an offering (ahdi)." Just as it is said of a gift which a man gives to another: "I gave a gift to so-and-so, and I give it." A camel is also called "hadiyyah," and from it is the saying of Zuhayr ibn Abi Sulma, describing a man who was taken captive, likening him in his sanctity to the camel that is offered:

"I have not seen a folk who took captive an offering... nor have I seen a neighbour of the House who is violated!"
[[From his Diwan: 79, from a noble poem, composed to blame Banu 'Ulaym ibn Jinab of Kalb. A man from Banu 'Abd Allah ibn Ghatafan had come to them; they honoured him and treated his protection well, but he was addicted to gambling, and they forbade him, yet he refused except to gamble. He gambled once and they returned his stakes, then gambled a second time and they returned them, then gambled a third time and they did not return them, and his wife was taken in his gambling debt. The "hady" is a man of sanctity who seeks protection with the people, and they named him as al-Tabari said, because of what he offers to the House; he is not to be repulsed from the House nor harmed. His words "fa-yustabā'" mean his wife is seized and taken in marriage. Then after the House he said to them: "The neighbour of the House and the man who calls out in the assembly before the tribe, their pledge is equal." And the "munadi" is one who sits in the assembly; as for the houses of the tribe...]]

* *

The discussion on the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And do not shave your heads until the offering reaches its place﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By this, mighty and majestic is He means: If you are prevented, and you wish to be released from your ihram, then upon you is what is easy of the offering. And do not release yourselves from your ihram when you are prevented, until the offering — which Allah, mighty and majestic is He, has obligated upon you for your release from the ihram in which you were prevented, before its completion and the end of its rites and rituals — reaches its place.
[[Ibn Kathir said in his Tafsir 1: 446: "And His words, 'And do not shave your heads until the offering reaches its place,' are conjoined with His words, 'And complete the Hajj and the 'Umrah for Allah,' and are not conjoined with His words, 'But if you are prevented, then what is easy of the offering,' as Ibn Jarir (may Allah have mercy on him) claimed. For the Prophet (ﷺ) and his companions in the year of al-Hudaybiyyah, when the disbelievers of Quraysh prevented them from entering the Sacred Precinct, shaved their heads and slaughtered their offerings outside the Haram. But in a state of safety and access to the Haram, shaving is not permitted, 'until the offering reaches its place,' and the pilgrim finishes the acts of Hajj and 'Umrah — even if he is a qarin — or the act of one of them, if he is a mufrid or mutamatti', as is established in the two Sahihs from Hafsah, who said: 'O Messenger of Allah, what is the matter with the people? They released themselves from the 'Umrah, and you have not released yourself from your 'Umrah!' He said: 'I have locked my hair and garlanded my offering, so I will not release myself until I slaughter.'"
As for Ibn Kathir's criticism of Abu Ja'far, there is scrutiny and detail which is not the place for this, as it would be lengthy.]] This is because shaving the head is a release from the ihram which the one in ihram had obligated upon himself. So Allah forbade him from releasing himself from his ihram by shaving, [[al-hallaq is a verbal noun like al-halq and al-tahallaq; it is said: a head of good al-hallaq (with a kasrah on the ḥā'). Malik made frequent use of this verbal noun in the Muwatta' (see: 395, 396).]] until the offering — which Allah, mighty and majestic is He, permitted for him to release himself by offering — reaches its place.

* *

Then the scholars differed about the "place" (mahall) of the offering that Allah, exalted is His name, meant, which, when it reaches its place, the one prevented is permitted release from his ihram in which he was prevented.

Some of them said: The place of the offering of the one prevented, by which he is released and permitted to shave his head when it reaches it, is — if his being prevented is by fear of an enemy who blocked its slaughter, if it is something to be slaughtered, or its sacrifice if it is something to be sacrificed — in the Hill, slaughtered or sacrificed, or in the Haram [where he was detained]. [[The parenthetical addition is necessary for the sentence to be sound.]] And if it is without fear of an enemy, he is not released until he circumambulates the House and runs between al-Safa and al-Marwah. This is the view of those who say: prevention means prevention by an enemy and nothing else.

Mention of those who said that:

3287 - Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Malik ibn Anas informed me that it reached him that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his companions were released at al-Hudaybiyyah; they slaughtered the offering, shaved their heads, and released themselves from everything before circumambulating the House, and before the offering reached it. Then we do not know that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) commanded any of his companions, nor any of those who were with him, to make up anything, nor to return to anything. [[The report 3287 has passed on p. 24, without a chain.]]

3288 - Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Malik informed me, from Nafi': that Abdullah ibn Umar went out to Makkah for 'Umrah during the strife, and said: "If I am turned away from the House, we will do as we did with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)." So he assumed ihram for 'Umrah, because the Prophet had assumed ihram for 'Umrah in the year of al-Hudaybiyyah. Then Abdullah ibn Umar considered his matter and said: "The two rulings are only one." He turned to his companions and said: "The two rulings are only one; I call you to witness that I have made the Hajj obligatory together with the 'Umrah." He then performed one circumambulation, and considered that it sufficed for him, and offered an offering.
Yunus said: Ibn Wahb said: Malik said: "And this is the ruling among us for one prevented by an enemy, as the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) and his companions were prevented."
As for one prevented without an enemy, he is not released short of the House.
He said: Malik was asked about one prevented by an enemy who was kept from the House, and he said: He is released from everything, and slaughters his offering, and shaves his head where he was detained, and there is no making up for it, unless he had never performed Hajj, in which case he must perform the Hajj of Islam.
[[The report 3288 is in the Muwatta': 360-361 with slight variation in some wording. From the words "He said: Malik was asked" at the end of this report, it has passed as number 3238, and it is in the Muwatta': 360, before the aforementioned text.]]

3289 - Yunus related to us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Malik informed us, saying: Yahya ibn Sa'id related to me, from Sulayman ibn Yasar: that Abdullah ibn Umar, Marwan ibn al-Hakam, and Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr issued a fatwa to Ibn Hazabah al-Makhzumi, [[In the Muwatta': "Sa'id ibn Hazabah al-Makhzumi."]] who fell ill during Hajj on part of the road, that he should treat himself with what was indispensable, [[In the printed edition: "that he should begin with what is indispensable," and the correct reading is from the Muwatta', and it has passed in the same way on p. 25; see footnote no. 2.]] and make a ransom, then make it an 'Umrah, and perform Hajj the following year and offer an offering.
Yunus said: Ibn Wahb said: Malik said: "And that is the ruling among us for one prevented without an enemy." [[Muwatta': 362; part of this has passed on p. 25.]]
He said: Malik said: "Everyone who is kept from Hajj after he has entered ihram, whether by illness, a mistake in counting, or the crescent being hidden from him, is prevented, and upon him is what is upon the one prevented — meaning remaining in his ihram — until he circumambulates or runs, then Hajj in the following year and the offering."

3290 - Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Abd al-Wahhab related to us, saying: I heard Yahya ibn Sa'id say: Ayyub ibn Musa informed me that Dawud ibn Abi 'Asim informed him: that he performed Hajj once, and fell ill, so he returned to al-Ta'if and did not run between al-Safa and al-Marwah. He wrote to 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah asking him about that, and 'Ata' wrote back to him: "Shed blood..."

* *

The reasoning of those who held Malik's view — that the place of the offering in prevention by an enemy is where its owner was detained — is:

3291 - Abu Kurayb and Muhammad ibn Ammarah al-Asadi related it to us, both saying: Ubaydullah ibn Musa related to us, saying: Musa ibn Ubaydah informed us, saying: Abu Murrah, mawla of Umm Hani', informed me, from Ibn Umar, who said: When the offering was short of the mountains that overlook the valley of al-Thaniyyah, the polytheists confronted them and turned them back. He said: The Prophet (ﷺ) slaughtered the offering where they had detained it — which was al-Hudaybiyyah — and shaved, and some people followed his example and shaved when they saw him shave, while others waited and said: "Perhaps we will circumambulate the House." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "May Allah have mercy on the shavers!" It was said: "And the shorteners!" He said: "May Allah have mercy on the shavers!" It was said: "And the shorteners!" He said: "And the shorteners."
[[The report 3291: its chain is very weak, because of "Musa ibn Ubaydah." Its condition has passed: 1875, 1876.
Abu Murrah, mawla of Umm Hani': his name is "Yazid," and he is also called "mawla of 'Aqil ibn Abi Talib," and he is known by his kunyah. He is a reliable known Successor, and the authors of the six books related from him.
The meaning of the hadith is established and well known from many routes, in the collections of hadith and books of sirah; indeed, something like this meaning is established from Ibn Umar with a sound chain, in the Musnad: 6067, al-Bukhari 5: 224, and 7: 391 (from al-Fath). The supplication for the shavers and the shorteners is also established from his hadith, sound, in the Musnad: 4657, the Muwatta' and the two Sahihs, as we have explained there.]]

3292 - Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim related to me, saying: Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Qattan related to us, saying: Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak related to us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from 'Urwah, from al-Miswar ibn Makhramah and Marwan ibn al-Hakam, both saying: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) wrote the treaty between himself and the polytheists of Quraysh — that was at al-Hudaybiyyah, in the year of al-Hudaybiyyah — he said to his companions: "Arise, slaughter, and shave." He said: By Allah, not one of them rose, until he said that three times. When none of them rose, he got up and entered upon Umm Salamah, and mentioned that to her. Umm Salamah said: "O Prophet of Allah, go out, and do not speak a word to any of them until you slaughter your camel and call your barber, and he shaves you." So he rose and went out, and did not speak to any of them until he did that. When they saw that, they rose and slaughtered, and some of them began shaving others, until some of them nearly killed one another out of grief.
[[The report 3292 is part of a long hadith about the treaty of al-Hudaybiyyah, and is well known and famous.
Ahmad related it in the Musnad 4: 328-331 (Halabi) from 'Abd al-Razzaq from Ma'mar with this chain, then he related it after that from Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Qattan from Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak from Ma'mar, without giving its wording, referring to the preceding narration. Al-Tabari related it here through Yahya al-Qattan.
Al-Bukhari related it, 5: 241-260 (Fath al-Bari) from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from 'Abd al-Razzaq, like the Musnad version. A concise portion is related 3: 433 from the route of Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak, from Ma'mar.]]

* *

They said: The Prophet (ﷺ) slaughtered his offering when the polytheists prevented him from the House at al-Hudaybiyyah, and he and his companions were released. They said: Al-Hudaybiyyah is not part of the Haram. They said: In a case like that there is clear proof that the meaning of His words, "until the offering reaches its place," is that it reaches — by slaughter or sacrifice — the place of its eating and benefit, at the place of its slaughter and sacrifice.

3293 - As is also related from the Prophet of Allah (peace be upon him) concerning its parallel, when meat was brought to him — Barirah had sent it — from alms which had been given to her, and he said: "Bring it near, for it has reached its place." [[The report 3293: this is a reference by al-Tabari to a well-known hadith. It is the story of Barirah, whom 'A'ishah bought from her masters who had made a contract of manumission with her, and she freed her, and she became her mawla; it is in the two Sahihs and elsewhere. The wording established in the two Sahihs, regarding the meat that was given in charity to Barirah, which she gave as a gift to 'A'ishah, and that the Prophet (ﷺ) ate from it, is that he said: "It is a charity for her and a gift for us," or something like this, from the hadith of 'A'ishah and from the hadith of Anas. I did not find the wording "then it has reached its place," which al-Tabari related in the story of Barirah. Perhaps it came to him from a route that is hidden from us.
Indeed, similar wording has come in two other stories with this meaning:
The first: from the hadith of Umm 'Atiyyah al-Ansariyyah, that she sent to 'A'ishah some meat that had come to her from alms, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) entered and asked about food, and they informed him of that — because charity is not lawful for him — and he (ﷺ) said: "It has indeed reached its place." Related by Ahmad in the Musnad 6: 407-408 (Halabi), al-Bukhari 3: 245, 281-282, and 5: 149-150 (Fath), Muslim 1: 297.
The second: from the hadith of Juwayriyah bint al-Harith, the Mother of the Believers, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) entered upon me one day and said: 'Is there any food?' I said: 'No, except some bones which a freedwoman of ours was given from charity.' He (ﷺ) said: 'Bring it near, for it has reached its place.'" Related by Ahmad in the Musnad 6: 429 (Halabi), and Muslim 1: 296.]]

* *

That is: it has reached the place of its good and its lawfulness for him by its being given to him as a gift, after it had been a charity to Barirah.

* *

Others said: The place of the offering of one prevented is the Haram, and it has no place other than it.
Mention of those who said that:

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 196 (part 5 of 7):

3294 - Yaʿqub ibn Ibrahim told me, saying: Hushaym related to us, from al-Aʿmash, from ʿUmara ibn ʿUmayr, from ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Yazid: that ʿAmr ibn Saʿid al-Nakhaʿi assumed ihram for ʿumra, and when he reached Dhat al-Shuqsuq he was stung there by a scorpion. His companions went out to the road, looking out for people, and came upon Ibn Masʿud. They mentioned that to him, and he said: "Let him send a sacrificial animal, and set between you a day as a signal. When the sacrificial animal is slaughtered, he may exit ihram, but he must make up his ʿumra." [[The report: 3294 - ʿUmara ibn ʿUmayr al-Taymi: trustworthy; the authors of the six canonical books narrated from him.
ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Yazid ibn Qays ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Malik al-Nakhaʿi: a trustworthy Successor (tabiʿi), who narrated much hadith.
ʿAmr ibn Saʿid al-Nakhaʿi: I have not found any mention of him. He has no role in the transmission of the report; rather, he is the one being spoken of, and the one for whose case Ibn Masʿud issued a ruling. His name will appear again in report 3299. See the note on report 3297. Al-Tabari related this report repeatedly with several chains, as you see; see also the note on report 3297.
Dhat al-Shuqsuq: a station on the road to Makkah, from Kufa. Tashawwuf al-shay': to stretch oneself upward to look at something.]]

3295 - Tamim ibn al-Muntasir told me, saying: Ishaq related to us, from Sharik, from Sulayman ibn Mihran, from ʿUmara ibn ʿUmayr and Ibrahim, from ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Yazid, that he said: "We set out assuming ihram for ʿumra, and al-Aswad ibn Yazid was among us, until we alighted at Dhat al-Shuqsuq. A companion of ours was stung, and that caused him severe hardship, and we did not know how to deal with him. Some of us went out to the road, and there we came upon a caravan in which was ʿAbd Allah ibn Masʿud. We said to him: 'O Abu ʿAbd al-Rahman, a man among us has been stung; what should we do with him?' He said: 'Let him send with you the price of a sacrificial animal, and set between you and him a day as a signal. When the animal is slaughtered, he may exit ihram, and he owes an ʿumra in the future.'" [[The report: 3295 - Sulayman ibn Mihran: he is al-Aʿmash. Here he narrates the report from ʿUmara ibn ʿUmayr, as in the previous report, and from Ibrahim: that is Ibn Yazid ibn al-Aswad ibn ʿAmr al-Nakhaʿi, the well-known trustworthy jurist, who was the nephew (son of the sister) of ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Yazid ibn Qays. So al-Aʿmash narrates it from both of them, from ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Yazid.
The report will also come from his narration alone, from his maternal uncle ʿAbd al-Rahman: 3297.]]

3296 - Ibn Bashshar told me, saying: Muʾammal related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from al-Aʿmash, from ʿUmara ibn ʿUmayr, from ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Yazid, who said: "While we were at Dhat al-Shuqsuq, a man among us assumed ihram for ʿumra, and was stung. ʿAbd Allah passed by us and we asked him, and he said: 'Set between you and him a day as a signal, and let him send the price of the sacrificial animal; when it is slaughtered he may exit ihram, and he owes the ʿumra.'" [[Al-Ammar and al-amara: the sign and the time.]]

3297 - Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told me, saying: Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar related to us, saying: Shuʿba related to us, from al-Hakam, who said: I heard Ibrahim al-Nakhaʿi narrating from ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Yazid, who said: "A man among us assumed ihram for ʿumra, and was stung. A caravan came in sight, in which was ʿAbd Allah ibn Masʿud. They asked him, and he said: 'Let him send a sacrificial animal, and set between you and him a day as a signal. When that day comes, he may exit ihram'" = and ʿUmara ibn ʿUmayr said: "So ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Yazid's narration from ʿAbd Allah was sufficient for you" = "and he owes the ʿumra from the future." [[The report: 3297 - al-Hakam: he is Ibn ʿUtayba (with a damma on the ʿayn, a fatha on the taʾ, and a bāʾ after the yāʾ). He is a trustworthy, authoritative, well-known jurist Successor. Ahmad ibn Hanbal considered him the most reliable of people in narrating from Ibrahim al-Nakhaʿi.
Al-Tahawi also related this report in Sharh Maʿani al-Athar 1: 432, through Bishr ibn ʿUmar, from Shuʿba with this chain, in similar wording, and in it he named the man who was stung, saying: "A man of the Nakhaʿ assumed ihram for ʿumra, who is called ʿUmayr ibn Saʿid..." If this is correct, then he is "ʿUmayr ibn Saʿid al-Nakhaʿi," the Successor whose biography has already passed: 1683. Thus the name "ʿAmr ibn Saʿid" in reports 3294 and 3299 is a corruption of this. What supports this is that his name also occurs corrupted as "ʿAmr ibn Saʿid" in the printed edition there, at 1683.]]

3298 - Abu al-Sa'ib told me, saying: Abu Muʿawiya related to us, from al-Aʿmash, from ʿUmara, from ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Yazid, who said: "We set out as ʿUmmar [pilgrims for ʿumra], and when we were at Dhat al-Shuqsuq a companion of ours was stung. We stopped on the road asking what to do with him, and there was ʿAbd Allah ibn Masʿud in a caravan. We said to him: 'A companion of ours has been stung.' He said: 'Set between you and your companion a day, and let him send the sacrificial animal; when the animal is slaughtered he may exit ihram, and then he owes the ʿumra.'"

3299 - Yaʿqub told me, saying: Hushaym related to us, from al-Hajjaj, who said: ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn al-Aswad related to me, from his father, from Ibn Masʿud: that ʿAmr ibn Saʿid al-Nakhaʿi assumed ihram for ʿumra, and when he reached Dhat al-Shuqsuq he was stung there. His companions went out to the road, looking out for people, and came upon Ibn Masʿud. They mentioned that to him, and he said: "Let him send a sacrificial animal, and set between you and him a day as a signal. When the sacrificial animal is slaughtered he may exit ihram, and he owes making up his ʿumra." [[The report: al-Hajjaj: he is Ibn Artat ibn Thawr ibn Hayra al-Nakhaʿi, and in our judgment he is trustworthy according to the preferred view. See also the note on report 3297.
ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn al-Aswad ibn Yazid ibn Qays al-Nakhaʿi: a trustworthy Successor. His father al-Aswad ibn Yazid al-Nakhaʿi was the brother of ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Yazid al-Nakhaʿi, who appeared in the previous reports; he was a senior Successor, trustworthy and among the people of goodness, as Ahmad said.]]

3300 - Al-Muthanna told me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Muʿawiya told me, from ʿAli, from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding "But if you are prevented, then what is feasible of offerings" (Q 2:196), that he said: "Whoever assumes ihram for hajj or ʿumra, and is then held back from the House by an illness that exhausts him or an excuse that restrains him, must slaughter what is feasible of offerings, a sheep or more, to be slaughtered on his behalf. If it is the obligatory pilgrimage (Hajj al-Islam), he must make it up; but if it is a pilgrimage after the obligatory pilgrimage, or an ʿumra, there is no making up for him."
Then he said: "And do not shave your heads until the offering reaches its place of sacrifice" (Q 2:196). If he assumed ihram for hajj, its place is the Day of Sacrifice; and if he assumed ihram for ʿumra, the place of his offering is when he reaches the House.

3301 - Muhammad ibn Saʿd told me, saying: My father told me, saying: My paternal uncle told me, saying: My father told me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding his words: "But if you are prevented, then what is feasible of offerings" (Q 2:196): "It refers to a man among the companions of Muhammad ﷺ who was held back from the House, so he sent an offering to the House and remained in his state of ihram until the offering reached its place of sacrifice. When the offering reached its place, he shaved his head, and God completed his hajj for him. Also, being prevented means that a person is kept from the hajj; then he owes an offering: if he is wealthy, a camel; otherwise, a cow; otherwise, a sheep; and he makes his hajj an ʿumra and sends his offering to the House. When the offering is slaughtered, he has exited ihram, and he owes the hajj in the future."

3302 - Al-Muthanna told me, saying: Ishaq related to us, saying: Bishr ibn al-Sari related to us, from Shuʿba, from ʿAmr ibn Murra, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Salama, who said: "ʿAli, may God be pleased with him, was asked about the words of Almighty God: 'But if you are prevented, then what is feasible of offerings.' If the pilgrim is prevented, he sends an offering; when it is slaughtered on his behalf, he exits ihram, and he may not exit until his offering is slaughtered."

3303 - Muhammad ibn ʿAmr told me, saying: Abu ʿAsim related to us, saying: ʿIsa related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, who said: I heard ʿAta' say: "Whoever is held back in his ʿumra, and sends a gift offering but it is intercepted, must give something in charity or fast. Whoever has his offering intercepted while he is a pilgrim, the place of sacrifice of the offering and the ihram is the Day of Sacrifice, and there is nothing upon him."

3304 - Al-Muthanna told me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa related to us, saying: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from ʿAta', the like of it.

3305 - Musa told me, saying: ʿAmr related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi regarding his words: "But if you are prevented, then what is feasible of offerings; and do not shave your heads until the offering reaches its place of sacrifice." This concerns a man who assumes ihram and then sets out and is prevented, either by a scorpion sting or illness, so he cannot bear to travel; or his mount breaks down. He remains, then sends an offering, a sheep or more. If he recovers and travels and catches up, he owes no offering. If the hajj has escaped him, it becomes an ʿumra, and he owes a hajj in the future. If he returns, he remains in ihram until the offering is slaughtered on his behalf on the Day of Sacrifice.
If he learns that his companion has not slaughtered on his behalf, he returns to ihram and sends another offering, and arranges with his companion for the day it will be slaughtered on his behalf in Makkah; it is slaughtered on his behalf in Makkah, and he exits ihram; and he owes a hajj and an ʿumra in the future. Some people say: two ʿumras. And if he had assumed ihram for ʿumra, then returned and sent his offering, he owes two ʿumras in the future. Others say: No, rather three ʿumras, in the manner they did regarding the hajj when they did it, he owes a hajj and two ʿumras.

3306 - ʿAbd al-Hamid ibn Bayan al-Qannad told me, saying: Ishaq al-Azraq informed us, from Abu Bishr, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid and ʿAta', from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: "If a man is prevented, he sends his offering, if he cannot reach the House because of the enemy. If he finds someone who can deliver it to Makkah on his behalf, he sends it in his place, and arranges with the owner of the offering. When he is safe, he must perform hajj and ʿumra. If an illness holds him back and he has no offering with him, he exits ihram where he is held back. If he has an offering with him, he does not exit until the offering reaches its place of sacrifice, when he has sent it; and he need not perform hajj or ʿumra in the future, unless he wishes."

* *

Abu Jaʿfar said: The reasoning of those who held this view, that the place of sacrifice of offerings and camels is the Haram, is that God, Mighty and Majestic, mentioned camels and offerings, saying: "And whoever honours the sacred rites of God, that is indeed from the piety of hearts. For you therein are benefits until a specified term; then their place of sacrifice is at the Ancient House" (Q 22:32-33). So He made their place of sacrifice the Haram, and there is no place of sacrifice for the offering other than it.

They said: As for what those who argue from the Prophet ﷺ slaughtering his offerings at al-Hudaybiyya when he was barred from the House, that is not an agreed-upon position, because:

3307 - al-Fadl ibn Sahl told me, saying: Makhwal ibn Ibrahim related to us, saying: Israʾil related to us, from Mujazza' ibn Zahir al-Aslami, from his father, from Najiya ibn Jundub al-Aslami, who said: "I came to the Prophet ﷺ when he was barred from the offering, and I said: 'O Messenger of God, send with me the offering and we will slaughter it in the Haram!' He said: 'How will you handle it?' I said: 'I will take it through valleys where they cannot reach it!' So I set off with it until I slaughtered it in the Haram." [[The report: 3307 - al-Fadl ibn Sahl ibn Ibrahim al-Aʿraj, Tabari's teacher: one of the trustworthy memorizers; al-Shaykhan (Bukhari and Muslim) narrated from him in their Sahihs. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib, Ibn Abi Hatim 3/1/63, Tarikh Baghdad 12: 364-365, and Tadhkirat al-Huffaz 2: 120.
Makhwal (with a khaʾ with a dot, on the pattern of "Muhammad") ibn Ibrahim ibn Makhwal ibn Rashid al-Nahdi al-Hannat. Al-Dhahabi said in al-Mizan: "a vehement Rafidi, truthful in himself." Ibn Abi Hatim 4/1/399 said: "My father was asked about him and said: 'He is truthful.'" Ibn Hibban mentioned him among the trustworthy.
Israʾil: he is Ibn Yunus ibn Abi Ishaq al-Sabiʿi. Makhwal's narrations are mostly from Israʾil, and he narrated from him what no one else narrated, as Ibn ʿAdi said.
Mujazza' ibn Zahir: a trustworthy Successor, narrated by the two Shaykhs and others.
His father, Zahir ibn Aswad ibn Hajjaj ibn Qays al-Aslami: a well-known companion, among those who pledged allegiance under the tree. Najiya ibn Jundub al-Aslami: a well-known companion, and he was the keeper of the offerings of the Messenger of God ﷺ. There is also Najiya ibn Kaʿb al-Khuzaʿi, who was also keeper of the offerings of the Messenger of God ﷺ, and some narrators confused the two. The Hafiz, in al-Tahdhib and al-Isaba, established that this is not that.
The report was also related by al-Tahawi in Sharh Maʿani al-Athar 1: 427, from Ibrahim ibn Abi Dawud, from Makhwal ibn Ibrahim with this chain, except that he made it "from Mujazza' from Najiya" directly, without "from his father" between them. Mujazza' does narrate from Najiya. However, the Hafiz mentioned this very report in al-Isaba in the biography of Najiya, 6: 222-223, saying that Ibn Manda related it "through Mujazza' ibn Zahir, from his father, from Najiya ibn Jundub," and then mentioned that "al-Tahawi related it through Makhwal." I do not know whether the phrase "from his father" fell out of al-Tahawi's copy, or whether it is a difference of transmission.
After mentioning Ibn Manda's narration, the Hafiz said: "Ibn Manda said: Makhwal ibn Ibrahim alone narrated it from Israʾil, from him (i.e., from Mujazza'), and Abu Hatim al-Razi and others narrated it from him (i.e., from Makhwal)." Thus he said. And al-Nasaʾi indeed related it through ʿUbayd Allah ibn Musa from Israʾil in the same way." I did not find it in al-Nasaʾi, so it appears that it is in al-Sunan al-Kubra.]] They said: This report makes clear that the Prophet ﷺ slaughtered his offerings in the Haram, so there is no proof for one who argues from his slaughtering at al-Hudaybiyya outside the Haram.

* *

Others said: The meaning and interpretation of this verse, apart from these two aspects we described from the statements of the two groups whose disagreement we mentioned, as we mentioned, is: "If you are prevented, O believers, from your pilgrimage, being barred from proceeding with its ihram by an obstacle of illness or fear of an enemy, and from performing what is incumbent upon you of your pilgrimage, so that you miss standing at ʿArafa, then upon you is what is feasible of offerings for what you missed of your pilgrimage, along with making up the hajj you missed." Those who held this view said: For the one barred from hajj by illness and other impediments, there is no exit from ihram except by circumambulating the House and running between al-Safa and al-Marwa, if he has missed the hajj. They said: As for one who is able to attend the sacred sites, he is not barred. They said: As for ʿumra, there is no barring in it, because its time is always present. They said: The one performing ʿumra does not exit except by another action which is obligatory for him in his ihram.

They said: The one performing ʿumra is not included in this verse; it refers only to the pilgrim.

* *

Then those who held this view differed. Some of them said: There is no barring by an enemy today, just as there is no barring by illness, for one who has missed the hajj, from exiting ihram before circumambulating the House and running between al-Safa and al-Marwa.

Those who said that:

3308 - Yaʿqub ibn Ibrahim told me, saying: Ibn ʿUlayya related to us, from Layth, from Mujahid, from Tawus, who said: Ibn ʿAbbas said: "There is no barring today."

3309 - Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Wahhab related to us, saying: I heard Yahya ibn Saʿid say: ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn al-Qasim informed me that ʿAʾisha said: "I do not know of a muhrim who exits by anything other than the House."

3310 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya told us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Maʿmar informed us, from Ibn Tawus, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: "There is no barring except for one whom an enemy has held back; he exits by an ʿumra, and there is no obligation on him of hajj or ʿumra."

* *

Others among them said: Barring by an enemy is established today and after today, in the manner of the three statements of theirs we have related.

Those who said that, and said: The meaning of the verse is: "If you are barred from hajj until it escapes you, then upon you is what is feasible of offerings for its missing you":

3311 - Yunus told me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Yunus informed me, from Ibn Shihab, from Salim, who said: ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUmar used to deny the stipulation in hajj, and say: "Is not the Sunna of the Messenger of God ﷺ enough for you? If one of you is held back from hajj, he circumambulates the House and al-Safa and al-Marwa, then exits from everything until he performs hajj the following year, and offers a sacrifice, or fasts if he finds no offering."

3312 - Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told me, saying: ʿAbd al-Wahhab related to us, saying: ʿUbayd Allah ibn ʿUmar related to us, from Nafiʿ, from Ibn ʿUmar, who said: "The one barred does not exit from anything until he reaches the House, and remains in his ihram as he is, unless an injury or wound afflicts him, so he treats it with what cures it and pays a ransom. When he reaches the House, if it is an ʿumra he makes it up; and if it is a hajj, he converts it into an ʿumra, and he owes hajj in the future and the offering. If he does not find one, then three days of fasting in hajj and seven when he returns."

3313 - Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Yahya ibn Saʿid related to us, from ʿUbayd Allah, who said: Nafiʿ informed me that Ibn ʿUmar passed by Ibn Hizaba while he was at al-Suqya, and saw that he had a fracture, and he asked him for a legal ruling, and he instructed him to stand as he was, not exiting from anything until he reaches the House, unless he suffers harm, in which case he treats it, and he owes what is feasible of offerings. He had assumed ihram for hajj. [[See what has passed, number 3289.]]

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 196 (part 6 of 7):**

3314. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: al-Layth narrated to me, saying: Uqayl narrated to me, from Ibn Shihab, who said: Salim ibn Abdullah informed me that Abdullah ibn Umar said: Whoever is prevented (uhsira) after he has pronounced the talbiyah for Hajj, and he is held back by fear, or illness, or a lame mount that carries him, [[Khalaat al-naqah takhla khala'an (with a kasra on the kha') fa-hiya khali, meaning: when the she-camel kneels and refuses to rise. In the hadith: "The she-camel of the Prophet (ﷺ) knelt with him on the day of al-Hudaybiyah, and they said: 'al-Qaswa' has knelt!' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'She has not knelt, and it is not her habit! Rather, the one who held her back is the One who held back the elephant.' And al-zahr: the camels on which one is carried and rides.]] or some other matter of any kind, then he shall seek treatment for his being held back with whatever he needs, except that he may not be relieved (from ihram) with respect to women and perfume, and he shall make expiation with the fidyah (compensation) which Allah has enjoined: fasting, or charity, or a sacrifice (nusuk). If he misses Hajj while he is in that state of being held back, or misses standing at the stations of Arafah before dawn on the night of Muzdalifah, then he has missed Hajj, and his pilgrimage becomes an Umrah: he comes to Makkah, circumambulates the House and performs sa'y between al-Safa and al-Marwah. If he has a hady (sacrificial animal) with him, he slaughters it in Makkah near the Sacred Mosque; then he shaves his head or trims it, and then he is relieved from women, perfume and other things. Then he must perform Hajj in the following year and offer whatever hady is feasible.

3315. Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Malik ibn Anas narrated to me, from Ibn Shihab, from Salim ibn Abdullah, from Abdullah ibn Umar that he said: The one who is prevented is not relieved until he circumambulates the House and (performs sa'y) between al-Safa and al-Marwah. If he is compelled to wear some clothing he must have, or to use medicine, he may do so and make fidyah. [[Al-Muwatta', p. 361, with slight variation in its wording, and in it: "The one who is prevented by illness is not relieved..."]]

* *

This is what was transmitted from Ibn Umar regarding being prevented by illness and what is similar to it. As for one prevented by an enemy, he used to say with something like the view we mentioned earlier from Malik ibn Anas, which he used to hold. [[See what preceded, nos. 3238, 3287, 3288.]]

3316. Tamim ibn al-Muntasir narrated to me, saying: Abdullah ibn Numayr narrated to us, saying: Ubaydullah informed us, from Nafi': Ibn Umar wanted to perform Hajj when al-Hajjaj descended upon Ibn al-Zubayr, and his two sons Salim and Ubaydullah spoke to him, saying: "It will not harm you not to perform Hajj this year. We fear that fighting will break out among the people and you will be prevented from the House!" He said: "If I am prevented from the House, I will do as we did with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when the disbelievers of Quraysh prevented him from the House, and he shaved and returned."

* *

As for what we mentioned from them concerning Umrah, their saying: "There is no ihsar (being prevented) in it, nor hasr (restriction)," then:

3317. Yaqub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to me, from Abu Bishr, from Yazid ibn Abdullah ibn al-Shikhkhir that he pronounced the talbiyah for Umrah and was prevented. He said: He wrote to Ibn Abbas and Ibn Umar, and they wrote back to him that he should send the hady and then remain until he is relieved from his Umrah. He said: So he remained six or seven months.

3318. Yaqub narrated to me, saying: Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, saying: Yaqub informed us, from Abu al-Ala' ibn al-Shikhkhir, who said: I set out as a pilgrim for Umrah, and I was thrown from my camel and broke my leg. We sent to Ibn Abbas and Ibn Umar to ask them, and they said: "Umrah has no fixed time like the time of Hajj; one is not relieved until one circumambulates the House." He said: So I remained at al-Dathinah, or near it, for seven or eight months. [[al-Dathinah (with a fatha on its first letter and a kasra on its second): a dwelling of Banu Sulaym on the road from Basra to Makkah, and it was also called "al-Dafinah." Al-Bakri said in Mu'jam ma Asta'jam: "al-Dathinah" with a fatha on its first and second letters, followed by a nun and a doubled ya'. Then he quoted Abu Ali al-Qali: "al-Dafinah and al-Dathinah: a dwelling of Banu Sulaym; I have transmitted it from the book of Ya'qub on substitution (al-ibdal)." The correct reading is what Yaqut mentioned in its vocalization, due to the verse of al-Nabighah al-Dhubyani:
"And at al-Rumaythah, from Sukayn, present, and at al-Dathinah, from Banu Sayyar."]]

3319. Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Malik narrated to me, from Ayyub ibn Abi Tamimah al-Sakhtiyani, from a man of Basra, an old man, who said: I set out for Makkah, and when I was on part of the road I broke my thigh. I sent to Makkah to Abdullah ibn Abbas, and there were Abdullah ibn Abbas, Abdullah ibn Umar and the people there. None of them gave me leave to be relieved, so I remained in that state for seven months, until I was relieved by Umrah. [[Al-Muwatta', p. 361, with some slight variation in some of its wording, and in it also: "So I remained in that state at the water for seven months," and this is probably the correct version.]]

3320. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Suwayd narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Ma'mar, from Ibn Shihab, concerning a man who suffered a break while he was performing Umrah. He said: He remains in his state of ihram until he comes to the House and circumambulates it and (performs sa'y) between al-Safa and al-Marwah, and he shaves or trims (his hair), and there is nothing upon him.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of these views regarding the interpretation (ta'wil) of this verse is the view of the one who said: Allah, may He be exalted, meant by His saying: ﴿And if you are prevented, then (send) what is feasible of the hady, and do not shave your heads until the hady reaches its place of sacrifice﴾ — every one who is prevented while in ihram, whether his ihram is for Umrah or for Hajj. He made the place of his hady the place where he was prevented, and He made his release from ihram conditional upon his hady reaching its place. [[Qawluhu: "wa ta'awwal..." is conjoined to his saying: "...the view of the one who said..."]] And he interpreted "al-mahall" (the place of sacrifice) as the place of slaughter or the place of cutting the throat, at the time when its slaughter or cutting becomes permissible, whether in the sacred precinct or outside it. And He made it obligatory upon him to make up what he was released from of his ihram before completing it, if he finds a way to do so. This is because of the consistent reports from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he was prevented from the House in the year of al-Hudaybiyah while he and his companions were in the state of Umrah, so he and his companions slaughtered the hady at his command and were released from their ihram before reaching the House, and then they performed the ihram which they had been released from in the following year. No one among the people of knowledge of the biographical accounts or others has claimed that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) or any of his companions remained in his ihram waiting to reach the House and be released by circumambulating it and performing sa'y between al-Safa and al-Marwah, and the arrival of his hady at the Sacred Precinct is not unknown. [[In the printed edition: "and the arrival of his hady at the Haram is not unknown (la yakhfa)," which makes no sense. Tahfa means: to investigate thoroughly and exert oneself to know a thing; from their saying: "he is hafi by it," meaning he is intensely concerned with it. This is what I deduced from reading this word. And Allah is the One who grants success to what is correct.]]

So the most appropriate of actions to follow is the action of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), since no report has come forbidding it, and no proof has established its prohibition. Given that this is so, and the people of knowledge differed regarding the view we have chosen on this matter, some interpreting the meaning of the verse as we have interpreted it, and others disagreeing; and given that what we have stated from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is established by transmission, then what has been transmitted from him is the most appropriate matter for interpreting the verse, since the people of knowledge do not dispute that this verse was revealed on that occasion and was revealed in the context of the polytheists' preventing him from the House.
