[[In the printed edition: "that it was revealed on that day in the context of the polytheists..." The addition of the wa' is necessary for the sentence to be sound and balanced.]]

And a report has been transmitted similar to what we have said regarding this:

3321. Yaqub narrated to me, saying: Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, saying: al-Hajjaj ibn Abi Uthman narrated to me, saying: Yahya ibn Abi Kathir narrated to me, that Ikrimah, mawla of Ibn Abbas, narrated to him, saying: al-Hajjaj ibn Amr al-Ansari narrated to me that he heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Whoever is broken or lamed has been released, and he has another Hajj obligatory upon him." He said: I related that to Ibn Abbas and Abu Hurayrah, and they both said: "He has spoken truthfully." [[Hadith 3321: al-Hajjaj ibn Abi Uthman al-Sawwaf: trustworthy and a memorizer; the authors of the six canonical collections transmitted from him.
This hadith was narrated by Ahmad in al-Musnad, no. 15796 (3: 450, Halabi), from Yahya al-Qattan and from Ibn Ulayyah, both from Hajjaj al-Sawwaf with this chain.
Abu Dawud narrated it, no. 1962, through the route of Yahya from Hajjaj. Al-Mundhiri said: "al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah also transmitted it." A second chain will follow directly after this.]]

3322. Yaqub narrated to me, saying: Marwan narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj al-Sawwaf narrated to us. And Humayd ibn Mas'adah narrated to us, saying: Sufyan ibn Habib narrated to us, from al-Hajjaj al-Sawwaf, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from Ikrimah, from al-Hajjaj ibn Amr, from the Prophet (ﷺ) similarly, and from Ibn Abbas and Abu Hurayrah. [[Hadith 3322: Marwan: he is Ibn Mu'awiyah al-Fazari, whose biography has already passed (no. 1222). This hadith repeats the preceding one. Al-Hakim transmitted it in al-Mustadrak 1: 470 through the route of Marwan ibn Mu'awiyah al-Fazari with this chain, and said: "This is a sahih hadith according to the condition of al-Bukhari, though they did not include it." Al-Dhahabi agreed with him.
In the printed copy of al-Mustadrak it reads: "Marwan narrated to us, Mu'awiyah al-Fazari!" which is a typographical error that should be corrected.]]

* *

The meaning of this report is the command to make up the Hajj from which one was released, similar to what the Prophet (ﷺ) and his companions did when they made up the Umrah from which they were released in the year of al-Hudaybiyah, in the following year, in the Umrah of the Qada' (making up).

* *

It is said to whoever claims that the one prevented by an enemy, when released from voluntary ihram, has no obligation of making up, while the one prevented by ailments must make it up: What is the reason that made making up obligatory for one of them and dropped it from the other, when both have been released from an ihram that it was obligatory for them to complete, were it not for the impeding cause?
If he says: "Because the verse was revealed only concerning the one prevented by an enemy, so it is not permissible for us to extend its ruling to what it was not revealed about," it is said to him: A group of the people of knowledge has refuted you on this, but we grant you what you have said. Then why would the ruling for being prevented by illness and being prevented in general not be the ruling for being prevented by an enemy, since both agree in preventing one from reaching the House and completing the rites of their ihram, even though the causes of their prevention differ, one being prevented by a cause in his body and the other by a preventer's obstruction? Then ask him to explain the difference between them, from a basis or by analogy, and he will say nothing regarding one of them without being obliged to say the same regarding the other.

* *

As for those who said: There is no ihsar in Umrah, it is said to them: You know that the Prophet (ﷺ) was only prevented from the House while he was in the state of Umrah, so he was released from his ihram. So what is your proof for there being no ihsar in it? Or what do you think if someone said: There is no ihsar in Hajj; there is only missing it (fawt), and the one who misses Hajj must remain in his ihram until he circumambulates the House and performs sa'y between al-Safa and al-Marwah, because it has not been authentically reported from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he established any sunnah regarding ihsar in Hajj? A group of the leaders of the religion has said this. But as for Umrah, the Prophet (ﷺ) established in it what he established, and Allah, blessed and exalted, revealed in its ruling what He clarified of release and making up, which the Prophet (ﷺ) did. So is there ihsar in Umrah but not in Hajj? Is there a difference between them? Then reverse the argument on him regarding this, and he will say nothing regarding one of them without being obliged to say the same regarding the other.

* *

**On the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So whoever among you is ill, or has an affliction of the head, then (he must pay) a ransom of fasting, or charity, or sacrifice﴾**

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His praise be exalted, He means: ﴿And if you are prevented, then (send) what is feasible of the hady, and do not shave your heads until the hady reaches its place of sacrifice﴾, [[See what preceded on p. 36, and the note no. 1]] except that one of you may be compelled to shave out of necessity, either because of illness, or because of an affliction of his head from lice or something else; so he shaves at that point because of the necessity that has befallen him, even though the hady has not reached its place. Then, by shaving his head in that condition, he becomes obliged to a fidyah of fasting, or charity, or sacrifice.

* *

Those who interpret the Qur'an (ahl al-ta'wil) have said something similar to what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said that:

3323. Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Ibn Jurayj narrated to us, saying: I asked Ata': What is "an affliction of his head"? He said: Lice and other things, and a headache, and whatever is on his head.

* *

Others said: He does not shave if he wishes to make the fidyah of Hajj by a sacrifice or by feeding, except after making the expiation. And if he wishes to make the fidyah by fasting, he shaves and then fasts.

Mention of those who said that: . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .

3324. Ubaydullah ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, from his father, from Ash'ath, from al-Hasan, who said: If a person in ihram has an affliction of his head, he shaves when he sends a sheep, or feeds the poor; and if it is fasting, he shaves and then fasts afterwards. [[Hadith 3324: Ubaydullah ibn Mu'adh ibn Mu'adh al-Anbari, the memorizer: trustworthy; the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim) and others transmitted from him. He died in the year 237. He was from Basra, and Ibn Jarir was born in the year 224, so he was thirteen years old at the time of Ubaydullah's death, and it is not unlikely that he heard from him, though he did not travel in search of hadith at that age. I have not found anything that confirms the apparent sense of this chain, that he heard from Ubaydullah. This chain will appear in another report, no. 3374, with an intermediary between al-Tabari and Ubaydullah, and it is not impossible for a narrator to transmit from a shaykh directly at one time and through an intermediary at another. I suspect, however, the correctness of the printed text of al-Tabari at this point, lest a shaykh's name between them has dropped out.
I placed dots before and after this report, because I am certain there is a gap and confusion here which I was unable to identify. Nevertheless, I am in doubt about the wording of this report, and I fear it may be Tabari's own words rather than al-Hasan's. The saying of al-Hasan with this chain will come in no. 3374.
In that place the chain reads: "Ibn Abi Imran narrated to us, saying: Ubaydullah ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, from his father..." Likewise Ibn Kathir transmitted it in his Tafsir 1: 448. So there is no doubt that this chain also has a deficiency, and the correct version is: "Ibn Abi Imran narrated to us, saying: Ubaydullah ibn Mu'adh narrated to us..."]] . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .

* *

Mention of those who said that:

3325. Ubayd ibn Isma'il al-Hubbari narrated to me, saying: Abdullah ibn Numayr narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, from Alqamah, who said: If a man has pronounced the talbiyah for Hajj and is prevented, he sends what is feasible of the hady, a sheep; but if he hastens before the hady reaches its place and shaves his head, or applies perfume, or treats himself, he is obliged to a fidyah of fasting, or charity, or sacrifice. Ibrahim said: I mentioned that to Sa'id ibn Jubayr, and he said: "Ibn Abbas said likewise."

3326. Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding: ﴿And if you are prevented, then (send) what is feasible of the hady﴾, he said: Whoever is prevented by illness or injury should send what is feasible of the hady, and he should not shave his head, and he is not released until the Day of Sacrifice. So whoever is ill, or applies kohl, or applies oil, or treats himself, or has an affliction of his head and shaves, then there is a fidyah of fasting, or charity, or sacrifice.

3327. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.

3328. Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿And do not shave your heads until the hady reaches its place of sacrifice; so whoever among you is ill, or has an affliction of his head, then (he must pay) a fidyah of fasting, or charity, or sacrifice﴾: This is when he has sent his hady, then he needs to shave his head because of illness, or needs perfume, or needs a garment to wear, a shirt or something else; then he is obliged to the fidyah.

3329. And al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih, the scribe of al-Layth, narrated to us, saying: al-Layth narrated to me, from Uqayl, from Ibn Shihab, who said: If someone is prevented from Hajj, and during his confinement he suffers illness or an affliction of his head, and he shaves his head during that confinement, then he is obliged to a fidyah of fasting, or charity, or sacrifice.

3330. Al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: al-Layth narrated to me, saying: Uqayl narrated to us, from Ibn Shihab, who said: Salim ibn Abdullah informed me that Abdullah ibn Umar said: Whoever is prevented after pronouncing the talbiyah for Hajj, and he is held back by illness or fear, then he seeks treatment during that confinement with whatever he needs, except that women and perfume are not permitted to him, and he makes the fidyah which Allah has enjoined: fasting, or charity, or sacrifice.

3331. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Bishr ibn al-Sari narrated to me, from Shu'bah, from Amr ibn Murrah, from Abdullah ibn Salamah, who said: Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, was asked about the saying of Allah, may His praise be exalted: ﴿So whoever among you is ill, or has an affliction of his head, then (he must pay) a fidyah of fasting, or charity, or sacrifice﴾. He said: This is before the hady is slaughtered; if something befalls him, he owes the expiation.

* *

Others said: The meaning of that is: whoever among you is ill, or has an affliction of his head, then he owes a fidyah of fasting, or charity, or sacrifice before shaving, when he wants to shave.

Mention of those who said that:

3332. Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿So whoever among you is ill, or has an affliction of his head, then (he must pay) a fidyah of fasting, or charity, or sacrifice﴾: Whoever's illness becomes severe, or whose head pains him while he is in ihram, he owes fasting, or feeding, or sacrifice. And he does not shave his head until he has first paid his fidyah.

* *

The reasoning behind those who said this statement: -

3333 - Al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Suwayd narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Ya'qub, who said: I asked Ata' about His words: ﴿So whoever among you is ill or has an ailment of the head, then an expiation of fasting, or charity, or sacrifice﴾. He said: Ka'b ibn 'Ujrah passed by the Prophet ﷺ while his head was full of lice and nits. The Prophet ﷺ said to him: "Do you have a sheep?" Ka'b said: "I do not find one!" The Prophet ﷺ said to him: "If you wish, feed six poor people, and if you wish, fast three days, then shave your head."

[[The hadith: 3333 – from this hadith up to hadith 3358, then hadith 3364, are all chains for the hadith of Ka'b ibn 'Ujrah by different routes, with varying wordings and contexts, then hadith 3359 concerning the story of Ka'b as well. That makes 28 hadiths, and I found the takhrij for most of them. Among them are 10 chains whose takhrij I did not manage to locate, so they are to be benefited from in this great tafsir; perhaps some of them exist in our sources, but I have not reached them.
The numbers of the chains whose takhrij I did not find are: 3333, 3339, 3343, 3344, 3349, 3350, 3355, 3357, 3358, 3359.
This chain: 3333 – the first of them, and I did not find it in another place.
As for Ata' in this chain: the apparent one is Ata' ibn Abi Rabah. It is possible that it is "Ata' ibn 'Abdullah al-Khurasani", because the hadith will come from his narration: 3353 from an unnamed shaykh, from Ka'b ibn 'Ujrah.
Whatever the case, this chain is weak due to its being mursal, because Ata' relates an incident from the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ which he did not witness, and then did not mention who narrated it to him.
The hadith will come again at 3357 from the narration of Ibn Jurayj from Ata', also mursal.
Its meaning is established and sound from the connected sound narrations that follow, and there are many of them, all praise be to Allah.
Al-sa'aban is the plural of sa'b (with damma then fatha), plural of sa'ubah: it is the eggs of lice (nits).]]
* *
Abu Ja'far said: As for the "illness" for which treatment with perfume and shaving the head is permitted, it is every illness whose cure requires shaving it, like brain fever (al-birsam), which in some cases requires shaving the sufferer's head, and similar conditions, [[Al-birsam: a hot swelling that affects the membrane between the liver and the intestines, then spreads to the brain until the sufferer becomes delirious during this illness.]] and wounds on the human body which require treatment with medicine containing perfume and the like, and sores and ailments afflicting bodies.
As for the "harm" which, when it is on a person's head specifically, calls for shaving it, it is like headache and hemicrania (al-shaqiqah), and similar conditions, [[Al-shaqiqah: a headache that takes hold of half the head and face, treated by cupping.]] and an abundance of lice in the head, and everything harmful to the head in which shaving brings its cure and removes the present harm, so that this falls under the general meaning of the words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿or has an ailment of the head﴾.
* *
Reports have been widely transmitted from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that this verse was revealed concerning Ka'b ibn 'Ujrah, when he complained of the great harm to his head from lice, and that was in the year of al-Hudaybiyyah.
Mention of the reports narrated on this:
3334 - Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Malik ibn Abi al-Shawarib and Humayd ibn Mas'adah narrated to us, both saying: Yazid ibn Zurai' narrated to us, saying: Dawud narrated to us, from al-Sha'bi, from Ka'b ibn 'Ujrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed by me at al-Hudaybiyyah while I had a thick head of hair in which there were vermin, between the root of every hair and its tip were lice and nits. He said: "Indeed this is a harm!" I said: Yes indeed, O Messenger of Allah, it is severe! He said: "Do you have a sacrifice?" I said: No! He said: "If you wish, fast three days, and if you wish, give charity of three sa' of dates to six poor people, half a sa' for each poor person."

[[The two hadiths: 3334, 3335 – Dawud: he is Ibn Abi Hind. The hadith was narrated by Ahmad in al-Musnad 4: 343, and Abu Dawud: 1858, both through Dawud from al-Sha'bi.
Al-wafrah: larger than al-jummah, which is hair reaching beyond the earlobes, then al-lummah, which is hair reaching the shoulders. Al-hawam, singular hamah: serpents and the like, which "yuhimm", i.e., crawl. Al-hamim means crawling. They used the term "hawam" to refer to lice because they crawl in the head, i.e., move in it and harm it. Asa' is the plural of sa', and its original form is "a'sa'" with a hamza, with damma (like jabal and ajbal), the hamza was moved in place of the sad, as they said in dar, adwar and adar (al-Maghrib from Abu Ali al-Farisi and Mi'yar al-lughah by al-Shirazi). The sa' is a measure used by the people of Madinah, and jurists differ greatly in its estimation, which will come (asa') at number 3346.]]
3335 - Ishaq ibn Shahin al-Wasiti narrated to me, saying: Khalid al-Tahhan narrated to us, from Dawud, from 'Amir, from Ka'b ibn 'Ujrah, from the Prophet, similarly.
3336 - Muhammad ibn 'Ubayd al-Muharibi narrated to us, saying: Asad ibn 'Amr narrated to us, from Ash'ath, from 'Amir, from 'Abdullah ibn Ma'qil, from Ka'b ibn 'Ujrah, who said: I went out with the Prophet ﷺ during the time of al-Hudaybiyyah, and I had a thick head of hair, which had become infested with lice, and the nits were eating me. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw me and said: "Shave!" So I did, and he said: "Do you have a sacrifice?" I said: I do not find one! He said: "It is what is easy of sacrifice," and I said: I do not find one! He said: "Fast three days, or feed six poor people, half a sa' for each poor person."
He said: It was concerning me that this verse was revealed: ﴿So whoever among you is ill or has an ailment of the head, then an expiation of fasting, or charity, or sacrifice﴾, to the end of the verse.

[[The hadith: 3336 – Asad ibn 'Amr al-Bajali al-Qadi: a jurist from the companions of Abu Hanifah, whom Imam Ahmad narrated from and said: "He was truthful." Ibn Sa'd rated him reliable (7/2/74). His biography is in al-Ta'jil. He is highly disputed, between being declared reliable and being declared a liar. The fair assessment is what Ahmad said. Ash'ath: he is Ibn Sawwar al-Kindi, and he is reliable. 'Amir: he is al-Sha'bi.
'Abdullah ibn Ma'qil ibn Muqarrin al-Muzani: a reliable Successor, from the best of the Successors. "Ma'qil" with a fatha on the mim, sukun on the ayn, and kasra on the qaf. "Muqarrin" with damma on the mim, fatha on the qaf, shaddah on the kasra-marked ra, and ending with a nun.
The hadith was narrated by Ahmad 4: 243 (Halabi) from Hushaym from Ash'ath with this chain. It will come at 3364 through the route of Hushaym.]]

Abu Ja'far said: This report indicates that the correct view is that the expiation is only obligatory upon the one who shaves, after the shaving, and that the view of those who say: he pays the expiation then shaves, is false; because Ka'b reports that the Prophet ﷺ commanded him with the expiation after he had commanded him to shave, and he shaved.

[[The author's discussion has been abridged due to its great length.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 197 (part 1 of 6):

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿The Hajj is in well-known months﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His praise be exalted, He means: the time of the Hajj is well-known months.

* *

"Al-ashhur" (the months) is in the nominative case as the subject of "al-Hajj," although the Hajj has a time, not as a descriptive attribute (sifa) or adjective (na't), since they are not restricted by definiteness through being attached to a definite noun or a known referent. Thus the nominative case applies to them just as in the Arabs' saying in a similar context: "The Muslims are one side, and the disbelievers are one side," with "one side" in the nominative, since it is not restricted to a known limit. If it were said: "one side of their land, or their country," then the accusative would be the proper form of speech. [[See the detailed discussion of this in al-Farra's Ma'ani al-Qur'an, 1:119.]]

* *

Then the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed regarding His saying: "The Hajj is in well-known months."

Some of them said: By "the well-known months" is meant: Shawwal, Dhu al-Qa'dah, and ten days of Dhu al-Hijjah.

Those who said this:

3518 - Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, he said: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, he said: Shurayk narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu al-Ahwas, from Abd Allah, regarding His saying: "The Hajj is in well-known months," he said: Shawwal, Dhu al-Qa'dah, and ten (days) of Dhu al-Hijjah.

3519 - Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, he said: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, he said: Sufyan and Shurayk narrated to us, from Khusayf, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, the like of it.

3520 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, he said: al-Thawri informed us, from Khusayf, from Muqsim, from Ibn Abbas, the like of it.

3521 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, he said: Ibrahim ibn Isma'il ibn Nasr al-Sulami narrated to us, he said: Ibrahim ibn Isma'il ibn Abi Habibah narrated to us, from Dawud ibn Husayn, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas that he said: The months of the Hajj are Shawwal, Dhu al-Qa'dah, and ten days of Dhu al-Hijjah. [[Omitted from our numbering: no. 3522.]]

3523 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, he said: Abu Salih narrated to us, he said: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: "The Hajj is in well-known months," and they are: Shawwal, Dhu al-Qa'dah, and ten days of Dhu al-Hijjah. God, glory be to Him, made these for the Hajj and the rest of the months for the 'Umrah. So it is not proper for anyone to enter into ihram for the Hajj except during the months of the Hajj, whereas 'Umrah may be entered into ihram in any month.

3524 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, he said: al-Hammani narrated to us, he said: Shurayk narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: "The Hajj is in well-known months," he said: Shawwal, Dhu al-Qa'dah, and ten days of Dhu al-Hijjah.

3525 - Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, he said: Abd al-Rahman and Abu 'Amir narrated to us, both said: Sufyan narrated to us. = And al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq informed us. = He said: al-Thawri informed us, from al-Mughirah, from Ibrahim, the like of it.

3526 - Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, he said: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, he said: Abu 'Awanah narrated to us, from Mughirah, from Ibrahim and al-Sha'bi, the like of it.

3527 - Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, he said: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, he said: Sufyan and Israil narrated to us, from Mughirah, from Ibrahim, the like of it.

3528 - Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, he said: Israil narrated to us, from Jabir, from Amir, the like of it.

3529 - Musa narrated to me, he said: Amr narrated to us, he said: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, the like of it.

3530 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, he said: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, he said: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

3531 - al-Qasim narrated to me, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hushaym narrated to me, he said: Hajjaj informed us, from al-Hakam, from Muqsim, from Ibn Abbas. = And Mughirah informed us, from Ibrahim and al-Sha'bi. = And Yunus informed us, from al-Hasan. = And Juwaybir informed us, from al-Dahhak. = And Hajjaj informed us, from Ata' and Mujahid, the like of it. [[The report 3531: the speaker in "And Mughirah informed us... = And Juwaybir informed us... = etc." is Hushaym.]]

3532 - Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, he said: Abu al-Walid narrated to us, he said: Hammad narrated to us, from Ubayd Allah, from Nafi', from Ibn Umar, he said: Shawwal, Dhu al-Qa'dah, and ten (days) of Dhu al-Hijjah, in "The Hajj is in well-known months."

3533 - Ahmad ibn Hazim narrated to me, he said: Abu Nu'aym narrated to us, he said: Warqa' narrated to us, from Abd Allah ibn Dinar, from Ibn Umar, he said: "The Hajj is in well-known months," he said: Shawwal, Dhu al-Qa'dah, and ten (days) of Dhu al-Hijjah.

3534 - Ahmad ibn Hazim narrated to us, he said: Abu Nu'aym narrated to us, he said: Husayn ibn Aqil narrated to us, from al-Dahhak, he said: Shawwal, Dhu al-Qa'dah, and ten days of Dhu al-Hijjah.

3535 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to me, he said: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, he said: Husayn ibn Aqil al-Khurasani informed us, he said: I heard al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim say, and he mentioned the like of it.

* *

Others said: Rather, by that is meant Shawwal, Dhu al-Qa'dah, and all of Dhu al-Hijjah.

Those who said this:

3536 - Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, he said: Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, he said: Ibn Jurayj narrated to us, he said: I said to Nafi': Did Abd Allah used to name the months of the Hajj? He said: Yes, Shawwal, Dhu al-Qa'dah, and Dhu al-Hijjah.

3537 - Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Bakr narrated to us, he said: Ibn Jurayj narrated to us, he said: I said to Nafi': Did you hear Ibn Umar name the months of the Hajj? He said: Yes, he would name Shawwal, Dhu al-Qa'dah, and Dhu al-Hijjah.

3538 - Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, he said: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, he said: Shurayk narrated to us, from Ibrahim ibn Muhajir, from Mujahid, from Ibn Umar, he said: Shawwal, Dhu al-Qa'dah, and Dhu al-Hijjah.

3539 - Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Bakr narrated to us, he said: Ibn Jurayj informed us, he said: Ata' said: "The Hajj is in well-known months," Ata' said: they are Shawwal, Dhu al-Qa'dah, and Dhu al-Hijjah.

3540 - It was narrated to me from Ammar, he said: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi', the like of it.

3541 - Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah regarding His saying: "The Hajj is in well-known months," the months of the Hajj: Shawwal, Dhu al-Qa'dah, and Dhu al-Hijjah. = And sometimes he said: and ten (days) of Dhu al-Hijjah.

3542 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, he said: Ma'mar informed us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding His saying: "The Hajj is in well-known months," he said: Shawwal, Dhu al-Qa'dah, and Dhu al-Hijjah.

3543 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, he said: Ma'mar informed us, from Ibn Tawus, from his father, the like of it.

3544 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, he said: Abu Salih narrated to us, he said: al-Layth narrated to me, he said: Uqayl narrated to me, from Ibn Shihab, he said: The months of the Hajj: Shawwal, Dhu al-Qa'dah, and Dhu al-Hijjah.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: If someone says to us: What is the reasoning of those who said this, when you know that the act of Hajj is not performed after the days of Mina have passed?

It is said: The meaning of that is other than what you have imagined. Rather, by their saying, "The Hajj is three complete months," they meant that these are the months of the Hajj and not the months of 'Umrah, and that the months of 'Umrah are other than these months of the year. What indicates that this was their meaning in that statement is what was reported:

3545 - Yaqub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, he said: Ayyub informed us, from Nafi', he said: Ibn Umar said: Your separating the months of the Hajj from the 'Umrah, so that you make the 'Umrah in other than the months of the Hajj, is more complete for the Hajj of one of you and more complete for his 'Umrah.

3546 - Nasr ibn Ali al-Jahdami narrated to me, he said: my father narrated to me, he said: Shu'bah narrated to us, he said: Ayyub - or he said: I met Ayyub - did not meet me except that he asked me about the hadith of Qays ibn Muslim, from Tariq ibn Shihab, who said: I said to Abd Allah: A woman from among us has performed Hajj, or she wants to perform Hajj; should she add an 'Umrah to her Hajj? He said: I do not see these except as months of the Hajj. He said: Ayyub and those with him would say to me: Has Qays ibn Muslim narrated to you a hadith like this, from Tariq ibn Shihab, that he asked Abd Allah?

3547 - Ya'qub narrated to me, he said: Hushaym narrated to us, from Ibn Awn, he said: I heard al-Qasim ibn Muhammad say: Indeed, the 'Umrah in the months of the Hajj is not complete. He was asked: The 'Umrah in Muharram? He said: They used to consider it complete.

3548 - Abd al-Hamid ibn Bayan narrated to us, he said: Ishaq ibn Yusuf informed us, from Ibn Awn, he said: I asked al-Qasim ibn Muhammad about the 'Umrah in the months of the Hajj. He said: They did not consider it complete.

3549 - Ibn Bayan al-Wasiti narrated to us, he said: Ishaq informed us, from Abd Allah ibn Awn, from Ibn Sirin, that he used to prefer the 'Umrah in Muharram. He said: Would it be in the months of the Hajj? He said: They did not consider it complete.

3550 - Ibn Bayan narrated to us, he said: Ishaq narrated to us, from Ibn Awn, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, he said: Ibn Umar said to al-Hakam ibn al-A'raj or someone else: If you obey me, wait until Muharram begins, then go out to Dhat 'Irq and enter into ihram from there for 'Umrah.

3551 - Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, he said: Wahb ibn Jarir narrated to us, he said: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abu Ya'qub, he said: I heard Ibn Umar say: For me to perform 'Umrah in the first ten (days) of Dhu al-Hijjah is more beloved to me than to perform 'Umrah in the twenties.

3552 - Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, he said: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, he said: Sufyan narrated to us, from Qays ibn Muslim, from Tariq ibn Shihab, he said: I asked Ibn Mas'ud about a woman from among us who wished to combine an 'Umrah with her Hajj. He said: I hear God say: "The Hajj is in well-known months." I do not see her except in the months of the Hajj.

3553 - Ahmad ibn al-Miqdam narrated to me, he said: Hazzam al-Qati'i narrated to us, he said: I heard Muhammad ibn Sirin say: No one of the people of knowledge doubted that 'Umrah outside the months of the Hajj is more excellent than 'Umrah in the months of the Hajj.

= And the like of these, which would take too long to fully recount in this book, indicate that the meaning of the saying of whoever said: the time of the Hajj is three complete months, is that they are other than the months of 'Umrah, and that they are months for the act of Hajj and not the act of 'Umrah, even though the act of Hajj is only performed in some of them, not all of them.

* *

As for those who said that the interpretation of this is: Shawwal, Dhu al-Qa'dah, and ten (days) of Dhu al-Hijjah, they said: Allah, may His praise be exalted, by His saying "The Hajj is in well-known months" intended to inform His creation of the appointed time of their Hajj, not to report the time of 'Umrah. They said: As for 'Umrah, the entire year is a time for it, because the reports from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) are consistent that he performed 'Umrah in some months of the Hajj, and no report contrary to that has been authenticated from him. They said: Since that is so, and since the act of Hajj ends its time with the passing of the tenth day of Dhu al-Hijjah, it is known that the meaning of His saying "The Hajj is in well-known months" is only the appointed time of the Hajj: two months and part of the third.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct view in this matter, in our opinion, is the view of whoever said: the meaning of that is: the Hajj is two months and ten days of the third; because that is a report from God about the appointed time of the Hajj, and there is no act of Hajj to be performed after the passing of the days of Mina. It is therefore known that He did not mean by that the entire third month, and when it is not meant in its entirety, the saying of whoever said "and ten (days) of Dhu al-Hijjah" is correct.

* *

If someone says: How, then, was it said: "The Hajj is in well-known months," when it is two months and part of the third?

It is said: The Arabs do not refrain, especially with respect to times, from using the like of this. They say: "Today there are two days since I have not seen him," and they mean by that: one day and part of another. Likewise His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Whoever hastens in two days, there is no sin upon him﴾ [al-Baqarah: 203], whereas he hastens in one day and a half. And one of them may do an action in an hour, then express it as general over a year or a month, saying: "I visited him this year," or "I came to him today," and he does not mean by that that his action took place from the beginning of the time he mentioned to its end, but rather that he did it at that time and in that period. Likewise "The Hajj is in months," and what is meant by it is: the Hajj is two months and another part. [[See the detailed discussion of this in al-Farra's Ma'ani al-Qur'an, 1:152.]]

* *

So the meaning of the verse is then: The appointed time of your Hajj, O people, is two months and part of the third, and it is Shawwal, Dhu al-Qa'dah, and ten (days) of Dhu al-Hijjah.

* *

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So whoever imposes upon himself the Hajj therein﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His saying, may His praise be exalted: "So whoever imposes upon himself the Hajj therein," meaning: whoever makes the Hajj obligatory upon himself and binds himself to it during them, that is, during the well-known months that He has explained. Making it obligatory upon himself means the resolve to carry out all that God has made obligatory upon the pilgrim to do, and to abandon all that God has commanded him to abandon.

* *

The people of interpretation differed concerning the meaning by which a man becomes one who imposes the Hajj, after they all agreed that the meaning of "fard" is: obligating and binding.

Some of them said: The imposing of the Hajj is the talbiyah (the invocation "Labbayk").

Those who said this:

3554 - Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, he said: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, he said: Warqa' narrated to us, from Abd Allah al-Madani ibn Dinar, from Ibn Umar, regarding His saying: "So whoever imposes upon himself the Hajj therein," he said: One who declares ihram for Hajj.

3555 - Ibn Wakee' narrated to us, he said: my father narrated to us. = And al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq informed us. = He said: al-Thawri informed us, from al-Ala' ibn al-Musayyib, from Ata', he said: The talbiyah.

3556 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Mihran narrated to us. = And Ali narrated to us, he said: Zayd narrated to us. = All of them, from Sufyan al-Thawri: "So whoever imposes upon himself the Hajj therein," he said: The obligation is ihram, and ihram is the talbiyah.

3557 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, he said: al-Hammani narrated to us, he said: Shurayk narrated to us, from Ibrahim - meaning Ibn Muhajir - from Mujahid: "So whoever imposes upon himself the Hajj therein," he said: The obligation is the talbiyah.

3558 - Ahmad ibn Hazim narrated to us, he said: Warqa' narrated to us, from Abd Allah ibn Dinar, from Ibn Umar: "So whoever imposes upon himself the Hajj therein," he said: Ihlal (declaring the talbiyah).

3559 - Ahmad ibn Hazim narrated to me, he said: Abu Nu'aym narrated to us, he said: Shurayk narrated to us, from Mughirah, from Ibrahim, he said: The obligation is the talbiyah, and he may return if he wishes, as long as he has not entered ihram.

3560 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, he said: Ma'mar informed us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "So whoever imposes upon himself the Hajj therein," he said: The obligation: the ihlal.

3561 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, he said: Ma'mar informed us, from Ibn Tawus, from his father: "So whoever imposes upon himself the Hajj therein," he said: The talbiyah.

3562 - Ibrahim ibn Abd Allah ibn Muslim narrated to us, he said: Abu Amr al-Darir narrated to us, he said: Hammad ibn Salamah informed us, from Jabr ibn Habib, he said: I asked al-Qasim ibn Muhammad about: "Whoever imposes the Hajj therein," and he said: When you have bathed, put on your garment and recited the talbiyah, then you have imposed the Hajj.

[[Note on report 3562: Ibrahim ibn Abd Allah ibn Muslim ibn Ma'iz, Abu Muslim al-Kaji, the hafiz: a trustworthy and noble transmitter, praised by al-Buhturi. He wrote a book on the Sunan. He died in 292 AH, having nearly reached a hundred. Biographies in Tadhkirat al-Huffaz 2:176–177 and Tarikh Baghdad 6:120–124. "Abu 'Amr al-Darir al-Akbar" is Hafs ibn Umar al-Basri, a trustworthy man, very firm in the Sunnah, and among the scholars of inheritance, arithmetic, poetry, the days of the people, and jurisprudence. He died in 220 AH, aged over seventy. In the printed edition it reads "Abu 'Amr," which is an error. Jabr ibn Habib: trustworthy and an imam in language. Biography in al-Tahdhib and al-Kabir 1/2/242, and Ibn Abi Hatim 1/1/533. They mention no narration from him except from Umm Kulthum bint Abi Bakr al-Siddiq, and it is thus useful here to note his narration also from her nephew, al-Qasim ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr.]]

Others said: The imposing of the Hajj is entering into ihram for it.

Those who said this:

3563 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, he said: Abu Salih narrated to us, he said: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas: "So whoever imposes upon himself the Hajj therein," he means: whoever enters into ihram for Hajj or 'Umrah.

3564 - Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, he said: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us. = And Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, he said: Abu Ahmad narrated to us. = And al-Muthanna narrated to me, he said: Abu Nu'aym narrated to us. = All of them said: Sufyan narrated to us, from Mughirah, from Ibrahim: "So whoever imposes upon himself the Hajj therein," he said: Whoever enters into ihram. The wording is that of the hadith of Ibn Bashshar.

3565 - Ahmad narrated to us, he said: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, he said: Shurayk and al-Hasan ibn Salih narrated to us, from Layth, from Ata', he said: The obligation is the ihram.

3566 - al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hushaym narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj informed us, from Ata' and some of our shaykhs, from al-Hasan, regarding His saying: "So whoever imposes upon himself the Hajj therein," both said: The imposing of the Hajj is the ihram.

3567 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: "So whoever imposes upon himself the Hajj therein," he said: This is at the time of ihram.

3568 - Ahmad ibn Hazim narrated to us, he said: Abu Nu'aym narrated to us, he said: Husayn ibn Aqil narrated to us, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn Abbas, he said: The obligation is the ihram.

3569 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, he said: Husayn ibn Aqil al-Khurasani informed us, he said: I heard al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim say, and he mentioned the like of it.

3570 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, he said: al-Thawri informed us, he said: al-Mughirah informed us, from Ibrahim: "So whoever imposes upon himself the Hajj therein," he said: Whoever enters into ihram.

* *

The commentator Abu Ja'far said: This second opinion may mean what we said, that the state of ihram (the sacred state entered upon for pilgrimage), in the view of the one who held it, is the obligation undertaken by resolve. It may also mean that in his view it is resolve together with the talbiyah (the chant "Labbayk"), as those who held the first opinion said.

We said that the obligation of the Hajj is the ihram because of the ijma' (scholarly consensus) of all on this. We also said that ihram is a man's binding himself to what the one in ihram must bind himself to, as we described just above. This is because the matter cannot be free of one of three possibilities:

Either a man is not in ihram except by the talbiyah and by doing everything that the one who obligates himself to ihram must do. If that is so, then it would follow that he is not in ihram except by stripping for ihram, and whoever has not stripped is not in ihram. But the consensus of all that a person may be in ihram even without having stripped of his clothes, by his obligating himself to ihram, indicates that he may be in ihram even if he has not chanted the talbiyah, since the talbiyah is one of the rites of ihram just as stripping is one of its rites. And their consensus that a person may be in ihram while leaving some of the rites of his Hajj indicates that the ruling on his other rites is the same as the ruling on these.

Or, since this view is invalid, one might say that a person may be in ihram even without the talbiyah, without stripping, and without the resolve we described. But the consensus of all that one who has not resolved to enter ihram and has not obligated himself to it, if he is a person of legal capacity, is not in ihram, indicates the falsity of this view.

When these two views are shown to be invalid, the third view is shown to be correct: that a man may be in ihram by obligating himself to it through his resolve, in the manner we explained, even if this is not manifested by stripping, the talbiyah, and performing some of the acts required of him in his rites. And if this is established, then what we said is established: that the obligation of the Hajj is that whose binding is joined to resolve, [[In the printed edition: "هو ما مر إيجابه بالعزم" ("is that whose binding has passed by resolve"), which is a corrupt distortion with no meaning. The evidence for the correctness of my reading of this text is his statement at the beginning of the explanation of this word in the verse: "and his binding it upon himself is the resolve to perform all that God has obligated the pilgrim to perform..." and then what follows regarding the detailed meaning of "al-fard" (the obligation). The context therefore requires what I have established in my reading of the text.]] in the manner we explained before.

Abu Ja'far said: The correct view on this matter, in my opinion, is that Allah, exalted is His praise, forbade, from the time the Hajj becomes obligatory during the months of Hajj, the rafath, when He said: "Whoever undertakes the Hajj in them, there shall be no rafath." And "al-rafath" in the speech of the Arabs originally means indecency in speech, as we have explained previously, and then it is used as a metaphor for intercourse. [See what has passed in Part 3: 487, 488.] Since this is so, [In the printed edition: "fa-in kana dhalika kadhalika," which is an error; the correct reading is what I have established.] and since the people of knowledge have differed in its interpretation, and regarding this prohibition from Allah, whether it concerns some meanings of "rafath" or all of its meanings, it is necessary that it be (understood as) covering all of its meanings, since no report has come [specifying] the restriction of "rafath" to the speech of men with women, to the exclusion of the other meanings of "rafath" [Context: "since no report has come that must be accepted"], which must be accepted, since it is not permissible to transfer the ruling of the apparent wording of a verse to an inner interpretation except by a established proof.

* *

If one says: Its ruling, moving from the general apparent meaning to the inner interpretation, is transmitted by consensus. That is because all of them are in agreement that "rafath," in the presence of others than women, is not forbidden to one in the state of ihram. It was therefore known from this that the verse refers to some of "rafath" and not to all of it. Since this is so, nothing of the meanings of "rafath" should be forbidden to the one in ihram except what consensus has agreed upon forbidding to him, or what a binding proof has established as forbidden, which must be accepted.

It is said: What the verse has specified and permitted is excluded from the prohibition, and the prohibition remains valid for all of the meaning of "rafath" that the proof has not specified by the verse, just as its ruling would have been had nothing been specified from it. For what has been specified from it and removed from its generality, we are only obliged to remove its ruling of prohibition by the command of One whose command may not be opposed. So the ruling of what the meaning of the verse encompasses, after what has been specified from it, is the ruling that the servants are bound to fulfil by it had nothing been specified from it, because the reason in what has not been specified from it, after what has been specified from it, is analogous to the reason in it before anything was specified from it.

Abu Ja'far said: The most preferable of the sayings we have mentioned regarding the interpretation of the verse is the saying of those who said: the meaning of His words "and no fusuq" is the prohibition of disobedience to Allah in hunting game, and the doing of what Allah forbade the muhrim to do in his state of ihram.

This is because Allah, exalted is His praise, said: "Whoever undertakes the Hajj in them, there shall be no rafath and no fusuq," meaning by that: one shall not commit rafath, nor commit fusuq, that is, one shall not do what Allah forbade him to do in his state of ihram, nor shall he depart from obedience to Allah during his ihram. We know that Allah, exalted is His praise, has forbidden His acts of disobedience to every person, whether in ihram or not; likewise He forbade mutual insulting by nicknames in the state of ihram and otherwise, by His words: ﴿And do not defame one another, nor call one another by offensive nicknames﴾ [Al-Hujurat: 11], and He forbade the Muslim to abuse his brother in every state, whether or not he has undertaken Hajj.

Since this is so, there is no doubt that what Allah forbade the servant of fusuq in his state of ihram and his undertaking of Hajj is what was not fusuq in his state of non-ihram and before he entered ihram for his Hajj, just as the rafath which He forbade him in the state of his undertaking Hajj is that which was permitted for him absolutely before his ihram. For there is no sense in saying regarding what Allah has forbidden to His creatures in all states: "Let none of you do in the state of ihram what is forbidden for him to do in every state." For the specificity of the state of ihram has no basis, since it applies generally to all states, both non-ihram and ihram.

Since this is so, it is evident that what the muhrim was forbidden from in "fusuq," specified to his state of ihram, and it was said to him: "When you undertake Hajj, do not do it," is what was permitted for him absolutely before the state of his undertaking Hajj. That is what we have described and mentioned: that Allah, exalted is His praise, specified for the muhrim in his state of ihram the prohibition of: perfume, clothing, shaving, paring nails, killing game, and all else that Allah specified for the prohibition of the muhrim in his state of ihram.

* *

The interpretation of the verse, then, is: whoever undertakes Hajj during the months of Hajj and enters ihram in them, then he shall not commit rafath with women, by openly speaking to them of intercourse, nor have intercourse with them, nor commit fusuq by doing what Allah forbade in his state of ihram for his Hajj, such as killing game, taking hair, paring nails, and other things Allah forbade him to do while in ihram.

* *

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿and no jidal (disputing) in the Hajj﴾

Abu Ja'far said: The exegetes differed regarding this.

Some of them said: the meaning of that is the prohibition for the muhrim to dispute with anyone.

Then those who held this view differed.

Some of them said: He forbade disputing with one's companion until one angers him.

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 197 (part 4 of 6):**

[[Report 3682: Waqid al-Khalqani is "Waqid ibn 'Abd Allah al-Khalqani al-Kufi al-Hanzali." Al-Bukhari mentioned him in *al-Kabir* (4/2/173) and said: "He heard from 'Ata'." 3716 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid regarding His words: "*wa la jidal fi al-hajj*," he said: God has made clear the matter of the pilgrimage and its markers, so there is no speech in it.

* *

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: The most correct of these interpretations of His words, "*wa la jidal fi al-hajj*," is the saying of the one who said: The meaning is: disputing in the pilgrimage and its time has been nullified; its matter and its time have become steady upon one time and uniform rites, not differing, and there is no contention or quarreling in it. That is because God, may His remembrance be exalted, informed that the time of the pilgrimage is "*ashhur ma'lumat*" (well-known months), then He negated from its time the disagreement in which the Jahiliyya, in their polytheism, used to differ.

We chose this interpretation and saw it as more correct than what contradicts it, because of what we have already set forth just now in the explanation of His words: "*wa la fusuq*," that it is not permissible for what was specifically forbidden in that situation [except what is] an absolutely permitted matter in the situation that contradicts it,[[This addition is necessary for the sentence to be sound. In the original also: "that it is not permissible that God specifically..." and the soundness of the sentence requires what I have established.]] which is the state of *al-ihlal* (being out of ihram). That is because the ruling on what was singled out for it is the ruling of the state of ihram; if the state of ihram and the state of ihlal are equal in it, then there is no reason to single it out for one state rather than another, while it has been applied generally to all states. Since that is so, and there is no sense in the saying of one who interprets His words, "*wa la jidal fi al-hajj*," to mean: do not dispute with your companion until you anger him, except one of two meanings:

Either he intended: do not dispute with him in falsehood until you anger him, and that has no basis, because God, the Mighty and Majestic, has forbidden disputing in falsehood in every state, whether the one disputing is in ihram or out of it. So there is no basis for singling out the state of ihram for the prohibition, since the state of ihram and the state of ihlal are equal in God's prohibition of it.

Or he intended: do not dispute with him in truth, and that too has no basis. For if a man in ihram saw someone intending a grave sin, it would be obligatory for him to dispute with him in repelling him from it; or if he saw him trying to wrong him and take from him a right which he had seized from him, it would be incumbent upon him to dispute with him about it and argue until he rescues it from him. Disputing and quarreling among people occur only in one of two ways: either from wrongdoing or from rightness. So if one of its two aspects is impermissible to do in any state, and the other aspect is impermissible to abandon in any state, then which of its aspects was singled out for prohibition in the state of ihram?

Likewise, there is no basis for the saying of one who interpreted it to mean *al-sibab* (abuse), because God, may His remembrance be exalted, has forbidden the believers to abuse one another through the tongue of His Messenger (ﷺ) in every state. He (ﷺ) said:

3717 - "Abusing a Muslim is *fusuq* (wickedness), and fighting him is *kufr* (disbelief)."

[[Hadith 3717: Al-Tabari narrated it without an isnad. It is a sound and established hadith from many transmissions. Ahmad in the *Musnad* (3647) narrated it from the hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud. Likewise the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim), al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah narrated it. See the rest of its numbers in the *Musnad* in *al-Istidrak* (886). It is also established from the narration of other Companions; see *al-Fath al-Kabir* (2:150–151).]]

= So if a Muslim is forbidden from abusing a Muslim in every one of his states, whether in ihram or not in ihram, then there is no basis for saying: "Do not abuse him in the state of ihram" if you are in ihram. = And in what was related from the Messenger of God (ﷺ) is the report that:

3718 - Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated it to us, saying: Wahb ibn Jarir narrated to me, saying: Shu'ba narrated to us, from Sayyar, from Abu Hazim, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Whoever makes the pilgrimage to this House and does not commit *rafath* (lewd speech) nor *fusuq* (wickedness), will come out like the day his mother bore him."

3719 - 'Ali ibn Sahl narrated to me, saying: al-Hajjaj narrated to us, saying: Shu'ba narrated to us, from Sayyar, from Abu Hazim, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Whoever makes the pilgrimage to this House and does not commit *rafath* nor *fusuq*, will come out from his sins like the day his mother bore him."

[[Hadith 3718–3720: "Sayyar" is with a fathah on the sin and a shaddah on the ya'; his biography has passed at 39. Abu Hazim here is al-Ash'ja'i, whose name is "Salman," mawla of 'Izza al-Ash'jaʻiyya. He is a Tabi'i and trustworthy; the authors of the six books narrated from him. This "Abu Hazim" is not Abu Hazim Salama ibn Dinar, the companion of Sahl ibn Sa'd, for Salama did not hear from Abu Hurayra, as the Hafiz stated in *al-Fath* (3:302). The hadith was narrated by Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi (2519) from Sayyar and Mansur, both from Abu Hazim. Ahmad in the *Musnad* (9302; 2:410 Halabi) and al-Bukhari (3:302–303) both narrated it through the route of Shu'ba from Sayyar. It will come a fourth time through the route of Shu'ba from Sayyar: 3725.]]

3720 - Ahmad ibn al-Walid narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'ba narrated to us, from Sayyar, from Abu Hazim, from Abu Hurayra, from the Prophet (ﷺ), like the hadith of Ibn al-Muthanna, from Wahb ibn Jarir.

3721 - Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'ba narrated to us, from Mansur, from Abu Hazim, from Abu Hurayra, from the Prophet (ﷺ), the like of it also.

3722 - Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Walid narrated to us, saying: Shu'ba narrated to us, saying: Mansur informed me, saying: I heard Abu Hazim narrate from Abu Hurayra, from the Prophet (ﷺ), something similar. [[Hadiths 3721, 3722: Mansur is Ibn al-Mu'tamir. Mansur did hear this hadith from Abu Hazim, as he stated in the second isnad. Thus the doubt that he did not hear it from him is removed, as will be explained at 3726, 3727. This hadith through this route is narrated by al-Tayalisi (2519) from Shu'ba, as we indicated before. It is also narrated by Ahmad in the *Musnad* (9300; 2:410 Halabi) and al-Bukhari (4:17, *Fath*), both through the route of Shu'ba from Mansur.]]

3723 - Tamim ibn al-Muntasir narrated to us, saying: Ishaq informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn 'Ubayd Allah informed us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Hazim, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Whoever makes the pilgrimage to this House and does not commit *rafath* nor *fusuq*, comes out from his sins as the day his mother bore him." [[Hadith 3723: It has the same meaning as the hadiths before and after it. Al-Daraqutni narrated it in his *Sunan* (p. 282) through the route of Hajjaj ibn Arta'a from al-A'mash with this isnad, with the wording: "Whoever makes the pilgrimage or the 'umra, and does not commit *rafath* nor *fusuq*, returns in his state the day his mother bore him." Hajjaj ibn Arta'a thus added the wording "or 'umra."
The Hafiz in *al-Fath* (3:302) pointed to this narration of al-Daraqutni and said: "But in the isnad to al-A'mash there is weakness."]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 197 (part 5 of 6):

3724 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' and Abu Usama narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Abu Hazim, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said, and he mentioned the like of it, except that he said: "He returns as his mother bore him."

[[Hadith 3724: Sufyan is al-Thawri. This hadith by this route is narrated by Ahmad in al-Musnad, 10279 (2: 484, Halabi), from Waki' and Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi, both from Sufyan. Likewise al-Bukhari narrated it, 4: 17 (Fath), from Muhammad ibn Yusuf, who is al-Firyabi, from Sufyan.
Ahmad also narrated it, 7375 (2: 248, Halabi), from Sufyan, from Mansur. The Sufyan here is Ibn Uyayna.]]

3725 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Abu Usama narrated to us, from Shu'ba, from Sayyar, from Abu Hazim, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said, and he mentioned something similar, except that he said: "He returns to his family like the day his mother bore him."

3726 - Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Yahya ibn Abi Bukayr narrated to us, from Ibrahim ibn Tahman, from Mansur, from Hilal ibn Yasaf, from Abu Hazim, from Abu Hurayra, that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said, and he mentioned something similar, except that he said: "He returns to his family like the day his mother bore him."

3727 - Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Yahya ibn Abi Bukayr narrated to us, from Ibrahim ibn Tahman, from Mansur, from Hilal ibn Yasaf, from Abu Hazim, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Whoever performs the Hajj to this House, meaning the Ka'ba, and does not commit obscenity (rafath) or transgression (fusuq), returns as on the day his mother bore him."

[[Hadiths 3726 and 3727: they are one repeated chain for a single hadith. In the first he did not mention its full wording, and in the second he mentioned it. I do not know the reason for this.
Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim is al-Dawraqi, the memorizer (al-Hafiz), who has passed several times, the last being 3223. Yahya ibn Abi Bukayr, with a damma on the ba' and a fatha on the kaf, al-Asadi al-Qaysi: a well-known reliable narrator, from whom the authors of the six canonical books narrated. He died in 208 or 209. In the printed edition here it appears as "Yahya ibn Abi Kathir," which is an error, for Ibn Abi Kathir died long before, in 129 or 132, and al-Dawraqi was born in 166, so it is not conceivable that he narrated from him.
Ibrahim ibn Tahman al-Khurasani: reliable, sound in hadith; the six imams narrated from him. Mansur is Ibn al-Mu'tamir, as has passed in some earlier chains.
Hilal ibn Yasaf, also said to be Isaf, al-Ashja'i al-Kufi: a major reliable Successor (tabi'i). Perhaps he is older than Abu Hazim. "Yasaf" is with a kasra on the yā' and a fatha on the sīn, lightened. Likewise "Isaf" with a hamza in place of the yā'. In the printed edition here, in both chains, it appears as "Hilal ibn Yasar," which is a plain error.
This hadith by this route is narrated by al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan al-Kubra, 5: 262, through Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Sa'igh, from Yahya ibn Abi Bukayr, with this chain.
Mansur heard this hadith directly from Abu Hazim, as he stated in the earlier narration, 3722. Al-Hafiz said in Fath al-Bari, 4: 17: "Thus the objection of one who gave it a defect by the disagreement over Mansur is dismissed, because al-Bayhaqi reported it through Ibrahim ibn Tahman, from Mansur, from Hilal ibn Yasaf, from Abu Hazim, adding a man. If Ibrahim memorized it, perhaps Mansur heard it from Hilal, then met Abu Hazim and heard it from him, and narrated it in both forms."
We add here that Ahmad also narrated the hadith in al-Musnad, 10414 (2: 494, Halabi), from Jarir, from Mansur, from Abu Hatim [sic], and likewise Muslim narrated it, 1: 382, through Jarir.
Muslim also narrated it through Abu Awana, Abu al-Ahwas, Mis'ar, al-Thawri and Shu'ba, all from Mansur, from Abu Hazim. Likewise al-Nasa'i narrated it, 2: 3-4, through al-Fudayl ibn Iyad, from Mansur, with it.]]

3728 - Al-Fadl ibn al-Sabbah narrated to us, saying: Hushaym ibn Bashir narrated to us, from Sayyar, from Abu Hazim, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Whoever performs the Hajj for God, and does not commit obscenity or transgression, returns in the likeness of the day his mother bore him."

[[Hadith 3728: Ahmad narrated it in al-Musnad, 7136, from Hushaym by this chain. Likewise Muslim narrated it, 1: 382-383, from Sa'id ibn Mansur, from Hushaym with it. See also what will come, number 3059.]]

* *

[[The beginning of this discussion is on p. 150, his statement: "concerning what is reported from the Messenger of God (ﷺ) of the report... an indication." I have separated the report from its subject by the successive hadiths.]]

It is a clear indication that His saying "no disputing in the Hajj" means a negation concerning the Hajj, namely that during its time there should be no dispute or wrangling, not a prohibition against people disputing among themselves about matters that concern them or do not concern them.

For he (ﷺ) informed that whoever performs the Hajj and does not commit obscenity or transgression deserves from God the honour which he described as deserved by his pilgrimage, having abstained from the obscenity and transgression which God forbade the pilgrim in his Hajj, without adding disputing to them. So if the disputing which God mentioned in His saying "no disputing in the Hajj" were something God forbade by this verse, in the manner of the interpretation of one who interpreted it as wrangling and quarrels, or abuse and the like, then he (ﷺ) would not have singled out, for the honour that he mentioned the pilgrim deserves, the one whose matter he described, by abstaining from two of the things God forbade in his Hajj, without the third which is joined with them.

But since the meaning of the third differs from the meaning of its two companions, in that it is a report, according to the meaning we have described, while the other two carry the meaning of prohibition, which the Prophet (ﷺ) informed is what the one who abstains from them in his Hajj deserves, of the honour from God which he described, the honour of God that he reported He would bestow on him, since they carry the meaning of prohibition [[In the printed edition: "idha kanata bi-ma'na al-nahy" ("when they are in the sense of prohibition"), which is an error; the correct reading is what I have given.]] and the one who refrains from them is obedient to God by his refraining from them, he omitted mentioning the third, [[In the printed edition: "wa-tark dhikr al-thalitha" with a wa, which is an interpolation by the copyists without doubt. The construction of this whole sentence is: "But since the meaning of the third differs from the meaning of its two companions... since they carry the meaning of prohibition, and the one who refrains from them is obedient to God by refraining from them... he omitted mentioning the third." By this the correction in the two previous places is shown to be right.]] since it was not in their meaning, and its way was different from theirs.

* *

Given that this is so, then of the readings that differ in the i'rab (grammatical inflection) between "al-jidal" and "al-rafath wa-al-fusuq," the one most deserving of recitation is that which lets the hearer, if he is one of the people of understanding in the languages, know that the reason why the two i'rabs were differentiated is the difference in their meanings.

And if it were correct to recite all of it with a uniform i'rab, despite the difference in meanings, since the Arabs sometimes make one part of speech follow another in inflection while their meanings differ, especially in this type of speech, then...

Thus, the reading most pleasing to me in this matter, since the matter is as I have described, is the reading of the one who recites: "fa-la rafatha wa-la fusuqa wa-la jidala fi al-hajj" (so there is no obscenity, no transgression, and no disputing in the Hajj), with "al-rafath" and "al-fusuq" in the nominative and with tanwin, and "al-jidal" in the accusative without tanwin. This is the reading of the majority of the Basrans and many of the people of Mecca, among them Abd Allah ibn Kathir and Abu Amr ibn al-'Ala'. [[For a full detailed account of this, see al-Farra's Ma'ani al-Qur'an, 1: 120-122.]]

* *

As for the statement of the one who said: its meaning is a prohibition against the disagreement of those who differ over who has performed the more complete Hajj, and those who said: its meaning is a prohibition against one saying "the Hajj is tomorrow," contradicting the other who says "the Hajj is today," this is an opinion whose transmission is enough to dispense with citing evidence for its weakness and feebleness, [[Thus in the original: "'ala wahna'ihi" ("on its feebleness"), which is an old error in the speech of the jurists. Al-Mutarrizi said in al-Maghrib, 2: 265: "His saying, 'if she menstruates while the kingdom is in a state of wahaʾ, it is not counted.' The wahaʾ with a long vowel is an error; the correct form is al-wahy (with a fatha then a sukun), the verbal noun of 'wahiya al-habl yahya wahyan,' meaning it weakened." I fear that this is from the copyist of the commentary and not from Abu Ja'far, and that the original was "'ala wahyihi wa-da'fihi" (on its weakness and feebleness), since he has used the word al-wahy repeatedly in earlier passages. But I have not been able to find it in this part of the text, though I later found it in this part of the text, 4: 18, line 7.]] for it is a statement whose soundness cannot be recognized except by a widely transmitted report or a truthful report that makes knowledge necessary that this was so, and then the verse would have come down prohibiting it; or the meaning would be in some of the meanings of jidal and not others, and there is no report about this in the manner we have described.

* *

As for our evidence for what we have said, that it is a negation by God, mighty and majestic, concerning the months of the Hajj, it is the disagreement which the pre-Islamic people used to have among themselves about them, before, as we have described. [[In the printed edition: "al-ikhtilaf" with the fa' dropped; the correct form includes it, otherwise the sentence is disjointed.]]

As for our evidence that the Jahiliyya used to do this, it is the widely transmitted report among the people of reports that the Jahiliyya used to do that, together with the indication in the saying of God, exalted is His name: ﴿Indeed, the postponing (al-nasi') is an increase in disbelief by which those who disbelieve are led astray; they make it lawful one year and forbidden another year﴾ [al-Tawba: 37].

* *

The interpretation of His, exalted be He, words: ﴿And whatever good you do, God knows it﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His praise be great, He means: Do, O believers, what I have commanded you in your Hajj, of completing its rites and performing your obligation which is incumbent upon you in your ihram, and avoiding what I have commanded you to avoid, obscenity and transgression in your Hajj, so that you may deserve by it abundant reward. For whatever you do of that or other good and righteous deeds, seeking my pleasure and desiring my reward, I know it, and I have counted all of it, until I pay you its reward and recompense you for it, for nothing is hidden from me, and what you intend by your deeds is not concealed from me, since I am aware of your inner secrets and know the thoughts of your souls.

* *

The interpretation of His, exalted be He, words: ﴿And take provision, for the best provision is piety﴾

Abu Ja'far said: It is mentioned that this verse came down concerning people who used to perform the Hajj without provisions, and some of them, when they entered the state of ihram, would throw away what they had of provisions and take on other provisions. So God, may His praise be great, commanded those among them who had not been taking provisions to take provisions for their journey, and those who had provisions to keep their provisions and not throw them away.

Mention of the reports transmitted concerning that:

3729 - Al-Husayn ibn Ali al-Sada'i narrated to me, saying: Amr ibn Abd al-Ghaffar narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Suqa narrated to us, from Nafi', from Ibn Umar, who said: When they entered ihram and had provisions with them, they would throw them away and take other provisions. So God revealed: "And take provision, for the best provision is piety." They were forbidden from that and commanded to take provisions of biscuit, flour and roasted barley meal.

3730 - Muhammad ibn Abd Allah al-Makhrami narrated to us, saying: Shababa narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, from Amr ibn Dinar, from Ikrima, from Ibn Abbas, who said: They used to perform the Hajj without taking provisions, so this was revealed: "And take provision, for the best provision is piety." [[Report 3730: Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak al-Qurashi al-Makhrami (with a damma on the mim, a fatha on the kha', and a shadda on the ra' with a kasra), Abu Ja'far al-Baghdadi al-Mada'ini, the memorizer (al-Hafiz), judge of Hulwan. He died in 254 in Baghdad. He was one of the reliable narrators of great standing. In the printed edition it was "al-Makhzumi," which is an error, as you see.]]

3732 - Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, from Ibn Uyayna, from Ibn Suqa, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: It is biscuit and roasted barley meal.

So God said: Take provisions that will keep your faces from the people.

٣٧٥٠ - I was told by ʿAmmar, who said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabiʿ, regarding His words: "And take provision, for the best provision is taqwa (God-consciousness)." Some people from Yemen used to perform Hajj without taking provisions, so God commanded them to take provisions, and informed them that the best provision is taqwa.

٣٧٥١ - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, who said: Abu Nuʿaym narrated to us, who said: Sufyan narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Suqah, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, regarding "And take provisions": he said: sawiq (roasted-grain flour), daqiq (flour), and kaʿk (bread rings).

٣٧٥٢ - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, who said: Waki narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Muhammad ibn Suqah, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, regarding "And take provisions, for the best provision is taqwa," he said: khushkanaj and sawiq. [[In Lisan (kaʿk) and in al-Muʿarrab by al-Jawaliqi, p. 134: "khushkanan" has been used by the Arabs. The rajaz poet said: "O how wonderful is the kaʿk with shredded meat, / and khushkanan and sawiq mixed (with fat)." Khushkanaj is khushkanan, which is a food made of prepared flour.]]

٣٧٥٣ - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, who said: Waki narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿAta al-Bakkaʾi, who said: I heard al-Shaʿbi say regarding His words "And take provisions, for the best provision is taqwa": he said: It is food, and food was scarce at that time. He said: I asked: And what is food? He said: Dates and sawiq. [[The report 3753: The biography of "ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿAta" has passed at 3734, and that he is "al-Bakkaʾi". In the printed edition here it appears as "al-Bakkali" with a lam instead of a hamza, which is an error and a misreading.]]

٣٧٥٤ - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, who said: Ishaq narrated to us, who said: Abu Zuhayr narrated to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak regarding His words: "And take provisions, for the best provision is taqwa." The best provision of this world is the benefit from clothing, food and drink.

٣٧٥٥ - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, who said: Jarir narrated to us, from Mughirah, from Ibrahim: "And take provisions, for the best provision is taqwa." He said: People used to take provisions up to the ʿaqabah; when they reached that ʿaqabah they relied on God and did not take provisions. [[The ʿaqabah (with a damma and then a sukun) is the distance a traveler covers until he stops to rest.]]

٣٧٥٦ - Nasr ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman al-Awdi narrated to me, who said: al-Muharibi narrated to us, who said: Sufyan said regarding His words "And take provisions": they were commanded to take sawiq and kaʿk.

٣٧٥٧ - Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, who said: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, who said: My father informed me that he heard ʿIkrimah say regarding His words "And take provisions": it is sawiq and daqiq.

٣٧٥٨ - Yunus narrated to me, who said: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words "And take provisions, for the best provision is taqwa": Some Arab tribes used to forbid themselves provisions when they set out as pilgrims (hujjaj) and visitors (ʿummar), in order to be hosted by people. So God, blessed and exalted, said to them: "And take provisions, for the best provision is taqwa."

٣٧٥٩ - ʿAmr ibn ʿAbd al-Hamid al-Amili narrated to us, who said: Sufyan narrated to us, from ʿAmr, from ʿIkrimah, who said: People used to come to Makkah without provisions, so God revealed: "And take provisions, for the best provision is taqwa." [[The report 3759: ʿAmr ibn ʿAbd al-Hamid al-Amili, a teacher of al-Tabari: I do not know who he is, I have not found a biography of him, and perhaps he is a corruption of someone I do not know.]]

* *

Abu Jaʿfar said: The interpretation of the verse, then, is: whoever has made Hajj obligatory upon himself in the months of Hajj and has entered the state of ihram in them, then let him not commit obscenity (rafath) or transgression (fusuq). For the matter of Hajj has been made straight for you, and your Lord has made known to you its appointed times and limits. So be mindful of God regarding what He has commanded you and forbidden you concerning the matter of your Hajj and its rites; for whatever good you do, which He has commanded you or urged you to, He knows it. And take from your sustenance what will suffice you to reach the fulfilment of your Lord's obligation upon you in your Hajj and its rites. For there is no righteousness before God, may His praise be exalted, in your leaving off provisioning for yourselves and asking people (for help), nor in squandering your sustenance and spoiling it. Rather, righteousness lies in the God-consciousness of your Lord, by abstaining from what He has forbidden you during your journey for Hajj and by doing what He has commanded you, for that is the best provision, so take provision from it.

It is in a similar sense to what we have said that the report has been transmitted from al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim.

٣٧٦٠ - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, who said: Ishaq narrated to us, who said: Abu Zuhayr narrated to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak regarding His words "for the best provision is taqwa": He said: And taqwa is acting in obedience to God.

We have already explained the meaning of "taqwa" previously, in a way that makes repeating it unnecessary. [[See what has passed: 1:232, 233, 364.]]

* *

The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: {And be mindful of Me, O people of understanding (ulu al-albab)} (197).

Abu Jaʿfar said: By this, may His praise be exalted, He means: Be mindful of Me, O people of intellect and understanding, by performing My obligations upon you, which I have made incumbent upon you in your Hajj and its rites and other than that of My religion which I have prescribed for you; and fear My punishment by avoiding My prohibitions which I have forbidden you. Through that you will be saved from what you fear of My anger and punishment, and you will attain what you seek of success in My gardens.

* *

God, may His remembrance be exalted, specified the address of this to the people of understanding (ulu al-albab), because they are the people who distinguish between truth and falsehood, the people of sound thought and of knowledge of the realities of things, which are perceived by the intellects and understood by the minds. He did not give any share in this address to others among the ignorant, since they are like shapes of livestock and forms of beasts; rather, they are even more astray in the path.

And "al-albab" is the plural of "lubb," which is intellect. [[See what has passed in volume 3: 383.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 198 (part 1 of 3):

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿There is no blame upon you for seeking bounty from your Lord﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: By this, may His mention be exalted, He means: there is no blame (junah) upon you, O believers.

And "junah" means sin/blame (haraj), [[See what has preceded in the explanation of "junah" in volume 3: 230, 231.]] as:

3761 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn Abbas: "There is no blame upon you for seeking bounty from your Lord," meaning: there is no sin upon you in buying and selling before the ihram and after it.

And His saying, "to seek bounty from your Lord," means: to seek bounty from your Lord's side.

It is said of this: "I sought bounty from Allah – and from the bounty of Allah – I seek it (abtaghihi) seeking (ibtigha')," when you ask for it and search for it, and "I sought it (bagha, abghihi) bagyan," [[See what has preceded in the explanation of "ibtagha" in volume 3: 508.]] as the poet 'Abd Bani al-Hasahas said:

"He sought you, and you did not seek him until you found him, as if you had promised him a meeting yesterday."
[[His Diwan: 41. It will come in the commentary at 4: 15–16 / 5: 45 (Bulaq). This verse is connected to three verses before it, and its meaning completes them in the matter of death: "I saw that death-events have not spared Muhammad... nor anyone, nor left anything immortal. Ah, I see no one granted respite from fate... and no one remaining, except that death lies in ambush for him. A band will meet you whose fighting you do not desire, as one who, when he resolves to meet the enemy, aims at him. He sought you, and you did not seek him..."
As for his saying "until (hatta) you found him": the Diwan's version is "illa wajadtahu" (except you found him). The version in al-Tabari is rare, and it is a witness that one rarely finds, for "hatta" to come in the sense of "illa" in exception. Ibn Hisham mentioned this in al-Mughni 1: 111, saying after mentioning the senses of "hatta": "And in the sense of 'illa' in exception, and this is the least of them, and few mention it."]]
That is, your seeking and searching.

And it was said: the meaning of "seeking the bounty from Allah" is seeking the provision of Allah through trade, and that this verse was revealed concerning people who would not trade once they had entered the state of ihram, thinking that this was righteousness; so He, may His praise be exalted, informed them that there is no righteousness in that, and that they may seek His bounty through buying and selling.

Those who said this:

3762 - Nasr ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Azdi narrated to me, saying: al-Maharibi narrated to us, from Amr ibn Dharr, from Mujahid, who said: They used to perform Hajj but not trade, so Allah revealed: "There is no blame upon you for seeking bounty from your Lord," he said: in the season (of Hajj).
