3860 – Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Zuhayr narrated to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak: "Remember God as you remember your fathers," meaning the remembrance of children of their fathers.

3861 – Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: 'Ata' said to me: "as you remember your fathers": "Abah! Ummah!" [i.e., "Daddy! Mummy!"]

3862 – Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Salih ibn 'Umar narrated to us, from 'Abd al-Malik, from 'Ata', who said: Like the child who clings to his father and mother.

3863 – It was reported to me by 'Ammar, who said: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi', regarding His words: "So when you have completed your rites, then remember God as you remember your fathers, or with even more remembrance," he says: as the children's remembrance of the fathers, or with even more intensity.

3864 – Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: My father related to me, saying: My uncle related to me, saying: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, His words: "So when you have completed your rites, then remember God as you remember your fathers, or with even more remembrance," he says: as children remember their fathers.

3865 – It was reported to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words: "as you remember your fathers," meaning the remembrance of children of their fathers.

* *

Others said: Rather, it was said to them: "Remember God as you remember your fathers," because when they completed their rites and called upon their Lord, they mentioned none but their fathers. So they were commanded to remember God in the manner of the remembrance of their fathers.

Those who said this:

3866 – Musa ibn Harun related to me, saying: 'Amr ibn Hammad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "So when you have completed your rites, then remember God as you remember your fathers, or with even more remembrance," he said: When the Arabs completed their rites and stayed in Mina, a man would stand and ask God, saying: "O God, my father was one of great platter and great tent, of much wealth; so give me the like of what You gave my father!" He does not mention God; he mentions only his fathers, and asks to be given in this world.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct interpretation in my view of this is to say: God, the Mighty and Majestic, commanded His believing servants to remember Him by obedience to Him, in submission to His command and in worship of Him, after the completion of their rites. That "remembrance" may well be the glorification (takbir) which He commanded in His words: ﴿And remember God during the numbered days﴾ [Qur'an 2:203], which He made obligatory upon whoever has completed his rite, after he has completed it; and He then obliged him to remember Him in a way that was not obligatory upon him before that. He urged him to be scrupulous in it, as children are scrupulous about remembering their fathers, through humbling himself before Him, and imploring Him with eagerness, in his needs, like the child's imploring of his parent, and of the infant to his mother and father, or even more so, since whatever blessing there was upon them and their fathers was from Him, and He is their Guardian.

We only said that the "remembrance" which God, the Mighty and Majestic, commanded the pilgrim after completing his rites, in His words: "So when you have completed your rites, then remember God as you remember your fathers, or with even more remembrance," is "possibly the glorification which we described," because there is no remembrance of God which He commanded His servants to perform after completing their rites, which had not been obligatory upon them before completing their rites, other than the glorification which God specified for the days of Mina.

Since that is so, and since it is known that He, the Mighty and Majestic, obligated upon His creatures, after completing their rites, a remembrance of Him which had not been obligatory upon them before that, and since none of His remembrances was specific to that time other than the glorification we mentioned, the soundness of what we have said regarding the interpretation of this has become clear, in accordance with what we described.

* *

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿So among the people is he who says, "Our Lord, give us in this world," and he has no share in the Hereafter﴾ (200)

Abu Ja'far said: By this, the Mighty and Majestic means: "So when you have completed your rites, O believers, then remember God as you remember your fathers, or with even more remembrance; and turn to Him with longing for what is with Him of good in this world and the Hereafter, with humility and supplication. Make your deeds purely for His face and for seeking His pleasure, and say: 'Our Lord, give us good in this world and good in the Hereafter, and protect us from the punishment of the Fire.' Do not be like those who have bought the life of this world at the price of the Hereafter, whose deeds were for this world and its adornment; so they ask their Lord only for its enjoyment, and have no portion in the reward of God, nor share in His gardens and the noble things He has prepared for His friends." This is as the people of interpretation have said.

3867 – Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from 'Asim, from Abu Wa'il: "So among the people is he who says, 'Our Lord, give us in this world,'" [meaning]: "Grant us sheep! Grant us camels!" "and he has no share in the Hereafter."

3868 – Ahmad ibn Ishaq related to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from 'Asim, from Abu Wa'il, who said: In the Jahiliyyah they used to say: "Grant us camels!" Then he mentioned the like of it.

3869 – Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: I heard Abu Bakr ibn 'Ayyash regarding His words: "So among the people is he who says, 'Our Lord, give us in this world,' and he has no share in the Hereafter," he said: They used to stand, meaning the people of the Jahiliyyah, after completing their rites, and say: "O God, provide us with camels! O God, provide us with sheep!" So God revealed this verse: "So among the people is he who says, 'Our Lord, give us in this world,' and he has no share in the Hereafter." Abu Kurayb said: I said to Yahya ibn Adam: "From whom is this?" He said: Abu Bakr ibn 'Ayyash narrated to us, from 'Asim, from Abu Wa'il.

3870 – Tamim ibn al-Muntasir related to us, saying: Ishaq informed us, from al-Qasim ibn 'Uthman, from Anas: "So among the people is he who says, 'Our Lord, give us in this world, and he has no share in the Hereafter,'" he said: They used to circumambulate the House naked and supplicate, saying: "O God, give us rain, grant us victory over our enemy, and return us righteous to the righteous!"

3871 – Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, from 'Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the words of God, blessed and exalted: "So among the people is he who says, 'Our Lord, give us in this world,'" [meaning] victory and provision, and they ask nothing for their Hereafter.

3872 – Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

3873 – Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding God's words: "So among the people is he who says, 'Our Lord, give us in this world, and he has no share in the Hereafter,'" [he said:] this is a servant who intends the world; for it he works, and for it he toils.

3874 – Musa narrated to us, saying: 'Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi regarding His words: "So among the people is he who says, 'Our Lord, give us in this world, and he has no share in the Hereafter,'" he said: When the Arabs completed their rites and stayed in Mina, none of them would remember God; rather he would mention his father and ask to be given in this world.

3875 – Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words: "So when you have completed your rites, then remember God as you remember your fathers, or with even more remembrance," he said: They were of three categories in those places that day: the Messenger of God (ﷺ), the people of disbelief, and the people of hypocrisy. "So among the people is he who says, 'Our Lord, give us in this world, and he has no share in the Hereafter'": they performed the pilgrimage only for the world and for asking, not desiring the Hereafter, nor believing in it. "And among them is he who says, 'Our Lord, give us good in this world,'" to the end of the verse. He said: The third category is: "And among the people is he who pleases you with his speech concerning the life of this world," to the end of the verse.

As for the meaning of "khalaq" (portion, share), we have explained it in another place, and mentioned the differences of those who differ regarding its interpretation, and the sound view we hold of its meaning, with evidence from proofs, and that it means "portion." That is sufficient to dispense with repeating it here.[[See what has preceded: 2:452–454.]]

The Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 2, Verse 201:

**The interpretation of His words, may He be exalted: ﴿And among them is he who says, "Our Lord, give us in this world good and in the Hereafter good, and protect us from the punishment of the Fire."﴾ (2:201)**

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: The people of *ta'wil* (interpretation, *tafsir*) differed regarding the meaning of "good" (*hasanah*) mentioned by God in this verse.

Some of them said: What is meant is: "And among the people is he who says: Our Lord, give us well-being in this world and well-being in the Hereafter."

Mention of those who said this:

3876 – Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: "Our Lord, give us in this world good and in the Hereafter good." He said: In this world, well-being; and in the Hereafter, well-being.

Qatadah said: A man said: "O God, whatever You would punish me with in the Hereafter, hasten it for me in this world." So he fell ill to the point that he was wasted away on his bed. [[*Adna* (أضنى) the man: when he is confined to bed from *dana*, which is severe illness until the body becomes emaciated.]] His condition was mentioned to the Prophet ﷺ, and the Prophet (ﷺ) came to him. It was said to him: "He prayed with such-and-such." The Prophet ﷺ said: "No one has the strength for God's punishment. Rather, say: 'Our Lord, give us in this world good and in the Hereafter good, and protect us from the punishment of the Fire.'" So he said it, and he did not remain more than a few days – or: a little – until he recovered.

3877 – Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Sa'id ibn al-Hakam narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Ayyub informed us, saying: Humayd narrated to me, saying: I heard Anas ibn Malik say: The Messenger of God ﷺ visited a man who had become like a plucked chick. The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "Were you supplicating God for something? Or asking God for something?" He said: I said: "O God, whatever You would punish me with in the Hereafter, punish me with it in this world!" He (ﷺ) said: "Glory be to God! Can anyone bear that or endure it? Why did you not say: 'O God, give us in this world good and in the Hereafter good, and protect us from the punishment of the Fire'?" [[The hadith (3877): Sa'id ibn al-Hakam is "Sa'id ibn Abi Maryam al-Jumahi," whose reference was previously mentioned at 22; he is trustworthy and authoritative. "Yahya ibn Ayyub" is al-Ghafiqi Abu al-Abbas al-Misri; he is trustworthy and retentive, and the authors of the six canonical books related from him.

Humayd is Ibn Abi Humayd al-Tawil; he is a trustworthy Successor (*tabi'i*) who heard from Anas ibn Malik and heard from Thabit al-Bunani from Anas. Some claimed that he did not hear from Anas except a few hadiths, and that the rest are only "from Thabit from Anas." The Hafiz (Ibn Hajar) rejected this strongly, saying: "Humayd explicitly stated his hearing from Anas of much material, and in Sahih al-Bukhari there is a considerable amount of that."

I have elaborated on this because the transmission of this hadith here includes Humayd's explicit statement of hearing from Anas. However, Ahmad and Muslim related it from the narration of Humayd, from Thabit, from Anas. Perhaps he heard it from Anas and from Thabit from Anas.

Ahmad related it in al-Musnad (12074; 3:107, Halabi edition) from Ibn Abi Adi and Abd Allah ibn Bakr al-Sahmi – both from Humayd from Thabit from Anas. Likewise Muslim related it (2:309) by way of Ibn Abi Adi from Humayd, then by way of Khalid ibn al-Harith from Humayd.

Ibn Kathir mentioned it (1:472–473) from the narration of al-Musnad, then said: "Muslim alone related it," meaning he alone related it apart from al-Bukhari.

Al-Suyuti mentioned it (1:233) and added its attribution to Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Abi Shaybah, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i, Abu Ya'la, Ibn Hibban, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Bayhaqi in *Shu'ab al-Iman*. But he erred, for he also attributed it to al-Bukhari, and I did not find it there, along with Ibn Kathir's definitive statement that Muslim alone related it.]]

* *

Others said: Rather, God, mighty and majestic, meant by "good" in this place – in this world – knowledge and worship, and in the Hereafter – Paradise.

Mention of those who said this:

3878 – Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Abbad narrated to us, from Hisham ibn Hassan, from al-Hasan, regarding: "And among them is he who says, 'Our Lord, give us in this world good and in the Hereafter good'": He said: The good in this world is knowledge and worship, and in the Hereafter, Paradise.

3879 – Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Amr ibn Awn narrated to us, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, from Sufyan ibn Husayn, from al-Hasan regarding His words: "Our Lord, give us in this world good, and in the Hereafter good, and protect us from the punishment of the Fire": He said: Worship in this world, and Paradise in the Hereafter.

3880 – Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abd al-Rahman ibn Waqid al-Attar narrated to us, saying: Abbad ibn al-Awwam narrated to us, from Hisham, from al-Hasan regarding His words: "Our Lord, give us in this world good": He said: The good in this world is understanding of the Book of God and knowledge.

3881 – Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: I heard Sufyan al-Thawri say regarding this verse: "Our Lord, give us in this world good and in the Hereafter good": He said: The good in this world is knowledge and good provision, and in the Hereafter the good is Paradise.

* *

Others said: "Good" in this world is wealth, and in the Hereafter, Paradise.

Mention of those who said this:

3882 – Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding: "And among them is he who says, 'Our Lord, give us in this world good and in the Hereafter good, and protect us from the punishment of the Fire'": He said: These are the Prophet ﷺ and the believers.

3883 – Musa ibn Harun narrated to me, saying: Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi regarding: "And among them is he who says, 'Our Lord, give us in this world good and in the Hereafter good'": These are the believers. As for the good of this world, it is wealth; as for the good of the Hereafter, it is Paradise.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct view on this matter, in my judgment, is to say that God, may His praise be exalted, informed of a people among the believers in Him and His Messenger, among those who performed the pilgrimage to His House, who ask their Lord for good in this world and good in the Hereafter, and that He protect them from the punishment of the Fire. "Good" (*hasanah*) from God, mighty and majestic, may encompass well-being in the body, livelihood, provision, and other things, as well as knowledge and worship.

As for the Hereafter, there is no doubt that it is Paradise, for whoever does not attain it on that day has been deprived of all good and has departed from all meanings of well-being.

We have said that this is the most appropriate interpretation of the verse because God, mighty and majestic, did not specify, in His words reporting about the one who says this, any of the meanings of "good," nor did He establish any indication, specific to it, showing that the intended meaning is some and not others. Therefore, what is obligatory in this matter is what we have said: that it is not permissible to restrict any of its meanings, and that its generality is to be applied to what God has made general.

* *

As for His words, "and protect us from the punishment of the Fire," He means by it: turn away from us the punishment of the Fire.

* *

It is said from this: "I protected him (*waqaytuhu*) such-and-such, I protect him (*aqihi*), protection (*wiqayah*), safeguarding (*waqayah*), and shielding (*wiqa'*)," with the long vowel; and they sometimes say: "God protected you (*waqaka*) with protection (*waqyan*)," when you repel from someone harm or something disliked.

Commentary on the words of the Exalted: ﴿Those will have a share of what they have earned, and Allah is swift in reckoning﴾ (2:202)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: By His saying, may His praise be exalted, "Those" (أولئك, ulā'ika), He means those who, after completing their rites (manāsik), say: "Our Lord, give us good in this world and good in the Hereafter, and protect us from the punishment of the Fire" (Q. 2:201). They say this out of desire for what is with Allah, may His praise be exalted, and out of knowledge that all good is from Him and that bounty is in His hand; He gives it to whom He wills. So He, may His praise be exalted, informs that they have a portion and a share of their Hajj and their rites, and a great reward for their deed which they have earned, and whose toil they undertook with their wealth and their selves, this being specifically theirs in distinction from the other group, who endured what they endured of the exhaustion and fatigue of their deeds, and bore the hardships of their journeys, without desire for what is with their Lord of reward and recompense, but only for a base hope of the worldly goods and a pursuit of its swift, fleeting trash. As:

3884 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Zurai' narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning His saying: "Among the people is one who says: 'Our Lord, give us in this world,' and he has no share in the Hereafter" (Q. 2:200). He said: This is a servant who intended the world; for it he does deeds and exerts himself. "And among them is one who says: 'Our Lord, give us good in this world and good in the Hereafter, and protect us from the punishment of the Fire.' Those will have a share of what they have earned" (Q. 2:201–202), that is, a portion of their deeds.

3885 - And Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said concerning: "Among the people is one who says: 'Our Lord, give us in this world,' and he has no share in the Hereafter" (Q. 2:200): They performed Hajj only for the world and for requests; they do not desire the Hereafter and do not believe in it. "And among them is one who says: 'Our Lord, give us good in this world and good in the Hereafter, and protect us from the punishment of the Fire'" — he said: These are the Prophet ﷺ and the believers. "Those will have a share of what they have earned, and Allah is swift in reckoning" — for these there is a reward for what they did in this world.

* *

As for His saying: "and Allah is swift in reckoning," He, may His praise be exalted, means: He encompasses the deeds of both groups, the one whose request is "Our Lord, give us in this world," and the other whose request is "Our Lord, give us good in this world and good in the Hereafter, and protect us from the punishment of the Fire." So He takes account of him with the swiftest reckoning [[His saying "fa-muhsin" (so He counts) is coordinated with His saying "annahu muhit" (that He encompasses)]], and then He recompenses each of the two groups for their deeds.

He, may His praise be exalted, described Himself with swiftness of reckoning because He, may His praise be exalted, counts what is counted of His servants' deeds without counting on fingers, and without thought or deliberation, as the weak and feeble of creation do. Rather, nothing is hidden from Him in the earth or in the heavens, and there is not lost from Him the weight of an atom's ember in them; then He recompenses His servants for all of that. Therefore He praised Himself, may His praise be exalted, with swiftness of reckoning, and informed His creation that He has no equal, so that He would need, in His reckoning, to count on the palm of a hand or the recollection of a breast.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 203 (part 1 of 3):

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, saying: ﴿And remember God during appointed days﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, means: Remember God with monotheism and glorification during numbered days, which are the days of stoning the pillars (ramy al-jimar). On that day He commanded His servants to say the takbir (proclaiming God's greatness) after the prescribed prayers and at the stoning, with each pebble of the pillars that one throws at a pillar (jamrah).

Abu Ja'far said: If someone says: When the Prophet (ﷺ) said about the days of Mina that they are days of eating and drinking and the remembrance of God, he did not inform his community that they are the "numbered days" mentioned by God in His Book. Why do you deny that the Prophet (ﷺ) meant by his saying "and remembrance of God" the "known days"?

It is said: It is impossible that he meant that. For God did not make obligatory in the "known days" the remembrance that He made obligatory in the "numbered days." Rather, God, may His remembrance be exalted, described the "known days" as the days in which the name of God is mentioned over the cattle, saying: ﴿That they may witness benefits for themselves and mention the name of God on known days over what He has provided for them of the livestock of cattle﴾ [al-Hajj: 28]. He did not make obligatory in the "known days" the remembrance that He made obligatory in the "numbered days," but rather informed that they are days of remembering Him over the cattle. So it was known—when he (ﷺ) said of the days of tashriq: "Indeed they are days of eating and drinking and the remembrance of God," and he gave the phrase "and the remembrance of God" in unrestricted form, without condition or attachment, not attached to the remembrance over cattle—that he meant by it the remembrance that God mentioned in His Book and made obligatory on His servants without restriction or condition, in the sense of the "numbered days." And if he had intended by this (ﷺ) to describe the "known days" with it, he would have connected "and remembrance" to the remembrance of God over what He provided them of the livestock of cattle, as God described it that way. But he used the term "remembrance" without linking it to anything, just as the Blessed and Exalted One used the term "remembrance" unrestricted, saying: "And remember God during numbered days." So this is among the clearest evidence that he meant by it what God mentioned in His Book and made obligatory in the "numbered days."

* *

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, saying: ﴿Whoever hastens in two days, there is no sin upon him, and whoever delays, there is no sin upon him, for him who fears God﴾

Abu Ja'far said: The interpreters differed regarding the interpretation of this:

Some of them said: Its meaning: whoever hastens in two days of the days of tashriq, departing on the second day, there is no sin upon him in his departure and his hastening in departing. And whoever delays from departing on the second day of the days of tashriq until the third day, so that he departs on the third day, there is no sin upon him in his delay.

3918 - Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, from 'Awf, from al-Hasan, the same.

3919 - Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, from Mughirah, from 'Ikrimah, the same.

And whoever is overtaken by night in Mina on the second day before departing, there is no departure for him until the sun declines the next day. "And whoever delays, there is no sin upon him," he says: whoever delays until the third day of the days of tashriq, there is no sin upon him.

* *

Others said: Rather, its meaning is: whoever hastens in two days, he is forgiven and there is no sin upon him, and likewise whoever delays.

Those who said this:

3933 - Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Isra'il narrated to us, from Thuwayr, from his father, from 'Abd Allah: "Whoever hastens in two days, there is no sin upon him, and whoever delays, there is no sin upon him," he said: there is no sin upon him.

3934 - Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, from 'Abd Allah: "Whoever hastens in two days, there is no sin upon him," that is, he is forgiven; "and whoever delays, there is no sin upon him," he said: he is forgiven.

3935 - Ahmad ibn Hazim narrated to us, saying: Abu Nu'aym narrated to us, saying: Mis'ar narrated to us, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, from 'Abd Allah: "Whoever hastens in two days, there is no sin upon him," that is, he is forgiven.

3936 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: al-Mihribi narrated to us; and Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, both from Sufyan, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, from 'Abd Allah, regarding His saying: "Whoever hastens in two days, there is no sin upon him, and whoever delays, there is no sin upon him," he said: He has indeed been forgiven.

3937 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, regarding His saying: "Whoever hastens in two days, there is no sin upon him, and whoever delays, there is no sin upon him," he has been forgiven.

3938 - Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'ba narrated to us, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, from 'Abd Allah, who said concerning this verse: "Whoever hastens in two days, there is no sin upon him, and whoever delays, there is no sin upon him," he said: he is free of sin.

3939 - Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Hammad ibn Salama narrated to us, from 'Ali ibn Zayd, from al-Hasan, from Ibn 'Umar: "Whoever hastens in two days, there is no sin upon him," he said: he returned forgiven.

3940 - Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayya narrated to us, from Layth, from Mujahid regarding His saying: "Whoever hastens in two days, there is no sin upon him, and whoever delays, there is no sin upon him," he said: He has been forgiven.

3941 - Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Jabir, from Abu 'Abd Allah, from Ibn 'Abbas: "Whoever hastens in two days, there is no sin upon him," he said: He has been forgiven. They interpret it in other than its proper sense. Indeed the 'umrah expiates what is with it of sins, so how much more the hajj!

3942 - Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Isra'il narrated to us, from Abu Husayn, from Ibrahim and 'Amir: "Whoever hastens in two days, there is no sin upon him, and whoever delays, there is no sin upon him," both said: he has been forgiven.

3943 - al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: someone whose truthfulness I trust narrated to me, from Ibn Mas'ud, his saying: "there is no sin upon him," he said: he has come out of all sin, "and whoever delays, there is no sin upon him," he said: he is free of all sin, and this is at the return from the hajj. Ibn Jurayj said: I also heard a man narrate from 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: "there is no sin upon him," he said: he has been forgiven, "and whoever delays, there is no sin upon him," he said: he has been forgiven.

3944 - Ahmad ibn Hazim narrated to me, saying: Abu Nu'aym narrated to us, saying: Aswad ibn Sawada al-Qattan narrated to us, saying: I heard Mu'awiya ibn Qurra say: He comes out of his sins. [[Narration 3944: I have not found "Aswad ibn Sawada al-Qattan"; perhaps it is "Sawada ibn Abi al-Aswad al-Qattan," the one from whom Abu Nu'aym narrates, whose name is "Abd Allah," also said to be Muslim ibn Mukhariq al-Qattan. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib.]]

* *

Others said: the meaning is: "Whoever hastens in two days, then there is sin upon him, and whoever delays, there is no sin upon him," concerning what lies between him and the following year.

Those who said this:

3945 - Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Ishaq ibn Yahya ibn Talha narrated to us, saying: I asked Mujahid about the saying of God, Mighty and Majestic: "Whoever hastens in two days, there is no sin upon him, and whoever delays, there is no sin upon him," he said: for the one who is in the hajj, there is no sin upon him until the hajj of the following year.

* *

Others said: rather its meaning is: "there is no sin upon him if he fears God regarding what remains of his life."

Those who said this:

3946 - Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Abu Ja'far al-Razi narrated to us, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, from Abu al-'Aliya: "Whoever hastens in two days, there is no sin upon him, and whoever delays, there is no sin upon him," he said: all his sin has gone if he fears God regarding what remains.

3947 - It was related to me from 'Ammar, who said: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Mughira, from Ibrahim, the same.

3948 - It was related to me from 'Ammar, who said: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi', from Abu al-'Aliya, the same.

3949 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying: "Whoever hastens in two days, there is no sin upon him, and whoever delays, there is no sin upon him," he said: it is for the one who fears God, on condition.

3950 - Musa ibn Harun narrated to me, saying: 'Amr ibn Hammad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "Whoever hastens in two days, there is no sin upon him," there is no blame upon him; "and whoever delays," until the third day, there is no blame upon him for the one who fears God. And Ibn 'Abbas used to say: I wish I were among those upon whom the name of taqwa falls.

3951 - al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, saying: Ibn Jurayj said: It is in the codex of 'Abd Allah: "li-man ittaqa Allah" (for the one who fears God).

3952 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: 'Abd Allah narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas: "Whoever hastens in two days, there is no sin upon him, and whoever delays, there is no sin upon him," there is no blame upon him; he means: for the one who fears the disobedience of God, Mighty and Majestic. [[Narration 3952: In the printed edition: "'Ali narrated to us, saying: 'Abd Allah narrated to us." "'Ali" is a misreading, and the correct form is what we have set down; see the earlier narration no. 3931 and the note on it.]]

* *

Others said: rather the meaning is: "Whoever hastens in two days" from the days of al-tashriq, "then there is no sin upon him," meaning there is no blame upon him for hastening the departure, if he fears killing game until the third day has passed; and whoever delays until the third day and does not depart, there is no blame upon him.

Those who said this:

3953 - al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Abi Salih informed us: "for the one who fears" to strike any game until the third day has passed.

3954 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas: "Whoever hastens in two days, there is no sin upon him," and it is not lawful for him to kill game until the days of tashriq have passed.

* *

Others said: rather its meaning is: "Whoever hastens in two days" from the days of al-tashriq and departs, "then there is no sin upon him," meaning he is forgiven; "and whoever delays" and departs on the third day, "then there is no sin upon him," meaning he is forgiven, if he fears, regarding his pilgrimage, committing anything God has forbidden him.

Those who said this:

3955 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His saying: "for the one who fears" — he said: He says, for the one who fears regarding his pilgrimage. Qatada said: It was mentioned to us that Ibn Mas'ud used to say: whoever fears in his pilgrimage, his earlier sin is forgiven, or: his past sin.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of these views is the view of the one who said: the interpretation of that is: "Whoever hastens in two days" from the three days of Mina and departs on the second day, "then there is no sin upon him," God erasing his sins, if he has feared God in his pilgrimage, avoided in it what God commanded him to avoid, did in it what God commanded him to do, and obeyed Him by performing it according to the limits He imposed on him; "and whoever delays" until the third of them and does not depart until the second departure, until he departs on the day after the first departure, "then there is no sin upon him," God forgiving him what has passed of his transgressions and crimes, if he has feared God in his pilgrimage by performing it within its limits.

We said that this is the most correct of its interpretations because of the multiplicity of reports from the Messenger of God ﷺ that he said: "Whoever performs this House's pilgrimage and neither commits obscenity nor transgresses comes out of his sins as on the day his mother bore him." And he ﷺ said: "Follow the hajj with the 'umrah, for they remove poverty and sins as the bellows removes the impurity of iron, gold and silver."

3956 - 'Abd Allah ibn Sa'id al-Kindi narrated to us, saying: Abu Khalid al-Ahmar narrated to us, saying: 'Amr ibn Qays narrated to us, from 'Asim, from Shaqiq, from 'Abd Allah, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "Follow the hajj with the 'umrah, for they remove poverty and sins as the bellows removes the impurity of iron, gold and silver, and the accepted hajj has no reward but Paradise." [[Hadith 3956: 'Abd Allah ibn Sa'id al-Kindi Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj: a trustworthy, retentive narrator, one of the teachers of the authors of the six books. Abu Khalid al-Ahmar: Sulayman ibn Hayyan (with a lower dot on the y) al-Azdi, a trustworthy teacher of Ahmad and Ishaq, from whom a group narrated. 'Amr ibn Qays: al-Mala'i. 'Asim: Ibn Abi al-Najud. Shaqiq: Ibn Salama Abu Wa'il al-Asadi. 'Abd Allah: Ibn Mas'ud.
This hadith is related by Ahmad in al-Musnad (3669) through Abu Khalid al-Ahmar with this chain, and by al-Tirmidhi (2:78) and al-Nasa'i (2:4), both through Abu Khalid al-Ahmar.
al-Suyuti mentions it (1:211) and attributes it additionally to Ibn Abi Shayba, Ibn Khuzayma and Ibn Hibban.
al-Kir: a skin or thick leather bag with edges, into which the smith blows to kindle the fire. Khabath al-hadid and the like: what the bellows and fire remove from iron when melted, which is what has no good in it.]]

3957 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: al-Hakam ibn Bashir narrated to us, from 'Amr ibn Qays, from 'Asim, from Zirr, from 'Abd Allah, from the Prophet ﷺ, similarly. [[Hadith 3957: This is another sound chain for this hadith that I have not found except in al-Tabari. It shows that 'Asim ibn Abi al-Najud narrated it from two teachers, Abu Wa'il and Zirr ibn Hubaysh, both from Ibn Mas'ud.]]

3958 - al-Fadl ibn al-Sabbah narrated to us, saying: Ibn 'Uyayna narrated to us, from 'Asim ibn 'Ubayd Allah, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amir ibn Rabi'a, from his father, from 'Umar, the report reaching the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Follow the hajj with the 'umrah, for following between them removes poverty and sins as the bellows removes impurity, or: the impurity of iron." [[Hadith 3958: 'Asim ibn 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Asim ibn 'Umar ibn al-Khattab: weak; we explained his weakness in the commentary on the Musnad (128, 5229).
This hadith is related by Ibn Majah (2887) through two chains, one through Ibn 'Uyayna and one through 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Umar, both from 'Asim ibn 'Ubayd Allah. al-Busiri said in his Zawa'id: "The two chains revolve around 'Asim ibn 'Ubayd Allah, who is weak. The text is sound from the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud, related by al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i," meaning the two previous hadiths.
al-Suyuti mentions it (1:211) and attributes it additionally to Ibn Abi Shayba and al-Bayhaqi.]]

3959 - Ibrahim ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Sa'd ibn 'Abd al-Hamid narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi al-Zinad narrated to us, from Musa ibn 'Uqba, from Salih, mawla of al-Tawama, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "When you have completed your hajj, you are like the day your mother bore you." [[Hadith 3959: Ibrahim ibn Sa'id is al-Jawhari; he passed in 3355. Sa'd ibn 'Abd al-Hamid ibn Ja'far ibn 'Abd Allah al-Ansari al-Madani: Ibn Hibban weakened him greatly, while Ibn Ma'in said: "there is nothing wrong with him." What I favour is that he is trustworthy, for al-Bukhari included him in al-Kabir (2/2/62) without mentioning any criticism, and neither he nor al-Nasa'i mentioned him in al-Du'afa', and Ibn Abi Hatim included him (2/1/92) without criticising him either.
Salih, mawla of al-Tawama: Salih ibn Nabhan, passed in 1020; the narration of one who heard from him in early times, before his memory changed, is authenticated. Musa ibn 'Uqba heard from him in early times, as we explained in the commentary on the Musnad (2604).
This hadith with this chain I have not found elsewhere from Ibn 'Abbas. Its meaning is established in other sound hadiths; see al-Targhib wa'l-Tarhib (2:105-113), Majma' al-Zawa'id (3:207-209, 274-277), and what preceded from no. 3718-3728.]]

* *

= And other reports similar to these, the mention of all of which would lengthen the book, indicating that whoever performs the hajj and completes it within its limits as God commanded is free of his sins, as the Mighty and Majestic said: "there is no sin upon him for the one who fears" God in his pilgrimage. Thus in the Messenger of God's ﷺ statement there is what clarifies that the meaning of His saying, Mighty and Majestic, "there is no sin upon him," is that he has come out of his sins, his transgressions have been lifted from him, and his crimes forgiven. And there is no sense in the view of those who interpreted His saying "there is no sin upon him" as meaning "there is no blame upon him in departing on the second day, nor blame upon him in remaining until the third day." For blame is only lifted from the doer concerning what it was incumbent upon him to leave undone, so that he is permitted to do it by lifting the blame from him in doing it; or concerning what it was incumbent upon him to do, so that he is permitted to leave it by lifting the blame from him in leaving it. As for what is incumbent upon the doer to do, there is no sense in lifting blame from him concerning it if he does it, since it is his obligation to do it, for it is impossible that one who performs an obligation upon himself be blamed for performing it. [[The word "haraj" (blame) in the form "faraḥ" meaning sinful: al-Tabari previously used this pattern in volume 2:423, where I noted that the lexicographers object to it and say the correct form is "haraj." al-Tabari repeats its use here, and I have also seen al-Qadi al-Baqillani use it in his al-Tamhid p. 221, saying: "...the imam was not sinful in that nor blameworthy," and it seems to me al-Shafi'i also used it in al-Umm, but its location has escaped me.] So it is permissible to say: we have lifted blame from you in it.

And since that is so: the pilgrim could not be free, according to those who interpreted His saying, "there is no sin upon him" (﴿فلا إثم عليه﴾), to mean "there is no blame upon him" or "there is no fault upon him," from one of two cases. Either his obligation was to depart on the second day of the Tashriq days, so the blame was lifted from him for remaining, or his obligation was to remain until the third day, so the blame was lifted from him for departing on the second day. If his obligation on the second day of the Tashriq days was to remain until the third day of them, and the blame was lifted from him for his departure on the second day of them, which is the early departure (ta'ajjul) that is meant by "whoever hastens in two days, there is no sin upon him," then there is no meaning, on the interpretation of whoever interpreted it so, to His saying "there is no sin upon him," "there is no fault upon him," and "whoever delays, there is no sin upon him." This is because one who delays until the third day is delaying from performing an obligation upon him, forsaking the acceptance of the concession to depart, so there is no basis for saying, "There is no blame upon you for remaining in your place, when you are performing the duty upon you," as we have described before. Or his obligation was to depart on the second day, and he was granted a concession to remain until the third day. Then there is no meaning in saying, "There is no blame upon you for your hastening to depart, which is your obligation and which you must perform," for the reason we have already mentioned.

Likewise there is no meaning to the saying of whoever said: its meaning is "whoever hastens in two days, there is no sin upon him, and no blame upon him in that departure, if he avoids killing game until the end of the third day." For if that interpretation were accepted by its proponent, then His saying "and whoever delays, there is no sin upon him" would refute his claim, because there is no disagreement among the Community that game is lawful for the pilgrim after his departure from Mina on the third day. So what is the reason for which He lifted the blame from him in His saying "and whoever delays, there is no sin upon him," if he delays until the third day and then departs? This is in addition to the consensus (ijma') of the authoritative scholars that when the muhrim has thrown the pebbles, slaughtered, shaved, and circumambulated the House, everything has become lawful for him, and to the explicit statement of the report transmitted from the Messenger of God (ﷺ) to that effect, [[In the printed edition: "the transmitted report," and I have restored it to al-Tabari's phrasing, which he frequently uses; see above 4:33, line 19, and in many places I have not been able to find it now.]] which:

3960 - Hannad ibn al-Sarri al-Hanzali narrated it to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahim ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from Hajjaj, from Abu Bakr ibn Muhammad ibn 'Amr ibn Hazm, from 'Amrah, who said: I asked 'A'ishah, the Mother of the Believers (may God be pleased with her), "When does the muhrim become lawful?" She said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "When you have thrown, slaughtered, and shaved, everything becomes lawful for you except women." He said: And al-Zuhri mentioned, from 'Amrah, from 'A'ishah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), the like of it. [[The hadith 3960: Hannad ibn al-Sarri al-Darimi; his biography has passed at 2058. He is here attributed as "al-Hanzali," as al-Bukhari attributed him in al-Kabir. Both are correct, for he is of the Banu Darim ibn Hanzalah ibn Malik ibn Zayd Manat ibn Tamim. See Jamharat Ibn Hazm, pp. 211, 217.
Hajjaj: he is Ibn Artah, and he is trustworthy according to the preponderant view with us, as we mentioned at 2299.
Hajjaj narrated this hadith by two chains. He narrated it from Abu Bakr ibn Muhammad ibn 'Amr ibn Hazm, from 'Amrah, who was the daughter of 'Abd al-Rahman, and she was the maternal aunt of Abu Bakr ibn Hazm, from 'A'ishah, and he mentioned the wording of the hadith. Then he narrated it from al-Zuhri, from 'Amrah, from 'A'ishah, "the like of it," without mentioning its wording. This is part of Hajjaj ibn Artah's scrupulousness and precision, as will be shown from what follows.
The hadith, through the narration of Abu Bakr ibn Hazm, was narrated by Ahmad in al-Musnad 6:143 (Halabi), from Yazid ibn Harun, from Hajjaj, with this chain, similar to it. But the phrase "and you have slaughtered" is not in it. Likewise al-Bayhaqi narrated it in al-Sunan al-Kubra 5:136 through the route of Malik ibn Yahya, from Yazid ibn Harun, then said: "Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr narrated it from Yazid ibn Harun, and he added in it: 'and you have slaughtered, then everything has become lawful for you, perfume and garments, except women.'" Then al-Bayhaqi mentioned its chain to Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr. Then al-Bayhaqi declared it defective (a'allahu), and we will mention what he said and the response to it, God willing.
Al-Suyuti erred when he mentioned this hadith in the Zawa'id of al-Jami' al-Saghir (1:117 of al-Fath al-Kabir), attributing it to Sahih Muslim together with al-Bayhaqi, and this is certainly an error, for it is not in Sahih Muslim.
As for the narration of Hajjaj from al-Zuhri: Abu Dawud narrated it in al-Sunan (1978), from Musaddad, from 'Abd al-Wahid ibn Ziyad, from Hajjaj, from al-Zuhri, from 'Amrah, from 'A'ishah, raised to the Prophet with the wording: "When one of you throws the pebble of al-'Aqabah, everything has become lawful for him except women." Then Abu Dawud declared it defective, saying: "This hadith is weak. Hajjaj did not see al-Zuhri and did not hear from him." This is a good defect (ta'lil) from Abu Dawud, for Ibn Abi Hatim narrated in Kitab al-Marasil, p. 18, with his chain, from Hushaym who said: "Hajjaj ibn Artah said to me: 'Did you hear from al-Zuhri?' I said: 'Yes.' He said: 'But I did not hear anything from him.'"
As for al-Bayhaqi, he declared defective the narration of Hajjaj from Abu Bakr ibn Hazm with a defect that I do not consider sound. He said after narrating it: "This is among the confusions of Hajjaj ibn Artah, and the hadith is from 'Amrah, from 'A'ishah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), as all people narrated it from 'A'ishah." Then he mentioned her hadith, in which she said: "The Messenger of God (ﷺ) perfumed himself for his ihram when he entered upon it, and for his lawfulness before he performed the circumambulation of return, with the best perfume I found." This is a sound hadith narrated by Muslim.
We do not see the defect of that by this: this is an action-report (hadith fi'li), from 'A'ishah's account, and that is a verbal report (hadith qawli) from her narration from the Prophet (ﷺ), and each of them corroborates the soundness of the other. So how can the defect be sound?
A similar hadith has also come from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas, raised: "When you have thrown the pebble, everything has become lawful for you except women." Ahmad narrated it in al-Musnad (2090, 3204, 3491). But it is through a disconnected chain (munqati'), because it is from the narration of al-Hasan al-'Urani from Ibn 'Abbas. He did not hear from Ibn 'Abbas, as al-Bukhari said in al-Saghir, p. 136. Yet in any case it serves as a corroborating witness (shahid) for this hadith.]]

As for the one who interpreted it to mean "there is no sin upon him until the following year," there is no basis for limiting that to a time, and for his removing sin from the pilgrim for the coming year but not for his past sins. This is because God, mighty is His praise, did not confine that to the negation of sin for a future time by the apparent meaning of the revelation, nor by the tongue of the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him. Rather the indication of the apparent meaning of the revelation shows that the one who hastens in two days and the one who delays, neither of them has sin upon him in the state he is in, not in other states.

And the report from the Messenger (ﷺ) explicitly states that by the completion of his pilgrimage according to what he was commanded, he emerges from his sins like the day his mother bore him. In that is, from the indication of the apparent meaning of the revelation and the explicit saying of the Messenger (ﷺ), a clear indication of the corruption of the view of whoever said: the meaning of "there is no sin upon him" is "there is no sin upon him from the time of the completion of his pilgrimage until the following year."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: If someone asks us: What is the particle "al-lam" in His saying "for the one who is mindful (li-man ittaqa)?" And what is its meaning?
It is said: What brings it is the meaning of His saying "there is no sin upon him." For in His saying "there is no sin upon him" is the meaning: We have removed his sins and expiated his misdeeds. So in that there is the meaning: We made the expiation of sins for the one who fears God in his pilgrimage. The phrase "We made the expiation of sins" is omitted, being satisfied with the indication of His saying "there is no sin upon him."
Some grammarians of Basra claimed that when this concession is mentioned, he has informed about a matter, so He said "for the one who is mindful," meaning: this is for the one who is mindful. Some of them denied this from his saying, and claimed that the predicate (sifah) must have something to which it attaches, [[al-sifah: it is the prepositional particle, and it is the set of attributive prepositions; see above 1:299 note 1, and then 3:475 note 1.]] for it does not stand by itself, but it is, as he claimed, dependent on an omitted "qala" (said), so the meaning of the speech in his view is "we said": [[In the printed edition: "so the meaning of the speech in his view was 'mā qulnā'" with an added "mā," which is an evident error, as the context of this interpretation indicates.]] "And whoever delays, there is no sin upon him for the one who is mindful," and his saying "and whoever delays, there is no sin upon him" stands in the place of "saying."
Some scholars of Arabic claimed that the place where sin is removed is for the hastener, and it was applied to the one who delays, who has fulfilled and did not fall short, the same as what was applied to the one who falls short, as one says in speech: "If you give charity secretly, it is good, and if you show it, it is good," and these two are different, because the one who gives charity openly, if he does not intend showing off, is good, though secrecy is better.
In describing the two states of the charitable as good there is no description of one of them as sinful. God, mighty and majestic, has informed about those who depart by negating sin from both of them, and it is impossible that He negate of them anything except what would be sin in leaving it, according to what the proponents of this view interpreted. And in the consensus of all that if both of them had left the departure and remained at Mina, neither would have been sinful, there is something that indicates the corruption of the interpretation of those whose view we have reported.
He also said: In it there is another aspect, which is the meaning of forbidding each of the two groups from charging the other with sin, as if he meant by His saying "there is no sin upon him": the hastener should not say to the one who delays, "you are sinful," nor should the one who delays say to the hastener, "you are sinful," meaning: neither of them should charge the other with sin.
And this too is an interpretation contrary to the saying of all the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil), and that is enough as evidence of its error.

* *

On the interpretation of His exalted saying: ﴿وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّكُمْ إِلَيْهِ تُحْشَرُونَ﴾ (And be mindful of God, and know that to Him you will be gathered).

Abu Ja'far said: By this, mighty is His praise, He means: Be mindful of God, O believers, regarding what He has made obligatory upon you of His obligations, so fear Him in neglecting them and falling short in them; and regarding what He has forbidden you in your pilgrimage and its rites, that you commit or approach it; and regarding what He has charged you in your ihram for your pilgrimage, that you fall short in fulfilling and upholding it. "And know that to Him you will be gathered," so He will recompense you for your deeds: the good-doer among you by His goodness, and the wrongdoer by his wrongdoing, and He will pay every soul in full what it has done, and you will not be wronged.

The interpretation of His words, the Exalted: "And among the people is one whose speech may impress you in the life of this world, and he calls Allah to witness what is in his heart, yet he is the most contentious of opponents."

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: This is a description by Allah, blessed and exalted, of the hypocrites, through His saying, may His praise be exalted: "And among the people is one whose speech may impress you, O Muhammad, in its outward appearance and openness, and he calls Allah to witness what is in his heart, and he is the most contentious of opponents, a disputer through falsehood."

* *

Then the people of interpretation differed concerning who this verse was revealed about.

Some of them said: It was revealed about al-Akhnas ibn Shariq. He came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and claimed that he wished to embrace Islam, and swore that he had come only for that. Then he left and corrupted the property of the Muslims.

Those who said this:

3961 - Musa ibn Harun told me, saying: Amr ibn Hammad told us, saying: Asbat told us, from al-Suddi: "And among the people is one whose speech may impress you in the life of this world, and he calls Allah to witness what is in his heart, yet he is the most contentious of opponents." He said: It was revealed about al-Akhnas ibn Shariq al-Thaqafi, who was an ally of the Banu Zuhrah. He came to the Prophet ﷺ in Medina and showed him Islam, and the Prophet ﷺ was impressed by that from him, and he said: "I came only wishing Islam, and Allah knows that I am truthful!" This is His saying: "and he calls Allah to witness what is in his heart." Then he left from the presence of the Prophet ﷺ and passed by the crops of some Muslims and their donkeys, and he burned the crops and hamstrung the donkeys. So Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed: "And when he turns away, he strives in the land to cause corruption therein and destroy crops and lineage." As for "the most contentious of opponents," it means the most crooked of disputants. And concerning him was revealed: "Woe to every slanderer, backbiter" [al-Humazah: 1], and revealed concerning him was: "And do not obey every vile swearer... a cruel, ignoble wretch, moreover, of illegitimate birth" [al-Qalam: 10-13].

[[Note on the report no. 3961: al-Tabari did not mention in his commentary on "Surat al-Humazah" and "Surat al-Qalam" this report that the two verses were revealed concerning al-Akhnas ibn Shariq. This is further evidence of the truth of what they reported about him, that he greatly abridged this tafsir, as came in their reports.

Part of this report will come later under number 3978.]]

* *

Others said: Rather, that was revealed about a group of hypocrites who spoke about the expedition that was struck against the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at al-Raji'.

Those who said this:

3962 - Abu Kurayb told us, saying: Yunus ibn Bukayr told us, from Abu Ishaq, who said: Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, mawla of Zayd ibn Thabit, told me, saying: Sa'id ibn Jubayr or Ikrimah told me, from Ibn Abbas, who said: When the expedition of the companions of Khubayb was struck at al-Raji' between Mecca and Medina, some men of the hypocrites said: "Woe to these slain men who perished in this way! Neither did they remain in their homes, nor did they deliver the message of their companion!" So Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed concerning that the words of the hypocrites, and what befell those men of martyrdom and goodness from Allah: "And among the people is one whose speech may impress you in the life of this world," meaning: what he displays with his tongue of Islam, "and he calls Allah to witness what is in his heart," meaning of hypocrisy, "yet he is the most contentious of opponents," meaning: full of argument when he speaks to you and disputes with you. "And when he turns away," meaning: he leaves from your presence, "he strives in the land to cause corruption therein and destroy crops and lineage, and Allah does not like corruption," meaning: He does not like his deed nor approve of it. "And when it is said to him, 'Fear Allah,' he is seized by pride in sin, so Hell is sufficient for him, and it is an evil resting place. And among the people is one who sells himself seeking the pleasure of Allah," meaning those who sold themselves to Allah by striving in the way of Allah and upholding His right, until they perished in that, meaning this expedition.

3963 - Ibn Humayd told us, saying: Salamah told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq told me, from Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, mawla of Zayd ibn Thabit, from Ikrimah, mawla of Ibn Abbas, or from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: When the expedition in which were 'Asim and Marthad was struck at al-Raji', some men of the hypocrites said: — then he mentioned a report similar to that of Abu Kurayb. [[The reports 3962 and 3963: Sirat Ibn Hisham 3: 183-184, and part of it will come under number 3973 and then number 3980.]]

* *

Others said: Rather, it meant all the hypocrites, and by His saying: "And among the people is one whose speech may impress you in the life of this world, and he calls Allah to witness what is in his heart," it meant the difference between their inner state and their outward appearance.

Those who said this:

3964 - Muhammad ibn Abi Ma'shar told me, saying: My father Abu Ma'shar Najih told me, saying: I heard Sa'id al-Maqburi discussing with Muhammad ibn Ka'b, and Sa'id said: "In some books it is said that Allah has servants whose tongues are sweeter than honey, and whose hearts are more bitter than aloe, who wear the wool of sheep to people, [[Al-Sabr (with a fathah on the sad and a kasrah on the ba): the sap of a bitter tree. Al-masuk is the plural of misk: the skin, the hide of sheep and others.]] who graze the world with religion. Allah, blessed and exalted, says: 'Do they dare against Me, and do they deceive Me?! By My might, I will send upon them a trial that leaves the forbearing among them bewildered!'" Then Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: "This is in the Book of Allah, may His praise be exalted." Sa'id said: "And where is it in the Book of Allah?" He said: The saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: "And among the people is one whose speech may impress you in the life of this world, and he calls Allah to witness what is in his heart, yet he is the most contentious of opponents. And when he turns away, he strives in the land to cause corruption therein and destroy crops and lineage, and Allah does not like corruption." Sa'id said: "You have known about whom this verse was revealed!" Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: "The verse is revealed concerning a man, and then it becomes general afterward."

3965 - Yunus ibn Abd al-A'la told me, saying: Ibn Wahb told us, saying: Al-Layth ibn Sa'd told me, from Khalid ibn Yazid, from Sa'id ibn Abi Hilal, from al-Qurazi, from Nawf — and he used to read the books — who said: "Indeed I find the description of people from this Ummah in the revealed Book of Allah: 'A people who gain the world by religion, [[In the original: "yahtalun"; the correct reading is what is given here. Ijtal a man's property: he took it away, drove it off and herded it. Ijtal the army their wealth: he took it away.]] whose tongues are sweeter than honey, and whose hearts are more bitter than aloe, who dress to people in the clothing of sheep's wool, while their hearts are the hearts of wolves; they dare against Me! And they deceive Me! I swear by Myself that I will send upon them a trial that leaves the forbearing among them bewildered.'" Al-Qurazi said: "I reflected on it in the Qur'an, and behold, they are the hypocrites. I found it: 'And among the people is one whose speech may impress you in the life of this world, and he calls Allah to witness what is in his heart, yet he is the most contentious of opponents,' and: 'And among the people is one who worships Allah on an edge; if good befalls him, he is content with it'" [al-Hajj: 11].

[[The report 3965: Khalid ibn Yazid al-Jumahi Abu Abd al-Rahim al-Misri was a jurist and mufti, trustworthy, died in 139 AH, biography in al-Tahdhib. "Nawf" is Nawf ibn Fudalah al-Himyari al-Bakali, who was trustworthy in narrating stories, and he was the son of the wife of Ka'b al-Ahbar, died between 90 and 100 AH, biography in al-Tahdhib.]]

3966 - And al-Hasan ibn Yahya told us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq told us, saying: Ma'mar told us, from Qatadah concerning His saying: "And among the people is one whose speech may impress you in the life of this world, and he calls Allah to witness what is in his heart," he said: He is the hypocrite.

3967 - Muhammad ibn Amr told me, saying: Abu Asim told us, from Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "And among the people is one whose speech may impress you," he said: his openness in the world, "and he calls Allah to witness in the dispute, he only wants the truth."

3968 - I was told from Ammar, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far told us, from his father, from al-Rabi' concerning His saying: "And among the people is one whose speech may impress you in the life of this world, and he calls Allah to witness what is in his heart, yet he is the most contentious of opponents," he said: This is a servant who had good speech and bad deeds, who came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and spoke well to him, "and when he turns away, he strives in the land to cause corruption therein."

3969 - And al-Qasim told us, saying: Al-Husayn told us, saying: Hajjaj told me, from Ibn Juraij, who said: I said to Ata: "And among the people is one whose speech may impress you in the life of this world, and he calls Allah to witness what is in his heart," he said: He says a saying whose opposite is in his heart, and Allah knows that.

* *

Regarding His saying: "and he calls Allah to witness what is in his heart," there are two readings. The majority of readers recited it: "and he calls Allah to witness what is in his heart," meaning that the hypocrite whose speech impresses the Messenger of Allah ﷺ calls Allah to witness what is in his heart, that his speech agrees with his belief, and that he believes in Allah and His Messenger, while he is lying. As follows:

3970 - Yunus told me, saying: Ibn Wahb told us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: "And among the people is one whose speech may impress you in the life of this world," to "and Allah does not like corruption." A man used to come to the Prophet ﷺ and say: "O Messenger of Allah, I bear witness that you have come with truth and sincerity from Allah!" He said: until the Prophet ﷺ was impressed by his speech. Then he would say: "Indeed, by Allah, O Messenger of Allah, Allah knows what is in my heart just as my tongue has uttered!" That is His saying: "and he calls Allah to witness what is in his heart." He said: These are the hypocrites. And he recited the saying of Allah, blessed and exalted: "When the hypocrites come to you, they say, 'We bear witness that you are indeed the Messenger of Allah,'" until: "Indeed, the hypocrites are liars" [al-Munafiqun: 1], by what they testify, that you are the Messenger of Allah.

* *

As-Suddi said: "and he calls Allah to witness what is in his heart," meaning: Allah knows that I am truthful, that I wish Islam.

3971 - Musa ibn Harun told me this, saying: Amr ibn Hammad told us, from Asbat.

* *

Mujahid said: "and he calls Allah to witness in the dispute, he only wants the truth."

3972 - Muhammad ibn Amr told me this, saying: Abu Asim told us, saying: Isa told us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from him.

* *

Others recited: "wa-yushhidu Allahu 'ala ma fi qalbihi" (and Allah bears witness to what is in his heart), meaning: Allah bears witness to what is in his heart of hypocrisy, and that he conceals in his heart other than what he shows with his tongue, and to his lying in his heart. This is the reading of Ibn Muhaysin, and Ibn Abbas interpreted it in this sense. We have mentioned the narration from him in that regard earlier in the report of Abu Kurayb, from Yunus ibn Bukayr, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq which we mentioned just now. [[See no. 3962.]]

* *

What we choose among the readings is the reading of the one who recited: "ويشهد الله على ما في قلبه" (wa-yushhidu Allah), meaning "yastashhidu Allah" (he calls Allah to witness), because of the consensus of the authoritative readers upon it.

* *

The interpretation of His words: "and he is the most contentious of opponents" [2:204].

Abu Ja'far said: "al-Alladd" among men is the one who is intensely contentious. It is said of the form "fa'ala" from it: "You have been contentious, O man, and you were not the most contentious; you are contentious with contentiousness (laddan wa-ladadatan)." [[His saying "ladadah" is a verbal noun I have not found in the lexicon books available to me.]] As for when he overcomes the one he disputes with, it is said: "Laddta, O so-and-so, so-and-so, you contend him (talummuhu) with contention (laddan)," and from it is the saying of the poet:

Then I drive them, and whoever drives... you contend the rivals of the contentious opponents.
[[I do not know who said it. The second verse is in Lisan al-Arab (ladd) with the reading "alladd aqran al-khusum." Both verses are in Ma'ani al-Qur'an by al-Farra' 1:123, with the second verse placed before the first. ]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The people of interpretation differed concerning the explanation of this.

Some of them said: Its meaning is that he is one of much argument.

Those who said this:

3973 - Abu Kurayb told us, saying: Yunus ibn Bukayr told us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad told me, saying: Sa'id ibn Jubayr or Ikrimah told me, from Ibn Abbas: "and he is the most contentious of opponents," that is: full of argument, when he speaks to you and disputes with you. [[This is part of the earlier report no. 3962.]]

3974 - Bishr told us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatadah concerning His saying: "and he is the most contentious of opponents," he says: harsh in disobedience to Allah, a disputer through falsehood; and if you wish, you see him knowing in tongue and ignorant in deed, speaking with wisdom and acting with sin.

3975 - Al-Hasan ibn Yahya told us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq told us, saying: Ma'mar told us, from Qatadah concerning His saying: "and he is the most contentious of opponents," he said: a disputer through falsehood.

* *

Others said: The meaning of that is that he is not upright in disputation, but crooked in it.

Those who said this:

3976 - Muhammad ibn Amr told me, saying: Abu Asim told us, saying: Isa told us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "and he is the most contentious of opponents," he said: an unjust one who does not go straight.

3977 - Al-Qasim told us, saying: Al-Husayn told us, saying: Hajjaj told us, from Ibn Juraij, who said: Abd Allah ibn Kathir told me, from Mujahid, who said: "Al-alladd al-khusam," the one who does not remain upright in dispute.

3978 - Musa ibn Harun told me, saying: Amr ibn Hammad told us, saying: Asbat told us, from al-Suddi: "alladd al-khusam," crooked in dispute. [[This is part of the earlier report no. 3961.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: These two sayings are close in meaning, because crookedness in dispute is from contention and obstinacy.

* *

Others said: The meaning of that is: he is lying in his speech.

Those who said this:

3979 - Al-Qasim told us, saying: Al-Husayn told us, saying: Waki' told us, from some of his companions, from al-Hasan: "al-Alladd al-khusam," the one whose speech is false.

* *

This saying may have a meaning like the first two, if its speaker meant that he disputes with falsehood in speech, and lies, being contentious and deviating from the truth.

* *

As for "al-khisam," it is a verbal noun from the saying of the speaker: "I disputed with so-and-so, khisaman and mukhasamah."

* *

This is a report from Allah, blessed and exalted, about the hypocrite whom He informed His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ that his speech and eloquence impress him when he speaks, and Allah calls to witness that he is right in that saying, due to the intensity of his contention and his disputing with falsehood and false speech.

The interpretation of the words of the Most High: ﴿And when he turns away, he strives in the land to cause corruption therein﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His words, may His praise be great, "And when he turns away" — that is, when this hypocrite departs from you, O Muhammad, turning away from you. (See the meaning of "tawalli" (turning away) in what has preceded: 2:162–163, 298, 535; then 3:115, 131.) As follows:

3980 - Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salamah related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq related to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad related to me, saying: Sa'id ibn Jubayr or Ikrimah related to me, from Ibn 'Abbas: "And when he turns away," he said: that is, when he goes out from you, "he strives." (The report 3980 is part of the earlier report No. 3962.)

* *

Some of them said: "And when he becomes angry."

Those who said this:

3981 - al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, saying: Ibn Jurayj said concerning His words, "And when he turns away," he said: when he becomes angry.

* *

So the meaning of the verse: And when this hypocrite goes out from you, O Muhammad, angry, he works in the land by that which God has forbidden him, seeks therein disobedience to God, cuts off the road and spreads corruption on the path of God's servants, as we have already mentioned just before, concerning the deed of al-Akhnas ibn Shariq al-Thaqafi, of whom al-Suddi mentioned that this verse was revealed concerning him, by his burning the crops of the Muslims and killing their donkeys. (See report No. 3961 above.)

* *

"Sa'y" in the speech of the Arabs means work. It is said of it: "So-and-so strives for his family," meaning: he works for what returns benefit to them. From this is the saying of al-A'sha:

"And he strove for Kindah the striving of one who does not depend on others, Qays, so that he harmed its enemy and built for it..." (His Diwan: 25. In the printed edition it read "wa-nabaaliha," which is an error. Qays is Qays ibn Ma'dikarib al-Kindi, whom he often praised and extolled.)

He means by this: he worked for them in noble deeds.

* *

Mujahid also said in accordance with what we have said.

3982 - Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning God's words, "And when he turns away, he strives," he said: he works.

* *

The people of interpretation differed concerning the meaning of "corruption" (ifsad), which God, may He be exalted, attributed to this hypocrite.

Some of them said: its interpretation is what we have said of it: his cutting off the road and frightening the path, as we have already mentioned before concerning the deed of al-Akhnas ibn Shariq.

* *

Others said: rather, the meaning of that is severing the ties of kinship and shedding the blood of the Muslims.

Those who said this:

3983 - al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, concerning His words, "he strives in the land to cause corruption therein": severing the ties of kinship and shedding blood, the blood of the Muslims. If he is asked, "Why did you do such and such?" he says, "I seek nearness to God, may He be exalted, by it."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct statement on this matter is to say that God, blessed and exalted, described this hypocrite as one who, when he turns away, withdrawing from the Messenger of God (ﷺ), works corruption in the land of God. "Corruption" (ifsad) may include all acts of disobedience (see the meaning of "corruption in the land" in what has preceded: 1:287–290, 416; then the meaning of "fasad" in what will follow: 243, 244). This is because working at acts of disobedience is corruption in the land, and God did not restrict His description to some meanings of "corruption" over others. It is permissible that this corruption from him was in the sense of cutting off the road, and it is permissible that it was otherwise. Whichever of these was from him, it was corruption in the land, since that was disobedience to God, the Mighty and Majestic. However, what best matches the apparent sense of the revelation is that he was cutting off the road and frightening the path, because God, may His remembrance be exalted, described him in the context of the verse as one who "strives in the land to cause corruption therein and to destroy the tillage and the progeny," and that is more like the deed of one who frightens the path than of one who severs kinship.

* *

The interpretation of the words of the Most High: ﴿And He destroys the tillage and the progeny﴾

Abu Ja'far said: The people of interpretation differed concerning the manner of this hypocrite's "destruction," whom God described by what He described him with, of "destroying the tillage and the progeny."

Some of them said: that was from him by burning the crops of a people among the Muslims and hamstringing their donkeys.

3984 - Musa ibn Harun related this to me, saying: 'Amr ibn Hammad related to me, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi. (That is, the earlier report No. 3961.)

* *

Others said, with what follows:

3985 - Abu Kurayb related this to us, saying: 'Uthам related to us, saying: al-Nadr ibn 'Arabi related to us, from Mujahid: "And when he turns away, he strives in the land to cause corruption therein and to destroy the tillage and the progeny," the verse. He said: when he turns away he strives in the land through aggression and injustice, so God withholds the rain by that, and the tillage and progeny perish, "and God does not love corruption." He said: then Mujahid recited: ﴿Corruption has appeared on land and sea by what the hands of men have earned, that He may make them taste part of what they have done, that they might return﴾ [Al-Rum: 41]. He said: then he said: "By God, it is not by your sea here, but every town on flowing water is a 'sea.'" (This report will come in the commentary of the verse of Surah al-Rum, vol. 21, p. 32, Bulaq edition.)

* *

What Mujahid said, although it is a line of interpretation the verse can bear, what is closer to the apparent sense of the revelation is what we have mentioned from al-Suddi, and therefore we have chosen it.

* *

As for "tillage" (harth), it is the crops, and "progeny" (nasl) is descendants and offspring.

* *

"His destroying the crops" is by burning them. It is also possible that it was, as Mujahid said, by the withholding of rain because of his disobedience to his Lord and his striving to spread corruption in the land. It may also be that it was by killing those who tend it and maintain it, until it became corrupt and perished. Likewise it is permissible regarding "his destroying the progeny": that it was by killing their mothers or fathers from whom offspring come, so that killing the fathers and mothers would cut off their offspring. It is also permissible that it was as Mujahid said. However, although the verse can bear that, what is more fitting to its apparent sense is what al-Suddi said, except that al-Suddi mentioned that the one concerning whom this verse was revealed was revealed only regarding his killing the donkeys of a people among the Muslims and burning their crops. Although it may be so, it is not unsound that the verse was revealed concerning him while its meaning is intended to include everyone who follows his path in killing any animal whose killing is not permitted in any circumstance, and any animal whose killing is permitted in some circumstances when it is killed without right. Indeed, that is how I see it, because God, blessed and exalted, did not single out any part of that over another, but generalized it.

Those among the people of interpretation who said the general meaning also said so.

Those who said this:

3986 - Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Yahya and 'Abd al-Rahman related to us, both saying: Sufyan related to us, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Tamimi, that he asked Ibn 'Abbas concerning "and destroys the tillage and the progeny," and he said: the progeny of every creature.

3987 - Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Ibn 'Atiyyah related to us, saying: Isra'il related to us, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Tamimi, that he asked Ibn 'Abbas. He said: I said, "Do you see His words 'the tillage and the progeny'?" He said: The tillage is your tillage, and the progeny is the progeny of every creature.

3988 - Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Hakkam related to us, from 'Anbasah, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Tamimi, who said: I asked Ibn 'Abbas about "the tillage and the progeny," and he said: the tillage is what you cultivate, and the progeny is the progeny of every creature.

3989 - Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Hakkam related to us, from 'Amr, from Mutarrif, from Abu Ishaq, from a man of Tamim, from Ibn 'Abbas, the like of it. (The reports 3986–3989: "al-Tamimi" was discussed by my brother Sayyid Ahmad in his note on report No. 2095. But it appears from report No. 3989 that he is a man of the Banu Tamim, whose name is apparently unknown, who used to ask Ibn 'Abbas as the questioners of the community did; this is clear in the Musnad of Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi, No. 2739, p. 358.)

3990 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas: "and destroys the tillage and the progeny," the progeny of every creature, and people as well.

3991 - Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to me, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "and destroys the tillage," he said: the vegetation of the earth; "and the progeny" of every creature that walks among animals, of people and beasts.

3992 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, concerning His words "and destroys the tillage," he said: the vegetation of the earth; "and the progeny": the progeny of everything.

3993 - Ahmad ibn Ishaq related to us, saying: Abu Ahmad al-Zubayri related to us, saying: Hushaym related to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, he said: the tillage is the plants, and the progeny is the progeny of every creature.

3994 - 'Umar ibn al-Hasan related to me, from 'Ammar ibn al-Hasan, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far related to us, from his father, from al-Rabi': "and destroys the tillage," he said: the "tillage" which people cultivate is the vegetation of the earth; "and the progeny" is the progeny of every creature.
