This was hard for them, so they mentioned that to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed: "They ask you about orphans. Say: Setting things right for them is best. And if you mix with them, they are your brothers," so they mixed their food with their food and their drink with their drink.

4184 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us, from Amr, from Ata', from Sa'id, who said: When there was revealed ﴿And do not approach the property of the orphan except in the way that is best﴾, [he said]: We used to prepare food for the orphan, and some of it would be left over, so they would leave it until it spoiled. Then Allah revealed: "And if you mix with them, they are your brothers."

4185 - Yahya ibn Dawud al-Wasiti narrated to us, saying: Abu Usama narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Layla, from al-Hakam, who said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla was asked about the property of the orphan, and he said: When there was revealed ﴿And do not approach the property of the orphan except in the way that is best﴾, mixing with them was avoided, and they guarded against everything, even to the point of guarding against water. Then when there was revealed "And if you mix with them, they are your brothers," he said: So they mixed with them.

4186 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, concerning His words: "They ask you about orphans," the whole verse. He said: Allah had previously revealed in "Surat Bani Isra'il" [i.e., Surat al-Isra'] ﴿And do not approach the property of the orphan except in the way that is best﴾, and it weighed heavily upon them, so they did not mix with them in food or anything else. This was difficult for them, so Allah revealed the concession and said: "And if you mix with them, they are your brothers."

4187 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada, who said: When there was revealed ﴿And do not approach the property of the orphan except in the way that is best﴾, people withdrew from the orphans and did not mix with them in food, drink or property. He said: This was difficult for the people, so they asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed: "They ask you about orphans. Say: Setting things right for them is best. And if you mix with them, they are your brothers."

4188 - It was related to me from Ammar, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi', concerning His words: "They ask you about orphans. Say: Setting things right for them is best. And if you mix with them," the verse. He said: It was mentioned to us, and Allah knows best, that it was revealed concerning "the Children of Israel" [i.e., Surat al-Isra'] ﴿And do not approach the property of the orphan except in the way that is best until he reaches maturity﴾, and it was difficult for them, so they did not mix with them in food, drink or anything else. This was hard for them, so Allah revealed the concession and said: "They ask you about orphans. Say: Setting things right for them is best. And if you mix with them, they are your brothers," meaning: mixing with them in riding an animal, drinking milk and being served by a servant. That is to say: the guardian who is in charge of their affairs – there is no harm upon him in riding the animal, drinking the milk or being served by the servant.

* *

Others said concerning this:

4189 - Amr ibn Ali narrated to me, saying: Imran ibn Uyayna narrated to us, saying: Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His words: "Indeed, those who consume the property of orphans unjustly, they are only consuming fire into their bellies," the verse. He said: A man would have an orphan under his guardianship, and he would set aside his food, his drink and his vessels. This was difficult for the Muslims, so Allah revealed: "And if you mix with them, they are your brothers, and Allah knows the corrupter from the reformer," so He permitted their mixing with them.

4190 - Abu al-Sa'ib narrated to me, saying: Hafs ibn Ghiyath narrated to us, saying: Ash'ath narrated to us, from al-Sha'bi, who said: When this verse was revealed: "Indeed, those who consume the property of orphans unjustly, they are only consuming fire into their bellies, and they will [soon] burn in a Blaze," he said: The people avoided the orphans, and a man would set aside his food from their food, his property from their property and his drink from their drink. He said: This was difficult for the people, so there was revealed: "And if you mix with them, they are your brothers, and Allah knows the corrupter from the reformer." Al-Sha'bi said: Whoever mixes with an orphan should be generous to him, and whoever mixes with him in order to eat from his property should not do so.

4191 - Ali ibn Dawud narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His words: "They ask you about orphans. Say: Setting things right for them is best." That was because when Allah revealed: "Indeed, those who consume the property of orphans unjustly, they are only consuming fire into their bellies, and they will [soon] burn in a Blaze," the Muslims disliked taking orphans in, and they were reluctant to mix with them in anything. So they asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and Allah revealed: "Say: Setting things right for them is best. And if you mix with them, they are your brothers."

4192 - al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: I asked Ata' ibn Abi Rabah about His words: "They ask you about orphans. Say: Setting things right for them is best, and if you mix with them, they are your brothers." He said: When "Surat al-Nisa'" was revealed, the people set aside their food and did not mix with them. He said: Then they came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: "It is hard for us to set aside the food of the orphans while they eat with us!" So there was revealed: "And if you mix with them, they are your brothers." Ibn Jurayj said: Mujahid said: They set their food apart from their food, their milk apart from their milk and their condiments apart from their condiments. This was difficult for them, so there was revealed: "And if you mix with them, they are your brothers." He said: Mixing with the orphan is in pasture and condiments. Ibn Jurayj said: Ibn Abbas said: [it is in] milk, serving by a servant and riding an animal. Ibn Jurayj said: And in dwellings, and dwellings in that day were scarce.

4193 - Muhammad ibn Sinan narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan al-Ashqar narrated to us, saying: Abu Kudayna informed us, from Ata', from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: When there was revealed "And do not approach the property of the orphan except in the way that is best," and "Indeed, those who consume the property of orphans unjustly," the people avoided the property and food of the orphan, until it would spoil, whether it was meat or something else. This was hard on the people, so they complained to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and Allah revealed: "They ask you about orphans. Say: Setting things right for them is best."

4194 - Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to us, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Qays ibn Sa'd – or Isa, from Qays ibn Sa'd, Abu Asim doubted – from Mujahid: "And if you mix with them, they are your brothers," he said: Mixing with the orphan is in pasture and condiments.

* *

Others said: Rather, avoiding and shunning the property of the orphan was one of the customs of the Arabs. So they asked for a ruling on this because of its difficulty for them, and they were given a ruling by what Allah explained in His Book.

Mention of those who said this:

4195 - Musa ibn Harun narrated to me, saying: Amr ibn Hammad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "They ask you about orphans. Say: Setting things right for them is best. And if you mix with them, they are your brothers, and Allah knows the corrupter from the reformer." He said: The Arabs used to be strict regarding the orphan, to the extent that they would not eat with him from one dish, nor ride his camel, nor employ his servant. So they came to the Prophet ﷺ and asked him about it, and he said: "Say: Setting things right for them is best," setting right his property and his affairs is best for him. "And if you mix with them, then they eat with you, you feed them, you ride their mount, you carry them, and you employ their servant and they serve you, then they are better" – "and Allah knows the corrupter from the reformer."

4196 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas concerning His words: "They ask you about orphans. Say: Setting things right for them is best," up to "Indeed, Allah is Mighty and Wise." The people, when an orphan was in the care of one of them, would put his food in one place and his milk in another, out of fear of sin. The believers were struck by hardship, and they did not have what they could give as servants to the orphans. So Allah said: "Say: Setting things right for them is best, and if you mix with them," to the end of the verse.

4197 - It was related to me from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, saying: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say concerning His words: "They ask you about the people." They used to glorify the status of the orphan in the Jahiliyya, so they would not touch any of their property, nor ride their animals, nor feed them any food. Then in Islam they suffered severe hardship, to the point that they needed the property of the orphans, so they asked the Prophet of Allah ﷺ about the matter of the orphans and about mixing with them, and Allah revealed: "And if you mix with them, they are your brothers," meaning by "mixing": riding the animal, being served by a servant, and drinking milk.

* *

Abu Ja'far [al-Tabari] said: The interpretation of the verse, then, is: Your companions ask you, O Muhammad, about the property of the orphans, and about their mixing their property with theirs in expenditure, in food, in drink, in lodging and in service. So say to them: Your showing favour to them by setting right their property – without diminishing any of their property at all, and without taking any compensation from their property for your setting that right for them – is better for you with Allah and greater in reward for you, because of the reward and recompense that is yours in that. And it is better for them regarding their property in their immediate worldly life, because of the abundance of their property that results for them. "And if you mix with them," by sharing your property with their property in your expenditure, your food, your drink and your lodging, and you take from their property a compensation for your undertaking their affairs and their means and setting right their property – then they are your brothers, and brothers help one another and support one another. So the one with property helps the one in need, and the one strong in body helps the one weak. He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: So you, O believers, and your orphans are likewise: if you mix with them with your property – so you mix your food with their food, your drink with their drink and all your property with their property, and you gain some advantage from their property through your undertaking of their affairs and their guardianship, and your toil over their means, with the regard of a compassionate brother toward his brother, acting between himself and them in accordance with what Allah has made obligatory and required of him – then that is lawful for you, because you are brothers to one another, as:

4198 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: "And if you mix with them, they are your brothers," he said: A man may mix with his brother.

4199 - Ahmad ibn Hazim narrated to me, saying: Abu Nu'aym narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu Maskin, from Ibrahim, who said: I truly dislike that the property of the orphan should be like filth. [Note: al-'urra means filth and the excrement of people; he means that one should avoid it as one avoids filth.]

4200 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Hisham al-Dastawa'i, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, from A'isha, who said: I truly dislike that the property of the orphan should be filth for me, until I mix his food with my food and his drink with my drink. [Note: This report is in Tafsir Ibn Kathir 1:505 and al-Durr al-Manthur 1:256, and I did not find it anywhere else. Regarding "al-'urra," its explanation has already passed. In Tafsir Ibn Kathir the reading is "'indi hidda" (in my possession, a sharpness), and perhaps its correct form is what is in the tafsir.]

* *

Abu Ja'far [al-Tabari] said: If someone says to us: How is it that He said "fa-ikhwanukum" (then they are your brothers) with "al-ikhwan" in the nominative, while He said in another place ﴿And if you fear, then [pray] on foot or riding﴾ [Surah al-Baqarah: 239]?

It is said: Because the two meanings differ. That is because the orphans of the believers are brothers of the believers, whether or not the believers mix with them with their property. So the meaning of the sentence is: "And if you mix with them, then they are your brothers." "Al-ikhwan" is in the nominative by the implied word that has been omitted, which is "hum" (they), as the sentence indicates it. And the mention of "al-ikhwan" was not intended as information that they were brothers because of the guardians' mixing with them. Had that been the intended meaning, the reading would have been in the accusative, and its meaning would then be: "And if you mix with them, then mix with your brothers." But it was read in the nominative because of what I have described: that they are brothers of the believers who are in their charge, whether or not they mix with them.

As for His words ﴿rijalan aw rukbanan﴾ [on foot or riding], it is in the accusative, because they are circumstantial clauses (hal) of the verb, not permanent ones, and "huwa" (he/it) cannot be used with them. That is because if you made "huwa" apparent with them, the sentence would become impossible. Do you not see that if someone said: "If you fear from your enemy that you will pray standing, then he is on foot or riding," the intended meaning of the sentence would be void? That is because the interpretation of the sentence is: "If you fear from your enemy that you will pray standing, then pray on foot or riding." So it is in the accusative in accordance with what precedes it in the speech, just as you say in similar speech: "If you wear garments, then white," so you put it in the accusative, because you mean: "If you wear garments, then wear white" – and you do not mean to inform that all garments worn are white. If you intended to inform of that, you would say: "If you wear garments, then white" in the nominative, since the form of the speech would be information from you about the wearer, that every garment worn is white. Because you then mean: "If you wear garments, then they are white." [Note: See the detailed explanation of this in al-Farra's Ma'ani al-Qur'an as well, 1:141–142.]

If he says: Is it permissible to read "fa-ikhwanukum" in the accusative?

It is said: It is permissible in Arabic. As for in recitation, we have prohibited it only because the reciters are unanimous in reading it in the nominative. As for in Arabic, we have permitted it, because it is good with it to repeat the verb implied in the preceding clause in both: "And if you mix with them, then [you mix with] your brothers, you mix" – and that would be permissible in the speech of the Arabs. [Note: See the detailed explanation of this in al-Farra's Ma'ani al-Qur'an as well, 1:141–142.]

The exegesis of the words of Him, exalted is He: ﴿And Allah knows the corrupter from the reformer﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His remembrance be exalted, He means: Your Lord has indeed permitted you to mix with orphans in the manner He has permitted, [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "Indeed your Lord, though He permitted you..." which is a disordered statement, and what has been established here is probably closer to the correct meaning.]] so fear Allah regarding yourselves, lest you mix with them while you intend to consume their wealth through falsehood, and make your mixing with them a means for you to corrupt their property and devour it without right, thereby incurring from Him the punishment against which you have no power. For He knows whoever among you mixes with his orphan, sharing with him in his food, drink, dwelling, servants and herds during that mixing, what it is that he intends by his mixing with him: corrupting his property and consuming it falsely, or reforming it and increasing it? For nothing of that is hidden from Him, [[In the manuscript: "lā nahā ʿalayhi minhu shayʾ," and there is a corruption in it that I have not clarified; what is in the printed edition is good in the context of the meaning.]] and He knows which of you intends the reform of his property and which intends its corruption. As follows:

4201 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning the words of Allah, may His remembrance be exalted: "And Allah knows the corrupter from the reformer." He said: Allah knows when you mix your property with his: do you intend to reform his property, or to corrupt it so that you consume it without right?

4202 - Abu al-Sa'ib narrated to me, saying: Hafs ibn Ghiyath narrated to us, saying: Ash'ath narrated to us, from al-Sha'bi: "And Allah knows the corrupter from the reformer." Al-Sha'bi said: Whoever mixes with an orphan, let him be generous to him; and whoever mixes with him in order to consume his property, let him not do so. [[The report 4202: In the manuscript and the printed edition: "Abu al-Sa'ib narrated to me, saying: Ash'ath narrated to us..." This is a defective chain, having dropped "saying: Hafs ibn Ghiyath narrated to us." This chain has passed several times; the nearest is 4190, and this report is its abridgment.]]

* *

The exegesis of the words of Him, exalted is He: ﴿And if Allah had willed, He would have burdened you﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His remembrance be exalted, He means: And if Allah had willed, He would have prohibited to you what He made lawful for you of mixing your orphans' affairs with your property and their property with yours; it would have strained you and been hard upon you, and you would not have been able to carry out what was obligatory upon you of the right of Allah, exalted is He, and the duty He imposed upon you in that. But He granted you license in it and made it easy for you, out of mercy and compassion for you.

* *

The people of interpretation differed concerning the interpretation of His words: "la-a'natakum" (would have burdened you). Some of them said:

4203 - Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, from 'Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Qays ibn Sa'd - or 'Isa, from Qays ibn Sa'd - from Mujahid (Abu 'Asim doubted), concerning the words of Allah, may His remembrance be exalted: "And if Allah had willed, He would have burdened you": it would have prohibited you the pasture and the condiment.

Abu Ja'far said: Mujahid meant by this: the grazing of the guardian's livestock together with the livestock of the orphan, and eating from his condiment. For he interpreted His words: "And if you mix with them, they are your brothers," as meaning the mixing of the guardian with the orphan in pasturing and condiment. [[See the earlier report No. 4194.]]

* *

4204 - Ali ibn Dawud narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talha, from Ibn 'Abbas: "And if Allah had willed, He would have burdened you," meaning: If Allah had willed, He would have distressed you and constrained you, but He made it wide and easy, and said: ﴿And whoever is rich, let him abstain, and whoever is poor, let him eat in a reasonable manner﴾ [Surah an-Nisa: 6].

4205 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada: "And if Allah had willed, He would have burdened you," meaning: He would have exhausted you, so you would not fulfil the right nor perform the obligation.

4206 - It was narrated to me from 'Ammar, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi' the like of it, except that he said: so you would not act upon the right.

4207 - Musa narrated to me, saying: 'Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "And if Allah had willed, He would have burdened you," meaning: He would have made it hard upon you.

4208 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning the words of Allah: "And if Allah had willed, He would have burdened you," he said: It would have been hard for you in the matter. That is the 'anat (burden).

4209 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mansur, from al-Hakam, from Miqsam, from Ibn 'Abbas, his statement: "And if Allah had willed, He would have burdened you," he said: If Allah had willed, He would have made what you took of the orphans' wealth a cause of ruin (mu'biqan).

* *

These statements that we have mentioned from those whom we have named, although the wording of their speakers differs, are close in meaning. For whoever is forbidden something is thereby constrained in that thing, and whoever is constrained in something is put in difficulty regarding it, and whoever is put in difficulty regarding something or constrained in it has been strained. All of that returns to the meaning I described: that its meaning is hardship and difficulty.

Hence it is said: "'Anita fulan" (so-and-so was distressed) when the matter was hard upon him and strained him, so that "he is 'a'nat, 'anat (distressed)," as Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, said: ﴿It grieves him that you suffer﴾ [Surah at-Tawbah: 128], meaning: what was hard upon you, harmed you, and strained you. And from it His words, may His remembrance be exalted: ﴿That is for him who fears 'anat (sin/hardship) among you﴾ [Surah an-Nisa: 25]. So this is when the one who is distressed becomes distressed. If another makes him so, it is said: "a'natahu fulan fi kadha" (so-and-so burdened him with such-and-such) when he strained him and imposed on him a matter he strained to carry out, "yu'nituhu i'natan." Likewise His words "la-a'natakum" mean: it would have necessarily caused you distress by prohibiting you what strains and constrains you, what you are unable to abstain from and to fulfil the obligation regarding it.

* *

Others said: The meaning of that is: He would have ruined you and destroyed you.

Those who said so:

4210 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Talq ibn Ghannam narrated to us, from Za'ida, from Mansur, from al-Hakam, from Miqsam, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: He recited to us: "And if Allah had willed, He would have burdened you." Ibn 'Abbas said: If Allah had willed, He would have made what you took of the orphans' wealth a cause of ruin.

4211 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Adam narrated to us, from Fudayl - and Jarir, from Mansur = and Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mansur = from al-Hakam, from Miqsam, from Ibn 'Abbas: "And if Allah had willed, He would have burdened you," he said: He would have made what you took a cause of ruin. [[Report 4211: It has already passed with the second chain, No. 4209.]]

* *

The exegesis of the words of Him, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, Allah is Mighty and Wise﴾ (220)

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His remembrance be exalted, He means: Indeed Allah is "Mighty" in His authority; no preventer can stop Him from the punishment He might bring upon you if He burdened you with what would strain you to carry out of His obligations, so that you fell short in carrying it out; and no repeller can repel Him from that, nor from anything else which He does to you or to others of that kind, should He do it. [[In the printed edition: "should He do it Himself, but," and the correct good reading is from the manuscript.]] But by the bounty of His mercy He has favoured you by not burdening you with that. And He is "Wise" in that, were He to do it to you or in His other judgments and arrangements; no defect, deficiency, weakness or fault enters His acts, for it is the act of one of wisdom who does not ignore the consequences of matters, so that his arrangement would incur blame in its outcome, as blame enters the acts of creatures due to their ignorance of the consequences of matters, through the badness of their initial choices in them.

**The Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 2, Verse 221 (Part 1 of 2)**

**On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Do not marry idolatresses until they believe﴾**

Abu Ja'far said: The people of interpretation (ta'wil, the explanation of the Qur'an's meaning) differ regarding this verse. Was it revealed to refer to every idolatress, or does its ruling refer only to some idolatresses and not others? [[In the printed edition: "or was its ruling intended" in the accusative case; I have kept what is in the manuscript.]] And was any part of it abrogated (naskh, the cancellation of a ruling by a later revelation) after the ruling became binding, or not?

Some said: It was revealed to forbid the marriage of every idolatress to every Muslim, of whatever kind of polytheism she was: a worshipper of idols, [[In the printed edition: "a worshipper of idols or she was a Jewess..." In the manuscript: "a worshipper of idols was a Jewess..." Both are corrupt; the correct reading is what I have given, with the addition of "was".]] or a Jewess, a Christian, a Magian, or of any other kind of polytheism. Then the prohibition on marrying the People of the Book was abrogated by His words: ﴿They ask you what is lawful for them. Say: The good things are made lawful for you...﴾ up to ﴿and the food of those who were given the Scripture is lawful for you, and your food is lawful for them, and the chaste women from among the believers and the chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture before you﴾ [Surah al-Ma'idah: 4–5].

Mention of those who said this:

4212 – ʿAli ibn Waqid narrated to me, saying: ʿAbd Allah ibn Salih narrated to me, saying: Muʿawiya ibn Salih narrated to me, from ʿAli ibn Abi Talha, from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding His words: "Do not marry idolatresses until they believe," and then he made an exception for the women of the People of the Book, saying: ﴿and the chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture﴾ are lawful for you ﴿when you have given them their bridal payments﴾. [[The report 4212: In the manuscript and the printed edition it reads "ʿAli ibn Waqid narrated to me, he said: ʿAbd Allah ibn Salih narrated to me," and the correct reading is what I have given. This chain recurs often, both before and after, and the nearest instance is no. 4204. The verse in the printed edition and the manuscript is divided by the words "are lawful for you," with the words "from before you" omitted, and I fear a copyist may have confused this. But I keep what all the copies agree upon.]]

4213 – Muhammad ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, from al-Husayn ibn Waqid, from Yazid al-Nahwi, from ʿIkrima and al-Hasan al-Basri, both said: "Do not marry idolatresses until they believe." Then the women of the People of the Book were abrogated from this, and God made them lawful to the Muslims.

4214 – Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, from ʿIsa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding His words: "Do not marry idolatresses until they believe." He said: The women of the people of Mecca and others of the idolaters. Then He made lawful from them the women of the People of the Book.

4215 – al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the same.

4216 – It was reported to me from ʿAmmar, who said: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi' regarding His words: "Do not marry idolatresses," up to His words: "that they may remember." He said: God forbade idolatresses in this verse. Then He revealed in Surah al-Ma'idah, making an exception for the women of the People of the Book, saying: ﴿and the chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture before you, when you have given them their bridal payments﴾.

* *

Others said: Rather, this verse was revealed with its ruling intended for the idolatresses of the Arabs. No part of it was abrogated, nor was any exception made. It is rather a verse whose outward meaning is general and whose inner meaning is specific. [[In the manuscript and the printed edition: "Rather, it is a general verse in its outward meaning..." The correct reading is what I have given.]]

Mention of those who said this:

4217 – Bishr ibn Muʿadh narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Zurayʿ narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatada regarding His words: "Do not marry idolatresses until they believe," meaning: the idolatresses of the Arabs, those among whom there is no Scripture they recite. [[In the manuscript: "a Scripture they recite from," which is better.]]

4218 – al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Maʿmar informed us, from Qatada regarding His words: "Do not marry idolatresses until they believe." He said: The idolatresses are those who are not from the People of the Book, and Hudhayfa married a Jewess or a Christian woman. [[This means Hudhayfa ibn al-Yaman, companion of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and he was the keeper of his secret (ﷺ) concerning the hypocrites. No one knew them except Hudhayfa; the Messenger of God (ﷺ) informed him of them. See the following report, no. 4221.]]

4219 – It was reported to me from ʿAmmar, who said: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from Qatada regarding His words: "Do not marry idolatresses until they believe," meaning the idolatresses of the Arabs, who have no Scripture they recite.

4220 – Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Hammad, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr regarding His words: "Do not marry idolatresses until they believe." He said: The idolatresses of the idol-worshippers.

* *

Others said: Rather, this verse was revealed with its ruling intended for every idolatress of whatever kinds of polytheism she was, none of them being singled out from another, whether she was an idol-worshipper, a Magian, or a follower of a Scripture, and no part of it was abrogated.

Mention of those who said this:

4221 – ʿUbayd ibn Adam ibn Abi Iyas al-ʿAsqalani narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Hamid ibn Bahram al-Fazari narrated to us, saying: Shahr ibn Hawshab narrated to us, saying: I heard ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAbbas say: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) forbade the various kinds of women, except for the believing emigrant women, and he forbade every woman of a religion other than Islam. God, may His remembrance be exalted, said: ﴿And whoever disbelieves in faith, his deed has become void﴾ [Surah al-Ma'idah: 5]. Talha ibn ʿUbayd Allah married a Jewess, and Hudhayfa ibn al-Yaman married a Christian woman. ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, became exceedingly angry, to the point that he intended to attack them both. They said: "We will divorce them, O Commander of the Faithful, so do not be angry!" He said: "If their divorce is lawful, then their marriage is lawful too. But I will take them from you, humbled and debased." [[The report 4221: "ʿAbd al-Hamid ibn Bahram al-Fazari" in the printed edition is "ʿAbd al-Hamid ibn Barham." He is biographically recorded in al-Tahdhib. Abu Dawud, Ibn Maʿin and others declared him trustworthy. Shuʿba said: "Truthful, except that he narrates from Shahr ibn Hawshab, and they found fault with him for narrating much from Shahr, and Shahr is weak." My brother's discussion of the trustworthiness of Shahr has already preceded, at no. 1389, and regarding ʿAbd Allah ibn Bahram, at no. 1605. Ibn Kathir said in his Tafsir (1:507) after narrating the report: "It is a very strange report, and this report is strange from ʿUmar." The later discussion by al-Tabari judges it weak.
The word al-saghra is the plural of saghir, meaning one who accepts humiliation. Qama' is the plural of qami', meaning one who is humbled and debased even if he is not short. Al-qami' means short. In the manuscript and in Ibn Kathir it reads "qam'a," which is not a regular plural and is not found in the lexicons. But if the report is sound, it is an echo (ittiba') of "saghra," and similar things are common in their speech.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of these sayings for the interpretation of the verse is that of Qatada: that God, may His remembrance be exalted, meant by His words "Do not marry idolatresses until they believe" those idolatresses who are not from the People of the Book; and that the verse is general in its outward meaning and specific in its inner meaning, and no part of it was abrogated; and that the women of the People of the Book are not included in it. This is because God, may His remembrance be exalted, made lawful by His words ﴿and the chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture before you﴾ for the believers to marry their chaste women, just as He permitted them to marry the women of the believers.

We have explained in another place in this book of ours, and in our book ﴿The Book of the Subtle Explanation﴾: [[See what has preceded, 2:534–535, then 3:385, 563.]] that whenever two verses or two reports exist, one of which negates the ruling of the other by the nature of reason, it is not permissible to judge that one of them abrogates the ruling of the other, unless there is a proof from a report whose arrival is a decisive excuse. That does not exist here: that His words ﴿and the chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture﴾ abrogate what had become obligatory to forbid of women by His words "Do not marry idolatresses until they believe." [[In the printed edition: "that His words." I have kept what is in the manuscript, which is more eloquent in Arabic.]] Since that is not established in this way, [[In the manuscript and the printed edition: "If that is not established," which is a plain error. The correct reading is what I have given. Otherwise Abu Ja'far's speech would contradict itself.]] then the statement of one who says "this one abrogates that one" is a claim for which he has no proof, and the one who makes a claim without proof is arbitrary, and arbitrariness is something no one is unable to do. [[Abu Ja'far's arguments in his reasoning, which are decisive against every opponent who differs from him, are the arguments of one who is perceptive of meanings, supported by reason, able to clarify hidden meanings and to distinguish between intertwined meanings.]]

* *

As for the saying that was narrated from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Ibn ʿAbbas, from ʿUmar, may God be pleased with him, regarding his separation between Talha, Hudhayfa and their two wives, who were both People of the Book: it is a saying with no meaning, because it contradicts what the whole community agrees upon regarding its permissibility, from the Book of God, may His remembrance be exalted, and the report of His Messenger (ﷺ). It has been narrated from ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, a statement contrary to that, with a chain that is more sound than it, and it is what follows:

4222 – Musa ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman al-Masruqi narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Sufyan ibn Saʿid narrated to us, from Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad, from Zayd ibn Wahb, who said: ʿUmar said: "The Muslim man may marry a Christian woman, but a Christian man may not marry a Muslim woman." [[The report 4222: This is a sound chain, continuous up to ʿUmar. Muhammad ibn Bashshar ibn al-Farafisa ibn al-Mukhtar al-ʿAbdi, the memorizer (al-Hafiz), is trustworthy by general agreement. Sufyan ibn Saʿid is al-Thawri. Zayd ibn Wahb al-Juhani is a major Successor (tabiʿi) who lived in the period between the Prophet and the Companions (mukhadram); he travelled to the Prophet (ﷺ) but died on the way. He is trustworthy and narrated much. He has a biography in Tarikh Baghdad 8:440–442 and in al-Isaba 3:46–47.
This report was narrated by al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan al-Kubra 7:172, by way of Sufyan, who is al-Thawri, with this chain.
Ibn Kathir mentioned it (1:507–508) from al-Tabari's narration and declared its chain sound.]]

* *

ʿUmar mentioned to Talha and Hudhayfa, may God have mercy on them, their marriage to a Jewess and a Christian woman, out of fear that people would follow them in that, and so would shun Muslim women, or for other meanings; so he commanded them to release them. As follows:

4223 – Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Idris narrated to us, saying: al-Salt ibn Bahram narrated to us, from Shaqiq, who said: Hudhayfa married a Jewess, and ʿUmar wrote to him: "Release her." He wrote back: "Do you think she is forbidden, so that I should release her?" He said: "I do not think she is forbidden, but I fear that you will take up the prostitutes among them." [[The report 4223: al-Salt ibn Bahram al-Taymi al-Kufi is trustworthy; Ahmad, Ibn Maʿin and others declared him trustworthy. I discussed his case at length in my edition of Sahih Ibn Hibban, no. 81.
Shaqiq is Ibn Salama al-Asadi, the great and well-known Successor. Already mentioned at no. 177.
This report was also narrated by al-Bayhaqi 7:172, by way of Sufyan, with this chain.
Ibn Kathir mentioned it (1:507) from al-Tabari's narration and said: "This is a sound chain. Al-Khallal narrated, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Waki', from al-Salt, something similar." Al-Suyuti mentioned it (1:256) and attributed it additionally to ʿAbd al-Razzaq.
Al-Jassas mentioned it in Ahkam al-Qur'an 1:333 and al-Qurtubi in his Tafsir 3:68, without a chain. In the printed edition here, and in Ibn Kathir and al-Suyuti, the word "al-mu'minat" appears instead of "al-mumisat"!! This is a strange distortion, occurring in three books. The correct reading, confirmed by al-Bayhaqi, al-Jassas and al-Qurtubi, is "al-mumisat."]]

And:

4224 – Tamim ibn al-Muntasir narrated to us, saying: Ishaq al-Azraq informed us, from Sharik, from Ash'ath ibn Sawwar, from al-Hasan, from Jabir ibn ʿAbd Allah, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "We marry the women of the People of the Book, but they do not marry our women." [[The report 4224: Ishaq al-Azraq is Ishaq ibn Yusuf, already mentioned at no. 332. Sharik is Ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Nakhaʿi the judge, already mentioned at no. 2527. Al-Hasan is al-Basri.
I have not found this hadith in any of the collections of hadith, except in this place. Ibn Kathir narrated it from him (1:508), then mentioned al-Tabari's comment that follows it, and then said: "Thus said Ibn Jarir, may God have mercy on him."
Ibn Jarir's remark that "although there is in its chain what there is" perhaps refers, may God have mercy on him, to the view that al-Hasan al-Basri did not hear from Jabir. In al-Marasil of Ibn Abi Hatim, p. 13: "Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn al-Bara' narrated to us, saying: ʿAli ibn al-Madini said: al-Hasan did not hear anything from Jabir ibn ʿAbd Allah. Abu Zurʿa was asked: Did al-Hasan meet Jabir ibn ʿAbd Allah? He said: No. Muhammad ibn Saʿid ibn Baladj narrated to us, saying: I heard ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn al-Hakam say: I heard Jarir ask Bahz about al-Hasan: which of the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) did he meet? He said: He did not hear from Jabir ibn ʿAbd Allah. I asked my father: Did al-Hasan hear from Jabir? He said: I do not think so, but Hisham ibn Hassan says: 'From al-Hasan, Jabir ibn ʿAbd Allah narrated to us,' and I deny this; al-Hasan's narration from Jabir is only a book, although he did reach Jabir."
I hold that the narration of Hisham ibn Hassan is sufficient to establish al-Hasan's hearing from Jabir. Ibn ʿUyayna said: "Hisham was the most knowledgeable of people about the hadith of al-Hasan."
The meaning of this hadith is established from Jabir as a statement of his own, halted (mawquf) at him. al-Shafi'i narrated it in al-Umm, vol. 5, p. 6, by way of Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, and likewise al-Bayhaqi narrated it, 7:172, by way of al-Shafi'i.
The halted report, in our view, is not used to put a flaw in the raised (marfu') report; rather it supports and confirms it, as we have explained in other places in our books. Praise be to God.]]

* *

So this report, although there is in its chain what there is, the saying based on it, because of the consensus of all on the soundness of saying it, is more preferable than the report of ʿAbd al-Hamid ibn Bahram, from Shahr ibn Hawshab.

* *

So the meaning of the speech is then: "Do not marry, O believers, idolatresses other than the People of the Book, until they believe, so that they affirm belief in God, His Messenger, and what was revealed to him."

* *

**On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And a believing slave-woman is better than an idolatress﴾**

Abu Ja'far said: By His words "And a believing slave-woman," God, may His remembrance be exalted, means: a woman who believes in God, His Messenger, and what he brought from God, is better in the sight of God and superior to a free idolatress, unbelieving, even if her lineage is noble and her origin honourable. He means: Do not seek marriages with women of rank from among the people of polytheism, for the believing slave-women are a better match in the sight of God than them.

* *

It has been mentioned that this verse was revealed concerning a man who married a slave-woman, and was blamed for that, and a free idolatress was offered to him.

Mention of those who said this:

4225 – Musa ibn Harun narrated to me, saying: ʿAmr ibn Hammad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding "Do not marry idolatresses until they believe. A believing slave-woman is better than an idolatress, even if she pleases you": He said: It was revealed concerning ʿAbd Allah ibn Rawaha, who had a black slave-woman, and he became angry with her and slapped her. Then he was frightened and went to the Prophet (ﷺ) and informed him of her case. The Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: "What is she, O ʿAbd Allah?" He said: "O Messenger of God, she fasts, prays, performs the ablution well, and bears witness that there is no god but God and that you are the Messenger of God." He said: "She is a believer!" ʿAbd Allah said: "By Him who sent you with the truth, I will free her and marry her!" He did so, and some of the Muslims criticised him, saying: "He married a slave-woman!" They wanted to marry into the idolaters and to marry them off, desiring their lineage. So God revealed concerning them: "A believing slave-woman is better than an idolatress," and "A believing slave is better than an idolater."

4226 – al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: al-Hajjaj narrated to me, who said: Ibn Jurayj said regarding His words: "Do not marry into the idolatresses until they believe," He said: idolatresses, because of their nobility, until they believe.

* *

**On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿even if she pleases you﴾**

Abu Ja'far said: God, may His remembrance be exalted, means by this: Even if the idolatress from among those other than the People of the Book pleases you in beauty, lineage and wealth, do not marry her, for the believing slave-woman is better in the sight of God than her.

* *

We have placed "law" (lau) in the position of "in" (in), because the two are close in their articulation and meaning; and for this reason each of them is answered with the answer of the other, as we explained earlier. [[See what has preceded, 2:458, and al-Farra's Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1:143.]]

* *

**On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And do not marry [your women] to the idolaters until they believe, and a believing slave is better than an idolater, even if he pleases you﴾**

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His mention be exalted, He means that God has forbidden believing women to marry any polytheist, whatever he may be and whatever kind of polytheism he holds. So do not marry them to polytheists, O believers. That is forbidden to you. And a believing slave who affirms belief in God, His Messenger, and what came to him from God is better for you than a free polytheist, even if his lineage is noble and his origin honorable, and even if his lineage and descent impress you.
* *
Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali used to say: This statement of God, may His mention be exalted, is evidence that the guardians (awliya', sing. wali, the marriage guardian) of a woman have more right to marry her off than the woman herself.
4227 - Muhammad ibn Yazid Abu Hisham al-Rifa'i narrated to us, saying: Hafs ibn Ghiyath informed us, from a shaykh whom he did not name. Abu Ja'far said: Marriage by a guardian (wali) is in the Book of God. Then he recited: "And do not marry off [your women] to polytheists until they believe," with the ta' raised (tunkihu, passive form read as "tunkahu" with the tā' vowelled as a nominative).
4228 - Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah and al-Zuhri, regarding His words: "And do not marry polytheists." He said: It is not lawful for you to marry a Jewish or Christian woman, nor a polytheist from outside your religion.
4229 - Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, saying: Ibn Jurayj said: "And do not marry polytheists" - because of their nobility - "until they believe."
4230 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, from al-Husayn ibn Waqid, from Yazid al-Nahwi, from Ikrimah and al-Hasan al-Basri: "And do not marry polytheists until they believe." He said: He forbade Muslim women to marry their men, meaning the men of the polytheists.
* *
Concerning the interpretation of His words, may He be exalted: "Those invite to the Fire, but God invites to Paradise and forgiveness by His permission, and He makes clear His signs to the people that they may remember" (2:221).
Abu Ja'far said: By His words "Those" (ula'ika), He means these people whose marriage with the men and women of polytheism has been forbidden to you, O believers. "They invite you to the Fire," meaning: they invite you to act in ways that will cause you to enter the Fire, and that is the action they themselves perform, namely disbelief in God and His Messenger. The meaning is: do not accept what they say, do not seek their counsel, do not marry them, and do not marry into their families, for they will not spare you corruption. Rather, accept from God what He has commanded you, act upon it, and refrain from what He has forbidden you, for He invites you to Paradise, meaning He invites you to act in ways that will admit you into Paradise and make salvation from the Fire obligatory for you if you act upon it, and to what erases your sins or wrongdoings, pardoning them and concealing them from you.
* *
As for His words "by His permission" (bi-idhnihi), [[see the meaning of "idhn" (permission) above in vol. 2, p. 449, and in this part vol. 4, p. 286]], it means: He invites you to that by informing you of His way and path by which one reaches Paradise and forgiveness.
* *
Then He, may His mention be exalted, said: "And He makes clear His signs to the people that they may remember," meaning: He clarifies His proofs and evidences in His Book, which He sent down through His Messenger to His servants, so that they may remember, take heed, and distinguish between the two matters, one of which calls to the Fire and eternal abiding therein, and the other of which calls to Paradise and the forgiveness of sins, so that they may choose the better of the two for themselves. None fails to distinguish between these two except a dull-minded person of corrupted intellect.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 222 (part 1 of 3):

The exegesis of His words, ﴿They ask you concerning menstruation. Say: It is a harm﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His words "They ask you concerning menstruation," Exalted is He, He means: "Your companions ask you, O Muhammad, about menstruation (al-haydh)."

* *

It has been said that "al-mahid" (menstruation) is the verbal noun (masdar) of a verb whose past tense has a vowelled ayn with fatha and whose present has kasra, like the saying of the speaker: "daraba yadribu, habasa yahbisu, nazala yanzilu." The Arabs form its verbal noun on the pattern "mafal" and its noun on the pattern "mafil," like "al-madrab" and "al-madrib" from "darabtu," and "I stayed in a manzil and a manzil." What is heard in the doubled and the weak forms (with yaʾ and alif) is "al-maʿish and al-maʿash" and "al-maʿib and al-maʿab," as Ru'ba said regarding al-maʿish:

To You I complain of the hardship of livelihood (al-maʿish)
And the passing of years which plucked my feathers.

[The verse is from his Diwan, p. 78, from a qasida in which he praises al-Harith ibn Sulaym al-Hujaymi. Between the two verses in the Diwan is: "A time that squeezed the marrow with the pounding (of hardship)." The version in the Diwan, after it, is:
"And the toil of years that wore away my feathers,
The plucking of the bustard from a sparse, thin pasture."]

* *

The people asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about menstruation, as has been reported to us, because before Allah explained to them what they should know about its ruling, they would not share a house with a menstruating woman, nor eat from the same vessel with her, nor drink with her. So Allah informed them through this verse that what is required of them during the days of their women's menstruation is to abstain only from intercourse with them, and not from anything else such as lying down with them, eating with them, or drinking with them, as:

4231 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words, "They ask you concerning menstruation," up to His words, "until they are purified." The people of the Jahiliyyah would not share a house with a menstruating woman, nor eat with her from one vessel. So Allah, Exalted is He, sent down regarding that: He forbade her private part as long as she is menstruating, and permitted everything else: that you dye your head with her, that she eat your food, that she lie with you on your bed when she has a wrapper tied around her, apart from you.

[Ihtajaza bil-izar means: when he tied it around his waist. The hujzah (with a damma on the ha and sukun on the jim) is the place where the wrapper is tied, then the wrapper itself is called hujzah, and its plural is hujaz.]

4232 - It was narrated to me from Ammar, who said: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi' the like of it.

* *

It has also been said that they asked about this because during their women's days of menstruation they would avoid entering them at the place of the blood, and would have intercourse with them in their anuses. So Allah forbade them from approaching them during their days of menstruation until they are purified, then permitted them, once they had purified themselves from their menstruation, to approach them from where He had commanded them to keep away, and forbade approaching them in their anuses in every case.

Mention of those who said this:

4233 - Muhammad ibn Abd al-Malik ibn Abi al-Shawarib narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Wahid narrated to us, saying: Khusayf narrated to us, saying: Mujahid narrated to me, saying: They would avoid women during menstruation and would have intercourse with them in their anuses. So they asked the Prophet (ﷺ) about that, and Allah sent down: "They ask you concerning menstruation," up to: "So when they are purified, come to them from where Allah has commanded you" — in the vagina, do not go beyond it.

[In the printed edition: "wa la ta'duhu" (with a waw); the correct reading in the manuscript is without the waw.]

* *

It has been said that the questioner who asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about this was Thabit ibn al-Dahdah al-Ansari.

4234 - Musa ibn Harun narrated to me this, saying: Amr ibn Hammad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi.

* *

The exegesis of His words, ﴿Say: It is a harm﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By this, Exalted is He means: Say, O Muhammad, to whoever of your companions asks you about menstruation: "It is a harm."

* *

"Al-adha" is what one is harmed by of something disliked in it. In this place it is called "adha" because of the stench of its smell, its filth, and its impurity. It comprises many meanings of harm, more than one.

* *

The people of interpretation have differed in explaining the meaning of this, and some of what they said is close in meaning to other of it.

Some of them said: His words, "Say: It is a harm," mean: Say: It is filth (qadhar).

Mention of those who said this:

4235 - Musa ibn Harun narrated to me, saying: Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His words, "Say: It is a harm," he said: As for "adha," it is filth.

4236 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah regarding His words, "Say: It is a harm," he said: "Say: It is a harm," he said: filth.

* *

Others said: Say: It is blood.

Mention of those who said this:

4237 - Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Mu'ammal narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding His words, "They ask you concerning menstruation. Say: It is a harm," he said: The harm is the blood.

* *

The exegesis of His words, ﴿So keep away from women during menstruation﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His words, "So keep away from women during menstruation," Exalted is He means: So keep away from intercourse with women and marriage with them during their menstruation, as:

4238 - Ali ibn Dawud narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas regarding His words, "So keep away from women during menstruation," he says: keep away from marrying their private parts.

* *

The scholars differed regarding what it is obligatory for a man to keep away from in a menstruating woman.

Some of them said: What is obligatory for the man is to keep away from her entire body, so that he does not touch her body with any part of his own.

Mention of those who said this:

4239 - Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Hammad ibn Mas'adah narrated to us, saying: Awf narrated to us, from Muhammad, who said: I said to Ubaydah: What is lawful for me from my wife when she is menstruating? He said: The bed is one, and the covering is different. [Report 4239: In the printed edition and the manuscript: "al-lihaf wahid wa al-firash shatta" (the covering is one and the bed is different). This is meaningless, and the correct version will come by another route under number 4241.]

4240 - Tamim ibn al-Muntasir narrated to me, saying: Yazid informed us, saying: Muhammad narrated to us, from al-Zuhri, from Urwah, from Nadbah, client of the family of al-Abbas, who said: Maymunah bint al-Harith, or Hafsah bint Umar, sent me to the wife of Abdullah ibn Abbas, and there was a kinship between them through women. I found her bed separate from his bed, so I thought that this was due to estrangement. I asked her about his bed being separate from hers, and she said: I am menstruating, and when I menstruate he keeps his bed away from mine. So I returned and informed Maymunah, or Hafsah, and she sent me back to Ibn Abbas, saying: Your mother says to you: Have you turned away from the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)? By Allah, the Prophet (ﷺ) used to sleep with one of his wives while she was menstruating, and there was nothing between him and her except a garment that did not go beyond the knees. [Hadith 4240: Yazid is Ibn Harun. Muhammad is Ibn Ishaq. Nadbah, client of the family of Ibn Abbas: she was the client of Maymunah bint al-Harith, Mother of the Believers, the maternal aunt of Ibn Abbas. Perhaps she is described here as "client of the family of Ibn Abbas" because of the kinship between Ibn Abbas and Maymunah. She is reliable; Ibn Hibban mentioned her among the reliable narrators (al-Thiqat), p. 359, but he erred in stating that al-Zuhri narrated from her directly; al-Zuhri narrated from her through an intermediary. Ibn Sa'd included her biography, 8:364. Ibn Mandah and Abu Nu'aym mentioned her among the Companions.
Her name has been differently vocalized: it was said with a damma on the nun or a fatha, with a sukun on the dal, then a fatha on the bi'. It was also said: Dibyah, with a damma on the ba' (ba' muwahhadah), then a fatha on the dal, then a fathah on the shaddah yaʾ.
The hadith was narrated by Ahmad in al-Musnad 6:332 (Halabi edition) from Yazid ibn Harun, by this isnad, similar to it, with some abridgment. In his narration from Maymunah it is certain, without the doubt between her and Hafsah. This is the correct version; perhaps the doubt here is from al-Tabari, or from his teacher Tamim ibn al-Muntasir.
Then Ibn Ishaq erred here in making the hadith "from al-Zuhri, from Urwah." The error may be from Yazid ibn Harun. The correct version is "from al-Zuhri, from Habib, client of Urwah, from Nadbah." Accordingly the narrations converge in this isnad, as will come. It is supported by Ibn Sa'd having mentioned in her biography that she narrates from Urwah, and he narrated with his isnad a report from her, from Urwah ibn al-Zubayr.
"Habib, client of Urwah" is Habib al-A'war, client of Urwah ibn al-Zubayr. He is a reliable Successor (tabi'i); Ibn Sa'd said: "He died early, at the end of the rule of the Umayyads." Muslim included him in his Sahih.
The hadith was narrated, in its correct form, by al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan al-Kubra 1:313, through Bishr ibn Shu'ayb ibn Abi Hamzah, from his father, from al-Zuhri, who said: "Habib, client of Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, informed me that Nadbah, client of Maymunah, wife of the Prophet (ﷺ), informed him that Maymunah sent her to Abdullah ibn Abbas..." and he mentioned it at length.
Then the hadith is known from this route in its correct form, abridged without the story of Ibn Abbas. Ahmad narrated it in al-Musnad 6:332 (Halabi) from Hajjaj and Abu Kamil, from al-Layth, from Ibn Shihab, from Habib, client of Urwah, without mentioning its wording, referring it to the previous narration. Then he narrated it again, pp. 335-336, from Hajjaj and Abu Kamil, by the same isnad, and mentioned its wording in abridged form from Maymunah, without the story.
Likewise Abu Dawud narrated it, p. 267, and Ibn Hibban in his Sahih 2:569 (manuscript of al-Ihsan), and al-Bayhaqi 1:313, all through al-Layth ibn Sa'd, with this isnad. Likewise al-Nasa'i narrated it, 1:54-55, 67, through Yunus and al-Layth, both from Ibn Shihab, with this isnad, abridged.
From all these narrations I am certain that Ibn Ishaq's narration here and in Ahmad's, "from al-Zuhri, from Urwah," is an error.]

4241 - Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, from Ayyub and Ibn Awn, from Muhammad, who said: I said to Ubaydah: What is permitted for a man from his wife when she is menstruating? He said: The bed is one, and the covering is different. If he finds nothing except that he draw some of his garment over her, he draws some of it over her.

* *

Those who held this view argued: Allah, Exalted is He, commanded keeping away from women during their menstruation, and did not single out any part of them over another; this is general over all their bodies, and it is obligatory to keep away from every part of their bodies during their menstruation.

* *

Others said: Rather, what Allah, Exalted is He, commanded keeping away from in them is the place of harm, and that is the place from which the blood comes out.

Mention of those who said this:

4242 - Hamid ibn Mas'adah narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Zari' narrated to us, saying: Uyaynah ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Jawshan narrated to me, saying: Marwan al-Asfar narrated to us, from Masruq ibn al-Ajda', who said: I said to Aisha: What is permitted for a man from his wife when she is menstruating? She said: Everything except intercourse. [Hadith 4242: Marwan al-Asfar, Abu Khalaf: a reliable Successor. "Al-Asfar" is with a fa', and in the printed edition it appears with a ghayn, which is a distortion.
Masruq ibn al-Ajda' al-Hamdani: a great and reliable Successor, among the leaders and jurists of the Successors.
This hadith was quoted by Ibn Kathir 1:510 from this place. Likewise al-Suyuti quoted it, 1:260, and neither of them attributed it to anyone other than al-Tabari.
It is, to us, a hadith raised in meaning (marfu' bil-ma'na), even though its wording stops at Aisha. Because when a Companion relates what is lawful and unlawful, the trust is that he does not relate that except from one from whom the lawful and unlawful are taken, and he is the teacher of good, (ﷺ). This applies when it is unqualified, unless indications show that he says this by ijtihad (independent reasoning) and deduction from the evidences of the Qur'an and the Sunnah. See the hadiths following this one.]

4243 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Sa'id ibn Zari' narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us. = And Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us; both from Qatadah, who said: It was mentioned to us from Aisha that she said: Where were the one with two lower garments and the one with two coverings?! [In the manuscript: "wa ayyuna kana..."]

4244 - Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd, from Masruq, who said: I said to Aisha: What is forbidden for a man from his wife when she is menstruating? She said: Her private part. [Hadith 4244: Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd: a well-known reliable Successor, from whom the six major compilers narrated. This hadith is similar in meaning to the previous hadith, 4242, from another route and with different wording. Its isnad is sound.]

4245 - Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us, saying: Ayyub narrated to us, from a document of Abu Qilabah: that Masruq rode to Aisha and said: Peace be upon the Prophet and upon his household. Aisha said: Abu Aisha! Welcome! They gave him permission, and he entered, and said: I want to ask you about something, and I am shy! She said: I am only your mother, and you are my son! He said: What is permitted for a man from his wife when she is menstruating? She said to him: Everything except her private part. [Hadith 4245: This is similar in meaning to the two previous hadiths, with detail in the story of the question and answer. Its isnad is also sound.]

4246 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Za'idah narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, from Maymun ibn Mihran, from Aisha, who said: For him is what is above the wrapper. [Hadith 4246: Ibn Abi Za'idah is Yahya ibn Zakariyya ibn Abi Za'idah, who passed earlier at 2338. Hajjaj is Ibn Artah. This is similar in meaning to what preceded.]

4247 - Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, saying: Ayyub informed us, from Nafi': that Aisha said concerning lying down with a menstruating woman: There is no harm in that, if she has a wrapper on.

4248 - Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, from Ayyub, from Abu Ma'shar, who said: I asked Aisha: What is permitted for a man from his wife when she is menstruating? She said: Everything except the private part. [Hadith 4248: This isnad, as it stands here, is certainly incomplete. "Abu Ma'shar" is Ziyad ibn Kulayb al-Tamimi al-Hanzali, who narrates from Successors. He is reliable, but he did not meet Aisha, so he cannot say: "I asked Aisha."
The correct isnad, as in al-Muhalla of Ibn Hazm 2:183, is: "We have related from Ayyub al-Sakhtiyani, from Abu Ma'shar, from Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, from Masruq, who said: I asked Aisha: What is lawful for me from my wife when she is menstruating? She said: Everything except the private part." Two men dropped from the isnad: Ibrahim al-Nakha'i and Masruq, who is the one who asked Aisha. Ibn Hazm mentioned it in this way, without mentioning its isnad to Ayyub.
Al-Tahawi narrated it in Ma'ani al-Athar 2:22, with its isnad, through Amr ibn Khalid, from Ubaydullah, who is Ibn Amr al-Raqqi al-Jazari, "from Ayyub, from Abu Ma'shar, from Ibrahim, from Masruq, from Aisha." He did not mention its wording, referring to an earlier narration with the same meaning.]

4249 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Za'idah narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Amr, from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn al-Harith, who said: Ibn Abbas said: If a menstruating woman places a cloth over her private part, or something that holds back the harm, then there is no harm in her skin touching her husband. [Report 4249: This is a broken isnad (munqati'). Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn al-Harith al-Taymi: a well-known reliable Successor. But his narration from Ibn Abbas is mursal (a report in which a Successor omits the Companion), as Ibn Abi Hatim declared in al-Jarh wa al-Ta'dil 18/184.]

4250 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Idris narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas: that he was asked: What is permitted for a man from his wife when she is menstruating? He said: What is above the wrapper.

4251 - Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, saying: Hashim ibn al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Hakam ibn Fudayl narrated to us, from Khalid al-Hadhdha', from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Guard against the blood the size of the place of a sandal. [Report 4251: al-Hakam ibn Fudayl, Abu Muhammad al-Wasiti: reliable; Ibn Ma'in and others declared him reliable. He is biographed in al-Kabir 1/2/337, Ibn Abi Hatim 1/2/126-127, al-Ta'jil, al-Mizan, and Lisan al-Mizan. He has a full biography in Tarikh Baghdad 8:221-223. al-Bukhari did not find any fault in him.
This report was narrated by al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan al-Kubra 1:314, through al-Hasan ibn Makram, from Abu al-Nadr Hashim ibn al-Qasim, by this isnad.]

4252 - Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, saying: Ayyub informed us, from Ikrimah, from Umm Salamah, who said concerning lying down with a menstruating woman: There is no harm in it, if there is a rag over her private part. [Hadith 4252: This is a sound isnad. Although it stops at Umm Salamah, its meaning is also established from her as raised (marfu'):
Al-Bayhaqi narrated, 1:311, through Yazid ibn Zari', "Khalid narrated to us, from Ikrimah, from Umm Salamah: that she was with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) under a blanket, and she got her menses, so he said to her: Get up, wrap yourself, then come back."
Something similar to its meaning is also established from Umm Salamah, in a longer form than this, through the narration of Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Zaynab bint Abi Salamah, from Umm Salamah, raised (marfu'). Muslim narrated it, 1:95, and al-Bayhaqi 1:311, and mentioned that al-Bukhari and Muslim both narrated it.]

4253 - Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-A'la narrated to us, from Sa'id, from Qatadah, from al-Hasan, who said: For a man from his wife is everything except the private part, meaning while she is menstruating.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 222 (part 2 of 3):

4254 - Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Ibn Abi 'Adi related to us, from 'Awf, from al-Hasan, who said: "They may sleep under one covering, meaning the menstruating woman, provided there is a garment over her private part."

4255 - Tamim related to us, saying: Ishaq informed us, from Shurayk, from Layth, who said: "We discussed in the presence of Mujahid a man who plays with his wife while she is menstruating." He said: "Insert your penis wherever you wish between the thighs, the buttocks and the navel, so long as it is not in the anus or the menstrual area." [[In the printed edition: "حيثما شئت" ("wherever you wish"); I have adopted what is in the manuscript.]]

4256 - Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Ibn Abi Za'ida related to us, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from 'Amir, who said: "Should a man have physical contact with his wife while she is menstruating?" He said: "If she holds back the harm."

4257 - Hamid ibn Mas'ada related to us, saying: Yazid ibn Zuray' related to us, saying: Imran ibn Hudayr told me, saying: I heard 'Ikrima say: "Everything from a menstruating woman is lawful to you except the place of the blood flow."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The basis of the view of the one who holds this position is the establishment of the proof through the widely transmitted (mutawatir) reports from the Messenger of God (ﷺ) that he would have physical contact with his wives while they were menstruating. Had the obligation been to withdraw from all of them, the Messenger of God (ﷺ) would not have done that. When this was confirmed from the Messenger of God (ﷺ), it was known that the intent of God's words, mentioned, "So keep away from women during menstruation," is withdrawal from some of her body and not from other parts. If that is so, then it must be the intercourse on which there is consensus regarding its prohibition for the husband, namely in her front passage, rather than what has been disputed concerning intercourse with the rest of her body.

* *

Others said: Rather, what God, mentioned, commanded withdrawal from them during their menstruation is what lies between the navel and the knee, and what is above and below that.

Mention of those who said that:

4258 - Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Ibn Abi Za'ida related to us, from Ibn 'Awn, from Ibn Sirin, from Shurayh, who said: "He may have what is above the navel," and he mentioned the menstruating woman.

4259 - Abu Kurayb and Abu al-Sa'ib related to us, both saying: Ibn Idris related to us, saying: Yazid informed us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: "Ibn 'Abbas was asked about the menstruating woman: What is lawful for her husband from her?" He said: "What is above the waist-wrapper."

4260 - Ya'qub told me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayya related to us, from Ayyub and Ibn 'Awn, from Muhammad, who said: Shurayh said: "He may have what is above her navel."

4261 - Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Ibn Abi 'Adi related to us, from Shu'ba, from Waqid ibn Muhammad ibn Zayd ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar, who said: "Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib was asked: What is lawful for a man from a menstruating woman?" He said: "What is above the waist-wrapper."

* *

The basis of the one who holds this position is the soundness of the report from the Messenger of God (ﷺ), which is:

4262 - Ibn Abi al-Shawarib told me this, saying: 'Abd al-Wahid ibn Ziyad related to us, saying: Sulayman al-Shaybani related to us. And Abu al-Sa'ib told me, saying: Hafs related to us, saying: al-Shaybani related to us, who said: 'Abd Allah ibn Shaddad ibn al-Had related to us, saying: I heard Maymuna say: "Whenever the Messenger of God (ﷺ) wished to have physical contact with one of his wives while she was menstruating, he would order her to wrap a garment."

4263 - al-Muthanna related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from al-Shaybani, from 'Abd Allah ibn Shaddad, from Maymuna: that the Prophet (ﷺ) would have physical contact with her while she was menstruating, above the waist-wrapper. [[The two reports, 4262 and 4263: Hafs is Ibn Ghiyath; al-Shaybani Sulayman is Abu Ishaq al-Shaybani Sulayman ibn Abi Sulayman. Sufyan in the second report is al-Thawri. The two reports have the same meaning. Ibn Kathir mentioned it at 1:511 with the wording of the first, from the two Sahihs; likewise al-Suyuti at 1:259, and he added its attribution to Ibn Abi Shayba, Abu Dawud and al-Bayhaqi. See al-Bukhari 1:64, Muslim 1:95, and al-Sunan al-Kubra 1:311.]]

4264 - Sufyan ibn Wakf related to me, saying: Jarir related to us, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, from al-Aswad, from 'A'isha, who said: "When one of us was menstruating, he would order her to wrap herself with a waist-wrapper, and then he would have physical contact with her."

4265 - Sufyan ibn Wakf related to us, saying: al-Muharibi related to us, from al-Shaybani, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Aswad, from his father, from 'A'isha, who said: "When one of us was menstruating, the Prophet (ﷺ) would order her to wrap herself, and then he would have physical contact with her." [[The two reports, 4264 and 4265, are one report with two chains. Al-Suyuti mentioned it at 1:259, from Ibn Abi Shayba, the two Sahihs, Abu Dawud and Ibn Majah, with an addition at its end. See al-Bukhari 1:63, Muslim 1:95, Abu Dawud 112-113, al-Nasa'i 1:54, 67, and al-Bayhaqi 1:310-311.]]

And similar reports, the full mention of which would make the book too long.

They said: What the Prophet (ﷺ) did in this regard is permissible, namely physical contact with a menstruating woman below the waist-wrapper and above it, that being below the knee and above the navel. Whatever is other than that from the body of the menstruating woman must be avoided, because of the generality of the verse.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of the opinions on this matter is the view of the one who said: For a man, from his menstruating wife, is what is above the waist-wrapper and below it, for the reason we mentioned for them. [[In the manuscript, the words "lahum" ("for them") are omitted.]]

* *

On the interpretation (ta'wil) of God's words, the Exalted: ﴿And do not approach them until they have become pure﴾

Abu Ja'far said: The reciters (qira'at, variant readings) differed in reciting this. [[In the printed edition: "اختلف القراء", but this has occurred many times before; in some places we left it as it is in the printed edition. From this point to the end of the book, God willing, we will follow the manuscript without further reference to this.]] Some of them recited: "hatta yathurna" with a ḍamma on the "hā'" and light emphasis. Others recited it with a shadda on the "hā'" and a fatḥa.

As for those who recited it with light emphasis and a ḍamma, they directed its meaning to: Do not approach women during their menstruation until the flow of menstrual blood stops from them and they become pure. This interpretation was held by a group of the people of interpretation.

Mention of those who said that:

4266 - Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Ibn Mahdi and Mu'ammal related to us, both saying: Sufyan related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words: "And do not approach them until they become pure," he said: "The cessation of the blood."

4267 - Muhammad ibn 'Amr told me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, from Sufyan - or 'Uthman ibn al-Aswad -: "And do not approach them until they become pure," until the blood stops from them.

4268 - Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih related to us, saying: 'Ubayd Allah al-'Atki related to us, from 'Ikrima, regarding His words: "And do not approach them until they become pure," he said: "Until the blood stops." [[The report 4268: "'Ubayd Allah al-'Atki" is 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Abd Allah Abu al-Munib al-'Atki. He saw Anas and narrated from 'Ikrima, Sa'id ibn Jubayr and others among the Successors (tabi'un).]]

* *

As for those who recited it with a shadda on the "hā'" and a fatḥa, they meant by it: until they wash themselves with water. They doubled the "ṭā'" because they said: the meaning of the word is "hatta yatatahharna," and the "tā'" was assimilated into the "ṭā'" because their points of articulation are close.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The more correct of the two recitations is the recitation of the one who recited: ﴿hatta yaṭṭahharna﴾ with its shadda and fatḥa, meaning: until they wash themselves, because of the consensus of all that it is forbidden for a man to approach his wife after the cessation of her menstrual blood until she becomes pure.

* *

What has been disputed is the "purity" (taṭahhur) that God, mentioned, intended, which makes intercourse with her lawful for him.

Some of them said: It is the washing with water. It is not lawful for her husband to approach her until she has washed her entire body. [[In the printed edition: "ولا يحل..." with an added waw; the manuscript has no waw.]]

Others said: It is the ablution (wudu') for prayer.

And others said: Rather, it is washing the private part. When she has washed her private part, that is her purity by which it becomes lawful for her husband to have intercourse with her.

* *

When there is consensus from all of them that she is not lawful to her husband merely by the cessation of blood until she becomes pure, it becomes clear that the more correct of the two recitations is the one that is more free from confusion for the listener's understanding. That is what we have chosen, since in the recitation of one who reads it with light emphasis and a ḍamma there is something that does not secure against the listener's error in its interpretation, so that he thinks that it is lawful for the husband of a menstruating woman to have intercourse with her after the cessation of her menstrual blood, and before her washing and purifying herself. [[In the printed edition: "أن للزوج غشيانها"; I have adopted what is in the manuscript.]]

* *

The interpretation of the verse, therefore, is: "They ask you about menstruation. Say: It is harm. So keep away from intercourse with your wives during the time of their menstruation, and do not approach them until they wash themselves and become purified from their menstruation after it has ceased."

* *

On the interpretation of God's words, the Exalted: ﴿So when they have purified themselves, then come to them from where God has commanded you﴾

Abu Ja'far said: God, mentioned, means by His words: "So when they have purified themselves, then come to them," that when they have washed themselves and become clean with water, then have intercourse with them.

* *

If someone says: Is intercourse with them then obligatory?

It is said: No.

If he says: Then what is the meaning of His words: "then come to them"?

It is said: That is permission for what had been prohibited before that, and the release of what had been forbidden during menstruation. It is like His words: ﴿And when you are released (from ihram), then hunt﴾ [Surah al-Ma'ida: 2], and His words: ﴿And when the prayer has been concluded, disperse in the land﴾ [Surah al-Jumu'a: 10], and what is similar to that.

* *

The people of interpretation differed on the interpretation of His words: "So when they have purified themselves."

Some of them said: The meaning of that is: when they have washed themselves.

Mention of those who said that:

4269 - al-Muthanna told me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiya ibn Salih told me, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talha, from Ibn 'Abbas: "So when they have purified themselves," he says: when she has become clean from the blood and has purified herself with water.
