4270 - Muhammad ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Ibn Mahdi and Mu'ammal told me, both saying: Sufyan related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "So when they have purified themselves," when they have washed themselves. [[Report 4270: in the printed edition it was "Muhammad ibn Mahdi," which is an error and an incorrect addition; the correct form is from the manuscript. "Ibn Mahdi" is 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi, the eminent scholar. Al-Shafi'i said: "I do not know his equal in this world." He died in 198 AH. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib and elsewhere.]]

4271 - Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih related to us, saying: 'Ubayd Allah al-'Atki related to us, from 'Ikrima, regarding His words: "So when they have purified themselves," he says: they have washed themselves.

4272 - Muhammad ibn 'Amr told me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, from Sufyan - or 'Uthman ibn al-Aswad: "So when they have purified themselves," when they have washed themselves.

4273 - Imran ibn Musa related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Warith related to us, saying: 'Amir related to us, from al-Hasan, regarding a menstruating woman who sees purity: He said: "Her husband should not approach her until she has washed and the prayer has become lawful for her." [[A number is missing from the numbering: 4274.]]

4275 - Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim told me, saying: Hushaym related to us, from Mughira, from Ibrahim: that he disliked that he have intercourse with her until she washes - meaning the woman when she has become pure.

* *

Others said: The meaning of that is: "So when they have purified themselves" for the prayer.

Mention of those who said that:

4276 - Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim told me, saying: Hushaym related to us, saying: Layth informed us, from Tawus and Mujahid, that they both said: "If a woman has become pure from blood, and her husband wishes to order her to perform ablution before she washes - if desire overtakes him, let him ejaculate."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The more correct of the two interpretations of the verse is the statement of the one who said: the meaning of His words: "So when they have purified themselves" is: when they have washed themselves, because of the consensus of all that she does not become pure, with a purity by which prayer becomes lawful for her, merely by performing ablution with water. The statement cannot be free of one of two matters:

= Either its meaning is: "So when they have purified themselves from impurity, then come to them."

If that is its meaning, then it would follow that as soon as the blood stops from her, intercourse with her is permissible for her husband, provided there is no visible impurity. This holds if His words "fa-idha tathahharna" are permissibly used for purification from impurity, and I do not know it to be permissible except by forcing the sense of the speech.

= Or its meaning is: "So when they have purified themselves" for the prayer. And in the consensus of all of the proofs, that it is not lawful for her husband to approach her merely because her menstrual blood has stopped, when there is no impurity, apart from purification with water when she is able to do so, is the strongest proof that its meaning is: when they have purified themselves with the purity that suffices them for prayer.

And in the consensus of all of the community that prayer is not lawful for her except by washing, is the clearest evidence for the soundness of what we have said: that approaching her is forbidden except after washing, and that the meaning of His words "fa-idha tathahharna" is: when they have washed and have become pure with the purity that suffices them for prayer.

* *

On the interpretation of God's words, the Exalted: ﴿then come to them from where God has commanded you﴾

Abu Ja'far said: The people of interpretation differed on the interpretation of His words: "Then come to them from where God has commanded you."

Some of them said: The meaning of that is: then come to your wives when they have purified themselves, from the place which I forbade you from approaching them during their menstruation, and that is: the private part, which God commanded to abandon intercourse in during menstruation. [["Al-ityan" (coming to) is a figurative expression for the term "al-jima'" (intercourse), and its explanation will come at p. 398.]]

Mention of those who said that:

4277 - Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim told me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayya related to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, who said: Aban ibn Salih told me, from Mujahid, who said: Ibn 'Abbas said regarding His words: "Then come to them from where God has commanded you," he said: from where He commanded you to withdraw from them.

4278 - al-Muthanna told me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiya ibn Salih related to us, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talha, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words: "Then come to them from where God has commanded you," he says: in the private part, do not go beyond it to anything else. Whoever does any of that has transgressed.

4279 - Ya'qub told me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayya related to us, saying: Khalid al-Hadhdha' related to us, from 'Ikrima, regarding His words: "Then come to them from where God has commanded you," he said: from where He commanded you to withdraw.

4280 - Yunus told me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Abu Sakhr related to us, from Abu Mu'awiya al-Bajali, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, that he said: While I and Mujahid were sitting with Ibn 'Abbas, a man came and stood over his head and said: "O Abu al-'Abbas - or: O Abu al-Fadl - will you not explain to me the verse about menstruation?" He said: "Yes!" Then he recited: "They ask you about menstruation," until he reached the end of the verse. Ibn 'Abbas said: "From where the blood comes, from there you were commanded to come." [[In the printed edition: "ثم أمرت" without "min"; this is an error. The correct form is from the manuscript, and matches what will come at 4325, meaning: there. The report will come in full at 4325, and we will mention the biographies of its narrators there.]]

4281 - Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Ibn Abi Za'ida related to us, from 'Uthman, from Mujahid, who said: "The posterior of a woman is like that of a man." Then he recited: "They ask you about menstruation" until "then come to them from where God has commanded you," and said: "from where He commanded you to withdraw from them." [[Report 4281: in the printed edition: "'Amra 'an Mujahid", which is an error; the correct form is from the manuscript. "Ibn Abi Za'ida" is Yahya ibn Zakariyya ibn Abi Za'ida. "'Uthman" is 'Uthman ibn al-Aswad, client of the Banu Jumah. His narration from Mujahid has already passed, the nearest being 2782.]]

4282 - Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Mu'ammal related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words: "Then come to them from where God has commanded you," he said: They were commanded to approach them from where they were forbidden.

4283 - Ibn Abi al-Shawarib related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Wahid related to us, saying: Khusayf related to us, saying: Mujahid told me, regarding His words: "Then come to them from where God has commanded you": in the private part, and do not go beyond it.

4284 - Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to us, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words: "Then come to them from where God has commanded you," he says: when they have purified themselves, then come to them from where it was forbidden during menstruation.

4285 - Muhammad ibn 'Amr told me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, from Sufyan - or 'Uthman ibn al-Aswad -: "Then come to them from where God has commanded you," by withdrawing from it.

4286 - Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, regarding His words: "Then come to them from where God has commanded you," that is: from the place from which menstruation comes, when she is pure and not menstruating, and do not transgress that to anything else.

4287 - Muhammad ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, regarding His words: "Then come to them from where God has commanded you," he said: pure women, without intercourse and without menstruation, from the place from which menstruation comes, and not going beyond it to anything else. Sa'id said: I do not know it except from Ibn 'Abbas. [[The word "tawahir" is the plural of the woman "tahir," and it is not in the dictionaries; rather "tahirat" is found there. But it is a regular plural, like hamil and hawamil. It will come at 4295 and 4296, and its plural "tahr" will come at 4298 and 4300. In the printed edition: "ولا يتعدى إلى غيره"; the correct form, from the manuscript, is "ولا يتعدَّه إلى غيره."]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 222 (part 3 of 3):

4288 - I was told on the authority of ʿAmmar, who said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabiʿ, concerning His words: "So when they have purified themselves, then come to them as Allah has commanded you," [meaning:] from where you were forbidden during menstruation. And from his father, from Layth, from Mujahid, concerning His words: "So when they have purified themselves, then come to them as Allah has commanded you," [meaning:] from where I forbade you, and beware of the posteriors.

4289 - Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, who said: Ibn Idris narrated to us, who said: I heard my father, from Yazid ibn al-Walid, from Ibrahim, concerning His words: "Then come to them as Allah has commanded you," he said: [it means] in the vagina.

* *

Others said: its meaning is: "Then come to them from the direction in which Allah has commanded you to come to them." That direction is the state of purity, not the state of menstruation. So the meaning, according to the one who said this about the verse, is: come to them at the onset of their purity, not at the onset of their menstruation. ["Qabl" (with a short vowel on the first letter and a sukun on the second) is said in the sense of "that happened at the beginning of winter and at the beginning of summer," meaning at its start and as it approaches. In the hadith: "Divorce the women at the beginning of their waiting period" (and it is narrated as "at the beginning of their purity"), meaning at its approach and its start, when it is possible for her to enter the waiting period and begin it, so that it is counted for her. That is in the state of purity. Likewise His words here, "from the beginning of purity," mean: in the state of purity.]

Those who said this:

4290 - Muhammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, who said: my father narrated to me, who said: my paternal uncle narrated to me, who said: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas: "So come to them as Allah has commanded you," meaning that he comes to her while she is pure, not menstruating.

4291 - Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, who said: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, who said: Sufyan narrated to us, from Mansur, from Abu Razin, concerning His words: "So come to them as Allah has commanded you," he said: from the beginning of purity. [See p. 390, note 2.]

4292 - Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, who said: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated to us, who said: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Abu Razin, the like of it.

4293 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, who said: Hakkam narrated to us, from ʿAmr, from Mansur, from Abu Razin: "So come to them as Allah has commanded you," he says: come to them from the time of purity.

4294 - Muhammad ibn ʿUbayd al-Muharibi narrated to me, who said: ʿAli ibn Hashim narrated to us, from al-Zabarqan, from Abu Razin: "So come to them as Allah has commanded you," he said: from the beginning of purity, and do not come to them from the beginning of menstruation. [In the printed edition: "al-hayd" (menstruation); we have kept what is in the manuscript.]

4295 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, who said: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, who said: ʿUbayd Allah al-ʿAtaki narrated to us, from ʿIkrima, concerning his words: "So come to them as Allah has commanded you," he says: when they have bathed, come to them as Allah has commanded you. He says: pure, not menstruating. [See what preceded, no. 4287, and the commentary on it.]

4296 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, who said: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, who said: Maʿmar informed us, from Qatada concerning His words: "So come to them as Allah has commanded you," he said: he says: pure, not menstruating. [See what preceded, no. 4287, and the commentary on it.]

4297 - Musa ibn Harun narrated to me, who said: ʿAmr ibn Hammad narrated to us, who said: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi concerning His words: "as Allah has commanded you," from the state of purity.

4298 - Ibn Wakiʿ narrated to us, who said: my father narrated to us, from Salama ibn Nubayt, from al-Dahhak: "Then come to them," [meaning] pure, not menstruating. [The word "tuhr," the plural of the woman "tahir" (pure), is a regular plural not recorded in the lexicons, like the earlier "tawahir." For the adjective "fa'il," if it has a visible feminine "ta'," like "darriba," or an implied one like "ha'id," its regular plural is "fawa'il," and "fa'l" (with the first letter vowelled and its middle letter doubled and vowelled).]

4299 - I was told on the authority of al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Muʿadh say: ʿUbayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from al-Dahhak concerning His words: "So come to them as Allah has commanded you," he said: come to them pure, not menstruating.

4300 - ʿAmr ibn ʿAli narrated to us, who said: Waki' narrated to us, who said: Salama ibn Nubayt narrated to us, from al-Dahhak: "So come to them as Allah has commanded you," he said: pure, not menstruating, in the vagina. [The word "tuhr," the plural of "tahir," is a regular plural not recorded in the lexicons, like the earlier "tawahir." For the adjective "fa'il," if it has a visible feminine "ta'," like "darriba," or an implied one like "ha'id," its regular plural is "fawa'il," and "fa'l" (with the first letter vowelled and its middle letter doubled and vowelled).]

* *

Others said: indeed, the meaning of that is: "Come to women in the manner of marriage, not in the manner of immorality."

Those who said this:

4301 - ʿAmr ibn ʿAli narrated to us, who said: Waki' narrated to us, who said: Ismaʿil al-Azraq narrated to us, from Abu ʿUmar al-Asadi, from Ibn al-Hanafiyya: "So come to them as Allah has commanded you," he said: from the lawful direction, from the direction of marriage.

* *

Abu Jaʿfar said: The most correct of the sayings in the interpretation of this, in my view, is the saying of the one who said: its meaning is: "So come to them from the direction of their purity." This is because every command is a prohibition of its opposite and its contrary, and likewise the prohibition of a thing is a command to its opposite and contrary. If the meaning of His words, "So come to them as Allah has commanded you," were "come to them from the place of the blood from which I forbade you to come to them during their menstruation," then His words "and do not approach them until they are purified" would have to mean: do not approach them at the place of the blood, but anywhere else on her body. Then, during menstruation, coming to them in their posteriors would be permitted.

And there is consensus of all on the fact that Allah, exalted is His remembrance, did not permit during menstruation coming to them in their posteriors anything that He forbade in the state of purity, nor did He forbid in the state of purity anything that He permitted in the state of menstruation. This is what shows the corruption of this view.

Furthermore, if the meaning were as those who held this view interpret it, the statement would have to be: "So when they have purified themselves, then come to them as Allah has commanded you" [In the manuscript and the printed edition: "from where Allah has commanded you," which is the text of the verse, but he meant "in where," as the rest of his speech shows; so we have written it correctly, God willing.

See also what supports this in al-Farra's Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1:143.] so that the meaning of the statement would then be according to the interpretation he gave, and that would be a command to come to them in their vaginas. For the known way of speech, when that is meant, is to say: "So-and-so came to his wife from her vagina," and not "he came to her from her vagina," unless he came to her from her vagina in a place other than the vagina.

* *

If someone says to us: even if that is so, the meaning of the statement is not "come to them in their vaginas," but rather "come to them from the direction of their front parts in their vaginas," just as one says, "I came to this matter from its source."

It is said to him: if that is so, then there is no doubt that the source of a matter and its direction are other than the matter itself, and that it is its objective. If it were as you claim, then the meaning of His words "So come to them as Allah has commanded you" would have to be other than what you claim it means by your saying: come to them from the place of the blood, and from where you were commanded to keep away from them. Rather, the necessary interpretation is that it be: "So come to them from the front of their faces in their approaches," just as the saying of the speaker, "Come to the matter from its source," means only: seek it from its object, and the object of a matter is other than the matter sought.

Likewise, the source of the vagina, which Allah commanded them to approach according to their saying, must be other than the vagina. [In the manuscript: "So likewise the source of the vagina must," and in the printed edition: "So likewise it must that the source of the vagina"; what I have written is more suited to the context and to correctness.]

If that is so, and the meaning of the statement in their view is: "come to them from the front of their faces in their vaginas," then it would necessarily follow, by their view, that coming to them in their vaginas from their posteriors is forbidden. And if they said this, the one who said it would have departed from the consensus of the people of Islam and would have contradicted the explicit text of the Book of Allah, exalted is His remembrance, and the saying of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. For Allah says: ﴿Your wives are a tilth for you, so come to your tilth however you wish﴾, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ permitted coming to them in their vaginas from their posteriors.

Thus it has become clear, since the matter is as we have described, that the interpretation of the one who said: "So come to them in their vaginas where I forbade you to come to them during their menstruation" is corrupt, and that the correct saying is the one we have stated: its meaning is: "So come to them in their vaginas from the direction which Allah has permitted you to come to them, and that is the state of their purity and their purification, not the state of their menstruation."

* *

On the interpretation of His exalted words: ﴿Indeed, Allah loves those who turn often [to Him] and He loves those who purify themselves﴾ (222)

Abu Jaʿfar said: By His exalted words "Indeed, Allah loves those who turn often," He means those who turn back from disobedience to Allah and from His obedience, toward Him and toward His obedience. We have already explained the meaning of "tawba" (repentance) earlier. [See what preceded 1:547, 2:72-73, 3:81, 259-261.]

* *

There is disagreement about the meaning of His words "and He loves those who purify themselves."

Some said: they are those who purify themselves with water.

4303 - Ahmad ibn Hazim narrated to me, who said: Abu Nuʿaym narrated to us, who said: Talha narrated to us, from ʿAta', the like of it.

4304 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, who said: Waki' narrated to us, from Talha ibn ʿAmr, from ʿAta': "Indeed, Allah loves those who turn often" from sins, which they did not commit, "and He loves those who purify themselves" with water for the prayers. [In the printed edition: "lil-salat" (for the prayer); I have kept what is in the manuscript.]

Others said: the meaning of that is: "Indeed, Allah loves those who turn often" from sins, "and He loves those who purify themselves" from the posteriors of women, that they not come to them.

Those who said this:

Others said: the meaning of that is: "and He loves those who purify themselves" from sins, that they return to them after repentance from them.

Those who said this:

4306 - al-Qasim narrated to us, who said: al-Husayn narrated to us, who said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid: "He loves those who turn often," from sins, which they did not commit, "and He loves those who purify themselves," from sins, that they do not return to them.

* *

Abu Jaʿfar said: The most correct of the sayings in this matter is the saying of the one who said: "Indeed, Allah loves those who turn often from sins, and He loves those who purify themselves with water for prayer." This is because that is the most prevalent of its apparent meanings.

This is because Allah, exalted is His remembrance, mentioned the matter of menstruation, and forbade them from practices they used to do in their pre-Islamic ignorance: their avoidance of living with a menstruating woman, eating and drinking with her, and other things which He, exalted is His remembrance, disliked in His servants. When the Companions of the Messenger of Allah asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about that, [In the printed edition: "the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about that," omitting the second "Messenger of Allah"; I have kept the correct text from the manuscript.] Allah revealed to him concerning it, and he explained to them what He dislikes and what He is pleased with and loves, and informed them that He loves from among His creation whoever turns back to His pleasure and His love, repentant from what He dislikes.

Among what He explained to them in this regard, [In the manuscript and printed edition: "with that," and what I have written is the true correct reading.] was that He had forbidden them to approach their wives even if they became pure from their menstruation until they bathe. Then He said: "and do not approach them until they are purified; so when they have purified themselves, then come to them, for Allah loves those who purify themselves," meaning by that: those who purify themselves from major impurity and minor impurities for prayer, and the women who purify themselves with water from menstruation, postpartum bleeding, major impurity and minor impurities.

* *

He said "those who purify themselves" (masculine), not "those who purify themselves" (feminine), though the mention of purification before this concerned women, because by the mention of "al-mutatahhirin" (the masculine plural) it includes both men and women. Had it been mentioned as "al-mutatahharat" (feminine plural), men would have had no share in it, and it would have been for women alone. So Allah, exalted is His remembrance, by this general mention addressed all His accountable servants, since He had charged all of them with purifying themselves with water, though the causes that make purification with water obligatory on them differ in some respects and agree in others.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 223 (part 1 of 4):

The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Your women are a tilth for you﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By this, exalted is His remembrance, He means: Your women are the field of your children's sowing, so come to your field however you wish and wherever you wish.

* *

What is meant by "tilth" (ḥarth) is the sown field, and "tilth" is the crop. [[See the meaning of "tilth" in what passed earlier in this volume, 4: 239, 240. Note: the printed edition had here: "What is meant by the tilth, which is the sown crop, the ploughed field and the sown field," and this is worthless. The manuscript was garbled, so the printed edition became garbled too. It read thus: "What is meant by the crop, which is the tilth, the sown field and the sown field," with "by the crop" struck out and "by the tilth" written, and then a mīm placed above "the tilth and the sown field" on each of the two words, meaning to put one before the other; but the sentence remained corrupt in the extreme, and neither the copyist nor the printer of the edition could restore it to a correct context. I have restored it to the correct context, God willing.]] But since they are among the causes of tilling, they were called "tilth," since the meaning of the speech was understood.

Those who interpret the Qur'an said in accordance with what we have said regarding this.

* *

The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿So come to your tilth however you wish﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By this, exalted is His remembrance, He means: Have intercourse with the field of your children's sowing from whatever direction you wish of the ways of approach.

* *

"Coming" (al-ityān) in this place is a metaphor for the term for sexual intercourse. [[See what passed shortly before, p. 388, and footnote 1.]]
