? I said: No! He said: It was revealed concerning intercourse with women in their anuses.) [[Hadith 4326 (repeated). We have added this hadith from Ibn Kathir 1:516-517, where he transmits it from al-Tabari in this same wording, both isnad and matn. Its authenticity in this place is further supported by al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar, who mentions it in Fath al-Bari 8:141, citing al-Tabari, where he reports a narration from the Musnad of Ishaq ibn Rahawayh and its tafsir. He then said: "Thus Ibn Jarir reported it through Isma'il ibn Ulayyah, from Ibn 'Awn, the same." He then pointed to the following hadith, 4327, and said: "And through Isma'il ibn Ibrahim al-Karabisi, from Ibn 'Awn, similarly." Al-Hafiz also mentioned it in al-Talkhis, p. 307, saying: "Al-Tabari likewise transmitted it through Ibn Ulayyah, from Ibn 'Awn." Thus the existence of this hadith in the tafsir of al-Tabari is established, and its place here is clearly determined. And praise be to God.]]

4327: Ibrahim ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Muslim Abu Muslim told me, saying: Abu 'Umar al-Darir told us, saying: Isma'il ibn Ibrahim, companion of the karabis (cloth-sellers), told us, from Ibn 'Awn, from Nafi', who said: "I was holding the mushaf for Ibn 'Umar when he recited this verse: ﴿Your women are a tilth for you, so go to your tilth however you wish﴾, and he said: that he should come to her from her behind." [[Hadith 4327. Abu 'Umar al-Darir is Hafs ibn 'Umar al-Akbar, who passed in 3562. In the printed edition there it reads "Abu 'Amr," which is an error, as we have shown; here it is correctly given. Isma'il ibn Ibrahim, companion of the karabis: he is trustworthy (thiqah). Al-Bukhari included him in al-Kabir 1/1/342 and did not mention any criticism of him. Ibn Hibban mentioned him among the trustworthy narrators. "Companion of the karabis" means the cloth-seller; hence he is called al-Karabisi with the ya' of nisba, relating to its sale. In the printed edition the phrase appears as "companion of al-Karabisi," using the nisba form with the word "companion," which is an error.
These three hadiths are authentic and established from Ibn 'Umar. They are one hadith with three isnads. A similar meaning will also come later: 4331.
Al-Bukhari, 8:140-141, transmitted its meaning from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, through three isnads, but he referred to that act by a euphemism and did not state it explicitly. Al-Hafiz extensively pointed to many of its isnads.
Al-Suyuti mentioned it, 1:265, attributing it to those we have cited.
Al-Hafiz, in Fath al-Bari 8:141, quoted Ibn 'Abd al-Barr as saying: "The narration of Ibn 'Umar for this meaning is sound and well-known, from Nafi' transmitting from him." Al-Suyuti, 1:266, likewise quoted this from Ibn 'Abd al-Barr.]]

4328: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Hakam told me, saying: 'Abd al-Malik ibn Maslamah told us, saying: al-Darawardi told us, saying: It was said to Zayd ibn Aslam: "Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir forbids intercourse with women in their anuses." Zayd said: "I bear witness about Muhammad that he told me he does it." [[Report 4328. 'Abd al-Malik ibn Maslamah al-Misri: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Hakam narrated from him much in his book Futuh Misr. He is weak. Ibn Abi Hatim, 2/2/371, mentioned his biography, and noted that his father narrated from him, and that he said: "He is unstable in hadith, not strong," and that he narrated to him a fabricated hadith. Abu Zur'ah said: "Not strong; he is a munkar al-hadith (rejected in hadith)." He has an entry in al-Mizan and Lisan al-Mizan.]]

4329: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Hakam told me, saying: Abu Zayd 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ahmad ibn Abi al-Ghamr told us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Qasim told me, from Malik ibn Anas, that it was said to him: "O Abu 'Abd Allah, people narrate from Salim: 'The slave lied, or: the non-Arab (ilj), concerning my father!'" Malik said: "I bear witness about Yazid ibn Ruman that he told me, from Salim ibn 'Abd Allah, from Ibn 'Umar, the same as what Nafi' said." It was then said to him: "Al-Harith ibn Ya'qub narrates from Abu al-Habbab Sa'id ibn Yasar that he asked Ibn 'Umar, saying: 'O Abu 'Abd al-Rahman, we buy slave-girls and do tahmid (?) for them?' He said: 'And what is al-tahmid?' He said: 'The rear.' Ibn 'Umar said: 'Uff! Uff! Would a believer do that?' — or he said: 'a Muslim!'" Malik said: "I bear witness about Rabi'ah that he told me, from Abu al-Habbab, from Ibn 'Umar, the same as what Nafi' said. [[Report 4329. Abu Zayd 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ahmad ibn Abi al-Ghamr al-Misri al-Faqih: he is listed in al-Tahdhib, and Ibn Abi Hatim, 2/2/274-275, under the name "'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi al-Ghamr," without mentioning his father's name "Ahmad." He is one of al-Bukhari's teachers; he narrated from him outside the Sahih.
'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Qasim ibn Khalid, the Egyptian jurist, the transmitter of fiqh from Malik: trustworthy and reliable, among the most reliable companions of Malik.
This report was transmitted by Ibn Kathir, 1:521-522, from this place. However, an error occurred in the name of Ibn Abi al-Ghamr, as follows: "Abu Zayd Ahmad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ahmad ibn Abi al-Ghamr."
Al-Hafiz transmitted it in Fath al-Bari 8:142, and in al-Talkhis, p. 308, in abridged form, attributing it also to al-Nasa'i and al-Tahawi. In Fath he said: "al-Daraqutni also reported it, through 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Qasim, from Malik, and said: 'This is preserved from Malik and sound.'"
Al-Suyuti transmitted it, 1:266, in extended form, and quoted al-Daraqutni's statement.]]

4330: Muhammad ibn Ishaq told me, saying: 'Amr ibn Tariq told us, saying: Yahya ibn Ayyub told us, from Musa ibn Ayyub al-Ghafiqi, who said: "I said to Abu Majid al-Ziyadi: 'Nafi' narrates from Ibn 'Umar about the rear of a woman.' He said: 'Nafi' lied! I accompanied Ibn 'Umar, and Nafi' was a slave, and I heard him say: I have not looked at my wife's private part since such-and-such.'" [[Report 4330. 'Amr ibn Tariq: he is 'Amr ibn al-Rabi' ibn Tariq al-Hilali al-Misri, and he is trustworthy. He is here attributed to his grandfather. He is listed in al-Tahdhib and Ibn Abi Hatim, 3/1/233. Yahya ibn Ayyub: he is al-Ghafiqi al-Misri. He passed in 3877.
Musa ibn Ayyub ibn 'Amir al-Ghafiqi al-Hibari al-Misri: trustworthy; al-Layth ibn Sa'd and Ibn al-Mubarak narrated from him, and Ibn Ma'in declared him trustworthy.
Abu Majid al-Ziyadi: a Successor (tabi'i). Al-Bukhari included him in al-Kuna, no. 688, and Ibn Abi Hatim, 4/2/455, and both narrated this report, in two different wordings that differ from what is here.
Al-Bukhari said: "Abu Majid al-Ziyadi heard Ibn 'Umar, and said: 'I have not looked at a woman's private part since I became Muslim.' Yahya ibn Sulayman transmitted it, from Ibn Wahb, who heard Musa ibn Ayyub, from Abu Majid."
Ibn Abi Hatim said: "Abu Majid al-Ziyadi heard 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, and said: 'I have not looked at my private part since I became Muslim.' Musa ibn Ayyub al-Ghafiqi narrated from him. I heard my father say this."
It appears that "'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr," in Ibn Abi Hatim, is a scribal or printing distortion. But the difference in meaning remains between these two narrations, and between them and this narration of al-Tabari. I have found nothing that favors one of them over the others.]]

4331: Abu Qilabah told me, saying: 'Abd al-Samad told us, saying: My father told me, from Ayyub, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar: ﴿so go to your tilth however you wish﴾, he said: "In the rear." [[Report 4331. Abu Qilabah, the teacher of al-Tabari: he is al-Raqashi al-Darir al-Hafiz, whose name is 'Abd al-Malik ibn Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad. He is trustworthy; the imams narrated from him, including Ibn Khuzaymah, Ibn Jarir, and Abu al-'Abbas al-Asamm. Abu Dawud Sulayman ibn al-Ash'ath said: "A truthful man, trustworthy and reliable; I wrote from him in Basra." Al-Tabari said: "I have not seen anyone more retentive than him." He is listed in al-Tahdhib; Ibn Abi Hatim, 2/2/369-370; Tarikh Baghdad 10:425-427; and Tadhkirat al-Huffaz 2:143-144. 'Abd al-Samad is Ibn 'Abd al-Warith.
This report was narrated by al-Bukhari, 8:140-141, from Ishaq, who is Ibn Rahawayh, from 'Abd al-Samad. However, he omitted the place after the particle "fi" (in), so its wording is not stated. The hadith scholars mentioned in Fath that it is explicit in this narration of al-Tabari.
Ibn Kathir transmitted it, 1:517, from al-Tabari with its isnad. Al-Suyuti transmitted it, 1:265, attributing it to al-Bukhari and Ibn Jarir.]]

4332: Abu Muslim told me, saying: Abu 'Umar al-Darir told us, saying: Yazid ibn Zurai' told us, saying: Rawh ibn al-Qasim told us, from Qatadah, who said: "Abu al-Darda' was asked about intercourse with women in their anuses, and he said: 'Would anyone do that except a disbeliever!'" Rawh said: "I witnessed Ibn Abi Mulaykah being asked about that, and he said: 'I desired a slave-girl of mine last night, and it resisted me, so I sought help with some oil or fat.' I said to him: 'Subhan Allah!! Qatadah told us that Abu al-Darda' said: Would anyone do that except a disbeliever!' He said: 'May God curse you and curse Qatadah!' I said: 'I will never narrate anything from you again!' Then I regretted that afterward." [[Report 4332. This is in reality two reports: the first from Abu al-Darda', and the second an athar from Ibn Abi Mulaykah, which is not suitable as evidence. Our discussion concerns the report from Abu al-Darda'.
Al-Tabari transmitted it here with its isnad to Qatadah, "He said: Abu al-Darda' was asked...", and this is mursal (broken in its chain). Ahmad in al-Musnad (no. 6968 m) transmitted it with its isnad to Qatadah, who said: "'Uqbah ibn Wassaj narrated to me, from Abu al-Darda', who said: 'Would anyone do that except a disbeliever?!'" Likewise al-Bayhaqi transmitted it in al-Sunan al-Kubra 7:199. We have taken it out in our explanation of the Musnad.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said [[From here begins a section of the old division of the tafsir, as it appears; it was written after what preceded. The following text, as it appears: "Followed by: those who argued for this view stumbled," "And may God bless Muhammad the Prophet, his family, and companions abundantly," then a new page began with: "In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Compassionate," "Lord, help, O Generous."]] Those who held this view argued for their saying with what follows:

4333: Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Hakam told me with it, saying: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Uways al-A'sha told us, from Sulayman ibn Bilal, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from Ibn 'Umar: that a man came to his wife from behind, and he felt guilt about that, so God revealed: ﴿Your women are a tilth for you, so go to your tilth however you wish﴾. [[Hadith 4333. Abu Bakr ibn Abi Uways: he is 'Abd al-Hamid ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Uways al-Madani al-A'sha, and he is trustworthy.
Sulayman ibn Bilal Abu Ayyub al-Madani: a well-known trustworthy narrator; the six major imams narrated from him.
Ibn Kathir transmitted this hadith, 1:517, from the narration of al-Nasa'i, from Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Hakam, identical to al-Tabari's narration and its isnad. Al-Hafiz mentioned it in al-Talkhis, pp. 307-308, and al-Suyuti, 1:265-266, and they attributed it only to al-Nasa'i and al-Tabari.]]

4334: Yunus told me, saying: Ibn Nafi' informed me, from Hisham ibn Sa'd, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from 'Ata' ibn Yasar: that a man had intercourse with his wife in her anus during the time of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and people denounced that and said: "He has made her ithfar!" So God, may His remembrance be exalted, revealed: ﴿Your women are a tilth for you, so go to your tilth however you wish﴾, etc. [[Report 4334. This is a mursal hadith, because 'Ata' ibn Yasar is a Successor (tabi'i). The word "ithfar": from "al-thafr," with the thа (th) and fa' vowelled, and it is what is placed for the beast under its tail, to which the saddle is tied. That act was likened to placing the thafr on the rear of the animal.]]

* *

Others said: the meaning of that is: "Come to your tilth however you wish, whether you withdraw (coitus interruptus) or do not withdraw."

Mention of those who said that:

4335: Ahmad ibn Ishaq told us, saying: Abu Ahmad told us, saying: al-Hasan ibn Salih told us, from Layth, from 'Isa ibn Sinan, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab: ﴿so go to your tilth however you wish﴾: if you wish, withdraw, and if you wish, do not withdraw.

4336: Abu Kurayb told us, saying: Waki' told us, from Yunus, from Abu Ishaq, from Za'idah ibn 'Umayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "If you wish, withdraw, and if you wish, do not withdraw." [[Report 4336. Abu Ishaq: he is al-Sabi'i. Za'idah ibn 'Umayr al-Ta'i al-Kufi: a trustworthy Successor, declared trustworthy by Ibn Ma'in and others. Al-Bukhari said in al-Kabir 2/1/394: "He heard Ibn 'Abbas." He is listed by Ibn Abi Hatim, 1/2/612, and Ibn Sa'd mentioned him in al-Tabaqat 6:218.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: As for those who said: the meaning of His saying: "however you wish," is: facing forward or backward, in the vagina and not the anus, they said: the verse was revealed concerning the denunciation of a group of Jews, who denounced intercourse with women from the rear in their fronts. They said: in that is evidence for the soundness of what we have said, that the meaning of that is what we have said. They argued for their saying with what follows:

4337: Abu Kurayb told me with it, saying: al-Muharibi told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq told us, from Aban ibn Salih, from Mujahid, who said: "I presented the mushaf to Ibn 'Abbas three times, from its opening to its end, stopping at each verse and asking him about it, until I reached this verse: ﴿Your women are a tilth for you, so go to your tilth however you wish﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: 'This tribe of Quraysh used to lie with women in Mecca (sharaha, meaning to throw a woman down and have intercourse with her while she lies on her back), and they would enjoy them facing forward and from behind. When they came to Medina and married among the Ansar, they went to do with them as they used to do with women in Mecca, and the women denounced that and said: "This is something we were never approached in!" The matter spread until it reached the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and God, may His remembrance be exalted, revealed concerning that: ﴿Your women are a tilth for you, so go to your tilth however you wish﴾: if you wish facing forward, and if you wish from behind, and if you wish crouching. What is meant by that is the place of the child, as tilth. He says: come to the tilth from wherever you wish.'" [[Shara'a al-rajul imra'atahu sharhan: when he threw her down and had intercourse with her while she lay on her back.]]

4338: Abu Kurayb told us, saying: Yunus ibn Bukayr told us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq with its isnad, similarly. [[Reports 4337-4338. They are one hadith with two isnads. Aban ibn Salih ibn 'Umayr ibn 'Ubayd: trustworthy; Ibn Ma'in, Abu Zur'ah, Abu Hatim, and others declared him trustworthy.
This hadith was transmitted by Abu Dawud, 2164, al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak 2:195, 279, and al-Bayhaqi 7:195-196, in extended and abridged forms, through Muhammad ibn Ishaq. Al-Hakim said at the first place: "This hadith is sound in isnad according to the condition of Muslim, but they did not transmit it in this full form." Al-Dhahabi concurred.
Ibn Kathir transmitted it, 1:516, from Abu Dawud's narration. Likewise al-Hafiz in al-Talkhis, p. 308.
Al-Suyuti transmitted it, 1:263, and added its attribution to Ibn Rahawayh, al-Darimi, Ibn al-Mundhir, and al-Tabarani.]]

4339: Muhammad ibn Bashshar told us, saying: Ibn Mahdi told us, saying: Sufyan told us, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, who said: "I heard Jabir say: The Jews used to say: 'If a man has intercourse with his wife in her vagina from behind, their child will be squint-eyed (ahwal).' So God, may His remembrance be exalted, revealed: ﴿Your women are a tilth for you, so go to your tilth however you wish﴾."

4340: Mujahid ibn Musa told us, saying: Yazid ibn Harun told us, saying: al-Thawri informed us, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, who said: "The Jews said: 'If a man comes to his wife in her front from her rear, and there is a child between them, it will be squint-eyed.' So God, may His remembrance be exalted, revealed: ﴿Your women are a tilth for you, so go to your tilth however you wish﴾." [[Reports 4339-4340. They are one hadith with two isnads and closely similar wordings. It is a sound, well-known hadith. Al-Bukhari, 8:141-143, transmitted it through Sufyan, who is al-Thawri, from Ibn al-Munkadir, from Jabir.
Ibn Kathir transmitted it, 1:514, from al-Bukhari's narration, then from Ibn Abi Hatim's narration. Al-Suyuti mentioned it, 1:261, and added its attribution to the authors of the four Sunan, al-Bayhaqi, and others.
It is in al-Sunan al-Kubra of al-Bayhaqi 7:195-196, through three routes, from Ibn al-Munkadir, from Jabir. He mentions that Muslim transmitted it in his Sahih through those three routes.
It will come similar to it: 4346, from the narration of Shu'bah, from Ibn al-Munkadir, from Jabir.
See al-Muntaqa: 3652, 3653.]]

4341: Abu Kurayb told us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahim ibn Sulayman told us, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Uthman ibn Khutaym, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Sabit, from Hafsah bint 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr, from Umm Salamah, wife of the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "A man married a woman and wanted to make her lie prostrate (jabbiyaha), but she refused him, [[Jabba al-rajul aw al-mar'ah yajbi tajbiyatan: to bow down on his face, kneeling, which is prostration. It was likened to the posture of prostration.]] and said: 'Until I ask the Messenger of God (ﷺ)!' Umm Salamah said: 'She mentioned that to me, and Umm Salamah mentioned that to the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and he said: "Send for her." When she came, the Messenger of God (ﷺ) recited to her: ﴿Your women are a tilth for you, so go to your tilth however you wish﴾, one passage, one passage." [[Hadith 4341. 'Abd Allah ibn 'Uthman ibn Khutaym al-Qari al-Makki: a Successor, trustworthy and reliable, as Ibn Ma'in said. "Khutaym" is with a diminutive form, with a dammah on the kha and a fathah on the thа (th). In the printed edition here, and in 4344, it reads "Jushm," which is a misreading. 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Sabit: a known Successor; his biography passed at 599.
Hafsah bint 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr al-Siddiq: a trustworthy Successor woman.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 223 (part 3 of 4):

The hadith was related by Ahmad in al-Musnad 6: 305 (Halabi), from ʿAffan, from Wuhayb, from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUthman ibn Khuthaym, with this chain, similar to it, in extended form. Ibn Kathir transmitted it in 1: 515 from the narration of the Musnad. There are distortions and misreadings in his printed edition.

Al-Bayhaqi related it in 7: 195, in a shorter form similar to it, by way of Sufyan and by way of Rawh ibn al-Qasim, both from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUthman ibn Khuthaym.

Al-Suyuti mentioned it in 1: 262, in extended form, and he added its attribution to Ibn Abi Shaybah, al-Darimi, ʿAbd ibn Humayd and Ibn Abi Hatim.

It will come after this, in extended and abridged forms: 4342–4345.

Al-Sammam is what is inserted into the mouth of a bottle to seal it. So the vagina was named by it, because it is a place of sealing (sammam), by way of metaphor and with an elided genitive. Its meaning: in one single passage.

4342 – Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Muʿawiyah ibn Hisham narrated to us, from Sufyan, from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUthman, from Ibn Sabit, from Hafsah daughter of ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr, from Umm Salamah, who said: The emigrants arrived and married among the Ansar, and they used to practise jabb, whereas the Ansar did not do that. A woman said to her husband: "Until I go to the Prophet ﷺ and ask him about that!" She went to the Prophet ﷺ but was too shy to ask him, so I asked, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ summoned her and recited to her: "Your women are a tilth for you, so come to your tilth however you wish" [2:223], and "one single passage, one single passage." [[The hadith: 4342 – Sufyan is al-Thawri, who narrated the hadith from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUthman. But in the printed edition it reads "Sufyan ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUthman", which is a ridiculous error. In the manuscript it reads "ʿan Ibn Sulayt" instead of "Ibn Sabit", which is an error. The hadith repeats the previous one in similar form.]]

4343 – Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to me, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUthman, from ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Sabit, from Hafsah daughter of ʿAbd al-Rahman, from Umm Salamah, from the Prophet ﷺ, similar to it. [[The hadith: 4343 – Abu Ahmad is al-Zubayri, Muhammad ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Zubayr al-Asadi. The hadith repeats the previous one.]]

4344 – Ibn Bashshar and Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, both saying: Ibn Mahdi narrated to us, saying: Sufyan al-Thawri narrated to us, from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUthman ibn Khuthaym, from ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Sabit, from Hafsah daughter of ʿAbd al-Rahman, from Umm Salamah, from the Prophet ﷺ, his saying: "Your women are a tilth for you, so come to your tilth however you wish," and he said: "one single passage, one single passage." [[The hadith: 4344 – It repeats the previous one in abridged form. Al-Tirmidhi also related it in 4: 75, in abridged form, from Ibn Abi ʿUmar, from Sufyan, who is al-Thawri, with it.]]

4345 – Muhammad ibn Maʿmar al-Bahrani narrated to me, saying: Yaʿqub ibn Ishaq al-Hadrami narrated to us, saying: Wuhayb narrated to me, saying: ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUthman narrated to me, from ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Sabit, who said: I said to Hafsah, "I want to ask you about something, but I am shy to ask you?" She said: "Ask, my son, whatever occurs to you!" I said: "I ask you about having intercourse with women in their posteriors?" She said: Umm Salamah related to me, saying: The Ansar did not practise jabb, whereas the emigrants did practise jabb, so a man from the emigrants married a woman from the Ansar = then he mentioned something similar to the hadith of Abu Kurayb, from Muʿawiyah ibn Hisham. [[The hadith: 4345 – Yaʿqub ibn Ishaq ibn Zayd al-Hadrami, the reciter and grammarian, is trustworthy; Muslim included him in his Sahih.
Wuhayb (diminutive): is Ibn Khalid ibn ʿAjlan, a trustworthy, firm and authoritative narrator.
The hadith repeats 4342, similar to it, where al-Tabari referred the wording of this one to the wording of that one.]]

4346 – Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Wahb ibn Jarir narrated to me, saying: Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Ibn al-Munkadir, who said: I heard Jabir ibn ʿAbd Allah say: "The Jews used to say: when a man comes to his wife in a reclining position, the child comes out squint-eyed." So the verse was revealed: "Your women are a tilth for you, so come to your tilth however you wish." [[The hadith: 4346 – It repeats 4339 and 4340. The manuscript reads "bakiran" instead of "bakirah", which is an error.]]

4347 – Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Tusi narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan ibn Musa narrated to us, saying: Yaʿqub al-Qummi narrated to us, from Jaʿfar, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: ʿUmar came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I am ruined!" He said: "What has ruined you?" He said: "I turned my mount tonight!" He said: So he did not answer him with anything. He said: Then Allah revealed to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ this verse: "Your women are a tilth for you, so come to your tilth however you wish," [meaning] come forward and back, and beware of the posterior and menstruation. [[The hadith: 4347 – Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Tusi: I do not know him and found no biography of him. al-Hasan ibn Musa al-Ashyab: a trustworthy, meticulous, firm narrator, one of Ahmad's teachers, from whom he narrates frequently in the Musnad. Yaʿqub al-Qummi: his biography has passed at 617. Jaʿfar: is Ibn Abi al-Mughirah, also passed at 617. The hadith was related by Ahmad in al-Musnad: 2703 from his teacher al-Hasan ibn Musa al-Ashyab with this chain, and we have takhrij'd it there. We add that Ibn Hibban also related it in his Sahih 6: 364–365 (Ihsan manuscript) and al-Bayhaqi 7: 198.]]

4348 – Zakariyya ibn Yahya al-Misri narrated to us, saying: Abu Salih al-Harrani narrated to us, saying: Ibn Lahiʿah narrated to us, from Yazid ibn Abi Habib, that ʿAmir ibn Yahya informed him, from Hanash al-San'ani, from Ibn ʿAbbas: that some people from Himyar came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ asking him about things, and a man among them said: "O Messenger of Allah, I am a man who loves women, so what do you think about that?" So Allah, may He be exalted, revealed in "Surat al-Baqarah" the explanation of what they asked about, and revealed concerning what the man asked: "Your women are a tilth for you, so come to your tilth however you wish." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Go to her facing and from behind, when it is in the vagina." [[The hadith: 4348 – Zakariyya ibn Yahya ibn Salih al-Qudaʿi al-Misri: a trustworthy narrator, one of Muslim's teachers in his Sahih.
Abu Salih al-Harrani: is ʿAbd al-Ghaffar ibn Dawud ibn Mihran, a trustworthy narrator, one of al-Bukhari's teachers in his Sahih.
Yazid ibn Abi Habib al-Misri: trustworthy, the whole group narrated from him. al-Layth ibn Saʿd said: "Yazid ibn Abi Habib is our leader and our scholar." Ibn Saʿd said: "He was the mufti of the people of Egypt in his time, and he was forbearing and intelligent." Hanash al-San'ani: passed at 1914.
The hadith was mentioned by Ibn Kathir in 1: 514–515 from the narration of Ibn Abi Hatim in his Tafsir, from Yunus, from Ibn Wahb, from Ibn Lahiʿah, with this chain. Al-Suyuti mentioned it in 1: 262–263 and added its attribution to al-Tabarani and al-Kharaʾiti. Ahmad related in the Musnad: 2414 something similar, but in it the questioners were from the Ansar. Its chain is weak, because of Rushdin ibn Saʿd in its chain.]]

* *

Abu Jaʿfar said: The correct view on this matter, in our opinion, is the view of those who said: the meaning of His saying "anna shi'tum" is: from whatever direction you wish. This is because "anna" in the speech of the Arabs is a word which, when a statement begins with it, indicates asking about the ways and directions. So it is as if the speaker, when he says to a man: "Anna laka hadha al-mal?" (From where did you get this wealth?), means: from which directions is it yours? For this reason the one answering replies with: "From such and such," as the Exalted said, reporting about Zakariyya in his question to Maryam: ﴿Anna laki hadha? Qalat huwa min ʿinda Allah﴾ [Surat Al ʿImran: 37]. Its meaning is close to "ayna" (where) and "kayfa" (how), and for this reason their meanings overlapped, so "anna" became unclear to its hearers and interpreters, until some of them interpreted it as meaning "ayna", and some as meaning "kayfa", and others as meaning "matā" (when). But it differs from all of these in meaning, and they differ from it.

This is because "ayna" is only an interrogative particle about places and locations. The difference in meaning of these particles is shown by the difference in their answers. Do you not see that if one person asked another, "Ayna maluk?" (Where is your property?), he would say, "In such and such a place," and if he said to him, "Ayna akhuk?" (Where is your brother?), the answer would be, "In such and such a town or such and such a place," informing him about the location of what he asked about. So it is known that "ayna" is a question about location.

If one speaker said to another, "Kayfa anta?" (How are you?), he would say, "Good, or well, or in health," and inform him of his state in which he is, and then it is known that "kayfa" is a question about the state of the one asked about.

If he said to him, "Anna yuhyi Allah hadha al-mayyit?" (How will God revive this dead one?), the answer would be, "In such a way and such a way," describing a statement similar to what the Exalted described for the one who said: ﴿Anna yuhyi hadhihi Allah baʿda mawtiha﴾ [Surat al-Baqarah: 259], "an act," [[The word "fi'lan" is the object of the phrase: "similar to what God described… an act." It means that God after that described "an act", and this act is His raising him after his death, which is the saying of God the Exalted after that:
﴿fa-amatahu Allah mi'ata ʿamin thumma baʿathahu﴾ ]] when He raised him after his death.

The poets have distinguished between these in their poetry. Al-Kumayt ibn Zayd said:

Remember from where and from which direction his drinking [came]; he consults his two souls, like the owner of the herd of camels.

[[Al-Lisan (abl): "amarahu yu'ammiruhu" means he consulted him. His saying "nafsayhi" made the soul two souls, because the soul commands a person to do a thing and forbids him from it; this is in every disliked or feared matter, so what it commands is called "a soul" and what it forbids is called "a soul." Al-Mumazziq al-ʿAbdi has clarified it in his saying: Is there anyone for an eye whose close one has been wounded, and whose sorrows have kept me awake after sleep? So two different souls spent the night in him, their sorrows: one soul comforts it and one soul blames it. "Al-hajmah": the large portion of camels from seventy to a hundred. It is said: "rajul abl" when he is skilled in the welfare of camels and in tending them. I did not find the poetry of al-Kumayt, but I incline to think that this verse is from verses about a wild donkey, which has taken its females (they are its mares) to drink water, so it stopped with them at the place of an old spring from which it had drunk; it is hesitant in its position, so it resembles the herdsman of many camels, when he is experienced in their pasture, so he stops with them looking where to go to the water and pasture.]]

And he also said:

Anna wa min ayna — ābak — al-tarab — min ḥaythu lā ṣabwatun wa lā rayb?

[[Al-Hashimiyyat: 31. His saying "ābak" is an interjection between two statements, as you say "wayhak" between two statements, and its context is "Anna wa min ayna al-tarab?" And "ābak" means "waylak" (woe to you), said to one whom you advise and who does not accept, then falls into what you warned him against, as if it meant: may God remove you! A curse on him. From that is the saying of a man from the Banu ʿUqayl: "Did you tell me, O heart, that you are a lover of Layla? Then taste what you used to say!" "So āḇak! Would that, while nights come with a glimpse [of ease] and days have forgetfulness of you!" However, Abu Jaʿfar interpreted "ābak" as meaning "the joy returned to you" from "awba", which is one interpretive possibility, but the better is what I explained, and the poetry after it indicates the correctness of what I went to.]]

So "anna" is used for asking about the manner, and "ayna" for asking about the place. It is as if he said: From which manner, and from which place did the joy return to you?

What shows the corruption of the view of those who interpreted the saying of God, the Exalted, "fa-'tū ḥarthakum anna shi'tum" as meaning "kayfa shi'tum" (how you wish), or interpreted it as "ḥaythu shi'tum" (where you wish), or "matā shi'tum" (when you wish), or "ayna shi'tum" (wherever you wish), is that if one speaker said to another, "Anna ta'tī ahlaka?" (How do you come to your wife?), the answer would be, "From her front, or from her back," as God the Exalted reported about Maryam when she was asked: ﴿Anna laki hadha﴾, that she said: ﴿Huwa min ʿinda Allah﴾.

Since that is the answer, it is known that the meaning of the saying of God, the Exalted, "fa-'tū ḥarthakum anna shi'tum" is only: "so come to your tilth from whatever directions of approach you wish," and that whatever else of interpretations is not an interpretation of the verse.

Since that is the correct view, it is clear that the error of the one who claimed that His saying "fa-'tū ḥarthakum anna shi'tum" is evidence for the permissibility of intercourse with women in their posteriors is manifest, because the posterior is not a tilth, [[In the printed edition: "la yukhtarathu fihi" (there is no tilling in it), and both are close, but what is in the manuscript is better.]] and He, the Exalted, only said: "a tilth for you," so come to the tilth from whatever directions you wish. And what tilling is there in the posterior, that it is said: come to it from its direction? And it is clear, by what we have shown, [[In the printed edition: "wa-tabayyana bima bayyana" and the correct reading is from the manuscript, and it is conjoined with his earlier saying: "so the error of one who claimed is clear."]] the soundness of the meaning of what was related from Jabir and Ibn ʿAbbas: that this verse was revealed concerning what the Jews used to say to the Muslims: "When a man comes to his wife from behind, in the vagina, the child comes out squint-eyed."

[[The argument of Abu Jaʿfar in this section is among the best clarifications of the meanings of the Qur'an, and of the meanings of its words and letters, and it is evidence that knowledge of Arabic, mastery of it, and deep immersion in its poetry, its eloquence and its styles, is one of the foundations, and it is not permitted for one who speaks about the Qur'an to speak about it until he has perfected it and mastered it. May God have mercy on Ibn Idris al-Shafiʿi, when he said, as related by al-Khatib al-Baghdadi from him in the book "al-Faqih wa al-Mutafaqqih":
"It is not permitted for anyone to issue a fatwa in the religion of God except a man who knows the Book of God: its abrogating and abrogated, its decisive and ambiguous, its interpretation and revelation, its Meccan and Medinan, and what is intended by it. After that he should be discerning in the hadith of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and in abrogation and abrogated, and know of the hadith as much as he knows of the Qur'an; and be discerning in the language, discerning in poetry, and in what he needs for the Sunnah and the Qur'an, and use this with fairness; and after this be aware of the disagreements of the people of the regions; and have a natural disposition. When he is like this, he may speak and issue fatwas on the lawful and unlawful; and if he is not like this, he may not issue fatwas."
Would that those among the people of our time who speak about the Qur'an and religion would be cautious out of fear of their Lord, and out of dread of His punishment on the day when people stand before the Lord of the worlds.]]

* *

The explanation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Wa qaddimu li-anfusikum﴾

Abu Jaʿfar said: The people of interpretation differed about the meaning of that:

Some of them said: the meaning of that is: "Send forward for yourselves the good."

Those who said that:

4349 – Musa narrated to me, saying: ʿAmr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: As for His saying "wa qaddimu li-anfusikum," it is "the good."

* *

Others said: rather the meaning of that is: "And send forward for yourselves the remembrance of God at intercourse and at coming to the tilth before coming to it."

Those who said that:

4350 – al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Kathir narrated to me, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Waqid, from ʿAta' — he said: I think it is from Ibn ʿAbbas: "Wa qaddimu li-anfusikum," he said: he says: "Bismillah," the saying of the name at intercourse. [[In the printed edition: "qal: al-tasmiyah ʿinda al-jimaʿ yaqulu: bismillah," in reversed order.]]

* *

Abu Jaʿfar said: The view that is closer to the interpretation of the verse is what we related from al-Suddi, namely that His saying "wa qaddimu li-anfusikum" is a command from God, the Exalted, to His servants to send forward the good and righteous deeds for the day of their return to their Lord, as provision for themselves at their meeting with Him at the station of reckoning. For He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Wa ma tuqaddimu li-anfusikum min khayrin tajidūhu ʿinda Allah﴾ [Surat al-Baqarah: 110 / Surat al-Muzzammil: 20].

We only said that this is closer to the interpretation of the verse because God, the Exalted, followed His saying "wa qaddimu li-anfusikum" with a command to fear Him in committing His disobedience. So what is more appropriate to come before the threat against disobedience — since the threat against disobedience is general — is that the command to obedience should be general. [[In the manuscript and the printed edition: "alladhi huwa awla an yakuna qabl al-tahaddud ʿamman," and in the printed edition: "al-tahdid," which is an ungrammatical sentence, so I deleted "alladhi" and added: "idh kana al-tahaddud ʿala al-maʿsiyah," so that the meaning and context of the speech are sound.]]

* *

If someone says to us: What is the connection of the command to obedience in His saying "wa qaddimu li-anfusikum" with His saying: "Your women are a tilth for you, so come to your tilth however you wish"?

It was said: this was not intended to mean what you have supposed. Rather, what is meant is: "And send forward for yourselves [good deeds]" — the good things which We have urged you to by Our saying: ﴿They ask you what they should spend. Say: Whatever wealth you spend should be for parents and relatives﴾, and what follows it of the rest of the matters they asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about, which they were answered concerning, as Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, mentioned in these verses. Then Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, said: We have made clear to you that in which is your right guidance and your being guided to what pleases your Lord with respect to you. So send forward for yourselves the good which He has commanded you, and take with Him a covenant through it, so that you may find it with Him when you meet Him in your return [to Him]. ﴿And fear Him⦆ regarding His disobedience, lest you draw near to it, and regarding His limits, lest you neglect them. And know that you are certainly going to meet Him in your return, so He will reward the good-doer among you for his goodness and the wrongdoer for his wrongdoing. [[In the printed edition: "fa-mujāzī" with a yā' at its end. The correct form is what has been established here.]]
* *
Regarding the interpretation of His saying, exalted is His remembrance: ﴿And fear Allah, and know that you will meet Him, and give good tidings to the believers﴾
Abu Ja'far said: This is a warning from Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, to His servants: that they should not commit any of the things He has forbidden them of His disobediences; and a frightening of them with His punishment at the time of meeting Him, as we have already explained; and a command to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) to give good tidings to those of His servants who were righteous believers in His books and His messengers, and in their meeting with Him, confirming their faith by their deeds, doing what their Lord commanded them and what He obligated upon them of His duties concerning what He required of their rights, and avoiding what He commanded them to avoid of His disobediences—of success on the Day of Resurrection, of the honour of the Hereafter, and of eternal abiding in Paradise. [[See what has preceded, al-Tabari's discussion of "those who will meet their Lord," vol. 2: pp. 20–22.]]
* *
Regarding the interpretation of His saying: ﴿And do not make Allah an obstacle for your oaths that you be righteous and fear Allah and make peace among the people﴾
Abu Ja'far said: The people of interpretation differed concerning the interpretation of His saying: "And do not make Allah an obstacle (ʿurḍa) for your oaths."
Some of them said: its meaning is: do not make Him a pretext (ʿilla) for your oaths. That is, when one of you is asked for something of good and reconciling between people, he says: "An oath by Allah is upon me that I will not do that," or "I have sworn by Allah that I will not do it," and he makes the swearing by Allah an excuse for abandoning doing good and reconciling between people.
Those who said this:
4351 – al-Ḥasan ibn Yaḥyā narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, saying: Maʿmar informed us, from Ibn Ṭāwūs, from his father, regarding "And do not make Allah an obstacle for your oaths": he said: It is the man who swears about a matter that is not right, then makes his oath an excuse, [while] Allah says: "that you be righteous and fear Allah" is better for him than to proceed in what is not right; and if he swears, let him expiate his oath and do what is better for him.
4352 – al-Muthannā narrated to us, saying: Suwayd ibn Naṣr narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubārak informed us, from Maʿmar, from Ibn Ṭāwūs, from his father, the like of it, except that he said: "And if he swears, let him expiate his oath and do what is good."
4353 – Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: ʿUbayd Allāh narrated to us, from Isrā'īl, from al-Suddī, from one who narrated to him, from Ibn ʿAbbās regarding His saying: "And do not make Allah an obstacle for your oaths that you be righteous and fear Allah and make peace among the people": he said: It is that a man swears that he will not speak to his relatives nor give charity, or that there is between him and a person a quarrel, so he swears he will not make peace between them, saying: "I have sworn." He said: he should expiate his oath. "And do not make Allah an obstacle for your oaths."
4354 – Bishr ibn Muʿādh narrated to us, saying: Yazīd ibn Zurayʿ narrated to us, saying: Saʿīd narrated to us, from Qatādah regarding His saying: "And do not make Allah an obstacle for your oaths that you be righteous and fear Allah": he says: Do not make Allah an excuse—that one of you says he has sworn not to keep the ties of kinship, nor strive for reconciliation, nor give charity from his wealth. [[Ta'alla al-rajul: he swore by Allah; similarly ʾāla.]] Gently, gently—may Allah bless you—for this Qur'an came only to abandon the command of Satan; so do not obey him, and do not carry out any command of his in any of your vows or oaths.
4355 – Muḥammad ibn Bashshār narrated to us, saying: Ibn Mahdī narrated to us, saying: Sufyān narrated to us, from Abū Ḥuṣayn, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr: "And do not make Allah an obstacle for your oaths": he said: It is the man who swears he will not reconcile between people nor be righteous; then when it is said to him, he says: "I have sworn."
4356 – al-Qāsim narrated to me, saying: al-Ḥusayn narrated to us, saying: Ḥajjāj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: I asked ʿAṭāʾ about His saying: "And do not make Allah an obstacle for your oaths that you be righteous and fear Allah and make peace among the people." He said: A person swears he will not do good, the beautiful matter, and says: "I have sworn!" Allah says: Do what is better and expiate your oath, and do not make Allah an obstacle.
4357 – It was narrated to me from al-Ḥusayn, who said: I heard Abū Muʿādh say: ʿUbayd ibn Sulaymān informed us, saying: I heard al-�daḥḥāk say regarding His saying: "And do not make Allah an obstacle for your oaths," the verse: It is the man who forbids upon himself what Allah has made lawful for him, and says: "I have sworn! It is not right unless I fulfil my oath." So Allah commanded them to expiate their oaths and to take what is lawful. [[The report: 4357 — in the printed edition: "narrated to me from ʿAmmār ibn al-Ḥasan, who said: I heard Abū Muʿādh," which is a clear error; the correct reading is from the manuscript, and it is a recurring chain in the tafsir, the closest of which is no. 4324. "al-Ḥusayn" is "al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Faraj."]]
4358 – Mūsā narrated to us, saying: ʿAmr narrated to us, saying: Asbāṭ narrated to us, from al-Suddī: "And do not make Allah an obstacle for your oaths that you be righteous and fear Allah and make peace among the people." As for "ʿurḍa": the matter comes between you and a man, so you swear by Allah that you will not speak to him nor join him. As for "tabarrū": a man swears he will not be righteous to his kinsman, so he says: "I have sworn!" Allah commanded that one should not place his oath between himself and his kinsman, and that he should be righteous to him and not mind his oath. As for "tuṣliḥū": a man reconciles between two people, and they disobey him, so he swears he will not reconcile between them; it is fitting that he reconcile and not mind his oath. And this was before the expiations were revealed. [[See Abū Ja'far's discussion of this report below, p. 426.]]
4359 – al-Muthannā narrated to us, saying: Suwayd narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubārak informed us, from Hushaym, from Mughīra, from Ibrāhīm regarding His saying: "And do not make Allah an obstacle for your oaths": he said: He swears that he will not fear Allah, nor keep the ties of kinship, nor reconcile between two people; so his oath does not prevent him.
* *
Others said: the meaning of that is: do not set up the swearing by Allah as an obstruction in your speech among yourselves, making that a proof for yourselves in abandoning the doing of good.
Those who held this view:
4360 – al-Muthannā ibn Ibrāhīm narrated to me, saying: Abū Ṣāliḥ narrated to us, saying: Muʿāwiya narrated to me, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa, from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding His saying: "And do not make Allah an obstacle for your oaths," he says: Do not make Me an obstacle to your oath that you will not do good; rather, expiate your oath and do good.
4361 – Muḥammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās regarding His saying: "And do not make Allah an obstacle for your oaths that you be righteous and fear Allah and make peace among the people": a man would swear about something of righteousness and piety that he would not do; so Allah, mighty and majestic, forbade that, saying: "And do not make Allah an obstacle for your oaths that you be righteous."
4362 – Yaʿqūb ibn Ibrāhīm narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Mughīra informed us, from Ibrāhīm regarding His saying: "And do not make Allah an obstacle for your oaths": he said: It is the man who swears that he will not be righteous to his kin, nor keep the ties of kinship, nor reconcile between two people. He says: let him do it, and let him expiate his oath.
4363 – Ibn Ḥumayd narrated to us, saying: Jarīr narrated to us, from Mughīra, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Yazīd, from Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī regarding His saying: "And do not make Allah an obstacle for your oaths that you be righteous and fear Allah and make peace among the people": he said: Do not swear that you will not fear Allah, nor swear that you will not be righteous nor do good, nor swear that you will not keep the ties of kinship, nor swear that you will not reconcile between people, nor swear that you will kill and cut off.
4364 – al-Muthannā narrated to me, saying: ʿAmr ibn ʿAwn narrated to us, saying: Hushaym informed us, from Dāwūd, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr — and Mughīra, from Ibrāhīm, regarding His saying: "And do not make Allah an obstacle" to the end of the verse — they both said: It is the man who swears that he will not be righteous, nor fear Allah, nor reconcile between people. He is commanded to fear Allah, reconcile between people, and expiate his oath.
4365 – Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abū ʿĀṣim narrated to us, from ʿĪsā — and al-Muthannā narrated to me, saying: Abū Ḥudhayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us — from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid regarding His saying: "And do not make Allah an obstacle for your oaths": they were commanded to join ties, to do the good, and to reconcile between people. If someone swears that he will not do that, let him do it and abandon his oath. [[The report: 4365 — in the manuscript it appears as a single chain, written thus: "Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abū ʿĀṣim narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ..." The printed edition's reading is the correct one; these are two chains recurring in the tafsir, the first of which is closest at no. 4132 and the second at no. 3872.]]
4366 – al-Muthannā narrated to me, saying: Isḥāq narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abī Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabīʿ regarding His saying: "And do not make Allah an obstacle for your oaths," to the end of the verse: he said: That is concerning a man who swears that he will not be righteous, nor keep the ties of kinship, nor reconcile between people. So Allah commands him to abandon his oath, keep the ties of kinship, enjoin what is right, and reconcile between people.
4367 – al-Muthannā narrated to me, saying: Isḥāq narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad ibn Ḥarb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Lahī'a narrated to us, from Abū al-Aswad, from ʿUrwa, from ʿĀ'isha regarding His saying: "And do not make Allah an obstacle for your oaths that you be righteous and fear Allah and make peace among the people": she said: Do not swear by Allah even if you are righteous.
4368 – al-Qāsim narrated to us, saying: al-Ḥusayn narrated to us, saying: Ḥajjāj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: I was told that His saying: "And do not make Allah an obstacle for your oaths," to the end of the verse, was revealed concerning Abū Bakr, regarding the matter of Mistaḥ.
4369 – Hannād narrated to us, saying: Ibn Fuḍayl narrated to us, from Mughīra, from Ibrāhīm regarding His saying: "And do not make Allah an obstacle for your oaths," to the end of the verse: he said: A man swears that he will not enjoin what is right, nor forbid what is wrong, nor keep the ties of kinship.
4370 – al-Muthannā narrated to me, saying: Suwayd narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubārak informed us, from Hushaym, from al-Mughīra, from Ibrāhīm regarding His saying: "And do not make Allah an obstacle for your oaths": he said: He swears that he will not fear Allah, nor keep the ties of kinship, nor reconcile between two people; so his oath does not prevent him. [[The report: 4370 — this report is not in this place in the manuscript, and that is the correct reading. It is a repetition of the one that passed as no. 4359. In the printed edition here it reads "so his oath does not benefit him," which is an evident error. It would seem better to delete it, but I have left it to indicate the variation among the copies.]]
4371 – Ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥīm al-Barqī narrated to me, saying: ʿAmr ibn Abī Salama narrated to us, from Saʿīd, from Makḥūl that he said regarding the saying of Allah, may His remembrance be exalted: "And do not make Allah an obstacle for your oaths": it is that a man swears he will not do good, nor keep the ties of kinship, nor reconcile between people. Allah forbade them from that.
* *
Abu Ja'far said: The more correct of the two interpretations of the verse is the interpretation of those who said: the meaning is: "Do not make swearing by Allah a proof for yourselves in abandoning the doing of good, between yourselves and Allah and between people."
* *
That is because "ʿurḍa," in the speech of the Arabs, means strength and vehemence. It is said of it: "this matter is an ʿurḍa for you," meaning: a strength for you in your means. And it is said: "such-and-such a woman is an ʿurḍa for marriage," meaning: a strength (or, a fit one). [[I fear the better reading may be: "i.e., a ready one."]] From it is the saying of Kaʿb ibn Zuhayr describing she-camels:
"Of every one sweating at the dhifrā when they sweat, / its ʿurḍa is a faded road-marker, unknown."
[[His Dīwān: 9; it will come in the tafsir 5: 79 / 11: 108 / 27: 62 (Bulaq) from his famous ode. "Nadaḥa" for a man with sweat means he sweated profusely until it flowed. "Naḍḥa" is intensely sweating. The dhifrā is the spot on a camel that sweats behind the ear, and in humans and animals alike it is the protruding bone behind the ear; the flowing of its sweat there is praised in camels. "Ṭāmis" is the faded one whose trace has been effaced. "Aʿlām" are the road-markers, built along the main path so that one who goes astray may be guided by them. And "unknown land" is one in which there are no markers nor mountains, so the traveller cannot find his way in it. He means: when one descends into these trackless wastes, one then recognizes their strength and vehemence and their patience with thirst and travel through the wilds.]]
He means by "ʿurḍatuhā": its strength and vehemence.
* *
So the meaning of His saying, may His remembrance be exalted: "And do not make Allah an obstacle for your oaths" is: do not make Allah a strength for your oaths that you will not be righteous, nor fear Allah, nor reconcile between people. Rather, when one of you swears and sees that what is better than what he swore to—such as abandoning righteousness and reconciliation between people—then let him break his oath, and be righteous, and fear Allah, and reconcile between people, and expiate his oath.
* *
The omission of "lā" from the speech is because the context indicates it, and what is mentioned suffices for what is omitted, as Imru' al-Qays said:
"So I said: By Allah's oath, I will not cease sitting, / even if they cut off my head before you and my joints."
[[His Dīwān: 141; it will come in the tafsir 13: 28 (Bulaq), from his incomparable and famous ode; what precedes and follows the verse is well known.]]
Meaning: "So I said: By Allah's oath, I will not cease," so "lā" is omitted, the context indicating it.
* *
As for His saying: "that you be righteous" (an tabarrū), there has been disagreement about the interpretation of "al-birr" (righteousness) which Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, intended.
Some of them said: it is doing all good. Others said: it is being righteous to one's kin; and I have already mentioned those who said that. [[See what has preceded on the meanings of "al-birr," vol. 2: p. 8; then vol. 3: pp. 336–338, 556.]]
* *
The more correct interpretation is the view of the one who said: "It is intended as doing all good." That is because all acts of good are of "al-birr," and Allah did not specify in His saying "an tabarrū" any meaning over another of the meanings of "al-birr"; so it is on its general sense, and being righteous to the kin is one of the meanings of "al-birr."
* *
As for His saying: "and fear Him" (wa tattaqū), its meaning is: that you fear your Lord, beware of Him and beware of His punishment regarding His obligations and limits, lest you neglect them or transgress them. We have already mentioned the interpretation of those who understood it to mean "taqwā" (piety). [[See the reports nos. 4361, 4363, 4364.]]
* *
Others said in its interpretation:
4372 – Muḥammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me this report, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās regarding His saying: "that you be righteous and fear Allah": he said: A man would swear about something of righteousness and piety that he would not do; so Allah, mighty and majestic, forbade that, saying: "And do not make Allah an obstacle for your oaths that you be righteous and fear Allah and make peace among the people," to the end of the verse. He said: It is said: Let not some of you be pious toward others by Me—you swear by Me while you are liars—so that people may believe you and you may reconcile among them; that is His saying: "that you be righteous and fear Allah," to the end of the verse. [[The report: 4372 is the earlier report no. 4361 with its continuation.]]
* *
As for His saying: "and make peace among people" (wa tuṣliḥū bayn al-nās), it is reconciling between them in the right way, in what involves no sin, and in what Allah loves rather than what He dislikes.
* *
As for what we have mentioned from al-Suddī: that this verse was revealed before the revelation of the expiations of oaths [[meaning the report that passed as no. 4358]], it is a saying for which there is no evidence from the Book or the Sunnah. Knowledge of what has happened cannot be verified except through a truthful report; otherwise it is a claim whose like, or its opposite, cannot be ruled out for anyone. [[In the manuscript: "lā yubʿad mithluhā..." unpointed, as if "lā saʿd," and the reading in the printed edition is better.]]
And it is not impossible that this verse was revealed after the explanation of the expiations of oaths in Sūrat al-Mā'ida, and that its mention there sufficed rather than repeating it here, since those addressed by this verse already knew the obligation of expiation for oaths in which the swearer breaks his oath.

Commentary on the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And Allah is Hearing, Knowing﴾ (2:224)

Abu Ja'far said: By this, exalted is His remembrance, He means: "And Allah is Hearing" of what the one of you who swears by Allah says when he swears, "By Allah, I will not be righteous, I will not be pious, and I will not reconcile between people," and of other than that from your speech and your oaths. "Knowing" of what you intend and seek by that oath of yours: do you desire good or other than it? For I am the Knower of the unseen and of what the breasts conceal; nothing hidden is concealed from Me, and no matter is kept from Me, whether it is manifest and apparent or hidden and concealed.

This, from Allah, exalted is His remembrance, is a warning and a threat. Exalted is His remembrance, He says: Be wary of Me, O people, lest you manifest with your tongues any speech, or with your bodies any action, that I have forbidden you, or lest you conceal within yourselves and resolve in your hearts, as intentions and aims, to do what I have prohibited you from, thereby deserving from Me the punishment that I have made you aware of. For I am fully aware of everything you make public or keep secret.

**The interpretation of God's words: ﴿God will not hold you accountable for the idle oaths in your oaths﴾**

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: The interpreters differed over the meaning of His words, "God will not hold you accountable for the idle oaths in your oaths," and over the meaning of "al-laghw" (idle, or inadvertent, oaths).

Some of them said that its meaning is: God will not hold you accountable for what your tongues have hastily and quickly uttered of oaths, so that He makes you liable for an expiation (kaffarah) for it when you did not intend to swear an oath. This is like the speaker's saying: "I did this, by God," or "I will do it, by God," or "I will not do it, by God," where his tongue has run ahead (sabbaq) with it, and his speech has been joined with an oath. [[The word "sabbuq," a verbal noun of "sabaqa," does not appear in the lexicons, but Abu Ja'far has repeated its use. See what has preceded in this volume 4: 287 and note 4, and what will come: 456, note 4.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 225 (part 2 of 4):

4422 - Ahmad ibn Hazim narrated to us, saying: Abu Nu'aym narrated to us, saying: Umar ibn Bashir narrated to us, saying: Amir (al-Sha'bi) was asked about this verse: "Allah will not hold you accountable for the unintentional oaths in your oaths" [2:225]. He said: Al-laghw (the unintentional oath, "lagha") is when a man swears that he will not fail to speak the truth, and then it turns out to be otherwise. That is the laghw for which he is not held accountable. [Note on the narration: Umar ibn Bashir al-Hamdani Abu Hani narrated from al-Sha'bi. Waki' and Abu Nu'aym narrated from him. Ahmad said: "Saalih al-hadith" (of acceptable narrations). Ibn Ma'in said: "Da'if" (weak). Abu Hatim said: "Laysa bi-qawiyy, yuktabu hadithuhu" (not strong; his hadith is recorded). He is biographed in al-Jarh wa al-Ta'dil. "Amir" is Amir al-Sha'bi, who has passed several times.]

4423 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding his statement: "Allah will not hold you accountable for the unintentional oaths in your oaths." Al-laghw is the oath made in error, not deliberately: that you swear on a matter while you think it is as you swore, and then it is not so. For this there is no expiation (kaffarah) upon him, nor any sin in it.

4424 - Musa narrated to us, saying: Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "Allah will not hold you accountable for the unintentional oaths in your oaths." As for al-laghw: it is the man who swears an oath while he believes it to be so, and it is not so. There is no expiation upon him.

4425 - I was told from Ammar, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi' regarding his statement: "Allah will not hold you accountable for the unintentional oaths in your oaths." He said: Al-laghw is the oath made in error, not deliberately: that he swears on a matter while he believes it is as he swore. And for this there is no expiation upon him.

4426 - Hannad narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Ahwas narrated to us, from Husayn, from Abu Malik, who said: As for the oath for which its swearer is not held accountable, it is the man who swears an oath while he believes he is truthful in it. That is the laghw.

4427 - Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Husayn informed us, from Abu Malik, the like of it, except that he said: A man swears on a matter, believing it is as he swore, and it is not so. There is no expiation upon him for it, and that is the laghw.

4428 - Yunus narrated to us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Mu'awiya ibn Salih informed me, from Yahya ibn Sa'id, and from Ibn Abi Talha (so said Ibn Abi Ja'far) [Note: this isnad is as it appears in the manuscript and the printed edition, and I could not establish its correct form, so I have left it as it is until it becomes clear from what follows how it should be. I fear that another isnad may have dropped between the two statements.] They both said: Whoever says, "By Allah, I did such and such," while he thinks he has done it, and then it becomes clear to him that he did not do it, this is the laghw of the oath, and there is no expiation upon him for it.

4429 - Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from a man, from al-Hasan regarding his statement: "Allah will not hold you accountable for the unintentional oaths in your oaths." He said: It is the error, not deliberate, like the saying of a man: "By Allah, this is such and such," while he believes he is truthful, and it is not so. Ma'mar said: Qatada also said this.

4430 - Ibn al-Barqi narrated to me, saying: Amr narrated to us, saying: Sa'id was asked about al-laghw in oaths. Sa'id said, and Makhul said: It is the error, not deliberate, but the expiation is for what your hearts have bound.

4431 - Ibn al-Barqi narrated to me, saying: Amr narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Abd al-Aziz, from Makhul that he said: The laghw for which Allah will not hold one accountable is that a man swears on a matter which he thinks he is truthful about, and then it turns out to be otherwise. There is no expiation upon him for it, and Allah has pardoned him.

4432 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mansur, from Ibrahim regarding his statement: "Allah will not hold you accountable for the unintentional oaths in your oaths." He said: If he swears an oath while he believes he is truthful in it, and he is lying, [Note: in the manuscript: "annahu sadiq" (that he is truthful), with "fihi" omitted.] then he is not held accountable for it. But if he swears an oath while he knows he is lying, that is what he is held accountable for.

* *

Others said: Rather, al-laghw of the oaths is those oaths which their swearer utters in a state of anger, without any intention of the heart or resolve, but as a connector of speech.

Those who said this:

4433 - Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Malik ibn Isma'il narrated to us, from Khalid, from Ata', from Wasim, [from Tawus], from Ibn Abbas, who said: The laghw of an oath is that you swear while you are angry. [Note on the narration: Malik ibn Isma'il Abu Ghassan al-Nahdi, al-Bukhari narrated from him; he was precise and trustworthy, and died in 219. "Khalid" is Khalid ibn Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Wasiti. Al-Bukhari said in al-Kabir 2/1/147: "Ali said: Khalid's hearing from Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib was late, and Hammad ibn Zayd's hearing from Ata' is sound." He died in 182 and is biographed in al-Tahdhib. "Ata'" is Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib. "Wasim" is biographed in al-Jarh wa al-Ta'dil 4/2/46 and in al-Kabir of al-Bukhari 4/2/181, where he said: "Wasim, from Tawus, from Ibn Abbas, concerning the oath of laghw; this was said by Khalid ibn Abd Allah from Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib." In the printed edition it reads "Rustum," which is an error. In both the printed and manuscript editions "an Tawus" (from Tawus) is omitted, and the correct reading is what is placed between the brackets, as stated by al-Bukhari and as narrated by al-Bayhaqi. This report was noted by al-Bukhari in al-Kabir as we quoted from him. Al-Bayhaqi narrated it in al-Sunan al-Kubra 10:49, through Sa'id ibn Mansur: "from Khalid, from Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Wasim, from Tawus, from Ibn Abbas." From this, and from what follows, it appears that "an Tawus" dropped from the copies of al-Tabari here, between "Wasim" and "Ibn Abbas." Ibn Kathir (1:527) also quoted it from the Tafsir of Ibn Abi Hatim with its isnad through Musaddad: "Khalid narrated to us, Ata' narrated to us, from Tawus, from Ibn Abbas," so it appears that a omission occurred in the printed edition of Ibn Kathir, dropping "from Wasim" between Ata' and Tawus. Al-Suyuti (1:269) also mentioned it and attributed it to Sa'id ibn Mansur, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Bayhaqi, "through the route of Tawus from Ibn Abbas." This report is a good supporting witness to the marfu' hadith from Ibn Abbas that follows at 4435.]

4434 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, saying: Abu Hamza narrated to us, from Ata', from Tawus, who said: Every oath a man swears while he is angry, there is no expiation upon him for it, the saying of Allah: "Allah will not hold you accountable for the unintentional oaths in your oaths." [Note: Abu Hamza is Muhammad ibn Maymun al-Marwazi, Abu Hamza al-Sukkari, who died in 166. This report, being a statement of Tawus, supports his earlier narration from Ibn Abbas. It is another witness to the marfu' hadith that follows it.]

* *

The reasoning of those who held this view is what follows:

4435 - Ahmad ibn Mansur al-Marwazi narrated this to me, saying: Umar ibn Yunus al-Yamami narrated to us, saying: Sulayman ibn Abi Sulayman al-Zuhri narrated to us, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from Tawus, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "There is no oath in anger." [Note: This isnad is sound. Ahmad ibn Mansur ibn Rashid, Abu Salih al-Hanzali al-Marwazi, the teacher of al-Tabari: trustworthy. Umar ibn Yunus ibn al-Qasim al-Yamami: trustworthy and firm; Ahmad and Ibn Ma'in deemed him trustworthy. Sulayman ibn Abi Sulayman al-Zuhri al-Yamami: trustworthy. Al-Bukhari included him in al-Kabir 2/2/20, and mentioned that he narrated from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir and that Umar ibn Yunus heard from him, and he did not mention any objection in him. Ibn Abi Hatim included him in 2/1/122 with a biography similar to al-Bukhari's, then narrated from his father Abu Hatim that he said: "He is a weak shaykh." Ibn Hibban mentioned him in al-Thiqat and said: "He sometimes differed." This was also quoted from him by al-Hafiz in Lisan al-Mizan 3:95. Some have confused him with another very weak narrator, "Sulayman ibn Dawud al-Yamami," because the latter often narrates from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir. But this is other than that one, as al-Bukhari, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Hibban distinguished between them, and al-Hafiz established this in Lisan al-Mizan. However, al-Hafiz's words give the impression that al-Bukhari weakened the narrator here, because he claimed that Abu Hatim followed al-Bukhari in this. But al-Bukhari mentioned no criticism in al-Kabir, nor did he include him in al-Saghir, nor mention him among the weak narrators. So the truth is that he is trustworthy. This hadith I have not found elsewhere, except that al-Hafiz mentioned it in al-Fath 11:490 and attributed it to al-Tabarani in al-Awsat, then said: "Its isnad is weak." I did not find it in Majma' al-Zawa'id. It appears to me, and Allah knows best, that al-Hafiz weakened it because he went to weaken Sulayman ibn Abi Sulayman; I differ with him in that, as I have shown before.]

* *

Others said: Rather, al-laghw in oaths is swearing to do what Allah has forbidden, and to abandon what Allah has commanded to be done.

Those who said this:

4436 - Hannad narrated to us, saying: Hafs ibn Ghiyath narrated to us, from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: It is the one who swears to an act of disobedience, and does not fulfil it, and makes expiation for his oath. [Quranic reference:] "Allah will not hold you accountable for the unintentional oaths in your oaths."

4437 - Muhammad ibn Abd al-Malik ibn Abi al-Shawarib narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Zuray' narrated to us, saying: Dawud narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: The laghw of the oath is that a man swears to an act of disobedience to Allah; Allah will not hold him accountable for nullifying it. [Note: In the manuscript and printed edition: "bi-iyfa'iha" (by fulfilling it), and the correct reading is what I have set down. See p. 441, note 1.]

4438 - Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Adi narrated to us, from Dawud, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, similarly, and he added in it, he said: And upon him is expiation. [Note: In the printed edition: "wa-alayhi kaffarah," and I have set down what is in the manuscript.]

4439 - Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Abd al-A'la and Yazid ibn Harun narrated to me, from Dawud, from Sa'id, similarly.

4440 - Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us, saying: Dawud narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr: "Allah will not hold you accountable for the unintentional oaths in your oaths," he said: It is the man who swears to an act of disobedience, so Allah will not hold him accountable for expiating his oath, and he does what is better.

4441 - Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'ba narrated to us [and Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Shu'ba], from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr regarding this verse: "Allah will not hold you accountable for the unintentional oaths in your oaths," he said: The man who swears to an act of disobedience, Allah will not hold him accountable for abandoning it.

4442 - Al-Hasan ibn al-Sabbah al-Bazzar narrated to us, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, from Isa, son of the daughter of Dawud ibn Abi Hind, who said: Khalid ibn Ilyas narrated to us, from his paternal grandmother [Note: "umm abihi"], that she swore she would not speak to the daughter of her son, the daughter of Abu al-Jahm. She went to Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, Abu Bakr and Urwa ibn al-Zubayr, and they said: There is no oath in disobedience, and there is no expiation upon it. [Note: Al-Hasan ibn al-Sabbah al-Bazzar al-Wasiti: al-Bukhari, Abu Dawud and al-Tirmidhi narrated from him; he was trustworthy and a man of the Sunna, died in 249. Khalid ibn Ilyas ibn Sakhr Abu al-Haytham al-Adawi: Ahmad said: "matruk al-hadith" (abandoned in hadith). Ibn Ma'in said: "laysa bi-shay'" (nothing) and "his hadith is not recorded."]

4443 - Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr regarding his statement: "Allah will not hold you accountable for the unintentional oaths in your oaths," he said: It is the man who swears to an act of disobedience, so Allah will not hold him accountable for abandoning it, if he abandons it. I said: Then what should he do? He said: He makes expiation for his oath and abandons the disobedience.

4444 - Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Hushaym informed us, from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr regarding his statement: "Allah will not hold you accountable for the unintentional oaths in your oaths," he said: It is the man who swears to what is forbidden, so Allah will not hold him accountable for abandoning it.

4445 - Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn Ulayya narrated to us, saying: Dawud informed us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said regarding the laghw of oaths: It is the oath in disobedience. He said: Do you not recite and understand? Allah says: "Allah will not hold you accountable for the unintentional oaths in your oaths, but He will hold you accountable for what you have bound by the oaths" [5:89]. He said: So He does not hold him accountable for nullifying it, but He holds him accountable for persisting in it. [Note: In the printed edition: "bi-al-iyfa'" and in the manuscript: "bi-al-iyfad"; the correct reading is "bi-al-ilgha'" (nullifying). Algha al-shay': annulled and removed it. Tamma 'ala al-amr tamaman: persisted in it and carried it out.] He said: And he said: "Do not make Allah an obstacle to your oaths" up to his saying: "Indeed Allah is Forgiving, Forbearing." [Note: In the manuscript and printed edition: "wa-Allahu ghafur halim"; the writer slipped, and this is the correct reading.]

4446 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Suwayd ibn Nasr narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Hushaym, from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr regarding his statement: "Allah will not hold you accountable for the unintentional oaths in your oaths," he said: It is the man who swears to an act of disobedience, so Allah will not hold him accountable for abandoning it, and he makes expiation.

4447 - Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Wahb ibn Jarir narrated to us, saying: Shu'ba narrated to us, from Asim, from al-Sha'bi, from Masruq, regarding the man who swears to an act of disobedience, he said: Shall he make expiation for the steps of Satan? There is no expiation upon him.

4448 - Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Wahb ibn Jarir narrated to us, saying: Shu'ba narrated to us, from Asim, from Ikrima, from Ibn Abbas, the like of that.

4449 - Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Adi narrated to us, from Dawud, from al-Sha'bi, regarding the man who swears to an act of disobedience, he said: Its expiation is that he repents from it.

4450 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Mughira informed us, from al-Sha'bi, that he used to say: He abandons the disobedience and does not make expiation; and if I ordered him to make expiation, I would order him to persist in his statement.

4451 - Yahya ibn Dawud al-Wasiti narrated to us, saying: Abu Usama narrated to us, from Mujalid, from Amir, from Masruq, who said: Every oath which it is not lawful for you to fulfil, there is no expiation in it.

* *

The narrations reasoning of those who held this view are what follows:

4452 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Abu Usama narrated to us, from al-Walid ibn Kathir, who said: Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Harith narrated to me, from Amr ibn Shu'ayb, from his father, from Abd Allah ibn Amr, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever vows concerning what he does not possess, there is no vow for him; whoever swears to an act of disobedience to Allah, there is no oath for him; and whoever swears to severing ties of kinship, there is no oath for him." [Note: al-Hakim narrated it in al-Mustadrak 4:300 through al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Affan al-Amiri, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan al-Kubra 10:23 through Ahmad ibn Abd al-Hamid al-Harithi, both from Abu Usama, with this isnad. Al-Hakim said: "This hadith has a sound isnad, but they did not record it." Al-Dhahabi responded: "Abd al-Rahman: matruk" (abandoned), and Abu Hatim said: "shaykh." "Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Harith ibn Abd Allah ibn Ayyash ibn Abi Rabi'a": trustworthy, as passed at 3827. The meaning of the hadith is established from many routes, collectively and separately, in al-Musnad: 6732, 6780, 6781, 6932, 6990.]

4453 - Ali ibn Sa'id al-Kindi narrated to me, saying: Ali ibn Mushir narrated to us, from Haritha ibn Muhammad, from Amra, from A'isha, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever swears an oath of severing kinship or disobedience to Allah, his righteousness is to break it and retract his oath." [Note: This hadith is very weak. Ali ibn Mushir al-Qurashi al-Kufi al-Hafiz: trustworthy and firm, one of those who gathered hadith and fiqh; the six imams narrated from him. Haritha ibn Muhammad: he is Haritha ibn Abi al-Rijal Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman, who narrates from his paternal grandmother Amra bint Abd al-Rahman, and he is very weak. Al-Bukhari said in al-Kabir 2/1/87, al-Saghir: 174, and al-Du'afa': 11: "munkar al-hadith" (rejected in hadith). Ahmad said: "da'if laysa bi-shay'." Al-Bukhari said in al-Saghir: "Ahmad did not rely on Haritha ibn Abi al-Rijal." The hadith I have not found in any of the references.]

* *

Others said: Laghw among oaths is every oath which a man joins to his speech, without intending by it to bind himself.

Those who said this:

4454 - Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Ibn Ulayya narrated to us, saying: Hisham narrated to us, saying: Hammad narrated to us, from Ibrahim, who said: The laghw of the oath is that a man joins his speech with the oath: "By Allah, he will eat! By Allah, he will drink!" and the like of this, without intending by it an oath and without wishing it to be an oath. There is no expiation upon him.

4455 - Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Ibn Ulayya narrated to us, from Hisham al-Dastawa'i, from Hammad, from Ibrahim: The laghw of the oath is what a man joins to his speech: "By Allah, you will eat! By Allah, you will drink!"

4456 - Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mansur, from al-Hakam, from Mujahid: "Allah will not hold you accountable for the unintentional oaths in your oaths" [sic: "iymanikum"]. He said: They are two men who haggle over a thing, and one of them says: "By Allah, I will not buy it from you for such and such," and the other says: "By Allah, I will not sell to you for such and such."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 225 (part 3 of 4):

4457: Yunus told me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Yunus informed me, from Ibn Shihab: that Urwa told him that Aisha, the wife of the Prophet (ﷺ), said: "The vain oaths (ayman al-laghw) are what is said in jest, in dispute, and in argument, and in speech upon which the heart does not rely." [[I fear the correct reading is: "upon which the heart does not settle..."]]
* *
The basis for those who held this view from the transmitted reports is what follows:
4458: Muhammad ibn Musa al-Harashi narrated it to me, saying: 'Ubayd Allah ibn Maymun al-Muradi told us, saying: Awf al-A'rabi told us, from al-Hasan ibn Abi al-Hasan, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) passed by a people who were shooting arrows at a target, meaning they were throwing, and with the Prophet (ﷺ) was a man from among his Companions. A man from the people shot and said: "By God, I hit it, and I missed!" The one who was with the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The man has broken his oath, O Messenger of God!" He said: "No. The oaths of archers are vain; there is no expiation (kaffara) for them and no punishment." [[The hadith 4458: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn Nafi al-Harashi, the teacher of al-Tabari, is trustworthy (thiqa); Ibn Hibban mentioned him in al-Thiqat, and al-Nasa'i said: "Salih" (acceptable). 'Ubayd Allah ibn Maymun al-Muradi: I do not know who he is, and I have found no biography of him.
