Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 227 (part 2 of 3):

4601 - Al-Muthanna related to me, who said: Ishaq related to us, who said: Abu Wahb related to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, regarding ﴿Those who swear off [sexual relations with] their wives﴾ (the verse): It refers to the one who swears that he will not approach his wife. If four months pass and he has neither returned (fa'a) nor divorced, she is separated from him by the ila' (the oath of abstention). If she returns to him, [it is] a new dowry, a new marriage contract with witnesses, and the consent of the guardian. [[In the printed edition: "and the consent of the mawla," which is an error; the correct reading, from the manuscript, is as given.]]

* *

Others said: Rather, what separates her upon the passing of the four months is one divorce, in which the husband retains the right of return (raj'a).
Mention of those who said this:

4602 - Abu Kurayb related to us, who said: Ibn Idris related to us, who said: Malik related to us, from al-Zuhri, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab and Abu Bakr ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Harith ibn Hisham, who both said: If a man takes an oath of abstention from his wife and four months pass, [it is] one [divorce], and he has the greater right to take her back. [[Report 4602: In the Muwatta' (557) it appears with different wording. In the printed edition: "li-raj'atiha," the correct reading being from the manuscript.]]

4603 - Abu Hisham related to us, who said: Ibn Idris related to us, from Malik, from al-Zuhri, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, who said: When four months pass, it is one divorce in which he holds the right of return. [[Report 4603: I have not found it in these words in the Muwatta'; it seems to be an abridgment of the preceding one.]]

4604 - Abu Hisham related to us, who said: Ibn Mahdi related to us, who said: Sufyan related to us, from Isma'il ibn Umayya, from Makhul, who said: When four months pass, it is one divorce, in which he holds the right of return.

4605 - Al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, who said: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, who said: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from Abu Bakr ibn Abd al-Rahman, who said: It is one [divorce], and he has the greater right to her, meaning when the four months have passed. Al-Zuhri used to issue fatwas in accordance with this opinion of Abu Bakr.

4606 - Al-Muthanna related to me, who said: Abu Salih related to us, who said: al-Layth related to us, who said: Yunus related to me, who said: Ibn Shihab (al-Zuhri) said: Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab related to me that he said: If a man takes an oath of abstention from his wife and the four months pass before he returns, it is one divorce, and he has the greater right to her as long as she is in her waiting period ('idda).

4607 - Abu Hisham related to us, who said: Yahya ibn Yaman related to us, who said: Abu Yunus al-Qawi related to us, who said: Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab said to me: "Where are you from?" I said: "From the people of Iraq." He said: "Perhaps you are one of those who say: 'When four months pass, she is separated,' No! Even if four years pass." [[Report 4607: "Abu al-Qawi" is al-Hasan ibn Yazid ibn Farrukh al-Damri, also called al-'Ajli. He settled in Kufa. Ibn Ma'in said: "He is the one called al-Tawwaf." He was called "al-Qawi" for his strength in worship. Waki' said: "He wept until he went blind, prayed until his back was bent, and circumambulated until he could not sit." Ibn Ma'in and al-Nasa'i deemed him trustworthy. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib.]]

4608 - Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Hakam related to us, who said: Hajjaj ibn Rishdin related to us, who said: Abd al-Jabbar ibn Umar related to us, from Rabi'a: that he said regarding the ila': When four months pass, it is one divorce, and she begins her waiting period, and her husband has the greater right to take her back. [[Report 4608: "Hajjaj ibn Rishdin ibn Sa'd al-Misri" related from his father and Haywa ibn Shurayh; Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Hakam related from him. Ibn Abi Hatim said: "I asked my father about him, and he said: 'I have no knowledge of him; I did not write from anyone who related from him.'" Ibn Hibban mentioned him among the trustworthy, and Ibn Adi deemed him weak. He died in the year 211. He is biographed in Lisan al-Mizan and al-Jarh wa-al-Ta'dil 1/216. "Abd al-Jabbar ibn Umar al-Ayli" heard from al-Zuhri, Rabi'a, Ata' al-Khurasani and Abu al-Zinad. Ibn Wahb and Sa'id ibn Abi Maryam related from him. Yahya ibn Ma'in was asked about him and said: "Weak, of no account." Abu Zur'a said: "Weak in hadith, not strong." He is biographed in al-Jarh wa-al-Ta'dil 3/1/31-32.]]

4609 - Abu Kurayb related to us, who said: Ibn Idris related to us, who said: Ibn Shubruma used to say: When four months pass, he has the right of return, and he argued with the Qur'an, interpreting this verse: ﴿And their husbands have more right to take them back in that [period]﴾ [Surah al-Baqarah: 228]. Then he recited: [[To recite (nazaʿa) with the verse and the poetry means to cite them; it is also said of a man who derives the meaning of a verse of the Book of God: "He has derived a good meaning," i.e., extracted it.]] "For those who swear off [sexual relations with] their wives is a waiting of four months; then if they return, indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful. And if they are determined upon divorce, indeed Allah is Hearing and Knowing."

4610 - Ali ibn Sahl related to us, who said: al-Walid ibn Muslim related to us, who said: Abu Amr said: And we, regarding this matter, meaning the ila', hold the view of our companions al-Zuhri and Makhul that it is one divorce, meaning the passing of the four months, and he has the greater right to her in her waiting period. [[Report 4610: "al-Walid ibn Muslim al-Qurashi" of Damascus, the scholar of Syria. Ahmad said: "I have never seen anyone more intelligent than him." Marwan ibn Muhammad said: "If you write the hadith of al-Awza'i from al-Walid, do not worry about whatever you missed." He also said: "al-Walid was knowledgeable in the hadith of al-Awza'i." He died after returning from the pilgrimage in the year 194. "Abu Amr" is the eminent imam Abu Amr al-Awza'i, "Abd al-Rahman ibn Amr ibn Yuhmid," the renowned jurist.]]

* *

Others said: The meaning of His saying: ﴿For those who swear off [sexual relations with] their wives﴾ up to His saying: ﴿indeed Allah is Hearing and Knowing﴾ = "For those who swear off," by withdrawing from their wives, a waiting period of four months by their command and hers; "then if they return" after the four months have ended, to them, returning to good treatment of them and abandoning their avoidance, and coming to them for intercourse and sexual relations; "indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful. And if they are determined upon divorce" then they bring about a divorce to them after the four months; "indeed He is Hearing" of their divorcing them; "Knowing" of what they did to them of kindness or harm.

Those who held this interpretation said: The passing of the four months necessitates that the woman demand, from her husband who has sworn off her, either a return or a divorce. It is obligatory upon the ruler to have the husband stopped for this; if he returns or divorces, well and good; otherwise the ruler divorces on his behalf.

Mention of those who said this:

[[Report 4611: "This is al-Muthanna ibn al-Sabah al-Yamani." Originally from the people of Yemen in Persia, he related from Tawus, Mujahid, Ata' ibn Abi Rabah and Amr ibn Shu'ayb. Yahya ibn Sa'id, when he was mentioned in his presence, said: "We did not abandon him on account of Amr ibn Shu'ayb, but there was confusion in his narrations from Ata'." Ahmad said: "His hadith is worth nothing; it is unsound." Ibn Ma'in and others deemed him weak. He died in the year 149.]]

As for "Najiya ibn Bakr," I have not found anyone with this name among the narrators; but Ibn Wahb narrates from "Bakr ibn Mudar al-Misri," so I fear there is an addition and a corruption in the text, and God knows best. In the printed edition and the manuscript it reads "Ibn Abi al-As," and the correct reading is as given here; see Nasab Quraysh, 312.]]

4634 - Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna related to us, who said: Yahya ibn Sa'id related to us, from Ubayd Allah, from Nafi', from Ibn Umar, who said regarding the one who has sworn off: It is not lawful for him except what God has made lawful to him: either he returns or he divorces.

4635 - Tamim ibn al-Muntasir related to us, who said: Abd Allah ibn Numayr informed us, who said: Ubayd Allah informed us, from Nafi', from Ibn Umar, the like of it. [[Report 4635: In the manuscript, "from Abd Allah, from Nafi'" appears in this place only.]]

4636 - Abu Kurayb related to us, who said: Ibn Idris related to us, who said: Ubayd Allah related to us, from Nafi', from Ibn Umar, who said: It is not permissible for the one who has sworn off not to do what God has commanded him. He says: He must clarify the return, or divorce, at the end of the four months. He must clarify the return, or divorce. Abu Kurayb said: Ibn Idris said, and added to it: I questioned him about it, and he said a statement whose meaning is: He has the right of return.

4637 - Abu Kurayb related to us, who said: Ibn Idris related to us, who said: Shu'ba related to us, from Simak, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr: that Umar said something similar to the statement of Ibn Umar.

4638 - Mujahid ibn Musa related to us, who said: Yazid ibn Harun related to us, who said: Jarir ibn Hazim informed us, who said: Nafi' informed us: that Ibn Umar said regarding the ila': He is stopped at the end of the four months.

4639 - Yunus related to me, who said: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ubayd Allah ibn Umar related to me, from Nafi', from Ibn Umar: that he said: If a man swears not to touch his wife and four months pass, then either he retains her as God commanded, or he divorces her, and what he did does not oblige a divorce upon him, nor anything else.

4640 - Abu Hisham related to us, who said: Ibn Uyayna related to us, from Ayyub, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: I asked Ibn Umar about the ila', and he said: The rulers judge by that.

4641 - Al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, who said: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, who said: Ma'mar informed us, from Ayyub, from Nafi', from Ibn Umar, who said: The one who has sworn off is stopped upon the end of the four months. Either he divorces, or he returns.

4642 - Abd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Shabbawayh related to us, who said: Ibn Abi Maryam related to us, who said: Yahya ibn Ayyub related to us, from Ubayd Allah ibn Umar, from Suhayl ibn Abi Salih, from his father, who said: I asked twelve men from the companions of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) about a man who swears off his wife, and all of them said: There is nothing upon him until the four months pass, and then he is stopped; if he returns, well and good; otherwise he divorces.

٤٦٤٣ - Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us, saying: Dawud narrated to us, from Said ibn al-Musayyib, concerning a man who takes an oath of abstinence (ila') from his wife, that he [Said] said: "He did not consider that she should enter upon him in his [chamber] until he divorces her." [[The phrase "فرقه" is as it stands in the manuscript; in the printed edition it reads "فرقة". It is most likely a corruption of a word meaning "his house" or "his room."]]

٤٦٤٤ - Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Adi narrated to us, from Dawud, from Said ibn al-Musayyib, concerning the ila': "When four months have passed, [the husband] is not permitted to exceed [this period] until he returns (yafi') or divorces. If he exceeds it, he has disobeyed God, but his wife is not made unlawful to him."

٤٦٤٥ - Abu Hisham narrated to us, saying: Ibn Fudayl narrated to us, from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from Said ibn al-Musayyib, who said: "When four months have passed, he must either return or divorce."

٤٦٤٦ - Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, both saying: Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Said narrated to us, from Qatada, from Ibn al-Musayyib, concerning the ila': "He is made to stand (yuqaf) at the end of the four months; then either he returns or he divorces."

٤٦٤٧ - Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, saying: Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, from Ma'mar - or [Ibn Ulayyah said:] "I narrated it from him" [the printed edition reads "haddathtuhu"; I have kept what is in the manuscript] - from Ata al-Khurasani, who said: "I asked Ibn al-Musayyib about the ila', and he said: 'He is made to stand (yuqaf).'"

٤٦٤٨ - al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Ata al-Khurasani, from Ibn al-Musayyib - and from Ibn Tawus, from his father - both said: "The one who has made the ila' is made to stand after the four months have passed; then either he returns or he divorces." [[At this point the section of the manuscript from which our copy was transcribed ends, and the following colophon appears:
"May God bless our master Muhammad, his family and companions, and grant them abundant peace.
* *
Collated with the original.
I completed the reading of it from its beginning, by hearing it from al-Qadi Abu al-Hasan al-Khasib ibn Abd Allah, from Abu Muhammad al-Farghani, from Abu Ja'far al-Tabari. My brother Ali - may God preserve him - heard it with me, along with Ahmad ibn Umar ibn Madida al-Jihari, Nasr ibn al-Husayn al-Tabari, and Muhammad ibn Ali al-Umawi. Muhammad ibn Isa al-Sa'di copied it in Sha'ban of the year 408, while the qadi was comparing it with his book."]]

٤٦٤٩ - [[The beginning of this section reads:
"In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate"]] Ali ibn Sahl narrated to us, saying: al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us, saying: Malik ibn Anas narrated to me, from al-Zuhri, from Said ibn al-Musayyib and Abu Bakr ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Harith ibn Hisham, the like of that - meaning the like of the statement of Umar ibn al-Khattab concerning the ila': "There is nothing upon him until he is made to stand; then he either divorces or retains [his wife]." [[The report: 4649 is another chain for the report 4602 mentioned earlier. As for the report of Umar, it is the one that passed under number 4611.]]

٤٦٥٠ - Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'ba narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, that he said concerning the ila': "He is made to stand."

٤٦٥١ - Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, from Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih - and al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih - from Mujahid, concerning God's words: "For those who swear abstinence from their wives, a waiting period of four months." He said: "When four months have passed, he is seized and made to stand until he returns to his wife or divorces."

٤٦٥٢ - Abu Hisham narrated to us, saying: Ibn Uyayna narrated to us, from Ayyub, from Sulayman ibn Yasar: that Marwan made him stand after six months.

٤٦٥٣ - Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us, saying: Dawud narrated to us, from Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz concerning the ila', who said: "He is made to stand at the end of the four months until he returns or divorces."

٤٦٥٤ - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, concerning God's words: "For those who swear abstinence from their wives, a waiting period of four months." He said: "It is the man who swears to his wife by God that he will not marry her, and so he waits four months. If he then marries her, he expiates his oath. If four months pass before he marries her, the ruler compels him either to return and resume the marriage, or to resolve and divorce, as God the Exalted said."

٤٦٥٥ - Musa ibn Harun narrated to us, saying: Amr ibn Hammad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, concerning God's words: "For those who swear abstinence from their wives, a waiting period of four months. Then if they return..." to the end of the verse. He said: "Ali and Ibn Abbas used to say: When a man makes ila' from his wife and the four months pass, he is made to stand and it is said to him: 'Either you retain her or you divorce.' If he retains her, she is his wife; and if he divorces, she is divorced."

٤٦٥٦ - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said concerning God's words: "For those who swear abstinence from their wives." He said: "It is the man who swears that he will not come near his wife for such and such [a period]. God has given him a four-month period in which to wait with her." He said: "God's words, may He be mentioned, 'a waiting period of four months,' mean he waits with her: 'Then if they return, God is Forgiving and Merciful. And if they resolve upon divorce, God is Hearing and Knowing.' So when you bring him before the ruler, he sets for him a term of four months. If he returns, [well and good]; otherwise he is divorced against his will. But if you do not bring him [before the ruler], it is a right of hers that he has abandoned." [[In the printed edition it reads "ajila arba'a ashhur"; I have kept what is in the manuscript.]]

٤٦٥٧ - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, from Malik, who said: "No divorce falls upon the one who made ila' until he is made to stand. He is not a mu'li (one who has made ila') unless he swears for more than four months. If he swears for four months, there is no ila' upon him, because he is made to stand at the end of the four months, and the oath has by then lapsed from him; so the ila' is gone." [[Report 4657: I did not find its wording in the Muwatta', but its meaning is in it (Muwatta': 556-558).]]

٤٦٥٨ - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, from Ibn Zayd, who said: Ibn Umar said: "Until he is brought before the ruler." My father used to say this, and he would say: "No, by God, even if four years pass, he is to be made to stand."

٤٦٥٩ - Ahmad ibn Hazim narrated to us, saying: Abu Nu'aym narrated to us, saying: Fitr narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi said, and I was with him: "If a man makes ila' from his wife for four years, we will not separate them from him until we bring them together. If he returns, he returns; and if he resolves on divorce, he resolves." [[In the printed edition it reads "lam nukabbha minhu"; this seems to be a copyist's corruption, and the correct reading is from the manuscript.]]

٤٦٦٠ - Ahmad ibn Hazim narrated to us, saying: Abu Nu'aym narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Aziz al-Majishun narrated to us, from Dawud ibn al-Husayn, who said: "I heard al-Qasim ibn Muhammad say: He is made to stand when the four months have passed."

* *
Others said: "The ila' is nothing."
Mention of those who said this:

٤٦٦١ - Ahmad ibn Hazim narrated to us, saying: Abu Nu'aym narrated to us, saying: Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, from Amr ibn Dinar, who said: "I asked Ibn al-Musayyib about the ila', and he said: 'It is nothing.'"

٤٦٦٢ - Ahmad ibn Hazim narrated to us, saying: Abu Nu'aym narrated to us, saying: Ja'far ibn Burqan narrated to me, from Maymun ibn Mihran, who said: "I asked Ibn Umar about a man who made ila' from his wife, and four months passed and he did not return to her. He recited this verse: 'For those who swear abstinence from their wives, a waiting period of four months,' to the end of the verse."

٤٦٦٣ - Ahmad ibn Hazim narrated to us, saying: Abu Nu'aym narrated to us, saying: Mis'ar narrated to us, from Habib ibn Abi Thabit, who said: "I sent to Ata asking him about the mu'li, and he said: 'I have no knowledge of it.'"

* *
Others from among the people of this view said: "Rather, the meaning of His words 'and if they resolve upon divorce' is: 'and if they refuse to return, after the ruler has made them stand to choose return or divorce.'"
Mention of those who said this:

٤٦٦٤ - Abu al-Sa'ib narrated to me, saying: Abu Mu'awiya narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, who said: "The mu'li is made to stand at the end of the four months. If he returns, he keeps her as his wife; if he does not return, [the ruler] makes it one irrevocable (ba'in) divorce."

٤٦٦٥ - Abu Hisham narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, who said: "The mu'li is made to stand at the end of the four months. If he does not return, it is one irrevocable divorce."

* *
Abu Ja'far said: The most likely of these opinions in agreement with the apparent meaning of God's Book, the Exalted, is the saying of Umar ibn al-Khattab, Uthman and Ali, may God be pleased with them, and of those who held their view concerning divorce: that His words, "Then if they return, God is Forgiving and Merciful; and if they resolve upon divorce, God is Hearing and Knowing," mean only: "If they return after the ruler has made them stand following the end of the four months, and go back to fulfilling God's right over them concerning the wives whom they had sworn off, then God is Forgiving and Merciful to them." "And if they resolve upon divorce" means they divorce them. "God is Hearing" of their divorce if they divorce. "Knowing" of what they did to them.

We have said this because it is more in keeping with the interpretation of the verse. God, may He be mentioned, when He said, "And if they resolve upon divorce," then concluded the verse with "God is Hearing and Knowing" [[We separated the two halves of the verse because that is what al-Tabari intends: that God, when He said "and if they resolve upon divorce," ended the verse with His words "God is Hearing and Knowing."]]. It is known that the passing of the four months is not something heard; it is only something known. So if "resolving upon divorce" meant the passing of the four months, the verse would not have been concluded with the mention of God's report that He is "Hearing and Knowing." Likewise, the verse in which the return to His obedience is mentioned, namely the mu'li's return to the wife from whom he swore off and his fulfilling of her right, was not concluded with the report that He is "severe in punishment," since it is not a place of warning against disobedience. Instead, He concluded it with the report describing Himself, may He be mentioned, as "Forgiving and Merciful," since it is a place of promise to the one who turns back in repentance to obedience. Thus He concluded the verse in which the speech is mentioned with a description of Himself as "Hearing" of speech and "Knowing" of action. He, may He be mentioned, said: "And if the men who swear abstinence from their wives resolve upon divorce of those whom they have sworn off, then God is Hearing" of their divorce of them if they divorce them, "Knowing" of what they do to them that is lawful or forbidden for them. [[This is Abu Ja'far's understanding of the meanings of his Lord's Book, and his exposition of the proofs of eloquence and clarity in a Book into which falsehood cannot come from before it or behind it. In it is proof for whoever seeks the truth from its sources, with scrupulousness, patience, insight, and knowledge of what the words require in meaning.]]

We have fully explained the evidence for the soundness of this view in our book [[Kitab al-Latif min al-Bayan 'an Ahkam Shara'i' al-Din]], so we disliked repeating it in this place.

**The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Divorced women shall wait by themselves for three periods﴾**

Abu Ja'far said: He, exalted is His remembrance, means: "The divorced women," those whom their husbands divorced after they had consummated the marriage and been intimate with them, if they are women who menstruate and have periods of purity, "shall wait by themselves" from marrying other husbands, "for three quru'" (ﷻ).

* *

The people of ta'wil (interpretation of the Qur'an, tafsir) differed over the interpretation of the qur', which Allah meant in His words, "shall wait by themselves for three quru'." Some of them said: it is the menstrual period (hayd).

Those who said this:

4666: Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the words of Allah: "And divorced women shall wait by themselves for three quru'," he said: "Hiyad (menstrual periods)." [[The hayda (with a kasra on the ha') is the noun for menstruation and the state a menstruating woman is bound by in terms of abstention; the plural is "hiyad" (with a fatha on the ha' and a fatha on the ya'). As for "hayda," it is a single occurrence of menstruation, whose plural is "hayadat" (with a fatha and a sukun).]]

4667: Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi': "three quru'," meaning three hiyad. He says: she observes the 'idda of three menstrual periods.

4668: Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, saying: Hammam ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: I heard Qatadah regarding the words of Allah: "And divorced women shall wait by themselves for three quru'," he says: "The 'idda of divorced women is three menstrual periods. Then there was abrogation (naskh) from it regarding the woman who was divorced before her husband had consummated the marriage, and those who have despaired of menstruation, those who have not menstruated, and the pregnant woman."

4669: Ali ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: al-Muharibi narrated to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, who said: "The quru' are the hiyad." [[The report 4669: In the printed edition and the manuscript it reads "Ali ibn Abd al-A'la," and see what preceded as number 4485. I fear the correct reading is "Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la," which has occurred many times before.]]

4670: Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ata' al-Khurasani, from Ibn Abbas, regarding "And divorced women shall wait by themselves for three quru'," he said: "Three hiyad."

4671: Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: Ibn Jurayj narrated to us, saying: Amr ibn Dinar said: "al-aqra' are the hiyad, from the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ)."

4672: al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from a man who heard Ikrimah, who said: "al-aqra' are the hiyad, and not the purity. Allah, exalted is He, said: 'So divorce them for their 'idda' (Qur'an 65:1), and He did not say 'for their quru''."

4673: Yahya ibn Abi Talib narrated to us, saying: Yazid informed us, saying: Juwaybir informed us, from al-Dahhak, regarding His words: "And divorced women shall wait by themselves for three quru'," both said: "three hiyad."

4674: Musa narrated to us, saying: Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding "And divorced women shall wait by themselves for three quru'": as for "three quru'," it is "three hiyad."

4675: Humayd ibn Mas'adah narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Zuray' narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Abu Ma'shar, from Ibrahim al-Nakha'i: that a case was brought before Umar, and he said to Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud: "You must give a ruling on it." He said: "You are more entitled to give a ruling!" He said: "You must." He said: "I say: her husband has more right to her as long as she has not washed from the third menstrual period." He said: "That is my opinion, and it agrees with what is in my mind!" So Umar ruled accordingly. [[The report 4675: al-Suyuti said it was narrated by Abd al-Razzaq and Abd ibn Humayd. Al-Bayhaqi narrated it in al-Sunan 7:417 at length, with different wording, through the chain "al-Thawri, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, from Alqamah: that a woman came to Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, and said..." See al-Muhalla 10:258, and it will come through other chains.]]

4676: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Abu Ma'shar, from al-Nakha'i, from Qatadah, that Umar ibn al-Khattab said to Ibn Mas'ud, and he mentioned something similar.

4677: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Abu Ma'shar, from al-Nakha'i, that Umar ibn al-Khattab and Ibn Mas'ud both said: "Her husband has more right to her as long as she has not washed," or they said: "The prayer becomes permissible for her." [[That is, until the prayer becomes permissible for her.]]

4678: Humayd ibn Mas'adah narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Zuray' narrated to us, saying: Sa'id ibn Abi Arubah narrated to us, saying: Mutar narrated to us, that al-Hasan told them: a man divorced his wife and appointed a man from his family to act on his behalf, or a person from his family. The one he had appointed neglected it until his wife entered her third menstrual period and brought near her water to wash. The one who had been appointed went to the husband, and the husband came while she was about to wash. He said: "O so-and-so!" She said: "What do you want?" He said: "I have indeed taken you back!" She said: "By Allah, you have no right to that!" He said: "Yes, by Allah!" They brought their dispute to Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, who took her oath by Allah, who there is no god but Him: "Did you indeed wash when he called you?" She said: "No, by Allah, I had not done so, and I had indeed brought near my water in order to wash." So he returned her to her husband and said: "You have more right to her as long as she has not washed from the third menstrual period."

4679: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Mutar, from al-Hasan, from Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, with something similar.

4680: Imran ibn Musa narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Warith narrated to us, saying: Yunus narrated to us, from al-Hasan, who said: Umar said: "He has more right to her as long as she has not washed from the third menstrual period."

4681: Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Walid narrated to us, saying: Abu Hilal narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Yunus ibn Jubayr: that Umar ibn al-Khattab divorced his wife, and she wanted to wash from the third menstrual period. Umar ibn al-Khattab said: "My wife, by the Lord of the Ka'bah!" and he took her back. Ibn Bashshar said: I mentioned this report to Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi, and he said: "I heard this report from Abu Hilal, from Qatadah, and Abu Hilal cannot bear this." [[The report 4681: "Abu al-Walid" is Hisham ibn Abd al-Malik al-Bahili al-Basri, Abu al-Walid al-Tayalisi, the memorizer and trustworthy authority, who was a reliable, firm, and proof-worthy man among the intelligent people. He died in the year 227 and was born in 133. "Abu Hilal" is Muhammad ibn Sulaym Abu Hilal al-Rasibi al-Basri, from whom Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated. Ahmad said: "His narration can be tolerated, except that he differs regarding Qatadah, and he is unreliable in his narrations (mudtarib al-hadith)." He died in the year 167.]]

4682: Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, from Alqamah, who said: "We were with Umar ibn al-Khattab, when a woman came and said: 'My husband divorced me once or twice, then he came back when I had put my water (for washing), had closed my door, and taken off my clothes.' Umar said to Abd Allah: 'What do you think?' He said: 'I think she is still his wife, as long as the prayer has not become permissible for her.' Umar said: 'I also think so.'" [[The report 4682: It is one of the chains of the report previously mentioned as number 4675, and likewise the reports that follow it.]]

4683: Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from al-Hakam, from Ibrahim, from al-Aswad: that he said, concerning a man who divorced his wife and then left her until she entered her third menstrual period, and she wanted to wash, and put her water for washing, and he took her back: "Umar and Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud permitted it."

4684: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Adi narrated to us, from Shu'bah, from al-Hakam, from Ibrahim, from al-Aswad, with the like of it, except that he said: "She had put the water for washing, and he took her back, so they asked Abd Allah and Umar, and he said: 'He has more right to her as long as she has not washed.'"

4685: Abu al-Sa'ib narrated to me, saying: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, who said: "Umar and Abd Allah used to say: if a man divorces his wife with a single divorce that allows him to return to her, he has more right to her as long as she has not washed from her third menstrual period."

4686: Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Mughirah informed us, from Ibrahim, that Umar ibn al-Khattab used to say: "If a man divorces his wife with one or two divorces, he has more right to taking her back, and between them is the inheritance, as long as she has not washed from the third menstrual period."

4687: Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, from Ayyub, from al-Hasan: that a man divorced his wife with one or two divorces, then appointed some of his family to act on his behalf, and the person neglected it until she entered her place of washing and brought near her washing water. He came to him and informed him, so he came and said: "I have indeed taken you back!" She said: "No, by Allah!" He said: "Yes, by Allah!" She said: "No, by Allah!" He said: "Yes, by Allah!" He said: "They disagreed, so they brought their dispute to al-Ash'ari, who made her swear by Allah: 'You had indeed washed, and the prayer has become permissible for you.'" She refused to swear, so he returned her to him. [[The report 4687: Another chain of the report previously mentioned as number 4678.]]

4688: Mujahid ibn Musa narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Abu Ma'shar, from al-Nakha'i, that Umar consulted Ibn Mas'ud about a man who divorced his wife with one or two divorces, and she menstruated for the third time. Ibn Mas'ud said: "I think he has more right to her as long as she has not washed." Umar said: "You agreed with what was in my mind." So he returned her to her husband.

4689: Humayd ibn Mas'adah narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Zuray' narrated to us, saying: al-Nu'man ibn Rashid narrated to us, from al-Zuhri, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab: that Ali used to say: "He has more right to her as long as she has not washed from the third menstrual period." [[The report 4689: "al-Nu'man ibn Rashid al-Jazari" narrated from al-Zuhri. Ahmad said: "Unreliable in his narrations; he narrated rejected (munkar) hadiths." Ibn Ma'in said: "Weak and unreliable in his narrations," and at another time he said: "Trustworthy." Al-Bukhari and Abu Hatim said: "There is much error in his narration, though he is originally truthful."]]

4690: Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Amr ibn Dinar, who said: "I heard Sa'id ibn Jubayr say: 'When the blood stops, there is no taking back.'"

4691: Abu al-Sa'ib narrated to us, saying: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, who said: "If a man divorces his wife while she is in a state of purity, she observes the 'idda of three menstrual periods apart from the menstrual period from which she became pure."

4692: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated to me, saying: Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Mutar, from Amr ibn Shu'ayb, that Umar asked Abu Musa about her, and he had heard of his ruling on it. Abu Musa said: "I ruled that her husband has more right to her as long as she has not washed."

Umar said: "If you had ruled otherwise, I would have given you a headache."

He said: "I think that he has more right to her until she washes from the third menstrual period and the prayer becomes permissible for her." He said: "I do not know that Uthman took anything other than this." [[The report 4694: Zayd ibn Rafi' al-Jazari narrated from Abu Ubaydah ibn Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, and Ma'mar narrated from him, as did Zayd ibn Abi Unaysah. 4696: al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Zayd ibn Rafi', from Ma'bad al-Juhani, who said: "If the divorced woman washes her private part from the third menstrual period, she is separated from him, and becomes lawful to other husbands." [[The report 4696: "Ma'bad al-Juhani" is said to be "Ma'bad ibn Abd Allah ibn Ukaym," and it is said to be "Ma'bad ibn Abd Allah ibn Uwaym," and it is said to be "Ma'bad ibn Khalid." 4699: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-A'la narrated to us, from Sa'id, from Durust, from al-Zuhri, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, from Ali, the like of it. Others said: rather, the qar' which Allah, exalted is His remembrance, commanded divorced women to observe as their 'idda is the purity (tuhr).

Those who said this:

4700: Abd al-Hamid ibn Bayan narrated to us, saying: Sufyan informed us, from al-Zuhri, from Amrah, from A'ishah, who said: "al-aqra' are the periods of purity (atuhar)."

4701: Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Abd Allah ibn Umar narrated to me, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Qasim, from his father, from A'ishah, the wife of the Prophet (ﷺ), that she used to say: "al-aqra' are the periods of purity."

4702: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from Amrah and Urwah, from A'ishah, who said: "When the divorced woman enters her third menstrual period, she has become separated from her husband and lawful to other husbands." Al-Zuhri said: Amrah said: "A'ishah used to say: 'The qar' is the purity, and not the menstrual period.'"

4703: al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from Abu Bakr ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Harith ibn Hisham, the like of the saying of Zayd and A'ishah.

4704: al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Ayyub, from Nafi', from Ibn Umar, the like of the saying of Zayd.

4705: al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab and Sulayman ibn Yasar: that Zayd ibn Thabit said: "When the divorced woman enters her third menstrual period, she has become separated from her husband and lawful to other husbands." Ma'mar said: "al-Zuhri used to issue fatwas according to the saying of Zayd."

4706: Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us, saying: I heard Yahya ibn Sa'id say: "It reached me that A'ishah said: 'The aqra' are only the periods of purity.'"

4707: Humayd ibn Mas'adah narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Zuray' narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, from Zayd ibn Thabit, who said: "When she enters the third menstrual period, he has no right of return to her."

4708: Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Adi and Abd al-A'la narrated to us, from Sa'id, from Qatadah, from Ibn al-Musayyab, regarding a man who divorced his wife with one or two divorces, he said: Zayd ibn Thabit said: "When she enters the third menstrual period, he has no right of return to her." Ibn Abi Adi added: "Ali ibn Abi Talib said: 'He has more right to her as long as she has not washed.'"

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 228 (part 2 of 5):

4709 - Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Ibn Abi 'Adi related to us, from Sa'id, from Qatadah, from Ibn al-Musayyib, from Zayd and 'Ali, the like of it.

4710 - Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Abu al-Zinad, from Sulayman ibn Yasar, from Zayd ibn Thabit, who said: "When she enters the third menstrual period, there is no inheritance for her."

4711 - Ya'qub related to us, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah related to us. And Muhammad ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Wahhab related to us. Both of them said together: Ayyub related to us, from Nafi', from Sulayman ibn Yasar: that al-Ahwas, a man of the nobles of the people of Syria, divorced his wife with one or two pronouncements, and he died while she was in her third menstrual period. The matter was referred to Mu'awiyah, but he had no knowledge concerning it. He asked about it Fadalah ibn 'Ubayd and those of the Companions of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) who were there, but they had no knowledge concerning it. So Mu'awiyah sent a rider to Zayd ibn Thabit, who said: "She does not inherit from him, and if she had died he would not have inherited from her." Ibn 'Umar used to hold that view. [[Report: 4711-4713 - Transmitted by al-Shafi'i in al-Umm 5: 192 by way of Malik from Nafi' and Zayd ibn Aslam from Sulayman ibn Yasar. Al-Bayhaqi also transmitted it in al-Sunan al-Kubra 7: 415 by another, abridged, route. "Al-Ahwas" is: al-Ahwas ibn Hakim ibn 'Umayr (he is 'Amr) ibn al-Aswad al-'Ansi al-Hamdani. He saw Anas, and 'Abd Allah ibn Bisr narrated from him, and his father, Tawus and others narrated from him. Al-Bukhari said: "He heard Anas." Sufyan narrated from him, and Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah narrated from him; he is truthful, his hadith is not strong. Al-Ahwas was a devout, diligent man, and he held the administration of Homs. 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hakam said: "He was a chief of police and one of the abbasid partisans." Ibn Humayd said: "al-Ahwas came to al-Rayy with al-Mahdi, and his arrival was in the year 168." He is biographed in al-Tahdhib and Tarikh Ibn 'Asakir 2: 332-333.]]

4712 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Ayyub, from Sulayman ibn Yasar: that a man called al-Ahwas, from the people of Syria, divorced his wife with one pronouncement, and he died while she had entered her third menstrual period. The matter was referred to Mu'awiyah, who did not know what to say, so he wrote concerning it to Zayd ibn Thabit, and Zayd wrote back to him: "When a divorced woman enters her third menstrual period, there is no inheritance between them."

4713 - Muhammad ibn Yahya related to us, saying: 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Ayyub, from Nafi', from Sulayman ibn Yasar, that a man called al-Ahwas, and he mentioned something similar concerning Mu'awiyah and Zayd.

4714 - Muhammad ibn Yahya related to us, saying: 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Ayyub, from Nafi', who said: Ibn 'Umar said: "When she enters the third menstrual period, he has no right of return to her."

4715 - Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Wahhab related to us, saying: 'Ubayd Allah related to us, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar that he said concerning the divorced woman: "When she enters the third menstrual period, she has become separated."

4716 - Yunus related to us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: 'Umar ibn Muhammad related to me, that Nafi' informed him, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar and Zayd ibn Thabit, that they both used to say: "When the woman enters the blood of the third menstruation, she does not inherit from him and he does not inherit from her, and she has been cleared of him and he has been cleared of her." [[Report: 4716 - 'Umar ibn Muhammad ibn Zayd ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar ibn al-Khattab related from his father and grandfather, and from his paternal uncle Salim, and from Nafi' mawla of Ibn 'Umar and others. In the manuscript his name is garbled, but it is read as it is in the printed edition, which is correct. Also in the manuscript: "she may inherit from him and he may inherit from her," and the correct reading is in the printed edition and in al-Bayhaqi's al-Sunan al-Kubra.]]

4717 - Muhammad ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Wahhab related to us, saying: Yahya ibn Sa'id related to us, saying: It reached me, from Zayd ibn Thabit, who said: "When a woman is divorced and enters the third menstrual period, there is no inheritance between them and no right of return."

4718 - Muhammad ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Wahhab related to us, saying: I heard Yahya ibn Sa'id say: I heard Salim ibn 'Abd Allah say the like of the saying of Zayd ibn Thabit.

4719 - Muhammad ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Wahhab related to us, saying: I heard Yahya say: It reached me from Aban ibn 'Uthman that he used to say that.

4720 - Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Wahhab related to us, saying: 'Ubayd Allah related to us, from Zayd ibn Thabit, the like of that. [[Report: 4720 - In the printed edition: "Muhammad ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Wahhab related to us," and I have kept what is in the manuscript, which is a slip of the pen by another copyist.]]

4721 - Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Wahb ibn Jarir related to us, saying: Shu'bah related to us, from 'Abd Rabbih ibn Sa'id, from Nafi': that Mu'awiyah sent to Zayd ibn Thabit, and Zayd wrote back to him: "When she enters the third menstrual period, she has become separated," and Ibn 'Umar used to say this.

4723 - Mujahid ibn Musa related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Hisham ibn Hassan informed us, from Qays ibn Sa'd, from Bukayr ibn 'Abd Allah ibn al-Ashajj, from Zayd ibn Thabit, who said: "If a man divorces his wife and she sees blood in the third menstruation, her waiting period has ended."

[[Report: 4725 - This isnad occurred before as no. 4699. Its biographer is "Durust," and in the printed edition here also it is "Durusb" with a ba', which is an error as we have noted. The isnad in the manuscript reads: "...related to us, 'Abd al-A'la, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, that 'A'ishah..." It omits from the isnad what is established in the printed edition, which is correct.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: "Al-quru'" in the speech of the Arabs is the plural of "qur'" [[In the printed edition: "al-qar' in the speech of the Arabs, its plural is quru'." I have kept what is in the manuscript.]], and the Arabs may pluralize it as "aqra'". It is said of its verb form: "aqra'at al-mar'ah" when she becomes one who has menstruation and purity, so she "tuqri'" iqra'. The root of "al-qur'" in the speech of the Arabs is: the time for the arrival of a thing customarily arriving at a known time, and the departure of a thing customarily departing at a known time. For this reason the Arabs said: "The need of so-and-so has drawn near to me," meaning its fulfilment has drawn near and the time of its fulfilment has come [[In the printed edition: "and the time of its fulfilment has arrived." I have kept what is in the manuscript.]]; "al-najm qara'a" when the time of its setting came; and "aqra'a" when the time of its rising came, as the poet said:

When al-Thurayya has aqra'at, the sky perceives its setting.

[[I have not found this verse, and it is probably tied to a verse following it, so I have left its explanation until I find its full meaning.]]

It is also said: "aqra'at al-rih" when the wind blew at its time, as al-Hudhali said: [[He is Malik ibn al-Harith, of Banu Kahil ibn al-Harith ibn Tamim ibn Sa'd ibn Hudhayl.]]

I hated al-'Aqr, the 'Aqr of Banu Shulayl,
when the winds blow for its reciter.

[[Diwan al-Hudhaliyyin 3: 83. "Sha'a" (shay' yashna'uhu) means he disliked it. Al-'Aqr is a place name, and the Khalil to whom it is attributed is the grandfather of Jarir ibn 'Abd Allah al-Bajali.]]

meaning: it blew at its time and its moment of blowing. For this reason some Arabs named the time of the arrival of menstruation "qur'," since it is blood which customarily appears from the woman's private part at a time and hides at another, so they called the time of its arrival "qur'," just as those who named the time of the arrival of the wind at its time "qur'" did.

4726 - For this reason the Prophet (ﷺ) said to Fatimah bint Abi Hubaysh: "Leave off prayer during your days of qur'" [[Report: 4726 - He related it without an isnad. The hadith of Fatimah bint Abi Hubaysh is established by several routes. Ibn Kathir in his Tafsir 1: 534 mentioned this hadith and said: "Abu Dawud and al-Nasa'i transmitted it by way of al-Mundhir ibn al-Mughirah, from 'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, from Fatimah bint Abi Hubaysh, that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said to her: 'Leave off prayer during your days of qur'.'" Then he said: "But this al-Mundhir is unknown, not well known, and Ibn Hibban mentioned him among the trustworthy." Ibn Abi Hatim likewise said in al-Jarh wa al-Ta'dil 4/1/242. See Sunan Abi Dawud 1: 114-117 for details of this. See also al-Bukhari (Fath al-Bari 1: 348 and following, chapters on menstruation) and Muslim 4: 16-21. Fatimah bint Abi Hubaysh ibn al-Muttalib ibn Asad ibn 'Abd al-'Uzza ibn Qusayy, the Qurashi.]]

meaning: "Leave off prayer during the days of the arrival of your menstruation."

Others among the Arabs named the time of the arrival of purity "qur'," since the time of its arrival is a time for the departure of the blood of menstruation, and the arrival of purity, customarily arriving at a known time. Maymun ibn Qays al-A'sha said concerning this:

Every year you are the one who undertakes a raid,
which strains to its farthest point the resolve of your endurance.

[[His Diwan: 67, Majaz al-Qur'an of Abu 'Ubaydah 1: 74, and others besides. He praises Hawdhah ibn 'Ali al-Hanafi, and in it he mentions some of Hawdhah's virtues and noble deeds. "Jasham al-amr" (yajshimuhu jathman wa jashamatan): he undertook it with effort and hardship. "Rakaba ajsamahu" and "al-'azim," "al-'azimah," and "al-'azm": determination and firm resolve upon a matter that you will do. "Al-'aza'": good patience in the face of the loss of what a person loses. He says to Hawdhah: how many a good pleasure the soul has been patient to forgo in the cause of establishing your kingdom through continuous raiding, year after year.]]

*mu'arrithatin malan wa fi al-dhikri rif'atan* [making wealth an inheritance, and in remembrance an elevation]
*li-ma da'a fihā min quruʾi nisā'ika* [for what was lost in it of the qurū' of your women]

[[Its qualifier: "mu'arrithah" is an adjective of "ghazwah" (raid). He says: you consoled yourself for every comfort, so you forsook your women in the time of their purity, did not approach them, and preferred the raid over them; so your raids were a source of wealth, an elevation in renown, and a distance in reputation.]]

So he made "al-qur'" the time of purity.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: Given what we have described of the meaning of "al-qur'," the saying of God, "And the divorced women shall wait by themselves for three qurū'," became unclear to the people of interpretation.

Some of them held that what the divorced woman with menstrual periods was commanded to observe was menstrual periods, which is the time of their arrival at their customary time; so they made it obligatory for her to wait three menstrual cycles on her own, away from the proposals of husbands.

* *

Others held that what she was commanded was purity periods, which is the time of their arrival at their customary time; so they made it obligatory for her to wait three periods of purity.

* *

Since the meaning of "al-qur'" is as we have described, for the reasons we have shown, and since God, exalted is His remembrance, commanded the man who wishes to divorce his wife not to divorce her except in a state of purity in which he has not had intercourse with her, and forbade him to divorce her while she is menstruating, it follows that the divorced woman who has been consummated, if she has menstrual periods, must wait a fixed period by herself after her husband's divorce, namely to observe three qurū', between the two purities of each qur' there being a qur', which is different from what she reckoned as the qurū' she waits through. [[In the manuscript and printed edition: "and it is different." The correct reading omits the waw of coordination, meaning: this qur' between the two purities is different from what she reckoned as the qurū' she waits through. This is because the word "qur'" is shared in meaning between menstruation and purity. In the manuscript and printed edition: "then she waits," which is a corruption; the correct reading is what I have given. This meaning will become clear in what follows.]] When they have passed, she is lawful to the husbands and her waiting period has ended. For when she does this, she has entered the category of divorced women who wait by themselves three qurū', between the two purities of each qur' there being a different qur'. When she does this, she is fulfilling what her Lord, exalted is His remembrance, obligated her to by the apparent sense of the revelation.

It is therefore clear, since the matter is as we have described, that the third qur' of hers, by what we have explained, is the third purity; and that with its ending and the arrival of the menstrual qur' that follows it, her waiting period ends.

* *

If someone of dullness [[In the printed edition: "dhu ghabawah." I have kept what is in the manuscript.]] supposes that, since we call the time of the arrival of purity "qur'" and the time of the arrival of menstruation "qur'," it is necessary for us to make a woman's waiting period end with the ending of the second purity, since the purity in which he divorced her, and the menstruation that follows it, and the purity that follows that, are all "qurū'" [[That is: the purity of divorce is a qur', the menstruation is a qur', and the second purity is a qur'; so they are three qurū' that the divorced woman waits through.]], then he has supposed in ignorance.

This is because the ruling, in our view, concerning everything God has sent down in His Book, is according to what the apparent sense of the revelation allows, unless God, exalted is His remembrance, makes clear to His servants that His intended meaning is a specific one, either by revelation in His Book or on the tongue of His Messenger (ﷺ). When part of it is specified, what has been specified from it is not included in the general statement by which the ruling was made obligatory, and the rest remains on its generality, as we have already explained in our book: *Kitab latif al-qawl min al-bayan 'an usul al-ahkam* [The Book of Subtle Speech on the Explanation of the Foundations of Rulings] and our other books.

So the "aqra'" which are menstrual periods, between the two purities of the periods of purity, are not counted among the qurū' of the woman who waits by herself after divorce, by the consensus of all the people of Islam: that the "qurū'" which God obligated her to wait through, three qurū', between each qur' of them there are periods whose meanings differ from the qurū' she waits through. Since they are, in our view, entitled to the name "aqra'," the consensus of all holds that she may wait only as we described before.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: In this verse there is clear evidence against the view of those who said: "The wife of one who has sworn abstinence (mu'li), from whom he swore, becomes lawful to the husbands upon the passing of the four months, if she has menstruated three menstrual periods within the four months." For God, exalted is His remembrance, only made the waiting period obligatory for her after the mu'li's resolve to divorce her and the actual pronouncement of divorce upon her, by His saying: "And if they resolve upon divorce, then God is All-Hearing, All-Knowing. And the divorced women shall wait by themselves for three qurū'." He made it obligatory, exalted is His remembrance, upon the woman, when she becomes divorced, to wait three qurū'. It is known that she was not divorced on the day her husband swore abstinence from her, since there is consensus that the oath of abstinence is not a divorce that makes the one who swore subject to a waiting period.

Since that is so, the waiting period is obligatory for her only after divorce, and divorce applies to her only in the manner we have explained before.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: As for the meaning of His words "wa-l-mutallaqat" (and divorced women), it means: those who are left free to go (al-mukhallayat al-sabil), not prevented by husbands and not being proposed to. The saying of the speaker, "So-and-so is divorced (mutallaqah)," is only a "mufa"alah" form from the speaker's saying, "The man divorced (tallaqa) his wife, so she is divorced (mutallaqah)." As for their saying, "She is divorced (taliq)," it comes from their saying, "Her husband divorced her (tallaqaha), so she became divorced (talaqat), and she divorces (tatlaqu) a divorce (talaqan), and she is divorced (taliq)." It has been related that some of the Arab tribes say, "The woman divorced (talaqat)." ["Talaq" here with a fatha on the ta' and lam, whereas the one before it has a fatha on the ta' and a damma on the lam, like "karum."] It is only said of her when her husband lets her go, just as a she-goat left unattended, without a shepherd or a keeper, when it goes out alone from its people to graze, left free to go, is called "hiya taliq." So the woman left free to go is likened to it, and she was named with what the she-goat we have described was named. As for their saying, "The woman was divorced (tulliqat)," it has a different meaning and is said of her when she has given birth (nufisat). [Nufisat (with damma then kasra) and nafisat (with fatha then kasra): she gave birth, so she is nafsa'. Al-talq: the labour pains at childbirth, the verb of which is in the passive with damma on the ta' and kasra on the lam.] This is from "al-talq" (labour pangs), while the first is from "al-talaq" (divorce).

* *

It has been shown that "al-tarabbus" (waiting) is only refraining from marriage and restraining oneself from it, in other places. [See what preceded regarding the meaning of "tarabbus" in this part 4: 456.]

* *

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And it is not lawful for them to conceal what Allah has created in their wombs, if they believe in Allah and the Last Day﴾

The people of interpretation differed regarding its interpretation:

Some of them said: its interpretation is: "And it is not lawful," for them, meaning for the divorced women, "to conceal what Allah has created in their wombs," of menstruation when they are divorced. It is forbidden for them to conceal from their husbands who divorced them, in the divorce in which the husbands have the right of return, seeking by that to nullify their rights of return over them. [In the manuscript: "haqquhunna" (their rights), and the correct reading is what is in the printed edition.]

Those who said this:

4727 - Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abu Salih told us, he said: al-Layth told me, from Yunus, from Ibn Shihab, he said: Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, said: "And divorced women shall wait by themselves for three periods" up to His words "and men have a degree over them, and Allah is Mighty, Wise." He said: It has reached us that "what He created in their wombs" is the pregnancy, and it has reached us that it is the menstrual period. So it is not lawful for them to conceal that, so that the waiting period may end and he does not possess the right of return if he has it.

4728 - Ibn Bashshar told us, he said: Yahya ibn Sa'id told us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Ibrahim: "And it is not lawful for them to conceal what Allah has created in their wombs." He said: the menstruation.

4729 - Muhammad ibn Bashshar told us, he said: Abu Ahmad told us, he said: Sufyan told us, from Mansur, from Ibrahim: "And it is not lawful for them to conceal what Allah has created in their wombs." He said: the greatest part of that is menstruation. [Report 4729: in al-Durr al-Manthur 1: 276 with its wording here, then he said: "And in another wording: the most of what is meant by it is menstruation," and it will come likewise under no. 4733. But the manuscript differs from all of them: in it, "if that menstruation increases," and all are close in meaning, some to others.]

4730 - Abu Kurayb told us, he said: Ibn Idris told us, he said: I heard Mutarrif, from al-Hakam, he said: Ibrahim said regarding His words: "And it is not lawful for them to conceal what Allah has created in their wombs," he said: the menstruation.

4731 - Ya'qub told me, he said: Ibn 'Ulayyah told us, he said: Khalid al-Hadhdha' told us, from Ikrimah regarding His words: "And it is not lawful for them to conceal what Allah has created in their wombs," he said: the menstruation. Then Khalid said: the blood.

* *

Others said: it is menstruation, except that what Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, forbade her to conceal regarding what He created in her womb is that she tells her divorcing husband, when he wants to take her back before the third menstruation: "I have had the third menstruation," lying, so as to nullify his right by her false saying in that.

Those who said this:

4732 - Ibn Humayd told us, he said: Jarir told us, from 'Ubaydah ibn Mu'tib, from Ibrahim regarding His words: "And it is not lawful for them to conceal what Allah has created in their wombs," he said: the menstruation. The woman observes two periods, then her husband wants to take her back, so she says: "I have had the third." [Report 4732: in the manuscript "'Abdah ibn Mughayyib" (unpointed), and in the printed edition "ibn Mughayth," an error. 'Ubaydah ibn Mu'tib al-Dabbi related from Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, al-Sha'bi, Asim ibn Bahdalah and others. Related from him Shu'bah, al-Thawri, Waki', Hushaym, Ali ibn Mushir and others. He had poor memory, was blind, and his narrations are abandoned. Ibn Hibban said: "He became confused in his later years, so reliance on him is invalid."]

4733 - Ibn Humayd told us, he said: Jarir told us, from Mansur, from Ibrahim: "And it is not lawful for them to conceal what Allah has created in their wombs," he said: The greatest part of what is meant is menstruation. [Report 4733: see the comment on the preceding report no. 4729.]

* *

Others said: rather, what they were forbidden to conceal from their divorcing husbands is both pregnancy and menstruation.

Those who said this:

4734 - Humayd ibn Mas'adah told us, he said: Yazid ibn Zurai' told us, he said: al-Ash'ath told us, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar: "And it is not lawful for them to conceal what Allah has created in their wombs," from menstruation and pregnancy. It is not lawful for her, if she is menstruating, to conceal her menstruation, and it is not lawful for her, if she is pregnant, to conceal her pregnancy.

4735 - Abu Kurayb told us, he said: Ibn Idris told us, he said: I heard Mutarrif, from al-Hakam, from Mujahid regarding His words: "And it is not lawful for them to conceal what Allah has created in their wombs," he said: the pregnancy and the menstruation. Abu Kurayb said: Ibn Idris said: this was the first hadith I heard from Mutarrif.

4736 - Abu al-Sa'ib told me, he said: Ibn Idris told us, from Mutarrif, from al-Hakam, from Mujahid, the like of it, except that he said: the pregnancy.

4737 - Isma'il ibn Musa al-Fazari told us, he said: Abu Ishaq al-Fazari told us, from Layth, from Mujahid regarding His words: "And it is not lawful for them to conceal what Allah has created in their wombs," he said: of the menstruation and the child.

4738 - Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Muslim ibn Khalid al-Zanji informed me, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "And it is not lawful for them to conceal what Allah has created in their wombs," he said: of the menstruation and the child.

4739 - Muhammad ibn 'Amr told me, he said: Abu 'Asim told us, from 'Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding the saying of Allah, may His remembrance be exalted: "And it is not lawful for them to conceal what Allah has created in their wombs," he said: It is not lawful for the divorced woman to say, "I am menstruating," when she is not menstruating; nor to say, "I am pregnant," when she is not pregnant; nor to say, "I am not pregnant," when she is pregnant.

4740 - Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said: Shibl told us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

4741 - Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Suwayd ibn Nasr told us, he said: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from al-Hajjaj, from Mujahid, he said: the menstruation and the pregnancy. He said: its explanation is that she should not say, "I am menstruating," when she is not menstruating, "nor am I not menstruating," when she is menstruating; nor "I am pregnant," when she is not pregnant, nor "I am not pregnant," when she is pregnant.

4742 - Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Suwayd told us, he said: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from al-Hajjaj, from al-Qasim ibn Nafi', from Mujahid, similar to this explanation regarding this verse. [Report 4742: "al-Qasim ibn Nafi' ibn Abi Bazzah," who is al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazzah. He related from Abu al-Tufayl, Abu Ma'bad, Mujahid and Sa'id ibn Jubayr. Related from him 'Amr ibn Dinar, 'Abd al-Malik ibn Abi Sulayman, Ibn Jurayj, Ibn Abi Layla and Hajjaj ibn Artah. Biography in al-Jarh wa-l-Ta'dil 3/2/122.]

4743 - Ibn Humayd told us, he said: Jarir told us, from Layth, from Mujahid, the like of it, and he added in it: He said: all of that is in the woman's hatred of her husband and her love of him.

4744 - It was related to me from 'Ammar, he said: Ibn Abi Ja'far told us, from his father, from al-Rabi' regarding His words: "And it is not lawful for them to conceal what Allah has created in their wombs," he says: It is not lawful for them to conceal what Allah has created in their wombs, of menstruation and pregnancy. It is not lawful for her to say, "I have menstruated," when she has not menstruated; nor is it lawful for her to say, "I have not menstruated," when she has menstruated; nor is it lawful for her to say, "I am pregnant," when she is not pregnant; nor to say, "I am not pregnant," when she is pregnant.

4745 - Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words: "And it is not lawful for them to conceal what Allah has created in their wombs," the verse: He said: they should not conceal the menstruation nor the child, and it is not lawful for her to conceal it while he does not know when she becomes lawful, so that he does not take her back, causing her harm (tudarruhu).

4746 - Yahya ibn Abi Talib told me, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Juwaybir informed us, from al-Dahhak regarding His words: "And it is not lawful for them to conceal what Allah has created in their wombs," meaning the child, he said: The menstruation and the child are what women were entrusted with.

* *

Others said: rather, by it is meant pregnancy.

Then those who said this differed regarding the reason for which they were forbidden to conceal that from the man. [His words "the man" are in the accusative by the verbal noun, which is his words "concealing that," as the object.] Some of them said: they were forbidden from that so that she does not nullify the husband's right of return, if he wants to take her back before she gives birth and her pregnancy ends.

Those who said this:

4747 - Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Suwayd ibn Nasr told us, he said: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Qabath ibn Razin, from Ali ibn Rabah, that he told him: that 'Umar ibn al-Khattab said to a man: Recite this verse. So he recited it. He said: So-and-so is among those who conceal what Allah has created in their wombs. She had been divorced while pregnant, and she concealed it until she gave birth. [Report 4747: Qabath ibn Razin ibn Humayd ibn Salih al-Lakhmi Abu Hashim al-Misri related from his paternal uncle Salamah, Ali ibn Rabah, and Ikrimah; related from him Ibn al-Mubarak, Ibn Lahi'ah and Ibn Wahb. Ibn Hibban mentioned him among the reliable (al-thiqat). Abu Hatim said: there is no harm in his narration. A story about him is mentioned in al-Tahdhib: that the Roman emperor ordered him to debate the patriarch... Ibn Hajar said: a similar story happened to the judge Abu Bakr al-Baqillani when he was sent with a message to the Roman king... Qabath died in the year 156. And Ali ibn Rabah ibn Quseir al-Lakhmi related from 'Amr ibn al-'As, Saraqah ibn Malik, Mu'awiyah ibn Abi Sufyan, Abu Qatadah al-Ansari, Abu Hurayrah and others of the Companions. He visited Mu'awiyah, and Ibn Sa'd mentioned him in the second class of the people of Egypt, and said: he was trustworthy. He campaigned in Ifriqiyah and lost his eye on the day of Dhat al-Sawari at sea with Ibn Abi Sarh in the year 34 AH. He was born in the tenth year of the Hijrah and died in the year 114.]

4748 - Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abdullah ibn Salih told us, he said: Mu'awiyah ibn Salih told me, from Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn 'Abbas, he said: If a man divorces his wife once or twice while she is pregnant, he has more right to take her back as long as she has not given birth, and this is His words: "And it is not lawful for them to conceal what Allah has created in their wombs, if they believe in Allah and the Last Day."

4749 - Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Suwayd told us, he said: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Yahya ibn Bishr, that he heard Ikrimah say: Divorce is twice, with a return between them; if it occurs to him to divorce her after these two, she is a third; and if he divorces her three times, she has become forbidden to him until she marries another husband. The ones mentioned in the Qur'an are only: "And it is not lawful for them to conceal what Allah has created in their wombs, if they believe in Allah and the Last Day, and their husbands have more right to take them back," are those who were divorced once or twice, then concealed their pregnancy in order to escape from their husband. As for when he has pronounced the three divorces, he has no right of return over her until she marries another husband. [Report 4749: Yahya ibn Bishr al-Khurasani; his biography was given under report 4549.]

* *

Others said: the reason for which they were forbidden to conceal that is that in the Jahiliyyah they used to conceal it from their husbands, fearing their taking them back, until they married others, so that the lineage of the pregnancy, which is from the divorcing husband, would be attributed to the one she married. So Allah forbade them that.

Those who said this:

4750 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh told us, he said: Suwayd told us, he said: Sa'id told us, from Qatadah regarding His saying: "And it is not lawful for them to conceal what Allah has created in their wombs," he said: When a woman was divorced, she would conceal what was in her belly and her pregnancy, in order to attribute the child to other than its father; so Allah disliked that for them.

4751 - Muhammad ibn Yahya told me, he said: Abd al-A'la told us, he said: Sa'id told us, from Qatadah: "And it is not lawful for them to conceal what Allah has created in their wombs," he said: Allah knew that among them were concealers who would hide the child. And the people of the Jahiliyyah, a man would divorce his wife while she was pregnant, [His words "And the people of the Jahiliyyah, a man..." are good, eloquent Arabic, not an error; the omission of the predicate of kana is preferable because what follows suffices. See a similar case below in report 4781, also from Qatadah with this chain.] so she would conceal the child and take it to another, and she would conceal out of fear of the return, so Allah forbade that and decreed concerning it. [Report 4751: this chain has passed many times, and was repeated in nos. 4676, 4677, 4679, 4692, 4713, 4714, 4725 and others. The narrators must be identified: "Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Abi Hazm al-Qatta'i," Abu 'Abd Allah al-Basri, related from his paternal uncle Hazm ibn Mihran, Abd al-A'la ibn Abd al-A'la, Abd al-Samad ibn Abd al-Warith and others. Related from him Muslim, Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi and al-Bukhari outside the Jami'. Abu Hatim said: he is salih al-hadith, truthful. He died in 253. And "Abd al-A'la ibn Abd al-A'la ibn Muhammad al-Qurashi al-Sami al-Basri," called Abu Hammam, and he was angered by it; he related from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, Sa'id al-Jurayri, Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah, Humayd al-Tawil, Khalid al-Hadhdha' and others. Related from him Ishaq ibn Rahawayh, Ali ibn al-Madini, Muhammad ibn Bashshar Bundar, Nasr ibn al-Jahdami and others. Ibn Ma'in said: reliable. He was skilled in hadith, a Qadari but not one who called to it. He died in 198.
"And His saying: 'and decreed concerning it'," meaning He commanded in it what He commanded.]

4752 - Al-Hasan ibn Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, he said: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah: "And it is not lawful for them to conceal what Allah has created in their wombs," he said: The woman would conceal her pregnancy until she attributed it to another man.

* *

Others said: rather, the reason for which they were forbidden to conceal that is that when a man wanted to divorce his wife, he would ask her whether she had a pregnancy, so that he would not divorce her, while she was pregnant by him, due to the harm that would befall him and his child in separating from her if he divorced her. So they were commanded to be truthful in that and forbidden to lie.

Those who said this:

4753 - Musa told me, he said: Asbat told us, from al-Suddi: [Report 4753: in the printed edition and manuscript: "Musa told me, he said: Asbat told us" with the omission of "he said: Amr told us," which is a clear error. It is a chain that circulates repeatedly in tafsir; the closest is no. 4674.] "And it is not lawful for them to conceal what Allah has created in their wombs," so the man wants to divorce his wife, and he asks her: Do you have a pregnancy? So she conceals it, intending that he separate from her, and he divorces her while she has concealed it until she gives birth. And when he learns of that, she is returned to him as punishment for what she concealed, and her husband has more right to take her back, humiliated.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most preferable of these sayings as the interpretation of the verse is the saying of the one who said: what the divorced woman was forbidden to conceal from her husband who divorced her once or twice, of what Allah created in her womb, is the menstruation and the pregnancy. Because there is no disagreement among all that the waiting period ends by the giving birth to the child that Allah created in her womb, just as it ends by the blood when she sees it after the third purity, according to the one who says "qur'" means purity, and according to the one who says it means menstruation, when it ceases from the third menstruation, and she purifies herself by ritual bathing. [In the printed edition: "tatahharat lil-ightisal," which is grossly erroneous; the correct reading is from the manuscript.]

So when that is the case, and God, dhikruhu, forbade them only to conceal what the divorcing husband, whose situation we have described, is entitled to, namely his right of return (ruju') that God gave him over them after the divorce until their waiting period (iddah) ends. [[Regarding his words "ما يكون بكتمانهن..": the clause is an object in the accusative governed by the verbal noun "kitman" (concealment). "Butul" (lapsing) is a verbal noun from "batala al-shay' yabtulu butulan wa-butlanan". This was discussed earlier at 2:426, then 3:205, note 6, and in this part, 4:146.]] That right lapses when they give birth to what is in their wombs, if they are pregnant, and when the three menstrual periods end, if they are not pregnant. [[Regarding his words "علم" (he knew): this is the answer to his earlier words "وإذ كان ذلك كذلك..", and the clauses between them are coordinated with one another.]] It is known that they are forbidden to conceal from their husbands, each of whom has divorced them, what is in the wombs, that is, the menstruation and pregnancy, in the same way as they are forbidden the other. Nor is there any sense in singling out one of the two, claiming that the verse means only one of them and not the other, since both are among what God created in their wombs, and each of them involves the lapsing of the husband's right by its reaching a fixed end, just as the other does.

Whoever singles out one of the two meanings, and makes the verse refer only to it, should be asked for proof of the soundness of his claim, from a principle or argument that must be accepted. Then his own position should be reversed on him: whatever he says about one of them, he will be obliged to say the same about the other.

* *

As for what al-Suddi said, [[This is the report mentioned earlier, no. 4753.]] that the verse refers to the prohibition on women concealing their pregnancy from their husbands when the men intend to divorce them, this is a view that contradicts the apparent meaning of the revelation. God, dhikruhu, said: ﴿The divorced women shall wait by themselves for three periods﴾ and ﴿it is not lawful for them to conceal what God has created in their wombs﴾, meaning: it is not lawful for them to conceal what God has created in their wombs of the three periods, if they believe in God and the Last Day.

This is because God, dhikruhu, mentioned the prohibition of that for them after describing them in the way He described them, namely separating from their husbands by divorce, and informing them of the waiting period that is incumbent on them, thereby making clear to them what is forbidden and permitted to them, and what their waiting period requires and what is obligatory for them during it. Among what He informed them of was that it is obligatory for them not to conceal from their husbands their menstruation and pregnancy, which occurs by the delivery of this or the end of that at a specified limit, by which the rights of their husbands would lapse, out of harm they intend to inflict on them. So His prohibition of what He forbade them from that is more fitting to be a description of what precedes and follows it, than to be a description of something for which no mention has preceded.

* *

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: If someone says, "What is the meaning of His words, ﴿if they believe in God and the Last Day﴾? Is it lawful for them to conceal that from their husbands if they do not believe in God and the Last Day, so that the prohibition is restricted to believing women in God and the Last Day?"

It is said: The meaning of that is other than what you have taken it to be. Its meaning is that the concealment by a divorced woman of what God created in her womb, of menstruation and child, during the days of her waiting period after her husband's divorce, is done out of harm to him, [[Regarding his words "زوجها المطلقها": "zawjaha" is in the accusative as the object of the verbal noun "kitman", and "al-mutallaqaha" is in the accusative as an adjective of "zawjaha". The "ha" and "alif" are the object of the active participle "al-mutallaq", as mentioned in the previous note.]] and is not the act or manner of one who believes in God and the Last Day. It is the act and manner of women who do not believe in God and the Last Day, the unbelieving women. So do not adopt their manners, O believing women, for that is not lawful for you if you believe in God and the Last Day and are Muslim women.
