[[Regarding his words "لا أن المؤمنات...": this follows from the context of the first sentence: "...and its meaning is that the concealment by a divorced woman... not that the believing women..."]] It is not that believing women are the only ones singled out for the prohibition of that, to the exclusion of unbelieving women. Rather, it is obligatory on every woman upon whom God's obligations fall, who has periods, if she is divorced after consummation during her waiting period, not to conceal from her husband what God created in her womb of menstruation and pregnancy.

* *

On the interpretation of His words, the Exalted: ﴿And their husbands have more right to take them back in that [period], if they desire reconciliation﴾

Abu Ja'far said: "Al-bu'ulah" is the plural of "ba'l", which is the husband of a woman. From this is the verse of Jarir:

"Prepare with the perfume (al-hilyi) the saffron-scent, for Jarir is your husband and you are his wives."

[[His Diwan: 482. Also al-Naqa'id: 650, and Tabaqat Fuhul al-Shu'ara': 347. It is from a famous naqidah (poetic exchange). The matter concerned al-Hajjaj telling the two poets: "Come to me in the clothes of your fathers in pre-Islamic times." Al-Farazdaq came wearing silk brocade and sat in a tent. Jarir consulted the shrewd men of his tribe, Banu Yarbu', and they said: "The clothing of our fathers is nothing but iron!" So Jarir put on a coat of mail, girded on a sword, took a spear, mounted a horse, and came with forty horsemen from his tribe. When he saw al-Farazdaq, he said: "I have put on my weapons, while al-Farazdaq is a plaything for him, with a wide belt of kurj and its bells..." "Prepare with the perfume..." The "kurj" is a puppet-shadow figure that effeminate men play with, as I think, like a shadow puppet. The "jalajil" are bells. It is also narrated as "Prepare with the silk," which is silk. The "mallab" is a perfume of saffron with which a bride perfumes herself in her adornment. "Halaʼil" is the plural of "halilah", meaning wife. And how greatly Jarir mocked his cousin!]]

"Al-bu'ulah" may also be pluralized as "al-bu'ul" and "al-bu'ulah", just as "al-fahl" is pluralized as "al-fuhul" and "al-fuhulah", and "al-dhakar" as "al-dhukur" and "al-dhukurah". Likewise, plurals of the pattern "fu'ul", the Arabs often add the "ha'" to them. As for those of the pattern "fi'al", the addition of "ha'" to them in their speech is rare, though it is reported from them: "al-'izam" and "al-'izamah" (bones). From this is the saying of the admonisher: [[I do not know who said it.]]

"Then you buried the dung and the bones."

[[Al-Jamharah: 3:121, and Lisan al-'Arab under (ʿaẓm) and (hdhm). The verse differs from al-Tabari's version, which is:

"Woe to the dung of Abu Na'amah from you and from your sharp knife, the al-Hadhdhamah. When you kneel down and dig a pit, then you scatter the dung and the bones."

The first line in Lisan (hdhm) reads "Bani Na'amah", and in al-Jamharah "Bani Thamamah". The last line in al-Jamharah reads: "then you ate the meat and the bones." His words "al-hadhdhamah": "tahadhdhama al-lahm" means he hastens in cutting it. "Ibtarak" means he squatted and placed his chest on the ground. I think he is describing a lion or a wolf.]]

It has also been said: "al-hijarah" and "al-hijar" (stones), "al-mihārah" and "al-mihār" (female camel-drivers?), and "al-dhikkārah" and "al-dhikkār", for males.

* *

As for the interpretation of the speech, it is: And the husbands of the divorced women, those for whom We have obligated that they wait by themselves three periods, and forbade them to conceal what God has created in their wombs, have more right and priority to take them back to themselves [[In the manuscript: "ilā anfusihin" (to themselves, masc.), which is a mistake in meaning.]] during the time of their waiting, the three periods and the days of pregnancy, and to resume them into their bonds [[In the manuscript: "ilā ḥabālihin" (to their bonds, fem.), which is also a mistake in meaning. "Al-hibal" is the plural of "habl", meaning ties, bonds, and also covenant. He means by it their retention, which derives from "al-habl", the rope that binds.]] more than they have over themselves, to prevent them from themselves from that. [[In the manuscript and the printed edition: "an yamna'hunna" (to prevent them), which is a third mistake in meaning. The correct reading is what I have adopted. His words "minhunna bi-anfusihinna..." follow the context: "ahaqqu wa-awla bi-raddihinna... minhunna bi-anfusihinna..."]] As the following narrations report:

4754: Al-Muthanna told us, saying: ʿAbdullah ibn Salih told us, saying: Mu'awiyah told me, from ʿAli ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His words: "And their husbands have more right to take them back in that [period], if they desire reconciliation." He said: If a man divorces his wife with one or two divorces, and she is pregnant, he has more right to take her back as long as she has not given birth.

4755: Ibn Bashshar told us, saying: Yahya ibn Sa'id told us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Ibrahim: "And their husbands have more right to take them back." He said: during the waiting period.

4756: Ibn Humayd told us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih told us, saying: al-Husayn ibn Waqid told us, from Yazid al-Nahwi, from ʿIkrimah and al-Hasan al-Basri, who said: God, dhikruhu, said: "The divorced women shall wait by themselves three periods, and it is not lawful for them to conceal what God has created in their wombs, if they believe in God and the Last Day. And their husbands have more right to take them back in that [period], if they desire reconciliation." That was because when a man divorced his wife, he had more right to take her back even if it was three divorces. So this was abrogated, and He said: ﴿The divorce is twice﴾ and the rest of the verse.

4757: Muhammad ibn ʿAmr told us, saying: Abu ʿAsim told us, saying: ʿIsa told us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding His words: "And their husbands have more right to take them back in that," during their waiting period. [[Narration 4757: in the manuscript and printed edition, "Musa ibn ʿAmr" is a clear error; the correct is "Muhammad ibn ʿAmr". This isnad recurs frequently in the tafsir, the nearest instance being no. 4739.]]

4758: Al-Muthanna told us, saying: Abu Hudhayfah told us, saying: Shibl told us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, similarly.

4759: Ibn Wakiʿ told us, saying: my father told us, from Sufyan, from Layth, from Mujahid, who said: during the waiting period.

4760: Bishr ibn Mu'adh told us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatadah regarding His words: "And their husbands have more right to take them back in that," meaning: during the three periods, which are menstrual periods, or three months, or if she was pregnant. If her husband divorces her with one or two divorces, he may take her back as long as she is within her waiting period, if he wishes. [[In the printed edition: "fi al-qurū' al-thalāth ḥayḍ" (the three periods are menstruations) with the second "fi" omitted.]]

4761: Al-Hasan ibn Yahya told us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah regarding His words: "And their husbands have more right to take them back in that." He said: A woman used to conceal her pregnancy until she attributed it to another man. [[Meaning in the pre-Islamic period, as mentioned in the earlier narrations.]] So God forbade them from that and said: "And their husbands have more right to take them back in that." Qatadah said: More right to take them back during the waiting period.

4762: It was reported to me from ʿAmmar, who said: Ibn Abi Ja'far told us, from his father, from al-Rabi' regarding His words: "And their husbands have more right to take them back in that," meaning: during the waiting period, as long as he has not divorced her three times.

4763: Musa told me, saying: ʿAmr told me, saying: Asbat told us, from al-Suddi: "And their husbands have more right to take them back in that," meaning: more right to take her back in humiliation, as punishment for her having concealed her pregnancy from her husband. [[Narration 4763: see the earlier narration no. 4753.]]

4764: Yunus told me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words: "And their husbands have more right to take them back," more right to take them back, as long as the waiting period has not ended.

4765: Yahya ibn Abi Talib told me, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Juwaybir informed us, from al-Dahhak: "And their husbands have more right to take them back in that," he said: whatever is in the waiting period if he wishes to resume.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: If someone asks us: [[In the manuscript: "fa-ma li-zawjin wāḥidah" with the word "ṭalliqa" dropped by the copyist between the two words.]] Then what right does a husband who divorced his wife once or twice after consummation have to take her back during her three periods, unless he intends by taking her back to reform her affairs and his?

It is said: As for what lies between him and God, it is not lawful if he intends to harm her by taking her back, not to reform her affairs and his, that he resume her. [[In the printed edition: "bi-murājaʿatihā" (by resuming her), which is grossly wrong. The context is: "...fa-ghayr jā'iz... murājaʿatuhā" with an intervening segment, as is Abu Ja'far's habit.]]

As for legal judgment, he is ruled to have the right to take her back, just as we have ruled that his return to her lapses if she concealed from him her pregnancy created by God in her womb, or her menstruation, until her waiting period ended, out of harm she intended to him. God has forbidden her to conceal that from him, so in the ruling it is equal: in the lapsing of her husband's right of return over her, and she has sinned by concealing from him what she concealed until her waiting period ended, she and the one who obeyed God by not concealing that from him, even though they differ in obeying or disobeying God in that. Likewise the husband who takes back his wife after one or two divorces after consummation, when both are free, [[His words "and both are free": because a slave's divorce is two, after which he becomes unlawful to her, unlike a free man's three.]] and even if he intends to harm her by taking her back, he is ruled to have the right of return, although he is sinful in his intention, [[In the manuscript: "āthiman bi-rabbih" (sinful with his Lord), not dotted, appearing to read "bi-rabbih", but I found no lexicographic record of "athima bi-rabbih", though I fear it might be correct in a way I have not verified. In the printed edition: "bi-ra'yih" (in his opinion), as they found it objectionable and assumed a misreading, so they read it that way. The best reading, I think, is what I have adopted, because the act of one taking back, who intends harm, is undoubtedly a show of hypocrisy.]] and is acting in a way God did not permit him, and God is the one who will repay him for what he has done. As for people, it is not lawful for them to prevent him from his wife whom he has resumed by the judgment of God, dhikruhu, that she is his wife at that time. If he attempts to harm her after resuming her, by something other than the right God gave him, then her rights, which God, dhikruhu, obligated husbands to give wives, are enforced for her, [[In the printed edition: "akhadha lahā al-ḥuqūq" (he took her rights), but the correct reading from the manuscript is adopted. "Akhadha" is in the passive: it means he was compelled and held until he gives her her rights.]] until the harm of what he intended falls back on him, and not on her.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: In His words, "And their husbands have more right to take them back in that," is a clear indication of the soundness of the view of those who say that if a man who has sworn off intercourse (mawli) resolves to divorce, and divorces the wife from whom he swore off, he has a right of return in that divorce, [[The context: "In His words... is a clear proof of the soundness of the view of those who say..." and "and of the unsoundness of the view of those who say..."]] and of the unsoundness of the view of those who say that after the four months have passed, the resolve to divorce has been made, and it is an irrevocable (ba'inah) divorce. For God, dhikruhu, only informed His servants of what is incumbent on them when they swear off their wives, and what the women are required in this verse by the men's oaths and divorces, when they resolve on that and refrain from returning.

* *

On the interpretation of His words, the Exalted: ﴿And they have rights similar to those upon them, according to what is reasonable﴾

Abu Ja'far said: The people of interpretation differed concerning the interpretation of that.

Some of them said: Its meaning is: they have from good companionship and proper living, according to what is reasonable, over their husbands, a similar right to what is due to the husbands from them in obedience in what God, dhikruhu, obligated for him over her.

Those who said this:

4766: Al-Muthanna told us, saying: Ishaq told us, saying: Abu ʿAsim told us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak regarding His words: "And they have rights similar to those upon them, according to what is reasonable." He said: If they obey God and obey their husbands, then he must treat them well, refrain from harming them, and spend on them from his wealth.

4767: Yunus told me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words: "And they have rights similar to those upon them, according to what is reasonable." He said: They fear God regarding them, as they must fear God regarding their husbands.

* *

Others said: The meaning of that is: they have over their husbands, through adornment and seeking to please, a right similar to what is due to them from them in that. [[Al-tasannu': adornment. "Tasannaʿat al-mar'ah" and "sanaʿat nafsaha": when a woman adorns herself with beautification and treatment. Among the fine verses on the meaning of "sana'a nafsahu" is what ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAziz recited:

"Indeed I give to whoever keeps company with me a pure sincerity, not a diluted one.
And when a brother of mine deviates from character, I treat it with gentleness.
A man shapes his own self, and whenever he is tested, he returns to his origin."]]

Al-Mu'ataah (المؤاتاة) means good compliance (حسن المطاوعة). One says: "I complied with him in that matter (آتيته على ذلك الأمر مؤاتاة)" when I agreed with him and obeyed him. The common people say "واتيته" (wa'attaytuhu), and it is a dialect form that makes the hamza a waw by softening the hamza.

Mention of those who said this:

4768. Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to us, from Bishr ibn Salman, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: "I like to adorn myself for my wife, just as I like her to adorn herself for me, because Allah, may He be remembered, says: ﴿And they have rights similar to their obligations, according to what is reasonable﴾."

[[Report 4768: Bishr ibn Salman al-Kindi, Abu Isma'il al-Kufi. He narrated from Mujahid, ʿIkrimah, Abu Hazim al-Ashja'i, Sayyar Abu al-Hakam, and al-Qasim ibn Safwan. Waki', Abu Nuʿaym, his son al-Hakam, the two Sufyans, and Ibn al-Mubarak, among others, heard from him. He is trustworthy (thiqah), sound in narration, and his narrations are few. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib and al-Kabir (2/199), and in al-Jarh wa-l-Ta'dil (1/1374). In the printed edition it reads "Bishr ibn Salman," which is an error.]]

* *

Abu Jaʿfar (al-Tabari) said: The interpretation of the verse that is more correct in my view is: "And for the divorced women, one or two [divorces] after they have been intimate with their husbands, it is not permitted for the husbands to take them back during their three menstrual periods [[In the printed edition: "that they not take them back in harm" – it added "ḍirāran" here, which corrupts the sentence and is not in the manuscript.]] if they wish to take them back during those periods, unless they intend to set right their affairs and their own, and that they not take them back in harm [[In the printed edition: "so they should not take them back in harm," a change forced on them by the corruption in the preceding clause. The correct reading is from the manuscript.]] – just as it is incumbent on the women toward them, if the men wish to take them back during those periods, that they not conceal what Allah has created in their wombs of offspring and of menstrual blood, out of harm from them toward the men, to outdo them by themselves [[In the printed edition: "li-tayaqqunihinna," which is a gross error and nonsense. In the manuscript: "li-tanfahum," with letters mixed and blurred, as if the copyist, when he wanted to write "liyasbaqahum" (to outrun them), then corrected himself and wrote a line over the sīn to make it "liyaftanahum" (to tempt them). The correct reading is what I have set down. This expression appears in the hadith of Fatimah bint Qays, sister of al-Dahhak ibn Qays. She was married to Abu ʿAmr ibn Hafs ibn al-Mughirah, who divorced her with two divorces, then sent to her the third divorce by oath. She came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) seeking a ruling, and he said to her: "He has no claim to take you back, and you must observe the waiting period." He ordered her to move to the house of Ibn Umm Maktum. Then he said to her: "When you are free, do not outrun me with yourself." She said: "By Allah, I did not think the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) wanted me at that time except for himself. When I was free, he proposed to me for Usamah ibn Zayd, and I married him" (Musnad Ahmad 6:414).
And the meaning of "fa'tahu bi-nafsihi" is that he outran him to a place where he could not reach him, and was beyond his power and out of his grasp. Had it been "liyasbiqannahum bi-anfusihinna," it would be correct, and it is similar to it in meaning.]]
That is because Allah, may He be remembered, forbade the divorced women from concealing from their husbands, during their menstrual periods, what Allah has created in their wombs, if they believe in Allah and the Last Day; and He made their husbands more entitled to taking them back in that case if they desired reconciliation. So Allah forbade each of the two from harming the other, and made each of them know what is theirs and what is due from them in this. Then He followed that with His saying: ﴿And they have rights similar to their obligations, according to what is reasonable﴾. It is therefore clear that what is incumbent on each of them toward the other, of refraining from harming him, is like what is due to him from the other in this regard.
This interpretation is closer to the apparent indication of the revelation than any other.
It is also possible that everything that each of them owes the other is included in this, even though the verse was revealed concerning what we have described, because Allah, may He be remembered, has given each of them a right over the other. So each of them has, over the other, the fulfilment of his right to him, like what is owed to him by the other. Thus there enters into the verse what al-Dahhak and Ibn ʿAbbas and others have said.

* *

Concerning the interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And the men have a degree over them﴾.

Abu Jaʿfar said: The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed about the interpretation of this.

Some of them said: The meaning of "the degree" (al-darajah) that Allah made for men over women is the superiority that Allah gave them over women in inheritance, in jihad, and what is similar to that.

Mention of those who said this:

4769. Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, from ʿIsa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid concerning His saying: ﴿And the men have a degree over them﴾, he said: the superiority that Allah gave him over her in jihad, and his share of inheritance over her share, and everything in which he was preferred over her.

4770. al-Muthannā narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.

4771. al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Maʿmar informed us, from Qatadah: ﴿And the men have a degree over them﴾, he said: men have a degree of superiority over women.

* *

Others said: Rather, that degree is authority (al-imarah) and obedience.

Mention of those who said this:

4772. Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Zayd ibn Aslam concerning His saying: ﴿And the men have a degree over them﴾, he said: it is authority (imarah).

4773. Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said concerning His saying: ﴿And the men have a degree over them﴾, he said: it is obedience. He said: the wives obey their husbands, and the men do not obey them.

4774. al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Azhar narrated to us, from Ibn ʿAwn, from Muhammad concerning His saying: ﴿And the men have a degree over them﴾, he said: I do not know except that they have a right similar to what is due from them, when they recognise that degree.

[[Report 4774: "Azhar" is Azhar ibn Saʿd al-Samman, Abu Bakr al-Bahili al-Basri. He narrated from Sulayman al-Taymi, Ibn ʿAwn, and Hisham al-Dastawa'i. Ibn al-Mubarak, who was older than him, narrated from him, as did ʿAli ibn al-Madini, ʿAmr ibn ʿAli al-Fallas, and Bundar. Ibn Saʿd said: trustworthy. He died in the year 203.]]

* *

Others said: That degree that he has over her is due to the dowry he has given her, and that if she accuses him she is punished with the prescribed penalty (hadd), and if he accuses her he performs the oath of condemnation (li'an).

Mention of those who said this:

4775. Muhammad ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from ʿUbaydah, from al-Shaʿbi concerning His saying: ﴿And the men have a degree over them﴾, he said: by what he gave her of her dowry; and that if he accuses her, he performs li'an against her; and if she accuses him, she is flogged and remains with him.

* *

Others said: That degree that he has over her is his bounty toward her, his fulfilment of her right to her, and his forgiveness of what is owed to him from her, or of part of it.

Mention of those who said this:

4776. Ibn Wakīʿ narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to us, from Bishr ibn Salman, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: "I do not like to take all of my right from her, because Allah, may He be remembered, says: ﴿And the men have a degree over them﴾."

[[Report 4776: In the printed edition it reads "Bishr ibn Salman," and the correct form is "Bishr," as was noted in the comment on report no. 4768 above.
"Istanzafa al-shay'": when one takes all of it, exhausts it, and seizes all of it. In the hadith: "And there will be a trial that exhausts the Arabs," meaning it will destroy them entirely. O Allah, protect us from Your punishment and save us from every destructive trial.]]

* *

Others said: Rather, that degree he has over her is that He made him a beard and forbade her that.

Mention of those who said this:

4777. Musa ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman al-Masruqi narrated to me, saying: ʿUbayd ibn al-Sabbah narrated to us, saying: Humayd narrated to us, "And the men have a degree over them": he said: a beard.

[[Report 4777: "ʿUbayd ibn al-Sabbah al-Khazzaz" narrated from ʿIsa ibn Tahman, Musa ibn ʿAli ibn Rabah, Fudayl ibn Marzuq, ʿAmr ibn Abi al-Miqdam, and ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Mulayl. Musa ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman al-Masruqi and Ahmad ibn Yahya al-Sufi narrated from him. Abu Hatim said: weak in narration. Ibn Hibban mentioned him among the trustworthy (al-thiqat). He is biographed in al-Jarh wa-l-Ta'dil (2/2/408) and Lisan al-Mizan (4:119).
As for "Humayd," I do not know who he is; there are many named Humayd, and I did not find, among those named "Humayd," a narration by ʿUbayd ibn al-Sabbah from him. Perhaps it was "Fudayl ibn Marzuq," since "Humayd" in the manuscript is garbled in its writing, as if the copyist did not read well from the original from which he copied; but I consider that unlikely. This report was transmitted by al-Qurtubi in his tafsir (3:125): "If this is authentically from him, it is weak and neither the wording of the verse nor its meaning supports it." Then he said: "Blessed is the servant who refrains from what he does not know, especially in the Book of Allah, the Exalted."
How right Ibn al-ʿArabi was, and perhaps he was admonishing some people of our time.]]

* *

Abu Jaʿfar said: The most correct of these sayings for the interpretation of the verse is what Ibn ʿAbbas said, namely that the "degree" which Allah, may He be remembered, mentions in this place is the man's forgiveness of his wife for some of what is owed to him from her, his overlooking it for her, and his fulfilment of all that is owed to her from him.

That is because Allah, may He be remembered, said: ﴿And the men have a degree over them﴾ after His saying: ﴿And they have rights similar to their obligations, according to what is reasonable﴾. So He informed, may He be exalted, that it is incumbent on the man to refrain from harming her in taking her back during her three periods and in other matters concerning her affairs and rights, just as it is incumbent on her, in return, to refrain from harming him by concealing from him what Allah has created in her womb, and other rights of his.
Then He urged men to take from women with graciousness if they leave off fulfilling some of what Allah has made obligatory for them, so He said, may He be remembered: ﴿And the men have a degree over them﴾, through their graciousness toward them and their forgiveness of some of what is owed to them. This is the meaning that Ibn ʿAbbas intended by his saying: "I do not like to take all of my right from her," because Allah, may He be remembered, says: ﴿And the men have a degree over them﴾.

* *

The meaning of "al-darajah" is rank and station.

* *

This statement from Allah, may He be remembered, although its outward form is that of a report, its meaning is the meaning of urging men to take from women with graciousness, so that they may have over them a degree of superiority.

[[It is the right of Abu Jaʿfar, may Allah be pleased with him, that I stop the reader of his book at a situation like this in his tafsir, to say once more: he was an imam in tafsir who surpassed the predecessors in their efforts. No successor has reached him in insight into the meanings of his Lord's Book, in eagerness to explain its meanings, or in the extreme precision in establishing the connections between the verses. Whoever wishes to know the merit of this imam and to verify it through knowledge of the secrets of this Book, let him read what the commentators after him wrote on the explanation of this sentence of the verse. He will find, in comparing the two statements, what helps him grasp the reality of Abu Jaʿfar's method in tafsir, and what shows him the truth of what I have said: that this man laid down for the commentators a path few have followed, or were able to walk in his footsteps. Abu Jaʿfar did not write what he wrote in the manner of exhortation, as the authors of soft-hearted treatises (raqa'iq) and the Sufis and their like do; rather he wrote with proof, argument and binding reasoning, and he drew this out from the sequence of the successive verses, from the beginning of the verse of ilaʾ (oath of abstention), ﴿Those who swear to abstain from their wives﴾, and what follows it of the explanation of the divorce by one who has sworn, how the divorcing man acts and how the divorced woman acts, what she is commanded to do in not concealing what Allah has created in her womb and in entrusting this hidden matter in her inward parts to him, what the men have of the right to take them back as reformers, not harmers, and the equality of the rights of the man over the woman and the rights of the woman over the man. Then he followed that with urging men to a virtue of manliness that a person cannot attain except through resolve and striving upward: that he overlook some of his rights over his wife. When he does that, he has reached such a height of noble character that it makes for him a degree over his wife.
Because of this precise connection between the meanings of this eloquent Book, Abu Bakr made this sentence an incitement and urging for men to rise toward virtue, not a report of a virtue that Allah has written for them, whether they do well or badly in what He commanded them.
Abu Jaʿfar, may Allah be pleased with him, never neglected this precise interlinking of the meanings of the Book, whether in verses of rulings, verses of stories, or other texts of this Book. He takes the meaning at the beginning of the verse and follows it word by word, letter by letter, then clause by clause, never leaving aside anything of it, nor passing over any meaning that its context indicates. This is not all: he never forgets that this Book came to teach people and bring them out of darknesses into light, and that it came to discipline them with the discipline of the Lord of the worlds. He connects this discipline, indicated by the revelation and explained by the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah, and draws from it this precise understanding of the meanings of the Book of Allah, supported by proof and argument.
I wish to say that adorning oneself with the manners of the Book of Allah guides to correct tafsir, just as knowledge of the Arabic language, knowledge of the abrogating and abrogated verses of the Qur'an, and the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) guide to it. Good character is an instrument of knowledge like the other instruments. Had it not been for the great character and noble manners of this imam, he would not have stood alone among all the commentators at this verse, drawing from it this noble and great meaning by which Allah disciplined the divorcing men, urged them to it, and made them know the excellence of the difference between exacting obligatory rights and pardoning these rights, for one whom Allah has placed under his hand, so that he holds the power of divorcing and separating from her, and she does not hold from that such power as he holds. O Allah, forgive us, guide us, grant us understanding in our religion, and teach us what we did not know. You are indeed the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.]]

* *

Concerning the interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And Allah is Mighty and Wise﴾ (2:228).

Abu Jaʿfar said: By that, He, may He be remembered, means: "Allah is Mighty" in His vengeance against whoever opposes His command and transgresses His limits, who has intercourse with women during menstruation, and has made Allah a target for their oaths, that they be righteous and pious and reconcile between people; and who restrains his wife through his oath of abstention and harms her in taking her back after divorcing her; and against the women who conceal from their husbands what Allah has created in their wombs, and who marry during their waiting period and leave off the waiting that Allah set for them to the time He appointed, and who commit other disobedience to Him. "Wise" in what He ordained in His creation, and in what He judged and decreed among them of His rulings, as:

4778. al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd Allah ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabiʿ concerning His saying: ﴿Allah is Mighty and Wise﴾, he says: Mighty in His retribution, Wise in His command.

* *

Allah, may He be remembered, only threatened His servants with this statement because He had earlier made clear what He forbade them or prohibited them from, from the beginning of His saying: ﴿And do not marry polytheistic women until they believe﴾ to His saying: ﴿And the men have a degree over them﴾. Then He followed that with a warning, so that those of understanding would be restrained, and those of intellect would be mindful, so that they would fear His punishment and beware of His chastisement. [[Once more, let the observer see how the meanings of the verses are connected to one another, and that this is proof that this imam of tafsir connects the meanings of all these long verses from the beginning of verse 221 to verse 228.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 229 (part 1 of 7):

The discussion of the interpretation (ta'wil) of His saying, ﴿Divorce is twice; then either retention in kindness or release with good treatment﴾

Abu Ja'far said: The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed regarding the interpretation of this.

Some of them said: It is an indication of the number of divorces in which a man has the right of return (raj'ah) to his wife, and the number by which his wife becomes irrevocably separated from him.

* *

Mention of those who said that this verse was revealed because the people of the Jahiliyyah (Pre-Islamic Age of Ignorance) and the people of Islam, before its revelation, had no limit to their divorces by reaching which a man's wife would be separated from him, so long as he took her back during her 'iddah (waiting period). So Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, set a limit for this. By reaching the end of the divorces, He made it unlawful for the man to have his divorced wife, except after a husband (another marriage), and thereafter made her more entitled to herself than him.

[[At this point the old division ends in the copy from which our old manuscript was transcribed, and what follows is this text:
"And may Allah send blessings upon our master Muhammad, the Prophet, and upon his family, abundantly.
Compared with the original.
The hearing (al-sama') of it from its beginning was completed for Muhammad and 'Ali, the two sons of Ahmad ibn 'Isa al-Sa'di, and Ahmad ibn 'Umar al-Jahhari (??), and Nasr ibn al-Husayn al-Tabari, and Muhammad ibn 'Ali al-Abhari, by the reading of Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn 'Isa to the Imam Abu al-Hasan al-Khasibi while he was looking at his book, from Abu Muhammad al-Furghani, from Abu Ja'far al-Khasibi, in Sha'ban of the year 408 (AH)."]]

* *

[[The beginning of this division:
"In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful.
My Lord, make it easy."]] Mention of the reports transmitted supporting what we have said in this regard:

4779 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father, who said: A man would divorce as many times as he wished, and if he took back his wife before her 'iddah ended, she was his wife. A man from the Ansar became angry with his wife, and said to her: "I will not come near you, nor will you be lawful to me." She said to him: "How?" He said: "I will divorce you, and when your term (ajal) draws near, I will take you back; then I will divorce you, and when your term draws near, I will take you back." She complained of that to the Prophet (ﷺ), and Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, revealed: ﴿Divorce is twice; then either retention in kindness﴾ — the verse.

4780 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Idris narrated to us, from Hisham, from his father, who said: A man said to his wife in the time of the Prophet (ﷺ): "I will not give you shelter, nor will I leave you so that you may be lawful." She said to him: "How will you act?" He said: "I will divorce you, and when the end of your 'iddah approaches I will take you back, so when will you become lawful?" So she came to the Prophet (ﷺ), and Allah revealed: ﴿Divorce is twice; then either retention in kindness or release with good treatment﴾. So the people began anew, both those who had divorced and those who had not divorced.

[[The two reports, 4779 and 4780, have the same meaning with two chains going back to Hisham ibn 'Urwah, and they are mursal (with a break in the chain, the Successor being omitted), because 'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr is a Successor (tabi'i). The hadith is established and is sound as a connected (mawsul) report, as we will mention, Allah willing.
Jarir in the first chain is Ibn 'Abd al-Hamid al-Dabbi. Ibn Idris in the second chain is 'Abd Allah ibn Idris al-Awdi.
The hadith was transmitted by al-Tirmidhi, 2:219, from Abu Kurayb Muhammad ibn al-'Ala' — the teacher of al-Tabari in the second chain — with this chain. He did not mention its wording, referring to the connected narration, as will come.
Malik also transmitted it in al-Muwatta', p. 588, with similar wording, from Hisham ibn 'Urwah from his father, mursal; and al-Shafi'i likewise transmitted it from Malik (Musnad al-Shafi'i, arranged by Shaykh 'Abid al-Sindi, 2:34).
Al-Bayhaqi transmitted it in al-Sunan al-Kubra, 7:333, by way of al-Shafi'i from Malik.
'Abd ibn Humayd transmitted it in his tafsir from Ja'far ibn 'Awn from Hisham, mursal, as Ibn Kathir quoted from him, 1:537-538. Al-Bayhaqi, 7:444, also transmitted it by way of Abu Ahmad Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Wahhab from Ja'far ibn 'Awn.
Likewise Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted it in his tafsir from Harun ibn Ishaq from 'Abdah ibn Sulayman from Hisham ibn 'Urwah from his father, mursal, quoted from him by Ibn Kathir, 1:537.
As for the connected narration: al-Tirmidhi transmitted it, 2:218-219, from Qutaybah ibn Sa'id from Ya'la ibn Shabib from Hisham ibn 'Urwah from his father from 'A'ishah, similarly, marfu' (traced to the Prophet) and connected.
Al-Hakim transmitted it, 2:279-280, by way of Ya'qub ibn Humayd ibn Kasib from Ya'la ibn Shabib, similarly. Al-Hakim said: "This is a hadith with a sound chain. No one has spoken against Ya'qub ibn Humayd with a valid proof." al-Dhahabi objected to him, saying: "Many have declared him weak!" This is a surprise from the Hafiz al-Dhahabi, as if this hadith were transmitted in its connected form by Ya'qub alone, so that the disagreement over his reliability and weakness would be established, while before him in al-Tirmidhi is the narration of Qutaybah from Ya'la!!
Al-Bayhaqi also transmitted it, 7:333, by way of Ya'qub ibn Humayd from Ya'la with it. Then he said: "It was also transmitted by Qutaybah ibn Sa'id and al-Humaydi from Ya'la ibn Shabib, and likewise Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar said it with a similar meaning, and narrated the revelation of the verse concerning it, from Hisham ibn 'Urwah from his father from 'A'ishah."
The narration of Ibn Ishaq, to which al-Bayhaqi pointed, was mentioned by Ibn Kathir, 1:538, from the narration of Ibn Mardawayh, by way of Salamah ibn al-Fadl from Muhammad ibn Ishaq from Hisham ibn 'Urwah from his father from 'A'ishah.
Ibn Kathir also mentioned — a few lines before that — that Ibn Mardawayh transmitted it "by way of Muhammad ibn Sulayman from Ya'la ibn Shabib, client of al-Zubayr, from Hisham ibn 'Urwah from his father from 'A'ishah, [and] mentioned it with a wording similar to what preceded." He means the narration of 'Abd ibn Humayd from Ja'far ibn 'Awn.
So these are two trustworthy narrators who transmitted it from Hisham ibn 'Urwah as marfu', and raising (rafs) added by a trustworthy narrator is accepted, as is well known. A marfu' report is not discredited by a mawquf one; rather, the mawquf report serves as support for the marfu' and confirms its soundness.
As for Ya'la ibn Shabib al-Asadi, client of the family of al-Zubayr: he is trustworthy; Ibn Hibban mentioned him among the trustworthy (al-thiqat). Al-Bukhari recorded his biography in al-Kabir, 20/40/20/418-419, and Ibn Abi Hatim in 4/2/301, and neither of them mentioned any criticism of him. He was transmitted from by al-Asadi, who was nicknamed "Lawin."
As for Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar: he is trustworthy, and those who spoke against him have no valid proof.]]

4781 - Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-A'la informed us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, who said: The people of the Jahiliyyah — a man would divorce three times, ten times, and more than that, then take her back during the 'iddah. So Allah set the limit of divorce at three pronouncements.
[[His saying: "The people of the Jahiliyyah, a man would..." has already passed under number 4751, in a hadith of Qatadah also with this same chain — this eloquent Arabic expression, as we pointed out in the note on p. 522.]]

4782 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, who said: The people of the Jahiliyyah, one of them would divorce his wife and then take her back, with no limit to that; she was his wife so long as he took her back during her 'iddah. [[In the manuscript: "ma dahiqaha fi 'iddatiha," which I believe is a copyist's error (tashif), but how could such a error come from a scribe!!] So Allah set the limit of that to reach three periods (qurū'), and set the limit of divorce at three pronouncements.

4783 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: "Divorce is twice": Divorce — before Allah made divorce three — had no fixed term. A man would divorce his wife a hundred times; then if he wished to take her back before she became lawful, that was his right. And a man divorced his wife until, when she was about to become lawful, he took her back; then he began a new divorce with her afterwards, to harm her by leaving her, until, when it was before the end of her 'iddah, he took her back. He did this repeatedly. When Allah knew this of him, He made divorce three: twice, and after the two, either retention in kindness or release with good treatment.

4784 - Musa narrated to me, saying: 'Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "Divorce is twice; then either retention in kindness or release with good treatment." As for His saying: "Divorce is twice," it is the appointed time (mīqat) during which she has the right of return.

4785 - Hannad narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Ahwas narrated to us, from Simak, from 'Ikrimah, regarding His saying: "Divorce is twice; then either retention in kindness or release with good treatment," he said: If a man wished to divorce his wife, he would divorce her with two pronouncements. If he wished to take her back, he had the right of return over her; then if he wished, he would divorce her again, and she would not be lawful to him until she married another husband.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The interpretation of the verse according to this report which we have mentioned is: the number of divorces in which you, O people, have the right of return over your wives, when they have been consummated with, is two pronouncements. Then it is obligatory upon whoever among you takes back after the two pronouncements, to retain in kindness or release with good treatment, for he has no right of return after two pronouncements if he releases her by pronouncing the third.

* *

Others said: This verse was only revealed to the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) as a teaching from Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, to His servants about the sunnah (prescribed practice) of their divorcing their wives when they wish to divorce them — not as an indication of the number by which a woman becomes separated from her husband. [[In the printed edition: "la dalala 'ala al-qadr" — a distortion and an error; the correct reading is from the manuscript.]]

Mention of those who said that:

4786 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mutarrif, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu al-Ahwas, from 'Abd Allah (ibn Mas'ud), regarding His saying: "Divorce is twice; then either retention in kindness or release with good treatment," he said: He divorces her after she has become pure from intercourse; then he leaves her until she becomes pure again; then he divorces her if he wishes. Then if he wishes to take her back, he takes her back; then if he wishes, he divorces her; otherwise he leaves her until three menstrual periods (hiyad) are completed, and she becomes separated from him thereby. [[The report 4786 was transmitted by al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan, 6:140, with other wording, likewise al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan, 7:332, and Ibn Majah, 1:651.]]

4787 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah ibn Salih narrated to me, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn 'Abbas, his saying: "Divorce is twice; then either retention in kindness or release with good treatment." He said: If a man divorces his wife with two pronouncements, let him fear Allah regarding the third pronouncement: either he retains her in kindness, treating her companionship well, or he releases her with good treatment, not wronging her of any of her rights.

4788 - Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, from 'Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: "Divorce is twice; then either retention in kindness or release with good treatment," he said: A man divorces his wife while she is pure, without intercourse. When she menstruates and then becomes pure, the qur' (menstrual period, also used for the purity interval) is completed. Then he divorces her a second time, just as he divorced her the first time, if he wishes to do so. When he has divorced her the second time, and she then menstruates the second menstruation, they are two pronouncements and two qur's. Then Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, said regarding the third: "either retention in kindness or release with good treatment." So he divorces her during that whole qur' if he wishes, when she has gathered her garments about her. [[In the manuscript: "tajma'u 'alayhi" [with "alayhi"], which is an error. It is said: "I gathered my garments over me" when one dresses in the clothes in which one goes out before people — izar, rida' and turban. And a woman "gathered her garments" when she put on the shift, the headcloth and the veil. By his saying "she gathered her garments" he refers metaphorically to her washing from her menstruation and her putting on her clothes in a state of purity.]]

4789 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, similarly — except that he said: "She menstruated the second menstruation, just as he divorced her the first time; so these are two pronouncements and two qur's." Then he said: "The third..." And the rest of the hadith is like the hadith of Muhammad ibn 'Amr from Abu 'Asim.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The interpretation of the verse according to the view of these people is: the sunnah of divorce which I have prescribed and permitted for you, if you wish to divorce your women, is that you divorce them two at a time, one in each state of purity. Then the obligation after that upon you is: either to retain them in kindness, or to release them with good treatment.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: What is more appropriate to the apparent meaning of the revelation is what 'Urwah and Qatadah said, and whoever said the like of their view, that the verse is only an indication of the number of divorces by which prohibition takes effect, and by which the right of return ends, and in which return is possible. This is because Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, said in the verse that follows: ﴿Then if he divorces her, she is not lawful to him thereafter until she marries another husband﴾, and so He informed His servants of the amount by which a woman becomes unlawful to her husband except after another husband. He did not explain in it the time at which divorce is permitted, nor the time at which it is not permitted. Therefore the interpretation of the verse would be directed to what was related from Ibn Mas'ud, Mujahid, and whoever said the like of their view in it.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿then either retention in kindness or release with good treatment﴾, there is a difference among the people of interpretation regarding its interpretation and what it means.

Some of them said: Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, meant by it an indication of what is binding upon husbands of wives divorced twice — after they take them back from the second pronouncement — namely, either to live with them in kindness, or to separate from them by divorce. [[In the manuscript: "al-lazim lil-azwaj al-mutallaqat ithnatayn," and in the printed edition: "al-lazim lil-azwaj al-mutallaqat," and what I have affirmed is the best of the three wordings.]] [[In the manuscript: "aw bi-firaqihinna" with an extra "ba'" that has no place here.]]

Mention of those who said that:

4790 - Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: I said to 'Ata': "Divorce is twice." He said: At the third he says: either he retains her in kindness, or he releases her with good treatment. Another said it [[In the printed edition: "wa-ghayruhu qalaha," and the correct reading is from the manuscript — meaning: another said this statement, then he mentioned Mujahid's statement on the interpretation of the verse. This is what I saw, unless there is a distortion in the wording.]]. He said: Mujahid said: A man has more right over his wife with two pronouncements than another, but when he pronounces the third, he has no more claim over her, and she observes her 'iddah for another.

4791 - Abu al-Sa'ib narrated to me, saying: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from Isma'il ibn Sami', from Abu Razin, who said: A man came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, what do you think of His saying: 'Divorce is twice; then either retention in kindness or release with good treatment' — then where is the third?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Either retention in kindness, or release with good treatment" — it is the third.

4792 - Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Sa'id and 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us, both saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Isma'il ibn Sami', from Abu Razin, who said: A man came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, 'Divorce is twice' — then where is the third?" He said: "Retention in kindness, or release with good treatment."

4793 - Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: al-Thawri informed us, from Isma'il, from Abu Razin, who said: A man said: "O Messenger of Allah, Allah says: 'Divorce is twice; then either retention in kindness'; then where is the third?" He said: "Release with good treatment." [[The reports 4791 to 4793 are all one hadith with three chains. It is a mursal and weak hadith, as we will mention, Allah willing.
Sufyan in the second chain is al-Thawri, as in the third chain.
Isma'il ibn Sami' — with a damma on the sin, diminutive — al-Hanafi: trustworthy and reliable, as Ibn Ma'in said. Whoever spoke against him did so only because he held the opinion of the Kharijites.
Abu Razin — with a fatha on the ra' and a kasra on the zay — is al-Asadi, of the Asad Khuzaymah, whose name is "Mas'ud," and he is a trustworthy Kufan Successor. Some call him "Mas'ud ibn Malik," which is confused with another narrator named "Mas'ud ibn Malik ibn Ma'bad," client of Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who is later than Abu Razin. We have verified this in detail in al-Musnad: 3551, 7432m, and in its supplement: 707.
This "Abu Razin al-Asadi" is a Successor, as we said. He is different from that "Abu Razin al-Uqayli," the Companion whose name is "Luqayt ibn 'Amir," whose biography has passed: 3223.
The chain of 4793 is in the tafsir of 'Abd al-Razzaq, pp. 28-29, where it reads "asma' Allah yaqul" [I heard God say] instead of "yaqul Allah"; likewise it is in al-Musannaf of 'Abd al-Razzaq, vol. 3, p. 301.
Ibn Kathir mentioned the hadith, 1:538-539, from the narration of Ibn Abi Hatim, 'Abd ibn Humayd, Sa'id ibn Mansur and Ibn Mardawayh — with their chains, all from Abu Razin similarly, mursal. Al-Bayhaqi, 7:340, also transmitted it with his chain from the narration of Sa'id ibn Mansur.
The Hafiz Ibn Kathir, may Allah have mercy on him, made a serious error in attributing this mursal hadith to the narration of the Musnad, saying: "Imam Ahmad also transmitted it."
The hadith was also mentioned by al-Suyuti, 1:277, who added its attribution to Waki', Abu Dawud in his Nasikh, Ibn al-Mundhir and al-Nahhas.
Abu Ja'far will say shortly, pointing to this hadith: "The following of the report from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is more fitting for us than other than it." This is a tendency on his part toward proof by mursal hadith, which is a position some scholars choose.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 229 (part 2 of 7):

I had responded to Abu Ja'far, may Allah have mercy on him, in my book "Nizam al-Talaq fi al-Islam" in paragraph 29, after I had quoted his words, and I said: "Indeed, the report from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is more deserving of our following than anything else, and we accept with full obedience what has come from him, peace and blessings be upon him, if it is authentic and established. But this report of Abu Razin is not authentic, for it is a mursal report, not connected (to the Prophet ﷺ). Abu Razin al-Asadi was a Successor (tabi'i), not a Companion (sahabi). A mursal report carries no proof, since it comes from an unknown narrator. Moreover, it is a report whose meaning is utterly false. Far be it from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to interpret the third divorce by this, when it is established in the verse that follows it in the context of the discourse: ﴿Then if he divorces her, she is not lawful to him after that until she marries another husband﴾. Otherwise it would be a fourth divorce, and that contradicts what is known of the religion by necessity."

4794 - Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid: "or release with kindness" – he said: it refers to the third (divorce).

4795 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, who said: Divorce had no set limit until Allah revealed: "Divorce is twice" – he said: the third: "then retain with fairness or release with kindness."

* *

Others said: Rather, Allah meant by this an indication of what is due to them after the second divorce, namely taking them back with fairness or releasing them with kindness, by leaving off taking them back until their waiting period (iddah) ends, whereupon they become more entitled to themselves. They rejected the view of the earlier ones who said that it is an indication of the third divorce.

Those who said this:

4796 - Musa narrated to me, saying: Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His words: "Then retention with fairness or release with kindness": if he divorces once or twice, he either retains (yumsik, i.e., takes back [yurajiʿu]) her with fairness, or he leaves her until her waiting period ends, so that she is more entitled to herself.

4797 - Ali ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: al-Muharibi narrated to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak: "or release with kindness" – and release (al-tasrih) is that he leaves her until her waiting period passes.

[Note on the report 4797: I have not found among al-Tabari's teachers one named "Ali ibn Abd al-A'a" (sic). It appears in report 4799 as "Ali ibn Abd al-A'la al-Muharibi" and in no. 4804. The one from whom he most often narrates in tafsir is "Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la al-San'ani," so I do not know what the correct reading is.]

4798 - Yahya ibn Abi Talib narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Juwaybir informed us, from al-Dahhak regarding His words: "Divorce is twice; then retention with fairness or release with kindness," – he said: it means two divorces between which there is taking back, so He commanded that he retain or release with kindness. He said: If he divorces her a third time, she is not lawful to him until she marries another husband.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: It seems that those who said this view reported from al-Suddi and al-Dahhak went to the meaning: "Divorce is twice; then retention, in each of the two, of them with fairness, or release of them with kindness."

This is a position that the apparent sense of the revelation may allow, were it not for the report I have mentioned from the Prophet ﷺ, narrated by Isma'il ibn Sumay' from Abu Razin, for following a report from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is more deserving of us than anything else.

Since that is the obligation, it is clear that the interpretation of the verse is: the divorce in which husbands have the right of return over their wives is twice. Then the command, after that, when they take them back after the second, is either retention with fairness, or their release by them with kindness through the third divorce, until they are separated from them, whereupon the right of return they had over them is void, and they become more entitled to themselves than they are.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: If someone says: What is that retention which is with fairness? It is said: it is what:

4799 - Ali ibn Abd al-A'la al-Muharibi narrated this to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad al-Muharibi narrated to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak regarding His words: "then retention with fairness" – he said: fairness is that he treats her companionship well.

4800 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya ibn Salih narrated to me, from Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn Abbas: "then retention with fairness" – he said: let him fear Allah regarding the third divorce; so either he retains her with fairness, treating her companionship well.

* *

If someone says: What then is release with kindness?

It is said: it is what:

4801 - al-Muthanna narrated this to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas: "or release with kindness" – it is said: he releases her and does not wrong her in any of her rights.

4802 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas: "then retention with fairness or release with kindness" – he said: it is the solemn covenant.

4803 - Musa narrated to me, saying: Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "or release with kindness" – he said: kindness is that he pays her what is due to her, so he does not harm her nor revile her.

4804 - Ali ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad al-Muharibi narrated to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak: "or release with kindness" – he said: release with kindness is that he leaves her until her waiting period ends, and gives her a dower if she is owed one from him when he divorces her. That is release with kindness, and provision according to one's means.

4805 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Suwayd ibn Nasr narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ata' al-Khurasani, from Ibn Abbas regarding His words: "and they have taken from you a solid covenant" – he said: His words: "then retention with fairness or release with kindness."

* *

If someone says: What is the element that governs the retention and the release?

It is said: it is an omitted element, left out because of what has appeared of its mention in the discourse, and its meaning is: "Divorce is twice, so the command then obligatory is retention with fairness or release with kindness." We have already explained this in detail in His words: ﴿Then pursuit with fairness and payment to him with kindness﴾ [Surah al-Baqarah: 178], which makes it unnecessary to repeat it here. [See what has passed, 3:372.]

* *

Regarding the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿It is not lawful for you to take anything of what you have given them, unless they both fear that they will not keep within the limits of Allah﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, means by His words: "It is not lawful for you to take anything of what you have given them" – it is not lawful for you, O men, when you wish to divorce your wives, to take from them, by your divorcing and separating from them, anything of what you have given them of the dowry and conveyed to them. Rather, it is obligatory upon you to release them with kindness, which means fulfilling their rights of dowry, provision and whatever else is owed to them from you – "unless they both fear that they will not keep within the limits of Allah."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The reciters differed in reading this. Some read: "unless they both fear that they will not keep within the limits of Allah," and this is the reading of the majority of the people of the Hijaz and Basra, meaning: unless the man and the woman fear that they will not keep within the limits of Allah. It is mentioned that in the reading of Ubayy ibn Ka'b it is: ﴿unless they both suspect that they will not keep within the limits of Allah﴾.

4806 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, saying: Thawr informed me, from Maymun ibn Mihran, who said: In the codex of Ubayy ibn Ka'b, the ransom is a single divorce. He said: I mentioned that to Ayyub, and we went to a man who had an old copy of Ubayy's Qur'an that had come from a trustworthy source; we read it and in it was: ﴿unless they both suspect that they will not keep within the limits of Allah. So if they both suspect that they will not keep within the limits of Allah, there is no blame upon them in what she gives up for it. It is not lawful for him after that until she marries another husband﴾.

* *

The Arabs sometimes put "al-zann" (suspicion/thought) in the place of "al-khawf" (fear), and "al-khawf" in the place of "al-zann" in their speech, because their meanings are close, as the poet said:

"There came to me speech from Nasib, saying it,
and, O Salam, you did not fear that you would blame me."

Meaning: you did not think.

* *

Others read: ﴿unless they both fear that they will not keep within the limits of Allah﴾, the reading of some people of Madinah and Kufa.

As for the reader of this reading from the people of Kufa, [he is the Kufan scholar Hamzah ibn Habib al-Zayyat, one of the seven readers], it is reported that he read it thus, relying on the reading of Ibn Mas'ud, and it is mentioned that in the reading of Ibn Mas'ud it is: ﴿unless you fear that they will not keep within the limits of Allah﴾. Reading it thus, relying on the reading of Ibn Mas'ud that was reported from him, is an error. That is because if Ibn Mas'ud read it as reported, he only applied the fear to "an" (that) alone, which is not a rejected validity, as the poet said:

"When I die, bury me beside a vine
whose roots will water my bones after my death.
And do not bury me in the desert, for I
fear, when I die, that I will not taste it."

As for the one who reads "unless they both fear" with that meaning, he has applied the verb to a passive subject omitted and to "an," (the clause after "an"), and "an" then serves two things: the omitted passive subject and "an" that stands in for two elements. The Arabs do not say in their speech: "they both thought that they would stand."

Rather, reading it thus is correct, but not in the manner of those who read it thus, relying on the reading of Ibn Mas'ud that we described. Rather, it is to be understood, when read thus, as: "unless they fear that they will not keep within the limits of Allah," or "that they will not keep within the limits of Allah," so that the governing element for "an" is other than "fear," and "fear" governs what has no named agent. That is what we consider the correct reading, because what follows it supports its soundness, which is His words: "But if you fear that they will not keep within the limits of Allah," so it is clear that the first means: unless you fear that they will not keep within the limits of Allah.

* *

If someone says: What is the circumstance in which they both fear that they will not keep within the limits of Allah, such that it is permissible for the man to take from her then what he gave her?

It is said: it is the circumstance of her ill-conduct (nushuz) and her showing him her hatred, so that one fears for her the abandonment of obedience to Allah in what her husband is owed of right, and one fears for her husband, through her shortcoming in fulfilling his rights that Allah has imposed on her, his abandonment of performing what is owed to her from him. That is the time when they both fear that they will not keep within the limits of Allah, so that they obey him in what is imposed on each of them toward the other. And it is the circumstance in which the Prophet ﷺ permitted Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas to take back what he had given his wife, when she showed ill-conduct toward him out of hatred for him, as:

4807 - Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: al-Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman narrated to us, saying: I read to Fudayl, from Abu Hariz, that he asked Ikrimah whether there was a precedent for khul' (divorce by ransom). He said: Ibn Abbas used to say: The first khul' in Islam was the sister of Abd Allah ibn Ubayy, who came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "O Messenger of Allah, no thing will ever join my head and his! I raised the side of the tent, and I saw him coming in a crowd, and he was the blackest of them, the shortest in stature, and the ugliest in face!" Her husband said: "O Messenger of Allah, I gave her my best property, a garden. Let her return my garden to me!" He said: "What do you say?" She said: "Yes, and if he wishes I will add to it!" He said: So he separated them.

[Hadith 4807 notes: al-Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman ibn Tarkhan al-Taymi is trustworthy; the great imams narrated from him, including Ibn Mahdi, Abd al-Razzaq, Ahmad, Ishaq and others. Fudayl (diminutive) is Ibn Maysarah al-Azdi al-Uqayli, trustworthy, deemed so by Ibn Ma'in and others. Abu Hariz is Abd Allah ibn al-Huyayn al-Azdi al-Basri, judge of Sijistan; he is disputed, but the truth is he is trustworthy, deemed so by Ibn Ma'in, Abu Zur'ah and others. "Abu Hariz" is with a non-pointed ha vocalized with fatha and a ra with kasra, ending in a marked zay. The printed edition and Ibn Kathir and Fath al-Bari have "Abu Jarir," which is a misprint, and the Isabah has "Ibn Jarir," which is an error compounded. This hadith has a sound chain. Ibn Kathir (1:542) transmitted it from this place, and al-Suyuti (1:280-281) mentioned it without attributing it to anyone other than al-Tabari. Al-Hafiz (Fath 9:351) transmitted it, saying: "In the narration of Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman..." with some variation in wording, which shows he took it from another narration, though he did not identify its compiler as is his habit. A similar meaning is established from the hadith of Ibn Abbas, reported by al-Bukhari in several chains (9:349-352). Ibn Kathir transmitted it from al-Bukhari's narrations (1:541-542), then said: "This hadith is unique to al-Bukhari from this route." He then transmitted something similar from Abu Abd Allah ibn Battah with his chain from Qatadah, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, then mentioned that Ibn Mardawayh narrated it in his tafsir and Ibn Majah, and said: "It is a good, sound chain." The narration of Ibn Majah is in his Sunan, number 2056.

As for his words, "the sister of Abd Allah ibn Ubayy": she is Jamilah bint Abd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul, chief of the hypocrites. She was the sister of Abd Allah ibn Abd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul, the noble Companion. She and her brother were both attributed to their grandfather for brevity. This is the sound view that al-Hafiz and others preferred.

The name of her husband whom she sought khul' from is not mentioned in this report in al-Tabari; it is Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas, as other reports indicate. This Thabit fathered a son, Muhammad ibn Thabit, who is biographed in al-Isabah (6:152) and Ibn Sa'd (5:58-59). It is firmly stated that his mother was Jamilah bint Abd Allah ibn Ubayy. She refused to nurse him, because she hated his father, so he brought him to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who spat into his mouth, rubbed his palate, and named him Muhammad, saying: "Make him grow, for Allah will provide for him." I came to him on the first day, the second and the third, and there was a woman from the Arabs asking about Thabit ibn Qays, so I said: "What do you want from him? I am Thabit." She said: "I saw in my dream that I was nursing a son of his called Muhammad," so he said: "I am Thabit, and this is my son Muhammad." He said: "Her shift was dripping with her milk." This was narrated by al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak (2:210-211), who said: "This hadith has a sound chain, though they (al-Bukhari and Muslim) did not include it." Al-Dhahabi agreed. It is a sound, connected chain, because the context shows that this Muhammad heard it from his father and narrated it from him. al-Hafiz mentioned it in his biography in al-Isabah in a similar form.

It is well known that the one who sought khul' from Thabit was this Jamilah.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 229 (part 3 of 7):

[[In the printed edition it occurred: "fa-l-turaddid 'ala hadiqati" (then let her return my garden to me). The correct reading is what we have established: "fa-in raddat 'alayya hadiqati" (if she returns my garden to me). We corrected it from the manuscript, Ibn Kathir and al-Suyuti. The answer to the conditional clause is omitted, as is evident. This is a common eloquent usage in the speech of the eloquent.
See: 4810.]]

4808 - Muhammad ibn Mu'ammar narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Amir narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Amr al-Sadusi narrated to us, from Abdullah, meaning Ibn Abi Bakr, from 'Amra, from 'A'isha: that Habiba bint Sahl was under Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas. [[In the printed edition: "bint Sahl," and I have established what is in the manuscript.]] He struck her and broke her nughd (the thin bone on the edge of the shoulder blade), so she came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ after the dawn prayer and complained about him. The Messenger of Allah called Thabit and said: "Take some of her property and separate from her." He said: "Is that permissible, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Yes." He said: "I have given her as dower two gardens, and they are in her possession." The Prophet ﷺ said: "Take them and separate from her." He did so. [[The hadith: 4808. Abu 'Amir: he is al-Aqadi, Abd al-Malik ibn Amr.
Abu 'Amr al-Sadusi: he is Sa'id ibn Salama ibn Abi al-Hisam al-Madani, and he is trustworthy (thiqah). Abu Salama al-Tabudhaki said: "I have not seen a book more sound than his book." Ibn Hibban mentioned him in al-Thiqat. Ibn Ma'in did not know him well, as Ibn Abi Hatim related from him, and al-Nasa'i declared him weak. However, al-Bukhari included him in al-Kabir (2/1/438) and did not mention any fault in him. This is sufficient for his authentication, especially since Muslim included him in his Sahih.
Al-Bukhari did not affirm that Sa'id ibn Salama is the Abu 'Amr who narrated this hadith. He said: "Abu 'Amir said: Abu 'Amr al-Sadusi al-Madani narrated to us. I do not know whether he is this one or another."
He is mentioned in al-Tahdhib in al-Asma (4: 41-42) and in al-Kuna (12: 181-182). The Hafiz established by strong evidence that they are one and the same narrator, as will become clear from the takhrij (tracing of sources), God willing.
Abdullah is Ibn Abi Bakr ibn Amr ibn Hazm.
This hadith was also narrated by Abu Dawud (2228) from Muhammad ibn Mu'ammar, the teacher of al-Tabari in it, with this isnad (chain of transmission).
Ibn Kathir mentioned it (1: 541) from Abu Dawud and al-Tabari, then said: "Abu 'Amr al-Sadusi is Sa'id ibn Salama ibn Abi al-Hisam."
The Hafiz mentioned it in al-Tahdhib (4: 41-42) in brief from the narration of Abu Dawud, then said: "Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Shu'ayb al-Rijali narrated this hadith from Muhammad ibn Mu'ammar, from Abu 'Amir al-Aqadi, from Sa'id ibn Salama, from Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr, with its isnad. This narration shows that the Abu 'Amr mentioned in Abu Dawud's narration is Sa'id ibn Salama." Then he said: "What establishes that they are one is mentioned later in al-Kuna." Then he said in "al-Kuna" from al-Tahdhib (12: 181-182): "Abu Muhammad Ibn Sa'id narrated in the fifth part of his hadith: Muhammad ibn Mu'ammar al-Qaysi narrated to us, Abu 'Amir al-Aqadi narrated to us, Abu 'Amr al-Sadusi, that is Sa'id ibn Salama, narrated to us. Hisham ibn Ali al-Sirafi narrated to us in Basra, Abdullah ibn Raja' narrated to us, Sa'id ibn Salama ibn Abi al-Hisam narrated to us, Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr narrated to me," and he mentioned that same hadith. It is thus established that the Abu 'Amr al-Madini al-Sadusi mentioned is Sa'id ibn Salama.
Al-Bayhaqi also narrated it (7: 315) by way of Hisham ibn Ali, from Abdullah ibn Raja': "Sa'id ibn Salama ibn Abi al-Hisam informed us, Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr narrated to us..." and he mentioned it with an addition at the end.
This route is like the route the Hafiz related just before from Abu Muhammad Ibn Sa'id, and it confirms what he said and what we said.
Al-Suyuti mentioned it (1: 280) and added its attribution to Abd al-Razzaq, but I did not find it in the Tafsir nor in al-Musannaf of Abd al-Razzaq. Perhaps it escaped notice in its place in one of the two.
As for his saying "fa-kasara nughdaha": al-nughd, with a damma on the nun, a sukun on the ghayn with a dot, and a dad with a dot at the end, is the thin bone on the edge of the shoulder. This is the correct reading of this word here. In the printed edition it appears as "ba'daha" (some of her), and likewise in the printed copies of Sunan Abi Dawud, except for one copy in the margin of the Hind edition, which mentions the correct reading. The correct and established reading is in the manuscript of Shaykh Abid al-Sindi, clear and vocalized, admitting no misreading. What confirms and strengthens this is that the narration of al-Bayhaqi says "fa-kasara yadaha" (he broke her arm). As for the word "ba'daha" (some of her), it is awkward and unacceptable in this place.
See the hadith following this one.]]

4809 - Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Rawh narrated to us, saying: Malik narrated to us, from Yahya, from 'Amra, that she informed him concerning Habiba bint Sahl al-Ansariyya: that she was under Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas, and that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw her at his door in the dark before dawn. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Who is this?" She said: "I am Habiba bint Sahl," [no, not I and not Thabit ibn Qays!!] = to her husband = Then when Thabit came, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: "This is Habiba bint Sahl, and she mentions what Allah wills her to mention!" Habiba said: "O Messenger of Allah, all that he gave me is with me." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Take from her." So he took from her, and she sat in her house. [[The hadith: 4809. Ibn Bashshar is Muhammad ibn Bashshar, a teacher of al-Tabari and of the authors of the six canonical books; his biography has passed at 304. In the printed edition it occurred as "Abu Yasar"!! This is an ugly misreading. Corrected from the manuscript. Rawh is Ibn Ubada.
Yahya, Malik's teacher, is al-Ansari al-Najjari; his biography has passed at 2154, where in his biography "al-Bukhari" occurred, which is a printing error, and it passed correctly at 3395. He is Yahya ibn Sa'id ibn Qays ibn Amr ibn Sahl ibn Tha'laba. Thus "Habiba bint Sahl ibn Tha'laba," the woman of the hadith and the story, is the paternal aunt of his grandfather Qays ibn Amr.
The hadith is in al-Muwatta, p. 564. Al-Shafi'i narrated it from Malik in al-Umm (5: 101, 179).
Ahmad narrated it in al-Musnad (6: 433-434, Halabi) from Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi from Malik. Abu Dawud narrated it (2227) from al-Qa'nabi from Malik. al-Nasa'i narrated it (2: 104) by way of Ibn al-Qasim from Malik. Ibn Hibban narrated it in his Sahih (6: 436-437, from the manuscript of al-Ihsan) by way of Abu Mus'ab Ahmad ibn Abi Bakr, from Malik. Al-Bayhaqi narrated it (7: 312-313) by way of Abu Dawud.
Abd al-Razzaq narrated it in al-Musannaf (photographed manuscript), vol. 4, folio 17, from Ibn Juraij, from Yahya ibn Sa'id, with it.
Al-Shafi'i narrated it in al-Umm, in both places after his narration from Malik, from Sufyan ibn Uyayna, from Yahya ibn Sa'id.
Ibn Sa'd narrated it in al-Tabaqat (8: 326) in the biography of "Habiba," from Yazid ibn Harun, from Yahya ibn Sa'id, from 'Amra: "that Habiba bint Sahl..." and mentioned it as a mursal (a hadith in which the Successor reports directly from the Prophet, omitting the Companion).
Then he narrated it from Arim ibn al-Fadl, from Hammad ibn Zayd, from Yahya ibn Sa'id, and mentioned it as mu'dal (a chain in which two or more consecutive narrators are omitted), omitting both the Successor and the Companion. It has become clear from the earlier narrations that this and the preceding one are connected (muttasil), despite the apparent break in their outward form. Ibn Kathir (1: 541) and al-Suyuti (1: 280) mentioned it as connected.]]

4810 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, saying: al-Hasan ibn Waqid narrated to us, from Thabit, from Abdullah ibn Rabah, from Jamila bint Abi Ibn Salul: that she was with Thabit ibn Qays, and she rebelled against him (nashazat). He sent for her, and the Prophet ﷺ sent for her and said: "O Jamila, what did you dislike about Thabit?" She said: "By Allah, I did not dislike in him any religion or character, except that I disliked his ugliness!" He said to her: "Will you return the garden?" She said: "Yes!" So she returned the garden and they were separated. [[The hadith: 4810. Yahya ibn Wadih is Abu Tamila, whose biography has passed at 392.
al-Husayn ibn Waqid al-Marwazi, judge of Marw: trustworthy. Ibn Ma'in declared him trustworthy and Ahmad praised him. Ibn al-Mubarak said of him: "Who among us is like al-Husayn?" In the printed edition it occurred as "al-Hasan," which is a clear error. Thabit is al-Bunani.
Abdullah ibn Rabah al-Ansari: a trustworthy Successor. Ibn Sa'd, al-Nasa'i and others declared him trustworthy, and Ibn Khurash said: "He is a distinguished man."
This isnad is sound. I have not found it except here in al-Tabari and in Ibn Abd al-Barr's al-Isti'ab. Ibn Abd al-Barr narrated it (pp. 732-733) from Abd al-Warith ibn Sufyan, from Qasim ibn Asbagh, from Ahmad ibn Zuhayr, from Muhammad ibn Humayd al-Razi, the teacher of al-Tabari here, with this isnad.
It has become clear from these four hadiths, 4807 to 4810, and from other sound narrations, that there is disagreement about who was the one who gave up her marriage to Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas through khul' (divorce initiated by the wife with compensation): is it Jamila bint Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul, or Habiba bint Sahl? The more likely view is that both of them gave up the marriage. This is what the Hafiz preferred in Fath al-Bari (9: 350) and approved. He said: "What appears is that they are two stories that occurred for two women, because of the fame of the two reports, the soundness of the two routes, and the difference in their wording."
See al-Isaba (8: 39-40, 42, 49).]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: It has been mentioned that this verse was revealed concerning the two of them, that is, concerning Thabit ibn Qays and this wife of his.

4811 - al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, from Ibn Juraij, who said: This verse was revealed concerning Thabit ibn Qays and Habiba. He said: She had complained about him to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Will you return his garden to him?" She said: "Yes!" So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ called him and mentioned that to him. He said: "Will that be permissible for me?" He said: "Yes." Thabit said: "I have done it."
