Then this was revealed: ﴿And it is not lawful for you to take anything of what you have given them, unless both fear that they will not keep within the limits of Allah. But if you fear that they will not keep within the limits of Allah, then there is no blame upon them concerning that by which she ransoms herself. These are the limits of Allah, so do not transgress them.﴾ (2:229)

* *

As for the people of ta'wil (interpretation), they differed about the meaning of "fear" in their case, that they will not keep within the limits of Allah.

Some of them said: It means that ill conduct and bad treatment of the husband appear from the woman, and when that appears from her toward him, it becomes lawful for him to take what she gave him as ransom for separating from her.

Those who said this:

4812 - Ali ibn Dawud narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from Ali ibn Abi Talha, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿And it is not lawful for you to take anything of what you have given them﴾, unless the rebellion and ill conduct come from her side, so that she asks you to ransom yourself from her, and then there is no blame upon you concerning what she ransoms herself with.

4813 - Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn Ulayya narrated to us, saying: Ibn Juraij said: Hisham ibn Urwa informed me that Urwa used to say: Ransom is not lawful until the corruption comes from her side. He did not say "it is not lawful for him" until she says: "I will not fulfil your right of the night, and I will not bathe for you from major impurity."

4814 - Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn Ulayya narrated to us, from Ibn Juraij, who said: Amr ibn Dinar informed me, saying: Jabir ibn Zayd said: If the evil comes from her side, ransom becomes lawful. [[In the printed edition: "idha kana al-nushz" (if it was the rebellion), as if he thought it was a verbal noun of "nashaza," but the verbal noun is "nushuz" only, and this is an error by the typesetter. As for the manuscript, it contains what I have established, which is the pure correct reading.]]

4815 - al-Rabi' ibn Sulayman narrated to us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Abi al-Zinad narrated to me, from Hisham ibn Urwa, that his father used to say: If bad character and bad treatment come from the wife, then that makes her khul' lawful.

4816 - Ali ibn Sahl narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Kathir narrated to us, from Hammad, from Hisham, from his father, that he said: Khul' is not proper until the corruption comes from the wife's side.

4817 - Abd al-Hamid ibn Bayan al-Qannad narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yazid narrated to us, from Isma'il, from Amir, concerning a woman who said to her husband: "I will not fulfil your right of the night, I will not obey your command, and I will not bathe for you from major impurity!" He said: "What is this?" — and he moved his hand — "'I will not fulfil your right of the night, and I will not obey your command'!!" When a woman dislikes her husband, let him take it and leave her.

4818 - Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us, saying: Ayyub narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, that he said concerning the woman who seeks khul': he admonishes her; if she desists, well and good, and if not, he abandons her (hajr); if she desists, well and good, and if not, he strikes her; if she desists, well and good, and if not, her matter is referred to the authority, and he sends an arbiter from his family and an arbiter from her family. The arbiter from her family says: "Do this to her and do that to her!" And the arbiter from his family says: "Do this to him and do that to him!" Whichever of them is more unjust, the authority restrains him and takes from him beyond his hand. And if she is rebellious (nashiz), he orders her to seek khul'.

4819 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi' concerning His saying: ﴿Divorce is twice; then either keep [her] in an acceptable manner﴾ up to His saying: ﴿there is no blame upon them concerning that by which she ransoms herself﴾. He said: If the woman is content, happy and obedient, it is not lawful for him to strike her until she ransoms herself from him. If he takes something from her for that, what he takes from her is unlawful. But if the rebellion, hatred and wrongdoing come from her side, then it becomes lawful for him to take from her what she ransoms herself with.

4820 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri concerning His saying: ﴿And it is not lawful for you to take anything of what you have given them, unless both fear that they will not keep within the limits of Allah﴾. He said: It is not lawful for a man to seek khul' from his wife unless she commits that (an offence) from her side. As for him harming her until she seeks khul', that is not proper. But if she rebels, shows him hatred and treats him badly, then khul' becomes lawful for him. [[In the printed edition: "illa an yara dhalika" (unless he sees that), which is nothing. In the manuscript: "illa an laka lawnan," unpointed, and this is, God willing, the correct reading of it.]]

4821 - Yahya ibn Abi Talib narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Jawaybir informed us, from al-Dahhak concerning His saying: ﴿And it is not lawful for you to take anything of what you have given them﴾: he said: the dower. ﴿unless both fear that they will not keep within the limits of Allah﴾ — and the limits of Allah are that the woman be rebellious. Allah commanded the husband to admonish her with the Book of Allah. If she accepts, well and good; if not, he abandons her. Abandonment means that he does not have intercourse with her and does not lie with her on one bed, and he turns his back to her and does not speak to her. If she persists, he speaks harshly to her with insults, so that she returns to obedience to him. [[In the printed edition: "ghallaza 'alayha" (he was harsh toward her), and the good reading in the manuscript is what I have established.]] If she persists, then striking, a non-severe striking. If she persists in obstinacy, then the ransom becomes lawful for him from her.

* *

Others said: Rather, the "fear" concerning that is that she does not fulfil his right of the night, does not obey his command, and says: "I will not bathe for you from major impurity, and I will not obey your command." Then at that point, in their view, it becomes lawful for him to take what he gave her in exchange for his separating from her.

Those who said this:

4822 - Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: al-Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from his father, who said: al-Hasan said: If she says: "I will not bathe for you from major impurity, I will not fulfil your right of the night, and I will not obey your command," then at that point khul' becomes lawful.

4823 - Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, from al-Hasan, who said: If a woman says to her husband: "I will not fulfil your right of the night, I will not obey your command, I will not bathe for you from major impurity, and I will not establish a limit of the limits of Allah," then it becomes lawful for him to take her property.

4824 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Harun ibn al-Mughira narrated to us, from Anbasa, from Muhammad ibn Salim, who said: I asked al-Sha'bi: When is it lawful for a man to take from his wife's property? He said: When she shows her hatred of him and says: "I will not fulfil your right of the night, and I will not obey your command."

4825 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mughira, from al-Sha'bi, that he used to be surprised at the saying of those who say: Ransom is not lawful until she says: "I will not bathe for you from major impurity." And he said: An adulterer commits adultery, then bathes!

4826 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mughira, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, concerning the rebellious wife, who said: A woman may disobey her husband and then obey him, but if she disobeys him and does not fulfil his right of the night, then at that point the ransom becomes lawful.

4827 - Musa narrated to me, saying: [[In the printed edition: "Yunus narrated to me," which is a pure error; the correct reading is from the manuscript, and it is in addition a recurring isnad in the tafsir that is not disputed about.]] Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿And it is not lawful for you to take anything of what you have given them﴾: it is not lawful for him to take anything of her dower = ﴿unless both fear that they will not keep within the limits of Allah﴾. So if they do not keep within the limits of Allah, then the ransom becomes lawful for him, and that is that she says: "By Allah, I will not fulfil your right of the night, I will not obey your command, I will not honour myself for you, and I will not bathe for you from major impurity." That is the limits of Allah. So if the woman says that, the ransom becomes lawful for the husband to take it and divorce her.

4828 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us, saying: Anbasa narrated to us, from Ali ibn Badhima, from Muqsim, concerning His saying: ﴿And do not restrain them to take back part of what you have given them, unless they commit a clear immorality﴾ (4:19), in the reading of Ibn Mas'ud. He said: If she disobeys you and harms you, then what you took from her has become lawful for you. [[The report: 4828. This report will come later with its text and isnad in the tafsir of surah al-Nisa' (4: 212, Bulaq edition). It was in the manuscript and printed edition here: "...bi-ba'di ma ataytumuhunna yaqulu illa an yafhusha" (some of what you gave them, he says, unless she commits immorality), with the addition of "yaqulu" (he says) from the copyists, and the correct reading is from that passage of the tafsir of the verse of al-Nisa'. There it reads: "idh 'adalatka wa adhatka" (when she disobeyed you and harmed you), and the correct reading is what is here.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 229 (part 4 of 7):

4829 - Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿And it is not lawful for you to take anything of what you have given them﴾, he said: this is khul' (divorce initiated by the wife through compensation). He said: "It is not lawful for him except that the woman says: 'I will not fulfil his right of sexual intimacy and I will not obey his command,' and so he accepts it out of fear that if he keeps her he will mistreat her and transgress the right." [[In the printed edition: "or transgress the right" (aw yata'adda al-haqq); the correct reading from the manuscript is as given.]]
* *
Others said: rather, "the fear" in this is that she initiates to him with her tongue that she dislikes him.
Those who said this:
4830 - Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Hakam al-Misri narrated to us, saying: my father and Shu'ayb ibn al-Layth narrated to us, from al-Layth, from Ayyub ibn Musa, from 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah, who said: khul' is permissible when the woman says to her husband: "I truly dislike you, and I do not love you, and I have feared that I will sleep beside you without fulfilling your right" — and she is content with the khul' (lit. her soul is pleased with the khul'). [[In the printed edition: "wa-tatibu nafsuka" (your soul is pleased), a clear error; the correct reading from the manuscript is as given. It means that the woman says this to the man and then she herself is content with the khul'.]]
* *
Others said: what permits him to take the ransom is that there be a fear that neither of the two will keep the limits of God, both of them disliking the companionship of the other.
Those who said this:
4831 - Humayd ibn Mas'ada narrated to us, saying: Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Dawud narrated to us, from 'Amir. — Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayya narrated to us, from Dawud, who said: 'Amir said: "It is lawful for him to take her property because of his disobedience and her disobedience."
4832 - Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayya narrated to us, saying: Ibn Jurayj said, Tawus said: "The ransom is lawful for him according to what God, may He be exalted, said. He did not say what the foolish say: 'I will not fulfil your right of sexual intimacy.' Rather, the ransom is lawful for him according to what God, may He be exalted, said: ﴿unless they both fear that they will not keep the limits of God﴾, regarding what God has obligated for each of them toward the other in marital life and companionship."
4833 - Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayya narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, who said: I heard al-Qasim ibn Muhammad say: ﴿unless they both fear that they will not keep the limits of God﴾ — he said: "regarding what God has obligated upon them in marital life and companionship."
4834 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: al-Layth narrated to me, saying: Ibn Shihab narrated to me, saying: Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab informed me, saying: "Khul' is not lawful until both fear that they will not keep the limits of God in the marital life that is between them."
* *
Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of these sayings is the saying of those who said: it is not lawful for a man to take a ransom from his wife for his separation from her until there is fear of disobedience to God from each of them regarding their own soul — in neglecting what is obligatory upon him toward his companion — from both of them together, according to what we have reported from Tawus and al-Hasan, and whoever said what they said. This is because God, may He be exalted, only permitted the husband to take a ransom from his wife when the Muslims fear for the two of them that they will not keep the limits of God.
* *
If someone says: If the matter is as you have described, then it must be unlawful for the man to accept the ransom from her when the rebellion (nushuz) comes from her alone and not from him, unless he too has the same dislike for her as she has for him. It is said to him: The matter in this is contrary to what you supposed. In her rebellion against him there is a motive for him to fall short in her due and to requite her with harm for her conduct toward him, and that is the meaning that makes the Muslims fear for the two of them that they will not keep the limits of God. As for when the neglect by each of them of the right of the other has already occurred, and bad companionship and marital life have become apparent to the Muslims, then there is no place for fear, since what was feared has already occurred. Fear is only of a thing before it happens; after it has happened, there is no sense in fearing it or in adding to its harm. [[This is from understanding and insight into human nature; God has taught Abu Ja'far how to speak in the exegesis of the Book and how to derive proof for the correct view from every angle, where the clarification is subtle and difficult for one whom God has not granted understanding and perception.]]
* *
The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿But if you fear that they will not keep the limits of God﴾
Abu Ja'far said: The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of His words, exalted is He: "But if you fear that they will not keep the limits of God" — the limits which, if it is feared that the husband and wife will not keep them, make the ransom lawful for him because of the fear for them that they will neglect them. [[In the printed edition: "bi-sun'iha" (by her conduct), which is meaningless here; the manuscript has the unpointed word, which should be read as "tadyi'iha" (their neglecting it), the object of the verbal noun "al-khawf" (fear), meaning: because of the fear for them that they will neglect the limits of God.]] Some of them said: it is the woman's contempt for her husband's right and her bad obedience to him and her harming him with speech.
Those who said this:
4835 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿But if you fear that they will not keep the limits of God, there is no blame on them concerning what she gives up for it﴾ — he said: it is her abandonment of keeping the limits of God, and her contempt for her husband's right, [[In the printed edition: "wa-istikhfafiha" with an extra waw; the correct reading is from the manuscript, and it is an explanation of his words "her abandonment of keeping the limits of God," as if he came back and said: "and her abandonment of keeping the limits of God is her contempt..."]] and her bad temper; so she says to him: "By God, I will not fulfil your right of sexual intimacy, nor will I lie down for you, nor will I obey your command." If she does that, then the ransom becomes lawful for him from her.
4836 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Abi ibn Abi Za'ida narrated to us, from Yazid ibn Ibrahim, from al-Hasan regarding His words: ﴿But if you fear that they will not keep the limits of God, there is no blame on them concerning what she gives up for it﴾, he said: "If she says: 'I will not bathe for you from impurity,' it becomes lawful for him to take from her." [[The narrator: Yazid ibn Ibrahim al-Tustari, Abu Sa'id al-Basri al-Tamimi, narrated from al-Hasan, Ibn Sirin, Ibn Abi Mulayka, 'Ata' and Qatada, and others. Narrated from him Waki', Bahz ibn Asad, Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi, Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi and others. He is trustworthy and firm, among the middle companions of al-Hasan and Ibn Sirin. Died in 161 AH.]]
4837 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Habban ibn Musa narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, saying: Yunus narrated to us, from al-Zuhri who said: "Khul' becomes lawful when they both fear that they will not keep the limits of God, and the fulfilment of the limits of God in the marital life that is between them."
* *
Others said: the meaning of that is: "But if you fear that they will not obey God."
Those who said this:
4838 - Sufyan ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to us, from Isra'il, from 'Amir: ﴿But if you fear that they will not keep the limits of God﴾ — he said: that they will not obey God.
4839 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas who said: "The limits are obedience."
* *
Abu Ja'far said: The correct statement regarding this is: "But if you fear that they will not keep the limits of God" — that is, the obligations God imposed upon them, in what each of them is bound to the other, in good treatment in marriage and good companionship. So there is no blame on them concerning what she gives up for it. [[In the printed edition: "in fa khiftum an la yuqimu hudud Allah ma awjab Allah" with the extra words "hudud Allah" between the two halves of the sentence; the correct reading from the manuscript is as given.]]
This includes what we have reported from Ibn 'Abbas and al-Sha'bi, and what we have reported from al-Hasan and al-Zuhri, because among what is obligatory for the husband upon the wife is obeying him in what God has made obedience to him obligatory, and that she should not harm him with speech, and should not refuse him when he calls her for his need. If she opposes what God commanded her in this, then she has neglected the limits of God which He commanded her to keep. [[In the printed edition: "amara biidamatiha" (commanded her to sustain them), followed by "amma ma'na idamat hudud Allah," which is a clear error in this place.]]
* *
As for the meaning of "keeping the limits of God," it is acting upon them, adhering to them, and abandoning their neglect — and we have already explained this earlier in this book with what indicates its correctness. [[See what has passed in the interpretation of "establishing the prayer," 1:241, and "the limits of God," 3:546, 547.]]
* *
The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿there is no blame on them concerning what she gives up for it﴾
Abu Ja'far said: By His words, may He be exalted and remembered, He means: "But if you, O believers, fear that the spouses will not keep what God has set as limits for each of them toward the other, and what He has imposed upon each of them as obligation, and you fear for them the neglect of God's obligation and the transgression of His limits in that, then there is no blame on them concerning what the woman gives up for herself from her husband, nor any sin on them" — in what she gives for her husband's separating from her, and nor on him regarding what he takes from her of compensation and payment for it. [[In the manuscript: "'ala muwafiq zawjiha iyyaha," an unpointed word that was probably "'ala mufaraqat" (on separation), then corrupted by a copyist. What is in the printed edition is also acceptable.]]
* *
If someone says: Would the woman be sinful if the harm came from the man against her, regarding what she gives up for herself, so that "there is no blame on them" would apply to her giving of the ransom for her separation from him when the rebellion is from her side? [[In the manuscript and printed edition: "hatta iftadat" (until she ransomed), which does not fit the context of the verse; what the context indicates is "fima iftadat" (regarding what she ransomed), as I have written. The sense of the context is: "Would the woman be sinful... regarding what she ransomed herself with, if the harm came from the man against her?"
As for his word "harijah" (sinful), it means: sinful. It has already passed that I annotated Abu Ja'far's and al-Baqillani's use of this description and that it is correct even though the lexicographers consider it an error; see what has passed, 2:423 note 1; then this part 4:224 note 1; also p. 475 note 2; and what will come on this page and the following pages.]]
It is said: If you knew that in a state of his harm to her, aiming to take from her what he had given her, his harm is only to take from her what God has forbidden him to take in the manner which God forbade him from taking it from her, and then you supposed that she could refrain from giving him that without harm to herself in her person, or her religion, or a right of hers she fears being lost — then it would not be lawful for her to give him that, except with good pleasure on her part in giving him what it is lawful for him to take from her. Because if she gives him what it is not lawful for him to take from her, while she is able to prevent him from that without harm to herself in her person, her religion, or a right of hers she fears losing, then she has shared with him in the sin by giving him what it is not lawful for him to take from her in the manner in which she gave it. Therefore the blame is lifted from her when the rebellion came from her side, and she gave him what she gave as ransom with good pleasure, seeking thereby her safety and his safety from burden and sin. [[In the printed edition: "fa-kadhalika wada'a al-junah," which is an error; the correct reading is from the manuscript.]]
And she, if she gives him in this manner, seeking the reward and recompense from God, may He be exalted, is more deserving, God willing, of being free from blame and fault. [[The sentence structure: "wa-hiya... bi-istihqaq al-ajr... awla min al-junah wa-al-haraj."]] For this reason God, may He be remembered, said: "there is no blame on them," removing the fault from her regarding what she gave in this manner as ransom for his separating from her, and from him regarding what he received from her, since she was giving in the sense we have described, and he was receiving what she gave without harm, but seeking safety for himself and for her in their religions and avoiding burdens and sins. [[In the manuscript: "talab al-salama li-nafsihi wa-laha fi awraliha," unpointed and unclear; I kept what is in the printed edition since it matches the context.]]
It may also be that His words "there is no blame on them" bear another interpretation: that if she gives what she gives as ransom in a manner other than the one the Prophet ﷺ permitted for the wife of Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas — namely, her dislike of her husband's character or his ugliness of disposition, and similar matters people dislike in one another — but rather she turns away from him to another man in a corrupt way that is not lawful for her, it would be forbidden for her to give anything in exchange for his separating from her in that manner, because her asking him for separation in that manner is disobedience on her part. [[In the printed edition: "ma'siyatun minha li-Allah" with an added phrase; I kept the manuscript reading.]] And she is the one who seeks khul' in this manner, whom the Prophet ﷺ is reported to have called "a hypocrite," as:

4840 - Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: al-Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman narrated to me, from Layth, from Abu Idris, from Thawban, freed slave of the Messenger of God ﷺ, from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "Any woman who asks her husband for divorce without any hardship, God has forbidden her the scent of Paradise." [[The hadith: Layth is Ibn Abi Sulaym. Abu Idris is al-Khawlani 'A'idh Allah ibn 'Abd Allah, a trustworthy senior Successor and early jurist. Layth did not hear this hadith from him, as appears from the following chain, where there are two narrations between them.]]

The hadith is in reality two hadiths, and the takhrij (tracing of sources) of each will follow. He said: "The *mukhtal'at* (women who seek khul', divorce by the wife's payment) are the hypocrite women."

4841 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Muzahim ibn Dawud ibn Aliyyah narrated to us, from his father, from Layth ibn Abi Sulaym, from Abu al-Khattab, from Abu Zur'ah, from Abu Idris, from Thawban, the freedman of the Messenger of Allah, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who said: "The *mukhtal'at* are the hypocrite women."

[Note on hadith 4841: Muzahim ibn Dawud ibn Aliyyah (written "Ibn Dawud ibn Alayya" in some sources): at least good in hadith (hasan al-hadith). Indeed he is reliable (thiqah). Abu Hatim said: "His hadith is written down but not used as proof." Al-Nasa'i said: "There is no harm in him." Al-Bukhari included him in al-Kabir (4/2/23) and mentioned no criticism of him.
His father, Dawud ibn Alayya: his biography has already passed in the commentary at no. 851.
Abu al-Khattab: Ibn Abi Hatim recorded him (4/2/365) and asked his father about him, and he said: "He is unknown (majhul)." He asked Abu Zur'ah, who said: "I do not know him." Al-Bukhari mentioned him in al-Kuna (no. 220) and mentioned no criticism of him, so he is at least good in hadith.
Abu Zur'ah: the Hafiz (Ibn Hajar) in al-Tahdhib, in the biography of Abu al-Khattab (12: 86-87), preferred that he is "Abu Zur'ah ibn 'Amr ibn Jarir," the reliable Successor (tabi'i), following Ibn Mandah and Ibn 'Abd al-Barr, and he noted that they were followed in this by Ibn Abi Hatim, who said in the biography of Abu al-Khattab that he "narrated from Abu Zur'ah ibn 'Amr ibn Jarir." Ibn Abi Hatim indeed said that, but the Hafiz overlooked that Ibn Abi Hatim retracted it in the biography of "Abu Zur'ah" alone without a lineage (4/2/374), where he mentioned that he narrated from Abu Idris from Thawban, and that Abu al-Khattab narrated from him. He mentioned that he asked his father: "Who is this Abu Zur'ah?" and he said: "Unknown." Al-Bukhari also mentioned him in al-Kuna (no. 283) and mentioned no criticism of him either.
The hadith was narrated by al-Tirmidhi (2: 216-217) from Abu Kurayb, the teacher of al-Tabari here, with this isnad.
He then said: "This is a gharib (singular) hadith from this route, and its isnad is not strong."
See the two following hadiths: 4843, 4844.]

4842 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Hafs ibn Bishr narrated to us, saying: Qays ibn al-Rabi' narrated to us, from Ash'ath ibn Sawwar, from al-Hasan, from Thabit ibn Yazid, from 'Uqbah ibn 'Amir al-Juhani, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Indeed, the *mukhtal'at* and the *muntaza'at* are the hypocrite women."

[Note on hadith 4842: Hafs ibn Bishr: I have not found a biography of him except in Ibn Abi Hatim (1/2/170), who said: "He narrated from Ya'qub al-Qummi; Abu Kurayb narrated from him." He mentioned no criticism of him.
Qays ibn al-Rabi' al-Asadi al-Kufi: disputed (mukhtalaf fihi), and we preferred to consider him reliable in al-Musnad (661, 7115). He was declared reliable by al-Thawri, Shu'bah and others. Al-Hasan: this is al-Basri.
Thabit ibn Yazid: this is how it is here, and in Ibn Kathir, quoting al-Tabari. I could not be certain about anything concerning him, for among the men of the Six Books there is no one with this name in this generation, the generation of the Successors from whom al-Hasan al-Basri narrated.
There is "Thabit ibn Yazid al-Khawlani": al-Bukhari recorded him in al-Kabir (1/2/172) and Ibn Abi Hatim (1/1/459-460). He narrates from Ibn 'Umar, and some have said "from his paternal cousin, from Ibn 'Umar," and this is the correct version, since this man is somewhat later. It is possible that he is the one here. The Hafiz recorded him in Lisan al-Mizan (2: 80), describing him as "al-Misri" (the Egyptian), and mentioned that he narrated from Abu Hurayrah and from Ibn 'Abbas, and that Ibn Hibban recorded him in al-Thiqat. It is well known that 'Uqbah ibn 'Amir was governor of Egypt in the years 44-47 AH by appointment of Mu'awiyah, and he lived there until he died and was buried at al-Muqattam, may Allah be pleased with him. His death is dated to the year 58 AH. So his time is close to the death of Abu Hurayrah and Ibn 'Abbas.
There is another man whose lineage was not mentioned, recorded under the name "Thabit al-Ta'ifi" in al-Bukhari (1/2/165) and Ibn Abi Hatim (1/1/461). Both of them mentioned that he "saw Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah come to 'Uqbah ibn 'Amir" and asked him about a hadith.
The hadith was transmitted by Ibn Kathir (1: 540) from al-Tabari, and he did not attribute it to anyone else. He said: "Gharib from this route, da'if (weak)." Al-Suyuti also mentioned it (1: 283) and did not attribute it to anyone other than al-Tabari.
Al-Haythami also mentioned it in Majma' al-Zawa'id, vol. 5, p. 5, and said: "It was narrated by al-Tabarani, and in its isnad is Qays ibn al-Rabi', who was declared reliable by al-Thawri and Shu'bah, but there is weakness in him. The rest of its narrators are narrators of the Sahih." Thus he said! I do not know whether he erred or was correct. If the isnad of al-Tabarani above Qays ibn al-Rabi' is like the isnad of al-Tabari, then it is a strange error, for Thabit ibn Yazid is not known as we see! And there is no one among the narrators of the Sahih by this name except "Thabit ibn Yazid al-Ahwal," from whom the authors of the Six Books narrated, but he is much later than this generation; he died in 169 AH, that is, more than a hundred and ten years after 'Uqbah ibn 'Amir and about sixty years after al-Hasan al-Basri.
As for his saying "al-muntaza'at": the apparent meaning is the same as that of "al-mukhtal'at," as if they tear themselves away from the marriage contract and from the husband's authority over them. This word stands thus in all the sources for this hadith, except the manuscript of al-Tabari, in which it is "al-mutabarri'at" (?), and this has no meaning in this context, so it is a tashif (scribal distortion).
There is a hadith with this meaning containing a word close to this one: Abu Nu'aym narrated it in al-Hilyah 8: 375-376, by way of Muhammad ibn Harun al-Hadrami, Abu Hamid, from al-Husayn ibn 'Ali ibn al-Aswad al-'Ijli, from Waki', from al-Thawri, from al-A'mash, from Abu Wa'il, from 'Abd Allah (who is Ibn Mas'ud), as a marfu' (traced to the Prophet): "The *mukhtal'at* and the *mutabarrijat* (women who display their adornment) are the hypocrite women." So this word "*mutabarrijat*" may be a distortion of "*muntaza'at*," for I do not trust the edition of the book al-Hilyah. An additional error occurred in the isnad of this very hadith in it, where it reads "Hadathana Fulayh" in place of "Hadathana Waki'"! Whereas Abu Nu'aym's remark after it indicates the correct reading, for he said: "Gharib from the hadith of al-A'mash and al-Thawri; Waki' alone transmitted it."
This very hadith, I mean the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud, was narrated by al-Khatib in Tarikh Baghdad 3: 358, in the biography of "Abu Hamid Muhammad ibn Harun," by way of al-Daraqutni, from Muhammad ibn Harun, from Husayn ibn 'Ali ibn al-Aswad, from Waki', with this isnad, as a marfu': "The *mukhtal'at* are the hypocrite women," without mention of "*al-mutabarrijat*." Al-Khatib said: "Al-Hasan told me: al-Daraqutni said: No one narrated it except Abu Hamid."
The most authentic of all these reports is what Ahmad narrated in al-Musnad 9347 (2: 414, Halabi) from the hadith of al-Hasan, from Abu Hurayrah, as a marfu': "The *mukhtal'at* and the *muntaza'at* are the hypocrite women." It is a sahih (sound) hadith. We have demonstrated its soundness and explained at length its takhrij in al-Musnad, in the commentary on hadith 7138, vol. 12, pp. 114-116.]

4843 - Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us = and Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us = both of them said together: Ayyub narrated to us, from Abu Qilabah, from one who narrated to him, from Thawban: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Any woman who asks her husband for divorce without any need, the fragrance of Paradise is forbidden to her."

[Note on hadith 4843: In this isnad there is an unknown narrator, and it has become clear from the following isnad that he is "Abu Asma' al-Rahabi." Thus Ahmad narrated it in al-Musnad 5: 277 (Halabi) from Ibn 'Ulayyah, with this isnad. Likewise al-Tirmidhi narrated it (2: 217) from Muhammad ibn Bashshar, from 'Abd al-Wahhab al-Thaqafi, with it. This is the first route of al-Tabari here in this isnad. Al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a hasan hadith."]

4844 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: 'Arim narrated to us, saying: Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us, from Ayyub, from Abu Qilabah, from Abu Asma' al-Rahabi, from Thawban, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, something similar.

[Note on hadith 4844: This is a sahih isnad. Abu Asma' al-Rahabi is 'Amr ibn Marthad al-Dimashqi, and he is a reliable Successor.
The hadith was narrated by Ahmad in al-Musnad 5: 283 (Halabi) from 'Abd al-Rahman (who is Ibn Mahdi), from Hammad ibn Zayd.
It was also narrated by Abu Dawud (2226) from Sulayman ibn Harb; Ibn Majah (2055), by way of Muhammad ibn al-Fadl; al-Hakim (2: 200), by way of Sulayman ibn Harb; and al-Bayhaqi (7: 316) from al-Hakim, by way of Ibn Harb — all from Hammad ibn Zayd with this isnad. Al-Hakim said: "This is a sahih hadith according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim), though they did not narrate it." Al-Dhahabi agreed with him.
Al-Bayhaqi also narrated it (7: 316) by way of Musa ibn Isma'il al-Tabudhaki, from Wuhayb, from Ayyub, with it. This too is a sahih isnad.
The Hafiz mentioned it in al-Fath (9: 354) and said: "The authors of the Sunan narrated it, and Ibn Khuzaymah and Ibn Hibban declared it sahih."
Al-Tirmidhi pointed to it after the previous isnad that contained the unidentified narrator, saying: "This hadith is also narrated from Ayyub, from Abu Qilabah, from Abu Asma', from Thawban."]

* *

If there are ways by which a woman frees herself from her husband in which she becomes liable to blame, and in her ransoming herself from him there is blame and sin upon her for that; and among its ways there are some in which the blame and sin fall upon the man but not upon the woman, and some in which neither of them incurs blame or sin — then it is said: the way in which neither of them incurs blame, there is no sin upon them in it [[in the printed and manuscript edition: "la junah" without the conjunction waw, and the correct reading is what I have recorded]], since in what they both intended and aimed at, namely their separation through the compensation that the woman gave to her husband, [it is] "there is no sin upon them both in what she ransoms herself with," in the manner that was permitted to them, and that is, that they both fear that they will not keep the limits of Allah in their conduct toward each other.

* *

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: Some people of Arabic grammar have claimed that in this there are two aspects: [[The one who claimed this is al-Farra' in Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1: 147-148. What al-Tabari transmitted is an abridgement of al-Farra's statement.]] One of them is that it means: "there is no sin upon the man for what the woman ransoms herself with," not upon the woman, even though both have been mentioned together, as He said in "Surat al-Rahman": ﴿From them come forth the pearl and the coral﴾ [Surat al-Rahman: 22], while they are from the salt water and not from the sweet water. He said: "Similar to this is: ﴿So when they reached the meeting-place of the two seas, they forgot their fish﴾ [Surat al-Kahf: 61], whereas the one who forgot was only the companion of Musa." He said: "Similar to this in speech is when you say: 'I have two riding animals; I ride them and draw water with them,' whereas you only ride one of them and draw water with the other [[in the printed edition: "wa-asqa... wa-tusqa," and the correct reading is from the manuscript and the Ma'ani al-Qur'an of al-Farra']]. This is from the breadth of the Arabic language, by whose breadth it is argued in speech."
They said: The other aspect is that both of them share in there being no sin upon them, since she gives what the husband has been cleared of sin in. She has shared in it [[in Ma'ani al-Qur'an: "ashraka fihi," in the passive form, and it is the better reading]], for when she gives what removes the sin from him, she needs something similar.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: He did not hit the correct view in either of the two aspects, nor in his argument from His words: [[In the manuscript and the printed edition: "ihtajja bihi qawluhu," and the correct reading is with the addition of "min"]] ﴿From them come forth the pearl and the coral﴾.
As for His words "there is no sin upon them both," we have already shown its correct sense, and we will show the meaning of His words "From them comes forth the pearl and the coral" in its place, when we come to it, if Allah the Exalted wills. We only rejected his statement because Allah the Exalted has informed us that He removed blame from the spouses if the woman ransoms herself from her husband in the manner He permitted, and He informed us about the two seas that from them comes forth the pearl and the coral, and He attributed it to two. So if someone could say: "It is intended as a report about one of them, in what is not impossible for it to apply to both of them," then it would be permissible in every report that concerns two, whose truth is not impossible to apply to both, to say: "It is a report about only one of them."
That is an inversion of the meaning of human speech and of its familiar usage in their communication, and it is not permissible to interpret the Book of Allah and His revelation, may He be exalted, as rare usages, when it has a sound and existing meaning according to what is customary among people.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: Then the people of ta'wil (exegesis) differed regarding the interpretation of His words: "there is no sin upon them both in what she ransoms herself with." Does He mean by it that the blame is lifted from both of them in everything the woman ransoms herself with, or in some of it?

Some of them said: He meant by it: "there is no sin upon them both in what she ransoms herself with" from her dower (sadaq) which her husband had given her, from whom she seeks khul'. They argued for their view that the end of the verse refers back to its beginning, and that the meaning of the speech is: "It is not lawful for you to take anything of what you have given them, except that they both fear that they will not keep the limits of Allah. So if you fear that they will not keep the limits of Allah, then there is no sin upon them both in what she ransoms herself with of what you have given them." They said: So what Allah permitted them of that, when they fear that they will not keep the limits of Allah, is what had been forbidden to them before the state of their fear of that. They argued for this by the story of Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas, and that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ only commanded his wife, when she was disobedient (nashazat) toward him, that she return what Thabit had given her as dower, and that she offered an increase, but the Prophet ﷺ did not accept it.

[[The report: 4845 — Al-Tabari's refutation of what al-Rabi' said and his addition to the verse of what is not part of it will come on pp. 582-583.]]

* *

Others said: rather, by this he meant: "there is no blame upon either of them regarding what she ransoms herself with, whether little or much of what she owns." They based their view on the generality of the verse, and held that it is not permissible to turn an apparent general ruling into a particular inner meaning except by a proof to which submission is obligatory. They said: "There is no proof to which submission is obligatory that the verse intends only part of the ransom rather than part of it, whether from a source text or by analogy. So it stands on its apparent and general meaning."

Mention of those who said this:

4860 - Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim related to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah related to us, saying: Ayyub informed us, from Kathir, the client of Samurah: that 'Umar was brought a woman who was defiant (nashiz), so he ordered her to be placed in a house full of dung for three days. Then he summoned her and said: "How did you find it?" She said: "I have found no comfort since I was with him, except these nights in which you have held me!" So he said to her husband: "Divorce her by khul', even if it is for her earring."

[Report 4860: al-Bayhaqi 7:315, and al-Muhalla 10:240. His words "even if it is for her earring" mean: even if she has no property other than her earring, take it and divorce her.]

4861 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Ayyub, from Kathir, the client of Samurah, who said: 'Umar ibn al-Khattab took a defiant woman, admonished her, but she did not accept good counsel, so he confined her in a house full of dung for three days. [He] mentioned something similar to the report of Ibn 'Ulayyah.

4862 - Ibn Bashshar and Muhammad ibn Yahya related to us, both saying: 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, from Humayd ibn 'Abd al-Rahman: that a woman came to 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) and complained about her husband. He said: "Is she defiant?" So he had her spend the night in the dung house. When morning came, he said to her: "How did you find your place?" She said: "I was never with him for a night more pleasing to my eyes than this night!" So he said: "Take even her hair-braid."

[Report 4862: "Humayd ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf al-Zuhri" narrated from his father, 'Umar, 'Uthman, Abu Hurayrah, Ibn 'Abbas and others. His son 'Abd al-Rahman, al-Zuhri, Qatadah and others narrated from him. It is said: "He did not see 'Umar nor heard anything from him," and his death date indicates this, though he may have heard from 'Uthman since he was his maternal uncle. He was trustworthy and narrated much. He died in 95 AH at the age of seventy-three. Ibn Sa'd said: "I heard someone say he died in 105 AH." Ibn Hajar said: "This is the view of al-Fallas, Ahmad ibn Hanbal and Abu Ishaq al-Harbi," then he said: "Even if it is correct, based on the accuracy of what is said about his age, his narration from 'Umar is definitely disconnected (munqati'), and likewise from 'Uthman and his father, and Allah knows best."

Al-'Iqas: a thread with which a woman ties the ends of her braids. From "'aqasat al-mar'ah sha'raha" (the woman braided her hair) when she plaited it. The plait is the 'aqisah. Al-'Iqas also means al-madari (plural) or al-midri (singular). The midri is an object made of iron or wood, shaped like a tooth of a comb but longer, used to comb tangled hair, which is used by someone who has no comb. It appears in the poetry of Imru' al-Qays: "His tresses bristling upward to the heights... the braid-thread goes astray in folded and loose [strands]." It is also narrated as "yadill al-'iqas" with the meaning of the singular. See the note on report 4871.

4863 - Nasr ibn 'Ali related to us, saying: 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: 'Ubayd Allah related to us, from Nafi': that a client-woman of Safiyyah sought khul' from her husband with everything she owned except her clothes, and Ibn 'Umar did not object to that.

[Report 4863: Muwatta' 565, al-Muhalla 10:240, al-Bayhaqi 7:315, and what will come as report 4874 and others.]

4864 - Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la and Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna related to us, both saying: Mu'tamir related to us, saying: I heard 'Ubayd Allah narrate, from Nafi', who said: It was mentioned to Ibn 'Umar that a client-woman of his sought khul' from her husband with all her property, and he did not find fault with her for that nor denounce it.

4865 - Yahya ibn Talhah al-Yarbu'i related to me, saying: Hushaym related to us, from Humayd, from Raja' ibn Haywah, from Qabisah ibn Dhu'ayb: that he did not see any harm in taking from her more than she had given him. Then he recited this verse: "There is no blame upon them for what she ransoms herself with."

4866 - Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from al-Mughirah, from Ibrahim, who said regarding khul': "Take what is less than the braid of her hair, and indeed a woman may ransom herself with part of her property."

[Reports 4866-4869: Ibn al-Athir mentioned this report in al-Nihayah with different wording, saying: "In the hadith of al-Nakha'i: khul' is a divorce that is irrevocable, and it is what is less than the braid of the head." He means: the divorcee who seeks khul' has the right to take what is less than her hair from all her wealth. Thus in al-Nihayah, and in Lisan al-'Arab's quotation from it: "what is less than her hair." The interpretation of "'iqas" here as "hair" is very strange, and I do not know whether so great a scholar as Ibn al-Athir could confuse things like this. Perhaps the meaning of Ibrahim al-Nakha'i's words in the following reports, "Take from her even her braid," is: take from her even her hair! Perhaps there is a lacuna in the text, making it: "to take what is less than the tie of her hair." But the Lisan's quotation of the text of al-Nihayah is a doubt in favour of this view. It seems Ibn al-Athir overlooked the meaning of "dun" (less than) in this context, and so a great scholar slipped. His words "what is less than the braid of her hair" mean: what is less than the braid or lesser than it. See the following report 4870, for its wording contains the cure for this meaning, God willing.]

Others said: this verse is abrogated by His saying: ﴿And if you desire to exchange one wife for another, and you have given one of them a heap of gold, take not from it anything﴾ [Surah an-Nisa': 20].

Ma'n ibn 'Isa narrated from him. I heard my father say so," said by Ibn Abi Hatim.]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of these views is the view of the one who said: if it is feared from the man and the woman that they will not keep the limits of Allah, in the manner we have already explained, then there is no blame upon the two of them regarding what the woman ransoms herself with from her husband, whether little or much of what she owns that it is permissible for Muslims to own, even if it takes all of her property. For Allah, may His mention be exalted, did not restrict what He permitted them in that to a limit that may not be exceeded, but rather He stated it absolutely in whatever she ransoms herself with. However, I choose for the husband, as a recommendation and not as an obligation, that when it is clear that her seeking ransom from him is not disobedience to Allah, but rather out of fear for her religion, he should separate from her without ransom or compensation. If he is stingy with that, then what he takes from her should not reach all that he gave her.

* *

As for what Bakr ibn 'Abd Allah said, that this ruling in the whole verse is abrogated by His saying: ﴿And if you desire to exchange one wife for another, and you have given one of them a heap of gold, take not from it anything﴾, this is a view without meaning. We will occupy ourselves with clarifying his error for two reasons. The first: the consensus of all the Companions, the Successors and those after them among the Muslims, on the error of this view and on the permissibility of taking ransom from the woman herself for her husband. That is enough, so there is no need to prove his error by other means.

The second: the verse in Surah an-Nisa' only forbids the husband from taking anything of what he gave her, when the man desires to exchange one wife for another without there being any fear from the Muslims that the two of them will not keep the limits of Allah in their marriage, and without any nushuz (defiance) from the woman against the husband. Given that this is the case, it is established that the husband taking property from his wife by way of coercion and harm to her, until she gives him some of her wealth in exchange for separation, is forbidden, even if it were a single grain of silver or more. [The habbah is a weight in their system: the weight of a medium barley grain not husked, with both ends cut off (Risalat al-Nuqud by al-Maqrizi: 3).]

As for the verse in Surah al-Baqarah, it only indicates Allah's permission to the husband to take ransom from her in the situation of fear that the two will not keep the limits of Allah, due to the woman's nushuz and her seeking separation and the man's desire for her. So the command that Allah permitted the husband in taking ransom from the woman in Surah al-Baqarah is the opposite of the command for which He forbade taking ransom in Surah an-Nisa', just as the prohibition in Surah an-Nisa' is different from the permission and license in Surah al-Baqarah. Two rulings may be said to abrogate one another only when the subject of the rulings is the same, and then the rulings differ because of differing times and periods.

The wisdom and reason of the matter lie in the fact that rulings differ according to the differing meanings of what is being ruled upon, within a single situation and at a single time. This is understood by reason and natural disposition, and it does not fall under abrogation (naskh).

* *

As for what al-Rabi' ibn Anas said, that the meaning of the verse is: "There is no blame upon them for what she gives up to him," meaning by that: from what you have given them, then his claim is like Bakr's claim that the words "There is no blame upon them for what she gives up to him" were abrogated by his words, "And if you have given one of them a heap of gold, take nothing from it." [His claim] was made in respect of something in the Book of God that is not present in the written codices of the Muslims.

It is said to whoever holds his view: some of the imams of the religion whom you know have said that the meaning of that is: "There is no blame upon them for what she gives up to him from her property." So is there any proof by which you can distinguish yourselves from them other than mere assertion? [[In the printed edition it reads "tabayyun tahafutahum" ("their incoherence becomes evident"), from the phrase "bayyana al-shay' yubayyinu" with a doubled yā'. But the meaning does not fit the context of this discussion. In the manuscript it reads "tabayyan minhum" without diacritical dots, so I have read it in the way that best fits the sense of the context. "Bana minhum yabayyinu" means: to separate and be distinguished. The sense is: "Is there any proof that makes a distinction between you and them, other than assertion? They argue that this is the apparent meaning of the verse, while you claim that the verse has a specific application! What proof is there in this that gives you an advantage over them?"]] For they have argued from the apparent wording of the revelation, while you have claimed a specific application for it. Then the argument can be turned back against you, so that whatever position you take on that matter, the same will be required of you in the other case. We have already set out the evidence, with supporting examples, for the correctness of the view of those who say that the husband may take from her everything that the woman who ransoms herself gave him, whom God permitted to ransom herself, in our book *Kitab al-Latif*, and we disliked repeating it in this place.

* *

[[What shows that the copyist of this passage was hasty and not careful, as we have explained from examples of his handwriting, owing to the many errors in his copying, is that he wrote the text of the verse here as "Those are the limits of God, so do not approach them"!!]]

The discussion concerning the interpretation (ta'wil) of His words, exalted is He: ﴿These are the limits of God, so do not transgress them. And whoever transgresses the limits of God, those are the wrongdoers﴾ (2:229).

Abu Ja'far said: By this, exalted is His mention, He means: These are the boundaries of His distinctions, showing what He has made lawful for you and what He has made unlawful for you, O people. So do not transgress what He has made lawful for you, among the matters that He has explained and distinguished for you as lawful, toward what He has made unlawful for you, so that you pass from obedience to Him into disobedience.

By His words, exalted is His mention, "These are the limits of God, so do not transgress them," He means these matters that were explained to you in the verses that preceded: the marriage of idolatrous polytheist women, the giving of Muslim women in marriage to polytheist men, sexual relations with women during menstruation, and what had been explained in the earlier verses before His words "These are the limits of God," of what He made lawful and unlawful for His servants, and what He commanded and forbade.

Then He, exalted is His mention, said to them: These matters, whose lawful from unlawful He has made clear to you, are "My limits," meaning: the boundaries of the distinctions between My obedience and My disobedience. So do not transgress them, meaning: do not go beyond what I have made lawful for you to what I have made unlawful for you, nor from what I have commanded you to what I have forbidden you, nor from My obedience to My disobedience. [[See the meaning of "al-hudud" and "al-ta'addi wa al-'udwan" in the glossary of the earlier volumes.]] For whoever exceeds that, meaning whoever oversteps and passes beyond it to what I have made unlawful for him or forbidden him, then he is indeed the wrongdoer, meaning the one who does what is not his to do and places a thing in other than its proper place. We have already shown the meaning of "injustice" (zulm) and its root in earlier passages with evidence indicating its meaning, and we disliked repeating it in this place. [[See what has passed: 1:523–524; 2:101–102, 369, 519.]]

* *

Those who engaged in interpretation (ta'wil) have said something similar to what we have said on this matter, although the wording of their interpretation differs from our wording, but the meaning of what they said on it [returns] to the meaning of what we have said. [[In the printed edition: "... ma qalu fi dhalika ila ma'na ..." and I have put the addition between brackets because its place in the manuscript is blank; I judged that the missing word was the one I have supplied.]]

Mention of those who said that:

4879 – Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: My father related to me, saying: My paternal uncle related to me, saying: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His words, "These are the limits of God, so do not transgress them": by "the limits" he means obedience.

4880 – Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Ishaq related to us, saying: Abu Zuhayr related to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, concerning His words, "These are the limits of God, so do not transgress them": he says: whoever divorces for other than the waiting period has transgressed and wronged himself. "And whoever transgresses the limits of God, those are the wrongdoers."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: What was related from al-Dahhak has no meaning in this place, because no mention had been made of divorce within the waiting period, so that it could be said "These are the limits of God." Rather, what was mentioned is the number (of divorces) in which the husband has the right of return, and the number in which he does not have that right, without any explanation regarding divorce in the waiting period.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 230 (part 1 of 2):

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So if he divorces her, she is not lawful to him after that until she marries another husband﴾

Abu Ja'far said: The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed about what this statement of God, may His remembrance be exalted, indicates.

Some of them said: It indicates that if a man divorces his wife with the third divorce, after the two divorces about which God, may His remembrance be exalted, said: ﴿The divorce is twice﴾, then that wife is not lawful to him after the third divorce until she marries another husband, meaning other than the one who divorced her.

Mention of those who said this:

4881 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Zurayʿ narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, who said: God made divorce three. If he divorces her once, he has more right to her as long as the waiting period (iddah) has not ended, and her waiting period is three menstrual cycles. If the waiting period ends before he has taken her back, she has been separated from him by one divorce, and she becomes more entitled to herself, and becomes one of the suitors (khatib min al-khitab). So when a man wanted to divorce his wife, he would observe her menstrual cycle, and when she became clean, he would divorce her with one divorce at the beginning of her waiting period, in the presence of two just witnesses. [[The word "qabl ʿiddatiha" (with a damma and then a sukun) means: at the onset of her waiting period and at the start of it.]] If it appeared to him to take her back, he would take her back while she was still in her waiting period. If he left her until her waiting period ended, she had been separated from him by one divorce. If it appeared to him to divorce her after the first divorce while she was still in her waiting period, he would observe her menstrual cycle, and when she became clean, he would divorce her with another divorce at the beginning of her waiting period. If it appeared to him to take her back, he would take her back, and she would remain with him under one divorce. If it appeared to him to divorce her, he would divorce her a third time when she became clean. This is the third divorce about which God, may His remembrance be exalted, said: ﴿Then she is not lawful to him after that until she marries another husband﴾. [[Thus it is in the manuscript: the meaning of the verse, not its wording. But in the printed edition it reads: "Then she is not lawful to him after that until she marries another husband", which quotes the verse's text. It was altered without clear justification.]]

4882 - Al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah ibn Salih narrated to me, from ʿAli ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding His saying: ﴿So if he divorces her, she is not lawful to him after that until she marries another husband﴾, he said: If he divorces her three times, she is not lawful until she marries another husband.

4883 - Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Juwaybir informed us, from al-Dahhak, who said: If he divorces once or twice, he has the right of return as long as the waiting period has not ended. He said: As for the third, His saying: ﴿So if he divorces her﴾, meaning with the third, then he has no right of return to her until she marries another husband.

4884 - Yahya ibn Abi Talib narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Juwaybir informed us, from al-Dahhak, similarly.

4885 - Musa ibn Harun narrated to me, saying: ʿAmr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿So if he divorces her﴾, after the two divorces, ﴿she is not lawful to him after that until she marries another husband﴾, and this is the third.

* *

Others said: Rather, this statement indicates what is required for one who releases his wife in kindness after the two divorces about which God, may His remembrance be exalted, said: ﴿The divorce is twice﴾. They said: God, may His remembrance be exalted, only clarified by this statement the ruling concerning His saying: ﴿or release with kindness﴾. And it means that if a man releases his wife after the two divorces, she who is released in this manner is not lawful to him except after another husband.

Mention of those who said this:

4886 - Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, from ʿIsa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿So if he divorces her, she is not lawful to him after that until she marries another husband﴾, he said: It returns to His saying: ﴿Then either retain with good provision or release with kindness﴾.

4887 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: What Mujahid said about this is, in our view, more correct, because of what we have mentioned from the Messenger of God (ﷺ) in the report we have transmitted from him, that he said, or was asked and it was said: "This is God's statement: ﴿The divorce is twice﴾. Then where is the third?" He said: ﴿Then either retain with good provision or release with kindness﴾. [[Meaning the earlier reports: 4791–4793.]] So he (ﷺ) informed that the third is only His saying: ﴿or release with kindness﴾. Since releasing with kindness is the third, it is known that His saying: ﴿So if he divorces her, she is not lawful to him after that until she marries another husband﴾ is far from indicating the third divorce, and that it is only an explanation of what is lawful to one who releases his wife with kindness after the two divorces, what is forbidden to him from her, and the state in which it is permissible for him to marry her again, and an informing of His servants that after the release, as described, the man has no right of return to his wife. [[Here ends the earlier division from which our copy was transcribed. After it is the following text: "And may God bless Muhammad the Prophet, and his family and companions, abundantly." Because of the copyist's haste, he omitted to copy what he had been copying in earlier passages from the copy's audition (sama').]]

* *

[[The beginning of this division starts with: "In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate."]] Abu Ja'far said: If someone asks: Which of the two marriages did God mean by His saying: ﴿she is not lawful to him after that until she marries another husband﴾: the marriage that is intercourse, or the marriage that is the contract of marriage?

It is said: Both. That is because if a woman marries a man in a marriage contract, and then he does not have intercourse with her in that marriage, and he does not have relations with her until he divorces her, she is not lawful to the first. Likewise, if someone has intercourse with her without a marriage, she is not lawful to the first by the consensus (ijma') of the entire community. [[In the printed edition: "by the consensus of the community," which is weak and has no merit.]] Since this is so, it is known that the interpretation of His saying: ﴿she is not lawful to him after that until she marries another husband﴾ is a valid marriage, in which he then has intercourse with her, and then divorces her.

If he says: Since mention of intercourse does not exist in the Book of God, what is the evidence that its meaning is what you said?

It is said: The evidence for that is the consensus of the entire community that this is its meaning. Moreover, God, may His remembrance be exalted, said: ﴿So if he divorces her, she is not lawful to him after that until she marries another husband﴾. If she married another husband immediately after the divorce, before her waiting period ended, there is no doubt that she would be marrying in a way other than the meaning by which God, may His remembrance be exalted, permitted her to marry. And even if mention of the waiting period is not linked to His saying: ﴿she is not lawful to him after that until she marries another husband﴾, it indicates that this is so by His saying: ﴿And divorced women await by themselves for three periods﴾. Likewise, His saying: ﴿So if he divorces her, she is not lawful to him after that until she marries another husband﴾, even if mention of intercourse, touching, or consummation is not linked to it, indicates that this is so through His revelation to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and his explanation of it on his tongue to His servants.

* *

Mention of the reports transmitted from the Messenger of God (ﷺ) about this.

4888 - ʿUbayd Allah ibn Isma'il al-Hubari, Sufyan ibn Waki', and Abu Hisham al-Rifa'i narrated to me, they said: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, from al-Aswad, from ʿA'ishah, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) was asked about a man who divorced his wife, and she married another man, and he entered upon her, then divorced her before he had relations with her. Is she lawful to her first husband? The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "She is not lawful to her first husband until the second tastes her honey and she tastes his." [[Hadith 4888. This hadith and the ones after it up to 4897 are ten chains for ʿA'ishah's report on the necessity of consummation with a woman divorced three times before she becomes lawful to her first husband. This is a matter agreed upon, established by abundant evidence. The second husband must be desirous of the woman and intend lasting companionship, which is the proper purpose of marriage. But if he marries her and consummates it intending to make her lawful for the first husband, or if that was understood from the actual circumstances, then this is the muhallil (the one who makes lawful) whom the Messenger of God (ﷺ) cursed, and cursed the one for whom he makes it lawful. That second marriage is void, and cohabitation is not made lawful by it.

Then Abu Ja'far narrated after these ten: two hadiths from Abu Hurayrah, one hadith from Anas, one hadith from ʿUbayd Allah ibn ʿAbbas, and three hadiths from Ibn ʿUmar. So they are seventeen hadiths. We will summarize as much as we can in their takhrij (sourcing), God willing.

ʿUbayd Allah ibn Isma'il al-Hubari, the teacher of al-Tabari: his biography has passed under "ʿUbayd" without addition at 2890. Likewise it passed under "ʿUbayd" at 3185 and 3325. He is the same person. In al-Tahdhib 7:59: "It is said that his name is ʿUbayd Allah, and ʿUbayd is a laqab (epithet)."

Abu Hisham al-Rifa'i, the teacher of al-Tabari: he is Muhammad ibn Yazid ibn Muhammad ibn Kathir, judge of Baghdad. Some have spoken against him, and the more likely view is that he is trustworthy, and Muslim narrated from him in his Sahih. His mention has passed at 3286.

Ibrahim: he is Ibn Yazid ibn al-Aswad al-Nakha'i. Al-Aswad: he is Ibn Yazid ibn Qays al-Nakha'i, the maternal uncle of Ibrahim.

The hadith was narrated by Ahmad in al-Musnad 6:42 (Halabi edition) from Abu Mu'awiyah, from al-A'mash, with this chain.

Ibn Kathir cited it at 1:549 from al-Tabari's narration, then said: "Likewise Abu Dawud narrated it from Musaddad, and al-Nasa'i from Abu Kurayb, both from Abu Mu'awiyah."

al-Suyuti mentioned it at 1:284 and added its attribution to Ibn Abi Shaybah and Ibn Majah.

His saying: "until the second tastes her honey…" Ibn al-Athir said: "He likened the pleasure of intercourse to tasting honey, and he used for it the metaphor of tasting. He used the feminine form because he meant a portion of honey. It is also said: because of giving it the meaning of a drop of semen. It is also said: honey originally may be masculine or feminine, and whoever diminutivizes it as feminine says 'ʿusaylah'… and he diminutivized it to indicate the small amount by which the lawfulness is achieved."]]

4889 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Suwayd ibn Nasr narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Hisham ibn ʿUrwah, from his father, from ʿA'ishah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), similarly. [[Hadith 4889: Muslim narrated it at 1:407 in similar wording via Abu Usamah from Hisham ibn ʿUrwah from his father. Ahmad narrated it in al-Musnad 6:229 (Halabi) from Abu Mu'awiyah from Hisham. Muslim also narrated it via Ibn Fudayl and via Abu Mu'awiyah, both from Hisham.

Ibn Kathir cited it at 1:549 from Sahih Muslim, and mentioned that al-Bukhari narrated it via Abu Mu'awiyah.

Then he said: Thus Ibn Jarir narrated it via ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Mubarak from Hisham ibn ʿUrwah from his father from ʿA'ishah, traced to the Prophet (marfu'), similarly or like it. This is a good chain."]]

4890 - Sufyan ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Ibn ʿUyaynah narrated to us, from al-Zuhri, from ʿUrwah, from ʿA'ishah, who said: I heard her say: The wife of Rifa'ah al-Qurazi came to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and said: "I was with Rifa'ah, and he divorced me, finishing my divorce (batta talaqi). Then I married ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn al-Zubayr, and with him is only like the fringe of a garment." He said to her: "Do you want to return to Rifa'ah? No, until you taste his honey and he tastes yours." [[Hadith 4890: Ahmad narrated it in al-Musnad 6:37–38 (Halabi) from Sufyan ibn ʿUyaynah with this chain, and he added at its end the words of Khalid ibn Sa'id ibn al-ʿAs, similar to what will come at 4893.

"ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn al-Zubayr" — with a fatha on the za' and a kasra on the ba' — is al-Qurazi al-Madani, a well-known companion.

al-Suyuti mentioned it at 1:283–284 and attributed it also to al-Shafi'i, ʿAbd al-Razzaq, Ibn Abi Shaybah, the two Sahihs, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i, Ibn Majah, and al-Bayhaqi.

His saying: "wa-innama maʿahu mithl hudbat al-thawb" — the word "wa-innama" was printed in the printed edition as two letters, "wa-in ma," and the correct reading, agreeing with all the other transmissions, is what we have written.]]

4891 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: al-Layth narrated to me, saying: Yunus narrated to me, from Ibn Shihab, from ʿUrwah, from ʿA'ishah, similarly.

4892 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: ʿAbd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: al-Layth narrated to me, saying: ʿUqayl narrated to me, from Ibn Shihab, who said: ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr narrated to me, that ʿA'ishah, the wife of the Prophet (ﷺ), informed him that the wife of Rifa'ah al-Qurazi came to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of God," and he mentioned the like of it. [[Hadiths 4891 and 4892: They are repetitions of the hadith before them via two other chains from al-Zuhri.

Al-Tabari did not mention the wording of these two narrations here. Muslim narrated it at 1:407 via Ibn Wahb from Yunus from al-Zuhri, and gave its wording in full.]]

4893 - Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from ʿUrwah, from ʿA'ishah, that Rifa'ah al-Qurazi divorced his wife, finishing her divorce, and then she married ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn al-Zubayr after him. She came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "O Prophet of God, she was with Rifa'ah, and he divorced her with the last three divorces. Then after him she married ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn al-Zubayr, and by God, O Messenger of God, with him is only like the fringe!" The Messenger of God (ﷺ) smiled, then said to her: "Perhaps you want to return to Rifa'ah? No, until you taste his honey and he tastes yours." She said: Abu Bakr was sitting beside the Prophet (ﷺ), and Khalid ibn Sa'id ibn al-ʿAs was at the door of the chamber, not given permission. So Khalid began calling: "O Abu Bakr! Will you not restrain this one from raising her voice before the Messenger of God (ﷺ)?" [[Hadith 4893: It is in the Musannaf of ʿAbd al-Razzaq (a photographed manuscript we have) 3:305 from Ma'mar and Ibn Jurayj together, from Ibn Shihab.

Ahmad narrated it in al-Musnad 6:226 (Halabi) from ʿAbd al-Razzaq from Ma'mar from al-Zuhri. Ahmad also narrated it at 6:34 from ʿAbd al-Aʿla from Ma'mar.

Muslim narrated it at 1:407 from ʿAbd ibn Humayd, from ʿAbd al-Razzaq from Ma'mar. He did not give its full wording, referring to the narration before it.

Ibn Kathir cited it at 1:549–550 from Ahmad's narration via ʿAbd al-Aʿla. Then he attributed it to the authors of the six books except Abu Dawud.

See the takhrij of 4890, as it has the same meaning.]]

4894 - Muhammad ibn Yazid al-Adami narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Sulaym narrated to us, from ʿUbayd Allah, from al-Qasim, from ʿA'ishah, that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "No, until she tastes of his honey what the first one tasted." [[Hadith 4894: Muhammad ibn Yazid al-Adami al-Khazzaz al-Baghdadi al-Maqabiri, known as al-Ahmar: trustworthy; al-Daraqutni and others declared him trustworthy. al-Sarraj said: "He was ascetic, one of the best of the Muslims." In the printed edition it reads "al-Awdi" instead of "al-Adami," a distortion that we corrected from the manuscript and the biographical sources. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib and in Ibn Abi Hatim 4/1129–130. In al-Tahdhib: "It is said that they are two," meaning that "al-Ahmar" is other than "al-Adami," and on this view al-Khatib in Tarikh Baghdad made them two biographies, 3:374 no. 1488, and 377 no. 1491. The more likely view is that they are two biographies of one person.

Yahya ibn Sulaym, with a damma on the sin, al-Qurashi al-Ta'ifi: trustworthy; Ibn Ma'in and others declared him trustworthy. al-Shafi'i said: "We used to count him among the abdal (substitutes)." The compilers of the six books narrated from him.

ʿUbayd Allah is Ibn ʿUmar ibn Hafs al-ʿUmari. al-Qasim is Ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr al-Siddiq. ʿA'ishah is his paternal aunt.]]

4895 - Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, saying: Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman narrated to us, saying: I heard ʿUbayd Allah say: I heard al-Qasim narrate from ʿA'ishah, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "No, until she tastes of his honey what her companion tasted." [[Hadith 4895: This one and the one before it are abridged versions of the hadith that follows them.]]

4896 - Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Yahya narrated to us, from ʿUbayd Allah, who said: al-Qasim narrated to us, from ʿA'ishah, that a man divorced his wife three times, and she married another husband, who divorced her before he had touched her. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) was asked: "Is she lawful to the first?" He said: "No, until he tastes her honey as the first one tasted." [[Hadith 4896: Yahya in this chain is Ibn Sa'id al-Qattan, the imam.

This hadith is the longer version of the two before it.

Ahmad narrated it in al-Musnad 6:193 (Halabi) from Yahya, meaning al-Qattan, with this chain.

Ibn Kathir cited it at 1:548–549 from this place in al-Tabari. Then he said: "al-Bukhari, Muslim and al-Nasa'i narrated it from several chains from ʿUbayd Allah ibn ʿUmar al-ʿUmari from al-Qasim ibn Abi Bakr from his paternal aunt ʿA'ishah, with it."

al-Suyuti mentioned it at 1:284 and added its attribution to al-Bayhaqi.]]

4897 - Sufyan ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Musa ibn ʿIsa al-Laythi narrated to us, from Za'idah, from ʿAli ibn Zayd, from Umm Muhammad, from ʿA'ishah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "If a man divorces his wife three times, she is not lawful to him until she marries another husband, and each of them tastes the honey of the other." [[Hadith 4897: Musa ibn ʿIsa al-Laythi, the reciter, of Kufa, is trustworthy; Muslim narrated from him in the Sahih.

Za'idah: he is Ibn Qudamah al-Thaqafi, and he is a trustworthy, retentive (hafiz), reliable man, a proponent of the Sunnah.

ʿAli ibn Zayd: he is Ibn Jud'an, and he is trustworthy; we preferred his authentication in Sharh al-Musnad: 783.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 230 (part 2 of 2):

Umm Muhammad: her name is "Umayya bint Abdullah," and it is said "Umayna." She was the wife of the father of Ali ibn Zayd ibn Jud'an. The Hafiz (Ibn Hajar) said in al-Tahdhib (12: 402): "In some copies of al-Tirmidhi it occurs: 'from Ali ibn Zayd ibn Jud'an, from his mother.' This is an error, for Ali ibn Zayd narrated from his father's wife, Umm Muhammad, several hadiths." I say: she was his stepmother, so there is no harm in calling her his mother by way of extension (tawassu').
She was a Successor (tabi'iyya) whose name and kunya are known, and this is sufficient for judging her reliable (tawthiq), especially with the statement of al-Dhahabi in al-Mizan (3: 395), when mentioning the unknown women, he said: "I do not know of any woman among them whom they accused or whom they abandoned."
The hadith was narrated by Ahmad in al-Musnad (6: 96, Halabi) from Affan, from Hammad ibn Salama, from Ali ibn Zayd with this chain, similar in wording. This isnad is sahih according to the conditions of Muslim, and it is more authentic than the isnad of al-Tabari.
Abu Dawud and al-Tayalisi in his Musnad (no. 1560) narrated it in abridged form from Hammad ibn Salama, from Ali ibn Zayd, from his paternal aunt (amma), from Aisha. Perhaps his saying "from his aunt" is also a laxity, if it is not a distortion by a copyist or printer.
Its meaning is established from Aisha through the sound narrations mentioned earlier and others. Ibn Kathir (1: 549) referred to it from this narration of al-Tabari. It would have been more fitting for him, as is his habit, to cite it from the narration of Ahmad, whose isnad is more authentic.

4898 - Al-Abbas ibn Abi Talib narrated to me, saying: Sa'id ibn Hafs al-Talhi informed us, saying: Shayban informed us, from Yahya, from Abu al-Harith al-Ghifari, from Abu Hurayra, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "Until she tastes his honey (usayla)."
[[Hadith 4898: Al-Abbas ibn Abi Talib, the teacher of al-Tabari, his biography has passed at 880. Sa'd ibn Hafs al-Talhi, known as al-Dakhm, mawla of the family of Talha: trustworthy, one of the teachers of al-Bukhari. In the printed edition it reads "Sa'id," which is an error.
Shayban: he is Ibn Abd al-Rahman, Abu Mu'awiya al-Nahwi. His biography has passed at 2340.
This hadith is an abridgement of the one that follows, and the full discussion of it will come.]]
