4899 - Ubayd ibn Adam ibn Abi Iyas al-Asqalani narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: Shayban narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Abi Kathir narrated to us, from Abu al-Harith al-Ghifari, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said concerning a woman whose husband divorces her three times, then she marries another husband, who divorces her before he consummates with her, and the first wants to take her back: "No, until she tastes his honey."
[[Hadith 4899: Abu al-Harith al-Ghifari: al-Bukhari included him in al-Kuna, no. 177, saying: "Abu al-Harith heard Abu Hurayra. Sa'id ibn Hafs [sic; correct: Sa'd] said: Shayban narrated to us from Yahya from Abu al-Harith from Abu Hurayra from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: 'No, until she tastes the honey.' And Waki' said: from Ali ibn al-Mubarak, from Yahya, from Abu Yahya [sic; correct: from Abu al-Harith], al-Ghifari, from Abu Hurayra, as his own statement." This means that in Shayban's narration it is marfu' (traced to the Prophet), while in Ali ibn al-Mubarak's narration it is mawquf (stopping at Abu Hurayra).
Ibn Abi Hatim included him (4/2/358), saying: "Abu al-Harith al-Ghifari heard Abu Hurayra from the Prophet (ﷺ): 'No, until she tastes the honey.' Ali ibn al-Mubarak narrated from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir from him. I heard my father say so."
Thus the narration of Ibn al-Mubarak in Abu Hatim's work is marfu'. The fact that al-Bukhari's narration stops at Abu Hurayra does not negate this, for the addition of a trustworthy narrator (ziyadat al-thiqa) is accepted, and a narrator may sometimes raise a hadith and sometimes limit himself to transmitting it as mawquf.
Al-Hafiz also included him in Lisan al-Mizan and added that al-Tahawi narrated another hadith from him, mawquf upon Abu Hurayra, from the narration of Harb ibn Shaddad from Yahya. Then he said: "Abu Ahmad al-Hakim mentioned him in al-Kuna among those whose names are not known, and he related the hadith of the honey by the chain of al-Bukhari in al-Tarikh, from Sa'id ibn Hafs, from Shayban, and he did not mention any criticism of him."
This hadith was mentioned by Ibn Kathir (1: 548) from these two narrations of al-Tabari. Then he said: "Abu al-Harith is not well known." The response to this: al-Bukhari and Abu Hatim both identified him and mentioned no criticism of him, so he is trustworthy, especially since he is a Successor, and they hold to his reliability until a clear criticism is established.
al-Suyuti mentioned it (1: 284) and attributed it only to Ibn Abi Shayba and Ibn Jarir. al-Tirmidhi referred to it (2: 185) in his words "and in the chapter" (wa fi al-bab). His commentator al-Mubarakfuri said: "As for the hadith of Abu Hurayra, al-Tabarani and Ibn Abi Shayba narrated it." I incline to think that the word "al-Tabarani" is an error, for if it were in al-Tabarani, al-Haythami would have mentioned it in Majma' al-Zawa'id, and he did not. Likewise al-Suyuti did not attribute it to al-Tabarani but to al-Tabari.
As for his saying "her husband divorces her three times": the word "thalatha" (three) is not in the manuscript. It is established in Ibn Kathir and al-Suyuti, so its inclusion is more sound and reliable.]]

4900 - Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Anmati narrated to me, saying: Hisham ibn Abd al-Malik narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Dinar narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Yazid al-Hanna'i narrated to us, from Anas ibn Malik, from the Prophet (ﷺ), concerning a man who divorced his wife three times, and then another man married her and divorced her before he consummated with her. Would she return to her first husband? He said: "No, until he tastes her honey and she tastes his honey."
[[Hadith 4900: Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Anmati, teacher of al-Tabari: he is the one nicknamed "Murabba'," companion of Yahya ibn Ma'in and student of Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal. Ibn Abi Hatim (3/2/187) included him and said: "a Baghdadi among the huffaz (memorizers)." al-Khatib included him in Tarikh Baghdad (1: 388-389) with a good biography and said: "He was one of the perceptive huffaz." He mentioned that Yahya ibn Ma'in was the one who gave him the nickname "Murabba'," among a group of his companions: "These are the senior companions and memorizers of hadith." Qadi Ibn Abi Ya'la included him in Tabaqat al-Hanabila (1: 266-267) with a brief biography from the history of his teacher al-Khatib. In al-Tahdhib (9: 11) there is a teacher of this same generation who may be confused with him, "Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Asbati," but he is a Kufan who settled in Egypt, and he is a different person. Ibn Abi Hatim also included him (3/2/186).
Hisham ibn Abd al-Malik: he is Abu al-Walid al-Tayalisi, the memorizer, whose biography passed at 28.
Muhammad ibn Dinar al-Tahi, Abu Bakr ibn Abi al-Furat: some have spoken about him, but the truth is that he is trustworthy. Ibn Ma'in said: "There is no harm in him," and Abu Zur'a said: "Truthful (saduq)." al-Bukhari included him in al-Kabir (11/77) and mentioned no criticism of him.
Yahya ibn Yazid al-Hana'i al-Basri: a trustworthy Successor. Ibn Hibban mentioned him in al-Thiqat, and al-Bukhari included him in al-Kabir (4/2/310) and mentioned no criticism of him. Shu'ba narrated from him, and he narrates only from the trustworthy. Muslim included him in his Sahih.
"Al-Hana'i" is with a dammed ha' and a lightened nun, a nisba to Hana'a ibn Malik ibn Fahm of the Azd, as stated by Ibn al-Athir in al-Lubab.
The hadith was narrated by Ahmad in al-Musnad (no. 14069; 3: 284, Halabi) from Affan, from Muhammad ibn Dinar with this chain, similar, slightly more extended.
al-Bayhaqi narrated it (7: 375-376) by the route of Yahya ibn Hammad, from Muhammad ibn Dinar.
Ibn Kathir (1: 548) quoted it from the narration in the Musnad, then referred to this narration in al-Tabari. al-Suyuti mentioned it (1: 284) attributed to these.
al-Haythami mentioned it in Majma' al-Zawa'id (4: 340), attributing it to Ahmad, al-Bazzar, Abu Ya'la and al-Tabarani in al-Awsat, and said: "Its narrators are the narrators of the Sahih, except Muhammad ibn Dinar al-Tahi, whom Abu Hatim, Abu Zur'a and Ibn Hibban declared trustworthy. There is some discussion of him which does not harm."]]

4901 - Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim and Ya'qub ibn Mahan narrated to me, both saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Abi Ishaq informed us, from Sulayman ibn Yasar, from Ubayd Allah ibn al-Abbas: that al-Ghumaysa' (or: al-Rumaysa') came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) complaining about her husband, claiming that he could not reach her. He said: Not long after, her husband came, and he claimed she was lying, but that she wanted to return to her first husband. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "It is not for you until another man tastes your honey."
[[Hadith 4901: Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim, teacher of al-Tabari: he is al-Dawraqi the memorizer, who has passed several times. Ya'qub ibn Mahan, his teacher also: he is al-Baghdadi al-Bannaa, and he is trustworthy. Hajjaj ibn al-Sha'ir said: "There is no one in Baghdad like Ya'qub ibn Mahan."
This hadith was narrated by Ahmad in al-Musnad (no. 1837). It is a sahih hadith, and we discussed it fully there, and in the supplement to al-Musnad, no. 1448 (vol. 8, pp. 312-313 in our commentary).
al-Suyuti mentioned it (1: 284) attributed only to Ahmad and al-Nasa'i. However, in his work it reads "from Abd Allah ibn Abbas," and in my view this is a copyist's or printer's error, as occurred in the printed edition of al-Nasa'i.]]

4902 - Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'ba narrated to us, from Alqama ibn Murthad, from Salim ibn Razin al-Ahmari, from Salim ibn Abd Allah, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, from Ibn Umar, from the Prophet (ﷺ), concerning a man who marries a woman and divorces her before consummating with her, irrevocably (alba), and then she marries another husband, who divorces her before consummating with her. Would she return to the first? He said: "No, until she tastes his honey and he tastes her honey."

4903 - Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Alqama ibn Murthad, from Razin al-Ahmari, from Ibn Umar, from the Prophet, that he was asked about a man who divorces his wife three times, and a man marries her, then closes the door (to her), then divorces her before consummating with her. Would she return to her other husband? He said: "No, until he tastes her honey."

4904 - Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Alqama ibn Murthad, from Sulayman ibn Razin, from Ibn Umar, that he asked the Prophet (ﷺ) while he was delivering a sermon about a man who divorced his wife, and she married after him, then he divorced her or died leaving her: would the first husband marry her? He said: "No, until she tastes his honey."
[[Hadiths 4902-4904: these are one hadith with three isnads, and all its isnads are weak. I have discussed it fully in the sharh of al-Musnad: 4776, 4777, 5277, 5278, 5571.
Al-Bukhari mentioned the disagreement about it in al-Kabir (2/214) under the biography of "Sulayman ibn Razin." Then he said: Ibrahim ibn al-Mundhir said: Anas ibn Iyad narrated to us, from Musa ibn Uqba, from Nafi', from Ibn Umar, who said: "If anyone did this while Umar was alive, he would have stoned them both." Abu Abd Allah [that is, al-Bukhari himself] said: "This is more well known, and the proof is not established by Salim ibn Razin nor by Razin, because it is not known whether he heard from Salim or from Ibn Umar."
This mawquf report of Ibn Umar was also narrated by Abd al-Razzaq in al-Musannaf (3: 305, photographed manuscript): "from Ibn Jurayj, from Musa ibn Uqba, from Nafi', from Ibn Umar, who said: 'If a man divorced his wife three times, then another man married her after him, then divorced her before he had intercourse with her, then her first husband married her again, and this were done while Umar was alive, he would have stoned them both.'"]]

* *

Interpretation of the words of the Exalted: ﴿And if he divorces her, then there is no blame upon them both for returning to one another, if they think that they can keep within the limits of Allah﴾

Abu Ja'far said: The Exalted means by His words "And if he divorces her" — if he divorces the woman who was separated from her husband by the last of the three divorces, after her second husband had married her — [[The phrase "her husband" (zawjuha) is the subject of the opening phrase: "if he divorces the woman..." and the full construction is: "if he divorces the woman... her husband who married her..." and between them is a long clause on the description of "the woman."]] her husband who married her after her separation from the first — "then there is no blame upon them both" — the Exalted means: there is no fault upon the woman whom this second husband divorced after her separation from the first, and after his marrying her — [[The phrase "upon the husband" ('ala al-zawj) is coordinated with "upon the woman," and the full construction is: "there is no fault upon the woman... and upon the husband... that they return to one another." Thus I was compelled to vary the types of pausal endings so that the reader can connect the speech with itself.]] and upon the first husband, who had made her forbidden to him by her separation from him by the last of the divorces — that they return to one another by a new marriage. As:

4905 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya ibn Salih narrated to me, from Ali ibn Abi Talha, from Ibn Abbas: "And if he divorces her, then there is no blame upon them both for returning to one another, if they think that they can keep within the limits of Allah." [[In the manuscript the verse is cut at "for returning to one another," and the commentary continues.]] He says: If she marries after the first, and the second one consummates with her, then there is no fault on the first if he marries her when the second divorces her or dies leaving her. She has become lawful to him.

4906 - Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hisham narrated to us, saying: Juwaybir informed us, from al-Dahhak, who said: If he divorces once or twice, he has the right of return (raj'a) as long as the waiting period has not ended. He said: As for the third, His words "And if he divorces her" mean the third; then he has no right of return over her until she marries another husband who consummates with her. "And if he divorces her" — this last one, after he has consummated with her — "then there is no blame upon them both for returning to one another" — meaning the first — "if they think that they can keep within the limits of Allah."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: As for His words "if they think that they can keep within the limits of Allah," their meaning is: if they hope with a prospect that they can keep within the limits of Allah. Keeping within the limits of Allah means acting by them. The limits of Allah are what He commanded them and made obligatory on each of them toward the other, and bound each of them by reason of the marriage that exists between them. We have already explained the meaning of "limits" and the meaning of "keeping" them, in a way that makes repeating it unnecessary here. [[See the explanation of "limits" earlier in this volume, 4: 584, and the meaning of "keeping the limits and the prayer" earlier, 1: 241, and in this volume 4: 564, 565.]]

* *

Mujahid used to say concerning His words "if they think that they can keep within the limits of Allah":

4907 - Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, from Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His words "if they think that they can keep within the limits of Allah": if they think that their marriage is free of deceit (dalsa). [[The dalsa (with a dammah and a sukun) is darkness, and similar is "dals" (with two fatahs). Among its figurative uses: "dalasa yudalisu mudalasa," meaning he deceived and betrayed, because he conceals the thing from you, as if he brings it to you in the dark. I have not found anyone using "dalsa" figuratively for deception and cheating except in this report. It is an ancient, eloquent Arabic word.]]

4908 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, similarly.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: Some interpreters have directed His words "if they think" to mean "if they are certain" [[This is Abu Ubayda in Majaz al-Qur'an (1: 74).]]. That has no basis, because no one knows what will happen except Allah, the Exalted. Since this is so, what is the meaning by which a man and a woman become certain that if they return to one another they will keep the limits of Allah? Rather, the meaning of it, as the Exalted said: "if they think," means hoping for that and expecting it.

* *

The "an" in His words "an yuqimaa" (that they keep) is in the accusative position governed by "zanna" (thought), and the "an" in "an yatarajja'a" (that they return) — some scholars of Arabic grammar placed it in the accusative position through the omission of the governing preposition [[This means al-Farra' in Ma'ani al-Qur'an (1: 148).]], because the meaning of the speech is: "there is no blame upon them both in that they return to one another," and when the preposition "fi" that governed it in the genitive was omitted, it became accusative, as if he said: "there is no blame upon them both for their returning."
Some of them said: [[This is al-Kisa'i, as reported by al-Farra' in his book (1: 148) too.]] its position is genitive even though its governing particle is not present, and if it is omitted its position is still known.

* *

Interpretation of the words of the Exalted: ﴿And these are the limits of Allah, which He makes clear for a people who know﴾ (230)

Abu Ja'far said: The Exalted means by His words "And these are the limits of Allah" these matters which He made clear to His servants concerning divorce, return, ransom, the waiting period, the oath of abstinence (ila') and other things which He makes clear to them in these verses — "the limits of Allah" — the landmarks of the distinctions of His lawful and unlawful, and His obedience and disobedience — "He makes them clear" — He details them, distinguishes between them, and makes known to them their rulings — "for a people who know" them, when Allah has made them clear to them, so that they know that they are from Allah, and so they affirm them, and act by what Allah has entrusted them with of His knowledge — unlike those upon whose hearts Allah has set a seal and decreed that they will not believe in them, nor affirm that they are from Allah; they are ignorant that they are from Allah and that they are a revelation from the Wise, the Praiseworthy. For this reason He specified the people who know for the clarification, rather than those who are ignorant, since those who are ignorant that it is from Him had caused His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) to despair of the affirmation of many of them of it, even though He made it clear to them in terms of the proof against them and the obligation for them to act by it. He removed it from being a clarification for them only by way of their refusal to acknowledge and affirm it.

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 231 (part 1 of 2)**

**On the interpretation (ta'wil) of His saying, Exalted is His mention:** ﴿And when you divorce women and they reach their term, then either retain them honorably or release them honorably, and do not retain them to harm them so that you transgress.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By this, Exalted is His mention, He means: "And when you divorce" (O men, your wives), "then they reach their term," meaning their appointed time which He set for them, which is the completion of the three menstrual periods (qurû', sing. qar'), if the woman is one who has menstrual periods, [[In the printed edition: "min ahl al-aqra'" (from among those with periods), which is correct, but I do not know why it was changed from what is in the manuscript.]] and the completion of the months if she is one who has months. "Then retain them" means: take them back, if you wish to restore them in the divorce in which there is a right of return (raj'a). This is either in a single pronouncement or in two, as Exalted is His mention said: ﴿Divorce is twice; then either retain honorably or release with kindness﴾ [Q 2:229].

As for His saying "honorably," He means: by what He has permitted of return, namely calling witnesses to the return before the end of the waiting period ('idda), not returning by intercourse and sexual relations. For that is only permissible for the man after the return, and with the companionship and good treatment that goes with it, in the manner that God commanded and clarified for you, O people. "Or release them honorably" means: or let them go, so that they complete their waiting period and the remainder of their term that He set for them for their count, honorably. That is, by fulfilling their full rights upon you, [[In the manuscript: "bi-infaqihinna" (by spending on them), which is an error of the hasty copyist, as I have already mentioned.]] in accordance with what He obligated you to give them of dower, provision, maintenance, and other rights they have over you.

"And do not retain them to harm them" means: do not take them back, if you take them back during their waiting period, to cause them harm, so that you prolong the period of their waiting, or so that you take from them some of what you gave them, by their asking you for khul' (release by compensation), because of your harming them by retaining them and taking them back as harm and transgression.

As for His saying "so that you transgress" (li-ta'tadu), it means: so that you wrong them by exceeding in their matter the limits I have made clear to you.

* * *

Those who engaged in ta'wil (exegesis) said the same as what we have said on this. Those who said that:

4909. Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Jarir related to us, from Mansur, from Abu al-Duha, from Masruq, regarding "and do not retain them to harm them": He said: He divorces her, and when her waiting period is about to end he takes her back; then he divorces her again and leaves her, and when her waiting period is about to end he takes her back, not intending to keep her. This is the harm, and it is taking the signs of God in mockery.

4910. Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim related to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayya related to us, from Abu Raja', who said: Al-Hasan was asked about the saying of Exalted is His mention: "And when you divorce women and they reach their term, then retain them honorably or release them honorably, and do not retain them to harm them so that you transgress." He said: A man would divorce a woman, then take her back, then divorce her, then take her back, harming her; so God forbade them from that.

4911. Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding His saying: "And when you divorce women and they reach their term, then retain them honorably or release them honorably": He said: God forbade harm ("darar"): that a man divorces his wife and then takes her back at the last day remaining of the term, until he has fulfilled for her nine months, in order to harm her thereby.

4912. Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa related to us, saying: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, similarly, except that he said: He forbade harm, and harm in divorce is that a man divorces his wife and then takes her back. The rest of the report is like the report of Muhammad ibn 'Amr.

4913. Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: My father related to us, saying: My paternal uncle related to us, saying: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas: "And when you divorce women and they reach their term, then retain them honorably or release them honorably, and do not retain them to harm them so that you transgress." A man would divorce his wife, then take her back near the end of her waiting period, then divorce her again. He did this to harm her and to 'adl her, so God revealed this verse. [[''Adl al-mar'a yu'dluhā: he did not treat her well, so as to compel her thereby to ransom herself from him with the dower he had given her.]]

4914. Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Ishaq related to us, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far related to us, from his father, from al-Rabi' regarding His saying: "And when you divorce women and they reach their term, then retain them honorably or release them honorably, and do not retain them to harm them so that you transgress." He said: A man would divorce his wife with a single pronouncement, then leave her, until when her waiting period was almost over he would take her back; then he would divorce her again, until when her waiting period was almost over he would take her back. [[Khala al-shay' yakhlu khulūwan: it passed and ended.]] He had no need of her, but only wished to harm her by this. So God forbade that, and warned against it, and said: ﴿Whoever does that has wronged himself﴾.

4915. Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Al-Layth related to me, from Yunus, from Ibn Shihab, who said: Exalted is His mention said: "And when you divorce women and they reach their term, then retain them honorably or release them honorably, and do not retain them to harm them so that you transgress." So when a man divorces a woman and her term has come to an end, let him take her back honorably or release her with kindness. It is not lawful for him to take her back in harm, when he has no desire for her, unless it is to harm her.

4916. Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Ishaq related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada regarding His saying: "and do not retain them to harm them so that you transgress." He said: This concerns a man who swears an oath of divorce against his wife; then when some of her waiting period remains he takes her back, harming her thereby and prolonging it for her. So God forbade them from that.

4917. Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Ishaq related to us, saying: Isma'il ibn Abi Uways related to us, from Malik ibn Anas, from Thawr ibn Zayd al-Dili: that a man would divorce his wife and then take her back, having no need of her and not wishing to keep her, in order that the waiting period would be prolonged for her by this, to harm her. So God, Exalted is His mention, revealed: "and do not retain them to harm them so that you transgress. And whoever does that has wronged himself," magnifying that. [[The report: 4917 — al-Muwatta' 588, in its wording, except his saying "yu'azzimu dhālik" (magnifying that), in which it reads "yu'azzimuhum Allāh bi-dhālik" (God magnifies them by that). In the printed edition: "li-yu'azzima dhālik."]]

4918. Related to me from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh al-Fadl ibn Khalid say: 'Ubayd ibn Sulayman al-Bahili related to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying: "and do not retain them to harm them": It is the man who divorces his wife with one pronouncement, then takes her back, then divorces her, then takes her back, then divorces her, so as to harm her by this, that she may seek khul' from him.

4920. Musa related to us, saying: 'Amr related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi: "And when you divorce women and they reach their term, then retain them honorably or release them honorably, and do not retain them to harm them so that you transgress. And whoever does that has wronged himself. And do not take the signs of God in mockery." He said: It was revealed concerning a man of the Ansar called Thabit ibn Yasar [[In the printed edition: "Thabit ibn Bashshar." The correct reading is from the manuscript, and from al-Durr al-Manthur 1:285, Usd al-Ghaba, where the report is mentioned and attributed to al-Tabari and Ibn al-Mundhir.]] who divorced his wife until, when her waiting period had ended except for two or three days, he took her back, [[In the printed edition: "aw thalāthan" (or three); the correct reading is from the manuscript.]] then divorced her again, and did this to her until nine months had passed for her, harming her by it. So God, Exalted is His mention, revealed: "and do not retain them to harm them so that you transgress."

4921. Al-'Abbas ibn al-Walid related to me, saying: My father informed me, saying: I heard 'Abd al-'Aziz being asked about the divorce of harm. He said: He divorces, then takes her back, then divorces, then takes her back. This is the harm that God spoke of: "and do not retain them to harm them so that you transgress."

4922. Ahmad ibn Ishaq related to us, saying: Abu Ahmad related to us, saying: Fudayl ibn Marzuq related to us, from 'Atiyya: "and do not retain them to harm them so that you transgress." He said: A man divorces his wife with one pronouncement, then leaves her until she menstruates three periods, then takes her back, then divorces her with one pronouncement, then refrains from her until she menstruates three periods, then takes her back. "So that you transgress" — he said: He does not prolong the matter over them.

* * *

Abu Ja'far said: The root of "tasrih" (release) is from "sarah al-qawm" (the people's herd), which is what is let out of their camels to pasture. One says of livestock sent out to graze, "this is the sarh of the people," meaning their livestock sent out to pasture. From this is the saying of Exalted is His mention: ﴿And the cattle He created for you; in them is warmth and benefits, and from them you eat. And in them is beauty for you when you bring them home and when you send them out to pasture﴾ [Q 16:5–6]. By His saying "when you send them out" He means when you release them to pasture. So it was said of a woman whom her husband released, separating her from himself: "sarrahahā" (he released her), by way of likening that to the "tasrih" of one who sends his livestock out to pasture, and as a comparison with it. [[This is further evidence that al-Tabari sometimes postponed explaining a word or forgot it, out of his desire for brevity. Otherwise "al-tasrih" was already mentioned earlier in the verse 229, and he did not explain it there.]]

* * *

**On the interpretation of His saying:** ﴿And whoever does that has wronged himself﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By this, Exalted is His mention, He means: whoever returns to his wife after divorcing her, in a divorce in which he has the right of return over her, does so to harm her, in order to transgress God's limit concerning her matter, then he has wronged himself. That is, he has thereby earned for himself sin, and made it incumbent upon himself to receive punishment from God for that.

* * *

We have already explained the meaning of "wrongdoing" (zulm) earlier: that it is placing a thing in other than its proper place, and doing what the doer has no right to do. [[See the references for "zulm" earlier, vol. 4, p. 584, note no. 2.]]

* * *

**On the interpretation of His saying:** ﴿And do not take the signs of God in mockery﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By this, Exalted is His mention, He means: do not take God's markers and His distinctions between His lawful and unlawful, His commands and prohibitions, in His revelation and His sending down, as mockery and play. For He has made clear to you in His sending down and in the verses of His Book what right of return you have over your wives in the divorce in which He has made the right of return for you over them, and what you do not have, and what the permissible manner of it is for you, and what is not permissible, and which divorce allows you a right of return over them, and which does not, and how the various ways of this are. This is out of mercy from Him to you and a blessing from Him upon you, so that by it He makes available for one of you, if there is some hardship in the spouse that troubles him, a way out and a release through divorce and separation, [[In the manuscript and the printed edition: "li-yaj'ala bi-dhālika li-ba'dikum min makrūh, in kāna fīhi min ṣāḥibihi mā yu'dhīhi" … and the sentence is barely coherent. I suspect that the hasty copyist in this part of the book hurried as usual, copying "yu'dhīhi" and "mimmā huwa fīhi" and turning the "ya'" into "hā'" and linking the "dhāl" to the "yā'" and making it "fā'". The context of the sentence is: "li-yaj'ala bi-dhālika li-ba'dikum al-makhraj wa-l-mukhallas... min makrūh, in kāna fīhi min ṣāḥibihi adhan lahu" — that is, "in this hardship from his companion there is harm to him," and the phrase "fīhi min ṣāḥibihi mā yu'dhīhi" is a qualifying clause for "makrūh."]] and makes the right of return that He has given you over them a path for you to reach what his desire draws him toward and calls him to, after separating from them, so that by this you may attain the fulfilment of your needs from them, as a blessing from Him upon you. Not so that you take what I have made clear to you about that in the verses of My Book and My sending down (out of My grace in clarifying it to you, and My blessing and mercy toward you) as play and mockery.

* * *

Those who engaged in ta'wil said the same meaning as what we have said on this. Those who said that:

4923. 'Abd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Shabawayh related to me, saying: My father related to us, saying: Ayyub ibn Sulayman related to us, saying: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Uways related to us, from Sulayman ibn Bilal, from Muhammad ibn Abi 'Atiq and Musa ibn 'Uqba, from Ibn Shihab, from Sulayman ibn Arqam: that al-Hasan informed them that people, in the time of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), would divorce or manumit (a slave), and it would be said to them: "What have you done?" He would say: "I was only joking!" The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Whoever divorces in jest or manumits in jest, it takes effect against him." Al-Hasan said: "And concerning this was revealed: 'and do not take the signs of God in mockery.'" [[The hadith: 4923 — 'Abd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Shabawayh: already mentioned in 1909. His father, "Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Thabit ibn 'Uthman al-Khuza'i, Abu al-Hasan ibn Shabawayh": trustworthy; Ibn Mu'in, who was among his contemporaries, related from him, and so did Abu Zur'a and Abu Dawud and others. Ayyub ibn Sulayman ibn Bilal al-Taymi: trustworthy, one of al-Bukhari's teachers; he narrates from his father through the mediation of Ibn Abi Uways. Abu Bakr ibn Abi Uways: he is 'Abd al-Hamid ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd Allah al-Madani al-A'sha, mentioned in 4333. Sulayman ibn Bilal: mentioned in 41 and 4333. Muhammad ibn Abi 'Atiq: he is Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr al-Siddiq, ascribed to "Abu 'Atiq," the kunya of his grandfather Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman. He is trustworthy, and al-Bukhari included him in his Sahih. Sulayman ibn Arqam, Abu Mu'adh al-Basri: very weak. Al-Bukhari said: "They abandoned him." Ibn Mu'in said: "He is not worth a fils, and is nothing." Abu Zur'a said: "Weak in hadith, of lost hadith." He was among the students of al-Zuhri, but al-Zuhri sometimes narrates from him, as in this chain. This hadith is weak, because of its mursal character, and because of the weakness of its narrator Sulayman ibn Arqam. This mursal hadith has also come with a better chain than this one, though still mursal: Ibn Abi Hatim related it from 'Isam ibn Rawwad, from Adam ibn Abi Iyas, from al-Mubarak ibn Fadala, from al-Hasan. Ibn Kathir mentioned it, 1:555. Then he pointed to al-Tabari's chain here. Al-Suyuti mentioned it, 1:286, and added its attribution to Ibn Abi Shayba.]]

4924. Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Ishaq related to us, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far related to us, from his father, from al-Rabi' regarding His saying: "and do not take the signs of God in mockery." He said: A man would divorce his wife and then say: "I only divorced her in jest!" They were forbidden from that, so Exalted is His mention said: "and do not take the signs of God in mockery."

4925. Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Ishaq ibn Mansur related to us, from 'Abd al-Salam ibn Harb, from Yazid ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from Abu al-'Ala', from Humayd ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Musa: that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) became angry with the Ash'aris. Abu Musa came to him and said: "O Messenger of God, you were angry with the Ash'aris!" He said: "One of you says: 'I have divorced, I have taken back!' This is not the divorce of Muslims. Divorce the woman at the beginning of her waiting period."

4926. Abu Zayd related to us, from Ibn Shabba, saying: Abu Ghassan al-Nahdi related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Salam ibn Harb related to us, from Yazid ibn Abi Khalid — meaning al-Dalani — from Abu al-'Ala' al-Awdi, from Humayd ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he said: "Why does one of you say to his wife: 'I have divorced you, I have taken you back'? This is not the divorce of Muslims. Divorce the woman at the beginning of her purity." [[The two hadiths: 4925 and 4926 — Ishaq ibn Mansur al-Sulami, in the first chain: trustworthy; the six imams related from him. "Abu Zayd from Ibn Shabba," in the second chain: I did not find anyone in this generation known as Abu Zayd, nor anyone in the generation above known as Ibn Shabba. It appears to be one teacher, distorted from "Abu Zayd 'Umar ibn Shabba." Abu Ghassan al-Nahdi is Malik ibn Isma'il ibn Durhum, mentioned in 2989. Yazid ibn 'Abd al-Rahman: in the first chain, he is "Yazid Abu Khalid al-Dalani"; in the second chain, his biography was given in 875. The phrase "'an Yazid ibn Abi Khalid" appearing in the second chain here, with the addition of "ibn," is an error. Abu al-'Ala' al-Awdi: he is Dawud ibn 'Abd Allah al-Awdi al-Za'afari. He is trustworthy; Ahmad, Ibn Mu'in and others declared him reliable. Whoever confused him with "Dawud ibn Yazid al-Awdi, the paternal uncle of Ibn Idris," erred. "Al-Za'afari" refers to "al-Za'afir," a branch of "Awd." Humayd ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Himyari al-Basri: a trustworthy Successor (tabi'i), from whom the six imams related. The hadith was also related by al-Bayhaqi, 7:323, through al-'Abbas ibn Muhammad al-Duri, from Malik ibn Isma'il, who is Abu Ghassan al-Nahdi, from 'Abd al-Salam ibn Harb, similarly. Its ending in his version is: "Divorce the woman at the beginning of her purity." In the second chain, his saying "anna-hu qāla: lam yaqul aḥadukum li-imra'atihi" — in the printed edition, "li-hum" instead of "li-" — the apparent reading is an error, so I corrected it from al-Bayhaqi's transmission. Both of al-Tabari's chains are sound, as is al-Bayhaqi's chain. Ibn Kathir transmitted it, 1:554, from al-Tabari's first chain and then pointed to the second. Al-Suyuti transmitted it, 1:285–286, attributing it to Ibn Majah, Ibn Jarir and al-Bayhaqi. Then he transmitted it similarly, 6:230, attributing it to 'Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Mardawayh.]]

The narration in Ibn Majah is not with this wording, nor by this route. Ibn Majah narrated it (2017) from Muhammad ibn Bashshar, from Mu'ammal ibn Isma'il, from Sufyan, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu Burdah, from Abu Musa, as a marfu' report: "What is the matter with people who play with the limits of Allah? One of them says: 'I have divorced you, I have taken you back, I have divorced you!!'" Al-Busiri said in his Zawa'id: "Its isnad is hasan. Mu'ammal ibn Isma'il has been disputed: it is said he is thiqah (trustworthy), it is said he makes many errors, and it is said he is munkar al-hadith (weak in narration)."

But al-Busiri erred in two respects. Mu'ammal ibn Isma'il is thiqah, as we have shown at (2057). Moreover, he did not narrate it alone, so that it could be faulted on his account.

Al-Bayhaqi narrated it (7: 322) by way of Musa ibn Mas'ud al-Nahdi, from Sufyan, who is al-Thawri, with this same isnad. Then he also narrated it by way of Mu'ammal ibn Isma'il, from al-Thawri. Musa ibn Mas'ud is thiqah, as we have shown at (280) and (1693).

* *

On the interpretation of His words, the Exalted: ﴿And remember the favour of Allah upon you and what He has sent down to you of the Book﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By this, the Exalted One means: remember the favour of Allah upon you through Islam, with which He has bestowed favour upon you and guided you to it, and His other favours which He has singled you out with, over the rest of His creation. So thank Him for that by obeying Him in what He has commanded you and forbidden you. And remember, along with that, what He has sent down to you of His Book, that is, the Qur'an which He sent down upon His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ). [In the printed edition: "from His Book that Qur'an", which is an error by the copyist; the correct reading is from the manuscript.] Remember it, act upon it, and guard its limits within it. "And the wisdom" means: and what He has sent down to you of wisdom, namely the sunnah (prophetic practice) which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) taught you and laid down for you.

I have already mentioned the differences of those who differ regarding the meaning of "wisdom" earlier, in His words: ﴿and teaches them the Book and the wisdom﴾ [Surah al-Baqarah: 129], so there is no need to repeat it here. [See what has preceded, 3: 87, 88.]

* *

On the interpretation of His words, the Exalted: ﴿He admonishes you thereby. And fear Allah, and know that Allah is Knowing of all things﴾ (231)

Abu Ja'far said: By His words, "He admonishes you thereby," the Exalted One means: He admonishes you with the Book that was sent down to you. The pronoun in "thereby" refers to the Book.

"And fear Allah" means: and be wary of Allah, in what He has commanded you and what He has forbidden you in His Book which He sent down to you, and in what He sent down and then made clear upon the tongue of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) for you, lest you neglect it and transgress its limits, thereby incurring what you have no power to bear of His painful punishment and the vengeance of His torment.

His words, "And know that Allah is Knowing of all things," mean: and know, O people, that your Lord, who set for you these limits, legislated for you these laws, and imposed upon you these obligations, in His Book and in what He sent down upon His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ), knows all that you do, of good and evil, of right and wrong, of obedience and disobedience. Nothing is hidden from Him of what is apparent or concealed, secret or open. He will requite you with good for good and with evil for evil, unless He pardons and forgives. So do not expose yourselves to His punishment and do not wrong yourselves. [In the printed edition: "and do not wrong yourselves," while the correct reading from the manuscript omits "not" here.]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 232 (part 1 of 2):

The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And when you divorce women and they reach their term, do not prevent them from marrying their husbands when they have agreed between themselves on a fair basis﴾.

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: It is mentioned that this verse was revealed concerning a man who had a sister whose husband was a paternal cousin of hers. He divorced her and left her, and did not take her back until her waiting period (iddah) had ended. Then he proposed to her again, but he refused to let her marry him, and prevented her from it, while she was willing.

* *

Then the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed about the man who had done this, concerning whom this verse was revealed. Some of them said that the man was Ma'qil ibn Yasar al-Muzani.

Those who said this:

4927. Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to me, who said: Abd al-A'la narrated to us, who said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, from al-Hasan, from Ma'qil ibn Yasar, who said: His sister was under a man, who divorced her, then left her [[khalā 'an al-shay': abandoned it. This triliteral verb is rarely found clearly in the lexicography books, but it is an authentic Arabic usage. It occurs within the entries for the root (kh-l-w) in Lisan al-Arab, and al-Shirazi clearly gave it in Mi'yar al-lugha. The narration that follows also confirms this meaning. Thus it appears in the manuscript and printed edition of al-Tabari as "khalā" (triliteral) in both places, while in the narration of al-Bukhari that we will mention later it appears as "khallā 'anhā" in both places, which has the same meaning.]] until her waiting period had ended. Then he proposed to her, and Ma'qil became angry at that, out of pride [[Ibn Hajar said in Fath al-Bari: "ḥamā, with a kasra on the second letter, and anafan, with a fatha on the hamza and the nun, meaning he abandoned the act out of rage and haughtiness." ḥamā: he was seized by ḥamiyya, which is pride and jealousy.]], and said: "He left her when he was able to take her back!!" [[khalā 'an al-shay': abandoned it. This triliteral verb is rarely found clearly in the lexicography books, but it is an authentic Arabic usage... (the same note as above)]] So he prevented him from her. Then God, may His remembrance be exalted, revealed: ﴿And when you divorce women and they reach their term, do not prevent them from marrying their husbands when they have agreed between themselves on a fair basis﴾. [[The narration: 4927. Al-Bukhari transmitted it with his chain through Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna, from Abd al-A'la (Fath 9: 425-426). In al-Bukhari's narration there is an addition: "The Messenger of God (ﷺ) summoned him and recited it to him. So he gave up his pride and submitted to the command of God." It will come in the mursal report of Qatadah below, no. 4930, and I will explain it in the commentary there.]]

4928. Abu Kurayb narrated to us, who said: Waki' narrated to us, from al-Fadl ibn Dalham, from al-Hasan, from Ma'qil ibn Yasar: that his sister's husband divorced her, then he wished to take her back, but Ma'qil prevented her, so God, may His remembrance be exalted, revealed: ﴿And when you divorce women and they reach their term, do not prevent them from marrying their husbands﴾ to the end of the verse. [[The narration: 4928. Al-Hakim transmitted it in al-Mustadrak 2: 280 and said: "This hadith has a sound chain, but the two (Bukhari and Muslim) did not record it." Al-Dhahabi commented: "Al-Fadl: Ibn Ma'in declared him weak, and others strengthened him." However, Ibn Abi Hatim mentioned in his biography in al-Jarh wa al-Ta'dil 3/2/61: "Yahya ibn Ma'in was asked about al-Fadl ibn Dalham and said: 'His hadith is acceptable.'" See the disagreement about al-Fadl in his biography in al-Tahdhib.]]

4929. Muhammad ibn Abd Allah al-Makhzumi narrated to us, who said: Abu Amir narrated to us, who said: Abbad ibn Rashid narrated to us, who said: al-Hasan narrated to us, who said: Ma'qil ibn Yasar narrated to me, who said: I had a sister who was sought in marriage, and I prevented people from her, until a paternal cousin of mine proposed to me, and I married her to him. They lived together as long as God willed, then he divorced her with a revocable divorce, then left her until her waiting period ended. Then she was proposed to me again, and he came to me proposing to her along with the other suitors. I said to him: "You proposed to me, and I prevented people from her and gave her preference to you. Then you divorced her with a revocable divorce, and when she was proposed to me, you came to me proposing to her with the suitors! By God, I will never marry her to you!" He said: Then this verse was revealed concerning this: ﴿And when you divorce women and they reach their term, do not prevent them from marrying their husbands when they have agreed between themselves on a fair basis﴾. He said: So I expiated for my oath, and married her to him. [[The narration: 4929. "Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak al-Qurashi al-Makhrami" (with a damma on the mim, a fatha on the kha and a shadda on the reddened ra, relating to "al-Makhram", a quarter in Baghdad between al-Rusafa and the river al-Mu'alla). He died in Baghdad in the year 260. Al-Nasa'i said: "He was one of the trustworthy transmitters; we have not seen anyone like him in Iraq." Al-Daraqutni said: "A trustworthy, excellent and precise transmitter." Al-Tabari's narration from him has passed as no. 3730. In the printed edition it was "al-Makhzumi".
This report was transmitted by al-Bukhari with his chain through Ubayd Allah ibn Sa'id, from Abu Amir al-Aqadi, but he mentioned only the beginning of the report, in order to establish the hearing (tahdith) of al-Hasan from Ma'qil, through his saying "Ma'qil ibn Yasar narrated to me" (Fath al-Bari 8: 143). Abu Dawud also transmitted it, through Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna, from Abu Amir al-Aqadi, and it is abridged.]]

4930. Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, who said: Yazid narrated to us, who said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿And when you divorce women and they reach their term, do not prevent them from marrying their husbands when they have agreed between themselves on a fair basis﴾. It was mentioned to us that a man divorced his wife with one divorce, then left her until her waiting period ended. Then after that he approached to propose to her, [and the woman was the sister of Ma'qil ibn Yasar,] so Ma'qil ibn Yasar was offended by this and said: "He left her while she was in her waiting period, and if he had wished, he could have taken her back. Now he wants to take her back after she has been separated from him!" So he refused to let her marry him. It was also mentioned to us that the Prophet of God, when this verse was revealed, summoned him and recited it to him, so he gave up his pride and submitted to the command of God. [[The narration: 4930. This is the chain of al-Tabari that recurs in the tafsir, from the tafsir of Qatadah, though it is in the sense of the narration of Qatadah from al-Hasan, no. 4927, and at the end of the addition to which we referred in the narration of al-Bukhari for the earlier report. "al-Hamiyya" is pride and anger. "Istafad lil-shay'": he submitted and obeyed, from "qada al-dabba yaqudu-ha" (he led the animal). That is, he gave it the reins, being neither unruly nor obstinate.]]

4931. It was reported to me from Ammar, who said: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from Yunus, from al-Hasan regarding His words, exalted is He: ﴿And when you divorce women and they reach their term, do not prevent them﴾, to the end of the verse. He said: This verse was revealed concerning Ma'qil ibn Yasar. Al-Hasan said: Ma'qil ibn Yasar narrated to me that it was revealed concerning him. He said: "I married a sister of mine to a man, and he divorced her, until when her waiting period ended he came proposing to her. So I said to him: 'I married you to her, and I furnished you with my sister and honored you. Then you divorced her, then you came proposing to her! She will never return to you!'" He said: That man was an honest man with no fault, and the woman wished to return to him. God, may His remembrance be exalted, said: ﴿And when you divorce women and they reach their term, do not prevent them from marrying their husbands when they have agreed between themselves on a fair basis﴾.
He said: So I said: "Now I will do it, O Messenger of God!" Then he married her to him. [[The narration: 4931. Transmitted by al-Bukhari. He said: "Ahmad ibn Abi Umar narrated to us, who said: my father narrated to us, who said: Ibrahim narrated to me, from Yunus." "Ahmad ibn Abi Umar" is Ahmad ibn Hafs ibn Abd Allah ibn Rashid. "Ibrahim" is Ibrahim ibn Tahman, and "Yunus" is Yunus ibn Ubayd (Fath 9: 160). Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar discussed it thoroughly, then mentioned it in (Fath 8: 143). Al-Hakim transmitted it in al-Mustadrak 2: 174, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan 7: 138, both through Ahmad ibn Hafs in the same wording as al-Bukhari's narration, and it is like al-Tabari's narration, although there is some difference in certain wording, as al-Hafiz noted in al-Fath, and he mentioned the narrations it contains. Here there is a difference that al-Hafiz did not mention, in the phrase "farashtaka ukhti" (I furnished you with my sister). This is how it is in the manuscript and the printed edition, and in al-Mustadrak and al-Dhahabi alike, while in all the other narrations it is "afrashtuka" (I furnished you). Both are correct in Arabic. From the expression "farasha fulanan bisatan" and "afrashtahu iyyahu" when one spreads a carpet for him. "Farasha lahu ukhtahu" and "afrashaha lahu" means: he made her a bed (firash) for him. The firash is a metaphor for the woman.]]

4932. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, who said: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, who said: Abu Bakr al-Hudhali narrated to us, from Bakr ibn Abd Allah al-Muzani, who said: The sister of Ma'qil ibn Yasar was under a man, who divorced her, then he proposed to her, but her brother prevented her [[In the manuscript: "ikhwatuha" (her brothers), while what is in the printed edition is more appropriate, for its agreement with all the other narrations.]], so this verse was revealed: ﴿And when you divorce women and they reach their term﴾ to the end of the verse.

4933. Al-Qasim narrated to us, who said: al-Husayn narrated to us, who said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid regarding His words: ﴿And when you divorce women and they reach their term, do not prevent them from marrying their husbands﴾, the verse. He said: It was revealed concerning a woman from Muzayna whose husband divorced her and she became separated from him (ubinat minhu), then another man married her, but her brother Ma'qil ibn Yasar prevented her, harming her, for fear that she would return to her first husband. Ibn Jurayj said: Akrimah said: It was revealed concerning Ma'qil ibn Yasar. Ibn Jurayj said: His sister was Jamal (or Jumal) daughter of Yasar, who was under Abu al-Bada'. [[In the printed edition: "Jamil" with the form of the diminutive, as Ibn Hajar said in al-Fath and al-Isaba (9: 160). The one in the manuscript is vocalized with the pen as "Jamal" with a damma on the jim. Ibn Hajar mentioned it there and in al-Isaba (with a damma on the first letter and a sukun on the mim). Ibn Hajar said that "Jamil" occurred in the tafsir of al-Tabari, but this manuscript bears witness to differences among the copies of al-Tabari. Its name and the name of "Abu al-Bada'" differ greatly; consult it in Fath al-Bari 9: 160 and al-Isaba. It will come in no. 4936 that her name was "Fatimah".]] She divorced her, her waiting period ended, he proposed to her, and Ma'qil ibn Yasar prevented her.

4934. Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, who said: Abu Asim narrated to us, from Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding His words: ﴿And when you divorce women and they reach their term, do not prevent them from marrying their husbands when they have agreed between themselves on a fair basis﴾. It was revealed concerning a woman from Muzayna whose husband divorced her, and her brother prevented her from returning to her first husband, and he was Ma'qil ibn Yasar, her brother.

4935. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, who said: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, who said: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it, except that he did not say in it: "and he was Ma'qil ibn Yasar."

4936. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, who said: Hibban ibn Musa narrated to us, who said: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, who said: Sufyan informed us, from Abu Ishaq al-Hamdani: that Fatimah daughter of Yasar was divorced by her husband, then he changed his mind and proposed to her, but Ma'qil refused. He said: "We married you and you divorced her and did what you did!" So God, may His remembrance be exalted, revealed: ﴿So do not prevent them from marrying their husbands﴾. [[The narration: 4936. "Abu Ishaq al-Hamdani" is "Abu Ishaq al-Sabi'i, Amr ibn Abd Allah ibn Ubayd, of Sabi', and Sabi' is of Hamdan." He narrated from Ali and al-Mughira ibn Shu'bah, and died in the year 126.]]

4937. Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, who said: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, who said: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Hasan and Qatadah regarding His words: ﴿So do not prevent them﴾. He said: It was revealed concerning Ma'qil ibn Yasar: his sister was under a man who divorced her, until when her waiting period ended he came and proposed to her, but Ma'qil prevented her and refused to let her marry him, so this verse was revealed concerning her. He meant by it the guardians (awliya'), saying: ﴿So do not prevent them from marrying their husbands﴾.

4938. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, who said: Jarir narrated to us, from Mansur, from a man, from Ma'qil ibn Yasar, who said: My sister was with a man who divorced her with a final divorce (bā'ina), then he proposed to her, and I refused to marry her to him, so God, may His remembrance be exalted, revealed: ﴿So do not prevent them from marrying their husbands﴾, the verse.

* *

Others said that the man was Jabir ibn Abd Allah al-Ansari.

Those who said this:

4939. Musa ibn Harun narrated to me, who said: Amr ibn Hammad narrated to us, who said: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿And when you divorce women and they reach their term, do not prevent them from marrying their husbands when they have agreed between themselves on a fair basis﴾. He said: It was revealed concerning Jabir ibn Abd Allah al-Ansari, who had a paternal cousin (female), whose husband divorced her with one divorce. Her waiting period ended, then he returned wishing to take her back. As for Jabir, he said: "You divorced our cousin, and now you want to marry her a second time!" The woman wanted her husband, and had agreed to him. So this verse was revealed.

* *

Others said: This verse was revealed as an indication of the prohibition on a man harming those women under his guardianship by preventing them from marrying.

Those who said this:

4940. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, who said: Abd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, who said: Mu'awiyah ibn Salih narrated to me, from Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn Abbas regarding His words: ﴿So do not prevent them from marrying their husbands﴾. This concerns a man who divorces his wife with one or two divorces, and her waiting period ends, then it occurs to him to marry her again and to take her back, and the woman wants that, but her guardians prevent her from it. So God, glorified is He, forbade them from preventing her.

4941. Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, who said: My father narrated to me, who said: My paternal uncle narrated to me, who said: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿And when you divorce women and they reach their term, do not prevent them from marrying their husbands when they have agreed between themselves on a fair basis﴾. A man would divorce his wife, she would become separated from him (tubayyinu minhu) and her term would end, and he would wish to take her back and she would agree, but her family would refuse. God, may His remembrance be exalted, said: ﴿So do not prevent them from marrying their husbands when they have agreed between themselves on a fair basis﴾. [[In the printed edition: "tubayyinu minhu" without the fa', and the correct form is from the manuscript.]]

4942. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, who said: Hibban ibn Musa narrated to us, who said: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Abu al-Duha, from Masruq regarding His words: ﴿So do not prevent them from marrying their husbands﴾. He said: A man would divorce his wife, then it would occur to him to marry her, but the guardians of the woman would refuse to let them marry. So God, may His remembrance be exalted, said: ﴿So do not prevent them from marrying their husbands when they have agreed between themselves on a fair basis﴾.

4943. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, who said: Jarir narrated to us, from Mughirah, from his companions, from Ibrahim regarding His words: ﴿And when you divorce women and they reach their term, do not prevent them from marrying their husbands﴾. He said: A woman is with a man, who divorces her, then wishes to return to her, and her guardian does not prevent him from marrying her.

4944. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, who said: Abd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, who said: al-Layth narrated to me, from Yunus, from Ibn Shihab: God, may His remembrance be exalted, said: ﴿And when you divorce women and they reach their term, do not prevent them from marrying their husbands﴾, the verse. So if a man divorces a woman and he is her guardian (waliyy), and her waiting period ends, then he has no right to prevent her in order to inherit from her, and to prevent her from being chaste (tasta'iff) with a husband.

4945. It was reported to me from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd ibn Salman informed us, who said: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words: ﴿And when you divorce women and they reach their term, do not prevent them﴾: It is the man who divorces his wife with one divorce, then keeps silent about her, so that he becomes one of the suitors. So God said to the guardians of the woman: ﴿do not prevent them﴾, meaning: do not prevent them from returning to their husbands in a new marriage, ﴿when they have agreed between themselves on a fair basis﴾, that is, when the woman is willing and wishes to return to her husband in a new marriage.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct statement regarding this verse is that it should be said: God, may His remembrance be exalted, revealed it as a prohibition on the guardians of women, against harming those women for whom they were guardians, by preventing them from marrying those husbands they had, who had separated from them by what a woman is separated from her husband by, whether divorce or annulment of the marriage. It may be that it was revealed concerning the matter of Ma'qil ibn Yasar and his sister, or concerning the matter of Jabir ibn Abd Allah and his paternal cousin. Whichever of these it was, the verse indicates what I have mentioned.

* *

What is meant by His words, exalted is He: ﴿So do not prevent them﴾, is: do not constrict them, O guardians, by your preventing them from returning to their husbands in a new marriage, seeking by that to harm them.

* *

It is said from this: "Adala fulan fulanah 'an al-azwaj ya'dulu-ha 'adlan" (a man prevented a woman from husbands, he prevents her with prevention). It has been mentioned to us that a tribe among the tribes of the Arabs, in its dialect, says "a'dala ya'dulu" (with the first vowel as kasra and second fatha as indicated in the manuscript). Whoever's dialect is "'adala", then if he转 to the form "yaf'ala", he says "ya'dala" with a fatha on the "dad". The recitation is with a damma on the "dad" and not a kasra, and the damma is from the dialect of the one who says "'adala".
[[This explanation is not found in the books of lexicography, and there is nothing in them of what he narrated about the dialect of this Arab tribe. His saying "'adala ya'dulu", with a kasra on the first letter and a fatha on the second, is vocalized with the pen in the manuscript, as all the other verbs are vocalized.]]

* *

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 232 (part 2 of 2):

The root of *"al-ʿadl"* (ʿ-d-l, here ʿ-ḍ-l) is *al-ḍayq* (constriction, narrowness). From it comes the saying of ʿUmar (may Allah have mercy on him): *"The people of Iraq have ʿaʿḍalūnī (put me in a bind); they are not pleased with any governor, and no governor is pleased with them."* [[Al-Zamakhshari and the author of Lisan al-ʿArab, under the root (ʿ-ḍ-l), report: "The people of Kufa have put me in a bind; they are not pleased with any amir, and no amir is pleased with them." Then al-Zamakhshari said: "It is also reported: The people of Kufa have overpowered me. If I appoint a believer over them, he grows weak, and if I appoint a dissolute man over them, he becomes dissolute!"]] He means: they burdened me with a severe and constricted matter that I cannot bear to carry out.

From the same root comes *"al-dāʾ al-ʿuḍāl"* (an incurable disease), the disease whose treatment cannot be endured, because of its constriction against treatment and because it exceeds the limit of diseases that have a cure. From it is the verse of Dhu al-Rummah:

*"And I have not slandered a chaste, virtuous believing woman, with Allah's permission, bringing upon her an ʿuḍāl (inescapable) accusation."* [[From his Diwan, p. 441, one of the verses in which he describes the craft of his poetry:

"A poem I have polished, strange, whose couplings and rhymes are foreign to the mountain-slopes and the wastelands.
Strange verses, known in every horizon of the horizons, fashioned with fashioning.
So I spent the night straightening it and cutting it, with rhymes for which I know no equal."

"Strange verses, known in every horizon... fashioned with fashioning."

"And I have not slandered..." [the rest of the line is missing].

This last verse satirizes the leaders of invective in his age: Jarir, al-Farazdaq, al-Akhtal and all who hurled abuse at one another. *Al-ḥaṣān* means the chaste, pure woman. *Al-mūjiba* means that which incurs the prescribed punishment for slander, or which incurs the Fire, from which Allah protect us! *Al-ʿuḍāl* means that from which there is no escape and for which there is no cure. The sense of the verse is: "I did not slander, with an accusation that incurs ʿuḍāl, a chaste believing woman," meaning: I did not hurl the disgraceful word and the foul abuse, seeking thereby to defame a chaste woman whom Allah has cleared of what is said. The Diwan's reading is *"bi-ḥamd Allah"* (with the praise of Allah), and it is better. This verse in the manuscript is corrupt: "la-ramathu ḥiṣāl" (!!).]]

From the same root is the saying: *"ʿaḍala al-faḍāʾ bi-l-jaysh li-kathratihim"* (the open space constricted the army because of their number), meaning that it became too narrow for them because of their multitude. It is also said: *"ʿaḍalat al-mar'ah"* (the woman was obstructed), when the child became lodged in her womb and it became difficult for it to come out. From it is the verse of Aws ibn Ḥajar:

*"Your brother, who keeps his covenant constantly, is not the one who blames you when he turns away, and pleases you when he approaches;*
*But rather the one who is far away when you are secure, and your close companion when the matter becomes ʿuḍāl (grave)."* [[From his Diwan, poem no. 31. These two verses unveil the inner secrets of people without deception. Rarely does one attain that.]]

* *

The *"an"* in His saying *"an yankiḥna"* (that they marry) is in the accusative position, as the object of *"taʿḍulūhunna"* (you prevent them).

The meaning of His saying *"idhā tarāḍaw baynahum bi-l-maʿrūf"* (when they agree among themselves in a fair manner) is: when the husbands and the women agree on what is lawful. It may also be that it refers to their *abḍāʿ* (intimate relations), from the dowries, and a new, fresh marriage contract. [[Al-abḍāʿ is the plural of *buḍʿ* (with a damma and a sukun): it means the private part, intercourse, the marriage contract, and the dowry; the first meaning is what is intended here.]] As follows:

4946. Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Raḥman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from ʿUmayr ibn ʿAbd Allah, from ʿAbd al-Malik ibn al-Mughirah, from ʿAbd al-Raḥman ibn al-Bayylamani, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: *"Marry off the single ones (al-ayama)."* A man said: "O Messenger of Allah, what are the ʿalāʾiq (conditions/bonds) between them?" He said: *"What their families agree upon."* [[Hadith 4946: ʿAbd al-Raḥman is Ibn Mahdi. Sufyan is al-Thawri. ʿUmayr ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Bishr al-Khathʿami: reliable (thiqa), declared reliable by Ibn Numayr and others. ʿAbd al-Malik ibn al-Mughirah al-Ṭāʾifi: a reliable Successor (tabiʿi), and here he narrates from another Successor. ʿAbd al-Raḥman ibn al-Bayylamani, client of ʿUmar: a reliable Successor, about whom some scholars spoke; the truth is that what is rejected in his narrations came from what his son Muhammad narrated from him. As for himself, he is reliable. This hadith is weak, because it is mursal (its chain omits a Companion). Al-Bayhaqi narrated it, 7:239, through Qays ibn al-Rabiʿ, from ʿUmayr ibn ʿAbd Allah, with this same chain. Then he narrated it through Ḥafs ibn Ghiyath and Abu Muʿawiya, from Ḥajjaj ibn Arṭa'ah, from ʿAbd al-Malik ibn al-Mughirah al-Ṭāʾifi, then said: "This is munqaṭiʿ (broken in its chain)."]]

4947. Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Ḥarith narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥman ibn al-Bayylamani narrated to us, from his father, from Ibn ʿUmar, from the Prophet (ﷺ), with something similar to it. [[Hadith 4947: It is a repetition of the hadith before it, but in this version it is connected (muttasil), by mention of "Ibn ʿUmar" in it. It is also weak, indeed weaker than that mursal narration. Muhammad ibn al-Ḥarith ibn Ziyad ibn al-Rabiʿ al-Ḥarithi: reliable, but spoken about. We have elaborated on his evaluation in the commentary on the Musnad, 5371. Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥman ibn al-Bayylamani: very weak. The affliction lies in the hadiths of his father, and then in the hadiths of Muhammad ibn al-Ḥarith al-Ḥarithi; it comes only from his side. He narrated from his father hadiths that are munkar (rejected), with no basis, or mursal narrations with no basis for their connection, and al-Ḥarithi narrated from him, so each of them was criticized because of the other. We have elaborated on his weakening in the commentary on the Musnad, 4910. This hadith was narrated by al-Bayhaqi, 7:239, through Bundar, who is Muhammad ibn Bashshar, the shaykh of al-Tabari here, with this same chain. Then he narrated it through Abu ʿAbd al-Raḥman al-Ḥaḍrami Ṣāliḥ ibn ʿAbd al-Jabbar, from Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥman ibn al-Bayylamani, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas! Then he quoted from Abu Ahmad ibn ʿAdi, who said: "Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥman ibn al-Bayylamani is weak, and Muhammad ibn al-Ḥarith is weak, and the weakness in their hadith is evident." Al-Suyuti, 1:287, also quoted it from the hadith of Ibn ʿUmar, attributing it to Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh, then he remained silent about its weakness.]]

* *

Abu Jaʿfar said: In this verse there is clear evidence for the correctness of the view of those who say: "There is no marriage except with a wali (guardian) from among the ʿaṣabah (male agnatic relatives)." This is because Allah, exalted is His remembrance, forbade the guardian from preventing the woman when she wishes to marry, and prohibited him from doing so. If it were the case that a woman could contract her own marriage without her guardian's contracting it for her, or that she had the right to appoint whomever she wished to contract it for her, then the prohibition against her guardian preventing her would have no understood meaning, since he would have no way to prevent her. For if she were able, whenever she wished to marry, to contract it herself, or to have it contracted by whomever she authorized, then there would be no preventing by anyone that would require a prohibition against the one who prevents her. And in the invalidity of the claim that there is no meaning in Allah's prohibition of what He prohibited, lies the soundness of the view that the woman's guardian has a right in her marriage without which its contract is not valid. This is the meaning by which Allah commanded the guardian to marry her off when a suitor proposes to her and she is pleased with him, and when her guardians are content, and when such a match is permissible in the judgment of the Muslims for one like her to marry one like him, and He forbade him to oppose this, by preventing her and keeping her from what she wished of that, while she and the suitor were in agreement.

* *

On the interpretation of His saying, exalted is His remembrance: ﴿That is admonished thereby whoever among you believes in Allah and the Last Day﴾

Abu Jaʿfar said: By His saying "that," exalted is His remembrance, He means what He mentioned in this verse: the prohibition of the woman's guardians from preventing her from marriage. He says: "This which I have forbidden you, of preventing them from marrying, is an admonition from Me to whoever among you, O people, believes in Allah and the Last Day," meaning: who affirms Allah, declares Him one, and acknowledges His lordship, [[See what has preceded regarding the meaning of "faith" (*al-īmān*) under the root (ʾ-m-n) in the language indexes in the earlier volumes.]] "and the Last Day," meaning: whoever believes in the Last Day, affirming the resurrection for reckoning, reward and punishment, [[See what has preceded regarding the interpretation of "the Last Day," 1:271 / 2:148.]] so that he fears Allah regarding himself, and does not wrong her by harming her through preventing her from marrying the one she has accepted for herself, from among those whom she has authorized to marry her.

* *

Abu Jaʿfar said: If someone says to us: "How is it said, 'That is admonished thereby,' when the address is to a plural group, and He had said previously, 'So do not prevent them'? And if it is permissible to say 'that' in addressing a group, may one say to a group of people while addressing them, 'O people, this is your boy, and this is your servant,' while you mean: 'This is your servant, and this is your boy'?"

It is said: No, that is not permissible with the *al-asmāʾ al-mawḍūʿāt* (the fixed nouns), [[*al-ism al-mawḍūʿ*, as if it means "the declinable or inflected noun," as opposed to "the indeclinable or indeclinable noun."]] because what is attached to these nouns is other than them, [[His saying "other than them" means other than the nouns.]] so no listener who hears a speaker say to a group, "O people, this is your boy," understands that he meant "this is your boys," except as a mistake by the speaker in his speech. If he seeks a correct justification for that speech, he diverts his words to having turned away from addressing the group with what he intended to address them, toward addressing one man from among them or from others, and leaves off going beyond the group with what he intended to go beyond them with in speech. [[In the printed edition: "mujāwazat al-qawm... mujāwazatihim", with the jim and zay in both places, which is meaningless. The correct reading is that of the manuscript and what the context requires.]] But this is not the case with "dhālika" (that), because of how frequently it runs on the tongues of the Arabs in their speech and discourse, until the *kāf* (the particle of the second-person address) in it became like a letter of the word that is attached to it. And the word, with it, became like someone saying "hādhā" (this), as if there were no second-person noun with it. [[He means that it has become like "hādhā" in its usage, as if it were a single word, and it is composed of the *hāʾ* and *dhā*, which is a demonstrative noun.]] So whoever says, "That is admonished thereby whoever among you believes in Allah and the Last Day," keeps the *kāf* in "dhālika" fixed and open, in addressing a single woman, a single man, the dual, and the plural. And whoever says, "Dhālikum yūʿaẓu bihi" (that is admonished thereby to you), makes the *kāf* kasra when addressing a single woman, and fatḥa when addressing a single man, so he says in addressing two of them: "dhālikumā," and in addressing the plural: "dhālikum." [[In both the printed edition and the manuscript: "fa-qāla fī khiṭāb" with a fāʾ, which does not stand.]]

It has been said that His saying, "That is admonished thereby whoever among you believes in Allah," is an address to the Prophet (ﷺ), and for that reason it is in the singular, then it returned to addressing the believers with His saying, "whoever among you believes in Allah." If the interpretation is directed toward this aspect, there is no difficulty in it. [[In the printed edition: "wa-li-dhālika wajh" (and for that there is a face/aspect), which is a meaningless statement; the correct reading is that of the manuscript.]]

* *

On the interpretation of His saying, exalted is His remembrance: ﴿That is purer for you and more pure, and Allah knows while you know not﴾ (2:232)

Abu Jaʿfar said: By His saying "that," exalted is His remembrance, He means their marrying their husbands and the husbands' returning to them, [[In the printed edition: "nikāḥ azwājihinna lahunna" (the marriage of their husbands to them), while in the manuscript: "nikāḥuhunna azwājahunna lahunna." What is in the printed edition is one way of correcting what is in the manuscript, but I have seen that the correction has another possibility, namely deleting "lahunna." This is because he intended by his saying "nikāḥuhunna azwājahunna" what occurs in the verse, "an yankiḥna azwājahunna," with the "marriage" ascribed to the women; for this reason I chose this correction, and so that there would not be a repetition in the speech after his saying "and the husbands' returning to them."]] by what He permitted them of marriage and a new dowry, "is purer for you," O guardians, husbands and wives.

* *

By His saying "purer for you" He means better and more excellent in the sight of Allah than their separation from their husbands. We have already explained the meaning of *al-zakāh* (purity/growth), so that is sufficient and needs no repetition. [[See what has preceded: 1:573-574 / 2:297 / 3:88.]]

* *

As for His saying "and more pure" (*wa-aṭhar*), He means by it: more pure for your hearts and their hearts and the hearts of their husbands from doubt (*al-rayb*). This is because if there is in the soul of each of the two of them, I mean the husband and the wife, a bond of love, one cannot be safe that they will go beyond that to what Allah has not made lawful for them, nor can their guardians be safe that thoughts may come to their hearts about them that they may well be free of. So Allah, exalted is His remembrance, commanded the guardians, when the husbands wish to return after the separation, by a new marriage contract, in the situation in which Allah has permitted them to return [[In the printed edition: "adhina Allah lahumā" (Allah permitted them both), while the manuscript has no addition of "Allah."]] = that they not prevent their ward from what she wishes of that, and that they marry her. For that is better for all of them, and more pure for their hearts from the disliked meanings whose coming to them is feared. [["Sabūq" is a verbal noun of *sabaqa*, which has not appeared in the lexicographical books, but al-Tabari frequently uses it, as we pointed out earlier in volume 4: 287, 288 / then 427 / then 446, and the notes on them.]]

Then Allah, exalted is His remembrance, informed His servants that He knows their secret thoughts and hidden affairs, which some of them do not know about others, and by His saying to them in this place, He indicated that He only commanded the guardians of women to marry off those under their guardianship when the woman and the suitor agree among themselves in a fair manner, and forbade them from preventing them from that, [because of what He knows of what is in the heart of the suitor and the one proposed to, from the dominance of desire and the inclination of each of them toward the other with affection and love]. So He, exalted is His remembrance, said to them: "Do what I have commanded you, if you believe in Me, and in My reward and My punishment in your return in the Hereafter, for I know what is in the heart of the suitor and the woman proposed to, which you do not know of desire and love. Your doing that is better for you in the sight of Allah and for them, and purer for your hearts and their hearts in this world." [[This is the speech of a learned, wise rabbi, whom Allah has granted understanding in the affairs of his religion, given wisdom in the affairs of his worldly life, and taught the interpretation of His Book. He bore the trust and fulfilled it, gave sincere counsel to the people, taught and enlightened them, and was not occupied, in interpreting the Book of his Lord, with grammar, language, jurisprudence or the principles of jurisprudence, as they have agreed upon, from unveiling the meanings for people, addressing their hearts and minds with them, so that he might make clear to them what Allah sent down to His Prophet, by the covenant that Allah took from the scholars. So may Allah have mercy on Abu Jaʿfar, and forgive the commentators after him. Rarely does one find anything like what is written in this book among the books of tafsir.]]

The commentary on His words, exalted is He: ﴿The mothers shall suckle their children for two full years, for whoever wishes to complete the suckling﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: By this, may His remembrance be exalted, He means: "And the women who are divorced by their husbands and who have children they bore by them before their separation through divorce, or whom they bore after separating from them, from intercourse that took place between them before the separation [[In the printed edition: "aw awladnahunna" ("or bore them"), which is a gross error. The correct reading is from the manuscript.]], shall suckle their children," meaning: they have more right to suckle them than anyone else.

This is not an obligation from God, may His remembrance be exalted, upon them to suckle them, when the child's father is a man of means who is alive [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "walidan" ("a father"), but the context requires what I have adopted.]]. This is because God, may His remembrance be exalted, said in "Surat al-Nisa' al-Qusra" [[This is "Surat al-Talaq," the sixty-fifth surah of the Book of God.
