They called it "al-Qusra" (the shorter) to distinguish it from the fourth surah of the Qur'an, which they called "Surat al-Nisa' al-Tulla" (the longer).]]: ﴿And if you disagree, then another woman shall suckle for him﴾ [Surat al-Talaq: 6]. So He informed, may His remembrance be exalted [[In the printed edition: "wa-akhbara ta'ala anna al-walidah..." with the addition from the manuscript. Both have "wa-akhbara" with a waw, but the context requires the fa' as I have adopted.]], that if the mother and the child's father disagree about the wage with which the woman suckles her child, another woman may suckle him instead. Thus He did not make it obligatory upon her to suckle her child. It was therefore clear from this that His words, "The mothers shall suckle their children for two years," indicate the limit of the period of suckling: when the two parents disagree about the suckling of the child after it, this period is set as a boundary to separate them. It is not an indication that suckling their children is an obligation upon mothers.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: As for His words, "two years" (ḥawlayn), it means two years, as follows:

4948. Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding "The mothers shall suckle their children for two full years": two years.

4949. Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa related to us, saying: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.

* *

The root of "ḥawl" (year) comes from the saying of the speaker: "This thing ḥāla" (changed), when it moved. From this it is said: "So-and-so taḥawwala from such-and-such a place" when he moved away from it.

* *

If someone says to us: What is the meaning of the mention of "full" (kāmilayn) in His words, "The mothers shall suckle their children two full years," after His words, "suckle two years"? And since "the two years" is mentioned, mention of "full" is unnecessary, since the meaning is not unclear to a hearer who hears His words, "The mothers shall suckle their children two years," so what is the reason for which "full" was added?

It is said: The Arabs do say: "So-and-so stayed in such-and-such a place two years, or two days, or two months," when in fact he stayed there one day and part of another, or one month and part of another, or one year and part of another. So "two full years" was said so that the hearers would know that what is meant is two complete years, not a year and part of another. [[In the printed edition: "li-ya'rif sami'u dhalik" (singular), and I have adopted the manuscript.]] That is like the saying of God, may His remembrance be exalted: ﴿And remember God during the numbered days. Whoever hastens in two days, there is no sin upon him, and whoever delays, there is no sin upon him﴾ [Surat al-Baqarah: 203]. It is known that one who hastens only hastens within a day and a half, and likewise the third day of the days of tashriq [[In the manuscript and the printed edition: "fa-kadhalika dhalik," with a fa', which is a confusing error; the correct reading is what I have adopted. In al-Farra's Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1:119: "wa-kadhalika huwa fi al-yawm..." His text. He means that the third day of the days of tashriq is also an incomplete day. See the following note, p. 33, no. 2, and its references.]] is also incomplete, and none of it is a complete day. But the Arabs do this with times in particular, saying: "Today is two days since I have not seen him," while meaning a day and part of another. They also attach the action they do in an hour or a moment to a year, a time or a day, saying: "I visited him in such-and-such a year [[In the printed edition: "razaqahu 'am kadha," which is meaningless; the correct reading is from the manuscript, though its letters are unpointed.]]," and "So-and-so killed so-and-so in the time of Siffin." They do this because they do not intend by it to report the number of days and years, but only to report the time at which the one reported about was (in that state). So it was permissible to say "two years" and "two days," as I described earlier, because the meaning of the statement is: I did it at that time and in that moment. [[This was mentioned earlier with different wording in vol. 4: 120, 121, and much of its wording appears here in al-Farra's Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1:119-120. From both passages we have corrected what we corrected above.]]

Likewise His words, "The mothers shall suckle their children two full years," since suckling was permissible within two years, though they are not exactly two years [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "lamma kana al-radla'" ("since suckling was..."), which is a very serious corruption; the context requires reading it as I have adopted, for the meaning to be correct.]], and the statement, had it been unqualified, without specifying the two years as complete [[In the printed edition: "tadmin al-hawlayn bi-al-kamal" ("specifying the two years as complete"). In the manuscript: "tadmin" without dots, the mim appearing like a short ha'. I think the copyist erred and the correct reading is "tabyin" (clarification), since he says shortly after: "And I clarify by His words, 'full'..." because clarification is explanation, and description includes explanation and clarification.]], would have been "The mothers shall suckle their children two years," which might have meant a year and part of another. With His words "full" he removed that ambiguity from the hearers, and by "full" he clarified the time of the completion of the limit of suckling: that it is the completion of the two years by their ending, not the ending of one of them and part of the other.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: Then the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed about what this verse indicates regarding the limit of the suckling period of the infants: is it a limit for every child, or a limit for some and not others? Some of them said: It is a limit for some and not others.

Those who said this:

4950. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Wahhab related to us, saying: Dawud related to us, from 'Ikrima, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding the woman who gives birth after six months: she suckles for two full years. And if she gives birth after seven months, she suckles twenty-three months, to complete thirty months. And if she gives birth after nine months, she suckles twenty-one months.

4951. Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Dawud related to us, from 'Ikrima, the same, but he did not trace it back to Ibn 'Abbas.

4952. Al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from Abu 'Ubayd, who said: A woman who had given birth after six months was brought to 'Uthman, and he said: "She was reported to me, and I do not see her as anything but having come with [...] — or something like this — and having given birth after six months!" Ibn 'Abbas said: "If she completed the suckling, the pregnancy was six months." He said: Ibn 'Abbas recited: ﴿And his carrying and weaning are thirty months﴾ [Surat al-Ahqaf: 15], so if she completed the suckling, the pregnancy was six months. So 'Uthman released her. [[The report 4952: Abu 'Ubayd is Sa'd ibn 'Ubayd, "mawla 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Azhar," and is also called "mawla 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf." Al-Bukhari said in al-Kabir 2/2/61: "Because they were paternal cousins." He also said in his Sahih 4:209: "Ibn 'Uyayna said: whoever says 'mawla Ibn Azhar' is right, and whoever says 'mawla 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf' is also right." He was an ancient, trustworthy Successor (tabi'i), one of the jurists of Medina, who narrated from 'Umar, 'Uthman, 'Ali, and others.
In the printed edition it appears as "'an Abi 'Ubayda," which is an error; we have corrected it from the book of al-Musannaf of 'Abd al-Razzaq, vol. 4, folio 97, where it reads: "'an Abi 'Ubayd, mawla 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf."
Al-Suyuti cited it at 6:40, attributing it only to 'Abd al-Razzaq and 'Abd ibn Humayd. In the manuscript and the printed edition it was: "innaha rufi'at la ara-ha," and in the Musannaf of 'Abd al-Razzaq: "rufi'at ila imra'a, la ara-hu illa qal: wa-qad ja'at bi-shar."]]

* *

And others said: Rather, that is the limit of suckling for every child whose two parents disagreed about its suckling, so one of them wants to go to the limit, and the other wants to fall short of it.

Those who said this:

4953. Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiya related to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His words: "The mothers shall suckle their children two full years": God, glorified is He, made suckling two full years for whoever wishes to complete the suckling. Then He said: "If they both desire weaning by mutual consent and consultation, there is no sin upon them," meaning if they both wish to wean him before the two years and after them.

4954. Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Suwayd related to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: I asked 'Ata': "The mothers shall suckle their children two full years." He said: If the mother wants to fall short of the two years, it is her right to reach it, but she should not exceed it unless he wishes. [[In the printed edition: "illa an tasha'" ("unless she wishes"), and the correct reading is what I have adopted from the manuscript: i.e., unless the husband wishes, and agrees with her about the increase she wants.]]

4955. Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us [[He is "Mihran ibn Abi 'Umar al-'Attar, Abu 'Abd Allah al-Razi." Abu Hatim said he was trustworthy and good in hadith. Ibn 'Adi related hadiths to him from the narration of Muhammad ibn Humayd from him, then said: "All these hadiths are from Mihran except a few, which Muhammad ibn Humayd narrates from him, and Ibn Humayd is busy with what he narrates from people! Mihran is better than him." Al-Saji said: "There is confusion in his hadith, and he is one of the most prolific narrators from al-Thawri." Al-'Uqayli said: "He narrated from al-Thawri hadiths that are not corroborated." Ibn Hibban said: "He embraced Islam at the hand of al-Thawri, and he compiled (al-Jami' al-Saghir)." From al-Tahdhib.]]
= And 'Ali ibn Sahl related to me, saying: Zayd ibn Abi al-Zarqa' related to us = all of them, from al-Thawri, regarding His words: "The mothers shall suckle their children two full years for whoever wishes to complete the suckling," and that completion is the two years. He said: So if the father wants to wean him before the two years and the woman does not agree, he has no right to do so. And if the woman says: "I will wean him before the two years," and the father says: "No," she has no right to wean him until the father agrees, until they both agree. If they agree, they may wean him before the two years, and if they disagree, they may not wean him before the two years. This is His words: "If they both desire weaning by mutual consent and consultation."

* *

And others said: Rather, God, may His remembrance be exalted, indicated by His words, "The mothers shall suckle their children two full years," that there is no suckling after the two years, for suckling is only within the two years.

Those who said this:

4956. Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Adam related to us, saying: Ibn Abi Dhi'b informed us, saying: al-Zuhri related to us, from Ibn 'Abbas and Ibn 'Umar, that both of them said: God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: "The mothers shall suckle their children two full years," and we do not see suckling after the two years making anything unlawful [[The wajur (with a fatha on the waw) is medicine that enters the mouth; the sa'ut (with a fatha on the sin) is medicine that enters the nose.]].

4957. Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak related to us, from Yunus ibn Yazid, from al-Zuhri, who said: Ibn 'Umar and Ibn 'Abbas used to say: There is no suckling after the two years.

4958. Abu al-Sa'ib related to us, saying: Hafs related to us, from al-Shaybani, from Abu al-Duha, from Abu 'Abd al-Rahman, from 'Abd Allah, who said: Whatever suckling is after two years, or within the two years after weaning, is not suckling.

4959. Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Yahya ibn Sa'id and 'Abd al-Rahman related to us, both saying: Sufyan related to us, from al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, from 'Alqama, that he saw a woman suckling after two years, and he said: "Do not suckle him."

4960. Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from al-Shaybani, who said: I heard al-Sha'bi say: Whatever wajur or sa'ut or suckling is within the two years, it makes unlawful, and whatever is after the two years does not make anything unlawful. [[The wajur (with a fatha on the waw) is medicine that enters the mouth. The sa'ut (with a fatha on the sin) is medicine that enters the nose.]]

4961. Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far related to us, saying: Shu'ba related to us, from al-Mughira, from Ibrahim, that he used to narrate from 'Abd Allah that he said: There is no suckling after weaning, or after two years.

4962. Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Hasan ibn 'Atiyya related to us, saying: Isra'il related to us, from 'Abd al-A'la, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Suckling does not make unlawful after completion; what makes unlawful is that which causes flesh to grow and bone to form. [[The report 4962: "al-Hasan ibn 'Atiyya ibn Najih al-Qurashi Abu 'Ali al-Bazzar" narrated from al-Hasan and 'Ali, the two sons of Salih, Ya'qub al-Qummi, Hamza al-Zayyat, Isra'il ibn Yunus, and their generation. From him narrated al-Bukhari in al-Tarikh, 'Abd al-A'la ibn Wasil, Abu Kurayb, Abu Zur'a, and Abu Hatim. He is truthful. He died in the year 211.]]

4963. Al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from 'Amr ibn Dinar, that Ibn 'Abbas said: There is no suckling after the weaning of the two years.

4964. Hilal ibn al-'Ala' al-Raqqi related to us, saying: My father related to us, saying: 'Ubayd Allah related to us, from Zayd, from 'Amr ibn Murra, from Abu al-Duha, who said: I heard Ibn 'Abbas say: "The mothers shall suckle their children two full years": There is no suckling except within these two years. [[Report 4964: Hilal ibn al-'Ala' ibn Hilal ibn 'Amr al-Bahili, Abu 'Amr al-Raqqi. Abu Hatim said: "Truthful." al-Nasa'i said: "Sound." He said in another place: "There is nothing wrong with him; he narrated odd hadiths from his father, so I do not know whether the doubt is from him or from his father." Ibn Hibban mentioned him among the trustworthy. He was born in the year 184 and died in 280. His father al-'Ala' ibn Hilal narrated from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr al-Raqqi, Khalaf ibn Khalifa, Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman, and a group. Abu Hatim said: "Munkar al-hadith, weak in hadith." Ibn Hibban mentioned him among the weak and said: "He inverts chains and changes names, so it is not permissible to argue with him." He was born in the year 150 and died in 215. "'Ubayd Allah" is 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Amr ibn Abi al-Walid al-Asadi al-Raqqi. He narrated from 'Abd al-Malik ibn 'Umayr, Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Ansari, Ibn Abi Unaysa, and others. Abu Hatim said: "Sound in hadith, trustworthy and truthful; I do not know any odd hadith from him." He was born in 101 and died in 180. "Zayd" is Zayd ibn Abi Unaysa al-Jazari al-Rahawi. Ibn Sa'd said: "He lived in al-Ruha and died there." He was trustworthy, abundant in hadith, a jurist, and a transmitter of knowledge. He died in 125 at the age of thirty-six.]]

* *

And others said: Rather, His words, "The mothers shall suckle their children two full years," were an indication from God, may His remembrance be exalted, to His servants [[The word "'ibadahu" ("His servants") is in the accusative as the object of the verbal noun "dalala" (indication).]], that it is an obligation upon mothers of infants to suckle them for two full years. Then God, may His remembrance be exalted, lightened this by His words, "for whoever wishes to complete the suckling," and made the choice in this to the fathers and mothers: if they wish completion, they complete two years, and if they wish before that to wean the infant, that is up to them, according to their consideration for the infant [[Consideration (al-nazar): choosing the best matters for him, in care, protection, and guardianship, and seeking his welfare.]].

Those who said this:

4965. Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada regarding His words: "The mothers shall suckle their children two full years." Then God sent ease and lightening after that, and He, may His remembrance be exalted, said: "for whoever wishes to complete the suckling."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 233 (part 2 of 6):

4966 - I was told on the authority of ʿAmmar, who said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar related to us, from his father, from al-Rabiʿ, concerning His words: "The mothers shall breastfeed their children for two complete years," meaning the divorced women: they shall breastfeed their children for two complete years. Then God revealed the concession and the lightening after that, saying: "for whoever wishes to complete the nursing."
* *
Mention of those who said that "the mothers" whom God mentioned in this passage are the women who have been irrevocably divorced by their husbands, as we described earlier. [[See what has passed at the beginning of the tafsir of this verse, pp. 30, 31.]]
4967 - Musa related to me, who said: ʿAmr related to us, who said: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, who said, regarding "The mothers shall breastfeed their children for two complete years" through "if you hand over what you have given in accordance with what is customary": as for "The mothers shall breastfeed their children for two complete years," a man divorces his wife while she has a child by him, and she nurses his child in the same way another woman would nurse it for him.
4968 - Al-Muthanna related to me, who said: Suwayd ibn Nasr related to us, who said: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak concerning His words: "The mothers shall breastfeed their children for two complete years," he said: This is when a man divorces his wife while she is nursing a child for him.
4969 - Al-Muthanna related to us, who said: Ishaq related to us, who said: Abu Zuhayr related to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, similarly.
* *
Abu Jaʿfar said: The most correct of the opinions regarding His words, "The mothers shall breastfeed their children for two complete years, for whoever wishes to complete the nursing," is the opinion transmitted by ʿAli ibn Abi Talha from Ibn ʿAbbas, which ʿAta' and al-Thawri agreed with, and the opinion transmitted from ʿAbdullah ibn Masʿud, Ibn ʿAbbas and Ibn ʿUmar: that it is an indication of the limit at which the nursing of a child ends when its parents disagree about its nursing, [[In the manuscript: "wa-idha ikhtalafa wa-anna la rada'a", with a gap of two or three words. In the printed edition: "idha ikhtalafa walidahu wa-anna la rada'a", and I added "fi rada'ihi" based on the wording of the reports transmitted from them above, pp. 34, 35, and on Abu Jaʿfar's explanation a few lines later.]] and that there is no nursing after the two years that makes anything forbidden, and that it refers to every child, whether born at six months, seven or nine.
* *
As for our statement, "it is an indication of the limit at which nursing ends when the parents disagree about it," it is because God, may His remembrance be exalted, when He set a limit in this matter, it was not permissible that what lies beyond His limit should share the same ruling as what falls short of it, for if that were so, the limit would have no rational meaning. Given this, there is no doubt that the period less than two years is a time for nursing, so what lies beyond it is not a time for it, and it is a time for ceasing nursing. And since the completion of nursing is the completion of two years, and since for complete things there is no meaning in adding to them [[In the printed edition: "wa-kana al-tamam min al-ashya' la ma'na lil-ziyada fihi", which is a statement with no real content. In the manuscript: "wa-lamma kana al-tamam min al-ashya' la ma'na lil-ziyada fihi," with a gap between the words, which shows the copyist thought something was missing; but the truth is there is a distortion, one reading "al-tamm" as "al-tamam." We have established the correct reading, of which there is no other.]] to it, there is no meaning in adding to nursing beyond two years. And since what is less than two years of nursing is forbidden, what lies beyond it is not forbidden.
As for our statement, "it is an indication that it refers to every child, whatever time of its birth, whether six months, seven or nine," it is because God, may His remembrance be exalted, spoke generally with His words, "The mothers shall breastfeed their children for two complete years," and did not restrict it to some children over others.
We have already demonstrated the falsity of the view that it is specific without a clarification from God, may His remembrance be exalted, in His Book, or on the tongue of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), in our book ﴿The Clarification on the Foundations of the Rulings﴾, with what makes it unnecessary to repeat here.
* *
If someone says to us: God, may His remembrance be exalted, has already clarified this with His words, ﴿And his carrying and his weaning is thirty months﴾ [Surah al-Ahqaf: 15], thereby setting it as a limit for both matters, so it is not permissible for pregnancy and nursing to exceed the limit God, may His remembrance be exalted, has set. Whatever falls short of nine months of pregnancy is an addition to the period of nursing, and whatever is added to the period of pregnancy is subtracted from the period of nursing. And it is not permissible to exceed thirty months for both of them together, as God, may His remembrance be exalted, has set.
It is said to him: According to this view, it would have to be that if the pregnancy reached two complete years, the child would only be nursed for six months, and if it reached four years, nursing would be annulled and she would not nurse, because the pregnancy would have exhausted the thirty months and gone beyond its limit. [[This is a continuation of the phrase, "then it would have to be that the period of pregnancy..." and "or the one who holds this view claims..."]] Or the proponent of this view would have to claim that the pregnancy will never exceed nine months, thereby departing from the consensus of all proofs and contradicting what is existent and observed, and both of these are sufficient as evidence against the error of his claim if he makes it. Whichever of the two alternatives the proponent of this view resorts to, its falsity becomes clear to those of understanding.
* *
If someone says to us: What then is the meaning of His words, if the matter is as you have described, "And his carrying and his weaning is thirty months," when you have already mentioned that it is not permissible for what exceeds the limit God, may His remembrance be exalted, has set to be equivalent in ruling to what falls short of it? And you have said that carrying and weaning may exceed thirty months?
It is said: God, may His remembrance be exalted, did not make His words, "And his carrying and his weaning is thirty months," a limit by which His servants are bound not to exceed, as He made His words, "The mothers shall breastfeed their children for two complete years, for whoever wishes to complete the nursing," a limit for the nursing of a child whose nursing is established, [[In the printed edition: "li-rada'i al-mawlud al-tamm al-rada'," which is also a phrase without clear meaning; they changed what is in the manuscript as we have recorded it, supposing it was not understandable! By his words "whose nursing is established," he means the child that has been established as one that "is nursed," as will become clear from the context of his speech below.]] and as a command for servants regarding the carrying of their parents when they disagree about it, and one of them intends harm to the child. This is because a command from God, may His remembrance be exalted, applies only to what is within the servants' power to obey by doing and to disobey by abandoning. [[That is: and to disobedience by abandoning it.]] As for what is neither within their power to do nor to abandon, it is not permissible to command it, forbid it, or make it an act of worship.
Given that this is so, and since carrying is something women have no way to shorten or prolong, so that they may bear it whenever they wish or delay its delivery whenever they wish, it becomes known that His words, "And his carrying and his weaning is thirty months," are merely information from God, may His remembrance be exalted, that whoever He created, carried, bore and weaned, did so in thirty months, not a command that carrying and weaning must not exceed thirty months, for the reasons we have described. Likewise our Lord, may His remembrance be exalted, said in His Book: ﴿And We have enjoined upon man goodness to his parents. His mother carried him with hardship and gave birth to him with hardship, and his carrying and his weaning is thirty months﴾ [[Here ends the old division from which our copy was taken. The text following it reads: "And may God bless Muhammad the Prophet, his family and companions, and grant them abundant peace."]] [Surah al-Ahqaf: 15].
[[The beginning of the old division, and the text before it reads:
"In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.
My Lord, help, O Generous One."]] If someone of dull understanding thinks that because God, may His remembrance be exalted, described that whoever He created was carried by his mother, given birth to and weaned in thirty months, then it is necessary that all His creatures have this attribute, and that this is evidence that the carrying and weaning of every one of His servants is thirty months, [[His words "then it is necessary" are the answer to "if someone of dull understanding thinks..."]] then it would be necessary that all His servants have the attribute of saying, when they reach their maturity and attain forty years: ﴿My Lord, enable me to be grateful for Your favor which You have bestowed upon me and upon my parents, and to do righteousness that You approve﴾ [Surah al-Ahqaf: 15], according to what God described in this verse. [[He means that the verse of Surah al-Ahqaf refers to a specific group of people and not to all people in general, as its apparent recitation indicates.]]
Among us there exist those whose disbelief in God has become firmly fixed, [[Wajada al-shay' yajiduhu wujudan. His words "man yastahkimu" are the object of the verbal noun.]] whose ingratitude for the blessings of their Lord is entrenched, and who are bold toward their parents with killing, insults and various kinds of harm, when they have completed forty years of age and reached their maturity. [[The context: "among us there exist those whose disbelief... what is known..." is a postponed subject.]] Do we not know that God did not mean by this verse the attribute of all His servants, but that He described only some of them and not others? That is something no one denies or disputes, for those born after seven months [[In the printed and manuscript texts: "li-tis'a ashhur," but the correct reading is "li-sab'a ashhur," as the flow of the argument shows.]] are more numerous than those born after four or two years, just as those born after nine months are more numerous than those born after six months or seven months.
* *
Abu Jaʿfar said: The readers differed in their recitation of this. The majority of the readers of Medina, Iraq and Syria recited "li-man arada an yatimma al-rada'a" with a "ya'" in "yatimma" and with "al-rada'a" in the accusative, meaning: for whoever of the fathers and mothers wishes to complete the nursing of his child.
Some of the people of the Hijaz recited, "li-man arada an tatimma al-rada'a," with a "ta'" in "tatimma," and "al-rada'a" in the nominative, as a description of it. [[He means by "as a description of it," that the intransitive verb serves as an adjective for it, so you say: nursing that is complete.]]
* *
Abu Jaʿfar said: The correct recitation in our view is that of those who recite with a "ya'" in "yatimma" and "al-rada'a" in the accusative, because God, may His remembrance be exalted, said, "The mothers shall breastfeed their children," so likewise they complete it when they and the one to whom the child belongs wish to complete it. And it is the recitation brought by the widespread transmission by which the proof is established, rather than the other recitation.
* *
It has been reported from the Arabs by hearing that the "ra'" in "al-rida'a" may be vowelled with a kasra. If that is sound, [[In the printed and manuscript texts: "wa-in takun," but the appropriate word here is "fa."]] it is like "al-wikala" and "al-wikala," and "al-dalala" and "al-dalala," and "mahirtu al-shay' mahara wa-mahara," so then "al-rada'" and "al-rida'" would be permissible, just as it is said "al-hasad" and "al-hisad." But as for the recitation, it is with a fatha only and nothing else.
* *
The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And upon the father of the child is their provision and their clothing according to what is customary﴾
Abu Jaʿfar said: By His words, exalted is His remembrance, "And upon the one to whom the child belongs," and upon the fathers of the infants for the wet nurses, "their provision," meaning the provision of their mothers.
* *
By "provision" is meant what sustains them of food, and what is indispensable to them of nourishment and sustenance.
* *
"And their clothing," and by "clothing" is meant attire.
* *
By His words, "according to what is customary," is meant what is due to one such as her from one such as him, since God, may His remembrance be exalted, knows the variation in the conditions of His creatures in wealth and poverty, and that among them are the well-off, the straitened, and those in between. So He commanded each to spend on those whose maintenance is obligatory upon him, his wife and his child, according to his means, as God, may His remembrance be exalted, said: ﴿Let the wealthy spend from his wealth, and he whose provision is restricted, let him spend from what God has given him. God does not burden a soul beyond what He has given it﴾ [Surah al-Talaq: 7], and as:
4970 - Al-Muthanna related to me, who said: Suwayd related to us, who said: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak concerning His words, "The mothers shall breastfeed their children for two complete years, for whoever wishes to complete the nursing; and upon the one to whom the child belongs is their provision and clothing according to what is customary," he said: If a man divorces his wife while she is nursing a child for him, and they agree that she should nurse for two complete years, then upon the father is the provision of the nursing mother and clothing according to what is customary, according to his means, "We do not burden any soul except according to its capacity."
4971 - Ali ibn Sahl al-Ramli related to me, who said: Zayd related to us, and Ibn Humayd related to us, who said: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, concerning His words: "The mothers shall breastfeed their children for two complete years, for whoever wishes to complete the nursing," and "the completion is the two years"; "and upon the one to whom the child belongs": upon the father is her food and clothing according to what is customary. [[The report 4971: see the chain of the earlier report 4955 and the following 4973.]]
4972 - I was told on the authority of ʿAmmar, who said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar related to us, from his father, from al-Rabiʿ, concerning His words: "And upon the one to whom the child belongs is their provision and clothing according to what is customary," he said: upon the father.
* *
The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿No soul is burdened except according to its capacity﴾
Abu Jaʿfar said: By this, exalted is His remembrance, is meant: no soul is made to bear any matter which would be a hardship for it, or whose existence it cannot easily attain when it wishes. What God, exalted is His remembrance, meant by this is: God does not impose upon men the maintenance of the nursing women among their wives whom they have irrevocably divorced, except what they are able to bear and have found the means for, as God, exalted is His remembrance, said: ﴿Let the one of wealth spend from his wealth, and he whose provision is restricted, let him spend from what God has given him﴾ [Surah al-Talaq: 7], as:
4973 - Ibn Humayd related to us, who said: Mihran related to us, and Ali related to me, who said: Zayd related to us, all of them from Sufyan: "No soul is burdened except what it can bear," except what it is able to do. [[The report 4973: see the chains of the two earlier reports 4955 and 4971.]]
* *
"Al-wus'" is the verbal noun from the saying of the speaker: "This matter has been within my capacity (wasi'ani hadha al-amr), so it is within my capacity (yasa'uni si'a)." It is also said: "This is what I gave you within my capacity," meaning: what is within my means to give you, so giving it to you is not burdensome for me. And "I gave you from my effort" when I give him what strains you so that giving it becomes hard on you.
* *
So the meaning of His words, "No soul is burdened except according to its capacity," is what I have described: that it is not burdened except with what is within its capacity to bear the burden it has been charged with, so it is not made hard or strained by it. Not what the ignorant among the Qadariyya thought, that its meaning is: no soul is burdened except with what it has been given power to do of obedience. For if that were as they claimed, then His words, exalted is His remembrance, "See how they strike similitudes for you, and they have gone astray, so they cannot find a way" [Surah al-Isra': 48; Surah al-Furqan: 9], would indicate that they are not able to find a way to what they were charged with, and it would necessarily follow that the people are in one and the same state, having been given the ability in the very state in which it was withheld from them. Such a claim, if its speaker makes it, is an absurdity in his speech and an assertion of falsehood whose length does not obscure it. [[His phrase "da'wa batil" here is in the construct form, not an adjective of "da'wa." Elsewhere one says "da'wa batil wa-batila" as an adjective. "Al-buṭul" is the verbal noun of "batala," as we explained in volume 4, p. 523, note 3. "Akhal al-shay' yakhal" means: to be unclear; one says "this matter does not khayyal (obscure) to anyone," meaning it is not unclear; and "shay' mukhayyal" means something ambiguous.]] Since the falsity of this view is evident, it is known that what God, exalted is His remembrance, informed that He charged souls with according to their capacity is other than what He informed that He charged them with that they cannot find a way to.
* *
The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿No mother shall be harmed because of her child, nor a father because of his child﴾
Abu Jaʿfar said: The readers differed in their recitation of this. The majority of the readers of the Hijaz, Kufa and Syria recited, "la tudarra walida bi-waladiha," with a fatha on the "ra'", interpreting it as: la tudarrar [[In the manuscript: "la tudarrarna" with an "n" at the end, which is an error.]], in the prohibitive mood; its place, when recited this way, is jussive, though it is vowelled, since the doubling is dropped and it is given the lightest vowel, which is fatha. If it were vowelled with a kasra, it would also be permissible, by following the vowel of the verb's second radical with the vowel of its middle radical. And if you wish, it is because when the jussive is vowelled it is vowelled with a kasra. [[This paragraph appears in this form in both the manuscript and the printed edition, and it is clearly corrupt and contradicts what Tabari says later on pp. 51–52. There is no doubt that some text has fallen out, which an early copyist skipped over, so that what Tabari intended to say became badly garbled, and then what he said afterwards became very confused. From what I have deduced from reading his commentary on the verse from its beginning to its end on p. 54, the flow of his argument here must be as follows:]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 233 (part 3 of 6):

"The readers (al-qurra') differed over the reading of this. The majority of the readers of the people of the Hijaz, Kufa and Sham read ﴿lā tuḍārra wālidatun bi-waladihā﴾ with a fatha on the rāʾ, in the passive form (ʿalā mā lam yusamma fāʿiluhu), interpreted as lā tuḍārrar, in the form of a prohibition. Its position, when read this way, is jussive (majzūm), except that it was given a vowel because the doubling was dropped, with the vowel of the first rāʾ.
Some of those who read it this way claimed that the reading of those who read ﴿lā tuḍārra﴾ with a fatha on the rāʾ in the active form (ʿalā mā summiya fāʿiluhu), interpreted as lā tuḍārrar, in the form of a prohibition. Its position, when read this way, is jussive, except that it was given a vowel, because the doubling was dropped, with the lightest of the vowels, which is the fatha. Had it been given a kasra, it would have been permissible, following the vowel of the verb's final consonant with the vowel of its middle consonant. And if you wish, it is because the jussive, when vowelled, is vowelled with a kasra. But this is an error in interpretation."
Perhaps some early copyists had something fall out of their copy, and then another thing came after it, so that he could not understand what he had written, nor identify where the omission lay, and so he altered his writing in the form that has been preserved in our manuscript and in all the printed editions. It is an error beyond doubt, and a clear contradiction that Abu Ja'far would not commit, let alone the severe disorder it contains. In the following notes I will show what links the following words to this sentence which I have deduced.]]
* *
Others of the people of the Hijaz and some of the people of Basra read ﴿lā tuḍārru wālidatun bi-waladihā﴾ with a damma. [[In the printed edition and the manuscript, in place of "rafaʿa" there is "faʿala," which is a distortion beyond doubt, as the preceding and following text shows, and as the reading itself shows. Before it in the manuscript: "lā tuḍārrar".]] Whoever reads it this way cannot have the meaning of prohibition in his reading; rather it is [in the sense of] a statement (khabar), [[In the printed edition: "wa-lakinnahā takūnu bi-l-khabar ʿaṭfan," but in the manuscript: "wa-lakinnahā takūnu al-khabar ʿaṭfan" without the preposition bi-. The context shows the necessity of the addition between the brackets.]] coordinated by his words ﴿lā tukallafu nafsun illā wusʿahā﴾ [no soul is burdened beyond its capacity]. [[In the manuscript: "lā tukallafu nafsan," as occurs in the verse on p. 45, note 1.]]
* *
Some grammarians of Basra claimed that the meaning of whoever reads ﴿lā tuḍārru wālidatun bi-waladihā﴾ with a damma is, in this judgment: "a mother must not be harmed through her child," i.e., "it is not fitting that she be harmed." When "yanbaghī" was dropped, and tuḍārru took its place, it took its form, and he cited in support of this the words of the poet: [[By Abu al-Lahham al-Taghlibi, whose name is Surayʿ ibn ʿAmr (ʿAmr being al-Lahham) ibn al-Harith ibn Malik ibn Thaʿlaba ibn Bakr ibn Habib; it is also said his name was "Hurayth." He was a pre-Islamic poet. (Cf. al-Naqaʾid: 458; Sharh al-Mufaḍḍaliyyat: 434; al-Khizana 3: 613–615.) In Sibawayh 1: 431 it is attributed to ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Umm al-Hakam according to al-Shantamari, and I have not found this attribution elsewhere. Abu al-Lahham has poetry in the Diwan of ʿAmr ibn Kulthum.]] "On the judgment that comes some day when he decides his case, that he does not transgress and intends..." [[Sibawayh 1: 431; al-Khizana 3: 613–615; Sharh Shawahid al-Mughni: 263. The author of al-Khizana said: "The verse is from a qasida of nineteen verses by Abu al-Lahham al-Taghlibi, or Abu ʿAmr al-Shaybani attributed it to the poetry of Taghlib, and Abu Tammam selected it, including five verses of it in Mukhtar Shiʿr al-Qabaʾil. This is its first verse: ʿUmirtu wa-aṭalt al-tafakkur khaliyan... wa-sāʾaltu ḥattā kāda ʿumrī yanfadu."]]
He claimed that the verb "yaqṣidu" [intends] in the nominative means "yanbaghī" [ought]. But what is transmitted from the Arabs by hearing is different from what he said. For it is transmitted from them by hearing: "fa-taṣnaʿu māḏā" [so what do you make?], when they want to say "fa-turīdu an taṣnaʿa māḏā" [so do you want to make what?], and they put it in the accusative with the intention of "an." But when they do not intend "an" and do not mean it, they say "fa-turīdu māḏā," and they put "turīdu" in the nominative, because there is no governing particle "an" before it, as there was a governing particle before "taṣnaʿu." So if the meaning of his words "lā tuḍārru" when read in the nominative were "yanbaghī an lā tuḍārra" or "mā yanbaghī an tuḍārra," and then "yanbaghī" and "an" were dropped, and "tuḍārru" was placed in the position of "yanbaghī," then it would have been necessary to read it, if it were read with that meaning, in the accusative, not the nominative, so that the omitted word before it would show the intended meaning, as he did with his words "fa-taṣnaʿu māḏā." But the meaning is as we have said when it is read in the nominative, as a coordination with "tukallafu" [is burdened]: [[In the printed edition: "lā tukallafu," with an added "lā," but I have kept what is in the manuscript.]] no soul is burdened beyond its capacity, and no mother is harmed through her child. By this he means that this is not part of the religion of God, His judgment, or the character of the Muslims.
* *
Abu Ja'far said: The more correct of the two readings in this matter is the reading of the one who reads with the accusative, because it is a prohibition from God, exalted is His remembrance, to each of the two parents of the child against harming the other through their child; it is forbidden to both of them by the consensus (ijmaʿ) of the Muslims. For if that were a statement, it would be forbidden for them to harm each other through it in that way. [[In the manuscript and printed edition: "la-kāna ḥarām" with a nominative, but what I have recorded is the better.]]
* *
What we have said regarding this, namely that it has the meaning of prohibition, is how the people of interpretation (ahl al-taʾwil) have interpreted it.
Those who said this:
4974 — Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to us, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, from ʿIsa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿lā tuḍārru wālidatun bi-waladihā﴾: she should not refuse to nurse him in order to distress his father, and the father should not harm his child by preventing his mother from nursing him in order to grieve her.
4975 — al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.
4976 — Bishr ibn Muʿadh narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Zurayʿ narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His words: ﴿lā tuḍārru wālidatun bi-waladihā wa-lā mawlūdun lahu bi-waladihi﴾ [a mother must not be harmed through her child, nor a father through his child]: He said: God, exalted is He, forbade harm and placed emphasis on it. God forbade the father to harm the mother by taking the child from her when she is content with what the child is nursed on by another woman, and the mother was forbidden to throw the child to its father out of harm.
4977 — al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Maʿmar informed us, from Qatada regarding His words: ﴿lā tuḍārru wālidatun bi-waladihā﴾: throwing him to his father out of harm; ﴿wa-lā mawlūdun lahu bi-waladihi﴾: he says: nor the father, by taking him from her out of harm, when she is content with the wage of nursing as the other woman is content with it; she has more right to him if she is content with that.
4978 — It was related from ʿAmmar, who said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, from his father, from Yunus, from al-Hasan: ﴿lā tuḍārru wālidatun bi-waladihā﴾: He said: that is when he has divorced her. He may not harm her by taking the child from her, when she is content with what another would be content with from him. Nor may she harm him by burdening him with what he cannot bear, when he is a poor man, by throwing her child to him.
4979 — al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abu Zuhayr narrated to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak: ﴿lā tuḍārru wālidatun bi-waladihā﴾: a mother must not be harmed through her child, nor a father through his child. He says: a mother must not be harmed through her child by throwing him to the father if the father is alive, or to his relatives (ʿaṣaba) if the father is dead. Nor may the father harm the woman if she wishes to nurse her child, nor take him from her.
[[In the printed edition: "wa-lā yantazaʿahu" and "wa-hūmā sawāʾ," but I have kept what is in the manuscript.]]
4980 — Musa narrated to me, saying: ʿAmr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿lā tuḍārru wālidatun bi-waladihā﴾: He says: a man must not take his child from his wife and give him to another woman for the same wage she would accept; nor must the mother harm her child by throwing her child to him, saying: "I will not be with him for an hour," so that she loses him; rather, it is her duty to nurse him until he seeks a wet nurse.
[[In the printed edition and manuscript: "yaqūlu lā ilayhi sāʿatan taḍʿuhu" — in the manuscript it is undotted, and I judged the correct reading of the sentence to be this, with "taḍʿuhu" as "tuḍayyiʿuhu," i.e., she loses him by her abandonment of him.]]
4981 — al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: ʿAbd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: al-Layth narrated to me, saying: ʿAqil narrated to me, from Ibn Shihab — when he was asked about the words of God, exalted is His remembrance: ﴿wa-l-wālidātu yurḍiʿna awlādahunna ḥawlayni kāmilayni﴾ [mothers shall nurse their children for two full years] up to ﴿lā tuḍārru wālidatun bi-waladihā wa-lā mawlūdun lahu bi-waladihi﴾ — Ibn Shihab said: Mothers have more right to nurse their children, as long as they accept nursing them for the wage given to others. A mother may not harm her child by refusing to nurse him in order to harm him, while she is given for it what others are given in wages. And the father may not take his child from his mother, harming her, while she accepts the wage that others are given.
4982 — Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, and ʿAli narrated to me, saying: Zayd narrated to us, all from Sufyan regarding His words: ﴿lā tuḍārru wālidatun bi-waladihā﴾: she should not throw her child to the father when she has parted from him, harming him by that. ﴿wa-lā mawlūdun lahu bi-waladihi﴾: nor should the father take her child from her, harming her by that.
4983 — Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words: ﴿lā tuḍārru wālidatun bi-waladihā wa-lā mawlūdun lahu bi-waladihi﴾: He said: he should not take him from her while she wishes to nurse him, harming her; nor should she throw him to him while he cannot find someone to nurse him, nor finds what he could give for nursing.
4984 — ʿAmr ibn ʿAli al-Bahili narrated to us, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: Ibn Jurayj narrated to me, from ʿAta' regarding His words: ﴿lā tuḍārru wālidatun bi-waladihā﴾: He said: she must not abandon him and his nursing out of enmity (shanaʾ) harming his father; nor should what he has with her prevent her, as a harm to her.
[[In the printed edition and manuscript: "min shaʾnihā" — the correct reading is what I have recorded; al-shanaʾ means hatred and aversion.]]
* *
Some of them said: the "mother" whom a man is forbidden to harm is the child's wet nurse (ẓiʾr). [[Al-ẓiʾr: one who is affectionate toward a child not her own, the one who nurses him.]]
Those who said this:
4985 — al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Muslim ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, saying: Harun al-Nahwi narrated to us, saying: al-Zubayr ibn al-Kharit narrated to us, from ʿIkrima regarding His words: ﴿lā tuḍārru wālidatun bi-waladihā﴾: He said: she is the wet nurse. [[The report 4985: Muslim ibn Ibrahim al-Azdi al-Farahidi, from whom al-Bukhari, Abu Dawud, Yahya ibn Maʿin, Abu Zurʿa, Abu Hatim and others narrated; reliable and truthful; he died in the year 222. "Harun al-Nahwi" and "Harun al-Aʿwar" is Harun ibn Musa al-Azdi al-ʿAtaki, the grammarian, the one-eyed, author of the readings, who was reliable and trustworthy. "al-Zubayr ibn al-Kharit" (with a kasra on the kha' and a doubled, kasra-vowelled rāʾ) is reliable. In the printed edition and manuscript it was "al-Zubayr ibn al-Harith," which is a plain error.]]
* *
So the meaning of the statement is: a father of a child must not harm the mother of his child through his child from her, nor a mother of a child harm the father of her child through her child from him. Then the agent of "yuḍārru" was omitted, and it was said: ﴿lā tuḍārrar wālidatun bi-waladihā wa-lā mawlūdun lahu bi-waladihi﴾ [lā tuḍārrar], just as it is said when one forbids honouring a particular man in the passive, without intending the prohibition to refer to a particular person: "ʿAmr must not be honoured, and he must not sit with his brother." Then the doubling was dropped, and it was said: "lā tuḍārra," so the second rāʾ, which would have been jussive had the doubling been shown, was given the vowel of the first rāʾ. [[From this place I took what I added there, pp. 46–47 note 3, in the commentary on the disordered sentence whose disorder I explained.]]
Some grammarians (ahl al-ʿarabiyya) claimed that it was given a fatha in this position only because it is the lightest of the vowels (ākhir al-ḥarakāt). [[In the printed edition: "li-annahu aḥad al-ḥarakāt," which is meaningless; the correct reading is what I have recorded. This same error occurred earlier in the tafsir, and I have not been able to locate it again. His words "ākhir al-ḥarakāt" mean: the lightest. The ḍamma is the heaviest vowel, then the kasra, then the fatha is the lightest and last. The sukūn is not counted among the vowels. What al-Tabari says here is decisive proof of the corruption of the sentence on pp. 46–47 (note 3), and that his reason for the fatha in the sense of prohibition was not "that it was given a vowel with the lightest vowel, which is the fatha"; and it is proof that the correct reading is what I deduced in the note. This will become clear in his refutation that follows this sentence.]] But this claim has no meaning here. For that would only be permissible if the meaning of the statement were: "lā tuḍārrin wālidatun" [a mother should not be harmed], and the one forbidden from harming were the mother. [[In the manuscript and printed edition: "lā tuḍārrin," which is meaningless; the correct form is what I have recorded: tuḍārru with a damma on the tā' and a kasra on the first rāʾ, and a sukūn on the last.]] Moreover, if the meaning of the statement were as he says, then the kasra in "tuḍārru" would be more eloquent than the fatha, and reading it with a kasra would be more correct than reading it with a fatha, just as "mudda bi-l-thawb" [he stretched with the garment] is more eloquent than "mudda bihi." [[See Sharh al-Shafiya 2: 243.]] And in the consensus of the readers upon reading ﴿lā tuḍārra﴾ with a fatha and not a kasra, there is clear evidence of the heedlessness (ighfāl) of those grammarians whose words I have related on this matter. [[Ighfal: entering heedlessness, as we mentioned at 1: 151, note 1; likewise the meaning of his words in the second place "aghfala," i.e., entered into heedlessness.]]
If the one who said this said it, imagining that the meaning is: "lā tuḍārrar wālidatun" [a mother must not be harmed], and that "wālidatun" is in the nominative by its verb, and that the first rāʾ should be kasra, then he has been heedless of the interpretation of the statement, [[Ighfal: entering heedlessness, as above.]] and has opposed the view of all those whose opinion we have related from the people of interpretation. That is because God, exalted is His remembrance, enjoined each of the two parents of the child (ʿalā kull aḥad min abawayi al-mawlūd) with the prohibition against harming the other through their child, not that He forbade each of them from harming the child. [[In the printed edition: "kull wāḥid," and they are close in meaning. "Taqaddama ilā kadhā bi-kadhā" means he commanded with a command or forbade with a prohibition.]] How could He forbid him from harming the infant, when the infant in the state of being a suckling cannot possibly harm anyone? If that were its meaning, the revelation would read: ﴿lā tuḍārru wālidatun bi-waladihā﴾ [in the manuscript: "lā tuḍārr," as in the verse] — which is undoubtedly an error.
* *
Others among the grammarians claimed that the kasra in "tuḍārru" is permissible. [[This is al-Farra' in Maʿani al-Qurʾan 1: 149. Al-Farra' meant by his view that when the first rāʾ became quiescent for its assimilation into the second quiescent rāʾ, two quiescent letters met, so it was given a kasra, because the kasra is the original vowel for two meeting quiescents; this is what he permitted.]] But in my view the kasra in this position is not permissible, [[In the printed edition: "wa-l-kasr fī dhālika ʿindī ghayr jāʾiz fī hādha al-mawḍiʿ," and I have kept what is in the manuscript.]] because if it is given a kasra, its meaning changes from the meaning of "lā tuḍārraru" [in the form of the passive], which is in the view of the one whose subject is not named, to the meaning of "lā tuḍārraru" [in the form of the active] (lā tuḍārrar), which is in the view of the one whose subject is named. [[This passage from Abu Ja'far's refutation of the one who said kasra also clearly shows the corruption of the first sentence which we corrected on pp. 46–47 note 3, and it shows you the correctness of what I deduced to be the original text of al-Tabari's words.]]
* *

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 233 (part 4 of 6):

Abu Ja'far said: Since God, may His remembrance be exalted, has forbidden each of the two parents of the child from harming the other because of their child, it is incumbent upon the imam of the Muslims (the ruler), when a man wants to take his child from its mother after she has been separated from him by divorce, while she is nursing, caring for and suckling him [[In the manuscript and the printed edition: "وترضعه" (and nurses him). The correct reading, with the ya', is as I have written it. The context of the sentence is: "فحق على إمام المسلمين... أن يأخذ الوالد" (it is incumbent upon the imam of the Muslims... that the father take), and what lies between them is a parenthetical clause of circumstance. His saying "ما دام محتاجا الصبي" (as long as the child needs her) is another interposed circumstantial clause. The sense of the discourse is "بتسليم ولدها... إليها في ذلك" (by handing over her child... to her in this matter).]] that the father take the child by handing it over to her, as long as the child needs her for this, in exchange for the wage that would be given to someone else. And it is incumbent upon him [the mother] if the child will not accept the breast of anyone other than his mother, or if the father who fathered him cannot find someone to nurse his child, even if the child would accept the breast of another woman, or if the father is destitute and cannot find the means to hire a wet-nurse, nor find anyone who would volunteer to nurse his offspring [[In the printed and manuscript texts: "ما يتبرع عليه" (what he can volunteer upon), which is a clearly corrupt reading, because he means that he has not found anyone who would do him a favour and volunteer to nurse his offspring. The context of this sentence is also: "وحق عليه... أن يأخذ والدته" (and it is incumbent upon him... that he take his mother), as in the preceding paragraph.]] = that he take his mother, who has been separated from his father, to nurse and care for him. [[In the manuscript: "أن يأخذ بوالدته الثانية من والدته البائنة من والده" (that he take with his second mother from his mother separated from his father). The printed edition has correctly removed "الثانية من والدته", so this is a scribal corruption and repetition.]] Because God, may His remembrance be exalted, has forbidden each of the two parents to harm the other because of him [[In the printed edition: "لأن الله تعالى ذكره حرم" with "إن" omitted. It is necessary to restore "إن" as it stands in the manuscript.]], then harming the child is more fitting to be forbidden, along with the harm to the other parent that it entails.

* *

On the interpretation of His saying: ﴿And upon the heir is the like of that﴾

Abu Ja'far said: The exegetes differed concerning the "heir" that God, may His remembrance be exalted, meant by His saying "And upon the heir is the like of that," and which heir it is, and whose heir he is.

Some of them said: He is the heir of the child. They said: The meaning of the verse is: and upon the heir of the child, if [his father] is dead, is the like of what was upon his father during his lifetime.

Those who said this:

4986 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, both saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: "And upon the heir is the like of that," [meaning] upon the heir of the child.

4987 - Musa narrated to me, saying: 'Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "And upon the heir is the like of that," [meaning] upon the heir of the child.

4988 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Suwayd narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: "And upon the heir is the like of that," he said: "And upon the heir of the child is the like of what was upon his father."

* *

Then those who held this view differed concerning the heir of the newborn, upon whom God imposed the like of what has been described. Some of them said: They are the heirs of the child on his father's side, from among his 'asabah (agnatic kinsmen), whoever they may be: a brother, or an uncle, or a paternal cousin, or a nephew.

Those who said this:

4989 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ibn Jurayj informed us: that 'Amr ibn Shu'ayb informed him: that Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab informed him: that 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, [[This phrase between the two lines is from the words of 'Amr ibn Shu'ayb, meaning that Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab informed him concerning God's saying "And upon the heir is the like of that," that 'Umar ibn al-Khattab detained. Others said: He is among its heirs, whoever of them is a mahram (a relative within the prohibited degrees, whom one may not marry) to the newborn. Those who held this view were Abu Hanifah, Abu Yusuf and Muhammad.

Another group said: Rather, the one God, may His remembrance be exalted, meant by His saying "And upon the heir is the like of that" is the newborn itself.

* *

On the interpretation of His saying: ﴿the like of that﴾

Abu Ja'far said: The exegetes differed concerning the interpretation of His saying "the like of that."

Some of them said: Its interpretation is: And upon the heir of the child, after the death of its two parents, [[In the printed edition: "على الوارث للصبي" (upon the heir of the child); I have kept what is in the manuscript.]] is the like of what was upon its father of the wage of its suckling and its maintenance, if the newborn has no wealth.

Those who said this:

5010 - Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, from Mughirah, from Ibrahim, concerning His saying "And upon the heir is the like of that," he said: Upon the heir is the suckling of the child.

5011 - 'Amr ibn 'Ali and Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, both saying: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Awanah narrated to us, from Mansur, from Ibrahim: "And upon the heir is the like of that," he said: The wage of the suckling.

5013 - 'Amr ibn 'Ali narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Awanah narrated to us, from al-Mughirah, from Ibrahim, concerning His saying "And upon the heir is the like of that," he said: The wage of the suckling.

5014 - Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Ayyub, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Utbah: "And upon the heir is the like of that," he said: The suckling.

5017 - Sufyan narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Mughirah, from Ibrahim, who said: The suckling and the maintenance.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 233 (part 5 of 6):

5027- Al-Muthanna told me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah told us, saying: Shibl told us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "And upon the heir is the like of that" — upon the guardian (al-wali) is its support (kafalah) and its suckling, if the infant has no property.

5028- Al-Qasim told us, saying: Al-Husayn told us, saying: Al-Hajjaj told me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, who said: "And upon the heir is the like of that." He said: "And upon the heir is the like of that," he said: "Upon the heir too is its support and its suckling, if he has no property, and that he should not harm its mother."

5029- Al-Qasim told us, saying: Al-Husayn told us, saying: Al-Hajjaj told me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ata al-Khurasani, from Ibn Abbas: "And upon the heir is the like of that," he said: "Its maintenance until it is weaned, if its father did not leave him any property."

5030- Bishr told us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatadah: "And upon the heir is the like of that," he said: "And upon the heir of the child is what was upon the father of the wage of suckling, if the child has no property."

5031- Abd Allah ibn Muhammad al-Hanafi told me, saying: Abd Allah ibn Uthman told us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: "And upon the heir is the like of that," he said: "Upon the heir of the child is the like of what was upon his father, if his father has died and he has no property [in the printed edition: "idh kana qad halaka" (since he had died), and the correct reading is from the manuscript] — then upon the heir is the wage of suckling."

5032- Ibn Humayd told us, saying: Jarir told us, from Mansur, from Ibrahim: "And upon the heir is the like of that," he said: "If he dies and has no property, upon the heir is the suckling of the infant."

* *

Others said: Rather, the interpretation of that is: "And upon the heir is the like of that" — that he should not cause harm.

Those who said this:

5033- Amr ibn Ali and Muhammad ibn Bashshar told us, both saying: Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi told us, saying: Hammad ibn Zayd told us, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim: "And upon the heir is the like of that," he said: "That he should not cause harm."

5034- Ibn Humayd told us, saying: Jarir told us, from Asim al-Ahwal, from al-Sha'bi, concerning His saying: "And upon the heir is the like of that," he said: "He should not cause harm, and there is no indemnity upon him."

5035- Ibn Wakic told us, saying: My father told us, from Sufyan, from Jabir, from Mujahid, concerning His saying: "And upon the heir is the like of that": that he should not cause harm.

5036- Al-Muthanna told me, saying: Abd Allah ibn Salih told us, saying: Al-Layth told us, saying: Aqil told me, from Ibn Shihab: "The mothers shall suckle their children two full years," he said: "Mothers have more right to suckle their children, so long as they accept their suckling for the wage given to others. It is not permitted for a mother to harm her child by refusing to suckle him out of harm, while she is given for it what is given to others. And it is not permitted for the father of the child to take his child from its mother to harm her, while she accepts for the wage what is given to others. [And] 'And upon the heir is the like of that' — like what was upon the father in that."

5037- Ibn Humayd told us, saying: Mihran told us, and Ali told us, saying: Zayd told us, from Sufyan: "And upon the heir is the like of that," he said: "That he should not cause harm, and upon him is the like of what is upon the father of maintenance and clothing."

* *

Others said: Rather, the interpretation of that is: "And upon the heir of the child" [in the printed edition: "upon the heir the child", and I have restored what is in the manuscript], the like of what was upon the father of the child, of the provision of his mother and her clothing in a reasonable manner.

Those who said this:

5038- Al-Muthanna told me, saying: Suwayd told us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak: "And upon the heir is the like of that," he said: "Upon the heir at death, the like of what is upon the father for the nursing woman of maintenance and clothing." He said: "By the heir is meant the child who is suckled: that there be taken from his property, if he has property, the wage of what his mother suckled."

If the child has no property nor his agnatic kin, then the mother has no wage, and she is compelled to suckle her child without wage.

5039- Musa ibn Harun told me, saying: Amr told us, saying: Asbat told us, from al-Suddi: "And upon the heir is the like of that," he said: "Upon the heir of the child, the like of what is upon the father of maintenance and clothing."

* *

Others said: The meaning of that is: "And upon the heir is the like of what God, may He be mentioned, mentioned."

Those who said this:

5040- Al-Muthanna told me, saying: Suwayd told us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: I said to Ata: "His saying, may He be mentioned and exalted: 'And upon the heir is the like of that'?" He said: "The like of what God, may He be mentioned, mentioned."

* *

Abu Ja'far [al-Tabari] said: The most correct of the interpretations regarding His saying "And upon the heir is the like of that" is that the one meant by the heir is what Qabisah ibn Dhu'ayb and al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim said, and what we mentioned above from whom: that the one meant by the heir is the child [i.e., the infant himself as heir]. As for His saying "the like of that," it means: the like of what was upon his father of the provision of his mother and her clothing in a reasonable manner, if she is among those in need, and one who has an affliction or disability, and has no trade [ihtiraf: earning] and no husband to rely on; and if she is among the wealthy and healthy, then the like of what was upon his father for her of the wage of suckling.

We have said that this interpretation is more correct than the rest of the interpretations we mentioned, because it is not permissible to state an interpretation of the Book of God, may He be mentioned, except with clear proof, as we have explained at the beginning of this book. Since that is so, and since His saying "And upon the heir is the like of that" admits, in its apparent sense: upon the heir of the infant child is the like of what was upon the father of the child; and admits: upon the heir of the father is the like of what was upon him during his life, of abstaining from harming the mother and of the child's maintenance, and other interpretations, as we previously mentioned [in the printed edition: "qadamna dhikrah" (we mentioned it), and I have restored what is in the manuscript]; and since the whole body of proof [the sentence "and since the whole body of proof" is coordinated with His saying: "And since that is so..."] agrees that among the child's heirs there is one upon whom there is no obligation of his maintenance and suckling wage — then the proof has established that the rest of his heirs, other than his parents, grandparents from his father or mother's side, are in the same ruling, in that they are not obligated to provide him maintenance or suckling wage, since the one who grants the favor is among his heirs, and he is one who is not obligated to provide maintenance or suckling wage. So it is necessary, by their consensus on that, that the ruling of all his other heirs, apart from those excepted, be his ruling.

And when it became invalid that the meaning is what we described — that it refers to the heirs of the child — then the other view is more fitting, namely that it refers to the heirs of the father other than the child. For the one who is closer in kinship to the child than another, if it is not valid that his maintenance and suckling wage are obligatory upon him, then the one who is more distant in kinship is more fitting not to have that obligation upon him.

As for what we said about the obligation of the mother's provision and clothing in a reasonable manner upon her child, when the mother is in the condition we described, in the same manner as what was obligatory for her upon the father, there is no disagreement about it among all the scholars. Thus our interpretation of the verse is confirmed by widespread transmission inherited from those whose opposition is not permissible. As for the other interpretations, they are disputed, and we have shown their invalidity.

* *

On the interpretation of His saying, may He be mentioned and exalted: ﴿Then if they both desire weaning by mutual consent and consultation, there is no blame upon them﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, may He be mentioned, means by His saying "Then if they both desire": if the father and mother of the child desire, "weaning" — meaning: the weaning of their child from milk.

* *

By "fisal" (weaning) is meant fitam (weaning), and it is a verbal noun from the speaker's saying: "faslitu fulanan ufasiluhu mufasalatan wa fisalan" (I separated from so-and-so, separation and parting), when he parts from an association that was between them. Likewise "fisal al-fatim" (the weaning of the infant) is only his being prevented from milk, the cutting of his drinking, and his separation from his mother's breast, except for nourishment with the foods by which an adult man is nourished.

* *

The people of interpretation have said likewise to what we have said about this.

Those who said this:

5041- Musa told me, saying: Amr told us, saying: Asbat told us, from al-Suddi, concerning His saying: "Then if they both desire weaning," he says: if they both desire that they wean him before the two years.

5042- Al-Muthanna told me, saying: Abd Allah told us, saying: Mu'awiyah told us, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas: "Then if they both desire weaning," — if they both desire to wean him before the two years and after it.

5043- Al-Muthanna told me, saying: Abu Zuhayr told us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak: "Then if they both desire weaning by mutual consent," he said: the weaning.

* *

As for His saying "by mutual consent and consultation," it means: by mutual consent of the child's two parents and consultation between them.

* *

Then the people of interpretation differed regarding the time at which God removed the blame from them, if they weaned him by mutual consent and consultation, and which period God, may He be mentioned, meant by His saying: "Then if they both desire weaning by mutual consent and consultation."

Some of them said: He meant by it: if they both desire weaning within the two years by mutual consent and consultation, then there is no blame upon them.

Those who said this:

5044- Musa told me, saying: Amr told us, saying: Asbat told us, from al-Suddi: "Then if they both desire weaning by mutual consent and consultation," he says: if they both desire that they wean him before the two years, and they agree to that, then let them wean him.

5045- Al-Hasan ibn Yahya told us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah: If the mother desires to wean her child before the two years, and that is by mutual consent and consultation, then there is no harm in it.

5046- Sufyan told us, saying: My father told us, from Sufyan, from Layth, from Mujahid: "Then if they both desire weaning by mutual consent and consultation," he said: The consultation is within less than the two years; she may not wean him unless he consents, and he may not wean him unless she consents.

5047- Al-Muthanna told me, saying: Suwayd told us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Sufyan, from Layth, from Mujahid, who said: The consultation is within less than the two years. "Then if they both desire weaning by mutual consent and consultation," within less than the two years, "then there is no blame upon them." If they do not agree, then she may not wean him before the two years.

5048- Al-Muthanna told me, saying: Abu Nu'aym told us, saying: Sufyan told us, from Layth, from Mujahid, who said: The consultation is within less than the two years; it is not for her until both of them agree.

5049- Al-Muthanna told me, saying: Abd Allah told us, saying: Al-Layth told me, saying: Aqil informed us, from Ibn Shihab: "Then if they both desire weaning," they wean their child, "by mutual consent and consultation," within less than the complete two years, "then there is no blame upon them."

5050- Ibn Humayd told us, saying: Mihran told us; and Ali told me, saying: Zayd told us — all from Sufyan, who said: The consultation is within less than the two years, if they agree on less than that; and that is His saying: "Then if they both desire weaning by mutual consent and consultation." If the woman says: "I will wean him before the two years," and the father says: "No," then she may not wean him before the two years. And if the mother does not consent, then he may not do so until both agree. If they both agree before the two years, they wean him; and if they disagree, they may not wean him before the two years. That is His saying: "Then if they both desire weaning by mutual consent and consultation, there is no blame upon them."

5051- Yunus told me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: "Then if they both desire weaning by mutual consent and consultation," he said: before the two years, "then there is no blame upon them."

* *

Others said: The meaning of that is: "Then if they both desire weaning by mutual consent and consultation, there is no blame upon them," at whatever time they desire that, whether before the two years or after them.

Those who said this:

5052- Al-Muthanna told me, saying: Abd Allah told us, saying: Mu'awiyah told me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas: "Then if they both desire weaning by mutual consent and consultation, there is no blame upon them," that they wean him before the two years and after.

* *

As for His saying "by mutual consent and consultation," it means: by mutual consent and consultation concerning what is in the interest of the child in weaning him, as:

5053- Muhammad ibn Amr told me, saying: Abu Asim told us, from Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "Then if they both desire weaning by mutual consent and consultation," he said: not wronging themselves nor their child, "then there is no blame upon them."

5054- Al-Muthanna told me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah told us, saying: Shibl told us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The more correct of the two interpretations is the interpretation of those who said: "Then if they both desire weaning within the two years by mutual consent and consultation," because the completion of the two years is the limit of the completion and end of suckling, and there is no consultation after its end; consultation and mutual consent occur only before the end of its term.

If someone heedless thinks that consultation after the end of the two years has a valid meaning — since some infants have an illness that requires leaving off and feeding on the milk of their mother — then, in that case, it is a treatment, like treatment by taking some medicines, not suckling. As for the suckling in which weaning occurs before its last period, with mutual consent and consultation between the parents of the child, for which God, may He be mentioned, removed the blame when they wean him before the end of its final term, its limit is the limit God, may He be mentioned, set by His saying: "The mothers shall suckle their children two full years for whoever wishes to complete the suckling," as we have already explained previously.

* *

As for "the blame" (al-junah), it is hardship (al-haraj), as:

5055- Al-Muthanna told me, saying: Abd Allah told us, saying: Mu'awiyah told me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas: "Then there is no blame upon them" — there is no hardship upon them.

* *

On the interpretation of His saying, may He be mentioned and exalted: ﴿And if you desire to seek wet-nurses for your children, there is no blame upon you if you pay what you give in a reasonable manner﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, may He be mentioned, means by that: and if you desire to seek wet-nurses other than their mothers for your children — if their mothers refuse to suckle them for the wage that others would accept for suckling them, or out of fear of loss to you regarding your children through the cessation of their mothers' milk, or other such reasons — then there is no hardship upon you in seeking them, if you pay what you gave in a reasonable manner.

* *

The people of interpretation have said something similar to what we have said about this.

Those who said this:

5056- Muhammad ibn Amr told me, saying: Abu Asim told us, saying: Isa told us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "And if you desire to seek wet-nurses for your children," out of fear of loss for the child, "then there is no blame upon you."

5057- Al-Muthanna told me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah told us, saying: Shibl told us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.

5058- Abd Allah ibn Muhammad al-Hanafi told me, saying: Abd Allah ibn Uthman told us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, saying: Abu Bishr Warqa' informed us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.

5059- Musa told me, saying: Amr told us, saying: Asbat told us, from al-Suddi: "And if you desire to seek wet-nurses for your children," if the woman says: "I have no strength for him, for my milk has gone," then another is sought to nurse him for him.

[5060] Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Suwayd narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, who said: It is not permissible for the woman to abandon her child after the two have agreed that she will nurse it, and they are both to be held to this and compelled to it. He said: If they disagree over nursing at the time of divorce or death, the infant is to be presented to wet-nurses. If it accepts a wet-nurse, that is permissible and she nurses it. [In the printed edition: "ṣāra dhālika" (it became that); in the manuscript the word is written without dots as "ḥāra," and what I have established is the correct reading.] If it does not accept a wet-nurse, then its mother is to nurse it for wages, if the child has property or if its paternal relatives do. If it has neither property nor paternal relatives, she is compelled to nurse it.
