[5061] Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us; and ʿAli narrated to me, saying: Zayd narrated to us, both from Sufyan, regarding: ﴿And if you wish to seek wet-nurses for your children, there is no blame upon you﴾: when the mother refuses to nurse it, there is no blame upon the father in seeking another woman to nurse it for him.

[5062] Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words: ﴿And if you wish to seek wet-nurses for your children, there is no blame upon you, when you hand over what you gave in accordance with what is customary﴾: If the mother is content to have her child nursed by another, and the father is content to have his child nursed by another, there is no blame upon either of them.

* *

They differed concerning His words: ﴿when you hand over what you gave in accordance with what is customary﴾.

Some of them said: its meaning is: when you hand over to their mothers what you parted with them upon as wages for their nursing, calculated according to what they earned up to the cessation of their milk; or the situation in which the father has an excuse to seek a wet-nurse for his child other than its mother, and to have it nursed by her.

Those who said this:

[5063] Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿASim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding: ﴿when you hand over what you gave in accordance with what is customary﴾: the calculation of what the child was nursed with.

[5064] Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿when you hand over what you gave in accordance with what is customary﴾: the calculation of what the child is nursed with.

[5065] Musa narrated to me, saying: ʿAmr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿when you hand over what you gave in accordance with what is customary﴾: if the mother says — meaning the mother — "I have no capacity for it, for my milk has gone," then another woman is sought to nurse him, and her wage is handed over to her according to the amount she nursed.

[5066] Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Suwayd narrated to me, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: I asked ʿAta' — meaning, about: ﴿And if you wish to seek wet-nurses for your children﴾? He said: its mother and others, ﴿there is no blame upon you when you hand over﴾, he said: when her wage is handed over to her — ﴿what you gave﴾, he said: what you gave.

* *

And others said: the meaning of that is: when you hand over to the seeking of a nurse, upon consultation from you and from the mothers of your children whom you seek nurses for, and mutual consent from you and them to their nursing. [In the printed edition and manuscript: "wa-minhum" (and from them); the correct reading is what I have established.]

Those who said this:

[5067] Bishr ibn Muʿadh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatadah regarding His words: ﴿there is no blame upon you when you hand over what you gave in accordance with what is customary﴾, he says: when that is by consultation and their consent.

[5068] Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: ʿAbd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: al-Layth informed me, saying: ʿUqayl narrated to me, from Ibn Shihab: there is no blame upon them if the two parents of the newborn seek nurses for their children, if they both consent and do not harm one another.

[5069] It was narrated to me on the authority of ʿAmmar, saying: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi: ﴿when you hand over what you gave in accordance with what is customary﴾, he says: when that is by consultation and their consent.

* *

And others said: rather, the meaning of that is: when you hand over what you gave in accordance with what is customary, to the one you sought to nurse, after the refusal of the nursing mother, of the wage, in a customary manner.

Those who said this:

[5070] Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us; and ʿAli narrated to me, saying: Zayd narrated to us, both from Sufyan regarding His words: ﴿when you hand over what you gave in accordance with what is customary﴾, he said: when you hand over to this one whose wage you hire in a customary manner — meaning: to the one who was sought to nurse the newborn, when the mother refuses to nurse it.

* *

Abu Jaʿfar said: The most correct of these interpretations, in my view, is the saying of the one who said: "Its interpretation: and if you wish to seek wet-nurses for your children until the completion of their nursing, and you and their mothers have not agreed on their weaning, and you do not see that as in their interest, then there is no blame upon you in seeking wet-nurses for them, [a term for a nurse who is not the child's mother; ẓu'ūra is the plural of ẓi'r (with kasra and sukun), meaning a nursing woman who is not the child's own mother. ẓu'ūra is like bu'ūla, the plural of "ba'l," or both are collective nouns, as Sibawayh says,] if their mothers refuse to nurse them, for a reason on their part or for no reason, provided that you hand over to their mothers and to the other nurse their rights which you gave them in a customary manner."

He means by that meaning: what Allah has made obligatory for them upon you, namely that you pay them their wages for what they parted with you upon, at the time of the nursing contract and the time of the hiring agreement.

This is the meaning that Ibn Jurayj stated, and Mujahid and al-Suddi agreed with part of it, as did those who spoke in accordance with their view.

We have decided that this interpretation is more worthy of the meaning of the verse than others, because Allah, exalted is He, mentioned before His words: ﴿And if you wish to seek wet-nurses for your children﴾, the matter of their weaning, and He explained the ruling on their weaning before the completion of the two full years, saying: ﴿If the two of them wish to wean by mutual consent﴾, within the two full years, ﴿then there is no blame upon them both.﴾ So what is more fitting to the ruling of the verse, since He has explained in it the manner of weaning before the two years, is that what follows it should be the ruling on abandoning weaning and completing the nursing up to its final term; and that, since He has explained the ruling concerning the mother when she chooses to nurse and what the wage is for other nurses, what follows that ruling should be an explanation of her ruling and the child's ruling if she refuses to nurse it, as was the case in another place in the Book of Allah, namely His words: ﴿And if they nurse for you, give them their wages, and consult among yourselves in a customary manner. And if you disagree, then another woman will nurse for him﴾ [Sura al-Talaq: 6]. So He followed the mention of explaining the mothers' consent to nurse their children with the mention of explaining their refusal to nurse them; likewise is His words: ﴿And if you wish to seek wet-nurses for your children﴾.

We chose this interpretation of His words: ﴿when you hand over what you gave in accordance with what is customary﴾ because Allah, exalted is He, obligated the father of the newborn to hand over to its mother what he gave her as wages for nursing it after their separation, just as He obligated him to do so for the one he hired for that purpose from outside the child's lineage, and commanded him to give each of them her due in a customary manner for nursing his child. So His words "when you hand over" are no more fitting to be understood as meaning: when you hand over to the mothers of your children who nurse their rights, than they are to be understood as meaning: when you hand that to other nurses besides them; nor are the strangers of the child more fitting to be understood by this than the mothers, since Allah, exalted is He, has obligated the father of the newborn, for each woman hired to nurse his child, to hand over her wage to her just as He obligated him in that regard for the other. Therefore it is not for us to shift the apparent sense of the revelation to its hidden sense, nor to restrict a general statement to a specific one, except by an argument to which submission is obligatory. Thus what we have said is sound.

* *

Abu Jaʿfar said: As for the meaning of His words "in a customary manner" (bi-l-maʿruf), its meaning is: with fairness and good conduct, and without diminishing or wronging what is due to the nursing women. [See what has preceded on the explanation of "al-maʿruf" in vol. 3: 371; then in vol. 4: 549; 5: 7, 44; and its explanation of the meaning of "al-maʿruf" here is clearer and more comprehensive.]

* *

The discourse on the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And fear Allah, and know that Allah is Seeing of what you do﴾ [2:233]

Abu Jaʿfar said: By His words "And fear Allah," exalted is His mention, He means: fear Allah regarding the rights that He has prescribed for some of you over others, and regarding what He has imposed on your women for your men and on your men for your women, and what He has made obligatory for you regarding your children. So beware of opposing Him, lest you transgress — in that and in His other obligations and rights — His limits, [In the printed edition: "wa-ḥudūdahu" with an extra waw that corrupts the sentence; the meaning is: "fa-taʿtadū fī dhālika ḥudūdahu" (so that you transgress His limits in that).] thereby deserving His punishment. "And know that Allah is, of what you do" of deeds, O people, whether secret or public, hidden or apparent, good or evil, "Seeing," seeing and knowing it, so nothing is hidden from Him and nothing of it is absent from Him, [In the printed edition: "lā yaghību" (does not hide); I have kept what is in the manuscript, and both are the same in meaning.] so He counts all of that against you until He recompenses you with its good and its evil.

* *

The meaning of "Seeing" (baṣīr) is: possessing sight, and it has the sense of "mubṣir" (one who sees).

[See what has preceded on the interpretation of "baṣīr" in vol. 2: 140, 376, 506, and other places in the index of language and the index of Arabic linguistic topics.]

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 234 (part 1 of 3):**

**On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Those of you who die and leave wives behind, they shall wait by themselves for four months and ten days﴾**

Abu Ja'far said: By this, exalted is His mention, He means: "Those of you, O people, who die, from among the men, and so they die and leave wives behind, their wives shall wait by themselves." [[In the manuscript and the printed edition it reads "yatarabbasna" (they shall wait), which in the manuscript is undotted; what I have established is the correct reading.]]

* *

If someone says: "Where is the predicate for 'those who die'?"

It is said: It is omitted, because the intent was not to state a predicate about them. Rather, the intent was to state the obligation upon the women observing the waiting period ('iddah) on account of the death of their husbands. So the predicate was turned away from those who were first mentioned, who are the dead, to the predicate about their wives and the obligation upon them of the waiting period, since the meaning intended by the speech was known and understood. This is like the speaker's saying: "Part of your robe is torn," [[That is, the correct form would be "ba'd jubbatika mutakharriq" [with the masculine] as a predicate about "ba'd" [part], but it was turned toward "jubbatika" [your robe].]] in leaving the predicate about what the speech began with, to a predicate about part of its causes. Likewise the wives who are obliged to wait, since it was their husbands' causes that obliged them to wait, the speech turned away from the predicate about the one first mentioned, to a predicate about the one whom the predicate was intended to concern, as the poet said: [[He is Thabit Qutna al-'Itaki, whose name was "Thabit ibn Ka'b." His eye was lost in battle, so he would stuff it with cotton (qutna), and he was a Persian poet from the poets of Khurasan in the Umayyad era. Hajib al-Fil said of him: "People know nothing of him except his cotton... and all other lineages are unknown."]]

*Perhaps, if the wind inclines me in a sway,*
*Upon Ibn Abi Dhabban, he will regret.*

[[Tarikh al-Tabari 8:160, Ma'ani al-Qur'an by al-Farra' 1:150, al-Sahibi: 185. It is from a qasida of his in which he mourns Yazid ibn al-Muhallab, who was killed in the year 102 AH in his rebellion against Yazid ibn 'Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan. "Ibn Abi Dhabban" is the son of "Abu Dhabban," the kunya of 'Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan, because they claimed he had foul breath, so flies would die when they came near his mouth because of the intensity of his stench. Al-Tabari's version in the History reads "fa-'ala" [then upon], and before it he says:

*I stayed awake while the mother of Khalid did not stay awake with me,*
*And my eyes were kept awake for a whole ill-omened year*
*Over a dead man whose loss broke the tribe,*
*Whom death called, and he responded and submitted.*
*Over a king, O friend, whose battalions were beaten back at Al-'Aqr,*
*And who brought death in upon himself as a guide.*
*He was struck and I was not present; had I been present,*
*I would have consoled myself that the tribe did not gather a funeral.*
*And in other days, O Hind, know this,*
*For one who seeks vengeance, a glance if you blame.*
*Then upon, if the wind inclines...*

In the printed edition and the manuscript it reads "Ibn Abi Zaban," which is an error as you see.]] He said "perhaps" and then said "he will regret," because the meaning of the speech is: "Perhaps Ibn Abi Dhabban will regret it, if the wind inclines me in a sway against him." [[In the manuscript and the printed edition: "Ibn Abi Zaban," which is an error.]] So he turned the predicate back to the one he intended, though he had first mentioned someone else. And from it is the poet's saying:

*Did you not know that Ibn Qays and his killing,*
*Without blood-price, the abode of humiliation has come to dwell?*

[[I do not know who said it. The verse is in Ma'ani al-Qur'an by al-Farra' 1:150 and al-Sahibi: 185, and their version reads "Bani Asad, indeed Ibn Qays and his killing."]]

So he dropped "Ibn Qays," though he had begun by mentioning him, and reported that his killing was humiliation. [[Most of what has preceded is the text of al-Farra' in Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1:150-151. In Ma'ani al-Qur'an it reads "fa-alqa Ibn Qays," and the correct reading is what is in al-Tabari.]]

* *

Some of the grammarians have claimed that the predicate of "those who die" is omitted, and that the meaning of the speech is: "Those of you who die and leave wives behind, it is incumbent upon them that they wait after their death." He claimed that "their death" was not mentioned, as some speech is omitted. He also claimed that "yatarabbasna" is in the nominative case, since it occupies the place of "yanbaghi" [it is fitting], and "yanbaghi" is nominative. We have already demonstrated the corruption of the view of whoever said that the nominative of "yatarabbasna" is due to its occupying the place of "yanbaghi," earlier, so there is no need to repeat it. [[See what has preceded in volume 5: 47, 48.]]

* *

Another of them said: [[In the printed edition: "Another of them said," and the correct reading is what is in the manuscript.]] "The reason 'those who' is not connected to anything is that those mentioned in its predicate become like the interpretation of a conditional: 'Whoever meets you from us, you will obtain good'" = "The one who meets you from us, you obtain good." [[In the printed edition: "Whoever meets you from us, he obtains good," and then "yusibu khayran." The correct reading is what I have established: "tusib" in the first clause is jussive, with a "ta" at its beginning, and then "tusibu" with a "ta" in the second.]] He said: "This is not permissible except in the sense of a conditional."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: In the two verses we have mentioned there is clear evidence for the view on this matter contrary to what the two of them said. [[In the printed edition: "the clear evidence," and I have established what is in the manuscript.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: As for His saying "they shall wait by themselves," He means by it: "They shall confine themselves, [[See what has preceded in the explanation of "tarabbus," 4: 456, 515.]] observing the waiting period away from husbands, from perfume, from adornment, and from moving out of the dwelling they used to live in during the lifetime of their husbands, for four months and ten days. Except if they are pregnant, in which case the same waiting period is incumbent upon them until the time they give birth to their offspring. When they give birth to their offspring, their waiting period is then concluded."

* *

The people of interpretation have differed regarding the interpretation of this:

Some of them said the same as we have said about it:

5071 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas: "Those of you who die and leave wives behind, they shall wait by themselves four months and ten days." So this is the waiting period of the woman whose husband has died, unless she is pregnant, in which case her waiting period is that she gives birth to what is in her womb.

5072 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: al-Layth narrated to me, saying: 'Uqayl narrated to me, from Ibn Shihab, concerning the saying of Allah: "Those of you who die and leave wives behind, they shall wait by themselves four months and ten days." Ibn Shihab said: Allah made this waiting period for the woman whose husband has died. If she is pregnant, her waiting period is ended by her giving birth to her burden. And if it extends beyond the four months and ten days, whatever extends, she is not released except by giving birth to her burden. [[In the manuscript and the printed edition: "concerning the saying of Allah," and what I have established is correct.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: We have said that "tarabbus" means what we have described, because of the concurrence of reports from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to that effect:

5073 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' and Abu Usama narrated to us, from Shu'ba. And Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, from Shu'ba, from Humayd ibn Nafi', who said: I heard Zaynab, daughter of Umm Salama, narrating. [[Abu Kurayb said: Abu Usama said: from Umm Salama] that a woman whose husband had died and whose eye was inflamed came to the Prophet (ﷺ) asking his ruling about kohl. He said: "Indeed, one of you used to be in the Jahiliyya in the worst of her rags, [[The ahlas is the plural of hills, which is a thin cloth beneath the saddle-pad, and everything spread under the heat of goods to protect them is a hils. What is meant here is the most despised of her garments.]] and she would remain in her house for a full year when her husband died. A dog would pass by her and she would throw a dung-pellet at it! Is it not four months and ten days?"! [[Hadith 5073: "Humayd ibn Nafi' al-Ansari al-Madani": a reliable Successor (tabi'i). He narrated from Abu Ayyub and 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar, and he narrated from Zaynab bint Umm Salama. He is the father of "Aflah ibn Humayd." He is also called "Humayd Safira." Al-Bukhari in al-Kabir 1/2/345 distinguished between "Humayd Safira, father of Aflah," the narrator from Abu Ayyub and Ibn 'Umar, and "Humayd," the narrator from Zaynab, considering them two, following his teacher 'Ali ibn al-Madini; but he himself narrated from Shu'ba that they are one. This is the correct view, which Imam Ahmad affirmed. He narrated in al-Musnad 6: 325-326 (Halabi) the hadith of Humayd ibn Nafi', from Zaynab bint Umm Salama, from Umm Habiba, Mother of the Believers, then he said after the hadith: "Humayd ibn Nafi': Abu Aflah, and he is Humayd Safira," and this is what Ibn Sa'd 5: 224 and Ibn Abi Hatim 1/2/229-230 restricted themselves to. "Safira" is Humayd's epithet. This is how it is correctly written in al-Musnad, and al-Tahdhib in the biography of "Aflah," and al-Bukhari in the biography of "Humayd." It is written in al-Tahdhib in the biography of "Humayd" as "Safir," which is a misreading. It also occurs in al-Tahdhib in the biography of "Humayd" that he narrates from "'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr," which is an error; the correct reading, as we have said, is "'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar." The hadith will come: 5079, with another chain, from the hadith of Umm Salama alone. It will come with other chains, in some of which it is "from Umm Salama and Umm Habiba," and in all the rest "from Umm Salama or Umm Habiba" (5076-5078, 5080). We will mention them in their places, God willing. As for the route here, Shu'ba's narration from Humayd: al-Tayalisi narrated it (1596), from Shu'ba, with this chain, similarly. Likewise Ahmad narrated it in al-Musnad 6: 291-292 (Halabi), from Yahya ibn Sa'id, who is al-Qattan; then he narrated it 6: 311, from Muhammad ibn Ja'far, and from Hajjaj, who is Ibn Muhammad al-Misisi, all three from Shu'ba, similarly. Al-Bukhari narrated it 9: 432, and 10: 131, in full and abridged, by two routes from Shu'ba. Likewise Muslim narrated it, 1: 434, by the route of Muhammad ibn Ja'far, from Shu'ba. Likewise Ibn al-Jarud narrated it in al-Muntaqa, p. 353-354, by the route of Yahya, who is al-Qattan, from Shu'ba. Likewise al-Bayhaqi narrated it in al-Sunan al-Kubra 7: 439, by the route of al-Tayalisi and Yahya ibn Abi Bukayr, both from Shu'ba. Malik narrated it in al-Muwatta, p. 596-598, from 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Bakr ibn Hazm, from Humayd ibn Nafi', from Zaynab bint Umm Salama, from her mother, the third of three hadiths Zaynab narrated to Humayd ibn Nafi', in similar meaning. From this route of Malik the imams narrated it: 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated it in al-Musannaf 4: 66-67 (photographed manuscript), and al-Bukhari 9: 427-428, Muslim 1: 433-434, Abu Dawud: 2299, al-Tirmidhi 2: 220, al-Nasa'i 2: 114, and Ibn Hibban in his Sahih (2: 91-92 manuscript al-Taqasim, and 6: 457-458 manuscript al-Ihsan). It is in al-Muntaqa of al-Majd ibn Taymiyya, under number 3811.]]

5074 - Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us, saying: I heard Yahya ibn Sa'id say: I heard Nafi' say, from Safiyya, daughter of Abu 'Ubayd: that she heard Hafsa, daughter of 'Umar, wife of the Prophet (ﷺ), narrating from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "It is not lawful for a woman who believes in Allah and the Last Day to mourn beyond three days, except for a husband; for her, she mourns him four months and ten days." [[Yahya said: Mourning, according to us, is that she does not apply perfume, does not wear a garment dyed with wars or saffron, [[Wars: a yellow plant from which a yellow dye is made to dye garments, and from it is that which is for adornment, like saffron.]] does not apply kohl, and does not adorn herself. [[The two hadiths: 5074 and 5075 are one hadith, in a full and abridged form, with two chains. 'Abd al-Wahhab in the first chain is Ibn 'Abd al-Majid al-Thaqafi. Yazid, in the second chain, is Ibn Harun. Yahya ibn Sa'id, in both chains, is al-Ansari. Nafi' is the client of Ibn 'Umar. Safiyya bint Abi 'Ubayd ibn Mas'ud al-Thaqafiyya: she is a reliable Successor, one of the excellent women, and some mention her among the Companions, which is not sound. She was the wife of 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar. She was the sister of al-Mukhtar ibn Abi 'Ubayd al-Thaqafi, the liar. How great is the difference between the two brothers! In her biography in al-Tahdhib 12: 430 it is recorded that "Nafi', client of Ibn 'Abbas" narrates from her, which is an error or a scribal mistake; rather, the one who narrates from her is "Nafi', client of Ibn 'Umar." She has a biography in Ibn Sa'd 8: 346-347 and al-Isaba 8: 131. The hadith was narrated by Muslim 1: 435, by the route of 'Abd al-Wahhab, from Yahya. This is the first route here, and he did not mention its full wording. Likewise al-Bayhaqi narrated it 7: 438, by the route of 'Abd al-Wahhab, and he mentioned its wording. Ahmad narrated it in al-Musnad 6: 286, from Yazid ibn Harun, which is the second route here.]]

5075 - Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Yahya informed us, from Nafi', from Safiyya bint Abi 'Ubayd, from Hafsa bint 'Umar: that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "It is not lawful for a woman who believes in Allah and the Last Day to mourn over a dead person beyond three days, except for a husband."

5076 - Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us, saying: I heard Yahya ibn Sa'id say: Humayd ibn Nafi' informed me that Zaynab, daughter of Umm Salama, informed him, from Umm Salama, or Umm Habiba, wife of the Prophet (ﷺ): that a woman came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and mentioned that her daughter's husband had died and that she feared for her eye. Humayd reported from Zaynab that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "One of you used to throw a dung-pellet at the end of the year, but it is only four months and ten." [[Hadith 5076 is the hadith that preceded, 5073, except that here it is "from Umm Salama or Umm Habiba," with doubt. Likewise in the chain after it, 5077. In the chain 5080 it will come that it is "from Umm Salama and Umm Habiba" together, without doubt about it.
As for his narrating it with doubt, with the particle "aw" [or], I have never found it. I fear it is a distortion by the copyists. Indeed, al-Darimi narrated (2: 167) another story about Umm Habiba, at the end of which is the hadith "It is not lawful for a woman who believes in Allah and the Last Day to mourn beyond three days..." etc. He narrated it from Hashim ibn al-Qasim, from Shu'ba, from Humayd ibn Nafi', from Zaynab bint Abi Salama, from Umm Habiba. Then he narrated after it, with the same chain to Zaynab, "narrating from her mother, or a woman from among the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ), similarly." But that is a different hadith from this hadith, and perhaps Zaynab also doubted in the narration here, as she doubted in the narration that is in al-Darimi.
Likewise Muslim narrated it 1: 434, from Ibn al-Muthanna, from Ibn Ja'far, from Shu'ba, in the story of Umm Habiba only. Then Humayd said: "Zaynab related it to me from her mother, and from Zaynab, wife of the Prophet (ﷺ), or from a woman from some of the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ)."
Then he narrated from 'Ubayd Allah ibn Mu'adh, from his father, from Shu'ba: "from Humayd ibn Nafi', both hadiths together: the hadith of Umm Salama about kohl, and the hadith of Umm Salama and another of the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ). Except that Zaynab did not name her, similar to the hadith of Muhammad ibn Ja'far." In any case, this doubt does not affect the soundness of the hadith, and the established narrations indicate that she narrated it from her mother and Umm Habiba, as will come.]]

5077 - Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Sa'id informed us, from Humayd ibn Nafi': that he heard Zaynab, daughter of Umm Salama, narrating from Umm Habiba or Umm Salama that she mentioned: that a woman came to the Prophet (ﷺ) whose husband had died, and her eye was inflamed, and she wanted to apply kohl to her eye. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "One of you used to throw a dung-pellet after the year, but it is only four months and ten." Ibn Bashshar said, Yazid said, Yahya said: I asked Humayd about her throwing the dung-pellet. He said: In the Jahiliyya, when a woman's husband died, she would make for the worst of her house and sit in it for a year. When a year passed, she would throw a dung-pellet behind her. [[Hadith 5077 is also the previous hadith, with another chain. In the printed edition "or Umm Salama" appears here with doubt, like the previous narration. But I am certain here that it is an error by Ibn Bashshar, the teacher of al-Tabari.
The hadith was narrated by Muslim 1: 434, from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shayba and 'Amr al-Naqid, both from Yazid ibn Harun, with this chain. In it: "that he heard Zaynab bint Abi Salama narrating from Umm Salama and Umm Habiba, both mentioning: that a woman..." etc. This is explicit in narrating from both of them together, not from one of them. Likewise Ibn Majah narrated it, 2084, from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shayba, from Yazid ibn Harun, similar to Muslim's narration. It is supported by the fact that al-Nasa'i narrated it 2: 115, by the route of Hammad, from Yahya al-Ansari, from Humayd, from Zaynab: "that a woman asked Umm Salama and Umm Habiba... and both said: a woman came to the Prophet (ﷺ)..."]]

5078 - Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Shu'ba narrated to us, from Yahya, from Humayd ibn Nafi', with this chain, similar to it. [[Hadith 5078 is a repetition of the hadith before it, without its wording being mentioned. It is from the narration of Yazid ibn Harun, from Shu'ba, from Yahya al-Ansari, from Humayd.]]

وأنا أخشى أن يكون في الإسناد تحريفٌ من النُّسّاخ، وأن يكون صوابه: "حدثنا شعبة، ويحيى". لأن الإسناد قبله هو من رواية يزيد بن هارون عن يحيى مباشرة. فقد تكون الفائدة في تكرار هذا الإسناد: أن يكون ابن بشار سمعه من يزيد مرتين: مرة عن يحيى وحده، ومرة عن يحيى وشعبة. وإذا كان ما ثبت في المطبوعة صحيحا، كان ابن بشار سمعه هكذا، ويكون من المزيد في متصل الأسانيد.]]

٥٠٧٩- حدثنا أبو كريب قال، حدثنا ابن إدريس قال، حدثنا ابن عيينة، عن أيوب بن موسى ويحيى بن سعيد، عن حميد بن نافع، عن زينب ابنة أم سلمة، عن أم سلمة: أن امرأة أتت النبي ﷺ فقالت: إن ابنتي مات زوجها فاشتكت عينها، أفتكتحل؟ [[في المخطوطة: "أفتكحل".]] فقال: قد كانت إحداكن ترمي بالبعرة على رأس الحول، وإنما هي الآن أربعة أشهر وعشر! = قال، قلت: وما "ترمي بالبعرة على رأس الحول"؟ قال: كان نساء الجاهلية إذا مات زوج إحداهن، لبست أطمار ثيابها، [[الأطمار جمع طمر (بكسر فسكون): وهو الثوب الخَلِق، والكساء البالي.]] وجلست في أخس بيوتها، فإذا حال عليها الحول أخذت بعرة فدحرجتها على ظهر حمار وقالت: قد حللت! [[الحديث ٥٠٧٩: أيوب بن موسى بن عمرو بن سعيد بن العاص بن سعيد بن العاص: قرشي مكي، ثقة حافظ فقيه. مذكور في "نسب قريش" للمصعب، ص: ١٨٣.
وهذا الحديث تكرار للحديث ٥٠٧٣، بأنه عن أم سلمة وحدها، كما قلنا هناك.
وقد رواه النسائي ٢: ١١٥ من طريق الليث بن سعد، عن أيوب بن موسى. ثم من طريق سفيان بن عيينة، عن يحيى الأنصاري، به، نحوه، مطولا ومختصرا.]]

٥٠٨٠- حدثنا أبو كريب قال، حدثنا أحمد بن يونس قال، حدثنا زهير بن معاوية قال، حدثنا يحيى بن سعيد، عن حميد بن نافع، عن زينب ابنة أم سلمة، عن أمها أم سلمة وأم حبيبة زوجي النبي ﷺ: أن امرأة من قريش جاءت إلى رسول الله ﷺ فقالت: إن ابنتي توفي عنها زوجها، وقد خفت على عينها، وهي تريد الكحل؟ قال: قد كانت إحداكن ترمي بالبعرة على رأس الحول! وإنما هي أربعة أشهر وعشر! = قال حميد: فقلت لزينب: وما رأس الحول؟ قالت زينب: كانت المرأة في الجاهلية إذا هلك زوجها، عمدت إلى أشرّ بيت لها فجلست فيه، [[قوله: "أشرّ" على وزن "أفعل"، هكذا جاء هنا. وقال أهل اللغة: إنه لغة قليلة أو رديئة. وقد جاء في كثير من أمثالهم وكلامهم "أشرّ" و"شرى"، كأفضل وفضلى. ومنه قول امرأة من العرب: "أعيذك بالله من نفس حرى، وعين شرى"، أي خبيثة. وفي المثل: "شراهن مراهن". وفي خبر العبادي قيل له: "أي حماريك أشرّ؟" قال: "هذا ثم هذا".]] حتى إذا مرت بها سنة خرجت، ثم رمت ببعرة وراءها. [[الحديث ٥٠٨٠: أحمد بن يونس: هو أحمد بن عبد الله بن يونس، مضى في ٢١٤٤. وهذا الحديث تكرار -في المعنى- للحديث ٥٠٧٣، وللأحاديث ٥٠٧٦-٥٠٧٩. وقد رواه هنا أحمد بن يونس عن زهير بن معاوية عن يحيى الأنصاري، وذكر فيه أنه "عن أم سلمة وأم حبيبة" معا.
ولكن رواه النسائي ٢: ١١٥ -بنحوه- من طريق ابن أعين، وهو الحسن بن محمد بن أعين، عن زهير بن معاوية، بهذا الإسناد، من حديث "أم سلمة"، ولم يذكر فيه أم حبيبة.]]

٥٠٨١- حدثنا ابن حميد قال، حدثنا ابن المبارك، عن معمر، عن الزهري، عن عروة، عن عائشة: أنها كانت تفتي المتوفى عنها زوجها، أن تحد على زوجها حتى تنقضي عدتها، ولا تلبس ثوبا مصبوغا ولا معصفرا، ولا تكتحل بالإثمد، ولا بكحل فيه طيب وإن وجعت عينها، ولكن تكتحل بالصبر وما بدا لها من الأكحال سوى الإثمد مما ليس فيه طيب، ولا تلبس حليا، وتلبس البياض ولا تلبس السواد. [[الخبر ٥٠٨١: هذا أثر من فتوى عائشة وكلامها. ولكن تدل على صحة فتواها الأحاديثُ الصحاح. وهذا إسناده إليها صحيح. ولم أجده في شيء من المراجع غير هذا الموضع.
المعصفر: هو الثوب المصبوغ بالعصفر. والإثمد: هو الكحل، أو حجر يتخذ منه الكحل، وهو أسود إلى الحمرة. والصبر (بفتح الصاد وكسر الباء): عصارة شجر، وهو مر، يتخذ منه الدواء.]]

٥٠٨٢- حدثنا ابن بشار قال، حدثنا مؤمل قال، حدثنا سفيان، عن موسى بن عقبة، عن نافع، عن ابن عمر في المتوفى عنها زوجها: لا تكتحل، ولا تطيب، ولا تبيت عن بيتها، ولا تلبس ثوبا مصبوغا، إلا ثوب عَصَب تجلببت به. [[قوله: "تبيت عن بيتها" أي تبيت بعيدة عن بيتها وتنتقل إلى غيره. والعصب: بُرود من اليمن، يُعصب غزلها -أي يُجمع ويُشد- ثم يُصبغ وينسج، فيأتي موشّى، لبقاء ما عُصب منه أبيض لم يأخذه صبغ. تجلببت المرأة: لبست جلبابها، وهو ملاءتها التي تشتمل بها.]]

٥٠٨٣- حدثنا حميد بن مسعدة قال، حدثنا سفيان قال، حدثنا ابن جريج، عن عطاء قال: بلغني عن ابن عباس قال: تُنهى المتوفى عنها زوجها أن تتزين وتتطيب.

٥٠٨٤- حدثنا نصر بن علي قال، حدثنا عبد الأعلى قال، حدثنا عبيد الله، عن نافع، عن ابن عمر قال: إن المتوفى عنها زوجها لا تلبس ثوبا مصبوغا، ولا تمس طيبا، ولا تكتحل، ولا تمتشط= وكان لا يرى بأسا أن تلبس البرد.

* *

وقال آخرون: إنما أُمرت المتوفى عنها زوجها أن تتربص بنفسها عن الأزواج خاصة، فأما عن الطيب والزينة والمبيت عن المنزل، فلم تُنه عن ذلك، ولم تؤمر بالتربص بنفسها عنه.

ذكر من قال ذلك:

٥٠٨٥- حدثنا يعقوب بن إبراهيم قال، حدثنا ابن علية، عن يونس، عن الحسن: أنه كان يرخص في التزين والتصنع، ولا يرى الإحداد شيئا. [[تصنعت المرأة تصنعا: تزينت وتجملت وعالجت وجهها وغيره حتى يحسن.]]

٥٠٨٦- حدثنا حميد بن مسعدة قال، حدثنا سفيان، عن ابن جريج، عن عطاء، عن ابن عباس: "والذين يتوفون منكم ويذرون أزواجا يتربصن بأنفسهن أربعة أشهر وعشرا"، لم يقل: تعتد في بيتها، تعتد حيث شاءت.

٥٠٨٧- حدثنا أبو كريب قال، حدثنا إسماعيل قال، حدثنا ابن جريج، عن عطاء قال، قال ابن عباس: إنما قال الله: "والذين يتوفون منكم ويذرون أزواجا يتربصن بأنفسهن أربعة أشهر وعشرا"، ولم يقل: تعتد في بيتها، فلتعتد حيث شاءت.

* *

واعتل قائلو هذه المقالة بأن الله تعالى ذكره إنما أمر المتوفى عنها بالتربص عن النكاح، وجعلوا حكم الآية على الخصوص= وبما:

٥٠٨٨- حدثني به محمد بن إبراهيم السلمي قال، حدثنا أبو عاصم، وحدثني محمد بن معمر البحراني قال، حدثنا أبو عامر = قالا جميعا: حدثنا محمد بن طلحة، عن الحكم بن عتيبة، عن عبد الله بن شداد بن الهاد، عن أسماء بنت عميس قالت: لما أصيب جعفر قال لي رسول الله ﷺ: "تسلّبي ثلاثا، ثم اصنعي ما شئت". [[الحديث ٥٠٨٨: محمد بن إبراهيم بن صدران الأزدي السلمي: ثقة، وثّقه أبو داود وغيره. وقد يُنسب إلى جده، ولذلك ترجمه ابن أبي حاتم ٣/٢/١٩٠ في اسم "محمد بن صدران". "السلمي": هكذا ثبت هنا، وكذلك في "التقريب"، وضبطه بفتح السين، وكذلك ثبت في نسخة بهامش "التهذيب". وفي "التهذيب" و"الخلاصة" "السليمي"، ونص صاحب "الخلاصة" على أنه بإثبات الياء. ولكني لا أطمئن إلى ضبطه.
وشيخه أبو عاصم: هو النبيل، الضحاك بن مخلد.
وأبو عامر -في الإسناد الثاني: هو العَقَدي، عبد الملك بن عمرو.
محمد بن طلحة بن مُصرّف -بفتح الصاد وتشديد الراء المكسورة- اليامي: ثقة، أخرج له الشيخان. وبعضهم تكلم فيه بما لا يجرحه.
عبد الله بن شداد بن الهاد: نُسب أبوه إلى جده، فهو "شداد بن أسامة بن عمرو"، و"عمرو": هو الهاد. قال ابن سعد: "وإنما سُمي الهادي، لأنه كان توقد ناره ليلا للأضياف، ولمن سلك الطريق". وعبد الله بن شداد: من كبار التابعين القدماء الثقات، ولد في حياة رسول الله ﷺ، حتى ذكره بعضهم في الصحابة. وله ترجمتان في "الطبقات" لابن سعد ٥: ٤٣-٤٤، و٦: ٨٦-٨٧، وفي "الإصابة" ٥: ٦٠-٦١، ١٤٥. وأمه "سلمى بنت عميس"، أخت أسماء بنت عميس، فهو يروي هذا الحديث عن خالته.
وأسماء بنت عميس: صحابية جليلة. وهي أخت ميمونة بنت الحارث -أم المؤمنين- لأمها. تزوجت أسماء جعفر بن أبي طالب، فقُتل عنها، ثم تزوجت أبا بكر الصديق، ثم علي بن أبي طالب. وولدت لهم جميعا. وهي أم محمد بن أبي بكر الصديق.
والحديث رواه ابن سعد في "الطبقات" ٨: ٢٠٦، في ترجمة أسماء، رواه عن عفان بن مسلم، وإسحاق بن منصور، كلاهما عن محمد بن طلحة. ووقع فيه "تسلمي" بالميم بدل الباء. وأنا أرجح أنه خطأ من النُّسّاخ لا من الرواة، وسيأتي أن هذا الخطأ وقع لابن حبان، لكن من الرواة.
ورواه أحمد في "المسند"، بمعناه، ٦: ٣٦٩، ٤٣٨، عن يزيد بن هارون، عن أبي كامل ويزيد بن هارون وعفان -ثلاثتهم عن محمد بن طلحة.
ورواه الطحاوي في "معاني الآثار" ٢: ٤٤ بخمسة أسانيد إلى محمد بن طلحة.
ورواه البيهقي ٧: ٤٣٨، من طريق مالك بن إسماعيل، عن محمد بن طلحة، بهذا الإسناد. ثم قال: "لم يثبت سماع عبد الله من أسماء، وقد قيل فيه: عن أسماء. فهو مرسل. ومحمد بن طلحة ليس بالقوي"!! وهو تعليل ضئيل متهافت. تعقّبه فيه ابن التركماني في "الجوهر النقي".
ورواه ابن حزم في "المحلى" ١٠: ٢٨٠، من وجهين آخرين، عن عبد الله بن شداد، مرسلا، ورده بعلة الإرسال. ولكن ثبت وصله عن غير روايته.
وذكره المجد في "المنتقى": ٣٨١٩، ٣٨٢٠، من روايتي المسند. ولم ينسبه إلى غيره.
ولم يُرو في واحد من الكتب الستة، على اليقين من ذلك. فهو من الزوائد عليها. ولكني لم أجده في "مجمع الزوائد"، بعد طول البحث، في أقرب المظان من أبوابه وأبعدها.
وذكره الحافظ في "الفتح" ٩: ٤٢٩، ووصفه بأنه "قوي الإسناد". وقال: "أخرجه أحمد، وصححه ابن حبان". ونسبه أيضا للطحاوي. ثم قال: "قال شيخنا في شرح الترمذي: ظاهره أنه لا يجب الإحداد على المتوفى عنها بعد اليوم الثالث، لأن أسماء بنت عميس كانت زوج جعفر بن أبي طالب بالاتفاق، وهي والدة أولاده: عبد الله، ومحمد، وعون، وغيرهم. قال: بل ظاهر النهي أن الإحداد لا يجوز". وأجاب بأن هذا الحديث شاذ مخالف للأحاديث الصحيحة، وقد أجمعوا على خلافه، ثم ذهب يجمع بينه وبين الأحاديث التي يعارضها، بآراء بعضها قد يُقبل، وبعضها فيه تكلف غير مستساغ. وأجود ما قال العلماء في ذلك -عندنا- ما ذهب إليه الطبري هنا في الفقرة الثالثة بعد الحديث ٥٠٩٠. وقريب منه ما قال المجد بن تيمية في "المنتقى": "وهو متأول على المبالغة في الإحداد والجلوس للتعزية".
وقال الحافظ، في آخر كلامه، في شأن رواية ابن حبان: "وأغرب ابن حبان، فساق الحديث بلفظ: تَسَمّلي، بالميم بدل الموحدة! وفسّره بأنه أمرها بالتسليم لأمر الله!! ولا مفهوم لتقييدها بالثلاث، بل الحكمة فيه كون القلق يكون في ابتداء الأمر أشد، فلذلك قيّدها بالثلاث! هذا معنى كلامه، فصحّف الكلمة وتكلف لتأويلها! وقد وقع في رواية البيهقي وغيره: فأمرني رسول الله ﷺ أن أتسلّب ثلاثا. فتبين خطؤه".
تسلّبت المرأة: لبست السلاب (بكسر السين): وهي ثياب الحداد السود، تلبسها في المأتم.]]

٥٠٨٩- حدثنا أبو كريب قال، حدثنا أبو نعيم وابن الصلت، عن محمد بن طلحة، عن الحكم بن عتيبة، عن عبد الله بن شداد، عن أسماء، عن النبي ﷺ بمثله.

* *

قالوا: فقد بيّن هذا الخبر عن النبي ﷺ: أن لا إحداد على المتوفى عنها زوجها، وأن القول في تأويل قوله: "يتربصن بأنفسهن أربعة أشهر وعشرا"، إنما هو يتربصن بأنفسهن عن الأزواج دون غيره.

* *

قال أبو جعفر: وأما الذين أوجبوا الإحداد على المتوفى عنها زوجها، وترك النقلة عن منزلها الذي كانت تسكنه يوم توفي عنها زوجها، فإنهم اعتلوا بظاهر التنزيل، وقالوا: أمر الله المتوفى عنها أن تتربص بنفسها أربعة أشهر وعشرا، فلم يأمرها بالتربص بشيء مسمى في التنزيل بعينه، بل عمّ بذلك معاني التربص. قالوا: فالواجب عليها أن تتربص بنفسها عن كل شيء، إلا ما أطلقته لها حجة يجب التسليم لها. قالوا: فالتربص عن الطيب والزينة والنقلة، مما هو داخل في عموم الآية، كما أن التربص عن الأزواج داخل فيها. قالوا: وقد صح عن رسول الله ﷺ الخبر بالذي قلنا في الزينة والطيب، أما في النقلة فإن:

٥٠٩٠- أبا كريب حدثنا قال، حدثنا يونس بن محمد، عن فليح بن سليمان، عن سعد بن إسحاق بن كعب بن عجرة، عن عمته، عن الفُريعة ابنة مالك، أخت أبي سعيد الخدري، قالت: قُتل زوجي وأنا في دار، فاستأذنت رسول الله ﷺ في النقلة، فأذن لي. ثم ناداني بعد أن توليت، فرجعت إليه، فقال: "يا فُريعة، امكثي في بيتك حتى يبلغ الكتاب أجله". [[الحديث ٥٠٩٠: يونس بن محمد بن مسلم، الحافظ البغدادي المؤدب: ثقة، أخرج له أصحاب الكتب الستة.
فليح -بالتصغير- بن سليمان بن أبي المغيرة المدني: ثقة، أخرج له أصحاب الكتب الستة. تكلم فيه ابن معين وغيره. والراجح توثيقه. وقال الحاكم: "اتفاق الشيخين عليه يقوي أمره". و"فليح" لقب غلب عليه، واسمه "عبد الملك".
سعد بن إسحاق بن كعب بن عجرة: ثقة لا يختلف فيه، كما قال ابن عبد البر. وهو تابعي روى عن أنس بن مالك.
وتكلم فيه ابن حزم في "المحلى" بما لا يضره، زعم أنه "غير مشهور الحال"، ومرة أنه "مضطرب في اسمه، غير مشهور الحال"، ومرة أنه "غير مشهور العدالة"! انظر "المحلى" ٣: ٢٧٣، و٤: ١٣٨، و١٠: ٣٠٢.
وفي المطبوعة هنا "سعيد" بدل "سعد". وهو خطأ قديم، وقع في "الموطأ"، ص: ٥٩١. وليس اختلاف رواية، ولا خطأ من مالك. إنما هو من يحيى بن يحيى راوي "الموطأ"، ومن رواة آخرين تبعوه. قال ابن عبد البر في "التقصي"، رقم: ١٢٣: "هكذا قال يحيى: سعيد بن إسحاق، وتابعه بعضهم. وأكثر الرواة يقولون فيه: سعد بن إسحاق. وهو الأشهر، وكذا قال شعبة وغيره".
وعلى الصواب "سعد"، رواه الشافعي في "الرسالة" و"الأم" عن مالك. وكذلك رواه عنه سويد بن سعيد، في روايته "الموطأ". وكذلك رواه عنه محمد بن الحسن في "الموطأ".
عمة سعد بن إسحاق: هي "زينب بنت كعب بن عجرة الأنصارية"، وهي تابعية ثقة. بل ذكرها بعضهم في الصحابة. انظر "الإصابة" ٨: ٩٧-٩٨، و"ابن سعد" ٨: ٣٥٢.
ووقع هنا في المطبوعة "عن عمته الفريعة"، بحذف "عن" بعد كلمة "عمته". وهو خطأ ناسخ أو طابع. فإن زينب عمة سعد هي زوجة أبي سعيد الخدري، وأما الفُريعة فإنها أخت أبي سعيد، كما في نص الحديث.
و"الفُريعة بنت مالك بن سنان": صحابية قديمة معروفة، شهدت بيعة الرضوان. رضي الله عنها. وهذا الحديث هنا مختصر. وقد جاء بأسانيد صحاح، من رواية سعد بن إسحاق، عن عمته، عن الفُريعة -مختصرا ومطولا. ويكفي أن نذكر مواضع روايته، فيما وصل إلينا:
فرواه مالك في "الموطأ"، مطولا، ص: ٥٩١، عن "سعد بن إسحاق". وذكر فيه خطأ باسم "سعيد"، كما بينا من قبل.
ورواه الشافعي في "الرسالة": ١٢١٤ (بتحقيقنا)، وفي "الأم" ٥: ٢٠٨-٢٠٩، ومحمد بن الحسن في "موطئه"، ص: ٢٦٨، وسويد بن سعيد في "موطئه"، ص: ١٢٣-١٢٤ (مخطوط مصور) -كلهم عن مالك، عن سعد بن إسحاق.
ورواه الدارمي ٢: ١٦٨، وابن سعد ٨: ٢٦٨، وأبو داود: ٢٣٠٠، والترمذي ٢: ٢٢٤-٢٢٥، والبيهقي ٧: ٤٣٤، وابن حبان في "صحيحه" ٦: ٤٤٧-٤٤٨ (من مخطوطة "الإحسان")، وابن حزم في "المحلى" ١٠: ٣٠١ -كلهم من طريق مالك، به.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 234 (part 3 of 3):

Also related by al-Tayalisi: 1664; ʿAbd al-Razzaq in al-Musannaf 4: 60-61 (photographic manuscript); Ahmad in al-Musnad 6: 370, 420-421 (Halabi edition); Ibn Saʿd 8: 267-268; al-Tirmidhi 2: 225; al-Nasaʾi 2: 113; Ibn Majah: 2031; Ibn al-Jarud, p. 349-350; Ibn Hibban 6: 449; al-Hakim 2: 208; and al-Bayhaqi 7: 434-435, by many chains of narration, both lengthy and abridged, through the route of Saʿd ibn Ishaq, from his paternal aunt, from al-Furayʿa. Al-Tirmidhi authenticated it, as did Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Dhuhli, as related from him by al-Hakim, and al-Dhahabi. Al-Suyuti mentioned it in 1: 289-290, attributing it to many of those we have indicated.

* *

They said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) thereby clarified the correctness of what we have said regarding the meaning of the waiting period (tarabbus) of the woman whose husband has died, and [nullified] what contradicts it. [The words in parentheses are necessary for the context of the discourse. The printed and manuscript texts are identical here.]

They said: As for what is related from Ibn ʿAbbas, it has no meaning, since it departs from the apparent sense of the revelation (tanzil) and from the established report from the Messenger (ﷺ).

They said: As for the report related from Asma bint ʿUmays, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), concerning his command to her to put off adornment (tasallub) for three days, and then to do whatever seems fit to her, it does not indicate that there is no mourning (ihdad) for the woman. [In the printed edition: "an la ihdad", and both are the same. "Haddat al-mara tahuddu huddan wa hidadan" and "ahadat tuhidu ihdadan." Labisat al-hidad (with a kasra on the ha), which are black mourning garments. "Al-hidad" is both a noun and a verbal noun.] Rather, it only indicates the Prophet's (ﷺ) command to her to put off adornment for three days, and then acting upon what seems fit to her, namely wearing whatever garments she wishes among those permitted to the woman in the waiting period, provided they are not adornment or perfumed, [In the printed edition: "wa la tatayyub". The correct reading is what I have recorded from the manuscript.] because there may be garments that are neither adornment nor garments of mourning-adornment (tasallub). This is like what the Prophet (ﷺ) permitted the widow to wear: garments of ʿasb and Yemeni striped cloths. For such are neither garments of adornment nor garments of tasallub. Likewise, every garment that has not been dyed after being woven, of the kind people dye to beautify it, is permitted for her to wear, because she wears it without adorning herself with the adornment that people recognize.

* *

Abu Jaʿfar said: If someone says to us: How is it said, "They shall wait with themselves for four months and ten [days]," and not "and ten" (ʿashara)? Since the revelation is thus, is the widow's waiting period counted by nights or by days?

It is said: Rather, she observes the waiting period by days along with their nights.

If he says: Since that is so, why is it said "wa ʿashran" and not "wa ʿashara"? For the form "ʿashr" without the ha is used for numbers of nights and not of days. If you permit that the meaning is what you have said, would you then permit saying "ʿindi ʿashr," while you mean ten men and women?

I say: That is permissible for numbers of nights and days, but the like of it is not permissible for the number of human beings, men and women. This is because the Arabs, specifically concerning days and nights, when they leave the number unspecified, give precedence to the nights, so much so that, as is related from them, they say: "We fasted ten (ʿashran) of the month of Ramadan," giving precedence to the nights over the days. This is because the counting among them has proceeded with the nights rather than the days. When they make the counted noun (mufassir) explicit with the number, [al-mufassir: the specified noun (al-mumayyiz). And al-tafsir: specification (al-tamyiz). See above 2: 338, note 1; and 3: 90, note 1.]
they drop the ha from the number of feminine nouns and affirm it with the number of masculine nouns, as the Exalted has said: ﴿He subjected them against them for seven nights and eight days, in continuous succession﴾ [Surah al-Haqqah: 7]. So the ha is dropped from "sabʿ" and affirmed in "al-thamaniya."

As for human beings, it is the habit of the Arabs, when men and women are gathered together and then they leave their number unspecified, to express it in the number of males rather than females. This is because the males of human beings have a singular and plural form marked differently from their females, whereas this is not so with other things. For the males of other things are sometimes marked with the feminine marker, as "shah" is said of both the male and the female, and "baqar" is said of both males and females of cattle. But this is not the case with human beings. [See the Maʿani al-Quran of al-Farraʾ 1: 151-152, for this is from his speech, not in his exact words.]

* *

If he says: What is the meaning of the addition of these ten days to the months?

It is said: It has been said regarding that, that:

5091. Ibn Wakiʿ related it to us, saying: My father related to us, saying: Abu Jaʿfar related to us, from al-Rabiʿ, from Abu al-ʿAliya, concerning His saying: "And those of you who die and leave wives behind, they shall wait with themselves for four months and ten [days]." He said: I asked: Why did these ten come to be with the four months? He said: Because the spirit is breathed into it in the ten.

5092. al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Abu ʿAsim related to me, from Saʿid, from Qatada, who said: I asked Saʿid ibn al-Musayyib: What about the ten? He said: In it the spirit is breathed.

* *

The interpretation (taʾwil) of His saying: ﴿So when they have reached their term, there is no blame upon you for what they do with themselves in an acceptable manner﴾

Abu Jaʿfar said: The Exalted means by that: When they reach the term that was made lawful for them, after what had been forbidden to them during their waiting period because of the death of their husbands, that is, after the completion of their waiting period and the passing of the four months and ten days, "then there is no blame upon you for what they do with themselves in an acceptable manner." He says: There is no sin upon you, O guardians, the guardians of the women, for what the widows then do with themselves, of perfuming, adorning, and moving out of the dwelling in which they were observing the waiting period, and marrying whomever it is lawful for them to marry, "in an acceptable manner," meaning: according to what God has permitted them and made lawful for them. [See above for the explanation of "al-maʿruf" in 5: 76 and the references there in the note.]

* *

It has been said: The meaning is specifically marriage. And it has been said that the meaning of His saying "in an acceptable manner" is only lawful marriage.

Those who said that:

5093. Muhammad ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Muammal related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "There is no blame upon you for what they do with themselves in an acceptable manner," he said: The lawful and good.

5094. Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Hakkam related to us, from ʿAnbasa, from Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman, from al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza, from Mujahid: "There is no blame upon you for what they do with themselves in an acceptable manner," he said: The acceptable is lawful and good marriage.

5095. al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ibn Jurayj said: Mujahid said concerning His saying "for what they do with themselves in an acceptable manner": It is lawful and good marriage.

5096. Musa related to me, saying: ʿAmr related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, who said: It is marriage.

5097. al-Muthanna related to me, saying: ʿAbd Allah ibn Salih related to us, saying: al-Layth related to me, saying: ʿAqil related to me, from Ibn Shihab: "for what they do with themselves in an acceptable manner," he said: In the marriage of whomever she loves, if it is acceptable. [In the printed edition: "huwayatuhu" in the plural with the nun; I have recorded what is in the manuscript.]

* *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And Allah is Aware of what you do﴾ [2: 234]

Abu Jaʿfar said: The Exalted means by that: "And Allah is aware of what you do," O guardians, concerning the affair of those women over whom you are guardians, of preventing them (ʿadl) and marrying them off to whom they wish to marry in an acceptable manner, and concerning your other affairs and theirs, "[is] Aware" (khabir), meaning: possessing knowledge and awareness, nothing of it is hidden from Him. [See above for the meaning of "khabir" in the indexes of language and the discussions of Arabic grammar.]

* *

Here ends the old division of the copy from which our manuscript was transcribed, and in it is the following text:

"And may Allah bless Muhammad the Prophet and his family, and grant them abundant peace.
Compared with the original, the reading and listening from its beginning were completed by the reading of Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn ʿIsa al-Saʿdi, to his brother ʿAli and Ahmad ibn ʿUmar al-Jahari (??) and Nasr ibn al-Husayn al-Tabari, before the judge Abu al-Hasan al-Khusaybi, from Abu Muhammad al-Farghani, from Abu Jaʿfar al-Tabari. It was collated with the book of the judge al-Khusaybi, and found correct, in Shaʿban of the year 408 [AH]."

* *

[This is the text of the beginning of the old division:
"In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.
My Lord, make it easy."]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 235 (part 1 of 3):

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿There is no blame upon you for what you imply of your proposal to women﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His remembrance be exalted, He means: There is no blame upon you, O men, for what you imply of a proposal to the women who are observing their waiting period (iddah) following the death of their husbands, during their waiting period, and you have not declared a marriage contract.

As for the allusion (ta'ridh) that is permitted in this matter, it is what:

5098 - Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Jarir related to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words: "There is no blame upon you for what you imply of your proposal to women," he said: The allusion is that he says: "I intend to marry," and "I truly love a woman with such-and-such a quality," implying to her with fair speech.

5099 - Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas: "There is no blame upon you for what you imply of your proposal to women," he said: "I intend to marry."

5100 - Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman related to us, saying: Shu'bah related to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The allusion is what does not aim directly at the proposal [[nasaba al-shay yansibu nasban: if he aimed at it and devoted himself to it.]] = Mujahid said: A man said to a woman at the funeral of her husband: "Do not outpace me with yourself!" She said: "You have already outpaced me!"

5101 - Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far related to us, saying: Shu'bah related to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas, who said regarding this verse: "There is no blame upon you for what you imply of your proposal to women," he said: The allusion is what does not aim directly at the proposal.

5102 - Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Hakkam related to us, from Amr, from Mansur, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas: "for what you imply of your proposal to women," he said: The allusion is that he says to the woman during her waiting period: "I do not intend to marry anyone other than you, God willing," and "I wish I had found a righteous woman," and he does not aim directly at her as long as she is in her waiting period.

5103 - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abd Allah ibn Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words: "There is no blame upon you for what you imply of your proposal to women," he said: He implies to her during her waiting period, saying to her: "If you see that you should not outpace me with yourself, and I wish that God had brought about between me and you," and similar speech, so there is no fault in it.

5104 - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Adam al-Asqalani related to us, saying: Shu'bah related to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas regarding His words: "There is no blame upon you for what you imply of your proposal to women," he said: It is that he says to her during her waiting period: "I intend to marry, and I wished that God would grant me a woman," and similar to this, without aiming directly at a proposal.

5105 - Yaqub related to me, saying: Ibn Ulayyah related to us, from Ibn Awn, from Muhammad, from Ubaydah regarding this verse, he said: He mentions her to her guardian, saying: "Do not outpace me with her."

5106 - Yaqub related to me, saying: Ibn Ulayyah related to us, from Layth, from Mujahid regarding His words: "There is no blame upon you for what you imply of your proposal to women," he said: He says: "Indeed you are beautiful, indeed you are chaste, indeed you are good."

5107 - Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Layth, from Mujahid that he disliked saying: "Do not outpace me with yourself."

5108 - Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, from Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding the words of God, may His remembrance be exalted: "There is no blame upon you for what you imply of your proposal to women," he said: It is the man's saying to the woman: "Indeed you are beautiful, indeed you are chaste, indeed you are good."

5109 - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Suwayd related to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Ma'mar, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding His words: "There is no blame upon you for what you imply of your proposal to women," he said: He implies to the woman during her waiting period, saying: "By God, you are beautiful, and women are of my need, and you are good, God willing."

5110 - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Adam related to us, saying: Shu'bah related to us, from Salamah ibn Kuhayl, from Muslim al-Batin, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: It is the man's saying: "I intend to marry, and if I marry I will treat my wife well," this is the allusion.

5111 - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Muslim ibn Ibrahim related to us, saying: Shu'bah related to us, from Salamah ibn Kuhayl, from Muslim al-Batin, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr regarding His words: "There is no blame upon you for what you imply of your proposal to women," he said: He says: "I will surely give you, I will surely be good to you, I will surely do such-and-such to you." [[In the manuscript and the printed edition it reads "la-uhsin ilayki" (I will be good to you), and the correct reading is what I have established.]]

5012 - Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Abd al-Wahhab related to us, saying: I heard Yahya ibn Sa'id say: Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Qasim informed me, regarding His words: "for what you imply of your proposal to women," he said: The man's saying to the woman in her waiting period, alluding to the proposal: "By God, I am eager for you, and I am keen upon you," and similar to this.

5113 - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Ishaq related to us, saying: Abd al-Wahhab al-Thaqafi related to us, saying: I heard Yahya ibn Sa'id say: Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Qasim informed me that he heard al-Qasim ibn Muhammad say: "for what you imply of your proposal to women," it is the man's saying to the woman: "Indeed you are beautiful, indeed you are chaste, indeed you are good."

5114 - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Suwayd related to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Ibn Jurayj who said: I asked Ata: How does the suitor speak? He said: He alludes with allusion and does not disclose anything. He says: "I have a need of you, and rejoice, and you, praise be to God, are chaste," and does not disclose anything. Ata said: And she says: "I hear what you say," and does not treat it as anything, and does not say: "Perhaps that is so."

5115 - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Suwayd ibn Nasr related to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Yahya ibn Sa'id who said: Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Qasim related to me that he heard al-Qasim say, regarding a woman whose husband has died, and a man who wishes to propose to her and wishes to speak to her: what is the fitting speech he may use? He said: He says: "I am eager for you, I am keen upon you, and I am impressed by you," and similar speech.

5116 - Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Jarir related to us, from Mughirah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim regarding His words: "There is no blame upon you for what you imply of your proposal to women," he said: There is no harm in a gift within an allusion to marriage.

5117 - Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim related to me, saying: Hushaym related to us, saying: Mughirah informed us, saying: Ibrahim did not see any harm in sending a gift to her during the waiting period, if she was of his concern. [[His words "min sha'nih" mean: from his need, his intention and his aim. It is said: sha'n sha'nahu, meaning: he aimed his aim.]]

5118 - Ibn Waki' related to us, saying: My father related to us, from Israil, from Jabir, from Amir regarding His words: "There is no blame upon you for what you imply of your proposal to women," he said: He says: "Indeed you are chaste, indeed you are impressive, indeed you are beautiful" [[In the manuscript: "wa-innaki la-mu'jiba, la-jamila," and both are the same.]] "and if God decrees something, it will be."

5119 - Related to us by Amar, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far related to us, from his father regarding His words: "There is no blame upon you for what you imply of your proposal to women," he said: Ibrahim al-Nakha'i used to say: "Indeed you are impressive, and I am eager for you."

5120 - Yunus ibn Abd al-A'la related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, and Shabib informed me, from Sa'id, from Shu'bah, from Mansur, from al-Sha'bi that he said regarding this verse: "There is no blame upon you for what you imply of your proposal to women," he said: He does not take her pledge that she will not marry anyone but you. [[In the printed edition: "la yakhudh mithaqaha an la tankih ghayrahu," and I have established what is in the manuscript.]]

5121 - Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words: "There is no blame upon you for what you imply of your proposal to women," he said: My father used to say: Everything that happens short of resolving the marriage bond is what God, may His remembrance be exalted, described in His words: "There is no blame upon you for what you imply of your proposal to women."

5122 - Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us = and Ali related to me, saying: Zayd related to us = both from Sufyan regarding His words: "There is no blame upon you for what you imply of your proposal to women," and the allusion, as we have heard, is that a man says while she is in her waiting period: "Indeed you are beautiful, indeed you are good, indeed you are chaste, indeed you please me," and similar to this; this is the allusion.

5123 - Al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Suwayd related to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Sulayman, from his maternal aunt Sakinah bint Hanzalah ibn Abd Allah ibn Hanzalah, who said: Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali entered upon me while I was in my waiting period, and said: "O daughter of Hanzalah, I am one whose kinship to the Messenger of God ﷺ is known, and the right of my grandfather over me, and my precedence in Islam." I said: "May God forgive you, O Abu Ja'far, do you propose to me during my waiting period, while you are one from whom knowledge is taken!" He said: "Or have you really done so! I only inform you of my kinship to the Messenger of God ﷺ and my station! The Messenger of God ﷺ entered upon Umm Salamah, and she was the widow of her cousin Abu Salamah, and when he died, the Messenger of God ﷺ kept mentioning to her his station with God while he was leaning upon his hand, until the mat left a mark on his hand from the strength of his leaning, and that was not a proposal." [[The report: 5123 - Abd al-Rahman ibn Sulayman ibn Abd Allah ibn Hanzalah, "Ghasil al-Mala'ikah" ibn Abi Amir al-Rahib, known as Ibn al-Ghasil, and he is the grandfather of his father, Hanzalah, whom the angels washed on the day of Uhud. Ibn Ma'in said: "There is nothing wrong with him," he would err and make mistakes; Ahmad said: reliable. He died in the year 171. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib. "Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali" is Muhammad al-Baqir ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib, and his son Ja'far al-Sadiq; he was among the jurists of Madinah and the chief of the Banu Hashim in his time, combining knowledge, jurisprudence, nobility, piety, trustworthiness and leadership, and he was fit for the caliphate; he is one of the twelve whom the Rafidah believe to be infallible, but there is no infallibility except for a prophet! He died in the year 114. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib and in Tarikh al-Islam by al-Dhahabi 4: 299. I have not found this report except in al-Baghawi in the margin of Tafsir Ibn Kathir 1: 567.]]

5124 - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abd Allah ibn Salih related to us, saying: al-Layth related to me, saying: Uqayl related to me, from Ibn Shihab: "There is no blame upon you for what you imply of your proposal to women," he said: There is no blame upon the one who implies a proposal to them before they are released from their waiting period, if they are concealed within themselves regarding that. [[Kanna al-shay fi sadrihi, wa akannahu, wa iktannahu: he hid it and concealed it.]]

5125 - Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Malik informed me, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Qasim, from his father, that he used to say regarding the words of God, may His remembrance be exalted: "There is no blame upon you for what you imply of your proposal to women": that a man says to a woman who is in the waiting period from the death of her husband: "Indeed you are noble to me, and I am eager for you, and God will drive good and provision to you," and similar speech.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The scholars of Arabic differed over the meaning of "al-khitbah" (proposal).

Some of them said: "Al-khitbah" is the mention, and "al-khutbah" is the sermon (tashahhud). [[This is the view of al-Akhfash; see also Tafsir al-Baghawi 1: 567.]]

It seems the speaker of this view interpreted the statement as: There is no blame upon you for what you mention of women in their presence. [[In the manuscript and the printed edition: "indahum" (in their presence), which is not sound; the correct reading is what I have established; see also Tafsir al-Baghawi 1: 567.]] The holder of this view claimed that he said: "Do not promise them secretly," because when He said: "There is no blame upon you," it was as if He said: mention them, but do not promise them in secret.

* *

Others among them said: "Khataba, khitbah and khutban." [[In the printed edition: "Others among them said: al-khitbah akhtub khutbah wa khutban," which is a corrupt construction containing an addition by a copyist. In the manuscript: "Others among them said: 'al-khutbah wa khutbah wa khutban'," which is also corrupt, and the correct reading is what I have established. If there is any deficiency or lacuna in al-Tabari's words, it is the explanation of this word, and the author of Asas al-Balaghah has clarified it, saying: "So-and-so yakhtubu a deed: he seeks it. And akhtabaka al-sayd, fa-rmihi: i.e. akthabaka and amkanaka. And akhtabaka al-amr, and it is an amr mukhtab: its meaning: I seek you... from 'talabtu ilayhi hajatan fa-atlubni'. And ma khatbuka: what is your matter that you seek. From it: hadha khatb yasir, and khatb jalil. He endures the calamities of time." Thus he has made clear what I quoted from al-Zamakhshari, that he intended to say: khataba al-amr yakhtubuhu khitbah and khutban, i.e. he sought it. Abu Ja'far did not fully treat the explanation of this word in Surah Taha, verse 95, and set out its explanation there.]] He said: And the words of God, may His remembrance be exalted: ﴿He said: What is your matter, O Samiri?﴾ [Surah Taha: 95], it is said that it is from this. He said: As for "al-khutbah," it is the thing proposed [by it], from their saying: [[This parenthetical addition is indispensable; it means: the speech proposed by it.]] "He gave a sermon (khataba) on the pulpit and delivered it (ikhtataba)."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: "Al-khitbah," in my view, is the "fi'lah" form from the speaker's saying: "Khataba fulan fulanah" (So-and-so proposed to so-and-so), like "al-jilsah" from "jalasa" (he sat) or "al-qa'dah" from "qa'ada" (he sat). [[He means that it is a verbal noun; see what preceded regarding the pattern "fi'lah" in the indexes of the Arabic topics in the earlier volumes, and see Ma'ani al-Qur'an by al-Farra' 1: 152, and Tafsir Abi Hayyan 2: 221.]]
The meaning of their saying "khataba fulan fulanah" is that he asked her for her hand in herself, and that is his need, from their saying: "ma khatbuka?" in the sense of: what is your need, and what is your matter?

* *

As for "al-ta'rid" (allusion), it is what occurs in the figurative speech by which the hearer understands what he would understand from the explicit statement. [[Lahn al-kalam: it is indication in speech without explicit statement; al-Tabari's expression in explaining this word is a fine expression, with no equal in the lexicographical books in explaining this term.]]

* *

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿or you conceal it within yourselves﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His words, may His remembrance be exalted, "or you conceal it within yourselves," He means: or you hide within yourselves and keep secret, from proposing to them, and resolving on marrying them while they are in their waiting period; there is no blame upon you in that either, so long as you do not resolve the marriage contract until the prescribed term reaches its end.

* *

It is said from this: "Akanna fulan hadha al-amr fi nafsihi, fa-huwa yukinnuhu ikanan" (So-and-so concealed this matter within himself, so he conceals it), and "kanahu," when he concealed it, "yukannuhu kannan wa kununan" (he conceals it), and "jalasa fi al-kunn" (he sat in shelter). It has not been heard "kannantuhu fi nafsi" (I concealed it in my self). [[The lexicographers mention that this was said, citing the words of Abu Qutaifah: "People may hide secrets, so I know them, and they do not attain, until death, my hidden thing."]] Rather, it is said "kanantuhu fi al-bayt aw fi al-ard" (I hid it in the house or in the ground), when you conceal it in it, and from it is His, may His remembrance be exalted, words: ﴿As if they were hidden eggs﴾ [Surah al-Saffat: 49], i.e. concealed; and from it is the words of the poet: [[I have not been able to identify who said it.]]

Three of the three feathered ones... of those that are hidden in the frost [[Ma'ani al-Farra' 1: 152, and al-Lisan (k-n-n). "Qadamiyat" is the plural of "qadama," and "al-qudama" is singular and plural, and here it is singular. "Al-qudama" and "al-qawadim" in birds are the ten feathers in each wing. His words "three of three qadamiyat" seem to mean that he chose three feathers from the primary feathers of a bird, three feathers from its plumage, apparently for his arrows, which he fletches with them. "Al-saqi'" is what falls at night, resembling snow.]]

And "takunn" with a "t" is the better, and "yakunn" [[In the printed edition: "bi-al-ta' huwa ajwad," and the waw is an addition from the manuscript. This sentence is not clear in meaning to me, and its correct form seems to be "wa-takunn bi-al-ta' al-madmummah, wa huwa ajwad wa takunn." It means that the first is from "akanna yukinnu," and the other is from "kanna yakunn," as is evident from his argument here. Al-Farra' commented on this verse, saying: "Some of them narrate it as 'takunn' from 'akננtu'." This supports what I have followed.]]. And it is said: "akannathu thiyabuhu min al-barad" (his garments sheltered him from the cold), and "akannahu al-bayt min al-rih" (the house sheltered him from the wind).

* *

The people of interpretation said what is similar to what we have said regarding this.

Those who said that:

5126 - Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "or you conceal it within yourselves," he said: The concealment is the mention of her proposal in one's self, without disclosing it to her. All of this is a known permissible matter.

5127 - Al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the like of it.

5128 - Musa related to me, saying: Amr related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi regarding His words: "or you conceal it within yourselves," he said: That he enters, greets and gives a gift if he wishes, without speaking anything.

5129 - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abd al-Wahhab al-Thaqafi related to us, saying: I heard Yahya ibn Sa'id say: Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Qasim informed me that he heard al-Qasim ibn Muhammad say, and he mentioned something similar.

5130 - Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words: "or you conceal it within yourselves," he said: You place her marriage within yourself and hold that concealed.

٥١٣١- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us. And ʿAli narrated to me, saying: Zayd narrated to us, both of them, from Sufyan: "Or you conceal it within yourselves" – that he feels secretly in himself that he would marry her.

٥١٣٢- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Hawdhah narrated to us, saying: ʿAwf narrated to us, from al-Hasan, regarding His words: "Or you conceal it within yourselves," he said: You kept it secret.
* *
Abu Jaʿfar said: In God's permission, may His remembrance be exalted, of what He permitted of allusion (taʿrid) to marrying a woman in her waiting period (ʿiddah) during her waiting period, and His prohibition of explicit statement (tasrih), [[His words "for her" relate to "allusion," meaning allusion directed to her. The context of this sentence and the one following it is: "In God's permission, may His remembrance be exalted... what distinguishes the divergence of the ruling on allusion." And His words "from it" in the following clause mean: the divergence of the ruling on allusion from the ruling on explicit statement.]] what distinguishes the divergence of the ruling on allusion in all meanings of speech from the ruling on explicit statement. When this is so, it becomes clear that allusion to slander (qadhf) is not the same as explicit slander, and that if the hadd punishment for allusion to slander were obligatory in the same way as for explicit slander, then the same sin would be incurred by allusion to betrothal during the waiting period as that incurred by resolving upon a marriage contract therein. And in God's distinguishing between the two rulings in this matter lies clear evidence that the rulings on this differ in the case of slander.
* *
The interpretation of His words: "God knows that you will remember them"
Abu Jaʿfar said: By this, may His remembrance be exalted, He means: God knows that you will mention the women in their waiting period through betrothal, in your hearts and with your tongues, as:

٥١٣٣- Ibn Wakiʿ narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Yazid ibn Ibrahim, from al-Hasan: "God knows that you will remember them," he said: It is the betrothal (khutbah).

٥١٣٤- Abu al-Sa'ib Salm ibn Janadah narrated to me, saying: Ibn Idris narrated to us, from Layth, from Mujahid regarding His words: "And there is no blame upon you for what you hint at of proposing to women," he said: Your remembering her in yourself. He said: That is the saying of God: "God knows that you will remember them."

٥١٣٥- Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Za'idah narrated to us, from Yazid ibn Ibrahim, from al-Hasan regarding His words: "God knows that you will remember them," he said: It is the betrothal.
* *
The interpretation of His words, may He be exalted: "But do not promise them in secret"
Abu Jaʿfar said: The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed regarding the meaning of "secret" (sirr) which God, exalted, forbade His servants from promising the women in their waiting period.

Some of them said: It is adultery (zina).
Those who said that:

٥١٣٦- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Hammam narrated to us, from Salih al-Dahhan, from Jabir ibn Zayd: "But do not promise them in secret," he said: Adultery. [[The narration 5136: "Salih al-Dahhan" is Salih ibn Ibrahim al-Dahhan al-Juhani, Abu Nuh. He is trustworthy (thiqah). He is biographed in al-Jarh wa-al-Ta'dil 2/1/393; see also al-Tahdhib 4: 388. Jabir ibn Zayd al-Azdi Abu al-Sha'tha' is biographed in al-Tahdhib, and narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas, Ibn ʿUmar and Ibn al-Zubayr. He died in the year 93.]]

٥١٣٧- Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, saying: al-Muʿtamir ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from his father, from Abu Mijlaz, his saying: "But do not promise them in secret," he said: Adultery.

٥١٣٨- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Yahya narrated to us, saying: Sulayman al-Taymi narrated to us, from Abu Mijlaz, the like of it.

٥١٣٩- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Sulayman al-Taymi, from Abu Mijlaz, the like of it.

٥١٤٠- al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Nuʿaym narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu Mijlaz: "But do not promise them in secret," he said: Adultery. It was said to Sufyan al-Taymi: Did he mention it? He said: Yes.

٥١٤١- Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, saying: al-Muʿtamir narrated to us, from his father, from a man, from al-Hasan regarding the promise, like the saying of Abu Mijlaz.

٥١٤٢- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, from al-Hasan, he said: Adultery.

٥١٤٣- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Yahya narrated to us, saying: Ashʿath and ʿImran narrated to us, from al-Hasan, the like of it.

٥١٤٤- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Rahman and Yahya narrated to us, both saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-Suddi, he said: I heard Ibrahim say: "Do not promise them in secret," he said: Adultery.

٥١٤٥- Ahmad ibn Hazim narrated to us, saying: Abu Nuʿaym narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-Suddi, from Ibrahim, the like of it.

٥١٤٦- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatadah regarding His words: "Do not promise them in secret," he said: Adultery.

٥١٤٧- Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Zaʿidah narrated to us, from Yazid ibn Ibrahim, from al-Hasan: "But do not promise them in secret," he said: Adultery.

٥١٤٨- al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Suwayd narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Maʿmar, from Qatadah, from al-Hasan regarding His words: "But do not promise them in secret," he said: The lewd act (fahishah).

٥١٤٩- al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abu Zuhayr narrated to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak; and Yahya ibn Abi Talib narrated to me, saying: Yazid ibn Harun informed us, saying: Juwaybir informed us, from al-Dahhak: "Do not promise them in secret," he said: The secret is adultery.

٥١٥٠- Muhammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas: "Do not promise them in secret," he said: That secret is suspicion (rība). [[In the printed edition: "al-zaniyah" in this place and the following one; the correct reading is from the manuscript. Al-rība (with a kasrah on the rāʾ): doubt, suspicion, accusation, and it is a metaphor for every ugly matter about which one is suspected, and about its companion.]] A man would enter upon her out of suspicion while alluding to marriage, so God forbade that, except for one who speaks what is honorable.

٥١٥١- al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Mansur informed us, from al-Hasan and Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak and Sulayman al-Taymi, from Abu Mijlaz, that they said: Adultery.

٥١٥٢- ʿAn ʿAmmar narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabiʿ, his saying: "But do not promise them in secret," for lewdness and softness of speech. [[Al-khudaʿ (with a fatha on the khāʾ and sukun): the verbal noun of khada'a al-rajul: he softened speech to a woman. It is vocalized in the manuscript with a damma on the khāʾ, but I have not found it so. "Khada'a" is of the pattern "nafaʿa," as stated by the author of Miʿyar al-Lughah. In the hadith of ʿUmar, a man in his time passed by a man and a woman who had spoken softly to each other, so he struck him until he wounded him; it was raised to ʿUmar, who annulled it, i.e., they softened their speech between them and spoke in a way that made each hope for the other. "Khada'a al-qawl" will also come in his tafsir 22: 3 (Bulaq), and will also come in the narration no. 5162.]]

٥١٥٣- al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Maʿmar informed us, from Qatadah, from al-Hasan: "But do not promise them in secret," he said: It is the lewd act.
* *
Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: do not take their pledges and covenants during their waiting period that they will not marry anyone other than you.
Those who said that:

٥١٥٤- al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: ʿAbd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Muʿawiyah ibn Salih narrated to me, from ʿAli ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn ʿAbbas: "Do not promise them in secret," meaning: Do not say to her: "I am in love with you, and pledge to me that you will not marry anyone but me," and the like of this.
