٥١٥٥- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Muslim al-Batin, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr regarding His words: "Do not promise them in secret," he said: He should not make a binding agreement with her on such and such, that she will not marry anyone other than him. [[In the printed edition: "la yuqasiha," and it is so in the manuscript undotted; the correct reading is what is given. Qadaha ʿalayhi al-amr: he decided it, sealed it, made it binding and completed it. In the treaty of al-Hudaybiyah: "This is what Muhammad made binding..." and it is similar to a covenant.]]

٥١٥٦- Ibn Wakiʿ narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Israʾil, from Jabir, from ʿAmir, and Mujahid and ʿIkrimah said: He should not take her pledge during her waiting period that she will not marry anyone other than him.

٥١٥٧- Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, saying: Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Mansur, who said: It was mentioned to me from al-Shaʿbi that he said regarding this verse: "Do not promise them in secret," he said: He should not take her pledge that she will not marry anyone other than you.

٥١٥٨- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us, from ʿAmr, from Mansur, from al-Shaʿbi: "But do not promise them in secret," he said: He should not take her pledge that she will not marry anyone other than him.

٥١٥٩- Yaʿqub narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Ismaʿil ibn Salim informed us, from al-Shaʿbi, who said: I heard him say regarding His words: "Do not promise them in secret," he said: He should not take her pledge that you will not marry anyone other than you, and he should not conclude the contract until the waiting period ends. [[In the printed edition: "wa-yakhudhu ʿalayha ʿahdan an la tankahi..." with the extra "an," and I have kept what is in the manuscript, which is the sound and good reading.]]

٥١٦٠- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mansur, from al-Shaʿbi: "Do not promise them in secret," he said: He should not take from her a pledge that she will not marry anyone other than him.

٥١٦١- Musa narrated to me, saying: ʿAmr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "But do not promise them in secret," meaning: "Keep yourself for me, for I will marry you" – and he takes from her a covenant: "Do not marry anyone other than me." [[In the printed edition: "wa-yakhudhu ʿalayha ʿahdan an la tankahi..." with the extra "an," and I have kept what is in the manuscript, which is the sound and good reading.]]

٥١٦٢- Bishr ibn Muʿadh narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Zurayʿ narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatadah: "But do not promise them in secret," he said: This is concerning a man who takes a woman's covenant while she is in her waiting period that she will not marry anyone other than him. God forbade that and gave precedence in it, and permitted betrothal and speech that is honorable, and forbade lewdness and softness of speech. [[See the comment on the previous narration: 5152.]]

٥١٦٣- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us; and ʿAli narrated to me, saying: Zayd narrated to us, both of them, from Sufyan: "But do not promise them in secret," he said: That you promise her secretly on such and such, "on condition that you will not marry anyone other than me."

٥١٦٤- al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Suwayd narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Maʿmar, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding His words: "Do not promise them in secret," he said: The promise of secrecy is that he takes from her a covenant and pledge that she will confine herself to him and not marry anyone else.

٥١٦٥- al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Maʿmar informed us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, with something similar.
* *
Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: that a man says to her: "Do not outpace me with yourself."
Those who said that:

٥١٦٦ - Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, from ʿIsa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding God's words: "But do not promise them in secret," he said: The saying of a man to a woman: "Do not escape me with yourself, for I will marry you" – this is not permissible.

٥١٦٧- al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: It is the saying of a man to a woman: "Do not escape me."

٥١٦٨- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Layth, from Mujahid: "But do not promise them in secret," he said: The promise is that he says: "Do not escape me with yourself."

٥١٦٩- al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Suwayd narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Sufyan, from Layth, from Mujahid: "But do not promise them in secret," that he says: "Do not escape me with yourself."
* *
Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: "And do not marry them secretly during their waiting period."
Those who said that:

٥١٧٠- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words: "But do not promise them in secret," he says: Do not marry them secretly, then keep her, until when her waiting period ends you announce that and bring her in.

٥١٧١- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words: "But promise them in secret," he said: My father used to say: "Do not promise them in secret," then you keep her, while you have already possessed the binding of her marriage contract; when her waiting period ends you announce that and bring her in.
* *
Abu Jaʿfar said: The most correct of the sayings regarding the interpretation of this is the interpretation of those who said that "secret," in this place, means adultery. This is because the Arabs call intercourse and a man's approach to a woman "secret" (sirr), since that is something that occurs between men and women in concealment, not visible or observed by others, so it is called "secret" because of its concealment. Among this is the verse of Ru'bah ibn al-ʿAjjaj:

Then he refrained from her secrets after persistent attachment,
and did not place her between hatred and love. [[His Diwan: 104; and al-Lisan (ʿ-s-q), (ʿ-sh-q), (f-r-k), (s-r-r). In some entries of al-Lisan it is "israri-ha" with a kasrah, which is an error; and in some it is "al-ghasaq," which is also an error. Al-asrar is the plural of sirr. Al-ʿasaq is the verbal noun of "ʿasaqa bihi yaʿsuqu": he adhered to it and was devoted to it. Al-faraku (with kasrah on the fāʾ and sukun on the rāʾ): a man's hatred of his wife, or a wife's hatred of her husband. A woman who is fāriq and farūq is one who dislikes her husband. A man who is mufarrak (with shaddah on the rāʾ) is one who is not favored by women. Al-ʿishq (with kasrah and sukun) and al-ʿashq (with two fatahs) are verbal nouns of "ʿashiqa yaʿshaqu." The pronoun in His words "fa-ʿaffa" refers to the wild ass that he describes and describes its female asses. The pronoun in "asrari-ha" refers to the female asses.]]
He means by it: he refrained from having intercourse with her after long persistence in that. From this is the saying of al-Hutay'ah:

And the secret of their neighbor is forbidden to them,
while their neighbor eats the tips of the bowls. [[His Diwan: 93; and al-Lisan (anf). He praises the Banu Riyah and the Banu Kulayb from the Banu Yarbu'. Anf (tip) of everything is its edge and beginning. Al-qisa' is the plural of qas'ah: a large bowl. He mentions their chastity, their guarding, and their refraining from violating the sanctity of the neighbor, and committing sin against her; and he describes their generosity and their preferring their neighbor with food over themselves, so they do not go ahead of him to the food until he takes from it what he desires and what suffices him. Before the verse: "So the neighbor is not the neighbor of the Banu Riyah / dismissed in the place, nor neglected."
"They prepared for their neighbor, and it is not / the hand of the clumsy woman like the hand of the craftsmen."]]

Likewise it is said of anything a person conceals within himself: "secret." And it is said: "He is in the secret of his people," meaning: among their best and most noble.

Since "secret" in its usage is directed to one of these three aspects, and it was known that none of them is intended by His words: "But do not promise them in secret," namely the secret that means the excellence and nobility, then only the other two remain: the "secret" in the sense of what the one promising conceals between the two promisers, and the "secret" in the sense of intercourse and copulation.

Since nothing else remains apart from these two, and the evidence is clear that one of them is not intended, it is correct that the other is the one intended.
* *
If someone says: What is the evidence that the secret promise of speech is not intended, according to what those said who held that the meaning is: a man taking a woman's pledge that she will not marry anyone other than him, or according to what those said: a man's saying to her: "Do not outpace me with yourself"?

It is said: Because "secret," if it has the meaning that those who interpreted it intended, then that secret must be either the man's promising the woman and his asking her that she not marry anyone other than him, or it is the marriage that he asked her to accept, after the end of her waiting period and after the contract is concluded with him, to the exclusion of others. If the "secret" that God forbade a man to promise the women in their waiting period is taking their pledge that they will not marry anyone other than him, then it has become invalid for "secret" to mean: what is concealed of matters within the souls, or what is spoken but not disclosed, while openness of the matter becomes a secret. And that is contrary to what is understood in the language of those to whose tongue the Qur'an was revealed.

Unless the one who makes this claim says: God only forbade men from promising them in secret between themselves and them, not that the speech itself, even if it is publicized, is a secret.

It is said to him: If he says that, then it should be permissible to promise them marriage and betrothal openly and publicly, since what is forbidden of promising is only what is done in secret.

If he says: That is so, he has departed from the consensus of the whole community. Moreover, that is not the saying of anyone among those who interpreted the verse that "secret" here means the covenant not to marry anyone other than the one covenanted with.

And if he says: That is not permissible.

It is said to him: Then it has become invalid that the meaning is: a man's whispering to a woman a promise. For if that were its meaning, it would not be forbidden for him to promise her openly and publicly. And the fact that this is forbidden to him both in secret and openly shows that the meaning of "secret" in this place is other than the man's whispering to the woman a covenant that she will not marry anyone other than him when her waiting period ends. Or, if this aspect is invalid, the meaning is: the betrothal and marriage that the woman promised the man she would not turn away from to another. That, if it is so, occurs with a guardian and witnesses publicly, not secretly. And how could it be called secret when it is public, and it is not permissible to keep it secret?

And in the invalidity of all these aspects, as an interpretation of His words: "But do not promise them in secret," according to the evidence we have indicated, the clear correctness of the interpretation that it means intercourse and copulation is established.

Given that this is correct, the meaning of the verse is: "There is no blame upon you, O people, for what you hint at to the women whose husbands have died, of proposing marriage to them, since you have need of them, when you do not openly declare to them the marriage and your need of them, if you conceal it within yourselves, keeping your need of them and your proposal to them secret within yourselves, for as long as they are in their waiting period ('iddah). God knew that you would mention a proposal to them while they were in their waiting period, so He permitted you to hint at that to them and removed blame for what your souls harbour, a judgement from Him [[In the printed edition: "ḥilman minhu" (a forbearance from Him), and I have adopted what is in the manuscript as more correct.]]. But He forbade you to make a promise to them of intercourse during their waiting period, by one of you saying to one of them during her 'iddah: 'I have decided to marry you in my heart, and I am only waiting for the end of your 'iddah,' whereby by that speech he asks her for the possibility of intercourse and sexual relations. God, exalted is His remembrance, forbade that."

* *

**On the interpretation of His words: ﴿Except that you say a fair word﴾**

Abu Ja'far said: Then He, exalted is His remembrance, said: "Except that you say a fair word." He made an exception of the fair speech from what was forbidden, namely a man's promise to a woman in secret. This is not of the same kind, but it is of the type of exception I mentioned before, where the exception comes with a meaning opposed to what precedes it in attribute only, and "illa" (except) carries the sense of "lakin" (but) [[See what has passed: 2:263–265, and then 3:204–206.]]. So His words "except that you say a fair word" mean: "but say a fair word." God, exalted is His remembrance, permitted one to say to her the fair speech during her 'iddah, and this is what He allowed by His words: "There is no blame upon you for what you hint at of proposing marriage to women," as:

5172 – Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Salamah ibn Kuhayl, from Muslim al-Batin, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, regarding "except that you say a fair word," he said: He says: "Indeed I am eager for you, and I hope that we will come together."

5173 – al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah ibn Salih narrated to me, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding "except that you say a fair word," he said: It is his saying: "If you see that you should not get ahead of me yourself."

5174 – al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Suwayd narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Sufyan, from Layth, from Mujahid, regarding "except that you say a fair word," he said: It means the allusion (ta'rid).

5175 – al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, regarding "except that you say a fair word," he said: It means the allusion.

5176 – Musa narrated to me, saying: 'Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding "there is no blame upon you for what you hint at of proposing marriage to women" up to "until the decreed term reaches its end," he said: It is the man who enters upon a woman who is in her 'iddah and says: "By God, you are equal (akfa') noble people, and you are an object of desire [[In the printed and manuscript texts: "la-ra'ah" (?) ; the manuscript is undotted and I have read it thus, because it is more fitting, and because I found no meaning for "ra'ah." He called the woman "raghbah" (object of desire), as he calls her "hawa" (love) by the verbal noun, meaning: he desires you. From it comes "al-raghibah," which is a thing desired.]], and you please me, and if something is decreed, it will be." This is the fair speech.

5177 – Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, and 'Ali narrated to me, saying: Zayd narrated to us, both of them together, Sufyan said regarding "except that you say a fair word," he said: He says: "Indeed I am eager for you, and I hope, God willing, that we will come together."

5178 – Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words "except that you say a fair word," he said: He says: "For you with me is such and such, and for you with me is such and such, and I will give you such and such." He said: All this, and whatever was before the conclusion of the marriage contract, all of it was abrogated (nasakha) by His words: "And do not resolve upon the marriage tie until the decreed term reaches its end."

5179 – Yahya ibn Abi Talib narrated to me, saying: Yazid informed us, saying: Juwaybir informed us, from al-Dahhak, regarding "except that you say a fair word," he said: The woman is divorced or her husband dies, and a man comes to her and says: "Hold yourself back for me, for I have a desire for you," and she says: "And I am like that," so his soul longs for her. That is the fair speech.

* *

**On the interpretation of His words: ﴿And do not resolve upon the marriage tie until the decreed term reaches its end﴾**

Abu Ja'far said: By His words, exalted is His remembrance, "and do not resolve upon the marriage tie," He means: do not validate the marriage tie during the waiting period of the woman in 'iddah, so as to make it binding between you and them, and conclude it before the end of the 'iddah. "Until the decreed term reaches its end" means: until they reach the term of the decree which God, exalted is His remembrance, specified by His words: ﴿Those of you who die and leave wives behind, they shall wait by themselves for four months and ten days﴾. So He made the reaching of the term to be for the decree, and the meaning is for those contracting the marriage: that a man should not marry a woman in 'iddah, nor resolve on the marriage tie with her, until her waiting period has ended, so that the term God specified in His Book reaches its completion, as:

5180 – Muhammad ibn Bashshar and 'Amr ibn 'Ali narrated to us, both saying: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us. And al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, from al-Thawri, from Layth, from Mujahid, regarding "until the decree reaches its term," he said: Until the 'iddah ends.

5181 – Musa narrated to me, saying: 'Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His words "until the decreed term reaches its end," he said: Until four months and ten days have passed.

5182 – Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words "until the decreed term reaches its end," he said: Until the 'iddah ends.

5183 – al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi', the same.

5184 – Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding "until the decreed term reaches its end," he said: The 'iddah ends.

5185 – al-Qasim narrated to me, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from 'Ata' al-Khurasani, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His words "and do not resolve upon the marriage tie until the decreed term reaches its end," he said: Until the 'iddah ends.

5186 – al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abu Zuhayr narrated to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak regarding His words: "until the decreed term reaches its end," he said: He shall not marry her until her term has expired. [[Khala al-shay' yakhlu khulwan: passed and ended.]]

5187 – 'Amr ibn 'Ali narrated to us, saying: Abu Qutaybah narrated to us, saying: Yunus ibn Abi Ishaq narrated to us, from al-Sha'bi regarding His words "and do not resolve upon the marriage tie until the decreed term reaches its end," he said: Fear that a woman might marry before the end of the 'iddah. [[The report 5187: "Abu Qutaybah" is Salm ibn Qutaybah al-Shu'ayri, Abu Qutaybah al-Khurasani. "Trustworthy, there is no harm in him, his narrations are written down." He died in the year 201. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib.]]

5188 – 'Amr ibn 'Ali narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: "and do not resolve upon the marriage tie until the decreed term reaches its end," until the 'iddah ends.

5189 – Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us [and 'Ali narrated to me, saying: Zayd narrated to us], both of them together, from Sufyan regarding His words "until the decreed term reaches its end," he said: Until the 'iddah ends.

* *

**On the interpretation of His words: ﴿And know that God knows what is in your souls, so beware of Him; and know that God is Forgiving, Forbearing﴾ (2:235)**

Abu Ja'far said: By this, exalted is His remembrance, He means: know, O people, that God knows what is in your souls of desire for them, of marrying them, and of other matters of yours, so beware of Him. That is: beware God and fear Him regarding your souls, lest you commit any of what He has forbidden you, such as resolving upon the marriage tie with them, or promising them secret intercourse during their waiting period, and other things He has forbidden you regarding them while they are in 'iddah, and in other matters. "And know that God is Forgiving" means: He is one who conceals the sins of His servants and covers them, regarding what men's souls hide of proposing marriage to women in 'iddah, and their remembering them during their waiting period, and other of their wrongdoings. His words "Forbearing" mean: He is one of patience who does not hasten to punish His servants for their sins.

* *

**On the interpretation of His words: ﴿There is no blame upon you if you divorce women as long as you have not touched them﴾**

Abu Ja'far said: By His words, exalted is His remembrance, "there is no blame upon you," He means: there is no sin (haraj) upon you if you divorce women [[See the interpretation of "al-junah" (blame) in what has passed: 3:230, 231; then 4:162, 566; then 5:71.]]. That is: there is no sin upon you in divorcing your women and your wives, "as long as you have not touched them" [[In the printed and manuscript texts the verse reads "tamassuhunna," and in the tafsir "tamasuhunna," and this is evidence that this was al-Tabari's reading in his original. As for the reading of the copyist of the manuscript, and our reading in this codex of ours, it is "tamassuhunna," and al-Tabari will mention the two readings.]], meaning: as long as you have not had intercourse with them.

* *

"Al-mumassah" (touching), in this context, is a euphemism for the term intercourse, as:

5190 – Humayd ibn Mas'adah narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Zuray' narrated to us [and Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us], both of them saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: Ibn 'Abbas said: "Al-mass" is intercourse, but God uses euphemism for what He wills by what He wills. [[In the printed edition: "ma yasha'u bi-ma yasha'" (what He wills by what He wills); I have adopted what is in the manuscript.]]

5191 – al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "Al-mass": marriage.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The reciters have differed concerning the reading of this. [[In the printed edition: "wa-qad ikhtalafat al-qira'" ; I have adopted what is in the manuscript. "Al-qara'ah" (with fatḥas) is the plural of qari' (reciter).]] The reading of the common reciters of Hijaz and Basra is "mā lam tamassūhunna" with the "ta" of "tamassūhunna" opened, without an alif, from your saying: "massastuhu amassuhu massan wa-masīsan wa-masīsā" (a short-vowelled, doubled, unpronounced form). It seems they chose this reading, joining it to the reading agreed upon in His words: ﴿And no human has touched me﴾ [Surah Al 'Imran: 47; Surah Maryam: 20].

* *

Others read it: "mā lam tamāsūhunna," with the "ta" and the alif after the "mim" vowelled with damma, joining it to the agreed reading in His words: ﴿So the freeing of a slave before they touch one another﴾ [Surah al-Mujadilah: 3], and they took this to mean the act of each of the man and the woman upon the other, from your saying: "māsastu al-shay' amāsuhu mamāsatan wa-msāsan" (I touched the thing, touching it).

* *

Abu Ja'far said: What we consider concerning this is that the two readings are both correct in meaning and agree in interpretation, even if one of them has an additional meaning, which does not necessitate any difference in ruling or understanding.

That is because no one of understanding would fail to grasp, when it is said: "I touched my wife," that the one touched has come into contact with the body of the toucher, as much as the toucher has come into contact with the body of the one touched. Each of them, even if the report is given about only one of them as the one who touched the other, is understood by that very report that his companion who was touched has also touched him. [[In the manuscript and printed editions: "mās ṣāḥibahu" (touched his companion), and the better is to say "massa ṣāḥibahu."]] [[In the manuscript: "fa-dhalika al-khabar nafsuhu," and in the printed edition: "kadhalika al-khabar..." and both are corrupt and deprived of meaning.]] So there is no basis for ruling in favour of one of the two readings, given that their meanings agree and that many reciters read each of them, to claim that one is more correct than the other. Rather, it is necessary that the reciter, with whichever of the two he recites, is correct in his reading. [[In the printed edition: "wa-kathrat al-qira'ah," which is corrupt; "al-qara'ah" is the plural of "qari'," as previously mentioned.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: God, exalted is His remembrance, only meant by His words: "There is no blame upon you if you divorce women as long as you have not touched them," the women divorced before intimacy with them, in a marriage in which a dowry had been named for them. We only say that this is so because every woman in marriage is one of two: either a dowry has been named for her, or no dowry has been named for her. We know from what follows it in His words, exalted is His remembrance, that the one intended by "There is no blame upon you if you divorce women as long as you have not touched them" is only the one for whom a dowry has been named. For if the one intended were one for whom no dowry had been set, then His words "or you have fixed for them an obligation" would have no comprehensible meaning, since there is no sense in a speaker's saying: "There is no blame upon you if you divorce women as long as you have not fixed for them an obligation in a marriage in which you have not touched them, or as long as you have not fixed for them an obligation." Since this has no meaning, it is evident that the sound interpretation of this is: There is no blame upon you if you divorce, from your women, those for whom a dowry has been fixed, before you touch them, and those for whom no obligation was fixed before the fixing.

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 2, Verse 236 (part 1 of 3)**

**On the interpretation of His words: ﴿or you specify for them an obligation﴾**

Abu Ja'far said: By His words "or you specify for them" He means: or you make obligatory for them. By "an obligation" He means: a required dower (*sadaq*).

As related by:

5192. Al-Muthanna related to me, he said: Abu Salih related to us, he said: Mu'awiyah related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding "or you specify for them an obligation," that he said: "The obligation is the dower."

* *

The root meaning of *al-fard* (obligation) is what is required, as the poet said:

*"What you gave was an obligation, just as*
*stoning was an obligation for adultery."* [[The verse is by al-Nabigha al-Ja'di. Its earlier sources and explanation appear in vol. 3, pp. 311–312, and vol. 4, p. 287.]]

That is: just as stoning was the required punishment for adultery. For this reason it is said, "The ruler imposed (*farada*) two thousand on so-and-so," meaning he made it obligatory for him and assigned him a stipend from the *diwan*. [[In the printed edition the text reads "...li-fulan alfayn" without *fi*; the correct reading is from the manuscript. Razaqa al-amir jundahu means he gave his troops their pay, which is the allotment he imposed on them. The *diwan* is the register in which the names of the army and of those entitled to allotments were recorded. The first to compile the *diwan* was 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him.]]

* *

On the interpretation of His words: ﴿And provide for them according to the means of the wealthy, according to his means, and according to the means of the poor, according to his means﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His words "and provide for them," He means: give them what they may enjoy from your wealth, according to your capacities and your situations, whether affluence or straitened means. [[On the meaning of *al-mata'* (provision), see earlier vol. 1, pp. 539–540, and vol. 3, pp. 53–55.]]

* *

Then the interpreters differed about the extent of what Allah commanded men to give in this matter.

Some of them said: The highest level is a servant, below that silver, and below that clothing.

Those who said this:

5193. Ibn Bashshar related to us, he said: Mu'ammal related to us, he said: Sufyan related to us, from Isma'il, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "The provision for divorce: the highest is a servant, below that silver, and below that clothing."

5194. Ahmad ibn Ishaq related to us, he said: Sufyan related to us, from Isma'il ibn Umayya, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, similarly.

5195. Ahmad related to us, he said: Abu Ahmad related to us, he said: Sufyan related to us, from Dawud, from al-Sha'bi, his statement regarding "and provide for them according to the means of the wealthy, according to his means, and according to the means of the poor, according to his means." I asked him: What is the middle provision for a divorced woman? He said: Her head-covering, her shift, her outer garment, and her wrapper.

5196. Al-Muthanna related to me, he said: Abu Salih related to us, he said: Mu'awiyah related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, his statement: "And provide for them according to the means of the wealthy, according to his means, and according to the means of the poor, according to his means, a provision in kindness, a duty upon the good-doers." This concerns a man who marries a woman without naming a dower for her, then divorces her before consummating the marriage. Allah, glorified is He, commanded that he provide for her according to his hardship and his ease. If he is wealthy, he provides her with a servant or something similar; if he is poor, he provides her with three garments or something similar.

5197. Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim related to me, he said: Ibn Ulayya related to us, from Dawud, from al-Sha'bi, regarding His words "and provide for them according to the means of the wealthy, according to his means, and according to the means of the poor, according to his means." He said: I asked al-Sha'bi: What is the middle of that? He said: Clothing her in her house: her shift, her head-covering, her wrapper, and her outer garment.

Al-Sha'bi said: Shurayh used to provide five hundred.

5198. Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, he said: Abd al-Wahhab related to us, he said: Dawud related to us, from Amir, that Shurayh used to provide five hundred. I asked Amir: What is the middle of that? He said: Her garments in her house: a shift, a head-covering, a wrapper, and an outer garment.

5199. Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, he said: Ibn Abi Adi related to us, from Dawud, from Amir al-Sha'bi, that he said: The middle of the provision is a woman's garments in her house: a shift, a head-covering, a wrapper, and an outer garment.

5200. Imran ibn Musa related to us, he said: Abd al-Warith related to us, he said: Dawud related to us, from al-Sha'bi, that Shurayh provided five hundred. And al-Sha'bi said: The middle of the provision is a shift, a head-covering, an outer garment, and a wrapper.

5201. Al-Muthanna related to me, he said: Ishaq related to us, he said: Ibn Abi Ja'far related to us, from his father, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, regarding His words: "There is no blame upon you if you divorce women as long as you have not touched them or specified for them an obligation, and provide for them according to the means of the wealthy, according to his means, and according to the means of the poor, according to his means, a provision in kindness, a duty upon the good-doers." He said: This concerns a man who marries a woman without naming a dower for her, then divorces her before he has consummated the marriage. For her there is a provision in kindness, and she has no dower. He said: The least of that is three garments: a shift, a head-covering, an outer garment, and a wrapper.

5202. Bishr ibn Mu'adh related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding "There is no blame upon you if you divorce women as long as you have not touched them," until "a duty upon the good-doers." This concerns the man who marries a woman without naming a dower for her, then divorces her before consummating the marriage. For her there is a provision in kindness, and she has no obligation (*fari'ah*). It used to be said: If he is able (*wajid*), there must be a waist-wrap, an outer garment, a shift, and a head-covering. [[*Al-wajid* means one who is capable, who finds what he can pay his debt with or something similar.]]

5203. Abu Kurayb related to us, he said: Ibn Abi Za'ida related to us, from Salih ibn Salih, who said: Amir was asked: How much should a man provide for his wife? He said: According to his wealth.

5204. Ali ibn Sahl related to me, he said: Mu'ammal related to us, he said: Shu'ba related to us, from Sa'd ibn Ibrahim, who said: I heard Humayd ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf narrating from his mother, who said: "It is as if I am looking at a black slave-girl whom Abd al-Rahman (ibn Awf) gave tahmim (provision) to, when he divorced her, the mother of Abu Salama." [[In the printed edition it reads "Abd al-Rahman ibn Umm Salama," which is a gross confusion; the correct reading is from the manuscript. Abu Salama is Abd Allah al-Asghar ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, and his mother was Tamadir bint al-Asbagh ibn Amr al-Kalbiyya, the first Kalbiyya married by a Qurashi man. The full siblings of Abu Salama through their mother Tamadir were Ahih, Khalid, and Maryam, the sons of Khalid ibn Uqba ibn Abi Mu'ayt. She was married after Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf to another husband. The Arabs called provision *al-tahmim*. The verb *hammamaha* takes two objects because it carries the sense of giving her it.]]

It was said to Shu'ba: What is *hammamaha*? He said: He provided for her.

[Note on the chain: Sa'd ibn Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf al-Zuhri saw Ibn Umar and related from his father and his two paternal uncles, Humayd and Abu Salama. He died in the year 127 AH and is biographed in *al-Tahdhib*. The mother of Humayd ibn Abd al-Rahman is Umm Kulthum bint Uqba ibn Abi Mu'ayt al-Umawiyya, the full sister of Uthman ibn Affan. She embraced Islam early, pledged allegiance, and was prevented from emigrating until she emigrated in the seventh year during the truce. She bore Humayd and Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Rahman to Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, and both narrated from her. She is biographed in *al-Tahdhib* and elsewhere.]

5205. Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far related to us, he said: Shu'ba related to us, from Sa'd ibn Ibrahim, from Humayd ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, from his mother, similarly, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf.

5206. Al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, he said: Ma'mar informed us, from Ayyub, from Ibn Sirin, who said: He used to provide a servant, or a maintenance allowance, or clothing. He said: And al-Hasan ibn Ali provided (his wife) with ten thousand, I think he said.

5207. Al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, he said: Ma'mar informed us, from Ayyub, from Sa'd ibn Ibrahim, that Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf divorced his wife and provided her with a servant.

5208. It was related to me from Abd Allah ibn Yazid al-Muqri, from Sa'id ibn Abi Ayyub, who said: Uqayl related to me, from Ibn Shihab, that he used to say regarding the provision for a divorced woman: the highest is a servant, and the lowest is clothing and maintenance. He held that this is according to what Allah, mentioned is He, said: "according to the means of the wealthy, according to his means, and according to the means of the poor, according to his means."

* *

Others said: The amount, if the husband and the wife disagree about it, is half the dower of a woman of her equivalent standing, when she was married without a named dower in the contract. This is the view of Abu Hanifa and his companions.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct view on this matter is what Ibn Abbas said, and whoever holds his view: that what is obligatory from this for a divorced woman upon her husband is according to his hardship and his ease, as Allah, mentioned is He, said, "according to the means of the wealthy, according to his means, and according to the means of the poor, according to his means," not according to the woman's standing. If it were obligatory for the woman according to her equivalent dower, up to half of it, then His words, "according to the means of the wealthy, according to his means, and according to the means of the poor, according to his means," would have no understandable meaning. The speech would have been: "and provide for them according to their standing, and according to half the dowers of their equivalents."

In Allah's informing His servants that this is according to the man's situation in hardship and ease, and not according to her situation and half the dower of her equivalent, there is evidence for the soundness of what we have said and the falsity of what opposes it. The woman's equivalent dower may be a great sum of money, while the man at the time of divorcing her is poor and owns nothing. If he were judged to pay half of her equivalent dower, he would be required to pay what even someone well-off would find hard, so how about one whose means are restricted? [[*Al-maqdur 'alayh* means one whose provision is restricted. *Qudira 'alayhi rizquhu* (in the passive) means his provision was constricted.]] If that were done to him, the judge who rules so would have transgressed the ruling of Allah's words, "according to the means of the wealthy, according to his means, and according to the means of the poor, according to his means." Rather, it is according to the man's hardship and ease. If the husband is wealthy, the provision does not exceed a servant or its value. If he is poor, and he is able to give her the least clothing, which is three garments or something like that, he is judged to provide that. If he is incapable of that, then according to his capacity. This depends on the discretion of the just ruler when the matter is brought before him in dispute.

* *

The interpreters differed about the meaning of His words "and provide for them": is it obligatory, or recommended?

Some said: It is obligatory, and the provision is judged from the divorcing man's property, just as he is judged to pay all other debts owed by him to others. They said: It is obligatory upon him for every divorced woman, whoever she may be among his wives.

Those who said this:

5209. Bishr ibn Mu'adh related to us, he said: Yazid ibn Zurayʻ related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, who said: Al-Hasan and Abu al-Aliya used to say: "For every divorced woman there is a provision, whether he consummated the marriage with her or not, even if a dower was set for her."

5210. Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim related to me, he said: Ibn Ulayya related to us, from Yunus, that al-Hasan used to say: "For every divorced woman there is a provision, and for the one he divorced before consummation and for whom no dower was set."

5211. Ibn Bashshar related to us, he said: Abd al-Wahhab related to us, he said: Ayyub related to us, from Sa'id, from Jubayr, regarding this verse: "And for divorced women there is a provision in kindness, a duty upon the God-fearing" [Surah al-Baqara 2:241]. He said: "Every divorced woman has a provision in kindness, a duty upon the God-fearing."

5212. Ya'qub related to me, he said: Ibn Ulayya related to us, from Ayyub, who said: I heard Sa'id ibn Jubayr say: "For every divorced woman there is a provision."

5213. Al-Muthanna related to me, he said: Ishaq related to us, he said: Ibn Abi Ja'far related to us, from his father, from al-Rabi', who said: Abu al-Aliya used to say: "For every divorced woman there is a provision." And al-Hasan used to say: "For every divorced woman there is a provision."

5214. Ibn Bashshar related to us, he said: Abu Amir related to us, he said: Qurra related to us, who said: al-Hasan was asked about a man who divorced his wife before consummating the marriage, and a dower had been set for her: Does she have a provision? Al-Hasan said: "Yes, by Allah!" Then it was said to the questioner, who was Abu Bakr al-Hudhali: "Do you not recite this verse: 'And if you divorce them before you have touched them, and you have already specified for them an obligation, then half of what you specified' [Surah al-Baqara 2:237]?" He said: "Yes, by Allah!"

* *

Others said: The provision for a divorced woman upon her husband who divorced her is obligatory, but it is obligatory for every divorced woman other than the divorced woman for whom a dower was specified. As for the divorced woman for whom a dower was specified, if she is divorced before consummation, she has no provision, but only half of the named dower.

Those who said this:

5215. Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, he said: Abd al-Wahhab related to us, he said: Ubayd Allah related to us, from Nafi', that Ibn Umar used to say: "For every divorced woman there is a provision, except the one he divorced without consummating the marriage, for whom a dower was specified. For her is half the dower, and she has no provision."

5216. Tamim ibn al-Muntasir related to us, he said: Abd Allah ibn Numayr informed us, from Ubayd Allah, from Nafi', from Ibn Umar, similarly.

5217. Muhammad ibn Bashshar related to us, he said: Ibn Abi Adi and Abd al-A'la related to us, from Sa'id, from Qatadah, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, regarding a man who divorces his wife after a dower was specified for her, that he said concerning the provision: "She had a provision in the verse in al-Ahzab. [[The verse of *Surat al-Ahzab* will come shortly in report no. 5220.]] When the verse in al-Baqara was revealed, half of her dower was made hers if it was named, and she has no provision. If it was not named, she has the provision."

5218. Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, he said: Ibn Abi Adi and Abd al-A'la related to us, from Sa'id, from Qatadah, from Sa'id, similarly.

5219. Bishr ibn Mu'adh related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, who said: Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab used to say: "If he has not consummated the marriage, a provision was prescribed for her in Surat al-Ahzab. Then the verse in Surat al-Baqara was revealed: 'And if you divorce them before you have touched them, and you have already specified for them an obligation, then half of what you specified,' and this verse abrogated what came before it, if he had not consummated the marriage and had named a dower for her. For her is half, and she has no provision."

5220. Ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Bashshar related to us, both said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far related to us, he said: Shu'ba related to us, from Qatadah, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, who said: "This verse abrogated: 'O you who have believed, when you marry believing women and then divorce them before you have touched them, you have no waiting period for them to count, so provide for them' [Surat al-Ahzab 33:49], the verse in al-Baqara."

5221. Ibn Bashshar and Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, both said: Abd al-Rahman related to us, he said: Sufyan related to us, from Humayd, from Mujahid, who said: "For every divorced woman there is a provision, except the one he separated from before consummating the marriage, for whom a dower was specified."

5222. Ibn Bashshar related to us, he said: Abd al-Rahman related to us, he said: Sufyan related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the woman whose husband separates from her before consummating the marriage, when a dower was specified for her: he said: "She has no provision."

5223. Ya'qub related to me, he said: Ibn Ulayya related to us, he said: Ayyub related to us, from Nafi', who said: "If a man marries a woman and a dower has been specified for her, then he divorces her before consummating the marriage, she has half the dower and no provision. If no dower was specified for her, then she has only the provision."

5224. Ya'qub related to us, he said: Ibn Ulayya related to us, he said: Ibn Abi Najih was asked while I was listening: About a man who marries and then divorces her before consummating, when a dower was specified for her: does she have a provision? He said: "Ata used to say: She has no provision."

5225. Al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, he said: Ma'mar informed us, from Ayyub, from Nafi', from Ibn Umar, regarding a woman for whom a dower was specified and who was not consummated: he said: "If she is divorced, she has half the dower and no provision."

5226. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna related to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far related to us, he said: Shu'ba related to us, from al-Hakam, from Ibrahim, that Shurayh used to say, regarding a man who divorces his wife before consummating the marriage, when he had named a dower for her: "She has a provision on the half."

5227. Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, he said: Abd al-Rahman related to us, from Shu'ba, from al-Hakam, from Ibrahim, from Shurayh, who said: "She has a provision on the half."

* *

Others said: The provision is a right of every divorced woman, but some of it is judged against the divorcing husband, and some is not judged against him, though it is incumbent upon him before Allah to give it.

Those who said this:

5228. Al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, he said: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: "There are two provisions: one is judged by the ruler, and the other is a right upon the God-fearing. Whoever divorces before a dower has been set and before consummation, he is judged to pay the provision, since there is no dower upon him. Whoever divorces after consummation or after a dower has been set, the provision is a right."

5229. Al-Muthanna related to me, he said: Abu Salih related to us, he said: al-Layth related to me, from Yunus, from Ibn Shihab, who said: Allah said: "There is no blame upon you if you divorce women as long as you have not touched them or specified for them an obligation, and provide for them according to the means of the wealthy, according to his means, and according to the means of the poor, according to his means, a provision in kindness, a duty upon the good-doers." So when a man marries a woman and no dower was set for her, then he divorces her before touching her and before a dower was set, there is upon him only a provision in kindness, which the ruler sets for her according to a measure. She has no waiting period. And Allah, mentioned is He, said: "And if you divorce them before you have touched them, and you have already specified for them an obligation, then half of what you specified." So when a man divorces a woman for whom a dower was set and he has not touched her, she has half her dower, and she has no waiting period.

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 236 (part 2 of 3):**

5230. Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahim al-Barqi narrated to me, saying: Amr ibn Abi Salamah narrated to us, saying: Zuhayr informed us, from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri, that he said: "There are two kinds of *mut'ah* (provision). One of them is ordered by the ruler, and the other is not ordered by the ruler. The *mut'ah* that the ruler orders is a right incumbent upon the good-doers (al-muhsinin), and the *mut'ah* that the ruler does not order is a right incumbent upon the God-fearing (al-muttaqin)."

[[Hadith 5230. Amr ibn Abi Salamah al-Tinnisi Abu Hafs al-Dimashqi, whose biography is in *al-Tahdhib*. "Zuhayr" is Zuhayr ibn Muhammad al-Tamimi, whose biography is also in *al-Tahdhib*. Ahmad said of Amr ibn Abi Salamah: "He narrated from Zuhayr hadiths that are fabrications; it seems he heard them from Sadaqah ibn Abd Allah, then confused them and attributed them to Zuhayr." Both of them have been criticized.]]

* *

Others said: The judge (al-hakim) and the ruler (al-sultan) do not order any of that for the divorced woman. Rather, it is from God, may His remembrance be exalted, a recommendation and guidance that the divorced woman be given *mut'ah*.

Mention of those who said this:

5231. Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from al-Hakam: A man divorced his wife, and she brought a lawsuit against him before Shurayh. He recited the verse: ﴿And for divorced women is a provision in kindness, a right upon the God-fearing﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 241], and said: "If you are one of the God-fearing, then the *mut'ah* is incumbent upon you." And he did not rule in her favour. Shu'bah said: "I found it written down for me from Abu al-Duha."

5232. Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, from Ayyub, from Muhammad, who said: Shurayh used to say concerning the provision of the divorced woman: "Do not refuse to be among the good-doers; do not refuse to be among the God-fearing."

5233. Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, that Shurayh said to the man who had consummated the marriage with her: "If you are among the God-fearing, then provide for her."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: It seems that those who hold this view, in their refusal to make the *mut'ah* an obligation (fard) for divorced women, went by the saying of God, may His remembrance be exalted, ﴿a right upon the good-doers﴾ and His saying ﴿a right upon the God-fearing﴾, as an indication that if it were obligatory in the manner of binding rights over property in every case, then the God-fearing and the good-doers would not have been singled out as those upon whom it is a right, to the exclusion of others; rather, that would be known to be binding upon every person.

As for those who make it obligatory upon everyone other than the divorced woman for whom a dowry (sadaq) has been fixed, they argued that when God, may His remembrance be exalted, said ﴿And for divorced women is a provision in kindness, a right upon the God-fearing﴾, this was an indication that every divorced woman has a provision other than those whom God, may His remembrance be exalted, has specified in His Book or upon the tongue of His Messenger ﷺ. Then, when He said ﴿And if you divorce them before you have touched them, and you have already fixed for them a portion, then half of what you have fixed﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 237], this was, in their view, evidence that her right is half of what was fixed for her, since the *mut'ah* in the preceding verse, according to them, was assigned to the woman for whom no portion had been fixed. Thus it was known to them, by God's specifying the *mut'ah* for the woman for whom no portion was fixed, that her ruling is different from the ruling for the woman for whom no portion was fixed when he divorces her before consummation (al-masis) [[al-Masis: touching, the verbal noun of "massa", as already mentioned above, p. 118]], concerning the rights she has over the husband.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The view that is closest to correct in my opinion is the view of those who say: "Every divorced woman has a *mut'ah*." Because God, may His remembrance be exalted, said ﴿And for divorced women is a provision in kindness, a right upon the God-fearing﴾, and He made that a provision for every divorced woman, without specifying some of them over others. So no one may turn the apparent meaning of a general revelation into a specific hidden meaning, except by a proof that must be accepted.

[[At this point the old division ends, from which our manuscript was copied, and after it the manuscript reads: "And may God bless Muhammad, his family and companions abundantly." Then the following begins: "In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate."]]

* *

If someone says: God, may His remembrance be exalted, has specified the divorced woman before consummation, for whom a portion has been fixed, by His saying: ﴿And if you divorce them before you have touched them, and you have already fixed for them a portion, then half of what you have fixed﴾, since He did not make for her anything other than half of the portion?

It is said: When God, may His remembrance be exalted, indicates the obligation of something in one part of His revelation, then His indication of its obligation in the place where it is indicated suffices, so there is no need to repeat it, unless He indicates that its obligation is to be abrogated. He has indicated, by His saying ﴿And for divorced women is a provision in kindness﴾, the obligation of *mut'ah* for every divorced woman, so there is no need for His servants to repeat that in every verse and surah. And His indication that the divorced woman before consummation for whom a dowry has been fixed has half of what was fixed for her does not indicate that the *mut'ah* is cancelled in her case. For it is not impossible in speech to say: ﴿And if you divorce them before you have touched them [[In the manuscript: "tamassuhunna", and we have already pointed out above, p. 118, n. 1, that this is the reading of Abu Ja'far, and that it was written thus in his original.]] and you have already fixed for them a portion, then half of what you have fixed﴾ and the *mut'ah*. [[That is: by conjoining "and the *mut'ah*" to his saying "then half of what you have fixed".]] Since that is not impossible in speech, it is known that when half of the portion becomes due to her, its being due to her does not negate her right to *mut'ah*. And since it is not impossible for the divorced woman to have both, and since God, may His remembrance be exalted, has indicated that this is due to her, even though the indication of the obligation of one of them is in a verse other than the verse indicating the obligation of the other, both are established and confirmed as due to her.

This is if there is no indication, other than the saying of God, may His remembrance be exalted, ﴿And for divorced women is a provision in kindness﴾, that the divorced woman for whom a dowry has been fixed, if divorced before consummation, has a claim [[In the printed edition: "li-l-mutallaqah al-mafrud al-sadaq", with "lahā" omitted; the correct reading is from the manuscript.]]. But how, when in the saying of God, may His remembrance be exalted, ﴿There is no blame upon you if you divorce women as long as you have not touched them or fixed for them a portion; and provide for them﴾, there is clear evidence that the woman for whom a portion has been fixed, if divorced before consummation, has from the *mut'ah* the same as what the woman for whom no portion has been fixed has? That is because when God, may His remembrance be exalted, said ﴿There is no blame upon you if you divorce women as long as you have not touched them or fixed for them a portion﴾, it was known from that that He indicated the ruling for two categories of divorce of women: one for whom a portion has been fixed, and the other for whom no portion has been fixed. For when He said ﴿or fixed for them a portion﴾, it was known that the other category is the one for whom a portion has been fixed, and that she is the divorced woman for whom a portion has been fixed before consummation. For He said ﴿There is no blame upon you if you divorce women as long as you have not touched them﴾, and then He, may His remembrance be exalted, said ﴿and provide for them﴾, so He made *mut'ah* obligatory for both categories of them, those for whom a portion has been fixed and those for whom none has been fixed. Whoever claims that this applies to only one of the two categories should be asked for proof of his claim from a principle or a parallel, and then the argument should be reversed against him. He will not say anything about any part of this except that the same will be imposed on him in the other.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: I see that the *mut'ah* for the woman is a due and obligatory right when she is divorced, upon her husband who divorces her, in accordance with what we have explained above. The husband is held to it just as he is held to her dowry, and he is not released from it except by paying it to her or to the one who stands in her place in receiving it from him, or by a discharge (bara'ah) that she gives him. And I see that her way is the way of her dowry and all her other debts owed to him: he may be imprisoned for them if he divorces her and has no apparent property that can be sold against him when he refuses to give her that.

We say this because God, may His remembrance be exalted, said ﴿and provide for them﴾. So He commanded men to provide for them, and His command is obligatory, unless God, may His remembrance be exalted, makes clear that He meant by it recommendation and guidance, as we have explained in our book called *Latif al-Bayan 'an Usul al-Ahkam* (Subtle Explanation Concerning the Principles of Rulings), based on His saying ﴿And for divorced women is a provision in kindness﴾. There is no disagreement among all the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) that the meaning of that is: "And for divorced women, upon their husbands, is a provision in kindness." And if that is so, then the husband will not be released from what is due to her from him except by what we have described before: payment or discharge, as we have explained.

* *

If someone of little understanding thinks that God, may His remembrance be exalted, when He said ﴿a right upon the good-doers﴾ and ﴿a right upon the God-fearing﴾, meant that it is not obligatory, because if it were obligatory it would be upon the good-doer and the non-good-doer, the God-fearing and the non-God-fearing: God, may His remembrance be exalted, has commanded all His creatures to be among the good-doers and among the God-fearing; and whatever right is binding upon the people of goodness and piety is even more binding upon others, and more compulsory upon them.

Furthermore, the consensus of the authoritative (al-hujjah) that the *mut'ah* for the divorced woman for whom no portion was fixed before consummation is obligatory, by His saying ﴿and provide for them﴾, is [an argument for] the obligation of half the dowry for the divorced woman for whom a portion was fixed before consummation, by the saying of God, may His remembrance be exalted [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "the obligation of half the dowry for the divorced woman for whom a portion was fixed before consummation, God, may His remembrance be exalted, said concerning what He made obligatory for her of that. . . ". I have long dwelt on this phrase, and no meaning became clear to me from it, and I did not think it right to leave it without explaining its corruption and establishing the correctness of what I have seen. Al-Tabari's intention in the course of this final argument that he began in this paragraph is to complete his proof in refuting the view of one who thought that the *mut'ah* is not obligatory, based on the saying of God, may He be exalted, ﴿a right upon the good-doers﴾ and ﴿a right upon the God-fearing﴾. He said: God's saying ﴿and provide for them﴾ has made *mut'ah* obligatory for the divorced woman for whom no portion was fixed before consummation, just as His saying ﴿then half of what you have fixed﴾ made half the dowry obligatory for the divorced woman for whom a portion was fixed before consummation, and this is the verse in which neither ﴿a right upon the good-doers﴾ nor ﴿a right upon the God-fearing﴾ is mentioned. So in the consensus of the authoritative that this is due to both of them, there is the clear proof that His saying ﴿And for divorced women is a provision in kindness﴾ makes *mut'ah* obligatory for every divorced woman, even though He said ﴿a right upon the God-fearing﴾ right after this verse. Then he explained this argument clearly in the following paragraph, saying that their consensus on making *mut'ah* obligatory for the divorced woman for whom no portion was fixed, by His saying ﴿and provide for them﴾, together with the following of that in the verse, ﴿a right upon the good-doers﴾, is evidence that it is so in His saying ﴿And for divorced women is a provision in kindness﴾, together with its following ﴿a right upon the God-fearing﴾; so the *mut'ah* is obligatory for every divorced woman, as it was obligatory in the other verse. Because of this context that I have explained, I judged that the text of the manuscript and the printed edition is corrupt and does not convey a meaning. So this required me to change "qala Allah ta'ala dhikruhu" ("God, may His remembrance be exalted, said") to "bi-qawl Allah ta'ala dhikruhu" ("by the saying of God, may His remembrance be exalted"), to add after it "then half of what you have fixed", and to change "fima awjaba laha" ("concerning what He made obligatory for her") to "fima awjaba lahuma" ("concerning what He made obligatory for both of them") in the dual. This is what appeared correct to me, was established and confirmed; and praise be to God first and last. It is probably the correct reading in al-Tabari's original, God willing.]] concerning what He made obligatory for both of them of that = [[His saying "the clear proof" is the subject of "inna" in his saying at the beginning of the paragraph: "for in the consensus of the authoritative. . . "]] the clear proof that this is a due and obligatory right for every divorced woman by His saying ﴿And for divorced women is a provision in kindness﴾, even though He said ﴿a right upon the God-fearing﴾.

As for whoever denies what we have said on this point, he should be asked about the *mut'ah* for the divorced woman for whom no portion was fixed before consummation. If he denies that this is obligatory, he has departed from the consensus of all the authoritative, and we should debate with the deniers as we debate on the zakat of twenty dinars, and with those who withhold zakat on trade goods when they are held for trade, and similar matters. [[This means: what is established by consensus, such as their consensus on the obligation of zakat on twenty dinars and the obligation of zakat on trade goods when they are held for trade; he is to be argued with regarding *mut'ah* in the same way that the denier and withholder of zakat on those two things is argued with.]] If he makes it obligatory for her, he should be asked to explain the difference between its being obligatory for her and its being obligatory for every divorced woman, when he has already conditioned what is given to her from that as a right upon the good-doers, just as he conditioned what is given to the other as a right upon the God-fearing. He will not say anything about one of them except that the same will be imposed on him regarding the other.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The entire community agrees that the divorced woman for whom no portion was fixed before consummation has nothing due to her from her divorcing husband except *mut'ah*.

Mention of some of those who said this from among the Companions and the Successors, may God be pleased with them:

5234. Abu Kurayb and Yunus ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, both saying: Ibn Uyaynah narrated to us, from Amr ibn Dinar, from Ata', from Ibn Abbas, who said: "If a man divorces his wife before a portion has been fixed for her and before he has consummated with her, then she has nothing except provision."

5235. Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, from Yunus, who said: al-Hasan said: "If a man divorces his wife, has not consummated with her, and has not fixed a portion for her, then she has nothing except provision."

5236. Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, saying: Ayyub informed us, from Nafi', who said: "If a man marries a woman and then divorces her without fixing a portion for her, then she has only provision."

5237. al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: al-Layth narrated to me, from Yunus, from Ibn Shihab (al-Zuhri), who said: "If a man marries a woman without fixing a portion for her, then divorces her before he has touched her and before he has fixed a portion for her, then she has nothing due to her from him except reasonable provision (mata' bi-l-ma'ruf)."

5238. Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, from Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning the saying of God: ﴿There is no blame upon you if you divorce women as long as you have not touched them or fixed for them a portion﴾, he said: "She has no dowry except reasonable provision."

5239. al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, similarly, except that he said: "And no provision except in kindness."

5240. Musa narrated to me, saying: Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿There is no blame upon you if you divorce women as long as you have not touched them﴾ up to ﴿and provide for them﴾. He said: "This is a man to whom a woman has been given (tuhab) [in marriage without dowry], and who divorces her before consummating with her; for him the obligation is only *mut'ah*."

5241. Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, who said concerning this verse: "It is the man who marries a woman and does not name a dowry for her, then divorces her before consummating with her. For her there is reasonable provision, and no obligatory portion (fari'dah) for her."

5242. al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi', the like of it.

5243. Narrated to us by al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say [Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us, who said]: I heard al-Dahhak say concerning His saying ﴿as long as you have not touched them or fixed for them a portion﴾: "This is a man to whom his wife has been given (wahabat lahu), and he divorces her before touching her. For her there is *mut'ah*, and no obligatory portion for her, and she has no waiting period ('iddah)."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: As for *al-muwassi'* (the affluent), he is the one whose livelihood has come to abundance and wealth. It is said of him: "Awsa'a fulan, fa-huwa yuwsi'u ii-sa'an, wa-huwa muwassi'" ("so-and-so became affluent, so he makes affluent, and he is affluent").

* *

As for *al-muqtir* (the straitened), he is the one who has little wealth. It is said: "Qad aqtara, fa-huwa yaqturu iqtaran, wa-huwa muqtir" ("he has become straitened, so he is straitened, and he is straitened").

* *

The reciters differed concerning the reading of *al-qadar*.

Some of them read: ﴿upon the affluent is his measure (qadaruhu), and upon the straitened is his measure﴾, with the *dal* vowelled with a fatha in *qadar*, considering it the noun from *taqdir* (measuring out), which is from the saying of the speaker: "Qadara fulan hadha al-amr" ("so-and-so measured out this matter").

* *

Others read it with the *dal* of it sukun, considering it the verbal noun of that, as the poet said: [[He is al-Farazdaq, it is said.]]

*wa-ma sabba rijlī fī ḥadīdi Mujāshi'in ... ma'a al-qadri, illā ḥājatun lī urīduhā*

[[His Diwan: 215, quoted from *Lisan* (s-b-b), and it is also in *Lisan* under (q-d-r), *Maqayis al-Lughah* 5:62, *al-Asas* (s-b-b), *Islah al-Mantiq*: 109, and *Tahdhib Islah al-Mantiq* 1:168. Abu Muhammad said: "Ya'qub mentioned that this verse is by al-Farazdaq, but I have not found it in his poetry or in his reports." It seems the verse is not by al-Farazdaq, because it mentions "Hadid Mujashi'," and that was his grandfather. Jarir used to taunt him that he was "the son of the smith," so I find it unlikely that al-Farazdaq would mention "Hadid Mujashi'" in his poetry. al-Tabrizi said in explaining the verse: "He says: my imprisonment was by a measure God had decreed for me, and I had a need for it, and I had no escape from it." This meaning is not clear. One says: "sabba al-qayd fi rijlihi," meaning he was fettered.]]

* *

My view on this is that both are two readings that the community has transmitted, and the reading of one of them does not produce a meaning contrary to the other; rather, they have the same meaning. Whichever of the two readings the reciter recites, he is correct.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 236 (part 3 of 3):

It is only permissible to choose some readings over others because the chosen reading is distinguished from the others by an added meaning which makes it sound, and not others. As for when the meanings of all of them agree, there is no basis for ruling that one of them is more deserving of being recited than another.
* *
Abu Ja'far said: The interpretation of the verse, then, is: There is no blame upon you, O people, if you divorce women when you have not yet touched them and have not yet set a dowry for them [[In the manuscript and the printed edition: "لأن طلقتم النساء" (because you divorce the women), but the context requires the correct reading as I have given.]] and if you divorce them before you have touched them or set a dowry for them. And provide for them all, the wealthy among you according to his means from their provision at that time, and the one of straitened circumstances among you according to his capacity and his restricted means.
* *
The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿a provision according to what is fair, a duty upon the doers of good﴾ (2:236)
Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His remembrance be exalted, He means: And provide for them with a provision. It is permissible for "matā'an" (provision) to be in the accusative as a qat' (circumstantial qualifier) of "qadr" (measure), because "matā'" is indefinite and "qadr" is definite.
* *
By His saying "bil-ma'rūf" (according to what is fair), He means: in accordance with what God has commanded you regarding giving them that, without injustice and without withholding it from them. [[In the printed edition: "من إعطائكم لهن ذلك"; in the manuscript "إعطائكم هن" with "إيا" omitted.]] [[For the meaning of "ma'rūf" see what has passed: 3:371; then 4:547, 548; 5:7, 44, 76, 93.]]
By His saying "ḥaqqan ʿalā al-muḥsinīn" (a duty upon the doers of good), He means: a provision according to what is fair, a true duty upon the doers of good. Since the presence of the definite article on "al-ḥaqq" (the truth/duty), which is a description of "al-ma'rūf" (what is fair), while "al-ma'rūf" is definite and "ḥaqq" is indefinite, it is put in the accusative as a qat' from it, as one says: "The man came to me riding."
It is also permissible that it be in the accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun) from the whole preceding statement, like the speaker's saying: "ʿAbd Allāh is truly a scholar" (ḥaqqan), where "ḥaqq" is accusative in the intention of the speaker's statement, as if he said: I inform you of that truly. [[See Ma'ani al-Qur'an by al-Farra' 1: 154-155.]]
The first interpretation is the proper sense of the speech, because the meaning of the speech is: so provide for them a provision according to what is fair, a true duty upon everyone among you who is a doer of good.
* *
Some have claimed that it is in the accusative with the meaning: "Is that a truth, truly?" But what he said on this matter contradicts what the apparent wording of the recitation indicates. For God, may His remembrance be exalted, made the provision a right owed to the divorced women from their husbands, and the speaker of this view claims that the meaning is that God, may His remembrance be exalted, informed about Himself that it is true that this is upon the doers of good. So the interpretation of the speech, then, since the matter is so, is: And provide for them, the wealthy according to his measure and the straitened according to his measure, a provision according to what is fair, the duty incumbent upon the doers of good.
* *
By His saying "al-muḥsinīn" (the doers of good), He means those who do good to themselves by hastening to obey God in what He has obliged them to, and by fulfilling the obligations He has imposed on them.
* *
Abu Ja'far said: If someone says: You have mentioned that "al-janāḥ" (blame) is hardship, and God, may His remembrance be exalted, has said: "There is no blame upon you if you divorce women before you have touched them", so is there any blame upon us if we divorce them after consummation, such that our divorcing them before consummation removes it from us? It is said: It has been related from the Messenger of God ﷺ that he said: "Indeed God does not love those who frequently divorce and remarry (dhawwāqīn) nor those women who do so (dhawwāqāt)." [[A man who is dhawwāq: one who divorces often and marries often, and likewise the woman. Al-dhawq: seeking the novelty of marriage from time to time, as if he tastes and tests, then moves on to taste another.]]
5244 - Ibn Bashshar narrated to us with this, saying: Ibn Abi ʿAdi and ʿAbd al-Aʿlā narrated to us, from Saʿid, from Qatada, from Shahr ibn Ḥawshab, from the Prophet ﷺ. [[Hadith 5244: Shahr ibn Ḥawshab is a trustworthy Successor, as we have explained at 1489. So the hadith with this chain is mursal (disconnected at the Companion level). Al-Haythami mentioned it in Majma' al-Zawa'id 4: 335, from the hadith of ʿUbada ibn al-Samit, and said: "Narrated by al-Tabarani, and in it is an unnamed narrator. The rest of its chain is good." He also mentioned a hadith of Abu Musa, marfu': "Do not divorce women except for a fault; indeed God, blessed and exalted, does not love those who frequently divorce and remarry, nor those women who do so." He said: "Narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Kabir and al-Awsat. One of al-Bazzar's chains contains ʿImran al-Qattan, whom Ahmad and Ibn Hibban deemed trustworthy, and Yahya ibn Saʿid and others deemed weak." I do not have the chains of these two hadiths before me, so as to know their grade, nor whether Shahr ibn Ḥawshab narrated either of them. As for "al-dhawwāqīn wal-dhawwāqāt": Ibn al-Athir said: "It means those who marry quickly and divorce quickly." Al-Zamakhshari mentioned it in al-Majaz from Kitab al-Asas and said: "Whenever a man marries or a woman marries, he or she casts their eye toward another."]]
* *
It has also been related from him ﷺ that he said: "What is wrong with people who play with the limits of God, saying: I have divorced you, I have taken you back, I have divorced you."
5245 - Ibn Bashshar narrated to us with this, saying: Mu'ammal narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu Burda, from his father, from the Messenger of God ﷺ. [[Hadith 5245: This is a sound chain. Ibn Majah narrated it: 2017, from Muhammad ibn Bashshar, the teacher of al-Tabari here, with this chain. Its indication has passed, along with what was said about its defect and the response to it, and the narration of al-Bayhaqi from this route and from the narration of Musa ibn Mas'ud from Sufyan al-Thawri, at 4925, 4926. We had not seen this narration of al-Tabari at that time.]]
* *
So it is permissible that the "janāḥ" (blame) which was removed from people in their divorcing women before consummation is the blame that would have fallen upon them after they had tasted them, as related from the Messenger of God ﷺ.
* *
Some of them used to say: The meaning of His saying in this place, "lā janāḥ" (there is no blame), is: there is no path for the women against you, if you divorce them before you have touched them and had not set an obligation for them, for pursuing you for a dowry or maintenance. That would be a view, were it not for what I have described: that the one meant by divorce before touching in this verse is of two categories of women: one for whom a obligation was set, and the other for whom none was set. Since that is so, there is no basis for saying: they have no claim against you for a dowry, when the matter is as we have described.
* *
This may also bear another meaning: that it means: There is no blame upon you if you divorce women before you have touched them, at whatever time you wish to divorce them. For there is no sunnah (prescribed mode) regarding divorcing them, so a man may divorce them, if he has not touched them, whether she is menstruating or pure, at any time he likes. That is not so for a woman who has been consummated, for her husband may not divorce her, if she is of those who have menstrual cycles, except for the waiting period, while she is pure in a purity in which he has not had intercourse. So the "janāḥ" (blame) removed from the one who divorces a woman he has not touched while she is menstruating is the same "janāḥ" by which the divorcer would have been held accountable after consummation with her during menstruation, or in a purity in which he had intercourse with her. [[In the manuscript: "لم يمسهن" which is an error and oversight.]]

**The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And if you divorce them before you have touched them, yet you had already appointed for them a due portion, then half of what you appointed, unless they forgo it.﴾**

Abu Ja'far said: This ruling from God, exalted is He, clarifies His words: "There is no blame upon you if you divorce women before you have touched them or appointed for them a due portion." Its meaning is: There is no blame upon you, O people, if you divorce women before you have touched them, when you have already appointed for them a due portion. Then they are owed from you half of what you had appointed for them before your divorce of them. That is, they are owed half of the dowry you gave them.

We said that its interpretation is this, because of what we have already explained: His words "or appointed for them a due portion" are God's clarification to His servants of the ruling for women for whom no portion was appointed when they are divorced before consummation. It is therefore known that the ruling for the women joined by "or" differs from the ruling for those joined to them by "and."

God, exalted is He, repeated His words "And if you divorce them before you have touched them, yet you had already appointed for them a due portion," though their mention had already passed in His words "There is no blame upon you if you divorce women before you have touched them," so that doubt would be removed from His hearers and confusion would not arise for them, lest they think that the women whose ruling is described in this verse are other than the ones He began with and whose ruling He mentioned in the preceding verse.

* *
