As for His words "unless they forgo it," it means: unless the women who are owed half of that due portion forgo it, leaving it to you and pardoning you from it, as a favor from them to you, if they are among those whose disposal of their property is lawful, being adults and capable of sound judgment. Then their forgoing is valid, so what they forgo for you is valid, and what they had forgone for you is dropped from you. That half which had become due to them from the portion after divorce is the forgoing, if they forgo it, or what they forgo of it.

* *

Scholars of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said something similar to what we have said on this matter.

Those who said that:

5246. Al-Muthanna told me, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Salih told us, saying: Mu'awiya ibn Salih told me, from Ali ibn Abi Talha, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding "And if you divorce them before you have touched them, yet you had already appointed for them a due portion, then half of what you appointed": A man marries a woman and has named a dowry for her, then divorces her before he has touched her. She is owed half her dowry, and she is not owed more than that.

5247. Muhammad ibn 'Amr told me, saying: Abu 'Asim told us, saying: 'Isa told us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding "And if you divorce them before you have touched them, yet you had already appointed for them a due portion, then half of what you appointed" [the printed edition gives the remainder of the verse; the scribe of the manuscript erred, giving the remainder and not completing it, and placed at the start of what he wished to omit "la" and at its end "ila," which was the sign of omission in earlier times, standing in place of striking it through with pen and ink]: He said: If a man divorces his wife and a dowry was appointed for her, then half of what was appointed, unless they forgo it.

5248. Al-Muthanna told me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa told us, saying: Shibl told us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.

5249. Bishr told us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatada, regarding "And if you divorce them before you have touched them, yet you had already appointed for them a due portion, then half of what you appointed": This verse abrogated what came before it, when he had not consummated the marriage and had named a dowry for her. So half was made hers, and she has no provision.

5250. Al-Muthanna told me, saying: Ishaq told us, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far told us, from his father, from al-Rabi', regarding "And if you divorce them before you have touched them, yet you had already appointed for them a due portion, then half of what you appointed": He said: It is the man who marries a woman and appoints a dowry for her, then divorces her before he consummates with her. Then half of what was appointed for her is hers, and she has the provision, and she has no waiting period ('idda).

5251. Al-Muthanna told me, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Salih told us, saying: al-Layth told us, from Yunus, from Ibn Shihab, regarding "And if you divorce them before you have touched them, yet you had already appointed for them a due portion, then half of what you appointed": He said: If a man divorces a woman for whom a dowry was appointed and he has not touched her, then she is owed half her dowry, and she has no waiting period.

* *

Those who said, regarding "unless they forgo it," the interpretation we have mentioned:

5252. Al-Muthanna told me, saying: Habban ibn Musa told us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, saying: Yahya ibn Bishr informed us that he heard 'Ikrima say: If he divorces her before he has touched her and a dowry was appointed for her, then half the due portion is hers from him, unless she forgoes it and leaves it.

5253. Al-Husayn told us, saying: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd ibn Sulayman informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words "unless they forgo it": The woman leaves what is hers.

5254. Al-Muthanna told me, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Salih told us, saying: Mu'awiya ibn Salih told me, from Ali ibn Abi Talha, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding "unless they forgo it": It refers to the previously married woman or the virgin whom someone other than her father has married off. God placed the forgoing in their hands: if they wish, they forgo and leave it, and if they wish, they take half the dowry.

5255. Muhammad ibn 'Amr told me, saying: Abu 'Asim told us, from 'Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding "unless they forgo it": The woman leaves half her dowry, and that is all that is hers.

5256. Al-Muthanna told me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa told us, saying: Shibl told us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.

5257. Al-Muthanna told me, saying: Ishaq told us, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far told us, from his father, from al-Rabi', his words "unless they forgo it" [the reading is "idh," which appears to be a scribal variant], He said: The woman leaves half to her husband.

5258. Hamid ibn Mas'ada told us, saying: Yazid ibn Zurai' told us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn 'Awn told me, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, from Shurayh, regarding "unless they forgo it": He said: If the woman wishes, she forgoes and leaves the dowry.

5259. Hamid ibn Mas'ada told us, saying: Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal told us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn 'Awn told us, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, from Shurayh, the same.

5260. Ibn al-Muthanna told us, saying: 'Abd al-Wahhab told us, saying: 'Ubayd Allah told us, from Nafi', regarding his words "unless they forgo it": It is the woman whose husband divorces her before he has consummated with her, and she forgoes half to her husband.

5261. Musa told me, saying: 'Amr told us, saying: Asbat told us, from al-Suddi, regarding "unless they forgo it": As for "they forgo," it is the previously married woman who leaves part of her dowry, or leaves all of it.

5262. Al-Muthanna told us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Salih told us, saying: al-Layth told me, from Yunus, from Ibn Shihab, regarding "unless they forgo it": He said: The forgoing is up to them. If the woman is previously married, she has the greater right to it, and no guardian has authority over her in that, because she has taken charge of her own affair. If she wishes to forgo and waive for him half of what is hers owed by him, that is valid. And if she wishes to take it, she has greater right to that.

5263. Al-Muthanna told me, saying: Habban ibn Musa told us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak told us, saying: Ma'mar told us, saying: and Ibn Shihab told me, regarding "unless they forgo it": He said: the women.

5264. Abu Hisham al-Rifa'i told us, saying: 'Ubayd Allah told us, from Isra'il, from al-Suddi, from Abu Salih, regarding "unless they forgo it": He said: The previously married woman leaves her dowry.

5265. Abu Hisham told us, saying: Abu Usama Hammad ibn Zayd ibn Usama told us, saying: Isma'il told us, from al-Sha'bi, from Shurayh, regarding "unless they forgo it": He said: The woman forgoes all that is hers.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: I have not heard anyone say "Hammad ibn Zayd ibn Usama" except Abu Hisham. [Note on 5265: It is "Hammad ibn Usama ibn Zayd," whose biography has already passed under nos. 29, 51, 223. What Abu Hisham al-Rifa'i said is not mentioned in the biographical works.]

* *

5266. Abu Hisham told us, saying: 'Abda told us, from Sa'id, from Qatada, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, who said: If she wishes, she forgoes her dowry, meaning in His words "unless they forgo it."

5267. Abu Hisham told us, saying: [In the manuscript and the printed edition: "Ibn Hisham," and the correct reading is Abu Hisham al-Rifa'i, who appeared in the earlier chains] 'Ubayd Allah told us, from Isra'il, from Abu Husayn, from Shurayh, who said: The woman forgoes and leaves half the dowry.

5268. Yaqub ibn Ibrahim told me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayya told us, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: al-Zuhri said: "unless they forgo it" refers to the previously married women.

5269. Yaqub told me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayya told us, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Mujahid said: "unless they forgo it": He said: The woman leaves her half.

5270. Muhammad ibn Sa'd told me, saying: My father told me, saying: My paternal uncle told me, saying: My father told me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, his words "unless they forgo it": It means the women.

5271. Yunus told me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: "unless they forgo it": If she is previously married, she forgoes.

5272. al-Hasan ibn Yahya told us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, his words: "unless they forgo it," meaning the woman.

5273. Ali ibn Sahl told me, saying: Zayd told us, and Ibn Humayd told us, saying: Mihran told us, all from Sufyan, regarding "unless they forgo it": He said: The woman, if she has not been consummated with: she leaves the bridal payment to him and takes nothing from him.

* *

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿or the one in whose hand is the marriage tie should pardon﴾

Abu Ja'far said: The scholars of interpretation differed about who God, exalted is He, meant by His words "the one in whose hand is the marriage tie" ('uqdat al-nikah).

Some of them said: It is the guardian of the virgin. They said: The meaning of the verse is: or the one who has authority over the woman's marriage contract from her guardians should leave to the husband the half that became owed to the divorced woman before he touched her, and pardon him from it, if the girl is one whose affairs are not lawful for her to dispose of in her property.

Those who said that:

5274. Yaqub told me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayya told us, from Ibn Jurayj, from 'Amr ibn Dinar, from 'Ikrima, who said: Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, said: God permitted pardoning and commanded it. If she forgoes, then it is as she forgoes; and if she is stingy and her guardian pardons, it is valid even if she refuses.

5275. Al-Muthanna told me, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Salih told us, saying: Mu'awiya ibn Salih told me, from Ali ibn Abi Talha, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding "or the one in whose hand is the marriage tie should pardon": It is the father of the virgin girl. God, glory be to Him, placed the pardoning in his hands; she has no authority with him if she is divorced, so long as she is in his custody.

5276. Abu Kurayb told us, saying: Hushaym told us, saying: al-A'mash informed us, from Ibrahim, from 'Alqama, regarding "the one in whose hand is the marriage tie": the guardian.

5277. Abu al-Sa'ib told me, saying: Abu Mu'awiya told us, from al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, who said: 'Alqama said: It is the guardian.

5278. Abu Hisham told us, saying: Waki' told us, from Sufyan, from al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, from 'Alqama, that he said: It is the guardian.

5279. Abu Kurayb told us, saying: Ma'mar told us, from Hajjaj, from al-Nakha'i, from 'Alqama, who said: It is the guardian.

5280. Abu Hisham told us, saying: 'Ubayd Allah told us, from Bayan al-Nahwi [as it stands in the manuscript and the printed edition, "Bayan al-Nahwi"; I lean toward it being Shayban ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Tamimi al-Nahwi, who is biographed in al-Tahdhib, narrating from al-A'mash, and from whom 'Ubayd Allah ibn Musa narrates. So the correct reading is probably "Shayban al-Nahwi"], from al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, from 'Alqama and the companions of 'Abd Allah, who said: It is the guardian.

5281. Abu Hisham told us, saying: Waki' told us, from Sufyan, from al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, from 'Alqama, that he said: It is the guardian.

5282. Abu Kurayb told us, saying: Ma'mar told us, from Hajjaj, that al-Aswad ibn Zayd said: It is the guardian.

5283. Abu Hisham told us, saying: Abu Khalid told us, from Shu'ba, from Abu Bishr, who said: Tawus and Mujahid said: It is the guardian. Then they both turned back and said: It is the husband.

5284. Yaqub told me, saying: Hushaym told us, saying: Abu Bishr informed us, who said: Mujahid and Tawus said: It is the guardian. Then they both turned back and said: It is the husband.

5285. Abu Hisham told us, saying: Ibn Fudayl told us, from al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, from 'Alqama, who said: It is the guardian.

5286. Ibn Humayd told us, saying: Jarir told us, from Mughira, from al-Sha'bi, who said: A man gave his sister in marriage, and her husband divorced her before he consummated with her. Her brother then pardoned the dowry, and Shurayh approved it. Then he said: I pardon on behalf of the women of Banu Murra. 'Amir said: No, by God, he never gave a judgment more fitting than this: that he approve the brother's pardon, according to His words "unless they forgo it or the one in whose hand is the marriage tie should pardon." Afterwards Shurayh said: It is the husband, if he pardons the whole bridal payment and hands all of it to her, or if she forgoes the half that he named for her. And if they both dispute, she takes half of her dowry. He said: "And that you pardon is nearer to piety." [Note on 5286: Al-Bayhaqi narrated it in al-Sunan 8:251 with his chain "from Sa'id ibn Mansur, from Jarir, from Mughira," with a different wording, but he authenticates it. The printed edition and the manuscript read "he never gave a judgment more fitting than him," and the correct wording is from al-Bayhaqi. I do not know what "the women of Banu Murra" means; perhaps Murra was among his relatives, a sister or his daughter. And God knows best.]

5287. Yaqub told me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayya told us, saying: Jarir ibn Hazim told us, from 'Isa ibn 'Asim al-Asadi: that 'Ali asked Shurayh about the one in whose hand is the marriage tie, and he said: It is the guardian.

5288. Abu Kurayb told us, saying: Hushaym told us, Mughira said: Informed us from al-Sha'bi, from Shurayh, that he used to say: The one in whose hand is the marriage tie is the guardian. Then he abandoned that and said: It is the husband.

5289. Yaqub told me, saying: Hushaym told us, saying: Sayyar informed us, from al-Sha'bi, that a man married a woman, found her ugly, and divorced her before he consummated with her. Her guardian pardoned half the dowry. He said: I brought her case before Shurayh, and Shurayh said to her: Your guardian has pardoned. He said: Then he returned afterwards and made the one in whose hand is the marriage tie to be the husband.

5290. Ibn Bashshar and Ibn al-Muthanna told us, both saying: 'Abd al-A'la told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatada, from al-Hasan, regarding "the one in whose hand is the marriage tie": He said: the guardian.

5291. Abu Kurayb told us, saying: Hushaym told us, from Mansur or someone else, from al-Hasan, who said: It is the guardian.

5292. Abu Hisham told us, saying: Ibn Idris told us, from Hisham, from al-Hasan, who said: It is the guardian.

5293. Yaqub told me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayya told us, from Abu Raja', who said: al-Hasan was asked about the one in whose hand is the marriage tie, and he said: It is the guardian.

5294. Abu Hisham told us, saying: Waki' told us, from Yazid ibn Ibrahim, from al-Hasan, who said: It is the one who married her off.

5295. Abu Kurayb told us, saying: Hushaym told us, from Mughira, from Ibrahim, who said: The one in whose hand is the marriage tie is the guardian.

5296. Abu Hisham told us, saying: Waki' and Ibn Mahdi told us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, who said: It is the guardian.

5297. Abu Hisham told us, saying: Ibn Mahdi told us, from Abu 'Awana, from Mughira, from Ibrahim and al-Sha'bi, both saying: It is the guardian.

5298. Yaqub told me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayya told us, saying: Ibn Jurayj informed us, from 'Ata', who said: It is the guardian.

5299. Abu Hisham told us, saying: 'Ubayd Allah told us, from Isra'il, from al-Suddi, from Abu Salih: "or the one in whose hand is the marriage tie should pardon," He said: the guardian of the virgin.

5300. Yaqub told me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayya told us, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: al-Zuhri said to me: "or the one in whose hand is the marriage tie should pardon": the guardian of the virgin.

5301. Muhammad ibn Sa'd told me, saying: My father told me, saying: My paternal uncle told me, saying: My father told me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas: "or the one in whose hand is the marriage tie should pardon": It is the guardian.

5302. al-Hasan ibn Yahya told us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, saying: Ibn Tawus informed us, from his father, and from a man, from 'Ikrima. Ma'mar said: al-Hasan also said it. They said: The one in whose hand is the marriage tie is the guardian.

5303. al-Hasan told us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: The one in whose hand is the marriage tie is the father.

5304. al-Hasan ibn Yahya told us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: al-Thawri informed us, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, from 'Alqama, who said: It is the guardian.

5305. Al-Muthanna told me, saying: al-Hammani told us, saying: Shurayk told us, from Salim, from Mujahid, who said: It is the guardian.

5306. Musa told me, saying: 'Amr told us, saying: Asbat told us, from al-Suddi, regarding "the one in whose hand is the marriage tie": It is the guardian of the virgin.

5307. Yunus told me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding the one in whose hand is the marriage tie: the father. He mentioned it from Ibn Zayd, from his father.

5308. Yunus told me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, from Malik, from Zayd and Rabi'a, regarding "the one in whose hand is the marriage tie": the father, concerning his virgin daughter, and the master, concerning his slave-girl. [Note on 5308: In the Muwatta' it is no. 528.]

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 237 (part 2 of 4):**

5309. Yunus told me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Malik said: "That is when she is divorced before consummation. He may then waive half of the dowry that became due to her from him, so long as no divorce has taken place..." [[A blank space in the printed edition and the manuscript marks the place of the dots. I have tried hard to find Malik's text in the books available to me, but I did not find it.]]

5310. al-Muthanna told me, saying: Abu Salih told us, saying: al-Layth told me, from Yunus, from Ibn Shihab (al-Zuhri), who said: "The one who holds the bond of marriage is the virgin whose guardian waives it. That is permitted. Her own waiver is not permitted."

5311. al-Muthanna told me, saying: Habban ibn Musa told us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, saying: Yahya ibn Bishr informed us, that he heard Ikrimah say, regarding ﴿unless they waive﴾: that the woman waives half of the obligatory portion due to her from him and leaves it. But if she is stingy and insists on taking it, then she and her guardian, the one who gave her in marriage, whether an uncle, a brother or a father, may waive the half. He may do so if he wishes, even if the woman dislikes it.

5312. Sa'id ibn al-Rabi' al-Razi told us, saying: Sufyan told us, from Amr ibn Dinar, from Ikrimah, who said: "God permitted the waiving and commanded it. If a woman waives, her waiver is valid. If she is stingy and withholds, her guardian may waive, and his waiver is valid." [[The report: 5312. Sa'id ibn al-Rabi' al-Razi, a teacher of al-Tabari. We have not found a biography of him after long search. He will also be cited later as a narrator in 5520, without the nisba "al-Razi". In the printed edition it is "al-Muradi", instead of "al-Razi", and this is an error. Ibn Kathir transmitted this report at 1:574 from this same place, and there it is "al-Razi". Likewise al-Tabari narrated from him in the book "Dhayl al-Mudhayyal", appended to his history, 13:53, where he says: "Haswarah ibn Muhammad al-Minqari and Sa'id ibn al-Rabi' al-Razi told me, saying: Sufyan told us, from Amr..." Then we have not found that they mention a son for al-Rabi' ibn Sulayman al-Muradi.]]

5313. Ibn Humayd told us, saying: Jarir told us, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, who said: "The one who holds the bond of marriage is the guardian."

* *

Others said: Rather, the one who holds the bond of marriage is the husband. They said: The meaning is: "or the one who holds the woman's marriage waives, and gives her the full dowry."

Those who said this:

5314. Muhammad ibn Bashshar told us, saying: Abu Shahmah told us, saying: Habib told us, from al-Layth, from Qatadah, from Khallas ibn Amr, from Ali, who said: "The one who holds the bond of marriage is the husband." [[The report: 5314. In the manuscript it is written "Abu Uthmah" without dots. In the printed edition it is "Abu Shahmah", which is an error, since we have not found anyone called by it. "Abu Uthmah" is, in our judgment, most likely "Muhammad ibn Khalid ibn Uthmah", whose biography has passed under numbers 90 and 91. There we showed that "Uthmah" was his mother. It is not unlikely that he was called by her name, especially since they did not mention another kunya for him. What supports that it is him is that among those who narrated from him in his biography is "Bundar", who is Muhammad ibn Bashshar, the narrator from him here. "Uthmah" is with a fatha on the unpointed ʿayn and a sukun on the triangular thaʾ. "Habib", who narrates here from al-Layth ibn Sa'd: we did not know who he is, and we found nothing that points to him. He is written so in the manuscript and in the printed edition. If it were a corruption of "Shu'ayb", meaning Shu'ayb ibn al-Layth, it would not be far-fetched. "Khallas", with a kasra on the dotted khaʾ and a light lam, is ibn Amr al-Hajari al-Basri: a major, trustworthy Successor. They spoke about his hearing from Ali, and that his narrations from him were from a written sheet he possessed. Al-Bukhari stated this in al-Tarikh al-Kabir 2/1/208.]]

5315. Ya'qub told me, saying: Ibn Ulayyah told us, saying: Jarir ibn Hazim told us, from Isa ibn Asim al-Asadi: that Ali asked Shurayh about the one who holds the bond of marriage, and he said: "It is the guardian." Ali said: "No, but it is the husband."

5316. Ibn Humayd told us, saying: Ibrahim told us, saying: Jarir ibn Hazim told us, from Isa ibn Asim, who said: I heard Shurayh say: Ali said to me: "Who is the one who holds the bond of marriage?" I said: "The woman's guardian." He said: "No, rather it is the husband."

5317. Abu Hisham al-Rifa'i told us, saying: Ibn Mahdi told us, saying: Hammad ibn Salamah told us, from Ammar ibn Abi Ammar, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "It is the husband."

5318. Ahmad ibn Hazim told me, saying: Abu Nu'aym told us, saying: I said to Hammad ibn Salamah: "Who is the one who holds the bond of marriage?" He mentioned from Ali ibn Zayd, from Ammar ibn Abi Ammar, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "The husband."

5319. Abu Hisham told us, saying: Ubayd Allah told us, saying: Isra'il informed us, from Khusayf, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "It is the husband."

5320. Abu Hisham told us, saying: Ibn Fudayl told us, from al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, from Ibn Abbas and Shurayh, who both said: "It is the husband."

5321. Abu Hisham told us, saying: Ibn Mahdi told us, from Abd Allah ibn Ja'far, from Wasil ibn Abi Sa'id, from Muhammad ibn Jubayr ibn Mut'im: that his father married a woman, then divorced her before he consummated the marriage. He sent the dowry and said: "I have more right to the waiver." [[The report: 5321. Abd Allah ibn Ja'far is al-Makhrami al-Zuhri, of the descendants of al-Miswar ibn Makhramah ibn Nawfal ibn Uhayb ibn Abd Manaf. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib. Wasil ibn Abi Sa'id is biographed in al-Jarh wa al-Ta'dil 4/2/30 and al-Kabir of al-Bukhari 4/2/172.]]

5322. al-Hasan ibn Yahya told us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Salih ibn Kaysan: that Jubayr ibn Mut'im married a woman, then divorced her before he had consummated the marriage, and completed the dowry for her, and interpreted: ﴿or the one who holds the bond of marriage waives﴾. [[The report: 5322. This report is so established here: "Salih ibn Kaysan: that Jubayr ibn Mut'im", which makes it disconnected (munqati'), because Salih ibn Kaysan did not meet Jubayr ibn Mut'im. Moreover, it contradicts what is established in the Musannaf of Abd al-Razzaq 3:284 (photographed manuscript), for the report is established there as: "from Salih ibn Kaysan: that Nafi' ibn Jubayr married..." Then the report has a connected chain, because Salih narrates from Nafi' ibn Jubayr ibn Mut'im. This is the correct version, God willing. Perhaps al-Tabari or his teacher al-Hasan ibn Yahya made a mistake in it.]]

5323. Abu Hisham told us, saying: Ibn Idris told us, from Muhammad ibn Amr, from Nafi', from Jubayr: that he divorced his wife before he consummated the marriage, so he completed the dowry for her and said: "I have more right to the waiver."

5324. Hamid ibn Mas'adah told us, saying: Yazid ibn Zurayi' told us, saying: Abd Allah ibn Awn told me, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, from Shurayh, regarding ﴿or the one in whose hand is the bond of marriage waives﴾, he said: "If the husband wishes, he gives her the full dowry."

5325. Hamid told us, saying: Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal told us, saying: Abd Allah ibn Awn told us, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, with something similar.

5326. Ibn Bashshar told us, saying: Abd al-Rahman told us, saying: Sufyan told us, from Abu Ishaq, from Shurayh, who said: "The one who holds the bond of marriage is the husband."

5327. Ibn al-Muthanna told us, saying: Abd al-Wahhab told us, saying: Dawud told us, from Amir: that Shurayh said: "The one who holds the bond of marriage is the husband." That was rejected against him.

5328. Abu al-Sa'ib told me, saying: Abu Mu'awiyah told us, from al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, from Shurayh, who said: "The one who holds the bond of marriage is the husband." He said: Ibrahim said: "And what does Shurayh know!"

5329. Abu Kurayb told us, saying: Ma'mar told us, saying: Hajjaj told us, from Shurayh, who said: "It is the husband."

5330. Abu Kurayb told us, saying: al-A'mash informed us, from Ibrahim, from Shurayh, who said: "It is the husband."

5331. Abu Hisham told us, saying: Abu Usamah Hammad ibn Zayd ibn Usamah told us, saying: Isma'il told us, from al-Sha'bi, from Shurayh, regarding ﴿or the one in whose hand is the bond of marriage waives﴾, and he said: "It is the husband." [[The report: 5331. "Hammad ibn Zayd ibn Usamah" is Hammad ibn Usamah ibn Zayd. See the earlier report number 5265 and the note on it.]]

5332. Abu Hisham told us, saying: Ubayd Allah told us, from Isra'il, from Abu Husayn, from Shurayh, regarding ﴿the one in whose hand is the bond of marriage﴾, who said: "The husband completes the dowry for her."

5333. Abu Hisham told us, saying: Abu Mu'awiyah told us, from Isma'il, from al-Sha'bi, and from al-Hajjaj, from al-Hakam, from Shurayh, and from al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, from Shurayh, who said: "It is the husband."

5334. Abu Hisham told us, saying: Waki' told us, saying: Isma'il told us, from al-Sha'bi, from Shurayh, who said: "It is the husband. If he wishes he completes the dowry for her, and if she wishes she waives what is hers."

5335. Ya'qub told me, saying: Ibn Ulayyah told us, from Ayyub, from Muhammad, who said: Shurayh said: "The one in whose hand is the bond of marriage" is the husband.

5336. Ya'qub told me, saying: Ibn Ulayyah told us, from Ibn Ayun, from Ibn Sirin, from Shurayh, regarding ﴿that the one in whose hand is the bond of marriage waives﴾, who said: "If the husband wishes, he waives and the dowry is completed."

5337. al-Hasan ibn Yahya told us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: al-Thawri informed us, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, from Shurayh, who said: "It is the husband."

5338. Ibn Bashshar and Ibn al-Muthanna told us, both saying: Ibn Abi Adi told us, from Abd al-A'la, from Sa'id, from Qatadah, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, who said regarding ﴿the one in whose hand is the bond of marriage﴾: "It is the husband."

5339. Ibn Bashshar told us, saying: Abdah told us, from Sa'id, from Qatadah, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, regarding ﴿or the one in whose hand is the bond of marriage waives﴾, who said: "It is the husband."

5340. Abu Hisham told us, saying: Ibn Mahdi told us, from Hammad ibn Salamah, from Qays ibn Sa'd, from Mujahid, who said: "It is the husband."

5341. Abu Hisham told us, saying: Waki' told us, saying: Sufyan told us, from Layth, from Mujahid, who said: "The husband."

5342. Muhammad ibn Amr told me, saying: Abu Asim told us, from Isa [and] al-Muthanna told me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah told us, saying: Shibl told us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿or the one in whose hand is the bond of marriage waives﴾: that her husband completes the full dowry for her.

5343. al-Hasan ibn Yahya told us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, [and] from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, [and] from Ayyub, and from Ibn Sirin, from Shurayh, [all] said: "The one in whose hand is the bond of marriage" is the husband.

5344. Ya'qub told me, saying: Ibn Ulayyah told us, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Mujahid said: "The one in whose hand is the bond of marriage" is the husband. "That the one in whose hand is the bond of marriage waives" means the husband's completing the entire dowry.

5345. Ya'qub told me, saying: Ibn Ulayyah told us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Abd Allah ibn Abi Mulaykah, who said: Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "The one in whose hand is the bond of marriage" is the husband.

5346. Ya'qub told me, saying: Hushaym told us, saying: Abu Bishr informed us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: "The one in whose hand is the bond of marriage is the husband." He said: Mujahid and Tawus said: "It is the guardian." I said to Sa'id: "But Mujahid and Tawus say it is the guardian?" Sa'id said: "Then what do you command me?" He said: "Tell me: if the guardian waived and the woman refused, would that be permitted?" So I returned to them both and told them, and they retracted their view and followed Sa'id. [[As printed: "Then what do you command me?" In the manuscript: "Then what am I to you, command me", without dots, and I did not find the report elsewhere, and I am in doubt about the soundness of this phrase. Ibn Hazm narrated this in al-Muhalla 9:512 through "al-Hajjaj ibn al-Minhal, from Abu Awanah, from Abu Bishr, who is Ja'far ibn Iyas ibn Abi Wahshiyyah, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: The one in whose hand is the bond of marriage is the husband. Mujahid, Tawus and the people of Madinah said: It is the guardian. He said: I informed them of the statement of Sa'id ibn Jubayr, and they returned from their view." See also al-Sunan al-Kubra 8:251, which is close to the wording of Ibn Hazm.]]

5347. Abu Hisham told us, saying: Humayd told us, from al-Hasan ibn Salih, from Salim al-Aftas, from Sa'id, who said: "It is the husband." [[The report: 5347. "Humayd" is Humayd ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Ru'asi, trustworthy, who died in 192. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib. "al-Hasan ibn Salih" is ibn Salih al-Thawri. Ibn Sa'd said: "He was an ascetic, a worshipper, a jurist, a proof, sound in report and abundant in it, and he was a Shi'i," who died in 169. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib. "Salim al-Aftas" is Salim ibn Ajlan al-Umawi, trustworthy, abundant in narrations. He used to dispute about Irja'. He was killed at Harran in 132. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib.]]

5348. Abu Hisham told us, saying: Abu Khalid al-Ahmar told us, from Shu'bah, from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id, who said: "It is the husband." [But] Tawus and Mujahid said: "It is the guardian." So I spoke to them both about that until they followed Sa'id.

5349. Ibn Bashshar told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far told us, saying: Shu'bah told us, from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Tawus and Mujahid, with something similar.

5350. Abu Hisham told us, saying: Abu al-Husayn, meaning Zayd ibn al-Hubab, told us, from Aflah ibn Sa'id, who said: I heard Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi say: "It is the husband, who gives what he has as a waiver." [[The report: 5350. In the manuscript and the printed edition: "Abu al-Hasan", and the correct form is "Abu al-Husayn". He is biographed in al-Tahdhib and al-Jarh wa al-Ta'dil 1/2/560. In the manuscript: "Aflah ibn Sa'd", and the correct form is what is in the printed edition.]]

5351. Abu Hisham told us, saying: Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi told us, from Zuhayr, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Sha'bi, who said: "It is the husband."

5352. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, saying: Abd al-Wahhab told us, saying: Abd Allah told us, from Nafi', who said: "The one in whose hand is the bond of marriage" is the husband. [As for] ﴿unless they waive or the one in whose hand is the bond of marriage waives﴾: he said: As for His saying ﴿unless they waive﴾, it refers to the woman whose husband divorces her before he consummates the marriage. Either she waives half for her husband, or the husband waives and completes her dowry for her.

5353. al-Muthanna told me, saying: Ishaq told us, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far told us, from his father, from al-Rabi': "The one in whose hand is the bond of marriage" is the husband.

5354. Ibn Wakī' told us, saying: My father told us, from al-Mas'udi, from al-Qasim, who said: Shurayh used to confront them on their knees [[Yujathi'uhum ʿala al-rukab: that is, he would sit to face them in dispute and argue with them fiercely. The opponent would kneel on his knees and dispute when the quarrel became intense.]] and say: "It is the husband."

5355. al-Muthanna told me, saying: Ishaq told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Harb told us, saying: Ibn Lahi'ah told us, from Amr ibn Shu'ayb, that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "The one in whose hand is the bond of marriage is the husband, who waives or she waives." [[The report: 5355. Ibn Kathir said in his commentary 1:573-574: "Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ibn Lahi'ah mentioned: Amr ibn Shu'ayb told me, from his father, from his grandfather, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: 'The guardian of the bond of marriage is the husband'. Likewise Ibn Mardawayh traced it through Abd Allah ibn Lahi'ah, and Ibn Jarir traced it from Ibn Lahi'ah, from Amr ibn Shu'ayb, that the Messenger of God... and mentioned it, but he did not say 'from his father, from his grandfather'." Al-Bayhaqi said in al-Sunan 8:251-252: "It is narrated from Ibn Lahi'ah, from Amr ibn Shu'ayb, from his father, from his grandfather, from the Prophet (ﷺ): 'The guardian of the bond of marriage is the husband.'" Al-Bayhaqi said: "This is not preserved, and Ibn Lahi'ah is not a valid proof, and God knows best."]]

5356. al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj told me, saying: I heard Abu Mu'adh al-Fadl ibn Khalid say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying ﴿or the one in whose hand is the bond of marriage waives﴾: "It is the husband. This is about a woman whose husband divorces her before he consummates the marriage, and a dowry has been fixed for her. She has half the dowry. If she wishes, she leaves what is hers, which is the half, and if she wishes, she takes it."

5357. Ibn Humayd told us, saying: Mihran told us, and Ali told me, saying: Zayd told us, all from Sufyan: ﴿or the one in whose hand is the bond of marriage waives﴾: "The husband."

5358. Yahya ibn Abi Talib told me, saying: Yazid ibn Harun told us, saying: Juwaybir informed us, from al-Dahhak, who said: "The one in whose hand is the bond of marriage" is the husband.

5359. Ibn al-Barqi told us, saying: Amr ibn Abi Salamah told us, from Sa'id ibn Abd al-Aziz, who said: I heard the interpretation of this verse: ﴿unless they waive﴾: the women, so they take nothing; ﴿or the one in whose hand is the bond of marriage waives﴾: the husband, so he leaves that and seeks nothing.

5360. Ibn Humayd told us, saying: Jarir told us, from Mansur, who said: Shurayh said regarding ﴿unless they waive﴾: "The women waive." ﴿Or the one in whose hand is the bond of marriage waives﴾: "The husband."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of the two views, in terms of the truth, is the view of the one who said: What is meant by ﴿the one in whose hand is the bond of marriage﴾ is the husband. This is because there is consensus (ijma') of all that if the guardian of a virgin or a previously married woman, whether a young child or a mature adult, were to release her husband from her dowry before he divorced her, or gift it to him, or waive it for him, then his releasing and his waiving it for him would be void, and her dowry would remain due from him as it was before he released it from him. So the ruling for what he releases of it after divorcing her is the same as the ruling for what he releases of it before divorcing her.

Another point: all agree that if a woman's guardian, whether she is under restraint or not, were to grant her husband who has divorced her, after her separation from him, a dirham of her property, not by way of pardoning him from what was due to her of her dowry before it, his grant of that is rejected and void. Yet they also all agree that her dowry is a part of her property, so its ruling is the ruling of all her other property.

Another point: all agree that the paternal cousins of a virgin woman and her full brothers (from both her father and mother) are among her guardians, and that if any of them pardons her property [for her husband, before he has consummated the marriage] or after he has consummated it [this clause between the brackets I have inferred from the context so that the statement is sound; and there is evidently a lacuna before his words "or after he has consummated it". The manuscript and the printed edition agree on this lacuna.]: his pardon of what he pardons is void, and the woman's right remains binding on him in its original state. Likewise is the case with the pardon of every guardian of hers, whoever he may be among the guardians, whether a father, a grandfather or a maternal uncle, because God, may His remembrance be exalted, did not single out some of those who hold the marriage contract over others in the permissibility of their pardon, provided they are of those whose judgment is valid regarding their own persons and property.

It is said to whoever rejects what we have said, from among those who claim that "the one who holds the marriage tie" is the woman's guardian: does the statement on this matter avoid one of two alternatives? Since, according to you, the one who holds the marriage tie is the guardian, either it is every guardian who may marry his ward, or some of them and not others? He will find no way out of one of these two divisions.

If he says: "It is so."
It is said to him: "Then which of them is meant?"
If he says: "Every guardian who may marry his ward."
It is said to him: "Is it permissible for a freed master of a female slave to marry off his former slave-woman with her permission after he has freed her?"
If he says: "Yes!"
It is said to him: "Is his pardon permissible if he pardons her dowry for her husband after he has divorced her before consummation?"
If he says: "Yes," he has departed from the consensus. If he says: "No!" it is said to him: "Why? What forbade this to him, when he is her guardian who holds the marriage tie?"
Then the argument is turned back upon him in this matter, and he is asked to explain the difference between his case and the pardon of all other guardians besides him.
If he says: "Some and not others."
He is asked for proof of this specific distinction, though God, may His remembrance be exalted, has stated it generally and did not single out some over others.
It is said to him: "Who is meant by it, if what is intended is some of the guardians and not others?"
If he gestures toward some of them, he is asked for proof of it, the argument is turned back on him, and his statement is countered with the opposite of his claim. Then he will not state any position in this matter without being bound to its counterpart in the other.

* *

If someone supposes that when a husband separates from his wife, the one holding the tie of her marriage has ceased to be in his hand, and God, may His remembrance be exalted, only permitted the pardon of the one who holds the marriage tie of the divorced woman, it would thereby be known that the husband is not meant, and that what is meant is the one who holds the marriage tie of the divorced woman after her separation from her husband. In that case it would follow that the marriage tie is in the hand of the husband, and the statement that it is in the hand of the guardian who has the authority to contract her marriage would be sound. And if that is so, the statement that the one holding the marriage tie is the guardian is sound—then he has been heedless and has supposed wrongly. [The phrase "then he has been heedless" is the apodosis of "if" in "if someone supposes". "Heedless" here means one who has fallen into negligence, as I have explained earlier (1:151) and elsewhere.]

The meaning is: "or the one in whose hand is the marriage tie of them pardons," and "the" with "marriage" has replaced the pronoun-suffix that "marriage" would have had were it not for "al" in it, as God, may His remembrance be exalted, said: ﴿فَإِنَّ الْجَنَّةَ هِيَ الْمَأْوَى﴾ [Surat an-Nazi'at: 41], meaning: "then the Garden is his refuge," and as the poet Nabigha of the Banu Dhubyan said:

They have a disposition that God has not given to others among people; their minds are not scattered (ghair 'awazib).

[From his diwan, p. 45. It will come later in the tafsir (13:4, Bulaq edition) from his qasida in praise of 'Amr ibn al-Harith al-Asghar al-A'raj al-Ghassani, when he fled from al-Nu'man ibn al-Mundhir to Syria over the matter of al-Mutajarrida. The pronoun in "lahum" refers to the kings of Ghassan from the Banu Jafna. Shima means nature/disposition. The diwan's version reads "from generosity" instead of "from people," but al-Tabari's version in this context is better, because the verse came after their description in war with severe fighting, until he said before it: "with a strike that removes the skulls from their places, and a thrust like the pregnant she-camels' fevered flank..." So the shima here is their patience in the hardships of battle, so their souls do not flutter from terror and their minds and planning are not disturbed when fighting reaches a point that scatters the wisdom of the wise. "Awazib" is the plural of "'azib," from the expression "his forbearance was absent" when it departed from him and went far away.]
meaning: "so their minds are not absent." The evidence for this is more than can be counted.

* *

So the sense of the statement is: "except that the women pardon, or he in whose hand is the marriage tie pardons," and this is the husband, who holds the marriage tie of himself in every case, before and after divorce. [In the manuscript and the printed edition it reads "the marriage tie," and the correct reading, required by the interpretation and the following context, is what I have adopted.] For its meaning is: "or he in whose hand is the marriage tie of them pardons," so the sense of the statement would be what those who claim it is the guardian suppose. For a woman's guardian does not hold the marriage tie of a woman without her permission, except in the case of her childhood, and that is a condition in which only some of her guardians can contract the marriage over her, according to the view of most who hold that the one who holds the marriage tie is the guardian. God, may His remembrance be exalted, did not single out some of them by His saying "or he in whose hand is the marriage tie pardons," so the interpretation could be directed to what they have interpreted, had there been any basis for what they said.

* *

Moreover, God, may His remembrance be exalted, only referred, by His saying "And if you divorce them before you have touched them and you have appointed for them an obligation, then half of what you have appointed, unless they pardon," to the women mentioned in the preceding verse, which is His saying: "There is no blame upon you if you divorce women as long as you have not touched them." Young girls are not called "women" (nisa'), but rather "girls" or "slave-girls." In the speech of all the Arabs, "nisa'" is the name for a woman, and the Arabs do not call a little girl, a young girl or a small girl "woman," just as they do not call a small boy "man."

Since this is so, and since His saying "or he in whose hand is the marriage tie pardons," according to those who claim that it means the guardian, is only: "or he in whose hand is the marriage tie pardons what is due to his ward whom he is entitled to have authority over as to her property, either because of minority or because of foolishness," and God, may His remembrance be exalted, only related in the two verses the accounts of divorced women in general, not particularly, and gave them the right of pardon by His saying "unless they pardon," it becomes known from His saying "unless they pardon" that those meant in the two verses in which He mentioned them are all of them, not some, since it is known that the pardon of those over whose property a guardian has authority is void.

Since that is so, it is clear that the interpretation of "or he in whose hand is the marriage tie of them pardons" requires that the guardians of mature, sound-minded women should have the authority to pardon what was given to them as dowry upon divorce before consummation, like the authority of guardians of young children over whose property foolishness is in effect. And in the denial by those who say "the one in whose hand is the marriage tie is the guardian" of the pardon of guardians of mature, sound-minded women, as we have described, and their distinction between their rulings and the rulings of the other guardians, there is a clear indication of the corruption of their interpretation.

Those who hold this view should be asked for the difference between this and a principle or a parallel; they will not state any position on any of this without being bound to its opposite in the same way.

* *

On the interpretation of His saying: ﴿وَأَنْ تَعْفُوا أَقْرَبُ لِلتَّقْوَى﴾ ("And that you pardon is nearer to piety").

Abu Ja'far said: The people of interpretation differed regarding whom the words "And that you pardon is nearer to piety" were addressed to.

Some said: it was addressed to men and women.

Those who said this:

5361. Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: I heard Ibn Jurayj narrate, from 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah, from Ibn 'Abbas: "And that you pardon is nearer to piety," he said: the nearer of the two to piety is the one who pardons.

5362. Ibn al-Barqi narrated to us, saying: 'Amr ibn Abi Salamah narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz, who said: I heard the explanation of this verse, "And that you pardon is nearer to piety," he said: they all pardon.

* *

The interpretation of the verse according to this view: "And that you, O people, pardon one another for what is due to one of you from the other of the dowry before separation at divorce, is nearer to him to the piety of God."

* *

Others said: rather, those addressed by it are the husbands of divorced women.

Those who said this:

5363. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mughira, from al-Sha'bi: "And that you pardon is nearer to piety": that he pardon is nearer to piety.

* *

The interpretation of this according to this view: "And that you, divorcing husbands, pardon, leaving to them what is due to you to recover from them of the dowry you gave them, or complete it for them—by giving them the dowry you had named for them in the marriage contract if you had not given it to them—is nearer to you to the piety of God."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The view that I hold to be the more correct of the two interpretations of the verse is what Ibn 'Abbas said, namely that the meaning is: "And that one of you pardon another, O husbands and wives, after your separation from one another, what is due to one of you from the other, so that he leaves it to him if any remains due to him from him; and if none remains, then by completing it in full—is nearer to you to the piety of God."

* *

Someone may say: what is there in forgiving that brings one nearer to the piety of God, such that it is said to the one who forgives and pardons what is due to him from his companion: "Is your doing what you did nearer to your piety to God?" It is said to him: what there is in it of nearness to the piety of God is his hastening in that pardon to what God has urged him toward, called him to and exhorted him to. So his act, when done seeking the pleasure of God and preferring what He urged him to over the desire of his own soul, is known by it, since he, preferring to do what He urged him to, which He did not make obligatory upon him, over his own desire, is shown that when He made it obligatory and required it, he prefers it even more strongly, and when He forbade him, he avoids it even more strongly. That is its nearness to piety.

* *

On the interpretation of His saying: ﴿وَلا تَنْسَوُا الْفَضْلَ بَيْنَكُمْ﴾ ("And do not forget graciousness among you").

Abu Ja'far said: May His remembrance be exalted, He means: do not neglect, O people, to take the initiative of graciousness of one of you over another, so that you leave it. Rather, let the man who divorces his wife before touching her be gracious, completing her full dowry if he had not given her all of it. If he had given her all that had been obligatory for him, then let him be gracious to her by pardoning what is due to him and he is permitted to recover from her, which is half of it. If the man is stingy with that and refuses except to recover half from her, then let the divorced woman be gracious to him by returning all of it to him, if she had received it from him. And if she had not received it, let her pardon [all of it]. [The bracketed word is an addition required by the context.] If they both do not do this, but are stingy and leave what God urged them to, namely that one of them takes the initiative of graciousness over the other, then she has half of what had been obligatory for her in the marriage contract, and he has half of it.

The people of interpretation have said the same as we have said on this.

Those who said this:

5364. Ahmad ibn Hazim narrated to us, saying: Abu Nu'aym narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Dhi'b narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr ibn Mut'im, from his father Jubayr: that he entered upon Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas and he offered him his daughter, and he married her. When he went out, he divorced her and sent her the dowry. He was told: "Why did you marry her?" He said: "She was offered to me, and I disliked to refuse her!" It was said: "Why did you send the dowry?" He said: "Then where is the graciousness?"

5365. Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Za'ida narrated to us, from Warqa', from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "And do not forget graciousness among you." He said: the husband completing the dowry, or the woman leaving the half.

5366. Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, from 'Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "And do not forget graciousness among you," he said: completing the dowry, or the woman leaving half of it.

5367. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.

5368. Sufyan ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Layth, from Mujahid: "And do not forget graciousness among you," in this and in other matters.

5369. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi' concerning His saying: "And do not forget graciousness among you," he said: He says, let them show kindness to one another.

5370. Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Zuray' narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada: "And do not forget graciousness among you; indeed God is Seeing of what you do." God encourages you toward what is good and urges you toward graciousness.

5371. Yahya ibn Abi Talib narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Juwaybir informed us, from al-Dahhak concerning His saying: "And do not forget graciousness among you," he said: a woman whose husband divorces her after a dowry has been fixed for her but before he has consummated the marriage: she has half the dowry. God commanded that her share be left to her, or if he wishes he may complete the dowry in full. This is what God mentioned: "And do not forget graciousness among you."

5372. Musa narrated to me, saying: 'Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "And do not forget graciousness among you," he urged each one to kindness—meaning the husband and the woman—to kindness.

5373. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Habban ibn Musa narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, saying: Yahya ibn Bishr informed us that he heard 'Ikrima say concerning God's saying: "And do not forget graciousness among you": that graciousness is half the dowry, and that the woman pardons it for the husband, or his guardian pardons it.

5374. Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said concerning His saying: "And do not forget graciousness among you," he said: it is pardoned, half the dowry or part of it.

5375. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, and 'Ali narrated to me, saying: Zayd narrated to us, both from Sufyan: "And do not forget graciousness among you," he said: urging some of them toward others in this and in other matters, including the woman's pardon of the dowry and the husband's completing it.

5376. Yahya ibn Abi Talib narrated to me, saying: Yazid informed us, saying: Juwaybir informed us, from al-Dahhak: "And do not forget graciousness among you," he said: the good deed.

5377. Ibn al-Barqi narrated to us, saying: 'Amr narrated to us, from Sa'id, who said: I heard the explanation of this verse: "And do not forget graciousness among you," he said: do not forget kindness.

* *

On the interpretation of His exalted saying: ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ بَصِيرٌ (٢٣٧)﴾ ("Indeed God is Seeing of what you do").

Abu Ja'far said: By this He, may His remembrance be exalted, means: "Indeed God is aware of what you do," O people, of what He has urged you toward and exhorted you to, of pardon by some of you for others regarding what is due to one of them from another by right of the marriage that was between you and your wives, and graciousness of some of you toward others in that and in other matters [in the manuscript "and other"; in the printed edition "and other" — the context requires what I have adopted] of what you do and leave in your affairs, in yourselves and in others, of what God has urged upon you and commanded you to do, or forbidden you from—"Seeing," meaning by that: possessing sight, nothing of it is hidden from Him; rather He counts it against you and preserves it, so that He repays the one of you who does good for his good, and the one of you who does evil for his evil.

[The portion of the old division from which our copy was taken ends at this point, and there is a note in it reading: "Followed by the discussion on His saying: Guard the prayers and the middle prayer, and may God bless our master Muhammad the Prophet, his family, companions and grant them peace." Then it begins afterwards: "In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate."]

"O Lord, assist me"]]

**The interpretation of His words, ﴿Guard strictly over the prayers, and over the middle prayer﴾**

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: By this, may His remembrance be exalted, He means: be constant in the obligatory prayers at their appointed times, attend to them, keep to them, and (guard) the middle one among them.

The people of ta'wil (interpretation, *ahl al-ta'wil*) have said what we have said about this.

Those who said so:

5378. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq ibn al-Hajjaj narrated to us, saying: Abu Zuhayr narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Muslim, from Masruq, regarding His words, "Guard strictly over the prayers." He said: Guarding them means guarding their time and not neglecting them.

5379. Yahya ibn Ibrahim al-Mas'udi narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to us, from his father, from his grandfather, from al-A'mash, from Muslim, from Masruq, concerning this verse, "Guard strictly over the prayers." So guarding them is praying at their time, and neglecting them is leaving their time.

[The report 5379: He is Yahya ibn Ibrahim ibn Abi Ubayda ibn Ma'n ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud al-Mas'udi. He narrated from his father and grandfather. Al-Nasa'i said: "Sadduq (truthful)." Ibn Hibban mentioned him among the reliable narrators (*al-thiqat*). His biography is in al-Tahdhib.]

* *

Then they differed concerning "the middle prayer." Some of them said: It is the afternoon prayer (*salat al-'asr*).

Those who said so:

5380. Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us. And Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us. Both said: Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Harith, from Ali, who said: "The middle prayer" is the afternoon prayer.

[The report 5380: Abu Ja'far here narrates 113 reports concerning the interpretation of "the middle prayer," between those traced to the Prophet (marfu'), those ending with a Companion (mawquf), and those that are athar (reports of the Companions or Successors), with variations in the transmissions. Some are sound and some weak, and I have not found them comprehensively collected in other than this place among the major collections. He strove, may God reward him, until he reached the limit, then made clear the preponderant and sound view: that it is the afternoon prayer, as is his custom in weighing opinions and choosing what he considers stronger in evidence. The first of them is this report from Ali, which is mawquf (ending with Ali), and its isnad is very weak.
Sufyan is al-Thawri, the Imam.
Abu Ishaq is al-Sab'i, the Imam.
Al-Harith is Ibn Abd Allah al-A'war al-Hamdani, who is very weak, as we explained earlier: 174.
This report was narrated by al-Tahawi in Ma'ani al-Athar 1:103, through Ibrahim ibn Tahman, from Abu Ishaq with this isnad, but he did not mention its wording, referring to the narrations before it. This view from Ali will come with isnads, among which are many sound ones: 5382–5386, 5422–5429, 5444.]

5381. Muhammad ibn Ubayd al-Muharibi narrated to me, saying: Abu al-Ahwas narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, who said: One who heard Ibn Abbas told me, while he was saying: "Guard strictly over the prayers and the middle prayer," he said: the afternoon prayer.

[The report 5381: This is also mawquf on Ibn Abbas. Its isnad is weak because of the unidentified man who heard Ibn Abbas, "one who heard Ibn Abbas," whose identity is not named.
Reports from Ibn Abbas will come by many routes: 5413, 5416, 5433–5435, 5468, 5472–5479, 5481.]

5382. Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Musa'ab ibn Salam narrated to us, from Abu Hayyan, from his father, from Ali, who said: "The middle prayer" is the afternoon prayer.

[The report 5382: This isnad is sound at least. Musa'ab ibn Salam al-Tamimi is truthful; some declared him reliable and others weakened him. From his biography, criticism of him concerns hadiths in which he erred, so what is not shown to be an error by him is accepted. He has a detailed biography in Tarikh Baghdad 13:108–110. Abu Hayyan is al-Taymi al-Kufi, the worshipper, whose name is Yahya ibn Sa'id ibn Hayyan. He is reliable; al-Thawri used to venerate and vouch for him. The authors of the six canonical books narrated from him. His father Sa'id ibn Hayyan is a reliable Successor who narrated from Ali and Abu Hurayra.]

5383. Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn Ulayya narrated to us, saying: Abu Hayyan narrated to us, from his father, from Ali, the like of it.

[The report 5383: This is a sound isnad. Ibn Ulayya's narration is a sound corroboration (*mutaba'a*) of Musa'ab ibn Salam in his previous report.
Ibn Hazm mentioned in al-Muhalla 4:259 something of this meaning: "From Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Qattan, from Abu Hayyan Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Taymi, my father told me: that a questioner asked Ali: 'Which of the prayers, O Commander of the Faithful, is the middle one?' And his crier had called for the afternoon prayer, and he said: 'It is this one.'"]

5384. Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Musa'ab narrated to us, from al-Ajlah, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Harith, who said: I heard Ali say: The middle prayer is the afternoon prayer.

[The report 5384: Al-Ajlah is Ibn Abd Allah al-Kindi. He is reliable, though some criticized him without proof. Al-Bukhari included him in al-Kabir 1/2/68 and mentioned no criticism of him.]

5385. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us, from Anbasa, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Harith, who said: I asked Ali about the middle prayer, and he said: the afternoon prayer.

[The report 5385: Anbasa is Ibn Sa'id ibn al-Dahhak al-Asadi. He has appeared many times, among them: 3356. This isnad and the preceding one are weak, because of al-Harith al-A'war, as we said at 5380.]

5386. Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Hakam al-Misri narrated to me, saying: Abu Zur'a Wahb ibn Rashid narrated to us, saying: Haywa ibn Shurayh informed us, saying: Abu Sakhr informed us that he heard Abu Mu'awiya al-Bajali, from the people of Kufa, saying: I heard Abu al-Sahba' al-Bakri say: I asked Ali ibn Abi Talib about the middle prayer, and he said: It is the afternoon prayer, and it is the one with which Sulayman ibn Dawud (ﷺ) was tested.

[The report 5386: Abu Zur'a, Wahb Allah ibn Rashid, has appeared at 2377 and 2891. In the printed edition here it reads "Wahb ibn Rashid," which is an error; the correct form is in the manuscript. Abu Sakhr is Humayd ibn Ziyad al-Kharrat, owner of the cloak, who lived in Egypt. He is reliable, and Muslim included him in his Sahih.
Abu Mu'awiya al-Bajali: the author of al-Tahdhib gave him a separate entry in al-Kuna 12:240, and related from Abu Ahmad al-Hakim that he is "Ammar al-Duhni," and made that a view. The correct identification is "Ammar ibn Mu'awiya al-Duhni al-Bajali," who is reliable, and Muslim narrated from him in his Sahih. Ibn Abi Hatim also gave him an entry, 3/1/390. "Al-Duhni" is with a dammed dal and a sukun on the ha, a nisba to "Duhn ibn Mu'awiya," a clan of Bajila.
Abu al-Sahba' al-Bakri: I have found no biography of him except in Ibn Abi Hatim's book, 4/2/394, where he says: "Abu al-Sahba' al-Bakri, who asked Ali ibn Abi Talib; Sa'id ibn Jubayr narrated from him." Then he said: "Abu Zur'a was asked about his name, and said: I do not know his name." No criticism of him is mentioned. From this place in al-Tabari we have learned that Abu Mu'awiya al-Bajali also narrated from him, so his obscurity is removed and his person is identified. This isnad is therefore sound.
Ibn Hazm mentioned in al-Muhalla 4:259 something similar in meaning from Ali, through another route, from the narration of Salama ibn Kuhayl, from Abu al-Ahwas, from Ali.
Al-Suyuti mentioned 1:305 something similar as well, and mentioned many who reported it, among them Waki', Ibn Abi Shayba, Abd ibn Humayd, and al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman.]

5387. Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Ibn Ulayya narrated to us, saying: Sulayman al-Taymi informed us. And Humayd ibn Mas'ada narrated to us, saying: Bishr ibn al-Fadl narrated to us, saying: al-Taymi narrated to us, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayra, that he said: "The middle prayer" is the afternoon prayer.

[The report 5387: Abu Salih is al-Samman al-Zayyat, mawla of Juwayriya bint al-Ahmas, whose name is Dhakwan. He is a reliable Successor, and the authors of the six books narrated from him. He is the father of Suhayl, Salih, and Abd Allah, and his children and others, Successors and those after them, narrated from him.
This report was mentioned by Ibn Hazm in al-Muhalla 4:258, "through Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Qattan, from Sulayman al-Taymi, from Abu Salih al-Samman, from Abu Hurayra," as a mawquf (ending with Abu Hurayra). Likewise al-Bayhaqi narrated it 1:460–461, through Ibrahim ibn Abd Allah al-Basri, from al-Ansari, who is Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn al-Muthanna al-Ansari, from Sulayman al-Taymi, who said: "He mentioned it as mawquf." Then he narrated it through Abd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Hanbal, from his father: "Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, from al-Taymi, and mentioned it as mawquf." Then he related from Abd Allah ibn Ahmad, with the same isnad connected to it, that he said: "My father said: This is not Abu Salih al-Samman, nor Badham. This one is Basri; I think he is Mizan, meaning his name is Badham." This suspicion from Imam Ahmad, may God have mercy on him, is negated by the explicit statement of the narrators we mentioned that he is "Abu Salih al-Samman." As for "Abu Salih Mizan," he is another reliable Successor, whose biography is in al-Tahdhib and al-Kabir of al-Bukhari 4/2/67, but they did not mention a narration from him from Abu Hurayra.
Indeed, al-Bayhaqi also narrated it earlier as marfu' (ascribed to the Prophet): he narrated it through Abd al-Wahhab ibn Ata, from Sulayman al-Taymi, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayra, as marfu'.
It will come as marfu' through this route: 5432.
It will come as mawquf through the narration of Sulayman al-Taymi, from Abu Salih: 5390.]

5388. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Suwayd narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Ma'mar, from Abd Allah ibn Uthman ibn Ghanm, from Ibn Lubayba, from Abu Hurayra: "Guard strictly over the prayers and the middle prayer," — indeed, it is the afternoon prayer, indeed, it is the afternoon prayer.

[The report 5388: Suwayd is Ibn Nasr ibn Suwayd al-Marwazi, who has appeared at 2941. Abd Allah ibn Uthman ibn Khuthaym has appeared at 4341, and his grandfather "Khuthaym" is with a dammed kha and an open tha. The printed edition has "Ghanm," which is an error; the correct form is in the manuscript.
Ibn Lubayba is Abd al-Rahman ibn Nafi' ibn Lubayba al-Ta'ifi. I have found no biography of him except in Ibn Abi Hatim 2/2/294, where he says: "He narrated from Abu Hurayra and Ibn Umar. Abd Allah ibn Uthman ibn Khuthaym and Ya'la ibn Ata narrated from him." He is a known Successor, and no criticism is recorded of him, so he is reliable. His name is given by al-Tahawi and al-Suyuti as "Abd al-Rahman ibn Lubayba," and by Ibn Hazm only as "Abd al-Rahman Nafi'," as will come in the takhrij.
The report was narrated by al-Tahawi in Ma'ani al-Athar 1:103–104, through Isma'il ibn Ayyash, from Abd Allah ibn Uthman ibn Khuthaym, "from Abd al-Rahman ibn Lubayba al-Ta'ifi: that he asked Abu Hurayra . . ." and mentioned it at length.
Al-Suyuti mentioned it at length, 1:304, like al-Tahawi's narration, and attributed it to him and to Abd al-Razzaq in al-Musannaf. This is a laxity on his part, because Abd al-Razzaq's narration is very abridged.
Ibn Hazm mentioned it at length in al-Muhalla 4:258–259, "through Isma'il ibn Ishaq, who said: Ali ibn Abd Allah narrated to us, that is Ibn al-Madini, who said: Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, who said: Abd Allah ibn Uthman narrated to us, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Nafi': that Abu Hurayra was asked about the middle prayer? . . ." and mentioned it.
As for the narration of Abd al-Razzaq in al-Musannaf 1:182 (manuscript, photographed), it is very abridged: "Abd al-Razzaq from Ma'mar, from Ibn Khuthaym, from Ibn Lubayba, from Abu Hurayra, who said: It is the afternoon prayer."]

5389. Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Hakam narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to us, and Shu'ayb ibn al-Layth, from al-Layth, from Yazid ibn al-Had, from Ibn Shihab, from Salim ibn Abd Allah, from Abd Allah, who said: I heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ) say: "Whoever misses the afternoon prayer, it is as if he has been deprived of his family and his property." — "Ibn Umar used to regard the afternoon prayer as having the merit of being the one about which the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said that it is the middle prayer.

[The report 5389: This is a very sound isnad. The root of the marfu' hadith, without Ibn Umar's opinion at its end, was narrated by Ahmad in al-Musnad: 4545, from Sufyan, that is Ibn Uyayna, from al-Zuhri, from Salim, from his father, from the Prophet (ﷺ). The authors of the six canonical books narrated it, as in al-Muntaqa: 556.
Ahmad also narrated it by many routes, from Nafi', from Ibn Umar. We explained them in the two addenda: 1299, 1542.
As for the hadith in the form narrated here by Abu Ja'far, with the addition of Abd Allah ibn Umar's opinion: it was narrated by Abd al-Razzaq in al-Musannaf 1:181, from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri, from Salim, from Ibn Umar, similar to it, somewhat abridged.
Al-Suyuti likewise mentioned it 1:304 and attributed it to Abd al-Razzaq and Abd ibn Humayd, and forgot to attribute it to al-Tabari. Something similar will come: 5391. Ibn Hazm mentioned in al-Muhalla 4:259 the opinion of Ibn Umar without mentioning the marfu' hadith. Likewise al-Tahawi in Ma'ani al-Athar 1:101 narrated the statement of Ibn Umar as mawquf on him, explicit in wording: "The middle prayer is the afternoon prayer," through Abd Allah ibn Salih, and through Abd Allah ibn Yusuf, both from al-Layth, from Ibn al-Had, from al-Zuhri, from Salim, from his father.
His saying "wa-tara ahlahu wa-malahu" (deprived his family and his property): it is in the passive voice (*bina' lima lam yusamma fa'iluh*). Ibn al-Athir said: "That is, diminished. It is said: 'wattartuhu,' if I diminished it. As if you made him a single one after he had been many. It was also said: it is from *al-watr*, the crime that a man commits against another, of killing, plundering, or capturing. So what befalls the one who misses the afternoon prayer is likened to one who has killed his close relative, or stripped his family and property. It is narrated with the accusative and the nominative of 'ahl' (family). Whoever puts it in the accusative makes it a second object of *watara*, and implies within it an unnamed object (*maf'ul*) referring to the one who missed the prayer. Whoever puts it in the nominative does not imply one, and makes 'ahl' stand in place of the unnamed agent, because they are the ones struck and taken. So whoever returns the diminishment to the man puts both in the accusative, and whoever returns it to the family and property puts both in the nominative."]

5390. Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to me, saying: Mu'tamir narrated to us, from his father, who said: Abu Salih claimed, from Abu Hurayra, that he said: It is the afternoon prayer.

[The report 5390: This is a repetition of the report 5387. Its proper place would have been after it, or after the one that follows it, because placing it here separates the two hadiths of Ibn Umar, 5389 and 5391, for no need or wisdom. And "Mu'tamir" in this isnad is Ibn Sulayman al-Taymi.]

5391. Ahmad ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Wahb narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle Abd Allah ibn Wahb narrated to me, saying: Amr ibn al-Harith informed me, from Ibn Shihab, from Salim, from his father, from the Messenger of God (ﷺ), similar to it — Ibn Shihab said: Ibn Umar used to regard it as the middle prayer.

[The report 5391: This is a repetition of the hadith 5389, separated from it, without need, by the report of Abu Hurayra. This creates the suspicion that his saying "similar to it" in this hadith refers to the report of Abu Hurayra. That is not so; rather it is a repetition of the marfu' hadith and of the opinion of Ibn Umar that he derived from the hadith.]

5392. Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Affan ibn Muslim narrated to us, saying: Hammam narrated to us, from Qatada, from al-Hasan, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: "The middle prayer" is the afternoon prayer.

[The report 5392: Affan ibn Muslim ibn Abd Allah al-Saffar is reliable, one of the teachers of Ahmad and al-Bukhari, and the authors of the six books narrated from him. He has a good biography in Tarikh Baghdad 12:269–277. Al-Hasan is al-Basri. Ibn Abi Hatim in al-Marasil, p. 15, narrated from Ali ibn al-Madini that al-Hasan did not hear anything from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, and likewise he narrated something similar from Bahz. So this report is disconnected (*munqati'*) for this reason.
This report was narrated by al-Tahawi in Ma'ani al-Athar 1:103, from Ibn Marzuq, from Affan, from Hammam, with this isnad. He did not mention its wording, referring to what came before it.
It will come at 5451, a narration from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri that it is the noon prayer (*al-zuhr*). This is what al-Suyuti mentioned 1:302, quoting al-Tabari.
Abu Sa'id is among those from whom it is narrated that it is the noon prayer, and it is narrated from him that it is the afternoon prayer, as in Ibn Kathir 1:577, 578, and Fath al-Bari 8:146. The hafiz (Ibn Hajar) in al-Fath mentioned that Ahmad narrated from Abu Sa'id, in his own words, that it is the afternoon prayer. I did not find this narration in the Musnad, so I do not know whether it is in another place incidentally, outside the Musnad of Abu Sa'id, or in another book of Ahmad's other than the Musnad? Although the presumption of the unqualified term is that the Musnad is meant!]

5393. Muhammad ibn Ma'mar narrated to me, saying: Ibn Amir narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Abi Humayd narrated to us, from Humayda, daughter of Abu Yunus, a freedwoman of A'isha, who said: A'isha bequeathed her belongings to us, and we found in A'isha's copy of the Qur'an: "Guard strictly over the prayers and the middle prayer, and it is the afternoon prayer, and stand before God in devotion."

[The report 5393: "Ibn Amir": this is how it is written in the manuscript and the printed edition! I do not know who he is. Our view is that it is an error, and the correct form is "Abu Amir," who is "Abu Amir al-Aqadi, Abd al-Malik ibn Amr," who narrates from Muhammad ibn Abi Humayd, and from whom Muhammad ibn Ma'mar, the teacher of al-Tabari, narrates.]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 238 (part 2 of 7):

Ḥumayda, daughter of Abu Yunus, a freedwoman of ʿĀʾisha: I do not know who she is or what her circumstances were. I have found no mention of her in any of the sources before me, nor in Ibn Ḥibbān's *Kitāb al-Thiqāt*, so her case is truly obscure. Two reports will come "from Abu Yunus, the freedman of ʿĀʾisha" (5466, 5467), and he is a known Successor (*tābiʿī*), as will come, so perhaps this is his daughter. al-Suyuti (1:304) mentioned a report similar to this one, as follows: "Waki' related from Ḥumayda, who said: I read in the Muṣḥaf of ʿĀʾisha: ﴿Guard the prayers and the middle prayer﴾, the afternoon prayer."

Ibn Abi Dawud also related it in *al-Maṣāḥif* (p. 84), from Muḥammad ibn Maʿmar, from Abu ʿĀṣim, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ibn Abi Ḥumayd, who said: "Ḥumayda informed me," but he did not mention her lineage.

Further reports from ʿĀʾisha will come: 5394–5397, 5400, 5401, 5466, 5467.

5394. Saʿid ibn Yaḥya al-Umawi related to me, saying: my father related to us, saying: Ibn Jurayj related to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥman informed us that his mother, Umm Ḥumayd bint ʿAbd al-Raḥman, asked ʿĀʾisha about the middle prayer. She said: "We used to recite it in the first reading during the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): ﴿Guard the prayers and the middle prayer, [Abu Jaʿfar said: he said:] the afternoon prayer, and stand before Allah in devotion﴾."

5395. ʿAbbas ibn Muḥammad related to me, saying: Ḥajjaj related to us, saying: Ibn Jurayj said: ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥman informed me, from his mother Umm Ḥumayd bint ʿAbd al-Raḥman: that she asked ʿĀʾisha, and he related a similar report, except that he said: ﴿Guard the prayers and the middle prayer and the afternoon prayer﴾.

[Notes on 5394–5395: ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥman ibn Khālid ibn Usayd (with a fatḥa on the hamza), al-Qurashi, is trustworthy (*thiqah*). Ibn Abi Ḥatim recorded his biography (2/2/355), saying: "He related from his mother Umm Ḥumayd, who said: I heard ʿĀʾisha. Ibn Jurayj related from him." al-ʿUqayli erred by not raising his lineage and said: "He is from the descendants of ʿAttab ibn Usayd." al-Ḥāfiẓ corrected this in *Lisan al-Mizan* (4:65–66), and quoted his biography from Ibn Ḥibbān's *Thiqat*, in terms similar to Ibn Abi Ḥatim's statement.

As for his mother, "Umm Ḥumayd bint ʿAbd al-Raḥman," I have not verified her biography. In *al-Tahdhib* (12:465) her entry reads: "Umm Ḥumayd, also called Umm Ḥumayda, daughter of ʿAbd al-Raḥman, from ʿĀʾisha; Ibn Jurayj related from her father, from her." If she is not her, then I do not know.

These two reports have the same meaning, except that in the first, "the afternoon prayer" appears without the *wāw*, while in the second it appears with the *wāw*: *wa-ṣalāt al-ʿaṣr*. In the version with the *wāw*, this conjunction is of the type where the attribute is coordinated with the thing described, not of the type that indicates a distinct item. This is shown by the later report (5397): "and it is the afternoon prayer." See *Fath al-Bari* (8:148) and what comes at 5465–5468.

This meaning, from ʿĀʾisha, was also related by ʿAbd al-Razzaq in *al-Muṣannaf* (1:182), from Ibn Jurayj, with this same chain, but he did not mention its wording, referring instead to a previous report that contains the *wāw*.

Ibn Ḥazm also related it in *al-Muḥalla* (4:257–258), with its chain, through ʿAbd al-Razzaq.

Ibn Abi Dawud related it in *al-Maṣāḥif* (p. 84) with two chains: one through Abu ʿĀṣim and one through Ḥajjaj, both from Ibn Jurayj, with the same wording. al-Ṭaḥawi related it in *Maʿani al-Athar* (1:102), through al-Ḥajjaj ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Jurayj.]

5396. Sufyan ibn Waki' related to us, saying: my father related to us, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr Abu Sahl al-Ansari, from al-Qasim ibn Muḥammad, from ʿĀʾisha, concerning His words: "the middle prayer." She said: the afternoon prayer.

[Notes on 5396: Abu Sahl Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr al-Ansari al-Waqifi al-Basri: in our view the stronger position is that he is trustworthy. al-Bukhari recorded him in *al-Kabir* (1/1/194) and mentioned no criticism of him. Ibn Ḥibbān listed him among the trustworthy and then among the weak. Ibn Abi Ḥatim recorded him (4/1/32) and mentioned only the statements that criticize him. Ibn Ḥazm said in *al-Muḥalla* (4:256): "Trustworthy. Ibn Mahdi, Waki', Maʿmar, ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Mubarak and others related from him."

In the printed edition appears: "Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr wa-Abu Sahl al-Ansari" — with an added *wāw* before the kunya — which is an error, and it also occurs in the manuscript.

Also in the printed edition: "qāla ṣalāt al-ʿaṣr" ("he said: the afternoon prayer"). This is a clear error; the correct reading is *qālat* ("she said").

Ibn Ḥazm mentioned in *al-Muḥalla* (4:256) that he related it "through ʿAbd al-Raḥman ibn Mahdi, from Abu Sahl Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr al-Ansari, from Muḥammad ibn Abi Bakr, from ʿĀʾisha, the Mother of the Believers, who said: The middle prayer is the afternoon prayer." Ibn Ḥazm then said: "This is the most authentic report from ʿĀʾisha."

As for his saying in the chain, "from Muḥammad ibn Abi Bakr," this is how it appears in *al-Muḥalla*. I do not know whether the narration from Ibn Mahdi is actually like this, which would mean Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr related it from al-Qasim ibn Muḥammad and from his father! Or is it an error of the copyists of *al-Muḥalla*? I incline to think it is an error, because Muḥammad ibn Abi Bakr al-Siddiq died long ago, the teachers of Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr were all of a generation close to al-Qasim ibn Muḥammad, and they did not mention Muḥammad ibn Abi Bakr among the teachers of Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr. Moreover, they never mentioned any transmitter from Muḥammad ibn Abi Bakr other than his son al-Qasim ibn Muḥammad.
