However, Ibn Ḥazm later refers (p. 259) to al-Qasim ibn Muḥammad's report from ʿĀʾisha, "similar to that." So it appears the error is old, in the books from which Ibn Ḥazm quoted.]

5397. al-Muthanna related to me, saying: al-Ḥajjaj related to us, saying: Ḥammad related to us, from Hisham ibn ʿUrwa, from his father, who said: In the Muṣḥaf of ʿĀʾisha there was: ﴿Guard the prayers and the middle prayer, and it is the afternoon prayer﴾.

[Notes on 5397: al-Muthanna, Tabari's teacher, is Ibn Ibrahim al-Amuli, as we explained earlier (186, 187). In Ibn Kathir, when quoting this passage, it appears as "Ibn al-Muthanna," which is an error.

al-Ḥajjaj is Ibn al-Minhal al-Anmati, as passed in the report of al-Muthanna from him (682, 1682, 1683). Ḥammad is Ibn Salama, as shown by the report of Ibn Ḥazm which we will mention.

Ibn Kathir quoted this report from this passage (1:580). al-Ḥafiẓ quoted it in *Fath al-Bari* (8:146), and al-Suyuti (1:304). They did not attribute it to anyone other than al-Tabari.

Ibn Ḥazm mentioned it in *al-Muḥalla* (4:254), "from Ḥammad ibn Salama, from Hisham ibn ʿUrwa." But in it appears: "wa-ṣalāt al-ʿaṣr," without the word "hiya" ("it is").

Likewise it appears in similar form in Ibn Abi Dawud's *Kitab al-Maṣāḥif* (p. 83), through Yazid, from Ḥammad, from Hisham, from his father.

ʿAbd al-Razzaq related it in *al-Muṣannaf* (1:182), from Maʿmar, from Hisham ibn ʿUrwa, who said: "I read in the Muṣḥaf of ʿĀʾisha, may Allah be pleased with her: ﴿Guard the prayers and the middle prayer and the afternoon prayer, and stand before Allah in devotion﴾." He did not mention the word "hiya." He made it a reading of Hisham himself from the Muṣḥaf of ʿĀʾisha, not a report from his father.

al-Suyuti mentioned this report (1:302) and attributed it to ʿAbd al-Razzaq and Ibn Abi Dawud. I have not found it in *Kitab al-Maṣāḥif*.]

5398. Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Waki' related to us, from Dawud ibn Qays, who said: ʿAbd Allah ibn Rafiʿ, freedman of Umm Salama, told me, saying: Umm Salama instructed me to write a Muṣḥaf for her, and she said: "When you reach the verse about the prayer, inform me." I informed her, and she dictated to me: ﴿Guard the prayers and the middle prayer, the afternoon prayer﴾.

[Notes on 5398: Dawud ibn Qays al-Farra' al-Dabbagh al-Madani: trustworthy and a memorizer, as al-Shafiʿi said. Ibn al-Madini and others also deemed him trustworthy.

ʿAbd Allah ibn Rafiʿ al-Makhzumi, Abu Rafiʿ al-Madani, freedman of Umm Salama, Mother of the Believers, by manumission: a trustworthy Successor. This report was related by ʿAbd al-Razzaq in *al-Muṣannaf* (1:182), from Dawud ibn Qays, but with the wording "wa-ṣalāt al-ʿaṣr," with the *wāw* added.

It is also so in *al-Muḥalla* (4:254), quoting ʿAbd al-Razzaq.

al-Suyuti likewise quoted it (1:303). He attributed it to Waki', Ibn Abi Shayba in *al-Muṣannaf*, ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Dawud in *al-Maṣāḥif*, and Ibn al-Mundhir, but he forgot to attribute it to ʿAbd al-Razzaq.

It appears in Ibn Abi Dawud's *Kitab al-Maṣāḥif* (pp. 87–88), through Ibn Nafiʿ, through Waki', and through Sufyan, all three from Dawud ibn Qays. In the first two chains it has the *wāw*, and in the third it lacks it.

al-Ḥafiẓ pointed to it in *Fath al-Bari* (8:148) and attributed it only to Ibn al-Mundhir. In it appears "ʿUbayd Allah ibn Rafiʿ," which is an error by a copyist or printer.]

5399. Ḥaddathana ʿAn ʿAmmar, who said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar related to us, from his father, who said: al-Ḥasan used to say: "The middle prayer is the afternoon prayer."

[Notes on 5399: This is a statement of al-Ḥasan, with a weak, unknown chain, since al-Tabari says: "I was told from ʿAmmar."

A different chain from al-Ḥasan will come (5419). A report similar in meaning from al-Ḥasan, as a *marfuʿ mursal* (a report attributed to the Prophet (ﷺ) whose chain omits the companion), will come (5441).]

5400. Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla related to us, saying: al-Muʿtamir related to us, from his father, who said: Qatada related to us, from Abu Ayyub, from ʿĀʾisha, that she said: "The middle prayer is the afternoon prayer."

5401. Muḥammad ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Yahya related to us, from Sulayman al-Taymi, from Qatada, from Abu Ayyub, from ʿĀʾisha, a similar statement.

[Notes on 5400–5401: al-Muʿtamir in the first chain is Ibn Sulayman al-Taymi. Yahya in the second chain is Ibn Saʿid al-Qattan.

Abu Ayyub is Yahya ibn Malik al-Maraghi al-Ataki al-Azdi. He is a trustworthy and reliable Successor.

"al-Maraghi" is a nisba to "al-Maraghh," a clan of the Azd. "al-ʿAtaki" is a nisba to "al-ʿAtik," a son of al-Azd. It appears that al-Maraghh is from al-ʿAtik. Ibn Ḥazm erred in *al-Muḥalla* by stating that Abu Ayyub's name was "Yahya ibn Yazid." This contradicts what is in the registers. His name is in fact confirmed in Sahih Muslim (1:170) in another hadith: "from Qatada, from Abu Ayyub, whose name is Yahya ibn Malik al-Azdi, and it is said al-Maraghi. al-Maraghh is a clan of the Azd."

Ibn Ḥazm related this report in *al-Muḥalla* (4:259), from Yahya ibn Saʿid al-Qattan, from Sulayman al-Taymi, with this chain. al-Suyuti mentioned it (1:305), saying: "Ibn Abi Shayba and Ibn Jarir related it through several chains from ʿĀʾisha."]

5402. Ḥaddathana Ibn Ḥumayd, who said: Ḥakkam related to us, who said: ʿAnbasa related to us, from al-Mughira, from Ibrahim, who said: It used to be said: "The middle prayer is the afternoon prayer."

5403. I was told from ʿAmmar, who said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar related to us, from his father, from al-Rabiʿ, who said: It was mentioned to us from ʿAli ibn Abi Talib that he said: "The middle prayer is the afternoon prayer."

5404. Yaʿqub ibn Ibrahim related to me, saying: Hushaym related to us, from Abu Bishr, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, who said: "The middle prayer is the afternoon prayer."

5405. Yaʿqub related to me, saying: Hushaym related to us, from Abu Bishr, from Salim, from Ḥafsa: that she instructed a man who was writing a Muṣḥaf for her, and she said: "When you reach this place, inform me." When he reached "Guard the prayers and the middle prayer," she said: "Write: the afternoon prayer."

[Notes on 5405: Abu Bishr is Jaʿfar ibn Abi Waḥshiya, who passed in (3348). This report will come in full (5461), through Shuʿba, from Abu Bishr, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Yazid al-Azdi, from Salim. There it reads: "wa-ṣalāt al-ʿaṣr." It thus becomes clear that this chain is disconnected (*munqaṭiʿ*) between Abu Bishr and Salim. We will leave discussion of it until that place, God willing.]

5406. al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Ḥajjaj ibn al-Minhal related to us, saying: Ḥammad ibn Salama related to us, saying: ʿUbayd Allah ibn ʿUmar informed us, from Nafiʿ, from Ḥafsa, wife of the Prophet (ﷺ): that she said to the scribe of her Muṣḥaf: "When you reach the times of the prayers, inform me, so that I may tell you what I heard from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)." When he informed her, she said: "Write, for I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: ﴿Guard the prayers and the middle prayer, and it is the afternoon prayer﴾."

[Notes on 5406: Nafiʿ, freedman of Ibn ʿUmar: a trustworthy Successor. However, his report from Ḥafsa bint ʿUmar is *mursal* (disconnected, i.e., with a missing link), as Ibn Abi Ḥatim stated explicitly in *al-Marasil* (p. 81), and it is likewise reported from him in *al-Tahdhib*. This report will also come (5463), through Asad ibn Musa, from Ḥammad ibn Salama, with this chain. In it: "wa-ṣalāt al-ʿaṣr," in place of "wa-hiya ṣalāt al-ʿaṣr."

Likewise it will come (5462), through ʿAbd al-Wahhab, from ʿUbayd Allah. What shows the disconnection of this chain and the two that follow is that Ibn Abi Dawud related it in *al-Maṣāḥif* (p. 85), from Muḥammad ibn Bashshar, who said: "We did not write it from anyone else": "Ḥaddathana Ḥajjaj ibn Minhal, Ḥaddathana Ḥammad ibn Salama, from ʿUbayd Allah, from Nafiʿ, from Ibn ʿUmar, from Ḥafsa..." In it too: "wa-ṣalāt al-ʿaṣr."

Then he related it (pp. 85–86) from his paternal uncle and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim, who said: "Ḥaddathana Ḥajjaj, Ḥaddathana Ḥammad, who said: ʿUbayd Allah ibn ʿUmar informed us, from Nafiʿ, from Ḥafsa, similarly." It did not mention Ibn ʿUmar in it.

It thus becomes clear that the chain through Ḥajjaj ibn al-Minhal varied, as to whether it was connected or disconnected. A connection is an added reliable detail, and so it is accepted. ʿAbd al-Razzaq related something similar in *al-Muṣannaf* (1:182), from Ibn Jurayj, who said: "Nafiʿ informed me that Ḥafsa..." In it too: "wa-ṣalāt al-ʿaṣr." This report of Ibn Jurayj was mentioned by Ibn Ḥazm in *al-Muḥalla* (4:253). We note here that in commenting on it we pointed to this Tabari report (5406) and said there: "Its chain is very sound." It has now become clear to us that this was an error, and that the chain is weak because of its disconnection, as we said. Indeed, the report of Ibn Abi Dawud, which contains the addition "from Ibn ʿUmar," shows the report to be connected, but it is sound only in that report, not in this report of Tabari.

Further chains from Ḥafsa will come: 5458, 5464, 5465, 5470.]

5407. al-Muthanna related to me, saying: al-Ḥajjaj related to us, saying: Ḥammad related to us, from ʿAsim ibn Bahdala, from Zirr ibn Ḥubaysh, who said: "The middle prayer is the afternoon prayer."

5408. Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Saʿid related to us, from Qatada, concerning his words: ﴿Guard the prayers and the middle prayer﴾: "We used to report that it is the afternoon prayer, preceded by two prayers of the day and followed by two prayers of the night."

5409. Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Hushaym related to us, saying: Juwaybir informed us, from al-Ḍaḥḥak, concerning His words: ﴿Guard the prayers and the middle prayer﴾. He said: "They were commanded to guard the prayers. He singled out the afternoon, 'and the middle prayer,' meaning the afternoon."

[Notes on 5409: In the printed edition "Jubayr" appears instead of "Juwaybir." This is an error.]

5410. I was told from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Muʿadh say: ʿUbayd Allah ibn Sulayman informed us, who said: I heard al-Ḍaḥḥak say concerning His words: ﴿And the middle prayer﴾: "It is the afternoon prayer."

[Notes on 5410: In the manuscript and the printed edition appears "ʿAbd Allah ibn Sulayman," which is an error. This is a chain that recurs in the tafsir; its nearest occurrence is number 5356.]

5411. I was told from ʿAmmar, who said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar related to us, from his father, from al-Rabiʿ, who said: It was mentioned to us from ʿAli ibn Abi Talib that he said: "The middle prayer is the afternoon prayer."

5412. Muḥammad ibn Saʿd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas: ﴿Guard the prayers﴾ (meaning the obligatory prayers) ﴿and the middle prayer﴾, meaning the afternoon prayer.

5413. Ahmad ibn Ishaq al-Ahwazi related to me, saying: Abu Ahmad related to us, saying: Qays related to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Rizin ibn ʿUbayd, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: I heard him say: ﴿Guard the prayers and the middle prayer﴾, and he said: "The afternoon prayer."

[Notes on 5413: Abu Ahmad is al-Zubayri, Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Zubayr al-Asadi. Qays is Ibn al-Rabiʿ al-Asadi al-Kufi; we judged him trustworthy (4842, and in the *Musnad*: 661, 7115).

Abu Ishaq is al-Subayʿi. In the printed edition it reads "ʿan Ibn Ishaq," which is an error by a copyist or printer. Rizin ibn ʿUbayd: a trustworthy Successor. al-Bukhari recorded him in *al-Kabir* (2/1/296), and Ibn Abi Ḥatim (1/2/507), and neither mentioned any criticism of him. This is sufficient to establish his reliability.

This report will come (5416) through Isra'il, who is Ibn Yunus ibn Abi Ishaq al-Subayʿi, from his grandfather Abu Ishaq.

Likewise al-Bukhari related it in *al-Kabir*, in the biography of "Rizin," through Isra'il.

Likewise al-Ṭaḥawi related it in *Maʿani al-Athar* (1:102), through Isra'il. An error occurred in it regarding the name of the Successor.

al-Suyuti mentioned it (1:305), "from Rizin ibn ʿUbayd: that he heard Ibn ʿAbbas recite it: 'and the middle prayer, the afternoon prayer.'" He mentioned it in this way, attributing it to Abu ʿUbayd, ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, al-Bukhari in his *Tarikh*, Ibn Jarir, and al-Ṭaḥawi. In this there is laxity, for the wording in al-Bukhari, al-Tabari, and al-Ṭaḥawi is not an explicit statement about the recitation of the verse in that way.

al-Haythami mentioned in *Majmaʿ al-Zawaʾid* (1:309) that al-Bazzar related from Ibn ʿAbbas: "that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'The middle prayer is the afternoon prayer.'" al-Haythami said: "Its narrators are trustworthy."]

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 238 (part 3 of 7):**

**5414.** Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to me, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Isra'il narrated to us, from Thuwayr, from Mujahid, who said: "The middle prayer (al-Salat al-Wusta) is the afternoon prayer (Salat al-'Asr)."

[[Report 5414: Thuwayr (diminutive form): he is Ibn Abi Fakhita, and he is very weak, as has passed in 3212. In the printed edition it is written "Thawr," which is an error; the correct reading is preserved in the manuscript.]]

**5415.** Yahya ibn Abi Talib narrated to me, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Juwaybir informed us, from al-Dahhak, who said: "The middle prayer is the afternoon prayer."

**5416.** Ahmad ibn Hazim narrated to us, saying: Abu Nu'aym narrated to us, saying: Isra'il narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Razin ibn Ubayd, who said: "I heard Ibn 'Abbas say: It is the afternoon prayer."

[[Report 5416: This is a repetition of report 5413, with the same meaning. Its discussion has already been given in detail.]]

**5417.** Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi 'Adi narrated to us, saying: Isma'il ibn Muslim informed us, from al-Hasan, from Samura, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "The middle prayer is the afternoon prayer."

[[Report 5417: Isma'il ibn Muslim is al-Makki, a Basran who settled in Mecca. His narration is, in our view, good (hasan), as we explained in the Musnad in another hadith (1689), and in the commentary on al-Tirmidhi (1:454). Al-Hasan is al-Basri. Samura is Ibn Jundab, the well-known Companion.

Whether al-Hasan heard from Samura has been the subject of a lengthy discussion among the hadith scholars. The preponderant view is that he did hear from him, as Ibn al-Madini, al-Bukhari, al-Tirmidhi, al-Hakim and others held. See our commentary on al-Tirmidhi (1:343), al-Jawhar al-Naqi (5:288-289), 'Awn al-Ma'bud (1:369-370), and other references.

The hadith will come with other chains of narration: 5438-5439.

Ahmad narrated it in the Musnad (5:7, 12, 13) with several chains, through Sa'id, namely Ibn Abi 'Aruba, from Qatada, from al-Hasan, from Samura.

Likewise al-Tirmidhi narrated it (no. 182 in our edition, Kitab al-Salat, 1:159-160 in the Mubarakfuri edition), and also in Kitab al-Tafsir (4:77 in the Mubarakfuri edition), through Ibn Abi 'Aruba. In the first place he said: "The hadith of Samura concerning the middle prayer is a good (hasan) hadith." In the second he said: "This is a good sound (hasan sahih) hadith."

Likewise al-Tahawi narrated it in Ma'ani al-Athar (1:103), through Rawh ibn 'Ubada, from Ibn Abi 'Aruba, with the same chain, as a marfu' (attributed to the Prophet) report. He did not mention its wording, referring to an earlier narration.

Al-Bayhaqi narrated it (1:460) through Hammam, from Qatada, from al-Hasan, from Samura.

Ibn Kathir (1:578-579) mentioned it from the narrations of the Musnad with their chains. Al-Suyuti (1:304) mentioned it and added its attribution to Ibn Abi Shayba, 'Abd ibn Humayd and al-Tabarani. Before it he mentioned, with the wording: "The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: Guard the prayers, and the middle prayer, and he named it for us, and it is only the afternoon prayer." He attributed this to Ahmad, Ibn Jarir and al-Tabarani. Thus he said. I have not found this wording in the Musnad, nor in the Tafsir of al-Tabari, although it agrees in meaning with what we have in both.]]

**5418.** Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Wahb ibn Jarir narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, saying: I heard Yahya ibn Ayyub relating, from Yazid ibn Abi Habib, from Marthad ibn Mikhmar, from Sa'id ibn al-Hakam, who said: "I heard Abu Ayyub say: The middle prayer is the afternoon prayer."

[[Report 5418: Marthad ibn Mikhmar: Ibn Abi Hatim translated him (4/1/366), saying: "Marthad ibn Mikhmar narrated from Sa'id ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Ayyub; Yazid ibn Abi Habib narrated from him." I have found no other biography of him. It is strange that al-Bukhari did not give him an entry, although he referred to him twice in pointing to this report, as will come, and his name appears in al-Dhahabi's al-Mushtabih (p. 6) as "Marra ibn Humayr"! This is an error. 

Sa'id ibn al-Hakam: a reliable Successor (tabi'i). Al-Bukhari translated him in al-Kabir (2/1/425), saying: "He heard Abu Ayyub: 'The middle is the afternoon.' Wahb said: My father narrated to us, I heard Yahya ibn Ayyub, from Yazid ibn Abi Habib, from Marra. It is said Sa'd ibn Ahkam." This is an allusion to this chain, since al-Tabari narrated it here through Wahb ibn Jarir from his father.

Then al-Bukhari translated him (2/2/53), saying: "Sa'd ibn Ahkam, from al-Sakfaka, a clan of Yahsib, then of Himyar; he heard Abu Ayyub. Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated it from his father, from Ibn Ishaq, from Yazid ibn Abi Habib, from Marra. Wahb ibn Jarir said, from his father." Then the discussion breaks off, and it appears there is a lacuna, whose content can be understood from the previous entry.

Ibn Abi Hatim translated him (2/1/13): "Sa'id ibn al-Hakam, an Egyptian, narrated from Abu Ayyub. Yazid ibn Abi Habib narrated from Marthad ibn Mikhmar, from him."

Ibn Abi Hatim translated him again (2/1/81-82): "Sa'd ibn al-Hakam, an Egyptian, from Himyar..." and then mentioned much the same as he said for "Sa'id."

What I have no doubt about is that Ibn Abi Hatim erred in the second entry, since he produced a third opinion that no one held, namely "Sa'd ibn al-Hakam." The disagreement is only between "Sa'id ibn al-Hakam" and "Sa'd ibn Ahkam," as al-Bukhari recorded. Al-Allama al-Shaykh 'Abd al-Rahman al-Yamani, in his note on the first passage of al-Tarikh al-Kabir, stated that Ibn Hibban mentioned him under both views, as did al-Bukhari, that the Amir Ibn Makula mentioned him likewise, and that he was also narrated by "Ibn Lahi'a, from Yazid ibn Abi Habib, from Marthad ibn Mikhmar al-Himyari, from Sa'd ibn Ahkam."

Likewise, al-Dhahabi in al-Mushtabih (p. 6) and Ibn Hajar in Tahrir al-Mushtabih (manuscript, photocopy in our possession) explicitly stated the vocalization "Sa'd ibn Ahkam."

In my view the narration "Sa'd ibn Ahkam" is preponderant and closer to the correct form, because two narrators have it thus from Yazid ibn Abi Habib: Ibn Ishaq, as al-Bukhari mentioned, and Ibn Lahi'a, as Ibn Makula mentioned. Yahya ibn Ayyub alone named him "Sa'id ibn al-Hakam," and two are more worthy of memorization and precision than one.

The report was narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Kabir, by allusion, as we mentioned. Al-Suyuti (1:305) mentioned it and added its attribution to Ibn al-Mundhir. Abu Ayyub is al-Ansari al-Khazraji, the illustrious Companion. His name is Khalid ibn Zayd.]]

**5419.** Ibn Sufyan narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, from Mubarak, from al-Hasan, who said: "The middle prayer is the afternoon prayer."

[[Report 5419: Ibn Sufyan, the teacher of al-Tabari: this is how it stands in the manuscript and the printed edition, and we do not know who he is. It may be a corruption of "Ibn Sinan," who is "Muhammad ibn Sinan al-Qazzaz." His narration from Abu 'Asim has passed, and al-Tabari's narration from him appears at 157, 485, 702.]]

* *

**The basis (ʿilla) of those who held this view is as follows:**

**5420.** Muhammad ibn Ma'mar narrated it to me, saying: Abu 'Amir narrated to us, saying: Muhammad, that is Ibn Talha, narrated to us, from Zubayd, from Murra, from 'Abd Allah, who said: "The idolaters occupied the Messenger of God (ﷺ) from the afternoon prayer until it turned yellow, or red." He said: "They occupied us from the middle prayer; may God fill their bellies and their graves with fire."

[[Hadith 5420: Abu 'Amir: he is al-'Aqadi, 'Abd al-Malik ibn 'Amr.
Muhammad ibn Talha ibn Musarrif al-Yami, has passed at 5088.
Zubayd (diminutive): he is Ibn al-Harith ibn 'Abd al-Karim, has passed at 2521.
Murra: he is Murra al-Tayyib, Ibn Sharahil al-Hamdani, also passed at 2521. 'Abd Allah is Ibn Mas'ud, the great Companion.

Al-Tabari narrated this hadith here through Abu 'Amir al-'Aqadi. He will narrate it again afterwards at 5421, through Yazid ibn Harun, and then at 5430, through Thabit ibn Muhammad. All three narrate from Muhammad ibn Talha ibn Musarrif.

Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi narrated it in his Musnad (366), from Muhammad ibn Talha, in abridged form. Ahmad narrated it in the Musnad (3716), from Yazid, that is Ibn Harun; (3829), from Khalaf ibn al-Walid; and (4365), from Hashim, that is Ibn al-Qasim Abu al-Nadr. All three narrate from Muhammad ibn Talha, in full and abridged versions.

Muslim narrated it (1:174), from 'Awn ibn Salam, from Muhammad ibn Talha.

Al-Tirmidhi narrated it (181 in our edition), abridged, through al-Tayalisi and Abu al-Nadr, both from Muhammad ibn Talha. Al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a good sound (hasan sahih) hadith."

Ibn Majah narrated it (686), through 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi and Yazid ibn Harun, both from Muhammad ibn Talha.

Al-Bayhaqi narrated it (1:460), through al-Fadl ibn Dukayn and 'Awn ibn Salam, both from Muhammad ibn Talha. Al-Suyuti (1:303) mentioned it, attributing it to some of those we have mentioned, and to 'Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn al-Mundhir.]]

**5421.** Ahmad ibn Sinan al-Wasiti narrated to me, saying: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Talha informed us, from Zubayd, from Murra, from 'Abd Allah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), in a similar manner, except that he said: "May God fill their houses and their graves with fire, as they occupied us from the middle prayer."

[[Hadith 5421: Ahmad ibn Sinan al-Wasiti, al-Qattan, the hafiz, teacher of al-Tabari: he is reliable, precise, and among the authorities. The two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim) and others narrated from him. He is biographed in Tadhkirat al-Huffaz (2:93-94). The hadith repeats the preceding one.]]

**5422.** Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, both saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'ba narrated to us, saying: I heard Qatada relating, from Abu Hassan, from 'Ubayda al-Salmani, from 'Ali, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said on the day of the Confederates (al-Ahzab): "They occupied us from the middle prayer until the sun set; may God fill their graves and their houses with fire," or "their bellies with fire." Shu'ba was uncertain whether it was "bellies" or "houses."

[[Hadith 5422: Abu Hassan al-A'raj: his name is "Muslim," with no mention of his father's name, in all the sources, except the Tahdhib and its branches and the Men of the Two Sahihs, where there is the addition "ibn 'Abd Allah." He is a reliable Successor, whose narrations Muslim included in his Sahih.
'Ubayda (with a fatha on the 'ayn): he is al-Salmani, whose biography has passed at 245.
The hadith was narrated by Muslim (1:174), through Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Muhammad ibn Bashshar, the teachers of al-Tabari here, with this chain.
Ibn Hazm narrated it in al-Muhalla (4:252), through Muslim.
Ahmad narrated it in the Musnad (1150), from Muhammad ibn Ja'far, from Shu'ba, with this chain.
Then he narrated it (1151) from Hajjaj, that is Ibn Muhammad, from Shu'ba.
Al-Nasa'i narrated it abridged (1:83), through Khalid, from Shu'ba.
The hadith will come from Abu Hassan's narration from 'Ubayda at 5429 and 5444. The saying of 'Ali, "The middle prayer is the afternoon prayer," has passed at 4380. We have pointed out the rest of the narrations to come from his hadith, including this one.]]

**5423.** Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from 'Asim, from Zirr, who said: I said to 'Ubayda al-Salmani: "Ask 'Ali ibn Abi Talib about the middle prayer." He asked him, and he said: "We used to consider it the dawn prayer, or the morning prayer, until I heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ) say on the day of the Confederates: 'They occupied us from the middle prayer, the afternoon prayer! May God fill their graves and their bellies with fire!'"

[[Hadith 5423: 'Abd al-Rahman: he is Ibn Mahdi. Sufyan: he is al-Thawri. 'Asim: he is Ibn Abi al-Najud. Zirr: he is Ibn Hubaysh.
This hadith is from the narration of Zirr ibn Hubaysh from 'Ali, in the presence of the question of 'Ubayda al-Salmani and the answer of 'Ali. It supports the narration of Abu Hassan al-A'raj from 'Ubayda (5422).
'Abd al-Razzaq narrated it in al-Musannaf (1:181-182), from al-Thawri, from 'Asim, from Zirr ibn Hubaysh, with this chain. It will come at 5428, from the narration of Isra'il, from 'Asim.
Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it, as transmitted by Ibn Kathir (1:578), from Ahmad ibn Sinan, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi, with this chain. Then Ibn Kathir said: "Ibn Jarir narrated it from Bundar, from Ibn Mahdi, with it." That is, this chain. Bundar is Muhammad ibn Bashshar, the teacher of al-Tabari.
Ibn Hazm narrated it in al-Muhalla (4:252-253), with his chain to Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr al-Muqaddami, from Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Qattan and 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi, both from Sufyan al-Thawri, with it.
Al-Bayhaqi narrated it (1:460), through Muhammad ibn Kathir, from Sufyan, from 'Asim, from Zirr.
Ibn Majah narrated it (684), abridged, through Hammad ibn Zayd, from 'Asim, from Zirr.
Ibn Hazm pointed to the narration of Hammad ibn Zayd (al-Muhalla 4:253).
Al-Suyuti (1:303) mentioned it and added its attribution to Ibn Abi Shayba, 'Abd ibn Humayd, al-Bukhari, al-Nasa'i, and Ibn al-Mundhir. This is a laxity on his part in attributing it to al-Bukhari, for I have not found it in al-Bukhari except from the narration of Ibn Sirin from 'Ubayda, as will come at 5427.
The chain of this hadith, from the narration of Sufyan, from 'Asim, from Zirr, is a sound chain. Nevertheless, Imam Ahmad did not narrate it in the Musnad through this route with a sound chain. Rather, he narrated something similar in abridged form (1287), through Shu'ba, from Jabir, that is al-Ju'fi, from 'Asim, from Zirr. This is a weak chain, because of Jabir al-Ju'fi. His son 'Abd Allah narrated in the Musnad (990) its meaning, in a very abridged form, with a chain that is also weak.]]

**5424.** Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu al-Duha, from Shutayr ibn Shakl, from 'Ali, who said: "They occupied us on the day of the Confederates from the afternoon prayer, until I heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ) say: 'They occupied us from the middle prayer, the afternoon prayer! May God fill their graves and their houses with fire!'" or "their bellies with fire."

[[Hadith 5424: Abu al-Duha: he is Muslim ibn Subayh, with a dammah on the unpointed sad, al-Hamdani al-Kufi. He is a reliable Successor who narrated many hadiths.
Shutayr ibn Shakl ibn Humayd al-'Absi: a reliable Successor, said to have reached the Jahiliyya (pre-Islamic era). For this reason the hafiz (Ibn Hajar) translated him in al-Isaba, in the section of the mukhadramun (those who lived through both eras), (3:219-220). "Shutayr" has a dammah on the shin (sh) and a fatha on the taa' (t). "Shakl" has a fatha on the shin and kaf. These two names are among the rarest names.
The hadith will come at 5426, in similar wording, through Abu Mu'awiya, from al-A'mash, from Muslim, who is Abu al-Duha.
'Abd al-Razzaq narrated it in al-Musannaf (1:182), from Sufyan al-Thawri, with it.
Ahmad narrated it in the Musnad (1245), from 'Abd al-Razzaq.
He also narrated it (1036), from 'Abd al-Rahman, that is Ibn Mahdi, from Sufyan.
Al-Bayhaqi narrated it (1:460), through Muhammad ibn Shurahbil ibn Ju'shum, from al-Thawri.
As for the route of Abu Mu'awiya that comes: Ahmad narrated it in the Musnad (617, 911), from Abu Mu'awiya, from al-A'mash. Muslim narrated it (1:174), through Abu Mu'awiya.
Ibn Hazm mentioned it (al-Muhalla 4:253), through Muslim.
Ahmad also narrated it (1298), from Muhammad ibn Ja'far, from Shu'ba, from al-A'mash.
Ibn Kathir mentioned it (1:578), from the narration of Ahmad from Abu Mu'awiya. Then he mentioned that Muslim and al-Nasa'i narrated it.]]

**5425.** Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'ba narrated to us, from al-Hakam, from Yahya ibn al-Jazzar, from 'Ali, from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he said on the day of the Confederates, at a gap (farda) of the trench: "They occupied us from the middle prayer until the sun set! May God fill their graves and their houses with fire," or "their bellies and their houses with fire."

[[Hadith 5425: al-Hakam: he is Ibn 'Utayba, has passed at 3297. Yahya ibn al-Jazzar al-'Urani al-Kufi: a reliable Successor. Shu'ba affirmed that he did not hear from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib except three hadiths, and this is one of them.
The hadith was narrated by Ahmad in the Musnad (1305), from Muhammad ibn Ja'far, from Shu'ba, with this chain. He also narrated it (1132), from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi, from Shu'ba.
Muslim narrated it (1:174), through Waki' and Mu'adh, that is al-'Anbari al-Hafiz, both from Shu'ba. Ibn Kathir (1:578) pointed to this narration of Muslim.
Al-Tahawi narrated it in Ma'ani al-Athar (1:103), through Abu 'Amir al-'Aqadi, from Shu'ba, with this chain.
Al-Farda: what slopes down from the side of the trench at the place where it was dug. It derives from "al-fard," which is cutting. From it comes "fardat al-nahr," which is the place where water is drawn from a river; it is a breach in its bank. And "fardat al-bahr" is the place where ships dock.]]

**5426.** Abu al-Sa'ib and Sa'id ibn Numayr narrated to me, both saying: Abu Mu'awiya narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Muslim, from Shutayr ibn Shakl, from 'Ali, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "They occupied us from the middle prayer, the afternoon prayer! May God fill their graves and their houses with fire!" Then he prayed it between the two evening prayers, between the sunset and the night prayers.

[[Hadith 5426: Abu al-Sa'ib, teacher of al-Tabari: he is Muslim ibn Janada, has passed several times.
Sa'id ibn Numayr, teacher of al-Tabari: I have not known who he is. I have found no mention of him or biography in any of the sources. I fear that it is a corruption of something I do not now recognize.
The word "Numayr" is written in the manuscript in an unclear form, which could be a corruption of "Yahya." If so, then he is "Sa'id ibn Yahya ibn al-Azhar al-Wasiti." He is reliable, narrates from Abu Mu'awiya, and belongs to the generation of al-Tabari's teachers. We neither affirm nor prefer this without firm evidence.
The hadith has passed at 5424, from the narration of al-Thawri from al-A'mash, and we pointed to this and its takhrij (sources) there.]]

٥٤٢٧- Al-Husayn ibn Ali al-Sada'i narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Asim narrated to us, from Khalid, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, from Ubayda al-Salmani, from Ali, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not pray the afternoon prayer (al-'asr) on the day of the Trench until after the sun had set. He said: "May Allah fill their hearts and their houses with fire! They kept us from the middle prayer until the sun set."

[[Hadith 5427: Al-Husayn ibn Ali al-Sada'i: his biography appeared earlier, at no. 2093.
Ali ibn Asim ibn Suhayb al-Wasiti: trustworthy (thiqah), one of the teachers of Ahmad and Ibn al-Madini. Some scholars spoke against him, but we preferred his reliability in the Musnad, no. 343.
Khalid: he is Ibn Mihran al-Hadhdha', whose biography appeared earlier, at no. 1683.
The hadith was narrated by Ahmad in his Musnad, somewhat abridged: no. 994, from Yahya, who is al-Qattan, from Hisham, who is Ibn Hassan, from Muhammad, who is Ibn Sirin. He also narrated it at no. 1220, from Yazid, who is Ibn Harun, from Hisham. Al-Bukhari narrated it at 6:76, 7:312, 8:145, and 11:165 (Fath al-Bari), through several chains from Hisham. Abu Dawud narrated it at no. 409, also through Hisham. Ibn Hazm narrated it in al-Muhalla 4:252, through al-Bukhari. See also what passed at no. 5423.]]

٥٤٢٨- Zakariya ibn Yahya al-Darir narrated to us, saying: Ubayd Allah narrated to us, from Isra'il, from Asim, from Zirr, who said: I and Ubayda al-Salmani went to Ali. I asked Ubayda to question him about the middle prayer. He said: "O Commander of the Faithful, what is the middle prayer?" He said: "We used to think it was the dawn prayer. Then, while we were fighting the people of Khaybar, they fought us until they overwhelmed us and kept us from the prayer, and that was shortly before sunset. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'O Allah, fill the hearts of these people who occupied us from the middle prayer, and their bellies, with fire'" — or "fill their hearts with fire" — "He said: So we knew that day that it was the middle prayer."

[[Hadith 5428: This hadith has the same meaning as hadith 5423. However, this narration contains an anomaly (shudhudh), in that it places the incident in the battle of Khaybar. All the sound narrations state that it occurred in the Battle of the Confederates (al-Ahzab). For this reason al-Suyuti singled it out, 1:303, saying: "Ibn Jarir narrated it from another route, from Zirr..." He attributed it to no one other than al-Tabari, and I did not find anything that supports it.
Rather, al-Tahawi narrated in Ma'ani al-Athar 1:103, through this same route, like the rest of the narrations: he narrated it through Za'ida ibn Qudama, from Asim, from Zirr, from Ali, and in it: "We fought the confederates." Then he narrated through Sufyan, from Asim, from Zirr, that he assigned Ubayda to ask Ali, and said: "He mentioned something similar."]]

٥٤٢٩- Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, from Abu Hassan al-A'raj, from Ubayda al-Salmani, from Ali ibn Abi Talib, that the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) said on the day of the Confederates: "O Allah, fill their hearts and their houses with fire, just as they kept us" — or "as they detained us" — "from the middle prayer until the sun set!"

[[Hadith 5429: Yazid is Ibn Zuray'. Sa'id is Ibn Abi 'Arubah. The hadith passed at no. 5422, through the narration of Shu'bah, from Qatada.
Ahmad narrated it in his Musnad, no. 591, from Muhammad ibn Abi 'Adi; no. 1134, from Abd al-Wahhab, who is Ibn 'Ata al-Khaffaf; and no. 1307, from Muhammad ibn Ja'far, all three from Sa'id, who is Ibn Abi 'Arubah. He also narrated it at no. 1313, from Bahz, and at no. 1326, from Affan, both from Hammam, from Qatada. al-Tirmidhi narrated it at 4:77, from Hannad, from 'Abdah, from Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah, and said: "This is a hasan sahih hadith, and it has been narrated through other routes from Ali."]]

٥٤٣٠- Sulayman ibn Abd al-Jabbar narrated to us, saying: Thabit ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Talha narrated to us, from Zubayd, from Murra, from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: The polytheists detained the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) from the afternoon prayer until the sun turned yellow" — or "reddened" — "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'They occupied us from the middle prayer! May Allah fill their houses and their hearts with fire'" — or "May Allah fill their hearts and their houses with fire."

[[Hadith 5430: Thabit ibn Muhammad, Abu Isma'il al-Shaybani al-'Abid: trustworthy. Al-Bukhari mentioned him in al-Kabir 1/2/170. In al-Tahdhib there is a misleading phrase, perhaps a slip of the pen by al-Hafiz: he said: "al-Bukhari mentioned him in the Du'afa' (weak narrators), and cited a hadith from him, and clarified that the defect was from someone else!" But al-Bukhari did not mention him among the weak narrators. He only narrated a hadith from him, as al-Hafiz said, and clarified that the defect lies with another person. So he has no bearing on the weakness of the hadith, if it were weak. This is a habit of al-Bukhari in many of his biographical entries.
The hadith passed at nos. 5420 and 5421, through two chains from Muhammad ibn Talha. See the hadith that follows this one.]]

٥٤٣١- Muhammad ibn Umara al-Asadi narrated to me, saying: Sahl ibn Amir narrated to us, saying: Malik ibn Mighwal narrated to us, saying: I heard Talha say: "I prayed with Murra in his house, and he forgot" — or he said: "he neglected" — "so he stood up and talked to us. I used to like to hear him from a trustworthy person." He said: "When the day of the Trench came, which is the day of the Confederates, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'What is wrong with them! They occupied us from the middle prayer, the afternoon prayer! May Allah fill their bellies and their graves with fire!'"

[[Hadith 5431: This hadith is weak for two reasons. The first is due to Sahl ibn Amir al-Bajali, who is very weak, as we explained at no. 1971. The second is that it is mursal (its chain is broken), because Murra is a Successor (tabi'i). Malik ibn Mighwal, with a kasra on the mim, sukun on the ghayn, and fatha on the waw, son of Asim al-Bajali: a well-known trustworthy narrator, from whom the authors of the six canonical books narrated.
Talha: he is Ibn Musarrif al-Yami, a trustworthy Successor by universal agreement. Ibn Idris said: "They used to call him the leader of the reciters."
The hadith itself is sound. It passed through three sound chains, from the narration of Muhammad ibn Talha ibn Musarrif, from Zubayd, from Murra, from Ibn Mas'ud: nos. 5420, 5421, and 5430.]]

٥٤٣٢- Ahmad ibn Mani' narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us, from Ibn 'Ata, from al-Taymi, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The middle prayer is the afternoon prayer."

[[Hadith 5432: Ahmad ibn Mani' al-Baghawi al-Asamm al-Hafiz, the teacher of al-Tabari: trustworthy, and the group narrated from him. Abd al-Wahhab ibn 'Ata al-Khaffaf: trustworthy, one of the teachers of Ahmad and Ishaq. Ibn Ma'in and others declared him reliable. In the printed edition here there appears: "Abd al-Wahhab 'an Ibn 'Ata," making them two narrators. This is an error beyond any doubt.
al-Taymi: he is Sulayman ibn Tarkhan.
This hadith passed as a mawquf report (a statement of Abu Hurayrah, not attributed to the Prophet) at nos. 5387, 5388, and 5390. Here it is marfu' (attributed to the Prophet) through a sound chain. An addition (ziyadah) from a trustworthy narrator is accepted.
al-Bayhaqi narrated it at 1:460, through Muhammad ibn Ubayd Allah ibn al-Manadi: "Abd al-Wahhab ibn 'Ata narrated to us, Sulayman al-Taymi narrated to us..."
Ibn Kathir quoted it at 1:579 from this place in al-Tabari.
Al-Hafiz mentioned it in Fath al-Bari 8:145 and attributed it to al-Tabari.
al-Suyuti mentioned it at 1:304 and attributed it to al-Tabari and al-Bayhaqi.]]

٥٤٣٣- Ali ibn Muslim al-Tusi narrated to me, saying: 'Abbad ibn al-'Awwam narrated to us, from Hilal ibn Khabbab, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) set out on a military campaign, and the polytheists detained him from the afternoon prayer until it was evening. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O Allah, fill their houses and their bellies with fire, just as they detained us from the middle prayer!"

[[Hadith 5433: Ali ibn Muslim al-Tusi, a teacher of al-Tabari: his biography passed at no. 4170. 'Abbad ibn al-'Awwam, with shadda on the ba' and the waw in both, al-Wasiti: trustworthy, one of the teachers of Ahmad.
Hilal ibn Khabbab, with a mu'jamah kha' and a shadda on the ba', al-'Abdi: trustworthy and reliable, one of the teachers of al-Thawri and Abu 'Awanah. We established in the explanation of the Musnad, no. 2303, that he did not become confused (ikhtilat) and did not change, contrary to those who said so.
The hadith was narrated by Ahmad in his Musnad, no. 2745, from Abd al-Samad, who is Ibn Abd al-Warith, from Thabit, who is Ibn Yazid al-Ahwal, from Hilal, who is Ibn Khabbab, with the same wording.
al-Tahawi narrated it in Ma'ani al-Athar 1:103, through Abu 'Awanah, from Hilal ibn Khabbab, with something similar. Then he narrated it through 'Abbad, from Hilal.
al-Haythami mentioned it in Majma' al-Zawa'id 1:309 and said: "Ahmad and al-Tabarani in al-Kabir and al-Awsat narrated it, and its narrators are trustworthy."
al-Suyuti mentioned it at 1:303-304 and attributed it only to Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Jarir.
It will follow after this, at nos. 5434 and 5435, with a similar wording, through the narration of Miqsam from Ibn Abbas.]]

٥٤٣٤- Musa ibn Sahl al-Ramli narrated to us, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, from Abd al-Wahid al-Mawsili, who said: Khalid ibn Abd Allah narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Layla, from al-Hakam, from Miqsam, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said on the day of the Confederates: "They occupied us from the middle prayer until the sun set! May Allah fill their graves and their houses with fire!"

[[Hadith 5434: Musa ibn Sahl al-Ramli, a teacher of al-Tabari: truthful and trustworthy, as Ibn Abi Hatim said, 4/1/146. Another narration of al-Tabari from him passed at no. 878.
Ishaq ibn Abd al-Wahid al-Mawsili al-Qurashi: trustworthy. Ibn Hibban mentioned him in al-Thiqat. In al-Tahdhib it is stated that Abu 'Ali al-Nisaburi al-Hafiz said of him: "matruk al-hadith" (abandoned in hadith), as transmitted by Ibn al-Jawzi. al-Dhahabi, in al-Mizan, definitively declared him weak without evidence. In al-Tahdhib it is also stated that al-Khatib narrated a false report through 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ahmad al-Mawsili, from Ishaq, this one, from Malik; and al-Khatib said: "The blame for it lies with 'Abd al-Rahman, and Ishaq ibn Abd al-Wahid is not objectionable." Ibn Abi Hatim mentioned him at 1/1/229 without citing any criticism of him. This is evidence of his reliability according to him.
Furthermore, Ishaq did not narrate this hadith alone; it will follow after it, through the narration of 'Amr ibn 'Awn, from Khalid.
In the printed and manuscript editions it reads: "Ishaq, from Abd al-Wahid al-Mawsili," which is an error.
Khalid ibn Abd Allah: he is al-Tahhan, whose biography passed at no. 4433.
Ibn Abi Layla: he is Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla. We explained earlier, in hadith no. 32, that he is truthful but poor in memory. However, he did not narrate this hadith alone, for a sound chain from Ibn Abbas preceded it.
al-Hakam: he is Ibn Utaybah, whose biography passed at no. 3297.
Miqsam: he is Ibn Bujra, whose biography passed at no. 4086.
In al-Tahdhib, on the authority of Ahmad, in the biography of al-Hakam, it is stated that al-Hakam did not hear from Miqsam except five hadiths, which he specified. This is not one of them, so the chain is then interrupted (munqati').
The hadith was mentioned by al-Hafiz in Fath al-Bari 8:146 and attributed only to Ibn al-Mundhir.
al-Suyuti mentioned it at 1:303 and added its attribution to al-Tabarani in al-Kabir, but he made it "through Miqsam and Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas." Perhaps the narration of Sa'id ibn Jubayr is in al-Tabarani.
Then I found the narration of Sa'id ibn Jubayr in al-Tahawi. He narrated it in Ma'ani al-Athar 1:103, through Muhammad ibn 'Imran ibn Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, from his father, from Ibn Abi Layla (who is Muhammad, the father of 'Imran), from al-Hakam, from Miqsam and Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas.
This is a good and connected chain (isnad). Muhammad ibn 'Imran ibn Abi Layla and his father are both trustworthy. As for al-Hakam ibn Utaybah, there is no disagreement about his hearing from Sa'id ibn Jubayr. Indeed, his narration from him is established in the Two Sahihs in other than this hadith, as in the book Rijal al-Sahihayn, p. 100.]]

٥٤٣٥- Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: 'Amr ibn 'Awn narrated to us, saying: Khalid informed us, from Ibn Abi Layla, from al-Hakam, from Miqsam, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Confederates occupied the Prophet (ﷺ) on the day of the Trench from the afternoon prayer until the sun set, so the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "They occupied us from the middle prayer! May Allah fill their graves and their houses with fire" — or "their bellies with fire."

[[Hadith 5435: 'Amr ibn 'Awn ibn Aws al-Wasiti al-Hafiz: trustworthy, and the group narrated from him. This hadith repeats the previous one.]]

٥٤٣٦- Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Sulayman ibn Ahmad al-Harashi al-Wasiti narrated to us, saying: al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us, saying: Sadaqah ibn Khalid informed me, saying: Khalid ibn Dihqan narrated to me, from Jabir ibn Saylan, from Kuhayl ibn Harmalah, who said: Abu Hurayrah was asked about the middle prayer, and he said: "We disagreed about it just as you disagreed about it, and we were in the courtyard of the house of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Among us was the righteous man Abu Hashim ibn Utbah ibn Rabi'ah ibn Abd Shams, and he said: 'I will inform you about that.' He stood up and asked permission to enter upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he entered upon him. Then he came out to us and said: 'He told us that it is the afternoon prayer.'"

[[Hadith 5436: Sulayman ibn Ahmad al-Jarshi al-Shami, resident of Wasit: weak, indeed some scholars accused him of lying, but he did not narrate this hadith alone, as will come. He is biographed in al-Kabir 2/2/4, where it is said: "There is something to examine in him" (fihi nazar). Also in Ibn Abi Hatim 2/1/101, Tarikh Baghdad 9:49-50, and Lisan al-Mizan 3:72.
Sadaqah ibn Khalid al-Umawi al-Dimashqi: trustworthy. Ahmad, Ibn Ma'in, Abu Zur'ah, and others declared him reliable. al-Bukhari narrated from him in his Sahih.
Khalid ibn Dihqan al-Dimashqi: trustworthy. al-Bukhari mentioned him in al-Kabir 2/1/135 and said: "Khalid heard Sablan; Sadaqah ibn Khalid and Muhammad ibn Shu'ayb narrated from him." Ibn Abi Hatim also mentioned him in the same way at 1/2/329.
Khalid Sablan: he is Khalid ibn Abd Allah ibn al-Faraj, Abu Hashim, a client of the Banu 'Abs. He is trustworthy; Abu Mushir declared him reliable, as Ibn 'Asakir transmitted. al-Bukhari mentioned him in al-Kabir 2/1/141, saying: "Khalid Sablan, from Kuhayl ibn Harmalah al-Shami. Khalid ibn Dihqan narrated from him, and Sa'id ibn Abd al-Aziz heard from him." Similar wording is in Ibn Abi Hatim 1/2/363, and neither of them mentioned any criticism of him. Ibn 'Asakir mentioned him in Tarikh Dimashq (5:67 of his abridgment by Shaykh Abd al-Qadir Badran), adding that he heard Mu'awiyah and 'Amr ibn al-'As.
"Sablan": with a fatha on the sin, a fatha on the ba' with a single dot, and a light lam, as Ibn Makula vocalized it, as transmitted by Ibn 'Asakir, and as in al-Mushtabih of al-Dhahabi, p. 256. It is a nickname (laqab) of this Khalid, given to him because of the greatness of his beard.
Al-Bukhari and Ibn Abi Hatim did not mention this Khalid's lineage. Rather, al-Bukhari mentioned him in the chapter on the letter sin among those named "Khalid." Ibn Abi Hatim mentioned him in the chapter "Khalid" among those who are not given a lineage.
It was Ibn 'Asakir, and Ibn Makula in al-Ikmal, who mentioned the lineage we have mentioned, as transmitted from him by the scholar Shaykh Abd al-Rahman al-Yamani in the margins of al-Tarikh al-Kabir and Ibn Abi Hatim. al-Dhahabi mentioned him in al-Mushtabih under the name "Khalid ibn Abd Allah." al-Hafiz mentioned in al-Tahdhib 3:87, among the teachers of "Khalid ibn Dihqan," under the name "Khalid ibn Abd Allah Sablan." So "Sablan" is the nickname of Khalid, as we explained.
His name appears in the printed edition here in a very distorted form: "Jabir ibn Saylan"!! The difference between this and that is vast. The more likely view, in my opinion, is that this is a distortion by the copyists, who did not find in al-Tahdhib or any of its branches the name "Khalid Sablan." Then they found the biography of "Jabir ibn Saylan" (al-Tahdhib 2:40), assumed it was him, and changed it to that, or something similar. His name is correctly preserved in Ibn Kathir, since he quoted it from this place in al-Tabari, but the word "ibn" was added between the name and the nickname. It appears that this was an alteration by the copyists.
Kuhayl ibn Harmalah al-Numayri: a trustworthy Successor. al-Bukhari mentioned him in al-Kabir 4/1/238 and said: "He heard Abu Hurayrah. Khalid Sablan narrated from him." Similar wording is in Ibn Abi Hatim 3/2/173, and neither of them mentioned any criticism of him. Ibn Hibban also mentioned him in al-Thiqat, p. 318.
Ibn Hibban narrated the hadith in al-Thiqat, in the biography of Kuhayl, through Abu Mushir, who is Abd al-A'la ibn Mushir al-Dimashqi, the trustworthy and firm, from Sadaqah ibn Khalid, with this chain.
Similarly, al-Tahawi narrated it in Ma'ani al-Athar 1:103, through Abu Mushir.
al-Hakim narrated it in al-Mustadrak 3:638, through al-'Abbas ibn al-Walid ibn Mazid, who is trustworthy and one of the teachers of al-Tabari, whose biography passed at no. 891, from Muhammad ibn Shu'ayb ibn Shabur, one of the great trustworthy narrators, from Khalid Sablan, with this chain.
Ibn 'Asakir narrated it in Tarikh Dimashq, with his chain to Khalid Sablan, in his biography, but Shaykh Abd al-Qadir Badran, in his abridgment, omitted the chain to him.
Ibn Kathir quoted it at 1:579 from this place. Then he said: "Strange (gharib) from this route, very much so."
al-Haythami mentioned it in Majma' al-Zawa'id 1:309 and said: "al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Kabir, and al-Bazzar. He said: 'We do not know that Abu Hashim ibn Utbah narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) except this hadith and one other.' I say [the speaker is al-Haythami]: Its narrators are trustworthy."
al-Hafiz quoted it in Fath al-Bari 8:145-146 and did not attribute it to anyone other than al-Tabari.
al-Suyuti quoted it at 1:304 and attributed it to Ibn Sa'd, al-Bazzar, Ibn Jarir, al-Tabarani, and al-Baghawi in his Mu'jam. Al-Hafiz greatly erred in al-Isabah, in the biography of "Abu Hashim ibn Utbah ibn Rabi'ah ibn Abd Shams," the narrator of this hadith, 7:197-198, when he attributed it to Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i, al-Baghawi, and al-Hakim Abu Ahmad!! As for the books of al-Baghawi and al-Hakim Abu Ahmad, they are not available to me, and I cannot say anything about his quoting them.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 238 (part 5 of 7):

As for the three Sunan, I can say with certainty that it is not in any one of them. That is why the Hafiz (Ibn Hajar) himself did not attribute it to them in al-Fath. That is also why the author of Majma' al-Zawa'id (al-Haythami), which is a collection of additions (al-Zawa'id) to the Six Books, mentioned it. And that is why al-Nabulsi did not mention it in Dhakha'ir al-Mawarith, in the biography of "Abu Hashim ibn 'Utba". I have already drawn attention to this error in my commentary on al-Tirmidhi, 1: 341-342.]]

5437 - al-Husayn ibn 'Ali al-Sada'i narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to us, and Ibn Ishaq al-Ahwazi narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, both of them together, saying: Fudayl ibn Marzuq narrated to us, from Shaqiq ibn 'Uqba al-'Abdi, from al-Bara' ibn 'Azib, who said: This verse was revealed: "Guard over the prayers and the middle prayer (wa-salat al-'asr)." He said: We recited it during the lifetime of the Messenger of God ﷺ for as long as God willed us to recite it. Then God abrogated it and revealed: "Guard over the prayers and the middle prayer, and stand before God in devotion." He said: A man who was with Shaqiq said: "Then it is the prayer of 'Asr!" He said: I have told you how it was revealed and how God abrogated it, and God knows best.

[[The hadith: 5437 - al-Husayn ibn 'Ali al-Sada'i (Shaykh of al-Tabari) and his father, both passed earlier at 2093. Ibn Ishaq al-Ahwazi (Shaykh of al-Tabari after the change of isnad): he is Ahmad ibn Ishaq ibn 'Isa, passed earlier at 1841.
Abu Ahmad: he is al-Zubayri, Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr al-Asadi.
Fudayl ibn Marzuq al-Aghar al-Kufi: reliable (thiqa), declared reliable by al-Thawri, Ibn Ma'in and others. Muslim included him in his Sahih. His name appears in the manuscript and the printed edition here as "Fudayl ibn Masruq"! This is an error by the copyists.
Shaqiq ibn 'Uqba al-'Abdi al-Kufi: a reliable Successor (tabi'i). Declared reliable by Abu Dawud and Ibn Hibban.
The hadith was narrated by Muslim in his Sahih 1: 75, from Ishaq ibn Rahawayh, from Yahya ibn Adam, from Fudayl ibn Marzuq, with the same chain. He then said: "It was also narrated by al-Ash'ari, from Sufyan al-Thawri, from al-Aswad ibn Qays, from Shaqiq ibn 'Uqba, from al-Bara' ibn 'Azib."
The author of al-Tahdhib erred in the biography of "Shaqiq ibn 'Uqba" 4: 363, when he said: "He has one hadith in Muslim on the middle prayer, and it is mu'allaq..." and then mentioned Muslim's words. He overlooked that Muslim had narrated it with a continuous chain directly before this mu'allaq transmission.
Ibn Hazm narrated it in al-Muhalla 4: 258, through Muslim's route.
al-Tahawi narrated it in Ma'ani al-Athar 1: 102, through Muhammad ibn Yusuf al-Faryabi, from Fudayl ibn Marzuq, with the same chain. But in al-Tahawi's copy it occurs as "Muhammad ibn Fudayl ibn Marzuq"! This is certainly an error, and there is no narrator among the transmitters with this name.
al-Hakim narrated it in al-Mustadrak 2: 281, through Yahya ibn Ja'far ibn al-Zabarqan, from Abu Ahmad al-Zubayri, from Fudayl ibn Marzuq, with the same chain. He said: "This hadith is sahih according to the condition of Muslim, though they did not record it." al-Dhahabi agreed! But both have a correction to make in this, since Muslim did record it, as we mentioned.
al-Bayhaqi narrated it in 1: 459, from al-Hakim, with his chain.
There is a blank in the printed Mustadrak at "Abu Ahmad al-Zubayri"; we have corrected it from al-Bayhaqi.
Then al-Bayhaqi mentioned that Muslim narrated it, then mentioned Muslim's indication of the mu'allaq transmission, the narration of al-Ash'ari from Sufyan al-Thawri. Then al-Bayhaqi narrated it through al-Ash'ari with a continuous chain.
The hadith was also mentioned by the Hafiz in al-Fath 1: 147, from Sahih Muslim.
al-Suyuti mentioned it at 1: 303, adding its attribution to 'Abd ibn Humayd and Abu Dawud in his Nasikh, but he did not attribute it to al-Hakim. Ibn Kathir mentioned it at 1: 582, from Sahih Muslim, then said: "Based on this, this recitation, which is the recitation of the majority, abrogates the wording of the narration of 'A'isha and Hafsa and its meaning, if the particle wa (and) indicates difference. Otherwise, it abrogates only its wording." This is subtle and original jurisprudence.
His words in the text of the hadith: "we recited it during the lifetime of the Messenger of God ﷺ" - this is the correct reading, consistent with the context of the statement "we recited it" and with all the other narrations. The printed edition has "fa-qara'tuha" (I recited it), which is not good. Perhaps the source manuscripts, written in the old script without alif or dots, read "faqara'tuha" (we recited it), and the copyist took it as the first-person ta', finding no alif after it. So he wrote it with ta' according to his assumption and knowledge.]]

5438 - Hamid ibn Mas'ada narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Zuray' narrated to us; and Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Bakr and Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Ansari narrated to us, both of them together, saying: Sa'id ibn Abi 'Uruba narrated to us; and Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: 'Abda ibn Sulayman narrated to us, and Muhammad ibn Bishr and 'Abd Allah ibn Isma'il, from Sa'id, from Qatada, from al-Hasan, from Samura, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: The middle prayer is the prayer of 'Asr.

[[The hadith: 5438 - al-Tabari narrated it from three of his Shaykhs: Hamid ibn Mas'ada, Muhammad ibn Bashshar, and Abu Kurayb Muhammad ibn al-'Ala'. Hamid narrated it from one Shaykh, Ibn Bashshar from two Shaykhs, and Abu Kurayb from three Shaykhs. These six: Yazid ibn Zuray', Muhammad ibn Bakr, Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Ansari, 'Abda ibn Sulayman, Muhammad ibn Bishr, and 'Abd Allah ibn Isma'il, all narrated it from Sa'id, who is Ibn Abi 'Uruba. Yazid ibn Zuray': his biography has passed at 1769.
Muhammad ibn Bakr ibn 'Uthman al-Barsani (with the ba' vowelled and the ra' sukun): reliable, declared reliable by Ibn Ma'in, Abu Dawud and others. The authors of the six books all narrated from him.
Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn al-Muthanna ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Anas ibn Malik al-Ansari: reliable, one of the Shaykhs of Ahmad and Ibn al-Madini; al-Bukhari and the majority narrated from him.
'Abda ibn Sulayman al-Kilabi: his biography has passed at 2323.
Muhammad ibn Bishr ibn al-Farafisa al-'Abdi: passed at 4222.
'Abd Allah ibn Isma'il: a Kufan. Abu Hatim claimed, as narrated from him by his son, that he was unknown (majhul), but the Hafiz al-Mizzi in al-Atraf affirmed that he is "'Abd Allah ibn Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid", as al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar also reported from him in al-Tahdhib.
The hadith passed at 5417, through the narration of Isma'il ibn Muslim, from al-Hasan, from Samura. There we takhrij it through the route of Sa'id ibn Abi 'Uruba, from Qatada, from al-Hasan, from Samura. This is that route.]]

5439 - 'Isam ibn Rawwad ibn al-Jarrah narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to us, saying: Sa'id ibn Bashir narrated to us, from Qatada, from al-Hasan, from Samura, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ informed us that the middle prayer is the 'Asr.

[[The hadith: 5439 - 'Isam ibn Rawwad ibn al-Jarrah and his father, both passed at 2183.
Sa'id ibn Bashir al-Azdi: passed at 126. He is truthful, though people have spoken about his memory, but Sufyan ibn 'Uyayna described him as "a memorizer (hafiz)". It seems that the criticism of him was made without verification, for they denied the large number of what he narrated from Qatada. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from his father, who said: "I said to Ahmad ibn Salih: Sa'id ibn Bashir is a Damascene Syrian; how is this large number from Qatada?" He said: "His father Bashir was a partner of Abu 'Uruba, and Bashir sent his son Sa'id to Basra to seek hadith with Sa'id ibn Abi 'Uruba." So this is the explanation. Therefore the chain is sahih, like the chain before it.]]

5440 - Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi 'Adi narrated to us, from Shu'ba, from Sulayman, from Abu al-Duha, from Shutayr ibn Shakl, from Umm Habiba, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said, on the day of the Trench: They occupied us from the middle prayer, the prayer of 'Asr, until the sun set. Abu Musa said: Thus said Ibn Abi 'Adi.

[[The hadith: 5440 - This is a sahih chain according to the condition of Muslim. Sulayman is al-A'mash.
This hadith - from Umm Habiba - I have not found in any other source besides this place in al-Tabari; indeed I have found no reference to it at all, except what Ibn Kathir 1: 578 reported from the Hafiz Abu Muhammad 'Abd al-Mu'min ibn Khalaf al-Damyati, that he mentioned "Umm Habiba" among those from whom the view was related that the middle prayer is the 'Asr. This reference is more likely to be an allusion to this hadith, without explicit statement.
Shutayr ibn Shakl: an early Successor, as we said at 5424. But al-Tahdhib, when mentioning the Companions from whom he narrated (4: 311), said: "And Umm Habiba, if it is preserved (in mahfuz)"; I strove to know to which hadith this refers: this hadith or another?
I found that Ahmad had narrated in the Musnad 6: 325 (Halabi), from Muhammad ibn Ja'far, from Shu'ba, from Mansur, from Abu al-Duha, from Shutayr ibn Shakl, from Umm Habiba: "that the Messenger of God ﷺ used to kiss while fasting." This is a chain as clear in soundness as the sun.
But Muslim narrated it in 1: 305, and Ibn Majah 1685, from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shayba and others, from Abu Mu'awiya, from al-A'mash, from Muslim - who is Abu al-Duha - from Shutayr ibn Shakl, from Hafsa. Then Muslim narrated the hadith of kissing for the fasting person - I mean that hadith - through Abu 'Awana and Jarir, both from Mansur, likewise, that is from the hadith of Hafsa.
So I understood that the indication in the words "if it is preserved" refers to the hadith of kissing for the fasting person, and that they preferred the narration of three: Abu Mu'awiya from al-A'mash, and Abu 'Awana and Jarir from Mansur - in their narration of that hadith from Hafsa - over the narration of Shu'ba, in his narrating it from Umm Habiba! This is an arbitrary preference, without evidence.
Shutayr ibn Shakl heard from 'Ali, Ibn Mas'ud and Hafsa. They died earlier than Umm Habiba. Contemporaneity - together with the reliability of the narrator and his freedom from the charge of tadlis - is sufficient for judging the hadith connected. The Successor's narration of a hadith from one Companion does not at all negate his narration of it from another Companion; rather each of the two narrations supports the other, unless strong evidence establishes error in one of them.
As for Shutayr's narration from Umm Habiba - even if a doubt were supposed in it in the hadith on kissing for the fasting person - his narration from her here, in the hadith of the middle prayer, removes every doubt and shows that his narration from her is preserved.
Moreover, the narration of that hadith was transmitted by Muhammad ibn Ja'far from Shu'ba, and the narration of this hadith was transmitted by Muhammad ibn Abi 'Adi from Shu'ba, and both do not detract from the memorization, precision, verification and knowledge. That one is from Shu'ba from Mansur from Abu al-Duha, and this is from his narration from al-A'mash from Abu al-Duha.
al-Tabari, may God have mercy on him, verified the narration of this hadith here, fearing that error might be attributed to him or to his Shaykh, so he related the words of his Shaykh "Ibn al-Muthanna", who is Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna Abu Musa al-Zaman al-Hafiz, just as he verified what his Shaykh "Ibn Abi 'Adi" said - who is Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Abi 'Adi - and said: "Abu Musa said: Thus said Ibn Abi 'Adi." This is a precise precaution, intended to remove the suspicion of error or defect from this narration of Shu'ba.
Shu'ba ibn al-Hajjaj: the Commander of the Faithful in hadith, as al-Thawri said. He who "was a community unto himself in this matter," as Ahmad said, is not to be disputed in a narration he transmits, nor is he judged in error in it, unless that is made clear by decisive evidence or something akin to decisive. It is not sufficient to explain away his narration of the two hadiths of Umm Habiba - on kissing for the fasting person and on the middle prayer - by the passing phrase "if it is preserved"!! Shu'ba is the memorizer, the proof, the reliable and trustworthy.]]

5441 - Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayya narrated to us, from Yunus, from al-Hasan, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "Guard over the prayers and the middle prayer," and it is the 'Asr.

[[The hadith: 5441 - This hadith is mursal. But its meaning is sound, by the sahih hadiths that have passed.]]

5442 - Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Salam narrated to us, from Salim, client of Abu Nusayr, who said: Ibrahim ibn Yazid al-Dimashqi narrated to me, who said: I was sitting with 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Marwan, and he said: "O so-and-so, go to so-and-so and say to him: What did you hear from the Messenger of God ﷺ concerning the middle prayer?" A man sitting there said: "Abu Bakr and 'Umar sent me when I was a small boy to ask him about the middle prayer, and he took my little finger and said: This is the Fajr - and he closed the one next to it. And he said: This is the Dhuhr - then he closed the thumb and said: This is the Maghrib - then he closed the one next to it and said: This is the 'Isha'. Then he said: Which of your fingers remains? I said: The middle one. He said: Which prayer remains? I said: The 'Asr. He said: It is the 'Asr."

[[The hadith: 5442 - This is an unknown (majhul) chain, as far as I am concerned at least. I do not know who "'Abd al-Salam", the Shaykh of Abu Ahmad, is, and this name is common.
Salim, client of Abu Nusayr: thus in the manuscript and the printed edition; and in Ibn Kathir 1: 579, citing this same place: "Muslim, client of Abu Jubayr"! But I have found neither this nor that. Indeed I did not find it in the biography of "Salm" either, given the possibility of a corruption by adding a mim at its beginning or adding an alif after the sin.
Ibrahim ibn Yazid al-Dimashqi: he is mentioned in al-Tahdhib, that he was one of the guards of 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz. al-Bukhari mentioned him in al-Kabir 1/1/335, Ibn Abi Hatim 1/1/145, and Ibn 'Asakir mentioned him in Tarikh Dimashq, attributing him as "al-Nasri, from the people of Damascus" (Mukhtasar Tarikh Ibn 'Asakir 2: 310). Ibn Hibban mentioned him in al-Thiqat, as in al-Tahdhib.
If we knew the source of this hadith, and knew the two narrators "'Abd al-Salam" and his Shaykh, and they were acceptable, the hadith would be good: hasan or sahih, because the man sitting with 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Marwan, who narrated it from the Messenger of God ﷺ, would be a Companion, since he reports that Abu Bakr and 'Umar sent him to ask the Messenger of God ﷺ, and they would not send for such a question - God willing - except a perceptive, discerning boy.
It appears to me that the Hafiz Ibn Kathir was unaware of its source, so after quoting it from al-Tabari he described it as "very strange (gharib jiddan)".
al-Suyuti also cited it at 1: 304, and said nothing about it except attributing it to al-Tabari.
Likewise, the Hafiz Ibn Hajar cited it in al-Fath 1: 146, from al-Tabari - in abridged form.]]

5443 - It was related to me from 'Ammar ibn al-Hasan, who said: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi', who said: We were told that the polytheists occupied them on the day of the Confederates from the 'Asr prayer until the sun set, so the Messenger of God ﷺ said: "They occupied us from the middle prayer, the prayer of 'Asr, until the sun set! May God fill their houses and their graves with fire!"

5444 - Ibn al-Barqi narrated to us, saying: 'Amr narrated to us, from Abu Salama, who said: Sadaqa narrated to us, from Sa'id, from Qatada, from Abu Hassan, from 'Ubayda al-Salmani, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said on the day of the Confederates: "O God, fill their houses and their graves with fire, as they occupied us from the middle prayer until the sun went down."

[[The hadith: 5444 - Ibn al-Barqi: he is Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Rahim, passed at 22, 160. 'Amr ibn Abi Salama al-Tinnisi al-Dimashqi: reliable, one of the Shaykhs of al-Shafi'i. He has a narration in the Muwatta' from Malik.
In the printed edition here it reads "'Amr 'an Abi Salama"! This is a clear error, by a copyist or a printer.
Sadaqa: he is Ibn 'Abd Allah al-Samin al-Dimashqi. He is very weak, as Ahmad said. Muslim said: "munkar al-hadith." al-Bukhari, Ibn Ma'in, Abu Zur'a and others declared him weak.
Sa'id: he is Ibn Abi 'Uruba.
The hadith - although this chain is weak - has passed with a sahih chain: 5429, through the narration of Yazid ibn Zuray', from Ibn Abi 'Uruba, with the same. We took takhrij of it there.
It also passed: 5422, with another sahih chain, through the narration of Shu'ba, from Qatada.
Its meaning has passed through many routes from 'Ali, to which we referred at 5380.]]

5445 - Muhammad ibn 'Awf al-Ta'i narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn 'Ayyash narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to us, saying: Dhamdham ibn Zur'a narrated to me, from Shurayh ibn 'Ubayd, from Abu Malik al-Ash'ari, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "The middle prayer is the prayer of 'Asr."

[[The hadith: 5445 - Muhammad ibn 'Awf ibn Sufyan al-Ta'i al-Himsi - a Shaykh of al-Tabari, a reliable hafiz, known for eminence and knowledge. He is among the narrators from Ahmad ibn Hanbal, from whom Ahmad has questions. Nevertheless Ahmad heard a hadith from him, as in Tadhkirat al-Huffaz, in his biography 2: 144-145; he is also biographed in al-Tahdhib. He died in 272.
Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn 'Ayyash al-Himsi: weak. Abu Dawud said: "He was not of that standard; I have seen him, and I entered Homs more than once while he was alive, and I asked 'Amr ibn 'Uthman about him and he disparaged him." It seems they weakened him for narrating from his father without hearing it directly. Abu Hatim said: "He did not hear anything from his father; they made him narrate, so he narrated!" Such a person is bold regarding hadith, and his narration is not to be relied upon.
His father Isma'il ibn 'Ayyash al-Himsi: reliable; some have spoken against him because of his errors in some of what he narrates from non-Syrians, but his hadiths from the people of Syria are accepted.
Dhamdham ibn Zur'a ibn Thawb (with the thaʼ vowelled, the waw fathah, ending in ba'): al-Hadrami al-Himsi: reliable; declared reliable by Ibn Ma'in, while Abu Hatim declared him weak. al-Bukhari mentioned him in al-Kabir 2/2/339, and mentioned no criticism of him; Ibn Hibban mentioned him in al-Thiqat.
Shurayh ibn 'Ubayd ibn Shurayh al-Hadrami al-Himsi: a reliable Successor.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 238 (part 6 of 7):

Ibn Kathir transmitted this report from this same location, 1:579, and then said: "Its isnad (chain of narration) is not objectionable" (la ba's bihi).

Al-Haythami mentioned it in Majma' al-Zawa'id, within a hadith, and said: "It was narrated by al-Tabarani, and in its chain is Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Ayyash, who is weak (da'if)."

Al-Suyuti mentioned it, 1:304, and attributed it to al-Tabari and al-Tabarani.

* *

Others said: Rather, the Middle Prayer (al-salat al-wusta) is the Dhuhr prayer.

Those who said this:

5446. Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Affan narrated to us, saying: Hammam narrated to us, saying: Qatadah narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, from Ibn Umar, from Zayd ibn Thabit, who said: "The Middle Prayer is the Dhuhr prayer."

[Report 5446: Its isnad is sahih (sound). It is a mawquf (a report ending with a Companion's statement) from the words of Zayd ibn Thabit.
al-Tahawi narrated it in Ma'ani al-Athar, 1:99, from Ibn Marzuq, from Affan, with this same isnad.
al-Bayhaqi narrated it, 1:459, by way of Ibrahim ibn Marzuq, from Affan, with it.
Abd al-Razzaq narrated it in al-Musannaf, 1:182, from Sa'id ibn Bashir, from Qatadah, from Ibn al-Musayyab, from Zayd ibn Thabit. In this isnad, "Ibn Umar," between Ibn al-Musayyab and Zayd, has dropped out. Either he narrated it this way, or it is an error by the copyists?
This meaning will come through various channels from Zayd ibn Thabit: 5447, 5448, 5449, 5450, 5452, 5453, 5454, 5458, 5459, 5460.]

5447. Muhammad ibn Abd Allah al-Makhrami narrated to us, saying: Abu Amir narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, from Ibn Umar, from Zayd, meaning Ibn Thabit, something similar.

[Report 5447: Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak al-Makhrami (with a damma on the m, a fatha on the kh, and a kasra on the shaddah-ed r): thiqah (trustworthy), hafiz (memorizer), hujjah (authoritative). It passed at 3730. He is biographed in Tarikh Baghdad 5:423-425 and Tadhkirat al-Huffaz 2:92-93. In the manuscript and the printed edition it is written "al-Makhzumi," which is an error.
Abu Amir is al-Aqadi, Abd al-Malik ibn Amr.
The report repeats the preceding one. Its isnad is also sahih.
Ibn Kathir mentioned it, 1:577, together with the preceding one, without attribution.
al-Suyuti mentioned both and added their attribution to Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, and Ibn al-Anbari in al-Masahif.
Then al-Suyuti said: "Malik, Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad, Abd ibn Humayd, al-Bukhari in his Tarikh, Ibn Jarir, and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated, by several routes, from Zayd ibn Thabit, who said: 'The Middle Prayer is the Dhuhr prayer.'"
This may serve as a reference to many of the subsequent reports from Zayd ibn Thabit.
Malik's narration is in al-Muwatta', p. 139, from Dawud ibn al-Husayn, from Ibn Yarbu' al-Makhzumi, who heard Zayd ibn Thabit.
Abd al-Razzaq's narration is in al-Musannaf, 1:182, from Malik, with it.]

5448. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Sa'd ibn Ibrahim, who said: I heard Hafs ibn Asim narrate from Zayd ibn Thabit, who said: "The Middle Prayer is the Dhuhr."

[Report 5448: Hafs is Ibn Asim ibn Umar ibn al-Khattab. He is a trustworthy Successor (tabi'i), agreed upon as such. The report repeats the preceding one, and its isnad is likewise sahih.]

5449. Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Sulayman ibn Dawud narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us. And Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, from Shu'bah, who said: Umar ibn Sulayman, a descendant of Umar ibn al-Khattab, informed me, saying: I heard Abd al-Rahman ibn Aban ibn Uthman narrate from his father, from Zayd ibn Thabit, who said: "The Middle Prayer is the Dhuhr."

[Report 5449: Its isnad is sahih.
Umar ibn Sulayman ibn Asim ibn Umar ibn al-Khattab: thiqah. Ibn Ma'in, al-Nasa'i, and others declared him trustworthy. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib and Ibn Abi Hatim 3/1/112. It is reported from Ibn Ma'in that he described him as "the one who was knowledgeable of Zayd ibn Thabit's hadith." In al-Tahdhib it says: "It was said his name is 'Amr'." It is confirmed with the name "Amr" in the narrations of al-Darimi and al-Tahawi, as we will mention in the takhrij (sourcing), God willing.
Abd al-Rahman ibn Aban ibn Uthman ibn Affan: thiqah, worshipful, of few narrations. Al-Nasa'i declared him trustworthy, and Ibn Hibban mentioned him in al-Thiqat.
His father Aban ibn Uthman: thiqah, one of the senior Successors. Yahya al-Qattan counted him among the jurists of Madinah.
This report is also mawquf upon Zayd ibn Thabit, like the three reports before it.
Ibn Kathir mentioned it, 1:577, and said: "Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi and others narrated, from Shu'bah . . .", and he related it with this isnad.
Likewise al-Tahawi narrated it in Ma'ani al-Athar, 1:99, by way of Hajjaj ibn Muhammad, from Shu'bah, from "Amr ibn Sulayman," with it. In this narration, Shu'bah's teacher is named "Amr." A raised (marfu') version of it will come after this. In my view, the claim that it is marfu' is a mistake by one who understood it that way.]

5450. Zakariya ibn Yahya ibn Abi Za'idah narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Samad narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Umar ibn Sulayman (thus said Abu Za'idah), from Abd al-Rahman ibn Aban, from his father, from Zayd ibn Thabit in his hadith, raising it (rafa'ahu): "The Middle Prayer is the Dhuhr prayer."

[Report 5450: Its isnad is sahih, except that there is a defect (illah) in its raising, which we will mention, God willing.
Zakariya ibn Yahya: his biography passed at 1219.
Abd al-Samad is Ibn Abd al-Warith al-Anbari.
"Umar ibn Sulayman": his biography passed in the report before this one. This is how it stands in the printed edition! So there is no meaning to al-Tabari's statement, "thus said Abu Za'idah," meaning his teacher Zakariya ibn Yahya, since there is no difference in his name between this narration and that one. In the manuscript it is written "Umar ibn Salman," so the difference between the two narrations would be real. But I lean toward thinking both are errors, since no statement about his name has been reported as "Umar ibn Salman." In my view, the correct reading in this isnad is "Amr ibn Sulayman," which is the second opinion about his name among some narrators, as we mentioned. As for his words in this narration, "in his hadith, raising it," meaning that the report was raised to the Prophet (ﷺ), and that the wording "The Middle Prayer is the Dhuhr prayer" is from his (ﷺ) speech, this is his statement.
Likewise al-Suyuti quoted, 1:302: "Ibn Jarir narrated in his Tahdhib, by way of Abd al-Rahman ibn Aban, from his father, from Zayd ibn Thabit, in a hadith he raises . . .". Perhaps he did not see it in al-Tabari's Tafsir, so he quoted it from the Tahdhib. The wording al-Suyuti quoted, "in a hadith" (fi hadith), is better than the wording established here, "in his hadith" (fi hadithih). Rather, it appears that this is a distortion by the copyists.
In my view, the claim that the report is raised is a mistake by whoever said it. He abridged a lengthy hadith, so he gave the impression that a phrase at its end was raised. In the original hadith, it is clearly mawquf.
Ahmad narrated it in al-Musnad, 5:183 (Halabi edition), in full, from Yahya ibn Sa'id, from Shu'bah, with this isnad to Aban ibn Uthman: "Zayd ibn Thabit went out from Marwan's place at about midday. We said: 'He was only sent for just now for something he asked him about.' So I got up and asked him, and he said: 'Indeed, he asked us about some matters which I heard from the Messenger of God (ﷺ). I heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ) say: May God make radiant the face of a man who hears a hadith from us and memorizes it . . .'" Then he mentioned a lengthy raised hadith, and then said at its end: "And he asked us about the Middle Prayer, which is the Dhuhr." This clearly shows that Marwan asked Zayd about the Middle Prayer and he answered. It was not mentioned in the raised hadith, nor was it connected to it.
Al-Darimi narrated it, 1:75, from Ismah ibn al-Fadl, from Harmi (with a fatha on the h and the r) ibn Imarah, from Shu'bah, from Amr ibn Sulayman, with this isnad, similar to the Musnad version, in full. At its end, after the raised hadith, it says: "He said: 'And I asked him about the Middle Prayer, and he said: It is the Dhuhr.'" In this route, Shu'bah's teacher is named "Amr."
The apparent sense of this narration is that Aban ibn Uthman is the one who asked Zayd ibn Thabit about the Middle Prayer. This matter is minor. The major matter, which the context of the two narrations (Ahmad's and al-Darimi's) does not support, is the claim that "the Middle Prayer" is a raised statement from the words of the Prophet (ﷺ). That is merely a mistake, as we said, by one who abridged the hadith and took its end without considering the context and meaning of the statement. The lengthy raised portion of this hadith was narrated by Ibn Hibban in his Sahih, number 66 in our edition, by way of Yahya ibn Sa'id (Ahmad's teacher in it), and he also omitted the mawquf sentence. We have sourced it there.
What supports what we have said: Zayd ibn Thabit said this only by inference (istinbat), as will come in 5459 and 5460. Had this been raised (marfu') in his view, he would not have gone beyond it to inference, God willing.]

5451. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Abd Allah ibn Yazid narrated to us, saying: Haywah ibn Shurayh and Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to us, both saying: Abu Aqil Zuhrah ibn Ma'bad narrated to us: that Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab narrated to him that he was sitting, he and Urwah ibn al-Zubayr and Ibrahim ibn Talhah. Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab said: "I heard Abu Sa'id al-Khudri say: 'The Middle Prayer is the Dhuhr.'" Then Ibn Umar passed by us, and Urwah said: "Send to Ibn Umar and ask him." So they sent a boy to him, and he asked him. Then the messenger came back to us and said: "He says: It is the Dhuhr prayer." We doubted the boy's words, so we all got up and went to Ibn Umar, asked him, and he said: "It is the Dhuhr prayer."
