[Report 5451: Abd Allah ibn Yazid is al-Muqri'. His biography passed at 3180.
Zuhrah ibn Ma'bad ibn Abd Allah ibn Hisham al-Taymi: a trustworthy Successor. Ibn Abi Hatim said (1/2/615): "He met Ibn Umar, but I do not know whether he heard from him or not." The Hafiz in al-Tahdhib criticized this, affirming that he did hear from him, and that al-Bukhari contains what shows this.
Ibrahim ibn Talhah: I have not determined who he is. He has no narration in the report, and no role in the isnad. He was only one of those present at the gathering.
The report was narrated by al-Bayhaqi, 1:458-459, by way of Muhammad ibn Sinan al-Basri, from Abd Allah ibn Yazid, with it.
It will come at 5457, by way of Nafi', from Zuhrah ibn Ma'bad, in similar wording.
al-Suyuti mentioned it, 1:302, and attributed it only to al-Bayhaqi and Ibn Asakir.
This report, even with the soundness of its isnad, indicates that Abu Sa'id al-Khudri and Abd Allah ibn Umar held that the Middle Prayer is the Dhuhr.
It has passed from Abu Sa'id, with a sound isnad as well, at 5392, that it is the Asr.
Likewise it has passed from Ibn Umar, with two sound isnads, at 5389 and 5391, that he held it to be the Asr.
Abu Sa'id and Ibn Umar are among those from whom reports differ on this matter, according to both views. The reason is that neither of them narrated a raised hadith on it that would be binding upon them. Rather, they exerted effort (ijtihad) and inferred as best they could. See Ibn Kathir 1:577.]

5452. Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: al-Awwam ibn Hawshab informed us, saying: A man of the Ansar narrated to me, from Zayd ibn Thabit, that he used to say: "It is the Dhuhr."

[Report 5452: al-Awwam (with a shaddah on the w) ibn Hawshab ibn Yazid al-Shaybani: thiqah, agreed upon. He narrates from senior Successors. But here he narrated from an unidentified man, and this made the isnad weak.]

5453. Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to me, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Dhi'b narrated to us. And al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Adam narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Dhi'b narrated to us, from al-Zubarqan ibn Amr, from Zayd ibn Thabit, who said: "The Middle Prayer is the Dhuhr prayer."

[Report 5453: This report is abridged. It will come in full at 5460, by this route, from the narration of Ibn Abi Dhi'b, from al-Zubarqan.]

5454. al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: al-Hajjaj narrated to us, saying: Hammad narrated to us, saying: Ubayd Allah informed us, from Nafi', from Zayd ibn Thabit, that he said: "The Middle Prayer is the Dhuhr prayer."

[Report 5454: al-Hajjaj is Ibn al-Minhal. Hammad may be Ibn Zayd or Ibn Salamah.
Ubayd Allah is Ibn Umar ibn Hafs ibn Asim. Nafi' is the freedman (mawla) of Ibn Umar. I fear that his narration from Zayd ibn Thabit is mursal (has a missing Companion in the chain). I do not think he reached that generation of Companions. Ibn Abi Hatim explicitly stated that his narration from Hafsah and Aishah is mursal.]

5455. Ibn al-Barqi narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Maryam narrated to us, saying: Nafi' ibn Yazid informed us, saying: al-Walid ibn Abi al-Walid Abu Uthman narrated to me, saying: Abd Allah ibn Dinar narrated to me, from Abd Allah ibn Umar: that he was asked about the Middle Prayer, and he said: "It is the one that comes right after the Duha (forenoon) prayer."

[Report 5455: Ibn Abi Maryam is Sa'id ibn Abi Maryam, who is Sa'id ibn al-Hakam, whose biography passed at 3877.
Nafi' ibn Yazid al-Kala'i al-Misri: thiqah, trustworthy, firm in hadith, with no disagreement about him.
al-Walid ibn Abi al-Walid Abu Uthman: a trustworthy Successor. We have verified his biography in the commentary on the Musnad, at 5721.
This report is abridged. It will come after it in full, from another Successor, other than Abd Allah ibn Dinar.]

5456. Ibn al-Barqi narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Maryam narrated to us, saying: Nafi' ibn Yazid narrated to us, saying: al-Walid ibn Abi al-Walid narrated to me: that Salamah ibn Abi Maryam narrated to him: that a group of Quraysh sent to Abd Allah ibn Umar to ask him about the Middle Prayer. He said to them: "It is the one that comes right after the Duha prayer." They said to him: "Go back and ask him again, for he has only increased us in confusion!" Then Abd al-Rahman ibn Aflah, the freedman of Abd Allah ibn Umar, passed by them, and they sent for him as well. He said: "It is the one in which the Messenger of God (ﷺ) turned to the qiblah."

[Report 5456: Muslim ibn Abi Maryam, whose father's name is Yasar, al-Sulami al-Madani: a trustworthy Successor. Shu'bah, Malik, Ibn Jurayj, al-Layth, and others narrated from him. In the manuscript and the printed edition his name is written "Salamah" instead of "Muslim," which is an error by the copyists. No biography lists anyone with this name.
The report was narrated, in similar wording, by al-Tahawi, 1:99, by way of Yahya ibn Abd Allah ibn Bukayr, from Musa ibn Rabi'ah, from al-Walid ibn Abi al-Walid al-Madini, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Aflah: "that a group of his Companions sent him to Abd Allah ibn Umar . . .", and he mentioned its meaning.
al-Haythami mentioned it, abridged, in Majma' al-Zawa'id, 1:309, similar in wording. He said: "And from Abd al-Rahman ibn Aflah: that a group of Companions sent me to Ibn Umar, asking him about the Middle Prayer. He said: 'We used to talk about it being the prayer in which the Messenger of God (ﷺ) turned to the qiblah, the Dhuhr.'" He said: "It was narrated by al-Tabarani, and its narrators are trustworthy." al-Suyuti quoted it, 1:301, in a wording more abridged than this one, and attributed it to al-Tabarani in al-Awsat "with a chain whose narrators are trustworthy." So the narrations of al-Tahawi and al-Tabarani support this narration of Ibn Jarir, because it is from "Abd al-Rahman ibn Aflah," whom this group of Quraysh sent to ask Ibn Umar.
Musa ibn Rabi'ah al-Misri: thiqah, trustworthy. Ibn Abi Hatim biographed him, 4/1/142-143, and said: "Abu Zur'ah was asked about him, and he said: 'He used to be in Egypt, and he is trustworthy, with nothing wrong with him.'" I have found no biography of him with anyone else.
al-Walid ibn Abi al-Walid, as he heard the report from Muslim ibn Abi Maryam, also heard it from the messenger whom the group of Quraysh sent to Ibn Umar.
As for "Abd al-Rahman ibn Aflah": he is biographed in Ibn Abi Hatim 2/2/210: "Abd al-Rahman ibn Aflah, freedman of Abu Ayyub. He is the brother of Kathir ibn Aflah. He narrated from . . . Abu al-Nadr narrated from him the hadith of seclusion (al-'uzlah). I heard my father say that." The place of the dots is blank in the original text of Ibn Abi Hatim's book. Its editor, the scholar Shaykh Abd al-Rahman al-Yamani, said: "In al-Thiqat: from the umm walad (concubine who bore a child) of Abu Ayyub."
Ibn Sa'd also biographed him, 5:220, thus: "Abd al-Rahman ibn Aflah, freedman of Abu Ayyub al-Ansari. He was the foster-nursling of al-Kharijah ibn Zayd ibn Thabit al-Ansari. He heard from Abd Allah ibn Umar ibn al-Khattab."
I have found no biography of him other than this, so he is the one mentioned in this report.
Perhaps some narrators erred in making him "freedman of Abd Allah ibn Umar."
As for his words, "except confusion about it" (illa 'iyaan biha): one says "'ayya bil-amr 'iyyan" (with a kasra) and "'iyaan," meaning he did not know it, and its matter became unclear to him. In a hadith: "The cure for confusion is asking" (shifa' al-'iyy al-su'al). The second masdar (verbal noun), 'iyaan, is mentioned in al-Mu'yar of al-Shirazi.]

5457. Ibn al-Barqi narrated to me, saying: Ibn Abi Maryam narrated to us, saying: Nafi' informed us, saying: Zuhrah ibn Ma'bad narrated to me, saying: Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab narrated to me: that he was sitting, he and Urwah and Ibrahim ibn Talhah. Sa'id said to him: "I heard Abu Sa'id say: 'The Dhuhr prayer is the Middle Prayer.'" Then Ibn Umar passed by us, and Urwah said: "Send to him and ask him." The boy asked him, and he said: "It is the Dhuhr." We doubted the boy's words, so we all went to him and asked him, and he said: "It is the Dhuhr."

[Report 5457: Nafi' in this isnad is Nafi' ibn Yazid, whom we biographed at 5455. This is a sound isnad. The report is abridged from the earlier report at 5451, by way of Haywah and Ibn Lahi'ah, from Zuhrah ibn Ma'bad.]

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 238 (part 7 of 7):**

5458. Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Uthman ibn Umar narrated to us, saying: Abu Amir narrated to us, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Qays, from Ibn Abi Rafi, from his father, who was a freedman of Hafsa, who said: Hafsa had me write a copy of the Qur'an (mushaf) for her, and she said to me: "When you come to this verse, inform me so that I may dictate it to you as she recited it to me." When I came to this verse, ﴿Guard strictly the prayers, and the middle prayer﴾, I came to her, and she said: "Write: ﴿Guard strictly the prayers, and the middle prayer, and the afternoon prayer﴾." I then met Ubayy ibn Ka'b or Zayd ibn Thabit and said: "O Abu al-Mundhir, Hafsa has said such and such!" He said: "It is as she said. Are we not most occupied at the time of the noon prayer with our sheep and our water-camels?"

[[Note on the hadith 5458: Uthman ibn Umar ibn Fares ibn Luqayt al-Abdi: trustworthy (thiqah), one of the shaykhs of Ahmad and Ishaq; the Jama'ah (the compilers of the six books) narrated from him.
Abu Amir: he is al-Khazzaz (with dotted letters), and his name is Salih ibn Rustum. He is trustworthy; al-Tayalisi, Abu Dawud and others declared him trustworthy.
Abd al-Rahman ibn Qays al-Ataki, Abu Rawh al-Basri: trustworthy. Ibn Hibban mentioned him in al-Thiqat, and he and Ibn Khuzaymah narrated from him in their Sahihs. Ibn Abi Hatim gave him two biographical entries (2/2/277-278, nos. 1320 and 1321), which are one and the same, and he mentioned no criticism of him.
"Ibn Abi Nafi, from his father": I do not know who this "Ibn Abi Rafi" is, and I have not found a biography of him, except that he is mentioned in al-Tahdhib in this form, in the biography of Abd al-Rahman ibn Qays al-Ataki, among his shaykhs from whom he narrated.
It is highly probable that he is the son of Amr ibn Rafi, who will be mentioned in the commentary on 5463.
In the isnad of 5464 [it is stated]: This hadith has an unknown isnad, as you see. It will come with this isnad and wording at 5470, except for one letter, which we will mention.
Al-Suyuti mentioned it (1: 302) in a somewhat abridged form, saying: "Abd al-Razzaq, al-Bukhari in his History, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Dawud in al-Masahif narrated from Abu Rafi, the freedman of Hafsa..."
As for Ibn Jarir, this is his narration. As for al-Bukhari in al-Tarikh, I did not know its place in it. As for Abd al-Razzaq and Ibn Abi Dawud, I did not find a narration from Abu Rafi in them, which is certain to me. So I do not know how this is!
It is a marfu hadith (one traced to the Prophet), as shown by Hafsa's words "until I dictate it to you as she recited it to me." In the later narration it is "as I was recited it" (kama uqri'tuha), with the passive form, since its doer is not named. The one who recited to Hafsa and from whom she took the Qur'an was her husband, upon whom the Book was revealed, (ﷺ), as her explicit statement of this will come at 5462, 5463 and 5465.
As for her saying "amlaha" (dictate it): this is what is established in the manuscript. In the printed edition it is "amlīhā". Both are correct; it is said: "amalaltu al-kitab" and "amaltuhu" (I dictated the book). Both were used in the Qur'an: ﴿So let his guardian dictate with justice﴾ (from amalla), and ﴿so it is dictated to him morning and evening﴾ (from amla). Al-Farra said: "amalla" is the dialect of the people of the Hijaz and Banu Asad, and "amla" is the dialect of Banu Tamim and Qays.
As for his saying "I met Ubayy ibn Ka'b, or Zayd ibn Thabit, and said: O Abu al-Mundhir" and so on: the narrator was in doubt as to which of them he met. He then preferred that it was Ubayy ibn Ka'b, since his kunyah is Abu al-Mundhir, whereas Zayd's kunyah is Abu Sa'id, and it is also said Abu Kharijah.
Al-nawadih: plural of nadih, which is a type of camel used for drawing water. "Nadaha zar'ahu" means he irrigated his crop with a bucket. The meaning is that they were busy irrigating their palm-groves with water-camels.]]

* *

As for the reason for those who said this:

5459. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated this to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, saying: Amr ibn Abi Hakim informed me, saying: I heard al-Zibriqan relate from Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, from Zayd ibn Thabit, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to pray the noon prayer at the hottest time of the day, and he did not pray any prayer that was harder on the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) than it. He said: Then it was revealed: ﴿Guard strictly the prayers, and the middle prayer﴾. And he said: "Before it are two prayers and after it are two prayers."

[[Note on the hadith 5459: Amr ibn Abi Hakim is Amr ibn Kurdi, Abu Sa'id al-Wasiti, and he is trustworthy; Abu Dawud and al-Nasai and others declared him trustworthy. Shu'bah's narration from him is also an indication of his trustworthiness in Shu'bah's view.
Al-Zibriqan is Ibn Amr ibn Umayyah al-Damri; Ibn Sa'd (5: 184) affirmed this, mentioning him after "Ja'far ibn Amr" and stating that al-Bukhari and those after him did not distinguish between them, except Ibn Hibban, who mentioned this in a separate biography from the one from whom Kulayb ibn Subh narrated. Then he criticised Ibn Hibban for doing so. This is a wonder of wonders! For al-Bukhari made a separate biography of "Zibriqan, from Amr ibn Umayyah, from whom Kulayb narrated." But they distinguished between them, so I do not know what the great hafiz (Ibn Hajar? or the author's reference) found objectionable in Ibn Hibban!
And al-Zibriqan ibn Amr is trustworthy.
The hadith was narrated by Ahmad in al-Musnad (5: 183), from Muhammad ibn Ja'far, from Shu'bah, with this isnad.
Abu Dawud narrated it (411), from Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna, the shaykh of al-Tabari here, with this isnad.
Al-Bukhari narrated it in al-Kabir, in the biography of al-Zibriqan, from Ishaq, from Abd al-Samad, from Shu'bah, with it, concisely, as is his habit.
Al-Tahawi narrated it in Ma'ani al-Athar (1: 99), through Amr ibn Marzuq, from Shu'bah, with it.
Likewise al-Bayhaqi narrated it (1: 458) through Amr ibn Marzuq.
Ibn Kathir mentioned it (1: 577), from the narration of the Musnad. Then he pointed to the narration of Abu Dawud.
Al-Suyuti mentioned it (1: 301) and added its attribution to al-Ruyani, Abu Ya'la and al-Tabarani.
These are sound isnads.
A longer version will come after this, not connected in its isnad.]]

5460. Mujahid ibn Musa narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Dhi'b informed us, from al-Zibriqan, who said: A group of Quraysh passed by Zayd ibn Thabit, and they sent to him two men asking him about the middle prayer. Zayd said: "It is the noon prayer." Then two men from them stood up and went to Usamah ibn Zayd and asked him about the middle prayer, and he said: "It is the noon prayer. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to pray the noon prayer at the hottest time of the day, and behind him there would be only one row or two rows, since people would be in their midday rest and in their trade." The Messenger of Allah said: "I was determined to burn the houses of people who do not attend the prayer!" He said: Then this verse was revealed: ﴿Guard strictly the prayers, and the middle prayer﴾.

[[Note on the hadith 5460: It is a longer version of the hadith before it, but here it is broken in its isnad, as we will mention.
Ahmad narrated it in al-Musnad (5: 206, Halabi edition), from Yazid, who is Ibn Harun, from Ibn Abi Dhi'b, with it. But in his narration there is an addition at its beginning: "Zayd ibn Thabit passed by them while they were gathered, so they sent to him two of their servant boys asking him about the middle prayer. He said: 'It is the Asr.' Then two men from them stood up to him and asked him, and he said: 'It is the Zuhr.'"
So in Ahmad's narration, Zayd ibn Thabit said to the two boys: "It is the Asr," and he said to the two men who stood up to him: "It is the Zuhr." The addition of the boys' question and Zayd's answer that it is the Asr has been omitted from al-Tabari's narration here. This addition is also established in Ibn Kathir (1: 577), in his transmission of the hadith from the Musnad of Ahmad.
I have not found it in any other source of this hadith apart from that.
In the Musnad there occurs "Yazid ibn Abi Dhi'b narrated to us, from al-Zibriqan," which is a confusion by the copyists; it also appears in the manuscript of the Musnad (M). There is no narrator by this name. The hadith is from "Yazid ibn Harun," from "Ibn Abi Dhi'b," as shown by al-Tabari's narration here.
Ibn Kathir's copy added confusion to confusion in quoting the Musnad: "Yazid ibn Abi Wahb narrated to us, from al-Zibriqan"! We do not know whether this is from the copyists or the printers.
Al-Tahawi also narrated the hadith in Ma'ani al-Athar (1: 99), from al-Rabi ibn Sulayman al-Muradi, from Khalid ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Ibn Abi Dhi'b, from al-Zibriqan. But it is abridged: the mention of Usamah ibn Zayd is omitted, and the words "the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to pray the noon prayer at the hottest time..." to the end of the hadith are made part of Zayd ibn Thabit's words, not Usamah's. Perhaps this abridgement is an error by some of the narrators.
Al-Bukhari pointed to it through the route of Ibn Abi Dhi'b, as is his habit of brevity, and established that it is from Zayd and Usamah. He mentioned it in the biography of al-Zibriqan (2/1/397), saying:
"Hisham said: Sadaqah narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Dhi'b, who said: Zibriqan al-Damri narrated to us, from Zayd and Usamah, similar to it," meaning similar to a hadith before it which we will mention.
Then he said: "Adam narrated to us, Ibn Abi Dhi'b narrated to us, who said: Zibriqan al-Damri narrated to us, similar to it."
Then he said: "Yahya ibn Abi Bukayr narrated it from Ibn Abi Dhi'b, similar to it."
So the narration of Usamah ibn Zayd is established in this hadith by this route in all the narrations, and omitting it is an error.
Likewise it is established in other sources. Al-Suyuti mentioned it in full (1: 301) and attributed it to Ahmad, Ibn Mani, al-Nasai, Ibn Jarir, al-Shashi and al-Diya.
Al-Tayalisi narrated something similar, in abridged form (628), from Abu Dhi'b, from al-Zibriqan, from Zahrah, who said: "We were sitting with Zayd ibn Thabit, and they sent for Usamah ibn Zayd and asked him about the middle prayer. He said: 'It is the noon prayer, which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to pray at the hottest time.'"
Likewise al-Bayhaqi narrated it (1: 458) through al-Tayalisi.
Al-Bukhari mentioned it in al-Kabir (2/1/396-397), from Abu Dawud, who is al-Tayalisi, with it.
Ibn Kathir quoted it (1: 577) from the Musnad of al-Tayalisi.
The longer hadith here has a broken isnad, as we said. What shows its break is the isnad before it, in which al-Zibriqan narrates from Urwah, and the narration of al-Tayalisi, in which he narrates from Zahrah.
Therefore Ibn Kathir said, after quoting it from the narration of the Musnad of Imam Ahmad: "Al-Zibriqan is Ibn Amr ibn Umayyah al-Damri. He did not meet any of the Companions. The correct version is what preceded from his narration from Zahr ibn Ma'bad and from Urwah ibn al-Zubayr."
Al-Haythami said in Majma al-Zawa'id (1: 308-309): "Ahmad narrated it, and its narrators are trustworthy, except that al-Zibriqan did not hear from Usamah ibn Zayd ibn Thabit."
It is worth noting that al-Suyuti attributed it to al-Nasai, as we mentioned, but I have not found it in al-Nasai. Al-Haythami said in Majma al-Zawa'id: "Al-Nasai narrated it. The Shaykh said in al-Atraf: It is not in the hearing (i.e., the narrator did not hear it), and Abu al-Qasim did not mention it." He means that the hafiz al-Mizzi said this. Perhaps it is established in the narration of some narrators of the Sunan of al-Nasai and not others.
Al-Hajirah and al-Hajir: the middle of the day from the decline of the sun until the Asr, and at that time it is at its most intense heat.
Al-Qa'ilah: the midday heat, the middle of the day. Al-qaylulah: the midday nap. It is said "qala yaqil" (he took a midday rest). The qaylulah is also called "al-qa'ilah," and this is what is meant here.]]

[[The author's speech has been abridged due to its great length.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 239 (part 1 of 2):

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿But if you fear, then on foot or riding﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By this, exalted is His mention, He means: "Stand before God in your prayers, obeying Him," for the reason we have already explained concerning its meaning, "if you fear an enemy of yours, O people, whom you dread for your own selves when you meet them, that you pray standing on your feet upon the ground, devoutly obedient to God, then pray ﴿on foot﴾, walking on your feet, while you are in your fighting, your battle, and your struggle against your enemy, ﴿or riding﴾, upon the backs of your beasts. For that suffices you then in place of your standing, devoutly obedient." [[In the manuscript: "min al-qiyam minkum aw qanitin" ("from your standing, or devoutly obedient"), with an added "aw," which has no meaning unless there is a lacuna in the text. I have left what is in the printed edition as it is, for it is sound.]]

* *

Because we have said that the meaning is thus, it is permissible to put "al-rijal" in the accusative by the implied meaning. This is because the Arabs do this specifically in the conditional (jaza', conditional construction), since its second part resembles what is coordinated with its first part. This is made clear by their saying: "in khayran fakhayran, wa in sharran fasharran" ("if [it is] good, then [it is] good; and if [it is] evil, then [it is] evil"), meaning: "If you do good, you will receive good, and if you do evil, you will receive evil." They thus coordinate the response with the first part, since the second is put in the jussive by the jussive of the first. Likewise His words: "fa-in khiftum fa-rijalan aw rukbanan" mean: "If you fear that you pray standing upon the ground, then pray on foot."

* *

"Al-rijal" is the plural of "rajil" and "rajl." As for the people of the Hijaz, they say for the singular of "al-rijal": "rajul," which is heard from them: "So-and-so walked to the House of God, barefoot, rajulan." [[This explanation of the Arabic dialects regarding "rajul" is not exhaustive in the books of lexicography.]] It has also been heard from some Arab tribes in its singular form "rajlan," as one of the Banu 'Aqil said:

"Ala idha absarat Layla bi-khalwatin ... an azdara bayta Llahi rajlan hafiya"
(Ala, when Layla sees me in privacy... that I visit the House of God barefoot, rajlan.) [[Lisan al-Arab (rajl), on the authority of Ibn al-A'rabi. Ibn Hisham cited it in the chapter on "al-hal" (the circumstantial accusative) and its use for the singular. Its version is: "... Layla bi-khufyatin ziyarata bayt Allah..." "Azdar" is the form "iftaʿala" from "al-ziyara" (visiting).]]

Whoever says "rajlan" for the masculine says "rajli" for the feminine, and in the plural of the masculine and feminine it is permissible to say: "ata al-qawmu rijali wa rijali," like "kusali wa kusali."

* *

It has been reported from some that he used to read it: "fa-in khiftum farijalan," with shaddah. And from some that he used to read: "farijalan," [[meaning with a damma on the ra' and a lightened jim, a form that is mentioned among the irregular readings (shawadhdh al-qira'at).]] Both readings are not permissible to recite by, in our view, because they contradict the transmitted, widely attested recitation in the cities of the Muslims. [[In the printed edition: "bi-khilaf al-qira'a al-mawruthah" ("contrary to the transmitted recitation"); the correct reading is what is in the manuscript.]]

* *

As for "al-rukban," it is the plural of "rakib." It is said: "huwa rakib, wa hum rukban, wa rukbatun, wa rikab, wa arkab, wa arkub." It is said: "ja'anā arkubun min al-nas wa arakib" ("a group of people came to us").

* *

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said in accordance with what we have said regarding this.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The fear that permits the worshipper to pray the obligatory prayer on foot, walking, or riding, moving about (ja'il), [[al-ja'il: the one who moves about in war in a sweep against his enemy; his ja'ula is his turning while on his horse in order to position himself against his opponent.]] is fear for one's life (al-mihjah) at the time of drawing swords (al-silah) and close combat (al-musayafah) in fighting against one whom it is ordered to fight, from an enemy of the Muslims, or a belligerent, or the pursuit of a wild beast, or a charging camel, or a flowing torrent in which one fears drowning. [[In the printed edition: "al-khawf 'ala al-muhimmah 'inda al-salmah," which is blatant nonsense. In the manuscript: "al-khawf 'ala al-muhimmah 'inda al-masalah," and the correct reading is what I have given from my reading of this text. Al-mihjah: the soul, the pure self. Al-sallah: drawing swords; it is said: "we came upon them at the drawing of swords," meaning at the drawing of swords when the fight grows hot. Sala al-jamal yasulu, so he is sa'il and sa'ul: that is when it leaps upon its herdsman and devours him, and attacks people, chasing them and driving them away from its fright.]]

And whatever circumstance usually makes a person perish if he performs the prayer of safety (salat al-amn), then if that is the case, he may pray the prayer of extreme fear wherever his face is, gesturing with a sign, according to the generality of God's Book: "fa-in khiftum farijalan aw rukbanan." He did not restrict the fear to any particular kind, provided the fear has the characteristics I have mentioned.

* *

We have said that the fear that permits the worshipper to pray in that manner is the kind where the usual outcome is death if he performs the prayer with its proper limits, and that is the state of extreme fear, because...

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 239 (part 2 of 2):

5566- Muhammad ibn Humayd and Sufyan ibn Waki' narrated to me, both saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Abdullah ibn Nafi', from his father, from Ibn Umar, who said: The Prophet ﷺ said concerning the prayer of fear: "The leader stands, and a group of the people stands with him, and they perform one prostration. Then another group stands between them and the enemy. Then those who prostrated with their leader depart, and they take the place of those who have not yet prayed. Those who have not prayed come forward and pray with their leader one prostration. Then their leader departs, having completed his prayer, and each of the two groups performs one prostration for itself after his prayer. And if the fear is more intense than that, [they pray] on foot or on horseback."

[Note on the hadith: Jarir is Ibn Abd al-Hamid al-Dabbi. Abdullah ibn Nafi', freedman of Ibn Umar, is very weak. Al-Bukhari said of him in al-Du'afa' (The Weak Narrators): "munkar al-hadith" (his narrations are rejected). I have discussed his weakness at length in al-Musnad, no. 4769.

This hadith was transmitted in this form by Jarir from Abdullah ibn Nafi', from his father, from Ibn Umar, as a marfu' report (traced directly to the Prophet ﷺ).

Ibn Majah also transmitted it, no. 12587, from Muhammad ibn al-Sabbah, from Jarir, from Ubayd Allah ibn Umar, from Nafi', from Ibn Umar, also as a marfu' report. Its chain is sahih (sound). Al-Hafiz (Ibn Hajar) in Fath al-Bari (the commentary on Sahih al-Bukhari, "Fath") 2:360 pointed to this transmission of Ibn Majah and said: "Its chain is jayyid" (good).

Malik transmitted it in the Muwatta', p. 184, in a similar sense: "From Nafi': that Abdullah ibn Umar, when asked about the prayer of fear, would say..." and he mentioned something similar as Ibn Umar's own words. Then at its end he said: "Malik said: Nafi' said: I do not think Abdullah ibn Umar related it to me except from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ."

Al-Bukhari also transmitted it, 8:150, from Abdullah ibn Yusuf, from Malik.

Al-Shafi'i in al-Umm 1:197 transmitted from Malik a fragment from its beginning, then referred to the rest and mentioned its end. Likewise al-Bayhaqi, 3:256, transmitted it through al-Shafi'i from Malik.

Al-Suyuti, 1:308, mentioned it from the narration of Malik and attributed it additionally to Abd al-Razzaq.

Thus the doubt of Malik about its being traced to the Prophet ﷺ from Nafi', followed by the affirmation of its being traced to the Prophet in the narration of Ubayd Allah ibn Umar al-Umari from Nafi' in Ibn Majah, strengthens the narration of Jarir from Abdullah ibn Nafi' that is here.]

5567- Sa'id ibn Yahya al-Umawi narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: Ibn Jurayj narrated to us, from Musa ibn Uqba, from Nafi', from Ibn Umar, who said: "If they become mixed up," meaning in the fighting, "then it is only remembrance (dhikr) and a gesture with the head." Ibn Umar said: The Prophet ﷺ said: "And if they are more than that, they pray standing and on horseback."

[Note on the hadith: Sa'id ibn Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Umawi, his biography has passed at no. 2255.

Al-Bukhari transmitted this hadith, 3:259 (Fath), from Sa'id ibn Yahya, Shaykh of al-Tabari, with this same chain, but did not mention its full wording. Al-Hafiz mentioned, p. 360, this narration of al-Tabari as clarification of al-Bukhari's narration.

Al-Bayhaqi transmitted it, 3:255-256, through al-Haytham ibn Khalaf al-Duri, from Sa'id ibn Yahya al-Umawi, with the same chain. He mentioned its wording in full, then referred to al-Bukhari's narration.

His words "ikhtalatu" (they became mixed up): meaning the two armies became intermingled during the sword-fighting and close combat. This word is thus established in Fath, quoting al-Tabari, and in al-Bayhaqi's al-Sunan al-Kubra. In the manuscript and the printed edition it appears as "ikhtalafu" (they differed), with the letter fa instead of ta. This is a copyists' error.

His words "wa-ishara bi-l-ra's" (and a gesture with the head): meaning that they pray by signalling, remembering and reciting, and indicating the bowing (ruku') and prostration (sujud) with the head. This is the established reading in Fath and al-Sunan al-Kubra. In the manuscript and the printed edition it appears as "wa-ashara bi-l-ra's" (and he gestured with the head), which is also an error.]

* *

= The Prophet ﷺ therefore distinguished between the ruling on the prayer of fear in circumstances other than sword-fighting and pursuit, and the ruling on the prayer of fear in circumstances of severe fear and sword-fighting, as we have narrated from Ibn Umar. It was thereby known that His saying, may His remembrance be exalted, "﴿If you fear, then [pray] on foot or riding﴾," refers only to the fear whose description we have given.

In the same way as what Ibn Umar narrated from the Prophet ﷺ, he also narrated from Ibn Umar that he used to say:

5568- Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, from Ayyub, from Nafi', from Ibn Umar, that he said concerning the prayer of fear: "A group of the people prays one rak'ah with him, and another group stands guard. Then those with whom he has prayed one rak'ah go away until they stand in the place of their companions. Then those others come, and he prays with them one rak'ah, then he gives the salam, and each group stands and prays one rak'ah." He said: "And if the fear is more intense than that, [they pray] on foot or riding."

[Note on the report: This is explicitly a mawquf report (traced to Ibn Umar only, not to the Prophet ﷺ), and it has the same meaning as the previous hadith, no. 5566.]

* *

As for the number of rak'at in that state of the prayer, I prefer that it not be reduced below the number in a state of security. If someone reduces it and prays only one rak'ah, I consider that acceptable, because:

5569- Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to me, saying: Abu Awana narrated to us, from Bukayr ibn al-Akhnas, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "Allah made the prayer obligatory through the tongue of your Prophet ﷺ: four [rak'at] in the settled state, two [rak'at] when travelling, and one [rak'ah] in fear."

[Note on the hadith: Bukayr ibn al-Akhnas al-Laythi al-Kufi is a reliable Successor (tabi'i). "Bukayr" is the diminutive form. In the printed edition it appears as "Bakr", without the ya', which is an error.

This hadith was transmitted in Ahmad's Musnad, no. 2124 from Yazid; no. 2293 from Affan; and no. 3332 from Waki'. All three transmitted it from Abu Awana, with the same wording.

Al-Bukhari transmitted it briefly, as is his habit, in his al-Tarikh al-Kabir, in the biography of Bukayr, 1/2/112, from Abu Nu'aym, from Abu Awana. Muslim transmitted it, 1:192, from four Shaykhs, from Abu Awana.

Al-Bayhaqi likewise transmitted it in al-Sunan al-Kubra, 3:135, through Yahya ibn Yahya, from Abu Awana. Ahmad also transmitted it, no. 2177, from al-Qasim ibn Malik al-Muzani, from Ayyub ibn A'idh, from Bukayr ibn al-Akhnas, with the same wording.

Muslim also transmitted it, 1:192, through al-Qasim ibn Malik.

Al-Bayhaqi transmitted it, 3:263-264, with two chains through Ayyub ibn A'idh. Ibn Kathir mentioned it, 1:585, and attributed it additionally to Abu Dawud, al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah.]

* *

On the interpretation of His saying: ﴿So when you are secure, remember Allah as He taught you what you did not know﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: Its interpretation is: "So when you are secure", O believers, from your enemy, who could be able to kill you while you are occupied with your prayer which He has made obligatory upon you, and from anyone else whom you were fearing for yourselves during your prayer; and you are at peace: "then remember Allah" in your prayer and in other than it, by thanking Him, praising Him and extolling Him for what He has bestowed upon you of success in attaining the truth from which your enemies, the people of disbelief in Allah, went astray; "as He guided you" by teaching you His rulings, His lawful and unlawful, and the reports of the nations before you, and the news that will happen after you, in the immediate life of this world and the deferred life of the Hereafter, which others did not know and were blind to, concerning that and other matters, as a favour from Him to you. Thus He taught you what you did not know before His teaching you.

* *

Mujahid used to say concerning His saying "So when you are secure," that:

5570- Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Layth, from Mujahid: "So when you are secure," he said: "You have left the abode of travel for the abode of residence."

* *

Ibn Zayd said, in agreement with what we have said on this:

5571- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said concerning His saying: "So when you are secure, remember Allah," he said: "So when you are secure, perform the prayer as Allah has made it obligatory upon you. When fear comes, they have a concession."

* *

And His saying here, "Remember Allah," he said: "The prayer," "as He taught you what you did not know."

[Note on the passage: From the beginning of the phrase "And His saying here: 'Remember Allah...'" to the end of this paragraph is, in my estimation, a statement of Mujahid in report no. 5570. I fear that the copyist has spoiled the flow of the text. I think that his earlier words, "And in agreement with what we have said on this, Ibn Zayd said," followed by report no. 5571, should precede report no. 5570. I also think that the phrase "And His saying here" is a corrupt statement, and that "here" (ha huna) in the original text was a sign directing that the passage from the beginning of "And Mujahid used to say..." through to after report no. 5571 be moved. The sequence would then be:

"...So He taught you what you did not know before His teaching you. And in agreement with what we have said on this, Ibn Zayd said:

5570- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us...

And Mujahid used to say concerning His saying: 'So when you are secure':

5571- Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Layth, from Mujahid: 'So when you are secure,' he said: 'You have left the abode of travel for the abode of residence.' And His saying: 'Remember Allah,' he said: 'The prayer,' 'as He taught you what you did not know.'"

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: "And this saying that we have mentioned from Mujahid..."

I have not dared to make this change in the printed edition, although I have no doubt about what I have concluded.]

* *

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: This saying that we have mentioned from Mujahid is not the most correct, and the saying of others is closer to the truth than his. This is because all agree that once fear has passed, the obligatory prayer must be performed, even if one is travelling, with its bowing, prostration and limits, standing on the ground, neither walking nor riding, just as is required of one who is settled in his city and land, except for the concession of shortening it during travel. No mention of travel has occurred in this verse, so that His saying "﴿Remember Allah as He taught you what you did not know﴾" could be directed toward it. Rather, mention of the prayer has occurred in the state of security and in the state of severe fear, and so Allah, glorified and exalted, made His servants aware of the description of what is obligatory upon them of the prayer in both states. Then He said: "﴿So when you are secure﴾", that is, the fear has gone, "so establish your prayer and remember Me in it and in other than it, in the same manner as I made obligatory upon you before the state of fear arose."

[Note on the phrase "wasf al-wajib" (the description of what is obligatory): In the manuscript it reads "wasfihi al-wajib 'alayhim" (its description, what is obligatory upon them), and the correct reading is what is in the printed edition.]

Moreover, if mention of travel had occurred, and then Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, wanted to make His creation aware of the description of what is obligatory upon them of the prayer after they have settled, He would have said: "﴿So when you settle, remember Allah as He taught you what you did not know﴾", and would not have said "﴿So when you are secure﴾".

[Note: In the printed edition the text reads: "Before the state of fear arose and after it. If mention of travel had occurred..." This is a bad confusion, and some correctors replaced "If mention of travel had occurred" with "Had mention of travel occurred..." leaving the sentence without a meaning, and corrected what did not need correcting! The correct reading is what is in the manuscript, as I have written it.]

And in His saying, may His remembrance be exalted, "﴿So when you are secure﴾", there is clear evidence for the soundness of the view of those who direct the interpretation of this to what we have said concerning it, and against the view of Mujahid.

[Note: In the printed edition it reads "and to the opposition of Mujahid's view", with the added "to", which is a corrupt and corrupting addition. The word "opposition" (khilaf) is conjoined to the phrase "on the soundness of the view of..."]

**The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And those of you who die and leave behind wives, [there is] a bequest for their wives, provision until the [end of the] year, without their being driven out﴾**

Abu Ja'far said: By this, the Exalted, may His remembrance be exalted, means: "And those of you who die," O men, "and leave behind wives," meaning wives who were theirs during their lifetime, by marriage, not by right of ownership (ملك يمين, *milk yamin*). Then the report turned away from the mention of those with whom the report had begun, like the similar instance that has passed in His saying: ﴿And those of you who die and leave behind wives, they shall wait by themselves for four months and ten days﴾ [Surat al-Baqarah: 234] [[The manuscript and the printed edition stop the verse at His saying "and leave behind wives," so I completed it for clarity.]], to the report about their wives. We have already mentioned the reason for this and shown the soundness of the view on it in its similar instance that came before it, so that is sufficient and there is no need to repeat it here. [[See what has passed in this volume: 77–79.]]

* *

Then the Exalted, may His remembrance be exalted, said: "a bequest for their wives." The readers (قراء, *qurra'*, reciters of the Qur'an) differed in reciting this. Some of them read: "وَصِيَّةً لأزواجهم" with the *wasiyya* in the accusative (نصب, *nasb*), meaning: "let them bequeath a bequest for their wives," or: "it is incumbent upon them [to bequeath] a bequest for their wives." [[What is between the brackets is an addition without which the sentence does not stand.]]

* *

Others read: ﴿وَصِيَّةٌ لأزْوَاجِهِمْ﴾ with the *wasiyya* in the nominative (رفع, *raf'*).

* *

Then the grammarians (أهل العربية, *ahl al-'Arabiyya*, the scholars of Arabic grammar) differed about the reason for the nominative of *wasiyya*.

Some of them said: it is nominative in the sense of "the bequest has been prescribed for them." He based this on the fact that it is so in the reading of ʿAbdullah [ibn Masʿud]. [[The reading of ʿAbdullah ibn Masʿud: ﴿كتب عليكم الوصية لأزواجكم﴾ ("the bequest for your wives has been prescribed for you"). See Shadhdh al-Qira'at by Ibn Khalawayh: 15, and Ma'ani al-Qur'an by al-Farra': 1/156, and others who have authenticated it.]] So the sense of the statement according to this speaker is: "And those of you who die and leave behind wives, a bequest has been prescribed for their wives," then the mention of "has been prescribed" was dropped, and "the bequest" was made nominative by that meaning, even though its mention is omitted.

* *

Others among them said: rather, the "bequest" is nominative by virtue of "for their wives," so the interpretation is: "for their wives is a bequest."

* *

The first view is more correct in this matter, namely that when *wasiyya* is nominative, it is nominative in the sense of: "a bequest has been prescribed for your wives." This is because the Arabs leave indefinite nouns (النكرات, *al-nakirat*) implicit together with their nominative markers (مرافع, *marafi'*) before them when they are left implicit; but when they state them explicitly, they begin with them. So they say: "A man came to me today," and when they say: "A man came to me today," they hardly say it except that the man is present, and they point to him with "this," or he is absent but the speaker is known to the hearer to be referring to him; or they omit "this" and leave it implicit, even though they omit it, because the hearer knows the speaker's meaning, as the Exalted has said: ﴿A surah which We have sent down﴾ [Surat al-Nur: 1] and ﴿A declaration of immunity from Allah and His Messenger﴾ [Surat al-Tawbah: 1]. Thus it is likewise in His saying: "a bequest for their wives."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The more correct of the two readings in our view is the reading of the one who read it in the nominative, because the apparent meaning of the Qur'an indicates that the right of a widow to remain in her deceased husband's house for a full year was a right for her before the revelation of His saying: ﴿And those of you who die and leave behind wives, they shall wait by themselves for four months and ten days﴾ [Surat al-Baqarah: 234], and before the revelation of the verse of inheritance [[See what will come, pp. 254–258.]]; and because the reports from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ are consistent with what the apparent meaning indicates, that their husbands bequeathed this to them before their deaths, or did not bequeath it to them.

* *

If someone asks: "What is the proof for this?"

It is said: When the Exalted, may His remembrance be exalted, said: "And those of you who die and leave behind wives, a bequest for their wives," and the one making a bequest—there is no doubt—bequeaths during his lifetime what he orders to be carried out after his death, and it was impossible for him to bequeath after his death, then the Exalted, may His remembrance be exalted, made the widow's residence for a year after her husband's death [[In the printed edition: "so the Exalted made," with a fa' instead of a waw; the manuscript's reading is correct. The printed edition has "residence for a year"; I have kept what is in the manuscript, and both are the same.]] = we know that it is a right owed to her from his property without any bequest from him to her, since it is impossible for the deceased to have made a bequest after his death. [[In the printed edition: "knowing that it is a right for her"; in the manuscript it is "we know it is a right," without dots; the correct reading is what I have given, and the context of the sentence is: "when Allah said... and the one making a bequest... and it was impossible... and Allah made... = we know that it is a right."]]

* *

If the meaning of the statement were according to the interpretation of the one who said "let him bequeath a bequest," the revelation would have been: "And those of you whose death approaches and who leave behind wives, [there is] a bequest for their wives," as He said: ﴿It has been prescribed for you, when death approaches one of you, if he leaves behind wealth, that he make a bequest﴾ [Surat al-Baqarah: 180]. [[This is al-Tabari's refutation of those who read it in the accusative.]]

* *

Furthermore, if that were obligatory for them as a bequest from their deceased husbands, it would not have been a right for them if their husbands had not bequeathed it to them before their deaths. And the heirs would have had the right to expel them before the year was over, but the Exalted said: "without their being driven out." However, the matter is contrary to what the reader understood in his interpretation: "a bequest for their wives," meaning that Allah had commanded their husbands to bequeath to them. Rather, the interpretation is: "And those of you who die and leave behind wives, Allah has prescribed for their wives, upon you, O believers, a bequest from Him for them, that you not drive them out of their husbands' dwellings for a year," just as the Exalted said in Surat al-Nisa': ﴿without causing harm, a bequest from Allah﴾ [Surat al-Nisa': 12]. Then the mention of "Allah has prescribed" is omitted, being sufficiently indicated by the context, and "the bequest" is nominative by the meaning we stated earlier.

* *

If someone says: "Is it permissible for *wasiyya* to be in the accusative [as a circumstantial accusative (حال, *hal*), meaning bequeathing for them a bequest]?" [[In the manuscript and the printed edition there is a blank where the material between the brackets should be; this addition between the brackets I have inferred from the context. He means, in his following statement, the circumstantial that comes as a verbal noun (مصدر, *masdar*), like their saying: "He came suddenly (بغتة), he came running (ركضا), I killed him in cold blood (صبرا), I met him face to face (كفاحا)." See Sibawayh 1: 186, and Awdah al-Masalik 1: 195, and others. This is what I could determine of Abu Ja'far's statement and his rejection of this view, and it is apparently correct, God willing.]]

It is said: No. That would only be permissible if the statement preceding "a bequest" contained something that the bequest could be understood as coming out of. But since nothing preceded it that would make it fitting for it to be in the accusative as coming out of that, it is not permissible to make it accusative in that sense.

* *

Mention of some who said: the full year's residence was a right for the widows of the deceased after their death = as we have said = [[See what has passed, p. 252 and footnote no. 3.]] their husbands bequeathed it to them or did not bequeath it to them, and that this was abrogated (منسوخ, *mansukh*) by what we have mentioned: the four months and ten days, and the inheritance.

5572 – Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: al-Hajjaj ibn al-Minhal narrated to us, saying: Hammam ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: I asked Qatadah about His saying: "And those of you who die and leave behind wives, a bequest for their wives, provision until the [end of the] year, without their being driven out," and he said: When a woman's husband died, she had residence and maintenance for a year from her husband's property, as long as she did not leave. Then that was abrogated later in Surat al-Nisa', and a fixed share was assigned to her: an eighth if he had children, and a quarter if he had no children; and her waiting period (عدة, *'idda*) is four months and ten days. The Exalted said: ﴿And those of you who die and leave behind wives, they shall wait by themselves for four months and ten days﴾ [Surat al-Baqarah: 234], so this verse abrogated what was before it concerning the year.

5573 – Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi' regarding His saying: "And those of you who die and leave behind wives, a bequest for their wives, provision until the [end of the] year, without their being driven out," the verse. He said: This was before the verse of inheritance was revealed. A widow had residence and maintenance for a year if she wished. Then that was abrogated in Surat al-Nisa', and a fixed share was assigned to her: she was given an eighth if he had children, and if he had no children she had a quarter; and her waiting period was set at four months and ten days. He said: ﴿And those of you who die and leave behind wives, they shall wait by themselves for four months and ten days﴾.

5574 – Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: ʿAbdullah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Muʿawiyah ibn Salih narrated to me, from ʿAli ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding His saying: "And those of you who die and leave behind wives, a bequest for their wives, provision until the [end of the] year, without their being driven out." He said: When a man died and left a wife, she observed the waiting period for a year in his house, and was maintained from his property. Then the Exalted sent down later: ﴿And those of you who die and leave behind wives, they shall wait by themselves for four months and ten days﴾, and this is the waiting period of a widow. Except if she is pregnant, then her waiting period is to give birth to what is in her womb. And concerning her inheritance He said: ﴿And for them is a quarter of what you leave, if you have no child; but if you have a child, then for them is an eighth﴾ [Surat al-Nisa': 12]. So Allah explained the woman's inheritance and left out the bequest and the maintenance.

5575 – Narrated to us from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: I heard ʿUbaydullah ibn Sulayman say: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying: "a bequest for their wives, provision until the [end of the] year, without their being driven out": When a man died, he would maintain his wife for a year until the year was over, and she would not remarry until she completed the year. And this is abrogated: the maintenance for her was abrogated by the quarter and the eighth from the inheritance, and the year was abrogated by four months and ten days.

5576 – Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abu Zuhayr narrated to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak regarding His saying: "And those of you who die and leave behind wives, a bequest for their wives, provision until the [end of the] year, without their being driven out," he said: When a man died, he maintained his wife until the year, and she would not remarry until the year had passed. Then Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿And those of you who die and leave behind wives, they shall wait by themselves for four months and ten days﴾, so the year's term was abrogated, and the maintenance was abrogated by the inheritance of the quarter and the eighth.

5577 – Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: I asked ʿAta' about His saying: "And those of you who die and leave behind wives, a bequest for their wives, provision until the [end of the] year, without their being driven out." He said: The woman's inheritance from her husband was from his dwelling (ربع, *rab'*): that she might reside, if she wished, from the day her husband died until the year, saying: "But if they leave, there is no blame upon you" [Surat al-Baqarah: 240], the verse; then what Allah prescribed of inheritance abrogated it. He said: And Mujahid said: "a bequest for their wives" is residence for a year, then this verse was abrogated by the inheritance. [[In the printed edition: "min rī'ihi" with a yā'; this has no meaning here. The rab' means a dwelling, house, or residence; in the hadith of Usamah, when he said to him: "Did ʿAqil leave us any rab' (property)?", meaning a dwelling; the plural is riba' and rubu' and arba'. The phrase "min rab'ihi" is omitted in al-Durr al-Manthur from its transmission of this report, 1: 309.]]

5578 – Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: When the bequest existed, the widows of the dead had a year's maintenance. Allah abrogated that which was prescribed for the wife of a year's maintenance by inheritance, so He gave her a quarter or an eighth. And regarding His saying: ﴿And those of you who die and leave behind wives, they shall wait by themselves for four months and ten days﴾, he said: this is the abrogating verse.

* *

Mention of those who said: that was to be for them by a bequest from their husbands to them:

5579 – Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: "And those of you who die and leave behind wives," the verse. He said: This was before the fixed shares, and a man would bequeath to his wife and to whomever he wished. Then that was later abrogated, and Allah assigned their inheritances to those entitled to inheritance, and prescribed for the wife an eighth if he had a child, and if he had no child she had a quarter. And the maintenance of the wife for a year from her husband's property was prescribed, after which she would leave his house. The waiting period of four months and ten days abrogated it, and the quarter or eighth abrogated the bequest for them, so the bequest became for the relatives who do not inherit.

5580 – Musa narrated to me, saying: ʿAmr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "And those of you who die and leave behind wives, a bequest for their wives," down to "what they do with themselves of what is reasonable." On the day this verse was revealed, when a man died he bequeathed to his wife her maintenance and residence for a year, and her waiting period was four months and ten days. If she left when the four months and ten days ended, the maintenance was cut off from her; this is His saying: "But if they leave." This was before the verses of the fixed shares were revealed, and then it was abrogated by the quarter and the eighth; she took her share, and she had neither residence nor maintenance.

5581 – Ahmad ibn al-Miqdam narrated to me, saying: al-Mu'tamir narrated to us, saying: I heard my father say: Qatadah claimed that a wife would be bequeathed her maintenance until the end of the year.

* *

Mention of those who said: "That which was for them of provision until the year was abrogated, without its being specified in what manner it was for them":

5582 – Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Habib, from Ibrahim regarding His saying: "And those of you who die and leave behind wives, a bequest for their wives, provision until the [end of the] year," he said: It is abrogated.

5583 – Al-Hasan ibn al-Zubriqan narrated to us, saying: Usamah narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Habib ibn Abi Thabit, who said: I heard Ibrahim say, and he mentioned something similar.

5584 – Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, from Husayn, from Yazid al-Nahwi, from ʿIkrimah and al-Hasan al-Basri, both said regarding "And those of you who die and leave behind wives, a bequest for their wives, provision until the [end of the] year, without their being driven out": That was abrogated by the verse of inheritance and what was fixed for them in it of the quarter and the eighth, and the year's term was abrogated by making her term four months and ten days.

5585 – Yaʿqub ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, saying: Ibn ʿUlayyah narrated to us, from Yunus, from Ibn Sirin, from Ibn ʿAbbas: that he stood up to address the people here, and he recited to them Surat al-Baqarah, and explained to them in it [[In the printed edition: "fa-bayyana lahum fīhā," and the correct reading is that of the manuscript and no. 2652: he explained to them from it what he explained.]], and when he came to this verse: ﴿It has been prescribed for you, when death approaches one of you, if he leaves behind wealth, that he make a bequest for the parents and the near relatives﴾ [Surat al-Baqarah: 180], he said: this one was abrogated. Then he recited until he came to this verse: "And those of you who die and leave behind wives," down to "without their being driven out," and he said: And this one. [[The report 5585 has passed in abridged form under no. 2652.]]

* *

Others said: this verse's ruling is established; nothing of it has been abrogated.

Mention of those who said that:

5586 – Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding Allah's saying: ﴿And those of you who die and leave behind wives, they shall wait by themselves for four months and ten days﴾ [Surat al-Baqarah: 234]. He said: This was for the woman observing the waiting period, who would observe it at her husband's family's house, as an obligation upon her. Then Allah revealed: "And those of you who die and leave behind wives, a bequest for their wives, provision until the [end of the] year, without their being driven out," down to His saying: "in what is reasonable." He said: Allah made for them the complete year, seven months and twenty nights, as a bequest: if she wished she would reside in accordance with her bequest, and if she wished she could leave. This is the saying of Allah the Exalted: "without their being driven out. But if they leave, there is no blame upon you." He said: And the waiting period remains as it is, obligatory.

5587 – Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 240 (part 2 of 2):

5588 – Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, from Isa. And al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Ata, from Ibn Abbas that he said: "This verse's ruling on their waiting period (iddah) was abrogated (nasakha) with respect to her household; she may observe the waiting period wherever she wishes. This is the statement of God: ﴿without being turned out﴾." Ata said: "If she wishes, she may observe the waiting period in her husband's household and reside in her bequest, and if she wishes, she may leave. This is due to God's statement, exalted is He: ﴿there is no blame upon you for what they do with themselves﴾." Ata said: "The inheritance came with the abrogation of the residence; she observes the waiting period wherever she wishes, and she has no right to residence."

* *

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: The most correct of these opinions in my view is to say: God, exalted is He, had made it so that the wives of men who died were to have a year's residence in his dwelling after their death, with their maintenance drawn from the estate of their deceased husband until the end of the year. [In the manuscript: "ila inqida' wajab," with a blank space between them; what is in the printed edition is closer to correct.] The heirs of the deceased were obligated not to expel them from the residence he had lived in before the full year was complete. If they waived their right to this and left, the heirs of the deceased would bear no blame for their departure. Then God, exalted is He, abrogated the maintenance by the verse of inheritance, and cancelled from what He had granted them of a year's residence, seven months and twenty nights, and returned them to four months and ten days, through the tongue of the Messenger of God (ﷺ).

5589 – Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Hakam narrated to me, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, saying: Haywa ibn Shurayh informed us, from Ibn Ajlan, from Sa'id ibn Ishaq ibn Ka'b ibn Ujra, and he informed him from his paternal aunt Zaynab bint Ka'b ibn Ujra, from Furay'a, sister of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri: that her husband went out in pursuit of a slave of his, and overtook him at a nearby place, and fought him, and the slaves who were with him helped against him, and they killed him. She came to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and said: "My husband went out in pursuit of a slave of his, and he met some non-Arab men (ulooj) who killed him, and I am in a place where there is no one except me, and I am resolved to move to my family!" The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said to her: "Rather, remain in your place until the prescribed term reaches its end."

[Notes on this hadith, from the editor: Hajjaj is Ibn Rushdin ibn Sa'd, who narrates from Haywa ibn Shurayh, and from whom Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Hakam narrates; in our view he is trustworthy, and his biography was detailed earlier at 763. Ibn Ajlan is Muhammad ibn Ajlan al-Madani, the trustworthy, mentioned at 304. Sa'd ibn Ishaq ibn Ka'b ibn Ujra was mentioned at 5090; the printed edition here has "Sa'id" in place of "Sa'd," as occurred earlier, and the more famous form is what we have recorded. The hadith was given in abridged form at 5090, from the narration of Fulayh ibn Sulayman, from Sa'd ibn Ishaq, with this same chain; we discussed its takhrij there at length and in brief, as if we had covered there what we found of its routes, except the narrations of al-Tahawi, who transmitted it in Ma'ani al-Athar 2:45-46 through nine chains, and except the route here, which we had not seen. We did not find this route in any of the major collections other than al-Tabari. As for the hadith itself, it is sahih, and its sound transmissions, to which we pointed there, are given there in more detail than here. Furay'a bint Malik, sister of Abu Sa'id: her name is in the diminutive form with a damma on the fa in most reports. Her name appears in the manuscript here as "al-Fari'a," which I have not found in any reports in this form, except in one of the narrations of al-Nasa'i 2:113; likewise, al-Hafiz did not mention this narration in al-Isaba except from the narration of al-Nasa'i. The hadith was mentioned by Ibn Kathir 1:588-589 from the narration of the Muwatta, which we pointed to earlier; it is in the Muwatta, p. 591.]

As for His saying, ﴿provision﴾, its meaning is: He made that for them as a provision, that is, the bequest which God wrote for them.

The word ﴿provision﴾ (matā') is in the accusative because in His saying ﴿a bequest for their wives﴾ there is the sense of "God has provided for them," so it was said ﴿provision﴾ as a verbal noun (masdar) derived from its meaning, not from its wording.

* *

As for His saying, ﴿not turning them out﴾, its meaning is that God, exalted is He, made what He granted them of the bequest a provision from Him for them until the year's end, and not an expulsion from their husband's dwelling; that is, there is to be no expulsion from it until the year has ended. So ﴿not﴾ (ghayr) is in the accusative as a qualifier (na't) of ﴿provision﴾, like the speaker's saying: "This is standing, not sitting," meaning: this is standing with no sitting with it, or: no sitting in it.

* *

Some have claimed that it is in the accusative in the sense of "do not turn them out, turning out," but that is a mistaken statement, because if it were accusative under this interpretation, its accusative would be from a separate sentence other than the first, whereas it is accusative only by what made ﴿provision﴾ accusative as its qualifier. [See al-Farra's Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1:156.]

* *

Regarding the interpretation of His saying: ﴿But if they leave, then there is no blame upon you for what they do with themselves of what is reasonable. And God is Exalted in Might and Wise.﴾ (2:240)

Abu Ja'far said: By this God, exalted is He, means: the provision which God made for them for a year from their husbands' estates after their death, and in their dwellings, and He forbade the heirs from expelling them, is only for them so long as they remain in their husbands' dwellings; and their rights in this are nullified if they leave the homes of their husbands before the year's end, of their own accord, without expulsion by the heirs of the deceased.

Then God, exalted is He, informed that there is no sin upon the guardians of the deceased for their leaving and their abandonment of mourning for their husbands. For remaining a year in their husbands' houses and mourning for him for a full complete year was not obligatory upon them; rather, it was a permission from God, exalted is He, for them if they remain mourning for the full year. As for if they leave, there is no blame upon the guardians of the deceased nor upon them for what they do with themselves of what is reasonable, and that is abandoning mourning. He says: there is no blame upon you regarding adornment if they adorn themselves and perfume themselves and marry, because that is permitted for them.

We have said, "there is no blame upon them in their leaving," although God, exalted is He, said, "there is no blame upon you," because if there were blame upon them in it, there would be blame upon the men's guardians for their abandoning them and letting them leave, while being able to prevent them from that. But since there is no blame upon them in leaving and abandoning mourning, the blame was lifted from the guardians of the deceased and others regarding what they do of what is reasonable, and that concerns themselves.

The reports from the people of interpretation supporting what we have said have already been given earlier.

* *

As for His saying, ﴿And God is Exalted in Might and Wise﴾, God, exalted is He, means: "And God is Exalted in Might" in His retribution against whoever opposes His command and prohibition and transgresses His limits, among men and women. He prevents men from giving their wives what was obligatory for them in the verses that preceded: the enjoyment, the dowry, and the bequest, and their leaving before the year's end, and neglecting the preservation of the prayers and their times; and He prevents women from what God obligated on them of waiting upon the death of their husbands, regarding the husbands, and who opposes His command in preserving the times of the prayers. "Wise" means: in what He has decreed among His servants of His judgments that were mentioned in the verses before His saying "And God is Exalted in Might and Wise," and in His other rulings and decrees.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 241:

The interpretation of His words, may His remembrance be exalted: ﴿And for divorced women there is provision according to what is reasonable, a duty upon the righteous (al-muttaqin)﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His remembrance be exalted, He means: and for whichever women are divorced from their husbands, "provision" (mata'). He means by it: what they enjoy of garments, clothing, maintenance, a servant, and other things with which they are provided. We have already explained the meaning of this earlier, and the disagreement of the scholars concerning it, and the correct view on it according to us, so there is no need to repeat it. [[See the meaning of "mata'" earlier: 1:539, 540 / then 3:53-55 / then the place al-Tabari meant here: 120-135.]]

* *

The scholars have differed concerning which divorced women are meant by this verse.

Some of them said: It refers to the previously-married women who have been consummated with. They said: We say this because the rights due to divorced women who were not consummated with, regarding provision (al-mut'ah), have already been specified by God, may His remembrance be exalted, in the verses before it, so we know that in this verse is the explanation of the matter of those who were consummated with in this regard.

Mention of those who said this:

5590- Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa ibn Maymun related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from 'Ata', concerning His words: "And for divorced women there is provision according to what is reasonable, a duty upon the righteous," he said: The married woman whom her husband has been intimate with, he provides for her according to what is reasonable.

5591- al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah related to us, saying: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same, and he added in it: Shibl mentioned it, from Ibn Abi Najih, from 'Ata'.

* *

Others said: Rather, this verse indicates that every divorced woman has a provision (mut'ah). God, may His remembrance be exalted, revealed it to His Prophet ﷺ because of the additional meaning it contains beyond the other verses on provision, since the other verses on provision only explain the ruling for the unconsummated woman when she is divorced, whereas this one explains the ruling for all divorced women regarding provision.

Mention of those who said this:

5592- Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Wahhab related to us, saying: Ayyub related to us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, concerning this verse: "And for divorced women there is provision according to what is reasonable, a duty upon the righteous," he said: For every divorced woman there is provision according to what is reasonable, a duty upon the righteous.

5593- al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Hibban ibn Musa related to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, saying: Yunus informed us, from al-Zuhri, concerning a slave woman whose husband divorces her while she is pregnant, he said: She observes her waiting period in her house. And he said: I have not heard anything I can mention about the provision of a female slave, and God, may His remembrance be exalted, has said: "provision according to what is reasonable, a duty upon the righteous," and she is entitled to the provision until she gives birth.

5594- al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Hibban ibn Musa related to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, saying: Ibn Jurayj informed us, from 'Ata', who said: I said to him: Does a slave woman have provision from a free man? He said: No. I said: What about a free woman under a slave husband? He said: No. And 'Amr ibn Dinar said: Yes, "And for divorced women there is provision according to what is reasonable, a duty upon the righteous."

* *

Others said: This verse was revealed because when God, may His remembrance be exalted, revealed His words: ﴿And provide for them, the wealthy according to his means and the poor according to his means, a provision according to what is reasonable, a duty upon the doers of good﴾ [Surah al-Baqarah: 236], a man among the Muslims said: We will not do it unless we wish to do good. So God revealed: "And for divorced women there is provision according to what is reasonable, a duty upon the righteous," so that became obligatory upon them.

Mention of those who said this:

5595- Yunus ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words: "And provide for them, the wealthy according to his means and the poor according to his means, a provision according to what is reasonable, a duty upon the doers of good," a man said: If I do good, I do it, and if I do not wish that, I will not do it! So God revealed: "And for divorced women there is provision according to what is reasonable, a duty upon the righteous."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct view on this is what Sa'id ibn Jubayr said, that God, may His remembrance be exalted, revealed it as evidence for His servants that every divorced woman has a provision. This is because God, may His remembrance be exalted, mentioned in the rest of the verses of the Qur'an that mention provision for women, specifically among women, so He clarified in the verse where He says: ﴿There is no blame upon you if you divorce women as long as you have not touched them or specified for them an obligation﴾ [Surah al-Baqarah: 236], and in His words: "O you who believe, when you marry believing women and then divorce them before you have touched them" [Surah al-Ahzab: 49], what they are owed of provision if they are divorced before consummation; and by His words: ﴿O Prophet, say to your wives: If you desire the worldly life and its adornment, then come, I will provide for you﴾ [Surah al-Ahzab: 28], the ruling for the consummated women; and the ruling for the young women who were divorced after consummation, and the ruling for the disbelieving women and the slave women remained. So God, may His remembrance be exalted, by His words "And for divorced women there is provision according to what is reasonable" included all of them, and informed that they have the provision, just as He singled out the divorced women described by their qualities in the rest of the verses of the Qur'an. Therefore He repeated the mention of all of them in this verse.

* *

As for His words: ﴿a duty upon the righteous﴾, we have already explained the meaning of "haqqan" (duty) and the reason for its accusative form, and the disagreement among the grammarians concerning His words: ﴿a duty upon the doers of good﴾ [Surah al-Baqarah: 236]. What was said there suffices, so there is no need to repeat it here. [[See what has preceded in this part: 137, 138.]]

* *

As for "al-muttaqun" (the righteous): they are those who fear God in His command, His prohibition and His limits, so they uphold them as He obligated them to uphold them, out of fear of Him and dread of His punishment.

The explanation of the interpretation of that has already been given with a transmitted text. [[See the language indexes earlier under the root "w-q-y".]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 242:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿Thus Allah makes clear to you His verses, that you may understand﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Just as I have explained to you what is incumbent upon you regarding your wives and what is incumbent upon your wives regarding you, O believers, and made known to you My rulings and the right that is obligatory for some of you over others in these verses, so I make clear to you the remaining rulings in My verses which I have sent down upon My Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) in this Book, so that you may understand, O believers in Me and My Messenger, My limits, and comprehend what is binding upon you of My obligations, and thereby know what is good for your religion and your worldly life, your immediate and your ultimate affairs, so that you may act upon it, and so that your mutual relations may be set right, and through it you may attain the abundant reward from Me in your return.

The commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 243 (part 1 of 2):

On the interpretation (ta'wil) of His saying: ﴿Have you not seen those who left their homes, and they were thousands, fearing death? Then Allah said to them, "Die," then He brought them to life.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, may He be exalted and remembered, means: "Have you not seen" – have you not known, O Muhammad? It is from "the seeing of the heart," not the seeing of the eye,[[See what has passed regarding the meaning of "seeing" in 3:75-79.]] because our Prophet Muhammad ﷺ did not witness those whom Allah informed about in this report. "The seeing of the heart" is seeing and knowing something. [[In the printed edition: "wa-ilmihi bihi" with an added waw, which is corrupt; the correct reading is from the manuscript.]] The meaning, then, is: Have you not known, O Muhammad, of those who left their homes while they were thousands?

* *

Then the people of interpretation differed regarding the interpretation of His saying: "and they were thousands."

Some of them said: it refers to the number, meaning the plural of "thousand."

Those who said this:

5596 – Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to us; and Amr ibn Ali narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Maysara al-Nahdi, from al-Minhal ibn Amr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: "Have you not seen those who left their homes, and they were thousands, fearing death?" They were four thousand. They left fleeing the plague, saying: "We will go to a land where there is no death!" Until, when they reached a certain place, Allah said to them: "Die." Then a prophet of the prophets passed by them and prayed to his Lord that He bring them back to life, so He brought them to life. Then he recited this verse: "Indeed, Allah is full of bounty toward mankind, but most of mankind do not give thanks."[[The two reports, 5596 and 5597: al-Hakim narrated it in al-Mustadrak (2:281) and said: "This is a sound hadith according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs, but they did not record it." al-Dhahabi said: "Maysara, they did not narrate from him; al-Bukhari narrated from him in al-Adab al-Mufrad." See Ibn Kathir (1:590) and al-Durr al-Manthur (1:310). "Maysara" is Maysara ibn Habib al-Nahdi, whose biography is in al-Tahdhib.]]

5597 – Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Maysara al-Nahdi, from al-Minhal, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas: "Have you not seen those who left their homes, and they were thousands, fearing death?" He said: They were four thousand who left fleeing the plague. Allah caused them to die, then a prophet of the prophets passed by them and prayed to his Lord that He bring them back to life so that they would worship Him, and He brought them to life.

5598 – Muhammad ibn Sahl ibn Askar narrated to us, saying: Isma'il ibn Abd al-Karim informed us, saying: Abd al-Samad told me that he heard Wahb ibn Munabbih say: Some people of the Children of Israel were struck by affliction and hardship of the times. They complained of what had befallen them and said: "Would that we had died so that we might find rest from what we are in!" So Allah revealed to Hizqil (Ezekiel): "Your people cry out from the affliction, and they claim that they wish they had died so they could rest. And what rest is there for them in death? Do they think I am not able to resurrect them after death? Go to such-and-such a graveyard, for in it are four thousand—" He said: Wahb said: They are the ones whom Allah mentioned: "Have you not seen those who left their homes, and they were thousands, fearing death?" "Stand among them and call out to them." Their bones had been scattered, torn apart by birds and beasts.
