When he came to them, they denied him and said: "You have hastened to prophethood before its time has come to you!" [in the printed edition: "wa lam tanal laka," which is a misreading. In the History of al-Tabari: "wa lam tabalak," from mubalah (concern), which is nothing. In al-Durr al-Manthur: "wa lam ya'ti laka," and in the manuscript: "wa lam tanal laka," and it is clear that it should be "ta'in." From "an yai'inu ainan," meaning "hana" (has come), like "anna laka ya'nni," with the same meaning, i.e., you have not yet reached the time for you to be a prophet]. They said: "If you are truthful, then appoint for us a king that we may fight in the cause of Allah, as a sign of your prophethood!" Shim'un said to them: "It may be that if fighting is prescribed for you, you will not fight." [The report: 5635 – in the History of al-Tabari 1: 242, and al-Durr al-Manthur 1: 315. In the printed edition the report ends with "wallahu a'lam" (and Allah knows best), an addition by a copyist that has no meaning here and is not in the manuscript.]
* *
Abu Ja'far said: It is not permissible, in the words of Allah the Exalted, ﴿nuqatil fi sabil Allah﴾ when read with the nun, to be other than jussive, in the sense of conditional and imperative. If someone supposes that the nominative is permissible there, since it is read with the nun, in the sense of "that with which we fight in the cause of Allah," [in the manuscript and printed edition: "alladhi nuqatil" without "bihi" (with it), which is an error indicated by the context and by what appears in Ma'ani al-Qur'an of al-Farra' 1: 157], that is not permissible, because the Arabs do not elide two particles [meaning "alladhi" and "bihi"]. But if it were read with the ya', the nominative would be permissible, because if read thus it would be a relative clause (silah) of "the king," so the meaning of the statement would be: "Appoint for us the one who fights in the cause of Allah," just as the Exalted said: ﴿And send among them a messenger from themselves who will recite to them Your verses﴾ [Surah al-Baqarah: 129], because the phrase "yatlu" is a relative clause of "rasul." [See Ma'ani al-Qur'an of al-Farra' 1: 157–162, for he has fully treated this reading and this aspect of Arabic. "Silah" means the dependent element, such as the adjective and the circumstantial, and here it refers to the qualifier of an indefinite noun.]
* *
The interpretation of His saying: ﴿He said: "Would you perhaps, if fighting is prescribed for you, not fight?" They said: "And why would we not fight in the cause of Allah while we have been expelled from our homes and our children?" But when fighting was prescribed for them, they turned away, except a few of them. And Allah is Knowing of the wrongdoers.﴾ (246)

Abu Ja'far said: By this, the Exalted means: The prophet whom they asked to appoint a king for them to fight in the cause of Allah said: "Would you perhaps," meaning: would you expect [see this explanation in Majaz al-Qur'an of Abu 'Ubaydah 1: 77], "if it is prescribed," meaning: if fighting is obligated upon you [see the meaning of "kataba" previously, 3: 357, 364–365, 409 / 4: 297], "that you will not fight," meaning: that you will not fulfill what you have promised Allah from yourselves, of jihad in His cause, for you are people of breaking covenants, treachery, and little fulfillment of what you promise? "They said: 'And why would we not fight in the cause of Allah?'" meaning: the chiefs of the Children of Israel said this to their prophet: "And what prevents us from fighting in the cause of Allah against our enemy and the enemy of Allah?" "While we have been expelled from our homes and our children," by subjugation and domination?
* *
If someone asks us: What is the reason for the presence of "an" in His saying "wa ma lana alla nuqatil fi sabil Allah," and its absence in ﴿Why do you not believe in Allah while the Messenger calls you﴾? [Surah al-Hadid: 8]
It is said: Both are eloquent dialects of the Arabs. They sometimes elide "an" with their saying "ma laka," so they say "ma laka la taf'alu kadha," meaning: what is the matter with you that you are not doing it, as the poet said: [I do not know who said it, though I recall reading it with other verses of the rajaz. It is in Ma'ani al-Qur'an of al-Farra' 1: 163, and in Lisan (kh-l-f). "Khalifah" (with a fatha on the kha and a kasra on the lam) is a pregnant she-camel, its plural being khalif, which is rare; this verse is its evidence, whereas the common plural is "makhad" for pregnant she-camels, as in "imra'ah" and "nuswah." This rajiz is saying to his she-camel: what is your bellowing, when pregnant ones do not bellow? He means that she bellows only out of longing for her lands and their lands, where she was separated from one she loved, as al-Shamatit al-Ghatafani said to his she-camel: May God make your marrow fly in your joints... to whoever with longing makes you yearn! For I am like what you feel, my longing, but I conceal and you reveal. And in me is like what is in you, except that I am released from the tether and you are tethered. Moreover, the printed edition had "malaka tar'ina wa la tar'u al-khalf," which in the manuscript is correct, though unpointed, as is its scribe's habit in many places.]
"Ma laka targhin wa la targhu al-khalf..."
That is the statement for which the speaker has no need to cite evidence for its soundness, due to its prevalence on the tongues of the Arabs.
= And "an" is affirmed in it in another form, as a justification of her saying "ma laka" to its meaning, since its meaning is: what prevented you? As the Exalted said: ﴿What prevented you from prostrating when I commanded you?﴾ [Surah al-A'raf: 12], then He said in another surah about its counterpart: ﴿What is the matter with you that you are not among those who prostrate?﴾ [Surah al-Hijr: 32]. So "ma mana'aka" is placed in the position of "ma laka," and "ma laka" in the position of "ma mana'aka," since their meanings agree though their wordings differ, as the Arabs do with similar things whose meanings agree and whose words differ, as the poet said: [He is al-Farazdaq.]
He says, when he mounts her and she becomes still: "Is there anyone with a pleasant life that lasts?"
[His Diwan: 863; al-Naqa'id: 753; Ma'ani al-Qur'an of al-Farra' 1: 164; Lisan (q-r-d, q-l-a, h-l-l). He is satirizing Jarir and alluding to resurrection; before it he alludes to the people of Jarir, Kulayb ibn Yarbu', who used to frequent female donkeys: "And no Kulaybi, when night falls, if he does not find the scent of the she-donkey, sleeps." He says, when... [In the printed edition: "taqulu." Ibn Barri explained this version very badly in "q-r-d," and Ibn al-A'rabi also explained it in "q-l-a" in a very corrupt way, even though he meant a woman to be violated. The correct meaning is that he meant what I mentioned of mounting female donkeys, not human females!! "Iqlawla" means he mounted her, restless and unsettled, not staying still. Al-Farazdaq's choice of this letter is astonishing in depicting what he intended. "Aqrada" means the man or another became still and feigned death; he means that the she-donkey has accepted and become compliant, so he became still for her. When this reached him and her, he said: "Is there anyone with a pleasant life that lasts?", revealing his intense love and passion for that, and that he regrets and grieves that it is a matter that ends and does not last. It is claimed that "hal" here means denial, i.e., no one with a pleasant life is lasting. (Lisan: h-l-l).]
Then he put "ba" into "da'im" along with "hal," which is interrogative. It is only placed in the predicate of "ma" when it has the sense of denial, because the meanings of interrogation and denial are close.
[See Ma'ani al-Qur'an of al-Farra' 1: 163–164, where he has fully discussed what al-Tabari opened.]
* *
Some grammarians used to say: [He is al-Kisa'i, as al-Farra' explicitly stated in Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1: 165.] "An" was inserted in "alla tuqatilu," because it has the sense of the speaker's saying: "What is your reason for not fighting?" If that were permissible, it would be permissible to say: "ma laka an qumta" (what is your reason that you stood) and "ma laka annaka qa'im" (what is your reason that you are standing), and that is not permissible, because prohibition applies only to future actions, as one says: "I forbade you to stand," and one does not say: "I forbade you that you stood." Therefore it is said "malaka alla taqum" (what prevents you from standing), not "ma laka an qumta."
* *
Others among them said: [He is Abu al-Hasan al-Akhfash, as is clear from the tafsirs of Abu Hayyan, al-Qurtubi and al-Mughni.] "An" here is superfluous after "ma lana," just as it is superfluous after "lamma" and "law," [in the printed edition: "superfluous after fa-lamma, lamma and law," which is garbled. In the manuscript: "after mlma..." is disordered; the correct reading in my view is "malana," and since the copyist erred in writing and reading, he dropped "as it is superfluous," and this is the correct meaning, praise be to God.] and it is very often superfluous in this sense. He said: Its meaning is: "What is the matter with us that we do not fight in the cause of Allah?" So "an" operated while being superfluous. Al-Farazdaq said:
Had Ghatafan not had any "dhunub" (portions)... [His Diwan: 283; it will come in the tafsir 9: 165; al-Khizanah 2: 87; al-'Ayni (al-Khizanah) 2: 322. He satirizes Umar ibn Hubayrah al-Fazari, one of the amirs and agents of Sulayman ibn Abd al-Malik, and his people, Fazarah ibn Dhubyan, descended from Ghatafan ibn Sa'd ibn Qays Aylan ibn Mudar. It is good poetry in its genre, and before the verse there are lines including: O Qays Aylan, I had told you: do not hasten in anger... For if I satirize a people, I leave them neither hearing nor sight when they listen to my voice. Then after that he said lines including: Had Ghatafan not... This is a gathering of those I have seen who go to the view that "dhunub" is the plural of "dhanb," which is for me nothing, and they have only followed the traces of al-Akhfash when he cited the verse as evidence for the operation of the superfluous "la." The correct reading of the verse for me is "la dhunub laha" (no portions for it), and there is no evidence in the verse then. It seems that al-Akhfash erred in citing it. "Dhunub" (with fatha on the dhal) is a share and portion, originally a full bucket. It has this meaning in His saying: ﴿For those who wronged, there is a portion like the portion of their companions﴾, meaning a share of punishment. Al-Farra' said: "Dhanub is a great bucket, but the Arabs take it to mean share and portion." Al-Zamakhshari said: "And they have dhunub of such-and-such," meaning a share. 'Amr ibn Shas said: "And among every tribe you have struck with a favour, so Shas deserves dhunub from your generosity." I say: al-Farazdaq says: Had Ghatafan not been base, with no share in nobility, lineage, or manliness, "the mothers of its nobles would have borne Umar." With that the verse is cleared of silliness and the grammarians' contrivance. See also al-Farazdaq's satire of Umar ibn Hubayrah in Tabaqat Fuhul al-Shu'ara', 287–288, and his saying: "Time has corrupted and its signs have changed, until Umayyah seeks refuge in Fazarah and takes its opinion." He says: the world has changed until Umayyah takes shelter in Fazarah and acts on its opinion, marveling at that because of Fazarah's baseness in his eyes.]
And the meaning is: Had Ghatafan had "dhunub" (portions)... "la" is superfluous, so it operated.
[He cited this as evidence for the operation of a superfluous particle, which is "la," as "an" operated in the verse.]
= Others denied what this speaker said that we have related from him, and said: It is not permissible to make "an" superfluous in speech when it is sound in meaning and the speech needs it. They said: The meaning is: "What prevents us from not fighting," so there is no basis for the claim of one who claims "an" is superfluous; the meaning is understood and sound. They said: As for his saying: "Had Ghatafan not had any dhunub..." "la" is not superfluous in this place, because it is a negation, and a negation when negated becomes an affirmation. They said: So his saying "Had Ghatafan not had dhunub" affirms that they have dhunub, as one says: "What is your brother not standing?", meaning: he is standing.
* *
Others said: The meaning of His saying "ma lana alla nuqatil" is: "What is the matter with us and not fighting?" then the "wa" was dropped and left out, as one says in speech: "What is your matter with and that you go to so-and-so?", so the "wa" was elided, because "an" is a particle not fully inflected in nouns. They said: We permit one to say "ma laka an taqum" (what is your matter that you stand), but we do not permit "ma laka al-qiyam" (what is your matter with standing), because "qiyam" is a sound noun and "an" is an unsound noun. They said: The Arabs do say: "iyyaka an tatakallam" (beware that you speak), meaning: beware of and that you speak.
* *
Others denied that saying and said: If it were permissible to say that on the interpretation of the one whose statement we related, it would be necessary to permit: "I struck you with the slave-girl while you are a guarantor," meaning: while you are a guarantor for the slave-girl; and to say: "I saw you us," meaning: "I saw you and us." [In the printed edition: "I saw you Aban and Yazid, meaning: I saw you and Aban Yazid," which is a fallen, ruined statement. The correct version is from the manuscript, though its letters are unpointed, and from Ma'ani al-Qur'an of al-Farra' 1: 165.] For the Arabs say: "iyyaka bil-batil tantiq" (beware, with falsehood you speak). They said: If "wa" were implied in "an," all that we mentioned would be permissible, but that is not permissible, because what follows "wa" of verbs may not have as its object what precedes it. ["Af'al" means verbs; their taking effect on what precedes them is either by operating on it or by being attached to it.] They cited to refute the view that "wa" is implied with "an" the poet's words:
So confide your secrets among their people, but beware of revealing them among others. [I do not know who said it; it is in Ma'ani al-Qur'an of al-Farra' 1: 165. "Sara'ir" is plural of "sarirah," meaning secret here.]
= If "an tabuh" had an implied "wa," it would not be permissible to place "fi ghayrihim" before it. [In the manuscript and printed edition: "taqdim ghayrihim" without "fi"; the correct reading is from Ma'ani al-Qur'an of al-Farra' 1: 166, where he has fully discussed this, and what is here seems to be quoted from him verbatim.]
* *
As for the interpretation of His saying, "and we have been expelled from our homes and our children," it means: those of our men and women who were overpowered were expelled from their homes and their children, and taken captive. This speech apparently has a general sense but an inner particular sense, because those who said to their prophet, "Appoint for us a king that we may fight in the cause of Allah," were in their homes and lands, and only those among them who were captured and subdued were expelled from their homes and children.
* *
As for His saying, "But when fighting was prescribed for them, they turned away, except a few of them," it means: when fighting against their enemy and jihad in His cause was prescribed for them, "they turned away, except a few of them," meaning: they turned their backs, retreating from fighting, and neglected what they had asked of their prophet, namely the prescription of jihad.
The few whom Allah excepted from them are those who crossed the river with Talut. We will mention the reason for the turning away of those who turned away, and the crossing of those who crossed the river, later, if Allah wills, when we reach it.
* *

Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: "And Allah is Knowing of the wrongdoers," meaning: Allah has knowledge of those among them who wronged themselves, breaking what Allah had promised from Himself, and opposing the command of their Lord regarding what they had asked Him to make obligatory for them from the outset.

* *

This is a rebuke from Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, directed at the Jews who were living among the emigrants of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), for their denial of our Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) and their opposition to the command of their Lord. Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says to them: "You, O assembly of Jews, disobeyed Allah and opposed His command regarding what you asked Him to make obligatory upon you from the outset, without your Lord having begun by prescribing it for you. Therefore, in disobeying Him concerning what He began by imposing upon you as an obligation, you are more deserving of [His punishment]."

* *

In this statement, something has been omitted, the mention of what was mentioned making the omitted part unnecessary. The meaning of the speech is: "They said: 'And what is wrong with us that we should not fight in the way of Allah, when we have been expelled from our homes and our children?'" So their prophet asked his Lord to send them a king whom they would fight alongside in the way of Allah. So He sent them a king, and prescribed fighting for them. "But when fighting was prescribed for them, they turned away, except for a few of them. And Allah is Knowing of the wrongdoers."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 247 (part 1 of 2):

The explanation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Their prophet said to them, "Indeed, Allah has sent to you Saul as a king." They said, "How can he have kingship over us while we are more entitled to kingship than he, and he has not been given a sufficient amount of wealth?"﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: By this, may His remembrance be exalted, He means: He said to the chiefs of the Children of Israel, their prophet Shamwil: "Indeed, Allah has given you what you asked for, and has sent to you Saul as king." When their prophet Shamwil said that to them, they said: "How can Saul have kingship over us, when he is from the tribe of Benjamin bin Ya'qub, and the tribe of Benjamin is a tribe in which there is neither kingship nor prophethood, and we are more entitled to kingship than him, because we are from the tribe of Judah bin Ya'qub?" "And he has not been given a sufficient amount of wealth": meaning, Saul was not given much wealth, because he was a water-carrier. It was also said that he was a tanner.

* *

The cause of Allah's making Saul king over the Children of Israel, and their saying to their prophet Shamwil what they said, "How can he have kingship over us while we are more entitled to kingship than he, and he has not been given a sufficient amount of wealth," is as follows:

5636 – Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salama bin al-Fadl narrated to us, saying: Muhammad bin Ishaq narrated to me, saying: Some of the people of knowledge narrated to me, from Wahb bin Munabbih, who said: When the chiefs of the Children of Israel said to Shamwil bin Bali what they said to him, Shamwil asked Allah to send them a king. Allah said to him: "Look at the horn which has oil in your house [[qarn: the horn of an ox or other animal; it seems he meant here the flask in which oil and perfume are kept; they seem to have made it from ox horns and the like, and they called the cupping vessel used for cupping a "qarn." I did not find this word with this meaning in the lexicons, but it is sound, as you have seen.]]. When a man enters upon you, and the oil in the horn bubbles [[nashsha al-ma' yanushshu nashan: wa-nashishan: a sound of boiling]], he is the king of the Children of Israel, so anoint his head with it and make him king over them, and inform him of what came to him [[In the manuscript: "bi-alladhi hah," undotted; were it not that the printed edition is also correct, I would say it is "bi-alladhi habahu Allah," meaning the kingship.]]." So he waited, expecting when that man would enter upon him. [[This sentence is found in this form in the printed edition, the manuscript, and al-Durr al-Manthur 1:351. I fear that "mata" is superfluous, or that it should be "ma'ta dhalika al-rajul ..."]] Saul was a tanner who worked with leather [[al-adam is the plural of adim, a rare plural; Sibawayh said it is a collective noun. Al-Tawzi said: "The hide, when first tanned, is adim; if it is returned to the tanning a second time, it is al-ladim."]], and he was from the tribe of Benjamin bin Ya'qub, and the tribe of Benjamin was a tribe in which there was neither prophethood nor kingship. Saul went out seeking a beast of his which had strayed [[It is said: adalla-hu al-amr: if it went away from him and parted from him, so he could not reach it. This is one of the wonders of Arabic. In the manuscript: "atalahu," which is an error; the correct reading is in the printed edition and al-Durr al-Manthur.]], and with him was a servant of his. They passed by the house of the Prophet (peace be upon him), and Saul's servant said to Saul: "If only we entered upon this prophet and asked him about the matter of our beast, so that he might guide us and pray for us concerning it for good!" Saul said: "There is no harm in what you have said!" So they entered upon him, and while they were with him, mentioning to him the matter of their beast and asking him to pray for them concerning it, the oil in the horn bubbled. The Prophet (peace be upon him) stood up to it and took it, then said to Saul: "Bring your head near!" So he brought it near, and he anointed him with it, then said: "You are the king of the Children of Israel whom Allah commanded me to make king over them!" = The name "Saul" in Syriac was Shaʼul [[In the manuscript and printed edition: "Shadil." The correct form is from al-Tarikh 1:247 and al-Durr al-Manthur 1:315, and it is so in the book of the people.]] bin Qays bin Abyal [[(Abyi'il) in the book of the people.]] bin Darar [[(Sarur) in the book of the people.]] bin Yahrab [[(Bakurah) in the book of the people; in al-Tarikh "Bahrat," and it seems to be the correct one.]] bin Afih bin Ays [[Not found in the book of the people; in al-Tarikh (Ayash).]] bin Benjamin bin Ya'qub bin Ishaq bin Ibrahim. So he sat with him, and the people said: "Saul has become king!" The great men of the Children of Israel came to their prophet and said to him: "What is the matter with Saul being king over us, when kingship is not in the house of prophethood? You know that prophethood and kingship are in the family of Levi and the family of Judah!" So he said to them: "Indeed, Allah has chosen him over you and increased him in knowledge and physique."

5637 – al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Isma'il narrated to us, from Abd al-Karim, from Abd al-Samad bin Ma'qil, from Wahb bin Munabbih, who said: The Children of Israel said to Ashmawil [[In al-Tarikh 1:244 "li-Ashmawil," and in what follows "Ashmawil" in the other places. Likewise in the manuscript. In the printed edition it is "li-Shamwil" and in the other places "Shamwil"; I have adopted what is in the manuscript and al-Tarikh.]]: "Send us a king, we will fight in the way of Allah!" He said: "Allah has already sufficed you the fighting!" They said: "We fear those around us, so let there be for us a king to whom we can turn for refuge!" So Allah revealed to Ashmawil: "Send them Saul as king, and anoint him with the oil of holiness." The donkeys of Saul's father strayed [[In the printed edition: "wa-dallat," and I have adopted what is in the manuscript and al-Tarikh.]], so he sent him and a servant of his to seek them. They came to Ashmawil asking him about them [[In the manuscript and printed edition: "fa-ja'u... yas'aluna-hu 'anha," and the correct reading is what is in al-Tarikh, as I have adopted.]], and he said: "Indeed, Allah has sent you as king over the Children of Israel." He said: "Me?" He said: "Yes!" He said: "Did you not know that my tribe is the lowest of the tribes of Israel?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Did you not know that my clan is the lowest of the clans of my tribe?!" He said: "Yes!" He said: "Did you not know that my house is the lowest of the houses of my clan?" He said: "Yes!" He said: "Then by what sign?" He said: "By the sign that you will return and your father will have found his donkeys, and when you are at such and such a place, revelation will descend upon you!" So he anointed him with the oil of holiness. Then he said to the Children of Israel: "Indeed, Allah has sent to you Saul as a king." They said: "How can he have kingship over us while we are more entitled to kingship than he, and he has not been given a sufficient amount of wealth?" He said: "Indeed, Allah has chosen him over you and increased him in knowledge and physique."

5638 – Musa bin Harun narrated to me, saying: Amr bin Hammad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, who said: When the Children of Israel denied Shamʻun, [[See the earlier report 5635, and what precedes it, on the difference regarding this prophet's name, peace be upon him.]] = and said to him: "If you are truthful, then send us a king, we will fight in the way of Allah, as a sign of your prophethood." Shamʻun said to them: "Is it possible that if fighting is prescribed for you, you will not fight?" "They said: 'And what is wrong with us that we should not fight in the way of Allah?'" the verse = he called upon Allah, and a staff was brought to him, of a length equal to the height of the man whom he would send among them as king. He said: "Your companion will be of the height of this staff." They measured themselves against it, but they were not like it. Saul was a water-carrier who carried water on his donkey, and his donkey strayed, so he set off seeking it on the road. When they saw him they called him, and they measured him against it, and he was like it. Their prophet said to them: "Indeed, Allah has sent to you Saul as a king." The people said: "You have never been more of a liar than you are now! We are from the tribe of kingship, and he is not from the tribe of kingship, and he has not been given a sufficient amount of wealth, so that we might follow him for that!" The prophet said: "Indeed, Allah has chosen him over you and increased him in knowledge and physique." [[The report 5638 is the continuation of the earlier report 5635, and it is in al-Tarikh with its chain, 1:242–243.]]

5639 – Ahmad bin Ishaq al-Ahwazi narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad al-Zubayri narrated to us, saying: Sharik narrated to us, from Amr bin Dinar, from Ikrimah, who said: Saul was a water-carrier who sold water.

5640 – Bishr bin Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, who said: Allah sent Saul as king, and he was from the tribe of Benjamin, a tribe in which there was neither kingship nor prophethood. Among the Children of Israel there were two tribes: a tribe of prophethood and a tribe of kingship. The tribe of prophethood was the tribe of Levi, from which came Moses, and the tribe of kingship was Judah, from which came David and Solomon. When he was sent from neither the tribe of prophethood nor the tribe of kingship, they denied that and were astonished by it, and said: "How can he have kingship over us while we are more entitled to kingship than he?" They said: "And how can he have kingship over us when he is neither from the tribe of prophethood nor from the tribe of kingship?" So Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, said: "Indeed, Allah has chosen him over you."

5641 – al-Hasan bin Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada, regarding His words: "Send us a king." Their prophet said to them: "Indeed, Allah has sent to you Saul as a king." They said: "How can he have kingship over us?" He said: "He was from a tribe in which there was neither kingship nor prophethood," and he said: "Indeed, Allah has chosen him over you and increased him in knowledge and physique."

5642 – al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abu Zuhayr narrated to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, regarding His words: "Their prophet said to them: Indeed, Allah has sent to you Saul as a king." Among the Children of Israel there were two tribes: a tribe of prophethood and a tribe of succession (khilafah), and therefore they said: "How can he have kingship over us?" They say: "And from where would kingship be his over us, when he is neither from the tribe of prophethood nor the tribe of succession?" He said: "Indeed, Allah has chosen him over you and increased him in knowledge and physique."

5643 – It was related from al-Husayn bin al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd bin Sulayman narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak bin Muzahim say regarding His words: "How can he have kingship over us?", and he mentioned something similar.

5644 – It was related from Ammar bin al-Hasan, who said: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi', who said: When the Children of Israel said to their prophet: "Ask your Lord to prescribe fighting for us!" that prophet said to them: "Would it be that if fighting is prescribed for you, you would not fight?" — the verse. He said: So Allah sent Saul as king. He said: Among the Children of Israel there were two tribes: a tribe of prophethood and a tribe of kingship, and Saul was neither from the tribe of prophethood nor from the tribe of kingship. When He sent him to them as king, they denied that and were astonished and said: "How can he have kingship over us while we are more entitled to kingship than he, and he has not been given a sufficient amount of wealth?" They said: "And how can he have kingship over us when he is neither from the tribe of prophethood nor from the tribe of kingship?" So he said: "Indeed, Allah has chosen him over you," the verse.

5645 – Muhammad bin Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, who said: As for the mention of Saul, when they said: "How can he have kingship over us while we are more entitled to kingship than he, and he has not been given a sufficient amount of wealth?" They only said that because among the Children of Israel there were two tribes: in one of them was prophethood, and in the other was kingship. So none is sent except from the tribe of prophethood, and none rules on earth except from the tribe of kingship. He (Allah) sent Saul when He sent him, and he was not from either of the two tribes, and He chose him over them and increased him in knowledge and physique. For this reason they said: "How can he have kingship over us while we are more entitled to kingship than he?" — and he is not from either of the two tribes? He said: "Indeed, Allah has chosen him over you," up to "And Allah is All-Encompassing, All-Knowing."

5646 – al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn Abbas said regarding His words: "Have you not considered the chiefs of the Children of Israel after Moses?" — the verse. This was when the Torah was lifted and the people of faith were taken out, and the tyrants had expelled them from their homes and their sons. "When fighting was prescribed for them," and that was when the Ark came to them. He said: Among the Children of Israel there were two tribes: a tribe of prophethood and a tribe of succession, so succession is only in the tribe of succession, and prophethood is only in the tribe of prophethood. So their prophet said to them: "Indeed, Allah has sent to you Saul as a king." They said: "How can he have kingship over us while we are more entitled to kingship than he?" — and he is not from either of the two tribes, neither the tribe of prophethood nor the tribe of succession? "He said: Indeed, Allah has chosen him over you," the verse. [[Report 5646 is the continuation of the earlier report 5633.]]

* *

It has been said: the meaning of "kingship" in this place is command over the army.

Those who said that:

5647 – al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Mujahid said regarding His words: "Indeed, Allah has sent to you Saul as a king," he said: He was the commander of the army.

5648 – Muhammad bin Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, from Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, with the like of it, except that he said: He was a commander over the army.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: We have already explained the meaning of "anna" and the meaning of "kingship" earlier, so that suffices instead of repeating it in this place. [[See the explanation of "anna" earlier, vol. 4: 398–416, and the explanation of the meaning of "kingship" earlier, vol. 1: 148–150, then vol. 2: 488.]]

* *

The explanation of His words: ﴿He said, "Indeed, Allah has chosen him over you and increased him in knowledge and physique."﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His words, may His remembrance be exalted, "Indeed, Allah has chosen him over you," their prophet Shamwil said to them: "Indeed, Allah has chosen him over you," meaning: He selected him over you, as:

5649 – Muhammad bin Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas: "Has chosen him over you," meaning: selected him. [[See the explanation of "al-istifa'" (choosing) earlier, vol. 3: 91.]]

5650 – al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abu Zuhayr narrated to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak: "Indeed, Allah has chosen him over you," he said: He selected him over you.

5651 – Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: "Indeed, Allah has chosen him over you," meaning: selected him.

* *

As for His words, "and increased him in knowledge and physique," it means that Allah expanded for him in knowledge and physique, and gave him knowledge beyond what He gave others of those addressed by this address. That is because it is mentioned that revelation came to him from Allah. As for "in physique," he was given an increase in height over them, which no one else among them was given, as:

5652 – al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Isma'il bin Abd al-Karim narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Samad bin Ma'qil narrated to me, from Wahb bin Munabbih, who said: When the Children of Israel said: "How can he have kingship over us while we are more entitled to kingship than he, and he has not been given a sufficient amount of wealth?" He said: "Indeed, Allah has chosen him over you and increased him in knowledge and physique." He said: The Children of Israel gathered, and Saul was taller than them by a head and shoulders or more.

* *

al-Suddi said: The Prophet (ﷺ) was brought a staff of a length equal to the height of the man who would be sent among them as king, and he said: "Your companion will be of the height of this staff." They measured themselves against it, but they were not like it. They measured Saul against it, and he was like it.

5653 – Musa narrated to me this, saying: Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi. [[Report 5653 is part of the earlier report 5638.]]

* *

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: "Indeed, Allah has chosen him over you and increased him," along with His choosing him, "in knowledge and physique." Meaning: He expanded for him, along with that, in knowledge and physique.

Those who said that:

5654 – Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: "Indeed, Allah has chosen him over you and increased him in knowledge and physique," after this.

* *

The explanation of His words: ﴿And Allah gives His kingship to whom He wills, and Allah is All-Encompassing, All-Knowing (247).﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His remembrance be exalted, He means: that kingship belongs to Allah, and it is in His hand alone, not another's; He gives it: "He gives it" means: He gives that to whomever He wills, placing it with him and specifying it for him, and withholding it from whom He loves of His creation. [[In the printed edition: "wa-yamnahu man ahabb..." and I have adopted what is in the manuscript.]] He says: So do not object, O assembly of the chiefs of the Children of Israel, that Allah should send Saul as king over you, even though he is not from the household of kingship, for kingship is not an inheritance from fathers and forebears, but it is in Allah's hand; He gives it to whomever He wills of His creation, so do not choose over Allah.

Something similar to what we have said regarding this was said by a group of the people of interpretation.

Those who said that:

5655 – Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, saying: Ibn Ishaq narrated to me, saying: Some of the people of knowledge narrated to me, from Wahb bin Munabbih: "And Allah gives His kingship to whom He wills": kingship is in the hand of Allah, He places it wherever He wills; it is not for you to choose in it.

5656 – al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, saying: Ibn Jurayj said: Mujahid said: "His kingship" means His authority.

5657 – Muhammad bin Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, from Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "And Allah gives His kingship to whom He wills," his authority.

* *

"And as for His saying, ﴿And Allah is All-Encompassing, All-Knowing﴾, it means: ﴿And Allah is All-Encompassing﴾ in His bounty, so He bestows it upon whom He loves, and He wills it for whom He wills [[In the manuscript: "فينعم له" (so He bestows it upon him). The correct reading is that of the printed edition. In the printed edition: "ويريد به من يشاء" (and He wills it for whom He wills); in the manuscript: "ويريد فيه ..." written without dots, and the correct reading of it is what I have adopted.]] — ﴿All-Knowing﴾ of who is worthy of the kingdom He grants and the bounty He gives, so He gives it to him because of His knowledge of him, and that he is fit for it when He gives it to him: either for it to be put to good use, or so that he himself benefits from it. [[In the manuscript: "وإما لا نه" with a blank space about the size of a word between them. I was unable to find a word for the blank space, so I have left the printed edition's wording as it stands, though I do not fully endorse it.]]"

The Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 2, Verse 248 (Part 1 of 3)

Discussion of the words of God, ﴿And their Prophet said to them, "Indeed, the sign of his kingship is that the Ark will come to you"﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: This report from God, exalted is His remembrance, about His Prophet, whom it was reported about, is evidence that the chiefs (al-mala') of the Children of Israel, to whom this statement was addressed, did not acknowledge that God had sent Talut (Saul) to them as king, even when their Prophet informed them of that and made known to them the excellence with which God had favoured him. Rather, they asked him for a proof of the truth of what he had told them and informed them of. So the meaning of the discourse, given that the matter is as we have described, is: "And God gives His kingship to whom He wills, and God is All-Encompassing, All-Knowing." Then they said to him: "What is the sign of that, if you are among the truthful?" [[In the printed edition: "They said to him: Bring a sign for that ...", and in the manuscript: "What he brought with that," where the letter bā' in "atā" has been struck through. I have preferred the reading as I have established it, because of God's later words: "Indeed, the sign of his kingship."]] ="Their Prophet said to them: Indeed, the sign of his kingship is that the Ark will come to you." This story, [[In the printed edition: "this story," without the waw, and its omission disrupts the sentence.]] although it is a report from God, exalted is His remembrance, about the chiefs of the Children of Israel and their Prophet, and about what occurred from their initiating with their Prophet the request that he ask God to send them a king to fight with them in God's cause, and a report about what they did in denying their Prophet after they knew of his prophethood, [[In the printed edition: "based on what they did in denying," which is weak in meaning. In the manuscript: "bnā ʿamā kān..." without dots, and the correct reading is what I have established, with the addition of the waw as a conjunction to his statement "although it is a report..."]] then their breaking the promise they had made to God and to His Messenger, namely fighting in God's cause, by staying behind when they were called to fight those who had called them to fight, and God gave victory to the few of the band, while the many of them were dissuaded from their king and sat back from jihad with him [[The construction of the sentence: "And this story, although it is a report from God... and a report about what occurred from them ... then it is a disciplinary admonition ..."]], this is a disciplinary admonition for those who lived among the emigrants of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), from their descendants and sons, the Jews of Qurayza and al-Nadir, and that they would not transgress in denying Muhammad (ﷺ) in what he commanded them and forbade them, [[The construction of this sentence: "and that they would not transgress in denying Muhammad ... that they would be like their predecessors."]] despite their knowledge of his truthfulness and their recognition of the reality of his prophethood, after they had sought God's help through him against their enemies before his mission, and before God sent him to them and to others. [[Their predecessors and forefathers who denied their Prophet Shamwil (Samuel) son of Bali, despite their knowledge of his truthfulness and their recognition of the truth of his prophethood, and their refusal to fight with Talut when God raised him as king over them, after they had asked their Prophet to appoint a king with whom they would fight their enemy and strive in the way of their Lord, initiated by them to their Prophet, and after their Prophet Shamwil had repeatedly argued with them about that.]] This is also an exhortation to the people of faith in God and His Messenger, from among the companions of Muhammad (ﷺ), to strive in His way, and a warning to them not to be like those who hung back from their Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) when he met the enemy and confronted the people of disbelief in God and in him, in the manner of the chiefs of the Children of Israel in their hanging back from their king Talut when he marched to fight the enemy of God, Jalut (Goliath), and their preferring ease and comfort to bearing the heat of jihad and fighting in God's way. [[The phrase "wa-ḥaḍḍ" (and exhortation) is a second conjunction to the earlier phrase "fa-innahu ta'dīb" (it is a disciplinary admonition).]] It is also an incitement from Him to them to advance to engage the people of disbelief in war and to abandon fear of fighting them even when their numbers are few and the numbers of their enemies are many and their might is great, through His saying: ﴿Those who were certain that they would meet God said: How many a small company has overcome a large company by God's permission. And God is with the patient﴾ [Surah al-Baqarah: 249]. [[The phrase "wa-i'lām" (and information) is a third conjunction to the phrase "fa-innahu ta'dīb."]] And it is information from Him, exalted is His remembrance, to His believing servants that victory, triumph, good and evil are in His hand.

* *

As for the interpretation of His words, "Their Prophet said to them," it means: to the chiefs of the Children of Israel who had said to their Prophet, "Send us a king that we may fight in God's way."

* *

As for His words, "Indeed, the sign of his kingship," it means: indeed, the sign of Talut's kingship [[On the meaning of "āyah" (sign), see what has preceded in volumes 1: 106; 2: 397, 398, 553; 3: 184; 4: 271.]] which you asked me for, is a proof of my truthfulness in my saying that God has sent him over you as king, even though he is not from the tribe of the kingship, "that the Ark will come to you, in which is tranquillity from your Lord." This is the Ark which the Children of Israel, whenever they met an enemy, would bring forward before them, and they would march with it, and no enemy could stand before them with it, and no adversary who opposed them could prevail over them, until they neglected God's command and their disputes with their prophets multiplied; so God took it away from them time after time, returning it to them each time, until He took it away from them for the last time and did not return it to them, and it will never be returned to them until the end of time. [[In the printed edition: "until He took it away from them a last time," and what is in the manuscript is the correct and good reading, although the other is close to the correct reading, though weak. In the manuscript: "and He did not return it to them until the end of time," which is a clear error.]]

* *

Then the people of ta'wil (interpretation) differed about the cause of the coming of the Ark, which God made its coming to the Children of Israel a sign of the truthfulness of their Prophet Shamwil in his saying, "Indeed God has sent Talut to you as king." They also differed over whether the Children of Israel had lost it before that, so that God returned it to them when He made its coming a sign of Talut's kingship, or whether they had not lost it before that, but God had begun with them with it as a new beginning?

Some of them said: Rather, it had been with them from the time of Moses and Aaron, passing it on to one another, [[In the printed edition: "It had been with them," without "rather."]] until kings from among the people of disbelief in it took it from them, then God returned it to them as a sign of Talut's kingship. And regarding the cause of its being returned to them, he said what I will mention, which is:

5658- It was narrated to me by al-Muthanna, who said: Ishaq related to us, who said: Isma'il ibn Abd al-Karim related to us, who said: Abd al-Samad ibn Ma'qil told me that he heard Wahb ibn Munabbih say: Eli, who raised Shamwil, had two young sons who introduced something into the offering which was not part of it. The stirring-rod of the offering, which they used to stir it, was a hooked spit [[In the printed edition and manuscript: "the lancet of the offering with which they lanced it," which is a mistake with no meaning, and the correct reading is from Tarikh al-Tabari 1: 243. The masuṭ (with a kasra on the mīm) is a stirring-stick, a piece of wood or something similar, with which what is in the pot is moved so that it mixes. Sāṭa al-shay' fi al-qidr yasūṭuhu sawṭan means to stir and mix it so that it blends and combines. This Jewish offering is the "minḥah," which was made of fine flour with oil and frankincense; a little of the offered flour and oil and all the frankincense is taken and burnt on the altar, or made into cakes on a griddle, while the rest was for the priest (Qamus al-Kitab al-Muqaddas 2: 208). The kalāb (with a ḍammah on the kāf and a shaddah on the lām) is a spit of iron or wood with a hooked end curved like a hook, and its plural is kalālīb.]] which they would have. When the offering was brought out, the spit would be given to the priest who stirred it, [[In the printed edition and manuscript: "to the priest who stirs it with it," which is an error; the correct reading is from the Tarikh.]] but his two sons would hook it, [[In the printed edition and manuscript: "so his sons hooked it," and the correct reading is from the Tarikh.]] and whenever women came to pray in the Holy Place, they would seize them. While Shamwil was sleeping before the room where Eli slept, he heard a voice saying: "O Shamwil!" He jumped up to Eli and said: "Here I am! What is it? Did you call me?" He said: "No! Go back and sleep!" So he went back and slept, then he heard another voice saying: "O Shamwil!" So he jumped up to Eli again and said: "Here I am! What is it? Did you call me?" He said: "I did not do it. Go back and sleep, and if you hear something, say: 'Here I am,' where you are, 'Command me and I will do it!'" So he went back and slept, and heard a voice again saying: "O Shamwil!" He said: "Here I am! Command me and I will do it!" He said: "Go to Eli and say to him: 'The love of his son has prevented him from restraining his two sons from introducing things into My Holy Place and My offering, and from disobeying Me. I will certainly strip him of the priesthood and from his descendants, and I will destroy him and them both!'" When morning came, Eli asked him and he informed him, and he was terrified by that, a severe terror. Then an enemy from those around them marched against them, so he ordered his two sons to go out with the people and fight that enemy. They went out, and took with them the Ark in which were the two tablets and the staff of Moses, so that they might be victorious by it. [[In the Tarikh: "that they might win for themselves," i.e., to bring victory to themselves by it.]] When they and their enemy had prepared for the fight, Eli kept awaiting news: "What have they done?" A man came to him, while he was sitting on his chair, and told him: "Your two sons have been killed, and the people have been routed!" He said: "What became of the Ark?" He said: "The enemy took it!" He gasped and fell backwards from his chair and died. Those who had captured the Ark went off and placed it in the house of their gods, where they had an idol they worshipped. They placed it beneath the idol, with the idol above it. The next morning the idol was beneath, and the Ark was above the idol. So they took it and placed it on top of the Ark, and they nailed its feet to the Ark. The next morning the idol's hands and feet had been cut off, and it lay fallen beneath the Ark. Some of them said to others: "You know that the God of the Children of Israel cannot be withstood by anything. Take it out of the house of your gods!" So they took the Ark out and placed it in a district of their town. The people of that district whom the Ark had been placed among were afflicted with a swelling in their necks, and they said: "What is this?!" A slave-girl who was among them, a captive of the Children of Israel, said to them: "You will not cease to see what you dislike as long as this Ark is among you! Take it out of your town!" They said: "You are lying!" She said: "The sign of that is that you bring two cows which have calves and on which no yoke has ever been placed. Then you put the calves behind them, then you put the Ark on the cart and send the two cows off, and you hold back their calves, for they will set off with it in submission, [[In the printed edition: "they set off submissively," and the correct reading is from the manuscript and the Tarikh. The nīr is the wooden yoke placed on the neck of the ox with its equipment.]] until when they have left your land and reach the land of the Children of Israel, they break their yoke and come back to their calves." They did that, and when they had left their land and reached the nearest land of the Children of Israel, they broke their yoke and came back to their calves, and they placed it in a ruin where there was a harvest belonging to the Children of Israel, [[In the printed edition: "ḥuḍār," and in the manuscript: "ḥiṣār," without dots. The correct reading is that in the Tarikh.]] and the Children of Israel came to it in alarm and approached it, but no one could draw near to it without dying. Their Prophet Shamwil said to them: "Line up, [[In the Tarikh: "uʿriḍū," and the two are equivalent.]] and whoever feels strength within himself, let him approach it." They lined the people up before him, but no one could draw near to it except two men of the Children of Israel. [[In the Tarikh: "no one was able to approach it," and what is in the manuscript and printed edition is good.]] He permitted them to carry it to the house of their mother, who was a widow. It remained in the house of their mother until Talut became king, and the affairs of the Children of Israel were set right with Ashmuwil. [[The report: 5658 is in the Tarikh 1: 243-244, and it is the beginning of the report numbered 5637 above, and al-Tabari presented both in the Tarikh as a single continuous report.]]

5659- Ibn Humayd related to us, who said: Salama related to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: some people of knowledge told me, from Wahb ibn Munabbih, who said: Shamwil said to the Children of Israel when they said to him: "How can he have kingship over us when we have more right to kingship than him, and he has not been given wealth in abundance?" He said: "Indeed God has chosen him over you and increased him in breadth of knowledge and physique, and indeed the sign of his kingship = and his appointment is from God = is that the Ark will come to you, and it will return to you what is in it of tranquillity and the remnant of what the family of Moses and the family of Aaron left, and it is that with which you used to defeat whoever met you of the enemy, and with which you used to prevail over him." They said: "If the Ark comes to us, then we are content and submit!" The enemy who had captured the Ark were below the mountain, the mountain of Iliya, between them and Egypt, and they were idol-worshippers, and among them was Jalut. Jalut was a man who had been given breadth of physique, strength in grasping, and severity in war, and he was renowned for that among the people. When the Ark was captured, it had been placed in a village of the villages of Palestine called "Azdud," [[In the printed edition: "called Ardun," which is an undoubted error. What is in the manuscript is "Ardud" with a rāʾ, but I think it is with a zāy, and I have established it that way, for in the book of their people, "The First Book of Samuel," chapter 5, it is "Ashdod." Their dictionary-maker said: "Ashdod" (a fortress, a stronghold), one of the five allied cities of Palestine ... and its location is three miles from the Mediterranean Sea between Gaza and Jaffa. He said: it is now a worthless village called Asdud, and in its vicinity are many ruins. What supports my opinion that it is with a zāy is that Ibn Kathir said in his commentary 1: 602 that it is called "Azdawah," and the editor of the commentary said in its margin that in the Azhar manuscript it is "Azdard." In al-Baghawi in the margin of Ibn Kathir 1: 601 it is "Azdud" as I have established it.]] so they had placed the Ark in a church where their idols were. When what the Prophet (ﷺ) did happened, namely the promise from the Children of Israel that the Ark would come to them, their idols began to be found every morning in the church overturned on their heads, and God sent a mouse upon the people of that village, which would attack a man at night so that he was dead in the morning, [[In the printed edition: "the mouse would fix," which is not correct; the manuscript has "tabīt" without dots, and the correct reading is what I have established. "Bayyata al-qawm al-ʿaduww" means they attacked the enemy at night, coming upon them in the depths of the night while they were heedless. The noun is "al-bayāt." In al-Baghawi 1: 601 (in the margin of Ibn Kathir): "The mouse would spend the night with the man."]] having eaten what was in his belly from his back. They said: "By God, you know that a calamity has befallen you which has not befallen any nation of the nations like it, [[In the printed edition: "a nation of the nations before you," and in the manuscript: "a nation of the nations before it." What I have established is closer to the manuscript's writing, with the corruption in it.]] and we do not know that it has struck us except since this Ark has been among us! Moreover, you have seen that your idols are found every morning overturned, something that was not done to them until this Ark was with them! So take it out from among you." They called for a cart, placed the Ark on it, then yoked it to two bulls, then struck their flanks, and the angels went out with the two bulls driving them, and the Ark did not pass over any land except that it became holy. Nothing alarmed them except the Ark on a cart pulled by the two bulls, until it stopped before the Children of Israel, and they exclaimed "God is greatest" and praised God, and they resolved on their war, and they gathered together under Talut. [[In the printed edition: "they were united," which is an error; the correct reading is in the manuscript. Its meaning is: they gathered in obedience to him. Its root is from "al-wasq," which is joining one thing to another. In the hadith of Uhud: "Gather together as the flock gathers," that is, unite and come together. In the hadith of al-Najashi: "The command of the Abyssinians came together under him," i.e., they gathered in obedience to him. This is the meaning intended here. See what will come in report 5707.]]

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 248 (part 2 of 3):**

5660. Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn 'Abbas said: When their prophet said to them, "God has chosen Talut (Saul) over you and has increased him in knowledge and physical stature," they refused to grant him leadership, until he said to them, "The sign of his kingship is that the Ark (al-tabut) will come to you, in which is a tranquillity from your Lord." So he said to them, "Do you not see that if the Ark comes to you, in which is a tranquillity from your Lord and a remnant of what the family of Musa (Moses) and the family of Harun (Aaron) left behind, carried by the angels?!" = When Musa threw down the Tablets, they were broken, and some of them were lifted up. So he (Musa) went and gathered what remained and placed it in that Ark. = Ibn Jurayj said: Ya'la ibn Muslim informed me, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, that only a sixth of the Tablets remained. He said: The Amaliqa (Amalekites) had captured that Ark, and the Amaliqa were a group from 'Ad who lived in Ariha (Jericho). Then the angels brought the Ark, carrying it between the heavens and the earth while they watched the Ark, until they set it down before Talut. When they saw that, they said, "Yes!" and they submitted to him and made him king. He said: Whenever the prophets attended a battle, they would place the Ark before them. And they would say: Adam descended with that Ark and with the Rukn (the Black Stone). It has reached me that the Ark and the staff of Musa are in the Lake of Tiberias, and that they will come out before the Day of Resurrection.

5661. Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: 'Abd al-Samad ibn Ma'qil informed us, that he heard Wahb ibn Munabbih say: When Armiya (Jeremiah) saw that Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem) had been destroyed and the books had been burned, he stood in a side of the mountain and said, "How will God bring this to life after its death?" So God caused him to die for a hundred years. Then God restored those among the Children of Israel whom He restored, at the end of seventy years from the time He had caused him to die, and they rebuilt it for thirty years, completing the hundred. When the hundred years had passed, God returned his spirit to him, and it had been rebuilt, and it was in its first condition. [[The report 5661: This same report will come again under no. 5912, and it is undoubtedly a "truncated" report (mabtur) that I was unable to complete. See the commentary on the following report mentioned above.]]
[[As for the place of these dots, there is undoubtedly a omission here, for the report of Armiya mentioned earlier cannot be the continuation of this speech, since it contains mention of the return of the Ark in the time of Talut and Dawud (David), and they are a long age before Armiya. I fear that the copyist moved one leaf ahead of another in the ancient manuscript, or skipped a page of the book from which he copied. It is not possible to complete this gap, so I have separated the two passages with these dots, until God provides a copy older than the copies we have in hand that fills this lacuna or corrects the place of the text.
What follows the dots is a report about the town in which the Ark was placed when it was captured, as mentioned in report no. 5658, a report whose beginning is lost, from Wahb ibn Munabbih, as is clear from the following context. I have not found its beginning in any of the books at hand. Our copy is very full of errors and inadvertent mistakes in this place, as is clear from the handwriting of its scribe and from the earlier errors I have noted in the annotations.]] ................................................................................
................................................................................
................................................................................
When he (Talut) wanted to return the Ark to them, God revealed to a prophet among their prophets, either Daniel or someone else: "If you want the illness to be removed from you, then send this Ark away from you!" They said, "By what sign?" He said, "By the sign that you will bring two heifers that are unruly and have never done work at all. When they look at it, they will lower their necks to the yoke until it is fastened upon them, then the Ark will be tied upon a cart, then it will be fastened to the two heifers, then they will be released and they will go wherever God wills to bring them." They did that, and God appointed four angels to drive them. The two heifers went quickly until, when they reached the outskirts of the holy land (al-Quds), they broke their yokes, cut their ropes, and departed. Then Dawud and those with him came down to them. When Dawud saw the Ark, he leaped toward it joyfully. = We said to Wahb: What is "hajal" (leaping)? He said: It is like dancing. = His wife said to him: You have made yourself light, so that people nearly despise you for what you have done! He said: Will you hold me back from obeying my Lord?! You will not be my wife after this. So he divorced her.

* *

Others said: Rather, the Ark which God made a sign of Talut's kingship was in the wilderness, and Musa (ﷺ) had left it with his servant Yusha' (Joshua), and the angels carried it until they placed it in Talut's house. [[At this point a part of the old division ended, from which our copy was taken, and there it has the following text: "Its continuation, God willing, is: mention of those who said this. And may God bless Muhammad the Prophet and his family abundantly." "Copied from the original." "I finished reading it from its beginning and listened to it upon the judge Abu al-Hasan al-Khasib, from 'Abd Allah, from Abu Muhammad al-Farghani, from Abu Ja'far al-Tabari, while the judge was looking at his book. My brother listened with me, may God protect him, and Abu al-Fath Ahmad ibn 'Umar al-Jahhari (??) and Nasr ibn al-Husayn al-Tabari, and Muhammad ibn 'Ali ... and 'Abd al-Rahim ibn Ahmad al-Bukhari. Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn 'Isa al-Sa'di wrote it, in Sha'ban of the year 408 in Egypt." "Then it continues at the beginning of the next part: 'In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. My Lord, make it easy.'"]]
Mention of those who said that:

5662. Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His words: "The sign of his kingship is that the Ark will come to you, in which is a tranquillity from your Lord," etc.: Musa had left it with his servant Yusha' ibn Nun while he was in the wilderness, and the angels brought it, carrying it until they placed it in Talut's house, and in the morning it was in his house.

5663. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi', regarding His words: "The sign of his kingship is that the Ark will come to you," etc. He said: Musa, as has been related to us, had left the Ark with his servant Yusha' ibn Nun while he was in the wilderness. It was related to us that the angels carried it from the wilderness until they placed it in Talut's house, and in the morning the Ark was in his house.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The more correct of the two views on this matter is what Ibn 'Abbas and Wahb ibn Munabbih said: that the Ark was in the possession of an enemy of the Children of Israel who had seized it from them. This is because God, may He be exalted, said, reporting about His prophet in that time, his words to his people from the Children of Israel: "The sign of his kingship is that the Ark will come to you," and the definite article (al-) does not enter into such nouns except for something known to the two parties addressing one another. The one reporting and the one being reported to both knew it. So it is known by this that the meaning of the speech is: "The sign of his kingship is that the Ark which you know will come to you, the one by which you used to seek victory, in which is a tranquillity from your Lord." If it were a Ark among the arks, whose status and benefit were not known to them before that, it would have been said: "The sign of his kingship is that an Ark will come to you, in which is a tranquillity from your Lord."

* *

If someone heedless thinks that they knew that Ark, its worth, and what was in it, while it was with Musa and Yusha', then the error of that is not hidden. This is because it has not reached us that Musa ever met an enemy with the Ark, nor his servant Yusha'. Rather, what is known of the affair of Musa and the affair of Pharaoh is what God related of their story, and likewise his affair and the affair of the tyrants. As for his servant Yusha', those who made this statement claim that Yusha' was his successor in the wilderness (al-tih) until he returned it to them when Talut became king. If the matter is as they describe it, then which state of the Ark is the state in which they knew it, so that it could be said: "The sign of his kingship is that the Ark which you know and you know its matter will come to you"? In the corruption of this view that we have mentioned, is the clearest evidence for the correctness of the other view, since there is no other opinion on this matter from the exegetes (ahl al-ta'wil) besides these two.

* *

The description of the Ark, as has reached us, is as follows:

5664. Muhammad ibn 'Askar and al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Bakkar ibn 'Abd Allah informed us, saying: We asked Wahb ibn Munabbih about the Ark of Musa: what was it? He said: It was about three cubits by two cubits. [[The report 5664: "Muhammad ibn 'Askar" is Muhammad ibn Sahl ibn 'Askar, mentioned earlier at no. 5598. Bakkar ibn 'Abd Allah al-Yamani, who narrated from Wahb ibn Munabbih. Ibn al-Mubarak, Hisham ibn Yusuf and 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated from him. Ahmad said: Trustworthy (thiqa). He is biographed in al-Kabir 1/2/120, and Ibn Abi Hatim 1/1/408.]]

* *

The interpretation of His words: "in which is a tranquillity from your Lord" (﴿فِيهِ سَكِينَةٌ مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ﴾)

Abu Ja'far said: By His words "in it" (fihi), He, may He be exalted, means: in the Ark is "a tranquillity from your Lord."

* *

The exegetes (ahl al-ta'wil) differed about the meaning of "tranquillity" (al-sakina).

Some of them said: It is a light, fluttering wind that has a face like the face of a human.

Mention of those who said that:

5665. Imran ibn Musa narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Warith ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Jihada narrated to us, from Salama ibn Kuhayl, from Abu Wa'il, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, who said: The tranquillity is a light, fluttering wind which has a face like the face of a human.

5666. Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us = and al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Sufyan informed us = from Salama ibn Kuhayl, from Abu al-Ahwas, from 'Ali, who said: The tranquillity has a face like the face of a human, and then it is a light, fluttering wind.

5667. Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, from al-Awwam ibn Hawshab, from Salama ibn Kuhayl, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, regarding His words: "in it is a tranquillity from your Lord," who said: A light, fluttering wind which has a form. = Ya'qub said in his report: It has a face. = [[In the manuscript: "kama wajh" (as a face), with a blank between them; the closest is probably what is in the printed edition.]] Ibn al-Muthanna said: Like the face of a human.

5668. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mansur, from Salama ibn Kuhayl, who said: 'Ali said: The tranquillity has a face like the face of a human, and it is a light, fluttering wind. [[In the manuscript: "hiya rih" without the waw.]]

5669. Hannad ibn al-Sirri narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Ahwas narrated to us, from Simak ibn Harb, from Khalid ibn 'Ar'ara, who said: 'Ali said: The tranquillity is a violent, swirling wind, and it has two heads. [[The report 5669: It is part of the report mentioned earlier at no. 2058 concerning the building of the Ka'ba.]]

5670. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'ba narrated to us, from Simak, who said: I heard Khalid ibn 'Ar'ara narrate from 'Ali, similarly.

5671. Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Abu Dawud narrated to us, saying: Shu'ba, Hammad ibn Salama and Abu al-Ahwas narrated to us, all from Simak, from Khalid ibn 'Ar'ara, from 'Ali, similarly. [[The reports 5670, 5671: see the earlier reports 2059, 2060.]]

* *

Others said: It has the head of a cat and two wings.

Mention of those who said that:

5672. Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding God's words: "in it is a tranquillity from your Lord," who said: The tranquillity [and the sard] and Jibril came with Ibrahim from Syria. = [[What is between the brackets is an addition from the reports narrated from Mujahid on this matter, in Azraqi's History of Mecca 1:22-28; its wording is in Lisan al-'Arab (sard). Al-sard (with a damma on the sad and a fatha on the ra') is a large, spotted bird found in trees and mountain crevices which no one can catch, and it is one of the predatory birds.]] Ibn Abi Najih said: I heard Mujahid say: The tranquillity has the head of a cat and two wings.

5673. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, similarly.

5674. Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Layth, from Mujahid, who said: The tranquillity has two wings and a tail.

5675. Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: al-Thawri informed us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: It has two wings and a tail like the tail of a cat.

* *

Others said: Rather, it is the head of a dead cat.

* *

Mention of those who said that:

5677. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from Wahb ibn Munabbih, from some people of knowledge among the Children of Israel, who said: The tranquillity is the head of a dead cat, which, when it cried out inside the Ark with the cry of a cat, they were certain of victory, and the conquest came to them.

* *

Others said: It is only a basin of gold from Paradise, in which the hearts of the prophets were washed.

Mention of those who said that:

5678. Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: 'Uthman ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: al-Hakam ibn Zuhayr narrated to us, from al-Suddi, from Abu Malik, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding "in it is a tranquillity from your Lord," who said: A basin of gold from Paradise, in which the hearts of the prophets were washed.

5679. Musa ibn Harun narrated to me, saying: 'Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "in it is a tranquillity from your Lord." The tranquillity: a basin of gold in which the hearts of the prophets were washed, which God gave to Musa, and in which the Tablets were placed. The Tablets, as has reached us, were of pearl, ruby and chrysolite.

* *

Others said: "The tranquillity" is a spirit from God that speaks.

Mention of those who said that:

5680. Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Bakkar ibn 'Abd Allah informed us, who said: We asked Wahb ibn Munabbih and said to him: The tranquillity? He said: A spirit from God that speaks; when they differed about something, it spoke and informed them with a clarification of what they wanted.

5681. Muhammad ibn 'Askar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, saying: Bakkar ibn 'Abd Allah narrated to us, that he heard Wahb ibn Munabbih, and mentioned something similar. [[The reports 5680, 5681: "Muhammad ibn 'Askar" and "Bakkar ibn 'Abd Allah". See the commentary on the report no. 5664.]]

Others said: "The tranquillity" is what they recognize of the signs, so that they become calm with it.

Mention of those who said that:

5682. Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: I asked 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah about His words: "in it is a tranquillity from your Lord," etc. He said: As for the tranquillity, it is what they recognize of the signs, by which they become calm.

* *

Others said: "The tranquillity" is mercy.

Mention of those who said that:

5683. It was reported from 'Ammar ibn al-Hasan, who said: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi': "in it is a tranquillity from your Lord," i.e., mercy from your Lord.

* *

Others said: "The tranquillity" is dignity (al-waqar).

Mention of those who said that:

5684. Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada, regarding His words: "in it is a tranquillity from your Lord," i.e., dignity.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of these views regarding the meaning of "tranquillity" is what 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah said: that it is a thing in which souls find rest, from the signs that you recognize. This is because "tranquillity" (al-sakina) in the speech of the Arabs is a pattern (fa'ila), from the saying of the speaker: "So-and-so found rest (sakana) in such-and-such," when he became content with it and his soul was calmed by it. "He rests, a resting and a tranquillity," like your saying: "So-and-so resolved this matter, a resolve and a resolution," and "The judge decided between the people, a decision and a determination." From it is the saying of the poet: [[Recited by Ibn Barri from Abu 'Arif al-Kulaybi. I am in doubt about the correctness of his name.]]

By God, the grave that has taken him! What is it that is hidden? ... It has hidden tranquillity and dignity.

* *

If the meaning of "tranquillity" is what I have described, then it is permissible that it is according to what 'Ali ibn Abi Talib said, as we have narrated from him, and it is permissible that it is according to what Mujahid said, as we have related from him, and it is permissible that it is what Wahb ibn Munabbih said and what al-Suddi said, because all of these are sufficient signs in which souls find rest and hearts are soothed. And if the meaning of "tranquillity" is what we have described, then it has become clear that the sign that was in the Ark, in which souls found rest because of their knowledge of its truth, is named by the verbal noun itself while being other than it, since the speech indicates it. [[He means by "the verbal noun" (al-fi'l) the infinitive of the verb "sakana", which is "al-sakina", just as it is said "a just man" (rajul 'adl); if you named the man "justice" ('adlan), he would be named by the verbal noun while being other than it.]]

* *

The interpretation of His words: "and a remnant of what the family of Musa and the family of Harun left behind" (﴿وَبَقِيَّةٌ مِمَّا تَرَكَ آلُ مُوسَى وَآلُ هَارُونَ﴾)

Abu Ja'far said: By His words "a remnant" (baqiyya), He, may He be exalted, means: the remaining thing, from the saying of the speaker: "A remnant of this matter has remained," and it is of the pattern (fa'ila) from it, like "al-sakina" from "sakana."

* *

And His words "of what the family of Musa and the family of Harun left behind" mean: from the estate of the family of Musa and the family of Harun.

* *

The exegetes (ahl al-ta'wil) differed about the "remnant" that had remained from their estate.

Some of them said: That "remnant" was the staff of Musa and the fragments of the Tablets. [[See page 332, note 1.]]

Mention of those who said that: [text ends]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 248 (part 3 of 3):

5685. Others said: Rather, that "remnant" is the staff of Moses and the staff of Aaron, and some of the Tablets. [[In the manuscript: "bal dhalika al-baqiyya…" and what is in the printed edition is the better correct reading.]]

[[The report 5694 appears at length in al-Durr al-Manthur 1:317. In the manuscript and the printed edition: "from Ismaʿil from Ibn Abi Khalid," but the correct reading is what I have established, since Jabir ibn Nuh, the translator of Tahdhib, narrates from him.]]

Others said: Rather, it is the staff and the two sandals.

* *

Others said: Rather, that was the fragments of the Tablets and what had been broken from them.

Mention of those who said this:

5698. al-Qasim told us, saying: Ḥajjaj told me, saying: Ibn Jurayj said: Ibn ʿAbbas said, concerning His words: ﴿And a remnant of what the family of Moses and the family of Aaron left behind﴾: "When Moses threw down the Tablets, they broke, and some of them were lifted up, so the remainder was placed in that chest."

5699. al-Qasim told us, saying: al-Husayn told us, saying: Ḥajjaj told me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: I asked ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abi Rabah about His words: ﴿And a remnant of what the family of Moses and the family of Aaron left behind﴾. [He said:] "Knowledge and the Torah." [[I added what is between the brackets, because I think it fell out from the copyist in his haste, as is apparent from his handwriting at this place.]]

* *

Others said: Rather, that is jihad in the way of God.

Mention of those who said this:

5700. I was told, from al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Muʿadh say: ʿUbayd Allah ibn Sulayman informed us, saying: I heard al-Ḍaḥḥak say, concerning His words: ﴿And a remnant of what the family of Moses and the family of Aaron left behind﴾: by "the remnant" is meant fighting in the way of God, and with that they fought alongside Talut, and with that they were commanded.

Abu Jaʿfar said: The most correct of these sayings, in terms of truth, is to say: God, exalted is His mention, informed us about the chest which He made a sign confirming the truth of His Prophet (ﷺ), who said to his community: [[In the printed edition: "li-ṣidq qawl nabiyyihi ﷺ li-ummatihi," with the addition of "wa-sallam" and the omission of "alladhi qāla." The correct reading is from the manuscript.]] "Indeed God has sent Talut to you as king," that in it is tranquility from Him, and a remnant of what the family of Moses and the family of Aaron left behind. [[In the printed edition: "mimma tarakahu āl Mūsā."
