[[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "or jam'an" (collectively), and the correct reading is what is established; it will come in the correct form shortly in the manuscript.]].

If they are "some," then it is impossible that this some be other than those on which Ibrahim had the means to scatter the parts of the four birds.

= Or they are "all," and it is likewise. [[In the printed edition: "jam'an", and I have kept what is in the manuscript.]].

God, may His remembrance be exalted, has informed that He commanded him to place that on "every mountain," and that is either every mountain whose people Ibrahim knew by their identities, [[In the printed edition: "from every mountain who Ibrahim knew..." in the manuscript: "... who Ibrahim knew" without the waw. I have added "min ajbal" so that the phrase is sound, relying on what preceded.]] or the mountains that are on the earth.

As for the saying of the one who said "that is four mountains," and the saying of the one who said "they are seven," we have no evidence for the correctness of either, so that we may permit saying it. God only commanded Ibrahim, peace be upon him, to place the four birds as scattered parts on every mountain, so that Ibrahim would see His power to gather their parts while they are dispersed and scattered in various places, until He joins some of them to others, and they return = as they were before being cut and torn apart and before their parts were scattered over the mountains = living birds that fly, so that Ibrahim's heart would be at rest and he would know that thus God gathers the joints of the dead for the resurrection, [[In the printed edition: "that thus God gathers..." I have kept what is in the manuscript.]] and His assembling of their parts after decay and returning every limb of theirs to its place as it was before perdition. [[In the printed edition: "before the return," and the correct reading is from the manuscript. Al-Rada: destruction.]].

* *

Abu Ja'far said: "Juz'" (part) of anything is a portion of it, whether the whole of it is divisible into equal shares or not. Thus its meaning differs from "sahm" (share). For "sahm" of a thing is a portion of it into which the whole is divided evenly. That is why people commonly use "sihām" (shares) rather than "ajzā'" (parts) when mentioning their portions of inheritance. [[This is a good distinction which lexicographers rarely hit upon, so note it.]].

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Then call them﴾, its meaning is what I mentioned earlier from Mujahid, that he said: it is a command that he say to the parts of the birds, after their being scattered over every mountain: "Come by God's permission."

* *

If someone says: Was Ibrahim commanded to call them while they were torn into parts on the mountaintops and dead, or after they had been revived? If he was commanded to call them while they were torn and had no spirits in them, what is the sense of commanding one without life to come? And if he was commanded to call them after they had been revived, what need did Ibrahim have to call them, when he had seen them rising up on the mountaintops? It is said: God's command to Ibrahim, peace be upon him, to call them while they were scattered parts is only a command of creation = like God's saying to those whom He transformed into apes after they had been humans: ﴿Be apes, despised﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 65] = not a command of worship, which would be impossible except after the existence of the one commanded and worshipping.

* *

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying: ﴿And know that God is Mighty, Wise (260)﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By this, He, may His remembrance be exalted, means: ﴿And know﴾, O Ibrahim, that the One who gave life to these birds after you tore them and scattered their parts over the mountains, then gathered them and returned the spirit to them, until He restored them to their form before you scattered them = ﴿is Mighty﴾ in His might when He seizes whoever among the tyrants and arrogant seizes, those who opposed His command, disobeyed His messengers, and worshipped other than Him, and in His vengeance until He takes revenge on them = ﴿Wise﴾ in His command.

* *

6026 - Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salamah related to us, saying: Ibn Ishaq related to us: ﴿And know that God is Mighty, Wise﴾, he said: Mighty in His seizing, Wise in His command.

6027 - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Ishaq related to us, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far related to us, from his father, from al-Rabi': ﴿And know that God is Mighty﴾ in His vengeance = ﴿Wise﴾ in His command.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 261:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿The likeness of those who spend their wealth in the way of Allah is that of a grain which grows seven ears, in each ear a hundred grains﴾

Abu Ja'far said: This verse is linked to His saying: ﴿Who is it that will lend to Allah a goodly loan, so He may multiply it for him many times over? And Allah withholds and extends [provision], and to Him you will be returned﴾ [al-Baqarah: 245]. The verses that follow up to His saying: ﴿The likeness of those who spend their wealth in the way of Allah﴾ concern the narratives of the Children of Israel and their account with Talut and Jalut, and what follows that concerning the one who disputed with Ibrahim regarding his Lord, and the matter of the one who passed by the township fallen upon its roofs, and the story of Ibrahim and his request of his Lord for what he asked, all of which we have mentioned before. [[Context of the sentence: "The verses that follow ... are an interjection from Allah the Exalted ..." – subject and predicate.]] It is an interjection from Allah, mentioned by Him, with what He interjected of their stories in between, as an argument by part of it against the polytheists who used to deny the resurrection and the coming of the Hour, and as an exhortation by part of it to the believers to fight in His way, which He had commanded them in His saying: ﴿And fight in the way of Allah, and know that Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing﴾ [al-Baqarah: 244], informing them that He is their helper even if their number is small and the number of their enemy is great, promising them victory over them, and teaching them His practice regarding those who follow their method in seeking the good pleasure of Allah: that He supports them, and regarding those who follow the path of their enemies among the disbelievers: that He forsakes them, scatters their gathering, and weakens their plot. And it is a decisive proof by part of it against the excuse of the Jews who were living among the Muhajirun of the Messenger of Allah ﹙ﷺ﹚, by what He made His Prophet aware of of their hidden affairs and concealed secrets of their forefathers and ancestors which no one else knew, so that they would know that what Muhammad ﹙ﷺ﹚ brought them was from Allah, and that it is not conjecture or fabrication; and it is a warning from Him to the hypocrites among them, so that they would beware, by their doubt about the matter of Muhammad ﹙ﷺ﹚, lest there befall them of His might and severity the like of what befell their forefathers who were in the township He destroyed, leaving it fallen upon its roofs.

Then the Exalted returned to the report about ﹛He who lends Allah a goodly loan﹜ and what He has of reward for his loan, saying: ﴿The likeness of those who spend their wealth in the way of Allah﴾, meaning: the likeness of those who spend their wealth on themselves in striving against the enemies of Allah with their persons and their wealth ﴿is like a grain﴾ of wheat or barley, or other plant of the earth whose yield [[In the printed edition: "tusanbil sunbulatan bazruha zari'" – "sunbulah" placed in the position of "rey'ha", thought to be a corruption. The "rey' al-bazr" is the surplus that comes out of the seed over its origin, from "al-rey'" meaning growth and increase. The meaning: its yield multiplies, increasing and abounding.]] ﴿then it grows﴾, meaning: it produces ﴿seven ears; in each ear a hundred grains﴾. He says: likewise the one who spends his wealth on himself in the way of Allah, for him is a reward of seven hundredfold for each unit of his expenditure. As:

6028 - Musa ibn Harun related to me, saying: Amr ibn Hammad related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿like a grain that grows seven ears, in each ear a hundred grains﴾. This is for the one who spends in the way of Allah; for him is his reward, seven hundred. [[In the printed edition: "fa-lahu sab' mi'ah" omitting "ajruhu"; in the manuscript: "fa-lahu sab'mi'ah" with a blank between the words; I completed the phrase from al-Durr al-Manthur 1:336, where it reads: "fa-lahu ajruhu sab'mi'ah marrah".]]

6029 - Yunus related to us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying: ﴿The likeness of those who spend their wealth in the way of Allah is like a grain that grows seven ears, in each ear a hundred grains; and Allah multiplies for whom He wills﴾: This is the one who spends on himself in the way of Allah and goes forth.

6030 - Al-Rabi' related to us from Amr, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far related to us, from his father, from al-Rabi', regarding His saying: ﴿The likeness of those who spend their wealth in the way of Allah is like a grain that grows seven ears...﴾ the verse, [he said]: It was for whoever pledged allegiance to the Prophet ﹙ﷺ﹚ on emigration, and stationed himself with the Prophet ﹙ﷺ﹚ in Madinah, and did not go to any direction except with his permission. [[In the manuscript: "lam yulif wajhan," and what is in the printed edition is acceptable, though I am in doubt about it. In al-Durr al-Manthur 1:336: "lam yadhhab wajhan."]] For him the good deed was seven hundredfold, and for whoever pledged allegiance upon Islam the good deed was ten times its like.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: If someone says: Have you seen an ear with a hundred grains, or has it reached you, that it was cited as a parable of one who spends his wealth in the way of Allah? [[In the margin of the manuscript is a comment on this question, the first comment I find on this copy in a hand other than its scribe's; it is Maghribi, as will become clear from what is written, and some letters are worn away at the edge of the margin, so I have made an effort to read them:

"I say: rather, that is established, verified, and witnessed in the lands, and more than that. For the ears of those lands have an abundance of grain and branches up to nearly the number... I counted from the branches of a single grain sixty-three branches, and I witnessed that many times. One of my companions showed me a quantity of that... The least we counted for a grain was thirteen ears, up to what reaches or exceeds the number I mentioned first. Written by Muhammad ibn Mahmud al-Jaza'iri al-Hanafi."

Then look at what al-Qurtubi and others said in the rest of the books of tafsir.]]

It is said: If that exists, then it is that. [[In the manuscript: "qila qila an yakun dhalika mawjud fa-huwa dhak" which is undoubtedly an error; the printed edition is good in context.]] Otherwise, it is permissible that its meaning is: like an ear that grows seven ears, in each ear a hundred grains, if Allah makes that in it.

It is also possible that its meaning is: in each ear a hundred grains; meaning that when it is sown, it produces a hundred grains. So what came from the seed that was from it of the hundred grains is attributed to it, because it was from it. Some of the interpreters have interpreted it this way.

Mention of those who said that:

6031 - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Ishaq related to us, saying: Abu Zuhayr related to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak regarding His saying: ﴿The likeness of those who spend their wealth in the way of Allah is like a grain that grows seven ears, in each ear a hundred grains﴾, he said: Each ear produced a hundred grains; this is for the one who spends in the way of Allah. ﴿And Allah multiplies for whom He wills; and Allah is All-Encompassing, All-Knowing﴾.

* *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And Allah multiplies for whom He wills﴾

Abu Ja'far said: The interpreters differed regarding the interpretation of His saying: ﴿And Allah multiplies for whom He wills﴾. Some of them said: Allah multiplies for whom He wills of His servants the reward of their good deeds, after what He gave to the one who does not spend in His way, beyond what He promised the one who spends in His way of multiplying one unit into seven hundred. As for the one who spends in His way, He does not diminish for him what He promised of multiplying seven hundred by one. [[In the printed edition this whole sentence read: "And Allah multiplies for whom He wills of His servants the reward of their good deeds, after what He gave the one who spends in His way of the multiplication of one unit into seven hundred. As for the one who spends in His way, he is not reduced in what He promised of the multiplication of seven hundred by one." They changed what was in the manuscript, because it is undoubtedly corrupt, and this is its text: "And Allah multiplies for whom He wills the reward of his good deeds, after what He gave the one who spends in His way of the multiplication of one unit into seven hundred. As for the one who spends in His way, 'amma wa'adahu...'" But I have deduced from the context of the tafsir afterward that the correct reading is other than what is in the printed edition, and that there is a corruption and omission in the sentence, which I completed with what agrees with the meaning these people stated, as is clear from Abu Ja'far's words later.]]

Mention of those who said that:

6032 - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Ishaq related to us, saying: Abu Zuhayr related to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, who said: This multiplies for the one who spends in the way of Allah, meaning the seven hundred: ﴿And Allah multiplies for whom He wills, and Allah is All-Encompassing, All-Knowing﴾, meaning for the one who does not spend in His way.

* *

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: ﴿And Allah multiplies for whom He wills﴾ among those who spend in His way, upon the seven hundred up to two thousand thousand-fold. This is a view reported from Ibn Abbas through a chain I did not find, so I left out mentioning it.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: What is more appropriate as the interpretation of His saying: ﴿And Allah multiplies for whom He wills﴾ is: Allah multiplies upon the seven hundred to whatever multiplication He wills, for whom He wills of those who spend in His way, because there has been no mention of reward and multiplication for one who does not spend in the way of Allah, so it would be permissible for us to direct what the Exalted promised in this verse of multiplication to being a promise from Him concerning [action other than in His way, or] other than spending in the way of Allah. [[I added what is between the brackets, because it is what the context and structure of the speech require.]]

* *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And Allah is All-Encompassing, All-Knowing (261)﴾

Abu Ja'far said: The Exalted means by this: ﴿And Allah is All-Encompassing﴾, that He increases whom He wills of His creatures who spend in His way beyond the multiples of the seven hundred that He promised to increase for him. ﴿All-Knowing﴾ of who among them deserves the increase, as:

6033 - Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying: ﴿And Allah multiplies for whom He wills; and Allah is All-Encompassing, All-Knowing﴾, he said: ﴿All-Encompassing﴾ that He increases from His vastness, ﴿All-Knowing﴾, knowing whom He increases.

* *

Others said: The meaning of that is: ﴿And Allah is All-Encompassing﴾ for those multiples, ﴿All-Knowing﴾ of what those who spend their wealth in obedience to Allah spend.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 262:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿Those who spend their wealth in the way of Allah and then do not follow what they have spent with reminders of their generosity or with injury, for them is their reward with their Lord, and there is no fear for them, nor will they grieve﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: By this, may His remembrance be exalted, He means: the one who gives his wealth to those who strive in the way of Allah, as an aid to them in fighting the enemies of Allah. He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: those who help those who strive in the way of Allah by spending on them and on their mounts, and other of their needs, [[In the manuscript and the printed edition: "those who help the strivers" in the plural, while the construction of the sentences after it is in the singular, and that is impermissible.]] . Then they do not follow their expenditure, which they spent on them, with reminders of favour by making that expenditure on them a burden, nor with injury to them. Their reminding them of it is by showing to them that they have done a kindness to them, by their action and their gift which they gave them as strengthening for them in fighting their enemy, and expressing that either by tongue or by deed. As for "injury", it is his complaining to them because of what he gave them and strengthened them with of expenditure in the way of Allah, that they did not perform the duty incumbent on them in jihad, and similar speech with which one injures the one he spent upon.

He only made that a condition for the one who spends in the way of Allah, and made the reward obligatory for the one who is neither reminding nor injuring the one on whom he spent in the way of Allah, because the expenditure which is in the way of Allah is that which is sought by it the Face of Allah and by which one seeks what is with Him. So when the meaning of spending in the way of Allah is what we have described, there is no basis for the spender to remind the one on whom he spent, because he has no hand over him nor any favour by which he would deserve, if he is not repaid, reminders and injury, since his expenditure on him was for the sake of reckoning and seeking the reward of Allah and seeking His good pleasure, and upon Allah is its recompense, not upon the one on whom it was spent.

* *

And those of the people of interpretation who said the like of the meaning we have stated said:

6034 - Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿Those who spend their wealth in the way of Allah, then do not follow what they have spent with reminders or injury, for them is their reward with their Lord﴾. [[The verse is completed in the printed edition; I have kept what is in the manuscript.]] . Allah knew that people would remind of their gifts, so He disliked that and preceded it, saying: ﴿A kind word and forgiveness are better than charity followed by injury. And Allah is Free of need and Forbearing﴾.

6035 - Yunus narrated to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said: Allah said to the others, meaning: Allah said to the others, who are those who do not go out to fight their enemy: ﴿Those who spend their wealth in the way of Allah, then do not follow what they have spent with reminders or injury﴾. He said: So He made a condition upon them. He said: And the one who goes out was not conditioned upon anything, little or much, meaning by the one who goes out, the one who goes out in the jihad which Allah mentioned in His saying: ﴿The example of those who spend their wealth in the way of Allah is like a grain﴾, the verse. Ibn Zayd said: My father used to say: If someone who gives something from this harms you, or [you are] strengthened, [then you are] strengthened in the way of Allah. So you think that your greeting is burdensome to him, so you withhold your greeting from him. Ibn Zayd said: So he forbade the best of Islam. He said: A woman said to my father: O Abu Usamah, point me to a man who truly goes out in the way of Allah, for they only go out to eat fruits!! I have a quiver and arrows in it. [[I fear the copyist erred as he erred before, and that the correct reading is "wa-fīhā asham" (and in it are arrows); what is here is acceptable.]] . So he said to her: May Allah not bless your quiver, nor your arrows, for you have injured them before you give them! He said: And a man used to say to them: Go out and eat fruits!

6036 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, he said: Ishaq narrated to us, he said: Abu Zuhayr narrated to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, regarding His saying: ﴿They do not follow what they have spent with reminders or injury﴾, he said: That a man not spend his wealth is better than that he spend it and then follow it with reminders and injury.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿for them is their reward with their Lord﴾, it means: for those who spend their wealth in the way of Allah as has been explained. The "ha" and "mim" in "lahum" refer back to "alladhina" (those who).

* *

The meaning of His saying: ﴿for them is their reward with their Lord﴾ is: for them is their reward and recompense for their expenditure which they spent in the way of Allah, then they did not follow it with reminders or injury. [[See the meaning of "ajr" (reward) previously at 2:148, 2:513.]] .

* *

As for His saying: ﴿nor is there fear for them, nor will they grieve﴾ [[See the interpretation of "nor is there fear for them, nor will they grieve" previously at 2:148, 2:513.]] . He says: they, together with what they have of recompense and reward for their expenditure which they spent on the condition we stipulated, ﴿there is no fear for them﴾ when they come before Allah and part from the world, nor in the terrors of the Resurrection, nor that some of its hardships befall them or that some punishment of Allah befall them in it, ﴿nor will they grieve﴾ over what they left behind them in the world. [[At this point the fourth volume of our manuscript ends, and at its end is the following text:

"End of the fourth volume of the book al-Bayan, to be followed in the fifth, God willing: The interpretation of His saying: 'A kind word and forgiveness are better than charity followed by injury, and Allah is Free of need and Forbearing.'

The completion of it was in the month of Dhu al-Hijjah in the year 714 AH, and praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds, and may Allah bless our master Muhammad and his family and companions, and grant them abundant peace."

Then the fifth part begins, and in its margin:

"The fifth part of Jami' al-Bayan fi Ta'wil al-Qur'an, composed by the Shaykh, the Imam Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Jarir al-Tabari"

Then follows a waqf text for Allah, may He be exalted, which we have dispensed with stating here. Then the part opens:

"In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful. My Lord, help [me]."]] .

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿A kind word and forgiveness are better than charity followed by injury. And Allah is Free of need, Forbearing﴾ (2:263)

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is He, by His saying ﴿A kind word﴾ He means a good utterance and a man's supplication for his Muslim brother [[See the explanation of "al-ma'ruf" above, 3:371, 372; then 4:547, 548; 5:7, 44, 76, 93, 173.]] = ﴿and forgiveness﴾, meaning: a concealment by him of the other's condition, because he knows his need and his bad circumstances [[See the explanation of "al-maghfirah" 2:109, 110, and the indexes of language.]] = ﴿is better﴾ with Allah = ﴿than charity﴾ that one gives to him = ﴿followed by injury﴾, meaning he complains to him about it and harms him because of it, as in the following:

6037 - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Ishaq told us, saying: Abu Zuhayr told us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, regarding ﴿A kind word and forgiveness are better than charity followed by injury﴾: he said, "Withholding his wealth is better than spending his wealth and then following it with reproach and injury."

* *

As for His saying ﴿Forbearing﴾, it means: "And Allah is Free of need" from what they give in charity = ﴿Forbearing﴾, in that He does not hasten punishment upon those among you who reproach with their charity and injure the one they give it to. [[See the explanation of "halim" above, 5:117.]]

It has also been related from Ibn Abbas regarding this, that:

6038 - Al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Abd Allah ibn Salih told us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿Al-Ghani﴾ is the one who is perfect in his self-sufficiency, and ﴿al-Halim﴾ is the one who is perfect in his forbearance.

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿O you who have believed, do not nullify your charities with reminders or injury, like one who spends his wealth to be seen by the people and does not believe in Allah and the Last Day﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His remembrance be exalted, He means: ﴿O you who have believed﴾, affirm Allah and His Messenger. ﴿Do not nullify your charities﴾, that is, do not nullify the rewards of your charities with reminders and injury, just as the disbelief of one who spends his wealth ﴿to be seen by the people﴾ nullified it. This is his showing off to people through his deed: he spends his wealth in what people outwardly see as seeking Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, so they praise him for it, while he does not intend Allah by it and does not seek reward from Him. [[In the manuscript and the printed edition: "and he intends by it other than Allah," which is a copyist's error; the context requires that "other than" be placed first, and this is the sense of the meaning.]] He spends it in this manner only outwardly, so that people will praise him for it and say: "He is generous and noble, and he is a righteous man," and so they will bestow praise upon him, while they do not know what is concealed in his intention in spending what he spends, and so they do not know what he is upon of denial of Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, and the Last Day.
* *
As for His words: ﴿and does not believe in Allah and the Last Day﴾, its meaning is: he does not affirm the oneness and lordship of Allah, nor that he will be resurrected after his death and recompensed for his deeds, so he would make his deed for the sake of Allah and seeking His reward and what is with Him in the Hereafter. This is the description of the hypocrite. We only said he is a hypocrite because the one who openly displays his disbelief and proclaims his polytheism is known not to be showing off with any of his deeds, because the show-off is one who shows off to people with a deed which is outwardly for Allah, while inwardly the intention of its doer is troubled, his aim in it being the praise of people for it. [[In the printed edition: "and inwardly the doer's intention is that he aims by it the praise of people," which is an editorial alteration; in the manuscript: "and inwardly his troubled intention is aimed at it the praise of people," which is not clear in meaning, and it is evident that "intention" (sarīrah) has fallen out of "troubled intention of its doer", which points to what was explained earlier in his commentary: "so they do not know what he is upon of denial of Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, and the Last Day." So I deemed the correct reading to be the addition of "sarīrah", to agree with the meanings that Abu Ja'far, may Allah have mercy on him, stated.]] The disbeliever does not have his matter confused for anyone, that all his actions are only for Satan - if he openly declares his disbelief - and not for Allah. Whoever is like this is not one who shows off with his deeds.
* *
Those of interpretation have said similarly to what we have said on this.
Mention of those who said that:
6039 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Abu Hani al-Khawlani said, from Amr ibn Huraith, who said: Indeed the man who fights in battle, does not steal, does not commit adultery, does not embezzle, does not return with mere sufficiency! It was said to him: Why is that? He said: Indeed the man goes out, [[In the printed edition: "He said: Indeed the man," and in the manuscript: "Indeed indeed the man," a distortion; the correct reading is what I have set down.]] and when there befalls him some of Allah's trial which He has decreed upon him, he curses and reviles his leader and curses the hour he went out to fight, and says: I will never return to fight with him again! So this is upon him, and it is not for him, like spending in the way of Allah followed by reminder and injury. Allah has struck the parable of it in the Qur'an: ﴿O you who have believed, do not nullify your charities with reminders and injury﴾, until he concluded the verse. [[The report 6039: "Abu Hani al-Khawlani" is Humayd ibn Hani al-Misri, one of the reliable Successors, who narrated from Amr ibn Huraith and others. Al-Layth, Ibn Lahi'ah, Ibn Wahb and others from the people of Egypt narrated from him; he died in the year 142. The "Amr ibn Huraith" who narrates from the people of Syria is a different one from "Amr ibn Huraith ibn Amr ibn Uthman al-Makhzumi al-Kufi". See his biography in al-Tahdhib 8:18.]]
* *
The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿So his example is like a smooth stone with dust on it, on which a heavy rain strikes and leaves it bare. They have no power over anything they have earned, and Allah does not guide the disbelieving people﴾ (264)

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His remembrance be exalted, He means: So the example of this one who spends his wealth to be seen by the people, and does not believe in Allah and the Last Day, is ... The "hā'" in His words ﴿his example﴾ refers back to "the one who" = ﴿like a smooth stone﴾, and "ṣafwān" is both singular and plural. Whoever makes it plural, its singular is "ṣafwānah", [[In the printed edition: "singular and plural, so whoever makes it plural," and I have set down what is in the manuscript.]] like "tamrah and tamr" and "nakhlah and nakhl". Whoever makes it singular, its plural is "ṣifwān, ṣufiyy, and ṣifiyy", [[See what has preceded in the explanation of "al-Ṣafā" 3:224, 225. His saying "its plural ṣifwān" means: with a kasra on the ṣād and a sukūn on the fā', and this is the view of al-Kisā'ī, though they have criticized and faulted him on his isolated doctrine. See al-Qurtubi 3:313, Tafsir Abi Hayyan 2:302, and for this reason the lexicographers omitted it from their books.]] as the poet said: [[He is al-Akhyal al-Ta'i.]]
the perching of birds upon the ṣufiyy * [[The explanation and takhrīj of this verse was given earlier at 3:224, and the place was omitted from the earlier takhrīj, so I have set it down there.]]
And "ṣafwān" is "al-ṣafā", which are smooth stones.
* *
His words ﴿on it is dust﴾ mean: on the stone there is dust. ﴿Then a heavy rain struck it﴾: a heavy rain struck the stone. ﴿Wābil﴾ is the intense, great rain, as Imru' al-Qays said:
"A while, then it aimed at it, a wābil, falling heavily on its sides, pouring and copious." [[His Dīwān: 90, Ṭabaqāt Fuḥūl al-Shu'arā': 79, and others, many. It is from a famous set of verses describing rain and flood.]]
From it one says: "The sky rained (wabalat al-samā'), so it rains a wabl," and "the earth was rained upon, so it is wābil."
* *
His words ﴿leaving it bare (ṣaldan)﴾ mean: the heavy rain left the stone bare.
"Ṣald" of stones is the hard one with nothing on it of plants or anything else, and of lands, that in which nothing grows, and likewise of heads. As Ru'bah said: [[This explanation of the meanings of "ṣald" is not found in many lexicons.]]
...

Those who have spoken on this matter include Yunus, Ibn Wahb, Ibn Zayd, al-Rabi', al-Suddi, Qatadah, Ibn Jurayj, Mujahid and others...

٦٠٥٤ - Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Ishaq told us, he said: Abu Zuhayr told us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak: ﴿فأصابه وابل﴾ "Wabil" means heavy rain.

٦٠٥٥ - Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Sa'id told us, from Qatadah, the same as this.

٦٠٥٦ - I was told on the authority of Ammar, he said: Ibn Abi Ja'far told us, from his father, from al-Rabi', the same as this.

* *

Discussion of the words of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿فَتَرَكَهُ صَلْدًا﴾

Mention of those who said the same as what we have said about it:

٦٠٥٧ - Musa told me, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, from al-Suddi: ﴿فتركه صلدًا﴾ means "clean" (naqiyyan).

٦٠٥٨ - Muhammad ibn Sa'd told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My paternal uncle told me, he said: My father told me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿فتركه صلدًا﴾ He said: He left it clean, with nothing on it.

٦٠٥٩ - Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Husayn told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, he said: Ibn Jurayj said: Ibn Abbas said regarding His words: ﴿فتركه صلدًا﴾ He said: There is nothing on it.

٦٠٦٠ - Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Ishaq told us, he said: Abu Zuhayr told us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak: ﴿صلدًا﴾ meaning He left it bare (jardan).

٦٠٦١ - Al-Hasan ibn Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, he said: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah: ﴿فتركه صلدًا﴾ There is nothing on it.

٦٠٦٢ - Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abu Salih told us, he said: Mu'awiyah told me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿فتركه صلدًا﴾ There is nothing on it.

The interpretation of the words of the Most High: ﴿And the example of those who spend their wealth seeking the approval of Allah and for the firm establishment of their own souls﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His praise be exalted, He means: ﴿And the example of those who spend their wealth﴾, giving it in charity, bearing its burdens in the way of Allah, and strengthening with it those in need among the warriors and the fighters in the way of Allah, and in other acts of obedience to Allah, seeking His approval = [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "seeking His approval, and tathbitan ya'ni bi-dhalika wa-tathbitan min anfusihim ya'ni lahum" — this is an incoherent statement, and it appears that the copyist stumbled in his writing, repeated and duplicated, so I removed "wa-tathbitan ya'ni bi-dhalika" and added "bi-dhalika wa-tathbitan" after "ya'ni" the second time, which remained.]].
= ﴿And for the firm establishment of their own souls﴾ means: and a firm establishment for them in spending that in the obedience of Allah, and confirmation; from the saying of the speaker: "I made so-and-so firm in this matter" — when I corrected his resolve, confirmed it, and strengthened his opinion in it — "he firmly established him (athbatahu) with firm establishment (tathbitan)", as Ibn Rawaha said:

So may Allah firmly establish what He has given you of good, the firm establishment of Moses, and a victory like that with which they were victorious. [[Sirat Ibn Hisham 4:16; Ibn Sa'd 3/2/81; al-Mukhtalif wal-Mu'talif of al-Amidi: 126; al-Isti'ab 1:305; Tabaqat Fuhul al-Shu'ara: 188, from verses in which he praises the Messenger of the Lord of the worlds. Al-Amidi and Ibn Hisham transmitted the second line as "among the messengers and a victory like that with which they were victorious." When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) heard this verse, he turned to him with his face smiling and said: "And may Allah firmly establish you."]]

* *

What Allah, mighty and majestic, meant by this is: that their souls were certain and confirmed in the promise of Allah to them regarding what they spent in His obedience without reproach or harm; so it firmly established them in spending their wealth seeking the approval of Allah, and it corrected their resolve and their opinions, [[In the manuscript: "fa-yuthabbituhum fi infaq amwalihim ..." which is an error by the copyist, or a misreading of the copy he drew from. In the printed edition: "fa-thabbatahum ... wa-sahha 'azmahum," which altered what is in the manuscript and made "sahhahat"/"sahha" incomprehensible to what al-Tabari intended. See the following note.]] with certainty of that, and confirmation of the promise of Allah to them, what He promised them. For this reason, those among the people of interpretation who said regarding His words "and firm establishment" — "confirmation" — and those among them who said "certainty" — because the firm establishment of the souls of those who spend their wealth seeking the approval of Allah for them, is only from certainty on their part and confirmation of the promise of Allah.
Mention of those who said this among the people of interpretation:

3. (6063) — Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Yahya narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu Musa, from al-Sha'bi regarding: ﴿and firm establishment from their souls﴾, he said: confirmation and certainty.

4. (6064) — Ahmad ibn Ishaq al-Ahwazi narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu Musa, from al-Sha'bi: ﴿and firm establishment from their souls﴾, he said: confirmation from their souls, steadfastness and support.

5. (6065) — al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah regarding His words: ﴿and firm establishment from their souls﴾, he said: certainty from their souls. He said: the firm establishment is certainty.

6. (6066) — Yunus narrated to me, saying: 'Ali ibn Ma'bad narrated to us, from Abu Mu'awiya, from Isma'il, from Abu Salih regarding His words: ﴿and firm establishment from their souls﴾, he says: certainty from their own souls.

* *

Others said: the meaning of His words ﴿and firm establishment from their souls﴾ is that they would be careful (yatathabbatun) in the place where they put their charities.
Mention of those who said this:

7. (6067) — Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Mu'ammal narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿and firm establishment from their souls﴾, he said: they are careful where they put their wealth.

8. (6068) — al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Suwayd ibn Nasr narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, from 'Uthman ibn al-Aswad, from Mujahid: ﴿and firm establishment from their souls﴾; I said to him: what is that firm establishment? He said: they are careful where they put their wealth.

9. (6069) — Ibn WakI' narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to us, from 'Uthman ibn al-Aswad, from Mujahid: ﴿and firm establishment from their souls﴾, he said: they used to be careful where they put it.

10. (6070) — Ibn WakI' narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to us, from 'Ali ibn 'Ali ibn Rifa'a, from al-Hasan regarding His words: ﴿and firm establishment from their souls﴾, he said: they used to be careful where they put their wealth — meaning their zakat.

11. (6071) — al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Suwayd narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, from 'Ali ibn 'Ali, who said: I heard al-Hasan recite: ﴿seeking the approval of Allah and firm establishment from their souls﴾, and he said: when a man was about to give charity, he would be careful; if it was for Allah he proceeded, and if doubt mixed with it he withheld.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: This interpretation that we have mentioned from Mujahid and al-Hasan is a meaning far from what the apparent recitation indicates. They interpreted His words ﴿and firm establishment from their souls﴾ as meaning "wa-tathabbutan" (careful deliberation), claiming that this was said in that form because the people were careful about where they placed their wealth. But if the interpretation were that, it would be "wa-tathabbutan min anfusihim," because the verbal noun of speech, if it is on the pattern of "tafa''ala," is "tafa''ul," as one says "takarrama takarruman" and "takallama takallaman," and as the Most High said: ﴿or He seizes them by gradual reduction (takhawwuf)﴾ [al-Nahl: 47], from the saying of the speaker "takhawwafa fulan hadha al-amr takhawwufan." So likewise His words ﴿and firm establishment from their souls﴾: had it been from "tathabbata al-qawm fi wad' sadaqatihim mawadi'aha" (the people were careful in placing their charities in their places), the expression would have been "wa-tathabbutan min anfusihim," not "wa-tathbitan." Rather, the meaning of that is what we have said: that it is a firm establishment from the souls of the people for them, with the soundness of resolve and certainty in the promise of Allah, may His mention be exalted.

* *

If someone says: What prevents you from holding that this is like the saying of Allah, mighty and majestic: ﴿and devote yourself to Him with complete devotion﴾ [al-Muzzammil: 8], where He did not say "tabattulan"?

It is said: This is different from that. For this only permitted saying "tabtilan" because "wa-tabattal ilayhi" is evident, and its evidence indicates an omitted speech from which "tabtilan" is said. The omitted speech is: "tabattal fa-yabtulaka Allahu ilayhi tabtilan." The Arabs sometimes do likewise: they bring verbal nouns out in forms other than the verbs preceding them, when the preceding verbs indicate what they were derived from, as the Most High said: ﴿And Allah has caused you to grow from the earth a growth (nabatan)﴾ [Nuh: 17], and He said: ﴿and He made it grow with a good growth (nabatan hasanan)﴾ [Al 'Imran: 37]; "nabat" is the verbal noun of "nabata." This was permitted because "anbata" preceded it, which indicates the omitted speech from which "nabatan" is said; the meaning being: "Allah made you grow, so you grew from the earth a growth." But His words ﴿and firm establishment from their souls﴾ are not a speech that could be supposed to be a verbal noun deviated from its form. The meaning of the speech is: "and they are careful in placing charities in their places," so it is directed to the meanings to which His words ﴿and devote yourself to Him with complete devotion﴾ are directed, and similar verbal nouns deviated from verbs that are apparent before them.

* *

Others said: the meaning of His words ﴿and firm establishment from their souls﴾ is "ihtisaban" (seeking reward) from their souls.
Mention of those who said this:

12. (6073) — Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿and firm establishment from their souls﴾, he says: ihtisaban (seeking reward) from their souls. [[Number 6072 was omitted from the numbering by mistake.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: This saying is also far from the meaning of "tathbit," because "tathbit" is not known in any speech to mean "ihtisab," unless its commentator intended that: that the souls of the spenders were seeking reward in establishing their owners. If that is what he meant, then the meaning of the speech is that, but "ihtisab" is not then a meaning of "tathbit," so it should not be translated by it.

* *

Commentary on the interpretation of the words of the Most High: ﴿like a garden on a height, struck by a heavy rain, which then yields its produce twofold; and if it is not struck by a heavy rain, then a light rain﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may He be exalted and majestic, He means: and the example of those who spend their wealth, giving it in charity, and sending it out in the obedience of Allah, without reproach toward those to whom they give it in charity, nor any harm from them to them with it, seeking the good pleasure of Allah and confirming from their souls His promise = ﴿like a garden﴾.

* *

"Al-jannah" is the orchard. We have already shown earlier that "al-jannah" is an orchard, by enough of its repetition. [[See what preceded: 1:384.]]

* *

= ﴿on a height (rabwah)﴾. The "rabwah" from the land is what rises from it and is elevated above the flood. He described it thus, may His praise be exalted, because what is raised above the watercourses and valleys is thicker, and the gardens of what is thick of the land are better and more productive of fruit, plants, and crops than what is thin. For this reason the poet of Banu Tha'laba said, describing a meadow:

What a meadow of the meadows of al-Hazn, green with growth, which a flowing, pouring rain has showered upon. [[From his famous eloquent qasida. Describing the fragrance of his beloved when she stands. The poetry lines are cited in the original; here only the first verse is given as is quoted in the text.]] So he described it as being among the meadows of al-Hazn, because the hazn (rugged uplands): its plants and vegetation are better and stronger than the plantings and crops of valleys and low slopes.

* *

There are three dialectal forms of "rabwah." Some reciters among a group of reciters read each of these forms: "Rubwah" with a damma on the ra, which is how the common reciters of Madina, the Hijaz and Iraq read. "Rabwah" with a fatha on the ra, which some people of Syria and some of Kufa read, and it is said to be a dialect of Tamim. "Ribwah" with a kasra on the ra, which, it is reported, Ibn 'Abbas read.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: It is not permissible in my view to read it except in one of the two dialects: either with a fatha on the "ra" or a damma on it, because the people's recitation in their regions is with one of them. I am more inclined to read it with a damma, because it is the more well-known of the two dialects among the Arabs. As for the kasra, abandoning recitation with it is a clear indication that recitation with it is not permissible.

* *

"Rabwah" was named so because it "rabat" (swelled), becoming thick and high, from the saying of the speaker: "rabā hadha al-shay' yarbu," when it swells and grows large.

* *

The people of interpretation said in agreement with what we have said regarding that.
Mention of those who said that:

13. (6074) — Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding His words: ﴿like a garden on a rabwah﴾, he said: the rabwah is the high, level place.

14. (6075) — al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, saying: Mujahid said: it is the level, elevated land.

15. (6076) — Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿like a garden on a rabwah﴾, he says: on a rise of land.

16. (6077) — al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abu Zuhayr narrated to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak: ﴿like a garden on a rabwah﴾; the rabwah is the high place where rivers do not flow, and where there are gardens.

17. (6078) — Musa narrated to me, saying: 'Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi regarding His words: ﴿on a rabwah﴾, on a hill of land.

18. (6079) — 'An 'Ammar narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi': ﴿like a garden on a rabwah﴾, and the rabwah is the rise of land.

19. (6080) — al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, saying: Ibn Jurayj said: Ibn 'Abbas said: ﴿like a garden on a rabwah﴾; he said: the high place where rivers do not flow.

* *

Others said: it is the level land.
Mention of those who said that:

20. (6081) — al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Hasan regarding His words: ﴿like a garden on a rabwah﴾, he said: it is level land which rises above the waters.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: As for His words ﴿struck by a heavy rain﴾, He, may His praise be exalted, means: the garden which is on the rabwah of the land was struck by a heavy rain, which is intense and great in its falling.

* *

As for His words ﴿which then yields its produce twofold﴾, He means the garden: its fruit doubled when the heavy rain struck it.

* *

"Al-ukul" is the thing eaten, and it is like "al-ru'b" and "al-huzw," and similar nouns that come on the pattern "fu'l." As for "al-akl" with a fatha on the alif and a sukun on the kaf, it is the act of eating; one says from it: "akaltu aklan" and "akaltu aklatan wahida," as the poet said:

And an eating, if I attain it by spoil, nor a hunger, if I suffer it, with torment (gharam).

[[Hamasa of al-Shajari: 24, from excellent verses, and before it, in its transmission, which I have given: ...]]

So the alif is fatha because it has the meaning of the verb. And what shows that this is so is His saying "and not a hunger," and if the alif of "al-akla" were damma, the meaning would be the food that was eaten, so the meaning then would be: "what food I ate is no spoil."

* *

As for His words ﴿but if a heavy rain does not strike it, then a light rain (tall)﴾: "al-tall" is the dew and the soft rain, as:

21. (6082) — 'Abbas ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, saying: Ibn Jurayj said: ﴿fa-tall﴾: dew — from 'Ata' al-Khurasani, from Ibn 'Abbas.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 265 (part 2 of 3):

3083 - Musa narrated to me, saying: Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: As for *al-tall* (light dew), it is *al-nada* (dew).

3084 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿But if heavy rain does not reach it, then light rain (ṭall)﴾: meaning *ṭashsh* (a fine, light drizzle).

3085 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abu Zuhayr narrated to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, regarding ﴿then light rain﴾: he said: *al-ṭall* is the *al-radhadh* (fine spray) of rain, meaning the gentlest of it.

3086 - It was related to me from Ammar, who said: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi': ﴿ṭall﴾, meaning *ṭashsh*.

* *

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: By this parable, may His remembrance be exalted, Allah means: just as the fruit of this garden whose description I have given is multiplied when heavy rain falls on it, so too, if the heavy rain misses it, the light rain suffices. Allah multiplies the charity of one who gives in charity, and who spends his wealth seeking His good pleasure and firming up his own soul, without reminding or harming, whether his expenditure is small or large. His spending is not wasted and does not fail, just as the garden whose description He, may His praise be exalted, has given is multiplied: whether little or much rain reaches it, its produce does not fail in any circumstance.

* *

Those who held the interpretation (ta'wil) that we have stated also said the same as this. Those who said so:

3087 - Musa narrated to me, saying: Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His saying: ﴿So it brings forth its produce twofold; but if heavy rain does not reach it, then light rain﴾: he says, just as the fruit of that garden was doubled, so too the fruit of this spender is multiplied twofold.

3088 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿So it brings forth its produce twofold; but if heavy rain does not reach it, then light rain﴾: This is a parable that Allah struck for the deed of the believer. He says: there is no failure in its good, just as there is no failure in the good of this garden in any condition, whether it is heavy rain or light rain.

3089 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abu Zuhayr narrated to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, who said: This is a parable of one who spends his wealth seeking the good pleasure of Allah.

3090 - It was related to me from Ammar, who said: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi', regarding His saying: ﴿Those who spend their wealth seeking the good pleasure of Allah﴾ ... the verse. He said: This is a parable Allah struck for the deed of the believer.

* *

If someone asks: How is it said, ﴿But if heavy rain does not reach it, then light rain﴾, when this is a report about a matter that has already passed?

It is said: the word *kāna* ("was") is implied, and the meaning of the statement is: it brings forth its produce twofold; but if heavy rain has not reached it, then light rain reaches it. This is in speech like the saying of a speaker: "I held two horses, and if I did not hold two, then one at its value," meaning "if I had not (held two)." It is necessary to imply *kāna*, because this is a report. [[All of this is in al-Farra's Ma'ani al-Qur'an, 1: 178.]] From it is the saying of the poet: [[Za'ida ibn Sa'sa'a al-Fiq'asi.]]

*When we are reckoned in lineage, a base woman did not bear me,*
*and you did not find any way other than that you should be nursed by her.* [[Its takhrij and explanation were previously given at 2: 165, 353.]]

* *

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying: ﴿And Allah is Seeing of what you do﴾ (2:265)

Abu Ja'far said: He means by this: ﴿And Allah is of what you do﴾, O people, in your expenditures that you spend, ﴿Seeing﴾, nothing of them is hidden from Him, nor anything of your deeds in them or in other than them. He knows which of you spends with reminders and harm, and who spends seeking the good pleasure of Allah and firming up his own soul. He will count it against you until He recompenses each of you for his deed: if good, then good; and if evil, then evil.

By this statement, may His remembrance be exalted, He intends to warn of His punishment regarding the expenditures that His servants spend, and other deeds, lest any of His creatures do what he has been forbidden from, or neglect what he has been commanded to do, because that is in the sight and hearing of Allah. He knows it and counts it against them, and He is ever on the watch over His creation. [[In the printed edition: "bi-khalqihi" (with His creation). The editor did not read the manuscript well.]]

* *

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying: ﴿Would one of you like to have a garden of palm trees and grapevines, with rivers flowing beneath it, having in it of all fruits, and old age has overtaken him while he has weak offspring, and then it is struck by a whirlwind containing fire, so it is burned?﴾

Abu Ja'far said: The meaning of that is: [[In the printed edition: "meaning, may His remembrance be exalted." I do not know why the printer changed it.]] ﴿O you who have believed, do not invalidate your charities with reminders and harm, like one who spends his wealth to be seen by people and does not believe in Allah and the Last Day. His example is like a smooth rock upon which is dust, and then a heavy rain strikes it and leaves it bare. They have no power over anything of what they have earned﴾ = (Would one of you like to have a garden of palm trees and grapevines, with rivers flowing beneath it, having in it of all fruits, and old age has overtaken him) ... the verse. [[Abu Ja'far means: this verse is linked back to the previous verse that he cited.]]

* *

The meaning of His saying: ﴿Would one of you like﴾: would one of you love, [[See the explanation of *wadda* in what has passed, 2: 470.]] ﴿to have a garden﴾, meaning an orchard [[See the explanation of *janna* earlier, just above: 535, note 1, and its references.]], ﴿of palm trees and grapevines, with rivers flowing beneath it﴾, meaning: beneath the garden, ﴿having in it of all fruits﴾. The pronoun in His saying ﴿lahu﴾ ("his") refers back to "one of you," and the pronoun and the feminine ending in ﴿fīhā﴾ ("in it") refer to the garden. ﴿And old age has overtaken him﴾, meaning: and old age has overtaken one of you, ﴿while he has weak offspring﴾.

* *

The reason that Allah, may His praise be exalted, made the orchard of palm trees and grapevines, which He, may His praise be exalted, spoke of to His believing servants ("Would one of you like to have...") = a parable for the expenditure of the hypocrite that he spends to be seen by people, not seeking the good pleasure of Allah. People, by what appears to them of his charity, his giving to whoever is given to, and his outward deeds, praise him and commend him for that deed during his life. [[Footnote: I placed this number at all these points so as to show the structure of this compound sentence. This is its structure, and between these are successive sections: "And Allah made the orchard ... a parable for the expenditure of the hypocrite ... in its goodness like the goodness of the orchard, which is the garden ... of palm trees and grapevines ..."]] In its goodness, like the goodness of the orchard, which is the garden that Allah, mighty and majestic, struck as a parable for his deed, of palm trees and grapevines, having in it of all fruits. This is because that deed which he does outwardly in this world has in it every good of the immediate world, by which he protects himself, his blood, his wealth, and his offspring, and by it he gains praise and a good reputation among people, and takes his share of the spoils, along with many other things that are too numerous to count. So he has in that, from every good in this world, just as Allah, may His praise be exalted, described the garden that He struck as a parable for his deed, that in it is of all fruits. [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "bi-'amalihi" (with his deed), but the correct reading is what I have given; the sentence's construction is: "as He, may His praise be exalted, described the garden ... that in it is of all fruits."]]

* *

Then He, may His praise be exalted, said: ﴿And old age has overtaken him while he has weak offspring﴾, meaning that the owner of the garden has been overtaken by old age, ﴿while he has weak offspring﴾, young children. ﴿Then it is struck﴾, meaning: then the garden is struck, ﴿by a whirlwind containing fire, so it is burned﴾. He means by this that the garden was burned by the wind in which there was fire, at a time when he was in need of it and dependent on its fruit because of his old age and his weakness in tending it, and at a time when his children were young and unable to restore it and maintain it. So he was left with nothing, at the time he most needed his garden and its fruit, because of the calamity that befell it from the whirlwind containing fire.

He says: Likewise, the one who spends his wealth to be seen by people, Allah extinguishes his light, removes the splendor of his deed, and nullifies his reward until he meets Him. He returns to it at a time when he is most in need of his deed, when there is no opportunity to make amends (*mustaʿtab*) [[*Lā mustaʿtab*: meaning no retraction, no making up, and no seeking of pleasure from Allah, mighty and majestic. From the expression "*istaʿtabtu fulānan*," meaning I asked him to make amends for what I had done, and sought his pleasure, and returned from wronging him.]], nor any pardon for his sins, nor repentance, and his deed is ruined, just as the garden whose description Allah, may His praise be exalted, has given is burned when its owner is old and his offspring are young, when he is most in need of it, so its benefits are lost to him.

* *

This parable that Allah struck for those who spend their wealth to be seen by people in this verse is a parallel to the other parable that He struck for them with His saying: ﴿His example is like a smooth rock with dust upon it, and then a heavy rain strikes it and leaves it bare. They have no power over anything of what they have earned﴾.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The people of interpretation have disputed the interpretation of this verse. However, although their statements differ in their expressions, their meanings return to the meaning we have stated. The best of them in clarifying its meaning and the closest to correctness in their view is al-Suddi.

3091 - Musa narrated to me, saying: Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding: ﴿Would one of you like to have a garden of palm trees and grapevines, with rivers flowing beneath it, having in it of all fruits, and old age has overtaken him, and he has weak offspring, and then it is struck by a whirlwind containing fire, so it is burned﴾. This is another parable for the expenditure of showing off. He spends his wealth showing off to people with it, so his wealth goes away from him while he is showing off, and Allah does not reward him for it. Then, when the Day of Resurrection comes and he needs his expenditure, he finds that it has been burned up by showing off, and gone, just as this man spent on his garden, until when it grew and his dependents multiplied and he needed his garden, a wind came in which there was a scorching heat (*samum*) and burned his garden, and he found nothing of it. [[In the manuscript: "rīḥ fīhā samra" (a wind in which there was samra). The final *h* is joined to the *r*, and I have found no sense for it. What is in the printed edition is what is in al-Durr al-Manthur, 1: 340, and in the other transmitted reports.]] So likewise is the one who spends to show off.

3092 - Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, from Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the saying of Allah, mighty and majestic: ﴿Would one of you like to have a garden of palm trees and grapevines﴾, like one who neglects obedience to Allah until he dies. He said: He says: Would one of you like to have a worldly life in which he does not act in obedience to Allah, like this man who has gardens with rivers flowing beneath them, ﴿having in it of all fruits, and old age has overtaken him, and he has weak offspring, then it is struck by a whirlwind containing fire, so it is burned﴾? So his state after death is like this, when his garden was burned while he was old, and it did not avail him anything, and his children were young and could not avail him anything. Likewise, the one who neglects (obedience) after death, everything is a regret for him.

3093 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

3094 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Abd al-Malik, from Ata', who said: Umar asked the people about this verse, and found no one who satisfied him, until Ibn Abbas, who was behind him, said: O Commander of the Faithful, I find something in myself regarding it. He said: So he turned to him and said: Move over here. Why do you belittle yourself? He said: This is a parable that Allah, mighty and majestic, struck, saying: Would one of you love to spend his life in the deeds of the people of good and the people of happiness, until, when he is most in need of concluding it with good, when his life has run out and his term has drawn near, he concludes it with a deed of the people of wretchedness, which ruins it all and burns it when he is most in need of it.

3095 - Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Sulaym, from Ibn Abi Mulaykah: that Umar recited this verse: "Would one of you like to have a garden of palm trees and grapevines?" He said: This is a parable struck for a human being: he does a righteous deed, until, when he is near the end of his life, when he is most in need of it, he does a deed of evil. [[Report 3095: "Muhammad ibn Sulaym al-Makki Abu 'Uthman." He related from Ibn Abi Mulaykah. The Hafiz Ibn Hajar said: "I have not seen any narration from him other than from him." Waki' ibn al-Jarrah, Abd Allah ibn Dawud al-Khuraybi, and Abu 'Asim al-Nabil related from him. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib. This report was pointed to in al-Fath 8: 151 in his discussion of report 3096.]]

3096 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Suwayd narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: I heard Abu Bakr ibn Abi Mulaykah report from Ubayd ibn Umayr that he heard him say: Umar asked the companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, saying: What do you think this was revealed about: "Would one of you like to have a garden of palm trees and grapevines?" They said: Allah knows best. Umar became angry and said: Say "we know" or "we do not know." Ibn Abbas said: I have something in myself about it, O Commander of the Faithful. Umar said: Speak, my nephew, and do not belittle yourself! Ibn Abbas said: I struck a parable for a deed. Umar said: What deed? He said: For a deed. Umar said: A man who is rich, who does good deeds, then Allah sends Satan to him, and he acts in acts of disobedience until he drowns all his deeds. He said: I also heard Abd Allah ibn Abi Mulaykah narrate something similar to this from Ibn Abbas, heard from him. [[Report 3096: al-Bukhari narrated it through Hisham ibn Yusuf, from Ibn Jurayj. The Hafiz pointed in al-Fath 8: 151 to al-Tabari's narration through Ibn al-Mubarak, from Ibn Jurayj. In the printed edition it read "rahala 'anni" with an unpointed letter, and the correct reading is what I have given from the sources. See the following note.]]

3097 - Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: I heard Abu Bakr ibn Abi Mulaykah report that he heard Ubayd ibn Umayr = Ibn Jurayj said: And I heard Abd Allah ibn Abi Mulaykah say: I heard Ibn Abbas = both of them together said: Umar ibn al-Khattab asked the companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he mentioned something similar, except that he said of Umar: "To the man who does good deeds, then Satan is sent to him, and he acts in acts of disobedience." [[Report 3097: al-Hakim narrated it in al-Mustadrak 2: 283, and al-Hafiz pointed to it in al-Fath 8: 151, and it is a repetition of the previous one. Al-Hakim graded it with the words "This is a sound hadith according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim), though they did not include it," and al-Dhahabi agreed with him.]]

3098 - Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: I asked Ata' about it = then Ibn Jurayj said: Abd Allah ibn Kathir also informed me, from Mujahid = both said: It is a parable struck for deeds. Ibn Jurayj said: Ibn Abbas said: It is a parable struck for deeds. A person begins by doing a righteous deed, which becomes a parable for the garden of palm trees and grapevines, with rivers flowing beneath it, having in it of all fruits. Then he does evil at the end of his life, and persists in the evil until he dies upon it. So the whirlwind containing the fire that burned the garden is a parable for his evil by which he died. Ibn Abbas said: The garden is his livelihood and the livelihood of his children, and it burned, so he could not defend his garden because of his old age, and his offspring could not defend their garden because of their youth, until it burned.

He says: This is his parable: he meets Me when he is most in need of Me, and he finds nothing with Me, and cannot defend himself from the punishment of Allah in any way. He cannot, with his old age and his children's youth, make a garden. [[In the manuscript: "min kibarihi wa-saghirihi an ya'malū jannatahu" (from his old age and his youth that they make his garden), and what is in the printed edition is closer to correct.]] Likewise, there is no repentance when the deed has ended upon death. = Ibn Jurayj said, from Mujahid: I heard Ibn Abbas say: It is a parable for the one who neglects obedience to Allah until he dies. = Ibn Jurayj said: Mujahid said: Would one of you like to have a worldly life in which he does not act in obedience to Allah, like this one who has a garden? His state after death is like this, when his garden was burned while he was old and did not avail him anything, and his children were young and did not avail him anything. Likewise, the one who neglects, after death, everything is a regret for him. [[In the printed edition: "when his garden was burned"; I have kept what is in the manuscript.]]

٦٠٩٩ - Hadith narrated to us by Bishr, who said: Yazid narrated to us, who said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: "Would any of you like to have a garden of palm trees and grapevines, beneath which rivers flow..." to the end of the verse. He said: a wind with intense scorching heat (samum) struck it. [[In the printed edition: "samum shadid" (intense scorching heat). "Al-samum" is masculine, but it may be feminine when it refers to a hot wind.]] "Thus does Allah make the signs clear to you, that perhaps you may reflect" — so this is a parable, so understand Allah's parables, may He be Majestic and Exalted, for He said: ﴿And these are the parables We set forth for mankind, but none understands them except those of knowledge﴾ [Surah al-Ankabut: 43]. This is a man whose age has grown great, whose bones have grown weak, and whose dependents have increased, [[In the manuscript and printed edition: "daqqa 'azmuhu" (his bones became fine/thin), but the correct reading is with the letter ra': "raqqa 'azmuhu" (his bones became weak). In the hadith of Uthman: "kabirat sini, wa raqqa 'azmi" (my years have grown great, and my bones have grown weak). The phrase "raqqa 'azm fulan" means he grew old and weak. Al-ruqq (with two fathas) is the weakness of bones. A poet said of his she-camel: "Khattarah ba'da ghibbi al-jahdi najiyah... lam talqa fi 'azmiha wahnan wa la ruqqa"]] then his garden was burned up in what remained of it, at a time when he most needed it. He says: Would any of you like his deeds to be lost on the Day of Resurrection when he most needs them?

٦١٠٠ - Hadith narrated to us by al-Hasan ibn Yahya, who said: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, who said: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah regarding His words: "Would any of you like to have a garden..." up to His words: "...and it was burned," he said: its garden was destroyed when he most needed it, when his age had grown great and he was weak in earning, "and he has weak offspring" who cannot benefit him. He said: al-Hasan used to say: "fa-ihtaraqat" (and it was burned) meaning it was destroyed when he most needed it. That is the meaning of His words: Would any of you like his deeds to be lost when he most needs them?

٦١٠١ - Hadith narrated to me by Muhammad ibn Sa'd, who said: my father narrated to me, who said: my paternal uncle narrated to me, who said: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas: Allah struck a good parable, and all His parables are good, blessed and exalted is He. He said: "Would any of you like to have a garden of palm trees..." up to His words: "...of all kinds of fruits," he said: he planted it in his youth, then old age overtook him while he had weak offspring at the end of his life. Then a whirlwind containing fire came to it and his garden was burned. He had no strength to plant the like of it, and his offspring had no good to return to him. Likewise the disbeliever on the Day of Resurrection, when he is returned to Allah, has no good by which he may seek to be restored, [[Between the words in the manuscript there was a blank space, as follows: "dhurriyyah du'afa'a 'umrihi fa-ja'ahu i'sar fihi nar fa-ihtaraqat 'indahu quwwah inna nasilahu khayr ya'udun al-kafir yawm al-qiyamah idha rudda ila khayr fa-yasta'tabu", which together with the blank is a confused text. I have adopted what is in the printed edition, which is the text of the report as recorded by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur 1:340, attributing it to Ibn Jarir and Abu Hatim. Also Ibn Kathir in his Tafsir 2:38, 39.]] just as he has no strength to plant a garden like his, [[In the manuscript and printed edition: "kama laysa lahu quwwah" (as he has no strength). The correct reading, from al-Durr al-Manthur and Ibn Kathir, is as given.]] and he does not find any good he sent ahead for himself that may return to him, just as his child did not avail him, and his reward is withheld at the time he is most in need of it, just as this man was deprived of his garden when he was most in need of it in his old age and the weakness of his offspring. This is a parable which Allah struck for the believer and the disbeliever regarding what each was given in this world: how He saves the believer in the Hereafter and stores up for him honour and bliss, and withholds wealth from him in this world, and extends to the disbeliever in this world wealth that is temporary, and stores up for him evil that will never leave him, and he will abide therein humiliated, because he [boasted over his companion] and trusted in what he had, [[The words in the brackets are what is established in the printed edition; in the manuscript there was a blank: "min akl annahu wa-thiqa bima 'indahu". I did not find the rest of the report in the earlier sources cited, so I left what the printed edition's editor inferred as it stands. Had I inferred, I would have said: "min ajl annahu kafara bi-liqa' rabbihi" (because he denied the meeting with his Lord), and Allah knows best.]] and did not feel certain that he would meet his Lord. [[The report: 6101 - in al-Durr al-Manthur 1:340, and Ibn Kathir 2:38, 39, as previously mentioned.]]

٦١٠٢ - Hadith transmitted to me from 'Ammar, who said: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi': "Would any of you like to have a garden..." the verse, he said: [This is a parable which Allah struck]: Would any of you like to have a garden of palm trees and grapevines [in which there is for him every kind of fruit], and the man [has grown old and weak], and he has young children [whom Allah tested] in their garden, [[What I placed between the brackets is what the editor of the printed edition inferred, I believe, and in the manuscript there was a blank.]] so Allah sent upon it a whirlwind containing fire and it was burned, [[In the manuscript: "fa-ba'atha Allah 'anha i'sar fihi nar" (Allah sent against it), which is a distortion and error; the printed edition is closer to correct.]] and the man could not, due to old age, defend his garden, nor could his children, due to their young age, so his garden was destroyed when he most needed it. He says: Would any of you like to live in error and sins until death comes to him, and then he comes on the Day of Resurrection with his deeds lost to him when he most needs them? Then he will say: Son of Adam, you came to Me at the time you most needed good, so where is what you sent ahead for yourself? [[In the manuscript: "min al-kufr" (from disbelief), which is a clear error.]]

٦١٠٣ - Hadith narrated to me by Yunus, who said: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd said, and he recited the words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: "O you who believe, do not nullify your charities with reminders and injury," then he struck a parable for that, saying: "Would any of you like to have a garden of palm trees and grapevines," until His words: "...so a whirlwind containing fire struck it and it was burned." He said: its rivers flowed and its fruits, and he had weak offspring, and a whirlwind containing fire struck it and it was burned. Would any of you like this? Just as one of you takes pride when he gives out his charity and expenditure, [[In the printed edition: "fa-ma yahmil" and in the manuscript "kama yahmil", then in both: "an yakhruj", which is meaningless. I have adopted the reading "yatajammal" (takes pride) because one who spends his wealth to be seen by people is only adorning himself before them with that. This is the correct meaning of the report's context. The manuscript, as shown by the previous notes, is thoroughly corrupt due to the editor's unclear handwriting, haste, or inability to read the copy from which he copied.]] until, when he has a garden with me, and its rivers flow and its fruits, and it is for his children and his children's children, a whirlwind of fire strikes it and burns it.

٦١٠٤ - Hadith narrated to me by al-Muthanna, who said: Ishaq narrated to us, who said: Zuhayr narrated to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak regarding His words: "Would any of you like to have a garden of palm trees and grapevines beneath which rivers flow," a man planted a garden containing every kind of fruit, then old age overtook him, and he had weak offspring, then a whirlwind containing fire struck it and it was burned, so he cannot defend his garden due to his old age, and his offspring could not defend his garden, so his livelihood and the livelihood of his offspring were lost. This is a parable which Allah struck for the disbeliever. He says: he will meet Me on the Day of Resurrection, while he is most in need of some good to reach him, but he will not find any good with Me for him, and he will not be able to defend himself from the punishment of Allah in any way.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: We have shown that the most correct interpretation of this is what we have mentioned, because Allah, may His praise be exalted, had previously commanded His believing servants to avoid reminders and injury in their charities, then He struck a parable for the one who reminded and injured the one to whom he gave charity, likening him to the hypocrites who show off, who spend their wealth to be seen by people. The story of this verse and what precedes it of the parable is similar to the parable He struck for them before it, so attaching it to its counterpart is more fitting than interpreting it as a parable that has no mention before it or with it. [[See what al-Qurtubi said in his Tafsir 3:318, in rejecting the choice of Ibn Jarir in his tafsir. The method of Ibn Jarir is more trustworthy and precise in explanation and in argumentation.]]

* *

If someone says to us: How is it said "and old age overtook him," which is a past verb, and it is conjoined to His words "Would any of you like"?
It is said: That is so, because His words "would" (yawaddu) may have "law" (if) placed in it instead of "an" (that); since "law" and "an" are both suitable, and their meaning both is future, the Arabs allowed the past verb to be placed, with the sense of "law," in the form of "yafʿalu" with "an." [[That is: that the past verb may be put, with the sense of "law," in the form of the present verb with "an."]] Therefore He said "fa-asabaha" (and it struck it), and it in his view stands in the position of "law," since it resembles "an" in meaning of conditional, so it is placed in its positions, and "an" is answered with the answer of "law" and "law" with the answer of "an." So it is as if it were said: Would any of you like that if he had a garden of palm trees and grapevines, beneath which rivers flow, in which there is for him every kind of fruit, and old age overtook him? [[This is the text of al-Farra's statement in Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1:175, and it fully covered the topic there. See also what preceded regarding the answer of "law" with a past verb, 2:458 / 3:184, 185, and the commentary there.]]

If he says: How is it said here "and he has weak offspring," while in [al-Nisa': 9] He says: ﴿And let those fear who, if they left behind them weak offspring, would be anxious for them﴾?
It is said: Because "fa'il" is pluralized as "fu'ala'" and "fi'al," so one says: "rajul zarif, min qawm zurafa' and zuraf" (a witty man, from a people of wits).

* *

As for "al-i'sar" (the whirlwind), it is the violent wind that blows from the earth to the sky like a pillar; its plural is "a'asir." From it is the saying of Yazid ibn Mufarrigh al-Himyari:
"Unasun ajarunā fa-kāna jiwāruhum... a'āṣīra min fasw al-'Irāq al-mubadhdhari"
[[Tarikh al-Tabari 6:178, and al-Aghani 17:178. It will come in the tafsir (15:53) with a different reading as well: "min fisq al-'Iraq al-mubadhdhar." In the printed edition and manuscript here the line appears as "min su' al-'Iraq al-mundhar," which is meaningless. However, I saw a commentator explain it on that basis, and I swear to God it nearly killed me with laughter! This is one of three verses Ibn Mufarrigh said concerning his story with Ibn Ziyad, when he satirized him and satirized Mu'awiya ibn Abi Sufyan (see what preceded 4:293 and footnote 2). He left 'Ibad heading to Basra, and went around its notables from Quraysh, begging them, but they only made promises. Then he came to al-Mundhir ibn al-Jarud (from 'Abd al-Qays), who gave him protection and admitted him to his house, and informers reported to 'Ubayd Allah ibn Ziyad that he was in al-Mundhir's house.
