Al-Mundhir was in the assembly of 'Ubayd Allah, and did not notice until Ibn Mufarrigh was set up at his head. Al-Mundhir stood and said: O Amir, I have given him protection! He said: O Mundhir, by God, he praises you and your father, and satirizes me and my father, and then you give him protection! He ordered him to be given medicine and carried on a donkey to be paraded, while he soiled his clothes from the effect of the medicine. Then he said to 'Ubayd Allah ibn Ziyad: "The water washes what you have done, but my words remain firmly in your bones, urinating..." Then he satirized al-Mundhir ibn al-Jarud, saying: "I left Quraysh, not to live as neighbour among them, and I lived as neighbour to 'Abd al-Qays, the people of al-Mushaqqar. Men gave me protection, and their protection was: a'asir of the farting of al-'Iraq, scattered..." "My neighbour became from Jadhima sleeping, and none protects neighbours except the one who is alert..." As for his saying "min fasw al-'Iraq": 'Abd al-Qays, Banu Hanifa and others from the people of Bahrain and its neighbourhood were taunted for flatulence, because their land was palm land, so they ate dates, and it caused wind and rumbling in their bellies. "Al-mubadhdhar" is from tabdhir, which is extravagance with wealth and scattering it. This is a quality which Ibn Mufarrigh borrowed most skilfully in this context, so his satire against al-Mundhir ibn al-Jarud became as biting as possible, along with the beauty of his phrase "a'asir"!!
After that al-Akhtal came and satirized his son Malik ibn al-Mundhir ibn al-Jarud also, saying to him: "And 'Abd al-Qays, its beards dyed yellow, as if its farts were pieces of fog!!"
So it reached him what it reached!! See Tabaqat Fuhul al-Shu'ara' 298, 299, and the commentary there.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of His words: "a whirlwind containing fire, so it was burned."
Some of them said: The meaning is: a wind in which is intense scorching heat.
Those who said that:
٦١٠٥ - Hadith narrated to me by Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Bazi', who said: Yusuf ibn Khalid al-Samti narrated to us, who said: Nafi' ibn Malik narrated to us, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His words: "a whirlwind containing fire": a wind in which is intense scorching heat.
٦١٠٦ - Hadith narrated to us by Abu Kurayb, who said: Ibn 'Atiyyah narrated to us, who said: Isra'il narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Tamimi, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding "a whirlwind containing fire," he said: the scorching samum from which the jinn were created, which burns.
٦١٠٧ - Hadith narrated to us by Ahmad [[In the printed edition and manuscript: "Hadathana Humayd"; the correct reading is "Ahmad," meaning Ahmad ibn Ishaq al-Ahwazi, as occurs hundreds of times in his narrations from Abu Ahmad al-Zubayri. Look him up in the indexes, and see the following report No. 6109.]] who said: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, who said: Sharik narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Tamimi, from Ibn 'Abbas: "So a whirlwind containing fire struck it and it was burned," he said: it is the scorching samum which does not leave anyone alive. [[In the printed edition the phrase "lā tubqī aḥadan" (which does not leave anyone alive) is omitted, and the editor noted that in some copies there is an addition: "allati la tadurr ahadan" (which does not harm anyone). This is in the manuscript too, but the copyist corrupted the word; its correct form is as I have given: "la tubqa ahadan." It will come in the report of al-Tamimi from Ibas, the next report: "allati taqtulu" (which kills). This is that.]]
٦١٠٨ - Hadith narrated to us by al-Muthanna, who said: al-Hammani narrated to us, who said: Sharik narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Tamimi, from Ibn 'Abbas: "a whirlwind containing fire, so it was burned," which kills.
٦١٠٩ - Hadith narrated to us by Ahmad ibn Ishaq, who said: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, who said: Isra'il narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from someone he mentioned, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The samum from which the jinn were created is one part of seventy parts of the fire.
٦١١٠ - Hadith narrated to me by Muhammad ibn Sa'd, who said: my father narrated to me, who said: my paternal uncle narrated to me, who said: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas: "a whirlwind containing fire, so it was burned," it is a wind in which is intense samum.
٦١١١ - Hadith narrated to us by al-Qasim, who said: al-Husayn narrated to us, who said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn 'Abbas said: "a whirlwind containing fire," he said: intense samum.
٦١١٢ - Hadith narrated to us by Bishr, who said: Yazid narrated to us, who said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: "a whirlwind containing fire," meaning: a wind in which is intense samum struck it.
٦١١٣ - Hadith narrated to us by al-Hasan ibn Yahya, who said: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, who said: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, similarly.
٦١١٤ - Hadith narrated to me by Musa, who said: 'Amr narrated to us, who said: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "a whirlwind containing fire, so it was burned": as for the i'sar, it is the wind, and as for the fire, it is the samum.
٦١١٥ - Hadith transmitted to me from 'Ammar, who said: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi': "a whirlwind containing fire," meaning: a wind in which is intense samum.

* *

Others said: It is a wind in which is intense cold.
Those who said that:
٦١١٦ - Hadith narrated to us by al-Hasan ibn Yahya, who said: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, who said: Ma'mar informed us, who said: al-Hasan used to say regarding His words: "a whirlwind containing fire, so it was burned": in it is frost and cold. [[Al-sirr (with a kasra on the sad): the cold that strikes plants and burns them.]]
٦١١٧ - Hadith narrated to me by al-Muthanna, who said: Ishaq narrated to us, who said: Abu Zuhayr narrated to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak: "a whirlwind containing fire, so it was burned," meaning by the i'sar: a wind in which is cold.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 266:

The explanation of His saying: ﴿Thus Allah makes clear to you the signs, that you may reflect﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His praise be exalted, He means: Just as your Lord, blessed and exalted, has made clear to you the matter of spending in His cause, how it is to be done, and what is permissible for you and what is not permissible for you to do with it, so too does He make clear to you the other signs besides that, informing you of their rulings, what is lawful and what is unlawful in them, and clarifying for you their proofs, as a favour from Him to you. ﴿That you may reflect﴾ means: that you may reflect with your minds, so that you may ponder and take heed from the proofs of Allah concerning them, and act upon what they contain of their rulings, and thereby obey Allah.

* *

And those who gave interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) said the same as what we have said concerning this.

Mention of those who said that:

6118 - Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: al-Thawri informed us, saying: Mujahid said: ﴿That you may reflect﴾ — he said: "That you may obey."

6119 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿Thus Allah makes clear to you the signs, that you may reflect﴾ — he meant: concerning the passing away of this world and its ending, and the approach of the Hereafter and its permanence.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 267 (part 1 of 2):

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿O you who have believed, spend﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His saying, "O you who have believed," He, mighty is His praise, means: those who have affirmed belief in Allah, His Messenger, and the verses of His Book.
* *
By His saying, "spend" (anfiqu), He means: give zakat and give charity, as related:
6120 - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: 'Abdullah related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: "Spend of the good things you have earned," he said: "Give charity."
* *
The interpretation of His saying: ﴿of the good things you have earned﴾

He, mighty is His praise, means by this: give zakat from the good of what you have earned through your own dealings, whether through trade or through craft, [of] gold and silver.
And by "the good things" (al-tayyibat) He means the choice ones. He says: Give zakat from your wealth which you have acquired lawfully, and give in your zakat gold and silver, choosing the best of it and not the inferior, as related:
6121 - Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far related to us, from Shu'bah, from al-Hakam, from Mujahid regarding this verse: "O you who have believed, spend of the good things you have earned," he said: "From trade."
6122 - Musa ibn 'Abd al-Rahman related to me, saying: Zayd ibn al-Hubab related to us, saying: And Shu'bah informed me, from al-Hakam, from Mujahid, the like of it.
6123 - Hatim ibn Bakr al-Dabbi related to me, saying: Wahb related to us, from Shu'bah, from al-Hakam, from Jahid, the like of it.
6124 - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Adam related to us, saying: Shu'bah related to us, from al-Hakam, from Mujahid regarding His saying: "Spend of the good things you have earned," he said: "Lawful trade."
6125 - Muhammad ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from 'Abdullah ibn Ma'qil: "Spend of the good things you have earned," he said: "There is nothing bad in the wealth of the believer, but do not intend the bad part of it to spend."
6126 - 'Isam ibn Rawwad ibn al-Jarrah related to me, saying: My father related to us, saying: Abu Bakr al-Hudhali related to us, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, from 'Ubaydah, who said: I asked 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah's blessings be upon him, about His saying: "O you who have believed, spend of the good things you have earned," and he said: "Of gold and silver."
6127 - Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, from 'Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding His saying: "of the good things you have earned," he said: "Trade."
6128 - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah related to us, saying: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.
6129 - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: 'Abdullah ibn Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying: "Spend of the good things you have earned," he said: "From the best of your wealth and the finest of it." [[The report: 6129 - in al-Durr al-Manthur 1: 346; the report will come in full at no. 6152. His saying, "min atyab amwalikum wa anfasihi" (the best of your wealth and its finest), is grammatically sound: the singular pronoun returns to the plural in the elative form "afʿal", and what we said about this in the commentary on report 5968 has already passed, though the two wordings differ and diverge. See Hamʿ al-Hawami 1: 59.]]
6130 - Musa related to me, saying: 'Amr related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi: "O you who have believed, spend of the good things you have earned," he said: "Of this gold and silver." [[In the printed edition: "hadhā" (this) is omitted for no reason.]]
* *
The interpretation of His, mighty and majestic, saying: ﴿and of what We have brought forth for you from the earth﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, mighty is His praise, means by this: "And spend also of what We have brought forth for you from the earth, giving charity and zakat from palm trees, vineyards, wheat and barley, and whatever plant of the earth upon which zakat is obligatory." As related:
6131 - 'Isam ibn Rawwad related to me, saying: My father related to me, saying: Abu Bakr al-Hudhali related to us, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, from 'Ubaydah, who said: I asked 'Ali, may Allah's blessings be upon him, about the saying of Allah, mighty and majestic: "and of what We have brought forth for you from the earth," and he said: "That is, of grain and fruit, and everything upon which there is zakat."
6132 - Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, from 'Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding His saying: "and of what We have brought forth for you from the earth," he said: "The palm tree."
6133 - Al-Qasim related to us, saying: Al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid: "and of what We have brought forth for you from the earth," he said: "From the fruit of the palm tree."
6134 - Al-Qasim related to us, saying: Al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hushaym related to us, saying: Shu'bah related to us, from al-Hakam, from Mujahid regarding His saying: "O you who have believed, spend of the good things you have earned," he said: "From trade." "And of what We have brought forth for you from the earth," from the fruits.
6135 - Musa related to me, saying: 'Amr related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi: "and of what We have brought forth for you from the earth," he said: "This is about dates and grain."
* *
The interpretation of His, mighty and majestic, saying: ﴿and do not aim at the bad﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His saying, mighty is His praise, "and do not aim at the bad," He means: do not intend, and do not purpose.
* *
It has been mentioned that in the recitation of 'Abdullah it is: ﴿wa la tu'ammu﴾ from "ammama" [[In the printed edition: "wa la ta'ammamu", as in al-Qurtubi; but Abu Hayyan in his tafsir 1: 328 states explicitly that al-Tabari related the recitation of 'Abdullah as "wa la ta'ammalu" from "amimtu", which agrees with the manuscript, so I have recorded it so, and it is correct, God willing.]] and this is from "yammamtu" [[In the manuscript and printed edition: "tayammamtu", which is faulty; the correct form is as recorded. "Amma al-makan" and "yammahu" have the same meaning, and it is a substitution, the hamza being replaced by yā'; for this reason it appears under the root (a-m-m) in the lexicons other than al-Jawhari.]], and the meaning is one, though the wordings differ.
* *
It is said: "ta'ammamtu fulanan," "tayammamtuhu," and "ammatuhu," meaning: I aimed at him and intended him, as Maymun ibn Qays al-A'sha said:

I aimed at Qays, and between me and him lay the land of a desolate wasteland, rugged of terrain.

And as related:
6136 - Musa related to us, saying: 'Amr related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi: "wa la tayammamu al-khabitha," meaning: do not intend.
6137 - Al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah: "wa la tayammamu," meaning: do not intend.
6138 - It was related to me from 'Ammar, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far related to us, from his father, from Qatadah, the like of it.
* *
The interpretation of His saying: ﴿and do not aim at the bad of it, which you spend﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, mighty is His praise, means by "the bad" (al-khabith): the inferior, not the good. He says: Do not intend the inferior of your wealth in your charities so that you give from it, but give from the good and the choice.
* *
That is because this verse was revealed concerning a man of the Ansar who hung a cluster (qinw) of dried-up dates (hashaf) [[The qinw is the kabasah, the full date-cluster with its stalks and its ripe dates; it is in dates what a bunch is in grapes, and its plural is aqna'. The hashaf is the date that has not ripened; when it dries it becomes hard and spoiled, with no taste, no pulp, and no sweetness.]] in the place where the Muslims would hang the charity of their fruit, as charity from his dates.
Mention of those who said that:
6139 - Al-Husayn ibn 'Amr ibn Muhammad al-'Anqazi related to me, saying: My father related to us, from Asbat, from al-Suddi, from 'Adi ibn Thabit, from al-Bara' ibn 'Azib regarding the saying of Allah, mighty and majestic: "O you who have believed, spend of the good things you have earned and of what We have brought forth for you from the earth," to His saying: "and Allah is Self-Sufficient, Praiseworthy," he said: It was revealed concerning the Ansar. When the time of the palm harvest came, the Ansar would bring out from their orchards clusters of unripe dates (busr), and hang them on a rope between the two pillars in the mosque of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the poor emigrants would eat from them. So a man among them would deliberately take dried-up dates and put them in with the clusters of unripe dates, thinking that this was permissible.
So Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed concerning those who did that: "and do not aim at the bad of it, which you spend," He said: do not aim at the dried-up dates of it, which you spend. [[The report: 6139 - al-Husayn ibn 'Amr ibn Muhammad al-'Anqazi, mentioned at no. 1625 (1883); he is weak, and they have spoken about him. His father, 'Amr ibn Muhammad, is trustworthy and acceptable in narration. Al-Hakim recorded it in al-Mustadrak 2: 285 by way of 'Amr ibn Talhah al-Qannad, from Asbat ibn Nasr, and said: "This is a strange, sound hadith by the conditions of Muslim, though they did not record it," and al-Dhahabi agreed. Ibn Kathir mentioned it in his tafsir 2: 40, 41 and attributed it to al-Hakim, saying that he said: "sound by the conditions of al-Bukhari and Muslim, though they did not record it," so the wording of al-Hakim's statement differs. Its full text will come at nos. 6159 and 6167.
His saying: "jadhadh al-nakhl" with a dhal here and in al-Mustadrak. Jadhdh al-nakhl (jadhdh) means cutting it. The more well-known form is with the unmarked dal: "jadda al-nakhl yajiduhu jaddan," meaning to cut it and pick its fruit. Al-hawa'it is the plural of hā'iṭ, the walled orchard of palms; if it has no wall, it is a dāḥiyah.
His saying: "aqna' al-busr": al-aqna' is the plural of qinw, which has passed in the previous note. Al-busr is the date before it ripens; it is so named for its freshness, its singular is busrah, and after busr it becomes rutab, then tamr.]] .
6140 - Musa related to me, saying: 'Amr related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, claimed al-Suddi, from 'Adi ibn Thabit, from al-Bara' ibn 'Azib, similarly, except that he said: "So some of them would deliberately put the cluster of dried dates" [in the great quantity of clusters placed there], "and they thought it was permissible for them" [to do so]. So concerning those who did this, He revealed: "and do not aim at the bad of it, which you spend," the cluster that has become dried, and if it were given to you as a gift, you would not accept it. [[The report: 6140 - this is a second chain for the earlier report, and its full text will come at no. 6160. Hashaf al-tamr means it became dried. Its explanation has passed in the note on p. 559, no. 1. His saying: "jā'iz 'anhu," meaning permissible and sufficient on his behalf, from the expression "jāza jawāzan," and "ajāza lahu al-shay'" and "jawwazahu": when he validated for him what he had done and approved it. This is a rare usage that the lexicons did not record, but it is genuine old Arabic.]] .
6141 - Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Mu'ammal related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from al-Suddi, from Abu Malik, from al-Bara' ibn 'Azib, who said: They used to come with the worst of their dates and the worst of their food for charity, so there was revealed: "O you who have believed, spend of the good things you have earned," to the end of the verse. [[The report: 6141 - al-Bayhaqi related it in al-Sunan 4: 136 by way of Abu Hudhayfah, from Sufyan, from al-Suddi, with a different wording and fuller than this.]] .
6142 - 'Isam ibn Rawwad related to me, saying: My father related to us, saying: Abu Bakr al-Hudhali related to us, from Ibn Sirin, from 'Ubaydah al-Salmani, who said: I asked 'Ali about the saying of Allah: "O you who have believed, spend of the good things you have earned and of what We have brought forth for you from the earth, and do not aim at the bad of it, which you spend," and 'Ali said: This verse was revealed concerning the obligatory zakat. A man would aim at the dates, cut them [[Sarm al-nakhl and al-shajar: yasrimuhu sarman and sirāman, meaning he cut its fruit and gathered it, like al-jidhadh and al-jiddād mentioned in the notes at p. 560.]] and set aside the good ones to one side. When the zakat collector came, he would give him from the inferior, and Allah, mighty and majestic, said: "and do not aim at the bad of it, which you spend."
6143 - Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: 'Abd al-Jalil ibn Humayd al-Yahsubi related to me, that Ibn Shihab related to him, saying: Abu Umamah ibn Sahl ibn Hunayf related to me concerning the verse in which Allah, mighty and majestic, said: "and do not aim at the bad of it, which you spend," he said: It is al-ja'rur and lawn Habiq, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade that it be taken in charity. [[The report: 6143 - 'Abd al-Jalil ibn Humayd al-Yahsubi, Abu Malik al-Misri. He related from al-Zuhri, Yahya ibn Sa'id, and Ayyub al-Sakhtiyani; Ibn 'Ajlan, who was among his contemporaries, related from him, as did Musa ibn Salamah, Ibn Wahb, and other Egyptians. al-Nasa'i said: "There is no harm in him," and Ibn Hibban mentioned him among the trustworthy. He died in 148 AH; he is biographed in al-Tahdhib. This report was related by al-Nasa'i from Yunus ibn 'Abd al-A'la and al-Harith ibn Miskin, from Ibn Wahb, from 'Abd al-Jalil ibn Humayd, in al-Sunan 5: 43, and its end: "...that the charity of the vile be taken." It was related by other routes in Sunan Abi Dawud 2: 149 no. 1607, and al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak 2: 284 by way of Sufyan ibn Husayn from al-Zuhri, and by way of Sulayman ibn Kathir from al-Zuhri, and he said: "sound by the conditions of the two Shaykhs, though they did not record it," and al-Dhahabi agreed; and al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan 4: 136. See also Ibn Kathir's tafsir 2: 42, 43.
Al-ja'rur (with a damma on the jim): a kind of small date with no goodness in it. Al-lawn: a type of palm; it is said to be the daqal, and it is said that all palms except the barni and the 'ajwa are called "al-alwan" by the people of Medina. Ibn Habiq: a man to whom this poor palm was attributed, so it was said "lawn al-Habiq." Its dates are poor, dusty, small, with a long stone.]] .
6144 - Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, from 'Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "and do not aim at the bad of it, which you spend," he said: They used to give charity from the palm tree with its dried-up dates and its worthless ones, so they were forbidden from that, and commanded to give charity from its good.
6145 - Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah: "O you who have believed, spend of the good things you have earned," to His saying: "and know that Allah is Self-Sufficient, Praiseworthy," it was mentioned to us that a man would have two orchards in the time of the Prophet of Allah ﷺ, and he would aim at the worse of them in dates and give charity from it, mixing in dried-up dates, so Allah blamed them for that and forbade them from it.
6146 - Al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah regarding His saying: "and do not aim at the bad of it, which you spend," he said: You aim at the refuse of your property and give it in charity, [[The refuse (raḍālah) of everything is its worst part, when its good is selected and its bad left behind; it is from the refuse of people and their scum (both with a damma on the ra' in each).]] while you would not take it yourself unless you overlooked it.
6147 - Ibn WakI' related to us, saying: My father related to us, from Yazid ibn Ibrahim, from al-Hasan, who said: A man would give in charity the refuse of his wealth, so there was revealed: "and do not aim at the bad of it, which you spend."
6148 - Al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: 'Abdullah ibn Kathir informed us that he heard Mujahid say: "and do not aim at the bad of it, which you spend," he said: concerning the clusters that are hung, [[His saying "al-latī tu'allaq" (which are hung): a blank space is in the manuscript at this place. His later saying, "fa-ra'a fīhā ḥashafan" (then he saw in them dried-up dates), means that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw it.]] and he saw in them dried-up dates, and said: "What is this?" = Ibn Jurayj said: I heard 'Ata' say: A man hung dried-up dates among the clusters that were hung in Medina, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "What is this? How evil is what this hangs!" So there was revealed: "and do not aim at the bad of it, which you spend."
* *
Others said: The meaning of that is: "and do not aim at the bad, of the unlawful of it, which you spend," [[In the manuscript and printed edition: "fīhi tunfiqūn," which is a clear error.]]
and you give up spending the lawful good.
Mention of those who said that:
6149 - Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, when I asked him about the saying of Allah, mighty and majestic: "and do not aim at the bad of it, which you spend," he said: The bad is the unlawful; do not aim at it to spend from it, for Allah, mighty and majestic, does not accept it.
* *
Abu Ja'far said: The interpretation of the verse is the interpretation we have related from those among the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ whom we have related from, [for the soundness of its chain] and the agreement of the people of interpretation on it, [[The addition between the brackets is necessary for the sentence to be sound. ("'anhu," meaning "from him," is missing from the manuscript and the printed edition. As for the second addition, there is a blank in the manuscript at its place, which the printer overlooked, and ran the sentence on in one flow.]]
rather than what Ibn Zayd said. [[In the manuscript: "qalahu Ibn," and after that a blank. What is in the printed edition is the correct reading.]] .
* *
The interpretation of His saying: ﴿and you would not take it except that you overlook in it﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, mighty is His praise, means by that: "and you would not take the bad in your rights," and the "hā'" in His saying "bi-ākhidhīhi" refers to the bad, "except that you overlook in it," meaning: except that you be lax in your taking of it from some of what is due to you from your right, and grant yourselves leniency regarding it.
It is said from this: "aghmaḍa fulān li-fulān 'an ba'ḍi ḥaqqihi," meaning someone overlooked part of his right for another, "fahuwa yughmiḍu," and from this is the saying of Al-Tirimmah ibn Hakim:

Those who were not dissuaded from vengeance by a people, and among the humiliated there are men who accept overlooking,

[[Diwan: 86, from a qasidah in which he praised his people, and before it: "We are a people whose character is patience, when fear sways the ... "; "a support for the humble in the assembly of the tribe, ... cursed for the disgraced" ... "whoever seeks their gathering will find them ... "]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 267 (part 2 of 2):

*al-Ahfad*: young, weak camels; it also means weak people who do not endure in war. *Mara'ib*: from *ra'b*, which means repair; they are the reformers. *Al-tha'a*: corruption. *Al-minhad*: that which has been corrupted after being sound, so that its repair is hoped for only with hardship. *Maraji'*: forbearing people whom nothing makes light-headed. *Al-ahraad*: the weak who do not fight. *Al-ighmad*: overlooking and leniency. The meaning is: "We are people of might and power. No one has harmed us and escaped our retaliation. We are not like peoples who accept wrongdoing and overlook the reclaiming of their dues from those who have wronged them."

* *

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: The people of *ta'wil* (interpretation of the Qur'an) differed concerning the interpretation of this.

Some of them said: The meaning is: "You would not take the inferior from your debtors in what is due to you from them, except by overlooking, on your part, what is owed to you by them."

Those who said this:

6150. Asim ibn Rawwad related to us, saying: My father related to us, saying: Abu Bakr al-Hudhali related to us, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, from Ubaydah, who said: I asked Ali about it, and he said: "You would not take it except by overlooking it," meaning: none of you takes this inferior thing until it is diminished for him.

6151. Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Mu'ammal related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from al-Suddi, from Abu Malik, from al-Bara' ibn Azib: "You would not take it except by overlooking it." He said: If a man were owed something by another, and the other gave him that, he would not take it unless he saw that it fell short of his right. [[The report 6151 is a continuation of report 6141.]]

6152. Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abdullah related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to us, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, concerning his saying: "And do not aim at the bad of it, spending from it, while you would not accept it except by overlooking it." He said: If you had a right over someone and he brought you less than your right, you would not accept it at the price of the good unless you diminished it. That is His saying: "except by overlooking it." So how do you accept for Me what you do not accept for yourselves, when My right over you is from your best wealth and its best souls? [[In the printed edition it reads "wa-anfusuha" (and its souls); I have kept what is in the manuscript, "wa-anfusuha," as printed in the manuscript. This report in its full text is in al-Durr al-Manthur 1:346; see the note on report 6129, and his saying "wa-anfusihi" in the singular.]]

And this is His saying: "Never will you attain righteousness until you spend of that which you love" (Q 3:92).

6153. Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, from Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "You would not take it except by overlooking it." He said: You do not take it from your debtors, nor in your sales, except with an addition over what is good in measure.

6154. Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: My father related to me, saying: My paternal uncle related to me, saying: My father related to us, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, concerning his saying: "O you who have believed, spend from the good things you have earned and from what We have produced for you from the earth, and do not aim at the bad of it, spending from it, while you would not accept it except by overlooking it." That was because men used to give the zakat of their wealth in dates, and they would give the worst dates (*al-hashaf*) as zakat. So he said: If one of them demanded something from another and then the other paid him, he would not accept it unless he saw that his right had been overlooked.

6155. It was related to me from Ammar, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far related to us, from his father, from al-Rabi', concerning his saying: "You would not take it except by overlooking it." He says: If you were owed a debt by a man and he paid you something worse than what you were owed, would you take it from him unless you were hating it?

6156. Yahya ibn Abi Talib related to me, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Juwaybir related to us, from al-Dahhak, concerning his saying: "O you who have believed, spend from the good things you have earned," to his saying: "except by overlooking it." He said: When Allah commanded them to pay zakat, a man of the hypocrites would come with the worst food he had, of dates or other things. Allah disliked that and said: "Spend from the good things you have earned and from what We have produced for you from the earth," meaning: "You would not take it except by overlooking it," meaning: no man among you has a right over a man, and he gives him less than his right, and he takes it, unless he knows that he has diminished it. So do not accept for Me what you do not accept for yourselves, so that he takes something while he has overlooked a part of his right, which is less than what he is owed.

* *

Others said: The meaning is: "You would not take this inferior, bad thing if it were given to you as a price for the good, unless you overlook its price." That is, if you buy it from its owners at the price of the good thing, you would not take it except with leniency from them regarding its price.

Those who said this:

6157. Ibn Wakī' related to us, saying: My father related to us, from Imran ibn Hudayr, from al-Hasan: "You would not take it except by overlooking it." He said: If you found it being sold in the market, you would not take it until its price is reduced for you.

6158. Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah concerning his saying: "You would not take it except by overlooking it." He says: You would not take this inferior thing at the price of that good thing unless it is overlooked for you.

* *

Others said: The meaning is: "You would not take this inferior, bad thing if it were given to you as a gift, except by overlooking it, accepting it while you dislike it, out of shame before the one who gave it to you."

Those who said this:

6159. Al-Husayn ibn Amr ibn Muhammad al-Anqazi related to me, saying: My father related to us, from Asbat, from al-Suddi, from Adi ibn Thabit, from al-Bara' ibn Azib: "You would not take it except by overlooking it." He said: If it were given to you as a gift, you would not accept it except with shame before its giver, that he sent you something for which he had no need. [[The report 6159 is the continuation of the earlier report 6139.]]

6160. Musa related to me, saying: Amr related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, saying: al-Suddi claimed, from Adi ibn Thabit, from al-Bara', similarly, except that he said: "except with shame before its giver, and with anger that he sent you something for which he had no need." [[The report 6160 is the continuation of the earlier report 6140.]]

* *

Others said: The meaning is: "You would not take this inferior thing from your right except by overlooking some of your right."

Those who said this:

6161. Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Jarir related to us, from Ata', from Ibn Ma'qil: "You would not take it," meaning: you would not take it from a right that is yours, "except by overlooking it," meaning: I overlook for you some of my right.

* *

Others said: The meaning is: "You would not take the forbidden except by overlooking the sin upon you in taking it."

Those who said this:

6162. Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb related to us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: I asked him about his saying: "You would not take it except by overlooking it." He said: It means: "I would not take that forbidden thing unless you overlook the sin in it." He said: In the speech of the Arabs: "By God, he has taken it, and he has overlooked what is in it [of sin]," while he knows that it is forbidden and false.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The view that is most correct in the interpretation of this, in our opinion, is to say: Allah, mighty and majestic, urged His servants to give charity and to pay zakat from their wealth, and made it obligatory for them in their wealth. What He made obligatory of that in their wealth became a right of the recipients of the shares of charity (*ahl al-sahamān*). Then He, may His remembrance be exalted, commanded them to bring forth from the good, which is the best of their wealth, the good. This is because the recipients of the shares are partners of the owners of wealth in their wealth, through what has become due to them from it as charity after its becoming obligatory. [[The second "al-tayyib" is the object of "yukhrijū."]]

There is no doubt that any two partners in a property each have a share according to their ownership, and neither of them has the right to withhold from his partner his right in the ownership in which he is a partner, by giving him, in the amount of his right, something from other than it that is worse or more base. [[The printed edition has "aw ahsan" (or better), which is utterly corrupt; the correct reading is from the manuscript.]] Likewise, the one who pays zakat on his wealth: Allah forbade him to give the recipients of the shares, from what is due to them in his wealth, of the good and excellent, the rightful portion, while they become partners in it, something else from the bad and inferior, and to deny them what is theirs as their rights in the good of his excellent wealth. This is like the case where the owner's property is entirely inferior and not good: zakat becomes obligatory on it, and the recipients of the shares of charity become partners in it through what Allah made due to them in it. He is not obliged to give them the good and excellent from other than the property from which their right comes.

So the Blessed and Exalted said to the owners of wealth: Pay zakat from the excellent part of your excellent wealth, and do not aim at the bad, inferior thing, giving it to the recipients of the shares of charity while withholding from them what is due to them of the good and excellent in your wealth. [[In the printed edition: "wa-tamna'unahum al-wājib" (and you withhold from them what is due); the manuscript is correct, as it is coordinated with "wa-lā tayammamū al-khabītha."]] You would not accept the inferior for yourselves in place of the due good that is owed to you by those who owe it to you, from your partners, your debtors, and others, except by overlooking it, and by leniency on your part toward them, and by your aversion to taking it. He says: Do not treat those who have a due right in your wealth in a way that you would not accept from others treating you thus regarding your due rights in their wealth.

As for when a man voluntarily gives a charity that is not obligatory, then although I dislike that he should give anything in it except his best and most excellent wealth, because Allah, mighty and majestic, is most worthy of being drawn near to with the most noble and excellent wealth, and charity is an offering of the believer, I do not forbid him to give in it something other than the good. This is because what is less than the good may sometimes be of greater benefit due to its abundance, or because of its great value, and it may be more fitting in its place for the needy and for the one to whom I give it as a means of drawing near to Allah, mighty and majestic, than the good, due to its scarcity, or the smallness of its value and the lack of benefit to the one to whom I give it. [[The structure of this sentence: "perhaps it is of greater benefit due to its abundance ... and more fitting in its place for the needy ... than the good, due to its scarcity ..."]]

* *

Similar to what we have said on this, a group of the scholars said.

Those who said this:

6163. Muhammad ibn Abd al-Malik ibn Abi al-Shawarib related to us, saying: Yazid ibn Zuray' related to us, saying: Salamah ibn Alqamah related to us, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, who said: I asked Ubaydah about this verse: "O you who have believed, spend from the good things you have earned and from what We have produced for you from the earth, and do not aim at the bad of it, spending from it, while you would not accept it except by overlooking it." He said: That is concerning zakat. A counterfeit dirham is dearer to me than a date.

6164. Ya'qub related to me, saying: Ibn Ulayyah related to us, saying: Salamah ibn Alqamah related to us, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, who said: I asked Ubaydah about that, and he said: It is only concerning zakat, and a counterfeit dirham is dearer to me than a date.

6165. Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Ibn Idris related to us, from Hisham, from Ibn Sirin, who said: I asked Ubaydah about this verse: "O you who have believed, spend from the good things you have earned and from what We have produced for you from the earth, and do not aim at the bad of it, spending from it, while you would not accept it." Ubaydah said: This is only concerning the obligatory. There is no harm in a man giving a date voluntarily, and a counterfeit dirham is better than a date.

6166. Abu al-Sa'ib related to me, saying: Ibn Idris related to us, from Hisham, from Ibn Sirin, concerning his saying: "and do not aim at the bad of it, spending from it." He said: This is only concerning obligatory zakat. As for voluntary charity, there is no harm if a man gives in charity a counterfeit dirham, and a counterfeit dirham is better than a date.

* *

Concerning the interpretation of His saying: ﴿And know that Allah is Free of need and Praiseworthy﴾ (Q 2:267).

Abu Ja'far said: By this, His mention, may His praise be great, means: "And know, O people, that Allah, mighty and majestic, is free of need of your charities and of other than them [[See the explanation of "ghina" (sufficiency/wealth) earlier in this part, 5:521.]], and He only commanded you to give them and made them obligatory on your wealth out of mercy from Him toward you, so that by them He may enrich your poor [[al-ʿāʾil: the poor man; ʿāla al-rajul yaʿīl ʿaylatan: he became poor.]], strengthen your weak, and abundantly reward you for them in the Hereafter, not out of any need He has for you in them."

* *

By His saying "Praiseworthy" (ḥamīd), He means that He is praised by His creatures for the blessings He has bestowed upon them and the bounty He has spread for them, as:

6167. Al-Husayn ibn Amr ibn Muhammad al-Anqazi related to me, saying: My father related to us, from Asbat, from al-Suddi, from Adi ibn Thabit, from al-Bara' ibn Azib, concerning His saying: "And Allah is Free of need and Praiseworthy," [meaning] free of need of your charities. [[The report 6167 is the continuation of the earlier report 6139.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 268:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿The Satan threatens you with poverty and orders you to indecency, while God promises you forgiveness from Him and bounty﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His remembrance be exalted, He means: "The Satan threatens you," O people, with regard to giving charity and paying the zakat that is obligatory upon you in your wealth [[His words "with regard to giving charity..." mean: because of giving charity, which is a separate clause; the context "threatens you... that you become poor" is clear.]] - "that you become poor." "And orders you to indecency" means: and orders you to disobey God, may He be mighty and majestic, and to abandon His obedience [[See what has passed in the explanation of "indecency" (al-fahsha') 3: 302.]]. "And God promises you forgiveness from Him" [[See the explanation of "forgiveness" (al-maghfira) in the earlier indexes of vocabulary.]] means: God, may He be mighty and majestic, promises you, O believers, that He will cover your indecency for you, by pardoning you and not punishing you for it, and will forgive your sins through the charity you give. "And bounty" means: and He promises to replace for you from your charity, bestowing upon you of His gifts and abundantly providing for you in your sustenance. [[See the explanation of "bounty" (al-fadl) above 2: 344, and then 5: 164.]]

As follows:

6168 - Muhammad ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn ibn Waqid narrated to us, from Yazid al-Nahwi, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Two come from God and two from Satan. "The Satan threatens you with poverty": he says, do not spend your wealth, but hold it back for yourself, for you will need it. "And orders you to indecency" [and] "God promises you forgiveness from Him" for these sins. "And bounty" in provision.

6169 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah concerning His saying: "The Satan threatens you with poverty and orders you to indecency, while God promises you forgiveness from Him and bounty," he says: forgiveness for your indecency, and bounty in place of your poverty.

6170 - Hannad narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Ahwas narrated to us, from Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Murrah, from Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, the Satan has an inspiration (lamma) toward the son of Adam, and the angel has an inspiration: as for the inspiration of Satan, it is a promise of evil and a denial of the truth; as for the inspiration of the angel, it is a promise of good and an affirmation of the truth. Whoever finds that, let him know that it is from God and let him praise God; and whoever finds the other, let him seek refuge in God from Satan." Then he recited: "The Satan threatens you with poverty and orders you to indecency."

[[Hadith 6170 - Abu al-Ahwas: he is Salam ibn Sulaym al-Kufi, the hafiz. His reliability was established previously at 20158.

Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib: it has passed at 158 and 4433 that he changed toward the end of his life, and that whoever heard from him in earlier times, his narration is sound. The apparent sense of their collective statements is that his confusion occurred when he came to Basra. Abu Hatim said: "In the narrations of the Basrans from him there are many confusions, for he came to them at the end of his life." Ata' was Kufan, and the narrator from him here, Abu al-Ahwas, was also Kufan. So it is apparent that he heard from him before the confusion.

Murrah: he is Murrah al-Tayyib, the son of Shurahil al-Hamdani al-Kufi. His biography has passed at 2521.

Abdullah: he is Ibn Mas'ud.

This hadith was also transmitted by al-Tirmidhi (4: 77-78), from Hannad - that is Ibn al-Sari, the teacher of al-Tabari here - with this chain. He said: "This is a good, strange hadith [and in some copies: good, sound, strange]. It is the hadith of Abu al-Ahwas; we do not know it as marfu' except from the hadith of Abu al-Ahwas."

Ibn Kathir (2: 44) also mentioned it, from the narration of Ibn Abi Hatim, from Abu Zur'ah, from Hannad. Some scribes' errors occurred in its chain there. Then he pointed to some of its narrations as marfu' and mawquf.

Ibn Kathir mentioned that al-Nasa'i also transmitted it in the Book of Tafsir of his Sunan, from Hannad ibn al-Sari, and that Ibn Hibban transmitted it in his Sahih from Abu Ya'la al-Mawsili, from Hannad. The Book of Tafsir in al-Nasa'i is in the Sunan al-Kubra.

al-Suyuti (1: 348) mentioned it and added its attribution to Ibn al-Mundhir and al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman.

Similar narrations, mawquf upon Ibn Mas'ud, will come: 6171, 6172, 6174, 6176, from the narration of Ata', from Murrah, from Mas'ud. Also mawquf will come: 6173, from the narration of al-Zuhri, from Ubayd Allah, from Ibn Mas'ud. And: 6175, from the narration of al-Musayyib ibn Rafi', from Amir ibn Abdah, from Ibn Mas'ud.

It seems that al-Tirmidhi - and Ibn Kathir following him - intend to point to a flaw in this marfu' chain, by the narration of the hadith as mawquf. But this is a flaw that does not undermine it once the chain is sound, for raising (rafa') is an addition from a trustworthy narrator, and it is accepted.

Also: this hadith is of the kind that cannot be known by opinion, nor does analogy enter it, so it is known only by revelation from the Infallible (ﷺ). Thus the narrations that are mawquf in wording are marfu' in ruling.]]

6171 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: al-Hakam ibn Bashir ibn Sulayman narrated to us, saying: Amr narrated to us, from Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Murrah, from Abdullah, who said: Indeed, for the human being there is an inspiration from the angel and an inspiration from Satan. The inspiration from the angel is a promise of good and an affirmation of the truth; the inspiration from Satan is a promise of evil and a denial of the truth. And Abdullah recited: "The Satan threatens you with poverty and orders you to indecency, while God promises you forgiveness from Him and bounty." Amr said: We have also heard in this hadith that it used to be said: if one of you senses something from the inspiration of the angel, let him praise God and ask Him from His bounty; and if he senses something from the inspiration of Satan, let him seek forgiveness from God and seek refuge in God from Satan.

[[Hadith 6171 - al-Hakam ibn Bashir ibn Salman: his biography has passed at 1497. The name of his grandfather appears in the printed edition here as "Sulayman," which is an error.

Amr: he is Ibn Qays al-Mala'i. His biography has passed at 886.

The hadith is in the sense of the preceding one. Here it is mawquf in wording, but marfu' in ruling, as we mentioned. However, the saying of Amr ibn Qays at its end, "We have also heard in this hadith that it used to be said..." would be a disconnected report (balagh munqati') in this chain, although it is sound in itself through the other chains.]]

6172 - Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, saying: Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib narrated to us, from Abu al-Ahwas - or from Murrah - who said: Abdullah said: Indeed, for the angel there is an inspiration, and for Satan there is an inspiration. The inspiration of the angel: a promise of good and an affirmation of the truth; the inspiration of Satan: a promise of evil and a denial of the truth. And that is because God says:

"The Satan threatens you with poverty and orders you to indecency, while God promises you forgiveness from Him and bounty, and God is All-Embracing, All-Knowing." So if you find any of these, praise God for it, and if you find any of those, seek refuge in God from Satan.

[[Hadith 6172 - Abu al-Ahwas, the teacher of Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib: he is Awf ibn Malik ibn Nadlah, a known reliable Tabi'i, whose reliability was affirmed by Ibn Ma'in and others.

Ata's hesitation as to whether it is from "Abu al-Ahwas" or from "Murrah al-Tayyib" does not affect the soundness of the hadith, for it is a transfer from one reliable narrator to another reliable narrator. Perhaps it is among what Ata' erred in, for Ibn Ulayyah was Basran, so he would have heard from him after his change. al-Daraqutni explicitly stated this, as in Ata's biography in al-Tahdhib.

However, Ibn Kathir (2: 44) mentioned that it was transmitted by "Mis'ar, from Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Abu al-Ahwas Awf ibn Malik ibn Nadlah, from Ibn Mas'ud," making it his own statement. This establishes the preservation of Ata's narration of it from Abu al-Ahwas as well, for Mis'ar ibn Kidam was an early Kufan, of the rank of Shu'bah and al-Thawri, so he is among those who heard from him before his change.

Ibn Kathir did not point to any of the mawquf narrations of this hadith except the narration of Mis'ar alone. The mawquf narrations before him in al-Tabari are six, as you see.]]

6173 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from Ubayd Allah ibn Abdullah ibn Utbah, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud concerning His saying: "The Satan threatens you with poverty and orders you to indecency," he said: Indeed, for the angel there is an inspiration, and for Satan there is an inspiration. The inspiration of the angel is a promise of good and an affirmation of the truth, so whoever finds it, let him praise God; the inspiration of Satan is a promise of evil and a denial of the truth, so whoever finds it, let him seek refuge in God.

[[Hadith 6173 - This is another sound chain for the hadith, from a different route, supporting the narration of Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib. Although it is mawquf in wording, it is marfu' in ruling, as we said before.]]

6174 - al-Muthanna ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Hajjaj ibn al-Minhal narrated to us, saying: Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, saying: Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib informed us, from Murrah al-Hamdani, that Ibn Mas'ud said: Indeed, for the angel there is an inspiration, and for Satan there is an inspiration. The inspiration of the angel: a promise of good and an affirmation of the truth; the inspiration of Satan: a promise of evil and a denial of the truth. [[In the printed edition: "a promise of good... a promise of evil" without attaching them to the pronoun. I have kept what is in the manuscript, which is correct. Both "ida'a" and "ida'ah" could be read, in the sense of an occurrence from "al-i'ad."]] So whoever senses something from the inspiration of the angel, let him praise God for it, and whoever senses something from the inspiration of Satan, let him seek refuge in God from it. Then he recited this verse: "The Satan threatens you with poverty and orders you to indecency, while God promises you forgiveness from Him and bounty, and God is All-Embracing, All-Knowing."

[[Hadith 6174 - This is a sound chain, for Hammad ibn Salamah heard from Ata' before his change, as Ya'qub ibn Sufyan and Ibn al-Jarud stated, in what al-Tahdhib transmits from them, 7: 207.]]

6175 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Suwayd ibn Nasr narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Fitr, from al-Musayyib ibn Rafi', from Amir ibn Abdah, from Abdullah, with something similar.

[[Hadith 6175 - Fitr - with a kasra on the fa', a sukun on the ta', and a final ra': he is Ibn Khalifah al-Kufi, a reliable narrator, affirmed reliable by Ahmad, Ibn Ma'in and others.

al-Musayyib ibn Rafi' al-Kahili al-Kufi: a reliable Tabi'i, whose biography has passed at 128.

Amir ibn Abdah - with a fatha on the ayn, and the single-dotted ba' - al-Bajali, Abu Iyas al-Kufi: a reliable Tabi'i, and in al-Kuna of al-Dulabi 1: 115, and al-Mushtabih of al-Dhahabi, p. 339.

This is a third sound chain for the hadith, from another route, supporting the narrations of Ata' from Murrah, of Abu al-Ahwas from Ibn Mas'ud, and the narration of al-Zuhri from Ubayd Allah ibn Abdullah ibn Utbah from Ibn Mas'ud.]]

6176 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Ata', from Murrah ibn Shurahil, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: Indeed, for Satan there is an inspiration, and for the angel there is an inspiration. As for the inspiration of Satan, it is a denial of the truth and a promise of evil; as for the inspiration of the angel: a promise of good and an affirmation of the truth. Whoever finds that, let him know that it is from God and let him praise God for it. And whoever finds the other, let him seek refuge from Satan. Then he recited: "The Satan threatens you with poverty and orders you to indecency, while God promises you forgiveness from Him and bounty."

[[Hadith 6176 - This chain is good, for Jarir - that is Ibn Abd al-Hamid al-Dabbi - heard from Ata' after his change, but it rises to the level of soundness through the earlier sound supporting narrations.]]

* *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And God is All-Embracing, All-Knowing (268)﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He means, may His remembrance be exalted: "And God is All-Embracing" - the bounty that He promises to give you from His favour and the vastness of His treasuries [[See the explanation of "All-Embracing, All-Knowing" above 2: 537, and then 5: 516.]] - "All-Knowing" of your expenditures and your charities which you spend and give in charity, He counts them for you so that He may reward you for them when you come before Him in your Hereafter.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 269:

The explanation of His words: ﴿He gives wisdom to whom He wills, and whoever is given wisdom has indeed been given much good﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His praise be exalted, He means: God gives correctness (al-isabah) in speech and action to whomever He wills of His servants, and whoever among them is given correctness in that has indeed been given much good.

* *

The interpreters (ahl al-ta'wil) differed regarding this.

Some of them said: "wisdom" (al-hikmah) which God mentions in this place is: the Qur'an and understanding of it.

Those who said this:

6177 - Al-Muthanna related to us, he said: Abd Allah ibn Salih related to us, he said: Mu'awiyah related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿and whoever is given wisdom has indeed been given much good﴾, he means: knowledge of the Qur'an, its abrogating and abrogated verses (nasikh and mansukh), its clear and ambiguous verses (muhkam and mutashabih), its early and late parts, its lawful and unlawful, and its parables.

6178 - Al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, he said: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah regarding His words: "He gives wisdom to whom He wills", he said: Wisdom is the Qur'an, and understanding of the Qur'an.

6179 - Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah regarding His words: "He gives wisdom to whom He wills, and whoever is given wisdom has indeed been given much good", and wisdom is understanding of the Qur'an.

6180 - Muhammad ibn Abd Allah al-Hilali related to us, he said: Muslim ibn Ibrahim related to us, he said: Mahdi ibn Maymun related to us, he said: Shu'ayb ibn al-Hubhab related to us, from Abu al-'Aliyah: "and whoever is given wisdom has indeed been given much good", he said: The Book and understanding of it. [[The report 6180: "Muhammad ibn Abd Allah al-Hilali" is: Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Ubayd ibn Aqil al-Hilali, Abu Mas'ud al-Basri. He narrated from his grandfather Ubayd ibn Aqil, Uthman ibn Umar ibn Faris, Amr ibn Asim al-Kilabi and others, and Abu Dawud, al-Nasa'i, Ibn Majah and others narrated from him. Al-Nasa'i said: "There is no harm in him." Maslamah said: "Trustworthy." "Muslim ibn Ibrahim" al-Azdi al-Faradhi, Abu Amr al-Basri, the memorizer (al-Hafiz). Ibn Ma'in said: "Trustworthy and reliable." He used to say: "I never encountered anything lawful or unlawful." Abu Hatim said: "He was not in need of (narrating from others)." He was among the precise narrators. He died in 222. "Mahdi ibn Maymun" al-Azdi al-Mu'awili. He was trustworthy, and Ibn Hibban mentioned him among the trustworthy. He died in 171. "Shu'ayb ibn al-Hubhab" and "al-Mu'awili" with a kasrah on the mim, sukun on the unpointed ayn, and fathah on the waw.

In the printed edition it reads: "wa-al-fahm fihi" ("and the understanding of it"). It is correct in meaning and good in Arabic, and I have affirmed what is in the manuscript, which is also correct and good.]]

6181 - Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Jarir related to us, from Layth, from Mujahid regarding His words: "He gives wisdom to whom He wills", the verse, he said: It is not prophethood, but it is the Qur'an, knowledge and understanding.

6182 - Al-Qasim related to us, he said: Al-Husayn related to us, he said: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Juraij, who said: Ibn Abbas said: Understanding of the Qur'an.

* *

Others said: the meaning of "wisdom" is correctness in speech and action.

Those who said this:

6183 - Ibn Bashshar related to us, he said: Abd al-Rahman related to us, he said: Sufyan related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, who said: I heard Mujahid say: "and whoever is given wisdom", he said: Correctness.

6184 - Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, he said: Abu Asim related to us, from Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding the words of God, Mighty and Majestic: "He gives wisdom to whom He wills", he said: He gives His correctness to whom He wills.

6185 - Al-Muthanna related to me, he said: Abu Hudhayfah related to us, he said: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "He gives wisdom to whom He wills", he said: The Book; He gives its correctness to whom He wills.

* *

Others said: it is knowledge of the religion.

Those who said this:

6186 - Yunus related to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said: "He gives wisdom to whom He wills", intellect in religion; and he recited: "and whoever is given wisdom has indeed been given much good."

6187 - Yunus related to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said: Wisdom is intellect.

6188 - Yunus related to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: I said to Malik: "And what is wisdom?" He said: Knowledge of the religion, understanding of it, and following it.

* *

Others said: "wisdom" is understanding.

Those who said this:

6190 - Ibn Waki' related to us, he said: My father related to us, he said: Sufyan related to us, from Abu Hamzah, from Ibrahim, who said: Wisdom is understanding. [[The report 6190: "Abu Hamzah" is Abu Hamzah al-A'war al-Qassab al-Kufi, the companion of Ibrahim al-Nakha'i. Al-Bukhari said: "He is not that." And he said: "Weak, of lost narrations." Abu Musa said: "I never heard Yahya or Abd al-Rahman narrate from Sufyan, from Abu Hamzah, ever." Ibn Adi said: "His narrations specifically from Ibrahim are not corroborated." Biographed in al-Tahdhib.]]

* *

Others said: it is fear (al-khashyah).

Those who said this:

6191 - Al-Muthanna related to me, he said: Ishaq related to us, he said: Ibn Abi Ja'far related to us, from his father, from al-Rabi' regarding His words: "He gives wisdom to whom He wills, and whoever is given wisdom", the verse, he said: "Wisdom" is fear, because the head of everything is the fear of God. And he recited: ﴿Only those of His servants who have knowledge fear God﴾ [Surah Fatir: 28].

* *

Others said: it is prophethood.

Those who said this:

6192 - Musa related to me, he said: Amr related to us, he said: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi regarding His words: "He gives wisdom to whom He wills, and whoever is given wisdom", the verse, he said: Wisdom is prophethood.

* *

We have already explained earlier the meaning of "wisdom", that it is derived from "judgement" (al-hukm) and decisive judgement (fasl al-qada'), and that it is correctness, by what evidences its soundness, which suffices without repeating it in this place. [[See the explanation of "wisdom" earlier: 3:87, 88, 211; then 5:15, 16, 371.]]

* *

When that is its meaning, all the sayings of those whose views we have mentioned fall within what we have said, because correctness in matters arises only from understanding of them, knowledge and recognition. When that is so, the one who is correct through understanding of the right course in his affairs is one who understands, fears God, is a jurist and a scholar. [[In the printed edition: "fahman khashyan..." In the manuscript: "fafhman", and the correct reading is as I have given, by the evidence of the meaning he intended, including prophets within this meaning, and by his later words: "mufhimun..."]]

Prophethood is among its divisions, because the prophets are guided, made to understand, and granted success in correctness in some matters, and "prophethood" is some of the meanings of "wisdom."

* *

Thus the sense of the statement: God gives correctness in speech and action to whomever He wills, and whomever God grants that has indeed been given much good.

* *

The explanation of His words: ﴿And none will be mindful except the people of understanding﴾ (2:269)

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His praise be exalted, He means: none is admonished by what his Lord admonishes him in these verses, in which He admonishes those who spend their wealth with what others have admonished them, and in which and other verses of His Book He mentions His promise and His threat, so he refrains from what his Lord forbids him and obeys Him in what He commands him: "except the people of understanding", meaning: except those of intellect, who comprehend from God, Mighty and Majestic, His command and prohibition. [[See the explanation of "al-albab" earlier: 3:383; 4:162.]]

Thus He informs that admonitions benefit only the people of discernment and forbearance, and that reminders restrain only the people of restraint and intellect.

The Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 2, Verse 270:

Discussion of the interpretation of His words: ﴿And whatever expenditure you spend, or whatever vow you vow, indeed Allah knows it, and the wrongdoers have no helpers﴾ (2:270).

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His praise be exalted, He means: "Whatever expenditure you spend," meaning whatever charity you give [[See the explanation of "expenditure" (nafaqa) above, 5:555.]], "or whatever vow you vow," meaning by "vow" what a person obligates himself to, seeking to draw near to God through obedience to Him, whether a charity or a good deed. "Indeed Allah knows it," meaning that all of that is within the knowledge of Allah, nothing of it is hidden from Him, and neither a little nor a lot of it is concealed from Him. Rather, He counts it, O people, so that He may recompense you all for all of that. [[In the manuscript: "فإن الله يعلم" (indeed Allah knows), and the correct reading here is what is in the printed edition. Then in the printed edition: "جميع ذلك بعلم الله" (all of that is within the knowledge of Allah), and I have retained the correct reading from the manuscript.]]

So whoever among you gives his expenditure, charity, and vow seeking the pleasure of Allah and as a firm conviction from himself, He will recompense him with the multiplication He has promised. And whoever gives his expenditure and charity for show before people, and his vows are for Satan, He will recompense him with what He has threatened him: punishment and painful torment, as in what was narrated:

6193 - Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, from Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning the words of Allah, may He be mighty and majestic: "And whatever expenditure you spend or vow you vow, indeed Allah knows it," that He counts it.

6194 - al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa related to us, saying: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

* *

Then, may His praise be exalted, He threatened those whose expenditure is for show and whose vows are obedience to Satan, saying: ﴿And the wrongdoers have no helpers﴾, meaning: none for whoever spends his wealth for show before people and in disobedience to Allah, and whose vows are for Satan and in obedience to him, "helpers" being the plural of "naṣīr" (helper), as "ashraf" is the plural of "sharīf" (noble). [[See the meaning of "naṣr" (help) and "naṣīr" (helper) above, 2:489, 564.]] By His words "helpers" He means those who would help them against Allah on the Day of Resurrection, to ward off His punishment from them on that day by strength or by severe force, and not by ransom.

* *

We have already shown that "wrongdoer" (ẓālim) is one who places a thing in other than its proper place. [[See the explanation of "wrongdoing" (ẓulm) above, 1:523-524, 2:369, 519, 4:584, and other places; seek them in the index of language.]]

* *

Allah called the one who spends for show before people, and the one who vows in disobedience to Him, a wrongdoer, because he has placed the spending of his wealth in other than its proper place, and his vow in other than the place it should have been placed, and that was his wronging.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: If someone says to us: Why did He say ﴿indeed Allah knows it﴾ and not "knows them," when the vow and the expenditure have both been mentioned?

It is said: He only said "indeed He knows it" because He meant: indeed Allah knows what you have spent or vowed, and therefore He used the singular pronoun. [[The "kināya" (pronoun) and "mukannā" (the pronominal reference), is the pronoun in the terminology of the Kufans, the Baghdadis, and others.]]

Commentary on the interpretation of His words: ﴿If you disclose your charities, then they are good; but if you conceal them and give them to the poor, it is better for you﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His words, may His majesty be praised, "If you disclose the charities," He means: if you publicize the charities, giving them to those to whom you have given them, "then they are good," meaning: then the thing is good. "And if you conceal them," meaning: if you keep them hidden and do not publicize them, "and give them to the poor," meaning: and give them to the poor in secret. [See the meaning of "al-ita'" (giving) under the root "ataa" in the language indexes above.] "then it is better for you," meaning: your concealing them is better for you than publicizing them. This applies to voluntary charity, as:

6195 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: "If you disclose the charities, then they are good; but if you conceal them and give them to the poor, it is better for you," [he said:] every (charity) is accepted when the intention is sincere, and secret charity is superior. It was also mentioned to us that charity extinguishes sin just as water extinguishes fire.

6196 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi', regarding His words: "If you disclose the charities, then they are good; but if you conceal them and give them to the poor, it is better for you," he said: every (charity) is accepted when the intention is sincere, and charity in secret is superior. He used to say: charity extinguishes sin just as water extinguishes fire.

6197 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abdullah narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words: "If you disclose the charities, then they are good; but if you conceal them and give them to the poor, it is better for you," he said: God made secret voluntary charity superior to its public form by seventy times, and made obligatory charity: its public form is better than its secret form, [being multiplied] by twenty-five times, and likewise all obligatory and voluntary acts in all things.

6198 - Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Hanafi narrated to me, saying: Abdullah ibn Uthman narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, saying: I heard Sufyan say regarding His words: "If you disclose the charities, then they are good; but if you conceal them and give them to the poor, it is better for you," he said: it refers to what is other than zakat.

* *

Others said: God, mighty and majestic, only meant by His words, "If you disclose the charities, then they are good," that if you disclose charities given to the People of the Book, Jews and Christians, then they are good; and if you conceal them and give them to their poor, it is better for you. They said: as for what is given to the poor among the Muslims, whether zakat or voluntary charity, concealing it is better than publicizing it.

Those who said this:

6199 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Abd al-Rahman ibn Shurayh narrated to me, that he heard Yazid ibn Abi Habib say: this verse was only revealed: "If you disclose the charities, then they are good," concerning charity given to Jews and Christians.

6200 - Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Hanafi narrated to me, saying: Abdullah ibn Uthman informed us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, saying: Ibn Lahi'ah informed us, saying: Yazid ibn Abi Habib used to order that zakat be distributed in secret. Abdullah said: I prefer that it be given openly, meaning zakat.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: God did not specify in His words, "If you disclose the charities, then they are good," [any part over another], so it is general, except for obligatory zakat, [and the sentence is as it appears in the manuscript and printed edition; I added what is between the brackets to make the phrase somewhat sound, and I have no doubt that a copyist omitted something]. For the obligatory duties, all agree that the excellence lies in publicizing them, apart from zakat, concerning which there is disagreement, though all agree it is obligatory; its ruling regarding the superiority of giving it openly is the ruling of the other obligatory duties.

* *

On the interpretation of His words: ﴿And He will remove from you some of your misdeeds﴾

Abu Ja'far said: The reciters differed regarding the recitation of this.

It is narrated from Ibn Abbas that he recited it: "wa-tukaffiru 'ankum" with the letter ta'.

Whoever recites it thus means: the charities remove from you some of your misdeeds.

* *

Others recited: "wa-yukaffiru 'ankum" with the letter ya', meaning: God removes from you, by your charities, some of your misdeeds mentioned in the verse.

* *

The majority of the reciters of Madinah, Kufah and Basrah recited: "wa-nukaffiru 'ankum" with the letter nun and the final letter jussed, meaning: if you conceal them and give them to the poor, We will remove from you some of your misdeeds, meaning: God's recompense to the one who conceals his charity is the removal of some of his misdeeds through the charity he concealed.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct recitation in our view is the recitation of the one who recites "wa-nukaffiru 'ankum" with the nun and jussed final letter, as a report from God about Himself that He rewards the one who conceals his voluntary charity seeking His face, by removing his misdeeds. When read thus, it is jussed on the place of the "fa'" in His words "then it is better for you," because the "fa'" there takes the place of the answer of the conditional.

* *

If someone asks us: how did you choose the jussing on the basis of the place of the "fa'", and leave choosing its coordination with what follows the "fa'", although you know that the more eloquent usage in coordinating with the answer of the conditional is the raf' (nominative), and jussing is only permissible?

It is said: we chose that because jussing indicates that the removal—namely God's removal of misdeeds from the giver—is undoubtedly included in what God promised the giver as recompense for his charity. For when it is jussed, it necessarily indicates what we have said. Had it been raised, it could have been possible that it is included in what God promised him as recompense, or that it is a resumed report that He removes misdeeds from His believing servants, not as a recompense for their charities, because what follows the "fa'" in the answer of the conditional is a resumption, and what is coordinated with a resumed report has the same status as what it is coordinated with, in not being included in the recompense. For this reason we chose the jussing of "nukaffiru" as coordinated with the place of the "fa'" in His words "then it is better for you," and the reading with the nun.

[This is from the fine insight of Abu Ja'far into the meanings of interpretation, and his choice among the recitations. If his book on the recitations, which he mentioned in the first volume, page 148, and in which he set out his choice of recitation and the reasons establishing what he chose, had reached us, we would have had a work of subtle entrances and exits, as we surmise.]

* *

If someone asks: what is the purpose of the "min" in His words "and remove from you some of your misdeeds"? It is said: its purpose there is: "and remove from you some of your misdeeds, those which We wish to remove, not all of them, so that the servants may be in awe of God and not rely on His promise regarding the charities that the giver conceals, and thus become bold against His limits and His disobediences."

* *

Some grammarians of Basrah said: the meaning of "min" here is elision, and its interpretation is: "and We remove your misdeeds."

* *

On the interpretation of His words: ﴿And God is Aware of what you do﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His majesty be praised, He means: "And God is aware of what you do" in your charities, of concealing them, of publicizing them, of secret and open giving, and in your other deeds, "Aware" meaning one who has knowledge and awareness, nothing of that is hidden from Him; He encompasses all of it, and He will be watchful over its people, so that He may repay them the reward for all of it and the recompense for its little and its much.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 272:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿It is not upon you (O Muhammad) to guide them, but Allah guides whom He wills. And whatever you spend of good, it is for yourselves, and you spend not except seeking the Face of Allah. And whatever you spend of good will be repaid to you in full, and you will not be wronged﴾.

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His remembrance be exalted, He means: It is not upon you, O Muhammad, to guide the polytheists to Islam, so that you withhold voluntary charity from them, or so that you give them of it in order that they enter Islam, out of any need of theirs for it. Rather, Allah guides whom He wills of His creation to Islam and grants them success in it, so do not withhold charity from them. As:

6201 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Ash'ath, from Ja'far, from Shu'bah, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) would not give charity to the polytheists. Then it was revealed: ﴿And you spend not except seeking the Face of Allah﴾, so he gave charity to them.

6202 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Abu Dawud narrated to us, from Sufyan, from al-A'mash, from Ja'far ibn Iyas, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: They would not give (rud') to their relatives among the polytheists, so it was revealed: ﴿It is not upon you to guide them, but Allah guides whom He wills﴾.

[[The narration 6202: "Ja'far ibn Iyas" is Ibn Abi Wahshiyyah al-Yashkuri, Abu Bishr al-Wasiti. Trustworthy, and among the most reliable of people regarding Sa'id ibn Jubayr. Its date of death is disputed between 123 and 131 AH. Biographed in al-Tahdhib. Ibn Kathir narrated the report in his tafsir 2:49 from Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Nasa'i with its chain, and said: "Likewise Abu Hudhayfah, Ibn al-Mubarak, Abu Ahmad al-Zubayri, and Abu Dawud al-Hadrami narrated it from Sufyan (al-Thawri) with it." He did not attribute it to Abu Ja'far, and this is evidence for what I mentioned in the introduction to the earlier parts: that Ibn Kathir and others reduced their citations from Abu Ja'far after the first part of his tafsir.

"Radakha lahu min malihi yardukhu radkhan, wa radakha lahu min malihi radikhah": he gave him a gift approximating, between little and much.]]

6203 - Ibn WakI' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from a man, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: They used to avoid giving (rud') to their relatives among the polytheists, until it was revealed: ﴿It is not upon you to guide them, but Allah guides whom He wills﴾.

6204 - Muhammad ibn Bashshar and Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, both saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Ja'far ibn Iyas, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: They would not give (rud') to their kinsfolk among the polytheists, so it was revealed: ﴿It is not upon you to guide them, but Allah guides whom He wills﴾, and so He permitted them.

6205 - al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Suwayd narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Sufyan, from al-A'mash, from Ja'far ibn Iyas, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Some Ansar had kinsfolk and relatives among Qurayzah and al-Nadir, and they were careful not to give charity to them, and wanted them to become Muslim, so it was revealed: ﴿It is not upon you to guide them...﴾ the verse.

6206 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, who mentioned to us that some men among the companions of the Prophet of Allah said: Shall we give charity to those who are not of our religion? So Allah revealed concerning that: ﴿It is not upon you to guide them﴾.

6207 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi' regarding His words: ﴿It is not upon you to guide them, but Allah guides whom He wills﴾. He said: A man from the Muslims, if there was kinship between him and a man from the polytheists and he was in need, would not give him charity, saying: He is not of my religion!
