So Allah, may He be exalted, revealed: ﴿It is not upon you to guide them﴾ the verse.

6208 - Musa narrated to me, saying: [[Narration 6208: In the printed and manuscript editions it reads "Muhammad narrated to us, said: 'Amr narrated to us...", and the correct reading is "Musa", who is Musa ibn Harun, from 'Amr ibn Hammad, and this is a recurring chain from the beginning of the tafsir. This same report will come again, with its continuation, as number 6211, with its chain in its correct form. My brother al-Sayyid Ahmad's explanation of this chain has already passed under number 168.]] 'Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi regarding His words: ﴿It is not upon you to guide them, but Allah guides whom He wills. And whatever you spend of good, it is for yourselves﴾. As for ﴿It is not upon you to guide them﴾, it means the polytheists; and as for ﴿spending﴾, it is among its recipients.

6209 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: al-Himmani narrated to us, saying: Ya'qub al-Qummi narrated to us, from Ja'far ibn Abi al-Mughirah, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: They used to give charity [to the poor among the People of the Covenant (dhimmis). When the poor among the Muslims increased, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: Give charity only to the people of your religion. So this verse was revealed, permitting charity to those who are not of the religion of Islam].

[[Narration 6209: The text was broken off at this point in the manuscript and the printed edition, but the copyist ran it on as a single line: "They used to give charity, as Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us..." I have pointed out in p. 584, the footnote, and in my other earlier notes, the copyist's negligence and error here.

I have added what is between the brackets from what al-Qurtubi narrated in his tafsir 3:337, who said: Sa'id ibn Jubayr narrated as a mursal report from the Prophet (ﷺ) concerning the occasion of revelation of this verse: "The Muslims used to give charity to the poor among the People of the Covenant..." to the end of what I quoted. I concluded that this report had dropped out at this point, so I inserted its text from al-Qurtubi; but the beginning of the following statement remains broken, so I placed dots in place of that break.]]

* *

..........................................................................

..........................................................................

* *

As:

6210 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words: ﴿will be repaid to you in full, and you will not be wronged﴾: It is returned to you. So what is your concern with this, that you harm him and reproach him? Your spending is only for yourself and seeking the Face of Allah, and Allah will reward you.

[[Narration 6210: What precedes this report is broken, and I cannot estimate its extent. al-Suyuti narrated the report in al-Durr al-Manthur 1:357-358.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 273 (part 1 of 2):

The interpretation of His words: ﴿For the poor who are restrained in the way of Allah, who cannot move about in the land. The ignorant man thinks them wealthy because of their restraint; you know them by their mark. They do not beg of people importunately. And whatever good you spend, indeed Allah is Knowing of it.﴾ (273)

Abu Ja'far said: As for His words, "For the poor who are restrained in the way of Allah," this is an explanation from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, of the path and manner of spending. The meaning of the speech is: "And whatever good you spend, it is for yourselves, you spend for the poor who are restrained in the way of Allah."

The "lam" in "for the poor" is returned to the place of the "lam" in "it is for yourselves" — as if He had said: "And whatever good you spend," meaning: "And whatever wealth you give in charity, it is for the poor who are restrained in the way of Allah." Then, when the speech was interrupted by His words "it is for yourselves," and the "fa'" which is the answer of the conditional was introduced into it, its repetition was dropped in "for the poor," since the meaning of the speech was understood, as in:

6211 - Musa related to me, saying: 'Amr related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, concerning His words: "It is not for you to guide them, but Allah guides whom He wills. And whatever good you spend, it is for yourselves." As for "It is not for you to guide them," it refers to the polytheists. As for "spending," He explained its recipients, saying: "For the poor who are restrained in the way of Allah." [[The report: 6211 — see the preceding report no. 6208 and the comment on it.]]

* *

It was said: These poor whom Allah mentioned in this verse are the poor emigrants in general, to the exclusion of other poor people.

Those who said this:

6212 - Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His words: "For the poor who are restrained in the way of Allah," — the emigrants of Quraysh in Medina with the Prophet (ﷺ), he was commanded to give charity to them.

6213 - al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Ishaq related to us, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far related to us, from his father, concerning His words: "For the poor who are restrained in the way of Allah," etc., he said: They are the poor emigrants in Medina.

6214 - Musa related to me, saying: 'Amr related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi: "For the poor who are restrained in the way of Allah," he said: the poor emigrants.

* *

The interpretation of the words of the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿who are restrained in the way of Allah﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By this, His mention, exalted is He, means: those whom their fighting against their enemy has made restrained, confining themselves so that they are prevented from earning, so they are unable to earn. [[al-tasarruf: earning. It is said, "So-and-so spends on his dependents (yasrifu li-'iyalihi), and earns for them (yatasarraf lahum), and seeks gain (yasturif)," i.e., earns for them. It is from al-sarf and al-tasarruf: turning about and stratagem.]]

* *

We have already shown earlier that the meaning of "al-ihsar" is making a man who is restrained by his illness, his poverty, or his striving against an enemy, or other causes, reach a state in which he confines himself from acting upon his means of livelihood, as is sufficiently explained earlier. [[See what preceded, 4: 21–26.]]

* *

The people of interpretation have differed concerning the interpretation of this.

Some of them said: its meaning is similar to what we have said.

Those who said this:

6215 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, concerning His words: "Those who are restrained in the way of Allah," he said: they restrained themselves in the way of Allah for fighting.

6216 - Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words: "For the poor who are restrained in the way of Allah," he said: the whole earth was disbelief; no one could go out seeking of Allah's bounty, and if he went out, he went out in disbelief. And it was said: the whole earth was war against the people of this city, and they did not turn in any direction without having an enemy there; so Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: "For the poor who are restrained in the way of Allah," etc., they were here in the way of Allah.

* *

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: those whom the polytheists restrained, preventing them from acting freely.

Those who said this:

6217 - Musa ibn Harun related to me, saying: 'Amr related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi: "For the poor who are restrained in the way of Allah," the polytheists restrained them in Medina.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: Had the interpretation of the verse been as al-Suddi interpreted it, the wording would have been: "For the poor who have been restrained (huṣirū) in the way of Allah," but it is "uḥṣirū," which indicates that their fear of the enemy brought these poor to the state in which they restrained themselves — while being in the way of Allah — not that the enemy were the ones restraining them.

It is only said of one whom the enemy has held back: "the enemy restrained him" (ḥaṣarahu al-'aduww). When a man is held back out of fear of the enemy, it is said: "fear of the enemy restrained him" (aḥṣarahu khawfu al-'aduww). [[See the explanation of this in what preceded, 4: 21–26.]]

* *

The interpretation of His words: ﴿They cannot move about in the land﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By this, His mention, exalted is He, means: they cannot move about in the land, or travel through the regions, seeking livelihood and pursuing gains, so that they might be independent of charity, out of dread of the enemy and fear for themselves from them. As:

6218 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to me, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah: "They cannot move about in the land" — they restrained themselves in the way of Allah for the enemy, so they cannot trade.

6219 - Musa related to me, saying: 'Amr related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi: "They cannot move about in the land," meaning trade.

6220 - Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said concerning His words: "They cannot move about in the land," each of them could not go out seeking of Allah's bounty.

* *

The interpretation of His words: ﴿The ignorant man thinks them wealthy because of their restraint﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By this is meant: "The ignorant man" who does not know their affair and condition thinks them "wealthy" because of their abstention from asking, and their refraining from reaching for what is in people's hands, out of patient endurance of hardship and adversity. As:

6221 - Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah concerning His words: "The ignorant man thinks them wealthy," he says: the ignorant man, regarding their affair, thinks them wealthy because of their restraint. [[The report: 6221 — in the printed edition and the manuscript the isnad read: "as Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us..." the copyist dropped from the isnad "Bishr related to us, saying," which I have added as it is; it is a chain that recurs throughout the tafsir, the nearest instance being no. 6206.]]

* *

By His words "because of their restraint" is meant: from abstaining from asking people.

* *

It is "tafa''ul" from "'iffah" (chastity/abstention) from a thing, and "'iffah" from a thing is leaving it, as Ru'bah said:

"So he abstained from its secrets after the 'asaq"

meaning: he became free of it and avoided it.

* *

The interpretation of His words: ﴿You know them by their mark﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By this, His mention, exalted is He, means: "You know them," O Muhammad, "by their mark," meaning by their sign and traces, from the words of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Their mark is in their faces, from the trace of prostration﴾ [Surah al-Fath: 29]. This is the dialect of Quraysh. Some Arabs say "bi-sima'ihim" with a long vowel.

As for Thaqif and some of Asad, they say "bi-simi'ihim"; and from this is the saying of the poet: [[He is Ibn 'Unqa' al-Fazari, and 'Unqa' was his mother; his name has been disputed...]]

"A youth whom Allah has adorned with beauty in his youth... he has a mark that does not offend the eye"

[[This appears in the tafsir 4: 55 / 8: 141 (Bulaq)... The verse "la tashuqqu 'ala al-basar" means: it does not offend or annoy the eye, but rather delights the eye and gladdens the soul.]]

* *

The people of interpretation have differed concerning the "sima" that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said belongs to these poor whose description He gave, and by which they are recognized.

Some of them said: it is humility and modesty.

Those who said this:

6222 - Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, from 'Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid concerning His words: "You know them by their mark," he said: humility.

6223 - al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah related to us, saying: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

6224 - al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far related to us, from his father, from Layth, who said: Mujahid used to say: it is humility.

* *

Others said: the meaning is: you know them by the sign of poverty and the strain of need in their faces.

Those who said this:

6225 - Musa related to me, saying: 'Amr related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi: "You know them by their mark," by the mark of poverty upon them.

6226 - al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Ishaq related to us, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far related to us, from his father, from al-Rabi' concerning His words: "You know them by their mark," he says: the strain of need is recognized in their faces.

* *

Others said: the meaning is: you know them by the shabbiness of their clothing. They said: hunger is hidden.

Those who said this:

6227 - Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: "You know them by their mark," he said: the mark is the shabbiness of their clothing; hunger is hidden from people, and the clothes in which they go out could not hide it from people. [[What is between the parentheses is an addition that is necessary for the sentence to be sound.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of the sayings on this is that it should be said: Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, informed His Prophet (ﷺ) that he recognizes them by their signs and the traces of need upon them. The Prophet (ﷺ) perceived those signs and traces from them upon direct observation, and so he and his companions recognized them by them, just as a sick person is perceived to be sick by inspection.

It is possible that that mark was humility on their part, or that it was the trace of need and harm, or that it was the shabbiness of their clothing, or that it was all of that. The signs of need and the traces of harm in a person are perceived, and it is known that they arise from need and harm, by observation rather than by description. For the sick person may, in some states of his illness, bear the marks of illness akin to the traces of exertion from destitution and need; and a wealthy man of abundant property may wear shabby clothing and dress in the manner of the needy, so that nothing of that by its description indicates that the one so described is afflicted and in want. One only knows that by his mark upon observation, just as Allah described them — a parallel to how one knows that someone is sick upon observation, without being described by his condition.

* *

The interpretation of His words: ﴿They do not beg of people importunately﴾

Abu Ja'far said: It is said: "The beggar has pressed (alhafa) in his asking," when he insists, "and he presses in it with pressing (ilhāfan)."

* *

If one says: Did these people ask people without pressing?

It is said: It is not permissible that they asked people anything in the manner of charity, either with pressing or without pressing, for Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, described them as people of abstention, and that they were recognized only by their mark. Had asking been their practice, their description would not have been abstention, and the Prophet (ﷺ) would have had no need to know them by proofs and signs, and the open asking would have revealed their state and affair.

And in the report that:

6228 - Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, from Hilal ibn Husn, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: We were once in want, and it was said to me: "If you went to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and asked him!" So I set out to him, bent over, and the first thing he said to me was: "Whoever seeks to be chaste, Allah will keep him chaste; whoever seeks to be independent, Allah will make him independent; and whoever asks us, we do not withhold from him anything we can find." He said: I returned to myself and said: Should I not seek to be chaste so that Allah keeps me chaste! So I returned, and after that I did not ask the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) for anything of a matter of need, until the world inclined upon us and drowned us, except whom Allah protected. [[The hadith: 6228 — its isnad is sound.]]

Hilal ibn Hisn, brother of the Banu Murra ibn Abbad, of the Banu Qays ibn Tha'laba: a trustworthy Successor (tabi'i). Ibn Hibban mentioned him in al-Thiqat, p. 364, and al-Bukhari included him in al-Kabir 4/2/204, and Ibn Abi Hatim in 4/2/73, and neither of them mentioned any criticism of him. He is also listed in al-Ta'jil, p. 434.

The hadith was narrated by Ahmad in al-Musnad: 14221 and 14222 (vol. 3, p. 44, Halabi edition), from Muhammad ibn Ja'far and Hajjaj, and then from Husayn ibn Muhammad, all three from Shu'ba, from Abu Hamza, from Hilal ibn Hisn, from Abu Sa'id, who related something similar to it but more extensive.

This chain is also sound (sahih).

Abu Hamza is al-Basri, "the neighbour of Shu'ba," and he is known by this description. His name is Abd al-Rahman ibn Abd Allah al-Mazini; he is trustworthy, and he is listed in al-Tahdhib 6:219.

It is established in the biography of Hilal ibn Hisn, in al-Kabir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Thiqat and al-Ta'jil, that Abu Hamza also narrated from him. The scholar Shaykh Abd al-Rahman al-Yamani, who edited al-Tarikh al-Kabir, doubted the soundness of this, and suggested that the correct reading might be "Abu Jamra," meaning Nasr ibn Imran al-Dab'i. However, this doubt is removed by the fact that in the Musnad too it is "Abu Hamza," which agrees with what is established in the biographical works.

"A'waza al-rajul fa-huwa mu'awwaz": his condition became bad and poverty befell him.

"A'naqa al-rajul ila al-shay' ya'naqu": he hastened towards it with haste.

* *

[Context of the discussion: "And in the report ... the clear indication ..."]

The clear indication that abstinence (ta'affuf) is a meaning that negates the asking of people from the same person, and that whoever is described as abstinent is not described as asking, whether persistently or not persistently. [In the manuscript and the printed edition, in both places: "ilhafan wa ghayr ilhaf" with a waw; see the earlier footnote no. 1, p. 598.]

* *

If someone says: If the matter is as you have described, then what is the meaning of His words "they do not ask people persistently," when they do not ask people persistently or non-persistently? [In the manuscript and the printed edition, in both places: "ilhafan wa ghayr ilhaf" with a waw; see the earlier footnote no. 1, p. 598.]

It is said to him: The reason for that is that when God, may His remembrance be exalted, described them as abstinent, and informed His servants that they are by no means people who ask, by His words "the ignorant man thinks them wealthy because of their abstinence," and that they are recognised only by their mark, He added to His servants, to make their situation clear and to praise them well, the negation of the greed and humble importuning that occur among those who ask persistently. ["Al-su'al" is the plural of sa'il, on the pattern of "jahil and juhhal." The context is: "by the negation of greed ... from them."]

Some of those who spoke used to say: [In the printed edition: "wa qal: kana ba'd al-qa'ilin yaqulu fi dhalika nazira qawl al-qa'il" is a very faulty statement. In the manuscript: "wa qala kada ba'd al-qa'ilin yaqulu ..." and the rest as in the printed edition, which is even more defective and corrupt. The correct wording is what I have inferred and adopted. What Abu Ja'far related here is the saying of al-Farra' in Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1:181, as was mentioned earlier on p. 598, note 1.] That is like the saying of the speaker: "Rarely have I seen the like of so-and-so!" Perhaps he has never seen anyone like him, nor any equal.

* *

In accordance with what we have said about the meaning of ilhaf, the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have spoken.

Those who said that:

6229 - Musa ibn Harun narrated to me, saying: Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding "they do not ask people persistently": he said: they do not press in asking.

6230 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words "they do not ask people persistently," he said: it is the one who presses in asking.

6231 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His words "they do not ask people persistently": it was related to us that the Prophet (ﷺ) used to say: "Indeed God loves the forbearing, wealthy, abstinent one, and hates the wealthy, obscene, shameless one who asks and presses." He said: It was also related to us that the Prophet (ﷺ) used to say: Indeed God, the Mighty and Majestic, disliked three things for you: "qila wa qala" (idle talk), wasting wealth, and excessive asking. So if you wish, you will see him in idle talk all his day and the beginning of his night, until he is thrown a corpse on his bed, and God does not grant him any portion of his day or night. And if you wish, you will see him possessing wealth [which he spends] on his desires, pleasures and amusements, [and it diverts him] from the right of God; that is the wasting of wealth. And if you wish, you will see him stretching out his arms, asking people with his palms; if he is given, he exaggerates in praising them, and if he is refused, he exaggerates in blaming them. [Bracketed words supplied from the printed edition and al-Durr al-Manthur 1:363, as the manuscript has a gap here; the text is otherwise incomplete.]

[The dots indicate that the copyist omitted a passage whose content we do not know. In the manuscript, after the preceding report 6231, comes the following report 6232: "Yaqub ibn Ibrahim narrated to us ...". The editor of the printed edition noticed this and considered that the following report belongs to the commentary on the verse he has inserted, and we have followed him in this. What is beyond doubt is that a portion of the commentary on this passage has dropped out here: the explanation of the rest of the verse "and whatever good you spend, indeed God knows it," and something before and after it. I could not find a source in another book to guide me to it, but the context of the sayings Tabari cites points to this lacuna. This is further evidence of the copyist's serious error at this point in the book.]

The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Those who spend their wealth by night and by day, secretly and openly, they shall have their reward with their Lord, and there shall be no fear for them, nor shall they grieve.﴾ (2:274)

[Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said]:

..........................................................................

..........................................................................

* *

6232 - Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim related to us, saying: Mu'tamir related to us, from Ayman ibn Nabil, who said: A shaykh from Ghafiq told me: Abu al-Darda' used to look at horses tied between the baradhin (common horses) and the hujun (crossbred horses), and he would say: "The people of these - meaning the horses - are among those who spend their wealth by night and by day, secretly and openly; so they shall have their reward with their Lord, and there shall be no fear for them, nor shall they grieve." [[Report 6232 - Ayman ibn Nabil al-Habashi (Abu 'Imran al-Makki, resident of Asqalan, client of the family of Abu Bakr). He narrated from Qudamah ibn Abd Allah al-Amiri, from his father Nabil, al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, and Tawus. Narrating from him were Musa ibn Uqbah, who was of his generation, Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman, Waki', Ibn Mahdi, Abd al-Razzaq, and others. He is trustworthy (thiqah), and he had a slight speech impediment in his speech. He lived until the caliphate of al-Mahdi. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib.

Al-baradhin is the plural of baradhun (with a kasra on the ba', sukun on the ra', fatha on the dhal, and sukun on the waw): it is what is produced among horses from non-Arab (ʿirab) stock; it is inferior to the purebred horse (faras) and weaker than it. Al-hujun is the plural of hajin: it is a horse born of a baradhuna (mare of the baradhin type) by a non-Arab stallion; it is likewise not of the noble (ʿatiq) breed, and both are regarded as defective among them.]]

* *

Others said: By this is meant people who spent in the way of God without extravagance or stinginess.

Mention of who said this:

6233 - Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding his words: "Those who spend their wealth" up to "nor shall they grieve": these are the people of Paradise.

It was mentioned to us that the Prophet ﷺ used to say: "The most numerous (in wealth) are the lowest." They said: "O Prophet of God, except for whom?" He said: "The most numerous are the lowest." They said: "O Prophet of God, except for whom?" He said: "The most numerous are the lowest." They said: "O Prophet of God, except for whom?" until they feared that it had passed and there was no returning from it, until he said: "Except for one who says with his wealth, thus and thus, to his right and to his left, and thus before him, and thus behind him, and they are few." [[The words between the brackets are an addition that is necessary, for the following statement is undoubtedly the speech of Qatadah; al-Suyuti likewise cited it in al-Durr al-Manthur (1:363), saying: "Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir transmitted from Qatadah..." and he related this following portion of this report. As for its beginning, it is a mursal report, like the other earlier reports.]] These are people who spent in the way of God which He obligated and approved, without wastefulness, impoverishment, squandering, or corruption. [[His words "impoverishment" (iamlaq) derive from the expression "malaqa al-rajul ma ma'ahu malaqan, wa amlaqahu imlaqan," meaning when he spent it, expelled it from his hand, did not withhold it, and squandered it. Poverty follows spending and squandering, so they used the term of the cause in place of the effect, saying: "amlaqa al-rajul imlaqan" when he became poor, so he is "mumlaq," meaning a poor man with nothing with him.]]

* *

It has been said that these verses, from His words "If you show your charities, it is good" up to "nor shall they grieve," were among what was acted upon before the revelation of the taxation details in Surat Bara'ah (al-Tawbah). When Bara'ah was revealed, they were restricted to it.

Mention of who said this:

6234 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: My father related to me, saying: My paternal uncle related to me, saying: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas: "If you show your charities, it is good" up to "nor shall they grieve." This was acted upon before Bara'ah was revealed; when Bara'ah was revealed with the obligations of charity and their details, charities ended with it.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 275:

The explanation of His, may He be exalted, saying: ﴿Those who consume interest do not stand [before Allah on the Day of Resurrection] except as one stands who is being beaten by Satan into insanity.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His praise be exalted, He means: those who practise riba (increase).

* *

"Al-irba'" (increase) is an addition to a thing. It is said of it: "Arba fulan 'ala fulan" when he exceeds him, "yurbi irba'an." The increase itself is "al-riba." "Raba al-shay'" when a thing increases beyond what it was and grows, "fa-huwa yarbu rabwan." The elevated mound (rabiyah) is so called only because of its increase in size and its rising above the level land around it, from the saying "raba yarbu." From this is said: "Fulan fi rabawat qawmihi," meaning he is in an elevated and honoured position among them. So the root of "riba" is excess and increase; then it is said "arba fulan," i.e. he made his wealth excessive when he made it grow. It is only said of the one who gives interest, "murbin," because he multiplies the money which he had owed to his debtor immediately, or because he adds to it on account of the term he postpones for him, increasing it for its term, which he had before the debt fell due. Therefore He, may His praise be exalted, said: ﴿O you who believe, do not consume interest, doubled and redoubled.﴾ [Al 'Imran: 130].

* *

Those who interpret (the Qur'an) have said the same as what we have said on this:

Mention of those who said that:

6235 - Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, from 'Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said, concerning the riba which God forbade: In the Jahiliyyah a man would have a debt owed to him by another man, and he would say: "For you such-and-such, and you postpone (payment) for me!" and so he would postpone it for him.

- Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, similarly.

6237 - Bishr narrated to me, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: that the riba of the people of Jahiliyyah was: a man sells a sale for a specified term, and when the term falls due and his companion does not have payment, he increases it and postpones it for him.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: So He, may His praise be exalted, said: Those who practise the riba whose description we have given, in this world, "do not stand" in the Hereafter from their graves, "except as one stands who is beaten by Satan with madness," meaning by this: whom Satan confounds in this world, (confound: corrupts his intellect and his limbs), and who strangles him and throws him down, "from the touch," meaning: from madness.

And as those who interpret (the Qur'an) have said the same as we have said on this:

Mention of those who said that:

6238 - Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, from 'Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning the saying of God, mighty and majestic: "Those who consume riba do not stand except as one stands who is beaten by Satan with madness": on the Day of Resurrection, for consuming riba in this world.

6239 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, similarly.

6240 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Al-Hajjaj ibn al-Minhal narrated to us, saying: Rabi'ah ibn Kulthum narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to me, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas: "Those who consume riba do not stand except as one stands who is beaten by Satan with madness", he said: that is when he is raised from his grave.

6241 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Muslim ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, saying: Rabi'ah ibn Kulthum narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to me, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: It will be said on the Day of Resurrection to the consumer of riba: "Take your weapon for war," and he recited: "do not stand except as one stands who is beaten by Satan with madness," he said: that is when he is raised from his grave.

6242 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Ash'ath, from Ja'far, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr: "Those who consume riba do not stand except as one stands who is beaten by Satan with madness", the verse; he said: The consumer of riba will be raised on the Day of Resurrection as a madman being strangled.

6243 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning his saying: "Those who consume riba do not stand", the verse; and that is the sign of the people of riba on the Day of Resurrection: they are raised with an affliction from Satan upon them.

6244 - Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, concerning his saying: "do not stand except as one stands who is beaten by Satan with madness", he said: it is the derangement which Satan inflicts through madness.

6245 - It was narrated to me from 'Ammar, who said: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi', concerning his saying: "Those who consume riba do not stand except as one stands who is beaten by Satan with madness", he said: they will be raised on the Day of Resurrection with an affliction from Satan upon them. And it is in some readings: ﴿do not stand on the Day of Resurrection﴾.

6246 - Al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abu Zuhayr narrated to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, concerning his saying: "Those who consume riba do not stand except as one stands who is beaten by Satan with madness", he said: whoever dies while consuming riba will be raised on the Day of Resurrection staggering, like one whom Satan beats with madness.

6247 - Musa narrated to me, saying: 'Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "Those who consume riba do not stand except as one stands who is beaten by Satan with madness", he said: meaning: from madness.

6248 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning his saying: "Those who consume riba do not stand except as one stands who is beaten by Satan with madness". He said: this is their likeness on the Day of Resurrection; they will not stand on the Day of Resurrection with the people except as one stands who is strangled among the people, as if he were strangled, as if he were mad.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The meaning of His saying: "whom Satan beats with the touch", is: whom He confounds through his touching him. It is said of it: "The man has been touched and seized, so he is one touched and seized," all of which applies when the afflicting madness (lamam) attacks him and he goes mad. From this is the saying of God, mighty and majestic: ﴿Indeed, those who fear God, when a visitation from Satan touches them, remember﴾ [Al A'raf: 201]. And from it is the saying of al-A'sha:

"And she wakes after the fatigue of the night's journey, as if a madness (awlaq) from the phantom jinn had visited her."

Ruled out for the "madness" in that verse, the poet's praise of his she-camel: the sense of the line is that her vigour, after the long night's march, is so great that it is as if she were possessed.

* *

If someone says to us: "What do you say of one who does what God has forbidden of riba in his trade but does not consume it: does he deserve this threat from God?"

It is said: Yes. The intent in this verse is not only eating, but those to whom these verses were revealed at the time of revelation, their sustenance and food came from riba; so He mentions them by their description, magnifying through that the matter of riba against them, and disparaging to them the state they were in regarding their food. And in His saying, may His praise be exalted: ﴿O you who believe, fear God and leave what remains of riba, if you are believers. And if you do not, then be warned of war from God and His Messenger﴾ [Al Baqarah: 278-279], the verse, there is what indicates the soundness of what we have said on this, and that the prohibition from God concerning this applied to all meanings of riba, and that practising it, consuming it, taking it and giving it are equal.

[The commentator's note on the present-day situation: people of sedition in our time try to make light of the matter of riba for people, though God has magnified and disparaged it, and announced to whoever practises it war from God and His Messenger, in this world and the next.] As the traditions from the Messenger of God (ﷺ) have been widely reported, in his saying:

6249 - "May God curse the consumer of riba, its feeder, its writer, and its two witnesses, if they know of it."

* *

The explanation of His saying: ﴿That is because they said: "Trade is only like riba."﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By "that", may His praise be exalted, He means: that which He described them with, of standing on the Day of Resurrection from their graves like one whom Satan beats with madness. He, may He be exalted in remembrance, said: this which we mentioned, that it befalls them on the Day of Resurrection of the ugliness of their state, the desolation of their standing from their graves, and the evil that befell them, is because they used to lie and fabricate in this world and say: "Trade is only" like what God has made lawful for His servants, "like riba." That is because those among the people of Jahiliyyah who consumed riba, when one of them was owed money by his debtor and it fell due, the debtor would say to the creditor: "Increase me in the term and I will increase you in your money." It would be said to the two of them, when they did that: "This is riba, which is not lawful." When that was said to them they said: "It is the same for us whether we increase at the start of the sale or at the due date of the money!" So God refuted them in their saying, and said: "And God has made trade lawful."

* *

The explanation of His, may He be exalted, saying: ﴿But God has permitted trade and forbidden riba. Whoever has received an admonition from his Lord and desists, for him is what is past, and his affair is with God. But whoever returns, those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein forever.﴾ (2:275)

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His praise be exalted, means: God has made lawful the profits in commerce, buying and selling, "and forbidden riba," meaning the increase which the owner of money takes by reason of his debtor's increase of the term and his postponement of the debt owed to him. He, mighty and majestic, says: the two increases are not equal, one of which comes from the aspect of sale and the other from the aspect of postponing money and increasing the term. For I have forbidden the one, which comes from postponing money and increasing the term, and I have permitted the other, which is the increase over the capital with which the seller bought the goods he sells, so that he takes its surplus. So God, mighty and majestic, said: the increase from the aspect of sale is not the equivalent of the increase from the aspect of riba, because I have made sale lawful and forbidden riba, and the command is My command and the creation is My creation; I decide among them as I wish and I make them serve as I desire; none of them has the right to object to My judgement or to oppose My command, and upon them is only obedience to Me and submission to My ruling.

* *

Then He, may His praise be exalted, said: "Whoever has received an admonition from his Lord and desists," meaning by "admonition": the reminder and warning with which He reminded and frightened them in the verses of the Qur'an, and threatened them for their consumption of riba with punishment. He, may His praise be exalted, says: whoever receives that and "desists" from consuming riba, and refrains from practising it and holds back from it, "for him is what is past," meaning: what he consumed and took and it has passed, before the coming of the admonition and the prohibition from his Lord concerning it; "and his affair is with God," meaning: the affair of its consumer after the coming of the admonition from his Lord and the prohibition, and after he desists from consuming it, is with God in His protection and guidance: if He wills, He protects him from consuming it and keeps him steadfast in his desisting from it; and if He wills, He forsakes him in that. "But whoever returns," he says: whoever returns to consuming riba after the prohibition, and says what he used to say before the coming of the admonition from God by the prohibition, namely his saying: "Trade is only like riba," "those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein forever," meaning: those who do that and say that are the people of the Fire, meaning the fire of Hell, abiding therein.

* *

In a similar way to what we have said on this, the people of interpretation have said.

Mention of those who said that:

6250 - Musa narrated to me, saying: 'Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "Whoever has received an admonition from his Lord and desists, for him is what is past and his affair is with God": as for the "admonition", it is the Qur'an; and as for "what is past", it is what he consumed of riba.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 276:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, saying: ﴿Allah deprives usury of blessing, and gives increase for charities. And Allah loves not any ungrateful sinner﴾ (2:276).

Abu Ja'far said: By His saying, may He be mighty and majestic, "Allah deprives usury (al-riba) of blessing," He means: Allah diminishes usury and takes it away, as:

6251 - Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn Abbas said regarding "Allah deprives usury (yamhaqu Allahu al-riba)": he diminishes it.

* *

This is parallel to the report narrated from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he said:

6252 - "Usury, though it increases, its end is to decline." [[6252 - Recorded by al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak 2:37, through Israil, from al-Rukayn ibn al-Rabi', from his father al-Rabi' ibn Umaylah, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Usury, if it increases, its consequence leads to decline." Ibn Kathir also mentioned it from the Musnad through Shurayk, from al-Rukayn ibn al-Rabi', in its wording. Then he related what Ibn Majah narrated. However, Ibn Kathir (2:61) transmitted the wording of al-Tabari and related the report as it stands in the hadith, not as it appears in the printed and manuscript copies. See also al-Durr al-Manthur 1:365.]]

* *

As for His saying, "and gives increase for charities (wa yurbi al-sadaqat)," He, may His praise be exalted, means that He multiplies their reward, increasing it (yarubbuha) and developing it for him (yunammiha lahu).
[[In the manuscript and printed text: "He multiplies its reward for its owner (li-rabbiha)," as if he means for its owner; and the correct reading appears to be what was established: "rabb" (lord) of the benefaction, favour, and blessing, and other things – "yuriha rabban" – and "rabbabahu" (all with the doubled letter): he developed it, increased it and completed it. The clause "yurbiha wa yunammiha lahu" is an explanation of His saying "yudaʿifu ajraha." See the following report no. 6253.]]

* *

We have already explained the meaning of "al-riba" (usury) and "al-irbaʾ" (increase) earlier, and their root, sufficiently without repeating it. [[See what has passed shortly before, p. 7.]]

* *

If someone says to us: How does Allah give increase to charities?
It is said: By multiplying the reward for its owner, as He, may His praise be exalted, said: ﴿The likeness of those who spend their wealth in the way of Allah is as the likeness of a grain that grows seven ears, in every ear a hundred grains﴾ (2:261), and as He said: ﴿Who is it that would lend Allah a goodly loan, so that He may multiply it for him manifold?﴾ (2:245), and as:

6253 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, saying: Abbad ibn Mansur narrated to us, from al-Qasim: that he heard Abu Hurayrah say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah, mighty and majestic, accepts charity and takes it with His right hand, and He nurtures it for one of you as one of you nurtures his foal, until the morsel becomes like Uhud. And the confirmation of this in the Book of Allah, mighty and majestic, is: ﴿Did they not know that Allah is He who accepts repentance from His servants and takes charities?﴾ (9:104), and ﴿Allah deprives usury of blessing, and gives increase for charities﴾." [[Hadith 6253 - Abbad ibn Mansur al-Naji al-Basri al-Qadi: trustworthy; whoever spoke of him spoke without proof. We have verified his reliability in the commentary on the Musnad, and shown the error of those who criticised him without right.
Al-Qasim: he is Ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr al-Siddiq, the trustworthy, jurist, imam among the Successors.
The hadith will come in the commentary on Surah al-Tawbah (vol. 11, p. 15, Bulaq), from Abu Kurayb, with this chain, but "Waki' narrated to us" has dropped out there, which is a clear error.
Ahmad related it in the Musnad (no. 10090; 2:371, Halabi), from Waki', and from Isma'il – Ibn Ulayyah – both from Abbad ibn Mansur, with this chain, and gave it in the wording of Waki', as in al-Tabari's report here.
But a strange error occurred in the Musnad in the recitation of the first verse: it has "He it is who accepts repentance from His servants and takes charities." The verse recited in the hadith is that in al-Tabari's report here: "Did they not know that Allah is He who accepts repentance from His servants and takes charities," which is verse 104 of Surah al-Tawbah. The other is verse 25 of Surah al-Shura, whose recitation is: "He it is who accepts repentance from His servants and pardons evil deeds," and it is not the proof-point in this hadith.
This error is old in the copies of the Musnad, from early copyists, as shown by the fact that this error also appears in Hafiz Ibn Kathir's transmission of this hadith from the Musnad, in Jami' al-Masanid wa al-Sunan 7:320 (photographed manuscript).
Indeed, it became clear to me afterwards that the error is older than this. Perhaps it is from Waki' or from Abbad ibn Mansur, because al-Tirmidhi related the hadith (2:23), from Abu Kurayb – the teacher of al-Tabari here – from Waki', with it, and the error of the recitation of the verse is preserved in it, like Ahmad's report from Waki'. Al-Mubarakfuri, its commentator, quoted from Hafiz al-Iraqi that he said: "In this there is confusion from some narrators. The correct wording is: 'Did they not know that Allah is He who accepts repentance,' etc. We have related it in the Book of Zakat of Yusuf al-Qadi, in the correct form."
Indeed, Hafiz al-Mundhiri also overlooked this error: he mentioned the hadith in al-Targhib wa al-Tarhib (2:19), from al-Tirmidhi's transmission, and mentioned the verse as in the Musnad and al-Tirmidhi – contrary to the recitation.
If that is so, I incline to think that Abu Ja'far al-Tabari, may Allah have mercy on him, heard it from Abu Kurayb, from Waki', as in al-Tirmidhi's report from Abu Kurayb and Ahmad's report from Waki'; he did not consider it permissible to cite the verse with the error in its recitation, so he cited it correctly. In that he was right, excelled and did well.
Al-Tirmidhi said after relating it: "This is a hasan sahih hadith. It has been related from Aisha from the Prophet (ﷺ), something similar to this."
The report of Aisha will come: 6255.
Ibn Kathir mentioned it in his Tafsir (2:62), from the transmission of Ibn Abi Hatim in his Tafsir, from Amr ibn Abdullah al-Awdi, from Waki', with this chain, but he did not mention the first verse in which the error occurred.
al-Suyuti mentioned it (1:365), and added its attribution to al-Shafi'i, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Khuzaymah, Ibn al-Mundhir, and al-Daraqutni in al-Sifat.
Ahmad also related it (no. 9234), from Khalaf ibn al-Walid, from al-Mubarak – that is Ibn Fudalah – from Abd al-Wahid ibn Sabrah and Abbad ibn Mansur, from al-Qasim, from Abu Hurayrah – he related it in similar wording, abridged, and did not mention the two verses in it.
Ibn Kathir (2:62) pointed to this Musnad report, but confusion by copyists occurred in it.
The hadith will come with a similar meaning, lengthy and abridged, from Abu Hurayrah: 6254, 6256, 6257, and from Aisha: 6255.
We shall indicate the rest of its takhrij at its end: 6257.]]

6254 - Sulayman ibn Umar ibn Khalid al-Aqta' narrated to me, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Abbad ibn Mansur, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Abu Hurayrah – and I do not think he attributed it except to the Prophet – he said: "Indeed Allah, mighty and majestic, accepts charity, and accepts only the good." [[Hadith 6254 - Sulayman ibn Umar ibn Khalid al-Aqta', al-Qurashi al-Amiri al-Raqqi: Ibn Abi Hatim gave him a biography (2/1/131) and mentioned that his father wrote from him. He mentioned no criticism of him.
Ibn al-Mubarak is Abdullah. Sufyan is al-Thawri.
The hadith is an abridgement of the preceding one. The doubt about its being attributed to the Prophet here does no harm, since the hadith is established as marfu' by the previous chain and the other chains.
The hadith will also come with this chain (vol. 11, p. 15, Bulaq), but its wording is not given there; only its beginning is mentioned, then he said: "then he mentioned something similar," referring to the previous hadith. It seems he related it there in full, but without giving its complete context.
Ibn Kathir, in the commentary on Surah al-Tawbah (4:235), pointed to this report and the one before it, making them one hadith, from al-Thawri and Waki', from Abbad ibn Mansur, with it. But he did not mention its takhrij.]]

6255 - Muhammad ibn Umar ibn Ali al-Muqaddami narrated to me, saying: Rayhan ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Abbad narrated to us, from al-Qasim, from Aisha, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah, blessed and exalted, accepts charity, and accepts from it only the good, and He nurtures it for its owner as one of you nurtures his colt or his weaned young camel, until the morsel becomes like Uhud. And the confirmation of this in the Book of Allah, mighty and majestic, is: ﴿Allah deprives usury of blessing, and gives increase for charities﴾." [[Hadith 6255 - Muhammad ibn Umar ibn Ali ibn Ata' ibn Muqaddam, al-Muqaddami al-Basri: trustworthy, given a biography in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir (1/1/179) and Ibn Abi Hatim (4/1/21). In the printed text here there is an error in his father's name: "Amr" instead of "Umar." It occurs with greater confusion in the printed text later (6809), thus: "Muhammad ibn Amr and Ibn Ali from Ata al-Muqaddami"!!
"Al-Muqaddami" is with a shadda on the unvowelled dal, a nisba to his great-grandfather "Muqaddam."
Rayhan ibn Sa'id al-Naji al-Basri: among the teachers of Ahmad and Ishaq. Yahya ibn Ma'in said: "I see no harm in him." Some spoke of him, but al-Bukhari gave him a biography in al-Kabir (2/1/301) and mentioned no criticism. He was the imam of the mosque of Abbad ibn Mansur, as in al-Kabir and Ibn Abi Hatim (1/2/517). Ibn Hibban and al-Ajli criticised, with disapproval, some of what he related from Abbad; perhaps he knew him best, since he was the imam of his mosque.
Whatever the case, he did not stand alone against Abbad in this report, as will appear from the takhrij.
Ahmad related it in the Musnad (6:251, Halabi), from Abd al-Samad, from Hammad, from Thabit, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Aisha: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: Indeed Allah nurtures for one of you a date or a morsel, as one of you nurtures his colt or his weaned young camel, until it becomes like Uhud."
This is a sahih chain, but the hadith is abridged.
Likewise Ibn Hibban related it in his Sahih (5:234–235, from the manuscript of al-Ihsan), through Abd al-Samad, from Hammad ibn Salamah, from Thabit al-Bunani, from al-Qasim.
Al-Bazzar related it at length, through Yahya ibn Sa'id, from Amrah, from Aisha – and through al-Dahhak ibn Uthman, from Abu Hurayrah, in similar wording to al-Tabari's report here, except that he did not mention the verse at its end. Ibn Kathir transmitted this (2:62–63).
But al-Dahhak ibn Uthman's report from Abu Hurayrah is munqati', because he only relates from the Successors.
Al-Haythami mentioned it in Majma' al-Zawa'id (3:111) in abridged form like the Musnad report, and said: "Al-Tabarani related it in al-Awsat, and its narrators are the narrators of the Sahih." Then he mentioned it at length (3:112) and said: "Al-Bazzar related it, and its narrators are trustworthy," but he mentioned it only from the hadith of Aisha alone.
Al-Suyuti mentioned the wording of al-Tabari here (1:365), then was lax in its attribution, ascribing it to al-Bazzar, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Hibban, and al-Tabarani.]]

6256 - Muhammad ibn Abd al-Malik narrated to me, saying: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, saying: Ma'mar narrated to us, from Ayyub, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, when a servant gives charity from something good, Allah accepts it from him, takes it with His right hand, and nurtures it as one of you nurtures his colt or his weaned young camel. And indeed a man gives charity with a morsel, and it grows in the hand of Allah" – or he said: "in the palm of Allah, mighty and majestic" – "until it becomes like Uhud. So give charity." [[Hadith 6256 - "Muhammad ibn Abd al-Malik": my preference is that he is "Muhammad ibn Abd al-Malik ibn Zanjawayh al-Baghdadi," for he relates from Abd al-Razzaq, and he is of the generation of al-Tabari's teachers, though I have not found an explicit text showing that he related from him. But he is a Baghdadi like him, so it is very probable that he related from him; indeed this is the most common case in such situations. He is trustworthy; al-Nasa'i and others declared him reliable. Given a biography in al-Tahdhib and Ibn Abi Hatim (4/1/5), and Tarikh Baghdad (2:345–346).
Among al-Tabari's teachers whom he related from in the History is "Muhammad ibn Abd al-Malik ibn Abi al-Shawarib," who is also trustworthy, but it is not mentioned that he related from Abd al-Razzaq, and it is usual that such a thing be stated. He is given a biography in al-Tahdhib, Ibn Abi Hatim (4/1/5), and Tarikh Baghdad (2:344–345).
Ibn Kathir uniquely said something I do not know: when he mentioned this hadith (2:62), he said it was "related by Ibn Jarir from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Malik ibn Ishaq"!! I have not found any narrator by this name. I do not know whether this is an oversight from him or a confusion by copyists.
The hadith was related by Ahmad in the Musnad (no. 7622), from Abd al-Razzaq, with this chain.
Ibn Khuzaymah, the imam of imams, related it in Kitab al-Tawhid (p. 44), from Muhammad ibn Rafi' and Abd al-Rahman ibn Bishr ibn al-Hakam, both from Abd al-Razzaq, with it.
Al-Mundhiri mentioned in al-Targhib wa al-Tarhib (2:19) that Ibn Khuzaymah related it in his Sahih too.
Ibn Kathir quoted it from this place in al-Tabari, as we indicated, then said: "Thus Ahmad related it from Abd al-Razzaq. This is a strange chain, sound in its isnad, but its wording is strange. The preserved wording is that which preceded." He meant the report of Abbad ibn Mansur.
We do not see anything strange in this wording, nor any oddity in the isnad! It is sound by the conditions of the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim).
Moreover, Abd al-Razzaq did not stand alone in it from Ma'mar, for Muhammad ibn Thawr followed him in it. Al-Tabari related it – as will come (vol. 11, pp. 15–16, Bulaq) – from Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la, from Muhammad ibn Thawr, from Ma'mar, with it, similarly. This chain is also sound, for Muhammad ibn Thawr al-San'ani, the devout, is trustworthy; Ibn Ma'in and Abu Hatim declared him reliable, and Abu Zur'ah even preferred him over Abd al-Razzaq.]]

6257 - Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: al-Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman narrated to us, saying: I heard Yunus, from a companion of his, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, who said: Abu Hurayrah said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah, mighty and majestic, accepts charity with His right hand, and accepts from it only what is good. And Allah nurtures for one of you his morsel as one of you nurtures his colt or weaned young camel, until he meets it on the Day of Resurrection and it is greater than Uhud." [[Hadith 6257 - This chain contains an unnamed narrator, the one from whom Yunus related, and it is very probable that he is Ayyub. But the chain remains weak until evidence identifies this unnamed narrator.
As for the hadith itself, it is sound by the preceding chains and others.
The root meaning is established from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah through many routes:
Al-Bukhari related it (3:220–223, and 13:352), Muslim (1:277–278), al-Tirmidhi (2:22–23), al-Nasa'i (1:349), Ibn Majah (1842), Ibn Hibban in his Sahih (5:234–237, from the manuscript of al-Ihsan), and Ibn Khuzaymah in Kitab al-Tawhid (pp. 41–44).
Ahmad related it in the Musnad – other than what we indicated earlier: 8363 (2:331, Halabi), 8948, 8949 (pp. 381–382), 9234 (p. 404), 9413 (p. 418), 9423 (p. 419), 9561 (p. 431), 10958 (p. 538), 10992 (p. 541).
Al-Bukhari related it in al-Kabir, with the brief allusion customary for him (2/1/476).
Variants of this hadith include: "in the hand of Allah," "in the palm of Allah," "the palm of the Merciful," and similar wordings. Al-Tirmidhi said (2:23–24):
"Many people of knowledge have said, regarding this hadith and what resembles it of the reports on the Attributes, and the descent of the Lord, blessed and exalted, every night to the lowest heaven: the reports on this are established, and we believe in them, without imagining, and without saying 'how.' This was related from Malik ibn Anas, Sufyan ibn Uyaynah, and Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak, that they said regarding these hadiths: pass them on without asking how. This is also the position of the people of knowledge among the People of the Sunnah and the Community. As for the Jahmiyyah, they rejected these reports and said: this is anthropomorphism! Allah, blessed and exalted, has mentioned in more than one place in His Book: the hand, the hearing, and the sight. The Jahmiyyah interpreted these verses and explained them differently from how the people of knowledge explained them! They said: Allah did not create Adam with His hand! They said: the meaning of 'hand' is only power!! Ishaq ibn Ibrahim said: anthropomorphism occurs only if one says 'a hand like a hand,' or 'the like of a hand,' or 'hearing like hearing,' or 'the like of hearing.' If one says 'hearing like hearing' or 'the like of hearing,' this is anthropomorphism. But if one says as Allah said: hand, hearing, and sight, without saying 'how,' and without saying 'like hearing' or 'the like of hearing,' this is not anthropomorphism. It is as Allah, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿There is nothing like unto Him, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing﴾."]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: As for His saying, "and Allah loves not any ungrateful sinner (wa Allahu la yuhibbu kulla kaffarin athim)," He means by it: Allah does not love every one who persists in disbelief in his Lord, remaining upon it, considering the consumption and feeding of usury lawful, "sinner (athim)," persisting in sin in what He forbade him, such as consuming usury, unlawful things, and other of his disobediences, not restraining himself from them, nor heeding them, nor taking heed of the admonition of his Lord with which He admonished him in His revelation and the verses of His Book.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 277:

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds and establish prayer and give zakah will have their reward with their Lord, and no fear will there be concerning them, nor will they grieve.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: This is a report from Allah, mighty and majestic is He, that those who believe, meaning those who affirm belief in Allah and His Messenger, and in what he brought from their Lord, including the prohibition of riba (usury/interest) and consuming it, and other than that from all the laws of His religion, ﴿and do righteous deeds﴾, which Allah, mighty and majestic is He, commanded them to do, and which He urged them toward; ﴿and establish prayer﴾, the obligatory prayer, observing its limits, and performing it in accordance with its sunnahs; ﴿and give zakah﴾, which is obligatory upon them regarding their wealth, after what had passed from them of consuming riba before the admonition concerning it came to them from their Lord; ﴿for them is their reward﴾, meaning the reward for those deeds of theirs and their faith and their charity; ﴿with their Lord﴾ on the day they will need it in their return (to Him); ﴿and no fear will there be concerning them﴾ on that day from His punishment for what had passed from them in their jahiliyyah (pre-Islamic ignorance) and their disbelief before the admonition from their Lord came to them, concerning the consumption of what they had consumed of riba, by reason of their turning back and repentance to Allah, mighty and majestic is He, from that upon the arrival of the admonition from their Lord, and their affirmation of the promise and threat of Allah; ﴿nor will they grieve﴾ over their abandoning what they had abandoned in this world of consuming riba and acting upon it, when they witness the abundant reward of Allah, blessed and exalted is He, and they, in their abandonment of what they abandoned of that in this world, sought His pleasure in the Hereafter; so they attained what they had been promised for abandoning it.

**The interpretation of His words, exalted is He:** ﴿O you who have believed, fear Allah and give up what remains of interest (riba), if you are believers﴾ (2:278)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: By this, may His praise be exalted, He means: "O you who have believed," [meaning] who have affirmed Allah and His Messenger. "Fear Allah," [meaning] fear Allah for your own souls, so guard yourselves against Him by obeying Him in what He has commanded you and by refraining from what He has forbidden you. "And give up," meaning: leave off, "what remains of interest (riba)," [meaning] abandon seeking what remains owed to you of the excess over your principal, the capital that was yours before you charged interest on it. "If you are believers," [meaning] if you are truly fulfilling your faith in word, by affirming it with your tongues, through your deeds. [[His words "through your deeds" are connected to "truly fulfilling," i.e., truly fulfilling that through your deeds.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: It is mentioned that this verse was revealed concerning a people who embraced Islam while they had claims upon other people for interest-money (riba) that they had charged them. They had collected part of it from them, and part remained. Allah, may His praise be exalted, pardoned them for what they had already collected before the revelation of this verse, [[In the manuscript: "for what they had already collected," which is corrupt; the correct reading is what is in the printed edition.]] and He forbade them to demand what remained of it.

Those who said this:

6258. Musa ibn Harun narrated to me, saying: Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿O you who have believed, fear Allah and give up what remains of interest﴾ up to ﴿and you will not be wronged﴾: This verse was revealed concerning al-Abbas ibn Abd al-Muttalib and a man from the Banu al-Mughirah. The two were partners in the Jahiliyyah, and they used to lend at interest to some people from Thaqif, from the Banu Amr [[In the manuscript and printed edition: "they lent in interest to some people," with the past tense verb; the correct reading is what I have recorded from al-Durr al-Manthur 1:366 and al-Baghawi (in the margin of Ibn Kathir) 2:63. Al-salaf (with two fatha vowels): a loan. Its verbs: aslafa and salafa (with the lam doubled).]] — they are the Banu Amr ibn Umayr. Then Islam came while they both had great wealth in interest. So Allah revealed ﴿give up what remains﴾ of the excess that existed in the Jahiliyyah ﴿of interest﴾.

6259. Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, regarding His words ﴿O you who have believed, fear Allah and give up what remains of interest, if you are believers﴾: Thaqif had made a treaty with the Prophet (ﷺ) that whatever interest they were owed by people, and whatever interest people owed them, would be annulled. When the conquest came, he appointed Attab ibn Usayd over Makkah. The Banu Amr ibn Umayr ibn Awf used to take interest from the Banu al-Mughirah, and the Banu al-Mughirah had charged them interest in the Jahiliyyah. Then Islam came while they still had large sums owed to them. The Banu Amr came to them seeking their interest, but the Banu al-Mughirah refused to pay them under Islam, and they brought the matter to Attab ibn Usayd. Attab wrote to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and then ﴿O you who have believed, fear Allah and give up what remains of interest, if you are believers. And if you do not, then be warned of war from Allah and His Messenger﴾ up to ﴿and you will not be wronged﴾ was revealed. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) wrote with it to Attab and said: "If they consent, well and good; otherwise, warn them of war." [And] Ibn Jurayj said, from Ikrimah, regarding His words ﴿fear Allah and give up what remains of interest﴾: They used to take interest from the Banu al-Mughirah, claiming that they were Mas'ud, Abd Yalil, Habib and Rabi'ah, the sons of Amr ibn Umayr; they were the ones who held interest over the Banu al-Mughirah. Then Abd Yalil, Habib, Rabi'ah, Hilal and Mas'ud embraced Islam. [[Report 6259: See what the Hafiz said in al-Isabah in the biography of "Hilal al-Thaqafi." He said: "As for the mention of the treaty of Thaqif before His words 'Then when the conquest came,' there is something to be examined; I have explained its interpretation in the Asbab al-Nuzul (Occasions of Revelation)."]]

6260. Yahya ibn Abi Talib narrated to me, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Juwaybir narrated to us, from al-Dahhak, regarding His words ﴿fear Allah and give up what remains of interest, if you are believers﴾: It was a form of interest they used to trade in during the Jahiliyyah. When they embraced Islam, they were commanded to take their principal (ru'us amwalihim).

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 279 (part 1 of 2):

The interpretation of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿But if you do not, then be informed of a war from Allah and His Messenger﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His saying, may His praise be exalted, ﴿But if you do not﴾, He means: if you do not abandon what remains of the *riba* (usury, interest).

* *

The readers (qurra') differed concerning the recitation of His saying, ﴿then be informed of a war from Allah and His Messenger﴾.

The majority of the readers of Medina recited it as *fa-adhnū* (فَأْذَنُوْا), with the alif shortened in *fa-adhnū* and its *dhāl* vowelled with a fatha, meaning: be aware and have knowledge (of this).

Others recited it, and this is the reading of the majority of the readers of Kufa, as *fa-ādhinū* (فَآذِنُوا), with the alif of *fa-adhnū* lengthened and its *dhāl* vowelled with a kasra, meaning: inform others, let them know and tell them that you are at war with them.

Abu Ja'far said: The two readings most correct in this matter are the reading of the one who recites *fa-adhanū* with the alif shortened and the *dhāl* vowelled with a fatha, meaning: know this and be certain of it, and be in the permission (idhn) of Allah, may He be mighty, for you in this.

We chose this because Allah, may He be mighty, commanded His Prophet ﷺ to give notice to those among them who persist in their polytheism, which is not accepted to be maintained, and to kill the apostate from Islam among them in every case, unless he returns to Islam. The polytheists had informed him that they were at war with him, or they had not informed him. [[In the printed edition: "adhanahu al-mushrikūna bi-annahum ʿala ḥarbihi aw lam yadhanūhu" (أذنه المشركون بأنهم على حربه أو لم يأذنوه). That is a spelling error and, with this spelling, the meaning is corrupt. The correct spelling is in the manuscript, and it is the correct meaning.]] Since the one commanded in this matter cannot be outside one of two situations: either he was a polytheist persisting in his polytheism, which is not accepted, or he was a Muslim who apostatised and declared war. Whichever of the two it was, he was given notice of war, not that he was commanded to announce it if he resolved upon it. [[In the manuscript: "bi-l-inḏār bihā in ʿazama ʿala dhālika" (بالإنذار بها إن عزم على ذلك), which is correct in meaning, but what is in the printed edition seems more probable to me.]] Because if the matter were in his hands, and he persisted in consuming usury considering it lawful, and the Muslims did not announce war against him, they would not be obliged to fight him. Yet that is not his ruling in either of the two cases. It is thus known that he is the one who is commanded to be fought, not the one who announces it.

The exegetes (ahl al-ta'wil) interpreted it in accordance with this interpretation.

Mention of those who said that:

6261 – Al-Muthanna related to me, he said: ʿAbd Allah ibn Salih related to us, he said: Muʿawiya related to me, from ʿAli, from Ibn ʿAbbas, concerning His saying: ﴿O you who believe, fear Allah and abandon what remains of the usury﴾, to His saying: ﴿then be informed of a war from Allah and His Messenger﴾: Whoever persists in usury and does not desist from it, it is incumbent upon the leader of the Muslims to ask him to repent. If he desists, (well and good); otherwise he should strike his neck.

Abu Ja'far said: All these reports indicate that His saying, ﴿then be informed of a war from Allah﴾, is an announcement from Allah, may He be mighty, to them of war and killing, not a command to them to announce it to others.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His praise be exalted, He means: "if you repent", i.e., you abandon the consumption of usury and turn back to Allah, may He be mighty and majestic, ﴿then you shall have your principal sums﴾ from the debts that you are owed by people, without the surplus that you added to that as usury from yourselves, as (reported):

* *

The interpretation of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿You shall not wrong, nor shall you be wronged﴾ (279)

Abu Ja'far said: By His saying, "you shall not wrong", He means: by your taking your principal sums, which were yours before the usury, from your debtors, without their profits which you added as usury upon those from whom you took that from your debtors, such that you would take from them what it is not permitted for you to take, or what was not yours before. "Nor shall you be wronged" means: nor will the debtor who gives you that, apart from the usury which you had imposed upon him for the sake of the increase in the term, withhold from you a right owed to you by him, because what exceeded your principal sums was not a right owed to you by him, so that by withholding it from you he would be wronging you.

* *

Ibn ʿAbbas used to say in accordance with what we have said in this matter, and others of the exegetes as well.

Mention of those who said that:

6274 – Al-Muthanna related to me, he said: Abu Salih related to us, he said: Muʿawiya related to me, from ʿAli, from Ibn ʿAbbas: ﴿And if you repent, you shall have your principal sums, you shall not wrong﴾ — by increasing (usury), "nor shall you be wronged" — by being diminished.

6275 – Yunus related to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said concerning His saying: ﴿You shall have your principal sums, you shall not wrong nor be wronged﴾: He said: You shall not be diminished in your property, nor take unlawful gain that is not lawful for you.

* *

The interpretation of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And if the debtor is in hardship, then let there be postponement until a time of ease﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His praise be exalted, He means: "and if he is" — from those debtors from whom you collect your principal sums — "in hardship", i.e., unable to pay you your principal sums that were owed to you before the usury: "then grant him respite until a time of ease."

His saying "in hardship" (dhū ʿusra) is in the nominative case as the subject of *kāna* (was/is), and the predicate is omitted, which is what we have mentioned. The omission of its predicate is acceptable because the Arabs leave out the predicates of indefinite nouns. If *kāna* were construed in this position as a complete verb sufficient in itself, that would be a sound construction, and there would be no need for a predicate. The meaning of the speech would then be: if there is found among your debtors one who is in hardship regarding your principal sums, then let there be postponement until a time of ease.

It has been mentioned that in the reading of Ubayy ibn Kaʿb it is ﴿wa-in kāna dhā ʿusratin﴾, meaning: and if the creditor is in hardship, "then let there be postponement until a time of ease." Although this is permissible in Arabic, reciting it is not permissible in our view, because it contradicts the written form of the codices of the Muslims. [[See the Maʿani al-Qurʾan of al-Farra' 1:186.]]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿then let there be postponement (nazira)﴾, it means: you are obliged to grant him postponement until a time of ease, as He said: ﴿And whoever among you is ill or has an ailment of the head, then an expiation by fasting﴾ [Surah al-Baqara: 196]. We have explained the reason for the nominative case in similar constructions earlier, so there is no need to repeat it.

* *

"Maysara" is the *mafʿala* form from "yusr" (ease), like "marhama" and "mashʾama".

* *

The meaning of the speech: if there is among your debtors one who is in hardship, then you must grant him respite until he becomes prosperous through the debt owed to you, and so becomes one of the people of ease through it. [[In the manuscript and printed edition: "ḥattā yūsira bi-mā laysa lakum" (حتى يوسر بما ليس لكم). The editor of the printed edition guessed: "perhaps 'laysa' is an addition by the copyist." I do not think so. Rather, the phrase "bi-mā laysa" stands in the original source from which the copyist copied "bi-l-dayn" (بالدين) with its letters joined, as often happens in old manuscripts. The copyist did not read it well, read it as "bi-mā laysa", and omitted "alladhī", thinking it was an error added by a previous copyist. The correctness of what we have set down is confirmed by Tabari's own words later at the end of the tafsir of the verse. If it were read "bi-ra's mā lakum" (برأس ما لكم), it would be correct in meaning, as becomes clear from the following reports.]]

Others said: This verse is general, applying to everyone who has a right against a debtor in hardship, whatever the basis of that right, whether a lawful debt or usury. [[In the manuscript: "hādhihi al-āya ʿām" (هذه الآية عام), a copyist's error and oversight.]]
