He said: And likewise every debt owed to a Muslim: it is not lawful for a Muslim who is owed a debt by his brother, knowing him to be in hardship, to imprison him or pursue him until Allah makes it easy for him. The postponement was ordained only for lawful debts, and for this reason debts were (considered) on that basis.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 279 (part 2 of 2):

6296. Ali ibn Harb narrated to me, saying: Ibn Fudayl narrated to us, from Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas: "﴿And if the debtor is in hardship, then let there be postponement until [a time of] ease﴾" He said: "It was revealed concerning debt."

[[Report 6296: "Ali ibn Harb ibn Muhammad ibn Ali al-Ta'i." al-Nasa'i said: "Salih" (reliable). Abu Hatim said: "Saduq" (truthful). He died in the year 265 AH. His biography is in al-Tahdhib (Tahdhib al-Tahdhib).]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct view regarding His words "﴿And if the debtor is in hardship, then let there be postponement until [a time of] ease﴾" is that it refers to the creditors who had become Muslims in the time of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and who had lent money at interest (riba) in the Jahiliyyah (the pre-Islamic period), and whose debts were still outstanding when Islam reached them before they had collected them. So God commanded that the remaining interest be abolished after they had become Muslims, and that the principal of their capital be collected from those of their debtors who were well-off, or that those of their debtors who were in hardship be given postponement with respect to their principal until a time of ease. This is the ruling for everyone who became Muslim while he had interest owed to him on a debt owed by another. Islam nullifies for his debtor what he was owed on account of interest, and the creditor is required to return to him the principal he had taken from him, or which had been owed to him because of the interest added to it, if the debtor is well-off. [[The wording of the phrase "and he is required to return his principal... to him... " is continuous, and there is a break between these parts.]] If the debtor is in hardship, he is to be given postponement with respect to his creditor's principal until a time of ease, and the excess above the principal is nullified for him.

However, although the verse was revealed concerning those we have mentioned, and was meant by it, the ruling which God has decreed, namely that the creditor who is in hardship be given postponement with respect to the principal of the lender after the excess of interest has been removed from him, is a binding ruling for everyone who owes a debt to a man that has fallen due while he is unable to pay it. He is to be given postponement until his time of ease, because the debt of every creditor is owed from the wealth of his debtor, and the debtor's obligation is to pay it from his wealth, not from his person. So if his wealth is gone, the creditor has no way to seize his person by imprisonment or sale. This is because the wealth of the creditor must fall under one of three categories: either it is in the person of his debtor, or in his liability whereby he pays it from his wealth, or in a particular property belonging to him.

= If it is in a particular property of his, then once that property is lost and perishes, the creditor's debt is nullified, and no one says this.

= If it is in the person of the debtor, then once the debtor himself perishes, the creditor's debt is nullified, even if the debtor left behind an estate sufficient for his obligation and many times that. And no one says this either.

It is thus clear, since this is so, that the creditor's debt is a liability upon his debtor, to be paid from his wealth. So if his wealth is gone, the creditor has no way to seize his person, because he has lost what he was obliged to pay the creditor's right from, had it existed. And if there is no way to seize his person, there is no way to imprison him while he has nothing with which to pay his creditor's right. [[In the printed edition: "there was no way to imprison him with his right while he was destitute," with "with his right" placed earlier; I have adopted what is in the manuscript, which is a good and sound reading.]] This is because he is not withholding a right which the creditor has a way to collect, so he would not be punished by being imprisoned for delaying payment. [[In the printed edition: "so he is punished for his injustice toward him..." but in the manuscript: "so he is punished for delaying him," and the correct reading is what I have adopted. Matalla haqqahu yumatilu matalan means he delays the right; matala'a matalan means he deferred him with promises and excuses.] Moreover, Abu Ja'far, may God be pleased with him, was a man of sound argument, eloquent in speech, precise in reasoning, knowledgeable of meanings and their proper weight in opinion, and of their rightful placement in what is correct. This is a clear and decisive argument among his arguments, to which I have frequently referred in some of my notes on this noble commentary.]]

**The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿And that you give charity is better for you, if you only knew﴾ (2:280)**

Abu Ja'far said: By this, He, the Mighty and Majestic, means: "And that you give your capital (principal) to this debtor in difficulty, [is] better for you, O people, than that you grant him respite until his time of ease, so that you may collect your capital from him when he becomes well-off. ﴿If you only knew﴾ the merit of charity and the reward God has made obligatory for one who waives his insolvent debtor's debt."

* *

The exegetes (ahl al-ta'wil, those who interpret the Qur'an) differed concerning the interpretation of this.

Some of them said: The meaning is: "And that you give charity [of] your capital to the rich and the poor among them is better for you."

As for profit and surplus, they have no claim to it, and they should not take anything from it. ﴿And that you give charity is better for you﴾ means: that you give charity of the original capital is better for you. [[It is said: "I chose so-and-so over so-and-so," meaning: I preferred so-and-so over so-and-so, and that is why it takes 'ala. Similarly, "kharrara fulanan 'ala fulan," meaning: he preferred him over him. A report says: "He chose among the houses of the Ansar," meaning: he preferred some of them over others. You rarely find this expression.]] Charity is [recommended] for every debtor in difficulty, but not for the well-off.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The more correct of the two interpretations is that of those who said: its meaning is "And that you give charity to the debtor in difficulty of your capital is better for you," because it follows the mention of its ruling in both cases, and attaching it to what immediately precedes it is more preferable to me than attaching it to what comes further from it.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: It has been said that these verses concern the rulings on usury (riba), and that they are the last verses to have been revealed of the Qur'an.

Those who said this:

6308 - Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi 'Adi narrated to us, from Sa'id [[Sa'id: i.e., Ibn Abi 'Arubah.]] = and Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, from Sa'id, = from Qatadah, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab: that 'Umar ibn al-Khattab said: "The last of the Qur'an to be revealed was the verse on usury, and the Prophet of God (ﷺ) passed away before he explained it. So leave usury and what is doubtful." [[The hadith: 6308 — Sa'id is Ibn Abi 'Arubah. This hadith is narrated by Ahmad in the Musnad (246), from Yahya [al-Qattan], and (350) from Ibn 'Ulayyah, both from Ibn Abi 'Arubah with this chain. It is also narrated by Ibn Majah (2276), via Khalid ibn al-Harith, from Sa'id, i.e., Ibn Abi 'Arubah. Ibn Kathir mentions it (2:58) from the first place in the Musnad. al-Suyuti mentions it in al-Durr al-Manthur (1:365), adding its attribution to Ibn al-Darris and Ibn al-Mundhir. He alludes to it briefly in al-Itqan (1:33), attributing it only to Ahmad and Ibn Majah. This hadith, despite the eminence and trustworthiness of its narrators, is weak in its chain due to a break in continuity, for Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab did not hear from 'Umar, as we explained in the commentary on the Musnad (109). See also Ibn Abi Hatim's al-Marasil, pp. 26–27.]]

6309 - Hamid ibn Mas'adah narrated to us, saying: Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Dawud narrated to us, from 'Amir: that 'Umar, may God be pleased with him, stood, praised God and extolled Him, then said: "To proceed: by God, I do not know, perhaps we command you with a matter that is not right for you, and I do not know, perhaps we forbid you from a matter that is right for you. The verses on usury were among the last of the Qur'an to be revealed, and the Messenger of God (ﷺ) died before explaining them to us. So leave what makes you doubtful for what does not make you doubtful." [[The hadith: 6309 — Dawud is Ibn Abi Hind; 'Amir is al-Sha'bi. This chain is also weak, for al-Sha'bi did not meet 'Umar, as we said previously (1608), citing Ibn Kathir. al-Hafiz [Ibn Hajar] mentions it in Fath al-Bari (8:153), attributing it to al-Tabari, and says: "It is interrupted, for al-Sha'bi did not meet 'Umar." Ibn Kathir (2:58) mentions a similar meaning, saying: "Ibn Majah and Ibn Mardawayh narrated it through Hayyaj ibn Bistam, from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from Abu Nadrah, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: 'Umar addressed us…" etc. Hayyaj ibn Bistam al-Harawi: scholars differed greatly about him. Ahmad, Ibn Ma'in, Ibn Abi Hatim and others criticized him. al-Makki ibn Ibrahim, a teacher of al-Bukhari, said: "We know of Hayyaj only as a trustworthy, truthful, learned man." Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Dhuhli deemed him trustworthy. They objected to some of his reports, but it later became clear that the fault lay with his son Khalid, who transmitted them from him. Our preferred view is this, for al-Bukhari included him in al-Kabir (4/2/242) without mentioning any criticism. Apparently he followed what his two teachers, al-Makki ibn Ibrahim and Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Dhuhli, chose. Ibn Kathir did not specify who transmitted from Hayyaj. I also did not find its place in Ibn Majah, and I do not have Ibn Mardawayh's book. However, I found a chain to Hayyaj: al-Khatib narrated it in his biography in Tarikh Baghdad (14:80–81), through Muhammad ibn Bakkar ibn al-Rayyan, who is trustworthy, from Hayyaj, with this chain. From this it becomes clear that its chain is sound, praise be to God.]]

6310 - Abu Zayd 'Umar ibn Shabbah narrated to me, saying: Qabisah narrated to us, saying: Sufyan al-Thawri narrated to us, from 'Asim al-Ahwal, from al-Sha'bi, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "The last thing revealed to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) was the verse on usury, and we are commanded to do something without knowing whether there is harm in it, and forbidden from something which may not be harmful." [[The hadith: 6310 — Abu Zayd 'Umar ibn Shabbah, with a shin with a dot and the bâ' doubled, al-Numayri al-Nahwi: trustworthy, an authority in Arabic and literature. al-Khatib said: "He was trustworthy and knowledgeable about history and the days of the people." He is biographed in al-Tahdhib, Ibn Abi Hatim (3/1/116), and Tarikh Baghdad (11:208–210). Qabisah is Ibn 'Uqbah; his biography has passed in (489, 2792). This hadith is from his narration from Sufyan al-Thawri. We have shown there that his narration from him is sound, contrary to those who criticized it. 'Asim al-Ahwal is 'Asim ibn Sulayman, who has passed many times. In the printed edition here it reads "'Asim 'an al-Ahwal," which is a typographical error; it is correctly given in the manuscript. This hadith is narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Sahih (8:153, Fath), from Qabisah, with this chain, but he limited it to its beginning, up to his words "the verse on usury," because the rest is a statement of Ibn 'Abbas that is attributed to him (mawquf). al-Suyuti (1:365) mentions al-Bukhari's narration and adds its attribution to Abu 'Ubayd and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il. al-Hafiz said in Fath: "The meaning of being last regarding usury is the late revelation of the verses related to it in Surah al-Baqarah. As for the ruling on prohibiting usury, its revelation preceded that by a long time, as indicated by His words, the Exalted, in Al 'Imran, during the story of Uhud: (O you who have believed, do not consume usury, doubled and multiplied) [3:130]."]]

**The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿And fear a Day when you will be returned to Allah; then every soul will be paid in full what it earned, and they will not be wronged﴾ [2:281]**

It was said: this verse is also the last verse to be revealed of the Qur'an.

Those who said this:

6311 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Abu Tumayla narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn ibn Waqid narrated to us, from Yazid al-Nahwi, from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: The last verse revealed to the Prophet ﷺ was: "And fear a Day when you will be returned to Allah." [[Hadith 6311. Abu Tumayla (with a dammed ta', as in al-Mathnā): he is Yahya ibn Wadih. His biography has passed at no. 392.

al-Husayn ibn Waqid: his biography has passed at no. 4810. In our present edition the name there appears as "al-Hasan," which is a printing error, although we had already shown the correct form in the biography, so it should be corrected.

Yazid al-Nahwi: he is Yazid ibn Abi Saʿid al-Nahwi al-Marwazi, a mawla of Quraysh. He is trustworthy (thiqa); Abu Zurʿa, Ibn Maʿin and others declared him trustworthy. Abu Muslim killed him in the year 131 for enjoining the good upon him. "al-Nahwi" is a nisba to "Banu Nahw," a clan of al-Azd.

This chain is sound (sahih).

The hadith is mentioned by al-Hafiz (Ibn Hajar) in Fath al-Bari 8:153, where he attributes it only to al-Tabari.

Ibn Kathir mentions it at 2:69 on the authority of al-Nasa'i, meaning his al-Sunan al-Kubra. Al-Suyuti likewise did so in al-Itqan 1:33.

al-Haythami mentions it in Majma' al-Zawa'id 6:324 and says: "al-Tabarani narrated it with two chains, the men of one of which are trustworthy."

In al-Durr al-Manthur 1:369-370, its attribution is extended to Abu ʿUbayd, ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn al-Anbari in al-Masahif, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il.

The apparent sense of this report from Ibn ʿAbbas conflicts with the apparent sense of the earlier report from him, no. 6310, that the last verse revealed was the verse on usury (riba).

Al-Hafiz said in Fath al-Bari: "The way to reconcile these two statements [meaning the two reports] is that this verse is the conclusion of the verses revealed about usury, since it is connected to them by conjunction (ʿatf)."

Al-Bukhari's method, with his precision and penetrating insight, points to this. He narrated the earlier hadith under the chapter heading: "Chapter: (And fear a Day when you will be returned to Allah)." By this indication he made the subject one, and the two reports consistent rather than contradictory. May Allah have mercy on him.]]

6312 - Muhammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas: "And fear a Day when you will be returned to Allah..." the verse; so it is the last verse of the Book to be revealed.

6313 - Muhammad ibn ʿAmara narrated to me, saying: Sahl ibn ʿAmir narrated to us, saying: Malik ibn Mighwal narrated to us, from ʿAtiyya, who said: The last verse revealed was: "And fear a Day when you will be returned to Allah, then every soul will be paid in full what it earned, and they will not be wronged." [[Report 6313. Sahl ibn ʿAmir: his biography has passed at no. 1971, and he is extremely weak (da'if jiddan). In the manuscript and the printed text his name appears here as "Isma'il ibn Sahl ibn ʿAmir," which is a confusion by the copyists, since no narrator bears this name. Moreover, this same chain is the one that has already passed at no. 1971. Also passed is the narration of Muhammad ibn ʿAmara from Sahl from Malik ibn Mighwal at no. 5431.]]

6314 - Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to us, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from al-Suddi, who said: The last verse revealed was: "And fear a Day when you will be returned to Allah."

6315 - al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Abu Tumayla narrated to us, from ʿUbayd ibn Sulayman, [[In the printed edition: "ʿUbayd ibn Salman," which is an error; the correct form is from the manuscript and from the biographical dictionaries.]] from al-Dahhak, from Ibn ʿAbbas; and Hajjaj, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn ʿAbbas said: The last verse of the Qur'an to be revealed was: "And fear a Day when you will be returned to Allah, then every soul will be paid in full what it earned, and they will not be wronged." Ibn Jurayj said: They say that the Prophet ﷺ remained after it for nine nights, and he was afflicted (bud'iya) on a Saturday, and he died on a Monday. [[In the manuscript and the printed text: "wa-bada yawm al-sabt," which is a gross error; and even more crude is the explanation of one who glossed it as: "He means that he withdrew from people because of his illness, then came out to them on Saturday"! It is better for a person to leave aside what he does not understand well! The phrase is rather their saying: "bud'iya al-rajul" (in the passive), meaning he fell ill. One says: "When was so-and-so afflicted?", i.e., when did he fall ill. In the hadith of ʿA'isha, she said on the day the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was afflicted: "Oh my head!"

For this report, see what al-Suyuti cited in al-Itqan 1:33, and Ibn Kathir 2:69-70.]]

6316 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Yunus informed me, from Ibn Shihab, who said: Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab narrated to me that he had received word that the most recent part of the Qur'an to be delivered to the Throne was the verse on debt. [[Hadith 6316. This chain to Ibn al-Musayyab is sound, but the hadith is weak because it is mursal, since Ibn al-Musayyab did not mention who related it to him.

Ibn Kathir reported this hadith at 2:70-71 from this place with its chain. Al-Suyuti mentioned it at 1:370, "from Ibn Jarir, with a sound chain to Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab."]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His praise be exalted, He means: Beware, O people, of a Day when you will be returned to Allah, so that you meet Him therein, lest you come before Him with evil deeds that destroy you, or with disgraceful acts that shame you, or with revealing deeds that expose you, so that your coverings are torn away, or with ruinous deeds that ruin you, so that you incur from the punishment of Allah what you have no power to withstand. It is a Day of recompense for deeds, not a Day of seeking to be pleased (istiʿtab), nor a Day of retraction, repentance, or turning back, but a Day of reward, reckoning and accounting, on which every soul is paid in full its due for what it has sent ahead and earned of evil and good, leaving nothing, small or great, of good or evil, unbrought forth. [[In the printed text: "lā yughādiru," with a dot, whereas in the manuscript it is undotted; the correct form is what has been adopted here.]] Its recompense is paid in full with justice from its Lord, and they will not be wronged. [[In the printed text: "fa-tawaffā jazā'ahā," whereas in the manuscript: "fa-tuwaffiyat," wholly undotted; the sound reading of its recitation is what has been adopted here.]] How could one be wronged who is repaid for an evil with its like, and for a good deed with ten times its like?! [[In the printed text: "kayf" without the waw, whereas the manuscript has it; the correct reading is what the manuscript contains.]] Nay, rather, it is justice upon you, O evildoer, and graciousness toward you, so that you are favored and enriched, O doer of good. Let a man fear his Lord, take caution from Him, and guard against his Day overtaking him while his back is heavy with burdens and light in righteous deeds. For He, mighty and majestic, has warned and so has given excuse, and has admonished and so has conveyed.

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O you who have believed, when you contract a debt for a specified term﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By this, exalted is His praise, He means: O you who have affirmed God and His Messenger. "When you contract a debt" means: when you engage in a sale on credit, or buy on credit, or deal or take on a debt. "For a specified term" means: until a known time that you set between yourselves. This may include the loan (qard) and the advance-payment sale (salam, a contract in which the price is paid in advance for a known commodity to be delivered at a known time), and every transaction permitted by salam, whose term of sale is specified, becomes a debt owed by the seller to whom the payment was advanced. [[In the manuscript and the printed edition: "This may include the loan and the salam, in every case where salam is permitted, the term of its sale" – a phrase that is not understandable, corrupted by scribal error and distortion. I have tried to correct it in this way so that it is somewhat sound. Salam (with a fatha on each letter) means salaf (advance payment). One says: aslama and sallama (with the lam doubled) when one advances payment, which is that you give gold and silver for a known commodity at a known time, as if you had advanced the price to the owner of the commodity. Its definition according to some jurists: it is a sale of a known thing owed, specified by description, for an immediately present price or what is in its place, at a known time.]] It may also include the sale of present goods that are permitted to be sold, from among property, for deferred prices. All of these are debts deferred to a specified term, when their terms are known by a limit agreed upon.

* *

Ibn Abbas used to say: this verse was revealed concerning advance-payment sales specifically.

Mention of the report from him to that effect:

6317 – Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Isa al-Ramli narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, who said: Ibn Abbas said concerning: ﴿O you who have believed, when you contract a debt for a specified term﴾: "The advance-payment sale of wheat, by a known measure, for a known term." [[The report: 6317 – Yahya ibn Isa ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Ramli al-Hashli al-Khazzaz, heard from Sufyan, and died in the year 201. They have spoken about him. Abu Dawud said: "It reached me from Ahmad that he praised him highly." Ibn Ma'in said: "He is nothing." Al-Ajli said: "Trustworthy." Ibn Adi said: "Most of what he narrates is not corroborated."
He is biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir 4/2/296, and Ibn Abi Hatim 4/2/178.]]

6318 – Muhammad ibn Abd Allah al-Makhrami narrated to me, saying: Yahya ibn al-Samit narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Abu Hayyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿O you who have believed, when you contract a debt﴾, he said: It was revealed concerning the advance-payment sale, by a known measure, for a known term. [[The report: 6318 – Yahya ibn al-Samit: thus it occurs in the manuscript and the printed edition, and we do not know who he is. Perhaps it is a distortion of something else?
The one in this tabaqa (generation), and whom we incline to hold to be the narrator here, is Yahya ibn Ayyub al-Miqbari Abu Zakariyya al-Abid. He is the one who narrates from Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak, and Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak al-Makhrami narrates from him, as in his biography in al-Tahdhib 11:188. But in it is "Muhammad ibn Abd al-Aziz ibn al-Mubarak al-Makhrami," which is an error, "Abd al-Aziz" in place of "Abd Allah". This Yahya ibn Ayyub is trustworthy, one of the shaykhs of Muslim in his Sahih. "Al-Miqbari" is a nisba to the graves (maqabir), due to his frequent visits to them, as in al-Lubab 4:167. He has a biography in Ibn Abi Hatim 4/2/128 and Tarikh Baghdad 14:188-189.
It is possible – and he was a worshipful, ascetic man – that "al-Samit" was a laqab (epithet) for him, making it "Yahya al-Samit." But I have not found an explicit statement of this, nor anything that points to it.
Sufyan: this is al-Thawri.
Abu Hayyan: this is al-Taymi, Yahya ibn Sa'id ibn Hayyan. His biography has passed at 5382.
Ibn Abi Najih: this is Abd Allah ibn Yasar al-Thaqafi al-Makki. His father's kunya is "Abu Najih." He is trustworthy; the authors of the six books narrated from him. But his narration from Ibn Abbas is broken (munqati'), for he narrates from the Successors (tabi'un).
The hadith will come sound, by another sound isnad: 6321.
Between these two, there will come [a report] with two weak isnads.]]

6319 – Ali ibn Sahl narrated to us, saying: Zayd ibn Abi al-Zarqa' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Abu Hayyan, from Ibn Abbas, who said: This verse was revealed: ﴿when you contract a debt for a specified term, then write it﴾, concerning the advance-payment sale, of wheat, by a known measure, for a known term. [[The report: 6319 – Zayd ibn Abi al-Zarqa': his biography has passed at 1384. In the printed edition it is "Yazid" instead of "Zayd", and this is an error, for no one by this name is found among the narrators. Then this shaykh is the one who narrated from Sufyan al-Thawri, and Ali ibn Sahl al-Ramli narrates from him, as has passed in that isnad.
And the hadith is weak, like the one before it. The unnamed man from whom Abu Hayyan narrates is Ibn Abi Najih, and he did not meet Ibn Abbas.]]

6320 – Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Muhabbab narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu Hayyan al-Taymi, from a man, from Ibn Abbas, who said: This verse was revealed: ﴿O you who have believed, when you contract a debt for a specified term﴾, concerning the advance payment (salaf) in wheat, by a known measure, for a known term. [[The report: 6320 – Muhammad ibn Muhabbab ibn Ishaq al-Qurashi, Abu Hammam al-Dallal, "owner of the slaves" (sahib al-raqiq): trustworthy; Abu Dawud and Abu Hatim and others declared him trustworthy. Al-Mundhiri erred in Tahdhib al-Sunan 2537 when he said: "His hadith is not to be used as proof." He merely followed Ibn al-Jawzi when he mentioned him among the weak narrators. Al-Dhahabi corrected him on that in al-Mizan.
And "Muhabbab" is with two b's, on the pattern of "Muhammad". Abd al-Ghani thus vocalized it in al-Mu'talif, p. 123, and al-Dhahabi in al-Mushtabih, p. 467, and al-Hafiz in al-Tahdhib and al-Taqrib. Ibn Abi Hatim erred when he made it "Muhabbab" in al-Jarh 4/1/96.
"Sahib al-raqiq": with the letter ra, as in al-Kabir of al-Bukhari 1/1/247 and al-Jarh wa-l-Ta'dil of Ibn Abi Hatim. In al-Tahdhib and al-Khulasa it occurs as "al-daqiq" with the letter dal. Allama Shaykh Abd al-Rahman al-Yamani said in the margins of al-Jarh: "And al-raqiq, with ra, is closer to their saying al-dallal," and this is good.
The hadith repeats the one before it, and its isnad is weak like its like.]]

6321 – Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Mu'adh ibn Hisham narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to me, from Qatada, from Abu Hassan, from Ibn Abbas, who said: I testify that the guaranteed advance payment (al-salaf al-mudmun) for a specified term is something that God, mighty and majestic, has made lawful and permitted. And he recited this verse: ﴿when you contract a debt for a specified term﴾. [[The report: 6321 – Mu'adh ibn Hisham al-Dastawa'i: trustworthy, reliable. The six books narrated from him.
His father Hisham ibn Abi Abd Allah al-Dastawa'i: an imam, trustworthy, a proof, and he was among those named "Commander of the Believers in hadith" – so named by Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi. Shu'ba said: "Hisham had better memory than me regarding Qatada."
Abu Hassan – with the letter sin: this is Abu Hassan al-A'raj, whose biography has passed at 5422. In the manuscript and the printed edition it is "Abu Hayyan" – with the letter ya – and this is an error and confusion, as will be shown from the takhrij (sourcing).
The hadith was narrated by Abd al-Razzaq in al-Musannaf 4:252 (photographed manuscript), from Ma'mar, from Qatada, with it.
And al-Shafi'i narrated it in al-Umm 3:80-81, from Sufyan – that is Ibn Uyayna – "from Ayyub, from Qatada, from Abu Hassan al-A'raj, from Ibn Abbas," with it.
And al-Hakim narrated it in al-Mustadrak 2:286, through Ibrahim ibn Bashshar, from Sufyan, that is Ibn Uyayna, with it.
And al-Bayhaqi narrated it in al-Sunan al-Kubra 6:18, through Sa'id ibn Amir, from Shu'ba, from Qatada, with it.
Al-Hafiz al-Dhahabi was hasty in his abridgement of al-Mustadrak, and commented on it, as if he meant to weaken its isnad! He said: "Ibrahim has extra narrations from Ibn Uyayna!!"
But this is a careless statement without verification. Ibrahim ibn Bashshar al-Ramadi: his biography and tawthiq (authentication) have passed at 892, and we add here that he was prolific in narrating from Ibn Uyayna, with strangeness. But Ibn Hibban said: "He was precise and exact; he accompanied Ibn Uyayna for many years and heard his hadiths repeatedly." Thus it is not unlikely for such a man to narrate from his shaykh what others did not narrate. That is one point.
And another: he was not alone in it from Ibn Uyayna, as you see. And the narration of al-Shafi'i from Ibn Uyayna suffices as trustworthy and a proof.
Then Ibn Uyayna did not narrate it alone from Ayyub from Qatada, as is made clear from the isnads we have mentioned, and from the narration of al-Tabari here. For Hisham al-Dastawa'i, Ma'mar, and Shu'ba narrated it – all three from Qatada, as you see.
That is why Ibn Kathir mentioned it at 2:71-72, saying: "Qatada said, from Abu Hassan al-A'raj, from Ibn Abbas..." He did not mention who narrated it from Qatada, because its establishment from him is by more than one route.
And al-Suyuti mentioned it at 1:370, and added its attribution to Abd ibn Humayd, al-Bukhari, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Tabarani.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: If someone says: What is the purpose of His saying "for a debt" (bi-dayn), when His saying "when you contract" (idha tadayantum) already indicates it? Can there be a contracting (mudayana) without a debt, so that it needs to be said "for a debt"? It is said: Since among the Arabs it was understood that "tadayana" means "we requited one another," and means "we dealt with one another in taking and giving on credit," God clarified with His saying "for a debt" the meaning intended by one who hears His saying "you contracted": its ruling, and He informed them that it is the ruling of debt, not the ruling of requital. [[In the printed edition: "the meaning intended by the definition of His saying 'you contracted' its ruling," which is not correct; and in the manuscript: "its definition from His saying 'you contracted' its ruling," with a blank space between the words, and in the margin the letter (ta) indicating an error. So I preferred to restore the sentence by adding "heard" so that the speech is somewhat sound. And his saying "its ruling" is the object of the verbal noun in his saying "the definition of the one who heard." Then see al-Nasikh wa-l-Mansukh of Abu Ja'far al-Nahhas: 85, for he quoted al-Tabari's words in abridged form, ending with: "the meaning for which it was intended."]]

* *

Some have claimed that this is emphasis (ta'kid), like His saying: ﴿So the angels prostrated, all of them together﴾ [Surah al-Hijr 30; Surah Sad 73], but there is no sense in what he said on this point. [[I did not learn who said this, but it is well known in books of tafsir; see the tafsir of Abu Hayyan 1:343 and al-Qurtubi 3:377.]]

* *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿then write it﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His saying "then write it," exalted is His praise, He means: write down the debt that you have contracted for a specified term, whether it be a sale or a loan.

* *

The scholars differed concerning the writing of the document of this debt by the one who owes it, whether it is obligatory or recommended (nadb).

Some of them said: It is a binding right and a firm obligation.

Mention of those who said that:

6322 – Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abu Zuhayr narrated to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, concerning His saying: ﴿O you who have believed, when you contract a debt for a specified term, then write it﴾, he said: Whoever sells for a specified term is commanded to write it, whether young or old, for a specified term.

6323 – Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij concerning His saying: ﴿O you who have believed, when you contract a debt for a specified term, then write it﴾, he said: So whoever incurs a debt, let him write it, and whoever sells, let him call witnesses.

6324 – Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi' concerning His saying: ﴿when you contract a debt for a specified term, then write it﴾, he said: This was obligatory.

6325 – And it was narrated to me from Ammar, who said: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi', with its like – and he added in it, he said: Then the leniency and the ease became established. [[His saying: "then the leniency and the ease became established" means: it was confirmed and stood firm. "The truth stood among them" means it remained and did not depart. All of this is metaphorical.]] He said: ﴿Then if some of you trust others, let the one who is trusted deliver his trust, and let him fear God, his Lord﴾.

6326 – Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, who said: It was mentioned to us that Abu Sulayman al-Mar'ashi was a man who accompanied Ka'b. [[The report: 6326 – "Abu Sulayman al-Mar'ashi" in the manuscript is "al-Mad'as," and in Ibn Kathir 2:72. Others said: The writing of the document for the debt was an obligation, but it was abrogated (nasakha, abrogated) by His saying: ﴿Then if some of you trust others, let the one who is trusted deliver his trust﴾.

Mention of those who said that:

6327 – Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: al-Thawri informed us, from Ibn Shubruma, from al-Sha'bi, who said: There is no harm if you trust him that you do not write it nor call witnesses, because of His saying: "Then if some of you trust others." Ibn Uyayna said: Ibn Shubruma said, from al-Sha'bi: To this it ended.

6328 – Al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us, saying: Dawud narrated to us, from Amir, concerning this verse: ﴿O you who have believed, when you contract a debt for a specified term, then write it﴾ until he reached this point: ﴿Then if some of you trust others, let the one who is trusted deliver his trust﴾, he said: He granted a concession regarding that, [[In the printed edition: "granted a concession in that," and what is in the manuscript is correct, but it will come in the manuscript as in the printed edition here at no. 6334.]] so whoever wishes to trust his companion, let him trust him.

6329 – Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Harun narrated to us, from Amr, from Asim, from al-Sha'bi, who said: If he trusts him, he does not call witnesses over it nor write it.

6330 – It was narrated to me from Ammar, who said: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from al-Sha'bi, who said: They used to hold that this verse: ﴿Then if some of you trust others﴾ abrogated what preceded it of writing and witnesses, as a concession and a mercy from God.

6331 – Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, who said: Others than Ata' said: [[His saying: "others than Ata'," there has not passed before, in the saying of Ata', any mention among those who said that the writing is a binding right and firm obligation. 6332 – Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: That was abrogated by His saying: ﴿Then if some of you trust others, let the one who is trusted deliver his trust﴾, he said: Were it not for this word, [[His saying: "were it not for this word," meaning: were it not for this saying of God, exalted is He. The use of "word" (harf) in the sense of "saying" I have not found in any book of lexicography, but it is a good metaphor, as they called the qasida a "kalima" (word), so it is permissible to call the verse, and the whole saying, a "harf."]] it would not have been permitted to anyone to contract a debt except with a document and witnesses, or a pledge. When this came, it abrogated all of that, and it passed to trust.

6333 – Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Zuray' narrated to us, from Sulayman al-Taymi, who said: I asked al-Hasan: Must everyone who sells a sale call witnesses? He said: Have you not seen that God, mighty and majestic, says: ﴿let the one who is trusted deliver his trust﴾?

6334 – Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us, saying: Dawud narrated to us, from Amir concerning this verse: ﴿O you who have believed, when you contract a debt for a specified term, then write it﴾, until he reached this point: ﴿Then if some of you trust others, let the one who is trusted deliver his trust﴾, he said: He granted a concession in that; so whoever wishes to trust his companion, let him trust him.

6335 – Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn Ulayya narrated to us, from Dawud, from al-Sha'bi concerning His saying: ﴿Then if some of you trust others﴾, he said: If you call witnesses, it is prudent; and if you do not call witnesses, there is latitude and ease.

6336 – Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, who said: I said to al-Sha'bi: Have you seen a man who borrows something from a man – must I insist that he call witnesses? He said: He recited up to His saying: [[In the manuscript: "He said: He said, up to His saying..." with a blank between the words, and "fa-qala" in place of "fa-qara'a." What is in the printed edition is closer to the correct reading.]] ﴿Then if some of you trust others﴾, which has abrogated what came before it.

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 282 (part 2 of 6):**

٦٣٣٧ - Amr ibn Ali narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Marwan al-Uqayli narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Malik ibn Abi Nadrah narrated to us, [from his father], from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, that he recited: "O you who have believed, when you contract a debt for a specified term" up to "and if one of you entrusts another" = [[In the printed edition: "He said, then he recited up to: and if one of you entrusts..." In the manuscript there is a repetition after his words "up to a specified term," its text being: "He said, he recited: O you who have believed, when you contract a debt for a specified term. This abrogated what came before it," and it does not mention "and if one of you entrusts..." which is the abrogating verse. I have restored the correct reading from al-Nasikh wa'l-Mansukh (al-Nahhas): 83, where he narrated the report, as will come later.]] He said: "This abrogated what came before it."

[[The report: 6337. "Muhammad ibn Marwan ibn Qudamah al-Uqayli": al-Bukhari reported from him in al-Ta'liq, and Abu Dawud in al-Marasil, and Musaddad, Yahya ibn Ma'in and others narrated from him. Ahmad said: "I saw Muhammad ibn Marwan al-Uqayli, and he narrated hadiths while I was present, and I did not write them down; I deliberately left them," as if he weakened him. Ibn Ma'in said: "There is no harm in him," and from Abu Dawud: "Truthful (saduq)." He is biographed in al-Tahdhib. "Abd al-Malik ibn Abi Nadrah al-Abdi" narrated from his father. al-Hafiz (Ibn Hajar) said in al-Tahdhib: "Ibn Hibban mentioned him among the trustworthy and said: he sometimes erred. He has a hadith in both (Sahihs) on the verse of debt: O you who have believed, when you contract a debt." I say: al-Daraqutni said: "There is no harm in him." al-Hakim said in al-Mustadrak: "Among the rarest of the Basrans in hadith." He is biographed in al-Tahdhib. His father "Abu Nadrah" is "al-Mundhir ibn Malik ibn Qut'ah al-Abdi," who narrated from Ali ibn Abi Talib, Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, Abu Dharr, Abu Sa'id, Ibn Abbas and others among the Companions. Ahmad said: "Trustworthy." Ibn Sa'd said: "Trustworthy, with many narrations, and not everyone is to be relied upon as proof." He is biographed in al-Tahdhib.

Furthermore, the manuscript and the printed edition omitted what we have placed between the brackets [from his father]; this is an error of the copyist, and it appears correctly in al-Nasikh wa'l-Mansukh: 83 with this very same chain, as I indicated in the earlier note.]]

* *

The discussion concerning the interpretation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿And let a scribe write between you justly; and let not any scribe refuse to write as Allah has taught him﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His praise be exalted, He means: let the scribe write the document of the debt for a specified term between the creditor and the debtor, "justly," meaning: with truth and equity in the document he writes between them, not wronging the one who holds the right of his right, nor diminishing it, [[In the printed edition: "not wronging the one who holds the right," which is an error; the correct reading is from the manuscript, where it is written without dots as I have given it. Haffa, yahuffu, haifan means: to incline and deviate; it is an intransitive verb, not transitive. As for "tahayyafahu malahu wa haqqahu," it means: he diminished him of his wealth and right, taking from its edges.]] nor imposing upon him a claim based on falsehood, nor obligating him to what is not due from him, as:

٦٣٣٨ - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah concerning His saying: "And let a scribe write between you justly," he said: "Let the scribe fear Allah in his writing; let him not omit any right from it, nor add any falsehood to it."

* *

As for His saying: "and let not any scribe refuse to write as Allah has taught him," it means: let no scribe who is asked to do this refuse to write the document of the debt between them, as Allah has taught him its writing, singling him out with knowledge of it and depriving many of His creation of it.

* *

The scholars have differed concerning whether writing is obligatory upon the scribe when he is asked to do it, similar to their disagreement over whether writing is obligatory upon the one who holds the right.

Mention of those who said so:

٦٣٣٩ - Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to us, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid concerning the saying of Allah, mighty and majestic: "and let not any scribe refuse," he said: "It is obligatory upon the scribe to write."

٦٣٤٠ - al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, who said: I said to Ata: "His saying: 'and let not any scribe refuse to write,' is it obligatory that he not refuse to write?" He said: "Yes." Ibn Juraij said: Mujahid also said: "It is obligatory upon the scribe to write."

٦٣٤١ - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "and let not any scribe refuse to write as Allah has taught him," the like of it.

٦٣٤٢ - Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to us, from Israil, from Jabir, from Amir and Ata concerning His saying: "and let not any scribe refuse to write as Allah has taught him," the two said: "If they do not find a scribe and are called upon, then do not refuse to write for them."

* *

Mention of those who said: "It is abrogated." We have already mentioned a group of those who said: "Everything in this verse concerning the command to write, to call witnesses, and to take a pledge is abrogated by the verse at its end," [[See what preceded from nos. 6327 to 6337.]] and I will mention the statement of those whose mention we omitted there, in some of its meanings.

٦٣٤٣ - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abu Zuhayr narrated to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak: "and let not any scribe refuse," he said: "It was a firm command, and it was abrogated by: ﴿and let no scribe or witness be harmed﴾."

٦٣٤٤ - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi': "And let a scribe write between you justly, and let not any scribe refuse to write as Allah has taught him," so this was obligatory upon the scribes.

* *

Others said: It is of obligatory character, but it is obligatory upon the scribe when he is free.

Mention of those who said so:

٦٣٤٥ - Musa narrated to me, saying: Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi concerning His saying: "And let a scribe write between you justly, and let not any scribe refuse to write as Allah has taught him," he says: "Let no scribe refuse to write if he is free."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct view on this matter, in our opinion, is that Allah, mighty and majestic, commanded those who contract a debt for a specified term to record the documents of the debt between them, and commanded the scribe to write that down between them justly. The command of Allah is an obligatory decree, unless there is a proof that it is guidance and recommendation. There is no indication that His, may His praise be exalted, command to record the documents in this matter, and His prior instruction to the scribe not to refuse to write it, is a recommendation and guidance; rather, it is an obligation upon them which they are not permitted to neglect, and whoever neglects it among them is sinful (haraj) by his neglect. [[His saying "haraj" means: sinful. See what has preceded many times in the commentary on this word: 2: 423; then 4: 224 (note 1); then 475 (note 2); then 566 (note 3); then p. 567 and what follows.]]

There is no basis for the argument of those who claim that the command to this is abrogated by His saying: "But if one of you entrusts another, let him who is entrusted discharge his trust." For that was only permitted by Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, where there is no way to a document or to a scribe. As for when the document and the scribe are both present, the obligation, if the debt is for a specified term, is what Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, commanded in His saying: "So write it down, and let a scribe write between you justly, and let not any scribe refuse to write as Allah has taught him, and let him write."

Abrogation occurs only when the ruling of the abrogating and the abrogated cannot both apply in one and the same situation, in the manner we have explained. [[Meaning what has preceded its explanation in 3: 385, 563; 4: 582, and what will come in this part: 118, note 1.] As for when one of the two does not negate the ruling of the other, there is nothing of abrogation in it at all.

And if it were necessary that His saying: ﴿And if you are on a journey and do not find a scribe, then a pledge taken in hand; and if one of you entrusts another, let him who is entrusted discharge his trust﴾ abrogate His saying: "When you contract a debt for a specified term, write it down, and let a scribe write between you justly, and let not any scribe refuse to write as Allah has taught him" — then it would be necessary that His saying: ﴿And if you are ill, or on a journey, or one of you comes from the place of relieving himself, or you have touched women, and you find no water, then take clean earth﴾ [Surah al-Ma'idah: 6] abrogates the ablution with water, both in the settled state when water is present and on a journey, which Allah, mighty and majestic, prescribed by His saying: ﴿O you who have believed, when you rise to prayer, wash your faces and your hands up to the elbows﴾ [Surah al-Ma'idah: 6]; and that His saying concerning the expiation for zihar: ﴿So whoever does not find [the means], then fasting for two consecutive months﴾ [Surah al-Mujadilah: 4] abrogates His saying: ﴿then the freeing of a neck before they touch one another﴾ [[Al-Tabari's view is summarized briefly by Abu Ja'far al-Nahhas in al-Nasikh wa'l-Mansukh: 83, 84, and al-Qurtubi in his tafsir 3: 403, 404.]] [Surah al-Mujadilah: 3].

* *

It is asked of the one who says that His, may His remembrance be exalted, saying: "But if one of you entrusts another, let him who is entrusted discharge his trust" abrogates His saying: "When you contract a debt for a specified term, then write it down": what is the difference between him and one who speaks about tayammum and what we mentioned [[In the printed edition: "what is the difference between him and the one who speaks about tayammum what we mentioned," which places the definite article on "speaker" and drops the waw from "and what we mentioned," so the sentence becomes riddled with error and confusion from every direction, and the context is violently disrupted. Al-Tabari's words "and what we mentioned" refer to what he mentioned in the preceding verse on zihar. By "and what we mentioned its saying," he means that it is abrogated by the completion of the verse.]] — he claimed that everything permitted in a state of necessity for the reason of necessity abrogates its ruling in a state of necessity, its ruling in all its states: like his saying that the command to record documents of debts and rights is abrogated by His saying: "And if you are on a journey and do not find a scribe, then a pledge taken in hand; and if one of you entrusts another, let him who is entrusted discharge his trust"?

If he says: "The difference between me and him is that His saying 'if one of you entrusts another' is a sentence cut off from His saying 'And if you are on a journey and do not find a scribe, then a pledge taken in hand,' and the ruling for the journey, when a scribe is lacking, has ended with His saying 'then a pledge taken in hand.' He only meant by His saying 'if one of you entrusts another': 'when you contract a debt for a specified term,' and one of you entrusts another, let him who is entrusted discharge his trust."

It is said to him: "What is the proof for that, from a source or analogy, when the ruling concerning the debt, for which there is a way to the scribe and the document, has been concluded by His saying: 'And Allah teaches you, and Allah is knowledgeable of all things'?" [[This is the argument of a learned scholar, perceptive of the meanings of speech.]]

* *

As for those who claimed that His saying "write it down" and His saying "and let not any scribe refuse" are on the basis of recommendation and guidance, they are asked for proof of their claim in that matter, and then they are confronted with the rest of Allah's command, mighty and majestic, which He commanded in His Book, and they are asked to explain the difference between what they asserted and denied in that case and in others. They have not stated a view on any of that without being obliged to adopt the same in the other.

* *

Mention of those who said that "justly" in His saying "And let a scribe write between you justly" means: the right (al-haqq).

.........................................................................
............................................................................ There is no way to complete this until a copy of the tafsir is found whose copyist has fewer errors and omissions.]]

* *

The discussion concerning the interpretation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿So let him write, and let the one upon whom is the truth dictate, and let him fear Allah, his Lord, and not diminish anything from it﴾

[[In the printed edition and the manuscript: the copyist omitted "fal-yaktub" (so let him write) before "wal-yumlil" (and let him dictate); I have restored it.]]

Abu Ja'far said: By this is meant: "so let him write" — the scribe; "and let the one upon whom is the truth dictate" — this is the debtor, the obligor, who says: let the obligor take charge of dictating the document of what is owed to the creditor to the scribe. "And let him fear Allah, his Lord" — the one who dictates, upon whom is the right, let him beware of His punishment in diminishing from the one who holds the right any part of his right, by wronging him in reducing it or by taking it away from him through transgression, so that he is seized for it, where he cannot repay it except from his good deeds, or that he bears some of his sins, as:

٦٣٤٦ - I was told by Ammar, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi': "So let him write, and let the one upon whom is the truth dictate," so this was obligatory, "and let him fear Allah, his Lord, and not diminish anything from it," he says: "let him not wrong him in any part of it."

٦٣٤٧ - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said concerning His saying: "and not diminish anything from it," he said: "Let him not reduce anything from the right of this man when he dictates."

* *

The discussion concerning the interpretation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿But if the one upon whom is the truth is foolish or weak, or unable to dictate himself, then let his guardian dictate with justice﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His saying, may His praise be exalted: "But if the one upon whom is the truth is foolish or weak," if the debtor upon whom the wealth is due is "foolish," meaning: ignorant of what is right concerning what is incumbent upon him to dictate to the scribe, as:

٦٣٤٨ - Musa narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "But if the one upon whom is the truth is foolish," as for the foolish: he is the one ignorant of dictation and affairs.

* *

Others said: Rather, "the foolish" in this place, whom Allah means, is the young child.

Mention of those who said so:

٦٣٤٩ - Musa ibn Harun narrated to me, saying: Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "But if the one upon whom is the truth is foolish," as for the foolish, he is the child.

٦٣٥٠ - Yahya ibn Abi Talib narrated to me, saying: Yazid informed us, saying: Juwaybir informed us, from al-Dahhak concerning His saying: "But if the one upon whom is the truth is foolish or weak," he said: "He is the small child, so let his guardian dictate with justice."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The more preferable of the two interpretations for the verse is the interpretation of the one who said: "The foolish in this place is the one ignorant of dictation and of the place of the correct and the erroneous in it," because of what we have already explained, that the meaning of "safah" (folly) in the speech of the Arabs is ignorance. [[See the explanation of "safah" in what preceded: 1: 293–295; 3: 90, 129, 130.]]

And in His saying: "But if the one upon whom is the truth is foolish," every ignorant person regarding the correctness of what is dictated and its error is included, whether a child or an adult, male or female. However, what is more preferable by the apparent meaning of the verse is that it intends: every person ignorant of the place of error and correctness in what is dictated, from the adult men who are not under guardianship, and women. For He, may His remembrance be exalted, began the verse with His saying: "O you who have believed, when you contract a debt for a specified term," and a child and one under guardianship may not be dealt with in debt; and Allah, mighty and majestic, has exempted from those whom He commanded to dictate the document of debt, along with the foolish, the weak and one who is unable to dictate. In His, may His praise be exalted, distinguishing the weak from the foolish and from one who cannot dictate the document, in the description by which each of them is described, [[In the manuscript: "So from His, may His praise be exalted, distinguishing of the weak from the foolish, then the description and one who is unable to dictate the document, which Allah has described each of them by..." which is disjointed; the printed edition has correctly amended it.]] there is an indication that each of the three categories whose descriptions He distinguished is other than the other two. [[In the manuscript: "...whose descriptions Allah has made clear," a correction of what was in the manuscript, which read "whose descriptions he sanctioned," undotted; I preferred this reading as I have given it.]]

And when that is so, it is known that the one described as foolish among them, not as weak, is the one capable of dictating, except that the obligation of dictation was lifted from him because of his ignorance of the place of correctness in it from error. And that the one described as weak among them is the one incapable of dictating, even if he is strong and sound of judgment, either because of a speech impediment or muteness. And that the one described as unable to dictate is the one prevented from dictating, either by imprisonment, in which he cannot be present with the scribe who writes the document so that he may dictate to him, or by being absent from the place of dictation, so that he is unable to dictate the document because of his absence.

So Allah, mighty and majestic, lifted from them the obligation of dictating that, for the reasons we have described, if they are present in them, and excused them for abandoning dictation on account of them. And when the obligation falls upon them, He commanded the holder of the right to dictate, saying: "But if the one upon whom is the truth is foolish or weak, or unable to dictate himself, then let his guardian dictate with justice," meaning: the guardian of the right.

* *

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 282 (part 3 of 6):

There is no basis for the view of those who claim that "the foolish" (al-safih) in this context is the young child, and that "the weak" (al-da'if) is the grown but stupid person. For if it were as they say, it would necessitate that the words "or he who is unable to dictate himself" refer to the incapable among sensible men who are permitted to manage their own property and persons, being unable to dictate because of an impediment in his tongue, such as muteness or other defects, or because he is absent from the place of the document. If that were the meaning, the meaning of His words "then let his guardian dictate with justice" would be nullified, [In the printed edition: "batala", and in the manuscript: "fa-batala"; I preferred its reading as I have established it.] because a sensible, mature man is not placed under guardianship in his property even if he is mute or absent, and no one may rule over his property except by his command. And in the soundness of this meaning there is what refutes the corruption of the view of those who claim that "the foolish" in this context is the young child, or the grown stupid person.
Mention of those who said that:
6351 - al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Ishaq related to us, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far related to us, from his father, from al-Rabi', regarding "If he who owes the debt is foolish or weak or unable to dictate himself, then let his guardian dictate with justice," he said: the guardian of the right (wali al-haqq).
6352 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words "If he who owes the debt is foolish or weak or unable to dictate himself, then let his guardian dictate with justice," he said: he means: if he is unable to do so, the creditor dictates with justice.
* *
Mention of the report from those who said: "By 'the weak' in this context is meant the stupid, and by His words 'then let his guardian dictate with justice' is meant the guardian of the foolish and the weak":
6353 - al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Ishaq related to us, saying: Abu Zuhayr related to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, regarding "If he who owes the debt is foolish or weak or unable to dictate himself," he said: he commanded the guardian of the foolish or the weak to dictate with justice.
6354 - Musa related to me, saying: Amr related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi: As for "the weak," it is the stupid.
6355 - al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa related to us, saying: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: As for "the weak," it is the stupid.
6356 - Yunus related to us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding "If he who owes the debt is foolish or weak": one who is not known, so that his right is established for this one while he is ignorant of that, so his guardian stands in his place until he gives this one his right.
* *
We have already shown which of the two interpretations is more correct.
* *
As for His words "then let his guardian dictate with justice," He means: with the truth.
* *
On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: "And call to witness two witnesses from among your men" (wa-istashhidu shahidayni min rijalikum).
Abu Ja'far said: He, may His praise be exalted, means by this: and call upon two witnesses for your rights.
* *
It is said: "So-and-so is my witness (shahidi) concerning this property, and my witness (shahidi) regarding it." [See the explanation of "shahid" earlier, 1:376, 377.]
* *
As for His words "from among your men," He means from among your free Muslims, excluding your slaves and excluding your free non-Muslims, as:
6357 - Ibn Waki' related to us, saying: my father related to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "And call to witness two witnesses from among your men," he said: the free.
6358 - Yunus related to me, saying: Ali ibn Sa'id informed us, from Hushaym, from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from Mujahid, the like of it.
* *
On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: "But if they are not two men, then a man and two women from those whom you accept as witnesses" (fa-in lam yakuna rajulayni fa-rajulun wa-imra'atani mimman tarda'una mina al-shuhada').
Abu Ja'far said: He, may His praise be exalted, means by this: if they are not two men, then let there be a man and two women as witnesses. The "man and two women" is in the nominative by being a response to "al-kawn" (being). If you wish, you may say: if they are not two men, then a man and two women shall bear witness to that. And if you wish: if they are not two men, then a man and two women are to be called upon to witness against him. And if you say: if they are not two men, then it is a man and two women, [In the printed edition and manuscript: "fa-rajulun wa-imra'atani"; the correct reading is as I have established it, which is the mode mentioned by al-Farra' in Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1:184.] it would be correct. All of these are permissible.
* *
If "rajulan wa-imra'atayn" were in the accusative, it would be permissible, on the interpretation: if they are not two men, then call upon a man and two women. [Most of this is the text of al-Farra's Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1:184. In the manuscript and printed edition: "fa-rajulun wa-imra'atani" in the accusative, and what I have established is better.]
* *
And His words "from those whom you accept as witnesses" mean: from the upright whose religion and righteousness are approved, as:
6359 - al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Ishaq related to us, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far related to us, from his father, from al-Rabi' regarding His words "And call to witness two witnesses from among your men," he says: in debt, "but if they are not two men, then a man and two women," and that is in debt, "from those whom you accept as witnesses," he says: upright.
6360 - al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Ishaq related to us, saying: Abu Zuhayr related to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak: "And call to witness two witnesses from among your men," God, mighty and majestic, commanded that they call to witness two men of justice from among their men, "but if they are not two men, then a man and two women from those whom you accept as witnesses."
* *
On the interpretation of His words: "that if one of them errs, the other of them may remind her" (an tadilla iḥdahuma fa-tudhakkira iḥdahuma al-ukhra).
Abu Ja'far said: The reciters have differed concerning the recitation of this.
The majority of the people of the Hijaz and Medina and some of the people of Iraq recited: "an tadilla iḥdahuma fa-tudhakkira iḥdahuma al-ukhra," with the "alif" of "an" vowelled with a fatha, and "tadilla" and "tudhakkira" in the accusative, meaning: if they are not two men, then a man and two women, so that one of them may remind the other if she errs. According to them, this is of the "advanced" (muqaddam) whose meaning is "delayed" (mu'akhkhar), because "reminding" according to them is what must be in place of "errs." For the meaning is what we have described in their saying. They said: we only put "tudhakkira" in the accusative because the conditional, when it precedes, is joined to what comes before it, so its answer becomes subordinate to it, as you say in speech: "It pleases me that the questioner asks and is given," meaning: it pleases me that the questioner be given if he asks, or: when he asks. What pleases you is the giving, not the asking. But His words "an yas'ala" (that he asks), since they precede, are joined to what comes before them, which is His words "yu'jibuni" (it pleases me), so the "an" is opened and governs the accusative, then "yu'ta" (is given) follows it, and it is put in the accusative by the accusative of His words "yu'jibuni an yas'ala," as a coordination with it, even though it has the meaning of a conditional. [See al-Farra's Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1:184.]
* *
Others recited it likewise, except that they read "tudhkira" with a sukun on the "dhal" and a lightened "kaf." Those who recite it so differ among themselves about the interpretation of their recitation.
Some of them directed it to mean: that she makes the other a male (dhakar) by their combination, meaning: that her testimony when joined with the testimony of her companion is valid, just as the testimony of one male is valid in debt, because the testimony of each one of them alone is not valid in what is valid in debts except by the joining of two women to the testimony of one man, so their testimony then becomes equivalent to the testimony of one male. Thus each of them, in the view of those who interpret it in this sense, makes her companion a male with her. They cite the Arabs' saying: "She has made a male (adhkarat) of so-and-so's mother," meaning she bore him a male, "so she gives birth to males (tudhkir bihi)," and "she is a woman who bears males (mudhkir)," when she bears male children. This is a view reported from Sufyan ibn 'Uyayna, that he used to say it.
6361 - It was related to me on the authority of Abu 'Ubayd al-Qasim ibn Sallam that he said: I was told on the authority of Sufyan ibn 'Uyayna that he said: The interpretation of His words "fa-tudhakkira iḥdahuma al-ukhra" is not from remembrance (dhikr) after forgetting, but is from dhakar (male), meaning: that when she testifies with the other, their testimony becomes like the testimony of a male.
* *
Others among them directed it to mean "remembrance" after forgetting.
* *
Others recited: "an tadilla iḥdahuma fa-tudhakkira iḥdahuma al-ukhra," with the "kasra" of "in" in His words "in tadilla," and the "raf'" of "tudhakkira" with its doubling (tashdid), as if it meant the beginning of a statement about what the two women do if one of them forgets her testimony: the other reminds her, [In the printed edition: "tudhakkiruha al-ukhra"; in the manuscript: "wa-dhakkaruha al-ukhra"; the context requires what I have established. What follows later indicates the correctness of what I preferred.] by fixing the forgetful one in memory and reminding her of that, and the cutting off of that from what precedes it. [His words "and the cutting off of that from what precedes it" are coordinated with his earlier words "meaning the beginning of a statement."] The meaning of the speech according to the reader thus recited is: "And call to witness two witnesses from among your men; but if they are not two men, then a man and two women from those whom you accept as witnesses; then if one of them errs, the other reminds her," as a resumption of a statement about what happens if one of them forgets her testimony, from the reminding by the other of her forgetful companion. [In the manuscript: "min tankir al-ukhra minhuma," a scribal error, like the one noted in footnote 3.]
This is a recitation which al-A'mash used to recite, and those who took it from him. Al-A'mash put "tadilla" in the accusative because it is in the place of the jussive by the conditional particle, which is "in." The meaning of the speech according to his recitation is "in tadlil" (if she errs); when the two lams merged into one, he moved it with the lightest vowel, and "tudhakkira" he put in the nominative by the "fa," because it is the answer of the conditional.
* *
Abu Ja'far said: The correct recitation in our view is the recitation of the one who recites with a fatha on "an" in His words "an tadilla iḥdahuma," and with a shadda on the "kaf" in His words "fa-tudhakkira iḥdahuma al-ukhra," and the accusative of the "ra'" in it, meaning: if they are not two men, then let a man and two women bear witness, so that if one of them errs, the other reminds her.
As for the accusative of "fa-tudhakkira," it is by coordination with "tadilla," and "an" was opened by its occupying the position of "kay" (so that), and it is in the position of a conditional, and the answer follows it, being satisfied by its being opened, meaning the opening of "an," from "kay," and the second, namely "fa-tudhakkira," is coordinated with "tadilla," so that it may be known that what took the place of what used to govern it, which is apparent, has indicated it and expressed its meaning and its governing function, namely "kay."
We only chose this in recitation because of the consensus of the authoritative early and later reciters upon it, and the isolation of al-A'mash and those who recite his recitation in what he is alone in against them. It is not permissible to abandon a recitation which the Muslims have brought in wide transmission among them in favor of another. As for our choice of "fa-tudhakkira" with a shadda on the "kaf," it means: the repetition of the remembrance from one of them upon the other, and informing her that she [forgot] that, so that she may remember. [The Bulaq printed edition reads: "fa-innahu bi-ma'na ta'diyat al-dhikr min iḥdahuma 'ala al-ukhra wa-ta'rifiha bi-annaha dhalika li-tudhakkira," which is a sentence without meaning. In another printed edition before it, with "bi-inha'a dhalika" instead of "bi-annaha dhalika," which is even more devoid of meaning. In the manuscript: "bi-ma'na yuwwiru al-dhikr... bi-annaha dhalika," undotted; the correct reading is what I have established, with the addition of "forgot," which I placed between brackets.] So the shadda is more fitting than the lightening.
* *
As for what is related from Ibn 'Uyayna of the interpretation we mentioned, it is a mistaken interpretation without meaning, for several reasons:
The first: that it contradicts the saying of all the people of interpretation.
The second: that it is known that the error of one of the two women in the testimony she bore is only her departing from it and her forgetting it, like a man's error in his religion when he is perplexed in it and turns away from the truth. [See the explanation of "dalal" (error) earlier, 1:195, and then 2:495, 496.] When one of them is in this state, how can the other become a male with her, while she has forgotten her testimony and erred in it? Indeed the one who is in error in her testimony at that time has more need for reminding than for being made to remember, unless it is meant that the remembering woman, when her companion is weak in remembering her testimony, sharpens her to remember what she has become weak in remembering and has forgotten, [In the printed edition: "tajri'uha 'ala dhikr ma di'fat 'an dhikrihi"; in the manuscript: "sahdatha," undotted; the correct reading is what I have established. It is a metaphor from the saying "sharpened the knife and the sword": honed it on the whetstone; and from "hunger sharpened his stomach," when it kindled and strengthened it for food and sharpened it. One says: "sharpen for him the reins of your mind," and "this speech is a whetstone for understanding."] and so strengthens her with the remembrance until she makes her like a man in strength in remembering what she has become weak in remembering of that, just as one says of a strong thing in its work: "dhakar" (male), and as one says of a sword that is effective in its striking: "a male sword," and "a male man," meaning: one who proceeds in his work, strong in his grip, sound in his resolve.
If Ibn 'Uyayna meant this, then it is one of the approaches to the interpretation of that, except that when it is interpreted thus, [In the printed edition: "idha ta'awwala dhalika"; I have kept what is in the manuscript.] its interpretation returns to something like our interpretation which we gave, even if the recitation differs in this meaning from the recitation we chose. [In the manuscript: "al-qira'a al-dhi ikhtarnaha," which is a slip by the scribe, who was very prone to slips!!] The meaning of the recitation then is correct with the one he chose as his recitation, with the lightening of the "kaf" in His words "fa-tudhakkira." [In the printed edition: "bi-an taghayyara al-qira'a hinna'idhin al-sahiha bi-al-ladhi ikhtara qira'atahu..." which is a sentence whose meaning has been lost in confusion. In the manuscript: "bi-an +ta'ayyan al-qira'a hinna'idhin al-sahih bi-al-ladhi ikhtara qira'atahu...," which is garbled, and I think the correct reading of the sentence is as I have given it, since it then accords with what Abu Ja'far intended.] We do not know of anyone who interpreted it thus and recommended its recitation thus in that meaning. So the correct recitation of it, since the matter is general as we have described, is what we have chosen. [In the printed edition and manuscript: "fa-al-sawab fi qawlihi," and the correct reading is what I have established. The sentence's construction is: "fa-al-sawab fi qira'atihi... ma ikhtarna."]
* *
Mention of one who interpreted His words "an tadilla iḥdahuma fa-tudhakkira iḥdahuma al-ukhra" in a way similar to our interpretation which we stated:
6362 - Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada regarding His words: "And call to witness two witnesses from among your men; but if they are not two men, then a man and two women from those whom you accept as witnesses, that if one of them errs, the other reminds her," God knew that there would be debts, so He took for some from others trust. So hold to God's trust, for it is more obedient to your Lord and more secure for your wealth. By my life, if he is pious the writing will only increase him in good, and if he is wicked, he is more deserving to pay when he knows that there are witnesses against him.
6363 - al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Ishaq related to us, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far related to us, from his father, from al-Rabi': "that if one of them errs, the other reminds her," he says: that if one of them forgets, the other reminds her.
6364 - Musa ibn Harun related to me, saying: Amr related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi: "that one of them errs," he says: one of them forgets the testimony, and the other reminds her.
6365 - al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Ishaq related to us, saying: Abu Zuhayr related to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak: "that one of them errs," he says: if one of them forgets, the other reminds her.
6366 - Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words "that one of them errs, so one of them reminds the other," he said: both are a dialect, and they are the same, and we recite: "fa-tudhakkira."
* *
On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: "And let not the witnesses refuse when they are called" (wa-la ya'ba al-shuhada' idha ma du'u).
Abu Ja'far said: The people of interpretation have differed concerning the circumstance in which God forbade the witnesses from refusing to answer when they are called, by this verse.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 282 (part 4 of 6):

Some of them said: its meaning is: the witnesses should not refuse to answer when they are called to bear witness regarding the document and the rights.
Mention of those who said this:
6367 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words, exalted is He: "And let not the witnesses refuse when they are called," that a man would go around the large al-hiwa' (al-hiwa', with a kasra on the ha': houses of people gathered around water) in which there were people, calling them to bear witness, and none of them would follow him. He said: Qatadah used to interpret this verse: "And let not the witnesses refuse when they are called" as meaning: to bear witness for one man against another.
6368 - I was told by Ammar, who said: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi' regarding His words: "And let not the witnesses refuse when they are called." He said: A man would go around among the many people calling them to bear witness, and none of them would follow him, so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent down: "And let not the witnesses refuse when they are called."
6369 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah regarding His words: "And let not the witnesses refuse when they are called." He said: Do not refuse to bear witness when you are called to testimony.
* *
Others said the same meaning as these, except that they said: it is obligatory upon the one who is called to bear witness regarding the rights if no one else is available. But if someone else is available, he has the choice in answering: if he wishes he may answer, and if he wishes he need not.
Mention of those who said this:
6370 - Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Jabir, from al-Sha'bi, who said: "And let not the witnesses refuse when they are called." He said: If he wishes he may bear witness, and if he wishes he need not bear witness; but if no one else is available, he bears witness.
* *
Others said: the meaning of that: "And let not the witnesses refuse when they are called" - to bear witness concerning what the caller wants him to bear witness about, and to uphold what he has of testimony - is to answer.
Mention of those who said this:
6371 - Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Amir narrated to us, from al-Hasan: "And let not the witnesses refuse when they are called." He said: al-Hasan said: the upholding and the testimony.
[[The report 6371: "Abu 'Amir" is Salih ibn Rustum al-Muzani, who narrated from Abdullah ibn Abi Mulaykah, Abu Qilabah, Humayd ibn Hilal, al-Hasan al-Basri, Ikrimah and others. Narrated from him his son 'Amir, Isra'il, Hushaym, Ma'mar, and Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi. Ibn Ma'in said: "Weak." Ahmad said: "Salih al-hadith."
