Ibn Abi Hatim said, from his father: "A shaykh, whose hadith is written." Abu Dawud said: "Trustworthy." It will come in the chains with numbers 6383, 6384, 6387.]]
6372 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us regarding His words: "And let not the witnesses refuse when they are called." He said: al-Hasan used to say: it combines two matters: do not refuse, if you have testimony, to bear witness; and do not refuse when you are called to testimony.
6373 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His words: "And let not the witnesses refuse when they are called." He means: whoever among the Muslims is needed, he should bear witness to a testimony if he has it, and it is not lawful for him to refuse when he is called.
6374 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: 'Amr ibn 'Awn narrated to us, saying: Hushaym informed us, from Yunus, from al-Hasan: "And let not the witnesses refuse when they are called." He said: for upholding it; he should not initiate it, when he is called to witness it and when he is called to uphold it.
* *
Others said: rather, the meaning of that: "And let not the witnesses refuse when they are called" - for upholding the testimony they have for the caller - is to answer his call to uphold it.
Mention of those who said this:
6375 - Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "And let not the witnesses refuse when they are called." He said: when he has borne witness.
6376 - Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, from 'Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "And let not the witnesses refuse when they are called." He said: when they have borne witness before that.
6377 - Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "And let not the witnesses refuse when they are called." He says: when they have been made to bear witness.
6378 - Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding His words: "And let not the witnesses refuse when they are called." He said: when you have testimony and are called.
6379 - Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, saying: al-Layth narrated to us, from Mujahid regarding His words: "And let not the witnesses refuse when they are called." He said: when there is a testimony, uphold it; when you are called to bear witness, if you wish go, and if you wish do not go.
6380 - Sawwar ibn 'Abd Allah narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Malik ibn al-Sabbah narrated to us, from 'Imran ibn Hudayr, who said: I said to Abu Mijlaz: "People call me to witness among them, and I dislike to witness among them?" He said: Leave what you dislike; but when you have borne witness, answer when you are called.
6381 - Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Jabir, from 'Amir who said: The witness has the choice as long as he has not borne witness.
6382 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: 'Amr narrated to us, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, from Yunus, from Ikrimah regarding His words: "And let not the witnesses refuse when they are called." He said: for the upholding of the testimony.
6383 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: 'Amr ibn 'Awn narrated to us, saying: Hushaym informed us, from Abu 'Amir, from 'Ata': He said: in the upholding of the testimony.
6384 - Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Amir al-Muzani narrated to us, saying: I heard 'Ata' say: That is in the upholding of the testimony, meaning His words: "And let not the witnesses refuse when they are called." [[The reports 6383, 6384: Abu "Amir" has had his biography given under number 6372.]]
6385 - Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Abu Hurrah informed us, from al-Hasan, that a questioner asked him, saying: "I am called to testimony and I dislike to bear witness regarding it." He said: Then do not answer, if you wish. [[The report 6385: Abu Hurrah al-Basri is Wasil ibn 'Abd al-Rahman. He narrated from Ikrimah ibn 'Abd Allah al-Muzani, al-Hasan, Ibn Sirin, Muhammad ibn Wasi' and others. Narrated from him Hammad ibn Salamah, Hushaym, al-Qattan, Ibn Mahdi, Waki' and others. al-Bukhari said: "They speak about his narration from al-Hasan." 'Abd Allah ibn Ahmad said: I asked Yahya ibn Ma'in about Abu Hurrah and he said: "Salih, and his hadith from al-Hasan is weak; they say he did not hear it from al-Hasan." Biographied in al-Tahdhib. In the printed edition it was "Abu Murrah," which is an error.]]
6386 - Ya'qub narrated to us, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, from Mughirah who said: I asked Ibrahim: I am called to testimony and I fear that I will forget? He said: Then do not bear witness, if you wish.
6387 - Bishr ibn ... narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Amir narrated to us, from 'Ata': He said: for upholding. [[Report 6387: "Abu 'Amir", see what has passed under number 6372.]]
6388 - Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Shurayk, from Salim al-Aftas, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr: "And let not the witnesses refuse when they are called," He said: when they have borne witness.
6389 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Suwayd ibn Nasr narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Shurayk, from Salim, from Sa'id: "And let not the witnesses refuse when they are called," He said: it is the one who has the testimony.
6390 - Musa narrated to me, saying: 'Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi regarding His words: "And let not the witnesses refuse when they are called," He means: the witness should not refuse to come forward and bear witness, when he is free.
6391 - al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj who said: I said to 'Ata': "And let not the witnesses refuse when they are called," He said: they are those who have borne witness. He said: It does not harm a person if he refuses to bear witness, if he wishes. I said to 'Ata': What is the matter with it? When he is called to write, it is obligatory upon him not to refuse; but when he is called to bear witness, it is not obligatory upon him to bear witness if he wishes! He said: Thus it is obligatory upon the scribe to write, and it is not obligatory upon the witness to bear witness if he wishes, since witnesses are many.
6392 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words: "And let not the witnesses refuse when they are called," He said: when he has borne witness, he should not refuse when called to come and render the testimony and uphold it.
6393 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: "And let not the witnesses refuse," He said: al-Hasan used to interpret it: when he has testimony and is called to uphold it.
6394 - Yahya ibn Abi Talib narrated to me, saying: Yazid informed us, saying: Juwaybir informed us, from al-Dahhak regarding His words: "And let not the witnesses refuse when they are called," He said: when a man writes his testimony, or is made to bear witness for a man and bears witness, and the scribe who writes the document is called to the point of the decision of the right, then they must answer and bear witness to what they were made to bear witness to. [[His words "maqta' al-haqq" (the point of the decision): the place of separation in judgment between right and wrong, from "al-qat'," which is separation between parts.]]
* *
Others said: it is a command from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, to the man and the woman to answer when called to bear witness regarding what they have not borne witness to from the rights, initially, not for upholding the testimony, but it is a command of recommendation, not obligation.
Mention of those who said this:
6395 - I was told by Abu al-'Aliyah al-'Abdi Isma'il ibn al-Haytham, who said: Abu Qutaybah narrated to us, from Fudayl ibn Marzuq, from 'Atiyah al-'Awfi regarding His words: "And let not the witnesses refuse when they are called," He said: You were commanded to bear witness; if you wish, bear witness, and if you wish, do not bear witness. [[The report 6395: Isma'il ibn al-Haytham, Abu al-'Aliyah al-'Abdi, Tabari's shaykh: we have found no biography or mention of him in any reference, except Tabari's narration of this report and the one after it, and his narration from him in the History once, 1:206, also from Abu Qutaybah. Abu Qutaybah: Salm ibn Qutaybah, whose biography has passed under 1924.]]
6396 - Abu al-'Aliyah narrated to me, saying: Abu Qutaybah narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Thabit al-'Asari, from 'Ata', the like of it.
* *
Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of these sayings is the saying of the one who said: [the meaning of] that: [[What is between the parentheses is an addition that cannot be dispensed with.]] "And let not the witnesses refuse to answer, when they are called to uphold the testimony and render it before a ruler or judge who takes from the one who owes what he owes, for the one to whom it is owed."
We have said that this saying is more correct than the others, because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: "And let not the witnesses refuse when they are called," so He only commanded them to answer the call to testimony, and He has already attached to them the name "the witnesses." It is not permissible to attach to them the name "the witnesses" unless they were called to witness before that and bore witness to what the name "the witnesses" was attached to them for. As for before they are called to witness regarding anything, it is not permissible to call them "witnesses." For if this name were attached to them while they had not yet been called to witness on anything for which they deserve this name by their testimony, there would be no one on earth of sound intellect who would not deserve to be called "witness," meaning that he will witness, or that he is fit to witness. Since it is wrong to name someone with that name except one who has testimony for another, or one who has upheld his testimony so the name clings to him for that reason, it was known that the one meant by His words: "And let not the witnesses refuse when they are called," is the one described by what we have described, of those who have been entrusted with testimony or have borne witness, and are called to uphold it. Because one who has not been called to witness and has not been entrusted with testimony before the calling does not deserve the name "shahid" or "shahid," for what we have described before.
Moreover, the definite article "al" in "al-shuhada'" is clear evidence that the ones addressed by the prohibition against refusing to answer for testimony are known individuals who are recognized for testimony, and that they are those whom Allah, Mighty and Majestic, commanded the holders of rights to call upon, by His words: "And call upon two witnesses from among your men. But if there are not two men, then a man and two women from among those you accept as witnesses." Since that is so, it was known that they were only commanded to answer the call of the one who summons them to uphold their testimony after they had been called to witness and had borne witness. And if this were a command for someone among the people who turns away and is called to testimony to bear witness regarding it, it would have said: "And let not a witness refuse when he is called."

However, although this is so, what we say regarding one who is called to bear witness, if he is in a place where no one else fit for testimony is present, is that it is obligatory upon him to answer the one calling him to it, just as it is obligatory upon the scribe, if he is asked to write in a place where no other scribe is present, that it is obligatory upon him to write, just as it is obligatory upon one who is in a place where no one else knows faith and the laws of Islam, and a person ignorant of faith and the obligations of Allah comes to him and asks him to teach him and explain that to him, that he must teach him and explain it to him. [[Context of this sentence: "just as it is obligatory upon one who is in a place..." that he should teach him.]] We did not make obligatory, by this verse, what we made obligatory upon the man of answering for testimony when he is called initially to bear witness regarding what he is asked to witness; rather, by other proofs, which are what we have mentioned. And it is an obligation upon a man to revive what he is able to revive of the right of his Muslim brother. [[In the printed edition: "And we have obligated upon the man...", which is a grave error and a distortion of what is in the manuscript, which is the pure correct reading.]]
* *
"Al-shuhada'" is the plural of "shahid" (witness). [[See what has passed on the explanation of "al-shuhada'" at 1/377, then 3:97, 145, and what passed just above, p. 60.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 282 (part 5 of 6):

And the writing is more just in the sight of God, and more correct for the testimony of the witnesses regarding what is in it, because it contains the terms to which the seller and the buyer, the creditor and the debtor who incurs the obligation upon himself, have acknowledged. Thus there will be no discrepancy among the witnesses in their words when testifying, since their testimony agrees on what the document contains. When their testimony agrees on that, the separation of judgment between them becomes clearer for the judges to whom the matter is referred, in addition to other reasons. And it is more just in the sight of God because He has commanded it. Following the command of God is undoubtedly more just and more equitable in His sight than abandoning it and deviating from it.
* *
The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And nearer to preventing doubt﴾
Abu Ja'far said: By His words, "and nearer" (wa-adna), He, may His praise be lofty, means "and closer," from "al-dunuw" (nearness), which is closeness.
* *
By His words, "that you do not doubt" (an la tartabu), He means that you do not doubt regarding the testimony. [In the printed edition and manuscript: "min an la tashukku" (from not doubting), and the correct reading is to delete "min," or to read it as "ay an la tashukku" (that is, that you not doubt).] As reported:
6399 - Musa narrated to us, saying: Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding "That is nearer to preventing doubt," he said: that you do not doubt regarding the testimony.
* *
It is of the form "tafta'ala" from "al-rayba" (doubt). [In the manuscript: "wa-huwa tafil," which is a pure error and distortion.]
* *
The meaning of the speech is: Do not be weary, O people, of writing down the right that you have over those with whom you have contracted a debt for a fixed term, whether that right is small or great. Indeed, your writing it down is more just in the sight of God, more correct for the testimony of your witnesses regarding it, and nearer to preventing you from doubting what your witnesses testify against you of the right and the term when it is written.
* *
The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Except that it be a present trade that you conduct among yourselves, then there is no blame upon you that you not write it down﴾
Abu Ja'far said: Then God, whose remembrance is great, made an exception to what He had forbidden them, namely wearying of writing documents of their rights against their debtors for the rights that they have over them: that which is due to them from them from a sale in ready money, hand to hand. So He permitted them to leave off writing documents for that. This is because each of them, I mean the sellers and the buyers, takes possession, when what is due between them in what they trade is in cash, of what is due to him from his trading partners before parting, [In the printed edition: "idha kana al-tawajub baynahum fima yutabayi'unahu ba'da ma wajaba lahu qabla mubayi'ihi..." and it is a meaningless sentence. In the manuscript: "idha kana al-tawajub baynahum fima yatabayi'una naqdan ma wajaba lahu qabla mubayi'ihi," and the phrase "++ ma wajaba" is unpointed. So I saw that the correct reading of the first is "al-wajib" and the correct reading of the other is "naqdan," and the sentence is consistent. The construction of the phrase is: "because each one of them... takes possession... what is due to him from his trading partners before parting," and his words "if what is due between them in what they trade is in cash" form a separate clause.] so there is no need for them, in that case, for either party to write a document against the other concerning what is due to them, since they have already taken possession of what is due to them from them. Therefore God, whose remembrance is great, said: "except that it be a present trade that you conduct among yourselves," with no term or deferral or credit in it, "then there is no blame upon you that you not write it down," meaning: there is no harm upon you that you not write it down, namely the present trade.
* *
Some of the people of interpretation said in agreement with what we have said on this matter. Those who said so:
6400 - Musa narrated to me, saying: Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi regarding His words: "except that it be a present trade that you conduct among yourselves," he said: present with you in the town, you see it, so one takes and gives, so there is no blame upon these people that they not write it down.
* *
6401 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abu Zuhayr narrated to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak: "And do not be weary of writing it, whether small or large, up to its term," up to His words "then there is no blame upon you that you not write it down," he said: God commanded that you not be weary of writing it, whether small or large, up to its term, and He commanded that what was hand to hand be witnessed, whether small or large, and He permitted them not to write it.
The reciters differed concerning the reading of this.
The majority of reciters of the Hijaz and Iraq and the common reciters read: ﴿Except that it be a present trade﴾ with the nominative (tijaratun).
Some reciters of Kufa alone read it in the accusative (tijaratan). This, though permissible in Arabic, since the Arabs put indefinite nouns and qualified nouns in the accusative after "kana," and supply an unspecified subject in "kana," so they say: "in kana ta'aman tayyiban fa-atina bihi" (if it be good food, bring it to us), and put it in the nominative, so they say: "in kana ta'amun tayyibun fa-atina bihi," thus making the indefinite noun follow its predicate in its case. But the reading I choose, and do not permit reciting otherwise, is the nominative in "present trade," because the reciters agree on it, and the one who reads it in the accusative is an anomaly among them, and an anomalous reading is not raised against the proof. Among what came in the accusative is the words of the poet: [The speaker is unknown to me, but I fear it is Mutammim ibn Nuwayra, as you will see in the next note.]
A'ayni hala tabkiyani 'if​aqan ... idha kana ta'nan baynahum wa-'inaqan
And the words of another: [He is Amr ibn Shas, with doubt about that, as you will see in the next note.]
Wa-lillahi qawmi: ayyu qawmin li-hurratin ... idha kana yawman dha kawakiba ash'ana!
And the Arabs do this only with indefinite nouns, for the reason we described: the predicates of indefinite nouns follow their names. "Kana" by its nature should have a nominative and an accusative with it, so when they put both in the nominative, they observe the agreement of the indefinite noun with its predicate, and when they put both in the accusative, they observe the companionship of "kana" with an accusative and a nominative. They found that the indefinite noun is followed by its predicate, and they left an unspecified subject in "kana," since it admits a pronoun.
* *
Some people have supposed that whoever reads "an takuna tijaratan hadiratan" [in the accusative] reads it on the meaning "unless there be a present trade," and claimed that the reader of it would be obliged to read "yakunu" with a ya', and neglected the correct place of his reading from the standpoint of grammar, and imposed on him something other than what is binding on him. That is because when the Arabs put a feminine indefinite noun after "kana," qualified by its adjective or predicate, they sometimes make "kana" feminine and sometimes masculine, saying: "in kanat jariyatun saghiratun fa-ushtawha, wa-in kana jariyatan saghiratan fa-ushtawha" (if it be a young slave-girl, buy her; and if it be a young slave-girl...). "Kana" is masculinized sometimes and feminized sometimes, whether the indefinite noun is accusative or nominative.
* *
Some grammarians of Basra claimed that in His words "an takuna tijaratun hadiratun," "present trade" is nominative, because "takuna" is in the sense of the complete verb, needing no predicate, in the sense of: unless it occur, or happen, or come into being. He imposed on himself what was not binding on it, because he only imposed that on himself, since he did not find an accusative for "kana," and found "present trade" in the nominative, and neglected the permissibility of His words "tudirunaha baynakum" being the predicate of "kana," thereby dispensing with imposing on himself what he imposed.
* *
What the Basran whose words we have related said is not an error in Arabic, but what we have said agrees more with the speech of the Arabs and is more correct in meaning: that in His words "tudirunaha baynakum" there are two possibilities. One is that it is in the accusative position, being in the place of the predicate of "kana," with "present trade" as its subject. The other is that it is in the nominative position, following "present trade," since the predicate of an indefinite noun follows it. Its interpretation would be: unless there be a present trade circulating among you.
* *
The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And call witnesses when you trade﴾
Abu Ja'far said: By this, He, whose praise is lofty, means: call witnesses to the small and large of your transactions and your rights, the immediate and the deferred of them, the cash and the credit. For My permission to you to leave off writing documents among you concerning what occurs among you of rights that pass between some of you and others from a present trade circulating among you hand to hand and in cash, is not a permission from Me to you to leave off calling witnesses from among you against whom you have sold something or from whom you have bought. This is because in your leaving off calling witnesses for that there is fear of harm to each of the two parties. As for the buyer, the seller may deny the sale, and he has evidence of his ownership of what he sold, while the buyer has no evidence of purchasing it from him, so the word then would be the seller's with his oath, and judgment is given for him, and the buyer's property goes to waste. As for the seller, the buyer may deny the purchase, and the seller's ownership of what he sold has ceased, and the price of what he sold is due to him from the buyer, so he would swear to that, and the seller's right against the buyer for the price of what he sold would be nullified. So God, mighty and majestic, commanded both parties to call witnesses, lest the right of one of the two parties be lost before the other.
* *
Then they differed concerning the meaning of His words, "and call witnesses when you trade": is it a binding command from God to call witnesses at the time of the sale, or is it recommendation?
Some said: "It is a recommendation: if he wishes he calls witnesses, and if he wishes he does not call witnesses."
Those who said that:
6402 - Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from al-Rabi', from al-Hasan and Shaqiq, from a man, from al-Sha'bi regarding His words: "and call witnesses when you trade," he said: If he wishes he calls witnesses, and if he wishes he does not call witnesses. Have you not heard His words: "But if one of you trusts another, let the one trusted fulfill his trust"?
6403 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: al-Hajjaj ibn al-Minhal narrated to us, saying: al-Rabi' ibn Subayh narrated to us, saying: I said to al-Hasan: Have you seen the words of God, mighty and majestic: "and call witnesses when you trade"? He said: If you call witnesses for it, it is a guarantee for what is yours, and if you do not call witnesses for it, there is no harm.
6404 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Suwayd narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from al-Rabi' ibn Subayh, who said: I said to al-Hasan: O Abu Sa'id, God's words, mighty and majestic: "and call witnesses when you trade": a man sells, and I know that he will not pay me for two months or three, do you see any harm if I do not call witnesses against him? He said: If you call witnesses, it is a guarantee for what is yours, and if you do not call witnesses, there is no harm. [The two reports 6403 and 6404: "al-Rabi' ibn Subayh al-Sa'di," who narrated from al-Hasan, Humayd al-Tawil and Mujahid ibn Jabr, and others. Al-Thawri, Ibn al-Mubarak, Ibn Mahdi, Waki' and others narrated from him. Harmala related from al-Shafi'i: "al-Rabi' ibn Subayh was a raider; and when a man is praised for other than his craft, he has been weakened." Ahmad said: "a righteous man, no harm in him." Ibn Mu'in, Ibn Sa'd and al-Nasa'i said: "weak in hadith." Ibn Hibban said: "He was among the worshippers and ascetics of Basra, and his house at night would resemble a beehive from the abundance of his night prayer, except that narration was not his craft, so he would err often in what he related, until dubious reports entered his narrations without his awareness. I do not like relying on him when he is alone." Biographed in al-Tahdhib.]
6405 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: al-Hajjaj narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Zuray' narrated to us, from Dawud, from al-Sha'bi: "and call witnesses when you trade," he said: If they wish they call witnesses, and if they wish they do not call witnesses.
* *
Others said: "Calling witnesses for that is obligatory."
Those who said that:
6406 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abu Zuhayr narrated to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak: "Except that it be a present trade that you conduct among yourselves, then there is no blame upon you that you not write it down," but call witnesses over it when you trade. God commanded that what was hand to hand be witnessed, whether small or large.
6407 - Yahya ibn Abi Talib narrated to me, saying: Yazid informed us, saying: Juwaybir informed us, from al-Dahhak, who said: As for what is of a present sale, if he wishes he calls witnesses, and if he wishes he does not call witnesses. As for what is a sale on a term, God commanded that it be written and witnessed. And that is in the present.
* *
Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of the sayings on this matter, as to the truth, is that calling witnesses for every sale and purchase is a binding right and an obligatory duty, for what we have already explained: that every command from God is an obligation, except what has an argument establishing that it is a recommendation and guidance from the aspect requiring acceptance of it as recommendation.
* *
We have already shown the weakness of the saying of those who said: that [command] is abrogated by His words: "let the one trusted fulfill his trust," earlier, so there is no need to repeat it.
* *
The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And let no scribe or witness be harmed﴾
Abu Ja'far said: The people of interpretation differed concerning the interpretation of this.
Some said: this is a prohibition from God to the scribe, who writes the document between the parties to rights, and to the witness, that they harm them, so this one writes what he was not dictated, and this one testifies to what he was not asked to testify. Those who said that:
6408 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to me, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Ibn Tawus, from his father regarding His words: "And let no scribe or witness be harmed," "let no scribe be harmed," so that he writes what was not dictated to him, "nor a witness," so that he testifies to what he was not asked to testify.
6409 - Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: IbnUlayya narrated to us, from Yunus, who said: al-Hasan used to say: "Let no scribe be harmed," so that he adds something or alters, "nor a witness," he said: he does not conceal the testimony, and he testifies only to the truth.
6410 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, who said: A witness fears God in his testimony, not diminishing from it any right nor adding to it any falsehood. A scribe fears God in his writing, so let him not leave out from it any right nor add to it any falsehood. [Report 6410: in the printed edition "qala haddathana Yazid ibn Qatada," and in the manuscript "qala haddathana Yazid, qala haddathana Yazid, an Qatada," which is a recurring chain in al-Tabari as I have given it; the nearest is no. 6393. This report was earlier given in abridged form as no. 6338.]
6411 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada: "And let no scribe or witness be harmed," he said: "let no scribe be harmed," so that he writes what was not dictated, "nor a witness," so that he testifies to what was not asked of him.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 282 (part 6 of 6):

6411 - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Ishaq related to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq related to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatadah: "Nor let a scribe or a witness be harmed," he said: "A scribe should not be harmed," so that he writes what was not dictated, "nor a witness," so that he testifies to what he was not asked to testify.

6412 - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Suwayd related to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Maʿmar, from Qatadah, similarly.

6413 - Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words: "Nor let a scribe or a witness be harmed," he said: "A scribe should not be harmed," so that he writes other than what was dictated to him. He said: The scribes at that time were few, and they did not know what should be written, so he is harmed and writes other than what was dictated to him, thereby nullifying their right. He said: As for the witness, he is harmed and alters his testimony, thereby nullifying their right.

* *

Abu Jaʿfar said: The root of the word, according to the interpretation of those we have mentioned, is: "wa-la yuḍārir kātibun wa-la shahīd" (nor let a scribe or a witness be harmed), then the first "rāʾ" was assimilated into the second "rāʾ," because they are of the same kind, and it was vocalized with a fatḥah though its position is jazm (a sukun), because fatḥah is the lightest of the vowels. [[See what has preceded at 5:46–53, regarding "tuḍārra" and its readings, and regarding his words "because fatḥah is the lightest of the vowels" at 5:52, with a note: 1; then this has preceded shortly, p. 65, line 2.]]

* *

Others who interpreted this word in this way said: the meaning is: "Nor let a scribe or a witness be harmed" by refusing those who call upon them to render what they have of knowledge or testimony.
Those who said this:

6414 - Al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ibn Jurayj informed us, from ʿAtaʾ, regarding His words: "Nor let a scribe or a witness be harmed," he says: that they render what is due from them.

6415 - Al-Qasim related to us, saying: Al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: I said to ʿAtaʾ: "Nor let a scribe or a witness be harmed"? He said: "Let them not be harmed," [by refusing] to render what knowledge they have. [[In the printed edition: "lā yuḍārā an yu'addiyā" which is an error and corrupt in meaning; I have adopted what is in the manuscript.]]

6416 - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Ishaq related to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Sufyan, from Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad, from Miqsam, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: "Lā yuḍārra" (nor let be harmed) "a scribe or a witness," he said: that one calls them, and they say: "Indeed we have a need." [[In the printed edition: "fa-yaqūlā," and the correct reading is from the manuscript.]]

6417 - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Ishaq related to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq related to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from ʿAtaʾ and Mujahid: "Nor let a scribe or a witness be harmed," they both said: it is obligatory upon the scribe to write; "nor a witness," they both said: if he has testified, accept him. [[The phrase "iqbalhu" (accept him), as it stands in the manuscript and the printed edition; I am uncertain about it, and I have vocalized it in accordance with the meaning closest to correct, but I fear there may be a distortion in the word whose nature I have not been able to determine.]]

* *

Others said: rather, the meaning is: "Nor let the one who seeks a scribe or seeks a witness harm the scribe or the witness." And the reading of the word according to their view is: "wa-la yuḍārarra," in the passive form of which the agent is not named.
Those who said this:

6418 - Al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, from Ibn ʿUyaynah, from ʿAmr, from ʿIkrimah, who said: ʿUmar used to read: "Wa-la yuḍārarra kātibun wa-la shahīd."

6419 - It was related to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muʿadh say: ʿUbayd informed us, who said: I heard al-Dahhak say: Ibn Masʿud used to read: "wa-la yuḍārarra."

6420 - Al-Qasim related to us, saying: Al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: ʿAbd Allah ibn Kathir informed me, from Mujahid, that he used to read: "Wa-la yuḍārarra kātibun wa-la shahīd," and that he used to say in its interpretation: the one who has the right goes and calls his scribe and his witness to write or to testify, and perhaps he is occupied with work or a need, so that he may make him sinful if he leaves that at that time because of his work and need. And Mujahid said: He should not rise from his work and need, so that he finds in himself [resentment] or is embarrassed.

6421 - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: ʿAbd Allah related to us, saying: Muʿawiyah related to me, from ʿAli, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: "Nor let a scribe or a witness be harmed," and harm is that a man says to another, who is free of need of him: "Indeed God has commanded you not to refuse when you are called!" and so he harms him by this, while he is content with someone else. So God, mighty and majestic, forbade that and said: "And if you do, then it is indeed wickedness in you."

6422 - Muhammad ibn Saʿd related to me, saying: My father related to me, saying: My paternal uncle related to me, saying: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: "Nor let a scribe or a witness be harmed," he says: the scribe or the witness may have a need from which there is no escape; so he says: "Let him go his way."

6423 - Yaʿqub related to me, saying: Ibn ʿUlayyah related to us, from Yunus, from ʿIkrimah regarding His words: "Nor let a scribe or a witness be harmed," he said: he has an illness, or he is occupied, and he says: so he is not harmed.

6424 - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah related to us, saying: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, that he used to say: "Nor let a scribe or a witness be harmed," he says: a man does not come and say: "Go and write for me, and testify for me," and he says: "Indeed I have a need, so seek someone other than me!" and he says: "Fear God, for you have been commanded to write for me!" This is the harm; and he says: "Leave him and seek someone else." The witness is in the same position.

6425 - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Ishaq related to us, saying: Abu Zuhayr related to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak regarding His words: "Nor let a scribe or a witness be harmed," he says: a man calls the scribe or the witness, and the scribe or witness says: "Indeed we have a need!" and the one who calls them says: "Indeed God, mighty and majestic, has commanded you to respond in writing and testimony!" God, mighty and majestic, says: let him not harm them.

6426 - It was related to me from al-Hasan, who said: I heard Abu Muʿadh say: ʿUbayd ibn Sulayman related to us, who said: I heard al-Dahhak regarding His words: "Nor let a scribe or a witness be harmed," it is the man who calls the scribe or the witness while they are on an important need, and they say: "Indeed we are on an important need, so seek others than us!" He says: "By God, He has commanded you to respond!" [[In the printed edition: "Allah amarakuma an tujībā," and the correct reading is from the manuscript.]] So He commands him to seek other than them and not harm them; meaning: he should not occupy them from their important need while he finds others.

6427 - Musa related to me, saying: ʿAmr related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi regarding His words: "Nor let a scribe or a witness be harmed," he says: it is not fitting that you confront a man who has a need and harm him by saying: "Write for me!" and you do not leave him until he writes for you, and his need escapes him [[In the manuscript and the printed edition: "ḥattā yaktuba lahu," but the context requires "laka." And his words after "nor a witness from your witnesses..." are coordinated with his earlier words: "to confront a man..."]] nor a witness from among your witnesses while he is busy, and you say: "Go and testify for me!" detaining him from his need, while you find someone else.

6428 - It was related to me from ʿAmmar, who said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar related to us, from his father, from al-Rabiʿ regarding His words: "Nor let a scribe or a witness be harmed," he said: When this verse was revealed: "Let not a scribe refuse to write as God has taught him," one of them would come to the scribe and say: "Write for me!" He says: "Indeed I am busy," or: "I have a need; go to someone else!" So he clings to him and says: "Indeed you have been commanded to write for me!" So he does not leave him and harms him by this while he finds someone else. And a man comes and says: "Go with me and testify for me!" He says: "Go to someone else, for I am busy," or: "I have a need!" So he clings to him and says: "You have been commanded to follow me." So he harms him by this while he finds someone else, and God, mighty and majestic, revealed: "Nor let a scribe or a witness be harmed."

6429 - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Suwayd related to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Maʿmar, from Ibn Tawus, from his father: "Nor let a scribe or a witness be harmed," he says: "Indeed I have a need, so leave me!" He says: "Write for me," and "nor a witness," likewise.

* *

Abu Jaʿfar said: The most correct of these sayings in interpretation is the saying of those who said: the meaning is: "Nor let a scribe or a witness be harmed," in the sense: nor let the one who asks this one to write or asks this one to testify harm them, by insisting on this one writing for him while he is occupied with his own affairs, and insisting on this one agreeing to testify for him while he is not free, as those who said that have stated in the saying we mentioned before.

We said this saying is more correct than others, because the address from God, mighty and majestic, in this verse from its beginning to its end, in the form of "do" or "do not do," is directed only to those with rights, the written document between them, and those for whom or against whom testimony is given concerning the debts they incur among themselves. As for what concerns command or prohibition regarding others in it, it is in the form of command and prohibition to an absent party, not one addressed, as in His words: "And let a scribe write between you," and His words: "Nor let the witnesses refuse when they are called," and what is similar to that. So the direction, since the ones commanded in it are addressed by His words: "And if you do, then it is indeed wickedness in you" [by its being a command returned to the one who seeks writing and the one who seeks testimony], is more fitting than that it be returned to the scribe and the witness. [[In the manuscript and the printed edition: "fa-l-wājib idh kāna al-ma'mūrūn mukhāṭabīn..." which is extremely disordered; in the printed edition it is even more disordered, making "idh kāna al-ma'mūrūn" into "idh kāna..." and I have placed between the brackets what more closely resembles the sense of the meaning, and it is probably correct, God willing.]] Moreover, if the scribe and the witness were the ones forbidden from harm, it would have been said: "And if they do, then it is indeed wickedness in both of them," because they are two, and because they are not addressed by His words: "nor let be harmed," rather the prohibition in "nor let be harmed" is a prohibition to an absent party, not one addressed. So directing the speech to what is parallel to what is in the context of the verse is more fitting than directing it to what departs from it.

* *

Regarding the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: "And if you do, then it is indeed wickedness in you."

Abu Jaʿfar said: By this, His praise be exalted, He means: And if you harm the scribe or the witness, and what you have been forbidden from that, "then it is indeed wickedness in you," meaning: sin in you and disobedience. [[See the interpretation of "fusuq" (wickedness) in what has preceded at 1:409, 410 / then 2:118, 119, 399 / then 4:135–140.]]

* *

The people of interpretation differed regarding the interpretation of this.
Some of them said in accordance with what we have said.
Those who said this:

6430 - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Ishaq related to us, saying: Abu Zuhayr related to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak: "And if you do, then it is indeed wickedness in you," he says: if you do other than what I command you, then it is indeed wickedness in you.

6431 - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: ʿAbd Allah related to us, saying: Muʿawiyah related to us, from ʿAli, from Ibn ʿAbbas: "And if you do, then it is indeed wickedness in you," and wickedness is disobedience.

6432 - It was related to me from ʿAmmar, who said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar related to us, from his father, from al-Rabiʿ: "And if you do, then it is indeed wickedness in you," wickedness is rebellion.

* *

Others said: the meaning is: And if a scribe is harmed and writes other than what the dictator dictated, and a witness is harmed and alters and changes his testimony, "then it is indeed wickedness in you," meaning: then it is indeed falsehood.
Those who said this:

6433 - Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: "And if you do, then it is indeed wickedness in you," wickedness is falsehood. He said: This is wickedness, because the scribe lied when he altered his writing, so he lied, and the witness lied when he altered his testimony, so God informed them that it is falsehood.

* *

Abu Jaʿfar said: We have already shown earlier that the meaning of His words: "Nor let a scribe or a witness be harmed," is only: let them not be harmed by the one who seeks writing and the one who seeks testimony, to the extent sufficient. So His words "And if you do" are only a report from God to the one who harms them of His judgment concerning them, and that whoever harms them has disobeyed his Lord and sinned by it, [[His words: "athima bihi" (sinned by it). It has already preceded at 4:530, note 3, with the text: "ātiman bi-rabbihi" written without dots, as if it were "bi-rabbihi," but I did not find in the books of language "ātima bi-rabbihi," although I feared it might be correct in some way I have not verified; and I changed it there to "ātiman bi-riyā'ihi" (sinning by his pretension)... Here this text has come confirming what I feared, so it is established that the correct reading there is "ātiman bi-rabbihi," so I restrict it there, and in the books of language. The meaning of "atham bi-rabbihi": that is, he sent his sin before his Lord through his disobedience, so the "bā'" in it is for the purpose, as in His words, exalted: "And He was indeed kind to me when He brought me out of the prison," and as Kuthayyir said: "Harm us or be kind to us, not blameworthy / to us, nor hated if she turns away." Thus this is the decisive proof of the correctness of the expression that came in al-Tabari's speech, and praise be to God, Lord of the worlds, for His good guidance to us toward the truth.]] and committed what is not lawful for him, and departed from obedience to his Lord in that.

* *

Regarding the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: "And fear God; and God teaches you, and God is knowing of all things" (2:282).

Abu Jaʿfar said: By His words, His praise be exalted, "And fear God," he means: fear God, you who deal in debts, in writing and witnessing, that you harm them, and in other matters, the limits of God, that you neglect them. By His words "And God teaches you," he means: and makes clear to you what is obligatory for you and against you, so act upon it. "And God is knowing of all things," meaning: [of all things] of your deeds and others; He counts them against you, to recompense you for them.

* *

Those of the people of interpretation said in accordance with what we have said about that.
Those who said this:

6434 - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Ishaq related to us, saying: Abu Zuhayr related to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, regarding His words: "And God teaches you," he said: This is a teaching that God has taught you, so take by it.

The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He: "And if you are on a journey and do not find a scribe, then pledges taken into possession (rihan maqbudah)."

Abu Ja'far said: The readers differed concerning the recitation of this.

The readers of the metropolitan cities all recited it as ﴿kātiban﴾, meaning: "and you do not find anyone who will write down for you the document of the debt which you contracted for a specified term," "then pledges taken into possession."

* *

A group of the early readers recited: ﴿wa-lam tajidū kātiban﴾, meaning: "and there is no way for you to have the debt document written," either because the inkwell and the writing sheet are unavailable, or because a scribe is unavailable even though you have found the inkwell and the sheet.

* *

The recitation that it is not permissible to depart from, in our view, is the recitation of the metropolitan cities: "and you do not find a scribe," meaning: one who writes, because that is how it stands in the codices of the Muslims.

* *

[Abu Ja'far said: By this, He, may His praise be great, means:] [[This addition between the brackets is indispensable so that the sense is sound.]] "And if you, the debtors, are on a journey such that you do not find a scribe to write for you, and there is no way for you to have the debt document written for the term you contracted, which I have commanded you to write and to have witnessed, then take pledges for your debts which you contracted for the specified term, pledges that you take possession of from those to whom you owe, so that it may be a security for your wealth."

Mention of those who said what we have said concerning this:

6435 - al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Ishaq related to us, saying: Abu Zuhayr related to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak concerning His words: "And if you are on a journey and do not find a scribe, then pledges taken into possession": whoever is on a journey and sells on credit to a term, and does not find a scribe, is granted permission to take pledges into possession, and he may not take a pledge if he finds a scribe.

6436 - Ammar related to me, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far related to us, from his father, from al-Rabi' concerning His words: "And if you are on a journey and do not find a scribe," he says: a scribe who writes for you, "then pledges taken into possession."

6437 - Yahya ibn Abi Talib related to me, saying: Yazid informed us, saying: Juwaybir informed us, from al-Dahhak, who said: Any sale on credit to a term, God, Mighty and Majestic, commanded that it be written down and witnessed, and that is when one is resident. If people on a journey trade on credit to a term and do not find [a scribe], then pledges taken into possession. [[The addition between the brackets, I fear, may have dropped from the copyist.]]

* *

Mention of those who interpreted it according to the recitation we have related:

6438 - Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Hushaym related to us, saying: Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad informed us, from Miqsam, from Ibn Abbas: "then if you do not find a document" - by the document he meant the scribe, the writing sheet, the inkwell and the pen.

6439 - Ya'qub related to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah related to us, saying: Ibn Jurayj informed us, saying: My father informed me, from Ibn Abbas that he recited: "then if you do not find a document," and said: A man may find the sheet but not a scribe.

6440 - Ya'qub related to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah related to us, saying: Ibn Abi Najih related to us, from Mujahid, that he used to recite it: "then if you do not find a document," and he would say: A scribe may be found but not the sheet or the ink, and similar words.

6441 - al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah related to us, saying: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "and if you are on a journey and do not find a document," he says: ink - he recited it so - he says: If you do not find ink, then at that point the pledges taken into possession ("fa-rihnun maqbudah"). He said: The pledge is only in a journey.

6442 - al-Muthanna related to me, saying: al-Hajjaj related to us, saying: Hammad ibn Zayd related to us, from Shu'ayb ibn al-Hubhab, who said: Abu al-'Aliyah used to recite it, "then if you do not find a document." Abu al-'Aliyah said: The inkwell may be found but not the sheet.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The readers differed concerning the recitation of His words: "fa-rihan maqbudah."

The majority of the readers of the Hijaz and Iraq recited: ﴿fa-rihānun maqbūdatun﴾, meaning the plural of "rahn" (pledge), as "al-kibash" is the plural of "kabsh" (ram), "al-bighal" the plural of "baghl" (mule), and "al-ni'al" the plural of "na'l" (sandal).

* *

Others recited it: ﴿fa-ruhunun maqbūdatun﴾, meaning the plural of "rihan," and "ruhun" is a plural of a plural. Some have directed it to being the plural of "rahn," like "saqf" and "suquf" (roof, roofs).

* *

Others recited it: ﴿fa-ruhnun﴾ with the ha lightened, meaning the plural of "rahn," as "al-saqf" is pluralized as "suqfan." They said: We know of no noun on the pattern "fa'l" that takes the plural "fu'ul" or "fu'l" except "al-ruhun" and "al-ruhn," and "al-suqf" and "al-suqf."

Abu Ja'far said: The recitation that is more correct in this matter is the recitation of the one who recited "fa-rihānun maqbūdatun," because the well-known plural of a noun on the pattern "fa'l" is as one says "habl" and "hibal," "ka'b" and "ka'ab," and similar nouns. As for the plural of "fa'l" on "fu'ul" or "fu'l," it is rare and infrequent, occurring only in a few words, and it is said: "saqf, suquf, suqf," "qalb, qulub, qulb" from "qalb al-nakhl," [[All of this is strange and is not found in the lexicographical books.]] "jadd, judd" for the "jadd" meaning fortune. [[This too is strange, and I have not found it in the lexicographical books; they said its plural is "ajdad, ajud, judud." In the printed edition it read "hadd, hadd" with the ha, and "al-khatt," which is an error; in the manuscript it was unpointed.]] As for what came as a plural of "fa'l" on "fu'l," it is "thatt, thutt," "ward, wurd," and "khawd, khud."

What led the one who recited "fa-ruhnun maqbudah" to his recitation, I think, despite its irregularity in the plural of "fa'l," is that he found "al-rihan" used for the racing of horses, and wanted to turn that wording away from the ambiguity with the horse-race "rihan," which is not the sense of "rihan" as the plural of "rahn," and he found "al-ruhun" used as the plural of "rahn," as Qa'nab said:

Su'ad has departed, and 'Adan has become beyond her, and the pledges of your heart were closed upon her ... [[Mukhtarat Ibn al-Shajari 1:6; Lubab al-Adab 402-404; Lisan (rahn). Its reading there is "min qablika," which I consider better. "Ghalaqa al-rahn" means: when one cannot find what redeems the pledge at the stipulated time, then the pledgee owns the pledge in his possession. This was the custom of the Jahiliyyah, which Islam abolished. He says: I parted from you after the covenants, pacts and affections that I had given, and they went away with all of that, as the pledge goes with one who has it in hand.]]

* *

The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He: "And if one of you trusts another, let him who is trusted fulfill his trust and let him fear God, his Lord."

Abu Ja'far said: By this, He, may His praise be great, means: If the debtor is trusted by the owner of the wealth and the debt, so that he did not take a pledge from him during the journey, because of his trustworthiness with him regarding his wealth and his reliability, "then let him fear God," the debtor, "his Lord," meaning: let him fear God his Lord regarding the debt owed to his companion, lest he deny it, or withhold it, [[It is said: "lataa al-gharim bi-l-haqq duna al-batil": he defended and withheld the right. "Lattta haqqahu, wa lattta 'alayhi" means he denied and withheld it.]] or try to make off with it, thereby exposing himself to the punishment of God for what he has no power against. And let him pay back the debt he was entrusted with, to him.

* *

We have already mentioned the view of those who said: "This ruling from God, Mighty and Majestic, abrogates the rulings in the preceding verse concerning the command of God, Mighty and Majestic, regarding witnesses and the document." We have shown which of these views is most correct, so that is sufficient and need not be repeated here. [[See what has passed just above: pp. 53-55.]] And:

6443 - Yahya ibn Abi Talib related to me, saying: Yazid informed us, saying: Juwaybir informed us, from al-Dahhak concerning His words: "And if one of you trusts another, let him who is trusted fulfill his trust," that is meant only in a journey; as for residence, no, when one finds a scribe, it is not permissible to take a pledge, and they should not trust one another.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: What al-Dahhak said, that the trust does not belong to the owner of the debt when the debtor is present and there is a way to the scribe, the document and witnessing it, even if they are on a journey, is as he said, since we have shown its soundness previously.

As for what he said, that the ruling on the pledge is also the same as the trust, in that it is not permissible for the owner of the right to take a pledge against his wealth when he can reach a scribe and a witness, whether resident or traveling, it is a view with no meaning, given the soundness of the report from the Messenger of God ﷺ:

6444 - that he bought food on credit and pledged his armor for it. [[The report: 6444 - al-Tabari mentioned it without a chain. It is narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (Fath 5:100-102) and Muslim in his Sahih 11:39, 40 by several routes, from A'ishah, Mother of the Believers. Also Sunan al-Bayhaqi 6:36. It is said "nasa'tu 'anhu dayna nasa'an" (with the alif and the nun open): I deferred it. And "ba'tuhu bi-nasi'ah," meaning: on deferred terms.]]

* *

So it is permissible for a man to pledge against what he owes, and to take a pledge against his right of wealth, whether on a journey or in residence, due to the soundness of the report we have mentioned from the Messenger of God ﷺ, and it is known that the Prophet ﷺ, when he pledged as we have mentioned, was not without a scribe or a witness, since the scribe and the witness were never unavailable to him in his city at any time. Yet if the two of them trade with a pledge, then it is obligatory upon them, when they find a way to a scribe and a witness, or when the sale or the debt is for a specified term [[In the printed edition: "wa-kana al-bay'..." and I have kept what is in the manuscript.]], that they write it down and have witnesses to the wealth and the pledge. Leaving the writing and the witnessing is permitted only where they have no way to it.

* *

The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He: "And do not conceal testimony, for whoever conceals it, his heart is sinful, and God is Knowing of what you do."

Abu Ja'far said: This is an address from God, Mighty and Majestic, to the witnesses whom He commanded the debtor and the owner of the wealth to call upon, so He said to them: "And let the witnesses not refuse when they are called." Do not conceal, O witnesses, after you have given your testimony before the judges, as you testified to what you testified to, but respond to the one for whom you testify when he calls you to establish your testimony against his opponent regarding his right before the judge who will take his right for him.

Then He, Mighty and Majestic, informed the witness of what is upon him in concealing his testimony and refusing to give it and to stand by it when the one seeking testimony needs him to stand by it before a judge or a person of authority, so He said: "And whoever conceals it." Meaning: whoever conceals his testimony, "his heart is sinful," meaning: his heart is wicked, acquiring by its concealment disobedience to God, as:

6445 - al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Ishaq informed us, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far related to us, from his father, from al-Rabi' concerning His words: "And do not conceal testimony, for whoever conceals it, his heart is sinful," so it is not lawful for anyone to conceal testimony that he has, even if it is against himself, his parents, and whoever conceals it has incurred a great sin.

6446 - Musa related to me, saying: Amr related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi concerning His words: "whoever conceals it, his heart is sinful," he says: his heart is wicked.

6447 - al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The greatest of the major sins is associating partners with God, because God says: "Indeed, whoever associates others with God, God has forbidden him Paradise, and his refuge is the Fire" [[In the manuscript and the print: "wa-man yushrik bi-llah," which is not its recitation; the copyist erred and was mistaken.]] [Surah al-Ma'idah: 72], and false testimony, and concealing testimony, because God, Mighty and Majestic, says: "whoever conceals it, his heart is sinful."

* *

It has also been related from Ibn Abbas that he used to say: "It is incumbent on the witness to testify wherever he is called upon to testify, and to inform wherever he is asked to inform."

6448 - al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Suwayd related to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said: Amr ibn Dinar informed us, from Ibn Abbas, who said: If you have a testimony and someone asks you about it, inform him of it, and do not say: "Inform of it before the governor." Inform him of it, perhaps he will reconsider or refrain.

* *

As for His words: "and God is Knowing of what you do," He means: of what you do in your testimony, by establishing it and standing by it, or by concealing it when the one who seeks your testimony needs it, and of other than that of your inward and outward deeds, "Knowing," counting it against you, so that He may recompense you for all of it with your due reward, whether good or evil, according to what you deserve.

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 284 (part 1 of 3)**

On the exegesis (ta'wil, "interpretation") of His words, exalted is He: ﴿To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And whether you show what is within yourselves or conceal it, Allah will call you to account for it. Then He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills﴾

[[Neither the manuscript nor the printed edition contains His words, "Then He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills," in this place or elsewhere up to the discussion of the remainder of the verse. I have inserted it in its proper place.]]

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: By His words, exalted is His praise, "To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth," He means: to Allah belongs the dominion over everything in the heavens and on the earth, small and great. To Him belongs the management of all of it, and in His hand is its disposal and its turning. Nothing of it is hidden from Him, because He is its manager, its owner, and its disposer.

He, exalted is His praise, meant by this the concealment of testimony by witnesses. He says: Do not conceal the testimony, O witnesses, and whoever conceals it, his heart is sinful (yafjur qalbuhu). His concealing of that will not be hidden from Me, because I have knowledge of everything, and in My hand is the disposal of everything in the heavens and the earth and its possession. I know its hidden and its manifest. [[In the manuscript and the printed edition: "a'lamuhu khafi. . ." The context requires what I have adopted. In the manuscript: "wa jalilihi," which is acceptable, but what is in the printed edition better suits the context.]] So fear My punishment of you for your concealment of the testimony. This is a warning from Allah to whoever conceals it, and a frightening of him with it.

Then He informed them of what He will do with them in their Hereafter, and with those of their kind who harbored disobedience in their hearts and hid it, or displayed a grave sin and made it manifest from themselves, regarding being called to account for it. So He said: ﴿And whether you show what is within yourselves or conceal it﴾, meaning: whether you reveal, regarding the testimony you hold about the right of the owner of the property, denial and rejection, or you conceal that and keep it hidden within yourselves, and other evil deeds of yours, ﴿Allah will call you to account for it﴾. He means by this: He will reckon it against you from your deeds. [[In the printed and manuscript editions: "yuhsibu bihi 'alayhi min a'malihi," with the singular pronoun, but the context requires the plural as I have adopted. One says "ihtasaba 'alayhi bil-mal," meaning: I counted it against him and called him to account for it. "Ihtasaba" from "al-hisab" (reckoning) is like "i'tadda" from "al-add" (counting).]] So He will recompense whomever of you He wills among the evildoers for the evil of his deeds, [[In the manuscript and printed edition: "fa-yujazi man sha'…," and the context requires what I have adopted.]] and He will forgive whomever He wills among you of the evildoers. [[In the manuscript and printed edition: "wa ghafirun minkum li-man sha'…," which is an inversion arising from haste of the copyist; the correct form is what I have adopted.]]

* * *

Then the interpreters differed regarding what He meant by His words, ﴿And whether you show what is within yourselves or conceal it, Allah will call you to account for it﴾.

Some of them said, in accordance with what we have said: He meant by it the witnesses in their concealment of testimony, and that there reaches them every one of their kind who harbored disobedience or displayed it.

Those who said that:

6449 – Abu Za'idah Zakariyya ibn Yahya ibn Abi Za'idah narrated to me, saying: Ibn Fudayl narrated to us, from Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words, ﴿And whether you show what is within yourselves or conceal it, Allah will call you to account for it﴾: he said: meaning in the testimony.
[[The report: 6449 – "Ibn Fudayl" is Muhammad ibn Fudayl, who has appeared many times before. In the manuscript and printed edition it was "Abu Nufayl," but there is no narrator called "Abu Nufayl" who transmits from Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad; the one who transmits from him is Ibn Fudayl.]]

6450 – Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad, from Muqsim, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words, ﴿And whether you show what is within yourselves or conceal it﴾, he said: in the testimony.

6451 – Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Dawud was asked regarding His words, ﴿And whether you show what is within yourselves or conceal it, Allah will call you to account for it﴾, and he related to us from 'Ikrimah, who said: It is the testimony when you conceal it.

6452 – Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from 'Amr and Abu Sa'id, that he heard 'Ikrimah say concerning this verse, ﴿And whether you show what is within yourselves or conceal it﴾: in the testimony.

6453 – Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-Suddi, from al-Sha'bi, regarding His words, ﴿And whether you show what is within yourselves or conceal it﴾, he said: in the testimony.

6454 – Ya'qub narrated to us, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad informed us, from Muqsim, from Ibn 'Abbas, that he said concerning this verse, ﴿And whether you show what is within yourselves or conceal it, Allah will call you to account for it﴾: it was revealed concerning the concealment of testimony and its establishment.

6455 – Yahya ibn Abi Talib narrated to me, saying: Yazid informed us, saying: Juwaybir informed us, from 'Ikrimah, regarding His words, ﴿And whether you show what is within yourselves or conceal it, Allah will call you to account for it﴾, meaning: the concealment of testimony and its establishment in its proper manner.

* * *

Others said: "Rather, this verse was revealed as an announcement from Allah, blessed and exalted, to His servants that He will hold them accountable for what their hands have earned and for what their souls have whispered to them of things they did not do."

Then those who interpreted it in this way differed.

Some of them said: "Then Allah abrogated that by His words, ﴿Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity. It will have [the consequence of] what it has earned, and it will bear [the consequence of] what it has earned﴾ [Surah al-Baqarah: 286]."

Those who said that:

6456 – Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ishaq ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from Mus'ab ibn Thabit, from al-'Ala' ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: When there was revealed, ﴿To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and whether you show what is within yourselves or conceal it, Allah will call you to account for it﴾, it weighed heavily upon the people, and they said: "O Messenger of Allah, indeed we will be held accountable for what we whisper to ourselves! We are destroyed!" So Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed: ﴿Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity﴾, to His words: ﴿Our Lord, do not impose blame on us if we forget or make mistakes﴾. My father said: Abu Hurayrah said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: Allah said: "Yes." ﴿Our Lord, and do not place upon us a burden like that You placed upon those before us﴾, to the end of the verse. My father said: Abu Hurayrah said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: Allah, mighty and majestic, said: "Yes."
[[The report: 6456 – Ishaq ibn Sulayman al-Razi al-'Abdi: trustworthy and firm in hadith, a great worshipper, among the excellent Muslims. The group of compilers narrated from him.
Mus'ab ibn Thabit ibn 'Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr: the imams spoke of him. Ahmad and Ibn Ma'in and others weakened him. al-Zuhri praised him. Abu Hatim said: "Truthful, frequently erring, not strong, and Ishaq ibn Sulayman narrates from him." Yet al-Bukhari included him in al-Kabir (4/1/353) and mentioned no criticism of him. It appears that whoever weakened him went only to his frequent error, as Abu Hatim did. In any case, he did not stand alone in this hadith, as will come in the takhrij (tracing of sources).
Part of the hadith will come: 6538, with this chain.
Ahmad related it in al-Musnad: 9333 (2: 412, Halabi), from 'Affan, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ibrahim al-Qass al-Madani, from al-'Ala' ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, with it, in a longer version than here.
This 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ibrahim is trustworthy; Ibn Ma'in and others declared him trustworthy. He is biographed in al-Ta'jil and in Ibn Abi Hatim (2/2/211).
Muslim related it, also in a longer version, (11: 46-47), and Ibn Hibban in his Sahih (139; 1: 225-226, from the manuscript of al-Ihsan). Both via Yazid ibn Zuray', from Rawh ibn al-Qasim, from al-'Ala', with it.
Ibn Kathir related it (2: 79-80) from the version in al-Musnad.
al-Hafiz (Ibn Hajar) pointed to it in al-Fath (8: 154), from Muslim's version.
al-Suyuti mentioned it (1: 374), and added its attribution to Abu Dawud in his Nasikh, and Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim. He did not attribute it to Sahih Ibn Hibban.]]

6457 – Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us; and Sufyan ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Adam ibn Sulayman, the client of Khalid ibn Khalid, who said: I heard Sa'id ibn Jubayr narrate, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: When this verse was revealed, ﴿And whether you show what is within yourselves or conceal it, Allah will call you to account for it, then He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills﴾, something entered their hearts from it that had not entered them from anything else. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "We hear and we obey and we submit." He said: So Allah, mighty and majestic, cast faith into their hearts. He said: So Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed: ﴿The Messenger believes in what was revealed to him from his Lord﴾. Abu Kurayb said: He recited: ﴿Our Lord, do not impose blame on us if we forget or make mistakes﴾. He said: He said: "You have done so." ﴿Our Lord, and do not place upon us a burden like that You placed upon those before us﴾. He said: "You have done so." ﴿Our Lord, and do not burden us with that which we have no ability to bear﴾. He said: "You have done so." ﴿And pardon us, and forgive us, and have mercy upon us. You are our protector, so give us victory over the disbelieving people﴾. He said: "You have done so."
[[The report: 6457 – Sufyan ibn Waki' narrates it from his father. His father narrates it from Sufyan, who is al-Thawri. In the printed edition the words "He said: My father narrated to us" have been omitted here, which is an error. The correct chain will come: 6537, where al-Tabari related part of it in abridged form, with this chain.
Adam ibn Sulayman al-Qurashi, client of Khalid ibn Khalid ibn 'Uqbah ibn Abi Mu'ayt: trustworthy. He is the father of Yahya ibn Adam, author of the book al-Kharaj.
The hadith was related by Ahmad in al-Musnad (2070), from Waki', with this chain.
Likewise Muslim related it (1: 47), from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, Abu Kurayb, and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim (that is, Ibn Rahawayh), all three from Waki', with it.
In al-Tahdhib, in the biography of Adam ibn Sulayman, it is stated that Muslim included this single hadith as a mutaba'ah (corroborating report). That is not so; rather it is an asl (primary report), not a mutaba'ah, since Muslim did not relate it through anyone other than him.
al-Hakim related it in al-Mustadrak (2: 286), via Ibn Rahawayh, from Waki'. He said: "This hadith has a sahih chain, though the two (Bukhari and Muslim) did not record it." al-Dhahabi agreed.
Ibn Kathir mentioned it (2: 81) from the version in al-Musnad, then pointed to Muslim's version.
al-Hafiz pointed to it in al-Fath (8: 154), from Muslim's version.
al-Suyuti mentioned it (1: 374), and added its attribution to al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i, Ibn al-Mundhir, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Asma' wa al-Sifat.
Part of its meaning will come: 6464, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, as a mursal (a report in which a Successor reports directly from the Prophet, omitting the companion) that is not connected, so its connection is established from this report.]]

6458 – Abu al-Raddad al-Misri 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Salam narrated to me, saying: Abu Zur'ah Wahb Allah ibn Rashid narrated to us, from Haywah ibn Shurayh, who said: I heard Yazid ibn Abi Habib say: Ibn Shihab said: Sa'id ibn Marjanah narrated to me, who said: I came to 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar, and he recited this verse: ﴿And whether you show what is within yourselves or conceal it, Allah will call you to account for it, then He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills﴾. Then Ibn 'Umar said: "If Allah holds us to account for this verse, we will surely perish!" Then Ibn 'Umar wept until his tears flowed. He said: Then I came to 'Abd Allah ibn al-'Abbas and said: "O Abu 'Abbas, I came to Ibn 'Umar and he recited this verse: ﴿And whether you show what is within yourselves or conceal it﴾, to the end of the verse, then said: 'If Allah holds us to account for it, we will surely perish!' Then he wept until his tears flowed!" Ibn 'Abbas said: "May Allah forgive 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar! The Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ were struck with fear by it just as Ibn 'Umar was struck with fear by it." So Allah revealed: ﴿Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity. It will have [the consequence of] what it has earned, and it will bear [the consequence of] what it has earned﴾. Then Allah abrogated the whispering, and established the speech and the deed.
[[The report: 6458 – Abu al-Raddad al-Misri, 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Salam, al-Tabari's teacher: trustworthy. Ibn Abi Hatim's biography (2/2/107) says: "We heard from him in Egypt, and he was truthful."
Abu Zur'ah Wahb Allah ibn Rashid: this is the first time his name is correctly recorded in the printed edition. It appeared earlier at 2377, 2891, and 5386, where it was distorted in the printed edition throughout. We gave his biography at the first of these.
Sa'id ibn Marjanah: he is Sa'id ibn 'Abd Allah, client of Quraysh. Marjanah, with a fatha on the mim and a sukun on the ra', was his mother. al-Hafiz said in al-Tahdhib: "Accordingly, it should be written: Ibn Marjanah, with an alif." He was a trustworthy Successor. His hearing from Abu Hurayrah is firmly established, contrary to those who claimed otherwise, as we showed in al-Musnad (7583).
The hadith will come after this: 6459, from another route via Ibn Shihab. We will mention its takhrij there.]]

6459 – Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Yunus ibn Yazid informed me, from Ibn Shihab, from Sa'id ibn Marjanah, who narrates: that while he was sitting, he heard 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar recite this verse, ﴿To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and whether you show what is within yourselves or conceal it﴾, to the end of the verse, and he said: "By Allah, if Allah holds us to account for this, we will surely perish!" Then Ibn 'Umar wept until his sobbing was heard. Ibn Marjanah said: "So I rose and came to Ibn 'Abbas and related to him what Ibn 'Umar had recited and what he did when he recited it." 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abbas said: "May Allah forgive Abu 'Abd al-Rahman! By my life, the Muslims were struck by it when it was revealed just as 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar was struck. Then Allah revealed after it: ﴿Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity﴾, to the end of the surah." Ibn 'Abbas said: "This whispering was something the Muslims had no capacity for, until Allah, mighty and majestic, decreed that for the soul is what it has earned and upon it is what it has earned, in speech and in deed."
[[The report: 6459 – It is the preceding hadith, similar to it.
Ibn Kathir mentioned it (2: 81-82) from this place in al-Tabari.
al-Hafiz mentioned it in abridged form (al-Fath, 8: 154) from this place also. He said: "al-Tabari related, with a sahih chain, from al-Zuhri..." etc.
al-Suyuti mentioned it (1: 374), attributing it to 'Abd ibn Humayd, Abu Dawud in his Nasikh, Ibn Jarir, al-Tabarani, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu'ab.
See the following hadiths: 6460–6464.]]

6460 – al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, saying: I heard al-Zuhri say regarding His words, ﴿And whether you show what is within yourselves or conceal it﴾: He said: Ibn 'Umar recited it and wept, and said: "Indeed we will be held accountable for what we whisper to ourselves!" He wept until his sobbing was heard. A man rose from his presence, came to Ibn 'Abbas, and mentioned that to him. He said: "May Allah have mercy on Ibn 'Umar! The Muslims were struck by something similar to what he was struck by, until there was revealed: ﴿Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity. It will have [the consequence of] what it has earned, and it will bear [the consequence of] what it has earned﴾."
[[The report: 6460 – This is a mursal hadith. al-Zuhri did not hear it from Ibn 'Umar, nor from Ibn 'Abbas. It is an abridgement of the two preceding hadiths and of hadith 6462. al-Zuhri heard the story from Sa'id ibn Marjanah and from Salim ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar.]]

6461 – al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, from Ja'far ibn Sulayman, from Humayd al-A'raj, from Mujahid, who said: I was with Ibn 'Umar and he recited: ﴿And whether you show what is within yourselves or conceal it﴾, the verse, and he wept. I entered upon Ibn 'Abbas and mentioned that to him. Ibn 'Abbas laughed and said: "May Allah have mercy on Ibn 'Umar! Does he not know concerning what it was revealed? When this verse was revealed, it greatly distressed the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and they said: 'O Messenger of Allah, we are destroyed!' The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to them: 'Say: "We hear and we obey."' So it was abrogated by: ﴿The Messenger believes in what was revealed to him from his Lord, and the believers. Each one believes in Allah and His angels and His books and His messengers. We make no distinction between any of His messengers﴾, to His words: ﴿It will bear [the consequence of] what it has earned﴾. Thus [the whisperings of] the soul were excused for them, and they were held to account for their deeds."
[[The report: 6461 – Ja'far ibn Sulayman: he is al-Dab'i, whose trustworthiness was established at 2905.
Humayd al-A'raj: he is Humayd ibn Qays al-Makki, reciter of the people of Mecca. His trustworthiness was established at 3352.
The hadith was related by Ahmad in al-Musnad (3071), from 'Abd al-Razzaq, from Ma'mar, from Humayd al-A'raj, with it.
It is thus apparent from this report of al-Tabari that 'Abd al-Razzaq heard it from two teachers: from Ma'mar, and from Ja'far ibn Sulayman, both of whom related it to him from Humayd al-A'raj.
Ibn Kathir mentioned it (2: 81) from Ahmad's version in al-Musnad, and likewise al-Hafiz mentioned it in al-Fath (8: 154) from Ahmad's version.
al-Suyuti mentioned it (1: 374), and added its attribution to 'Abd al-Razzaq and Ibn al-Mundhir.
It has the same meaning as the preceding hadiths: 6458–6460.
