His words, "I was with Ibn 'Umar and he said: (And whether you show what is within yourselves...)..." – thus in the manuscript and the printed edition. Perhaps the correct form is "fa-qara'a" (he recited), instead of "fa-qal" (he said). This is what is found in the version in al-Musnad and in those who transmitted from it.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 284 (part 2 of 3):

His saying at the end of the report, "fa-tajuzu lahum min hadith al-nafs" (so it passes over for them the speech of the soul), is thus in the manuscript and also in the printed edition. Perhaps the correct reading is "'an hadith al-nafs" (concerning the speech of the soul), as in the narration of the Musnad.]]

6462. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, from Sufyan ibn Husayn, from al-Zuhri, from Salim, that his father recited: "Whether you show what is in your souls or conceal it, Allah will call you to account for it," and his eyes welled with tears. His action reached Ibn Abbas, who said: "May Allah have mercy on Abu 'Abd al-Rahman! He did just as the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did when it was revealed. Then it was abrogated by the verse that follows it: ﴿Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity﴾."

[[The report: 6462. Sufyan ibn Husayn al-Wasiti: the discussion of his narration from al-Zuhri, and that it contains confusions, has passed at 3471. But it now appears to me that there is exaggeration in this from Ibn Hibban. For al-Bukhari included him in al-Kabir 2/2/90 and pointed to a narration from al-Zuhri, but did not mention any defect in it. Furthermore, the imams declared this hadith authentic from his narration from al-Zuhri, as will come.
The hadith was transmitted by Abu Ja'far ibn al-Nahhas in al-Nasikh wa al-Mansukh, p. 86, and by al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak 2:287. Both are from the route of Yazid ibn Harun, from Sufyan ibn Husayn, with this chain. Al-Hakim said: "This hadith has a sound chain, though they [al-Bukhari and Muslim] did not record it." Al-Dhahabi agreed with him.
Then Ibn Kathir mentioned it at this place, 2:82, after the previous narrations, then said: "These are sound routes from Ibn Abbas."
I had favored the reliability of Sufyan ibn Husayn, including in his narration from al-Zuhri, in what I wrote as a commentary on Tahdhib al-Sunan of al-Mundhiri, vol. 3 p. 402, but I forgot it when I wrote what passed at 3471.
The hadith was also mentioned by al-Suyuti 1:374, and he added its attribution to Ibn Abi Shaybah.]]

6463. Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: This verse was abrogated: "Whether you show what is in your souls or conceal it" by ﴿Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity﴾.

[[The report: 6463. Abu Ahmad: he is al-Zubayri, Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr al-Asadi. He narrates from Sufyan al-Thawri, and Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrates from him.
This hadith is mursal (a report where the Successor omits the Companion), because it is Sa'id ibn Jubayr relating the information that the verse was abrogated.
A narration from Sa'id ibn Jubayr from Ibn Abbas has preceded at 6457, which perhaps points to this meaning.]]

6464. Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Adam ibn Sulayman, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: When this verse was revealed: "If you show what is in your souls or conceal it," they said: "Will we be held accountable for what our souls speak to us, while our limbs do not act upon it?" He said: Then this verse was revealed: ﴿Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity. It has what it earned and it bears what it has earned. Our Lord, do not take us to task if we forget or err﴾. He said: "He says: 'I have done so.'" He said: "This Ummah was given the closing verses of Surat al-Baqarah, which were not given to the nations before it."

[[The report: 6464. This is also a mursal hadith, from the narration of Sa'id ibn Jubayr, but it is part of the meaning of the previous hadith, 6457, which Sa'id narrated from Ibn Abbas with a connected chain.
Part of it will come at 6539, with this chain, with a distortion in the name of the narrator from Sufyan, as we will mention there, God willing.]]

6465. Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Jabir ibn Nuh narrated to us, saying: Isma'il narrated to us, from Amir: "Whether you show what is in your souls or conceal it, Allah will call you to account for it. He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills." He said: It was abrogated by the verse after it, His saying: ﴿Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity. It has what it earned and it bears what it has earned﴾.

6466. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mughirah, from al-Sha'bi: "Whether you show what is in your souls or conceal it, Allah will call you to account for it." He said: It was abrogated by the verse after it: ﴿Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity﴾. And His saying "Whether you show" (he said): He calls to account for what one shows of a secret or conceals of a secret, and then the one after it abrogated it.

6467. Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Sayyar informed us, from al-Sha'bi, who said: When this verse was revealed: "Whether you show what is in your souls or conceal it, Allah will call you to account for it. He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills," it became severe, until this verse was revealed after it: ﴿It has what it earned and it bears what it has earned﴾. He said: So it abrogated what was before it.

6468. Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, from Ibn 'Awn, who said: They mentioned to al-Sha'bi: "Whether you show what is in your souls or conceal it," until reaching ﴿It has what it earned and it bears what it has earned﴾. He said: Al-Sha'bi said: "It came to this, it returned to the end of the verse."

6469. Yahya ibn Abi Talib narrated to me, saying: Yazid informed us, saying: Juwaybir informed us, from al-Dahhak, concerning His saying: "Whether you show what is in your souls or conceal it." He said: Ibn Mas'ud said: "The reckoning was before this was revealed: ﴿It has what it earned and it bears what it has earned﴾. When it was revealed, it abrogated the verse that was before it."

6470. It was narrated to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd narrated to us, who said: I heard al-Dahhak mention, from Ibn Mas'ud, the like of it.

6471. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Bayan, from al-Sha'bi, who said: "Whether you show what is in your souls or conceal it" was abrogated by ﴿It has what it earned and it bears what it has earned﴾.

6472. Ibn WakI' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Musa ibn 'Ubaydah, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b; and Sufyan, from Jabir, from Mujahid; and from Ibrahim ibn Muhajir, from Mujahid. They said: This verse was abrogated: ﴿Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity﴾, "Whether you show what is in your souls or conceal it," the verse.

6473. Ibn WakI' narrated to us, saying: [...] narrated to us, from Isra'il, from Jabir, from 'Ikrimah and 'Amir, the like of it.

6474. Al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Al-Hajjaj narrated to us, saying: Hammad narrated to us, from Humayd, from al-Hasan, concerning His saying: "Whether you show what is in your souls or conceal it," to the end of the verse. He said: It erased it: ﴿Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity. It has what it earned and it bears what it has earned﴾.

[[The report: 6474. "Hammad" is Hammad ibn Salamah, and "Humayd" is Humayd al-Tawil. In the printed edition and the manuscript it read "Hammad ibn Humayd," but there is no one among the narrators of this report known by this name. Hajjaj ibn al-Minhal narrates from Hammad ibn Salamah, and Hammad narrates from his maternal uncle Humayd al-Tawil, and Humayd al-Tawil narrates from al-Hasan.]]

6475. Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, that he said: This verse was abrogated, meaning His saying: ﴿Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity﴾, the verse that preceded it: "Whether you show what is in your souls or conceal it, Allah will call you to account for it."

6476. Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, concerning His saying: "Whether you show what is in your souls or conceal it, Allah will call you to account for it." He said: It was abrogated by His saying: ﴿Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity﴾.

6477. Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd narrated to me, saying: When this verse was revealed: "Whether you show what is in your souls or conceal it, Allah will call you to account for it," to the end of the verse, it was severe upon the Muslims and caused them great hardship. They said: "O Messenger of Allah, if something occurs in our souls that we do not act upon, will we be taken to account for it?" He (ﷺ) said: "Perhaps you say what the Children of Israel said: 'We hear and we disobey'!" They said: "Rather, we hear and we obey, O Messenger of Allah!" He said: Then the Qur'an was revealed to relieve them of it: "The Messenger believes in what was revealed to him from his Lord, and the believers. Each one believes in Allah, His angels, His books, and His messengers," to His saying: ﴿Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity. It has what it earned and it bears what it has earned﴾. He said: So He directed it to actions and left aside what occurs in the hearts.

6478. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Al-Hajjaj narrated to us, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, from Sayyar, from Abu al-Hakam, from al-Sha'bi, from Abu 'Ubaydah ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, concerning His saying: "Whether you show what is in your souls or conceal it, Allah will call you to account for it." He said: This verse that follows it abrogated it: ﴿It has what it earned and it bears what it has earned﴾.

6479. Musa narrated to me, saying: 'Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, His saying: "Whether you show what is in your souls or conceal it, Allah will call you to account for it." He said: On the day this verse was revealed, they were being held to account for what their souls whispered to them and what they did. They complained of that to the Prophet (ﷺ), and they said: "If one of us acts, or does not act, will he be taken to account for it? By Allah, we do not control whispering!" So Allah abrogated it by this verse that comes after it, His saying: ﴿Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity﴾, the verse. So the speech of the soul was among what you were unable to bear.

[[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "mimma lam tutiquu, al-Ayah" (of what you could not bear, the verse). The copyist placed "al-Ayah" late, and I have returned it to its place before.]]

* *

6480. It was narrated to me from 'Ammar, who said: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from Qatadah, that 'A'ishah, the Mother of the Believers, may Allah be pleased with her, said: It was abrogated by His saying: ﴿It has what it earned and it bears what it has earned﴾.

Others said, among those who held that the meaning of this is: "The announcement from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, to His servants that He will call them to account for what their hands earned and their limbs did, and for what their souls spoke to them of that they had not done":

[[See what passed at p. 103 and what follows.]] "This verse is muhkam (definitive) and not abrogated, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, calls His creation to account for what they did of deeds, and for what they did not do of what they harbored in their souls, intended, and desired. He forgives it to the believers, and He holds to account the people of disbelief and hypocrisy for it."

Those who said that:

6481. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His saying: "Whether you show what is in your souls or conceal it, Allah will call you to account for it." It was not abrogated, but when Allah, Mighty and Majestic, gathers the creation on the Day of Resurrection, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: "I will inform you of what you concealed in your souls, which My angels did not witness." As for the believers, He informs them and forgives them what their souls spoke to them, and this is His saying: "Allah will call you to account for it," meaning: He will inform you. As for the people of doubt and suspicion, He informs them of what they concealed of denial, [[In the manuscript and printed edition, after "of denial" there is: "And this is His saying: He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills." That is undoubtedly an addition by the copyist. If it is not from him, its place would be before that, after His saying "Allah will call you to account for it" and before "As for the people of doubt..." But I preferred to omit it, because al-Suyuti cited it in al-Durr al-Manthur 1:375 without mentioning this addition in both places.]] and this is His saying: ﴿But He will call you to account for what your hearts have earned﴾ [Surat al-Baqarah 2:225], of doubt and hypocrisy.

6482. Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas: "Whether you show what is in your souls or conceal it, Allah will call you to account for it." That is the secret of your deeds and their openness, Allah will call you to account for it. There is no believing servant who keeps secret in his soul a good thing to act upon; if he acts upon it, ten good deeds are recorded for him, and if he is not able to act upon it, one good deed is recorded for him, because he is a believer. Allah is pleased with the secret and open [deeds] of the believers. If it is evil that he speaks to himself about, Allah becomes aware of it and informs him of it on the Day when hidden things are tested. If he does not act upon it, Allah will not take him to account for it until he acts upon it; if he acts upon it, Allah will overlook it, as He said: ﴿Those are the ones from whom We accept the best of what they did and overlook their evil deeds﴾ [Surat al-Ahqaf 46:16].

6483. Yahya ibn Abi Talib narrated to me, saying: Yazid informed us, saying: Juwaybir informed us, from al-Dahhak, concerning His saying: ﴿Whether you show what is in your souls or conceal it, Allah will call you to account for it﴾, the verse. He said: Ibn 'Abbas said: "Allah will say on the Day of Resurrection: 'My scribes only recorded of your deeds what appeared of them. As for what you kept secret in your souls, I will call you to account for it today, so I will forgive whom I wish and punish whom I wish.'"

6484. Yahya ibn Abi Talib narrated to me, saying: 'Ali ibn 'Asim informed us, saying: Bayan informed us, from Bishr, from Qays ibn Abi Hazim, who said: When the Day of Resurrection comes, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says, making the creation hear: "My scribes used to record against you only what appeared from you. As for what you kept secret, they did not record it nor know it. I am Allah, who knows all of that about you better. I will forgive whom I wish and punish whom I wish."

6485. It was narrated to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd informed us, who said: I heard al-Dahhak say concerning His saying: "Whether you show what is in your souls or conceal it, Allah will call you to account for it." Ibn 'Abbas used to say: "When people are summoned to the reckoning, Allah informs them of what they used to conceal in their souls of what they did not do. Then He says: 'Indeed, nothing escaped Me, and I will inform you of the evil you used to conceal, and your guardian angels did not witness it.'" This is the reckoning.

6486. Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Abu Tumaylah narrated to us, from 'Ubayd ibn Sulayman, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn 'Abbas, the like of it.

6487. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi' concerning His saying: "Whether you show what is in your souls or conceal it, Allah will call you to account for it." He said: It is muhkam; nothing abrogated it. He says: "Allah will call you to account for it," meaning: Allah will make him know on the Day of Resurrection: "You concealed in your breast such and such!" He does not punish him for it.

6488. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from 'Amr ibn 'Ubayd, from al-Hasan, who said: It is muhkam, not abrogated.

6489. Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Najih narrated to us, from Mujahid, concerning His saying: "Whether you show what is in your souls or conceal it, Allah will call you to account for it." He said: From doubt and certainty.

6490. Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, from 'Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: "Whether you show what is in your souls or conceal it, Allah will call you to account for it." He means: in doubt and certainty. [[In the printed edition: "fi al-yaqin wa al-shakk" (in certainty and doubt). The order was reversed there, and I have restored what is in the manuscript.]]

6491. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: So the interpretation of this verse, according to the view of Ibn 'Abbas which 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah transmitted, is: "Whether you show" some matter of deeds, so that you make it manifest with your bodies and limbs, "or conceal it," so that you keep it secret in your souls, and no one among My creation has witnessed it, "Allah will call you to account for it. I will forgive all of that to the people of faith, and I will punish the people of polytheism and hypocrisy in My religion."

* *

As for the narration transmitted from him by al-Dahhak, through 'Ubayd ibn Sulayman from him, [[This is No. 6486.]] and what al-Rabi' ibn Anas said, [[This is No. 6487.]] its interpretation is: "If you show what is in your souls, so that you do the acts of disobedience, or intend it in your souls and conceal it, Allah will inform you of it on the Day of Resurrection, and He will forgive whom He wills and punish whom He wills."

* *

As for the statement of Mujahid, [[This is No. 6489 and what follows.]] its meaning resembles the meaning of the statement of Ibn 'Abbas transmitted by 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah.

* *

Others said, [those] who said: "This verse is muhkam (definitive), and it is not abrogated," and they agreed with those who said: "The meaning of that is: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, informed His servants of what He would do with them regarding what they showed and concealed of their deeds," [their] meaning is: Allah will call to account all His creation for everything they showed of their evil deeds and everything they kept secret, and He will punish them for it. Except that His punishment of them for what they concealed without doing, is what befalls them in this world of calamities and matters over which they grieve and suffer.

Those who said that:

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 284 (part 3 of 3):

6492 - Yahya ibn Abi Talib related to me, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Juwaybir informed us, from al-Dahhak, concerning His words: "Whether you show what is in your souls or conceal it, Allah will call you to account for it," the verse. He said: Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, used to say: Whoever resolves upon an evil deed and does not do it, Allah sends upon him worry and grief equal to what he resolved upon of the evil deed without doing it, and that is his expiation.

6493 - I was told on the authority of al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say concerning His words: "Whether you show what is in your souls or conceal it, Allah will call you to account for it." He said: Aisha used to say: Every servant who resolves upon disobedience, or whose soul speaks of it to him, Allah calls him to account for it in this world; he fears, grieves and worries.

6494 - al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Abu Tumaylah related to me, on the authority of Ubayd, on the authority of al-Dahhak, who said: Aisha said concerning that: Every servant who resolves upon evil and disobedience, and whose soul speaks of it to him, Allah calls him to account in this world; he fears, grieves, and his worry intensifies, and nothing of that reaches him, just as he resolved upon evil but did not do anything of it.

6495 - al-Rabi' related to us, saying: Asad ibn Musa related to us, saying: Hammad ibn Salamah related to us, on the authority of Ali ibn Zayd, on the authority of Umayyah, that she asked Aisha about this verse: "Whether you show what is in your souls or conceal it, Allah will call you to account for it," and "Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it" [Surah al-Nisa: 123]. She said: No one has asked me about it since I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He said: "O Aisha, this is Allah's reproach of the servant with what befalls him of fever, misfortune and thorn-prick, even the merchandise a man places in his sleeve and then loses, so he panics over it and finds it in his pocket. Indeed the believer comes out of his sins as red gold comes out of the furnace." [Note: On the hadith: Ali ibn Zayd is Ibn Jud'an. Umayyah is the daughter of Abdullah, a Tabi'iyah who narrated from Aisha only this hadith. Ali ibn Zayd is her step-son. Her biography was given earlier at 4897. The printed edition here reads "on the authority of his mother," which is an error; it occurs in some copies of al-Tirmidhi too. If those copies were correct there would be no harm, since it is not unlikely that he called his stepmother "his mother." The hadith was narrated by al-Tayalisi (1584), from Hammad ibn Salamah, from Ali ibn Zayd, from "Umayyah bint Abdullah." Ahmad in al-Musnad (6/218, Halabi) narrated it from Bahz, from Hammad, with "from Umayyah." al-Tirmidhi (4/78-79) narrated it through Rawh ibn Ubadah, from Hammad ibn Salamah, with "from Umayyah," and said: "This is a hasan gharib hadith from the hadith of Aisha, which we know only from the hadith of Hammad ibn Salamah." Ibn Abi Hatim, as transmitted by Ibn Kathir (2/85), narrated it through Sulayman ibn Harb from Hammad ibn Salamah, with "from his father" in place of "from Umayyah," which is a printing error. Ibn Kathir said: "Ali ibn Zayd ibn Jud'an is weak and unusual in his narrations. He narrates this hadith from his father's wife, Umm Muhammad Umayyah bint Abdullah, from Aisha, and she has no other narration from her in the books." I say: Ali ibn Zayd is not weak, as we stated at 4897 and as we preferred in the commentary on the Musnad (783). al-Suyuti (1/375) mentioned it and added its attribution to Ibn al-Mundhir and al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman. The phrase "this is Allah's reproach of the servant" means: what befalls a person that pains him, with which Allah reproaches him so that He expiates his sins by it. This is what is established in al-Tabari and al-Musnad. What is in al-Tayalisi, al-Tirmidhi and al-Durr al-Manthur is "mu'atabah Allah" (Allah's reproach), whose meaning is close to this. In Ibn Kathir it is "mubaya'ah" (pledge), which is an error. Al-nakbah, with the nun vowelled with a fatha: that a stone strikes his fingernail or finger. From this comes the term nakbah for what befalls a person. Al-bid'ah: a small amount of wealth that one sends into trade; then the goods were also called bid'ah. Al-dibn, with a kasra and then a sukun: the space between the armpit and the flank. Al-tibr: fragments of gold and silver before they are worked; once worked, it is gold or silver. Al-kir, with a kasra on the kaf, the blacksmith's bellows: a thick skin or leather bag with edges, which blows the fire until it blazes.]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of the interpretations we have mentioned for the verse is the saying of the one who said: "It is muhkam (decisive), not abrogated (mansukh)." That is because abrogation in a ruling occurs only by negating it with another, which negates it in all its aspects. [Note: In the printed edition: "illa yanfihi" with a yā' at its beginning, and in the manuscript it is undotted. In both: "bi-akhar lahu nafin," and the correct reading is to add "huwa" as I have set it. Thus the statement is sound. See what was said on "abrogation" earlier at p. 54, and the note: 1.] There is nothing in His words, mighty and majestic: "Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity; it has what it earned and it bears what it acquired," that negates the ruling He informed His servants of in His words: "or conceal it, Allah will call you to account for it." Because being called to account does not necessitate punishment, nor censure for what the servant is called to account for of his sins.

Allah, mighty and majestic, has informed us about the criminals that when their books of deeds are presented to them on the Day of Resurrection, they say: (Woe to us! What is this Book that leaves out nothing small or great but has counted it!) [Surah al-Kahf: 49]. So He informed that their books record against them their minor and major deeds. The books, though they count the minor and major sins, do not necessitate for the people of faith in Allah and His Messenger, and the people of obedience to Him, that they be punished for everything the books have counted of sins. Because Allah, mighty and majestic, promised them forgiveness of minor sins by their avoidance of major sins, saying in His revelation: "If you avoid the major sins that you are forbidden, We will expiate your bad deeds from you and admit you to a noble entrance" [Surah al-Nisa: 31]. That, then, is Allah's calling to account of His believing servants for what He calls them to account for of matters their souls concealed, without making punishment obligatory for them from it, [Note: In the printed edition: "fa-dall anna muhasabat Allah..." and I have kept what is in the manuscript. In the printed and manuscript editions after this: "ghayr muwajibah lahum minhu 'uqubah," and the context requires "ghayr muwajib..." as I have set it.] but rather His calling them to account, if Allah wills, for it, so that He makes them know His favour toward them by His pardon for them of it, as has reached us from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the report that:

6496 - Ahmad ibn al-Miqdam related to me, saying: al-Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman related to us, saying: I heard my father, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Safwan ibn Muhriz, on the authority of Ibn Umar, on the authority of the Prophet of Allah ﷺ, who said: Allah brings His believing servant near on the Day of Resurrection until He places His kanaf (covering) upon him, then makes him acknowledge his sins, saying: Do you know? He says: Yes! He says: I concealed them for you in the world and I forgive them for you today! Then He shows him his good deeds, and he says: "Here, read my book!" [Surah al-Haqqah: 19], or as he said. As for the disbeliever, he is called out upon the heads of witnesses.

[Note: On the hadith: Safwan ibn Muhriz al-Mazani is a reliable and eminent Tabi'i, with merit and piety. The hadith is an abridgement of the one that follows, and we will mention its takhrij there, Allah willing.]

6497 - Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Ibn Abi Adi related to us, on the authority of Sa'id and Hisham; and Ya'qub related to me, saying: Ibn Ulayyah related to us, saying: Hisham informed us; both said in their narration on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Safwan ibn Muhriz, who said: While we were circumambulating the House with Abdullah ibn Umar, and he was circumambulating, a man confronted him and said: O Ibn Umar, did you not hear the Messenger of Allah ﷺ speak about private conversation (najwa)? He said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: The believer draws near to his Lord until He places His kanaf upon him, and makes him acknowledge his sins, saying: "Do you know such-and-such?" He says: "My Lord, forgive" - twice - until when He has brought him to what Allah willed, He says: "Indeed I concealed them for you in the world, and I forgive them for you today." He said: He is given his book of good deeds - or his book - in his right hand. As for the disbelievers and hypocrites, they are called out against upon the heads of witnesses: "These are the ones who lied against their Lord. Surely the curse of Allah is upon the wrongdoers" [Surah Hud: 18].

[Note: On the hadith: Sa'id is Ibn Abi Arubah, the reliable, trustworthy, memorizing scholar. Hisham is Ibn Abi Abdullah al-Dastuwa'i. In the printed edition it reads: "Ibn Abi Adi related to us, and Sa'id, and Hisham," which is an error. The correct reading is "on the authority of Sa'id," because Ibn Abi Adi, who is Muhammad ibn Ibrahim, narrates from Ibn Abi Arubah and from Hisham al-Dastuwa'i; he is not of their generation, and he did not live to narrate from Qatadah. Likewise Ibn Bashshar, who is Muhammad ibn Bashshar, the teacher of al-Tabari, narrates from Ibn Abi Adi and his generation, and did not live to narrate from Ibn Abi Arubah and al-Dastuwa'i. Also, his phrase in the isnad after the transfer to Ibn Ulayyah from Hisham, "both said in their narration," refers to the dual pronoun for Sa'id and Hisham, excluding Ibn Abi Adi; for had he been with them, it would have said "they all said." Moreover, it is established that it is "on the authority of Sa'id" in Ibn Kathir's transmission of this hadith from this place (2/84), although another printing error occurs there: it reads "on the authority of Sa'id ibn Hisham" in place of "and Hisham." And after Ibn Ulayyah it reads "Ibn Hisham related to us," adding "ibn," an addition that is an unacceptable error. Then, the hadith will come in Tafsir al-Tabari (12/14, Bulaq) with this isnad, correctly. But he made it there two isnads, separating the isnad of Ibn Ulayyah from that of Ibn Abi Adi. The hadith was narrated by Ahmad in al-Musnad (5436), from Bahz and Affan, both from Hammam (Ibn Yahya), from Qatadah, with this isnad. He also narrated it (5825) from Abd al-Wahhab ibn Ata, from Sa'id, that is Ibn Abi Arubah, from Qatadah. al-Bukhari (5/70, Fath) and Muslim (2/329) both narrated it through Hisham al-Dastuwa'i, from Qatadah. al-Bukhari also narrated it (8/266-267) through Sa'id ibn Abi Arubah and Hisham al-Dastuwa'i, from Qatadah. He also narrated it (10/406-407 and 13/397-398) through Abu Awanah, from Qatadah. Abu Ja'far ibn al-Nahhas narrated it in Kitab al-Nasikh wa'l-Mansukh, pp. 86-87, through Ibn Ulayyah, from Hisham, and said: "Its isnad is an isnad in which no doubt can enter the heart, and it is among the hadiths of the People of the Sunnah and the Community." Ibn Kathir mentioned it (2/84-85), as we said earlier, from this place in al-Tabari. He also mentioned it (4/353) from the first narration in the Musnad. al-Suyuti mentioned it (3/325) and added its attribution to Ibn al-Mubarak, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi in al-Asma' wa'l-Sifat. al-Qastallani (4/206) attributed it to al-Nasa'i in al-Tafsir and al-Raqa'iq, and to Ibn Majah in al-Sunnah. In the manuscript here it reads "wa-amma al-kuffar aw al-munafiqun," which is a clear error.] [Surah Hud: 18].

* *

= That Allah does to His believing servant: [Note: The construction of this sentence follows the two earlier reports: "as has reached us from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ... that Allah does to His believing servant...", so the phrase "that Allah does" is the subject of "reached us".] by making him know the bad deeds of his actions, until He makes him know His favour toward him by His pardon for them. Likewise is His action, exalted be His remembrance, in calling him to account for what He has shown of himself and for what He has concealed of that; then He forgives him all of it after making him know His favour and generosity toward him, and He covers it over for him. That is the forgiveness which Allah promised His believing servants when He said: "He forgives whom He wills." [Note: In the printed edition: "yaghfiru liman yasha'" without a fa'; I have kept the text of the verse as it is in the manuscript.]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: If someone says: Surely His words, "It has what it earned and it bears what it acquired," indicate that all creation is not held to account except for what their souls have earned of sin, nor rewarded except for what they have earned of good?

It is said: That is so, and the servant is not held to account for anything of that except by doing what he was forbidden to do, or leaving what he was commanded to do.

If he says: Since that is so, what is the meaning of Allah's threat to us over what our souls conceal, by His words: "and He punishes whom He wills," if it is the case that "it has what it earned and it bears what it acquired," and what our hearts harbour and our souls conceal, of resolving upon a sin or intending disobedience, which our limbs have not earned?

It is said to him: Allah, mighty is His praise, has promised the believers that He will pardon them for what is greater than what any of them resolved upon of sins without doing it, namely what we have mentioned of His promise to them of forgiveness of minor sins if they avoid major ones. The threat from Allah, mighty and majestic, in His words "and He punishes whom He wills" is upon what the souls of those whose souls concealed doubt about Allah and uncertainty about His oneness, or about the prophethood of His Prophet ﷺ and what he brought from Allah, or about the return and resurrection, from among the hypocrites, in the manner that Ibn Abbas and Mujahid said, and whoever said the like of their saying, that the interpretation of His words "or conceal it, Allah will call you to account for it" concerns doubt and certainty. [Note: The sentence: "upon what the souls of those whose souls concealed doubt about Allah... from among the hypocrites", with the intervening descriptions separating them.]

Yet we say that the one threatened by "and He punishes whom He wills" is the one whose souls conceal doubt and uncertainty about Allah [Note: "doubt and uncertainty..." is the predicate of "kana".], and in which doubt about Allah is disbelief; and the one promised forgiveness by "He forgives whom He wills" is the one whose concealment is the resolve to advance upon some of what Allah forbade, of matters that were originally permissible to make lawful and allowed, but which He forbade to His creation, mighty is His praise, [Note: "or upon leaving..." is joined to the earlier phrase "by advancing upon some of what He forbade..."] or upon leaving some of what Allah commanded to be done, which was originally permissible to leave, but He made its doing obligatory upon His creation. For the one among the believers who resolves upon that, if he does not carry out his resolve and make real what his soul concealed of it by advancing upon it, he is not taken to account for it, as is related from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that he said:

6498 - "Whoever resolves upon a good deed and does not do it, a good deed is written for him; and whoever resolves upon an evil deed and does not do it, it is not written against him." [Note: On the report: al-Tabari did not mention its isnad. Hadiths of Allah's pardon for the stirrings of the soul are in Muslim (2/146-152) with other wording, and then the rest of the books of Sunnah.]

* *

This, then, is what we have described: it is what Allah calls the believing servants to account for, and then does not punish them for. As for the one whose souls conceal doubt about Allah and suspicion about the prophethood of His prophets, that is the one who is destroyed, abiding in the Fire, to whom His mighty and majestic praise promised the painful punishment by His words: "and He punishes whom He wills."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: So the interpretation of the verse is: "Whether you show what is in your souls," O people, so that you reveal it, "or conceal it," so that your souls hold it within, "Allah will call you to account for it," so that your believer knows His favour in pardoning him for it and forgiving him, so He forgives him, and He punishes your hypocrite for the doubt which his soul harboured about the oneness of his Creator and the prophethood of His prophets. [Note: In the manuscript: "fa-ya'rifu mu'minikum... wa-yu'adhdhibu munafiqikum" in the plural, while the printed one is more correct and better.]

* *

On the interpretation of His words, exalted be He: "And Allah is over all things Competent" (284)

Abu Ja'far said: By this, His words, mighty and majestic, mean: And Allah, mighty and majestic, is Competent — over pardoning what this believer's soul concealed of the resolve toward sin, and over punishing this disbeliever for what his soul concealed of doubt about the oneness of Allah, mighty and majestic, and the prophethood of His prophets, and over recompensing each of them for all that was from him, and over other matters besides.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 285:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, saying: ﴿The Messenger believes in what has been sent down to him from his Lord, and the believers. Each one believes in God, His angels, His books, and His messengers.﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: By this, may His praise be majestic, He means: the Messenger affirms it, meaning the Messenger of God ﷺ, so he acknowledges "what has been sent down to him", meaning: what was revealed to him from his Lord of the Book, and what is in it of lawful and unlawful, promise and threat, command and prohibition, and other than that of the various meanings it contains.

* *

It is mentioned that when this verse was revealed to the Messenger of God ﷺ, he said: "It is right for him."

6499 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: "The Messenger believes in what has been sent down to him from his Lord." It has been related to us that when this verse was revealed, the Prophet of God ﷺ said: "It is right for him to believe." [[The report: 6499 - Al-Hakim, in al-Mustadrak 2: 287, narrated through Khallad ibn Yahya, from Abu Aqil, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from Anas, who said: "When this verse was revealed upon the Prophet ﷺ: 'The Messenger believes in what has been sent down to him from his Lord,' the Prophet ﷺ said: 'And it is more fitting for him to believe.'" Then al-Hakim said: "This is a sound hadith according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs, though they did not record it." Al-Dhahabi objected to it, saying: "Munqati' (disconnected)."]]

* *

It has also been said that it was revealed after His saying: "Whether you show what is in your souls or conceal it, God will call you to account for it. He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills, and God has power over all things." This is because the believers among His Companions, who were with the Messenger of God, were distressed by what God had threatened them with regarding being held to account for what their souls concealed. They complained of that to the Prophet ﷺ, and the Messenger of God ﷺ said to them: "Perhaps you say: 'We hear and we disobey,' as the Children of Israel said!" They said: "Rather, we say: 'We hear and we obey!'" So God revealed, on account of that, from the saying of the Prophet ﷺ and his Companions: "The Messenger believes in what has been sent down to him from his Lord, and the believers. Each one believes in God, His angels, His books, and His messengers," meaning: the believers also affirmed, along with their Prophet, belief in God, His angels, His books, and His messengers, [the two verses]. We have already mentioned those who said this earlier. [[See what preceded, no. 6477.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The readers differed regarding the recitation of His saying: "wa-kutubihi" (and His books).

The majority of the readers of Medina and some of the readers of Iraq recited ﴿wa-kutubihi﴾ in the plural form of "the Book", with the meaning: "and the believers, each one believes in God, His angels, and all His books that He sent down to His prophets and messengers."

* *

A group of the readers of Kufa recited ﴿wa-kitabihi﴾ (and His Book), meaning: "and the believers, each one believes in God, His angels, and the Qur'an that He sent down to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ."

* *

It has been related from Ibn 'Abbas that he used to recite it as "wa-kitabihi," and he would say: "The Book (kitab) is more inclusive than the books (kutub)." It seems Ibn 'Abbas directed the interpretation of this toward something like His saying: ﴿By time, indeed mankind is in loss﴾ [Surah al-'Asr: 1-2], with the meaning of the category of "mankind" and the category of "the Book," as one says: "How abundant is so-and-so's dirham and dinar," meaning the category of dirhams and dinars. [[See what preceded, 4: 263.]] And this, though it is a well-known position among the positions, the reading I find more preferable is to recite it in the plural form. Because what precedes it is plural, and what follows it is likewise—I mean: "and His angels, and His books, and His messengers"—so attaching "books" to the plural in wording is more preferable to me than making it singular and expressing it in the singular form, so that it conforms in both wording and meaning to what precedes and follows it.

* *

Interpretation of His, may He be exalted, saying: ﴿We make no distinction between any of His messengers﴾

Abu Ja'far said: As for His saying: "We make no distinction between any of His messengers," He, may His praise be majestic, informed concerning the believers that they say this. In the reading of one who recites "We make no distinction between any of His messengers" with the "nun" (we), there is an omitted element, which is understood from what has been mentioned. That omitted element is "they say." The meaning of the statement is: "And the believers, each one believes in God, His angels, His books, and His messengers, saying: We make no distinction between any of His messengers." The mention of "they say" was omitted because the context indicates it, just as it was omitted in His saying: ﴿And the angels enter upon them from every gate: Peace be upon you, for you have been patient﴾ [Surah al-Ra'd: 23-24], meaning: they say: "Peace."

* *

Some of the earlier authorities also read it: ﴿lā yufarriqu bayna aḥadin min rusulihi﴾ with the "ya" (he), meaning: "and the believers, all of them, believe in God, His angels, His books, and His messengers; none of them makes a distinction between any of His messengers, believing in some and disbelieving in others. Rather, they affirm all of them, and acknowledge that what they brought was from God, and that they called to God and to obedience to Him. In this action they differ from the Jews, who acknowledged Moses and denied Jesus, and the Christians, who acknowledged Moses and Jesus and denied Muhammad ﷺ, rejecting his prophethood, and from those similar to them among the nations who denied some of God's messengers and affirmed others," as:

6500 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: "We make no distinction between any of His messengers," as the people did—meaning the Children of Israel—they said: "So-and-so is a prophet, and so-and-so is not a prophet; so-and-so we believe in, and so-and-so we do not believe in."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The recitation we do not permit any other than in this matter, according to us, is with the "nun": "We make no distinction between any of His messengers," because it is the recitation whose proof is established by widespread transmission, which precludes collusion, conspiracy, error, or mistake [[In the printed edition: "tasha'ur" with a dotted ghayn, which is an error. The correct reading is from the manuscript: "tasha'ur al-amr" meaning to agree upon something among themselves, from "sha'ara" meaning "to know." This word is rarely found in lexicons but is common in al-Tabari and his earlier contemporaries.]], in the sense of what we described: they say "We make no distinction between any of His messengers," and one does not object with an anomalous reading, against what the proof has brought down by transmission and inheritance. [[In the printed edition: "naql wa riwaya"; in the manuscript "naql wa wirathah," which is correct.]]

* *

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, saying: ﴿And they say: We hear and we obey. Your forgiveness, our Lord, and to You is the final return﴾ (285)

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His praise be majestic, He means: all the believers said: "We hear" the word of our Lord and His command to us with what He commanded us, and His prohibition of what He forbade us, "and we obey," meaning: we obey our Lord in what He obligated upon us of His duties, and what He enslaved us to of His obedience, and we submit to Him. And His saying: "Your forgiveness, our Lord," means: they said: "Your forgiveness, our Lord," meaning: "Forgive us, our Lord, Your forgiveness," just as one says "Glory to You" (subhanaka), meaning: "We glorify You, Glory to You."

* *

We have already explained earlier that "forgiveness" (ghufran) and "pardon" (maghfirah) mean God's covering over the sins of the one forgiven, and His pardoning him from exposure of his concealed faults in this world and the next, and His pardon from punishment.

* *

As for His saying: "And to You is the final return," He means, may His praise be majestic, that they said: "And to You, O our Lord, is our return and our resurrection, so forgive us our sins."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: If someone asks us: What is it that put "forgiveness" (ghufranaka) in the accusative?

It is said to him: Its position is that of a verbal noun that stands in the place of a command. The Arabs do this with verbal nouns and nouns when they occupy the place of the imperative and convey the sense of the command; they put them in the accusative, saying: "Thanks to God, O so-and-so," and "Praise to Him," meaning: "Thank God and praise Him." And "Prayer, prayer!" meaning: "Pray!" And they say of nouns: "God, God, O people!" If it were in the nominative, with the meaning "He is God," or "This is God"—directed toward a statement that contains the sense of a command—it would be permissible, as the poet said: [[I do not know the speaker.]]

Indeed, a people among them are 'Umayr, and Ashba... (Umayr and...), and among them is al-Saffah [[Ma'ani al-Qur'an by al-Farra' 1: 188, and al-'Ayni's shawahid (in the margin of al-Khizanah) 4: 306. I was unable to identify "'Umayr" and "al-Saffah," as they are common names.]] — they are worthy of fulfilling covenants when the man of valor calls: "The weapon! The weapon!"

And if His saying "Your forgiveness, our Lord" had come in the nominative in recitation, it would not have been an error, but would have been correct according to what we have described. [[Much of this is from Ma'ani al-Qur'an by al-Farra' 1: 188.]]

* *

It has been mentioned that when this verse was revealed upon the Messenger of God ﷺ as praise from God to him and to his community, Jibril ﷺ said to him: "Indeed God, mighty and majestic, has bestowed good praise upon you and your community, so ask your Lord."

6501 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Bayan, from Hakim ibn Jabir, who said: When this was revealed upon the Messenger of God ﷺ: "The Messenger believes in what has been sent down to him from his Lord, and the believers. Each one believes in God, His angels, His books, and His messengers. We make no distinction between any of His messengers. And they say: We hear and we obey. Your forgiveness, our Lord, and to You is the final return," Jibril said: "Indeed God, mighty and majestic, has bestowed good praise upon you and upon your community, so ask, and You will be given!" So he asked: "God does not burden any soul beyond its capacity," up to the end of the surah. [[The hadith: 6501 - Bayan is Ibn Bishr al-Ahmasi, whose biography has passed at 259. "Hakim ibn Jabir ibn Tariq ibn 'Awf al-Ahmasi": a major, trustworthy Successor, who narrated mursal from the Prophet ﷺ. He narrated from his father, 'Umar, Ibn Mas'ud, Talhah, and 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit. Ismail ibn Abi Khalid and Bayan narrated from him. Trustworthy. He died at the end of al-Hajjaj's governorship; it is said in 82, and it is said in 95. Biography in al-Tahdhib and al-Kabir 2/1/12. He explicitly stated that he heard 'Umar.

So this hadith is mursal.

Al-Suyuti mentioned it at 1: 376, and attributed it also to Sa'id ibn Mansur and Ibn Abi Hatim.

Ibn Kathir transmitted it at 2: 89 from this place in al-Tabari, but there is a distortion in the chain, from a copyist or printer—thus: "from Sinan, from Hakim, from Jabir"; so the chain appears to indicate that it is a continuous hadith from the narration of Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah the Companion. It should be corrected from this place.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 286 (part 1 of 2):

The explanation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His praise be exalted, He means: Allah does not burden a soul with worship except with what it can bear, so He does not constrict it or exhaust it.
* *
We have already explained earlier that "al-wus‘" (capacity) is a noun derived from the saying of the speaker, "This matter was within my capacity" (wasi‘anī hādhā al-amr), like "al-juhd" (exertion) and "al-wajd" (ability) from "jahadanī hādhā al-amr" (this matter exhausted me) and "wajadtu minhu" (I found it within reach). [[See what preceded at 5:45.]] As in:

6502 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: ʿAbd Allah narrated to us, saying: Muʿawiya narrated to me, from ʿAli, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His words: "Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity," he said: They are the believers; Allah made their religious affairs easy for them, and so the Mighty and Majestic One said: ﴿And He has not placed upon you any difficulty in religion﴾ [Surah al-Hajj: 78], and He said: ﴿Allah intends for you ease and does not intend for you hardship﴾ [Surah al-Baqarah: 185], and He said: ﴿So fear Allah as much as you are able﴾ [Surah al-Taghabun: 16]. [[In the manuscript and printed edition: "Fear Allah..." and I have restored the reading of the Qur'anic text.]]

6503 - Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from al-Zuhri, from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAbbas, who said: When it was revealed, the believers were thrown into a great uproar and said: "O Messenger of Allah, we are to repent of the deeds of the hand, the foot and the tongue! [[His words "hādhā natūbu..." are an eloquent expression used in astonishment; it has also come in poetry, but its exact place has now escaped me and I have not found it.]] How can we repent of whispering (al-waswasa)? How can we refrain from it?" Then Jibril (peace be upon him) brought this verse: "Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity," [to say]: You cannot refrain from whispering.

6504 - Musa narrated to me, saying: ʿAmr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity": wus‘ahā means its ability. And the inner speech of the soul was something they could not bear. [[In the printed edition: "what they cannot bear"; I have restored what is in the manuscript.]]
* *
The explanation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿It earns what it has earned, and against it is what it has earned﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His words, may His praise be exalted, "lahā" (for it) He means: for the soul concerning which He informed that He does not burden it beyond its capacity. He says: for every soul is what it has committed and done of good, "and against it" meaning: and against every soul, "is what it has earned", what it has done of evil. [[See the explanation of "al-kasb" and "al-iktisab" in what preceded at 2:273, 274 / then 3:100, 101, 128, 129 / then 4:449.]] As in:

6505 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatada regarding His words: "Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity: it has what it has earned," that is, of good, "and against it is what it has earned," that is, of evil, or he said: of bad.

6506 - Musa narrated to me, saying: ʿAmr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "It has what it has earned": he says: what it has done of good; "and against it is what it has earned": he says: and against it is what it has done of evil.

6507 - It was narrated to me from ʿAmmar, who said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, from his father, from Qatada, the like of it.

6508 - Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from al-Zuhri, from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAbbas: "It has what it has earned and against it is what it has earned": the deeds of the hand, the foot and the tongue.
* *
Abu Ja'far said: The interpretation of the verse, then, is: Allah does not burden a soul except with what it can bear, so He does not exhaust it, nor constrict it in matters of its religion, so that He would hold it accountable for an aspiration if it aspires, nor for a whisper if it arises in it, nor for a passing thought if it passes through its heart.
* *
The explanation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿Our Lord, do not impose blame upon us if we forget or make mistakes﴾

Abu Ja'far said: This is Allah, may He be exalted, teaching His believing servants how to supplicate Him and what they should say in their supplication to Him. Its meaning: Say: "Our Lord, do not hold us accountable if we forget" something You have obligated upon us to do and we did not do it, "or make mistakes" in doing something You forbade us from doing and we did it, not intentionally seeking to disobey You, but out of ignorance of it and error, as in:

6509 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words: "Our Lord, do not impose blame upon us if we forget or make mistakes": if we forget something of what You have made obligatory upon us, or make mistakes, [and so commit] something of what You have forbidden us. [[The words in brackets are a supplement, which the sense almost requires.]]

6510 - Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Maʿmar informed us, from Qatada regarding His words: "Our Lord, do not impose blame upon us if we forget or make mistakes," he said: It has reached me that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has overlooked for this community their forgetfulness and what their souls whisper about. [[Narration 6510: Muslim recorded it in his Sahih (2:146, 147) through several chains, from Qatada, from Zurara ibn Awfa, from Abu Hurayra, with the wording: "Indeed Allah has overlooked for my community what their souls whisper about, so long as they do not speak or act upon it."]]

6511 - Musa narrated to me, saying: ʿAmr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, saying: al-Suddi claimed that when this verse was revealed, "Our Lord, do not impose blame upon us if we forget or make mistakes," Jibril (peace be upon him) said to him: Then say that, O Muhammad.
* *
Abu Ja'far said: If someone says to us: Is it permissible for Allah, may He be exalted, to hold His servants accountable for what they forgot or made mistakes in, so that they would ask Him not to hold them accountable for that?

It is said: "Forgetfulness" is of two kinds: one is by way of the servant's neglect and negligence, and the other by way of the forgetful person's inability to retain what he was entrusted with and charged to keep, and the weakness of his intellect in bearing it.

As for what occurs from the servant by way of his neglect and negligence, it is his abandonment of what he was commanded to do. That is what the servant desires that God, may He be exalted, not hold him accountable for, and it is the "forgetfulness" with which Allah, may He be exalted, punished Adam, peace be upon him, causing him to leave Paradise, saying regarding it: ﴿And We had already taken a covenant from Adam before, but he forgot, and We found in him no determination﴾ [Surah Ta-Ha: 115]. And it is the "forgetfulness" of which His praise said: ﴿So today We forget them as they forgot the meeting of this day of theirs﴾ [Surah al-A‘raf: 51]. So the servant's plea to Allah, may He be exalted, with his words "Our Lord, do not hold us accountable if we forget or make mistakes," concerns forgetting what he was commanded to do in the manner we described, as long as his leaving it was not, in that, a negligence and neglect on his part, as disbelief in Allah, may He be exalted. For if that were disbelief in Allah, then asking Allah not to hold him accountable for it is impermissible, because Allah, may He be exalted, has informed His servants that He does not forgive them for associating others with Him, so asking Him to do what He has informed them He will not do is a mistake. Rather, the request for forgiveness is appropriate only for something like forgetting the Qur'an after memorizing it through preoccupation with other things and not reciting it, or forgetting a prayer or a fast through being occupied with other things until he neglected them.

As for what the servant is not held accountable for, due to his mind's inability to retain it and the weakness of his intellect in bearing what he was charged to safeguard, that is not disobedience on the servant's part, and he is not sinful for it. That is what there is no point in the servant asking his Lord to forgive him, for it is asking Him to forgive him for what is not a sin for him. This is like a matter that overcomes a person while he is eager to remember and retain it, such as a man who diligently strives to memorize the Qur'an and recites it, then forgets it without being preoccupied with something else, but due to his mind's inability to retain it and the weakness of his intellect in recalling what was deposited in his heart, and similar forgetfulness. Such forgetfulness is one for which it is impermissible to ask the Lord to forgive, because the servant has no sin in it for which he would be forgiven through his acquisition.
* *
Likewise, "mistake" has two aspects:

One: that which concerns something the servant was forbidden, and he commits it deliberately and willingly. That is a mistake on his part, and he is held accountable for it. It is said of him: "Khati'a fulan wa-akhta'a" (so-and-so erred and made a mistake) regarding the act he did, and "athima" (he sinned) if he commits what makes him sinful and engages in it. Among its usage is the verse of the poet: [[He is ʿUbayd ibn al-Abras al-Asadi; in the Hamasa of al-Buhturi, p. 236, it is "ʿUbayd ibn Mansur al-Asadi," which appears to be an error.]]

"The people blame the ruler when they ... err from what is right, and the guide is not blamed."

[[His Diwan: 54; Hamasa al-Buhturi 236; and al-Lisan (amr). The version in his Diwan reads: "The people blame the ruler when he goes astray ... departs from what is right..." The version in al-Lisan is as it appears in al-Tabari. Lahā yalḥāhu: he blamed and rebuked him. al-Amir: the one in command over them, who commands them and they obey him. al-Murshid (passive participle): one whom Allah has guided to what is right. It resembles the saying of al-Qatami: "And people, whoever meets him with good, they say to him what he desires, but may the mother of the one who errs be bereaved."]]

That is, they erred from the right. This is the aspect in which the servant seeks his Lord's pardon for whatever sin resulted from it, except what was disbelief.

The other: that which occurs through ignorance of it and the servant's supposition that it is permissible for him to do, such as one who eats at night in Ramadan while thinking that dawn has not yet risen, or who delays a prayer on a cloudy day while awaiting its time to enter, and then the time passes while he thinks its time has not yet entered. This is among the mistakes lifted from the servant, for which Allah, may He be exalted, has removed sin from His servants, so there is no point in the servant asking his Lord not to hold him accountable for it.
* *
Some people claimed that the servant's request to his Lord not to hold him accountable for what he forgot or erred in is only an act on his part in obedience to what his Lord commanded, or to what He encouraged him toward, namely humility before Him and submission in asking. As for asking for pardon in the sense of overlooking, they hold that it has no basis.

To clarify the position of these people there is a book, which we will come to, if Allah wills, in which we will cover what is sufficient for whoever is granted understanding of it.
* *
The explanation of His words, may He be exalted: ﴿Our Lord, and do not lay upon us a burden as You laid it upon those before us﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His praise be exalted, He means: Say: "Our Lord, do not lay upon us a burden," and by "al- işr" (burden) He means the covenant, as His praise said: ﴿He said, "Do you acknowledge and accept My commitment (işrī) on that?"﴾ [Surah Al ʿImran: 81]. He only meant by His words "and do not lay upon us a burden" (işran): do not lay upon us a covenant so that we would be unable to fulfill it and would not be able to do it, "as You laid it upon those before us," meaning upon the Jews and Christians, who were charged with deeds and had their covenants and pledges taken to carry them out, but they did not do so, and so they were hastened with punishment. So Allah, may He be exalted, taught the community of Muhammad (ﷺ) to plead with Him, asking that He not burden them with covenants and pledges, concerning deeds, which if they neglect, err in, or forget, would bring upon them what was brought upon those before them, through their error in it and neglect of it.
* *
Those who interpret the Qur'an have said something similar to what we have said.

Those who said so:

6512 - Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Maʿmar informed us, from Qatada regarding "do not lay upon us a burden," he said: Do not lay upon us a covenant and pledge, as You laid it upon those before us, meaning: as You made it severe upon those before us.

6513 - Ibn Wakiʿ narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Musa ibn Qays al-Hadrami, from Mujahid regarding His words: "Do not lay upon us a burden," he said: a covenant.
[[Narration 6513: "Musa ibn Qays al-Hadrami," al-Farra', al-Kufi, nicknamed "ʿUsfur al-Janna." He narrated from Salama ibn Kuhayl, Muhammad ibn ʿAjlan, Muslim al-Batin and others. Narrated from him Waki', Yahya ibn Adam, Abu Nuʿaym and others. Ahmad said: "I know nothing but good of him." Ibn Saʿd said: "He narrated little." Ibn Maʿin judged him reliable. al-ʿUqayli said: "He was among the extremists in Rafd... he narrates strange or false hadiths." Biography in al-Tahdhib.]]

6514 - Al-Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, from ʿIsa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding His words "işran," he said: a covenant.

6515 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: ʿAbd Allah narrated to us, saying: Muʿawiya narrated to us, from ʿAli, from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding His words "işran," he says: a covenant.

6516 - Musa narrated to me, saying: ʿAmr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "Our Lord, do not lay upon us a burden as You laid it upon those before us": al-işr is the covenant that was upon those before us from the Jews.

6517 - Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj regarding His words: "Do not lay upon us a burden," he said: a covenant we cannot bear and cannot undertake, "as You laid it upon those before us," the Jews and Christians, who did not fulfill it, so You destroyed them.

6518 - Yahya ibn Abi Talib narrated to me, saying: Yazid informed us, saying: Juwaybir informed us, from al-Dahhak: "işran," he said: the pledges.

6519 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd Allah ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabiʿ: "al-Işr" is the covenant. [And "and you took upon that My covenant (işrī)" (Al ʿImran: 81)], he said: my covenant.

6520 - Muhammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas: "And you took upon that My covenant (işrī)," he said: my covenant.

Others said: "The meaning of that is: do not lay upon us sins and wrongdoing, as You laid that upon the nations before us, so that You transform us into apes and swine as You transformed them."

Those who said so:

6521 - Husayn ibn ʿAmr al-Sakuni narrated to me, saying: Baqiyya ibn al-Walid narrated to us, from ʿAli ibn Harun, from Ibn Jurayj, from ʿAta' ibn Abi Rabah regarding His words "do not lay upon us a burden as You laid it upon those before us," he said: Do not transform us into apes and swine. [[Narration 6521: "Saʿid ibn ʿAmr al-Sakuni," whose biography was given at no. 5563. As for "ʿAli ibn Harun," I have not found him, and I suspect the correct name is "Yazid ibn Harun"; "Baqiyya ibn al-Walid" narrates from "Yazid ibn Harun" and died before him. All of them are in al-Tahdhib.]]

6522 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words "Our Lord, and do not lay upon us a burden as You laid it upon those before us": Do not lay upon us a sin for which there is no repentance or expiation.
* *
Others said: "The meaning of al-işr with a kasra on the alif is: the weight."

Those who said so:

6523 - It was narrated to me from ʿAmmar, who said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabiʿ regarding His words: "Our Lord, and do not lay upon us a burden as You laid it upon those before us," he says: the harshness You imposed on the People of the Book before us.

6524 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: I asked him, meaning Malik, about His words "and do not lay upon us a burden," and he said: al-işr is a severe command.
* *
Abu Ja'far said: As for "al-aṣr" with a fatha on the alif: it is what inclines a man toward another through kinship or relationship. It is said: "Asarathni rahm bayni wa-bayn fulan 'alayhi" (a bond of kinship between me and so-and-so inclined me toward him), meaning: it inclined me toward him. "Wa-ma ya'sirunī 'alayh" means: what inclines me toward it. "Wa-baynī wa-baynahu āṣiratu raḥimin ta'ṣiruhū 'alayh aṣran" means: a tie of kinship that inclines me toward him. [[In the manuscript and printed edition: "wa-baynī wa-baynahu aṣr raḥim ya'ṣiruhū 'alayh"; the flow of his explanation requires what the lexicons record, which is what I have adopted here.]]
* *
The explanation of His words: ﴿Our Lord, and do not burden us with what we have no ability to bear﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His praise be exalted, He means: And say also: "Our Lord, do not impose upon us deeds which we cannot bear, because of their heavy weight upon us."

Thus the community of the interpreters used to explain it.

Those who said so:

6525 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada: "Our Lord, and do not burden us with what we have no ability to bear": a severity by which He imposes hardship, as He imposed it on those who were before you.

6526 - Yahya ibn Abi Talib narrated to me, saying: Yazid informed us, saying: Juwaybir informed us, from al-Dahhak regarding His words: "and do not burden us with what we have no ability to bear," he said: do not burden us with deeds we cannot bear.

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 2, verse 286 (part 2 of 2):**

6527: Yunus told me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words, ﴿Our Lord, and do not burden us with what we have no ability to bear﴾: "Do not impose upon us of the religion what we have no ability to bear, so that we become unable to do it."

6528: Al-Qasim told us, saying: al-Husayn told us, saying: Hajjaj told me, from Ibn Jurayj, regarding ﴿and do not burden us with what we have no ability to bear﴾: "The transformation into apes and swine."

6529: Salam ibn Salim al-Khuza'i told me, saying: Abu Hafs Umar ibn Sa'id al-Tanukhi told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Shu'ayb ibn Shapur told us, from Salim ibn Shapur, regarding His words, ﴿Our Lord, and do not burden us with what we have no ability to bear﴾, he said: "al-Ghulma."

[Editor's note on the report 6529: Salam ibn Salim al-Khuza'i has had his biography given earlier, under number 252. As for Abu Hafs Umar ibn Sa'id al-Tanukhi, he is "Umar ibn Sa'id ibn Sulayman, Abu Hafs al-Qurashi al-Dimashqi," the transmitter of Sa'id ibn Abd al-Aziz al-Tanukhi, and it seems he was ascribed to him. He related from Muhammad ibn Shu'ayb ibn Shapur. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib and in Tarikh Baghdad (11: 200). As for "Muhammad ibn Shu'ayb ibn Shapur" al-Dimashqi, he is one of the great authorities. He related from al-Awza'i, Sa'id ibn Abd al-Aziz al-Tanukhi, and others. He resided in Beirut, and Ibn Hibban mentioned him among the trustworthy (al-thiqat). He died in the year 200.
Al-ghulma: the surging of the desire for sexual intercourse in men and women.]

6530: Musa told me, saying: Amr told us, saying: Asbat told us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿Our Lord, and do not burden us with what we have no ability to bear﴾: "[It refers to] the severities and the shackles that were upon them from the prohibitions."

\* \*

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: We have said that the interpretation of this is: "And do not impose upon us of the actions what we cannot bear to carry out," in the manner of what we have said regarding it, because it follows the believers' supplication to their Lord that He not take them to task if they forget or err, and that He not lay upon them a burden (isr) as He laid it upon those before them. Thus, linking this to the meaning of what precedes it, namely their request for ease in the religion, is more appropriate than contradicting that meaning.

\* \*

The discussion of the interpretation of His words: ﴿And pardon us and forgive us﴾

Abu Ja'far said: In this also, from the words of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, reporting of the believers' request of Him for that, there is clear evidence that they asked Him to ease His obligations upon them by His words, ﴿and do not burden us with what we have no ability to bear﴾, because they followed that with their saying, ﴿and pardon us﴾, a request from them to their Lord that He pardon them for any shortcoming, if there was any on their part in some of what He commanded them of His obligations, so that He would overlook it for them and not punish them for it, even if His obligations were light upon their bodies.

\* \*

Some of the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) said similarly to what we have said regarding this.

Those who said that:

6531: Yunus told me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding ﴿and pardon us﴾: "Pardon us if we fall short of something of Your command, which You commanded us."

\* \*

Likewise His words, ﴿and forgive us﴾, meaning: "and conceal from us a slip if we commit it between us and You, so do not expose it nor disgrace us by making it public."

\* \*

We have already explained the meaning of "forgiveness" earlier. [Editor's note: see what has preceded recently, 127, 128, note 1, and the references there. See also the language indexes under (gh-f-r).]

\* \*

6532: Yunus told me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: "[And forgive us] if we violate something of what You forbade us."

\* \*

The discussion of the interpretation of His words: ﴿and have mercy upon us﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His praise be exalted, He means: "Cover us with Your mercy by which You rescue us from Your punishment, for none is saved from Your punishment except by Your mercy toward him, apart from his deeds. Our deeds do not save us if You do not show mercy to us. So grant us success in what pleases You with regard to us," as follows:

6533: Yunus told me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words, ﴿and have mercy upon us﴾: "He says: We do not attain to acting upon what You have commanded us, nor to abandoning what You have forbidden us, except by Your mercy." [Editor's note: In the printed edition it reads "lā natruk" (we do not abandon); I have kept what is in the manuscript, which is correct, being governed by his words "tanāl" (attain), conjoined to "al-'amal" (the action).] He said: "And no one is saved except by Your mercy."

\* \*

The discussion of the interpretation of His words: ﴿You are our Protector, so give us victory over the disbelieving people﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His words, may His praise be exalted, "You are our Protector (mawlana)," He means: "You are our Patron (waliyyuna) through Your help, rather than those who oppose You and disbelieve in You, because we are believers in You and obedient to You in what You command and forbid us. So You are the Patron of whoever obeys You, and the enemy of whoever disbelieves in You and disobeys You." ﴿So give us victory﴾, because we are Your party, ﴿over the disbelieving people﴾, who denied Your oneness, worshipped the gods and rivals besides You, and obeyed Satan in disobedience to You.

\* \*

"Al-mawla" in this place is "al-maf'al," from: "Fulan wallā the affair of Fulan, so he takes charge of it (yalīhi) with authority (wilāya), and he is his patron (waliyyuhu) and his protector (mawlāhu)." [Editor's note: see the explanation of "al-wali" and "al-mawla" previously, 2: 489, 564; then 5: 424.] The "yā'" in "wallā" became an "alif" only because the letter before it is open (fatha), and it is the root letter ('ayn) of the word.

\* \*

They mentioned that when Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, sent down this verse upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited it, Allah answered him in all of it.

Mention of the reports that came with that:

6534: Al-Muthanna ibn Ibrahim and Muhammad ibn Khalaf told me, both saying: Adam told us, saying: Warqa' told us, from Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "When this verse was revealed: ﴿The Messenger believes in what has been sent down to him from his Lord﴾, [the Prophet] (ﷺ) recited it, and when he reached His words, ﴿Your forgiveness, our Lord﴾, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: 'I have forgiven you.' When he recited ﴿Our Lord, do not take us to task if we forget or err﴾, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: 'I will not burden you.' When he recited ﴿and forgive us﴾, Allah, blessed and exalted, said: 'I have forgiven you.' When he recited ﴿and have mercy upon us﴾, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: 'I have shown you mercy.' When he recited ﴿and give us victory over the disbelieving people﴾, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: 'I have given you victory over them.'"

[Editor's note on report 6534: Muhammad ibn Khalaf ibn Ammar al-Asqalani, Tabari's teacher: trustworthy, one of the teachers of al-Nasa'i, Ibn Majah, and Ibn Khuzayma. Another transmission of Tabari from him has passed at 126.
Adam: he is Ibn Abi Iyas al-Asqalani, and he is trustworthy and reliable. He was highly esteemed by Shu'ba. His biography has passed at 187.
Warqa': he is Ibn Umar al-Yashkuri, Abu Bishr. He is a trustworthy Kufan, whom Shu'ba praised greatly. The more probable view in my opinion is that Warqa' heard from Ata' in his earlier period, before Ata' changed, because he was one of the early figures of Shu'ba's generation, and because he was a Kufan, and Ata' changed in his final period when he came to Basra.
This hadith by this route, from the transmission of Ata' ibn Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, I have not found in any of the major collections (dawawin) except in the tafsir of al-Tabari. Here he narrates it as marfu' (traced to the Prophet), and later at 6540 he will narrate it similarly as mawquf (ending with Ibn Abbas).
That mawquf report is in reality marfu' in ruling, because it is not something known through opinion or analogy. Thus it supports the soundness of this marfu' report.
Then the raising of the hadith in this isnad is an addition from a trustworthy narrator, so it is accepted.
Indeed this isnad is more probably sound than that one, because Warqa' is early, and we concluded that he heard from Ata' before his change.
As for that isnad, it is from the transmission of Muhammad ibn Fudayl from Ata'. Ibn Fudayl heard from Ata' late, after his change, as Ibn Abi Hatim stated on the authority of his father (3/334).
The meaning of the hadith is established and sound from another route, as has passed at 6457, from the transmission of Adam ibn Sulayman, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas. There, the response after each supplication is "Indeed I have done it." Here the response is from the wording of the supplication. The meaning is one.
It appears that some part of the text of this hadith has dropped out here, by inadvertence of the copyists, at the words: "When he recited: (Our Lord, do not take us to task if we forget or err), Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: 'I will not burden you.'" In the coming transmission: "He said: 'I will not take you to task,'" and then there is mentioned there what follows of the supplication: (Our Lord, and do not lay upon us a burden as You laid it upon those before us), "He said: 'I will not lay it upon you.'" That is the correct and complete context, which shows the deficiency in this context here.
The scribe of the manuscript confused it even more than this, for he repeated in the text of the hadith: "When he reached His words (Your forgiveness, our Lord), Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: 'I have forgiven you'" — twice. Then he dropped the rest of the hadith and did not mention it.]

6535: Yahya ibn Abi Talib told me, saying: Yazid informed us, saying: Juwaybir informed us, from al-Dahhak, who said: "Gabriel came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: 'O Muhammad, say: (Our Lord, do not take us to task if we forget or err).' He said it, and Gabriel said: 'He has done it.' Gabriel said to him: 'Say: (Our Lord, and do not lay upon us a burden as You laid it upon those before us).' He said it, and Gabriel said: 'He has done it.' He said: 'Say: (Our Lord, and do not burden us with what we have no ability to bear).' He said it, and Gabriel (peace be upon him) said: 'He has done it.' He said: 'Say: (And pardon us, and forgive us, and have mercy upon us. You are our Protector, so give us victory over the disbelieving people).' He said it, and Gabriel said: 'He has done it.'"

6536: Musa told me, saying: Amr told us, saying: Asbat told us, who said: "al-Suddi claimed that when this verse was revealed: (Our Lord, do not take us to task if we forget or err), Gabriel said to him: 'Thus has he done it, O Muhammad.'
