(Our Lord, and do not lay upon us a burden as You laid it upon those before us. Our Lord, and do not burden us with what we have no ability to bear. And pardon us, and forgive us, and have mercy upon us. You are our Protector, so give us victory over the disbelieving people), and Gabriel said to him concerning all of that: 'He has done that, O Muhammad.'"

6537: Abu Kurayb told us, saying: Waki' told us, and Sufyan told us, saying: My father told us, from Sufyan, from Adam ibn Sulayman, client of Khalid, who said: "I heard Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: 'Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, sent down: (The Messenger believes in what has been sent down to him from his Lord), up to His words: (Our Lord, do not take us to task if we forget or err).' He recited: (Our Lord, do not take us to task if we forget or err), and He said: 'Indeed I have done it.' (Our Lord, and do not lay upon us a burden as You laid it upon those before us), and He said: 'Indeed I have done it.' (Our Lord, and do not burden us with what we have no ability to bear), and He said: 'Indeed I have done it.' (And pardon us, and forgive us, and have mercy upon us. You are our Protector, so give us victory over the disbelieving people), and He said: 'Indeed I have done it.'"

[Editor's note on report 6537: It is an abridgment of the hadith 6457, with this same isnad. The isnad has been correctly established here, as we pointed out there.]

6538: Abu Kurayb told us, saying: Ishaq ibn Sulayman told us, from Mus'ab ibn Thabit, from al-Ala' ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Ya'qub, from his father, from Abu Hurayra, who said: "Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, sent down: (Our Lord, do not take us to task if we forget or err)," and he said: "My father said: Abu Hurayra said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: Yes.'"

[Editor's note on report 6538: It is an abridgment of the hadith 6456, with this same isnad. We have pointed to it there.]

6539: Ibn Bashshar told us, saying: Abu Ahmad told us, from Sufyan, from Adam ibn Sulayman, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr: "Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity; it shall have [the reward of] what it earned, and it shall bear [the consequence of] what it earned. Our Lord, do not take us to task if we forget or err." He said: "He says: 'Indeed I have done it.'" [And] "Our Lord, and do not lay upon us a burden as You laid it upon those before us." He said: "He says: 'Indeed I have done it.'" Then this ummah was given the closing verses of Surat al-Baqara, which were not given to the nations before it.

[Editor's note on report 6539: It is a mursal hadith (one where the Successor omits the companion). It is part of the earlier hadith 6464, with this same isnad. However, in the manuscript and the printed edition there appears "Abu Humayd" instead of "Abu Ahmad." That is certainly an error, for it is "Abu Ahmad al-Zubayri, Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr," as we explained at 6463.
A blank space occurs in the manuscript between his saying "Abu Humayd" and "Sufyan," and another between his saying "from Sa'id ibn Jubayr" and the verse. It is likely that the scribe was unsure about the words "from Sufyan," and thought it was like the earlier transmission "Sufyan told us," so he left a blank in place of "told us." Then he was unsure of mentioning the verse after the name "Sa'id ibn Jubayr," without a preface like "then this verse was revealed," as in the earlier transmission, so he left a blank for that.]

6540: Ali ibn Harb al-Mawsili told us, saying: Ibn Fudayl told us, saying: Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib told us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, regarding the words of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: "The Messenger believes in what has been sent down to him from his Lord," up to His words: "Your forgiveness, our Lord." He said: "He has forgiven you." ["Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity"] up to His words: "Do not take us to task if we forget or err." He said: "I will not take you to task." ["Our Lord, and do not lay upon us a burden as You laid it upon those before us."] He said: "I will not lay it upon you." Up to His words: "And pardon us, and forgive us, and have mercy upon us. You are our Protector," up to the end of the surah. He said: "I have pardoned you, forgiven you, shown you mercy, and given you victory over the disbelieving people."

[Editor's note on report 6540: Ali ibn Harb ibn Muhammad ibn Ali, Abu al-Hasan al-Ta'i al-Mawsili: trustworthy and firm; al-Daraqutni and others declared him trustworthy. He was knowledgeable in the history of the Arabs, a literary man and poet. al-Nasa'i, Abu Hatim, and his son related from him; his biography is at 3/1/183. He also has a good biography in Tarikh Baghdad 11: 418-240.
This hadith is a repetition of the hadith 6534, in similar wording. This one is mawquf (ending with the companion) in wording but marfu' in meaning, while that one is marfu' in both wording and meaning. That one is more probable in isnad and more sound, as we explained there.
Ibn Kathir (2: 89) mentioned a portion of it from the transmission of Ibn Abi Hatim, from Ali ibn Harb al-Mawsili, with this same isnad. We do not know whether Ibn Abi Hatim related it in this abridged form, or whether Ibn Kathir abridged it.]

\* \*

= He also narrated from al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim that Allah's answering of the Prophet (ﷺ) was specific to him:

6541: I was told on the authority of al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd informed us, who said: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words, ﴿Our Lord, do not take us to task if we forget or err﴾: "Gabriel (peace be upon him) used to say to him: 'Ask it!'" [Editor's note: In the manuscript: "... or erred; Gabriel (peace be upon him) asked it, and the Prophet of Allah ..." and there is a blank in the text, and the printed edition is as you see. As for al-Durr al-Manthur 1: 378, it says: "Ibn Jarir reported from al-Dahhak regarding this verse, he said: Gabriel (peace be upon him) asked it, and the Prophet of Allah asked his Lord..." and the number "3" indicates a gap in the speech. It appears the gap is old in some copies, which is why al-Suyuti left a blank in his copy of al-Durr al-Manthur.] "So the Prophet of Allah asked his Lord, may His praise be exalted, and He gave it to him," [Editor's note: In the manuscript: "so He gave it to him," and I have kept what is in the printed edition, because it agrees with what is in al-Durr al-Manthur.] "and it was specific to the Prophet (ﷺ)."

6542: Al-Muthanna ibn Ibrahim told me, saying: Abu Nu'aym told us, saying: Sufyan told us, from Abu Ishaq: That Mu'adh, whenever he finished this surah, said at "and give us victory over the disbelieving people": "Amin."

[Editor's note on report 6542: It is in Ibn Kathir's tafsir (2: 91) and al-Durr al-Manthur (1: 378), where its takhrij (sourcing) is given.
At the end of the page from the ancient manuscript there is written:
"The end of the tafsir of Surat al-Baqara."
"Praise be to Allah first and last, and may Allah bless Muhammad the Prophet and his family and grant them peace."
"Followed by the tafsir of Surat Al 'Imran. Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds."]

\* \*

The end of the tafsir of Surat al-Baqara.
